[Open Source English Bible] [2023] [OSEN]
[Genesis] [1]:[1] In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
[Genesis] [1]:[2] The earth was formless and empty, darkness lay over the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters.
[Genesis] [1]:[3] And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light.
[Genesis] [1]:[4] God saw that the light was good, and he separated the light from the darkness.
[Genesis] [1]:[5] God called the light day, and the darkness he called night. And there was evening, and there was morning—the first day.
[Genesis] [1]:[6] And God said, "Let there be a vault in the midst of the waters, and let it separate water from water."
[Genesis] [1]:[7] So God made the vault and separated the water under the vault from the water above it. And it was so.
[Genesis] [1]:[8] And God called the vault the heavens. And there was evening, and there was morning—the second day.
[Genesis] [1]:[9] And God said, "Let the waters under the heavens be gathered into one place, and let the dry ground appear." And it was so.
[Genesis] [1]:[10] And God called the dry ground land, and the gathered waters he called seas. And God saw that it was good.
[Genesis] [1]:[11] Then God said, "Let the land bring forth green growth: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit with seed in it, according to its kind, upon the land." And it was so.
[Genesis] [1]:[12] The land brought forth green growth: seed-bearing plants, each according to its kind, and trees bearing fruit with seed in it, each according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
[Genesis] [1]:[13] And there was evening, and there was morning—the third day.
[Genesis] [1]:[14] And God said, "Let there be lights in the vault of the heavens to separate the day from the night, and let them be for signs and for seasons, for days and years,
[Genesis] [1]:[15] and let them be lights in the vault of the heavens to shine on the earth." And it was so.
[Genesis] [1]:[16] God made the two great lights—the greater light to govern the day and the lesser light to govern the night—and he made the stars.
[Genesis] [1]:[17] God set them in the vault of the heavens to shine on the earth,
[Genesis] [1]:[18] to govern the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.
[Genesis] [1]:[19] And there was evening, and there was morning—the fourth day.
[Genesis] [1]:[20] And God said, "Let the waters teem with swarms of living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth across the face of the vault of the heavens."
[Genesis] [1]:[21] So God created the great sea creatures and every living creature that moves, with which the waters teemed, according to their kinds, and every winged bird according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
[Genesis] [1]:[22] God blessed them and said, "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas, and let the birds multiply on the earth."
[Genesis] [1]:[23] And there was evening, and there was morning—the fifth day.
[Genesis] [1]:[24] And God said, "Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, creeping things, and wild animals of the earth, each according to its kind." And it was so.
[Genesis] [1]:[25] And God made the wild animals according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and everything that creeps along the ground according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
[Genesis] [1]:[26] Then God said, "Let us make man in our image, according to our likeness, and let them rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the sky, over the livestock and all the earth, and over every creature that creeps along the ground."
[Genesis] [1]:[27] So God created man in his own image; in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them.
[Genesis] [1]:[28] God blessed them and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply; fill the earth and subdue it. Rule over the fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, and every living thing that moves on the earth."
[Genesis] [1]:[29] And God said, "Look, I have given you every seed-bearing plant on the face of all the earth and every tree that bears fruit with seed in it. They will be your food.
[Genesis] [1]:[30] And to every wild animal of the earth, every bird of the sky, and every creature that moves on the ground—everything that has life in it—I give every green plant for food." And it was so.
[Genesis] [1]:[31] God saw all that he had made, and behold, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day.
[Genesis] [2]:[1] Thus the heavens and the earth were completed, and all their array.
[Genesis] [2]:[2] By the seventh day God had finished the work he had done, and on the seventh day he rested from all the work he had done.
[Genesis] [2]:[3] Then God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it he rested from all the work of creation he had done.
[Genesis] [2]:[4] This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, on the day the LORD God made the earth and the heavens.
[Genesis] [2]:[5] No shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, and no plant of the field had yet sprung up, for the LORD God had not sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to work the ground.
[Genesis] [2]:[6] But a mist would rise from the earth and water the whole surface of the ground.
[Genesis] [2]:[7] Then the LORD God formed the man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the man became a living being.
[Genesis] [2]:[8] And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, toward the east, and there he placed the man he had formed.
[Genesis] [2]:[9] And out of the ground the LORD God made grow every tree pleasing to the sight and good for food, with the tree of life in the middle of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
[Genesis] [2]:[10] Now a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided and became four headwaters.
[Genesis] [2]:[11] The name of the first is Pishon; it winds around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.
[Genesis] [2]:[12] The gold of that land is good; bdellium and onyx are also there.
[Genesis] [2]:[13] The name of the second river is Gihon; it winds around the whole land of Cush.
[Genesis] [2]:[14] The name of the third river is Tigris; it runs east of Asshur. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
[Genesis] [2]:[15] The LORD God took the man and settled him in the garden of Eden to work it and keep it.
[Genesis] [2]:[16] The LORD God commanded the man, "You may freely eat from every tree of the garden,
[Genesis] [2]:[17] but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for on the day you eat from it you will surely die."
[Genesis] [2]:[18] Then the LORD God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him."
[Genesis] [2]:[19] Now the LORD God had formed out of the ground every beast of the field and every bird of the sky, and he brought them to the man to see what he would call them. And whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.
[Genesis] [2]:[20] So the man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the sky, and to every beast of the field. But for himself the man found no suitable helper.
[Genesis] [2]:[21] So the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon the man, and while he slept, he took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh in its place.
[Genesis] [2]:[22] Then the LORD God built the rib that he had taken from the man into a woman, and he brought her to the man.
[Genesis] [2]:[23] And the man said, "This one at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called woman, for she was taken out of man."
[Genesis] [2]:[24] That is why a man leaves his father and mother and holds fast to his wife, and they become one flesh.
[Genesis] [2]:[25] The man and his wife were both naked, and they felt no shame.
[Genesis] [3]:[1] Now the serpent was more cunning than any other creature of the field that the LORD God had made. The serpent said to the woman, "Did God really say you must not eat from any tree in the garden?"
[Genesis] [3]:[2] The woman answered the serpent, "We may eat the fruit of the trees in the garden,
[Genesis] [3]:[3] but about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden God said, 'You must not eat from it or touch it, or you will die.'"
[Genesis] [3]:[4] The serpent said to the woman, "You will certainly not die."
[Genesis] [3]:[5] "For God knows that on the day you eat from it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil."
[Genesis] [3]:[6] The woman saw that the tree was good for food, that it was a delight to the eyes, and that it was desirable for gaining wisdom. So she took some of its fruit and ate, and she gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate.
[Genesis] [3]:[7] Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they knew that they were naked. So they sewed fig leaves together and made loincloths for themselves.
[Genesis] [3]:[8] They heard the sound of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.
[Genesis] [3]:[9] Then the LORD God called to the man and said to him, "Where are you?"
[Genesis] [3]:[10] He answered, "I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid."
[Genesis] [3]:[11] And God said, "Who told you that you are naked? Have you eaten from the tree I commanded you not to eat from?"
[Genesis] [3]:[12] The man said, "The woman you gave to be with me—she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate."
[Genesis] [3]:[13] Then the LORD God said to the woman, "What is this you have done?" The woman answered, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate."
[Genesis] [3]:[14] Then the LORD God said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, cursed are you above all livestock and above every beast of the field. On your belly you shall crawl, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life.
[Genesis] [3]:[15] And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel."
[Genesis] [3]:[16] To the woman he said, "I will greatly increase your pain in childbearing; in pain you will give birth to children. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you."
[Genesis] [3]:[17] And to the man he said, "Because you listened to your wife and ate from the tree about which I commanded you, 'You must not eat from it,' cursed is the ground because of you; through painful labor you will eat of it all the days of your life.
[Genesis] [3]:[18] It will yield thorns and thistles for you, and you will eat the plants of the field.
[Genesis] [3]:[19] By the sweat of your brow you will eat your bread until you return to the ground, since from it you were taken; for dust you are, and to dust you will return."
[Genesis] [3]:[20] The man named his wife Eve, because she would be the mother of all the living.
[Genesis] [3]:[21] And the LORD God made garments of skin for the man and his wife, and clothed them.
[Genesis] [3]:[22] Then the LORD God said, "See, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. And now, he must not reach out his hand and take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever."
[Genesis] [3]:[23] So the LORD God sent him out of the Garden of Eden to work the ground from which he had been taken.
[Genesis] [3]:[24] He drove the man out, and east of the Garden of Eden he stationed the cherubim, and a flaming sword flashing back and forth, to guard the way to the tree of life.
[Genesis] [4]:[1] Now Adam knew his wife Eve, and she conceived and gave birth to Cain. She said, "I have gained a man with the LORD's help."
[Genesis] [4]:[2] Later she gave birth to his brother Abel. Abel became a keeper of sheep, and Cain worked the ground.
[Genesis] [4]:[3] In the course of time Cain brought some of the fruit of the ground as an offering to the LORD,
[Genesis] [4]:[4] and Abel too brought an offering, some of the firstborn of his flock and their fat portions. The LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering,
[Genesis] [4]:[5] but on Cain and his offering he did not look with favor. Cain burned with fierce anger, and his face fell.
[Genesis] [4]:[6] Then the LORD said to Cain, "Why are you angry? Why has your face fallen?
[Genesis] [4]:[7] If you do what is right, will you not be lifted up? But if you do not do what is right, sin is crouching at the door. It desires to have you, but you must master it."
[Genesis] [4]:[8] Cain spoke to his brother Abel. And while they were out in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
[Genesis] [4]:[9] Then the LORD said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" He answered, "I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?"
[Genesis] [4]:[10] The LORD said, "What have you done? Listen—your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground!
[Genesis] [4]:[11] Now you are cursed, driven from the ground that opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.
[Genesis] [4]:[12] When you work the ground, it will no longer yield its strength to you. You will be a restless wanderer on the earth."
[Genesis] [4]:[13] Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is greater than I can bear.
[Genesis] [4]:[14] Look, today you are driving me from the face of the ground, and I will be hidden from your presence. I will be a restless wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."
[Genesis] [4]:[15] Then the LORD said to him, "Therefore, whoever kills Cain will suffer vengeance seven times over." And the LORD put a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would strike him down.
[Genesis] [4]:[16] So Cain went out from the LORD's presence and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
[Genesis] [4]:[17] Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to Enoch. Cain was building a city, and he named it after his son Enoch.
[Genesis] [4]:[18] To Enoch was born Irad, and Irad was the father of Mehujael, and Mehujael was the father of Methushael, and Methushael was the father of Lamech.
[Genesis] [4]:[19] Lamech took two wives for himself; one was named Adah, and the other Zillah.
[Genesis] [4]:[20] Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who live in tents and keep livestock.
[Genesis] [4]:[21] His brother's name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play the lyre and the pipe.
[Genesis] [4]:[22] Zillah also gave birth to Tubal-Cain, who forged all kinds of tools out of bronze and iron. Tubal-Cain's sister was Naamah.
[Genesis] [4]:[23] Lamech said to his wives: "Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to my words. I have killed a man for wounding me, a young man for striking me.
[Genesis] [4]:[24] If Cain is avenged seven times over, then Lamech seventy-seven times over."
[Genesis] [4]:[25] Adam knew his wife again, and she gave birth to a son and named him Seth, for she said, "God has granted me another child in place of Abel, since Cain killed him."
[Genesis] [4]:[26] Seth also had a son, and he named him Enosh. At that time people began to call on the name of the LORD.
[Genesis] [5]:[1] This is the book of the generations of Adam. When God created man, he made him in the likeness of God.
[Genesis] [5]:[2] Male and female he created them; he blessed them, and he named them Man on the day they were created.
[Genesis] [5]:[3] When Adam had lived a hundred and thirty years, he fathered a son in his own likeness, after his image, and named him Seth.
[Genesis] [5]:[4] After Adam fathered Seth, he lived eight hundred years, and he had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[5] In all, Adam lived nine hundred and thirty years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[6] When Seth had lived a hundred and five years, he fathered Enosh.
[Genesis] [5]:[7] After Seth fathered Enosh, he lived eight hundred and seven years, and he had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[8] In all, Seth lived nine hundred and twelve years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[9] When Enosh had lived ninety years, he fathered Kenan.
[Genesis] [5]:[10] After Enosh fathered Kenan, he lived eight hundred and fifteen years, and he had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[11] In all, Enosh lived nine hundred and five years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[12] When Kenan had lived seventy years, he fathered Mahalalel.
[Genesis] [5]:[13] After Kenan fathered Mahalalel, he lived eight hundred and forty years, and he had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[14] In all, Kenan lived nine hundred and ten years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[15] When Mahalalel had lived sixty-five years, he fathered Jared.
[Genesis] [5]:[16] After Jared was born, Mahalalel lived eight hundred and thirty years, and he had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[17] In all, Mahalalel lived eight hundred and ninety-five years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[18] When Jared had lived one hundred and sixty-two years, he fathered Enoch.
[Genesis] [5]:[19] Jared lived eight hundred years after he fathered Enoch, and he had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[20] In all, Jared lived nine hundred and sixty-two years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[21] When Enoch had lived sixty-five years, he fathered Methuselah.
[Genesis] [5]:[22] After he fathered Methuselah, Enoch walked with God three hundred years, and he had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[23] In all, Enoch lived three hundred sixty-five years.
[Genesis] [5]:[24] Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God took him.
[Genesis] [5]:[25] When Methuselah had lived one hundred eighty-seven years, he fathered Lamech.
[Genesis] [5]:[26] After he fathered Lamech, Methuselah lived 782 years, and he had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[27] In all, Methuselah lived nine hundred sixty-nine years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[28] When Lamech had lived one hundred eighty-two years, he fathered a son.
[Genesis] [5]:[29] He named him Noah, saying, "This one will bring us relief from our work and from the painful toil of our hands, because of the ground that the LORD has cursed."
[Genesis] [5]:[30] After Noah was born, Lamech lived 595 years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[31] In all, Lamech lived seven hundred seventy-seven years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[32] When Noah was 500 years old, he fathered Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
[Genesis] [6]:[1] When mankind began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them,
[Genesis] [6]:[2] the sons of God saw that the daughters of mankind were beautiful, and they took as wives any of them they chose.
[Genesis] [6]:[3] Then the LORD said, "My Spirit shall not contend* with man forever, for he is flesh. His days shall be a hundred and twenty years." [*Footnote: The meaning of the Hebrew verb is uncertain; it may also mean 'remain in' or 'abide with.']
[Genesis] [6]:[4] The Nephilim* were on the earth in those days—and afterward as well—when the sons of God went in to the daughters of mankind and they bore them children. These were the mighty men of old, men of renown. [*Footnote: The meaning of the Hebrew word Nephilim is uncertain; it is often understood as referring to giants.]
[Genesis] [6]:[5] The LORD saw how great the wickedness of mankind had become on the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of the human heart was nothing but evil all the time.
[Genesis] [6]:[6] And the LORD regretted that he had made mankind on the earth, and it grieved him to his heart.
[Genesis] [6]:[7] So the LORD said, "I will wipe from the face of the earth the human race I have created—from man to animals, to creatures that crawl and birds of the sky—for I regret that I made them."
[Genesis] [6]:[8] But Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
[Genesis] [6]:[9] This is the account of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless among the people of his time, and he walked with God.
[Genesis] [6]:[10] Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
[Genesis] [6]:[11] Now the earth was corrupt in God's sight, and the earth was filled with violence.
[Genesis] [6]:[12] God saw the earth, and behold, it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.
[Genesis] [6]:[13] So God said to Noah, "The end of all flesh has come before me, for the earth is filled with violence because of them. And behold, I am about to destroy them, along with the earth.
[Genesis] [6]:[14] Make yourself an ark of cypress wood;* make rooms in it and coat it with pitch inside and out. [*Footnote: Hebrew gopher wood; the exact kind of tree is unknown.]
[Genesis] [6]:[15] This is how you are to build it: the ark is to be three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
[Genesis] [6]:[16] Make a roof for the ark,* finishing it to a cubit from the top, and put a door in the side of the ark. Build it with lower, middle, and upper decks. [*Footnote: The Hebrew word rendered 'roof' is uncertain; it may mean an opening for light.]
[Genesis] [6]:[17] As for me, I am about to bring the floodwaters on the earth, to destroy all flesh under the heavens that has the breath of life in it. Everything on the earth will perish.
[Genesis] [6]:[18] But I will establish my covenant with you, and you will enter the ark—you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you.
[Genesis] [6]:[19] You are to bring into the ark two of every living creature, of all flesh, to keep them alive with you—male and female.
[Genesis] [6]:[20] Birds of every kind, animals of every kind, and creatures that crawl on the ground of every kind—two of each will come to you to be kept alive.
[Genesis] [6]:[21] And you—take for yourself every kind of food that is eaten, and gather it in; it will be food for you and for them."
[Genesis] [6]:[22] Noah did all that God had commanded him; yes, so he did.
[Genesis] [7]:[1] Then the LORD said to Noah, "Go into the ark, you and all your household, for I have seen that you alone are righteous before me in this generation.
[Genesis] [7]:[2] Take with you seven pairs of every clean animal, the male and its mate, and one pair of the animals that are not clean, the male and its mate,
[Genesis] [7]:[3] and also seven pairs of the birds of the sky, male and female, to keep their kind alive on the face of all the earth.
[Genesis] [7]:[4] For in seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe from the face of the ground every living thing I have made."
[Genesis] [7]:[5] And Noah did everything the LORD commanded him.
[Genesis] [7]:[6] Noah was six hundred years old when the floodwaters came upon the earth.
[Genesis] [7]:[7] Noah went into the ark, and with him his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives, to escape the waters of the flood.
[Genesis] [7]:[8] Of the clean animals and of the animals that are not clean, of the birds and of everything that creeps on the ground,
[Genesis] [7]:[9] two by two they came to Noah into the ark, male and female, just as God had commanded Noah.
[Genesis] [7]:[10] And after the seven days the waters of the flood came upon the earth.
[Genesis] [7]:[11] In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month—on that day all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the floodgates of the heavens were opened.
[Genesis] [7]:[12] And rain fell on the earth forty days and forty nights.
[Genesis] [7]:[13] On that very day Noah entered the ark, together with Shem, Ham, and Japheth, Noah's sons, and Noah's wife and the three wives of his sons.
[Genesis] [7]:[14] They came, and with them every wild animal according to its kind, all the livestock according to its kind, every creature that crawls on the earth according to its kind, and every bird according to its kind—every winged creature of every sort.
[Genesis] [7]:[15] They came to Noah into the ark, two by two, of all flesh that has the breath of life in it.
[Genesis] [7]:[16] Those that entered were male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded him. Then the LORD shut him in.
[Genesis] [7]:[17] The flood continued forty days on the earth. The waters rose and lifted the ark, and it was raised high above the earth.
[Genesis] [7]:[18] The waters surged and increased greatly on the earth, and the ark drifted on the surface of the waters.
[Genesis] [7]:[19] The waters rose higher and higher over the earth, until all the high mountains under the whole sky were covered.
[Genesis] [7]:[20] The waters rose fifteen cubits above them, and the mountains were covered.
[Genesis] [7]:[21] Every living thing that moved on the earth perished—birds, livestock, wild animals, all the swarming creatures that swarm on the earth, and all mankind.
[Genesis] [7]:[22] Everything on dry land that had the breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils died.
[Genesis] [7]:[23] He wiped out every living thing on the face of the ground—man and animals, creeping things and birds of the sky. They were wiped from the earth. Only Noah was left, and those with him in the ark.
[Genesis] [7]:[24] And the waters prevailed over the earth a hundred and fifty days.
[Genesis] [8]:[1] But God remembered Noah and every living creature and all the animals that were with him in the ark. God sent a wind sweeping over the earth, and the waters began to subside.
[Genesis] [8]:[2] The springs of the deep and the floodgates of heaven were closed, and the rain from the sky was held back.
[Genesis] [8]:[3] The waters steadily receded from the earth, and at the end of a hundred and fifty days they had gone down.
[Genesis] [8]:[4] On the seventeenth day of the seventh month the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
[Genesis] [8]:[5] The waters kept receding until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains appeared.
[Genesis] [8]:[6] After forty days Noah opened the window he had made in the ark
[Genesis] [8]:[7] and sent out a raven. It flew back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth.
[Genesis] [8]:[8] Then he sent out a dove to see whether the waters had gone down from the surface of the ground.
[Genesis] [8]:[9] But the dove found no place to set its foot, and it returned to him in the ark, for water still covered the whole earth. So he reached out his hand, took the dove, and brought it back to himself in the ark.
[Genesis] [8]:[10] He waited seven more days and again sent the dove out from the ark.
[Genesis] [8]:[11] Toward evening the dove came back to him, and there in its beak was a freshly plucked olive leaf. Then Noah knew that the waters had gone down from the earth.
[Genesis] [8]:[12] He waited seven more days and sent the dove out again, but this time it did not return to him.
[Genesis] [8]:[13] In the six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the waters had dried up from the earth. Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked out, and the surface of the ground was dry.
[Genesis] [8]:[14] By the twenty-seventh day of the second month the earth was completely dry.
[Genesis] [8]:[15] Then God said to Noah,
[Genesis] [8]:[16] "Come out of the ark, you and your wife, your sons and your sons' wives with you.
[Genesis] [8]:[17] Bring out with you every living creature of all flesh that is with you—birds, animals, and every creature that moves along the ground—so they may teem on the earth and be fruitful and multiply upon it.
[Genesis] [8]:[18] So Noah came out, together with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives.
[Genesis] [8]:[19] Every animal, every creeping thing, and every bird—everything that moves on the earth—came out of the ark, one kind after another.
[Genesis] [8]:[20] Then Noah built an altar to the LORD, and taking some of every clean animal and every clean bird, he offered burnt offerings on the altar.
[Genesis] [8]:[21] The LORD smelled the pleasing aroma and said in his heart: "Never again will I curse the ground because of man, for the inclination of the human heart is evil from his youth. Never again will I strike down every living thing as I have done.
[Genesis] [8]:[22] As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night will never cease."
[Genesis] [9]:[1] Then God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, "Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth.
[Genesis] [9]:[2] The fear and dread of you will rest on every animal of the earth and every bird of the sky, on everything that moves along the ground and all the fish of the sea; they are given into your hand.
[Genesis] [9]:[3] Every living creature that moves will be food for you. Just as I gave you the green plants, I now give you everything.
[Genesis] [9]:[4] But you must not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood.
[Genesis] [9]:[5] And I will surely require an accounting for your lifeblood. I will require it from every animal, and from every human being — from each man's brother — I will require an accounting for the life of a fellow human.
[Genesis] [9]:[6] Whoever sheds human blood, by humans will his blood be shed; for in the image of God has God made humankind.
[Genesis] [9]:[7] As for you, be fruitful and multiply; spread out over the earth and increase upon it."
[Genesis] [9]:[8] Then God said to Noah and to his sons with him,
[Genesis] [9]:[9] "I now establish my covenant with you and with your descendants after you,
[Genesis] [9]:[10] and with every living creature that is with you—the birds, the livestock, and all the wild animals with you, every creature that came out of the ark, every living thing on earth.
[Genesis] [9]:[11] I establish my covenant with you: never again will all flesh be destroyed by the waters of a flood; never again will there be a flood to devastate the earth."
[Genesis] [9]:[12] And God said, "This is the sign of the covenant I am making between me and you and every living creature with you, a covenant for all generations to come:
[Genesis] [9]:[13] I have set my bow in the clouds, and it will be the sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
[Genesis] [9]:[14] Whenever I bring clouds over the earth and the bow appears in the clouds,
[Genesis] [9]:[15] I will remember my covenant between me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and never again will the waters become a flood to destroy all flesh.
[Genesis] [9]:[16] When the bow is in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh on the earth."
[Genesis] [9]:[17] So God said to Noah, "This is the sign of the covenant I have established between me and all flesh on the earth."
[Genesis] [9]:[18] The sons of Noah who came out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
[Genesis] [9]:[19] These three were Noah's sons, and from them the whole earth was populated.
[Genesis] [9]:[20] Noah, a man of the soil, was the first to plant a vineyard.
[Genesis] [9]:[21] He drank some of the wine, became drunk, and lay uncovered inside his tent.
[Genesis] [9]:[22] Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father's nakedness and told his two brothers outside.
[Genesis] [9]:[23] So Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it across their shoulders, and walked in backward to cover their father's nakedness. Their faces were turned away, so that they did not see their father's nakedness.
[Genesis] [9]:[24] When Noah awoke from his wine and learned what his youngest son had done to him,
[Genesis] [9]:[25] he said, "Cursed be Canaan! He will be the lowest of slaves to his brothers."
[Genesis] [9]:[26] He also said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem! May Canaan be his slave.
[Genesis] [9]:[27] May God extend Japheth's territory, and may he dwell in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be his slave."
[Genesis] [9]:[28] After the flood Noah lived three hundred and fifty years.
[Genesis] [9]:[29] Noah lived a total of nine hundred and fifty years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [10]:[1] This is the family line of Noah's sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.
[Genesis] [10]:[2] The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
[Genesis] [10]:[3] The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
[Genesis] [10]:[4] The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittim, and the Dodanim.
[Genesis] [10]:[5] From these the coastland peoples spread out into their lands, each with its own language, by their clans within their nations.
[Genesis] [10]:[6] The sons of Ham: Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan.
[Genesis] [10]:[7] The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
[Genesis] [10]:[8] Cush fathered Nimrod, who was the first to become a mighty man on the earth.
[Genesis] [10]:[9] He was a mighty hunter before the LORD; that is why it is said, "Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD."
[Genesis] [10]:[10] The beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Akkad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
[Genesis] [10]:[11] From that land he went to Assyria, where he built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah,
[Genesis] [10]:[12] and Resen, between Nineveh and Calah — that is the great city.
[Genesis] [10]:[13] Egypt fathered the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehabim, the Naphtuhim,
[Genesis] [10]:[14] the Pathrusim, the Casluhim (from whom the Philistines came), and the Caphtorim.
[Genesis] [10]:[15] Canaan fathered Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,
[Genesis] [10]:[16] and the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
[Genesis] [10]:[17] the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
[Genesis] [10]:[18] the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. Later the clans of the Canaanites scattered,
[Genesis] [10]:[19] and the territory of the Canaanites reached from Sidon toward Gerar as far as Gaza, and toward Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, as far as Lasha.
[Genesis] [10]:[20] These are the sons of Ham, by their clans and languages, in their lands and nations.
[Genesis] [10]:[21] Sons were also born to Shem, the older brother of Japheth; he was the father of all the sons of Eber.
[Genesis] [10]:[22] The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.
[Genesis] [10]:[23] The sons of Aram: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
[Genesis] [10]:[24] Arpachshad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
[Genesis] [10]:[25] Two sons were born to Eber. One was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided; his brother's name was Joktan.
[Genesis] [10]:[26] Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
[Genesis] [10]:[27] Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
[Genesis] [10]:[28] Obal, Abimael, Sheba,
[Genesis] [10]:[29] Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
[Genesis] [10]:[30] Their settlements stretched from Mesha toward Sephar, the hill country of the east.
[Genesis] [10]:[31] These are the sons of Shem, by their clans and languages, in their lands and nations.
[Genesis] [10]:[32] These are the clans of Noah's sons, according to their family lines, within their nations. From these the nations spread out over the earth after the flood.
[Genesis] [11]:[1] Now the whole earth had one language and a common speech.
[Genesis] [11]:[2] As people migrated from the east, they came upon a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
[Genesis] [11]:[3] They said to one another, "Come, let us make bricks and fire them thoroughly." So they used brick instead of stone, and tar for mortar.
[Genesis] [11]:[4] Then they said, "Come, let us build ourselves a city, with a tower that reaches to the heavens, and make a name for ourselves, so that we will not be scattered over the face of the whole earth."
[Genesis] [11]:[5] But the LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the children of man were building.
[Genesis] [11]:[6] And the LORD said, "Look, they are one people with one language, and this is only the beginning of what they will do. Nothing they set their minds to will be beyond them.
[Genesis] [11]:[7] Come, let us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another's speech."
[Genesis] [11]:[8] So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of the whole earth, and they stopped building the city.
[Genesis] [11]:[9] That is why it was called Babel,* because there the LORD confused the language of the whole earth; and from there the LORD scattered them over the face of the whole earth. [*Footnote: The name Babel sounds like the Hebrew word meaning "to confuse."]
[Genesis] [11]:[10] This is the account of Shem. Two years after the flood, when Shem was a hundred years old, he became the father of Arpachshad.
[Genesis] [11]:[11] After he became the father of Arpachshad, Shem lived five hundred years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[12] When Arpachshad had lived thirty-five years, he became the father of Shelah.
[Genesis] [11]:[13] After he became the father of Shelah, Arpachshad lived four hundred and three years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[14] When Shelah had lived thirty years, he became the father of Eber.
[Genesis] [11]:[15] After he became the father of Eber, Shelah lived four hundred and three years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[16] When Eber had lived thirty-four years, he became the father of Peleg.
[Genesis] [11]:[17] After he became the father of Peleg, Eber lived four hundred and thirty years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[18] When Peleg had lived thirty years, he became the father of Reu.
[Genesis] [11]:[19] After he became the father of Reu, Peleg lived two hundred and nine years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[20] When Reu had lived thirty-two years, he became the father of Serug.
[Genesis] [11]:[21] After he became the father of Serug, Reu lived two hundred and seven years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[22] When Serug had lived thirty years, he became the father of Nahor.
[Genesis] [11]:[23] After he became the father of Nahor, Serug lived two hundred years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[24] When Nahor had lived twenty-nine years, he became the father of Terah.
[Genesis] [11]:[25] After he became the father of Terah, Nahor lived a hundred and nineteen years and had other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [11]:[26] After Terah had lived seventy years, he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
[Genesis] [11]:[27] This is the account of Terah. Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran, and Haran became the father of Lot.
[Genesis] [11]:[28] Haran died in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldeans, while his father Terah was still alive.
[Genesis] [11]:[29] Abram and Nahor both took wives. Abram's wife was named Sarai, and Nahor's wife was named Milcah, the daughter of Haran, who was the father of Milcah and Iscah.
[Genesis] [11]:[30] Now Sarai was barren; she had no child.
[Genesis] [11]:[31] Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai, the wife of his son Abram, and together they set out from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. But when they came to Haran, they settled there.
[Genesis] [11]:[32] Terah lived two hundred and five years, and he died in Haran.
[Genesis] [12]:[1] The LORD said to Abram, "Leave your land, your kindred, and your father's house, and go to the land I will show you.
[Genesis] [12]:[2] I will make you into a great nation, and I will bless you. I will make your name great, and you will be a blessing.
[Genesis] [12]:[3] I will bless those who bless you, and whoever curses you I will curse; and in you all the families of the earth will be blessed."
[Genesis] [12]:[4] So Abram went, as the LORD had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.
[Genesis] [12]:[5] Abram took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all the possessions they had acquired, and the people they had gained in Haran, and they set out for the land of Canaan. And they came to the land of Canaan.
[Genesis] [12]:[6] Abram traveled through the land as far as the site of Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites were in the land.
[Genesis] [12]:[7] The LORD appeared to Abram and said, "To your offspring I will give this land." So he built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
[Genesis] [12]:[8] From there he moved on to the hill country east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar to the LORD and called on the name of the LORD.
[Genesis] [12]:[9] Then Abram journeyed on, moving by stages toward the Negev.
[Genesis] [12]:[10] Now there was a famine in the land, so Abram went down to Egypt to stay there for a while, because the famine in the land was severe.
[Genesis] [12]:[11] As he was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, "Listen, I know what a beautiful woman you are.
[Genesis] [12]:[12] When the Egyptians see you, they will say, 'This is his wife,' and they will kill me but let you live.
[Genesis] [12]:[13] Say you are my sister, so that I will be treated well for your sake and my life will be spared because of you."
[Genesis] [12]:[14] When Abram came to Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.
[Genesis] [12]:[15] Pharaoh's officials saw her and praised her to Pharaoh, and she was taken into Pharaoh's house.
[Genesis] [12]:[16] He treated Abram well for her sake, and Abram acquired sheep and cattle, donkeys, male and female servants, female donkeys, and camels.
[Genesis] [12]:[17] But the LORD struck Pharaoh and his household with severe plagues because of Abram's wife Sarai.
[Genesis] [12]:[18] So Pharaoh summoned Abram and said, "What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me she was your wife?
[Genesis] [12]:[19] Why did you say, 'She is my sister,' so that I took her to be my wife? Now then, here is your wife. Take her and go!"
[Genesis] [12]:[20] Then Pharaoh gave orders concerning him to his men, and they sent him on his way with his wife and everything he had.
[Genesis] [13]:[1] So Abram went up from Egypt to the Negev, he and his wife and all he owned, and Lot with him.
[Genesis] [13]:[2] Abram had grown very wealthy in livestock, in silver, and in gold.
[Genesis] [13]:[3] He journeyed on by stages from the Negev as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had stood at the first, between Bethel and Ai—
[Genesis] [13]:[4] to the place of the altar he had built there earlier. And there Abram called on the name of the LORD.
[Genesis] [13]:[5] Lot, who traveled with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents,
[Genesis] [13]:[6] and the land could not support them living side by side. Their possessions were so great that they could not stay together.
[Genesis] [13]:[7] So quarreling broke out between Abram's herdsmen and Lot's herdsmen. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were living in the land.
[Genesis] [13]:[8] Abram said to Lot, "Let there be no quarreling between you and me, or between your herdsmen and mine, for we are kinsmen, brothers.
[Genesis] [13]:[9] Isn't the whole land before you? Please separate from me. If you go to the left, I will go to the right; if you go to the right, I will go to the left."
[Genesis] [13]:[10] Lot looked up and saw the whole Jordan Valley, that it was well watered everywhere—this was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah—like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, all the way to Zoar.
[Genesis] [13]:[11] So Lot chose the whole Jordan Valley for himself and set out eastward, and the two men parted from each other.
[Genesis] [13]:[12] Abram settled in the land of Canaan, while Lot settled among the cities of the valley and pitched his tents as far as Sodom.
[Genesis] [13]:[13] Now the men of Sodom were wicked, sinning greatly against the LORD.
[Genesis] [13]:[14] After Lot had parted from him, the LORD said to Abram, "Look up and look around from where you stand—north and south, east and west.
[Genesis] [13]:[15] All the land you see I will give to you and to your offspring forever.
[Genesis] [13]:[16] I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth: if anyone could count the dust of the earth, then your offspring could be counted.
[Genesis] [13]:[17] Rise up, walk through the land, its length and its breadth, for I am giving it to you."
[Genesis] [13]:[18] So Abram moved his tents, and he came and settled by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron, and there he built an altar to the LORD.
[Genesis] [14]:[1] In the days of Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of Goiim,
[Genesis] [14]:[2] these kings went to war against Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, that is, Zoar.
[Genesis] [14]:[3] All these joined forces in the Valley of Siddim, that is, the Salt Sea.
[Genesis] [14]:[4] For twelve years they had served Chedorlaomer, but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
[Genesis] [14]:[5] In the fourteenth year Chedorlaomer came with the kings who were allied with him, and they defeated the Rephaim at Ashteroth-karnaim, the Zuzim at Ham, the Emim at Shaveh-kiriathaim,
[Genesis] [14]:[6] and the Horites in the hill country of Seir, as far as El-paran on the edge of the wilderness.
[Genesis] [14]:[7] Then they turned back and came to En-mishpat, that is, Kadesh, and they struck down all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites who lived in Hazazon-tamar.
[Genesis] [14]:[8] Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah, the king of Admah, the king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, that is, Zoar, marched out and drew up their battle lines against them in the Valley of Siddim—
[Genesis] [14]:[9] against Chedorlaomer king of Elam, Tidal king of Goiim, Amraphel king of Shinar, and Arioch king of Ellasar: four kings against five.
[Genesis] [14]:[10] Now the Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits, and as the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, they fell into them, while the rest escaped to the hills.
[Genesis] [14]:[11] The victors seized all the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their provisions, and went on their way.
[Genesis] [14]:[12] They also took Lot, Abram's nephew, and his possessions, and departed—for he was living in Sodom.
[Genesis] [14]:[13] One who had escaped came and reported this to Abram the Hebrew, who was living by the oaks of Mamre the Amorite, the brother of Eshcol and Aner; these were allies of Abram.
[Genesis] [14]:[14] When Abram heard that his kinsman had been taken captive, he mustered his trained men, born in his household, three hundred eighteen of them, and pursued as far as Dan.
[Genesis] [14]:[15] During the night he divided his forces against them, he and his servants, and attacked them and pursued them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.
[Genesis] [14]:[16] He recovered all the goods, and also brought back his kinsman Lot with his possessions, together with the women and the other people.
[Genesis] [14]:[17] After Abram returned from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, the king of Sodom came out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh, that is, the King's Valley.
[Genesis] [14]:[18] And Melchizedek, king of Salem, brought out bread and wine. He was priest of God Most High,
[Genesis] [14]:[19] and he blessed him, saying: "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth;
[Genesis] [14]:[20] and blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand." And Abram gave him a tenth of everything.
[Genesis] [14]:[21] The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people, and keep the goods for yourself."
[Genesis] [14]:[22] But Abram said to the king of Sodom, "I have raised my hand in an oath to the LORD, God Most High, Maker of heaven and earth,
[Genesis] [14]:[23] that I will accept nothing that belongs to you, not a thread or a sandal strap, so that you can never say, 'I made Abram rich.'
[Genesis] [14]:[24] I will take nothing but what the young men have eaten, and the share belonging to the men who went with me—Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their share."
[Genesis] [15]:[1] After this, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision: "Do not be afraid, Abram. I am your shield; your reward will be very great."
[Genesis] [15]:[2] But Abram said, "Lord GOD, what will you give me? I remain childless, and the one who will inherit my house is Eliezer of Damascus."
[Genesis] [15]:[3] Abram said, "Look, you have given me no offspring, so a member of my household will be my heir."
[Genesis] [15]:[4] Then the word of the LORD came to him: "He will not be your heir. Your heir will be one who comes from your own body."
[Genesis] [15]:[5] He brought him outside and said, "Look up at the sky and count the stars—if you can count them." Then he said to him, "So shall your offspring be."
[Genesis] [15]:[6] And Abram believed the LORD, and he credited it to him as righteousness.
[Genesis] [15]:[7] He said to him, "I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land to possess."
[Genesis] [15]:[8] But Abram said, "Lord GOD, how can I know that I will possess it?"
[Genesis] [15]:[9] He answered him, "Take for me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon."
[Genesis] [15]:[10] So Abram took all these, cut them in two, and laid each half opposite the other; but the birds he did not cut in two.
[Genesis] [15]:[11] Birds of prey came down on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away.
[Genesis] [15]:[12] As the sun was setting, a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and suddenly a terror, a great darkness, fell upon him.
[Genesis] [15]:[13] Then the LORD said to Abram, "Know this for certain: your offspring will be strangers in a land not their own, where they will be enslaved and oppressed for four hundred years.
[Genesis] [15]:[14] But I will judge the nation they serve, and afterward they will come out with great wealth.
[Genesis] [15]:[15] As for you, you will go to your fathers in peace and be buried at a good old age.
[Genesis] [15]:[16] In the fourth generation your descendants will return here, for the sin of the Amorites has not yet reached its full measure."
[Genesis] [15]:[17] When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, a smoking firepot with a blazing torch appeared and passed between the pieces.
[Genesis] [15]:[18] On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying: "To your offspring I have given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates—
[Genesis] [15]:[19] the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
[Genesis] [15]:[20] the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim,
[Genesis] [15]:[21] the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites."
[Genesis] [16]:[1] Now Sarai, Abram's wife, had borne him no children. But she had an Egyptian slave girl named Hagar,
[Genesis] [16]:[2] and Sarai said to Abram, "Look, the LORD has kept me from bearing children. Go to my slave girl; perhaps I can build a family through her." And Abram listened to Sarai.
[Genesis] [16]:[3] So Sarai, Abram's wife, took Hagar the Egyptian, her slave girl, and gave her to her husband Abram as a wife. This was after Abram had lived ten years in the land of Canaan.
[Genesis] [16]:[4] He went to Hagar, and she conceived. But when she saw that she was pregnant, she began to despise her mistress.
[Genesis] [16]:[5] Then Sarai said to Abram, "This wrong done to me is your fault. I put my slave girl in your arms, and when she saw that she was pregnant, she began to despise me. Let the LORD judge between you and me!"
[Genesis] [16]:[6] Abram answered Sarai, "Your slave girl is in your hands. Do with her whatever you think best." So Sarai treated her harshly, and Hagar ran away from her.
[Genesis] [16]:[7] The angel of the LORD found her by a spring of water in the wilderness—the spring beside the road to Shur—
[Genesis] [16]:[8] and he said, "Hagar, slave girl of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?" "I am running away from my mistress Sarai," she answered.
[Genesis] [16]:[9] Then the angel of the LORD said to her, "Go back to your mistress and submit to her authority."
[Genesis] [16]:[10] And the angel of the LORD said to her, "I will greatly increase your descendants; they will be too many to count."
[Genesis] [16]:[11] The angel of the LORD also said to her, "You are pregnant, and you will give birth to a son. You shall name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard your cry of affliction. [Footnote: Ishmael means "God hears."]
[Genesis] [16]:[12] He will be like a wild donkey of a man: his hand against everyone, and everyone's hand against him, and he will live at odds with all his kin."
[Genesis] [16]:[13] So she gave a name to the LORD who had spoken to her: "You are the God who sees me," for she said, "Have I really seen him and lived, the One who sees me?"
[Genesis] [16]:[14] That is why the well was called Beer-lahai-roi; it lies between Kadesh and Bered. [Footnote: Beer-lahai-roi means "well of the Living One who sees me."]
[Genesis] [16]:[15] Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram named the son she bore him Ishmael.
[Genesis] [16]:[16] Abram was eighty-six years old when Hagar bore him Ishmael.
[Genesis] [17]:[1] When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, "I am God Almighty. Walk before me and be blameless.
[Genesis] [17]:[2] I will establish my covenant between me and you, and I will multiply you greatly."
[Genesis] [17]:[3] Abram fell facedown, and God spoke with him, saying:
[Genesis] [17]:[4] "As for me, this is my covenant with you: you will be the father of a multitude of nations.
[Genesis] [17]:[5] No longer will you be called Abram; your name will be Abraham, for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.
[Genesis] [17]:[6] I will make you exceedingly fruitful; I will make nations of you, and kings will come from you.
[Genesis] [17]:[7] I will establish my covenant between me and you and your descendants after you throughout their generations, an everlasting covenant: I will be your God and the God of your descendants after you.
[Genesis] [17]:[8] And I will give to you and to your descendants after you the land where you now live as a stranger—all the land of Canaan—as an everlasting possession, and I will be their God."
[Genesis] [17]:[9] Then God said to Abraham, "As for you, you are to keep my covenant, you and your descendants after you throughout their generations.
[Genesis] [17]:[10] This is my covenant, which you are to keep, between me and you and your descendants after you: every male among you shall be circumcised.
[Genesis] [17]:[11] You shall have the flesh of your foreskin circumcised, and it will be a sign of the covenant between me and you.
[Genesis] [17]:[12] Every male among you, throughout your generations, shall be circumcised when he is eight days old—whether born in your household or bought with silver from a foreigner, one who is not of your own offspring.
[Genesis] [17]:[13] Both the one born in your household and the one bought with your silver must be circumcised, so that my covenant may be in your flesh as an everlasting covenant.
[Genesis] [17]:[14] Any uncircumcised male who has not had the flesh of his foreskin circumcised shall be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant.
[Genesis] [17]:[15] God also said to Abraham, "As for Sarai your wife, you shall no longer call her Sarai; her name will be Sarah.
[Genesis] [17]:[16] I will bless her, and I will give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she will become nations; kings of peoples will come from her."
[Genesis] [17]:[17] Then Abraham fell facedown and laughed, saying to himself, "Can a child be born to a man a hundred years old? Can Sarah bear a child at ninety?"
[Genesis] [17]:[18] And Abraham said to God, "If only Ishmael might live in your presence!"
[Genesis] [17]:[19] But God said, "No—Sarah your wife will bear you a son, and you shall name him Isaac. I will establish my covenant with him as an everlasting covenant for his descendants after him.
[Genesis] [17]:[20] As for Ishmael, I have heard you. I will surely bless him; I will make him fruitful and multiply him greatly. He will father twelve princes, and I will make him into a great nation.
[Genesis] [17]:[21] But my covenant I will establish with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you at this time next year."
[Genesis] [17]:[22] When he had finished speaking with Abraham, God went up from him.
[Genesis] [17]:[23] That very day Abraham took Ishmael his son, everyone born in his household, and everyone bought with his silver—every male among the men of Abraham's household—and circumcised the flesh of their foreskins, just as God had told him.
[Genesis] [17]:[24] Abraham was ninety-nine years old when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised,
[Genesis] [17]:[25] and his son Ishmael was thirteen when the flesh of his foreskin was circumcised.
[Genesis] [17]:[26] Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised on that very day,
[Genesis] [17]:[27] and all the men of his household—those born in his house and those bought with silver from a foreigner—were circumcised with him.
[Genesis] [18]:[1] The LORD appeared to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre as he sat at the entrance of his tent in the heat of the day.
[Genesis] [18]:[2] He looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he ran from the tent entrance to meet them and bowed to the ground.
[Genesis] [18]:[3] "My lord," he said, "if I have found favor in your eyes, do not pass by your servant.
[Genesis] [18]:[4] Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest under the tree.
[Genesis] [18]:[5] Let me bring a piece of bread to refresh you, and then go on your way—since you have come by your servant." "Very well," they said, "do as you have said."
[Genesis] [18]:[6] Abraham hurried into the tent to Sarah. "Quick," he said, "three measures of the finest flour! Knead it and bake bread." [footnote: About twenty liters.]
[Genesis] [18]:[7] Then he ran to the herd, took a choice, tender calf, and gave it to his servant, who hurried to prepare it.
[Genesis] [18]:[8] He took curds and milk and the calf that had been prepared, and set it all before them, and he stood by them under the tree while they ate.
[Genesis] [18]:[9] They asked him, "Where is Sarah your wife?" "There, in the tent," he said.
[Genesis] [18]:[10] Then he said, "I will surely return to you about this time next year, and Sarah your wife will have a son." Now Sarah was listening at the entrance of the tent, behind him.
[Genesis] [18]:[11] Abraham and Sarah were old, well along in years, and Sarah was long past childbearing.
[Genesis] [18]:[12] So Sarah laughed to herself and thought, "Now that I am worn out, am I to have pleasure? And my husband is old."
[Genesis] [18]:[13] But the LORD said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh and say, 'Can I really bear a child, now that I am old?'
[Genesis] [18]:[14] Is anything too hard for the LORD? At the appointed time I will return to you, about this time next year, and Sarah will have a son."
[Genesis] [18]:[15] Sarah denied it: "I did not laugh"—for she was afraid. But he said, "Yes, you did laugh."
[Genesis] [18]:[16] Then the men got up to leave and looked down toward Sodom, and Abraham walked along with them to see them on their way.
[Genesis] [18]:[17] And the LORD said, "Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do?
[Genesis] [18]:[18] Abraham will surely become a great and mighty nation, and through him all the nations of the earth will be blessed.
[Genesis] [18]:[19] For I have chosen him, so that he will direct his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just, so that the LORD may bring about for Abraham what he has promised him."
[Genesis] [18]:[20] Then the LORD said, "The outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah is great, and their sin is very grave.
[Genesis] [18]:[21] I will go down now and see whether they have acted as badly as the outcry that has reached me. If not, I will know.
[Genesis] [18]:[22] The men turned from there and went toward Sodom, but Abraham remained standing before the LORD.
[Genesis] [18]:[23] Then Abraham came near and said, "Will you really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?
[Genesis] [18]:[24] Suppose there are fifty righteous people in the city. Will you really sweep it away and not spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous who are in it?
[Genesis] [18]:[25] Far be it from you to do such a thing—to kill the righteous with the wicked, treating the righteous and the wicked alike! Far be it from you! Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is just?"
[Genesis] [18]:[26] The LORD said, "If I find fifty righteous people in the city of Sodom, I will spare the whole place for their sake."
[Genesis] [18]:[27] Abraham answered, "Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord, though I am but dust and ashes—
[Genesis] [18]:[28] suppose the fifty righteous are five short. Will you destroy the whole city because of five?" "If I find forty-five there," he said, "I will not destroy it."
[Genesis] [18]:[29] Abraham spoke to him again: "What if only forty are found there?" He said, "For the sake of the forty, I will not do it."
[Genesis] [18]:[30] Then he said, "May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak. Suppose only thirty are found there?" He answered, "If I find thirty there, I will not do it."
[Genesis] [18]:[31] He said, "Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord, suppose only twenty are found there?" He said, "For the sake of the twenty, I will not destroy it."
[Genesis] [18]:[32] Then he said, "May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak just once more. Suppose only ten are found there?" He answered, "For the sake of the ten, I will not destroy it."
[Genesis] [18]:[33] When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, he went on his way, and Abraham returned home.
[Genesis] [19]:[1] The two angels came to Sodom in the evening, while Lot was sitting in the gateway of Sodom. When Lot saw them, he rose to meet them and bowed with his face to the ground.
[Genesis] [19]:[2] He said, "Please, my lords, turn aside to your servant's house. Spend the night and wash your feet, and you can rise early and go on your way." "No," they said, "we will spend the night in the square."
[Genesis] [19]:[3] But he pressed them so strongly that they turned aside to him and came into his house. He prepared a feast for them, baked unleavened bread, and they ate.
[Genesis] [19]:[4] Before they lay down for the night, the men of the city surrounded the house—the men of Sodom, young and old, the whole population to the last man.
[Genesis] [19]:[5] They called out to Lot and said to him, "Where are the men who came to you tonight? Bring them out to us so we can have our way with them."
[Genesis] [19]:[6] Lot went out to them at the entrance, shutting the door behind him,
[Genesis] [19]:[7] and said, "Please, my brothers, do not do such a wicked thing.
[Genesis] [19]:[8] Look, I have two daughters who have never been with a man. Let me bring them out to you, and do to them whatever you please. Only do nothing to these men, for they have come under the shelter of my roof."
[Genesis] [19]:[9] "Out of the way!" they said. And they said, "This fellow came here as a foreigner, and now he plays the judge! We will treat you worse than them." They pressed hard against the man, against Lot, and moved in to break down the door.
[Genesis] [19]:[10] But the men reached out, pulled Lot into the house with them, and shut the door.
[Genesis] [19]:[11] Then they struck the men at the entrance of the house with blindness, small and great alike, so that they wore themselves out trying to find the doorway.
[Genesis] [19]:[12] The men said to Lot, "Who else do you have here? Sons-in-law, sons, daughters—anyone of yours in the city—get them out of this place,
[Genesis] [19]:[13] because we are about to destroy it. The outcry against these people before the LORD is so great that the LORD has sent us to destroy it."
[Genesis] [19]:[14] So Lot went out and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were pledged to marry his daughters. "Get up, leave this place," he said, "for the LORD is about to destroy the city!" But to his sons-in-law he seemed to be joking.
[Genesis] [19]:[15] As dawn was breaking, the angels urged Lot on, saying, "Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters who are here, or you will be swept away in the punishment of the city."
[Genesis] [19]:[16] When he hesitated, the men grasped his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters, for the LORD had mercy on him. They led them out and left them outside the city.
[Genesis] [19]:[17] Once they had brought them out, one of them said, "Run for your life! Do not look back, and do not stop anywhere in the valley. Escape to the hills, or you will be swept away."
[Genesis] [19]:[18] But Lot said to them, "Please, no, my lord!
[Genesis] [19]:[19] Look, your servant has found favor in your eyes, and you have shown me great kindness in sparing my life. But I cannot flee to the hills, or the disaster will overtake me and I will die.
[Genesis] [19]:[20] Look, there is a town near enough to reach, and it is small. Let me flee there—it is only a small place—and my life will be spared."
[Genesis] [19]:[21] He said to him, "Very well, I grant you this request too: I will not overthrow the town you speak of.
[Genesis] [19]:[22] Hurry, escape there, for I can do nothing until you arrive." That is why the town was called Zoar.
[Genesis] [19]:[23] The sun had risen over the land when Lot came to Zoar.
[Genesis] [19]:[24] Then the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah—from the LORD out of the heavens.
[Genesis] [19]:[25] He overthrew those cities and the entire valley, along with all who lived in the cities and everything growing from the ground.
[Genesis] [19]:[26] But Lot's wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.
[Genesis] [19]:[27] Early the next morning Abraham went to the place where he had stood before the LORD.
[Genesis] [19]:[28] He looked down toward Sodom and Gomorrah and over all the land of the valley, and he saw smoke rising from the land like smoke from a furnace.
[Genesis] [19]:[29] So when God destroyed the cities of the valley, he remembered Abraham and brought Lot out of the catastrophe that overthrew the cities where Lot had lived.
[Genesis] [19]:[30] Lot went up from Zoar and settled in the hills with his two daughters, because he was afraid to stay in Zoar. He lived in a cave, he and his two daughters.
[Genesis] [19]:[31] The older daughter said to the younger, "Our father is old, and there is no man in the land to come to us as is the custom everywhere on earth.
[Genesis] [19]:[32] Come, let us give our father wine to drink and lie with him, so we can preserve offspring through our father."
[Genesis] [19]:[33] That night they gave their father wine to drink, and the older one went in and lay with her father. He was not aware of it when she lay down or when she got up.
[Genesis] [19]:[34] The next day the older said to the younger, "Last night I lay with my father. Let us give him wine to drink again tonight, and you go in and lie with him, so we can preserve offspring through our father."
[Genesis] [19]:[35] So that night also they gave their father wine to drink, and the younger one got up and lay with him. He was not aware of it when she lay down or when she got up.
[Genesis] [19]:[36] So both of Lot's daughters became pregnant by their father.
[Genesis] [19]:[37] The older gave birth to a son and named him Moab; he is the father of the Moabites to this day.
[Genesis] [19]:[38] The younger also gave birth to a son and named him Ben-Ammi; he is the father of the Ammonites to this day.
[Genesis] [20]:[1] From there Abraham journeyed toward the land of the Negev and settled between Kadesh and Shur, and he lived as a stranger in Gerar.
[Genesis] [20]:[2] And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, "She is my sister." So Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took Sarah.
[Genesis] [20]:[3] But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night and said to him, "You are a dead man because of the woman you have taken, for she is a married woman."
[Genesis] [20]:[4] Now Abimelech had not gone near her, so he said, "Lord, will you kill even a righteous nation?
[Genesis] [20]:[5] Did he not say to me, 'She is my sister'? And she herself said, 'He is my brother.' With an innocent heart and clean hands I have done this."
[Genesis] [20]:[6] Then God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I know that you did this with an innocent heart, and it was I who kept you from sinning against me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
[Genesis] [20]:[7] Now return the man's wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you will live. But if you do not return her, know that you shall surely die, you and all who are yours."
[Genesis] [20]:[8] Abimelech rose early in the morning, called all his servants, and told them all these things in their hearing, and the men were terrified.
[Genesis] [20]:[9] Then Abimelech summoned Abraham and said to him, "What have you done to us? How have I wronged you, that you have brought such great guilt on me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should never be done."
[Genesis] [20]:[10] And Abimelech said to Abraham, "What did you have in mind, that you did this?"
[Genesis] [20]:[11] Abraham said, "I thought, surely there is no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.
[Genesis] [20]:[12] Besides, she really is my sister, the daughter of my father though not the daughter of my mother, and she became my wife.
[Genesis] [20]:[13] And when God had me wander from my father's house, I said to her, 'This is the kindness you must show me: wherever we go, say of me, He is my brother.'"
[Genesis] [20]:[14] Then Abimelech took sheep and cattle, male and female servants, and gave them to Abraham, and he returned Sarah his wife to him.
[Genesis] [20]:[15] And Abimelech said, "See, my land lies before you. Settle wherever you please."
[Genesis] [20]:[16] And to Sarah he said, "I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. It is a covering of the eyes for you before all who are with you; in every way you are cleared."
[Genesis] [20]:[17] Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants, so that they bore children again;
[Genesis] [20]:[18] for the LORD had completely closed every womb in Abimelech's household because of Sarah, Abraham's wife.
[Genesis] [21]:[1] The LORD visited Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what he had promised.
[Genesis] [21]:[2] Sarah conceived and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the very time God had spoken of.
[Genesis] [21]:[3] Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son born to him, the son Sarah bore him.
[Genesis] [21]:[4] And Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.
[Genesis] [21]:[5] Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.
[Genesis] [21]:[6] Then Sarah said, "God has brought me laughter; everyone who hears will laugh with me."[^1] [^1]: The name Isaac sounds like the Hebrew word for 'he laughs'.
[Genesis] [21]:[7] And she said, "Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age."
[Genesis] [21]:[8] The child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
[Genesis] [21]:[9] But Sarah saw the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham mocking,
[Genesis] [21]:[10] and she said to Abraham, "Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not inherit along with my son, with Isaac."
[Genesis] [21]:[11] This troubled Abraham deeply, because of his son.
[Genesis] [21]:[12] But God said to Abraham, "Do not be troubled about the boy and about your slave woman. Listen to whatever Sarah says to you, for through Isaac your offspring shall be named.
[Genesis] [21]:[13] And I will also make a nation of the slave woman's son, because he is your offspring."
[Genesis] [21]:[14] So Abraham rose early in the morning, took bread and a skin of water and gave them to Hagar, placing them on her shoulder, and he sent her away with the boy. She went off and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
[Genesis] [21]:[15] When the water in the skin was gone, she left the boy under one of the bushes
[Genesis] [21]:[16] and went and sat down a good way off, about a bowshot away, for she said, "Let me not watch the boy die." And as she sat there, she lifted up her voice and wept.
[Genesis] [21]:[17] God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, "What troubles you, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is.
[Genesis] [21]:[18] Get up, lift the boy and hold him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation."
[Genesis] [21]:[19] Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.
[Genesis] [21]:[20] God was with the boy, and he grew up. He lived in the wilderness and became an archer.
[Genesis] [21]:[21] He settled in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
[Genesis] [21]:[22] At that time Abimelech, together with Phicol the commander of his army, said to Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do.
[Genesis] [21]:[23] Now swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me or with my offspring or with my posterity. Show to me and to the land where you have lived as a foreigner the same kindness I have shown to you.
[Genesis] [21]:[24] And Abraham said, "I swear it."
[Genesis] [21]:[25] Then Abraham confronted Abimelech about the well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized.
[Genesis] [21]:[26] Abimelech said, "I do not know who did this. You never told me, and I heard nothing of it until today."
[Genesis] [21]:[27] So Abraham took sheep and cattle and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant.
[Genesis] [21]:[28] Abraham also set apart seven ewe lambs from the flock,
[Genesis] [21]:[29] and Abimelech asked him, "What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs you have set apart?"
[Genesis] [21]:[30] He answered, "Accept these seven ewe lambs from my hand as my witness that I dug this well."
[Genesis] [21]:[31] That is why the place was called Beersheba, because there the two of them swore an oath.
[Genesis] [21]:[32] When they had made the covenant at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol the commander of his army set out and returned to the land of the Philistines.
[Genesis] [21]:[33] Abraham planted a tamarisk tree at Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.
[Genesis] [21]:[34] And Abraham lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines for a long time.
[Genesis] [22]:[1] Some time later God tested Abraham. He said to him, "Abraham!" And he answered, "Here I am."
[Genesis] [22]:[2] Then God said, "Take your son, your only son, whom you love, Isaac, and go to the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains I will tell you about."
[Genesis] [22]:[3] Early the next morning Abraham got up and saddled his donkey. He took his two servants with him, and his son Isaac. He split the wood for the burnt offering, then set out for the place God had told him about.
[Genesis] [22]:[4] On the third day Abraham looked up and saw the place in the distance.
[Genesis] [22]:[5] He said to his servants, "Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there to worship, and then we will come back to you."
[Genesis] [22]:[6] Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and laid it on his son Isaac, and he carried the fire and the knife in his own hand. So the two of them walked on together.
[Genesis] [22]:[7] Isaac spoke to his father Abraham: "Father?" "Yes, my son," he answered. Isaac said, "Here are the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?"
[Genesis] [22]:[8] Abraham said, "God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son." And the two of them walked on together.
[Genesis] [22]:[9] When they came to the place God had told him about, Abraham built an altar there and arranged the wood. He bound his son Isaac and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.
[Genesis] [22]:[10] Then Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son.
[Genesis] [22]:[11] But the angel of the LORD called to him from heaven, "Abraham! Abraham!" "Here I am," he answered.
[Genesis] [22]:[12] "Do not lay a hand on the boy," he said. "Do not do anything to him. Now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me."
[Genesis] [22]:[13] Abraham looked up, and there behind him was a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. He went over, took the ram, and offered it as a burnt offering in place of his son.
[Genesis] [22]:[14] So Abraham named that place The LORD Will Provide. And to this day it is said, "On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided."
[Genesis] [22]:[15] The angel of the LORD called to Abraham from heaven a second time
[Genesis] [22]:[16] and said, "By myself I have sworn, declares the LORD: because you have done this and have not withheld your son, your only son,
[Genesis] [22]:[17] I will surely bless you and greatly multiply your offspring, like the stars in the sky and like the sand on the seashore. Your offspring will possess the gate of their enemies,
[Genesis] [22]:[18] and in your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed, because you have obeyed my voice."
[Genesis] [22]:[19] Then Abraham returned to his servants, and together they set out for Beersheba. And Abraham settled in Beersheba.
[Genesis] [22]:[20] Some time later Abraham was told, "Milcah too has borne sons to your brother Nahor:
[Genesis] [22]:[21] Uz his firstborn, Buz his brother, Kemuel the father of Aram,
[Genesis] [22]:[22] Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel."
[Genesis] [22]:[23] Bethuel became the father of Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother.
