[Genesis] [23]:[1] Sarah lived a hundred and twenty-seven years; these were the years of Sarah's life.
[Genesis] [23]:[2] Sarah died at Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan, and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.
[Genesis] [23]:[3] Then Abraham rose from beside his dead wife and spoke to the Hittites:
[Genesis] [23]:[4] "I am a stranger and a sojourner among you. Give me a burial site among you, so that I may bury my dead."
[Genesis] [23]:[5] The Hittites answered Abraham:
[Genesis] [23]:[6] "Hear us, my lord. You are a prince of God among us. Bury your dead in the finest of our tombs. Not one of us will refuse you his tomb for burying your dead."
[Genesis] [23]:[7] Then Abraham rose and bowed to the people of the land, the Hittites,
[Genesis] [23]:[8] and he said to them, "If you are willing that I should bury my dead, then hear me and plead for me with Ephron son of Zohar,
[Genesis] [23]:[9] that he may sell me the cave of Machpelah, which belongs to him, at the end of his field. Let him sell it to me for the full price, so that I may have it among you as a burial site."
[Genesis] [23]:[10] Now Ephron was sitting among the Hittites, and he answered Abraham in the hearing of the Hittites, all who came to the gate of his city:
[Genesis] [23]:[11] "No, my lord, hear me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. In the presence of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead."
[Genesis] [23]:[12] Abraham bowed before the people of the land
[Genesis] [23]:[13] and said to Ephron in their hearing, "If you are willing, then hear me: I will pay the price of the field. Take it from me, so that I may bury my dead there."
[Genesis] [23]:[14] Ephron answered Abraham:
[Genesis] [23]:[15] "Hear me, my lord. Land worth four hundred shekels of silver—what is that between you and me? Bury your dead."
[Genesis] [23]:[16] Abraham agreed to Ephron's terms and weighed out for him the silver he had named in the hearing of the Hittites: four hundred shekels of silver, according to the merchants' weight.
[Genesis] [23]:[17] So the field of Ephron at Machpelah, facing Mamre—the field with the cave in it and all the trees within its borders—passed
[Genesis] [23]:[18] into Abraham's possession in the presence of the Hittites, all who came to the gate of his city.
[Genesis] [23]:[19] After this Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah, facing Mamre, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan.
[Genesis] [23]:[20] So the field and the cave in it passed from the Hittites to Abraham as his own burial ground.
[Genesis] [24]:[1] Abraham was now old, well advanced in years, and the LORD had blessed him in every way.
[Genesis] [24]:[2] So Abraham said to the senior servant of his household, the one in charge of all he owned, "Place your hand under my thigh,
[Genesis] [24]:[3] and I will make you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among whom I live,

[Genesis] [24]:[5] The servant said to him, "What if the woman is unwilling to come with me to this land? Should I then take your son back to the land you came from?"
[Genesis] [24]:[6] "See to it that you do not take my son back there," Abraham said.
[Genesis] [24]:[7] "The LORD, the God of heaven, who took me from my father's house and from the land of my birth, who spoke to me and swore to me, 'To your offspring I will give this land' — he will send his angel ahead of you, and you will take a wife for my son from there.
[Genesis] [24]:[8] And if the woman is unwilling to come with you, then you are released from this oath of mine. Only do not take my son back there."
[Genesis] [24]:[9] So the servant placed his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and swore to him concerning this matter.
[Genesis] [24]:[10] Then the servant took ten of his master's camels and set out, carrying with him all kinds of costly gifts from his master. He made his way to Aram Naharaim, to the city of Nahor.
[Genesis] [24]:[11] He had the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water. It was evening, the time when the women come out to draw water.
[Genesis] [24]:[12] And he said, "LORD, God of my master Abraham, grant me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
[Genesis] [24]:[13] Here I stand by the spring, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water.
[Genesis] [24]:[14] Let it be that the young woman to whom I say, 'Please tip your jar so I may drink,' and who answers, 'Drink, and I will water your camels as well' — let her be the one you have chosen for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown kindness to my master."
[Genesis] [24]:[15] Before he had finished speaking, there came Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah, who was the wife of Abraham's brother Nahor. She had her jar on her shoulder.
[Genesis] [24]:[16] The young woman was very beautiful, a virgin; no man had ever been with her. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up again.
[Genesis] [24]:[17] The servant hurried to meet her and said, "Please give me a little water from your jar."
[Genesis] [24]:[18] "Drink, my lord," she said, and she quickly lowered the jar to her hand and gave him a drink.
[Genesis] [24]:[19] When she had finished giving him a drink, she said, "I will draw water for your camels too, until they have finished drinking."
[Genesis] [24]:[20] She quickly emptied her jar into the trough, ran back to the well to draw more, and drew enough for all his camels.
[Genesis] [24]:[21] The man watched her in silence, wondering whether the LORD had made his journey a success or not.
[Genesis] [24]:[22] When the camels had finished drinking, the man took out a gold nose ring weighing half a shekel and two gold bracelets for her wrists weighing ten shekels.
[Genesis] [24]:[23] He asked, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me, is there room in your father's house for us to spend the night?"
[Genesis] [24]:[24] She answered, "I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son whom Milcah bore to Nahor."
[Genesis] [24]:[25] And she added, "We have plenty of straw and fodder, and room for you to spend the night."
[Genesis] [24]:[26] Then the man bowed down and worshiped the LORD,
[Genesis] [24]:[27] saying, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not withheld his kindness and faithfulness from my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master's relatives."
[Genesis] [24]:[28] The young woman ran and told her mother's household all that had happened.
[Genesis] [24]:[29] Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and he ran out to the man at the spring.
[Genesis] [24]:[30] When he saw the nose ring and the bracelets on his sister's wrists, and heard Rebekah say, "This is what the man said to me," he went out to the man and found him standing with the camels by the spring.
[Genesis] [24]:[31] "Come in, you who are blessed by the LORD," he said. "Why stand out here? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels."
[Genesis] [24]:[32] So the man came into the house. The camels were unloaded and given straw and fodder, and water was brought for him and his men to wash their feet.
[Genesis] [24]:[33] Then food was set before him, but he said, "I will not eat until I have told you what I have to say." "Speak," said Laban.
[Genesis] [24]:[34] So he said, "I am Abraham's servant.
[Genesis] [24]:[35] The LORD has blessed my master abundantly, and he has become wealthy. He has given him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, male and female servants, camels and donkeys.
[Genesis] [24]:[36] My master's wife Sarah bore him a son in her old age, and he has given him everything he owns.
[Genesis] [24]:[37] My master made me swear an oath and said, 'You must not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live,
[Genesis] [24]:[38] but go to my father's house and to my own clan, and take a wife for my son.'
[Genesis] [24]:[39] Then I said to my master, 'What if the woman will not come with me?'
[Genesis] [24]:[40] He answered, 'The LORD, before whom I have walked, will send his angel with you and make your journey a success, so that you may take a wife for my son from my own clan and from my father's house.
[Genesis] [24]:[41] Then you will be released from my oath when you come to my clan; and if they will not give her to you, you will be free from my oath.'
[Genesis] [24]:[42] "When I came to the spring today, I said, 'LORD, God of my master Abraham, if you will, grant success to the journey I have undertaken.
[Genesis] [24]:[43] Here I stand by the spring. Let it be that when a young woman comes out to draw water and I say to her, "Please give me a little water from your jar to drink,"
[Genesis] [24]:[44] and she answers, "Drink, and I will draw water for your camels too" — let her be the woman the LORD has chosen for my master's son.'
[Genesis] [24]:[45] "Before I had finished praying in my heart, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water, and I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'
[Genesis] [24]:[46] She quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, 'Drink, and I will water your camels too.' So I drank, and she watered the camels as well.
[Genesis] [24]:[47] Then I asked her, 'Whose daughter are you?' She said, 'The daughter of Bethuel son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.' So I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her wrists,
[Genesis] [24]:[48] and I bowed down and worshiped the LORD. I praised the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me on the right road to take the daughter of my master's kinsman for his son.
[Genesis] [24]:[49] Now then, if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me; and if not, tell me, so that I may turn to the right or to the left."
[Genesis] [24]:[50] Laban and Bethuel answered, "This comes from the LORD; we can say nothing to you, one way or the other.
[Genesis] [24]:[51] Here is Rebekah; take her and go. Let her become the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has spoken."
[Genesis] [24]:[52] When Abraham's servant heard their words, he bowed to the ground before the LORD.
[Genesis] [24]:[53] Then the servant brought out objects of silver and gold and fine garments and gave them to Rebekah, and he gave costly gifts to her brother and her mother.
[Genesis] [24]:[54] Then he and the men who were with him ate and drank and spent the night there. When they got up in the morning, he said, "Send me on my way to my master."
[Genesis] [24]:[55] But her brother and her mother replied, "Let the girl remain with us a while, ten days or so; after that she may go."
[Genesis] [24]:[56] But he said to them, "Do not detain me, now that the LORD has made my journey a success. Send me on my way so I may go to my master."
[Genesis] [24]:[57] They said, "Let us call the girl and ask her."
[Genesis] [24]:[58] So they called Rebekah and asked her, "Will you go with this man?" "I will go," she said.
[Genesis] [24]:[59] So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, along with her nurse, together with Abraham's servant and his men.
[Genesis] [24]:[60] And they blessed Rebekah, saying to her, "Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands; may your offspring possess the gates of their enemies."
[Genesis] [24]:[61] Then Rebekah and her maids mounted the camels and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and set out.
[Genesis] [24]:[62] Now Isaac had come from the direction of Beer Lahai Roi, for he was living in the region of the Negev.
[Genesis] [24]:[63] One evening he went out to the field to meditate, and as he looked up, he saw camels approaching.
[Genesis] [24]:[64] Rebekah also looked up and saw Isaac, and she got down from her camel.
[Genesis] [24]:[65] She asked the servant, "Who is that man coming through the field to meet us?" "He is my master," the servant answered. So she took her veil and covered herself.
[Genesis] [24]:[66] Then the servant told Isaac everything he had done.
[Genesis] [24]:[67] Isaac brought her into the tent of his mother Sarah, and he took Rebekah as his wife. He loved her, and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.
[Genesis] [25]:[1] Abraham took another wife, whose name was Keturah.
[Genesis] [25]:[2] She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
[Genesis] [25]:[3] Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan, and the sons of Dedan were the Asshurim, the Letushim, and the Leummim.
[Genesis] [25]:[4] The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.
[Genesis] [25]:[5] Abraham gave everything he owned to Isaac.
[Genesis] [25]:[6] But to the sons of his concubines Abraham gave gifts, and while he was still alive he sent them away from his son Isaac, eastward to the land of the east.
[Genesis] [25]:[7] This is the full span of Abraham's life: he lived a hundred and seventy-five years.
[Genesis] [25]:[8] Then Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, old and satisfied with life, and he was gathered to his people.
[Genesis] [25]:[9] His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, facing Mamre,
[Genesis] [25]:[10] the field Abraham had bought from the Hittites. There Abraham was buried with his wife Sarah.
[Genesis] [25]:[11] After Abraham's death God blessed his son Isaac, and Isaac settled near Beer-lahai-roi.
[Genesis] [25]:[12] This is the account of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's servant, bore to Abraham.
[Genesis] [25]:[13] These are the names of Ishmael's sons, listed in the order of their birth: Nebaioth, Ishmael's firstborn, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
[Genesis] [25]:[14] Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
[Genesis] [25]:[15] Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
[Genesis] [25]:[16] These were the sons of Ishmael, and these were their names according to their settlements and encampments—twelve princes, each with his own tribe.
[Genesis] [25]:[17] Ishmael lived a hundred and thirty-seven years. Then he breathed his last and died, and he was gathered to his people.
[Genesis] [25]:[18] His descendants settled from Havilah as far as Shur, near the border of Egypt, in the direction of Asshur; and they lived in hostility toward all their kindred.
[Genesis] [25]:[19] This is the account of Isaac, Abraham's son. Abraham fathered Isaac.
[Genesis] [25]:[20] Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan-aram and sister of Laban the Aramean.
[Genesis] [25]:[21] Isaac prayed to the LORD on behalf of his wife, because she was barren. The LORD answered his prayer, and his wife Rebekah became pregnant.
[Genesis] [25]:[22] The children struggled with each other inside her, and she said, "If it is like this, why should I go on living?" So she went to inquire of the LORD.
[Genesis] [25]:[23] And the LORD said to her: "Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will separate from within you. One people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger."
[Genesis] [25]:[24] When the time came for her to give birth, there were twins in her womb.
[Genesis] [25]:[25] The first came out red, his whole body like a hairy cloak; so they named him Esau.
[Genesis] [25]:[26] Then his brother came out, his hand gripping Esau's heel; so he was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when they were born.
[Genesis] [25]:[27] The boys grew up, and Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the open country, while Jacob was a quiet man who stayed among the tents.
[Genesis] [25]:[28] Isaac loved Esau, because he had a taste for wild game; but Rebekah loved Jacob.
[Genesis] [25]:[29] One day, while Jacob was cooking a stew, Esau came in from the open country, exhausted.
[Genesis] [25]:[30] Esau said to Jacob, "Quick, let me gulp down some of that red stuff, that red stuff there—I'm exhausted!" That is why he was called Edom.
[Genesis] [25]:[31] Jacob said, "First sell me your birthright."
[Genesis] [25]:[32] "Look," said Esau, "I'm about to die. What good is a birthright to me?"
[Genesis] [25]:[33] Jacob said, "Swear it to me here and now." So he swore to him and sold his birthright to Jacob.
[Genesis] [25]:[34] Then Jacob gave him bread and lentil stew. He ate and drank, got up, and went on his way. So Esau despised his birthright.
[Genesis] [26]:[1] There was a famine in the land, besides the earlier famine that had come in the days of Abraham, and Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
[Genesis] [26]:[2] The LORD appeared to him and said: "Do not go down to Egypt. Settle in the land I will tell you of.
[Genesis] [26]:[3] Live in this land as a stranger, and I will be with you and bless you; for to you and to your offspring I will give all these lands, and I will fulfill the oath I swore to Abraham your father.
[Genesis] [26]:[4] I will make your offspring as many as the stars of heaven, and I will give your offspring all these lands, and through your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed—
[Genesis] [26]:[5] because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws."
[Genesis] [26]:[6] So Isaac stayed in Gerar.
[Genesis] [26]:[7] When the men of the place asked about his wife, he said, "She is my sister." He was afraid to say "my wife," thinking, "The men of the place might kill me over Rebekah, because she is beautiful."
[Genesis] [26]:[8] After he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down through a window and saw Isaac caressing Rebekah his wife.
[Genesis] [26]:[9] Abimelech summoned Isaac and said, "So she is your wife! How could you say, 'She is my sister'?" Isaac answered him, "Because I thought I might die on account of her."
[Genesis] [26]:[10] Abimelech said, "What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have slept with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us."
[Genesis] [26]:[11] So Abimelech gave orders to all the people: "Whoever touches this man or his wife shall surely be put to death."
[Genesis] [26]:[12] Isaac sowed in that land, and that same year he reaped a hundredfold, for the LORD blessed him.
[Genesis] [26]:[13] The man grew rich, and he kept growing richer until he became very wealthy.
[Genesis] [26]:[14] He had flocks and herds and a large household, and the Philistines envied him.
[Genesis] [26]:[15] All the wells his father's servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father the Philistines had stopped up and filled with earth.
[Genesis] [26]:[16] Then Abimelech said to Isaac, "Move away from us, for you have become far too powerful for us."
[Genesis] [26]:[17] So Isaac left there, camped in the Valley of Gerar, and settled there.
[Genesis] [26]:[18] Isaac dug again the wells of water that had been dug in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham's death, and he gave them the same names his father had given them.
[Genesis] [26]:[19] Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found there a well of fresh water.
[Genesis] [26]:[20] But the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen, saying, "The water is ours!" So he named the well Esek, because they contended with him. [Footnote: Esek means "contention."]
[Genesis] [26]:[21] Then they dug another well, and they quarreled over that one too; so he named it Sitnah.
[Genesis] [26]:[22] He moved on from there and dug another well, and over that one they did not quarrel. He named it Rehoboth, saying, "Now the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land."
[Genesis] [26]:[23] From there he went up to Beersheba.
[Genesis] [26]:[24] That night the LORD appeared to him and said, "I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your offspring for the sake of Abraham my servant."
[Genesis] [26]:[25] So he built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD. He pitched his tent there, and there Isaac's servants dug a well.
[Genesis] [26]:[26] Then Abimelech came to him from Gerar with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army.
[Genesis] [26]:[27] Isaac said to them, "Why have you come to me, since you hated me and sent me away from you?"
[Genesis] [26]:[28] They answered, "We have seen clearly that the LORD has been with you, so we said: Let there be a sworn agreement between us—between us and you—and let us make a covenant with you,
[Genesis] [26]:[29] that you will do us no harm, just as we did not touch you but did you nothing but good and sent you away in peace. You are now blessed by the LORD."
[Genesis] [26]:[30] So he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
[Genesis] [26]:[31] Early in the morning they rose and exchanged oaths with one another. Then Isaac sent them off, and they left him in peace.
[Genesis] [26]:[32] That same day Isaac's servants came and told him about the well they had dug, and said to him, "We have found water!"
[Genesis] [26]:[33] He named it Shibah; therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day. [Footnote: Shibah sounds like the Hebrew words for "oath" and "seven"; Beersheba means "well of the oath" or "well of seven."]
[Genesis] [26]:[34] When Esau was forty years old, he married Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite.
[Genesis] [26]:[35] They were a bitter grief to Isaac and Rebekah.
[Genesis] [27]:[1] When Isaac had grown old and his eyes were so dim that he could no longer see, he called Esau, his older son, and said to him, "My son." And he answered, "Here I am."
[Genesis] [27]:[2] Isaac said, "Look, I am old, and I do not know the day of my death.
[Genesis] [27]:[3] So now take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, go out to the field, and hunt game for me.
[Genesis] [27]:[4] Then prepare me the kind of tasty food I love and bring it to me to eat, so that I may bless you before I die."
[Genesis] [27]:[5] Rebekah was listening while Isaac spoke to his son Esau. When Esau went off to the field to hunt game and bring it back,
[Genesis] [27]:[6] Rebekah said to her son Jacob, "Listen, I overheard your father say to your brother Esau,
[Genesis] [27]:[7] 'Bring me game and prepare me tasty food to eat, so that I may bless you in the presence of the LORD before I die.'
[Genesis] [27]:[8] Now then, my son, listen to me and do exactly what I tell you.
[Genesis] [27]:[9] Go out to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, and I will make them into tasty food for your father, the kind he loves.
[Genesis] [27]:[10] Then take it to your father to eat, so that he may bless you before he dies."
[Genesis] [27]:[11] But Jacob said to his mother Rebekah, "Look, my brother Esau is a hairy man, and my skin is smooth.
[Genesis] [27]:[12] What if my father touches me? Then I will seem to him like a fraud, and I will bring a curse on myself instead of a blessing."
[Genesis] [27]:[13] His mother said to him, "Let the curse fall on me, my son. Just listen to me and go get them for me."
[Genesis] [27]:[14] So he went and got them and brought them to his mother, and she made the tasty food his father loved.
[Genesis] [27]:[15] Then Rebekah took the finest clothes of her older son Esau, which she kept in the house, and put them on her younger son Jacob.
[Genesis] [27]:[16] She covered his hands and the smooth part of his neck with the skins of the young goats,
[Genesis] [27]:[17] and she placed the tasty food and the bread she had made into the hands of her son Jacob.
[Genesis] [27]:[18] He went to his father and said, "My father." And he answered, "Here I am. Which of my sons are you?"
[Genesis] [27]:[19] Jacob said to his father, "I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Please sit up and eat some of my game, so that you may bless me."
[Genesis] [27]:[20] Isaac said to his son, "How did you find it so quickly, my son?" He answered, "The LORD your God brought it my way."
[Genesis] [27]:[21] Then Isaac said to Jacob, "Come closer, my son, so I can touch you and know whether you really are my son Esau or not."
[Genesis] [27]:[22] So Jacob came close to his father Isaac, who touched him and said, "The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau."
[Genesis] [27]:[23] He did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like his brother Esau's hands. So he blessed him.
[Genesis] [27]:[24] He asked, "Are you really my son Esau?" And he answered, "I am."
[Genesis] [27]:[25] Then he said, "Bring it to me, and let me eat some of my son's game, so that I may bless you." He brought it to him, and he ate; and he brought him wine, and he drank.
[Genesis] [27]:[26] Then his father Isaac said to him, "Come here and kiss me, my son."
[Genesis] [27]:[27] So he came near and kissed him. And when Isaac smelled the scent of his clothes, he blessed him and said: "Ah, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field the LORD has blessed.
[Genesis] [27]:[28] May God give you the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth, an abundance of grain and new wine.
[Genesis] [27]:[29] May peoples serve you and nations bow down to you. Be master over your brothers, and may your mother's sons bow down to you. Cursed be those who curse you, and blessed be those who bless you."
[Genesis] [27]:[30] Isaac had just finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob had barely left his father's presence, when his brother Esau came in from his hunt.
[Genesis] [27]:[31] He too prepared tasty food and brought it to his father. He said to him, "Let my father sit up and eat some of his son's game, so that you may bless me."
[Genesis] [27]:[32] His father Isaac said to him, "Who are you?" He answered, "I am your son, your firstborn, Esau."
[Genesis] [27]:[33] Isaac trembled violently and said, "Who was it, then, who hunted game and brought it to me? I ate it all before you came, and I blessed him—and blessed he will remain!"
[Genesis] [27]:[34] When Esau heard his father's words, he let out a loud and bitter cry and said to his father, "Bless me too, my father!"
[Genesis] [27]:[35] But he said, "Your brother came with deceit and took your blessing."
[Genesis] [27]:[36] Esau said, "Is he not rightly named Jacob? He has cheated me twice now. He took my birthright, and look, now he has taken my blessing!" Then he asked, "Haven't you saved a blessing for me?"
[Genesis] [27]:[37] Isaac answered Esau, "I have made him your master and given him all his brothers as servants, and I have sustained him with grain and new wine. What then can I possibly do for you, my son?"
[Genesis] [27]:[38] Esau said to his father, "Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me too, my father!" And Esau wept aloud.
[Genesis] [27]:[39] Then his father Isaac answered him: "Look, your dwelling will be far from the richness of the earth, far from the dew of heaven above."[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew preposition can also be read as "away from" or "from," so the line may also mean "your dwelling will be of the richness of the earth and of the dew of heaven above," as in the blessing of verse 28.
[Genesis] [27]:[40] You will live by your sword, and you will serve your brother. But when you grow restless, you will break his yoke from your neck."
[Genesis] [27]:[41] Esau held a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing his father had given him, and Esau said to himself, "The days of mourning for my father are near; then I will kill my brother Jacob."
[Genesis] [27]:[42] When Rebekah was told what her older son Esau had said, she sent for her younger son Jacob and said to him, "Look, your brother Esau is comforting himself with the thought of killing you.
[Genesis] [27]:[43] Now then, my son, listen to me: get up and flee to my brother Laban in Haran.
[Genesis] [27]:[44] Stay with him a while, until your brother's fury subsides,
[Genesis] [27]:[45] until your brother's anger against you turns away and he forgets what you did to him. Then I will send for you and bring you back from there. Why should I lose both of you in a single day?"
[Genesis] [27]:[46] Then Rebekah said to Isaac, "I am weary of my life because of the Hittite women. If Jacob takes a wife from the Hittite women, such as these, from the daughters of this land, what good is my life to me?"
[Genesis] [28]:[1] Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and charged him: "Do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.
[Genesis] [28]:[2] Get up and go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel, your mother's father, and take a wife from there, from the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
[Genesis] [28]:[3] May God Almighty bless you, make you fruitful, and multiply you, so that you become a company of peoples.
[Genesis] [28]:[4] May he give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your offspring with you, so that you may take possession of the land where you now live as a stranger, the land God gave to Abraham."
[Genesis] [28]:[5] So Isaac sent Jacob off, and he went to Paddan-aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.
[Genesis] [28]:[6] Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to take a wife from there, and that when he blessed him he charged him, "Do not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,"
[Genesis] [28]:[7] and that Jacob had obeyed his father and mother and gone to Paddan-aram.
[Genesis] [28]:[8] Esau then realized how displeasing the daughters of Canaan were to his father Isaac,
[Genesis] [28]:[9] so he went to Ishmael and, in addition to the wives he had, married Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son, the sister of Nebaioth.
[Genesis] [28]:[10] Jacob left Beersheba and set out for Haran.
[Genesis] [28]:[11] He came to a certain place and stayed the night there, because the sun had set. Taking one of the stones of that place, he put it under his head and lay down to sleep.
[Genesis] [28]:[12] And he dreamed: there was a stairway set on the earth, its top reaching to heaven, and the angels of God were going up and coming down on it.
[Genesis] [28]:[13] And there was the LORD, standing above it,* saying: "I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land on which you are lying I will give to you and to your offspring. [*Footnote: Or "standing beside him."]
[Genesis] [28]:[14] Your offspring will be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread out to the west and the east, to the north and the south. In you and in your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed.
[Genesis] [28]:[15] And look, I am with you. I will keep you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land. I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you."
[Genesis] [28]:[16] Jacob woke from his sleep and said, "Surely the LORD is in this place, and I did not know it."
[Genesis] [28]:[17] He was afraid and said, "How awesome is this place! This is nothing less than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven."
[Genesis] [28]:[18] Early in the morning Jacob took the stone he had put under his head, set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on top of it.
[Genesis] [28]:[19] He named that place Bethel,* though the city had earlier been called Luz. [*Footnote: Bethel means "house of God."]
[Genesis] [28]:[20] Then Jacob made a vow: "If God will be with me and keep me on this journey I am making, and give me bread to eat and clothes to wear,
[Genesis] [28]:[21] and I return safely to my father's house, then the LORD will be my God,
[Genesis] [28]:[22] and this stone that I have set up as a pillar will be God's house; and of all that you give me I will surely give you a tenth."
[Genesis] [29]:[1] Then Jacob set out on his way and came to the land of the eastern peoples.
[Genesis] [29]:[2] There he saw a well in the open country, and three flocks of sheep lying beside it, for the flocks were watered from that well. A large stone lay over the mouth of the well.
[Genesis] [29]:[3] When all the flocks had gathered there, the shepherds would roll the stone from the mouth of the well, water the sheep, and put the stone back in its place over the mouth of the well.
[Genesis] [29]:[4] Jacob said to them, "My brothers, where are you from?" "We are from Haran," they answered.
[Genesis] [29]:[5] He said to them, "Do you know Laban, the son of Nahor?" "We know him," they said.
[Genesis] [29]:[6] "Is he well?" he asked. "He is well," they said, "and here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep."
[Genesis] [29]:[7] Then he said, "Look, the sun is still high; it isn't time to gather the livestock. Water the sheep and go on grazing them."
[Genesis] [29]:[8] But they said, "We can't, until all the flocks have been gathered and the stone is rolled from the mouth of the well. Only then can we water the sheep."
[Genesis] [29]:[9] While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep, for she was a shepherdess.
[Genesis] [29]:[10] When Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his mother's brother Laban, and Laban's sheep, he stepped up, rolled the stone from the mouth of the well, and watered the flock of his mother's brother Laban.
[Genesis] [29]:[11] Then Jacob kissed Rachel, and he wept aloud.
[Genesis] [29]:[12] He told Rachel that he was her father's kinsman, the son of Rebekah, and she ran and told her father.
[Genesis] [29]:[13] As soon as Laban heard the news about Jacob, his sister's son, he ran to meet him, embraced him, kissed him, and brought him to his house. And Jacob told Laban everything that had happened.
[Genesis] [29]:[14] Laban said to him, "You really are my own flesh and blood." So Jacob stayed with him a full month.
[Genesis] [29]:[15] Then Laban said to Jacob, "Just because you are my kinsman, should you work for me for nothing? Tell me what your wages should be."
[Genesis] [29]:[16] Now Laban had two daughters. The older was named Leah, and the younger Rachel.
[Genesis] [29]:[17] Leah's eyes were weak, but Rachel was shapely and beautiful.
[Genesis] [29]:[18] Jacob loved Rachel, so he said, "I will work for you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel."
[Genesis] [29]:[19] Laban said, "Better that I give her to you than to another man. Stay with me."
[Genesis] [29]:[20] So Jacob worked seven years for Rachel, and they seemed to him like only a few days, so great was his love for her.
[Genesis] [29]:[21] Then Jacob said to Laban, "Give me my wife. My time is fulfilled, and I want to be with her."
[Genesis] [29]:[22] So Laban gathered all the men of the place and gave a feast.
[Genesis] [29]:[23] When evening came, Laban took his daughter Leah and brought her to Jacob, and he slept with her.
[Genesis] [29]:[24] Laban also gave his slave girl Zilpah to his daughter Leah to be her slave girl.
[Genesis] [29]:[25] When morning came, there was Leah! So Jacob said to Laban, "What have you done to me? Wasn't it for Rachel that I served you? Why have you deceived me?"
[Genesis] [29]:[26] Laban answered, "It is not our custom here to give the younger before the firstborn.
[Genesis] [29]:[27] Finish this bridal week, and we will give you the other one as well, in return for another seven years of work."
[Genesis] [29]:[28] So Jacob did this. He finished the week, and Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.
[Genesis] [29]:[29] Laban also gave his slave girl Bilhah to his daughter Rachel to be her slave girl.
[Genesis] [29]:[30] Jacob slept with Rachel too, and he loved Rachel more than Leah. And he worked for Laban another seven years.
[Genesis] [29]:[31] When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, he opened her womb; but Rachel remained childless.
[Genesis] [29]:[32] Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she named him Reuben, for she said, "The LORD has seen my misery. Surely now my husband will love me."
[Genesis] [29]:[33] She conceived again and gave birth to a son, and she said, "Because the LORD heard that I am unloved, he has given me this one too." So she named him Simeon.
[Genesis] [29]:[34] She conceived again and gave birth to a son, and she said, "Now at last my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons." So he was named Levi.
[Genesis] [29]:[35] She conceived again and gave birth to a son, and she said, "This time I will praise the LORD." So she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing children.
[Genesis] [30]:[1] When Rachel saw that she was bearing Jacob no children, she envied her sister. She said to Jacob, "Give me children, or I will die!"
[Genesis] [30]:[2] Jacob became angry with Rachel and said, "Am I in the place of God, who has kept you from bearing children?"
[Genesis] [30]:[3] Then she said, "Here is my servant Bilhah. Sleep with her, so that she may give birth on my knees and I too may be built up through her."
[Genesis] [30]:[4] So she gave him her servant Bilhah as a wife, and Jacob slept with her.
[Genesis] [30]:[5] Bilhah conceived and bore Jacob a son.
[Genesis] [30]:[6] Then Rachel said, "God has judged in my favor; he has heard my voice and given me a son." So she named him Dan.
[Genesis] [30]:[7] Rachel's servant Bilhah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.
[Genesis] [30]:[8] Then Rachel said, "With a mighty struggle I have wrestled with my sister, and I have won." So she named him Naphtali.
[Genesis] [30]:[9] When Leah saw that she had stopped bearing children, she took her servant Zilpah and gave her to Jacob as a wife.
[Genesis] [30]:[10] Leah's servant Zilpah bore Jacob a son.
[Genesis] [30]:[11] Then Leah said, "Good fortune has come!" So she named him Gad.
[Genesis] [30]:[12] Leah's servant Zilpah bore Jacob a second son.
[Genesis] [30]:[13] Then Leah said, "How happy I am! The women will call me happy." So she named him Asher.
[Genesis] [30]:[14] During the wheat harvest Reuben went out and found mandrakes in the field, and he brought them to his mother Leah. Rachel said to Leah, "Please give me some of your son's mandrakes."
[Genesis] [30]:[15] But she answered her, "Is it a small thing that you took my husband? Will you take my son's mandrakes as well?" "Very well," Rachel said, "he may sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son's mandrakes."
[Genesis] [30]:[16] When Jacob came in from the field that evening, Leah went out to meet him and said, "You must come to me, for I have hired you with my son's mandrakes." So he slept with her that night.
[Genesis] [30]:[17] God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a fifth son.
[Genesis] [30]:[18] Then Leah said, "God has given me my wages, because I gave my servant to my husband." So she named him Issachar.
[Genesis] [30]:[19] Leah conceived again and bore Jacob a sixth son.
[Genesis] [30]:[20] Then Leah said, "God has given me a good gift. This time my husband will honor me, because I have borne him six sons." So she named him Zebulun.
[Genesis] [30]:[21] Later she bore a daughter and named her Dinah.
[Genesis] [30]:[22] Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and opened her womb.
[Genesis] [30]:[23] She conceived and bore a son, and she said, "God has taken away my disgrace."
[Genesis] [30]:[24] She named him Joseph, saying, "May the LORD add another son to me."
[Genesis] [30]:[25] After Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, "Send me on my way, so I can return to my own place and my own land.
[Genesis] [30]:[26] Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served you, and let me go. You know how hard I have worked for you."
[Genesis] [30]:[27] But Laban said to him, "If I have found favor in your eyes, please stay. I have learned by divination that the LORD has blessed me because of you."
[Genesis] [30]:[28] And he added, "Name your wages, and I will pay them."
[Genesis] [30]:[29] Jacob said to him, "You know how I have served you and how your livestock has fared under my care.
[Genesis] [30]:[30] The little you had before I came has increased greatly, and the LORD has blessed you wherever I set my foot. But now, when may I do something for my own household?"
[Genesis] [30]:[31] "What shall I give you?" Laban asked. "Don't give me anything," Jacob replied. "But if you will do this one thing for me, I will go on tending and watching over your flocks:
[Genesis] [30]:[32] Let me go through all your flocks today and remove from them every speckled or spotted sheep, every dark-colored lamb, and every spotted or speckled goat. These will be my wages.
[Genesis] [30]:[33] And my honesty will testify for me in the future, whenever you come to check on my wages. Any goat in my possession that is not speckled or spotted, or any lamb that is not dark-colored, will be counted as stolen."
[Genesis] [30]:[34] "Agreed," said Laban. "Let it be as you have said."
[Genesis] [30]:[35] That same day he removed all the male goats that were streaked or spotted, and all the speckled or spotted female goats—every one that had white on it—and all the dark-colored lambs, and he put them in the care of his sons.
[Genesis] [30]:[36] Then he put a three-day journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob continued to tend the rest of Laban's flocks.
[Genesis] [30]:[37] Jacob, however, took fresh-cut branches of poplar, almond, and plane trees, and peeled white stripes in them, exposing the white inner wood of the branches.
[Genesis] [30]:[38] Then he set the branches he had peeled in the troughs, in the watering channels where the flocks came to drink, directly in front of the animals. When they came to drink, they bred,
[Genesis] [30]:[39] and since they bred in front of the branches, they bore young that were streaked, speckled, or spotted.
[Genesis] [30]:[40] Jacob separated the lambs and made the flocks face toward the streaked and dark-colored animals in Laban's flock. He put his own droves by themselves and did not place them with Laban's flock.
[Genesis] [30]:[41] Whenever the stronger of the flock were breeding, Jacob would set the branches in the troughs before their eyes, so that they would breed near the branches.
[Genesis] [30]:[42] But when the animals were feeble, he did not place the branches there. So the weak ones went to Laban and the strong ones to Jacob.
[Genesis] [30]:[43] In this way the man grew exceedingly prosperous, and he came to own large flocks, as well as female and male servants, camels, and donkeys.
[Genesis] [31]:[1] Jacob heard that Laban's sons were saying, "Jacob has taken everything that belonged to our father, and out of what was our father's he has built up all this wealth."
[Genesis] [31]:[2] And Jacob saw from Laban's face that he was no longer disposed toward him as before.
[Genesis] [31]:[3] Then the LORD said to Jacob, "Return to the land of your fathers, to your kindred, and I will be with you."
[Genesis] [31]:[4] So Jacob sent word and called Rachel and Leah out to the field where his flock was,
[Genesis] [31]:[5] and he said to them, "I can see from your father's face that he is not disposed toward me as before. But the God of my father has been with me.
[Genesis] [31]:[6] You yourselves know that I have served your father with all my strength,
[Genesis] [31]:[7] yet your father has cheated me and changed my wages ten times over. But God did not let him harm me.
[Genesis] [31]:[8] If he said, 'The speckled ones will be your wages,' then the whole flock bore speckled young; and if he said, 'The striped ones will be your wages,' then the whole flock bore striped young.
[Genesis] [31]:[9] So God has taken away your father's livestock and given it to me.
[Genesis] [31]:[10] Once, when the flocks were breeding, I looked up and saw in a dream that the male goats mounting the flock were striped, speckled, and mottled.
[Genesis] [31]:[11] And the angel of God said to me in the dream, 'Jacob!' I answered, 'Here I am.'
[Genesis] [31]:[12] He said, 'Look up and see: all the male goats mounting the flock are striped, speckled, and mottled, for I have seen everything Laban has been doing to you.
[Genesis] [31]:[13] I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar and made a vow to me. Now get up, leave this land, and return to the land of your birth.'"
[Genesis] [31]:[14] Then Rachel and Leah answered him, "Do we still have any share or inheritance in our father's house?
[Genesis] [31]:[15] Are we not treated as strangers by him? He sold us, and then he devoured our purchase price.
[Genesis] [31]:[16] Surely all the wealth God has taken from our father belongs to us and to our children. So do whatever God has told you."
[Genesis] [31]:[17] Then Jacob set out. He put his children and his wives on the camels,
[Genesis] [31]:[18] and drove off all his livestock, along with all the possessions he had accumulated—the livestock he had acquired in Paddan-aram—to go to his father Isaac in the land of Canaan.
[Genesis] [31]:[19] Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep, and Rachel stole her father's household gods.
[Genesis] [31]:[20] Jacob also deceived Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was slipping away.
[Genesis] [31]:[21] So he fled with all he had. He crossed the River—that is, the Euphrates—and set his face toward the hill country of Gilead.
[Genesis] [31]:[22] On the third day Laban was told that Jacob had fled.
[Genesis] [31]:[23] He took his kinsmen with him and pursued Jacob for seven days, catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
[Genesis] [31]:[24] But that night God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream and said to him, "Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad."
[Genesis] [31]:[25] Laban overtook Jacob, who had pitched his tent in the hill country; Laban and his kinsmen camped there in the hill country of Gilead as well.
[Genesis] [31]:[26] Laban said to Jacob, "What have you done? You have deceived me and carried off my daughters like captives taken in war.
[Genesis] [31]:[27] Why did you run away in secret and deceive me instead of telling me? I would have sent you off with rejoicing and singing, with tambourine and lyre.
[Genesis] [31]:[28] You did not even let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye. What a foolish thing you have done!
[Genesis] [31]:[29] I have the power to do you harm, but last night the God of your father said to me, 'Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.'
[Genesis] [31]:[30] Now you have gone off because you longed for your father's house—but why did you steal my gods?"
[Genesis] [31]:[31] Jacob answered Laban, "I was afraid; I thought you would take your daughters from me by force.
[Genesis] [31]:[32] But if you find anyone here with your gods, that person shall not live. In the presence of our kinsmen, identify anything of yours that I have, and take it." For Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them.
[Genesis] [31]:[33] So Laban went into Jacob's tent, and into Leah's tent, and into the tent of the two servant women, but found nothing. When he came out of Leah's tent, he entered Rachel's tent.
[Genesis] [31]:[34] But Rachel had taken the household gods and put them in the camel's saddle and was sitting on them. Laban searched through the whole tent but found nothing.
[Genesis] [31]:[35] She said to her father, "Do not be angry, my lord, that I cannot rise before you; I am having my period." So he searched but did not find the household gods.
[Genesis] [31]:[36] Then Jacob became angry and confronted Laban. "What is my offense?" he said. "What sin have I committed that you hunt me down like this?
[Genesis] [31]:[37] You have searched through all my belongings. What have you found of your household goods? Set it here in front of my kinsmen and yours, and let them judge between the two of us.
[Genesis] [31]:[38] Twenty years I have been with you. Your ewes and your goats never miscarried, and I never ate a ram from your flock.
[Genesis] [31]:[39] I never brought you an animal torn by beasts; I bore the loss myself. You demanded it from my hand, whether stolen by day or stolen by night.
[Genesis] [31]:[40] The heat consumed me by day and the cold by night, and sleep fled from my eyes.
[Genesis] [31]:[41] For twenty years I have been in your household. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks, and you changed my wages ten times over.
[Genesis] [31]:[42] If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, you would surely have sent me away empty-handed. But God saw my hardship and the labor of my hands, and last night he rendered judgment."
[Genesis] [31]:[43] Laban answered Jacob, "The daughters are my daughters, the children are my children, the flocks are my flocks—everything you see is mine. Yet what can I do today about these daughters of mine, or about the children they have borne?
[Genesis] [31]:[44] Come now, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it stand as a witness between us."
[Genesis] [31]:[45] So Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar.
[Genesis] [31]:[46] Jacob said to his kinsmen, "Gather stones." So they took stones and made a heap, and they ate there beside the heap.
[Genesis] [31]:[47] Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.[^1] [^1]: Both names mean "heap of witness"—the first in Aramaic, the second in Hebrew.
[Genesis] [31]:[48] Laban said, "This heap is a witness between you and me today." That is why it was named Galeed.
[Genesis] [31]:[49] It was also called Mizpah, because he said, "May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are out of each other's sight.
[Genesis] [31]:[50] If you mistreat my daughters, or take other wives besides them—though no one is with us—remember that God is a witness between you and me."
[Genesis] [31]:[51] Laban also said to Jacob, "Here is this heap, and here is this pillar I have set up between you and me.
[Genesis] [31]:[52] This heap is a witness, and this pillar is a witness, that I will not go past this heap to your side, and that you will not go past this heap and this pillar to my side, to do harm.
[Genesis] [31]:[53] May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us." And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
[Genesis] [31]:[54] Then Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and invited his kinsmen to eat a meal. They ate and spent the night on the mountain.
[Genesis] [32]:[1] Early in the morning Laban kissed his grandchildren and his daughters and blessed them, and then he left and returned home.[^1] [^1]: Hebrew: *his sons*, here understood as his grandsons, the children of Jacob.
[Genesis] [32]:[2] Jacob also went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
[Genesis] [32]:[3] When Jacob saw them, he said, "This is God's camp!" So he named that place Mahanaim.[^1] [^1]: *Mahanaim* means "two camps," anticipating Jacob's division of his household in verse 8.
[Genesis] [32]:[4] Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom.
[Genesis] [32]:[5] He instructed them: "Say this to my lord Esau: 'This is what your servant Jacob says: I have been staying with Laban and have remained there until now.
[Genesis] [32]:[6] I have acquired oxen and donkeys, flocks, and male and female servants. I am sending this message to my lord in the hope of finding favor in your eyes.'"
[Genesis] [32]:[7] The messengers returned to Jacob and said, "We went to your brother Esau, and he is already on his way to meet you—with four hundred men."
[Genesis] [32]:[8] Jacob was terrified and distressed. He divided the people who were with him, along with the flocks, herds, and camels, into two camps,
[Genesis] [32]:[9] thinking, "If Esau comes and attacks the one camp, the camp that is left will escape."
[Genesis] [32]:[10] Then Jacob prayed, "God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac, LORD, you told me, 'Return to your country and to your kindred, and I will deal well with you.'
[Genesis] [32]:[11] I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness you have shown your servant. I crossed this Jordan with nothing but my staff, and now I have become two camps.
[Genesis] [32]:[12] Rescue me, I pray, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau, for I am afraid he will come and strike me down, mothers and children alike.
[Genesis] [32]:[13] But you said, 'I will surely deal well with you and make your offspring like the sand of the sea, too numerous to count.'"
[Genesis] [32]:[14] He spent that night there, and from what he had with him he selected a gift for his brother Esau:
[Genesis] [32]:[15] two hundred female goats and twenty males, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,
[Genesis] [32]:[16] thirty nursing camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten males.
[Genesis] [32]:[17] He put them in the care of his servants, each herd by itself, and told them, "Go on ahead of me, and keep some distance between the herds."
[Genesis] [32]:[18] He instructed the one in front: "When my brother Esau meets you and asks, 'Whose servant are you? Where are you going? And whose animals are these ahead of you?'—
[Genesis] [32]:[19] then you are to say, 'They belong to your servant Jacob. They are a gift sent to my lord Esau, and he himself is coming along behind us.'"
[Genesis] [32]:[20] He gave the same instructions to the second, the third, and all the others who followed the herds: "This is what you are to say to Esau when you meet him,
[Genesis] [32]:[21] and be sure to add, 'Your servant Jacob is right behind us.'" For he thought, "I will appease him with the gift that goes ahead of me; afterward, when I see his face, perhaps he will receive me."
[Genesis] [32]:[22] So the gift went on ahead of him, while he himself spent that night in the camp.
[Genesis] [32]:[23] That night he got up, took his two wives, his two servant women, and his eleven children, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.
[Genesis] [32]:[24] He took them and sent them across the stream, and he sent over all his possessions.
[Genesis] [32]:[25] So Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him until daybreak.
[Genesis] [32]:[26] When the man saw that he could not overpower him, he touched the socket of Jacob's hip, so that it was wrenched as they wrestled.
[Genesis] [32]:[27] Then he said, "Let me go, for the day is breaking." But Jacob said, "I will not let you go unless you bless me."
[Genesis] [32]:[28] The man asked him, "What is your name?" "Jacob," he answered.
[Genesis] [32]:[29] Then he said, "Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with men, and have prevailed."
[Genesis] [32]:[30] Jacob said, "Please tell me your name." But he replied, "Why do you ask my name?" And there he blessed him.
[Genesis] [32]:[31] So Jacob named the place Peniel, saying, "I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared."[^1] [^1]: *Peniel* (also spelled *Penuel* in verse 32) means "face of God."
[Genesis] [32]:[32] The sun rose above him as he passed Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.
[Genesis] [32]:[33] That is why to this day the Israelites do not eat the sinew of the hip that is on the hip socket, because the man touched Jacob's hip socket at that sinew.
[Genesis] [33]:[1] Jacob looked up and saw Esau coming, and with him four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two servant women.
[Genesis] [33]:[2] He put the servant women and their children first, Leah and her children next, and Rachel and Joseph last.
[Genesis] [33]:[3] He himself went on ahead of them, bowing to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.
[Genesis] [33]:[4] But Esau ran to meet him and embraced him; he threw his arms around his neck and kissed him, and they wept.
[Genesis] [33]:[5] Then Esau looked up and saw the women and the children, and he asked, "Who are these with you?" Jacob answered, "The children God has graciously given your servant."
[Genesis] [33]:[6] Then the servant women came forward with their children and bowed down.
[Genesis] [33]:[7] Leah also came forward with her children, and they bowed down. Last of all Joseph and Rachel came forward and bowed down.
[Genesis] [33]:[8] Esau asked, "What was the meaning of all those droves I met?" Jacob said, "To find favor in my lord's eyes."
[Genesis] [33]:[9] But Esau said, "I have plenty, my brother. Keep what is yours."
[Genesis] [33]:[10] Jacob replied, "No, please—if I have found favor in your eyes, then accept this gift from my hand. For to see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have received me so kindly.
[Genesis] [33]:[11] "Please take the blessing I have brought you, for God has been gracious to me, and I have all I need." So Jacob urged him, and he accepted it.
[Genesis] [33]:[12] Then Esau said, "Let us set out and be on our way, and I will travel alongside you."
[Genesis] [33]:[13] But Jacob said to him, "My lord knows that the children are frail, and that the flocks and herds are nursing their young and are my charge. If they are driven hard for even a single day, all the flocks will die.
[Genesis] [33]:[14] Let my lord go on ahead of his servant, and I will move along slowly, at the pace of the herds before me and the pace of the children, until I come to my lord in Seir."
[Genesis] [33]:[15] Esau said, "Then let me leave some of my men with you." "Why do that?" Jacob answered. "Only let me find favor in my lord's eyes."
[Genesis] [33]:[16] So that day Esau started back on his way to Seir.
[Genesis] [33]:[17] Jacob, however, journeyed on to Succoth, where he built himself a house and made shelters for his livestock. That is why the place is called Succoth.
[Genesis] [33]:[18] After coming from Paddan Aram, Jacob arrived safely at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan and camped within sight of the city.
[Genesis] [33]:[19] For a hundred pieces of silver he bought from the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father, the plot of ground where he had pitched his tent.[fn]
[Genesis] [33]:[20] There he set up an altar and called it El Elohe Israel—God, the God of Israel.
[Genesis] [34]:[1] Now Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the women of the land.
[Genesis] [34]:[2] And Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of that region, saw her; he seized her, lay with her, and violated her.
[Genesis] [34]:[3] And his soul clung to Dinah, Jacob's daughter; he loved the girl and spoke tenderly to her.
[Genesis] [34]:[4] So Shechem said to his father Hamor, "Get me this girl as my wife."
[Genesis] [34]:[5] Jacob heard that Shechem had defiled his daughter Dinah, but his sons were with his livestock in the field, so Jacob held his peace until they came home.
[Genesis] [34]:[6] Then Hamor, Shechem's father, went out to Jacob to speak with him.
[Genesis] [34]:[7] When Jacob's sons came in from the field and heard of it, the men were deeply grieved and burned with anger, because Shechem had done an outrageous thing in Israel by lying with Jacob's daughter—a thing that must never be done.
[Genesis] [34]:[8] Hamor said to them, "My son Shechem has his heart set on your daughter. Please give her to him as his wife.
[Genesis] [34]:[9] Intermarry with us: give us your daughters, and take our daughters for yourselves.
[Genesis] [34]:[10] Settle among us. The land is open before you—live in it, trade in it, and acquire property in it."
[Genesis] [34]:[11] And Shechem said to Dinah's father and brothers, "Let me find favor in your eyes, and I will give whatever you ask of me.
[Genesis] [34]:[12] Set the bride-price and the gift as high as you like, and I will pay whatever you demand. Only give me the girl as my wife."
[Genesis] [34]:[13] Jacob's sons answered Shechem and his father Hamor with deceit, because Shechem had defiled their sister Dinah.
[Genesis] [34]:[14] They said to them, "We cannot do such a thing—give our sister to a man who is uncircumcised. That would be a disgrace to us.
[Genesis] [34]:[15] We will consent to you on one condition only: that you become like us by having every male among you circumcised.
[Genesis] [34]:[16] Then we will give you our daughters and take your daughters for ourselves. We will live among you and become one people.
[Genesis] [34]:[17] But if you will not listen to us and be circumcised, we will take our daughter and go."
[Genesis] [34]:[18] Their proposal seemed good to Hamor and to his son Shechem.
[Genesis] [34]:[19] The young man lost no time in doing what they asked, because he was delighted with Jacob's daughter; and he was the most honored of all his father's household.
[Genesis] [34]:[20] So Hamor and his son Shechem went to the gate of their city and spoke to the men of the city:
[Genesis] [34]:[21] "These men are at peace with us. Let them settle in the land and trade in it; the land is large enough for them. We can take their daughters as our wives and give them our daughters.
[Genesis] [34]:[22] But the men will consent to live with us and become one people on this one condition: that every male among us be circumcised, as they are circumcised.
[Genesis] [34]:[23] Will not their herds, their property, and all their livestock become ours? Let us only give them our consent, and they will settle among us."
[Genesis] [34]:[24] All the men who went out from the city gate listened to Hamor and his son Shechem, and every male was circumcised.
[Genesis] [34]:[25] On the third day, while they were still in pain, two of Jacob's sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, took their swords, came against the unsuspecting city, and killed every male.
[Genesis] [34]:[26] They put Hamor and his son Shechem to the sword, took Dinah out of Shechem's house, and left.
[Genesis] [34]:[27] Jacob's sons came upon the slain and plundered the city, because its men had defiled their sister.
[Genesis] [34]:[28] They seized the flocks, the herds, the donkeys, and everything else in the city and in the fields.
[Genesis] [34]:[29] They took captive all their children and their wives, and carried off all their wealth and everything in the houses.
[Genesis] [34]:[30] Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, "You have brought disaster on me by making me a stench to the inhabitants of this land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites. My men are few; if they band together against me and attack me, I and my household will be destroyed."
[Genesis] [34]:[31] But they answered, "Should he treat our sister like a prostitute?"
[Genesis] [35]:[1] Then God said to Jacob, "Arise, go up to Bethel and settle there, and build an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you were fleeing from your brother Esau."
[Genesis] [35]:[2] So Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, "Get rid of the foreign gods among you, purify yourselves, and change your clothes.
[Genesis] [35]:[3] Let us set out and go up to Bethel, and there I will build an altar to the God who answered me in the day of my distress and who has been with me wherever I have gone."
[Genesis] [35]:[4] So they handed over to Jacob all the foreign gods they had and the rings in their ears, and Jacob buried them under the terebinth near Shechem.
[Genesis] [35]:[5] Then they set out, and the terror of God fell on the towns around them, so that no one pursued the sons of Jacob.
[Genesis] [35]:[6] Jacob came to Luz in the land of Canaan—that is, Bethel—he and all the people with him.
[Genesis] [35]:[7] There he built an altar and named the place El Bethel, because it was there that God had revealed himself to him when he was fleeing from his brother.
[Genesis] [35]:[8] Now Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died and was buried below Bethel under the oak; so he named it Allon Bakuth.
[Genesis] [35]:[9] God appeared to Jacob again after he came from Paddan Aram, and he blessed him.
[Genesis] [35]:[10] God said to him, "Your name is Jacob, but you will no longer be called Jacob; your name will be Israel." So he named him Israel.
[Genesis] [35]:[11] And God said to him, "I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation—indeed a company of nations—will come from you, and kings will descend from you.
[Genesis] [35]:[12] The land I gave to Abraham and Isaac I will give to you, and to your offspring after you I will give this land."
[Genesis] [35]:[13] Then God went up from him at the place where he had spoken with him.
[Genesis] [35]:[14] Jacob set up a pillar of stone at the place where God had spoken with him, and he poured out a drink offering on it and poured oil over it.
[Genesis] [35]:[15] And Jacob named the place where God had spoken with him Bethel.
[Genesis] [35]:[16] They moved on from Bethel, and while they were still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel went into labor, and her labor was severe.
[Genesis] [35]:[17] As she struggled in her labor, the midwife said to her, "Do not be afraid—you have another son."
[Genesis] [35]:[18] As her life slipped away and she was dying, she named him Ben-Oni, but his father called him Benjamin.
[Genesis] [35]:[19] So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem.
[Genesis] [35]:[20] Jacob set up a pillar over her grave, and to this day that pillar marks Rachel's grave.
[Genesis] [35]:[21] Israel moved on and pitched his tent beyond Migdal Eder.
[Genesis] [35]:[22] While Israel was living in that land, Reuben went and slept with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and Israel heard of it. Jacob had twelve sons:
[Genesis] [35]:[23] The sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.
[Genesis] [35]:[24] The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
[Genesis] [35]:[25] The sons of Bilhah, Rachel's servant: Dan and Naphtali.
[Genesis] [35]:[26] The sons of Zilpah, Leah's servant: Gad and Asher. These were the sons of Jacob, born to him in Paddan Aram.
[Genesis] [35]:[27] Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre in Kiriath Arba—that is, Hebron—where Abraham and Isaac had lived as strangers.
[Genesis] [35]:[28] Isaac lived a hundred and eighty years.
[Genesis] [35]:[29] Then Isaac breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years; and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
[Genesis] [36]:[1] This is the family history of Esau, that is, Edom.
[Genesis] [36]:[2] Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah daughter of Anah, granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite,[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew reads "daughter of Zibeon"; according to verses 24–25 Zibeon was Anah's father, so "granddaughter" is intended.
[Genesis] [36]:[3] and Basemath daughter of Ishmael, the sister of Nebaioth.
[Genesis] [36]:[4] Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau, and Basemath bore Reuel.
[Genesis] [36]:[5] Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These were the sons of Esau, born to him in the land of Canaan.
[Genesis] [36]:[6] Esau took his wives, his sons and daughters, and everyone in his household, along with his livestock, all his animals, and all the property he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and he moved to another land, away from his brother Jacob.
[Genesis] [36]:[7] Their possessions were too great for them to live together; the land where they were staying could not support them because of their livestock.
[Genesis] [36]:[8] So Esau settled in the hill country of Seir. Esau is Edom.
[Genesis] [36]:[9] This is the family history of Esau, the father of the Edomites, in the hill country of Seir.
[Genesis] [36]:[10] These are the names of Esau's sons: Eliphaz, son of Esau's wife Adah; Reuel, son of Esau's wife Basemath.
[Genesis] [36]:[11] The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.
[Genesis] [36]:[12] Timna was a concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz, and she bore Amalek to Eliphaz. These were the descendants of Esau's wife Adah.
[Genesis] [36]:[13] These were the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the descendants of Esau's wife Basemath.
[Genesis] [36]:[14] These were the sons of Esau's wife Oholibamah, daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon: she bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah to Esau.
[Genesis] [36]:[15] These are the chiefs among Esau's descendants. The sons of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn: Chief Teman, Chief Omar, Chief Zepho, Chief Kenaz,
[Genesis] [36]:[16] Chief Korah, Chief Gatam, Chief Amalek. These were the chiefs descended from Eliphaz in the land of Edom; they were the descendants of Adah.
[Genesis] [36]:[17] These were the sons of Esau's son Reuel: Chief Nahath, Chief Zerah, Chief Shammah, Chief Mizzah. These were the chiefs descended from Reuel in the land of Edom; they were the descendants of Esau's wife Basemath.
[Genesis] [36]:[18] These were the sons of Esau's wife Oholibamah: Chief Jeush, Chief Jalam, Chief Korah. These were the chiefs descended from Esau's wife Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.
[Genesis] [36]:[19] These were the sons of Esau, and these were their chiefs — that is, Edom.
[Genesis] [36]:[20] These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who lived in the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
[Genesis] [36]:[21] Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These were the Horite chiefs, the sons of Seir, in the land of Edom.
[Genesis] [36]:[22] The sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam, and Lotan's sister was Timna.
[Genesis] [36]:[23] These were the sons of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
[Genesis] [36]:[24] These were the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This is the Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness while pasturing the donkeys of his father Zibeon.[^1] [^1]: The meaning of the Hebrew word rendered "hot springs" is uncertain; it has also been understood as "water" or "wild donkeys."
[Genesis] [36]:[25] These were the children of Anah: Dishon, and Oholibamah, Anah's daughter.
[Genesis] [36]:[26] These were the sons of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
[Genesis] [36]:[27] These were the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
[Genesis] [36]:[28] These were the sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
[Genesis] [36]:[29] These were the Horite chiefs: Chief Lotan, Chief Shobal, Chief Zibeon, Chief Anah,
[Genesis] [36]:[30] Chief Dishon, Chief Ezer, Chief Dishan. These were the Horite chiefs, clan by clan, in the land of Seir.
[Genesis] [36]:[31] These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites.
[Genesis] [36]:[32] Bela son of Beor became king in Edom; his city was named Dinhabah.
[Genesis] [36]:[33] When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah, from Bozrah, succeeded him as king.
[Genesis] [36]:[34] When Jobab died, Husham, from the land of the Temanites, succeeded him as king.
[Genesis] [36]:[35] When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad succeeded him as king. He defeated Midian in the country of Moab, and his city was named Avith.
[Genesis] [36]:[36] When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah succeeded him as king.
[Genesis] [36]:[37] When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the River succeeded him as king.
[Genesis] [36]:[38] When Shaul died, Baal-Hanan son of Achbor succeeded him as king.
[Genesis] [36]:[39] When Baal-Hanan son of Achbor died, Hadar succeeded him as king. His city was named Pau, and his wife's name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-Zahab.
[Genesis] [36]:[40] These are the names of the chiefs descended from Esau, by their clans and their regions, name by name: Chief Timna, Chief Alvah, Chief Jetheth,
[Genesis] [36]:[41] Chief Oholibamah, Chief Elah, Chief Pinon,
[Genesis] [36]:[42] Chief Kenaz, Chief Teman, Chief Mibzar,
[Genesis] [36]:[43] Chief Magdiel, Chief Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom, according to their settlements in the land they possessed. This was Esau, the father of the Edomites.
[Genesis] [37]:[1] Jacob settled in the land where his father had lived as a stranger, the land of Canaan.
[Genesis] [37]:[2] This is the account of Jacob's family. Joseph, seventeen years old, was tending the flocks with his brothers. He was a young man, working alongside the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives, and he brought their father a bad report about them.
[Genesis] [37]:[3] Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his other sons, because he was the son of his old age, and he made him a richly ornamented robe.
[Genesis] [37]:[4] When his brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a kind word to him.
[Genesis] [37]:[5] Then Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, they hated him all the more.
[Genesis] [37]:[6] He said to them, "Listen to this dream I had.
[Genesis] [37]:[7] We were binding sheaves out in the field, and suddenly my sheaf rose up and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around it and bowed down to it."
[Genesis] [37]:[8] His brothers said to him, "So you're going to reign over us? You're going to rule us?" And they hated him all the more for his dreams and for what he said.
[Genesis] [37]:[9] He had another dream, and he told it to his brothers. "Listen," he said, "I had another dream. This time the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me."
[Genesis] [37]:[10] When he told it to his father and his brothers, his father rebuked him: "What is this dream of yours? Are your mother and I and your brothers really going to come and bow down to the ground before you?"
[Genesis] [37]:[11] His brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter in mind.
[Genesis] [37]:[12] Now his brothers had gone to graze their father's flocks near Shechem,
[Genesis] [37]:[13] and Israel said to Joseph, "Your brothers are pasturing the flocks at Shechem, aren't they? Come, I am sending you to them." "I am ready," he answered.
[Genesis] [37]:[14] So he said to him, "Go and see how your brothers are and how the flocks are doing, and bring word back to me." So he sent him off from the Valley of Hebron, and Joseph came to Shechem.
[Genesis] [37]:[15] A man found him wandering in the open country and asked him, "What are you looking for?"
[Genesis] [37]:[16] "I'm looking for my brothers," he said. "Tell me, please, where are they pasturing their flocks?"
[Genesis] [37]:[17] "They have moved on from here," the man answered. "I heard them say, 'Let's go to Dothan.'" So Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Dothan.
[Genesis] [37]:[18] They saw him in the distance, and before he reached them they plotted to kill him.
[Genesis] [37]:[19] "Here comes that dreamer!" they said to one another.
[Genesis] [37]:[20] "Come now, let's kill him and throw him into one of these cisterns. We'll say a wild animal devoured him. Then we'll see what becomes of his dreams."
[Genesis] [37]:[21] When Reuben heard this, he tried to rescue him from their hands. "Let's not take his life," he said.
[Genesis] [37]:[22] Reuben said to them, "Don't shed any blood. Throw him into this cistern here in the wilderness, but don't lay a hand on him." He said this to rescue him from them and take him back to his father.
[Genesis] [37]:[23] So when Joseph reached his brothers, they stripped him of his robe—the richly ornamented robe he was wearing—
[Genesis] [37]:[24] and they took him and threw him into the cistern. The cistern was empty; there was no water in it.
[Genesis] [37]:[25] Then they sat down to eat. Looking up, they saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, their camels loaded with gum, balm, and myrrh, on their way down to Egypt.
[Genesis] [37]:[26] Judah said to his brothers, "What do we gain by killing our brother and covering up his blood?
[Genesis] [37]:[27] Come, let's sell him to the Ishmaelites and not lay our hands on him. After all, he is our brother, our own flesh." His brothers agreed.
[Genesis] [37]:[28] So when the Midianite traders came by, they pulled Joseph up out of the cistern and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver, and they took Joseph to Egypt.
[Genesis] [37]:[29] When Reuben returned to the cistern and saw that Joseph was not there, he tore his clothes.
[Genesis] [37]:[30] He went back to his brothers and said, "The boy is gone! And I—where can I turn now?"
[Genesis] [37]:[31] Then they took Joseph's robe, slaughtered a young goat, and dipped the robe in the blood.
[Genesis] [37]:[32] They sent the ornamented robe to their father with this message: "We found this. Look it over and see whether it is your son's robe or not."
[Genesis] [37]:[33] He recognized it and said, "It is my son's robe! A wild animal has devoured him. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces."
[Genesis] [37]:[34] Then Jacob tore his garments, put on sackcloth, and mourned for his son many days.
[Genesis] [37]:[35] All his sons and daughters came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. "No," he said, "I will go down to the grave mourning for my son." So his father wept for him. [Footnote: Hebrew *Sheol*, the realm of the dead.]
[Genesis] [37]:[36] Meanwhile the Midianites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.
[Genesis] [38]:[1] About that time Judah left his brothers and went down to stay with a man from Adullam named Hirah.
[Genesis] [38]:[2] There Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite named Shua. He took her and slept with her,
[Genesis] [38]:[3] and she conceived and bore a son, and he named him Er.
[Genesis] [38]:[4] She conceived again and bore a son, and she named him Onan.
[Genesis] [38]:[5] Then she bore still another son and named him Shelah. Judah was at Chezib when she gave birth to him.
[Genesis] [38]:[6] Judah took a wife for Er, his firstborn; her name was Tamar.
[Genesis] [38]:[7] But Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the LORD's sight, and the LORD put him to death.
[Genesis] [38]:[8] Then Judah said to Onan, "Go to your brother's wife and do your duty as a brother-in-law, so that you may raise up offspring for your brother."
[Genesis] [38]:[9] But Onan knew that the offspring would not be his own, so whenever he slept with his brother's wife, he spilled his seed on the ground rather than give offspring to his brother.
[Genesis] [38]:[10] What he did was evil in the LORD's sight, so the LORD put him to death as well.
[Genesis] [38]:[11] Then Judah said to his daughter-in-law Tamar, "Live as a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah is grown up." For he thought, "He may die too, like his brothers." So Tamar went and settled in her father's house.
[Genesis] [38]:[12] After a long time Judah's wife, the daughter of Shua, died. When Judah had finished mourning, he went up to Timnah to the men shearing his sheep, together with his friend Hirah the Adullamite.
[Genesis] [38]:[13] Tamar was told, "Your father-in-law is on his way up to Timnah to shear his sheep."
[Genesis] [38]:[14] So she took off her widow's clothes, covered herself with a veil and wrapped herself up, and sat down at the entrance to Enaim, on the road to Timnah. For she saw that although Shelah was grown up, she had not been given to him as his wife.
[Genesis] [38]:[15] When Judah saw her, he took her for a prostitute, since she had covered her face.
[Genesis] [38]:[16] He turned aside to her by the road and said, "Come, let me sleep with you"—for he did not know she was his daughter-in-law. She said, "What will you give me for sleeping with you?"
[Genesis] [38]:[17] "I will send you a young goat from my flock," he said. "Will you give me a pledge until you send it?" she asked.
[Genesis] [38]:[18] "What pledge should I give you?" he said. She answered, "Your seal and its cord, and the staff in your hand." So he gave them to her and slept with her, and she conceived by him.
[Genesis] [38]:[19] Then she got up and left, took off her veil, and put on her widow's clothes again.
[Genesis] [38]:[20] Judah sent the young goat by his friend the Adullamite to retrieve the pledge from the woman, but he could not find her.
[Genesis] [38]:[21] He asked the men of the place, "Where is the shrine prostitute who was at Enaim by the road?" "There has been no shrine prostitute here," they said.
[Genesis] [38]:[22] So he went back to Judah and said, "I could not find her. And the men of the place said, 'There has been no prostitute here.'"
