[Genesis] [38]:[23] Judah said, "Let her keep what she has, or we will become a laughingstock. After all, I did send her this young goat, but you could not find her."
[Genesis] [38]:[24] About three months later Judah was told, "Your daughter-in-law Tamar has played the whore, and now she is pregnant by her immorality." Judah said, "Bring her out and let her be burned!"
[Genesis] [38]:[25] As she was being brought out, she sent this message to her father-in-law: "I am pregnant by the man who owns these." And she added, "See if you recognize whose seal and cord and staff these are."
[Genesis] [38]:[26] Judah recognized them and said, "She is more righteous than I, since I did not give her to my son Shelah." And he did not sleep with her again.
[Genesis] [38]:[27] When the time came for her to give birth, there were twins in her womb.
[Genesis] [38]:[28] As she was giving birth, one of them put out his hand, and the midwife took a scarlet thread and tied it around his wrist, saying, "This one came out first."
[Genesis] [38]:[29] But when he drew back his hand, his brother came out, and she said, "So this is how you have broken out!" And he was named Perez.
[Genesis] [38]:[30] Then his brother came out, the one with the scarlet thread on his wrist, and he was named Zerah.
[Genesis] [39]:[1] Joseph had been taken down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an Egyptian officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had brought him there.
[Genesis] [39]:[2] The LORD was with Joseph, and he prospered. He lived in the house of his Egyptian master,
[Genesis] [39]:[3] and his master saw that the LORD was with him and that the LORD gave success to everything he did.
[Genesis] [39]:[4] So Joseph found favor in his eyes and became his personal attendant. He put him in charge of his household and entrusted everything he owned to his care.
[Genesis] [39]:[5] From the time he put Joseph in charge of his house and all he owned, the LORD blessed the Egyptian's household because of Joseph. The blessing of the LORD rested on everything he had, both in the house and in the field.
[Genesis] [39]:[6] So he left everything he owned in Joseph's care and gave no thought to anything except the food he ate. Now Joseph was handsome and well built.
[Genesis] [39]:[7] After some time, his master's wife took notice of Joseph and said, "Come to bed with me."
[Genesis] [39]:[8] But he refused. "Look," he said to her, "my master gives no thought to anything in this house; he has put everything he owns into my hands.
[Genesis] [39]:[9] No one in this house stands above me, and he has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. How then could I do such a great evil and sin against God?"
[Genesis] [39]:[10] Day after day she kept at him, but he would not listen to her or lie with her or be with her.
[Genesis] [39]:[11] One such day he came into the house to do his work, and none of the household servants was there.
[Genesis] [39]:[12] She caught hold of his cloak and said, "Come to bed with me!" But he left his cloak in her hand and ran out of the house.
[Genesis] [39]:[13] When she saw that he had left his cloak in her hand and had fled outside,
[Genesis] [39]:[14] she called the men of her household and said to them, "Look, he has brought us a Hebrew to make sport of us! He came to me to lie with me, but I screamed at the top of my voice." [Footnote: "He" here refers to her husband, the master of the house — an accusation she repeats in verse 17.]
[Genesis] [39]:[15] When he heard me raise my voice and scream, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house."
[Genesis] [39]:[16] She kept his cloak beside her until his master came home,
[Genesis] [39]:[17] and then she told him the same story: "That Hebrew slave you brought us came to me to make sport of me.
[Genesis] [39]:[18] But when I raised my voice and screamed, he left his cloak beside me and fled outside."
[Genesis] [39]:[19] When his master heard what his wife told him—"This is how your slave treated me"—he burned with anger.
[Genesis] [39]:[20] Joseph's master took him and put him in the prison where the king's prisoners were held, and there he remained.
[Genesis] [39]:[21] But the LORD was with Joseph and showed him steadfast love, and he granted him favor in the eyes of the prison warden.
[Genesis] [39]:[22] The warden put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners in the prison, and everything that was done there was done by him.
[Genesis] [39]:[23] The warden paid no attention to anything under Joseph's care, because the LORD was with him and gave him success in whatever he did.
[Genesis] [40]:[1] Some time later, the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt offended their master, the king of Egypt.
[Genesis] [40]:[2] Pharaoh was furious with his two officials, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker,
[Genesis] [40]:[3] and he put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, in the prison where Joseph was confined.
[Genesis] [40]:[4] The captain of the guard assigned Joseph to them, and Joseph attended them. They remained in custody for some time.
[Genesis] [40]:[5] One night both of them—the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were being held in the prison—had a dream, each his own dream, and each dream had its own meaning.
[Genesis] [40]:[6] When Joseph came to them in the morning, he saw that they were troubled.
[Genesis] [40]:[7] So he asked Pharaoh's officials, who were with him in custody in his master's house, "Why do you look so downcast today?"
[Genesis] [40]:[8] They said to him, "We each had a dream, and there is no one to interpret it." Joseph said to them, "Do not interpretations belong to God? Tell me your dreams."
[Genesis] [40]:[9] So the chief cupbearer told Joseph his dream: "In my dream there was a vine before me,
[Genesis] [40]:[10] and on the vine were three branches. It had barely budded when its blossoms opened and its clusters ripened into grapes.
[Genesis] [40]:[11] Pharaoh's cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup and placed the cup in Pharaoh's hand."
[Genesis] [40]:[12] Joseph said to him, "This is what it means: the three branches are three days.
[Genesis] [40]:[13] Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and restore you to your position, and you will place the cup in Pharaoh's hand, just as you did before, when you were his cupbearer.
[Genesis] [40]:[14] But remember me when things go well for you, and show me kindness: mention me to Pharaoh and get me out of this house.
[Genesis] [40]:[15] For I was carried off by force from the land of the Hebrews, and here too I have done nothing to deserve being put in this pit."
[Genesis] [40]:[16] When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was favorable, he said to Joseph, "I too had a dream: there were three baskets of bread on my head.
[Genesis] [40]:[17] In the top basket were all sorts of baked goods for Pharaoh, and the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head."
[Genesis] [40]:[18] Joseph answered, "This is what it means: the three baskets are three days.
[Genesis] [40]:[19] Within three days Pharaoh will lift up your head—from off your body—and hang you on a tree, and the birds will eat the flesh from your body.
[Genesis] [40]:[20] Three days later it was Pharaoh's birthday, and he gave a banquet for all his servants. In the presence of his servants he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker:
[Genesis] [40]:[21] he restored the chief cupbearer to his office, so that he once again placed the cup in Pharaoh's hand,
[Genesis] [40]:[22] but he hanged the chief baker—just as Joseph had told them.
[Genesis] [40]:[23] The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot him.
[Genesis] [41]:[1] Two whole years later, Pharaoh had a dream: he was standing beside the Nile,
[Genesis] [41]:[2] and out of the Nile came seven cows, sleek and fat, and they grazed among the reeds.
[Genesis] [41]:[3] After them seven other cows came up out of the Nile, ugly and gaunt, and they stood beside the first cows on the bank of the river.
[Genesis] [41]:[4] Then the ugly, gaunt cows ate up the seven sleek, fat cows. And Pharaoh woke up.
[Genesis] [41]:[5] He fell asleep again and dreamed a second time: seven heads of grain, plump and good, were growing on a single stalk.
[Genesis] [41]:[6] After them seven heads of grain sprouted, thin and scorched by the east wind.
[Genesis] [41]:[7] And the thin heads swallowed up the seven plump, full heads. Then Pharaoh woke up, and it had been a dream.
[Genesis] [41]:[8] In the morning his spirit was troubled, so he sent for all the magicians of Egypt and all its wise men. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but no one could interpret them for him.
[Genesis] [41]:[9] Then the chief cupbearer said to Pharaoh, "Today I must confess my failings.
[Genesis] [41]:[10] Pharaoh was once angry with his servants and put me and the chief baker in custody in the house of the captain of the guard.
[Genesis] [41]:[11] We each had a dream the same night, he and I, and each dream had a meaning of its own.
[Genesis] [41]:[12] A young Hebrew was there with us, a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams, and he interpreted them for us, giving each man the meaning of his dream.
[Genesis] [41]:[13] And it turned out exactly as he told us: I was restored to my position, and the other man was hanged."
[Genesis] [41]:[14] So Pharaoh sent for Joseph, and they hurried him out of the dungeon. He shaved, changed his clothes, and came before Pharaoh.
[Genesis] [41]:[15] Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I have had a dream, and no one can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it."
[Genesis] [41]:[16] Joseph answered Pharaoh, "It is not in me. God will give Pharaoh the answer he needs."
[Genesis] [41]:[17] So Pharaoh said to Joseph, "In my dream I was standing on the bank of the Nile,
[Genesis] [41]:[18] and out of the Nile came seven cows, fat and sleek, and they grazed among the reeds.
[Genesis] [41]:[19] After them seven other cows came up, scrawny and very ugly and gaunt. I have never seen such wretched cows in all the land of Egypt.
[Genesis] [41]:[20] And the gaunt, ugly cows ate up the seven fat cows that came first.
[Genesis] [41]:[21] But when they had eaten them, no one could tell that they had, for they looked just as wretched as before. Then I woke up.
[Genesis] [41]:[22] I also saw in my dream seven heads of grain, full and good, growing on a single stalk.
[Genesis] [41]:[23] After them seven heads of grain sprouted, shriveled and thin and scorched by the east wind.
[Genesis] [41]:[24] And the thin heads swallowed up the seven good heads. I told this to the magicians, but none of them could explain it to me."
[Genesis] [41]:[25] Then Joseph said to Pharaoh, "Pharaoh's dreams are one and the same. God has revealed to Pharaoh what he is about to do.
[Genesis] [41]:[26] The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good heads of grain are seven years; it is one dream.
[Genesis] [41]:[27] The seven gaunt, ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and so are the seven empty heads scorched by the east wind: they are seven years of famine.
[Genesis] [41]:[28] It is as I have said to Pharaoh: God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.
[Genesis] [41]:[29] Seven years of great abundance are coming throughout the land of Egypt,
[Genesis] [41]:[30] but after them will come seven years of famine. Then all the abundance in Egypt will be forgotten, and the famine will devastate the land.
[Genesis] [41]:[31] The abundance will leave no trace in the land, because the famine that follows will be so severe.
[Genesis] [41]:[32] The dream came to Pharaoh twice because the matter has been firmly decided by God, and God will bring it about soon.
[Genesis] [41]:[33] So now let Pharaoh look for a discerning and wise man and set him over the land of Egypt.
[Genesis] [41]:[34] Let Pharaoh appoint officers over the land to take a fifth of the harvest of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.
[Genesis] [41]:[35] Let them gather all the food of these good years that are coming and store up the grain under Pharaoh's authority, to be kept as food in the cities.
[Genesis] [41]:[36] This food will be a reserve for the land during the seven years of famine that will come upon Egypt, so that the land will not perish in the famine."
[Genesis] [41]:[37] The plan seemed good to Pharaoh and to all his servants.
[Genesis] [41]:[38] So Pharaoh said to his servants, "Can we find anyone like this man, in whom is the spirit of God?"
[Genesis] [41]:[39] Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one so discerning and wise as you.
[Genesis] [41]:[40] You shall be over my house, and all my people shall submit to your command. Only in the throne will I be greater than you."
[Genesis] [41]:[41] And Pharaoh said to Joseph, "See, I hereby set you over all the land of Egypt."
[Genesis] [41]:[42] Then Pharaoh took his signet ring from his hand and put it on Joseph's hand. He clothed him in fine linen and put a gold chain around his neck.
[Genesis] [41]:[43] He had him ride in the chariot next to his own, while men called out before him, "Make way!" So he set him over all the land of Egypt.
[Genesis] [41]:[44] Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I am Pharaoh, but without your word no one in all the land of Egypt shall lift a hand or a foot."
[Genesis] [41]:[45] Pharaoh named Joseph Zaphenath-paneah and gave him Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, as his wife. And Joseph went out through the land of Egypt.
[Genesis] [41]:[46] Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. He left Pharaoh's presence and traveled throughout the land of Egypt.
[Genesis] [41]:[47] During the seven years of abundance the land produced in overflowing measure.
[Genesis] [41]:[48] Joseph collected all the food of those seven years in Egypt and stored it in the cities; in each city he laid up the food from the surrounding fields.
[Genesis] [41]:[49] He piled up grain like the sand of the sea, so much that he stopped counting, for it was beyond measure.
[Genesis] [41]:[50] Before the years of famine came, two sons were born to Joseph by Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.
[Genesis] [41]:[51] Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh, saying, "God has made me forget all my hardship and all my father's house."
[Genesis] [41]:[52] The second he named Ephraim, saying, "God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction."
[Genesis] [41]:[53] The seven years of abundance in the land of Egypt came to an end,
[Genesis] [41]:[54] and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in every land, but in all of Egypt there was food.
[Genesis] [41]:[55] When all Egypt began to hunger, the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread. And Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, "Go to Joseph; do whatever he tells you."
[Genesis] [41]:[56] The famine spread over the whole land, so Joseph opened all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians, for the famine grew severe in Egypt.
[Genesis] [41]:[57] And people from every land came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph, because the famine was severe in all the earth.
[Genesis] [42]:[1] When Jacob learned that there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, "Why do you keep staring at one another?"
[Genesis] [42]:[2] He said, "Listen, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy some for us, so that we may live and not die."
[Genesis] [42]:[3] So ten of Joseph's brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
[Genesis] [42]:[4] But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph's brother, with the others, for he thought, "Harm might come to him."
[Genesis] [42]:[5] So the sons of Israel came to buy grain along with the others who came, for the famine had reached the land of Canaan.
[Genesis] [42]:[6] Now Joseph was the governor of the land; he was the one who sold grain to all its people. So Joseph's brothers came and bowed down before him with their faces to the ground.
[Genesis] [42]:[7] When Joseph saw his brothers, he recognized them, but he acted as a stranger to them and spoke harshly. "Where do you come from?" he asked. "From the land of Canaan," they said, "to buy food."
[Genesis] [42]:[8] Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him.
[Genesis] [42]:[9] Then Joseph remembered the dreams he had dreamed about them, and he said to them, "You are spies! You have come to see where the land lies exposed."
[Genesis] [42]:[10] "No, my lord," they said. "Your servants have come to buy food.
[Genesis] [42]:[11] We are all sons of one man. We are honest men; your servants have never been spies."
[Genesis] [42]:[12] But he said to them, "No, you have come to see where the land lies exposed."
[Genesis] [42]:[13] They answered, "Your servants are twelve brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest is with our father today, and one is no more."
[Genesis] [42]:[14] But Joseph said to them, "It is just as I told you: you are spies.
[Genesis] [42]:[15] This is how you will be tested: as surely as Pharaoh lives, you will not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here.
[Genesis] [42]:[16] Send one of your number to bring your brother; the rest of you will be held in prison, so that your words may be tested to see whether you are telling the truth. And if not, then as surely as Pharaoh lives, you are spies."
[Genesis] [42]:[17] And he put them all in custody for three days.
[Genesis] [42]:[18] On the third day Joseph said to them, "Do this and you will live, for I fear God.

[Genesis] [42]:[20] But bring your youngest brother to me, so that your words may be proved true and you will not die." And they agreed to do so.
[Genesis] [42]:[21] They said to one another, "Surely we are guilty concerning our brother. We saw the anguish of his soul when he pleaded with us, and we would not listen. That is why this distress has come upon us."
[Genesis] [42]:[22] Reuben answered them, "Didn't I tell you not to sin against the boy? But you would not listen. Now comes the reckoning for his blood."
[Genesis] [42]:[23] They did not realize that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking with them through an interpreter.
[Genesis] [42]:[24] He turned away from them and wept. Then he came back and spoke to them again; and he took Simeon from among them and had him bound before their eyes.
[Genesis] [42]:[25] Joseph gave orders to fill their containers with grain, to put each man's silver back in his sack, and to give them provisions for the journey. This was done for them.
[Genesis] [42]:[26] They loaded their grain on their donkeys and set out.
[Genesis] [42]:[27] At the place where they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to give his donkey fodder, and he saw his silver lying there in the mouth of his sack.
[Genesis] [42]:[28] "My silver has been put back," he said to his brothers. "Here it is in my sack!" Their hearts sank, and trembling they turned to one another and said, "What is this that God has done to us?"
[Genesis] [42]:[29] When they came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan, they told him everything that had happened to them:
[Genesis] [42]:[30] "The man who is lord of the land spoke harshly to us and treated us as if we were spying out the country.
[Genesis] [42]:[31] But we said to him, 'We are honest men; we have never been spies.
[Genesis] [42]:[32] We are twelve brothers, sons of one father. One is no more, and the youngest is with our father now in the land of Canaan.'
[Genesis] [42]:[33] Then the man who is lord of the land said to us, 'This is how I will know whether you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, take grain for your starving households, and go.
[Genesis] [42]:[34] But bring your youngest brother to me, so I may know that you are not spies but honest men. Then I will give your brother back to you, and you may trade in the land.'"
[Genesis] [42]:[35] As they emptied their sacks, there in each man's sack was his pouch of silver! When they and their father saw the pouches of silver, they were afraid.
[Genesis] [42]:[36] Their father Jacob said to them, "You are robbing me of my children. Joseph is no more, and Simeon is no more, and now you would take Benjamin. Everything is against me!"
[Genesis] [42]:[37] Then Reuben said to his father, "You may put my two sons to death if I do not bring him back to you. Entrust him to my care, and I will return him to you."
[Genesis] [42]:[38] But Jacob said, "My son will not go down with you. His brother is dead, and he alone is left. If harm comes to him on the journey you are making, you will bring my gray head down to the grave in sorrow." [Footnote: Hebrew Sheol, the place of the dead.]
[Genesis] [43]:[1] The famine lay heavy on the land.

[Genesis] [43]:[4] If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy you food.
[Genesis] [43]:[5] But if you will not send him, we will not go, because the man told us, 'You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.'"

[Genesis] [43]:[7] They answered, "The man questioned us closely about ourselves and our family: 'Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?' We simply answered his questions. How could we possibly know he would say, 'Bring your brother down here'?"

[Genesis] [43]:[18] The men were afraid when they were taken into Joseph's house, and they said, "It is because of the silver that was put back in our sacks the first time. He has brought us here to fall on us and overpower us, to take us as slaves along with our donkeys."
[Genesis] [43]:[19] So they went up to the steward of Joseph's house and spoke to him at the entrance of the house.

[Genesis] [43]:[22] We have also brought more silver with us to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our sacks."
[Genesis] [43]:[23] He replied, "Peace to you. Do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father has given you treasure in your sacks; your silver reached me." Then he brought Simeon out to them.

[Genesis] [43]:[25] They got their gift ready for Joseph's arrival at noon, since they had heard that they were to eat there.

[Genesis] [45]:[9] Hurry, go up to my father and say to him, 'This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord over all Egypt. Come down to me; do not delay.
[Genesis] [45]:[10] You shall live in the land of Goshen, and you will be near me—you, your children and your grandchildren, your flocks and herds, and all that you have.
[Genesis] [45]:[11] There I will provide for you, for there are five more years of famine, so that you and your household and all that you have will not come to poverty.'
[Genesis] [45]:[12] And look, your own eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my own mouth speaking to you.
[Genesis] [45]:[13] Tell my father of all my honor in Egypt and of everything you have seen. Hurry and bring my father down here.
[Genesis] [45]:[14] Then he threw his arms around his brother Benjamin's neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.
[Genesis] [45]:[15] He kissed all his brothers and wept over them, and afterward his brothers talked with him.
[Genesis] [45]:[16] News reached Pharaoh's house: "Joseph's brothers have come." It pleased Pharaoh and his servants.
[Genesis] [45]:[17] Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Tell your brothers: Do this—load your animals and go back to the land of Canaan.
[Genesis] [45]:[18] Get your father and your households and come to me. I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you shall eat the fat of the land.
[Genesis] [45]:[19] And you are commanded: Do this—take wagons from the land of Egypt for your children and your wives, and bring your father and come.
[Genesis] [45]:[20] Do not worry about your possessions, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours."
[Genesis] [45]:[21] So the sons of Israel did this. Joseph gave them wagons, as Pharaoh had commanded, and he gave them provisions for the journey.
[Genesis] [45]:[22] To each of them he gave a change of clothes, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothes.
[Genesis] [45]:[23] And to his father he sent the following: ten donkeys loaded with the best of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread, and provisions for his father's journey.
[Genesis] [45]:[24] Then he sent his brothers on their way, saying to them, "Do not quarrel on the road."
[Genesis] [45]:[25] So they went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to their father Jacob.
[Genesis] [45]:[26] They told him, "Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt!" But his heart went numb, for he did not believe them.
[Genesis] [45]:[27] Then they told him everything Joseph had said to them, and when he saw the wagons Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of their father Jacob revived.
[Genesis] [45]:[28] And Israel said, "Enough! My son Joseph is still alive. I will go and see him before I die."
[Genesis] [46]:[1] So Israel set out with all that he had, and when he came to Beersheba, he offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.
[Genesis] [46]:[2] And God spoke to Israel in visions of the night: "Jacob, Jacob!" And he answered, "Here I am."
[Genesis] [46]:[3] He said, "I am God, the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for there I will make you into a great nation.
[Genesis] [46]:[4] I myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I myself will surely bring you up again; and Joseph's hand will close your eyes."
[Genesis] [46]:[5] Then Jacob rose up from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried their father Jacob, their little ones, and their wives in the wagons Pharaoh had sent to carry him.

[Genesis] [46]:[27] With the two sons born to Joseph in Egypt, the persons of Jacob's household who came to Egypt numbered seventy.
[Genesis] [46]:[28] Jacob sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph, to get directions to Goshen. And so they came to the land of Goshen.
[Genesis] [46]:[29] Joseph had his chariot made ready and went up to Goshen to meet his father Israel. As soon as he appeared before him, he threw his arms around his neck and wept on his neck a long while.
[Genesis] [46]:[30] Israel said to Joseph, "Now I can die, since I have seen your face and know that you are still alive."

[Genesis] [46]:[32] The men are shepherds, for they have been keepers of livestock, and they have brought their flocks and herds and everything they own.'
[Genesis] [46]:[33] So when Pharaoh calls you in and asks, 'What is your occupation?'
[Genesis] [46]:[34] you are to answer, 'Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth until now, we and our fathers before us.' Then you will be allowed to settle in the land of Goshen, for every shepherd is detestable to the Egyptians."
[Genesis] [47]:[1] Joseph came and told Pharaoh, "My father and my brothers have come from the land of Canaan with their flocks and herds and everything they own, and they are now in the land of Goshen."
[Genesis] [47]:[2] He had taken five of his brothers with him, and he presented them to Pharaoh.
[Genesis] [47]:[3] Pharaoh asked his brothers, "What is your occupation?" They answered Pharaoh, "Your servants are shepherds, as our fathers were before us."
[Genesis] [47]:[4] They said to Pharaoh, "We have come to live in this land for a while, because there is no pasture for your servants' flocks; the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Please, let your servants settle in the land of Goshen."
[Genesis] [47]:[5] Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Your father and your brothers have come to you.
[Genesis] [47]:[6] The land of Egypt lies open before you. Settle your father and your brothers in the best part of the land; let them live in the land of Goshen. And if you know of capable men among them, put them in charge of my own livestock."
[Genesis] [47]:[7] Then Joseph brought in his father Jacob and presented him to Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.
[Genesis] [47]:[8] Pharaoh asked Jacob, "How many are the years of your life?"
[Genesis] [47]:[9] Jacob answered Pharaoh, "The years of my sojourning are a hundred and thirty. Few and hard have been the years of my life, and they do not measure up to the years of my fathers during their sojourning."
[Genesis] [47]:[10] Then Jacob blessed Pharaoh and went out from his presence.
[Genesis] [47]:[11] So Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them property in the best part of the land of Egypt, in the district of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.
[Genesis] [47]:[12] And Joseph provided his father, his brothers, and all his father's household with food, according to the number of their children.
[Genesis] [47]:[13] There was no food anywhere in the land, for the famine was severe. Egypt and Canaan alike wasted away because of it.
[Genesis] [47]:[14] Joseph collected all the money to be found in Egypt and Canaan in payment for the grain the people were buying, and he brought it into Pharaoh's palace.
[Genesis] [47]:[15] When the money of Egypt and Canaan was gone, all the Egyptians came to Joseph and said, "Give us food! Why should we die before your eyes? Our money is spent."
[Genesis] [47]:[16] Joseph said, "Bring your livestock, and I will give you food in exchange for it, since your money is gone."
[Genesis] [47]:[17] So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and he gave them food in exchange for their horses, their flocks and herds, and their donkeys. That year he carried them through with food in exchange for all their livestock.
[Genesis] [47]:[18] When that year had ended, they came to him the next year and said, "We cannot hide it from my lord: our money is gone, and our herds belong to my lord. Nothing is left for my lord but our bodies and our land.
[Genesis] [47]:[19] Why should we perish before your eyes, we and our land as well? Buy us and our land in exchange for food, and we with our land will be servants to Pharaoh. Give us seed, so that we may live and not die, and the land may not become desolate."
[Genesis] [47]:[20] So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh. Every Egyptian sold his field, because the famine pressed hard upon them, and the land became Pharaoh's.
[Genesis] [47]:[21] As for the people, he moved them into the cities, from one end of Egypt to the other.
[Genesis] [47]:[22] Only the land of the priests he did not buy, for the priests had a fixed allowance from Pharaoh and lived on the allowance Pharaoh gave them; that is why they did not sell their land.
[Genesis] [47]:[23] Then Joseph said to the people, "Now that I have bought you and your land today for Pharaoh, here is seed for you. Sow the land.
[Genesis] [47]:[24] At harvest time you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh. The other four fifths will be yours as seed for the fields and as food for yourselves, your households, and your children."
[Genesis] [47]:[25] They said, "You have saved our lives. May we find favor in the eyes of my lord; we will be servants to Pharaoh."
[Genesis] [47]:[26] So Joseph made it a statute concerning the land of Egypt, still in force today, that a fifth belongs to Pharaoh. Only the land of the priests did not become Pharaoh's.
[Genesis] [47]:[27] Israel settled in Egypt, in the land of Goshen. They acquired property there, and they were fruitful and increased greatly in number.
[Genesis] [47]:[28] Jacob lived seventeen years in the land of Egypt, so that the years of his life came to a hundred and forty-seven.
[Genesis] [47]:[29] When the time drew near for Israel to die, he called for his son Joseph and said to him, "If I have found favor in your eyes, put your hand under my thigh and deal with me in kindness and faithfulness: do not bury me in Egypt.
[Genesis] [47]:[30] When I rest with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me where they are buried." Joseph said, "I will do as you say."
[Genesis] [47]:[31] "Swear it to me," he said. So Joseph swore to him, and Israel bowed down at the head of his bed.
[Genesis] [48]:[1] Some time later Joseph was told, "Your father is ill." So he took his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, with him.

[Genesis] [48]:[5] Now then, your two sons who were born to you in Egypt before I came to you here—they are mine. Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, just as Reuben and Simeon are.
[Genesis] [48]:[6] But any children born to you after them will be yours; in their inheritance they will be counted under the names of their brothers.
[Genesis] [48]:[7] As for me, when I came from Paddan, Rachel died beside me in the land of Canaan, on the way, while there was still some distance to go to Ephrath. I buried her there beside the road to Ephrath, that is, Bethlehem."

[Genesis] [48]:[10] Now Israel's eyes were dim with age, and he could hardly see. So Joseph brought them close to him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
[Genesis] [48]:[11] Israel said to Joseph, "I never expected to see your face again, and now God has let me see your offspring as well!"
[Genesis] [48]:[12] Then Joseph took them from his father's knees and bowed with his face to the ground.
[Genesis] [48]:[13] Joseph took them both, Ephraim on his right toward Israel's left hand, and Manasseh on his left toward Israel's right hand, and brought them close to him.
[Genesis] [48]:[14] But Israel reached out his right hand and laid it on Ephraim's head, though he was the younger, and crossing his hands, he laid his left hand on Manasseh's head, even though Manasseh was the firstborn.
[Genesis] [48]:[15] Then he blessed Joseph and said: "The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has been my shepherd all my life to this day,
[Genesis] [48]:[16] the Angel who has redeemed me from all evil—may he bless these boys. May my name be carried on through them, and the names of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth."
[Genesis] [48]:[17] When Joseph saw that his father was placing his right hand on Ephraim's head, he was displeased; so he took hold of his father's hand to move it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's.
[Genesis] [48]:[18] Joseph said to his father, "Not that way, my father. This one is the firstborn; put your right hand on his head."
[Genesis] [48]:[19] But his father refused and said, "I know, my son, I know. He too will become a people, and he too will be great. Yet his younger brother will be greater than he, and his descendants will become a multitude of nations."
[Genesis] [48]:[20] So he blessed them that day, saying: "By you Israel will pronounce this blessing: 'May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh.'" And so he put Ephraim ahead of Manasseh.
[Genesis] [48]:[21] Then Israel said to Joseph, "I am about to die, but God will be with you and will bring you back to the land of your fathers.
[Genesis] [48]:[22] And I have given you one portion more than your brothers—the ridge of land that I took from the Amorites with my sword and my bow.

[Genesis] [50]:[1] Joseph fell upon his father's face, wept over him, and kissed him.
[Genesis] [50]:[2] Then Joseph ordered the physicians in his service to embalm his father, and the physicians embalmed Israel.
[Genesis] [50]:[3] It took forty days, for that is the full time required for embalming. And the Egyptians mourned him seventy days.
[Genesis] [50]:[4] When the days of mourning were over, Joseph said to Pharaoh's household, "If I have found favor in your eyes, speak to Pharaoh on my behalf and say:
[Genesis] [50]:[5] 'My father made me swear an oath, saying, "I am about to die. Bury me in the tomb I dug for myself in the land of Canaan." Now let me go up and bury my father, and then I will return.'"
[Genesis] [50]:[6] Pharaoh answered, "Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear."
[Genesis] [50]:[7] So Joseph went up to bury his father, and with him went all Pharaoh's servants, the elders of his household, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
[Genesis] [50]:[8] along with all of Joseph's household, his brothers, and his father's household. Only their children, their flocks, and their herds were left behind in the land of Goshen.
[Genesis] [50]:[9] Chariots and horsemen went up with him as well; it was a very great company.
[Genesis] [50]:[10] When they came to the threshing floor of Atad, beyond the Jordan, they raised a great and solemn lament there, and Joseph observed seven days of mourning for his father.
[Genesis] [50]:[11] When the Canaanites who lived in the land saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, they said, "This is a deep mourning for the Egyptians." That is why the place beyond the Jordan was named Abel Mizraim.[fn]
[Genesis] [50]:[12] So Jacob's sons did for him just as he had commanded them:
[Genesis] [50]:[13] they carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave in the field of Machpelah, the field near Mamre that Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site.
[Genesis] [50]:[14] After burying his father, Joseph returned to Egypt, together with his brothers and all who had gone up with him to bury his father.
[Genesis] [50]:[15] When Joseph's brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, "What if Joseph holds a grudge against us and pays us back in full for all the wrong we did to him?"
[Genesis] [50]:[16] So they sent word to Joseph: "Before he died, your father gave this command:
[Genesis] [50]:[17] 'Say to Joseph: Please forgive your brothers' offense and their sin, the wrong they did you.' Now then, please forgive the offense of the servants of the God of your father." And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
[Genesis] [50]:[18] Then his brothers came in person and fell down before him. "We are your slaves," they said.
[Genesis] [50]:[19] But Joseph said to them, "Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God?
[Genesis] [50]:[20] You intended evil against me, but God intended it for good, to accomplish what is now being done: the saving of many lives.
[Genesis] [50]:[21] So do not be afraid. I will provide for you and your children." And he comforted them and spoke kindly to them.
[Genesis] [50]:[22] Joseph stayed in Egypt, he and his father's household, and he lived a hundred and ten years.
[Genesis] [50]:[23] He saw Ephraim's children to the third generation, and the children of Machir son of Manasseh were also placed at birth on Joseph's knees.
[Genesis] [50]:[24] Then Joseph said to his brothers, "I am about to die. But God will surely come to your aid and bring you up out of this land to the land he promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob."
[Genesis] [50]:[25] And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear an oath, saying, "God will surely come to your aid, and then you must carry my bones up from this place."
[Genesis] [50]:[26] So Joseph died at the age of a hundred and ten. They embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.
[Exodus] [1]:[1] These are the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob, each with his household:
[Exodus] [1]:[2] Reuben, Simeon, Levi and Judah;
[Exodus] [1]:[3] Issachar, Zebulun and Benjamin;
[Exodus] [1]:[4] Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
[Exodus] [1]:[5] All those who came from Jacob's own body numbered seventy persons, and Joseph was already in Egypt.
[Exodus] [1]:[6] Then Joseph died, and all his brothers, and that whole generation.
[Exodus] [1]:[7] But the Israelites were fruitful and swarmed; they multiplied and grew exceedingly strong, and the land was filled with them.
[Exodus] [1]:[8] Then a new king arose over Egypt, one who did not know Joseph.
[Exodus] [1]:[9] He said to his people, "Look, the people of Israel have become more numerous and stronger than we are.
[Exodus] [1]:[10] Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, or they will keep multiplying, and if war breaks out they will join our enemies, fight against us, and go up out of the land.
[Exodus] [1]:[11] So they set slave masters over them to crush them with heavy burdens, and they built the supply cities of Pithom and Rameses for Pharaoh.
[Exodus] [1]:[12] But the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and spread, until the Egyptians came to dread the Israelites.
[Exodus] [1]:[13] So the Egyptians made the Israelites serve as slaves with ruthless force,
[Exodus] [1]:[14] and made their lives bitter with hard labor in mortar and brick and with all kinds of work in the fields. In every task they ruthlessly drove them.
[Exodus] [1]:[15] Then the king of Egypt said to the Hebrew midwives, one named Shiphrah and the other Puah,
[Exodus] [1]:[16] "When you help the Hebrew women give birth and see them on the birthstool, if it is a boy, kill him; if it is a girl, let her live."
[Exodus] [1]:[17] But the midwives feared God, and they did not do as the king of Egypt had ordered them; they let the boys live.
[Exodus] [1]:[18] So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and asked them, "Why have you done this? Why have you let the boys live?"
[Exodus] [1]:[19] The midwives answered Pharaoh, "Hebrew women are not like Egyptian women. They are vigorous, and they give birth before the midwife reaches them."
[Exodus] [1]:[20] So God dealt kindly with the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew very strong.
[Exodus] [1]:[21] And because the midwives feared God, he gave them families of their own.
[Exodus] [1]:[22] Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, "Every boy that is born you shall throw into the Nile, but every girl you shall let live."
[Exodus] [2]:[1] Now a man from the house of Levi went and married a daughter of Levi.
[Exodus] [2]:[2] The woman conceived and gave birth to a son. When she saw how beautiful he was, she hid him for three months.
[Exodus] [2]:[3] When she could hide him no longer, she got a basket of papyrus, coated it with tar and pitch, laid the child in it, and set it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile.
[Exodus] [2]:[4] His sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.
[Exodus] [2]:[5] Then Pharaoh's daughter came down to bathe in the Nile while her attendants walked along the riverbank. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her slave girl to fetch it.
[Exodus] [2]:[6] When she opened it, she saw the child—a baby boy, crying. She felt sorry for him and said, "This is one of the Hebrew children."
[Exodus] [2]:[7] Then his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter, "Shall I go and find you a Hebrew woman to nurse the child for you?"
[Exodus] [2]:[8] "Yes, go," said Pharaoh's daughter. So the girl went and called the child's mother.
[Exodus] [2]:[9] Pharaoh's daughter said to her, "Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages." So the woman took the child and nursed him.
[Exodus] [2]:[10] When the child had grown older, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, saying, "Because I drew him out of the water." [Footnote: The name Moses sounds like the Hebrew word meaning "to draw out."]
[Exodus] [2]:[11] One day, after Moses had grown up, he went out to his own people and saw their hard labor. He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people.
[Exodus] [2]:[12] He looked this way and that, and seeing no one, he struck the Egyptian down and hid him in the sand.
[Exodus] [2]:[13] The next day he went out and found two Hebrews fighting. He said to the one in the wrong, "Why are you beating your neighbor?"
[Exodus] [2]:[14] The man answered, "Who made you ruler and judge over us? Do you mean to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?" Then Moses was afraid and thought, "So the thing is known."
[Exodus] [2]:[15] When Pharaoh heard of it, he tried to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and settled in the land of Midian, where he sat down by a well.
[Exodus] [2]:[16] Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters. They came to draw water and fill the troughs to water their father's flock.
[Exodus] [2]:[17] When some shepherds came and drove them away, Moses got up, came to their rescue, and watered their flock.
[Exodus] [2]:[18] When they returned to their father Reuel, he asked, "Why have you come back so early today?"
[Exodus] [2]:[19] They answered, "An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds. He even drew water for us and watered the flock."
[Exodus] [2]:[20] "Where is he?" their father asked. "Why did you leave him behind? Invite him to have something to eat."
[Exodus] [2]:[21] Moses agreed to stay with the man, who gave him his daughter Zipporah in marriage.
[Exodus] [2]:[22] She gave birth to a son, and Moses named him Gershom, saying, "I have been a stranger in a foreign land." [Footnote: The name Gershom sounds like the Hebrew words for "a stranger there."]
[Exodus] [2]:[23] A long time passed, and the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned under their bondage and cried out, and their cry for help rose up to God from their bondage.
[Exodus] [2]:[24] God heard their groaning, and he remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
[Exodus] [2]:[25] God saw the Israelites, and God took notice of them.
[Exodus] [3]:[1] Moses was tending the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock beyond the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.
[Exodus] [3]:[2] There the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire out of a bush. Moses looked, and though the bush was burning with fire, it was not consumed.
[Exodus] [3]:[3] So Moses said, "Let me turn aside and see this great sight—why the bush does not burn up."
[Exodus] [3]:[4] When the LORD saw that he had turned aside to look, God called to him out of the bush: "Moses, Moses!" And he answered, "Here I am."
[Exodus] [3]:[5] Then he said, "Do not come any closer. Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground."
[Exodus] [3]:[6] Then he said, "I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." At this Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.
[Exodus] [3]:[7] The LORD said, "I have surely seen the misery of my people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out because of their oppressors, and I know their sufferings.
[Exodus] [3]:[8] So I have come down to rescue them from the hand of the Egyptians and to bring them up out of that land into a good and spacious land, a land flowing with milk and honey—the home of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
[Exodus] [3]:[9] Now the cry of the Israelites has reached me, and I have seen how harshly the Egyptians are oppressing them.
[Exodus] [3]:[10] So now, go. I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring my people the Israelites out of Egypt."
[Exodus] [3]:[11] But Moses said to God, "Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of Egypt?"
[Exodus] [3]:[12] God answered, "I will be with you. And this will be the sign to you that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you will worship God on this mountain."
[Exodus] [3]:[13] Moses said to God, "Suppose I go to the Israelites and tell them, 'The God of your fathers has sent me to you,' and they ask me, 'What is his name?' What shall I tell them?"
[Exodus] [3]:[14] God said to Moses, "I AM WHO I AM. This is what you are to say to the Israelites: 'I AM has sent me to you.'"
[Exodus] [3]:[15] God also said to Moses, "Say this to the Israelites: 'The LORD, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has sent me to you.' This is my name forever, the name by which I am to be remembered from generation to generation.
[Exodus] [3]:[16] Go, gather the elders of Israel and say to them, 'The LORD, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—appeared to me and said: I have surely taken notice of you and of what has been done to you in Egypt.
[Exodus] [3]:[17] And I have promised to bring you up out of your misery in Egypt into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—a land flowing with milk and honey.'
[Exodus] [3]:[18] They will listen to you. Then you and the elders of Israel are to go to the king of Egypt and say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. Now let us take a three-day journey into the wilderness to sacrifice to the LORD our God.'
[Exodus] [3]:[19] But I know that the king of Egypt will not let you go unless a mighty hand compels him.[^1] [^1]: Or "not even by a mighty hand." The Hebrew is brief and has been understood both ways.
[Exodus] [3]:[20] So I will stretch out my hand and strike Egypt with all my wonders that I will perform in its midst. After that, he will let you go.
[Exodus] [3]:[21] And I will make the Egyptians favorably disposed toward this people, so that when you leave, you will not go empty-handed.
[Exodus] [3]:[22] Every woman is to ask her neighbor and any woman living in her house for articles of silver and gold and for clothing, and you will put them on your sons and daughters. So you will plunder the Egyptians."
[Exodus] [4]:[1] Then Moses answered, "But what if they do not believe me or listen to my voice? They will say, 'The LORD did not appear to you.'"
[Exodus] [4]:[2] The LORD said to him, "What is that in your hand?" "A staff," he answered.
[Exodus] [4]:[3] "Throw it on the ground," he said. Moses threw it on the ground, and it became a snake, and Moses fled from it.
[Exodus] [4]:[4] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Reach out your hand and take it by the tail." So he reached out and caught it, and it turned back into a staff in his hand—
[Exodus] [4]:[5] "This is so that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob—has appeared to you."
[Exodus] [4]:[6] The LORD said to him further, "Put your hand inside your cloak." So he put his hand inside his cloak, and when he drew it out, his hand was leprous, white as snow.
[Exodus] [4]:[7] "Put your hand back inside your cloak," he said. So he put his hand back inside his cloak, and when he drew it out, it was restored like the rest of his flesh.
[Exodus] [4]:[8] "If they will not believe you or heed the first sign, they may believe the second.
[Exodus] [4]:[9] But if they will not believe even these two signs or listen to your voice, then take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground. The water you take from the Nile will become blood on the ground."
[Exodus] [4]:[10] But Moses said to the LORD, "Please, Lord, I have never been a man of words—not yesterday, not the day before, not since you began speaking to your servant. I am slow of speech and slow of tongue."
[Exodus] [4]:[11] The LORD said to him, "Who gave man his mouth? Who makes him mute or deaf, seeing or blind? Is it not I, the LORD?
[Exodus] [4]:[12] Now go; I will be with your mouth and teach you what to say."
[Exodus] [4]:[13] But he said, "Please, Lord, send someone else."
[Exodus] [4]:[14] Then the LORD's anger burned against Moses, and he said, "What about your brother Aaron the Levite? I know he can speak well. He is already on his way to meet you, and when he sees you his heart will be glad.
[Exodus] [4]:[15] You are to speak to him and put the words in his mouth; I will be with your mouth and with his, and I will teach you both what to do.
[Exodus] [4]:[16] He will speak to the people for you; he will be your mouth, and you will be as God to him.
[Exodus] [4]:[17] And take this staff in your hand, for with it you shall perform the signs."
[Exodus] [4]:[18] Then Moses went back to Jethro his father-in-law and said to him, "Let me return to my relatives in Egypt to see whether they are still alive." Jethro said to Moses, "Go in peace."
[Exodus] [4]:[19] The LORD said to Moses in Midian, "Go back to Egypt, for all the men who wanted to kill you are dead."
[Exodus] [4]:[20] So Moses took his wife and his sons, set them on a donkey, and started back to the land of Egypt. And he took the staff of God in his hand.
[Exodus] [4]:[21] The LORD said to Moses, "When you return to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders I have put in your power. But I will harden his heart, and he will not let the people go.
[Exodus] [4]:[22] Then say to Pharaoh: This is what the LORD says: Israel is my firstborn son,
[Exodus] [4]:[23] and I told you, 'Let my son go, so that he may serve me.' But you refused to let him go; therefore I will kill your firstborn son."
[Exodus] [4]:[24] On the way, at a place where they stopped for the night, the LORD met him and sought to put him to death.
[Exodus] [4]:[25] But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off her son's foreskin, and touched it to his feet, saying, "Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me."
[Exodus] [4]:[26] So he let him alone. It was then that she said, "A bridegroom of blood," because of the circumcision.
[Exodus] [4]:[27] The LORD said to Aaron, "Go into the wilderness to meet Moses." So he went, and he met him at the mountain of God and kissed him.
[Exodus] [4]:[28] Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, and all the signs he had commanded him to perform.
[Exodus] [4]:[29] Then Moses and Aaron went and gathered all the elders of the Israelites.
[Exodus] [4]:[30] Aaron spoke all the words the LORD had said to Moses, and he performed the signs before the eyes of the people.
[Exodus] [4]:[31] And the people believed. When they heard that the LORD had taken notice of the Israelites and had seen their misery, they bowed down and worshiped.
[Exodus] [5]:[1] Afterward Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Let my people go, so they may hold a festival for me in the wilderness."
[Exodus] [5]:[2] But Pharaoh said, "Who is the LORD, that I should obey his voice and let Israel go? I do not know the LORD, and I will not let Israel go."
[Exodus] [5]:[3] Then they said, "The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Let us go three days' journey into the wilderness to sacrifice to the LORD our God, or he may strike us with plague or with the sword."
[Exodus] [5]:[4] But the king of Egypt said to them, "Moses and Aaron, why are you pulling the people away from their work? Get back to your labor!"
[Exodus] [5]:[5] And Pharaoh said, "Look how numerous the people of the land are now, and you would have them stop their labor!"
[Exodus] [5]:[6] That same day Pharaoh gave orders to the slave drivers over the people and to their foremen:
[Exodus] [5]:[7] "You shall no longer supply the people with straw for making bricks, as you did before. Let them go and gather their own straw.
[Exodus] [5]:[8] But require of them the same quota of bricks they made before; do not reduce it. They are lazy—that is why they cry out, 'Let us go and sacrifice to our God.'
[Exodus] [5]:[9] Make the work heavier for these men, so they keep at it and pay no attention to lying words."
[Exodus] [5]:[10] So the slave drivers and the foremen went out and said to the people, "This is what Pharaoh says: I will no longer give you straw.
[Exodus] [5]:[11] Go and get your own straw wherever you can find it—but your workload will not be reduced in the least."
[Exodus] [5]:[12] So the people scattered throughout the whole land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
[Exodus] [5]:[13] The slave drivers kept pressing them: "Finish your work—the same daily quota as when the straw was provided."
[Exodus] [5]:[14] And the foremen of the Israelites, whom Pharaoh's slave drivers had appointed over them, were beaten, and they were asked, "Why did you not complete your required quota of bricks yesterday or today, as you did before?"
[Exodus] [5]:[15] Then the Israelite foremen went to Pharaoh and cried out, "Why do you treat your servants this way?
[Exodus] [5]:[16] No straw is given to your servants, yet they tell us, 'Make bricks!' Your servants are being beaten, but the fault lies with your own people."
[Exodus] [5]:[17] But he said, "Lazy—that's what you are, lazy! That is why you say, 'Let us go and sacrifice to the LORD.'
[Exodus] [5]:[18] Now get to work! You will be given no straw, yet you must deliver the full number of bricks."
[Exodus] [5]:[19] The Israelite foremen saw that they were in trouble when they were told, "You must not reduce the daily number of bricks."
[Exodus] [5]:[20] When they left Pharaoh, they came upon Moses and Aaron, who stood waiting for them,
[Exodus] [5]:[21] and they said to them, "May the LORD look upon you and judge you! You have made us a stench to Pharaoh and his officials—you have put a sword in their hand to kill us."
[Exodus] [5]:[22] Then Moses turned to the LORD and said, "Lord, why have you brought harm on this people? Why did you ever send me?
[Exodus] [5]:[23] Ever since I went to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has brought harm on this people, and you have done nothing at all to rescue your people."
[Exodus] [6]:[1] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh: by a mighty hand he will let them go, and by a mighty hand he will drive them out of his land."
[Exodus] [6]:[2] God spoke to Moses and said to him, "I am the LORD.
[Exodus] [6]:[3] I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty, but by my name the LORD I did not make myself known to them.
[Exodus] [6]:[4] I also established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land where they lived as strangers.
[Exodus] [6]:[5] I have also heard the groaning of the Israelites, whom the Egyptians are holding in bondage, and I have remembered my covenant.
[Exodus] [6]:[6] Therefore say to the Israelites: 'I am the LORD. I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians and deliver you from their slavery. I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with mighty acts of judgment.
[Exodus] [6]:[7] I will take you as my own people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, who brings you out from under the burdens of Egypt.
[Exodus] [6]:[8] And I will bring you into the land I swore with uplifted hand to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob. I will give it to you as your possession. I am the LORD.'"
[Exodus] [6]:[9] Moses reported this to the Israelites, but they would not listen to him because of their broken spirit and their cruel slavery.
[Exodus] [6]:[10] Then the LORD said to Moses,
[Exodus] [6]:[11] "Go, tell Pharaoh king of Egypt to let the Israelites go out of his land."
[Exodus] [6]:[12] But Moses said in the LORD's presence, "See, the Israelites have not listened to me; how then will Pharaoh listen to me, since I speak with faltering lips?"
[Exodus] [6]:[13] Now the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron and gave them a charge concerning the Israelites and concerning Pharaoh king of Egypt: to bring the Israelites out of the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [6]:[14] These were the heads of their fathers' houses: The sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. These were the clans of Reuben.
[Exodus] [6]:[15] The sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman. These were the clans of Simeon.
[Exodus] [6]:[16] These were the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Levi lived 137 years.
[Exodus] [6]:[17] The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, by their clans.
[Exodus] [6]:[18] The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived 133 years.
[Exodus] [6]:[19] The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of Levi according to their generations.
[Exodus] [6]:[20] Amram married his father's sister Jochebed, and she bore him Aaron and Moses. Amram lived 137 years.
[Exodus] [6]:[21] The sons of Izhar: Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
[Exodus] [6]:[22] The sons of Uzziel: Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
[Exodus] [6]:[23] Aaron married Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon, and she bore him Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
[Exodus] [6]:[24] The sons of Korah: Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph. These were the clans of the Korahites.
[Exodus] [6]:[25] Eleazar son of Aaron married one of the daughters of Putiel, and she bore him Phinehas. These were the heads of the Levite families, clan by clan.
[Exodus] [6]:[26] It was this Aaron and Moses to whom the LORD said, "Bring the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by their divisions."
[Exodus] [6]:[27] They were the ones who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt about bringing the Israelites out of Egypt—this same Moses and Aaron.
[Exodus] [6]:[28] Now on the day the LORD spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
[Exodus] [6]:[29] the LORD said to him, "I am the LORD. Tell Pharaoh king of Egypt everything I say to you."
[Exodus] [6]:[30] But Moses said in the LORD's presence, "Since I speak with faltering lips, how will Pharaoh listen to me?"
[Exodus] [7]:[1] The LORD said to Moses, "See, I have made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.
[Exodus] [7]:[2] You are to speak everything I command you, and your brother Aaron is to tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites go out of his land.
[Exodus] [7]:[3] But I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and though I multiply my signs and wonders in the land of Egypt,
[Exodus] [7]:[4] Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will lay my hand on Egypt, and with mighty acts of judgment I will bring my divisions, my people the Israelites, out of the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [7]:[5] And the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I stretch out my hand against Egypt and bring the Israelites out from among them."
[Exodus] [7]:[6] Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded them.
[Exodus] [7]:[7] Moses was eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three when they spoke to Pharaoh.
[Exodus] [7]:[8] The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
[Exodus] [7]:[9] "When Pharaoh says to you, 'Perform a wonder,' say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw it down before Pharaoh, and it will become a serpent.'"
[Exodus] [7]:[10] So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just as the LORD had commanded. Aaron threw his staff down before Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a serpent.
[Exodus] [7]:[11] Then Pharaoh summoned the wise men and sorcerers, and the Egyptian magicians did the same thing by their secret arts.
[Exodus] [7]:[12] Each one threw down his staff, and they became serpents. But Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs.
[Exodus] [7]:[13] Yet Pharaoh's heart grew hard, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
[Exodus] [7]:[14] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Pharaoh's heart is unyielding; he refuses to let the people go.
[Exodus] [7]:[15] Go to Pharaoh in the morning as he is going out to the water. Stand and wait for him on the bank of the Nile, and take in your hand the staff that turned into a snake.
[Exodus] [7]:[16] Say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to tell you: Let my people go, so that they may worship me in the wilderness. But until now you have not listened.
[Exodus] [7]:[17] This is what the LORD says: By this you will know that I am the LORD. Watch: with the staff in my hand I will strike the water of the Nile, and it will turn to blood.
[Exodus] [7]:[18] The fish in the Nile will die, the river will stink, and the Egyptians will not be able to bear drinking water from the Nile.'"
[Exodus] [7]:[19] The LORD said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt—over their rivers and canals, their ponds and all their reservoirs—and they will turn to blood.' There will be blood everywhere in Egypt, even in vessels of wood and stone."
[Exodus] [7]:[20] Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded. In the sight of Pharaoh and his officials, Aaron raised the staff and struck the water of the Nile, and all the water in the river turned to blood.
[Exodus] [7]:[21] The fish in the Nile died, the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink its water. There was blood throughout the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [7]:[22] But the Egyptian magicians did the same thing by their secret arts, and Pharaoh's heart grew hard. He would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
[Exodus] [7]:[23] Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he paid no attention to this either.
[Exodus] [7]:[24] And all the Egyptians dug along the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink the water of the river.
[Exodus] [7]:[25] Seven days passed after the LORD struck the Nile.
[Exodus] [7]:[26] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Let my people go, so that they may worship me.
[Exodus] [7]:[27] If you refuse to let them go, I am about to plague your whole territory with frogs.
[Exodus] [7]:[28] The Nile will teem with frogs. They will come up and go into your palace, into your bedroom and onto your bed, into the houses of your officials and your people, into your ovens and your kneading troughs.
[Exodus] [7]:[29] The frogs will swarm over you and your people and all your officials.'"
[Exodus] [8]:[1] The LORD said to Moses, "Say to Aaron: Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, the canals, and the pools, and bring up the frogs upon the land of Egypt."
[Exodus] [8]:[2] So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [8]:[3] But the magicians did the same by their secret arts and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [8]:[4] Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Plead with the LORD to take the frogs away from me and my people, and I will let the people go to sacrifice to the LORD."
[Exodus] [8]:[5] Moses said to Pharaoh, "The honor is yours: name the time when I am to plead for you, your servants, and your people, that the frogs may be cut off from you and your houses and remain only in the Nile."
[Exodus] [8]:[6] "Tomorrow," he said. Moses replied, "As you say—so that you may know that there is no one like the LORD our God.
[Exodus] [8]:[7] The frogs will leave you and your houses, your servants and your people; they will remain only in the Nile."
[Exodus] [8]:[8] Then Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried to the LORD about the frogs he had brought upon Pharaoh.
[Exodus] [8]:[9] The LORD did as Moses asked, and the frogs died in the houses, the courtyards, and the fields.
[Exodus] [8]:[10] They piled them up in heap after heap, and the land reeked.
[Exodus] [8]:[11] But when Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he hardened his heart and would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
[Exodus] [8]:[12] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Say to Aaron: Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth, and it will become gnats throughout all the land of Egypt."
[Exodus] [8]:[13] They did so. Aaron stretched out his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the earth, and gnats came upon man and beast. All the dust of the earth became gnats throughout all the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [8]:[14] The magicians did the same by their secret arts, trying to produce gnats, but they could not. And the gnats were on man and beast.
[Exodus] [8]:[15] Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, "This is the finger of God." But Pharaoh's heart remained hard, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
[Exodus] [8]:[16] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and present yourself before Pharaoh as he goes out to the water, and say to him: Thus says the LORD: Let my people go, that they may serve me.
[Exodus] [8]:[17] For if you will not let my people go, I will send swarms of flies upon you and your servants, upon your people and into your houses. The houses of the Egyptians will be full of flies, and even the ground where they stand.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew word means simply "swarm"; the kind of insect is not specified.
[Exodus] [8]:[18] But on that day I will set apart the land of Goshen, where my people live; no swarms of flies will be there, so that you may know that I am the LORD in the midst of the land.
[Exodus] [8]:[19] I will make a distinction between my people and your people. Tomorrow this sign will take place."
[Exodus] [8]:[20] And the LORD did so. Dense swarms of flies came into the house of Pharaoh and the houses of his servants; throughout all the land of Egypt the land was ruined because of the flies.
[Exodus] [8]:[21] Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Go, sacrifice to your God here in the land."
[Exodus] [8]:[22] But Moses said, "That would not be right, for what we sacrifice to the LORD our God is detestable to the Egyptians. If we offer sacrifices detestable to the Egyptians before their eyes, will they not stone us?
[Exodus] [8]:[23] We must go a three days' journey into the wilderness and sacrifice to the LORD our God, as he commands us."
[Exodus] [8]:[24] Pharaoh said, "I will let you go to sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness—only you must not go very far. Now plead for me."
[Exodus] [8]:[25] Moses said, "As soon as I leave you, I will plead with the LORD, and tomorrow the flies will depart from Pharaoh, his servants, and his people. Only let Pharaoh not deal falsely again by refusing to let the people go to sacrifice to the LORD."
[Exodus] [8]:[26] Then Moses went out from Pharaoh and pleaded with the LORD.
[Exodus] [8]:[27] And the LORD did as Moses asked: he removed the flies from Pharaoh, his servants, and his people; not one remained.
[Exodus] [8]:[28] But Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also and would not let the people go.
[Exodus] [9]:[1] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and say to him: Thus says the LORD, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, so that they may serve me.
[Exodus] [9]:[2] For if you refuse to let them go and keep holding them back,
[Exodus] [9]:[3] the hand of the LORD will fall on your livestock in the field—on the horses, the donkeys, the camels, the cattle, and the sheep—with a severe plague.
[Exodus] [9]:[4] But the LORD will distinguish between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, so that nothing belonging to the Israelites will die."
[Exodus] [9]:[5] And the LORD set a time, saying, "Tomorrow the LORD will do this in the land."
[Exodus] [9]:[6] The next day the LORD did it: all the livestock of Egypt died, but not one animal belonging to the Israelites died.
[Exodus] [9]:[7] Pharaoh sent men to look, and indeed, not one of Israel's livestock had died. Yet Pharaoh's heart remained hard, and he would not let the people go.
[Exodus] [9]:[8] Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Take handfuls of soot from a furnace, and let Moses toss it toward the sky in Pharaoh's sight.
[Exodus] [9]:[9] It will become fine dust over the whole land of Egypt, and it will break out in festering boils on people and animals throughout the land of Egypt."
[Exodus] [9]:[10] So they took soot from the furnace and stood before Pharaoh, and Moses tossed it toward the sky, and festering boils broke out on people and animals.
[Exodus] [9]:[11] The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were on the magicians and on all the Egyptians.
[Exodus] [9]:[12] But the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had told Moses.
[Exodus] [9]:[13] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Get up early in the morning, stand before Pharaoh, and say to him: Thus says the LORD, the God of the Hebrews: Let my people go, so that they may serve me.
[Exodus] [9]:[14] For this time I will send all my plagues against your very heart, and against your officials and your people, so that you may know that there is no one like me in all the earth.
[Exodus] [9]:[15] By now I could have stretched out my hand and struck you and your people with a plague that would have wiped you from the earth.
[Exodus] [9]:[16] But this is why I have let you stand: to show you my power, and so that my name may be proclaimed in all the earth.
[Exodus] [9]:[17] You still set yourself against my people and refuse to let them go.
[Exodus] [9]:[18] So tomorrow at this time I will send down such a heavy hail as has never fallen on Egypt from the day it was founded until now.
[Exodus] [9]:[19] Now send word and bring to safety your livestock and everything you have in the field. Every person and animal left in the open, not brought inside, will die when the hail comes down on them."
[Exodus] [9]:[20] Those among Pharaoh's officials who feared the word of the LORD hurried their servants and livestock indoors,
[Exodus] [9]:[21] but those who paid no attention to the word of the LORD left their servants and livestock in the field.
[Exodus] [9]:[22] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the sky, so that hail may fall on the whole land of Egypt—on people and animals and on every plant of the field throughout the land of Egypt."
[Exodus] [9]:[23] So Moses stretched out his staff toward the sky, and the LORD sent thunder and hail, and lightning struck the earth. The LORD rained hail down on the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [9]:[24] Hail fell, and lightning flashed within the hail—a storm so severe that nothing like it had ever been seen in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.
[Exodus] [9]:[25] Throughout the land of Egypt the hail struck down everything in the field, both people and animals; it beat down every plant of the field and shattered every tree.
[Exodus] [9]:[26] Only in the land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived, did no hail fall.
[Exodus] [9]:[27] Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said to them, "This time I have sinned. The LORD is in the right; I and my people are in the wrong.
[Exodus] [9]:[28] Pray to the LORD, for there has been enough of God's thunder and hail. I will let you go; you need not stay any longer."
[Exodus] [9]:[29] Moses said to him, "When I have gone out of the city, I will spread out my hands to the LORD. The thunder will cease and there will be no more hail, so that you may know that the earth belongs to the LORD.
[Exodus] [9]:[30] But as for you and your officials, I know that you still do not fear the LORD God."
[Exodus] [9]:[31] The flax and the barley were destroyed, since the barley was in the ear and the flax in bud;
[Exodus] [9]:[32] but the wheat and the spelt were not ruined, because they ripen later.
[Exodus] [9]:[33] Moses left Pharaoh and went out of the city. He spread out his hands to the LORD, and the thunder and hail ceased, and the rain no longer poured down on the earth.
[Exodus] [9]:[34] But when Pharaoh saw that the rain, hail, and thunder had stopped, he sinned again: he and his officials hardened their hearts.
[Exodus] [9]:[35] So Pharaoh's heart was hard, and he would not let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had said through Moses.
[Exodus] [10]:[1] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh. I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials, so that I may perform these signs of mine among them,
[Exodus] [10]:[2] and so that you may tell your children and grandchildren how harshly I dealt with Egypt and what signs I did among them, and you will know that I am the LORD."
[Exodus] [10]:[3] So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said to him, "This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, so that they may serve me.
[Exodus] [10]:[4] If you refuse to let my people go, then tomorrow I will bring locusts into your land.
[Exodus] [10]:[5] They will cover the face of the ground so that no one can see the land. They will devour what little you have left after the hail, and they will strip every tree that grows in your fields.
[Exodus] [10]:[6] They will fill your houses and the houses of all your officials and of all the Egyptians—something neither your fathers nor your forefathers have ever seen from the day they first came to be on the earth until now." Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh.
[Exodus] [10]:[7] Pharaoh's officials said to him, "How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may serve the LORD their God. Don't you see yet that Egypt is ruined?"
[Exodus] [10]:[8] So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. "Go, serve the LORD your God," he said. "But just who is going?"
[Exodus] [10]:[9] Moses answered, "We will go with our young and our old, with our sons and our daughters, and with our flocks and herds, for we must hold a festival to the LORD."
[Exodus] [10]:[10] Pharaoh said, "The LORD be with you—if I ever let you go along with your children! Clearly you are bent on evil.
[Exodus] [10]:[11] No! Let the men go and serve the LORD, since that is what you have been asking for." And they were driven out from Pharaoh's presence.
[Exodus] [10]:[12] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt to bring the locusts. Let them come up over the land of Egypt and devour every plant in the land, everything the hail has left."
[Exodus] [10]:[13] So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and the LORD sent an east wind across the land all that day and all that night. By morning the wind had brought the locusts.
[Exodus] [10]:[14] They swarmed over all the land of Egypt and settled in every part of the country in vast numbers. Never before had there been such a swarm of locusts, nor will there ever be again.
[Exodus] [10]:[15] They covered the face of the whole land until it was black. They devoured every plant in the land and all the fruit on the trees that the hail had left. Nothing green remained on tree or plant in all the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [10]:[16] Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.
[Exodus] [10]:[17] Now forgive my sin just this once, and pray to the LORD your God to take this deadly plague away from me."
[Exodus] [10]:[18] Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD.
[Exodus] [10]:[19] And the LORD changed the wind to a very strong west wind, which carried the locusts away and swept them into the Red Sea.[^1] [^1]: Hebrew: the Sea of Reeds.
[Exodus] [10]:[20] But the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let the Israelites go.
[Exodus] [10]:[21] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the sky, and darkness will come over the land of Egypt—a darkness that can be felt."
[Exodus] [10]:[22] So Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and total darkness covered all the land of Egypt for three days.
[Exodus] [10]:[23] No one could see anyone else, and no one left his place for three days. Yet all the Israelites had light where they lived.
[Exodus] [10]:[24] Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, "Go, serve the LORD. Only your flocks and herds must stay behind; even your children may go with you."
[Exodus] [10]:[25] But Moses said, "You must also let us have sacrifices and burnt offerings to present to the LORD our God.
[Exodus] [10]:[26] Our livestock must go with us too; not a hoof is to be left behind. We have to use some of them in serving the LORD our God, and until we get there we will not know what we are to offer to the LORD."
[Exodus] [10]:[27] But the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.
[Exodus] [10]:[28] Pharaoh said to Moses, "Get away from me! Make sure you never appear before me again, for on the day you see my face you will die."
[Exodus] [10]:[29] "Just as you say," Moses replied. "I will never appear before you again."
[Exodus] [11]:[1] The LORD said to Moses, "One more plague I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt. After that he will let you go from here; indeed, when he lets you go, he will drive you out of here completely."
[Exodus] [11]:[2] "Speak now in the hearing of the people: let every man ask his neighbor, and every woman her neighbor, for articles of silver and articles of gold."
