[Exodus] [11]:[3] And the LORD gave the people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians. Moreover, the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the eyes of Pharaoh's servants and in the eyes of the people.
[Exodus] [11]:[4] So Moses said, "Thus says the LORD: About midnight I will go out through the midst of Egypt,
[Exodus] [11]:[5] and every firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne to the firstborn of the slave girl who is behind the millstones, and every firstborn of the livestock.
[Exodus] [11]:[6] Then there will be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as has never been and never will be again.
[Exodus] [11]:[7] But among all the Israelites not even a dog shall growl, neither at man nor beast, so that you may know that the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.
[Exodus] [11]:[8] And all these servants of yours will come down to me and bow before me, saying, 'Get out, you and all the people who follow you!' After that I will go out." And he went out from Pharaoh in burning anger.
[Exodus] [11]:[9] The LORD had said to Moses, "Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that my wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt."
[Exodus] [11]:[10] Moses and Aaron performed all these wonders before Pharaoh, but the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not let the Israelites go out of his land.
[Exodus] [12]:[1] The LORD said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt:
[Exodus] [12]:[2] "This month shall be for you the beginning of months; it shall be the first month of the year for you.
[Exodus] [12]:[3] Say to the whole congregation of Israel: On the tenth day of this month each man is to take a lamb for his household, one lamb per house.
[Exodus] [12]:[4] If a household is too small for a whole lamb, he and his nearest neighbor shall share one, according to the number of people; you shall apportion the lamb by what each one can eat.
[Exodus] [12]:[5] Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male a year old; you may take it from the sheep or from the goats.
[Exodus] [12]:[6] You shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month, and then the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it at twilight.
[Exodus] [12]:[7] They shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel of the houses where they eat it.
[Exodus] [12]:[8] That same night they shall eat the meat, roasted over the fire, with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
[Exodus] [12]:[9] Do not eat any of it raw or boiled in water, but roasted over the fire—its head with its legs and its inner parts.
[Exodus] [12]:[10] You shall leave none of it until morning; whatever is left over by morning you shall burn in the fire.
[Exodus] [12]:[11] This is how you shall eat it: with your belt fastened, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand. Eat it in haste—it is the LORD's Passover.
[Exodus] [12]:[12] For I will pass through the land of Egypt that night and strike down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast, and I will execute judgment on all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD.
[Exodus] [12]:[13] The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you are. When I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will come upon you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [12]:[14] This day shall be a day of remembrance for you, and you shall keep it as a festival to the LORD; throughout your generations you shall keep it as a lasting ordinance.
[Exodus] [12]:[15] For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. On the first day you shall remove all leaven from your houses, for whoever eats what is leavened, from the first day until the seventh, that person shall be cut off from Israel.
[Exodus] [12]:[16] On the first day you shall hold a holy assembly, and on the seventh day another holy assembly. No work shall be done on those days, except what each of you must prepare to eat—that alone you may do.
[Exodus] [12]:[17] You shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread, because on this very day I brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt. You shall keep this day throughout your generations as a lasting ordinance.
[Exodus] [12]:[18] In the first month, from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of the twenty-first day, you shall eat unleavened bread.
[Exodus] [12]:[19] For seven days no leaven is to be found in your houses, for whoever eats what is leavened shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether a foreigner or a native of the land.
[Exodus] [12]:[20] You shall eat nothing leavened; wherever you live you shall eat unleavened bread."
[Exodus] [12]:[21] Then Moses called all the elders of Israel and said to them, "Go, select lambs for your families, and slaughter the Passover lamb.
[Exodus] [12]:[22] Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and touch the lintel and the two doorposts with the blood in the basin. None of you shall go out the door of his house until morning.
[Exodus] [12]:[23] For the LORD will pass through to strike the Egyptians, and when he sees the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, the LORD will pass over the door and will not let the destroyer enter your houses to strike you.
[Exodus] [12]:[24] You shall keep this command as a statute for you and your children forever.
[Exodus] [12]:[25] And when you come into the land the LORD will give you, as he promised, you shall observe this rite.
[Exodus] [12]:[26] And when your children ask you, 'What does this rite mean to you?'
[Exodus] [12]:[27] you shall say, 'It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt when he struck the Egyptians but spared our homes.'" Then the people bowed down and worshiped.
[Exodus] [12]:[28] The Israelites went and did just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.
[Exodus] [12]:[29] At midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the prisoner in the dungeon, and every firstborn of the livestock.
[Exodus] [12]:[30] Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and all his officials and all the Egyptians, and there was a great outcry in Egypt, for there was not a house without someone dead.
[Exodus] [12]:[31] He summoned Moses and Aaron that night and said, "Get up, go out from among my people, both you and the Israelites! Go, worship the LORD as you have said.
[Exodus] [12]:[32] Take your flocks and herds as well, just as you said, and go. And bless me too."
[Exodus] [12]:[33] The Egyptians urged the people to hurry and leave the country, for they said, "We are all going to die!"
[Exodus] [12]:[34] So the people took their dough before it was leavened, with their kneading bowls wrapped in their cloaks on their shoulders.
[Exodus] [12]:[35] The Israelites had done as Moses told them: they asked the Egyptians for objects of silver and gold, and for clothing.
[Exodus] [12]:[36] The LORD had made the Egyptians favorably disposed toward the people, so they granted their request. Thus they plundered Egypt.
[Exodus] [12]:[37] The Israelites set out from Rameses for Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides the children.
[Exodus] [12]:[38] A large mixed company went up with them as well, along with flocks and herds, a great many livestock.
[Exodus] [12]:[39] They baked the dough they had brought out of Egypt into unleavened loaves, for it had not risen; they had been driven out of Egypt and could not delay, nor had they prepared any provisions for themselves.
[Exodus] [12]:[40] The time the Israelites lived in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years.
[Exodus] [12]:[41] And at the end of four hundred and thirty years, on that very day, all the hosts of the LORD went out of the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [12]:[42] It was a night of vigil for the LORD, to bring them out of the land of Egypt. This same night is a vigil for the LORD, to be kept by all the Israelites throughout their generations.
[Exodus] [12]:[43] The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "This is the statute of the Passover: no foreigner may eat of it.
[Exodus] [12]:[44] Any man's slave bought with money may eat of it once you have circumcised him.
[Exodus] [12]:[45] No temporary resident or hired worker may eat of it.
[Exodus] [12]:[46] It must be eaten in a single house; you shall not carry any of the meat outside, and you shall not break any of its bones.
[Exodus] [12]:[47] The whole congregation of Israel shall keep it.
[Exodus] [12]:[48] If a foreigner living among you wants to celebrate the LORD's Passover, all the males of his household must be circumcised; then he may take part like a native of the land. But no uncircumcised person may eat of it.
[Exodus] [12]:[49] The same law shall apply to the native and to the foreigner living among you."
[Exodus] [12]:[50] All the Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron; so they did.
[Exodus] [12]:[51] And on that very day the LORD brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by their hosts.
[Exodus] [13]:[1] The LORD said to Moses,
[Exodus] [13]:[2] "Consecrate to me every firstborn. The first offspring of every womb among the Israelites belongs to me, whether human or animal."
[Exodus] [13]:[3] Then Moses said to the people, "Remember this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, for the LORD brought you out of it with a mighty hand. No leavened bread is to be eaten.
[Exodus] [13]:[4] Today you are going out, in the month of Abib.
[Exodus] [13]:[5] When the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites—the land he swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey—you are to keep this observance in this month.
[Exodus] [13]:[6] For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a festival to the LORD.
[Exodus] [13]:[7] Unleavened bread is to be eaten throughout the seven days; no leavened bread is to be seen among you, and no yeast is to be seen anywhere within your borders.
[Exodus] [13]:[8] On that day you shall tell your son, 'This is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.'
[Exodus] [13]:[9] It shall be a sign for you on your hand and a reminder between your eyes, so that the law of the LORD may be on your lips; for with a mighty hand the LORD brought you out of Egypt.
[Exodus] [13]:[10] You shall keep this statute at its appointed time, year after year.
[Exodus] [13]:[11] "When the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you, as he swore to you and to your fathers,
[Exodus] [13]:[12] you shall give over to the LORD the first offspring of every womb. Every firstborn male of your livestock belongs to the LORD.
[Exodus] [13]:[13] Every firstborn donkey you shall redeem with a lamb; if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck. And every firstborn among your sons you shall redeem.
[Exodus] [13]:[14] When your son asks you in time to come, 'What does this mean?' you shall tell him, 'With a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
[Exodus] [13]:[15] When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of humans and the firstborn of animals. That is why I sacrifice to the LORD every firstborn male, and why I redeem every firstborn of my sons.'
[Exodus] [13]:[16] It shall be a sign on your hand and a symbol between your eyes that with a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt.
[Exodus] [13]:[17] When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them along the road through the land of the Philistines, though it was shorter. For God said, "If they face war, they may change their minds and return to Egypt."
[Exodus] [13]:[18] So God led the people around by the wilderness road toward the Red Sea. The Israelites went up out of Egypt in battle array.
[Exodus] [13]:[19] Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, because Joseph had made the Israelites swear a solemn oath, saying, "God will surely come to your aid, and then you must carry my bones up with you from here."
[Exodus] [13]:[20] They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
[Exodus] [13]:[21] By day the LORD went ahead of them in a pillar of cloud to guide them on their way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that they could travel by day and by night.
[Exodus] [13]:[22] Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night ever left its place in front of the people.
[Exodus] [14]:[1] Then the LORD said to Moses,
[Exodus] [14]:[2] "Tell the Israelites to turn back and camp in front of Pi Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. Camp facing Baal Zephon, right beside the sea.
[Exodus] [14]:[3] Pharaoh will say of the Israelites, 'They are wandering in confusion in the land; the wilderness has closed in on them.'
[Exodus] [14]:[4] I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and he will pursue them. But I will gain glory for myself through Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD." And they did so.
[Exodus] [14]:[5] When the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled, he and his officials had a change of heart about them and said, "What have we done? We have let Israel go and lost their service!"
[Exodus] [14]:[6] So Pharaoh had his chariot harnessed and took his army with him.
[Exodus] [14]:[7] He took six hundred of his best chariots, along with all the other chariots of Egypt, with officers over all of them.
[Exodus] [14]:[8] The LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued the Israelites, who were marching out boldly.
[Exodus] [14]:[9] The Egyptians pursued them—all Pharaoh's horses and chariots, his horsemen and his troops—and overtook them as they camped by the sea, near Pi Hahiroth, opposite Baal Zephon.
[Exodus] [14]:[10] As Pharaoh drew near, the Israelites looked up, and there were the Egyptians, marching after them. Terrified, the Israelites cried out to the LORD.
[Exodus] [14]:[11] They said to Moses, "Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us out to die in the wilderness? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt?
[Exodus] [14]:[12] Isn't this what we told you in Egypt: 'Leave us alone; let us serve the Egyptians'? It would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness!"
[Exodus] [14]:[13] Moses answered the people, "Do not be afraid. Stand firm and see the deliverance the LORD will bring you today. The Egyptians you see today you will never see again.
[Exodus] [14]:[14] The LORD will fight for you; you need only be still."
[Exodus] [14]:[15] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Why are you crying out to me? Tell the Israelites to move on.
[Exodus] [14]:[16] Raise your staff, stretch out your hand over the sea, and divide it, so that the Israelites can go through the sea on dry ground.
[Exodus] [14]:[17] And I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they will go in after them. I will gain glory for myself through Pharaoh and all his army, through his chariots and his horsemen.
[Exodus] [14]:[18] The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD when I gain glory through Pharaoh, his chariots and his horsemen."
[Exodus] [14]:[19] Then the angel of God, who had been traveling in front of Israel's camp, moved and went behind them. The pillar of cloud also moved from in front of them and stood behind them,
[Exodus] [14]:[20] coming between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. There was the cloud and the darkness, yet it lit up the night; so neither came near the other all night long.
[Exodus] [14]:[21] Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and all that night the LORD drove the sea back with a strong east wind and turned it into dry land. The waters were divided,
[Exodus] [14]:[22] and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with a wall of water on their right and on their left.
[Exodus] [14]:[23] The Egyptians pursued them, and all Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and horsemen followed them into the sea.
[Exodus] [14]:[24] During the last watch of the night the LORD looked down on the Egyptian army from the pillar of fire and cloud and threw it into confusion.
[Exodus] [14]:[25] He made the wheels of their chariots come off so that they could barely move. And the Egyptians said, "Let's get away from the Israelites! The LORD is fighting for them against Egypt."
[Exodus] [14]:[26] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea so that the waters may flow back over the Egyptians, over their chariots and horsemen."
[Exodus] [14]:[27] Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and at daybreak the sea went back to its place. The Egyptians tried to flee from it, but the LORD swept them into the sea.
[Exodus] [14]:[28] The waters flowed back and covered the chariots and horsemen—the entire army of Pharaoh that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them survived.
[Exodus] [14]:[29] But the Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground, with a wall of water on their right and on their left.
[Exodus] [14]:[30] That day the LORD saved Israel from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians lying dead on the shore.
[Exodus] [14]:[31] And when Israel saw the mighty hand of the LORD displayed against the Egyptians, the people feared the LORD and put their trust in him and in Moses his servant.
[Exodus] [15]:[1] Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD: I will sing to the LORD, for he is highly exalted. Horse and rider he hurled into the sea.
[Exodus] [15]:[2] The LORD is my strength and my song; he has become my salvation. He is my God, and I will praise him, the God of my father, and I will exalt him.
[Exodus] [15]:[3] The LORD is a warrior; the LORD is his name.
[Exodus] [15]:[4] Pharaoh's chariots and his army he cast into the sea; the best of his officers sank in the Red Sea.
[Exodus] [15]:[5] The deep waters covered them; they went down into the depths like a stone.
[Exodus] [15]:[6] Your right hand, LORD, is majestic in power; your right hand, LORD, shattered the enemy.
[Exodus] [15]:[7] In the greatness of your majesty you tore down those who rose against you. You sent out your burning anger; it consumed them like straw.
[Exodus] [15]:[8] At the blast of your nostrils the waters piled up; the surging waters stood firm like a wall; the deep waters congealed in the heart of the sea.
[Exodus] [15]:[9] The enemy said, "I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil; my desire will have its fill. I will draw my sword; my hand will destroy them."
[Exodus] [15]:[10] But you blew with your breath, and the sea covered them; they sank like lead in the mighty waters.
[Exodus] [15]:[11] Who among the gods is like you, LORD? Who is like you—majestic in holiness, awesome in praises, working wonders?
[Exodus] [15]:[12] You stretched out your right hand, and the earth swallowed them.
[Exodus] [15]:[13] In your mercy you led the people you redeemed; in your strength you guided them to your holy dwelling.
[Exodus] [15]:[14] The nations heard and trembled; anguish gripped the people of Philistia.
[Exodus] [15]:[15] Then the chiefs of Edom were terrified, the leaders of Moab were seized with trembling, all the inhabitants of Canaan melted away.
[Exodus] [15]:[16] Terror and dread fell upon them. By the might of your arm they became still as stone, until your people passed by, LORD, until the people you purchased passed by.
[Exodus] [15]:[17] You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of your inheritance— the place, LORD, you made for your dwelling, the sanctuary, Lord, your hands established.
[Exodus] [15]:[18] The LORD will reign forever and ever.
[Exodus] [15]:[19] For when Pharaoh's horses, his chariots and horsemen went into the sea, the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them, but the Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground.
[Exodus] [15]:[20] Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron's sister, took a tambourine in her hand, and all the women followed her with tambourines and dancing.
[Exodus] [15]:[21] And Miriam sang to them: Sing to the LORD, for he is highly exalted. Horse and rider he hurled into the sea.
[Exodus] [15]:[22] Then Moses led Israel on from the Red Sea, and they went out into the Desert of Shur. For three days they traveled through the desert without finding water.
[Exodus] [15]:[23] When they came to Marah, they could not drink its water because it was bitter. That is why the place is called Marah.
[Exodus] [15]:[24] So the people grumbled against Moses, saying, "What are we to drink?"
[Exodus] [15]:[25] Then Moses cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There the LORD gave them a statute and an ordinance, and there he tested them.
[Exodus] [15]:[26] He said, "If you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God and do what is right in his eyes, if you pay attention to his commands and keep all his statutes, I will not bring on you any of the diseases I brought on Egypt, for I am the LORD, who heals you."
[Exodus] [15]:[27] Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the water.
[Exodus] [16]:[1] The whole community of Israel set out from Elim and came to the wilderness of Sin, which lies between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they left Egypt.
[Exodus] [16]:[2] In the wilderness the whole community of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron.
[Exodus] [16]:[3] The Israelites said to them, "If only we had died by the LORD's hand in Egypt, where we sat beside pots of meat and ate all the bread we wanted! But you brought us out into this wilderness to starve this whole assembly to death."
[Exodus] [16]:[4] Then the LORD said to Moses, "I am going to rain down bread from heaven for you. Each day the people are to go out and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test them, to see whether they will follow my instruction or not.
[Exodus] [16]:[5] On the sixth day they are to gather twice as much as on the other days, and prepare it."
[Exodus] [16]:[6] So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, "This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of Egypt,
[Exodus] [16]:[7] and in the morning you will see the glory of the LORD, because he has heard your grumbling against him. Who are we, that you should grumble against us?"
[Exodus] [16]:[8] Moses also said, "The LORD will give you meat to eat in the evening and all the bread you want in the morning, because he has heard your grumbling against him. Who are we? Your grumbling is not against us but against the LORD."
[Exodus] [16]:[9] Then Moses said to Aaron, "Say to the whole community of Israel: 'Come before the LORD, for he has heard your grumbling.'"
[Exodus] [16]:[10] While Aaron was speaking to the whole community of Israel, they turned toward the wilderness, and there was the glory of the LORD appearing in the cloud.
[Exodus] [16]:[11] The LORD said to Moses,
[Exodus] [16]:[12] "I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them: 'At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will have your fill of bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.'"
[Exodus] [16]:[13] That evening quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew all around the camp.
[Exodus] [16]:[14] When the layer of dew lifted, there on the surface of the wilderness lay something thin and flaky, fine as frost on the ground.
[Exodus] [16]:[15] When the Israelites saw it, they said to one another, "What is it?"—for they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, "It is the bread the LORD has given you to eat." [Footnote: The Hebrew words behind "What is it?" sound like the name manna given in verse 31.]
[Exodus] [16]:[16] This is what the LORD has commanded: Each of you is to gather as much as you need—an omer for every person in your tent."
[Exodus] [16]:[17] The Israelites did so, and some gathered much, some little.
[Exodus] [16]:[18] But when they measured it by the omer, the one who gathered much had nothing left over, and the one who gathered little had no lack. Each had gathered as much as he needed.
[Exodus] [16]:[19] Then Moses said to them, "No one is to keep any of it until morning."
[Exodus] [16]:[20] But some paid no attention to Moses; they kept part of it until morning, and it was full of maggots and began to stink. So Moses was angry with them.
[Exodus] [16]:[21] Morning by morning they gathered it, each as much as he needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.
[Exodus] [16]:[22] On the sixth day they gathered twice as much—two omers for each person—and the leaders of the community came and reported it to Moses.
[Exodus] [16]:[23] He said to them, "This is what the LORD has said: Tomorrow is to be a day of rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you want to bake and boil what you want to boil, and save what is left, keeping it until morning."
[Exodus] [16]:[24] So they saved it until morning, as Moses commanded, and it did not stink or get maggots in it.
[Exodus] [16]:[25] "Eat it today," Moses said, "because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. Today you will not find any of it in the field.
[Exodus] [16]:[26] Six days you are to gather it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will be none."
[Exodus] [16]:[27] Even so, some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather it, but they found nothing.
[Exodus] [16]:[28] Then the LORD said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to keep my commands and my instructions?
[Exodus] [16]:[29] Understand that the LORD has given you the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. Everyone is to stay where he is on the seventh day; no one is to leave his place."
[Exodus] [16]:[30] So the people rested on the seventh day.
[Exodus] [16]:[31] The house of Israel called it manna. It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.
[Exodus] [16]:[32] Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded: Take a full omer of it and keep it for the generations to come, so they can see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of Egypt."
[Exodus] [16]:[33] So Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar and put a full omer of manna in it. Then place it before the LORD, to be kept for the generations to come."
[Exodus] [16]:[34] So Aaron placed it before the testimony, to be kept, as the LORD commanded Moses. [Footnote: That is, before the tablets of the covenant, which were kept in the ark.]
[Exodus] [16]:[35] The Israelites ate manna forty years, until they came to a land where people lived; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan.
[Exodus] [16]:[36] An omer is a tenth of an ephah.
[Exodus] [17]:[1] The whole community of Israel set out from the wilderness of Sin, traveling by stages at the LORD's command, and camped at Rephidim. But there was no water for the people to drink.
[Exodus] [17]:[2] So the people quarreled with Moses and said, "Give us water to drink!" Moses answered them, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you put the LORD to the test?"
[Exodus] [17]:[3] But the people were thirsty for water there, and they grumbled against Moses. "Why did you ever bring us up out of Egypt," they said, "to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?"
[Exodus] [17]:[4] Then Moses cried out to the LORD, "What am I to do with this people? A little more and they will stone me."
[Exodus] [17]:[5] The LORD said to Moses, "Go on ahead of the people. Take some of the elders of Israel with you, and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
[Exodus] [17]:[6] I will be standing there before you on the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it for the people to drink." So Moses did this in the sight of the elders of Israel.
[Exodus] [17]:[7] He named the place Massah and Meribah, because the Israelites quarreled there and because they tested the LORD, saying, "Is the LORD among us or not?"
[Exodus] [17]:[8] Then the Amalekites came and fought against Israel at Rephidim.
[Exodus] [17]:[9] Moses said to Joshua, "Choose men for us and go out to fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand."
[Exodus] [17]:[10] Joshua did as Moses had told him and fought against Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
[Exodus] [17]:[11] As long as Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; but whenever he let his hand down, Amalek prevailed.
[Exodus] [17]:[12] When Moses' hands grew heavy, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on each side, so that his hands remained steady until sunset.
[Exodus] [17]:[13] So Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
[Exodus] [17]:[14] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write this down in a book as a reminder, and make sure Joshua hears it: I will completely blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven."
[Exodus] [17]:[15] Moses built an altar and named it "The LORD Is My Banner."
[Exodus] [17]:[16] He said, "A hand upon the throne of the LORD! The LORD will be at war against Amalek from generation to generation."
[Exodus] [18]:[1] Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses' father-in-law, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel his people, how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
[Exodus] [18]:[2] So Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses' wife, after Moses had sent her home,
[Exodus] [18]:[3] along with her two sons. One was named Gershom, for Moses had said, "I have been a stranger in a foreign land,"
[Exodus] [18]:[4] and the other Eliezer, for he said, "The God of my father was my help; he rescued me from Pharaoh's sword."
[Exodus] [18]:[5] Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with Moses' sons and his wife to Moses in the wilderness, where he was camped at the mountain of God.
[Exodus] [18]:[6] He sent word to Moses: "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, and your wife with her two sons."
[Exodus] [18]:[7] Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, bowed down, and kissed him. They greeted each other warmly and then went into the tent.
[Exodus] [18]:[8] Moses told his father-in-law everything the LORD had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel's sake, and about all the hardships they had met along the way, and how the LORD had delivered them.
[Exodus] [18]:[9] Jethro rejoiced over all the good the LORD had done for Israel in rescuing them from the hand of the Egyptians.
[Exodus] [18]:[10] And Jethro said, "Blessed be the LORD, who rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of Pharaoh, who delivered the people from under Egypt's hand.
[Exodus] [18]:[11] Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods, for he acted against those who dealt so arrogantly with them." [Footnote: The end of this verse is difficult in Hebrew; it reads literally "for in the matter in which they acted arrogantly against them."]
[Exodus] [18]:[12] Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law in the presence of God.
[Exodus] [18]:[13] The next day Moses took his seat to judge the people, and they stood around him from morning until evening.
[Exodus] [18]:[14] When Moses' father-in-law saw everything he was doing for the people, he said, "What is this you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, with all the people standing around you from morning till evening?"
[Exodus] [18]:[15] Moses answered his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to inquire of God.
[Exodus] [18]:[16] Whenever they have a dispute, it comes to me, and I decide between one person and another, and I make known God's statutes and his laws."
[Exodus] [18]:[17] Moses' father-in-law said to him, "What you are doing is not good.
[Exodus] [18]:[18] You will wear yourself out, and these people with you, for the task is too heavy for you. You cannot do it alone.
[Exodus] [18]:[19] Now listen to me, and let me give you advice, and may God be with you. You represent the people before God and bring their cases to him.
[Exodus] [18]:[20] Teach them the statutes and the laws, and show them the way they are to walk and what they are to do.
[Exodus] [18]:[21] And you are to look out from all the people for capable men who fear God, trustworthy men who hate a bribe, and appoint them over the people as officers over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
[Exodus] [18]:[22] Let them judge the people at all times. Every major case they shall bring to you, but every minor case they shall decide themselves. So lighten your load and let them carry it with you.
[Exodus] [18]:[23] If you do this, and God so commands you, then you will be able to endure, and all these people will go home in peace."
[Exodus] [18]:[24] Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he said.
[Exodus] [18]:[25] He chose capable men from all Israel and made them heads over the people: officers over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
[Exodus] [18]:[26] They judged the people at all times. The difficult cases they brought to Moses, but every minor case they decided themselves.
[Exodus] [18]:[27] Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and he returned to his own land.
[Exodus] [19]:[1] In the third month after the Israelites left the land of Egypt, on that very day, they came to the wilderness of Sinai.
[Exodus] [19]:[2] They set out from Rephidim, entered the wilderness of Sinai, and camped in the wilderness; there Israel camped in front of the mountain.
[Exodus] [19]:[3] Then Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain: "This is what you are to say to the house of Jacob and tell the Israelites:
[Exodus] [19]:[4] 'You have seen for yourselves what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.
[Exodus] [19]:[5] Now then, if you will listen closely to my voice and keep my covenant, you will be my treasured possession out of all the peoples—for the whole earth is mine—
[Exodus] [19]:[6] and you will be for me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.' These are the words you are to speak to the Israelites."
[Exodus] [19]:[7] So Moses went and summoned the elders of the people and set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
[Exodus] [19]:[8] And all the people answered together, "Everything the LORD has spoken, we will do." And Moses brought the people's words back to the LORD.
[Exodus] [19]:[9] The LORD said to Moses, "Look, I am coming to you in a dense cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you and may always put their trust in you as well." Then Moses told the LORD what the people had said.
[Exodus] [19]:[10] The LORD said to Moses, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. Have them wash their garments,
[Exodus] [19]:[11] and be ready for the third day, because on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
[Exodus] [19]:[12] Set limits for the people all around, and say: 'Be careful not to go up the mountain or touch its edge. Whoever touches the mountain must surely be put to death.
[Exodus] [19]:[13] No hand shall touch him; he must be stoned or shot with arrows. Whether animal or human, he shall not live.' Only when the ram's horn sounds a long blast may they go up the mountain."
[Exodus] [19]:[14] Moses came down from the mountain to the people, consecrated them, and they washed their garments.
[Exodus] [19]:[15] He said to the people, "Be ready in three days; do not go near a woman."
[Exodus] [19]:[16] On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning, a thick cloud over the mountain, and a very loud blast of a horn. Everyone in the camp trembled.
[Exodus] [19]:[17] Then Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God, and they took their stand at the foot of the mountain.
[Exodus] [19]:[18] Mount Sinai was completely wrapped in smoke, because the LORD had come down on it in fire. Its smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain shook violently.
[Exodus] [19]:[19] As the sound of the horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice.
[Exodus] [19]:[20] The LORD came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain, and called Moses up to the top. So Moses went up.
[Exodus] [19]:[21] The LORD said to Moses, "Go down and warn the people not to break through to the LORD to look, or many of them will perish.
[Exodus] [19]:[22] Even the priests who come near the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them."
[Exodus] [19]:[23] Moses said to the LORD, "The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for you yourself warned us, saying, 'Set limits around the mountain and consecrate it.'"
[Exodus] [19]:[24] The LORD said to him, "Go down, and come up again, you and Aaron with you. But the priests and the people must not break through to come up to the LORD, or he will break out against them."
[Exodus] [19]:[25] So Moses went down to the people and told them.
[Exodus] [20]:[1] Then God spoke all these words:
[Exodus] [20]:[2] "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
[Exodus] [20]:[3] You shall have no other gods before me.
[Exodus] [20]:[4] You shall not make for yourself an idol, or any image of anything in the heavens above, or on the earth below, or in the waters under the earth.
[Exodus] [20]:[5] You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the guilt of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,
[Exodus] [20]:[6] but showing steadfast love to a thousand generations of those who love me and keep my commandments.
[Exodus] [20]:[7] You shall not misuse the name of the LORD your God, for the LORD will not hold guiltless anyone who misuses his name.
[Exodus] [20]:[8] Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy.
[Exodus] [20]:[9] Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
[Exodus] [20]:[10] but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you shall not do any work—you, your son or your daughter, your male or female servant, your livestock, or the foreigner residing within your gates.
[Exodus] [20]:[11] For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea and everything in them, but he rested on the seventh day. That is why the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
[Exodus] [20]:[12] Honor your father and your mother, so that you may live long in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
[Exodus] [20]:[13] You shall not murder.
[Exodus] [20]:[14] You shall not commit adultery.
[Exodus] [20]:[15] You shall not steal.
[Exodus] [20]:[16] You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.
[Exodus] [20]:[17] You shall not covet your neighbor's house. You shall not covet your neighbor's wife, or his male or female servant, his ox or his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor."
[Exodus] [20]:[18] All the people witnessed the thunder and the flashes of lightning, the blast of the trumpet, and the mountain wrapped in smoke. And when the people saw it, they trembled and stood far off.
[Exodus] [20]:[19] They said to Moses, "Speak to us yourself and we will listen. But do not let God speak to us, or we will die."
[Exodus] [20]:[20] Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid. God has come to test you, so that the fear of him will be with you and keep you from sinning."
[Exodus] [20]:[21] The people remained at a distance while Moses approached the thick darkness where God was.
[Exodus] [20]:[22] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Say this to the Israelites: You have seen for yourselves that I have spoken to you from heaven.
[Exodus] [20]:[23] You shall not make gods of silver to be alongside me, nor shall you make for yourselves gods of gold.
[Exodus] [20]:[24] Make an altar of earth for me, and on it sacrifice your burnt offerings and your fellowship offerings, your sheep and your cattle. Wherever I cause my name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
[Exodus] [20]:[25] If you make an altar of stones for me, do not build it with cut stones, for if you use a chisel on it, you will defile it.
[Exodus] [20]:[26] And do not go up to my altar on steps, so that your nakedness is not exposed on it."
[Exodus] [21]:[1] These are the ordinances you are to set before them:
[Exodus] [21]:[2] When you buy a Hebrew slave, he shall serve six years, and in the seventh he shall go free without payment.
[Exodus] [21]:[3] If he came alone, he shall go out alone; if he was married, his wife shall go out with him.
[Exodus] [21]:[4] If his master gave him a wife and she bore him sons or daughters, the wife and her children belong to her master, and he shall go out alone.
[Exodus] [21]:[5] But if the slave declares, "I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go free,"
[Exodus] [21]:[6] then his master shall bring him before God.[^1] [^1]: Or 'before the judges'; the Hebrew word can refer to God or to those who act as judges on his behalf.
[Exodus] [21]:[7] When a man sells his daughter as a slave, she shall not go free as male slaves do.
[Exodus] [21]:[8] If she does not please the master who designated her for himself, he shall let her be redeemed. He has no right to sell her to a foreign people, since he has broken faith with her.
[Exodus] [21]:[9] If he designates her for his son, he shall treat her according to the rights of daughters.
[Exodus] [21]:[10] If he takes another wife, he must not reduce the food, clothing, or marital rights of the first.
[Exodus] [21]:[11] And if he does not provide these three things for her, she shall go free without payment.
[Exodus] [21]:[12] Whoever strikes a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death.
[Exodus] [21]:[13] But if he did not lie in wait, and God let it happen by his hand, then I will appoint a place where he may flee.
[Exodus] [21]:[14] But if a man schemes against his neighbor to kill him by treachery, you shall take him even from my altar to be put to death.
[Exodus] [21]:[15] Whoever strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
[Exodus] [21]:[16] Whoever kidnaps a man—whether he sells him or the man is found in his possession—shall surely be put to death.
[Exodus] [21]:[17] Whoever curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
[Exodus] [21]:[18] If men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or with his fist, and the man does not die but is confined to bed,
[Exodus] [21]:[19] then if he gets up and walks outside with his staff, the one who struck him is not to be punished. He must only pay for his lost time and see that he is fully healed.
[Exodus] [21]:[20] If a man beats his male or female slave with a rod and the slave dies at his hand, he shall surely be punished.
[Exodus] [21]:[21] But if the slave survives a day or two, the owner is not to be punished, for the slave is his property.
[Exodus] [21]:[22] If men are fighting and they strike a pregnant woman so that she gives birth prematurely, but there is no serious injury, the offender shall be fined whatever the woman's husband demands and the judges allow.
[Exodus] [21]:[23] But if there is serious injury, you shall give life for life,
[Exodus] [21]:[24] eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
[Exodus] [21]:[25] burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
[Exodus] [21]:[26] If a man strikes the eye of his male or female slave and destroys it, he shall set the slave free in compensation for the eye.
[Exodus] [21]:[27] And if he knocks out the tooth of his male or female slave, he shall set the slave free in compensation for the tooth.
[Exodus] [21]:[28] If an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox shall be stoned and its flesh shall not be eaten, but the owner of the ox is not liable.
[Exodus] [21]:[29] But if the ox has been in the habit of goring and its owner has been warned yet did not keep it penned up, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned and its owner also shall be put to death.
[Exodus] [21]:[30] If a ransom is imposed on him, he shall pay whatever is imposed to redeem his life.
[Exodus] [21]:[31] If the ox gores a son or a daughter, the same rule applies.
[Exodus] [21]:[32] If the ox gores a male or female slave, the owner shall pay thirty shekels of silver to the slave's master, and the ox shall be stoned.
[Exodus] [21]:[33] If a man opens a pit, or digs one and fails to cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
[Exodus] [21]:[34] the owner of the pit shall make restitution; he shall pay the animal's owner in silver, and the dead animal shall be his.
[Exodus] [21]:[35] If one man's ox injures another's so that it dies, they shall sell the live ox and divide the money, and they shall also divide the dead animal.
[Exodus] [21]:[36] But if it was known that the ox had been in the habit of goring and its owner did not keep it penned up, he must make restitution, ox for ox, and the dead animal shall be his.
[Exodus] [21]:[37] If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he shall repay five head of cattle for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.
[Exodus] [22]:[1] If a thief is caught breaking in and is struck so that he dies, there is no bloodguilt for him.
[Exodus] [22]:[2] But if the sun has risen on him, there is bloodguilt. The thief must make full restitution; if he has nothing, he shall be sold to pay for his theft.
[Exodus] [22]:[3] If what he stole is found alive in his possession, whether ox or donkey or sheep, he shall pay back double.
[Exodus] [22]:[4] If a man puts his livestock into a field or a vineyard, and lets them loose so that they feed in another man's field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.
[Exodus] [22]:[5] If a fire breaks out and spreads through thornbushes, so that stacked grain or standing grain or a whole field is consumed, the one who started the fire shall make full restitution.
[Exodus] [22]:[6] If a man gives his neighbor silver or goods for safekeeping, and they are stolen from the man's house, then if the thief is found, he shall pay back double.
[Exodus] [22]:[7] If the thief is not found, the owner of the house shall be brought before God, to determine whether he has laid his hand on his neighbor's property. [Footnote: Or 'before the judges'; the Hebrew word can refer to God or to those who judge in his name.]
[Exodus] [22]:[8] In every case of dishonesty, whether it concerns an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost item that someone claims as his own, the case of both parties shall come before God. The one whom God declares guilty shall pay back double to his neighbor.
[Exodus] [22]:[9] If a man gives his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal for safekeeping, and it dies or is injured or is driven off with no one to see it,
[Exodus] [22]:[10] an oath before the LORD shall settle the matter between them, that he has not laid his hand on his neighbor's property. The owner shall accept this, and no restitution shall be made.
[Exodus] [22]:[11] But if it was in fact stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.
[Exodus] [22]:[12] If it was torn by wild animals, let him bring the remains as evidence; he need not pay for what was torn.
[Exodus] [22]:[13] If a man borrows an animal from his neighbor, and it is injured or dies while its owner is not present, he shall make full restitution.
[Exodus] [22]:[14] If the owner was present, no restitution shall be made. If the animal was hired, the loss is covered by the hiring fee.
[Exodus] [22]:[15] If a man seduces a virgin who is not engaged and lies with her, he must pay the bride-price and take her as his wife.
[Exodus] [22]:[16] If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he must still weigh out silver equal to the bride-price for virgins.
[Exodus] [22]:[17] You shall not let a sorceress live.
[Exodus] [22]:[18] Whoever lies with an animal shall surely be put to death.
[Exodus] [22]:[19] Whoever sacrifices to any god other than the LORD alone shall be devoted to destruction.
[Exodus] [22]:[20] You shall not wrong a foreigner or oppress him, for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [22]:[21] You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan.
[Exodus] [22]:[22] If you do mistreat them, and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry.
[Exodus] [22]:[23] My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword; your wives will become widows and your children fatherless.
[Exodus] [22]:[24] If you lend money to my people, to the poor among you, do not act as a creditor toward them; you shall not charge them interest.
[Exodus] [22]:[25] If you take your neighbor's cloak as a pledge, return it to him before the sun goes down,
[Exodus] [22]:[26] for it is his only covering, the garment for his body. What else does he have to sleep in? And when he cries out to me, I will hear, for I am compassionate.
[Exodus] [22]:[27] You shall not revile God, nor curse a leader of your people.
[Exodus] [22]:[28] Do not hold back the offering from your harvest or your winepress. The firstborn of your sons you shall give to me.
[Exodus] [22]:[29] Do the same with your cattle and your sheep: seven days the newborn shall stay with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to me.
[Exodus] [22]:[30] You shall be holy people to me. You shall not eat the meat of an animal torn by beasts in the field; throw it to the dogs.
[Exodus] [23]:[1] Do not spread a false report. Do not join hands with the guilty by giving malicious testimony.
[Exodus] [23]:[2] Do not follow the crowd in doing wrong. When you testify in a lawsuit, do not side with the majority and so pervert justice.
[Exodus] [23]:[3] And do not show favoritism to the poor in his lawsuit.
[Exodus] [23]:[4] If you come across your enemy's ox or donkey wandering off, be sure to take it back to him.
[Exodus] [23]:[5] If you see the donkey of someone who hates you collapsed under its load, do not leave it there; help him get it to its feet.
[Exodus] [23]:[6] Do not deny justice to the poor among you in their lawsuits.
[Exodus] [23]:[7] Keep far from a false charge. Do not put the innocent and the righteous to death, for I will not acquit the guilty.
[Exodus] [23]:[8] Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.
[Exodus] [23]:[9] Do not oppress a foreigner. You know how it feels to be a foreigner, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [23]:[10] For six years you shall sow your land and gather in its harvest.
[Exodus] [23]:[11] But in the seventh year let it rest and lie unused, so that the poor among your people may eat from it, and what they leave the wild animals may eat. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
[Exodus] [23]:[12] Six days you shall do your work, but on the seventh day you shall rest, so that your ox and your donkey may rest and the son of your slave woman and the foreigner may be refreshed.
[Exodus] [23]:[13] Be careful to keep everything I have said to you. Do not invoke the names of other gods; do not let them be heard on your lips.
[Exodus] [23]:[14] Three times a year you shall hold a festival to me.
[Exodus] [23]:[15] Keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread: for seven days eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in that month you came out of Egypt. No one is to appear before me empty-handed.
[Exodus] [23]:[16] Then keep the Festival of Harvest with the firstfruits of your labor, of what you sow in the field. And keep the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather in the fruit of your labor from the field.
[Exodus] [23]:[17] Three times a year all your men are to appear before the Sovereign LORD.
[Exodus] [23]:[18] Do not offer the blood of my sacrifice along with anything leavened, and do not let the fat of my festival offering remain until morning.
[Exodus] [23]:[19] Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
[Exodus] [23]:[20] See, I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.
[Exodus] [23]:[21] Pay attention to him and listen to his voice. Do not rebel against him, for he will not forgive your rebellion, since my name is in him.
[Exodus] [23]:[22] But if you listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and oppose those who oppose you.
[Exodus] [23]:[23] For my angel will go ahead of you and bring you into the land of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
[Exodus] [23]:[24] Do not bow down to their gods or worship them or follow their practices. You must utterly destroy their idols and smash their sacred stones to pieces.
[Exodus] [23]:[25] Serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and your water. I will take away sickness from among you,
[Exodus] [23]:[26] and none in your land will miscarry or be barren. I will give you a full span of life.
[Exodus] [23]:[27] I will send my terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every nation you encounter. I will make all your enemies turn their backs and flee.
[Exodus] [23]:[28] I will send hornets ahead of you to drive the Hivites, the Canaanites and the Hittites out of your way.
[Exodus] [23]:[29] But I will not drive them out in a single year, or the land would become desolate and the wild animals too numerous for you.
[Exodus] [23]:[30] Little by little I will drive them out before you, until you have increased enough to take possession of the land.
[Exodus] [23]:[31] I will establish your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the desert to the Euphrates River. I will give the inhabitants of the land into your hands, and you will drive them out before you.
[Exodus] [23]:[32] Do not make a covenant with them or with their gods.
[Exodus] [23]:[33] They must not live in your land, or they will cause you to sin against me. If you serve their gods, it will certainly become a snare to you.
[Exodus] [24]:[1] Now the LORD said to Moses, "Come up to the LORD—you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel's elders—and bow down at a distance.
[Exodus] [24]:[2] Moses alone shall approach the LORD; the others shall not come near, and the people shall not come up with him."
[Exodus] [24]:[3] Moses came and told the people all the words of the LORD and all the ordinances, and with one voice all the people answered, "Everything the LORD has spoken we will do."
[Exodus] [24]:[4] So Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. Early the next morning he built an altar at the foot of the mountain, with twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
[Exodus] [24]:[5] He sent young men of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed bulls as fellowship offerings to the LORD.
[Exodus] [24]:[6] Moses took half of the blood and put it in basins, and the other half he threw against the altar.
[Exodus] [24]:[7] Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it aloud to the people, and they said, "Everything the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will obey."
[Exodus] [24]:[8] Moses took the blood, scattered it over the people, and said, "This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you in accordance with all these words."
[Exodus] [24]:[9] Then Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel's elders,
[Exodus] [24]:[10] and they saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something like a pavement of sapphire, clear as the sky itself.
[Exodus] [24]:[11] But he did not raise his hand against the leaders of the Israelites; they beheld God, and they ate and drank.
[Exodus] [24]:[12] The LORD said to Moses, "Come up to me on the mountain and stay there, and I will give you the stone tablets with the law and the commandments I have written for their instruction."
[Exodus] [24]:[13] So Moses set out with Joshua his assistant, and Moses went up on the mountain of God.
[Exodus] [24]:[14] He said to the elders, "Wait here for us until we come back to you. Aaron and Hur are with you; whoever has a dispute can go to them."
[Exodus] [24]:[15] When Moses went up on the mountain, the cloud covered it,
[Exodus] [24]:[16] and the glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai. For six days the cloud covered the mountain, and on the seventh day the LORD called to Moses from within the cloud.
[Exodus] [24]:[17] To the eyes of the Israelites the glory of the LORD looked like a consuming fire on the mountaintop.
[Exodus] [24]:[18] Moses entered the cloud as he went up the mountain, and he stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
[Exodus] [25]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Exodus] [25]:[2] Tell the Israelites to take up an offering for me. You are to receive my offering from everyone whose heart moves him to give.
[Exodus] [25]:[3] This is the offering you are to receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
[Exodus] [25]:[4] blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goat hair;
[Exodus] [25]:[5] ram skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
[Exodus] [25]:[6] oil for the lamps, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
[Exodus] [25]:[7] onyx stones and other stones to be set in the ephod and the breastpiece.
[Exodus] [25]:[8] Have them make a sanctuary for me, and I will dwell among them.
[Exodus] [25]:[9] Make it exactly according to everything I show you—the pattern of the dwelling and the pattern of all its furnishings.
[Exodus] [25]:[10] They are to make an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
[Exodus] [25]:[11] Overlay it with pure gold, inside and out, and make a gold molding around it.
[Exodus] [25]:[12] Cast four gold rings for it and fasten them to its four feet, two rings on one side and two on the other.
[Exodus] [25]:[13] Make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
[Exodus] [25]:[14] Insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, so the ark can be carried with them.
[Exodus] [25]:[15] The poles are to remain in the rings of the ark; they must not be removed.
[Exodus] [25]:[16] Then place in the ark the testimony that I will give you.
[Exodus] [25]:[17] Make an atonement cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
[Exodus] [25]:[18] Make two cherubim of hammered gold at the two ends of the cover.
[Exodus] [25]:[19] Make one cherub at one end and the second at the other end; make the cherubim of one piece with the cover, at its two ends.
[Exodus] [25]:[20] The cherubim are to have their wings spread upward, overshadowing the cover with them. They are to face each other, looking toward the cover.
[Exodus] [25]:[21] Place the cover on top of the ark, and put in the ark the testimony that I will give you.
[Exodus] [25]:[22] There I will meet with you, and from above the cover, from between the two cherubim over the ark of the testimony, I will speak with you about everything I command you concerning the Israelites.
[Exodus] [25]:[23] Make a table of acacia wood, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
[Exodus] [25]:[24] Overlay it with pure gold and make a gold molding around it.
[Exodus] [25]:[25] Make a rim a handbreadth wide around it, with a gold molding around the rim.
[Exodus] [25]:[26] Make four gold rings for the table and fasten them to the four corners, where the four legs are.
[Exodus] [25]:[27] The rings are to be close to the rim, to hold the poles for carrying the table.
[Exodus] [25]:[28] Make the poles of acacia wood, overlay them with gold, and use them to carry the table.
[Exodus] [25]:[29] Make its plates and dishes, its pitchers and its bowls for pouring drink offerings; make them all of pure gold.
[Exodus] [25]:[30] And set the bread of the Presence on the table before me at all times.
[Exodus] [25]:[31] Make a lampstand of pure gold. The lampstand is to be hammered out of one piece—its base and shaft, its cups, buds, and blossoms all of one piece with it.
[Exodus] [25]:[32] Six branches are to extend from its sides, three on one side and three on the other.
[Exodus] [25]:[33] Three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with bud and blossom, are to be on one branch, and three on the next branch—the same for all six branches extending from the lampstand.
[Exodus] [25]:[34] On the lampstand itself there are to be four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their buds and blossoms.
[Exodus] [25]:[35] A bud is to be under the first pair of branches extending from it, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair—for all six branches extending from the lampstand.
[Exodus] [25]:[36] The buds and branches are to be of one piece with the lampstand—all of it one hammered work of pure gold.
[Exodus] [25]:[37] Make its seven lamps and set them up so that they light the space in front of it.
[Exodus] [25]:[38] Its wick trimmers and trays are to be of pure gold.
[Exodus] [25]:[39] A talent of pure gold is to be used for the lampstand and all these utensils.
[Exodus] [25]:[40] See that you make them according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.
[Exodus] [26]:[1] Make the tabernacle of ten curtains of finely twisted linen, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with cherubim worked into them by a skilled craftsman.
[Exodus] [26]:[2] Each curtain is to be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide; all the curtains are to be the same size.
[Exodus] [26]:[3] Five curtains are to be joined together into one set, and the other five joined together into a second set.
[Exodus] [26]:[4] Make loops of blue yarn along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and do the same along the edge of the end curtain in the second set.
[Exodus] [26]:[5] Make fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, with the loops opposite one another.
[Exodus] [26]:[6] Then make fifty gold clasps and join the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle is a single whole.
[Exodus] [26]:[7] Make curtains of goat hair for a tent over the tabernacle — eleven curtains in all.
[Exodus] [26]:[8] Each curtain is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide; all eleven curtains are to be the same size.
[Exodus] [26]:[9] Join five of the curtains into one set and the other six into another, and fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.
[Exodus] [26]:[10] Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the one set and fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the other set.
[Exodus] [26]:[11] Then make fifty bronze clasps, put them through the loops, and join the tent together so that it is a single whole.
[Exodus] [26]:[12] The extra length of the tent curtains — the half curtain that is left over — is to hang down over the back of the tabernacle.
[Exodus] [26]:[13] The extra cubit on each side, from the length of the tent curtains, is to hang over the sides of the tabernacle, on one side and the other, to cover it.
[Exodus] [26]:[14] Make for the tent a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
[Exodus] [26]:[15] Make upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
[Exodus] [26]:[16] Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide,
[Exodus] [26]:[17] with two tenons set parallel to each other. Make all the frames of the tabernacle this way.
[Exodus] [26]:[18] Make the frames for the tabernacle: twenty frames for the south side,
[Exodus] [26]:[19] and forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames — two bases under each frame, one for each of its two tenons.
[Exodus] [26]:[20] For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, make twenty frames
[Exodus] [26]:[21] and forty silver bases — two under each frame.
[Exodus] [26]:[22] For the rear of the tabernacle, on the west, make six frames,
[Exodus] [26]:[23] and make two frames for the corners at the rear.
[Exodus] [26]:[24] They are to be doubled at the bottom and joined together at the top, fitted into a single ring. Both corner frames are to be made this way.
[Exodus] [26]:[25] So there will be eight frames with their silver bases — sixteen bases, two under each frame.
[Exodus] [26]:[26] Make crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,
[Exodus] [26]:[27] five for the frames on the other side, and five for the frames at the rear of the tabernacle, on the west.
[Exodus] [26]:[28] The middle crossbar, halfway up the frames, is to run from end to end.
[Exodus] [26]:[29] Overlay the frames with gold, and make gold rings to hold the crossbars; overlay the crossbars with gold as well.
[Exodus] [26]:[30] Set up the tabernacle according to the plan you were shown on the mountain.
[Exodus] [26]:[31] Make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it by a skilled craftsman.
[Exodus] [26]:[32] Hang it on four posts of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with gold hooks, standing on four silver bases.
[Exodus] [26]:[33] Hang the curtain beneath the clasps, and bring the ark of the testimony in there, behind the curtain. The curtain will separate for you the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
[Exodus] [26]:[34] Place the mercy seat on the ark of the testimony in the Most Holy Place.
[Exodus] [26]:[35] Set the table outside the curtain, and the lampstand opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle; put the table on the north side.
[Exodus] [26]:[36] For the entrance to the tent make a screen of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.
[Exodus] [26]:[37] Make five posts of acacia wood for the screen and overlay them with gold, with gold hooks, and cast five bronze bases for them.
[Exodus] [27]:[1] Make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide. The altar shall be square, and three cubits high.
[Exodus] [27]:[2] Make horns for it on its four corners; the horns shall be of one piece with it, and overlay it with bronze.
[Exodus] [27]:[3] Make its pots for removing the ashes, and its shovels, its basins, its forks, and its firepans. Make all its utensils of bronze.
[Exodus] [27]:[4] Make a grating for it of bronze network, and on the network make four bronze rings at its four corners.
[Exodus] [27]:[5] Set it under the ledge of the altar, so that the network reaches halfway up the altar.
[Exodus] [27]:[6] Make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
[Exodus] [27]:[7] The poles are to be inserted into the rings, so that they are along the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
[Exodus] [27]:[8] Make the altar hollow, of boards. They shall make it just as you were shown on the mountain.
[Exodus] [27]:[9] Make the courtyard of the tabernacle. On the south side the courtyard shall have curtains of finely twisted linen, a hundred cubits long on that side,
[Exodus] [27]:[10] with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases. The hooks of the posts and their bands shall be of silver.
[Exodus] [27]:[11] Likewise along the north side there shall be curtains a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases; the hooks of the posts and their bands shall be of silver.
[Exodus] [27]:[12] For the width of the courtyard on the west side there shall be curtains fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases.
[Exodus] [27]:[13] The width of the courtyard on the east side shall be fifty cubits.
[Exodus] [27]:[14] On one side of the entrance there shall be curtains fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases,
[Exodus] [27]:[15] and on the other side curtains fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
[Exodus] [27]:[16] For the gate of the courtyard there shall be a screen twenty cubits long, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer, with four posts and four bases.
[Exodus] [27]:[17] All the posts around the courtyard shall have silver bands, silver hooks, and bronze bases.
[Exodus] [27]:[18] The courtyard shall be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide throughout, with curtains of finely twisted linen five cubits high, and bronze bases.
[Exodus] [27]:[19] All the equipment used in the service of the tabernacle, and all its pegs and all the pegs of the courtyard, shall be of bronze.
[Exodus] [27]:[20] You shall command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, so that the lamp may be kept burning continually.
[Exodus] [27]:[21] In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall tend it before the LORD from evening until morning. This shall be a lasting statute for their generations, binding on the Israelites.
[Exodus] [28]:[1] Now bring near to yourself your brother Aaron, and his sons with him, from among the Israelites, to serve me as priests: Aaron, and Aaron's sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
[Exodus] [28]:[2] Make holy garments for your brother Aaron, for glory and for beauty.
[Exodus] [28]:[3] Speak to all the skilled craftsmen whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, and have them make Aaron's garments, to consecrate him for service to me as priest.
[Exodus] [28]:[4] These are the garments they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban, and a sash. They shall make these holy garments for your brother Aaron and for his sons, so that they may serve me as priests.
[Exodus] [28]:[5] They shall use gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
[Exodus] [28]:[6] They shall make the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen, skillfully worked.
[Exodus] [28]:[7] It shall have two shoulder pieces attached to its two ends, so that it is joined together.
[Exodus] [28]:[8] Its woven waistband shall be of one piece with it and made like it: of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
[Exodus] [28]:[9] Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:
[Exodus] [28]:[10] six of their names on the one stone, and the remaining six names on the other stone, in the order of their birth.
[Exodus] [28]:[11] With the work of a gem cutter, as a seal is engraved, engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel, and mount them in settings of gold filigree.
[Exodus] [28]:[12] Fasten the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel. So Aaron will carry their names on his two shoulders before the LORD as a remembrance.
[Exodus] [28]:[13] Make settings of gold filigree,
[Exodus] [28]:[14] and two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords, and attach the corded chains to the settings.
[Exodus] [28]:[15] Make the breastpiece of judgment, skillfully worked, like the work of the ephod: of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
[Exodus] [28]:[16] It shall be square and folded double, a span long and a span wide.
[Exodus] [28]:[17] Set in it four rows of precious stones. The first row shall be carnelian, chrysolite, and emerald;
[Exodus] [28]:[18] the second row, turquoise, sapphire, and diamond;
[Exodus] [28]:[19] the third row, jacinth, agate, and amethyst;
[Exodus] [28]:[20] the fourth row, topaz, onyx, and jasper. They shall be mounted in gold filigree.
[Exodus] [28]:[21] There shall be twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
[Exodus] [28]:[22] For the breastpiece make chains of pure gold, twisted like cords.
[Exodus] [28]:[23] Make two gold rings for the breastpiece and fasten them to its two upper corners.
[Exodus] [28]:[24] Fasten the two gold cords to the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
[Exodus] [28]:[25] and fasten the other two ends of the cords to the two settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
[Exodus] [28]:[26] Make two more gold rings and attach them to the two lower corners of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
[Exodus] [28]:[27] Make two more gold rings and attach them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod on the front, close to the seam just above the woven waistband of the ephod.
[Exodus] [28]:[28] The breastpiece is to be bound to the ephod with a blue cord, ring to ring, so that it rests on the waistband and does not swing loose from the ephod.
[Exodus] [28]:[29] So whenever Aaron enters the Holy Place, he will carry the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the breastpiece of judgment, as a continual remembrance before the LORD.
[Exodus] [28]:[30] Also put the Urim and the Thummim in the breastpiece of judgment, so that they will be over Aaron's heart whenever he comes before the LORD. Thus Aaron will always carry the judgment of the Israelites over his heart before the LORD.
[Exodus] [28]:[31] Make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth,
[Exodus] [28]:[32] with an opening for the head in the center of it. Around this opening there shall be a woven binding, like the opening of a coat of armor, so that it will not tear.
[Exodus] [28]:[33] On its hem make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn all around, with gold bells between them,
[Exodus] [28]:[34] a gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe.
[Exodus] [28]:[35] Aaron is to wear it whenever he ministers, so that the sound of it will be heard as he enters the Holy Place before the LORD and as he leaves, and he will not die.
[Exodus] [28]:[36] Make a medallion of pure gold and engrave on it, as on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
[Exodus] [28]:[37] Fasten it with a blue cord to the turban, at the front of the turban.
[Exodus] [28]:[38] It shall be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron will bear the guilt involved in the holy gifts the Israelites consecrate, whatever their holy offerings may be. It shall be on his forehead continually, so that they may be accepted before the LORD.
[Exodus] [28]:[39] Weave the tunic of fine linen, make the turban of fine linen, and make the sash the work of an embroiderer.
[Exodus] [28]:[40] For Aaron's sons you shall make tunics, and sashes, and caps for them, for glory and for beauty.
[Exodus] [28]:[41] Clothe your brother Aaron and his sons with them. Then anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them, so that they may serve me as priests.
[Exodus] [28]:[42] Make linen undergarments for them to cover their nakedness, reaching from the waist to the thighs.
[Exodus] [28]:[43] Aaron and his sons are to wear them whenever they enter the tent of meeting or approach the altar to minister in the sanctuary, so that they do not bear guilt and die. This shall be a lasting statute for him and for his offspring after him.
[Exodus] [29]:[1] This is what you shall do to consecrate them as priests to serve me: Take one young bull and two rams without blemish,
[Exodus] [29]:[2] along with unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers brushed with oil; make them of fine wheat flour.
[Exodus] [29]:[3] Place them in a single basket and bring them in the basket, together with the bull and the two rams.
[Exodus] [29]:[4] Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
[Exodus] [29]:[5] Take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod itself, and the breastpiece; then fasten the ephod on him with its woven band.
[Exodus] [29]:[6] Set the turban on his head and place the holy crown on the turban.
[Exodus] [29]:[7] Then take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
[Exodus] [29]:[8] Bring his sons forward and clothe them with tunics.
[Exodus] [29]:[9] Gird Aaron and his sons with sashes and bind the headbands on them. The priesthood shall be theirs by a perpetual statute. So you shall ordain Aaron and his sons.
[Exodus] [29]:[10] Bring the bull before the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.
[Exodus] [29]:[11] Slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
[Exodus] [29]:[12] Take some of the bull's blood and put it with your finger on the horns of the altar, and pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.
[Exodus] [29]:[13] Take all the fat that covers the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
[Exodus] [29]:[14] But the flesh of the bull, its hide, and its dung you shall burn with fire outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
[Exodus] [29]:[15] Then take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.
[Exodus] [29]:[16] Slaughter the ram, take its blood, and splash it against the altar on every side.
[Exodus] [29]:[17] Cut the ram into pieces, wash its entrails and legs, and place them with the pieces and the head.
[Exodus] [29]:[18] Then burn the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
[Exodus] [29]:[19] Then take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on its head.
[Exodus] [29]:[20] Slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear and on the lobes of his sons' right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands and on the big toes of their right feet; then splash the blood against the altar on every side.
[Exodus] [29]:[21] Take some of the blood from the altar and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments and on his sons and their garments. So he and his garments, and his sons and their garments, shall be consecrated.
[Exodus] [29]:[22] From the ram take the fat, the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh, for this is the ram of ordination.
[Exodus] [29]:[23] Also take one loaf of bread, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
[Exodus] [29]:[24] Put all of it in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and wave it as a wave offering before the LORD.
[Exodus] [29]:[25] Then take it from their hands and burn it on the altar with the burnt offering, as a pleasing aroma before the LORD; it is a food offering to the LORD.
[Exodus] [29]:[26] Take the breast of Aaron's ram of ordination and wave it as a wave offering before the LORD; it shall be your portion.
[Exodus] [29]:[27] You shall consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution—what was waved and what was lifted up—from the ram of ordination, from what belongs to Aaron and to his sons.
[Exodus] [29]:[28] This shall belong to Aaron and his sons as a perpetual due from the Israelites, for it is a contribution. It is the contribution the Israelites are to give from their fellowship sacrifices, their offering to the LORD.
[Exodus] [29]:[29] The holy garments of Aaron shall pass to his sons after him; in them they shall be anointed and ordained.
[Exodus] [29]:[30] The son who succeeds him as priest and enters the tent of meeting to minister in the sanctuary shall wear them seven days.
[Exodus] [29]:[31] Take the ram of ordination and boil its meat in a holy place.
[Exodus] [29]:[32] At the entrance of the tent of meeting Aaron and his sons shall eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is in the basket.
