[Exodus] [29]:[33] They shall eat the things by which atonement was made, to ordain and consecrate them; but no outsider may eat them, for they are holy.
[Exodus] [29]:[34] If any of the meat of the ordination offering or any of the bread is left over until morning, burn it with fire. It must not be eaten, for it is holy.
[Exodus] [29]:[35] Do this for Aaron and his sons, just as I have commanded you. Take seven days to ordain them.
[Exodus] [29]:[36] Each day offer a bull as a sin offering for atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
[Exodus] [29]:[37] For seven days make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar shall be most holy, and whatever touches it shall become holy.
[Exodus] [29]:[38] This is what you are to offer on the altar continually, day by day: two lambs a year old.
[Exodus] [29]:[39] Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight.
[Exodus] [29]:[40] With the first lamb offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of pressed oil, and a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering.
[Exodus] [29]:[41] Offer the second lamb at twilight with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning—a pleasing aroma, a food offering to the LORD.
[Exodus] [29]:[42] This shall be a regular burnt offering throughout your generations, at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, where I will meet with you and speak to you.
[Exodus] [29]:[43] There I will meet with the Israelites, and the place will be consecrated by my glory.
[Exodus] [29]:[44] So I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar, and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests.
[Exodus] [29]:[45] I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God.
[Exodus] [29]:[46] They will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might dwell among them. I am the LORD their God.
[Exodus] [30]:[1] You shall make an altar for burning incense; make it of acacia wood.
[Exodus] [30]:[2] It shall be a cubit long and a cubit wide—square—and two cubits high, its horns of one piece with it.
[Exodus] [30]:[3] Overlay it with pure gold—its top, its sides all around, and its horns—and make a gold molding around it.
[Exodus] [30]:[4] Make two gold rings for it beneath the molding, on its two opposite sides, to hold the poles used to carry it.
[Exodus] [30]:[5] Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
[Exodus] [30]:[6] Place it in front of the curtain that hangs before the ark of the testimony—before the mercy seat that is over the testimony—where I will meet with you.
[Exodus] [30]:[7] Aaron shall burn fragrant incense on it; every morning, when he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.
[Exodus] [30]:[8] And when Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he shall burn it again—a regular offering of incense before the LORD throughout your generations.
[Exodus] [30]:[9] You shall not offer on it unauthorized incense, or a burnt offering, or a grain offering, and you shall pour no drink offering on it.
[Exodus] [30]:[10] Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on its horns; with the blood of the sin offering of atonement he shall make atonement for it once a year throughout your generations. It is most holy to the LORD.
[Exodus] [30]:[11] The LORD said to Moses:
[Exodus] [30]:[12] "When you take a census of the Israelites to count them, each one shall pay the LORD a ransom for his life when they are counted, so that no plague will come upon them as they are counted.
[Exodus] [30]:[13] This is what everyone included in the census shall give: half a shekel, by the sanctuary shekel—the shekel is twenty gerahs—half a shekel as an offering to the LORD.
[Exodus] [30]:[14] Everyone included in the census, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the LORD's offering.
[Exodus] [30]:[15] The rich shall not give more and the poor shall not give less than half a shekel when you give the LORD's offering to make atonement for your lives.
[Exodus] [30]:[16] Take the atonement money from the Israelites and devote it to the service of the tent of meeting. It shall be a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD, making atonement for your lives."
[Exodus] [30]:[17] The LORD said to Moses:
[Exodus] [30]:[18] "Make a bronze basin with a bronze stand for washing. Set it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
[Exodus] [30]:[19] Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and feet with water from it.
[Exodus] [30]:[20] When they enter the tent of meeting, they shall wash with water so that they do not die; likewise when they approach the altar to minister, to burn a food offering to the LORD.
[Exodus] [30]:[21] They shall wash their hands and feet so that they do not die. This shall be a lasting statute for them, for Aaron and his descendants throughout their generations."
[Exodus] [30]:[22] The LORD said to Moses:
[Exodus] [30]:[23] "Take the finest spices: five hundred shekels of liquid myrrh, half as much—two hundred fifty—of fragrant cinnamon, two hundred fifty of fragrant cane,
[Exodus] [30]:[24] and five hundred of cassia, by the sanctuary shekel, along with a hin of olive oil.
[Exodus] [30]:[25] Make of these a holy anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer. It shall be a holy anointing oil.
[Exodus] [30]:[26] With it anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,
[Exodus] [30]:[27] the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the altar of incense,
[Exodus] [30]:[28] the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
[Exodus] [30]:[29] Consecrate them, and they will be most holy; whatever touches them shall be holy.
[Exodus] [30]:[30] Anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve me as priests.
[Exodus] [30]:[31] Say to the Israelites: 'This shall be my holy anointing oil throughout your generations.
[Exodus] [30]:[32] It must not be poured on anyone's body, and you shall make nothing like it with the same formula. It is holy, and it shall be holy to you.
[Exodus] [30]:[33] Whoever blends anything like it, or puts any of it on an outsider, shall be cut off from his people.'"
[Exodus] [30]:[34] The LORD said to Moses, "Take fragrant spices—stacte, onycha, and galbanum—these spices with pure frankincense, in equal amounts.
[Exodus] [30]:[35] Make of them an incense blended as by a perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy.
[Exodus] [30]:[36] Grind some of it fine and place it before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be most holy to you.
[Exodus] [30]:[37] As for the incense you make, do not make any for yourselves with the same formula; it shall be holy to you, reserved for the LORD.
[Exodus] [30]:[38] Whoever makes anything like it to enjoy its fragrance shall be cut off from his people."
[Exodus] [31]:[1] The LORD spoke to Moses and said:
[Exodus] [31]:[2] "See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,
[Exodus] [31]:[3] and I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, understanding, and knowledge in every kind of craft,
[Exodus] [31]:[4] to design works of art in gold, silver, and bronze,
[Exodus] [31]:[5] to cut and set stones, to carve wood, and to work in every craft.
[Exodus] [31]:[6] And see, I have appointed Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, to work with him. I have also given skill to every craftsman, so they can make everything I have commanded you:
[Exodus] [31]:[7] the tent of meeting, the ark of the testimony and the atonement cover that goes on it, and all the furnishings of the tent;
[Exodus] [31]:[8] the table with its utensils, the pure lampstand with all its utensils, the altar of incense,
[Exodus] [31]:[9] the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the basin with its stand;
[Exodus] [31]:[10] the woven garments, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests,
[Exodus] [31]:[11] and the anointing oil and the fragrant incense for the sanctuary. They are to make them just as I have commanded you."
[Exodus] [31]:[12] The LORD said to Moses:
[Exodus] [31]:[13] "Say to the Israelites: 'Above all, keep my Sabbaths, for this is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, so you will know that I am the LORD, who makes you holy.
[Exodus] [31]:[14] Keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it must be put to death; anyone who does any work on that day must be cut off from among his people.
[Exodus] [31]:[15] For six days work is to be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Whoever does any work on the Sabbath day must be put to death.
[Exodus] [31]:[16] The Israelites are to keep the Sabbath, observing it throughout their generations as a lasting covenant.
[Exodus] [31]:[17] It is a sign between me and the Israelites forever, for in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day he rested and was refreshed.'"
[Exodus] [31]:[18] When the LORD had finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the testimony, tablets of stone written by the finger of God.
[Exodus] [32]:[1] When the people saw that Moses was taking so long to come down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said to him, "Get up, make us gods to go before us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we have no idea what has become of him."
[Exodus] [32]:[2] Aaron said to them, "Take off the gold rings in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me."
[Exodus] [32]:[3] So all the people took off the gold rings that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.
[Exodus] [32]:[4] He took the gold from their hands, shaped it with a tool, and made it into a molten calf. Then they said, "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!"
[Exodus] [32]:[5] When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before it and announced, "Tomorrow there will be a festival to the LORD."
[Exodus] [32]:[6] So the next morning they rose early, offered burnt offerings, and brought fellowship offerings. The people sat down to eat and drink, and then got up to indulge themselves.
[Exodus] [32]:[7] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go down, for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves.
[Exodus] [32]:[8] They have turned aside quickly from the way I commanded them. They have made themselves a molten calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, 'These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.'"
[Exodus] [32]:[9] The LORD said to Moses, "I have seen this people, and they are a stiff-necked people.
[Exodus] [32]:[10] Now leave me alone, so that my anger may burn against them and I may consume them. Then I will make you into a great nation."
[Exodus] [32]:[11] But Moses pleaded with the LORD his God: "LORD, why should your anger burn against your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?
[Exodus] [32]:[12] Why should the Egyptians say, 'He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them off the face of the earth'? Turn from your burning anger; relent from this disaster against your people.
[Exodus] [32]:[13] Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by your own self, saying, 'I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars of heaven, and all this land that I have spoken of I will give to your descendants, and they shall inherit it forever.'"
[Exodus] [32]:[14] So the LORD relented from the disaster he had said he would bring on his people.
[Exodus] [32]:[15] Then Moses turned and went down the mountain with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand, tablets written on both sides, front and back.
[Exodus] [32]:[16] The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
[Exodus] [32]:[17] When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting, he said to Moses, "There is the sound of war in the camp."
[Exodus] [32]:[18] But Moses replied, "It is not the sound of victory, nor the sound of defeat; what I hear is the sound of singing."
[Exodus] [32]:[19] As Moses came near the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, his anger burned. He threw the tablets out of his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
[Exodus] [32]:[20] He took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, scattered it on the water, and made the Israelites drink it.
[Exodus] [32]:[21] Then Moses said to Aaron, "What did these people do to you, that you brought such a great sin upon them?"
[Exodus] [32]:[22] Aaron answered, "Do not let my lord's anger burn. You know these people and how prone they are to evil.
[Exodus] [32]:[23] They said to me, 'Make us gods to go before us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we have no idea what has become of him.'
[Exodus] [32]:[24] So I said to them, 'Whoever has gold, take it off.' They gave it to me, I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf."
[Exodus] [32]:[25] Moses saw that the people were running wild, for Aaron had let them get out of control, to the derision of their enemies.
[Exodus] [32]:[26] So Moses stood at the entrance to the camp and said, "Whoever is for the LORD, come to me!" And all the Levites gathered around him.
[Exodus] [32]:[27] He said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Every man strap his sword to his side. Go back and forth through the camp from gate to gate, and each of you kill his brother, his companion, and his relative."
[Exodus] [32]:[28] The Levites did as Moses said, and about three thousand of the people fell that day.
[Exodus] [32]:[29] Then Moses said, "Consecrate yourselves to the LORD today, for each of you has gone against his own son and his own brother, so that the LORD may bestow a blessing on you this day."
[Exodus] [32]:[30] The next day Moses said to the people, "You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin."
[Exodus] [32]:[31] So Moses went back to the LORD and said, "Oh, this people has committed a great sin! They have made themselves gods of gold.
[Exodus] [32]:[32] And now, if you would only forgive their sin—but if not, then blot me out of the book you have written.
[Exodus] [32]:[33] The LORD answered Moses, "Whoever has sinned against me, that one I will blot out of my book.
[Exodus] [32]:[34] Now go, lead the people to the place I told you about. My angel will go before you. But when the day comes for punishment, I will punish them for their sin."
[Exodus] [32]:[35] And the LORD struck the people with a plague because they made the calf — the calf Aaron had made.
[Exodus] [33]:[1] The LORD said to Moses, "Go up from here, you and the people you brought out of the land of Egypt, to the land I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I said, 'I will give it to your offspring.'
[Exodus] [33]:[2] I will send an angel ahead of you, and I will drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
[Exodus] [33]:[3] Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up among you, because you are a stubborn people, and I might destroy you on the way."
[Exodus] [33]:[4] When the people heard this hard word, they mourned, and no one put on his ornaments.
[Exodus] [33]:[5] The LORD said to Moses, "Tell the Israelites: You are a stubborn people. If I went up among you for even a moment, I would destroy you. Now take off your ornaments, and I will decide what to do with you."
[Exodus] [33]:[6] So the Israelites stripped off their ornaments at Mount Horeb.
[Exodus] [33]:[7] Moses would take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, some distance away, and he called it the tent of meeting. Anyone who sought the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting outside the camp.
[Exodus] [33]:[8] Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise and stand, each at the entrance of his own tent, watching Moses until he had entered the tent.
[Exodus] [33]:[9] And whenever Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance of the tent, and the LORD would speak with Moses.
[Exodus] [33]:[10] When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, they would rise and bow down, each at the entrance of his own tent.
[Exodus] [33]:[11] The LORD would speak with Moses face to face, as one speaks with a friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his assistant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, never left the tent.
[Exodus] [33]:[12] Moses said to the LORD, "See, you tell me, 'Lead this people up,' but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, 'I know you by name, and you have found favor in my eyes.'
[Exodus] [33]:[13] Now then, if I have found favor in your eyes, please show me your ways, so that I may know you and continue to find favor in your eyes. Remember that this nation is your people."
[Exodus] [33]:[14] The LORD answered, "My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest."
[Exodus] [33]:[15] Then Moses said to him, "If your presence does not go with us, do not bring us up from here.
[Exodus] [33]:[16] How will anyone know that I and your people have found favor in your eyes unless you go with us? What else will set me and your people apart from every other people on the face of the earth?"
[Exodus] [33]:[17] And the LORD said to Moses, "I will do this very thing you have asked, for you have found favor in my eyes, and I know you by name."
[Exodus] [33]:[18] Then Moses said, "Please, show me your glory."
[Exodus] [33]:[19] And the LORD said, "I will make all my goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy.
[Exodus] [33]:[20] But he said, "You cannot see my face, for no one may see me and live."
[Exodus] [33]:[21] Then the LORD said, "There is a place near me where you shall stand on the rock.
[Exodus] [33]:[22] When my glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
[Exodus] [33]:[23] Then I will take away my hand, and you will see my back; but my face must not be seen."
[Exodus] [34]:[1] The LORD said to Moses, "Cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered.
[Exodus] [34]:[2] Be ready by morning, and in the morning come up on Mount Sinai and stand before me there on the top of the mountain.
[Exodus] [34]:[3] No one is to come up with you; no one is even to be seen anywhere on the mountain. Not even the flocks and herds may graze in front of that mountain."
[Exodus] [34]:[4] So Moses cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and early in the morning he went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, carrying the two stone tablets in his hand.
[Exodus] [34]:[5] Then the LORD came down in the cloud and stood there with him, and proclaimed the name of the LORD.
[Exodus] [34]:[6] The LORD passed before him and proclaimed: "The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness,
[Exodus] [34]:[7] keeping steadfast love for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin—yet he does not leave the guilty unpunished, but visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and the children's children, to the third and fourth generation."
[Exodus] [34]:[8] Moses quickly bowed to the ground and worshiped.
[Exodus] [34]:[9] He said, "If I have found favor in your eyes, Lord, then let the Lord go with us. Though this is a stiff-necked people, pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us as your own possession."
[Exodus] [34]:[10] And the LORD said: "See, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will do wonders never yet performed in any land or among any nation. All the people among whom you live will see the work of the LORD, for what I am about to do with you is awesome and terrifying.
[Exodus] [34]:[11] Keep what I command you today. I am driving out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
[Exodus] [34]:[12] Be careful not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land you are entering, or they will become a snare among you.
[Exodus] [34]:[13] Rather, you shall tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, and cut down their Asherah poles.
[Exodus] [34]:[14] You shall bow down to no other god, for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.
[Exodus] [34]:[15] Do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, for when they prostitute themselves to their gods and sacrifice to them, someone will invite you, and you will eat of his sacrifice.
[Exodus] [34]:[16] And when you take their daughters for your sons, their daughters will prostitute themselves to their gods and lead your sons to do the same.
[Exodus] [34]:[17] You shall not make cast idols for yourself.
[Exodus] [34]:[18] Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. For seven days eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.
[Exodus] [34]:[19] Every firstborn of the womb is mine, and all your male livestock — the firstborn of ox and of sheep.
[Exodus] [34]:[20] The firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb; if you do not redeem it, you must break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem. No one is to appear before me empty-handed.
[Exodus] [34]:[21] Six days you shall labor, but on the seventh day you shall rest; even in plowing time and harvest you shall rest.
[Exodus] [34]:[22] Celebrate the Feast of Weeks with the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the turn of the year.
[Exodus] [34]:[23] Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Sovereign LORD, the God of Israel.
[Exodus] [34]:[24] For I will drive out nations before you and enlarge your borders, and no one will covet your land when you go up three times a year to appear before the LORD your God.
[Exodus] [34]:[25] Do not slaughter my sacrifice, with its blood, while there is leaven present, and do not let the sacrifice of the Passover Feast remain until morning.
[Exodus] [34]:[26] Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
[Exodus] [34]:[27] Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write down these words, for in accordance with these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
[Exodus] [34]:[28] Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he ate no bread and drank no water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.
[Exodus] [34]:[29] When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand, he did not know that the skin of his face was radiant because he had spoken with the LORD.
[Exodus] [34]:[30] When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, the skin of his face was radiant, and they were afraid to come near him.
[Exodus] [34]:[31] But Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the assembly came back to him, and Moses spoke with them.
[Exodus] [34]:[32] Afterward all the Israelites came near, and he commanded them everything the LORD had told him on Mount Sinai.
[Exodus] [34]:[33] When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
[Exodus] [34]:[34] Whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with him, he would remove the veil until he came out. Then he would come out and tell the Israelites what he had been commanded,
[Exodus] [34]:[35] and the Israelites would see that the face of Moses was radiant. Then Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with the LORD again.
[Exodus] [35]:[1] Moses assembled the whole congregation of the Israelites and said to them, "These are the things the LORD has commanded you to do:
[Exodus] [35]:[2] For six days work may be done, but the seventh day shall be holy for you, a sabbath of complete rest to the LORD. Whoever does any work on it shall be put to death.
[Exodus] [35]:[3] You shall not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day."
[Exodus] [35]:[4] Moses said to the whole congregation of the Israelites, "This is what the LORD has commanded:
[Exodus] [35]:[5] Take from among you an offering to the LORD. Let everyone whose heart is willing bring it as the LORD's offering: gold, silver, and bronze;
[Exodus] [35]:[6] blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goats' hair;
[Exodus] [35]:[7] ram skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
[Exodus] [35]:[8] oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
[Exodus] [35]:[9] onyx stones and other stones to be set in the ephod and the breastpiece.
[Exodus] [35]:[10] Let everyone among you who is skilled come and make everything the LORD has commanded:
[Exodus] [35]:[11] the tabernacle with its tent and covering, its clasps and frames, its crossbars, pillars, and bases;
[Exodus] [35]:[12] the ark with its poles, the atonement cover, and the curtain that screens it;
[Exodus] [35]:[13] the table with its poles and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
[Exodus] [35]:[14] the lampstand for the light with its utensils and lamps, and the oil for the light;
[Exodus] [35]:[15] the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil and the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance to the tabernacle;
[Exodus] [35]:[16] the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;
[Exodus] [35]:[17] the hangings of the courtyard with its pillars and bases, and the screen for the gate of the courtyard;
[Exodus] [35]:[18] the pegs of the tabernacle and the pegs of the courtyard, and their ropes;
[Exodus] [35]:[19] the finely woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments for his sons to serve as priests."
[Exodus] [35]:[20] Then the whole congregation of the Israelites withdrew from Moses' presence.
[Exodus] [35]:[21] And everyone whose heart stirred him and everyone whose spirit moved him came and brought the LORD's offering for the work on the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.
[Exodus] [35]:[22] They came, both men and women; all who were willing in heart brought brooches, earrings, rings, and pendants—every kind of gold ornament—everyone presenting an offering of gold to the LORD.
[Exodus] [35]:[23] Everyone who had blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats' hair, ram skins dyed red, or fine leather brought them.
[Exodus] [35]:[24] Everyone who could give an offering of silver or bronze brought it as the LORD's offering, and everyone who had acacia wood for any part of the work brought it.
[Exodus] [35]:[25] Every skilled woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
[Exodus] [35]:[26] And all the women whose hearts stirred them with skill spun the goats' hair.
[Exodus] [35]:[27] The leaders brought the onyx stones and the other stones to be set in the ephod and the breastpiece,
[Exodus] [35]:[28] along with the spices and the oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
[Exodus] [35]:[29] So every man and woman whose heart moved them brought something for all the work the LORD had commanded through Moses; the Israelites brought it as a freewill offering to the LORD.
[Exodus] [35]:[30] Then Moses said to the Israelites, "See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,
[Exodus] [35]:[31] and has filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, understanding, and knowledge in every kind of craft,
[Exodus] [35]:[32] to design artistic works in gold, silver, and bronze,
[Exodus] [35]:[33] to cut and set stones and to carve wood—to work in every kind of artistic craft.
[Exodus] [35]:[34] And he has given both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, the ability to teach others.
[Exodus] [35]:[35] He has filled them with skill to do all kinds of work as engravers, designers, embroiderers in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and as weavers—masters of every craft and designers of artistic works.
[Exodus] [36]:[1] So Bezalel and Oholiab went to work, along with every skilled craftsman to whom the LORD had given wisdom and understanding to know how to carry out all the work of building the sanctuary, doing everything just as the LORD had commanded.
[Exodus] [36]:[2] Then Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled craftsman in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom—everyone whose heart moved him to come forward and take up the work.
[Exodus] [36]:[3] They received from Moses all the offerings the Israelites had brought for the work of building the sanctuary. And still the people kept bringing him freewill offerings, morning after morning.
[Exodus] [36]:[4] So all the skilled workers who were doing the work of the sanctuary left their tasks
[Exodus] [36]:[5] and came to Moses, saying, "The people are bringing far more than is needed for the work the LORD commanded to be done."
[Exodus] [36]:[6] Then Moses gave an order, and it was proclaimed throughout the camp: "No man or woman is to bring anything more as an offering for the sanctuary." So the people were kept from bringing more,
[Exodus] [36]:[7] for what they had already brought was more than enough to complete all the work.
[Exodus] [36]:[8] All the skilled workers among them made the tabernacle with ten curtains of finely twisted linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with cherubim woven into them by a master craftsman.
[Exodus] [36]:[9] Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide; all the curtains were the same size.
[Exodus] [36]:[10] He joined five of the curtains to one another, and the other five he joined to one another as well.
[Exodus] [36]:[11] He made loops of blue yarn along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and did the same along the edge of the end curtain in the second set.
[Exodus] [36]:[12] He made fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, so that the loops lined up with each other.
[Exodus] [36]:[13] He made fifty gold clasps and used them to fasten the two sets of curtains together, so that the tabernacle was a single whole.
[Exodus] [36]:[14] He made curtains of goat hair for the tent over the tabernacle—eleven curtains in all.
[Exodus] [36]:[15] Each curtain was thirty cubits long and four cubits wide; all eleven curtains were the same size.
[Exodus] [36]:[16] He joined five of the curtains into one set and six into another.
[Exodus] [36]:[17] He made fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain of the first set and fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain of the second set.
[Exodus] [36]:[18] He made fifty bronze clasps to fasten the tent together as a single whole.
[Exodus] [36]:[19] Then he made a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
[Exodus] [36]:[20] He made upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
[Exodus] [36]:[21] Each frame was ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide,
[Exodus] [36]:[22] with two tenons joined to each other. He made all the frames of the tabernacle this way.
[Exodus] [36]:[23] He made twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle
[Exodus] [36]:[24] and forty silver bases to go under them—two bases under each frame, one for each of its two tenons.
[Exodus] [36]:[25] For the other side of the tabernacle, the north side, he made twenty frames
[Exodus] [36]:[26] and forty silver bases, two under each frame.
[Exodus] [36]:[27] For the rear of the tabernacle, on the west, he made six frames,
[Exodus] [36]:[28] and two frames for the corners at the rear.
[Exodus] [36]:[29] These were doubled at the bottom and joined together at the top with a single ring. He made both corner frames the same way.
[Exodus] [36]:[30] So there were eight frames and sixteen silver bases, two under each frame.
[Exodus] [36]:[31] He also made crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle,
[Exodus] [36]:[32] five for the frames on the other side, and five for the frames at the rear of the tabernacle, on the west.
[Exodus] [36]:[33] He made the middle crossbar to run from end to end, halfway up the frames.
[Exodus] [36]:[34] He overlaid the frames with gold and made gold rings to hold the crossbars, and he overlaid the crossbars with gold as well.
[Exodus] [36]:[35] He made the veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it by a master craftsman.
[Exodus] [36]:[36] For it he made four posts of acacia wood, overlaid them with gold, made gold hooks for them, and cast four silver bases for them.
[Exodus] [36]:[37] He made a screen for the entrance to the tent of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer,
[Exodus] [36]:[38] with five posts and their hooks. He overlaid the tops of the posts and their bands with gold, and made their five bases of bronze.
[Exodus] [37]:[1] Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
[Exodus] [37]:[2] He overlaid it with pure gold, inside and out, and made a gold molding around it.
[Exodus] [37]:[3] He cast four gold rings for it, for its four feet: two rings on one side and two rings on the other.
[Exodus] [37]:[4] He made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold,
[Exodus] [37]:[5] and he inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, for carrying it.
[Exodus] [37]:[6] He made the mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
[Exodus] [37]:[7] He made two cherubim of gold, hammered out of one piece, at the two ends of the mercy seat:
[Exodus] [37]:[8] one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other. He made the cherubim of one piece with the mercy seat at its two ends.
[Exodus] [37]:[9] The cherubim spread their wings upward, overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings, facing each other; the faces of the cherubim were turned toward the mercy seat.
[Exodus] [37]:[10] He made the table of acacia wood, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
[Exodus] [37]:[11] He overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold molding around it.
[Exodus] [37]:[12] He made a rim around it a handbreadth wide, with a gold molding around the rim.
[Exodus] [37]:[13] He cast four gold rings for it and fastened the rings at the four corners, where its four legs were.
[Exodus] [37]:[14] The rings were set close to the rim, as holders for the poles used to carry the table.
[Exodus] [37]:[15] He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold, for carrying the table.
[Exodus] [37]:[16] He made the vessels that were to be on the table—its plates and dishes, its bowls and pitchers for pouring drink offerings—all of pure gold.
[Exodus] [37]:[17] He made the lampstand of pure gold. He hammered out the lampstand—its base and shaft, its cups, buds, and blossoms—of one piece with it.
[Exodus] [37]:[18] Six branches extended from its sides: three branches of the lampstand from one side and three from the other.
[Exodus] [37]:[19] Three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with bud and blossom, were on one branch, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with bud and blossom, on the next—so for all six branches extending from the lampstand.
[Exodus] [37]:[20] On the lampstand itself were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their buds and blossoms.
[Exodus] [37]:[21] A bud was under the first pair of branches extending from it, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair—for all six branches extending from it.
[Exodus] [37]:[22] The buds and the branches were of one piece with it, the whole of it a single hammered work of pure gold.
[Exodus] [37]:[23] He made its seven lamps, along with its tongs and trays, of pure gold.
[Exodus] [37]:[24] He made the lampstand and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold.
[Exodus] [37]:[25] He made the altar of incense of acacia wood, a cubit long and a cubit wide—square—and two cubits high, with its horns of one piece with it.
[Exodus] [37]:[26] He overlaid it with pure gold—its top, its sides all around, and its horns—and made a gold molding around it.
[Exodus] [37]:[27] He made two gold rings for it beneath the molding, on its two sides, on opposite sides of it, as holders for the poles used to carry it.
[Exodus] [37]:[28] He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
[Exodus] [37]:[29] He also made the holy anointing oil and the pure, fragrant incense, blended like the work of a perfumer.
[Exodus] [38]:[1] He made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide—square—and three cubits high.
[Exodus] [38]:[2] He made horns for it on its four corners, the horns being of one piece with it, and he overlaid it with bronze.
[Exodus] [38]:[3] He made all the utensils of the altar: the pots, the shovels, the basins, the forks, and the fire pans. All its utensils he made of bronze.
[Exodus] [38]:[4] For the altar he made a grating of bronze network, under its ledge, reaching halfway up.
[Exodus] [38]:[5] He cast four rings at the four corners of the bronze grating as holders for the poles.
[Exodus] [38]:[6] He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
[Exodus] [38]:[7] He inserted the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar, so that it could be carried with them. He made it hollow, out of boards.
[Exodus] [38]:[8] He made the bronze basin and its bronze stand from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
[Exodus] [38]:[9] Then he made the courtyard. On the south side the hangings of the courtyard were of finely twisted linen, a hundred cubits long,
[Exodus] [38]:[10] with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases; the hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver.
[Exodus] [38]:[11] On the north side the hangings were a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases; the hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver.
[Exodus] [38]:[12] On the west side the hangings were fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases; the hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver.
[Exodus] [38]:[13] On the east side, toward the sunrise, the courtyard was fifty cubits wide.
[Exodus] [38]:[14] The hangings on one side of the entrance were fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases,
[Exodus] [38]:[15] and on the other side of the courtyard gate—on this side and on that—the hangings were fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
[Exodus] [38]:[16] All the hangings around the courtyard were of finely twisted linen.
[Exodus] [38]:[17] The bases for the posts were bronze, the hooks of the posts and their bands were silver, and the tops of the posts were overlaid with silver; all the posts of the courtyard were banded with silver.
[Exodus] [38]:[18] The screen for the gate of the courtyard was the work of an embroiderer, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen. It was twenty cubits long and, like the hangings of the courtyard, five cubits high,
[Exodus] [38]:[19] with four posts and four bronze bases. Their hooks were silver, the overlay of their tops was silver, and their bands were silver.
[Exodus] [38]:[20] All the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the surrounding courtyard were of bronze.
[Exodus] [38]:[21] These are the records of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, drawn up at Moses' command by the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
[Exodus] [38]:[22] Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything the LORD had commanded Moses,
[Exodus] [38]:[23] and with him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, a craftsman and designer, and an embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
[Exodus] [38]:[24] All the gold used for the work, for every part of the sanctuary work—the gold of the wave offering—came to twenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
[Exodus] [38]:[25] The silver from those of the congregation who were counted came to a hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels, by the sanctuary shekel:
[Exodus] [38]:[26] one beka per person, that is, half a shekel by the sanctuary shekel, from everyone registered in the census, twenty years old and upward—six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty men.
[Exodus] [38]:[27] The hundred talents of silver were used to cast the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the curtain—a hundred bases from the hundred talents, one talent per base.
[Exodus] [38]:[28] From the one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels he made hooks for the posts, overlaid their tops, and made bands for them.
[Exodus] [38]:[29] The bronze from the wave offering came to seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
[Exodus] [38]:[30] With it he made the bases for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar with its bronze grating, and all the utensils of the altar,
[Exodus] [38]:[31] the bases around the courtyard and the bases of the courtyard gate, and all the tent pegs of the tabernacle and all the tent pegs around the courtyard.
[Exodus] [39]:[1] From the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn they made finely woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary, and they made the holy garments for Aaron, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Exodus] [39]:[2] He made the ephod of gold, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.
[Exodus] [39]:[3] They hammered out sheets of gold and cut them into threads to work into the blue, the purple, the scarlet yarn, and the fine linen—the work of a skilled craftsman.
[Exodus] [39]:[4] They made shoulder pieces for the ephod, joined to it at its two edges.
[Exodus] [39]:[5] The skillfully woven band on the ephod was of one piece with it and made like it: of gold, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Exodus] [39]:[6] They prepared the onyx stones, mounted in gold filigree settings and engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
[Exodus] [39]:[7] He fastened them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Exodus] [39]:[8] He made the breastpiece, the work of a skilled craftsman, like the work of the ephod: of gold, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.
[Exodus] [39]:[9] It was square, and they made the breastpiece doubled over—a span long and a span wide, doubled.
[Exodus] [39]:[10] They set in it four rows of stones. The first row was carnelian, topaz, and emerald.
[Exodus] [39]:[11] The second row was turquoise, sapphire, and diamond.
[Exodus] [39]:[12] The third row was jacinth, agate, and amethyst.
[Exodus] [39]:[13] The fourth row was beryl, onyx, and jasper. They were mounted in gold filigree settings.
[Exodus] [39]:[14] The stones corresponded to the names of the sons of Israel: twelve stones for their twelve names, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
[Exodus] [39]:[15] For the breastpiece they made braided chains of pure gold, like cords.
[Exodus] [39]:[16] They made two gold filigree settings and two gold rings, and fastened the two rings to the two ends of the breastpiece.
[Exodus] [39]:[17] They fastened the two gold cords to the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece,
[Exodus] [39]:[18] and the other two ends of the cords they fastened to the two settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
[Exodus] [39]:[19] They made two gold rings and put them at the two ends of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
[Exodus] [39]:[20] They made two more gold rings and attached them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front, close to the seam just above the woven band of the ephod.
[Exodus] [39]:[21] They bound the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it rested on the woven band and would not come loose from the ephod, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Exodus] [39]:[22] He made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue, the work of a weaver,
[Exodus] [39]:[23] with an opening in the center of the robe like the opening of a collar, and a binding around the opening so that it would not tear.
[Exodus] [39]:[24] On the hem of the robe they made pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, finely twisted.
[Exodus] [39]:[25] They made bells of pure gold and attached them between the pomegranates all around the hem of the robe,
[Exodus] [39]:[26] alternating a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe for ministering, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Exodus] [39]:[27] For Aaron and his sons they made tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver,
[Exodus] [39]:[28] and the turban of fine linen, the ornate headbands of fine linen, the linen undergarments of finely twisted linen,
[Exodus] [39]:[29] and the sash of finely twisted linen with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, the work of an embroiderer, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Exodus] [39]:[30] They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold and engraved on it, like an inscription on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
[Exodus] [39]:[31] They fastened a blue cord to it to attach it to the turban above, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Exodus] [39]:[32] So all the work on the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Exodus] [39]:[33] Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its furnishings, its clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases;
[Exodus] [39]:[34] the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the shielding curtain;
[Exodus] [39]:[35] the ark of the testimony with its poles and the mercy seat;
[Exodus] [39]:[36] the table with all its utensils and the bread of the Presence;
[Exodus] [39]:[37] the lampstand of pure gold with its lamps set in a row, and all its utensils, and the oil for the light;
[Exodus] [39]:[38] the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent;
[Exodus] [39]:[39] the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;
[Exodus] [39]:[40] the curtains of the courtyard with their posts and bases, the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard, its ropes and tent pegs, and all the equipment for the service of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting;
[Exodus] [39]:[41] and the finely woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary—the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.
[Exodus] [39]:[42] Just as the LORD had commanded Moses, so the Israelites did all the work.

[Exodus] [40]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Exodus] [40]:[2] "On the first day of the first month you shall set up the tabernacle, the tent of meeting.
[Exodus] [40]:[3] Place the ark of the testimony inside it, and screen the ark with the curtain.
[Exodus] [40]:[4] Bring in the table and set out what belongs on it. Bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.
[Exodus] [40]:[5] Put the golden altar of incense in front of the ark of the testimony, and hang the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.
[Exodus] [40]:[6] Set the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance to the tabernacle, the tent of meeting,
[Exodus] [40]:[7] and place the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
[Exodus] [40]:[8] Set up the courtyard all around, and hang the curtain at the gate of the courtyard.
[Exodus] [40]:[9] Then take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it. Consecrate it and all its furnishings, and it will be holy.
[Exodus] [40]:[10] Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils; consecrate the altar, and it will be most holy.
[Exodus] [40]:[11] Anoint the basin and its stand, and consecrate it.
[Exodus] [40]:[12] Then bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
[Exodus] [40]:[13] Clothe Aaron in the holy garments, anoint him, and consecrate him, so that he may serve me as priest.
[Exodus] [40]:[14] Bring his sons forward as well and clothe them in tunics.
[Exodus] [40]:[15] Anoint them as you anointed their father, so that they may serve me as priests. Their anointing shall install them in a priesthood that lasts for all generations to come."
[Exodus] [40]:[16] Moses did everything just as the LORD had commanded him.
[Exodus] [40]:[17] So the tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month in the second year.
[Exodus] [40]:[18] Moses set up the tabernacle: he laid its bases, put up its frames, inserted its crossbars, and raised its posts.
[Exodus] [40]:[19] He spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering of the tent on top of it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Exodus] [40]:[20] He took the testimony and placed it in the ark, attached the poles to the ark, and set the atonement cover on top of it.
[Exodus] [40]:[21] He brought the ark into the tabernacle, hung the shielding curtain, and screened off the ark of the testimony, just as the LORD had commanded him.
[Exodus] [40]:[22] He placed the table in the tent of meeting on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the curtain,
[Exodus] [40]:[23] and arranged the bread on it before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded him.
[Exodus] [40]:[24] He placed the lampstand in the tent of meeting opposite the table, on the south side of the tabernacle,
[Exodus] [40]:[25] and set up the lamps before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded him.
[Exodus] [40]:[26] He placed the golden altar in the tent of meeting, in front of the curtain,
[Exodus] [40]:[27] and burned fragrant incense on it, just as the LORD had commanded him.
[Exodus] [40]:[28] He hung the curtain at the entrance to the tabernacle.
[Exodus] [40]:[29] He set the altar of burnt offering at the entrance to the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, and offered on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, just as the LORD had commanded him.
[Exodus] [40]:[30] He placed the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar and put water in it for washing;
[Exodus] [40]:[31] Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet from it.
[Exodus] [40]:[32] They washed whenever they entered the tent of meeting or approached the altar, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Exodus] [40]:[33] He set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar and hung the curtain at the gate of the courtyard. And so Moses finished the work.
[Exodus] [40]:[34] Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
[Exodus] [40]:[35] Moses could not enter the tent of meeting, because the cloud had settled on it and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
[Exodus] [40]:[36] Whenever the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out, at every stage of their journeys;
[Exodus] [40]:[37] but if the cloud did not lift, they did not set out until the day it did.
[Exodus] [40]:[38] For the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel throughout all their journeys.
[Leviticus] [1]:[1] The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting:
[Leviticus] [1]:[2] Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When any of you brings an offering to the LORD, you shall bring your offering from the livestock, from the herd or from the flock.
[Leviticus] [1]:[3] If the offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he shall bring a male without defect. He shall bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting, so that it may be accepted on his behalf before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [1]:[4] He shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it shall be accepted for him, to make atonement for him.
[Leviticus] [1]:[5] He shall slaughter the young bull before the LORD, and Aaron's sons the priests shall present the blood and splash it against all sides of the altar at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
[Leviticus] [1]:[6] Then he shall skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
[Leviticus] [1]:[7] The sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
[Leviticus] [1]:[8] Then Aaron's sons the priests shall arrange the pieces, along with the head and the fat, on the wood on the fire on the altar.
[Leviticus] [1]:[9] The entrails and the legs he shall wash with water, and the priest shall burn all of it on the altar as a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [1]:[10] If the offering for a burnt offering is from the flock, from the sheep or the goats, he shall bring a male without defect.
[Leviticus] [1]:[11] He shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron's sons the priests shall splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
[Leviticus] [1]:[12] He shall cut it into pieces, with its head and its fat, and the priest shall arrange them on the wood that is burning on the altar.
[Leviticus] [1]:[13] The entrails and the legs he shall wash with water, and the priest shall present all of it and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [1]:[14] If the offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he shall bring turtledoves or young pigeons as his offering.
[Leviticus] [1]:[15] The priest shall bring it to the altar, wring off its head, and burn it on the altar; its blood shall be drained out against the side of the altar.
[Leviticus] [1]:[16] He shall remove the crop with its feathers and throw it beside the altar on the east side, at the place for the ashes.
[Leviticus] [1]:[17] He shall tear it open by its wings without severing it completely, and the priest shall burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [2]:[1] When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, his offering shall be of fine flour; he is to pour oil on it and place frankincense on it,
[Leviticus] [2]:[2] and bring it to Aaron's sons, the priests. The priest shall scoop out a full handful of its fine flour and its oil, together with all its frankincense, and burn this memorial portion on the altar as a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [2]:[3] The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the fire offerings to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [2]:[4] If you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it shall be of fine flour: unleavened loaves mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers spread with oil.
[Leviticus] [2]:[5] If your offering is a grain offering prepared on a griddle, it shall be of fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened.
[Leviticus] [2]:[6] Break it into pieces and pour oil over it; it is a grain offering.
[Leviticus] [2]:[7] If your offering is a grain offering cooked in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
[Leviticus] [2]:[8] Bring the grain offering made in any of these ways to the LORD; present it to the priest, who shall carry it to the altar.
[Leviticus] [2]:[9] The priest shall lift out the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar as a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [2]:[10] The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the fire offerings to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [2]:[11] No grain offering that you bring to the LORD shall be made with yeast, for you must not burn any yeast or any honey as a fire offering to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [2]:[12] As an offering of firstfruits you shall bring them to the LORD, but they must not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
[Leviticus] [2]:[13] Season every grain offering of yours with salt. Do not leave out the salt of the covenant of your God from your grain offering; add salt to all your offerings.
[Leviticus] [2]:[14] If you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, bring fresh grain roasted in the fire, crushed from ripe heads, as your offering of firstfruits.
[Leviticus] [2]:[15] Put oil on it and lay frankincense on it; it is a grain offering.
[Leviticus] [2]:[16] The priest shall burn the memorial portion of the crushed grain and the oil, together with all the frankincense, as a fire offering to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [3]:[1] If someone's offering is a fellowship sacrifice, if he brings it from the herd, whether male or female, he must present one without defect before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [3]:[2] He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the tent of meeting; then Aaron's sons, the priests, shall splash the blood against the altar on all sides.
[Leviticus] [3]:[3] From the fellowship sacrifice he shall present as a food offering to the LORD the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
[Leviticus] [3]:[4] and the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall remove along with the kidneys.
[Leviticus] [3]:[5] Then Aaron's sons shall burn it on the altar, on top of the burnt offering that lies on the wood over the fire—a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [3]:[6] If his offering to the LORD for a fellowship sacrifice comes from the flock, he must present a male or female without defect.
[Leviticus] [3]:[7] If he offers a lamb, he shall bring it before the LORD,
[Leviticus] [3]:[8] lay his hand on its head, and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons shall splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
[Leviticus] [3]:[9] From the fellowship sacrifice he shall present as a food offering to the LORD its fat: the entire fat tail, which he shall remove close to the backbone, the fat that covers the entrails, and all the fat that is on the entrails,
[Leviticus] [3]:[10] both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall remove along with the kidneys.
[Leviticus] [3]:[11] The priest shall burn it on the altar as food, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [3]:[12] If his offering is a goat, he shall present it before the LORD,
[Leviticus] [3]:[13] lay his hand on its head, and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron's sons shall splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
[Leviticus] [3]:[14] From it he shall present his offering as a food offering to the LORD: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails,
[Leviticus] [3]:[15] both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall remove along with the kidneys.
[Leviticus] [3]:[16] The priest shall burn them on the altar as food, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma. All the fat belongs to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [3]:[17] This is a lasting statute for your generations, wherever you live: you must not eat any fat or any blood.
[Leviticus] [4]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [4]:[2] Say to the Israelites: When someone sins unintentionally by doing any one of the things the LORD has commanded must not be done—
[Leviticus] [4]:[3] if it is the anointed priest who sins and so brings guilt on the people, he shall bring to the LORD a bull from the herd, without blemish, as a sin offering for the sin he has committed.
[Leviticus] [4]:[4] He shall bring the bull to the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the LORD, lay his hand on its head, and slaughter it before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [4]:[5] Then the anointed priest shall take some of the bull's blood and carry it into the tent of meeting.
[Leviticus] [4]:[6] He shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD, in front of the curtain of the sanctuary.
[Leviticus] [4]:[7] He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that stands before the LORD in the tent of meeting; the rest of the bull's blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
[Leviticus] [4]:[8] He shall remove all the fat of the bull of the sin offering: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on them,
[Leviticus] [4]:[9] the two kidneys with the fat on them at the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall take away with the kidneys—
[Leviticus] [4]:[10] just as they are removed from the ox of the fellowship offering. The priest shall burn them on the altar of burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [4]:[11] But the hide of the bull and all its flesh, with its head and legs, its entrails and its dung—
[Leviticus] [4]:[12] all the rest of the bull—he shall carry outside the camp to a clean place, to the ash heap, and burn it there on a wood fire. It shall be burned on the ash heap.
[Leviticus] [4]:[13] If the whole congregation of Israel sins unintentionally, and the matter escapes the notice of the assembly, so that they do what any of the LORD's commandments forbids and incur guilt,
[Leviticus] [4]:[14] then, when the sin they have committed becomes known, the assembly shall bring a bull from the herd as a sin offering and present it before the tent of meeting.
[Leviticus] [4]:[15] The elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the bull's head before the LORD, and it shall be slaughtered before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [4]:[16] Then the anointed priest shall bring some of the bull's blood into the tent of meeting.
[Leviticus] [4]:[17] He shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD, in front of the curtain.
[Leviticus] [4]:[18] He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that stands before the LORD in the tent of meeting; the rest of the blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
[Leviticus] [4]:[19] He shall remove all its fat and burn it on the altar.
[Leviticus] [4]:[20] He shall do with this bull exactly as he did with the bull of the sin offering. In this way the priest shall make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [4]:[21] Then he shall carry the bull outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first bull. This is the sin offering for the assembly.
[Leviticus] [4]:[22] If a leader sins unintentionally, doing what any of the commandments of the LORD his God forbids, and so incurs guilt,
[Leviticus] [4]:[23] and then the sin he has committed becomes known to him, he shall bring as his offering a male goat without blemish.
[Leviticus] [4]:[24] He shall lay his hand on the goat's head and slaughter it at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It is a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [4]:[25] The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of its blood at the base of that altar.
[Leviticus] [4]:[26] He shall burn all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the fellowship offering. So the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin, and he will be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [4]:[27] If one of the common people sins unintentionally, doing what any of the LORD's commandments forbids, and so incurs guilt,
[Leviticus] [4]:[28] and then the sin he has committed becomes known to him, he shall bring as his offering a female goat without blemish for the sin he has committed.
[Leviticus] [4]:[29] He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it at the place of the burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [4]:[30] The priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.
[Leviticus] [4]:[31] He shall remove all its fat, as the fat is removed from the fellowship offering, and the priest shall burn it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. So the priest shall make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [4]:[32] If he brings a lamb as his sin offering, he shall bring a female without blemish.
[Leviticus] [4]:[33] He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it as a sin offering at the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
[Leviticus] [4]:[34] The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.
[Leviticus] [4]:[35] He shall remove all its fat, as the fat of the lamb is removed from the fellowship offering, and the priest shall burn the fat pieces on the altar on top of the offerings made by fire to the LORD. So the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [5]:[1] If someone hears a public call to testify and, though he is a witness—having seen something or come to know it—does not speak up, he has sinned and must bear his guilt.
[Leviticus] [5]:[2] Or if someone touches anything unclean—whether the carcass of an unclean wild animal, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of an unclean swarming creature—and it escapes his notice, then he is unclean and has incurred guilt.
[Leviticus] [5]:[3] Or if he touches human uncleanness—any uncleanness by which a person becomes unclean—and it escapes his notice, but afterward he comes to know it, he has incurred guilt.
[Leviticus] [5]:[4] Or if someone swears rashly with his lips to do harm or to do good—whatever a person may rashly swear in an oath—and it escapes his notice, but afterward he comes to know it, he has incurred guilt in any of these ways.
[Leviticus] [5]:[5] When he becomes guilty in any of these ways, he shall confess the sin he has committed.
[Leviticus] [5]:[6] As his penalty for the sin he has committed, he shall bring to the LORD a female from the flock, a ewe lamb or a female goat, as a sin offering; and the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin.
[Leviticus] [5]:[7] But if he cannot afford a lamb, he shall bring to the LORD as his penalty for the sin he has committed two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[8] He shall bring them to the priest, who shall present first the one for the sin offering. He shall wring off its head at the neck without severing it,
[Leviticus] [5]:[9] and he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering against the side of the altar, while the rest of the blood is drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[10] The second bird he shall prepare as a burnt offering, according to the regulation. So the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [5]:[11] But if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall bring as his offering for the sin he has committed a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He shall put no oil on it and lay no frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[12] He shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take a handful of it as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar on top of the offerings made by fire to the LORD. It is a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[13] So the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed in any of these ways, and he will be forgiven. The rest shall belong to the priest, as with the grain offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[14] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [5]:[15] If someone commits a breach of faith and sins unintentionally against any of the holy things of the LORD, he shall bring to the LORD as his guilt offering a ram without blemish from the flock, valued in silver shekels by the sanctuary shekel, as a guilt offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[16] He shall make restitution for the holy thing in which he sinned, adding a fifth to it, and give it to the priest. The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [5]:[17] If someone sins by doing any of the things the LORD has commanded not to be done, even without knowing it, he is guilty and must bear his iniquity.
[Leviticus] [5]:[18] He shall bring to the priest a ram without blemish from the flock, at the set value, as a guilt offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for the error he committed unknowingly, and he will be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [5]:[19] It is a guilt offering; he has surely incurred guilt before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [5]:[20] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [5]:[21] If someone sins and commits a breach of faith against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor about something entrusted to him or left in his care, or by robbery, or by defrauding his neighbor,
[Leviticus] [5]:[22] or if he finds lost property and lies about it and swears falsely—in any of these things that people do and so sin—
[Leviticus] [5]:[23] then, when he has sinned and become guilty, he shall return what he took by robbery or gained by fraud, or the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost property he found,
[Leviticus] [5]:[24] or anything about which he swore falsely. He shall repay it in full and add a fifth to it, giving it to its owner on the day he brings his guilt offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[25] And he shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD: a ram without blemish from the flock, at the set value; he shall bring it to the priest.
[Leviticus] [5]:[26] The priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for any of the things he did that brought guilt upon him.
[Leviticus] [6]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [6]:[2] Command Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering is to remain on the hearth on the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.
[Leviticus] [6]:[3] The priest shall put on his linen robe, with linen undergarments next to his body. Then he shall remove the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire has consumed on the altar and place them beside the altar.
[Leviticus] [6]:[4] Then he shall take off his garments, put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
[Leviticus] [6]:[5] The fire on the altar shall be kept burning; it must not go out. Every morning the priest shall add wood to it, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat portions of the fellowship offerings on it.
[Leviticus] [6]:[6] A perpetual fire shall be kept burning on the altar; it must never go out.
[Leviticus] [6]:[7] This is the law of the grain offering. Aaron's sons shall present it before the LORD, in front of the altar.
[Leviticus] [6]:[8] The priest shall take from it a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering, with its oil and all the frankincense that is on the offering, and burn it on the altar as a memorial portion, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [6]:[9] Aaron and his sons shall eat what is left of it. It shall be eaten as unleavened bread in a holy place; they shall eat it in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
[Leviticus] [6]:[10] It must not be baked with leaven. I have given it to them as their share of my food offerings. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
[Leviticus] [6]:[11] Every male among Aaron's descendants may eat it. It is a perpetual statute for your generations from the food offerings of the LORD. Whatever touches them shall become holy.
[Leviticus] [6]:[12] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [6]:[13] This is the offering that Aaron and his sons shall present to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half in the evening.
[Leviticus] [6]:[14] It shall be prepared with oil on a griddle; bring it well mixed, and present the baked pieces of the grain offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [6]:[15] The anointed priest who takes his place from among his sons shall prepare it. It is a perpetual statute: it shall be burned entirely for the LORD.
[Leviticus] [6]:[16] Every grain offering of a priest shall be burned whole; it must not be eaten.
[Leviticus] [6]:[17] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [6]:[18] Say to Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the sin offering. The sin offering shall be slaughtered before the LORD in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered. It is most holy.
[Leviticus] [6]:[19] The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
[Leviticus] [6]:[20] Whatever touches its flesh shall become holy, and if any of its blood is spattered on a garment, you shall wash the spattered garment in a holy place.
[Leviticus] [6]:[21] A clay pot in which it is boiled must be broken; but if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, that vessel shall be scoured and rinsed with water.
[Leviticus] [6]:[22] Every male among the priests may eat it. It is most holy.
[Leviticus] [6]:[23] But no sin offering may be eaten if any of its blood has been brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place; it shall be burned in the fire.
[Leviticus] [7]:[1] This is the law of the guilt offering; it is most holy.
[Leviticus] [7]:[2] The guilt offering shall be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and its blood shall be thrown against the altar on every side.
[Leviticus] [7]:[3] All its fat shall be offered: the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails,
[Leviticus] [7]:[4] the two kidneys with the fat on them at the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which he shall remove along with the kidneys.
[Leviticus] [7]:[5] The priest shall burn them on the altar as a food offering to the LORD; it is a guilt offering.
[Leviticus] [7]:[6] Every male among the priests may eat of it. It shall be eaten in a holy place; it is most holy.
[Leviticus] [7]:[7] The guilt offering is like the sin offering; there is one law for them both. It belongs to the priest who makes atonement with it.
[Leviticus] [7]:[8] And the priest who offers anyone's burnt offering shall keep for himself the hide of the burnt offering he has offered.
[Leviticus] [7]:[9] Every grain offering baked in an oven, and everything prepared in a pan or on a griddle, belongs to the priest who offers it.
[Leviticus] [7]:[10] But every grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all the sons of Aaron alike, each one the same as his brother.
[Leviticus] [7]:[11] This is the law of the fellowship offering that one may present to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [7]:[12] If he offers it as a thank offering, then along with the thank offering he shall present unleavened loaves mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and loaves of fine flour well kneaded and mixed with oil.
[Leviticus] [7]:[13] Along with loaves of leavened bread he shall present his offering, together with his thanksgiving fellowship offering.
[Leviticus] [7]:[14] From each kind of offering he shall present one loaf as a contribution to the LORD; it belongs to the priest who throws the blood of the fellowship offering.
[Leviticus] [7]:[15] The meat of his thanksgiving fellowship offering shall be eaten on the day it is offered; none of it may be left until morning.
[Leviticus] [7]:[16] But if his offering is a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day he presents his sacrifice, and what is left over may be eaten the next day.
[Leviticus] [7]:[17] Whatever remains of the meat of the sacrifice on the third day shall be burned up.
[Leviticus] [7]:[18] If any of the meat of his fellowship offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not be credited to the one who offered it; it is tainted, and the person who eats of it will bear his guilt.
[Leviticus] [7]:[19] Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten; it shall be burned up. As for other meat, anyone who is clean may eat it.
[Leviticus] [7]:[20] But the person who eats meat from the LORD's fellowship offering while unclean shall be cut off from his people.
[Leviticus] [7]:[21] And if anyone touches something unclean—human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean, detestable creature—and then eats the meat of the LORD's fellowship offering, that person shall be cut off from his people.
[Leviticus] [7]:[22] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [7]:[23] Say to the Israelites: You shall not eat any fat of an ox, a sheep, or a goat.
[Leviticus] [7]:[24] The fat of an animal found dead or torn by wild beasts may be used for any other purpose, but you must not eat it.
[Leviticus] [7]:[25] For anyone who eats the fat of an animal from which a food offering is presented to the LORD shall be cut off from his people.
[Leviticus] [7]:[26] Wherever you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal.
[Leviticus] [7]:[27] Anyone who eats blood shall be cut off from his people.
[Leviticus] [7]:[28] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [7]:[29] Say to the Israelites: Whoever offers a fellowship offering to the LORD shall bring part of it as his gift to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [7]:[30] With his own hands he shall bring the food offerings of the LORD; he shall bring the fat together with the breast, so that the breast may be waved as a wave offering before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [7]:[31] The priest shall burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
[Leviticus] [7]:[32] You shall give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your fellowship offerings.
[Leviticus] [7]:[33] The son of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat of the fellowship offering shall have the right thigh as his portion.
[Leviticus] [7]:[34] For I have taken the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution from the Israelites, from their fellowship offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as a perpetual due from the Israelites.
[Leviticus] [7]:[35] This is the portion of Aaron and the portion of his sons from the food offerings of the LORD, assigned to them on the day they were presented to serve the LORD as priests.
[Leviticus] [7]:[36] On the day they were anointed, the LORD commanded that this be given them by the Israelites. It is a perpetual statute throughout their generations.
[Leviticus] [7]:[37] This is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the fellowship offering,
[Leviticus] [7]:[38] which the LORD commanded Moses on Mount Sinai on the day he commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai.
[Leviticus] [8]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [8]:[2] "Take Aaron and his sons with him, along with the garments, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread,
[Leviticus] [8]:[3] and gather the whole congregation at the entrance to the tent of meeting."
[Leviticus] [8]:[4] Moses did as the LORD commanded him, and the congregation gathered at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
