[Leviticus] [8]:[5] Moses said to the congregation, "This is what the LORD has commanded to be done."
[Leviticus] [8]:[6] Then Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
[Leviticus] [8]:[7] He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around him, clothed him with the robe, and placed the ephod on him. He tied the ephod's woven band around him, fastening it to him.
[Leviticus] [8]:[8] He set the breastpiece on him and put the Urim and the Thummim in the breastpiece.
[Leviticus] [8]:[9] He placed the turban on his head, and on the front of the turban he set the gold medallion, the holy crown, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [8]:[10] Then Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, consecrating them.
[Leviticus] [8]:[11] He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand, to consecrate them.
[Leviticus] [8]:[12] He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head and anointed him, to consecrate him.
[Leviticus] [8]:[13] Then Moses brought Aaron's sons forward, clothed them with tunics, tied sashes around them, and bound headdresses on them, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [8]:[14] He brought forward the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
[Leviticus] [8]:[15] It was slaughtered, and Moses took the blood and with his finger put it on all the horns of the altar, purifying the altar. He poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar and consecrated it, making atonement for it.
[Leviticus] [8]:[16] He took all the fat on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and burned them on the altar.
[Leviticus] [8]:[17] But the bull itself—its hide, its flesh, and its dung—he burned in the fire outside the camp, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [8]:[18] Then he presented the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
[Leviticus] [8]:[19] It was slaughtered, and Moses splashed the blood against all sides of the altar.
[Leviticus] [8]:[20] He cut the ram into pieces and burned the head, the pieces, and the fat.
[Leviticus] [8]:[21] He washed the entrails and the legs with water and burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [8]:[22] Then he presented the second ram, the ram of ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
[Leviticus] [8]:[23] It was slaughtered, and Moses took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
[Leviticus] [8]:[24] He brought Aaron's sons forward and put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then Moses splashed the blood against all sides of the altar.
[Leviticus] [8]:[25] He took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat on the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.
[Leviticus] [8]:[26] From the basket of unleavened bread that was before the LORD he took one loaf of unleavened bread, one loaf made with oil, and one wafer, and placed them on the fat portions and on the right thigh.
[Leviticus] [8]:[27] He placed all of these on the palms of Aaron and his sons and waved them as a wave offering before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [8]:[28] Then Moses took them from their hands and burned them on the altar along with the burnt offering. They were an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [8]:[29] Moses also took the breast and waved it as a wave offering before the LORD. This was Moses' portion of the ram of ordination, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [8]:[30] Then Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar and sprinkled it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. So he consecrated Aaron and his garments, and his sons and their garments with him.
[Leviticus] [8]:[31] Moses said to Aaron and his sons, "Boil the meat at the entrance to the tent of meeting and eat it there, along with the bread from the basket of the ordination offering, as I commanded: 'Aaron and his sons are to eat it.'
[Leviticus] [8]:[32] Whatever is left of the meat and the bread you shall burn in the fire.
[Leviticus] [8]:[33] You must not leave the entrance to the tent of meeting for seven days, until the days of your ordination are complete, for your ordination will take seven days.
[Leviticus] [8]:[34] As has been done today, so the LORD has commanded it to be done, to make atonement for you.
[Leviticus] [8]:[35] You must remain at the entrance to the tent of meeting day and night for seven days and keep the LORD's charge, so that you do not die—for this is what I was commanded."
[Leviticus] [8]:[36] And Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD had commanded through Moses.
[Leviticus] [9]:[1] On the eighth day Moses summoned Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
[Leviticus] [9]:[2] He said to Aaron, "Take a bull calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both without defect, and present them before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [9]:[3] And say to the Israelites: Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, both a year old and without defect, for a burnt offering,
[Leviticus] [9]:[4] and an ox and a ram for a fellowship offering, to sacrifice before the LORD, together with a grain offering mixed with oil. For today the LORD will appear to you."
[Leviticus] [9]:[5] So they brought what Moses had commanded to the front of the tent of meeting, and the whole congregation drew near and stood before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [9]:[6] Then Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you."
[Leviticus] [9]:[7] Moses said to Aaron, "Come to the altar and offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people. Then present the people's offering and make atonement for them, as the LORD has commanded."
[Leviticus] [9]:[8] So Aaron came to the altar and slaughtered the calf as his own sin offering.
[Leviticus] [9]:[9] His sons brought him the blood, and he dipped his finger in it and put it on the horns of the altar; then he poured out the blood at the base of the altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[10] On the altar he burned the fat, the kidneys, and the long lobe of the liver from the sin offering, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [9]:[11] The flesh and the hide he burned in the fire outside the camp.
[Leviticus] [9]:[12] Then he slaughtered the burnt offering. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against the sides of the altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[13] They handed him the burnt offering piece by piece, along with the head, and he burned them on the altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[14] He washed the internal organs and the legs and burned them on top of the burnt offering on the altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[15] Then he presented the people's offering. He took the goat for the people's sin offering, slaughtered it, and offered it for sin as he had done with the first one.
[Leviticus] [9]:[16] He presented the burnt offering and offered it in the prescribed way.
[Leviticus] [9]:[17] He also presented the grain offering, took a handful of it, and burned it on the altar in addition to the morning burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [9]:[18] He slaughtered the ox and the ram as the people's fellowship offering. His sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against the sides of the altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[19] But the fat portions of the ox and the ram—the fat tail, the fat covering the organs, the kidneys, and the long lobe of the liver—
[Leviticus] [9]:[20] these they laid on the breasts, and Aaron burned the fat on the altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[21] Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh before the LORD as a wave offering, as Moses had commanded.
[Leviticus] [9]:[22] Then Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them, and he came down from offering the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the fellowship offering.
[Leviticus] [9]:[23] Moses and Aaron then entered the tent of meeting. When they came out, they blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
[Leviticus] [9]:[24] Fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. When all the people saw it, they shouted for joy and fell facedown.
[Leviticus] [10]:[1] Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu each took his censer, put fire in it, laid incense on it, and offered unauthorized fire before the LORD, which he had not commanded them.
[Leviticus] [10]:[2] Then fire went out from before the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [10]:[3] Moses said to Aaron, "This is what the LORD meant when he said: 'Among those who draw near to me I will show myself holy, and before all the people I will be glorified.'" And Aaron was silent.
[Leviticus] [10]:[4] Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Uzziel, Aaron's uncle, and said to them, "Come here, carry your brothers away from the front of the sanctuary, outside the camp."
[Leviticus] [10]:[5] So they came and carried them, still in their tunics, outside the camp, as Moses had said.
[Leviticus] [10]:[6] Then Moses said to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Do not let your hair hang loose, and do not tear your garments, or you will die and wrath will come upon the whole congregation. But your brothers, the whole house of Israel, may mourn the burning that the LORD has kindled.
[Leviticus] [10]:[7] Do not leave the entrance of the tent of meeting, or you will die, for the LORD's anointing oil is upon you." And they did as Moses said.
[Leviticus] [10]:[8] The LORD spoke to Aaron:
[Leviticus] [10]:[9] "You and your sons with you are not to drink wine or strong drink when you enter the tent of meeting, or you will die. This is a lasting statute through all your generations,
[Leviticus] [10]:[10] so that you can distinguish between the holy and the common, between the unclean and the clean,
[Leviticus] [10]:[11] and so that you can teach the Israelites all the statutes that the LORD has spoken to them through Moses."
[Leviticus] [10]:[12] Moses said to Aaron and to his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, "Take the grain offering that is left from the food offerings of the LORD and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for it is most holy.
[Leviticus] [10]:[13] You must eat it in a holy place, because it is your portion and your sons' portion from the food offerings of the LORD; this is what I was commanded.
[Leviticus] [10]:[14] But the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution you may eat in a clean place, you and your sons and your daughters with you, for they are given as your portion and your sons' portion from the fellowship sacrifices of the Israelites.
[Leviticus] [10]:[15] They are to bring the thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering along with the food offerings of the fat portions, to wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. It will belong to you and your sons with you as a lasting portion, just as the LORD has commanded."
[Leviticus] [10]:[16] Then Moses made careful inquiry about the goat of the sin offering, and there it was—burned up! He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's remaining sons, and said,
[Leviticus] [10]:[17] "Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place? It is most holy, and the LORD gave it to you to take away the guilt of the congregation, to make atonement for them before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [10]:[18] Look, its blood was not brought inside the holy place. You should certainly have eaten it in the holy place, as I commanded."
[Leviticus] [10]:[19] Aaron said to Moses, "Look, today they presented their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, and things like these have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would that have been good in the LORD's eyes?"
[Leviticus] [10]:[20] When Moses heard this, it seemed good to him.
[Leviticus] [11]:[1] The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying to them:
[Leviticus] [11]:[2] Say to the Israelites: These are the creatures you may eat among all the animals on the earth.
[Leviticus] [11]:[3] Any animal that has a divided hoof, split in two, and that chews the cud—that you may eat.
[Leviticus] [11]:[4] But these you shall not eat among those that chew the cud or have divided hooves: the camel, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[5] The rock badger, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[6] The hare, because it chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[7] And the pig, because it has a divided hoof, split in two, but does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[8] You shall not eat their meat, and you shall not touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[9] Of all that lives in the water you may eat these: whatever has fins and scales, in the seas or in the streams—those you may eat.
[Leviticus] [11]:[10] But everything in the seas or streams that does not have fins and scales, among all the swarming creatures of the water and all the living creatures in the water—they are detestable to you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[11] They shall remain detestable to you. You shall not eat their meat, and you shall detest their carcasses.
[Leviticus] [11]:[12] Anything in the water that does not have fins and scales is detestable to you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[13] These are the birds you shall detest; they must not be eaten, for they are detestable: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
[Leviticus] [11]:[14] the kite, and every kind of falcon,
[Leviticus] [11]:[15] every kind of raven,
[Leviticus] [11]:[16] the ostrich, the nighthawk, the gull, and every kind of hawk,
[Leviticus] [11]:[17] the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
[Leviticus] [11]:[18] the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
[Leviticus] [11]:[19] the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
[Leviticus] [11]:[20] Every winged insect that walks on all fours is detestable to you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[21] Yet you may eat these among the winged insects that walk on all fours: those that have jointed legs above their feet for leaping on the ground.
[Leviticus] [11]:[22] Of these you may eat: every kind of locust, every kind of bald locust, every kind of cricket, and every kind of grasshopper.
[Leviticus] [11]:[23] But every other winged insect that has four feet is detestable to you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[24] By these you will make yourselves unclean: whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening,
[Leviticus] [11]:[25] and whoever carries any part of their carcasses must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[26] Every animal that has a hoof but does not have it fully split, and does not chew the cud, is unclean for you; whoever touches them becomes unclean.
[Leviticus] [11]:[27] Among the animals that walk on all fours, every one that walks on its paws is unclean for you; whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening,
[Leviticus] [11]:[28] and whoever carries their carcasses must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[29] Among the creatures that swarm on the ground, these are unclean for you: the mole rat, the mouse, every kind of large lizard,
[Leviticus] [11]:[30] the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
[Leviticus] [11]:[31] These are unclean for you among all the swarming creatures. Whoever touches them when they are dead will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[32] Anything one of them falls on when it is dead becomes unclean—any article of wood, clothing, leather, or sackcloth, any utensil used for work. It must be put in water, and it will be unclean until evening; then it will be clean.
[Leviticus] [11]:[33] If one of them falls into a clay pot, everything in it becomes unclean, and you must break the pot.
[Leviticus] [11]:[34] Any food that may be eaten becomes unclean if such water has come on it, and any liquid that may be drunk becomes unclean in any such vessel.
[Leviticus] [11]:[35] Anything that one of their carcasses falls on becomes unclean; an oven or a cooking stove must be broken up. They are unclean, and they shall be unclean for you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[36] A spring or cistern holding water remains clean, but whoever touches one of these carcasses becomes unclean.
[Leviticus] [11]:[37] If one of their carcasses falls on any seed intended for sowing, the seed remains clean.
[Leviticus] [11]:[38] But if water has been put on the seed and one of their carcasses falls on it, it is unclean for you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[39] If an animal you are allowed to eat dies, whoever touches its carcass will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[40] Whoever eats from its carcass must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening; and whoever carries its carcass must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[41] Every creature that swarms on the ground is detestable; it must not be eaten.
[Leviticus] [11]:[42] You shall not eat anything that moves on its belly, or that walks on all fours, or that has many feet—any creature that swarms on the ground—for they are detestable.
[Leviticus] [11]:[43] Do not make yourselves detestable with any creature that swarms. Do not make yourselves unclean by them, so that you become defiled through them.
[Leviticus] [11]:[44] For I am the LORD your God. Consecrate yourselves and be holy, for I am holy. Do not defile yourselves with any swarming creature that crawls on the ground.
[Leviticus] [11]:[45] For I am the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God. Be holy, for I am holy.
[Leviticus] [11]:[46] This is the law concerning animals and birds, every living creature that moves through the water, and every creature that swarms on the ground,
[Leviticus] [11]:[47] to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between the living creature that may be eaten and the living creature that may not be eaten.
[Leviticus] [12]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [12]:[2] Say to the Israelites: When a woman conceives and gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is unclean during her monthly period.
[Leviticus] [12]:[3] On the eighth day the boy's foreskin is to be circumcised.
[Leviticus] [12]:[4] Then she must wait thirty-three days to be purified from her bleeding. She must not touch anything holy or enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are complete.
[Leviticus] [12]:[5] If she gives birth to a daughter, she is unclean for two weeks, as during her period, and she must wait sixty-six days to be purified from her bleeding.
[Leviticus] [12]:[6] When the days of her purification are complete, whether for a son or a daughter, she is to bring to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [12]:[7] The priest shall present it before the LORD and make atonement for her, and she will be clean from her flow of blood. This is the law for the woman who gives birth to a boy or a girl.
[Leviticus] [12]:[8] If she cannot afford a lamb, she is to bring two doves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she will be clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[1] The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
[Leviticus] [13]:[2] "When someone has a swelling, a rash, or a bright spot on the skin of the body, and it develops into a case of a defiling skin disease, he must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.
[Leviticus] [13]:[3] The priest shall examine the sore on the skin. If the hair in the sore has turned white and the sore appears to be deeper than the surrounding skin, it is a defiling skin disease. When the priest has examined him, he shall declare him unclean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[4] But if the bright spot on the skin is white and does not appear deeper than the skin, and the hair in it has not turned white, the priest shall isolate the affected person for seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[5] On the seventh day the priest shall examine him, and if the sore looks unchanged and has not spread in the skin, the priest shall isolate him for another seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[6] On the seventh day the priest shall examine him again, and if the sore has faded and has not spread in the skin, the priest shall declare him clean; it is only a rash. He shall wash his clothes, and he will be clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[7] But if the rash does spread in the skin after he has shown himself to the priest and been declared clean, he must appear before the priest again.
[Leviticus] [13]:[8] The priest shall examine him, and if the rash has spread in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a defiling disease.
[Leviticus] [13]:[9] When anyone has a case of defiling skin disease, he must be brought to the priest.
[Leviticus] [13]:[10] The priest shall examine him, and if there is a white swelling in the skin that has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling,
[Leviticus] [13]:[11] it is a chronic skin disease, and the priest shall declare him unclean. He is not to isolate him, for he is already unclean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[12] If the disease breaks out all over the skin and, as far as the priest can see, covers the person's skin from head to foot,
[Leviticus] [13]:[13] then the priest shall examine him, and if the disease has covered his whole body, he shall declare the affected person clean. Since it has all turned white, he is clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[14] But whenever raw flesh appears on him, he will be unclean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[15] When the priest sees the raw flesh, he shall declare him unclean. The raw flesh is unclean; it is a defiling disease.
[Leviticus] [13]:[16] If the raw flesh changes and turns white, he must go to the priest.
[Leviticus] [13]:[17] The priest shall examine him, and if the sore has turned white, the priest shall declare the affected person clean; then he is clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[18] When someone has a boil on his skin and it heals,
[Leviticus] [13]:[19] and in the place of the boil a white swelling or a reddish-white spot appears, he must show himself to the priest.
[Leviticus] [13]:[20] The priest shall examine it, and if it appears lower than the surrounding skin and the hair in it has turned white, the priest shall declare him unclean. It is a defiling disease that has broken out where the boil was.
[Leviticus] [13]:[21] But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in it, and it is not lower than the surrounding skin but has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[22] But if it does spread further in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is an infection.
[Leviticus] [13]:[23] But if the spot stays where it is and does not spread, it is only the scar from the boil, and the priest shall declare him clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[24] When someone has a burn on his skin and a reddish-white or white spot appears in the raw flesh of the burn,
[Leviticus] [13]:[25] the priest shall examine it. If the hair in the spot has turned white and it appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a defiling disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest shall declare him unclean; it is a defiling skin disease.
[Leviticus] [13]:[26] But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the spot, and it is not lower than the surrounding skin but has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[27] On the seventh day the priest shall examine him, and if it has spread in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean; it is a defiling skin disease.
[Leviticus] [13]:[28] But if the spot stays where it is, has not spread in the skin, and has faded, it is only a swelling from the burn, and the priest shall declare him clean, for it is only the scar of the burn.
[Leviticus] [13]:[29] When a man or a woman has a sore on the head or the chin,
[Leviticus] [13]:[30] the priest shall examine the sore. If it appears to be deeper than the skin and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest shall declare that person unclean. It is a scaly infection, a defiling disease of the head or the chin.
[Leviticus] [13]:[31] But if the priest examines the infection and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest shall isolate the affected person for seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[32] On the seventh day the priest shall examine the sore, and if the infection has not spread, there is no yellow hair in it, and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin,
[Leviticus] [13]:[33] the person shall shave himself, but not the infected area, and the priest shall isolate him for another seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[34] On the seventh day the priest shall examine the infection, and if it has not spread in the skin and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, the priest shall declare him clean. He shall wash his clothes, and he will be clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[35] But if the infection does spread in the skin after he has been declared clean,
[Leviticus] [13]:[36] the priest shall examine him, and if the infection has spread in the skin, he need not look for yellow hair; the person is unclean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[37] But if in his judgment the infection is unchanged and black hair has grown in it, the infection has healed. He is clean, and the priest shall declare him clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[38] When a man or a woman has spots on the skin, white spots,
[Leviticus] [13]:[39] the priest shall examine them. If the spots on the skin are a dull white, it is only a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin; that person is clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[40] If a man loses the hair from his head, he is bald, but he is clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[41] If he loses the hair from the front of his head, he has a bald forehead, but he is clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[42] But if there is a reddish-white sore on the bald head or the bald forehead, it is a defiling disease breaking out on his bald head or bald forehead.
[Leviticus] [13]:[43] The priest shall examine him, and if the swollen sore on his bald head or forehead is reddish-white, like a defiling skin disease,
[Leviticus] [13]:[44] the man is diseased and unclean. The priest must declare him unclean; the sore is on his head.
[Leviticus] [13]:[45] Anyone with such a defiling disease must wear torn clothes, let his hair hang loose, cover the lower part of his face, and call out, "Unclean! Unclean!"
[Leviticus] [13]:[46] As long as he has the disease he remains unclean. He must live alone; his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
[Leviticus] [13]:[47] When a garment is contaminated with mildew—any woolen or linen garment,
[Leviticus] [13]:[48] any woven or knitted material of linen or wool, any leather, or anything made of leather—
[Leviticus] [13]:[49] and the contamination is greenish or reddish—in the garment, the leather, the woven or knitted material, or any leather article—it is a defiling mildew and must be shown to the priest.
[Leviticus] [13]:[50] The priest shall examine it and shall isolate the affected article for seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[51] On the seventh day he shall examine it, and if the contamination has spread in the garment, in the woven or knitted material, or in the leather, whatever its use, it is a destructive mildew; the article is unclean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[52] He must burn the garment, or the woven or knitted material of wool or linen, or any leather article that is contaminated, because it is a destructive mildew; it must be burned in the fire.
[Leviticus] [13]:[53] But if the priest examines it and the contamination has not spread in the garment, in the woven or knitted material, or in the leather article,
[Leviticus] [13]:[54] he shall order that the contaminated article be washed, and he shall isolate it for another seven days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[55] After the article has been washed, the priest shall examine it, and if the spot has not changed its appearance, then even though it has not spread, it is unclean. You must burn it in the fire; it is a rotting spot, whether on the inside or the outside.
[Leviticus] [13]:[56] But if the priest examines it and the spot has faded after the washing, he shall tear that part out of the garment, the leather, or the woven or knitted material.
[Leviticus] [13]:[57] If it appears again in the garment, in the woven or knitted material, or in any leather article, it is spreading, and whatever is contaminated must be burned.
[Leviticus] [13]:[58] Any garment, woven or knitted material, or leather article that has been washed and from which the contamination has disappeared, must be washed a second time, and it will be clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[59] These are the instructions concerning contamination by mildew in woolen or linen garments, in woven or knitted material, or in any leather article, for pronouncing them clean or unclean.
[Leviticus] [14]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [14]:[2] This is the law for the person with a skin disease on the day of his cleansing. He shall be brought to the priest,
[Leviticus] [14]:[3] and the priest shall go outside the camp and examine him. If the diseased man has been healed of his infection,
[Leviticus] [14]:[4] the priest shall give orders to take, for the one being cleansed, two live clean birds, cedar wood, crimson yarn, and hyssop.
[Leviticus] [14]:[5] The priest shall order one of the birds slaughtered over fresh water in a clay vessel.
[Leviticus] [14]:[6] Then he shall take the living bird, the cedar wood, the crimson yarn, and the hyssop, and dip them, along with the living bird, in the blood of the bird that was slaughtered over the fresh water.
[Leviticus] [14]:[7] He shall sprinkle it seven times on the one being cleansed of the disease. Then he shall declare him clean and release the living bird over the open country.
[Leviticus] [14]:[8] The one being cleansed shall wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and bathe in water; then he will be clean. After that he may enter the camp, but he must stay outside his tent for seven days.
[Leviticus] [14]:[9] On the seventh day he shall shave off all his hair—his head, his beard, his eyebrows—all his hair he shall shave. He shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he will be clean.
[Leviticus] [14]:[10] On the eighth day he shall take two male lambs without blemish, one ewe lamb a year old without blemish, three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and one log of oil.
[Leviticus] [14]:[11] The priest who performs the cleansing shall present the man who is being cleansed, together with these offerings, before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
[Leviticus] [14]:[12] The priest shall take one of the male lambs and present it as a guilt offering, along with the log of oil, and he shall wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [14]:[13] He shall slaughter the lamb in the holy place where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered, for the guilt offering belongs to the priest, like the sin offering; it is most holy.
[Leviticus] [14]:[14] The priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
[Leviticus] [14]:[15] Then the priest shall take some of the log of oil and pour it into his own left palm.
[Leviticus] [14]:[16] He shall dip his right finger into the oil in his left palm and sprinkle some of it with his finger seven times before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [14]:[17] Some of the oil remaining in his palm the priest shall put on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, over the blood of the guilt offering.
[Leviticus] [14]:[18] The rest of the oil in his palm he shall put on the head of the one being cleansed. So the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [14]:[19] Then the priest shall offer the sin offering and make atonement for the one being cleansed of his uncleanness. Afterward he shall slaughter the burnt offering
[Leviticus] [14]:[20] and offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. So the priest shall make atonement for him, and he will be clean.
[Leviticus] [14]:[21] But if he is poor and cannot afford this much, he shall take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, along with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, a log of oil,
[Leviticus] [14]:[22] and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whatever he can afford—one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [14]:[23] On the eighth day he shall bring them to the priest for his cleansing, at the entrance to the tent of meeting before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [14]:[24] The priest shall take the lamb of the guilt offering and the log of oil and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [14]:[25] He shall slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering, take some of its blood, and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
[Leviticus] [14]:[26] The priest shall pour some of the oil into his own left palm,
[Leviticus] [14]:[27] and with his right finger he shall sprinkle some of the oil from his left palm seven times before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [14]:[28] Then the priest shall put some of the oil from his palm on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, where the blood of the guilt offering was placed.
[Leviticus] [14]:[29] The rest of the oil in his palm the priest shall put on the head of the one being cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [14]:[30] Then he shall offer one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, whichever he can afford,
[Leviticus] [14]:[31] one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. So the priest shall make atonement before the LORD for the one being cleansed.
[Leviticus] [14]:[32] This is the law for the person who has a skin disease and cannot afford the regular offerings for his cleansing.
[Leviticus] [14]:[33] The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
[Leviticus] [14]:[34] When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as your possession, and I bring an infection of mildew upon a house in the land you possess,
[Leviticus] [14]:[35] Then the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest, "Something like an infection has appeared in my house."
[Leviticus] [14]:[36] The priest shall order the house emptied before he goes in to examine the infection, so that nothing in the house becomes unclean. After that the priest shall go in to inspect the house.
[Leviticus] [14]:[37] He shall examine the infection, and if it is in the walls of the house—greenish or reddish depressions that appear to be beneath the surface of the wall—
[Leviticus] [14]:[38] the priest shall go out the door of the house and shut it up for seven days.
[Leviticus] [14]:[39] On the seventh day the priest shall return and inspect it. If the infection has spread in the walls of the house,
[Leviticus] [14]:[40] he shall order the stones with the infection torn out and thrown into an unclean place outside the city.
[Leviticus] [14]:[41] The house shall be scraped all around inside, and the plaster that is scraped off shall be dumped into an unclean place outside the city.
[Leviticus] [14]:[42] Then other stones shall be brought and set in place of the first ones, and fresh plaster shall be taken and the house replastered.
[Leviticus] [14]:[43] But if the infection breaks out again in the house after the stones have been torn out and the house scraped and replastered,
[Leviticus] [14]:[44] the priest shall come and inspect it. If the infection has spread in the house, it is a destructive mildew in the house; the house is unclean.
[Leviticus] [14]:[45] It must be torn down—its stones, its timbers, and all its plaster—and carried out to an unclean place outside the city.
[Leviticus] [14]:[46] Whoever enters the house during the days it is shut up shall be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [14]:[47] Whoever sleeps in the house must wash his clothes, and whoever eats in the house must wash his clothes.
[Leviticus] [14]:[48] But if the priest comes again and inspects it and the infection has not spread in the house after it was replastered, he shall declare the house clean, for the infection is healed.
[Leviticus] [14]:[49] To purify the house he shall take two birds, cedar wood, crimson yarn, and hyssop.
[Leviticus] [14]:[50] He shall slaughter one of the birds over fresh water in a clay vessel,
[Leviticus] [14]:[51] and he shall take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the crimson yarn, and the living bird, dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
[Leviticus] [14]:[52] So he shall purify the house with the blood of the bird, the fresh water, the living bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the crimson yarn.
[Leviticus] [14]:[53] Then he shall release the living bird outside the city into the open country. So he shall make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.
[Leviticus] [14]:[54] This is the law for any infectious skin disease, for an itching disease,
[Leviticus] [14]:[55] for mildew in clothing and in a house,
[Leviticus] [14]:[56] and for a swelling, a rash, or a bright spot,
[Leviticus] [14]:[57] to determine when something is unclean and when it is clean. This is the law concerning infectious skin diseases.
[Leviticus] [15]:[1] The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
[Leviticus] [15]:[2] Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When any man has a discharge from his body, the discharge makes him unclean.
[Leviticus] [15]:[3] This is his uncleanness from the discharge: whether his body runs with the discharge or is stopped up by it, he is unclean.
[Leviticus] [15]:[4] Any bed the man with a discharge lies on becomes unclean, and anything he sits on becomes unclean.
[Leviticus] [15]:[5] Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[6] Whoever sits on anything the man with a discharge has sat on must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[7] Whoever touches the body of the man with a discharge must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[8] If the man with a discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[9] Every saddle the man with a discharge rides on becomes unclean.
[Leviticus] [15]:[10] Whoever touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[11] Anyone whom the man with a discharge touches without having rinsed his hands in water must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[12] A clay pot that the man with a discharge touches must be broken, and every wooden vessel must be rinsed with water.
[Leviticus] [15]:[13] When the man with a discharge is cleansed of it, he is to count off seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and bathe his body in fresh running water; then he will be clean.
[Leviticus] [15]:[14] On the eighth day he must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, come before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting, and give them to the priest.
[Leviticus] [15]:[15] The priest is to offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD because of his discharge.
[Leviticus] [15]:[16] When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[17] Any garment or leather that has semen on it must be washed with water, and it will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[18] When a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both of them must bathe in water, and they will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[19] When a woman has a discharge of blood from her body, she will be in her menstrual impurity for seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[20] Anything she lies on during her period becomes unclean, and anything she sits on becomes unclean.
[Leviticus] [15]:[21] Anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[22] Anyone who touches anything she has sat on must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[23] Whether it is the bed or anything she sits on, whoever touches it will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[24] If a man lies with her and her impurity comes upon him, he will be unclean for seven days, and every bed he lies on becomes unclean.
[Leviticus] [15]:[25] When a woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside the time of her period, or when her discharge continues beyond her period, she will be unclean as long as the discharge lasts, just as during the days of her period.
[Leviticus] [15]:[26] Every bed she lies on while her discharge continues will be like the bed of her period, and anything she sits on will be unclean, as during her period.
[Leviticus] [15]:[27] Anyone who touches these things becomes unclean; he must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
[Leviticus] [15]:[28] When she is cleansed of her discharge, she is to count off seven days, and after that she will be clean.
[Leviticus] [15]:[29] On the eighth day she must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
[Leviticus] [15]:[30] The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for her before the LORD because of her unclean discharge.
[Leviticus] [15]:[31] You must keep the Israelites separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness by defiling my dwelling place, which is among them.
[Leviticus] [15]:[32] This is the law for the man with a discharge, for anyone made unclean by an emission of semen,
[Leviticus] [15]:[33] for the woman in her menstrual impurity, for anyone with a discharge, male or female, and for the man who lies with a woman who is unclean.
[Leviticus] [16]:[1] The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron's two sons, who died when they drew near before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [16]:[2] The LORD said to Moses: Tell your brother Aaron that he must not come whenever he pleases into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain, before the atonement cover that is on the ark, or he will die; for I appear in the cloud above the atonement cover.
[Leviticus] [16]:[3] This is how Aaron is to enter the Most Holy Place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [16]:[4] He is to put on the holy linen tunic, with linen undergarments next to his body; he is to tie the linen sash around him and wrap the linen turban on his head. These are holy garments, so he must bathe his body in water before he puts them on.
[Leviticus] [16]:[5] From the congregation of the Israelites he is to take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [16]:[6] Aaron is to present the bull for his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household.
[Leviticus] [16]:[7] Then he is to take the two goats and set them before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
[Leviticus] [16]:[8] Aaron is to cast lots over the two goats—one lot for the LORD and one lot for Azazel.
[Leviticus] [16]:[9] Aaron is to bring forward the goat on which the lot for the LORD has fallen and offer it as a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [16]:[10] But the goat on which the lot for Azazel has fallen is to be presented alive before the LORD, so that atonement may be made over it and it may be sent away into the wilderness to Azazel.
[Leviticus] [16]:[11] Aaron is to present the bull for his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and his household; he is to slaughter the bull for his own sin offering.
[Leviticus] [16]:[12] Then he is to take a censer full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and bring them behind the curtain.
[Leviticus] [16]:[13] He is to put the incense on the fire before the LORD, and the cloud of incense will cover the atonement cover that is over the covenant law, so that he will not die.
[Leviticus] [16]:[14] He is to take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the atonement cover, on the east side; then he is to sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times before the atonement cover.
[Leviticus] [16]:[15] Then he is to slaughter the goat for the people's sin offering and bring its blood behind the curtain. He is to do with its blood as he did with the bull's blood: sprinkle it on the atonement cover and before it.
[Leviticus] [16]:[16] In this way he will make atonement for the sanctuary because of the uncleanness of the Israelites and their rebellious acts, whatever their sins have been. He is to do the same for the tent of meeting, which stands among them in the midst of their uncleanness.
[Leviticus] [16]:[17] No one is to be in the tent of meeting from the time Aaron goes in to make atonement in the Most Holy Place until he comes out, having made atonement for himself, his household, and the whole assembly of Israel.
[Leviticus] [16]:[18] Then he is to go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He is to take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood and put it on all the horns of the altar.
[Leviticus] [16]:[19] He is to sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, cleansing it and consecrating it from the uncleanness of the Israelites.
[Leviticus] [16]:[20] When he has finished making atonement for the Most Holy Place, the tent of meeting, and the altar, he is to bring forward the live goat.
[Leviticus] [16]:[21] Aaron is to lay both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the iniquities of the Israelites, all their rebellious acts, whatever their sins have been. He is to put them on the goat's head and send it away into the wilderness in the care of a man appointed for the task.
[Leviticus] [16]:[22] The goat will carry on itself all their iniquities to a solitary land; the man is to release it in the wilderness.
[Leviticus] [16]:[23] Then Aaron is to go into the tent of meeting, take off the linen garments he put on before entering the Most Holy Place, and leave them there.
[Leviticus] [16]:[24] He is to bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his own clothes. Then he is to come out and sacrifice his own burnt offering and the burnt offering for the people, making atonement for himself and for the people.
[Leviticus] [16]:[25] He is to burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
[Leviticus] [16]:[26] The man who sends the goat away to Azazel must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; afterward he may come into the camp.
[Leviticus] [16]:[27] The bull and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the Most Holy Place, are to be carried outside the camp; their hides, their flesh, and their dung are to be burned up.
[Leviticus] [16]:[28] The man who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; afterward he may come into the camp.
[Leviticus] [16]:[29] This is to be a lasting ordinance for you: On the tenth day of the seventh month you are to humble yourselves and do no work at all, whether the native-born or the foreigner residing among you.
[Leviticus] [16]:[30] For on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you; before the LORD you will be clean from all your sins.
[Leviticus] [16]:[31] It is a sabbath of complete rest for you, and you must humble yourselves; it is a lasting ordinance.
[Leviticus] [16]:[32] The priest who is anointed and ordained to serve as priest in his father's place shall make atonement. He shall put on the linen garments, the holy garments,
[Leviticus] [16]:[33] and he shall make atonement for the holy sanctuary; he shall make atonement for the tent of meeting and the altar, and he shall make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
[Leviticus] [16]:[34] This is to be a lasting ordinance for you: atonement is to be made once a year for the Israelites, for all their sins. And Aaron did as the LORD commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [17]:[1] The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
[Leviticus] [17]:[2] Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites, and say to them: This is what the LORD has commanded:
[Leviticus] [17]:[3] Anyone from the house of Israel who slaughters an ox, a lamb, or a goat inside the camp, or slaughters it outside the camp,
[Leviticus] [17]:[4] instead of bringing it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before the LORD's dwelling—that man shall be held guilty of bloodshed. He has shed blood, and he shall be cut off from among his people.
[Leviticus] [17]:[5] This is so that the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices they have been offering out in the open field. They must bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting and sacrifice them as peace offerings to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [17]:[6] The priest shall splash the blood against the altar of the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [17]:[7] They must no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat demons, after whom they prostitute themselves. This shall be a lasting statute for them through all their generations.
[Leviticus] [17]:[8] Say to them: Anyone from the house of Israel, or any foreigner residing among them, who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice
[Leviticus] [17]:[9] and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to the LORD—that man shall be cut off from his people.
[Leviticus] [17]:[10] If anyone from the house of Israel, or any foreigner residing among them, eats any blood, I will set my face against that person and cut him off from among his people.
[Leviticus] [17]:[11] For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives; for it is the blood that makes atonement by means of the life.
[Leviticus] [17]:[12] That is why I have said to the Israelites: None of you may eat blood, nor may any foreigner residing among you eat blood.
[Leviticus] [17]:[13] Anyone among the Israelites, or any foreigner residing among them, who hunts and catches an animal or a bird that may be eaten must drain out its blood and cover it with earth.
[Leviticus] [17]:[14] For the life of every creature is in its blood. Therefore I said to the Israelites: You must not eat the blood of any creature, because the life of every creature is its blood. Whoever eats it shall be cut off.
[Leviticus] [17]:[15] Anyone, whether native-born or foreigner, who eats an animal found dead or torn by wild beasts must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening; then he will be clean.
[Leviticus] [17]:[16] But if he does not wash his clothes and bathe himself, he will bear his guilt.
[Leviticus] [18]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [18]:[2] Speak to the Israelites and say to them: I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [18]:[3] You must not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you lived, and you must not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. Do not follow their statutes.
[Leviticus] [18]:[4] You shall carry out my ordinances and keep my statutes, walking in them. I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [18]:[5] Keep my statutes and my ordinances; the one who does them will live by them. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [18]:[6] No one is to approach any close relative to uncover their nakedness. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [18]:[7] You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father, which is the nakedness of your mother. She is your mother; you shall not uncover her nakedness.
[Leviticus] [18]:[8] You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's wife; it is your father's nakedness.
[Leviticus] [18]:[9] You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, whether your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, born at home or born elsewhere.
[Leviticus] [18]:[10] You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, for their nakedness is your own.
[Leviticus] [18]:[11] You shall not uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father; she is your sister.
[Leviticus] [18]:[12] You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister; she is your father's close relative.
[Leviticus] [18]:[13] You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, for she is your mother's close relative.
[Leviticus] [18]:[14] You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother; do not approach his wife, for she is your aunt.
[Leviticus] [18]:[15] You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law; she is your son's wife. You shall not uncover her nakedness.
[Leviticus] [18]:[16] You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife; it is your brother's nakedness.
[Leviticus] [18]:[17] You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You shall not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to uncover her nakedness; they are close relatives. It is depravity.
[Leviticus] [18]:[18] You shall not take a woman as a rival to her sister, uncovering her nakedness while her sister is still alive.
[Leviticus] [18]:[19] You shall not approach a woman to uncover her nakedness during the impurity of her monthly period.
[Leviticus] [18]:[20] You shall not have sexual relations with your neighbor's wife and defile yourself with her.
[Leviticus] [18]:[21] You shall not give any of your children to be passed through the fire to Molech, and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [18]:[22] You shall not lie with a male as one lies with a woman; it is detestable.
[Leviticus] [18]:[23] You shall not have sexual relations with any animal and defile yourself with it, nor shall a woman present herself to an animal to mate with it; it is a perversion.
[Leviticus] [18]:[24] Do not defile yourselves by any of these practices, for by all these the nations I am driving out before you have defiled themselves.
[Leviticus] [18]:[25] The land became defiled, so I punished it for its guilt, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
[Leviticus] [18]:[26] But you are to keep my statutes and my ordinances and must not commit any of these detestable acts—neither the native-born nor the foreigner residing among you.
[Leviticus] [18]:[27] For the people who lived in the land before you did all these detestable things, and the land became defiled.
[Leviticus] [18]:[28] So do not let the land vomit you out for defiling it, as it vomited out the nation that was before you.
[Leviticus] [18]:[29] For anyone who commits any of these detestable acts—every person who does them must be cut off from among their people.
[Leviticus] [18]:[30] Keep my charge, then, and do not practice any of the detestable customs that were practiced before you, and do not defile yourselves by them. I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [19]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [19]:[2] Speak to the whole congregation of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, for I, the LORD your God, am holy.
[Leviticus] [19]:[3] Each of you shall revere his mother and his father, and you shall keep my Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [19]:[4] Do not turn to idols, and do not make cast gods for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [19]:[5] When you offer a fellowship sacrifice to the LORD, offer it so that it will be accepted for you.
[Leviticus] [19]:[6] It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it, or on the next day; whatever is left over until the third day must be burned in the fire.
[Leviticus] [19]:[7] If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is tainted; it will not be accepted.
[Leviticus] [19]:[8] Whoever eats it will bear his guilt, because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD; that person shall be cut off from his people.
[Leviticus] [19]:[9] When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap all the way to the edges of your field, and do not gather the gleanings of your harvest.
[Leviticus] [19]:[10] Do not strip your vineyard bare or pick up the fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [19]:[11] You shall not steal. You shall not deceive or lie to one another.
[Leviticus] [19]:[12] You shall not swear falsely by my name and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [19]:[13] You shall not exploit your neighbor or rob him. Do not keep the wages of a hired worker with you until morning.
[Leviticus] [19]:[14] You shall not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block in front of the blind, but you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [19]:[15] You shall not pervert justice. Do not show partiality to the poor or favoritism to the great, but judge your neighbor fairly.
[Leviticus] [19]:[16] You shall not go about spreading slander among your people, and you shall not stand by when your neighbor's life is at stake. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [19]:[17] You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You must surely rebuke your fellow Israelite, so that you do not bear sin because of him.
[Leviticus] [19]:[18] You shall not take revenge or bear a grudge against the children of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [19]:[19] You shall keep my statutes. Do not mate different kinds of animals. Do not sow your field with two kinds of seed. Do not wear a garment woven of two kinds of material.
[Leviticus] [19]:[20] If a man sleeps with a woman who is a slave promised to another man but who has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there must be an inquiry. They shall not be put to death, because she had not been freed.
[Leviticus] [19]:[21] The man shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting: a ram as a guilt offering.
[Leviticus] [19]:[22] With the ram of the guilt offering the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD for the sin he has committed, and the sin he committed will be forgiven him.
[Leviticus] [19]:[23] When you enter the land and plant any kind of fruit tree, regard its fruit as forbidden. For three years you are to consider it forbidden; it must not be eaten.
[Leviticus] [19]:[24] In the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [19]:[25] But in the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that your harvest may increase. I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [19]:[26] You shall not eat anything with the blood still in it. You shall not practice divination or seek omens.
[Leviticus] [19]:[27] You shall not cut the hair at the sides of your head or clip off the edges of your beard.
[Leviticus] [19]:[28] You shall not make gashes in your flesh for the dead or put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [19]:[29] Do not degrade your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will turn to prostitution and be filled with depravity.
[Leviticus] [19]:[30] You shall keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [19]:[31] Do not turn to mediums or spiritists; do not seek them out and be defiled by them. I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [19]:[32] Stand up in the presence of the aged, show respect for the elderly, and fear your God. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [19]:[33] When a foreigner lives with you in your land, do not mistreat him.
[Leviticus] [19]:[34] The foreigner living among you must be treated as one of your native-born. Love him as yourself, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [19]:[35] You shall not act dishonestly in judgment, in measures of length, weight, or volume.
[Leviticus] [19]:[36] Use honest scales and honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
[Leviticus] [19]:[37] Keep all my statutes and all my ordinances, and do them. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [20]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [20]:[2] Say to the Israelites: Any Israelite, or any foreigner residing in Israel, who gives one of his children to Molech must be put to death. The people of the land are to stone him.
[Leviticus] [20]:[3] I myself will set my face against that man and cut him off from among his people, because he has given one of his children to Molech, defiling my sanctuary and profaning my holy name.
[Leviticus] [20]:[4] If the people of the land close their eyes to that man when he gives one of his children to Molech, and fail to put him to death,
[Leviticus] [20]:[5] then I myself will set my face against that man and his family, and I will cut off from among their people both him and all who follow him in prostituting themselves to Molech.
[Leviticus] [20]:[6] Whoever turns to mediums and spiritists, prostituting himself by following them, I will set my face against that person and cut him off from among his people.
[Leviticus] [20]:[7] Consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy, for I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [20]:[8] Keep my statutes and do them. I am the LORD, who makes you holy.
[Leviticus] [20]:[9] Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death. He has cursed his father or mother; his blood is on his own head.
[Leviticus] [20]:[10] If a man commits adultery with another man's wife—with the wife of his neighbor—both the adulterer and the adulteress must be put to death.
[Leviticus] [20]:[11] If a man sleeps with his father's wife, he has uncovered his father's nakedness. Both of them must be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.
[Leviticus] [20]:[12] If a man sleeps with his daughter-in-law, both of them must be put to death. What they have done is a perversion; their blood is on their own heads.
[Leviticus] [20]:[13] If a man lies with a man as one lies with a woman, both of them have done what is detestable. They must be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.
[Leviticus] [20]:[14] If a man marries both a woman and her mother, it is depravity. Both he and they must be burned in the fire, so that no depravity will be found among you.
[Leviticus] [20]:[15] If a man has sexual relations with an animal, he must be put to death, and you are to kill the animal.
[Leviticus] [20]:[16] If a woman approaches any animal to mate with it, you are to kill both the woman and the animal. They must be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.
[Leviticus] [20]:[17] If a man takes his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother, and they have sexual relations, it is a disgrace. They must be cut off before the eyes of their people. He has uncovered his sister's nakedness; he will bear his guilt.
[Leviticus] [20]:[18] If a man lies with a woman during her monthly period and has sexual relations with her, he has exposed her flow of blood, and she has uncovered it. Both of them must be cut off from among their people.
[Leviticus] [20]:[19] Do not have sexual relations with your mother's sister or your father's sister, for that would dishonor a close relative; both of them would bear their guilt.
[Leviticus] [20]:[20] If a man sleeps with his aunt, he has dishonored his uncle. They will bear the consequences of their sin; they will die childless.
[Leviticus] [20]:[21] If a man takes his brother's wife, it is an impurity. He has uncovered his brother's nakedness; they will be childless.
[Leviticus] [20]:[22] Keep all my statutes and all my ordinances and do them, so that the land where I am bringing you to live will not vomit you out.
[Leviticus] [20]:[23] Do not follow the customs of the nations I am driving out before you. They did all these things, and I abhorred them.
[Leviticus] [20]:[24] But I said to you: You will take possession of their land; I myself will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the LORD your God, who has set you apart from the peoples.
[Leviticus] [20]:[25] You therefore must distinguish between clean animals and unclean, and between unclean birds and clean. Do not defile yourselves with any animal or bird or anything that crawls on the ground—those I have set apart as unclean for you.
[Leviticus] [20]:[26] You are to be holy to me, because I, the LORD, am holy, and I have set you apart from the nations to be my own.
[Leviticus] [20]:[27] A man or woman who is a medium or a spiritist must be put to death. They are to be stoned; their blood is on their own heads.
[Leviticus] [21]:[1] The LORD said to Moses: Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: No priest shall make himself unclean for any of his people who dies,
[Leviticus] [21]:[2] except for his closest relatives — his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
[Leviticus] [21]:[3] or his virgin sister, close to him, who has never had a husband; for her he may make himself unclean.
[Leviticus] [21]:[4] He shall not make himself unclean for relatives by marriage among his people, and so profane himself.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew of this verse is obscure; it may mean that a priest must not defile himself for kin related to him only through marriage.
[Leviticus] [21]:[5] Priests shall not shave bald patches on their heads, or trim the edges of their beards, or cut gashes in their flesh.
[Leviticus] [21]:[6] They shall be holy to their God and shall not profane the name of their God, for they present the offerings by fire to the LORD, the food of their God; therefore they shall be holy.
[Leviticus] [21]:[7] A priest shall not marry a woman defiled by prostitution, nor one who has been dishonored, nor a woman divorced from her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.
[Leviticus] [21]:[8] You shall treat him as holy, for he offers the food of your God. He shall be holy to you, for I am holy — I, the LORD, who makes you holy.
[Leviticus] [21]:[9] If a priest's daughter defiles herself by prostitution, she profanes her father; she shall be burned with fire.
[Leviticus] [21]:[10] The priest who is highest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been ordained to wear the sacred garments, shall not let his hair hang loose or tear his clothes.
[Leviticus] [21]:[11] He shall not go near any dead body; he shall not make himself unclean even for his father or his mother.
[Leviticus] [21]:[12] He shall not leave the sanctuary or profane the sanctuary of his God, for the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is upon him. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [21]:[13] He shall marry a woman who is a virgin.
[Leviticus] [21]:[14] A widow, a divorced woman, or one dishonored by prostitution — these he shall not marry. He shall take as his wife a virgin from his own people,
[Leviticus] [21]:[15] so that he does not profane his offspring among his people; for I am the LORD, who makes him holy.
[Leviticus] [21]:[16] The LORD spoke to Moses:
[Leviticus] [21]:[17] Say to Aaron: For all generations to come, none of your descendants who has a defect may come near to offer the food of his God.
[Leviticus] [21]:[18] No man with a defect may come near: no one blind or lame, disfigured or deformed;
[Leviticus] [21]:[19] no one with a crippled foot or a crippled hand;
[Leviticus] [21]:[20] no one hunchbacked or dwarfed, or with a defect in his eye, or with festering or running sores, or with damaged testicles.
[Leviticus] [21]:[21] No descendant of Aaron the priest who has a defect shall come forward to present the offerings by fire to the LORD. Since he has a defect, he shall not come forward to offer the food of his God.
[Leviticus] [21]:[22] He may eat the food of his God, both the most holy and the holy;
[Leviticus] [21]:[23] but he shall not go near the curtain or approach the altar, because he has a defect, so that he does not profane my sanctuaries; for I am the LORD, who makes them holy.
[Leviticus] [21]:[24] So Moses told this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites.
[Leviticus] [22]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [22]:[2] Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with reverence the holy offerings of the Israelites, which they set apart for me, so that they do not profane my holy name. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [22]:[3] Say to them: For all your generations, if any of your descendants, while unclean, comes near the holy offerings that the Israelites consecrate to the LORD, that person shall be cut off from my presence. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [22]:[4] No descendant of Aaron who has a skin disease or a discharge may eat of the holy offerings until he is clean. The same is true of anyone who touches something made unclean by a corpse, or a man who has had an emission of semen,
[Leviticus] [22]:[5] or who touches any crawling creature that makes him unclean, or any person who makes him unclean, whatever the uncleanness may be.
[Leviticus] [22]:[6] Whoever touches any such thing will be unclean until evening. He must not eat any of the holy offerings unless he has washed his body with water.
[Leviticus] [22]:[7] When the sun sets he is clean, and afterward he may eat of the holy offerings, for they are his food.
[Leviticus] [22]:[8] He must not eat an animal found dead or torn by wild beasts, which would make him unclean. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [22]:[9] The priests must keep my charge, so that they do not incur guilt and die for profaning it. I am the LORD, who makes them holy.
[Leviticus] [22]:[10] No outsider may eat the holy offering. Neither a guest in a priest's house nor a hired worker may eat it.
[Leviticus] [22]:[11] But if a priest buys a slave with his own money, that slave may eat of it, and so may those born in his household; they may eat his food.
[Leviticus] [22]:[12] If a priest's daughter marries someone outside a priestly family, she may not eat of the holy contributions.
[Leviticus] [22]:[13] But if a priest's daughter is widowed or divorced, has no children, and returns to live in her father's house as in her youth, she may eat her father's food. No outsider, however, may eat it.
[Leviticus] [22]:[14] Anyone who eats a holy offering by mistake must repay it, adding a fifth to its value, and give it to the priest.
[Leviticus] [22]:[15] The priests must not profane the holy offerings of the Israelites, which they present to the LORD,
[Leviticus] [22]:[16] and so bring guilt upon the people when they eat what is holy. For I am the LORD, who makes them holy.
[Leviticus] [22]:[17] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [22]:[18] Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites and say to them: When anyone of the house of Israel, or a foreigner living in Israel, presents an offering to the LORD as a burnt offering, whether to fulfill a vow or as a freewill gift,
[Leviticus] [22]:[19] it must be a male without blemish, from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats, if it is to be accepted for you.
[Leviticus] [22]:[20] You must not offer anything with a defect, for it will not be accepted for you.
[Leviticus] [22]:[21] When anyone brings a fellowship offering to the LORD from the herd or the flock, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill gift, it must be without blemish to be accepted; it must have no defect at all.
[Leviticus] [22]:[22] You must not offer to the LORD anything blind, injured, maimed, or having a wart, a running sore, or scabs. You must not place any of these on the altar as a food offering to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [22]:[23] An ox or a sheep with a deformed or stunted limb you may present as a freewill offering, but it will not be accepted for a vow.
[Leviticus] [22]:[24] You must not offer to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn, or cut. You must not do this anywhere in your land,
[Leviticus] [22]:[25] nor may you accept such animals from a foreigner to present as the food of your God. They are deformed and defective, and they will not be accepted for you.
[Leviticus] [22]:[26] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [22]:[27] When a calf, a lamb, or a kid is born, it must remain with its mother seven days. From the eighth day on it will be acceptable as a food offering to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [22]:[28] Do not slaughter a cow or a sheep together with its young on the same day.
[Leviticus] [22]:[29] When you sacrifice a thank offering to the LORD, offer it in a way that will be accepted for you.
[Leviticus] [22]:[30] It must be eaten that same day; leave none of it until morning. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [22]:[31] Keep my commands and do them. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [22]:[32] Do not profane my holy name. I must be acknowledged as holy among the Israelites. I am the LORD, who makes you holy,
[Leviticus] [22]:[33] who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [23]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [23]:[2] Speak to the Israelites and say to them: These are the appointed festivals of the LORD, which you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies—these are my appointed festivals.
[Leviticus] [23]:[3] For six days work is to be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a sacred assembly. You are to do no work at all. Wherever you live, it is a Sabbath to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [23]:[4] These are the appointed festivals of the LORD, the sacred assemblies you are to proclaim at their appointed times:
[Leviticus] [23]:[5] The LORD's Passover begins at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month.
[Leviticus] [23]:[6] On the fifteenth day of that month the LORD's Festival of Unleavened Bread begins; for seven days you are to eat unleavened bread.
[Leviticus] [23]:[7] On the first day hold a sacred assembly; do none of your ordinary work.
[Leviticus] [23]:[8] For seven days present a food offering to the LORD. On the seventh day hold a sacred assembly and do none of your ordinary work.
[Leviticus] [23]:[9] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [23]:[10] Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land I am giving you and reap its harvest, bring to the priest a sheaf of the first grain you harvest.
[Leviticus] [23]:[11] He is to wave the sheaf before the LORD so it will be accepted on your behalf; the priest is to wave it on the day after the Sabbath.
[Leviticus] [23]:[12] On the day you wave the sheaf, you must sacrifice as a burnt offering to the LORD a lamb a year old without defect,
[Leviticus] [23]:[13] together with its grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with oil—a food offering presented to the LORD, a pleasing aroma—and its drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine.
[Leviticus] [23]:[14] You must not eat any bread, or roasted or new grain, until the very day you bring this offering to your God. This is a lasting statute for the generations to come, wherever you live.
[Leviticus] [23]:[15] From the day after the Sabbath, the day you brought the sheaf of the wave offering, count off seven full weeks.
[Leviticus] [23]:[16] Count off fifty days up to the day after the seventh Sabbath, and then present a new grain offering to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [23]:[17] From wherever you live, bring two loaves made of two-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour, baked with yeast, as a wave offering of firstfruits to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [23]:[18] Along with the bread present seven male lambs, each a year old and without defect, one young bull, and two rams. They will be a burnt offering to the LORD, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings—a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [23]:[19] Then sacrifice one male goat as a sin offering and two lambs, each a year old, as a fellowship offering.
[Leviticus] [23]:[20] The priest is to wave the two lambs before the LORD as a wave offering, together with the bread of the firstfruits. They are a holy offering to the LORD for the priest.
[Leviticus] [23]:[21] On that same day you are to proclaim a sacred assembly and do none of your ordinary work. This is a lasting statute for the generations to come, wherever you live.
[Leviticus] [23]:[22] When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [23]:[23] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [23]:[24] Say to the Israelites: On the first day of the seventh month you are to have a day of rest, a sacred assembly commemorated with trumpet blasts.
[Leviticus] [23]:[25] Do none of your ordinary work, but present a food offering to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [23]:[26] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [23]:[27] Also, the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. Hold a sacred assembly, deny yourselves, and present a food offering to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [23]:[28] Do no work on that day, because it is the Day of Atonement, when atonement is made for you before the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [23]:[29] Anyone who does not deny himself on that day must be cut off from his people.
[Leviticus] [23]:[30] And anyone who does any work on that day—I will destroy that person from among his people.
[Leviticus] [23]:[31] You are to do no work at all. This is a lasting statute for the generations to come, wherever you live.
[Leviticus] [23]:[32] It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you must deny yourselves. From the evening of the ninth day of the month until the following evening you are to observe your Sabbath.
[Leviticus] [23]:[33] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [23]:[34] Say to the Israelites: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month the LORD's Festival of Tabernacles begins, and it lasts for seven days.
[Leviticus] [23]:[35] The first day is a sacred assembly; do none of your ordinary work.
[Leviticus] [23]:[36] For seven days present food offerings to the LORD, and on the eighth day hold a sacred assembly and present a food offering to the LORD. It is the closing assembly; do none of your ordinary work.
[Leviticus] [23]:[37] These are the appointed festivals of the LORD, which you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies for bringing food offerings to the LORD—burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings—each on its own day.
