[Leviticus] [23]:[38] These offerings are in addition to those for the LORD's Sabbaths and in addition to your gifts and whatever you have vowed and all the freewill offerings you give to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [23]:[39] So beginning with the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after you have gathered the crops of the land, celebrate the festival of the LORD for seven days; the first day is a day of rest, and the eighth day also is a day of rest.
[Leviticus] [23]:[40] On the first day you are to take fruit from majestic trees, palm fronds, leafy branches, and willows from the streams, and rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
[Leviticus] [23]:[41] Celebrate this as a festival to the LORD for seven days each year. This is a lasting statute for the generations to come; celebrate it in the seventh month.
[Leviticus] [23]:[42] Live in temporary shelters for seven days. All native-born Israelites are to live in such shelters,
[Leviticus] [23]:[43] so that your descendants will know that I had the Israelites live in shelters when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [23]:[44] So Moses announced to the Israelites the appointed festivals of the LORD.
[Leviticus] [24]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [24]:[2] Command the Israelites to bring you clear oil of pressed olives for the light, to keep the lamps burning continually.
[Leviticus] [24]:[3] Outside the curtain of the testimony in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall tend them before the LORD from evening until morning, continually. This is a lasting statute for your generations.
[Leviticus] [24]:[4] He shall keep the lamps on the pure gold lampstand burning before the LORD continually.
[Leviticus] [24]:[5] Take fine flour and bake twelve loaves of bread, using two-tenths of an ephah for each loaf.
[Leviticus] [24]:[6] Arrange them in two rows, six to a row, on the pure gold table before the LORD.
[Leviticus] [24]:[7] Place pure frankincense along each row, to serve as the memorial portion for the bread, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [24]:[8] Sabbath after Sabbath the bread is to be set out before the LORD, continually, on behalf of the Israelites, as a lasting covenant.
[Leviticus] [24]:[9] It belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy to him from the offerings made to the LORD by fire—his portion forever.
[Leviticus] [24]:[10] Now the son of an Israelite woman whose father was an Egyptian went out among the Israelites, and a fight broke out in the camp between him and an Israelite.
[Leviticus] [24]:[11] The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name with a curse, so they brought him to Moses. (His mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
[Leviticus] [24]:[12] They put him in custody until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them.
[Leviticus] [24]:[13] Then the LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [24]:[14] Take the blasphemer outside the camp. All who heard him are to lay their hands on his head, and the whole assembly is to stone him.
[Leviticus] [24]:[15] Say to the Israelites: Anyone who curses his God is to bear the consequences of his sin.
[Leviticus] [24]:[16] Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD must be put to death; the whole assembly is to stone him. Foreigner and native-born alike, whoever blasphemes the Name must die.
[Leviticus] [24]:[17] Whoever takes a human life must be put to death.
[Leviticus] [24]:[18] Whoever kills an animal must make restitution for it—life for life.
[Leviticus] [24]:[19] Whoever injures his neighbor is to receive the same injury in return:
[Leviticus] [24]:[20] fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As he has injured another, so is he to be injured.
[Leviticus] [24]:[21] Whoever kills an animal must make restitution, but whoever kills a human being must be put to death.
[Leviticus] [24]:[22] You are to have the same law for the foreigner as for the native-born, for I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [24]:[23] Then Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him. So the Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [25]:[1] The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai:
[Leviticus] [25]:[2] Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land I am giving you, the land itself is to observe a sabbath to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [25]:[3] For six years you may sow your field and for six years prune your vineyard and gather in its produce.
[Leviticus] [25]:[4] But in the seventh year the land is to have a sabbath of complete rest, a sabbath to the LORD. You shall not sow your field or prune your vineyard.
[Leviticus] [25]:[5] You shall not reap what grows of itself from your harvest, nor gather the grapes of your untended vines. It is to be a year of complete rest for the land.
[Leviticus] [25]:[6] Whatever the land yields during its sabbath will be food for you—for yourself, your male and female servants, and the hired worker and the resident alien who live among you,
[Leviticus] [25]:[7] and for your livestock and the wild animals in your land. All its produce may be eaten.
[Leviticus] [25]:[8] You shall count off seven sabbaths of years—seven times seven years—so that the period of the seven sabbaths of years comes to forty-nine years.
[Leviticus] [25]:[9] Then, on the tenth day of the seventh month, you shall sound the ram's horn loud and long; on the Day of Atonement you shall sound the horn throughout your land.
[Leviticus] [25]:[10] You shall consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you: each of you is to return to his own property, and each of you to his own clan.
[Leviticus] [25]:[11] The fiftieth year shall be a jubilee for you. You shall not sow, nor reap what grows of itself, nor gather the grapes from the untended vines.
[Leviticus] [25]:[12] For it is a jubilee; it shall be holy to you. You shall eat what the field itself produces.
[Leviticus] [25]:[13] In this Year of Jubilee each of you shall return to his own property.
[Leviticus] [25]:[14] When you sell land to your neighbor or buy land from him, do not take advantage of one another.
[Leviticus] [25]:[15] You are to buy from your neighbor according to the number of years since the jubilee, and he is to sell to you according to the number of harvest years remaining.
[Leviticus] [25]:[16] When the years are many, raise the price; when they are few, lower it—for what he is selling you is a number of harvests.
[Leviticus] [25]:[17] Do not take advantage of one another, but fear your God, for I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [25]:[18] Keep my statutes and observe my ordinances, and carry them out; then you will live securely in the land.
[Leviticus] [25]:[19] The land will yield its fruit, and you will eat your fill and live there in safety.
[Leviticus] [25]:[20] You may ask, "What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or gather in our crops?"
[Leviticus] [25]:[21] I will send you such a blessing in the sixth year that the land will yield enough for three years.
[Leviticus] [25]:[22] You will sow in the eighth year and eat from the old crop; you will keep eating from the old harvest until the crop of the ninth year comes in.
[Leviticus] [25]:[23] The land must not be sold permanently, because the land is mine; you are but aliens and tenants with me.
[Leviticus] [25]:[24] Throughout the land you hold as your possession, you must allow the land to be redeemed.
[Leviticus] [25]:[25] If one of your countrymen becomes poor and sells part of his property, his nearest relative is to come and redeem what his brother has sold.
[Leviticus] [25]:[26] If a man has no one to redeem it for him but later prospers and acquires enough for its redemption,
[Leviticus] [25]:[27] he is to count the years since the sale and pay back the balance to the man to whom he sold it; then he may return to his property.
[Leviticus] [25]:[28] But if he cannot raise enough to repay him, what he sold remains in the hands of the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. In the jubilee it shall be released, and he may return to his property.
[Leviticus] [25]:[29] If a man sells a house in a walled city, he retains the right of redemption for a full year after the sale; during that time he may redeem it.
[Leviticus] [25]:[30] If it is not redeemed before a full year has passed, the house in the walled city belongs permanently to the buyer and his descendants. It is not to be released in the jubilee.
[Leviticus] [25]:[31] But houses in villages with no walls around them are to be considered as open country. They may be redeemed, and they are to be released in the jubilee.
[Leviticus] [25]:[32] As for the cities of the Levites, they always retain the right to redeem the houses in the cities they possess.
[Leviticus] [25]:[33] If it is not redeemed by one of the Levites, the house that was sold in the city he possesses is to be released in the Year of Jubilee, because the houses in the Levites' cities are their possession among the Israelites.
[Leviticus] [25]:[34] But the pastureland belonging to their cities must not be sold; it is their permanent possession.
[Leviticus] [25]:[35] If one of your countrymen becomes poor and cannot support himself among you, help him as you would an alien or a temporary resident, so that he can go on living with you.
[Leviticus] [25]:[36] Do not charge him interest or make a profit from him, but fear your God, so that your countryman may continue to live among you.
[Leviticus] [25]:[37] Do not lend him money at interest or sell him food at a profit.
[Leviticus] [25]:[38] I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
[Leviticus] [25]:[39] If one of your countrymen becomes poor among you and sells himself to you, do not make him work as a slave.
[Leviticus] [25]:[40] He is to be treated as a hired worker or a temporary resident among you; he is to work for you until the Year of Jubilee.
[Leviticus] [25]:[41] Then he and his children are to be released, and he will go back to his own clan and to the property of his fathers.
[Leviticus] [25]:[42] For they are my servants, whom I brought out of Egypt; they are not to be sold as slaves.
[Leviticus] [25]:[43] Do not rule over them harshly, but fear your God.
[Leviticus] [25]:[44] Your male and female slaves are to come from the nations around you; from them you may buy slaves.
[Leviticus] [25]:[45] You may also buy the children of the temporary residents living among you, and members of their clans born in your land, and they will become your property.
[Leviticus] [25]:[46] You may leave them to your children as an inherited possession and make them slaves for life. But you must not rule harshly over your fellow Israelites.
[Leviticus] [25]:[47] If an alien or a temporary resident among you prospers, and one of your countrymen becomes poor and sells himself to that alien or to a member of the alien's clan,
[Leviticus] [25]:[48] he retains the right of redemption after he has sold himself. One of his relatives may redeem him:
[Leviticus] [25]:[49] an uncle or a cousin or any blood relative in his clan may redeem him. Or, if he prospers, he may redeem himself.
[Leviticus] [25]:[50] He and his buyer are to count the years from the year he sold himself up to the Year of Jubilee. The price of his release is to be based on the number of years, figured at the rate paid to a hired worker.
[Leviticus] [25]:[51] If many years remain, he must pay for his redemption a larger share of the price paid for him.
[Leviticus] [25]:[52] If only a few years remain until the Year of Jubilee, he is to figure it out and pay for his redemption accordingly.
[Leviticus] [25]:[53] He is to be treated as a hired worker year by year, and his master must not rule over him harshly in your sight.
[Leviticus] [25]:[54] If he is not redeemed in any of these ways, he and his children are to be released in the Year of Jubilee.
[Leviticus] [25]:[55] For the Israelites belong to me as servants; they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [26]:[1] Do not make idols for yourselves; do not set up a carved image or a sacred pillar, and do not place a figured stone in your land to bow down before it, for I am the LORD your God.
[Leviticus] [26]:[2] Keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [26]:[3] If you live by my statutes and keep my commandments and carry them out,
[Leviticus] [26]:[4] I will give you rain in its season, the land will yield its produce, and the trees of the field will give their fruit.
[Leviticus] [26]:[5] Your threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest until sowing time. You will eat your bread until you are satisfied and live securely in your land.
[Leviticus] [26]:[6] I will grant peace in the land; you will lie down with no one to make you afraid. I will rid the land of dangerous beasts, and no sword will pass through your land.
[Leviticus] [26]:[7] You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
[Leviticus] [26]:[8] Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand; your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
[Leviticus] [26]:[9] I will turn toward you, make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will establish my covenant with you.
[Leviticus] [26]:[10] You will still be eating last year's harvest when you must clear it out to make room for the new.
[Leviticus] [26]:[11] I will set my dwelling among you, and I will not reject you.
[Leviticus] [26]:[12] I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people.
[Leviticus] [26]:[13] I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be their slaves. I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.
[Leviticus] [26]:[14] But if you will not listen to me and will not carry out all these commandments,
[Leviticus] [26]:[15] if you reject my statutes and despise my ordinances, refusing to keep all my commandments and breaking my covenant,
[Leviticus] [26]:[16] then I in turn will do this to you: I will bring terror upon you—wasting disease and fever that destroy the eyes and drain away life. You will sow your seed in vain, for your enemies will eat it.
[Leviticus] [26]:[17] I will set my face against you, and you will be struck down before your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when no one is chasing you.
[Leviticus] [26]:[18] If after all this you still will not listen to me, I will go on to discipline you seven times over for your sins.
[Leviticus] [26]:[19] I will break your stubborn pride. I will make your sky like iron and your land like bronze.
[Leviticus] [26]:[20] Your strength will be spent for nothing, for your land will not yield its produce, and the trees of the land will not give their fruit.
[Leviticus] [26]:[21] If you continue to defy me and refuse to listen to me, I will multiply your afflictions seven times over, as your sins deserve.
[Leviticus] [26]:[22] I will send wild animals against you; they will rob you of your children, destroy your livestock, and reduce your numbers, and your roads will lie deserted.
[Leviticus] [26]:[23] If even then you are not corrected by me but continue to defy me,
[Leviticus] [26]:[24] then I too will walk in hostility against you, and I myself will strike you seven times over for your sins.
[Leviticus] [26]:[25] I will bring the sword against you to avenge the covenant. When you withdraw into your cities, I will send a plague among you, and you will be handed over to the enemy.
[Leviticus] [26]:[26] When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven and dole it out to you by weight; you will eat and not be satisfied.
[Leviticus] [26]:[27] If after all this you still will not listen to me but continue to defy me,
[Leviticus] [26]:[28] then in furious defiance I will oppose you, and I myself will discipline you seven times over for your sins.
[Leviticus] [26]:[29] You will eat the flesh of your sons; the flesh of your daughters you will eat.
[Leviticus] [26]:[30] I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars, and pile your corpses on the lifeless forms of your idols; and I will reject you.
[Leviticus] [26]:[31] I will turn your cities into ruins and lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will take no delight in the pleasing aroma of your offerings.
[Leviticus] [26]:[32] I myself will lay the land waste, so that your enemies who settle in it will be appalled at it.
[Leviticus] [26]:[33] I will scatter you among the nations and unsheathe the sword after you. Your land will become a wasteland and your cities a ruin.
[Leviticus] [26]:[34] Then the land will enjoy its sabbaths all the days it lies desolate while you are in the land of your enemies; then the land will rest and enjoy its sabbaths.
[Leviticus] [26]:[35] All the days of its desolation it will have the rest it did not have during your sabbaths when you lived on it.
[Leviticus] [26]:[36] As for those of you who survive, I will fill their hearts with dread in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a windblown leaf will send them running; they will flee as though from the sword and fall when no one is chasing them.
[Leviticus] [26]:[37] They will stumble over one another as if fleeing the sword, though no one pursues. You will have no power to stand before your enemies.
[Leviticus] [26]:[38] You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will devour you.
[Leviticus] [26]:[39] Those of you who are left will waste away in the lands of your enemies because of their guilt; they will waste away because of their fathers' guilt as well.
[Leviticus] [26]:[40] But if they confess their guilt and the guilt of their fathers—their treachery against me and their defiance of me,
[Leviticus] [26]:[41] I too walked against them in hostility and brought them into the land of their enemies—if then their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they make amends for their guilt,
[Leviticus] [26]:[42] I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham I will remember; and I will remember the land.
[Leviticus] [26]:[43] But the land will be left empty by them and will enjoy its sabbaths while it lies desolate without them, and they will make amends for their guilt, because they rejected my ordinances and their soul despised my statutes.
[Leviticus] [26]:[44] Yet even then, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or despise them so as to destroy them completely and break my covenant with them, for I am the LORD their God.
[Leviticus] [26]:[45] For their sake I will remember the covenant with their ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, to be their God. I am the LORD.
[Leviticus] [26]:[46] These are the statutes, ordinances, and instructions that the LORD established between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai through Moses.
[Leviticus] [27]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [27]:[2] Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When anyone makes a special vow to the LORD involving the value set on a person,
[Leviticus] [27]:[3] the value for a male between twenty and sixty years old shall be fifty shekels of silver, by the sanctuary shekel.
[Leviticus] [27]:[4] If it is a female, the value shall be thirty shekels.
[Leviticus] [27]:[5] For someone between five and twenty years old, the value for a male shall be twenty shekels and for a female ten shekels.
[Leviticus] [27]:[6] For a child between one month and five years old, the value for a male shall be five shekels of silver and for a female three shekels of silver.
[Leviticus] [27]:[7] For someone sixty years old or over, the value for a male shall be fifteen shekels and for a female ten shekels.
[Leviticus] [27]:[8] If the person is too poor to pay the set value, he shall be brought before the priest, and the priest shall set the value according to what the one making the vow can afford.
[Leviticus] [27]:[9] If the vow concerns an animal that may be offered to the LORD, every such animal given to the LORD becomes holy.
[Leviticus] [27]:[10] He must not exchange it or substitute a good one for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one. If he does substitute one animal for another, both it and its substitute become holy.
[Leviticus] [27]:[11] If the vow concerns an unclean animal, one that may not be offered to the LORD, the animal shall be presented before the priest,
[Leviticus] [27]:[12] and the priest shall set its value, whether high or low. Whatever value the priest sets shall stand.
[Leviticus] [27]:[13] If the owner does redeem it, he must add a fifth to the set value.
[Leviticus] [27]:[14] If anyone dedicates his house as holy to the LORD, the priest shall set its value, whether high or low. Whatever the priest sets, that is what it shall be.
[Leviticus] [27]:[15] If the one who dedicated the house wishes to redeem it, he must add a fifth to its value in silver, and it shall be his again.
[Leviticus] [27]:[16] If anyone dedicates to the LORD part of the field he has inherited, its value shall be set according to the seed required for it: fifty shekels of silver for each homer of barley seed.
[Leviticus] [27]:[17] If he dedicates his field during the Year of Jubilee, the full value shall stand.
[Leviticus] [27]:[18] But if he dedicates it after the Jubilee, the priest shall calculate the price according to the years remaining until the next Year of Jubilee, and the value shall be reduced accordingly.
[Leviticus] [27]:[19] If the one who dedicated the field wishes to redeem it, he must add a fifth to its value in silver, and it shall revert to him.
[Leviticus] [27]:[20] But if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold it to someone else, it can never be redeemed.
[Leviticus] [27]:[21] When the field is released in the Jubilee, it becomes holy to the LORD, like a field placed under the ban; it shall become the priest's holding.
[Leviticus] [27]:[22] If anyone dedicates to the LORD a field he has bought, one that is not part of his inherited land,
[Leviticus] [27]:[23] the priest shall calculate its value up to the Year of Jubilee, and the man shall pay that amount on that day as something holy to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [27]:[24] In the Year of Jubilee the field shall return to the one from whom it was bought, the one whose inherited land it is.
[Leviticus] [27]:[25] Every value shall be set by the sanctuary shekel: twenty gerahs to the shekel.
[Leviticus] [27]:[26] But no one may dedicate the firstborn of an animal, since as a firstborn it already belongs to the LORD; whether ox or sheep, it is the LORD's.
[Leviticus] [27]:[27] If it is an unclean animal, the owner may buy it back at its set value, adding a fifth to it; if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold at its set value.
[Leviticus] [27]:[28] But nothing that a person devotes to the LORD from all he owns—whether human being or animal or inherited land—may be sold or redeemed. Everything so devoted is most holy to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [27]:[29] No person who has been devoted to destruction may be ransomed; he must be put to death.
[Leviticus] [27]:[30] Every tithe of the land, whether from the seed of the ground or the fruit of the trees, belongs to the LORD; it is holy to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [27]:[31] If anyone wishes to redeem part of his tithe, he must add a fifth to it.
[Leviticus] [27]:[32] Every tithe of the herd and flock—of all that passes under the shepherd's rod, every tenth animal—shall be holy to the LORD.
[Leviticus] [27]:[33] He must not examine whether it is good or bad, nor make any substitution. If he does substitute one for another, both it and its substitute become holy and cannot be redeemed.
[Leviticus] [27]:[34] These are the commandments the LORD gave Moses on Mount Sinai for the Israelites.
[Numbers] [1]:[1] The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month of the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt. He said:
[Numbers] [1]:[2] "Take a census of the whole community of Israel, clan by clan and family by family, listing every male by name, one by one—
[Numbers] [1]:[3] twenty years old and upward—everyone in Israel fit for military service. You and Aaron are to register them by their divisions.
[Numbers] [1]:[4] One man from each tribe shall assist you, each the head of his family.
[Numbers] [1]:[5] These are the names of the men who will stand with you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
[Numbers] [1]:[6] from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
[Numbers] [1]:[7] from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
[Numbers] [1]:[8] from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
[Numbers] [1]:[9] from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
[Numbers] [1]:[10] from the sons of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
[Numbers] [1]:[11] from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
[Numbers] [1]:[12] from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
[Numbers] [1]:[13] from Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran;
[Numbers] [1]:[14] from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
[Numbers] [1]:[15] from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan."
[Numbers] [1]:[16] These were the men appointed from the community, the leaders of their ancestral tribes, the heads of the clans of Israel.
[Numbers] [1]:[17] So Moses and Aaron took these men who had been designated by name,
[Numbers] [1]:[18] and on the first day of the second month they assembled the whole community. The people registered their ancestry by clan and family, and all the men twenty years old and upward were listed by name, one by one,
[Numbers] [1]:[19] just as the LORD had commanded Moses. And so he counted them in the wilderness of Sinai.
[Numbers] [1]:[20] The descendants of Reuben, Israel's firstborn: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, one by one, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
[Numbers] [1]:[21] The number from the tribe of Reuben was 46,500.
[Numbers] [1]:[22] The descendants of Simeon: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were counted and listed by name, one by one, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
[Numbers] [1]:[23] The number from the tribe of Simeon was 59,300.
[Numbers] [1]:[24] The descendants of Gad: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
[Numbers] [1]:[25] The number from the tribe of Gad was 45,650.
[Numbers] [1]:[26] The descendants of Judah: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
[Numbers] [1]:[27] The number from the tribe of Judah was 74,600.
[Numbers] [1]:[28] The descendants of Issachar: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
[Numbers] [1]:[29] The number from the tribe of Issachar was 54,400.
[Numbers] [1]:[30] The descendants of Zebulun: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
[Numbers] [1]:[31] The number from the tribe of Zebulun was 57,400.
[Numbers] [1]:[32] From the sons of Joseph—the descendants of Ephraim: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
[Numbers] [1]:[33] The number from the tribe of Ephraim was 40,500.
[Numbers] [1]:[34] The descendants of Manasseh: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
[Numbers] [1]:[35] The number from the tribe of Manasseh was 32,200.
[Numbers] [1]:[36] The descendants of Benjamin: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
[Numbers] [1]:[37] The number from the tribe of Benjamin was 35,400.
[Numbers] [1]:[38] The descendants of Dan: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
[Numbers] [1]:[39] The number from the tribe of Dan was 62,700.
[Numbers] [1]:[40] The descendants of Asher: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
[Numbers] [1]:[41] The number from the tribe of Asher was 41,500.
[Numbers] [1]:[42] The descendants of Naphtali: all the men twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were listed by name, according to their genealogy, by clan and family.
[Numbers] [1]:[43] The number from the tribe of Naphtali was 53,400.
[Numbers] [1]:[44] These were the men counted by Moses and Aaron and the twelve leaders of Israel, each one representing his family.
[Numbers] [1]:[45] So all the Israelites twenty years old and upward who were fit for military service were counted by their families.
[Numbers] [1]:[46] The total came to 603,550.
[Numbers] [1]:[47] The Levites, however, were not counted among them by their ancestral tribe.
[Numbers] [1]:[48] Then the LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [1]:[49] "The tribe of Levi, however, you are not to count; do not include them in the census of the Israelites.
[Numbers] [1]:[50] Instead, put the Levites in charge of the tabernacle of the covenant law, with all its furnishings and everything that belongs to it. They are to carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings; they are to care for it and camp around it.
[Numbers] [1]:[51] Whenever the tabernacle is to move, the Levites shall take it down, and whenever it is to be set up, the Levites shall raise it. Anyone else who comes near it must be put to death.
[Numbers] [1]:[52] The Israelites are to camp by divisions, each in his own camp under his own banner.
[Numbers] [1]:[53] But the Levites are to camp around the tabernacle of the covenant law, so that no wrath may fall on the community of Israel. The Levites are to keep watch over the tabernacle of the covenant law."
[Numbers] [1]:[54] The Israelites did just as the LORD had commanded Moses; everything he commanded, so they did.
[Numbers] [2]:[1] The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
[Numbers] [2]:[2] "The Israelites are to camp each under his own standard, with the banners of their fathers' houses. They shall camp at some distance facing the tent of meeting, around it on every side.
[Numbers] [2]:[3] On the east side, toward the sunrise, the divisions of the camp of Judah shall camp under their standard. The leader of the people of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab,
[Numbers] [2]:[4] and his division numbers 74,600.
[Numbers] [2]:[5] The tribe of Issachar shall camp next to them. The leader of the people of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar,
[Numbers] [2]:[6] and his division numbers 54,400.
[Numbers] [2]:[7] Then the tribe of Zebulun. The leader of the people of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon,
[Numbers] [2]:[8] and his division numbers 57,400.
[Numbers] [2]:[9] All those enrolled in the camp of Judah, by their divisions, number 186,400. They shall set out first.
[Numbers] [2]:[10] On the south side shall be the divisions of the camp of Reuben under their standard. The leader of the people of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur,
[Numbers] [2]:[11] and his division numbers 46,500.
[Numbers] [2]:[12] The tribe of Simeon shall camp next to them. The leader of the people of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai,
[Numbers] [2]:[13] and his division numbers 59,300.
[Numbers] [2]:[14] Then the tribe of Gad. The leader of the people of Gad is Eliasaph son of Reuel,
[Numbers] [2]:[15] and his division numbers 45,650.
[Numbers] [2]:[16] All those enrolled in the camp of Reuben, by their divisions, number 151,450. They shall set out second.
[Numbers] [2]:[17] Then the tent of meeting shall set out, with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. They shall set out in the same order in which they camp, each in his own position, under their standards.
[Numbers] [2]:[18] On the west side shall be the divisions of the camp of Ephraim under their standard. The leader of the people of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud,
[Numbers] [2]:[19] and his division numbers 40,500.
[Numbers] [2]:[20] Next to them shall be the tribe of Manasseh. The leader of the people of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,
[Numbers] [2]:[21] and his division numbers 32,200.
[Numbers] [2]:[22] Then the tribe of Benjamin. The leader of the people of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni,
[Numbers] [2]:[23] and his division numbers 35,400.
[Numbers] [2]:[24] All those enrolled in the camp of Ephraim, by their divisions, number 108,100. They shall set out third.
[Numbers] [2]:[25] On the north side shall be the divisions of the camp of Dan under their standard. The leader of the people of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai,
[Numbers] [2]:[26] and his division numbers 62,700.
[Numbers] [2]:[27] The tribe of Asher shall camp next to them. The leader of the people of Asher is Pagiel son of Ochran,
[Numbers] [2]:[28] and his division numbers 41,500.
[Numbers] [2]:[29] Then the tribe of Naphtali. The leader of the people of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan,
[Numbers] [2]:[30] and his division numbers 53,400.
[Numbers] [2]:[31] All those enrolled in the camp of Dan number 157,600. They shall set out last, under their standards."
[Numbers] [2]:[32] These were the Israelites enrolled by their fathers' houses. All those enrolled in the camps, by their divisions, numbered 603,550.
[Numbers] [2]:[33] But the Levites were not counted among the other Israelites, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [2]:[34] So the Israelites did everything the LORD had commanded Moses: that is how they camped under their standards, and that is how they set out, each with his clan and his father's house.
[Numbers] [3]:[1] These are the descendants of Aaron and Moses at the time when the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
[Numbers] [3]:[2] These are the names of Aaron's sons: Nadab the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
[Numbers] [3]:[3] These are the names of Aaron's sons, the anointed priests, ordained to minister in the priesthood.
[Numbers] [3]:[4] But Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during the lifetime of their father Aaron.
[Numbers] [3]:[5] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [3]:[6] Bring forward the tribe of Levi and present them to Aaron the priest, to assist him.
[Numbers] [3]:[7] They shall carry out duties for him and for the whole congregation before the tent of meeting, doing the work of the tabernacle.
[Numbers] [3]:[8] They shall take charge of all the furnishings of the tent of meeting and carry out the duties on behalf of the Israelites, doing the work of the tabernacle.
[Numbers] [3]:[9] Assign the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are given to him as a gift from among the Israelites.
[Numbers] [3]:[10] You shall appoint Aaron and his sons to guard their priesthood. Any outsider who comes near shall be put to death.
[Numbers] [3]:[11] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [3]:[12] I myself have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites. The Levites shall be mine,
[Numbers] [3]:[13] for every firstborn is mine. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to myself every firstborn in Israel, both human and animal. They are mine. I am the LORD.
[Numbers] [3]:[14] The LORD said to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai:
[Numbers] [3]:[15] Register the sons of Levi by their ancestral houses and clans. Count every male a month old and older.
[Numbers] [3]:[16] So Moses registered them at the command of the LORD, as he had been ordered.
[Numbers] [3]:[17] These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
[Numbers] [3]:[18] These are the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
[Numbers] [3]:[19] The sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
[Numbers] [3]:[20] The sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites by their ancestral houses.
[Numbers] [3]:[21] To Gershon belonged the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites; these are the Gershonite clans.
[Numbers] [3]:[22] Their enrollment, counting every male a month old and older, came to 7,500.
[Numbers] [3]:[23] The Gershonite clans were to camp behind the tabernacle, on the west.
[Numbers] [3]:[24] The leader of the ancestral house of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.
[Numbers] [3]:[25] The responsibility of the sons of Gershon at the tent of meeting was the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, the curtain at the entrance of the tent of meeting,
[Numbers] [3]:[26] the hangings of the courtyard, which enclose the tabernacle and the altar on every side, the curtain at the entrance of the courtyard, and its ropes—together with all the work connected with them.
[Numbers] [3]:[27] To Kohath belonged the clans of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites; these are the Kohathite clans.
[Numbers] [3]:[28] Counting every male a month old and older, they numbered 8,600, charged with the care of the sanctuary.
[Numbers] [3]:[29] The clans of the Kohathites were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
[Numbers] [3]:[30] The leader of the ancestral house of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
[Numbers] [3]:[31] Their responsibility was the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the utensils of the sanctuary used in ministering, the curtain, and all the work connected with them.
[Numbers] [3]:[32] The chief leader of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest; he had oversight of those charged with the care of the sanctuary.
[Numbers] [3]:[33] To Merari belonged the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites; these are the clans of Merari.
[Numbers] [3]:[34] Their enrollment, counting every male a month old and older, came to 6,200.
[Numbers] [3]:[35] The leader of the ancestral house of the Merarite clans was Zuriel son of Abihail. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
[Numbers] [3]:[36] The sons of Merari were appointed to care for the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, posts, and bases, all its equipment, and all the work connected with them,
[Numbers] [3]:[37] as well as the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, pegs, and ropes.
[Numbers] [3]:[38] Moses, Aaron, and Aaron's sons were to camp in front of the tabernacle, toward the east, before the tent of meeting, guarding the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Any outsider who came near was to be put to death.
[Numbers] [3]:[39] The total number of the Levites registered by Moses and Aaron at the LORD's command, clan by clan, every male a month old and older, was 22,000.
[Numbers] [3]:[40] The LORD said to Moses: Register every firstborn male of the Israelites a month old and older, and record their names.
[Numbers] [3]:[41] Take the Levites for me—I am the LORD—in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the livestock of the Israelites.
[Numbers] [3]:[42] So Moses registered every firstborn among the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded him.
[Numbers] [3]:[43] The total number of firstborn males a month old and older, listed by name, came to 22,273.
[Numbers] [3]:[44] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [3]:[45] Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites shall be mine. I am the LORD.
[Numbers] [3]:[46] As for the redemption of the 273 firstborn Israelites who exceed the number of the Levites,
[Numbers] [3]:[47] collect five shekels for each person, by the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.
[Numbers] [3]:[48] Give the silver to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for those who exceed the number.
[Numbers] [3]:[49] So Moses collected the redemption money from those left over beyond the ones the Levites had redeemed.
[Numbers] [3]:[50] From the firstborn of the Israelites he collected 1,365 shekels of silver, by the sanctuary shekel.
[Numbers] [3]:[51] Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons at the LORD's command, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [4]:[1] The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
[Numbers] [4]:[2] "Take a census of the Kohathites among the Levites, by their clans and their ancestral houses,
[Numbers] [4]:[3] from thirty years old up to fifty years old—everyone who is fit for service, to do the work of the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [4]:[4] This is the service of the Kohathites at the tent of meeting: the most holy things.
[Numbers] [4]:[5] When the camp is to set out, Aaron and his sons shall come and take down the veil that screens the Most Holy Place, and cover the ark of the testimony with it.
[Numbers] [4]:[6] Over that they shall put a covering of fine leather, spread a cloth of solid blue on top, and set its poles in place.
[Numbers] [4]:[7] Over the table of the Presence they shall spread a blue cloth and set on it the plates, the dishes for incense, the bowls, and the pitchers for the drink offering; the bread of the continual offering shall also be on it.
[Numbers] [4]:[8] They shall spread a scarlet cloth over these, cover the table with a covering of fine leather, and set its poles in place.
[Numbers] [4]:[9] They shall take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand for the light, with its lamps, its tongs, its trays, and all the vessels for its oil with which it is tended.
[Numbers] [4]:[10] Then they shall wrap it and all its utensils in a covering of fine leather and place it on the carrying frame.
[Numbers] [4]:[11] Over the golden altar they shall spread a blue cloth, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and insert its poles.
[Numbers] [4]:[12] They shall take all the utensils used for the service in the sanctuary, wrap them in a blue cloth, cover them with a covering of fine leather, and place them on the carrying frame.
[Numbers] [4]:[13] They shall remove the ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.
[Numbers] [4]:[14] On it they shall lay all the utensils used in serving at the altar: the fire pans, the forks, the shovels, and the basins—all the utensils of the altar. Then they shall spread over it a covering of fine leather and insert its poles.
[Numbers] [4]:[15] When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy things and all the holy furnishings as the camp sets out, then the Kohathites shall come to carry them. But they must not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the things the Kohathites are to carry in the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [4]:[16] Eleazar son of Aaron the priest shall have charge of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering, and the anointing oil. He shall have oversight of the whole tabernacle and everything in it, including the holy things and their utensils."
[Numbers] [4]:[17] The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
[Numbers] [4]:[18] "Do not let the clans of the Kohathites be cut off from among the Levites.
[Numbers] [4]:[19] Do this for them, so that they may live and not die when they come near the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall go in and assign each man his work and what he is to carry.
[Numbers] [4]:[20] But the Kohathites must not go in to look at the holy things, even for a moment, or they will die."
[Numbers] [4]:[21] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [4]:[22] "Take a census of the Gershonites as well, by their ancestral houses and their clans,
[Numbers] [4]:[23] from thirty years old up to fifty years old. Register all who are fit for service, to do the work of the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [4]:[24] This is the service of the Gershonite clans, their duties and their loads:
[Numbers] [4]:[25] They shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting with its covering and the covering of fine leather that goes over it, the screen for the entrance to the tent of meeting,
[Numbers] [4]:[26] the hangings of the courtyard, the screen for the entrance at the gate of the courtyard surrounding the tabernacle and the altar, their ropes, and all the equipment for their service. They shall do everything that needs to be done with these things.
[Numbers] [4]:[27] All the service of the Gershonites shall be under the direction of Aaron and his sons, both what they carry and all their other work. You shall assign to them the responsibility for everything they carry.
[Numbers] [4]:[28] This is the service of the Gershonite clans at the tent of meeting, and their duties shall be under the oversight of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
[Numbers] [4]:[29] Register the Merarites by their clans and their ancestral houses,
[Numbers] [4]:[30] from thirty years old up to fifty years old—all who are fit for service, to do the work of the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [4]:[31] This is what they are charged to carry as their whole service at the tent of meeting: the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, posts, and bases,
[Numbers] [4]:[32] as well as the posts of the surrounding courtyard with their bases, pegs, and ropes, and all their equipment and everything used with them. You shall assign by name the items each man is charged to carry.
[Numbers] [4]:[33] This is the service of the Merarite clans, their whole service at the tent of meeting, under the oversight of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest."
[Numbers] [4]:[34] So Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the congregation registered the Kohathites by their clans and their ancestral houses,
[Numbers] [4]:[35] from thirty years old up to fifty years old—all who were fit for service, for work at the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [4]:[36] The number registered, by their clans, was 2,750.
[Numbers] [4]:[37] These were all who were registered from the Kohathite clans, everyone who served at the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron registered at the LORD's command through Moses.
[Numbers] [4]:[38] The Gershonites were registered by their clans and their ancestral houses,
[Numbers] [4]:[39] from thirty years old up to fifty years old—all who came to serve, to do the work at the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [4]:[40] The number registered, by their clans and ancestral houses, was 2,630.
[Numbers] [4]:[41] These were all who were registered from the Gershonite clans, everyone who served at the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron registered at the LORD's command.
[Numbers] [4]:[42] The Merarites were registered by their clans and their ancestral houses,
[Numbers] [4]:[43] from thirty years old up to fifty years old—all who were fit for service, for work at the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [4]:[44] The number registered, by their clans, was 3,200.
[Numbers] [4]:[45] These were all who were registered from the Merarite clans, whom Moses and Aaron registered at the LORD's command through Moses.
[Numbers] [4]:[46] So all the Levites whom Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel registered by their clans and their ancestral houses,
[Numbers] [4]:[47] from thirty years old up to fifty years old—everyone who came to do the work of serving and carrying at the tent of meeting—
[Numbers] [4]:[48] numbered 8,580.
[Numbers] [4]:[49] At the LORD's command they were registered through Moses, each man to his own task and his own load; so they were counted, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [5]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [5]:[2] "Command the Israelites to send out of the camp everyone with a skin disease, everyone with a discharge, and everyone who is unclean through contact with a dead body.
[Numbers] [5]:[3] Send away male and female alike; send them outside the camp, so that they do not defile their camp, where I dwell among them."
[Numbers] [5]:[4] So the Israelites did this and sent them outside the camp. Just as the LORD had said to Moses, so the Israelites did.
[Numbers] [5]:[5] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [5]:[6] "Say to the Israelites: When a man or a woman commits any sin against another person, thereby breaking faith with the LORD, that person is guilty.
[Numbers] [5]:[7] They must confess the sin they have committed. The guilty one shall make full restitution, adding a fifth of its value to it, and give it to the one who was wronged.
[Numbers] [5]:[8] But if the wronged person has no close relative to receive the restitution, it belongs to the LORD and shall be given to the priest, along with the ram of atonement by which atonement is made for the guilty one.
[Numbers] [5]:[9] Every contribution from all the holy gifts that the Israelites bring to the priest belongs to him.
[Numbers] [5]:[10] Each person's holy gifts are his own, but whatever he gives to the priest belongs to the priest."
[Numbers] [5]:[11] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [5]:[12] "Speak to the Israelites and say to them: If a man's wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him,
[Numbers] [5]:[13] if another man sleeps with her and it is hidden from her husband—she has defiled herself in secret, with no witness against her, and she was not caught in the act—
[Numbers] [5]:[14] and if a spirit of jealousy comes over the husband and he suspects his wife, whether she has defiled herself or not—
[Numbers] [5]:[15] then the man shall bring his wife to the priest. He shall also bring on her behalf an offering of a tenth of an ephah of barley flour.* He must not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance that brings sin to mind. [*footnote: About 3.5 pounds, or 1.6 kilograms.]
[Numbers] [5]:[16] The priest shall bring her forward and have her stand before the LORD.
[Numbers] [5]:[17] Then the priest shall take holy water in a clay jar, and take some of the dust from the floor of the tabernacle and put it into the water.
[Numbers] [5]:[18] After the priest has had the woman stand before the LORD, he shall loosen her hair and place in her hands the grain offering of remembrance, the grain offering for jealousy, while he himself holds the bitter water that brings a curse.
[Numbers] [5]:[19] Then the priest shall put her under oath and say to her: 'If no man has slept with you and you have not gone astray into impurity while under your husband's authority, may you be free from this bitter water that brings a curse.
[Numbers] [5]:[20] But if you have gone astray while under your husband's authority and have defiled yourself by sleeping with a man other than your husband'—
[Numbers] [5]:[21] here the priest shall put the woman under this oath of cursing—'may the LORD make you a curse and a byword among your people, making your womb miscarry and your belly swell.
[Numbers] [5]:[22] May this water that brings a curse enter your body, so that your belly swells and your womb miscarries.' And the woman shall say, 'Amen. Amen.'
[Numbers] [5]:[23] Then the priest shall write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water.
[Numbers] [5]:[24] He shall have the woman drink the bitter water that brings a curse, and this water will enter her and cause bitter suffering.
[Numbers] [5]:[25] The priest shall take the grain offering for jealousy from her hand, wave it before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
[Numbers] [5]:[26] He shall take a handful of the grain offering as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar; after that, he shall have the woman drink the water.
[Numbers] [5]:[27] When he has made her drink the water, then if she has defiled herself and been unfaithful to her husband, the water that brings a curse will enter her and cause bitter suffering; her belly will swell and her womb will miscarry, and she will become a curse among her people.
[Numbers] [5]:[28] But if the woman has not defiled herself and is clean, she will be cleared of guilt and will be able to bear children.
[Numbers] [5]:[29] This, then, is the law for jealousy, when a wife goes astray and defiles herself while under her husband's authority,
[Numbers] [5]:[30] or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he suspects his wife. The priest shall have her stand before the LORD and carry out this entire law for her.
[Numbers] [5]:[31] The husband will be free from guilt, but the woman will bear the consequences of her sin."
[Numbers] [6]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [6]:[2] Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When a man or a woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to set themselves apart for the LORD,
[Numbers] [6]:[3] they must abstain from wine and strong drink. They must not drink vinegar made from wine or from strong drink, nor drink any juice of grapes, nor eat grapes, fresh or dried.
[Numbers] [6]:[4] As long as they are set apart, they must eat nothing that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or the skins.
[Numbers] [6]:[5] As long as their vow of separation lasts, no razor may touch their head. Until the time is complete for which they set themselves apart to the LORD, they are holy; they must let the hair of their head grow long.
[Numbers] [6]:[6] As long as they are set apart for the LORD, they must not go near a dead body.
[Numbers] [6]:[7] Even for their father or mother, brother or sister, they must not make themselves unclean when these die, because the sign of their separation to God is upon their head.
[Numbers] [6]:[8] Throughout the days of their separation they are holy to the LORD.
[Numbers] [6]:[9] If someone dies suddenly beside them, defiling their consecrated head, they must shave their head on the day of their cleansing—on the seventh day they shall shave it.
[Numbers] [6]:[10] On the eighth day they must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [6]:[11] The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and make atonement for them, because they sinned by being in the presence of the dead. That same day they shall consecrate their head again.
[Numbers] [6]:[12] They must dedicate themselves to the LORD for the full term of their separation and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The previous days do not count, because their separation was defiled.
[Numbers] [6]:[13] This is the law of the Nazirite: When the time of their separation is complete, the Nazirite shall be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [6]:[14] There they shall present their offering to the LORD: one year-old male lamb without defect for a burnt offering, one year-old ewe lamb without defect for a sin offering, one ram without defect for a fellowship offering,
[Numbers] [6]:[15] together with a basket of unleavened bread—loaves of fine flour mixed with oil and unleavened wafers spread with oil—along with their grain offerings and drink offerings.
[Numbers] [6]:[16] The priest shall present them before the LORD and make the sin offering and the burnt offering.
[Numbers] [6]:[17] He shall offer the ram as a fellowship offering to the LORD, together with the basket of unleavened bread, and shall also make the grain offering and the drink offering.
[Numbers] [6]:[18] Then at the entrance to the tent of meeting the Nazirite shall shave their consecrated head, take the hair, and put it on the fire that is under the fellowship offering.
[Numbers] [6]:[19] After the Nazirite has shaved off the hair of their consecration, the priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram, one loaf of unleavened bread from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and place them in the hands of the Nazirite.
[Numbers] [6]:[20] The priest shall then wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. They are holy and belong to the priest, together with the breast that was waved and the thigh that was presented. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.
[Numbers] [6]:[21] This is the law of the Nazirite who makes a vow: their offering to the LORD for their separation, besides whatever else they can afford. They must do exactly as they vowed, according to the law of their separation.
[Numbers] [6]:[22] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [6]:[23] Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
[Numbers] [6]:[24] The LORD bless you and keep you;
[Numbers] [6]:[25] the LORD make his face shine on you and be gracious to you;
[Numbers] [6]:[26] the LORD look upon you with favor and give you peace.
[Numbers] [6]:[27] So they will put my name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.
[Numbers] [7]:[1] On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and consecrated it along with all its furnishings, and he anointed and consecrated the altar with all its utensils.
[Numbers] [7]:[2] Then the leaders of Israel, the heads of their ancestral houses, came forward. These were the leaders of the tribes, the men who had presided over those who were counted.
[Numbers] [7]:[3] They brought their offering before the LORD: six covered wagons and twelve oxen, a wagon from every two leaders and an ox from each one, and they presented them before the tabernacle.
[Numbers] [7]:[4] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [7]:[5] "Accept these from them, and let them be used for the service of the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each man according to his service."
[Numbers] [7]:[6] So Moses took the wagons and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
[Numbers] [7]:[7] Two wagons and four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon, according to their service.
[Numbers] [7]:[8] Four wagons and eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari, according to their service under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
[Numbers] [7]:[9] But to the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the holy things was theirs; they were to carry them on their shoulders.
[Numbers] [7]:[10] On the day the altar was anointed, the leaders brought the dedication gifts for it; they presented their offering before the altar.
[Numbers] [7]:[11] And the LORD said to Moses, "Each day one leader shall present his offering for the dedication of the altar."
[Numbers] [7]:[12] The one who brought his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah.
[Numbers] [7]:[13] His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[14] one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
[Numbers] [7]:[15] one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[16] one male goat for a sin offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[17] and for the fellowship offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
[Numbers] [7]:[18] On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, brought his offering.
[Numbers] [7]:[19] The offering he brought was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[20] one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
[Numbers] [7]:[21] one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[22] one male goat for a sin offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[23] and for the fellowship offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
[Numbers] [7]:[24] On the third day it was Eliab son of Helon, the leader of the people of Zebulun.
[Numbers] [7]:[25] His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[26] one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
[Numbers] [7]:[27] one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[28] one male goat for a sin offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[29] and for the fellowship offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.
[Numbers] [7]:[30] On the fourth day it was Elizur son of Shedeur, the leader of the people of Reuben.
[Numbers] [7]:[31] His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[32] one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;
[Numbers] [7]:[33] one young bull, one ram, and one male lamb a year old for a burnt offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[34] one male goat for a sin offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[35] and for the fellowship offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five male lambs a year old. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.
[Numbers] [7]:[36] On the fifth day it was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, the leader of the people of Simeon.
[Numbers] [7]:[37] His offering was one silver plate weighing a hundred and thirty shekels and one silver basin of seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering;
[Numbers] [7]:[38] one gold dish of ten shekels, filled with incense;

[Numbers] [7]:[84] This was the dedication offering for the altar from the leaders of Israel on the day it was anointed: twelve silver plates, twelve silver basins, twelve gold dishes.
[Numbers] [7]:[85] Each silver plate weighed a hundred and thirty shekels and each basin seventy; all the silver of these vessels came to two thousand four hundred shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
[Numbers] [7]:[86] The twelve gold dishes filled with incense weighed ten shekels each, by the sanctuary shekel; all the gold of the dishes came to a hundred and twenty shekels.
[Numbers] [7]:[87] All the animals for the burnt offering were twelve bulls, twelve rams, and twelve male lambs a year old, with their grain offerings, and twelve male goats for the sin offering.
[Numbers] [7]:[88] The total livestock for the fellowship offering was twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty male lambs a year old. This was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.
[Numbers] [7]:[89] When Moses entered the tent of meeting to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat that was on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim; and He spoke to him.
[Numbers] [8]:[1] The LORD said to Moses,
[Numbers] [8]:[2] "Speak to Aaron and tell him: When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps are to give light toward the front of the lampstand."
[Numbers] [8]:[3] Aaron did so; he set up its lamps to shine toward the front of the lampstand, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [8]:[4] This was how the lampstand was made: hammered gold from its base to its blossoms, hammered work throughout. It was made according to the pattern the LORD had shown Moses.
[Numbers] [8]:[5] The LORD said to Moses,
[Numbers] [8]:[6] "Take the Levites from among the Israelites and cleanse them.
[Numbers] [8]:[7] This is what you are to do to cleanse them: sprinkle them with the water of purification; then have them shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes, and so they will be clean.
[Numbers] [8]:[8] They are to take a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, and you are to take a second young bull for a sin offering.
[Numbers] [8]:[9] Bring the Levites to the front of the tent of meeting and assemble the whole community of Israel.
[Numbers] [8]:[10] Present the Levites before the LORD, and the Israelites are to lay their hands on them.
[Numbers] [8]:[11] Then Aaron shall offer the Levites before the LORD as a wave offering from the Israelites, and they shall then do the service of the LORD.
[Numbers] [8]:[12] The Levites are to lay their hands on the heads of the bulls; then offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites.
[Numbers] [8]:[13] Have the Levites stand before Aaron and his sons, and present them as a wave offering to the LORD.
[Numbers] [8]:[14] In this way you are to set the Levites apart from the other Israelites, and the Levites will be mine.
[Numbers] [8]:[15] After you have cleansed them and presented them as a wave offering, the Levites are to come and do their work at the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [8]:[16] They are wholly given over to me from among the Israelites. I have taken them as my own in place of every firstborn, everyone who opens the womb among the Israelites.
[Numbers] [8]:[17] For every firstborn among the Israelites is mine, both human and animal. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set them apart for myself.
[Numbers] [8]:[18] And I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the Israelites.
[Numbers] [8]:[19] From among the Israelites I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons, to carry out the service of the Israelites at the tent of meeting and to make atonement for them, so that no plague will strike the Israelites when they come near the sanctuary."
[Numbers] [8]:[20] Moses, Aaron, and the whole community of Israel did with the Levites exactly as the LORD had commanded Moses concerning them; that is what the Israelites did for them.
[Numbers] [8]:[21] The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes. Then Aaron presented them as a wave offering before the LORD and made atonement for them to cleanse them.
[Numbers] [8]:[22] After that, the Levites came to do their work at the tent of meeting under the supervision of Aaron and his sons. They did with the Levites just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [8]:[23] The LORD said to Moses,
[Numbers] [8]:[24] "This is the rule for the Levites: from the age of twenty-five and upward a man shall enter the ranks of those who serve at the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [8]:[25] But at the age of fifty he shall retire from active service and work no longer.
[Numbers] [8]:[26] He may assist his brothers at the tent of meeting by keeping watch, but he is not to do the work himself. This is how you are to assign the duties of the Levites."
[Numbers] [9]:[1] The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt. He said:
[Numbers] [9]:[2] "Let the Israelites keep the Passover at its appointed time.
[Numbers] [9]:[3] On the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight, you shall keep it at its appointed time. You shall keep it according to all its statutes and all its rules."
[Numbers] [9]:[4] So Moses told the Israelites to keep the Passover,
[Numbers] [9]:[5] and they kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight, in the wilderness of Sinai. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [9]:[6] But there were some men who were unclean because of a dead body, so they could not keep the Passover on that day. They came before Moses and Aaron that same day
[Numbers] [9]:[7] and said to him, "We are unclean because of a dead body. Why should we be kept from presenting the LORD's offering at its appointed time along with the rest of the Israelites?"
[Numbers] [9]:[8] Moses answered them, "Wait here, and let me hear what the LORD commands concerning you."
[Numbers] [9]:[9] The LORD said to Moses,
[Numbers] [9]:[10] "Say to the Israelites: If any one of you or your descendants is unclean because of a dead body, or is away on a long journey, he may still keep the LORD's Passover.
[Numbers] [9]:[11] They shall keep it in the second month, on the fourteenth day, at twilight. They shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
[Numbers] [9]:[12] They shall leave none of it until morning, and they shall not break any of its bones. They shall keep it according to every statute of the Passover.
[Numbers] [9]:[13] But anyone who is clean and not on a journey, yet fails to keep the Passover, shall be cut off from his people, because he did not present the LORD's offering at its appointed time. That man will bear the guilt of his sin.
[Numbers] [9]:[14] If a foreigner living among you wants to keep the LORD's Passover, he shall do so according to the statute of the Passover and its rule. You shall have one statute, both for the foreigner and for the native of the land."
[Numbers] [9]:[15] On the day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, the tent of the testimony. From evening until morning it appeared over the tabernacle like fire.
[Numbers] [9]:[16] So it was continually: the cloud covered it, and by night it looked like fire.
[Numbers] [9]:[17] Whenever the cloud lifted from above the tent, the Israelites would then set out, and wherever the cloud settled, there the Israelites camped.
[Numbers] [9]:[18] At the LORD's command the Israelites set out, and at the LORD's command they camped. As long as the cloud rested over the tabernacle, they remained in camp.
[Numbers] [9]:[19] Even when the cloud lingered over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the LORD's charge and did not set out.
[Numbers] [9]:[20] Sometimes the cloud remained over the tabernacle only a few days; at the LORD's command they camped, and at the LORD's command they set out.
[Numbers] [9]:[21] Sometimes the cloud stayed only from evening until morning, and when it lifted in the morning, they set out. Whether by day or by night, when the cloud lifted, they set out.
[Numbers] [9]:[22] Whether it was two days, a month, or a longer time, as long as the cloud lingered over the tabernacle and settled upon it, the Israelites stayed in camp and did not set out; but when it lifted, they set out.
[Numbers] [9]:[23] At the LORD's command they camped, and at the LORD's command they set out. They kept the LORD's charge, according to his command through Moses.
[Numbers] [10]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [10]:[2] "Make yourself two trumpets of silver; make them of hammered work. You shall use them to summon the congregation and to set the camps in motion.
[Numbers] [10]:[3] When both are blown, the whole congregation shall gather to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [10]:[4] If only one is blown, then the leaders, the heads of the clans of Israel, shall gather to you.
[Numbers] [10]:[5] When you sound a blast, the camps on the east side shall set out.
[Numbers] [10]:[6] When you sound a second blast, the camps on the south side shall set out. A blast is to be sounded whenever they are to march.
[Numbers] [10]:[7] But when you call the assembly together, you shall blow a steady note, not a blast.
[Numbers] [10]:[8] The sons of Aaron, the priests, are the ones to blow the trumpets. This shall be a lasting statute for you throughout your generations.
[Numbers] [10]:[9] When you go to war in your land against an enemy who oppresses you, sound a blast on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and saved from your enemies.
[Numbers] [10]:[10] On your days of gladness, at your appointed festivals, and at the beginnings of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your fellowship offerings. They will be a remembrance for you before your God. I am the LORD your God."
[Numbers] [10]:[11] In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle of the testimony.
[Numbers] [10]:[12] Then the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai, stage by stage, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
[Numbers] [10]:[13] This was the first time they set out at the command of the LORD through Moses.
[Numbers] [10]:[14] The standard of the camp of Judah went first, company by company, and Nahshon son of Amminadab was over its company.
[Numbers] [10]:[15] Nethanel son of Zuar was over the company of the tribe of Issachar,
[Numbers] [10]:[16] and Eliab son of Helon was over the company of the tribe of Zebulun.
[Numbers] [10]:[17] Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites, who carried it, set out.
[Numbers] [10]:[18] Next the standard of the camp of Reuben set out, company by company, and Elizur son of Shedeur was over its company.
[Numbers] [10]:[19] Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the company of the tribe of Simeon,
[Numbers] [10]:[20] and Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the company of the tribe of Gad.
[Numbers] [10]:[21] Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things, and the tabernacle was set up before they arrived.
[Numbers] [10]:[22] Next the standard of the camp of Ephraim set out, company by company, and Elishama son of Ammihud was over its company.
[Numbers] [10]:[23] Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the company of the tribe of Manasseh,
[Numbers] [10]:[24] and Abidan son of Gideoni was over the company of the tribe of Benjamin.
[Numbers] [10]:[25] Finally the standard of the camp of Dan set out as rear guard for all the camps, company by company, and Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was over its company.
[Numbers] [10]:[26] Pagiel son of Ochran was over the company of the tribe of Asher,
[Numbers] [10]:[27] and Ahira son of Enan was over the company of the tribe of Naphtali.
[Numbers] [10]:[28] This was the marching order of the Israelites, company by company, as they set out.
[Numbers] [10]:[29] Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, the father-in-law of Moses, "We are setting out for the place of which the LORD said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised good things to Israel."
[Numbers] [10]:[30] But he answered, "I will not go. I am going back to my own land and my own people."
[Numbers] [10]:[31] Moses said, "Please do not leave us. You know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes.
[Numbers] [10]:[32] If you come with us, we will share with you whatever good the LORD gives us."
[Numbers] [10]:[33] So they set out from the mountain of the LORD and traveled for three days, with the ark of the covenant of the LORD going before them those three days to seek out a resting place for them.
[Numbers] [10]:[34] And the cloud of the LORD was over them by day whenever they set out from the camp.
[Numbers] [10]:[35] Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, "Rise up, O LORD! Let your enemies be scattered; let those who hate you flee before you."
[Numbers] [10]:[36] And whenever it came to rest, he would say, "Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel."
[Numbers] [11]:[1] Now the people began to complain bitterly, and it was evil in the LORD's hearing. When the LORD heard it, his anger blazed, and fire from the LORD burned among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp.
[Numbers] [11]:[2] Then the people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
[Numbers] [11]:[3] So that place was called Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.[^1] [^1]: Taberah means "burning."
[Numbers] [11]:[4] The rabble among them were seized with craving, and the Israelites too began to weep again, saying, "If only we had meat to eat!
[Numbers] [11]:[5] We remember the fish we ate in Egypt for nothing, and the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic.
[Numbers] [11]:[6] But now our appetite is gone; there is nothing at all, nothing but this manna to look at."
[Numbers] [11]:[7] The manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like that of resin.
[Numbers] [11]:[8] The people would go about and gather it, then grind it in a hand mill or crush it in a mortar. They boiled it in a pot and made cakes of it, and it tasted like something baked with olive oil.
[Numbers] [11]:[9] When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna came down with it.
[Numbers] [11]:[10] Moses heard the people weeping, family after family, each at the entrance of his tent. The LORD's anger blazed fiercely, and Moses too was displeased.
[Numbers] [11]:[11] So Moses said to the LORD, "Why have you treated your servant so badly? Why have I not found favor in your eyes, that you lay the burden of all this people on me?
[Numbers] [11]:[12] Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them, that you should say to me, 'Carry them in your arms, as a nurse carries an infant,' to the land you promised on oath to their fathers?
[Numbers] [11]:[13] Where am I to get meat for all this people? They keep weeping to me, 'Give us meat to eat!'
[Numbers] [11]:[14] I cannot carry all this people by myself; the load is too heavy for me.
[Numbers] [11]:[15] If this is how you are going to treat me, then kill me here and now—if I have found favor in your eyes—and let me not see my own misery."
[Numbers] [11]:[16] The LORD said to Moses, "Gather for me seventy of Israel's elders, men you know to be elders and officers of the people. Bring them to the tent of meeting and have them stand there with you.
[Numbers] [11]:[17] I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them. They will share the burden of the people with you, so that you will not carry it alone.
[Numbers] [11]:[18] And say to the people: Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat. For you have wept in the LORD's hearing, saying, 'If only we had meat to eat! We were better off in Egypt.' Now the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat.
[Numbers] [11]:[19] Not for one day will you eat it, nor two days, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days,
[Numbers] [11]:[20] but for a whole month—until it comes out of your nostrils and you are sick of it—because you have rejected the LORD who is among you and have wept before him, saying, 'Why did we ever leave Egypt?'"
[Numbers] [11]:[21] But Moses said, "Here I am among six hundred thousand men on foot, and you say, 'I will give them meat, and they will eat for a whole month'!
[Numbers] [11]:[22] Could enough flocks and herds be slaughtered for them? Could all the fish of the sea be caught to satisfy them?"
[Numbers] [11]:[23] The LORD answered Moses, "Is the LORD's hand too short? Now you will see whether my word comes true for you or not."
[Numbers] [11]:[24] So Moses went out and told the people what the LORD had said. He gathered seventy of the elders of the people and had them stand around the tent.
[Numbers] [11]:[25] Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke with him, and he took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied—but they did not do so again.
[Numbers] [11]:[26] Two men, however, had remained in the camp—one named Eldad, the other Medad. The Spirit rested on them as well. They were among those registered, yet they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
[Numbers] [11]:[27] A young man ran and reported to Moses, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp."
[Numbers] [11]:[28] Joshua son of Nun, Moses' assistant since his youth, spoke up: "My lord Moses, stop them!"[^1] [^1]: Or "one of his chosen men."
