[Numbers] [11]:[29] But Moses replied, "Are you jealous on my account? I wish that all the LORD's people were prophets and that the LORD would put his Spirit on them!"
[Numbers] [11]:[30] Then Moses returned to the camp, and the elders of Israel with him.
[Numbers] [11]:[31] Now a wind went out from the LORD and drove in quail from the sea. It brought them down around the camp, about a day's journey on each side, to a depth of some two cubits over the ground.
[Numbers] [11]:[32] All that day and night and all the next day the people were up gathering quail. No one collected less than ten homers, and they spread them out all around the camp.
[Numbers] [11]:[33] But while the meat was still between their teeth, before it was even chewed, the LORD's anger blazed against the people, and he struck them with a severe plague.
[Numbers] [11]:[34] So that place was named Kibroth Hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had given in to craving.[^1] [^1]: Kibroth Hattaavah means "graves of craving."
[Numbers] [11]:[35] From Kibroth Hattaavah the people set out for Hazeroth, and at Hazeroth they stayed.
[Numbers] [12]:[1] Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married—for he had married a Cushite woman.
[Numbers] [12]:[2] They said, "Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Has he not spoken through us as well?" And the LORD heard it.
[Numbers] [12]:[3] Now Moses was a very humble man, more so than anyone else on the face of the earth.
[Numbers] [12]:[4] Suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, "Come out, the three of you, to the tent of meeting." So the three of them went out.
[Numbers] [12]:[5] Then the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent. He called Aaron and Miriam, and the two of them stepped forward.
[Numbers] [12]:[6] He said, "Listen to my words: When there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, make myself known to him in a vision; I speak with him in a dream.
[Numbers] [12]:[7] Not so with my servant Moses; he is faithful in all my house.
[Numbers] [12]:[8] With him I speak face to face, plainly and not in riddles; he sees the form of the LORD. Why, then, were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?"
[Numbers] [12]:[9] The anger of the LORD burned against them, and he departed.
[Numbers] [12]:[10] When the cloud lifted from above the tent, there stood Miriam, her skin diseased, white as snow. Aaron turned toward her and saw that she was diseased.
[Numbers] [12]:[11] Aaron said to Moses, "Please, my lord, do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.
[Numbers] [12]:[12] Do not let her be like a stillborn child, coming from the womb with its flesh half wasted away."
[Numbers] [12]:[13] So Moses cried out to the LORD, "Please, God, heal her!"
[Numbers] [12]:[14] The LORD answered Moses, "If her father had spit in her face, would she not be in disgrace for seven days? Let her be confined outside the camp for seven days; after that she may be brought back in."
[Numbers] [12]:[15] So Miriam was confined outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on until she was brought back.
[Numbers] [12]:[16] After that the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the Desert of Paran.
[Numbers] [13]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [13]:[2] "Send men to scout out the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. Send one man from each ancestral tribe, each of them a leader among his people."
[Numbers] [13]:[3] So Moses sent them out from the Wilderness of Paran at the LORD's command. All of them were leading men among the Israelites.
[Numbers] [13]:[4] These are their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
[Numbers] [13]:[5] from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
[Numbers] [13]:[6] from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
[Numbers] [13]:[7] from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
[Numbers] [13]:[8] from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
[Numbers] [13]:[9] from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
[Numbers] [13]:[10] from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
[Numbers] [13]:[11] from the tribe of Joseph, that is, from the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;
[Numbers] [13]:[12] from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
[Numbers] [13]:[13] from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
[Numbers] [13]:[14] from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
[Numbers] [13]:[15] from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
[Numbers] [13]:[16] These are the names of the men Moses sent to scout out the land. And Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.
[Numbers] [13]:[17] When Moses sent them to scout out the land of Canaan, he told them, "Go up through the Negev and on into the hill country.
[Numbers] [13]:[18] See what the land is like, and whether the people living there are strong or weak, few or many.
[Numbers] [13]:[19] Is the land they live in good or bad? Are their towns open camps or fortified strongholds?
[Numbers] [13]:[20] Is the soil rich or poor? Are there trees on it or not? Be bold, and bring back some of the fruit of the land." It was the season of the first ripe grapes.
[Numbers] [13]:[21] So they went up and scouted out the land, from the Wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, near Lebo-hamath.
[Numbers] [13]:[22] They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, lived. (Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)
[Numbers] [13]:[23] When they reached the Valley of Eshcol, they cut off a branch bearing a single cluster of grapes, and two of them carried it on a pole between them, along with some pomegranates and figs.
[Numbers] [13]:[24] That place was called the Valley of Eshcol because of the cluster the Israelites cut down there.
[Numbers] [13]:[25] At the end of forty days they returned from scouting out the land.
[Numbers] [13]:[26] They came back to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation of Israel in the Wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh. There they gave their report to the whole assembly and showed them the fruit of the land.
[Numbers] [13]:[27] This is the account they gave Moses: "We went into the land where you sent us. It truly does flow with milk and honey, and here is its fruit.
[Numbers] [13]:[28] But the people who live there are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large. We even saw the descendants of Anak there.
[Numbers] [13]:[29] The Amalekites live in the land of the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan."
[Numbers] [13]:[30] Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, "We should go up at once and take possession of it, for we are well able to do it."
[Numbers] [13]:[31] But the men who had gone up with him said, "We cannot attack those people; they are stronger than we are."
[Numbers] [13]:[32] And they spread among the Israelites a bad report about the land they had scouted: "The land we traveled through to explore it devours those who live in it, and all the people we saw there are of enormous size.
[Numbers] [13]:[33] We even saw the Nephilim there—the descendants of Anak come from the Nephilim. In our own eyes we seemed like grasshoppers, and so we seemed to them.
[Numbers] [14]:[1] Then the whole congregation broke out in a loud cry, and the people wept through that night.
[Numbers] [14]:[2] All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, "If only we had died in Egypt! Or if only we had died in this wilderness!
[Numbers] [14]:[3] Why is the LORD bringing us to this land, only to fall by the sword? Our wives and children will become plunder. Wouldn't it be better for us to go back to Egypt?"
[Numbers] [14]:[4] And they said to one another, "Let's choose a leader and go back to Egypt."
[Numbers] [14]:[5] Then Moses and Aaron fell facedown before the whole assembled congregation of the Israelites.
[Numbers] [14]:[6] Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had explored the land, tore their clothes
[Numbers] [14]:[7] and said to the entire congregation of the Israelites, "The land we passed through and explored is an exceedingly good land.
[Numbers] [14]:[8] If the LORD delights in us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us—a land flowing with milk and honey.
[Numbers] [14]:[9] Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, for they are bread for us. Their protection is gone, and the LORD is with us. Do not fear them."
[Numbers] [14]:[10] But the whole congregation talked of stoning them. Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the tent of meeting to all the Israelites.
[Numbers] [14]:[11] The LORD said to Moses, "How long will this people treat me with contempt? How long will they refuse to believe in me, in spite of all the signs I have performed among them?
[Numbers] [14]:[12] I will strike them with a plague and destroy them, and I will make you into a nation greater and stronger than they."
[Numbers] [14]:[13] But Moses said to the LORD, "Then the Egyptians will hear of it—for by your power you brought this people up from among them—
[Numbers] [14]:[14] and they will tell the inhabitants of this land. They have already heard that you, LORD, are among this people, that you, LORD, are seen face to face, that your cloud stands over them, and that you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
[Numbers] [14]:[15] If you put this people to death as one man, the nations who have heard this report about you will say,
[Numbers] [14]:[16] 'The LORD was not able to bring this people into the land he swore to give them, so he slaughtered them in the wilderness.'
[Numbers] [14]:[17] Now let the Lord's power be displayed in its greatness, just as you have declared:
[Numbers] [14]:[18] 'The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, forgiving iniquity and transgression, yet he does not leave the guilty unpunished; he visits the iniquity of the fathers on the children to the third and fourth generation.'
[Numbers] [14]:[19] Please pardon the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your steadfast love, just as you have forgiven them from Egypt until now."
[Numbers] [14]:[20] The LORD answered, "I have pardoned them, as you asked.
[Numbers] [14]:[21] Nevertheless, as surely as I live and as surely as the glory of the LORD fills the whole earth,
[Numbers] [14]:[22] not one of those who saw my glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness, and yet tested me these ten times and did not obey my voice,
[Numbers] [14]:[23] will ever see the land I swore to give their fathers. None of those who treated me with contempt will see it.
[Numbers] [14]:[24] But my servant Caleb—because a different spirit is in him and he has followed me wholeheartedly—him I will bring into the land he entered, and his descendants will inherit it.
[Numbers] [14]:[25] Since the Amalekites and Canaanites are living in the valley, turn back tomorrow and set out toward the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea."
[Numbers] [14]:[26] The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
[Numbers] [14]:[27] "How long will this wicked congregation go on grumbling against me? I have heard the complaints the Israelites keep muttering against me.
[Numbers] [14]:[28] Tell them: As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you the very thing I heard you say.
[Numbers] [14]:[29] In this wilderness your bodies will fall—every one of you twenty years old or more who was counted in the census and who has grumbled against me.
[Numbers] [14]:[30] Not one of you will enter the land I swore with uplifted hand to settle you in, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
[Numbers] [14]:[31] As for your children, whom you said would become plunder—I will bring them in, and they will know the land you rejected.
[Numbers] [14]:[32] But as for you, your bodies will fall in this wilderness.
[Numbers] [14]:[33] Your children will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, bearing the penalty of your unfaithfulness, until the last of your bodies lies in the wilderness.
[Numbers] [14]:[34] For forty years—one year for each of the forty days you explored the land—you will suffer for your sins and know what it is to have me against you.
[Numbers] [14]:[35] I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will surely do this to this whole wicked congregation that has banded together against me. In this wilderness they will meet their end; here they will die."
[Numbers] [14]:[36] So the men Moses had sent to explore the land, who returned and made the whole congregation grumble against him by spreading a bad report about it—
[Numbers] [14]:[37] these men who spread the evil report about the land died of a plague before the LORD.
[Numbers] [14]:[38] Of the men who went to explore the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive.
[Numbers] [14]:[39] When Moses reported these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned bitterly.
[Numbers] [14]:[40] Early the next morning they climbed to the top of the mountain, saying, "Here we are. We will go up to the place the LORD promised, for we have sinned."
[Numbers] [14]:[41] But Moses said, "Why are you disobeying the LORD's command? This will not succeed.
[Numbers] [14]:[42] Do not go up, for the LORD is not among you. You will only be struck down before your enemies.
[Numbers] [14]:[43] The Amalekites and Canaanites will face you there, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from the LORD, he will not be with you."
[Numbers] [14]:[44] Yet in their presumption they pushed up toward the top of the hill country, though neither Moses nor the ark of the LORD's covenant moved from the camp.
[Numbers] [14]:[45] Then the Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down, struck them, and beat them back all the way to Hormah.
[Numbers] [15]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [15]:[2] Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land where you are to live, which I am giving you,
[Numbers] [15]:[3] and you present to the LORD an offering by fire from the herd or the flock—a burnt offering or a sacrifice, whether to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering or at your appointed festivals—to make a pleasing aroma for the LORD,
[Numbers] [15]:[4] then the one who brings his offering shall present to the LORD a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil.
[Numbers] [15]:[5] With the burnt offering or the sacrifice you shall prepare a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering for each lamb.
[Numbers] [15]:[6] For a ram you shall prepare a grain offering of two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil,
[Numbers] [15]:[7] and a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering. Present it as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Numbers] [15]:[8] When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a vow or as a fellowship offering to the LORD,
[Numbers] [15]:[9] a grain offering of three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil shall be brought with the bull,
[Numbers] [15]:[10] and you shall bring half a hin of wine as a drink offering—an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Numbers] [15]:[11] This is what shall be done for each bull, each ram, or each lamb or kid from the flock.
[Numbers] [15]:[12] Whatever the number you prepare, do this for each one, according to their number.
[Numbers] [15]:[13] Every native-born Israelite shall do these things in this way when he presents an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Numbers] [15]:[14] And if a foreigner is staying with you, or whoever lives among you throughout your generations, and he wishes to present an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, he shall do exactly as you do.
[Numbers] [15]:[15] For the assembly there shall be one statute for you and for the foreigner who resides with you—a lasting statute for all your generations. Before the LORD, you and the foreigner shall be alike.
[Numbers] [15]:[16] The same law and the same regulation shall apply both to you and to the foreigner residing among you.
[Numbers] [15]:[17] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [15]:[18] Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land to which I am bringing you,
[Numbers] [15]:[19] and you eat the food of that land, you shall present a contribution to the LORD.
[Numbers] [15]:[20] From the first of your dough you shall present a loaf as a contribution; present it like the contribution from the threshing floor.
[Numbers] [15]:[21] Throughout your generations you shall give the LORD a contribution from the first of your dough.
[Numbers] [15]:[22] Now if you stray unintentionally and fail to keep all these commands that the LORD gave Moses—
[Numbers] [15]:[23] everything the LORD commanded you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave the command and onward through your generations—
[Numbers] [15]:[24] then if it was done unintentionally, unnoticed by the congregation, the whole congregation shall offer one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, along with its prescribed grain offering and drink offering, and one male goat as a sin offering.
[Numbers] [15]:[25] The priest shall make atonement for the whole congregation of Israel, and they will be forgiven, for it was unintentional and they have brought their offering to the LORD—an offering by fire and their sin offering before the LORD for their unintentional wrong.
[Numbers] [15]:[26] The whole congregation of Israel will be forgiven, along with the foreigner residing among them, since it happened to all the people unintentionally.
[Numbers] [15]:[27] If a single person sins unintentionally, he shall bring a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
[Numbers] [15]:[28] The priest shall make atonement before the LORD for the person who erred by sinning unintentionally, and when atonement has been made for him, he will be forgiven.
[Numbers] [15]:[29] You shall have one law for the native-born Israelite and for the foreigner residing among you, for anyone who sins unintentionally.
[Numbers] [15]:[30] But the person who acts defiantly, whether native-born or foreigner, blasphemes the LORD; that person shall be cut off from among his people.
[Numbers] [15]:[31] Because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken his command, that person shall surely be cut off; his guilt remains on him.
[Numbers] [15]:[32] While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
[Numbers] [15]:[33] Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation,
[Numbers] [15]:[34] and they kept him in custody, because it had not been made clear what should be done to him.
[Numbers] [15]:[35] Then the LORD said to Moses, "The man must be put to death. The whole congregation shall stone him outside the camp."
[Numbers] [15]:[36] So the whole congregation took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [15]:[37] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [15]:[38] Speak to the Israelites and tell them that throughout their generations they are to make tassels on the corners of their garments, with a blue cord on each tassel.
[Numbers] [15]:[39] These tassels will be yours to look at, so that you may remember all the commands of the LORD and keep them, and not go chasing after your own heart and your own eyes, prostituting yourselves after them.
[Numbers] [15]:[40] So that you will remember and keep all my commands and be holy to your God.
[Numbers] [15]:[41] I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.
[Numbers] [16]:[1] Now Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, took action, along with Dathan and Abiram sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, descendants of Reuben.
[Numbers] [16]:[2] They rose up against Moses, together with two hundred and fifty men of Israel, leaders of the community, appointed members of the assembly, men of reputation.
[Numbers] [16]:[3] They gathered against Moses and Aaron and said to them, "You have gone too far! The whole community is holy, every one of them, and the LORD is among them. Why then do you set yourselves above the LORD's assembly?"
[Numbers] [16]:[4] When Moses heard this, he fell facedown.
[Numbers] [16]:[5] Then he said to Korah and all his followers: "In the morning the LORD will make known who belongs to him and who is holy, and he will bring that one near to himself. The one he chooses he will bring near to himself.
[Numbers] [16]:[6] Do this: take censers for yourselves, Korah and all your followers.
[Numbers] [16]:[7] Tomorrow put fire in them and lay incense on them before the LORD. The man the LORD chooses will be the holy one. You Levites have gone too far!"
[Numbers] [16]:[8] Moses also said to Korah, "Listen now, you Levites!
[Numbers] [16]:[9] Is it not enough for you that the God of Israel has set you apart from the rest of the community of Israel and brought you near to himself, to do the work at the LORD's dwelling and to stand before the community and serve them?
[Numbers] [16]:[10] He has brought you near, you and all your fellow Levites with you, and now you seek the priesthood as well!
[Numbers] [16]:[11] So it is against the LORD that you and all your followers have banded together. And Aaron—what is he, that you should grumble against him?"
[Numbers] [16]:[12] Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, "We will not come.
[Numbers] [16]:[13] Is it not enough that you brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness? Must you also lord it over us?
[Numbers] [16]:[14] Besides, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you gouge out the eyes of these men? We will not come!"
[Numbers] [16]:[15] Moses became very angry and said to the LORD, "Do not accept their offering. I have not taken so much as a donkey from them, nor have I wronged a single one of them."
[Numbers] [16]:[16] Then Moses said to Korah, "You and all your followers are to appear before the LORD tomorrow—you and they and Aaron.
[Numbers] [16]:[17] Each man is to take his censer and put incense on it—two hundred and fifty censers in all—and present it before the LORD. You and Aaron are each to bring your censer as well."
[Numbers] [16]:[18] So each man took his censer, put fire in it, laid incense on it, and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [16]:[19] When Korah had gathered the whole community against them at the entrance to the tent of meeting, the glory of the LORD appeared to the entire community.
[Numbers] [16]:[20] The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
[Numbers] [16]:[21] "Separate yourselves from this community, and I will consume them in an instant."
[Numbers] [16]:[22] But they fell facedown and cried out, "O God, God of the spirits of all flesh, will you be angry with the whole community when only one man sins?"
[Numbers] [16]:[23] Then the LORD said to Moses,
[Numbers] [16]:[24] "Say to the community: Get away from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram."
[Numbers] [16]:[25] Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
[Numbers] [16]:[26] He said to the community, "Move back from the tents of these wicked men! Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be swept away because of all their sins."
[Numbers] [16]:[27] So they moved away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram had come out and were standing at the entrances of their tents with their wives, their sons, and their little ones.
[Numbers] [16]:[28] Then Moses said, "This is how you will know that the LORD has sent me to do all these things and that it was not my own idea:
[Numbers] [16]:[29] If these men die a natural death and suffer only what usually comes to people, then the LORD has not sent me.
[Numbers] [16]:[30] But if the LORD brings about something entirely new—if the ground opens its mouth and swallows them with everything they own, so that they go down alive to the realm of the dead—then you will know that these men have treated the LORD with contempt."
[Numbers] [16]:[31] As soon as he finished speaking these words, the ground under them split open.
[Numbers] [16]:[32] The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households, along with all Korah's men and all their possessions.
[Numbers] [16]:[33] They went down alive to the realm of the dead, with everything they owned. The earth closed over them, and they perished from among the assembly.
[Numbers] [16]:[34] At their cries, all the Israelites around them fled, shouting, "The earth is going to swallow us too!"
[Numbers] [16]:[35] And fire came out from the LORD and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who were offering the incense.
[Numbers] [17]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [17]:[2] "Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to lift the censers out of the smoldering fire and scatter the coals far away, for the censers are holy.
[Numbers] [17]:[3] Take the censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their lives and hammer them into sheets to overlay the altar, for they were presented before the LORD and have become holy. They shall be a sign to the Israelites."
[Numbers] [17]:[4] So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that the men who were burned had presented, and they were hammered out as an overlay for the altar,
[Numbers] [17]:[5] a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider, no one who is not of Aaron's line, should ever come near to burn incense before the LORD, or he would become like Korah and his company—just as the LORD had spoken to Eleazar through Moses.
[Numbers] [17]:[6] But the next day the whole community of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron. "You have killed the LORD's people," they said.
[Numbers] [17]:[7] And as the assembly gathered against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the tent of meeting, and there was the cloud covering it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
[Numbers] [17]:[8] Then Moses and Aaron came to the front of the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [17]:[9] And the LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [17]:[10] "Get away from this assembly, so that I may consume them in an instant." And they fell facedown.
[Numbers] [17]:[11] Moses said to Aaron, "Take your censer, put fire on it from the altar and lay incense on it, then hurry to the assembly and make atonement for them. Wrath has gone out from the LORD; the plague has begun."
[Numbers] [17]:[12] Aaron took it, as Moses had said, and ran into the midst of the assembly. The plague had indeed begun among the people, but he put in the incense and made atonement for the people.
[Numbers] [17]:[13] He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped.
[Numbers] [17]:[14] Fourteen thousand seven hundred died in the plague, besides those who had died in the affair of Korah.
[Numbers] [17]:[15] Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance to the tent of meeting, and the plague had been stopped.
[Numbers] [17]:[16] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [17]:[17] "Speak to the Israelites and get a staff from each of them, one for every ancestral house, from all their leaders according to their ancestral houses—twelve staffs. Write each man's name on his staff,
[Numbers] [17]:[18] and write Aaron's name on the staff of Levi, since there is to be one staff for the head of each ancestral house.
[Numbers] [17]:[19] Place them in the tent of meeting in front of the ark of the testimony, where I meet with you.
[Numbers] [17]:[20] The staff of the man I choose will sprout, and I will rid myself of this constant grumbling of the Israelites against you."
[Numbers] [17]:[21] So Moses spoke to the Israelites, and each of their leaders brought him a staff, one for each ancestral house—twelve staffs in all—and Aaron's staff was among them.
[Numbers] [17]:[22] Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the tent of the testimony.
[Numbers] [17]:[23] The next day Moses went into the tent of the testimony, and there was Aaron's staff, the staff of the house of Levi: it had sprouted, put out buds, blossomed, and produced ripe almonds.
[Numbers] [17]:[24] Moses brought all the staffs out from before the LORD to all the Israelites. They looked, and each man took back his own staff.
[Numbers] [17]:[25] The LORD said to Moses, "Put Aaron's staff back in front of the ark of the testimony, to be kept as a warning sign to these rebels. This will put an end to their grumbling against me, so that they will not die."
[Numbers] [17]:[26] So Moses did it; just as the LORD commanded him, so he did.
[Numbers] [17]:[27] The Israelites said to Moses, "Look, we are dying! We are lost, all of us are lost!
[Numbers] [17]:[28] Anyone who so much as comes near the LORD's dwelling will die. Are we all to perish?"
[Numbers] [18]:[1] The LORD said to Aaron: "You and your sons and your father's house with you shall bear the guilt connected with the sanctuary, and you and your sons with you shall bear the guilt connected with your priesthood.
[Numbers] [18]:[2] Bring your brothers also, the tribe of Levi, your ancestral tribe, to join you and serve you while you and your sons are before the tent of the testimony.
[Numbers] [18]:[3] They shall keep your charge and the charge of the whole tent, but they must not come near the holy vessels or the altar, or both they and you will die.
[Numbers] [18]:[4] They shall join you and keep the charge of the tent of meeting, doing all the work of the tent, and no outsider shall come near you.
[Numbers] [18]:[5] You shall keep the charge of the sanctuary and the charge of the altar, so that wrath may never again fall on the Israelites.
[Numbers] [18]:[6] I myself have taken your brothers the Levites from among the Israelites; they are a gift to you, given to the LORD to do the work of the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [18]:[7] But you and your sons with you shall guard your priesthood in everything concerning the altar and inside the curtain, and you shall serve there. I give you the priesthood as a gift of service; any outsider who comes near shall be put to death."
[Numbers] [18]:[8] The LORD said to Aaron: "See, I myself have given you charge of the contributions made to me. All the holy gifts of the Israelites I give to you as your anointed portion, and to your sons as a perpetual statute.
[Numbers] [18]:[9] This shall be yours from the most holy offerings, from the fire: every offering of theirs—every grain offering, every sin offering, and every guilt offering that they render to me—is most holy for you and your sons.
[Numbers] [18]:[10] You shall eat it in a most holy place; every male may eat it. It shall be holy to you.
[Numbers] [18]:[11] This also is yours: the contribution of their gifts, all the wave offerings of the Israelites. I give them to you and to your sons and daughters with you as a perpetual statute. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
[Numbers] [18]:[12] All the best of the oil, and all the best of the new wine and the grain, the firstfruits that they give to the LORD, I give to you.
[Numbers] [18]:[13] The first ripe produce of everything in their land, which they bring to the LORD, shall be yours. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
[Numbers] [18]:[14] Everything devoted in Israel shall be yours.
[Numbers] [18]:[15] Every firstborn of the womb, of all flesh, that is offered to the LORD, whether human or animal, shall be yours. But you must redeem the firstborn of a human, and you shall redeem the firstborn of an unclean animal.
[Numbers] [18]:[16] Those to be redeemed you shall redeem from one month old, at your valuation of five shekels of silver by the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.
[Numbers] [18]:[17] But the firstborn of an ox, a sheep, or a goat you shall not redeem; they are holy. You shall dash their blood against the altar and burn their fat as a food offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Numbers] [18]:[18] Their meat shall be yours, just as the breast of the wave offering and the right thigh are yours.
[Numbers] [18]:[19] All the holy contributions that the Israelites present to the LORD I give to you and to your sons and daughters with you as a perpetual statute. It is an everlasting covenant of salt before the LORD for you and your offspring with you."
[Numbers] [18]:[20] The LORD said to Aaron: "You shall have no inheritance in their land, and no share among them. I am your share and your inheritance among the Israelites.
[Numbers] [18]:[21] To the Levites I have given every tithe in Israel as an inheritance, in return for the service they perform, the service of the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [18]:[22] From now on the Israelites must not come near the tent of meeting, or they will incur guilt and die.
[Numbers] [18]:[23] The Levites alone shall do the work of the tent of meeting, and they shall bear their guilt. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations: among the Israelites they shall receive no inheritance.
[Numbers] [18]:[24] For I have given the Levites as their inheritance the tithe that the Israelites present to the LORD as a contribution. That is why I said to them: Among the Israelites they shall receive no inheritance."
[Numbers] [18]:[25] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [18]:[26] "Speak to the Levites and say to them: When you receive from the Israelites the tithe that I have given you from them as your inheritance, you shall present from it a contribution to the LORD, a tithe of the tithe.
[Numbers] [18]:[27] Your contribution will be credited to you as though it were grain from the threshing floor and the fullness of the winepress.
[Numbers] [18]:[28] So you also shall present a contribution to the LORD from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites, and from them you shall give the LORD's contribution to Aaron the priest.
[Numbers] [18]:[29] From all the gifts you receive you shall present every contribution due to the LORD, taking the holy portion from the very best of it.
[Numbers] [18]:[30] Say to them: When you have presented the best of it, it will be credited to the Levites as the yield of the threshing floor and the yield of the winepress.
[Numbers] [18]:[31] You and your households may eat it anywhere, for it is your wages in return for your service in the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [18]:[32] You will incur no guilt because of it, once you have presented the best of it. But you must not profane the holy gifts of the Israelites, or you will die."
[Numbers] [19]:[1] The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
[Numbers] [19]:[2] This is the statute of the law that the LORD has commanded: Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer without defect, in which there is no blemish, and on which no yoke has ever been laid.
[Numbers] [19]:[3] Give it to Eleazar the priest, and he shall take it outside the camp, and it shall be slaughtered in his presence.
[Numbers] [19]:[4] Then Eleazar the priest shall take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [19]:[5] The heifer shall be burned in his sight—its hide, its flesh, and its blood, along with its dung.
[Numbers] [19]:[6] The priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet yarn, and throw them into the fire consuming the heifer.
[Numbers] [19]:[7] Then the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; afterward he may enter the camp, but he remains unclean until evening.
[Numbers] [19]:[8] The one who burns the heifer shall also wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water, and he remains unclean until evening.
[Numbers] [19]:[9] A man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer and put them outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept for the community of the Israelites, to make the water of purification; it is a purification offering.
[Numbers] [19]:[10] The one who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes and remain unclean until evening. This shall be a lasting statute for the Israelites and for the foreigner residing among them.
[Numbers] [19]:[11] Whoever touches the corpse of any human being shall be unclean for seven days.
[Numbers] [19]:[12] He must purify himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he will be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not be clean.
[Numbers] [19]:[13] Anyone who touches a corpse, the body of a person who has died, and does not purify himself, defiles the LORD's tabernacle. That person shall be cut off from Israel. Because the water of purification was not sprinkled on him, he remains unclean; his uncleanness is still on him.
[Numbers] [19]:[14] This is the law when a person dies in a tent: everyone who enters the tent and everyone who is in it shall be unclean for seven days,
[Numbers] [19]:[15] and every open container without a lid fastened on it is unclean.
[Numbers] [19]:[16] Anyone out in the open who touches someone killed by the sword, or a dead body, or a human bone, or a grave, shall be unclean for seven days.
[Numbers] [19]:[17] For the unclean person they shall take some of the ashes from the burned purification offering, and fresh running water shall be poured over them in a jar.
[Numbers] [19]:[18] Then a man who is clean shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent, all the vessels, and everyone who was there, as well as anyone who touched a bone, or one who was killed, or a dead body, or a grave.
[Numbers] [19]:[19] The clean person shall sprinkle the unclean one on the third day and on the seventh day, and on the seventh day he shall purify him. Then he shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and by evening he will be clean.
[Numbers] [19]:[20] But anyone who becomes unclean and does not purify himself shall be cut off from the assembly, for he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water of purification has not been sprinkled on him; he is unclean.
[Numbers] [19]:[21] This shall be a lasting statute for them. The one who sprinkles the water of purification shall wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water of purification shall be unclean until evening.
[Numbers] [19]:[22] Whatever the unclean person touches becomes unclean, and anyone who touches it shall be unclean until evening.
[Numbers] [20]:[1] In the first month the Israelites, the whole community, came to the wilderness of Zin, and the people settled at Kadesh. There Miriam died, and there she was buried.
[Numbers] [20]:[2] There was no water for the community, so they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
[Numbers] [20]:[3] The people quarreled with Moses and said, "If only we had died when our brothers died before the LORD!
[Numbers] [20]:[4] Why have you brought the LORD's assembly into this wilderness, for us and our livestock to die here?
[Numbers] [20]:[5] Why did you bring us up out of Egypt to this miserable place? It has no grain, no figs, no vines, no pomegranates—and there is no water to drink."
[Numbers] [20]:[6] Moses and Aaron went from the assembly to the entrance of the tent of meeting and fell on their faces, and the glory of the LORD appeared to them.
[Numbers] [20]:[7] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [20]:[8] "Take the staff, and you and your brother Aaron gather the community. Speak to the rock before their eyes, and it will yield its water. So you will bring water out of the rock for them and give the community and their livestock something to drink."
[Numbers] [20]:[9] So Moses took the staff from before the LORD, as he had commanded him.
[Numbers] [20]:[10] Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly in front of the rock, and he said to them, "Listen now, you rebels! Must we bring water out of this rock for you?"
[Numbers] [20]:[11] Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff. Water gushed out, and the community and their livestock drank.
[Numbers] [20]:[12] But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Because you did not trust me enough to honor me as holy in the sight of the Israelites, you will not bring this assembly into the land I have given them."
[Numbers] [20]:[13] These were the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD, and where he showed himself holy among them.
[Numbers] [20]:[14] From Kadesh Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom: "This is what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardship that has come upon us.
[Numbers] [20]:[15] Our fathers went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt many years. The Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers,
[Numbers] [20]:[16] but when we cried out to the LORD, he heard our voice and sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now here we are at Kadesh, a town on the edge of your territory.
[Numbers] [20]:[17] Please let us pass through your land. We will not cut through any field or vineyard, and we will not drink water from any well. We will travel along the king's highway and will not turn aside to the right or the left until we have passed through your territory."
[Numbers] [20]:[18] But Edom answered him, "You may not pass through here. If you try, we will come out against you with the sword."
[Numbers] [20]:[19] The Israelites said to him, "We will keep to the main road, and if we or our livestock drink any of your water, we will pay for it. It is nothing—we only want to pass through on foot."
[Numbers] [20]:[20] But he said, "You may not pass through." And Edom came out against them with a large force and a strong hand.
[Numbers] [20]:[21] Since Edom refused to let them pass through his territory, Israel turned away from him.
[Numbers] [20]:[22] The Israelites, the whole community, set out from Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.
[Numbers] [20]:[23] At Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
[Numbers] [20]:[24] "Aaron will be gathered to his people. He will not enter the land I have given to the Israelites, because both of you rebelled against my command at the waters of Meribah.
[Numbers] [20]:[25] Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor.
[Numbers] [20]:[26] Remove Aaron's garments and put them on his son Eleazar, for Aaron will be gathered to his people; he will die there."
[Numbers] [20]:[27] Moses did as the LORD commanded, and they went up Mount Hor in the sight of the whole community.
[Numbers] [20]:[28] Moses removed Aaron's garments and put them on his son Eleazar. And Aaron died there on top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain,
[Numbers] [20]:[29] and when the whole community saw that Aaron had died, all the house of Israel wept for him thirty days.
[Numbers] [21]:[1] When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming by the road to Atharim, he attacked Israel and took some of them captive.
[Numbers] [21]:[2] Then Israel made a vow to the LORD: "If you will deliver this people into our hands, we will utterly destroy their cities."
[Numbers] [21]:[3] The LORD listened to Israel's plea and gave the Canaanites over to them. They destroyed them and their cities, and the place was named Hormah.
[Numbers] [21]:[4] They set out from Mount Hor along the road toward the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. But on the way the people grew impatient,
[Numbers] [21]:[5] and they spoke against God and against Moses: "Why did you bring us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread and no water, and we are sick of this miserable food!"
[Numbers] [21]:[6] So the LORD sent venomous snakes among the people, and they bit them, and many Israelites died.
[Numbers] [21]:[7] The people came to Moses and said, "We have sinned by speaking against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD to take the snakes away from us." So Moses prayed for the people.
[Numbers] [21]:[8] The LORD said to Moses, "Make a snake and mount it on a pole; anyone who is bitten can look at it and live."
[Numbers] [21]:[9] So Moses made a bronze snake and mounted it on a pole. Then whenever anyone was bitten by a snake, he looked at the bronze snake and lived.
[Numbers] [21]:[10] The Israelites moved on and camped at Oboth.
[Numbers] [21]:[11] They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye Abarim, in the wilderness that faces Moab toward the sunrise.
[Numbers] [21]:[12] From there they moved on and camped in the Zered Valley.
[Numbers] [21]:[13] From there they moved on and camped beyond the Arnon, in the wilderness that stretches out from the territory of the Amorites; for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
[Numbers] [21]:[14] That is why the Book of the Wars of the LORD says: "Waheb in Suphah and the ravines, the Arnon,
[Numbers] [21]:[15] and the slopes of the ravines that run down to the site of Ar and lean toward the border of Moab."
[Numbers] [21]:[16] From there they went on to Beer, the well where the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people together, and I will give them water."
[Numbers] [21]:[17] Then Israel sang this song: "Rise up, O well! Sing to it!
[Numbers] [21]:[18] The well that the princes dug, that the nobles of the people sank with the scepter, with their staffs." From the wilderness they went on to Mattanah,
[Numbers] [21]:[19] from Mattanah to Nahaliel, from Nahaliel to Bamoth,
[Numbers] [21]:[20] and from Bamoth to the valley in the region of Moab, where the top of Pisgah looks out over the wasteland.
[Numbers] [21]:[21] Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites with this word:
[Numbers] [21]:[22] "Let us pass through your land. We will not turn aside into any field or vineyard, nor drink water from any well. We will travel along the King's Highway until we have passed through your territory."
[Numbers] [21]:[23] But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. He mustered his whole army and marched out into the wilderness against Israel. When he reached Jahaz, he fought with Israel.
[Numbers] [21]:[24] Israel put him to the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, for the border of the Ammonites was strongly held.
[Numbers] [21]:[25] Israel captured all these towns and settled in all the cities of the Amorites, including Heshbon and its surrounding villages.
[Numbers] [21]:[26] For Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and taken from him all his land as far as the Arnon.
[Numbers] [21]:[27] That is why the poets say: "Come to Heshbon, let it be rebuilt; let Sihon's city be restored.
[Numbers] [21]:[28] Fire went out from Heshbon, a blaze from the city of Sihon. It consumed Ar of Moab, the rulers of Arnon's heights.
[Numbers] [21]:[29] Woe to you, Moab! You are destroyed, people of Chemosh! He gave up his sons as fugitives and his daughters as captives to Sihon king of the Amorites.
[Numbers] [21]:[30] But we have overthrown them; Heshbon is destroyed all the way to Dibon. We laid them waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba."
[Numbers] [21]:[31] So Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
[Numbers] [21]:[32] After Moses had sent men to spy out Jazer, the Israelites captured its surrounding villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.
[Numbers] [21]:[33] Then they turned and went up along the road toward Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out with his whole army to meet them in battle at Edrei.
[Numbers] [21]:[34] The LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have given him into your hand, along with his whole army and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon."
[Numbers] [21]:[35] So they struck him down, together with his sons and his whole army, leaving him no survivor, and they took possession of his land.
[Numbers] [22]:[1] Then the Israelites set out and camped on the plains of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
[Numbers] [22]:[2] Balak son of Zippor saw everything Israel had done to the Amorites,
[Numbers] [22]:[3] and Moab was terrified of the people, because there were so many of them. Moab was filled with dread at the Israelites.
[Numbers] [22]:[4] So Moab said to the elders of Midian, "This horde will lick up everything around us the way an ox licks up the grass of the field." Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time,
[Numbers] [22]:[5] and he sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor, at Pethor on the River, in the land of his people, to summon him with this message: "A people has come out of Egypt. They cover the face of the land, and they have settled next to me.
[Numbers] [22]:[6] Now come and curse this people for me, for they are too strong for me. Perhaps then I will be able to strike them down and drive them out of the land. For I know that whomever you bless is blessed, and whomever you curse is cursed."
[Numbers] [22]:[7] So the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went, taking with them the fee for divination. They came to Balaam and told him what Balak had said.
[Numbers] [22]:[8] "Spend the night here," he said to them, "and I will bring you back whatever answer the LORD gives me." So the officials of Moab stayed with him.
[Numbers] [22]:[9] God came to Balaam and asked, "Who are these men with you?"
[Numbers] [22]:[10] Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent me this message:
[Numbers] [22]:[11] 'A people has come out of Egypt, and they cover the face of the land. Now come and put a curse on them for me. Perhaps then I will be able to fight them and drive them out.'"
[Numbers] [22]:[12] But God said to Balaam, "Do not go with them. You must not curse this people, for they are blessed."
[Numbers] [22]:[13] The next morning Balaam got up and said to Balak's officials, "Go back to your own country, for the LORD has refused to let me go with you."
[Numbers] [22]:[14] So the Moabite officials returned to Balak and said, "Balaam refused to come with us."
[Numbers] [22]:[15] Then Balak sent other officials, more numerous and more distinguished than the first.
[Numbers] [22]:[16] They came to Balaam and said, "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: Do not let anything keep you from coming to me,
[Numbers] [22]:[17] for I will reward you handsomely and do whatever you ask. Only come and put a curse on this people for me."
[Numbers] [22]:[18] But Balaam answered Balak's servants, "Even if Balak gave me his palace filled with silver and gold, I could not do anything, small or great, that would go beyond the command of the LORD my God.
[Numbers] [22]:[19] Now stay here tonight, as the others did, and I will find out what more the LORD may say to me."
[Numbers] [22]:[20] That night God came to Balaam and said, "Since these men have come to summon you, get up and go with them—but do only what I tell you."
[Numbers] [22]:[21] So Balaam got up in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the officials of Moab.
[Numbers] [22]:[22] But God's anger flared up because he was going, and the angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.
[Numbers] [22]:[23] When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand, she turned off the road into a field. Balaam beat her to get her back on the road.
[Numbers] [22]:[24] Then the angel of the LORD took his stand in a narrow path between two vineyards, with a wall on either side.
[Numbers] [22]:[25] When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she pressed against the wall, crushing Balaam's foot against it. So he beat her again.
[Numbers] [22]:[26] Then the angel of the LORD moved on ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn, either right or left.
[Numbers] [22]:[27] When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam. Balaam's anger blazed, and he beat her with his staff.
[Numbers] [22]:[28] Then the LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you, that you have beaten me three times?"
[Numbers] [22]:[29] Balaam answered the donkey, "You have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now."
[Numbers] [22]:[30] The donkey said to Balaam, "Am I not your own donkey, the one you have ridden all your life to this day? Have I ever been in the habit of treating you this way?" "No," he said.
[Numbers] [22]:[31] Then the LORD opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn. So he bowed low and fell facedown.
[Numbers] [22]:[32] The angel of the LORD asked him, "Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? I have come here to oppose you, because your way is reckless before me.
[Numbers] [22]:[33] The donkey saw me and turned away from me three times. If she had not turned aside, I would surely have killed you by now, and let her live."
[Numbers] [22]:[34] Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, "I have sinned. I did not realize you were standing in the road to oppose me. Now if this displeases you, I will go back."
[Numbers] [22]:[35] The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men, but speak only what I tell you." So Balaam went with Balak's officials.
[Numbers] [22]:[36] When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the Moabite town on the Arnon border, at the very edge of the territory.
[Numbers] [22]:[37] Balak said to Balaam, "Did I not send for you urgently? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to honor you?"
[Numbers] [22]:[38] Balaam answered, "Well, I have come to you now. But can I say whatever I please? I must speak only what God puts in my mouth."
[Numbers] [22]:[39] Then Balaam went with Balak to Kiriath Huzoth.
[Numbers] [22]:[40] Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and gave some to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
[Numbers] [22]:[41] The next morning Balak took Balaam up to Bamoth Baal, and from there he could see the outer edge of the people.
[Numbers] [23]:[1] Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here."
[Numbers] [23]:[2] Balak did as Balaam had said, and Balak and Balaam offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.
[Numbers] [23]:[3] Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your burnt offering while I go aside. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me, and whatever he shows me I will tell you." So he went off to a barren height.
[Numbers] [23]:[4] God met Balaam, and Balaam said to him, "I have set up seven altars, and on each altar I have offered a bull and a ram."
[Numbers] [23]:[5] The LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth and said, "Go back to Balak and speak this."
[Numbers] [23]:[6] So he returned to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offering, he and all the officials of Moab.
[Numbers] [23]:[7] Then Balaam took up his oracle and said: "From Aram Balak brought me, the king of Moab, from the eastern mountains: 'Come, curse Jacob for me; come, denounce Israel.'
[Numbers] [23]:[8] How can I curse those whom God has not cursed? How can I denounce those whom the LORD has not denounced?
[Numbers] [23]:[9] From the rocky peaks I see them, from the heights I behold them: a people living apart, not reckoning themselves among the nations.
[Numbers] [23]:[10] Who can count the dust of Jacob or number even a fourth of Israel? Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like theirs!"
[Numbers] [23]:[11] Then Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies, and instead you have blessed them—blessed them completely!"
[Numbers] [23]:[12] He answered, "Must I not say only what the LORD puts in my mouth?"
[Numbers] [23]:[13] Then Balak said to him, "Come with me to another place, where you can see them. You will see only part of them, not all of them—curse them for me from there."
[Numbers] [23]:[14] So he took him to the field of Zophim, on the top of Pisgah. There he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
[Numbers] [23]:[15] Balaam said to Balak, "Stay here beside your burnt offering while I go over there to meet the LORD."
[Numbers] [23]:[16] The LORD met Balaam and put a word in his mouth, saying, "Go back to Balak and speak this."
[Numbers] [23]:[17] So he came to him, and there he was, standing beside his burnt offering with the officials of Moab. Balak asked him, "What did the LORD say?"
[Numbers] [23]:[18] Then Balaam took up his oracle and said: "Rise, Balak, and listen; hear me, son of Zippor.
[Numbers] [23]:[19] God is not a man, that he should lie, nor a son of man, that he should change his mind. Does he speak and then not act? Does he promise and not fulfill?
[Numbers] [23]:[20] I have been given a word of blessing; he has blessed, and I cannot revoke it.
[Numbers] [23]:[21] He has seen no iniquity in Jacob, and observed no trouble in Israel. The LORD their God is with them; the shout of a king is among them.
[Numbers] [23]:[22] God brought them out of Egypt; they have the strength of a wild ox.
[Numbers] [23]:[23] There is no sorcery against Jacob, no divination against Israel. Now it will be said of Jacob and of Israel: 'See what God has done!'
[Numbers] [23]:[24] Look, a people rises like a lioness; like a lion it rears itself up. It does not lie down until it has devoured its prey and drunk the blood of the slain."
[Numbers] [23]:[25] Then Balak said to Balaam, "Do not curse them at all, then—but do not bless them either!"
[Numbers] [23]:[26] Balaam answered Balak, "Did I not tell you that I must do whatever the LORD says?"
[Numbers] [23]:[27] Then Balak said to Balaam, "Come, let me take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God to let you curse them for me from there."
[Numbers] [23]:[28] So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the wasteland.
[Numbers] [23]:[29] Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here."
[Numbers] [23]:[30] Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
[Numbers] [24]:[1] When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go off as before to seek omens, but turned his face toward the wilderness.
[Numbers] [24]:[2] Balaam looked up and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came upon him.
[Numbers] [24]:[3] He took up his oracle and said: "The word of Balaam son of Beor, the word of the man whose eye is opened,
[Numbers] [24]:[4] the word of one who hears the sayings of God, who sees the vision of the Almighty, who falls down with eyes uncovered:
[Numbers] [24]:[5] How lovely are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!
[Numbers] [24]:[6] They stretch out like valleys, like gardens beside a river, like aloes planted by the LORD, like cedars beside the waters.
[Numbers] [24]:[7] Water shall flow from his buckets, and his seed shall have abundant water. His king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.
[Numbers] [24]:[8] God brought him out of Egypt; he has the strength of a wild ox. He devours the nations that oppose him, breaks their bones to pieces, and shatters them with his arrows.
[Numbers] [24]:[9] He crouches, he lies down like a lion, like a lioness—who dares rouse him? Blessed is everyone who blesses you, and cursed is everyone who curses you."
[Numbers] [24]:[10] Then Balak's anger flared against Balaam. He struck his hands together and said to him, "I called you to curse my enemies, and look—you have blessed them three times over!
[Numbers] [24]:[11] Now get out of here, back to your own place! I said I would reward you richly, but the LORD has kept you from any reward."
[Numbers] [24]:[12] Balaam answered Balak, "Did I not tell the messengers you sent me:
[Numbers] [24]:[13] 'Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the LORD to do anything, good or bad, of my own accord. What the LORD says, that is what I will speak'?
[Numbers] [24]:[14] Now I am going back to my people, but come, let me tell you what this people will do to your people in the days to come."
[Numbers] [24]:[15] Then he took up his oracle and said: "The word of Balaam son of Beor, the word of the man whose eye is opened,
[Numbers] [24]:[16] the word of one who hears the sayings of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, who falls down with eyes uncovered:
[Numbers] [24]:[17] I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel. He shall crush the brow of Moab and break down all the sons of Sheth.
[Numbers] [24]:[18] Edom shall be his possession, and Seir, his enemy, shall be possessed, while Israel does mighty deeds.
[Numbers] [24]:[19] One from Jacob shall rule, and destroy the survivors of the city."
[Numbers] [24]:[20] Then Balaam looked at Amalek and took up his oracle and said: "Amalek was the first of the nations, but its end shall be destruction."
[Numbers] [24]:[21] He looked at the Kenites and took up his oracle: "Your dwelling is secure, your nest is set in the rock;
[Numbers] [24]:[22] yet Kain shall be laid waste. How long before Asshur takes you captive?
[Numbers] [24]:[23] He took up his oracle again and said: "Alas! Who can survive when God does this?
[Numbers] [24]:[24] Ships shall come from the coast of Kittim; they shall afflict Asshur and afflict Eber, and he too shall come to destruction.
[Numbers] [24]:[25] Then Balaam got up and went back home, and Balak also went his way.
[Numbers] [25]:[1] While Israel was staying at Shittim, the people began to commit sexual immorality with the women of Moab.
[Numbers] [25]:[2] These women invited the people to the sacrifices offered to their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods.
[Numbers] [25]:[3] So Israel yoked itself to Baal of Peor, and the LORD's anger burned against Israel.
[Numbers] [25]:[4] The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the leaders of the people and impale them before the LORD in the open sunlight, so that the LORD's burning anger may turn away from Israel."
[Numbers] [25]:[5] So Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Each of you put to death the men under you who have yoked themselves to Baal of Peor."
[Numbers] [25]:[6] Just then an Israelite man came and brought a Midianite woman to his family, in full view of Moses and the whole assembly of Israel, while they were weeping at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
[Numbers] [25]:[7] When Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he rose from the assembly, took a spear in his hand,
[Numbers] [25]:[8] followed the Israelite into the inner chamber, and drove the spear through both of them—the Israelite man and the woman, through her body. Then the plague against the Israelites was stopped.
[Numbers] [25]:[9] Those who died in the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.
[Numbers] [25]:[10] The LORD said to Moses,
[Numbers] [25]:[11] "Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the Israelites, for he was zealous with my own zeal among them; so I did not put an end to the Israelites in my zeal.
[Numbers] [25]:[12] Therefore say: I am giving him my covenant of peace.
[Numbers] [25]:[13] It will be a covenant of a lasting priesthood for him and his descendants after him, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites."
[Numbers] [25]:[14] The name of the Israelite who was killed along with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, the leader of a family within the tribe of Simeon.
[Numbers] [25]:[15] And the name of the Midianite woman who was killed was Cozbi daughter of Zur, a tribal chief of a family in Midian.
[Numbers] [25]:[16] The LORD said to Moses,
[Numbers] [25]:[17] "Treat the Midianites as enemies and strike them down,
[Numbers] [25]:[18] because they treated you as enemies when they deceived you in the affair of Peor, and in the affair of Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite leader, their own sister, who was killed on the day the plague came because of Peor."
[Numbers] [25]:[19] This was after the plague.
[Numbers] [26]:[1] The LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest,
[Numbers] [26]:[2] "Take a census of the whole community of Israel, by their fathers' houses, everyone twenty years old and upward who is fit for military service in Israel."
[Numbers] [26]:[3] So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho, and said,
[Numbers] [26]:[4] "Number those twenty years old and upward," as the LORD had commanded Moses. And these were the Israelites who had come out of the land of Egypt:
[Numbers] [26]:[5] Reuben, Israel's firstborn. The sons of Reuben: from Hanoch, the Hanochite clan; from Pallu, the Palluite clan;
[Numbers] [26]:[6] from Hezron, the Hezronite clan; from Carmi, the Carmite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[7] These were the clans of Reuben, and their number was 43,730.
[Numbers] [26]:[8] The son of Pallu was Eliab,
[Numbers] [26]:[9] and the sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. It was this Dathan and Abiram, chosen leaders of the community, who contended against Moses and Aaron in the company of Korah, when they contended against the LORD.
[Numbers] [26]:[10] The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them along with Korah, when that company died and the fire consumed 250 men, and they became a warning sign.
[Numbers] [26]:[11] The sons of Korah, however, did not die.
[Numbers] [26]:[12] The sons of Simeon by their clans: from Nemuel, the Nemuelite clan; from Jamin, the Jaminite clan; from Jachin, the Jachinite clan;
[Numbers] [26]:[13] from Zerah, the Zerahite clan; from Shaul, the Shaulite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[14] These were the clans of Simeon, numbering 22,200.
[Numbers] [26]:[15] The sons of Gad by their clans: from Zephon, the Zephonite clan; from Haggi, the Haggite clan; from Shuni, the Shunite clan;
[Numbers] [26]:[16] from Ozni, the Oznite clan; from Eri, the Erite clan;
[Numbers] [26]:[17] from Arod, the Arodite clan; from Areli, the Arelite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[18] These were the clans of the sons of Gad, and their number was 40,500.
[Numbers] [26]:[19] The sons of Judah were Er and Onan, but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
[Numbers] [26]:[20] The sons of Judah by their clans were: from Shelah, the Shelanite clan; from Perez, the Perezite clan; from Zerah, the Zerahite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[21] The sons of Perez were: from Hezron, the Hezronite clan; from Hamul, the Hamulite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[22] These were the clans of Judah, and their number was 76,500.
[Numbers] [26]:[23] The sons of Issachar by their clans: from Tola, the Tolaite clan; from Puah, the Punite clan;
[Numbers] [26]:[24] from Jashub, the Jashubite clan; from Shimron, the Shimronite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[25] These were the clans of Issachar, and their number was 64,300.
[Numbers] [26]:[26] The sons of Zebulun by their clans: from Sered, the Seredite clan; from Elon, the Elonite clan; from Jahleel, the Jahleelite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[27] These were the clans of Zebulun, and their number was 60,500.
[Numbers] [26]:[28] The sons of Joseph by their clans: Manasseh and Ephraim.
[Numbers] [26]:[29] The sons of Manasseh: from Machir, the Machirite clan; and Machir was the father of Gilead; from Gilead, the Gileadite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[30] These were the sons of Gilead: from Iezer, the Iezerite clan; from Helek, the Helekite clan;
[Numbers] [26]:[31] from Asriel, the Asrielite clan; from Shechem, the Shechemite clan;
[Numbers] [26]:[32] from Shemida, the Shemidaite clan; from Hepher, the Hepherite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[33] Now Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters, and the names of Zelophehad's daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
[Numbers] [26]:[34] These were the clans of Manasseh, and their number was 52,700.
[Numbers] [26]:[35] These were the sons of Ephraim by their clans: from Shuthelah, the Shuthelahite clan; from Becher, the Becherite clan; from Tahan, the Tahanite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[36] And these were the sons of Shuthelah: from Eran, the Eranite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[37] These were the clans of the sons of Ephraim, and their number was 32,500. These were the sons of Joseph by their clans.
[Numbers] [26]:[38] The sons of Benjamin by their clans: from Bela, the Belaite clan; from Ashbel, the Ashbelite clan; from Ahiram, the Ahiramite clan;
[Numbers] [26]:[39] from Shupham, the Shuphamite clan; from Hupham, the Huphamite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[40] The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: from Ard, the Ardite clan; from Naaman, the Naamite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[41] These were the sons of Benjamin by their clans, and their number was 45,600.
[Numbers] [26]:[42] These were the sons of Dan by their clans: from Shuham, the Shuhamite clan. These were the clans of Dan by their clans.
[Numbers] [26]:[43] All the Shuhamite clans numbered 64,400.
[Numbers] [26]:[44] The sons of Asher by their clans: from Imnah, the Imnite clan; from Ishvi, the Ishvite clan; from Beriah, the Beriite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[45] From the sons of Beriah: from Heber, the Heberite clan; from Malchiel, the Malchielite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[46] The name of Asher's daughter was Serah.
[Numbers] [26]:[47] These were the clans of the sons of Asher, and their number was 53,400.
[Numbers] [26]:[48] The sons of Naphtali by their clans: from Jahzeel, the Jahzeelite clan; from Guni, the Gunite clan;
[Numbers] [26]:[49] from Jezer, the Jezerite clan; from Shillem, the Shillemite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[50] These were the families of Naphtali, clan by clan, and those counted among them were 45,400.
[Numbers] [26]:[51] This was the total number of the Israelites: 601,730.
[Numbers] [26]:[52] The LORD said to Moses,
[Numbers] [26]:[53] "Among these the land shall be divided as an inheritance, according to the number of names.
[Numbers] [26]:[54] To a larger group give a larger inheritance, and to a smaller group a smaller one; each is to receive its inheritance in proportion to its numbers.
[Numbers] [26]:[55] But the land shall be apportioned by lot; they shall receive their inheritance according to the names of their ancestral tribes.
[Numbers] [26]:[56] By the decision of the lot their inheritance shall be assigned, whether the group is large or small."
[Numbers] [26]:[57] These were the Levites who were counted, by their clans: from Gershon, the Gershonite clan; from Kohath, the Kohathite clan; from Merari, the Merarite clan.
[Numbers] [26]:[58] These were the clans of Levi: the Libnite clan, the Hebronite clan, the Mahlite clan, the Mushite clan, the Korahite clan. And Kohath was the father of Amram.
[Numbers] [26]:[59] The name of Amram's wife was Jochebed, a daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt. To Amram she bore Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam.
[Numbers] [26]:[60] To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
[Numbers] [26]:[61] But Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD.
[Numbers] [26]:[62] Those counted among them numbered 23,000, every male a month old and upward. They were not counted among the Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites.
[Numbers] [26]:[63] These were the ones counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who numbered the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
[Numbers] [26]:[64] Among them there was not one of those counted by Moses and Aaron the priest when they numbered the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai,
[Numbers] [26]:[65] for the LORD had said to them, "You shall surely die in the wilderness." So not one of them was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
[Numbers] [27]:[1] Then the daughters of Zelophehad came forward—Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. These were the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
[Numbers] [27]:[2] They stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, and before the leaders and the whole assembly at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and said:
[Numbers] [27]:[3] "Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the company that banded together against the LORD with Korah; he died for his own sin, and he had no sons.
[Numbers] [27]:[4] Why should our father's name disappear from his clan just because he had no son? Give us a holding among our father's brothers."
[Numbers] [27]:[5] So Moses brought their case before the LORD,
[Numbers] [27]:[6] and the LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [27]:[7] "The daughters of Zelophehad are right. You shall certainly give them a holding as their inheritance among their father's brothers, and transfer their father's inheritance to them.
[Numbers] [27]:[8] And say to the Israelites: If a man dies and has no son, you shall transfer his inheritance to his daughter.
[Numbers] [27]:[9] If he has no daughter, you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.
[Numbers] [27]:[10] If he has no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to his father's brothers.
[Numbers] [27]:[11] And if his father had no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to the nearest relative in his clan, and that man shall take possession of it. This shall be a binding statute for the Israelites, as the LORD commanded Moses."
[Numbers] [27]:[12] The LORD said to Moses, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and look at the land I have given to the Israelites.
[Numbers] [27]:[13] When you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was gathered,
[Numbers] [27]:[14] because you rebelled against my command in the Wilderness of Zin, when the assembly quarreled and you failed to uphold my holiness before their eyes at the waters." These are the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin.
[Numbers] [27]:[15] Moses said to the LORD,
[Numbers] [27]:[16] May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the assembly,
[Numbers] [27]:[17] one who will go out and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the LORD's assembly will not be like sheep without a shepherd."
[Numbers] [27]:[18] The LORD said to Moses, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom there is spirit, and lay your hand on him.
[Numbers] [27]:[19] Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole assembly, and commission him in their sight.
[Numbers] [27]:[20] Give him some of your authority, so that the whole community of Israel will obey him.
[Numbers] [27]:[21] He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who will seek guidance for him from the LORD by the judgment of the Urim. At his word they shall go out and at his word they shall come in—he and all the Israelites with him, the entire assembly."
[Numbers] [27]:[22] Moses did as the LORD commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole assembly.
[Numbers] [27]:[23] He laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the LORD had spoken through Moses.
[Numbers] [28]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [28]:[2] Command the Israelites and say to them: My offering, my food, my offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to me—be careful to present it to me at its appointed time.
[Numbers] [28]:[3] Say to them: This is the offering by fire that you are to present to the LORD: two flawless year-old lambs each day as a regular burnt offering.
[Numbers] [28]:[4] Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight,
[Numbers] [28]:[5] along with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with a quarter of a hin of pressed oil.
[Numbers] [28]:[6] This is the regular burnt offering established at Mount Sinai, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
[Numbers] [28]:[7] With it goes a drink offering of a quarter of a hin for each lamb; pour it out in the sanctuary as a drink offering of strong drink to the LORD.
[Numbers] [28]:[8] Offer the second lamb at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning—an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
[Numbers] [28]:[9] On the Sabbath day, offer two flawless year-old lambs, together with two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and its drink offering.
[Numbers] [28]:[10] This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
[Numbers] [28]:[11] At the beginning of each month you are to present to the LORD a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven flawless year-old lambs,
[Numbers] [28]:[12] with three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each bull, two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for the ram,
[Numbers] [28]:[13] and one tenth of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each lamb. This is a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
[Numbers] [28]:[14] Their drink offerings shall be half a hin of wine for each bull, a third of a hin for the ram, and a quarter of a hin for each lamb. This is the burnt offering for the beginning of each month, month by month throughout the year.
[Numbers] [28]:[15] And one male goat is to be offered to the LORD as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its drink offering.
[Numbers] [28]:[16] On the fourteenth day of the first month there is to be the LORD's Passover.
[Numbers] [28]:[17] On the fifteenth day of that month there is to be a festival; for seven days unleavened bread is to be eaten.
[Numbers] [28]:[18] On the first day hold a sacred assembly; you must do no laborious work.
[Numbers] [28]:[19] Present to the LORD an offering by fire, a burnt offering: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old lambs—see that they are flawless.
[Numbers] [28]:[20] With each bull offer a grain offering of three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, and with the ram two tenths;
[Numbers] [28]:[21] with each of the seven lambs offer one tenth.
[Numbers] [28]:[22] Include one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
[Numbers] [28]:[23] Offer all this in addition to the morning burnt offering, which is part of the regular burnt offering.
[Numbers] [28]:[24] In this way you are to offer each day for seven days the food of the offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD; it is to be offered in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
[Numbers] [28]:[25] On the seventh day hold a sacred assembly; you must do no laborious work.
[Numbers] [28]:[26] On the day of firstfruits, when you present to the LORD a grain offering from the new harvest during your Feast of Weeks, hold a sacred assembly; you must do no laborious work.
[Numbers] [28]:[27] Present a burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven year-old lambs,
[Numbers] [28]:[28] with a grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil—three tenths of an ephah for each bull, two tenths for the ram,
[Numbers] [28]:[29] and one tenth for each of the seven lambs.
[Numbers] [28]:[30] Include one male goat to make atonement for you.
[Numbers] [28]:[31] Offer these in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. See that the animals are flawless, and present them with their drink offerings.
[Numbers] [29]:[1] On the first day of the seventh month you shall hold a holy assembly; you shall do no laborious work. It shall be a day of trumpet blasts for you.
