[Numbers] [29]:[2] You shall offer a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all without blemish.
[Numbers] [29]:[3] With them shall come their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for the bull, two tenths for the ram,
[Numbers] [29]:[4] and one tenth for each of the seven lambs.
[Numbers] [29]:[5] Also one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
[Numbers] [29]:[6] These are in addition to the new moon burnt offering with its grain offering, and the daily burnt offering with its grain offering, along with their drink offerings, according to the rule for them—a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
[Numbers] [29]:[7] On the tenth day of this seventh month you shall hold a holy assembly. You shall humble yourselves;* you shall do no work at all. [*Footnote: Literally "afflict your souls"; understood as fasting and self-denial.]
[Numbers] [29]:[8] You shall present a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma: one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old; they must be without blemish.
[Numbers] [29]:[9] With them shall come their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for the bull, two tenths for the one ram,
[Numbers] [29]:[10] and one tenth for each of the seven lambs.
[Numbers] [29]:[11] Also one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering of atonement and the daily burnt offering with its grain offering and their drink offerings.
[Numbers] [29]:[12] On the fifteenth day of the seventh month you shall hold a holy assembly; you shall do no laborious work, and you shall keep a feast to the LORD for seven days.
[Numbers] [29]:[13] You shall present a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old; they must be without blemish.
[Numbers] [29]:[14] With them shall come their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths of an ephah for each of the thirteen bulls, two tenths for each of the two rams,
[Numbers] [29]:[15] and one tenth for each of the fourteen lambs.
[Numbers] [29]:[16] Also one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the daily burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
[Numbers] [29]:[17] On the second day: twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish,
[Numbers] [29]:[18] with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, in proportion to their number, according to the rule;
[Numbers] [29]:[19] also one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the daily burnt offering with its grain offering and their drink offerings.
[Numbers] [29]:[20] On the third day: eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish,
[Numbers] [29]:[21] with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, in proportion to their number, according to the rule;
[Numbers] [29]:[22] also one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the daily burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
[Numbers] [29]:[23] On the fourth day: ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish,
[Numbers] [29]:[24] with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, in proportion to their number, according to the rule;
[Numbers] [29]:[25] also one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the daily burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
[Numbers] [29]:[26] On the fifth day: nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish,
[Numbers] [29]:[27] with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, in proportion to their number, according to the rule;
[Numbers] [29]:[28] also one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the daily burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
[Numbers] [29]:[29] On the sixth day: eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish,
[Numbers] [29]:[30] with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, in proportion to their number, according to the rule;
[Numbers] [29]:[31] also one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the daily burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offerings.
[Numbers] [29]:[32] On the seventh day: seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, without blemish,
[Numbers] [29]:[33] with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, in proportion to their number, according to the rule for them;
[Numbers] [29]:[34] also one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the daily burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
[Numbers] [29]:[35] On the eighth day you shall hold a solemn assembly; you shall do no laborious work.
[Numbers] [29]:[36] You shall present a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD: one bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, without blemish,
[Numbers] [29]:[37] with their grain offerings and drink offerings for the bull, the ram, and the lambs, in proportion to their number, according to the rule;
[Numbers] [29]:[38] also one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the daily burnt offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
[Numbers] [29]:[39] These you shall offer to the LORD at your appointed feasts, apart from your vow offerings and freewill offerings—your burnt offerings, your grain offerings, your drink offerings, and your peace offerings.
[Numbers] [30]:[1] So Moses told the Israelites everything just as the LORD had commanded him.
[Numbers] [30]:[2] Moses said to the heads of the tribes of Israel: This is what the LORD has commanded.
[Numbers] [30]:[3] When a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath binding himself by a pledge, he must not break his word. He must do everything he has said.
[Numbers] [30]:[4] When a young woman still living in her father's house makes a vow to the LORD or binds herself by a pledge,
[Numbers] [30]:[5] and her father hears about her vow and the pledge by which she has bound herself, and he says nothing to her, then all her vows stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself stands.
[Numbers] [30]:[6] But if her father forbids her on the day he hears of it, then none of her vows or the pledges by which she has bound herself will stand. The LORD will forgive her, because her father has forbidden her.
[Numbers] [30]:[7] If she marries while under a vow, or under some rash promise from her lips by which she has bound herself,
[Numbers] [30]:[8] and her husband hears of it and says nothing to her on the day he hears, then her vows stand, and the pledges by which she has bound herself stand.
[Numbers] [30]:[9] But if her husband forbids her on the day he hears of it, he nullifies the vow that binds her and the rash promise of her lips by which she bound herself, and the LORD will forgive her.
[Numbers] [30]:[10] Any vow of a widow or a divorced woman, everything by which she has bound herself, is binding on her.
[Numbers] [30]:[11] If a woman living with her husband makes a vow or binds herself by a pledge under oath,
[Numbers] [30]:[12] and her husband hears of it and says nothing to her and does not forbid her, then all her vows stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself stands.
[Numbers] [30]:[13] But if her husband nullifies them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that came from her lips, whether vows or pledges binding herself, will stand. Her husband has nullified them, and the LORD will forgive her.
[Numbers] [30]:[14] Her husband may confirm or nullify any vow she makes or any sworn pledge to deny herself.
[Numbers] [30]:[15] But if her husband says nothing to her about it from one day to the next, then he confirms all her vows or all the pledges binding her. He confirms them by saying nothing to her on the day he hears of them.
[Numbers] [30]:[16] If, however, he nullifies them some time after he hears of them, then he bears her guilt.
[Numbers] [30]:[17] These are the statutes the LORD commanded Moses concerning a man and his wife, and a father and his young daughter still living in his house.
[Numbers] [31]:[1] The LORD said to Moses,
[Numbers] [31]:[2] "Take vengeance for the Israelites on the Midianites. After that you will be gathered to your people."
[Numbers] [31]:[3] So Moses said to the people, "Arm some of your men for war, so they can go against Midian and carry out the LORD's vengeance on Midian.
[Numbers] [31]:[4] Send a thousand men to war from each of the tribes of Israel."
[Numbers] [31]:[5] So from the clans of Israel a thousand were enlisted from each tribe—twelve thousand men armed for war.
[Numbers] [31]:[6] Moses sent them out to war, a thousand from each tribe, along with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, who took with him the holy vessels and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.
[Numbers] [31]:[7] They fought against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
[Numbers] [31]:[8] Among the slain were the kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—the five kings of Midian. They also put Balaam son of Beor to the sword.
[Numbers] [31]:[9] The Israelites took the women of Midian and their children captive, and they plundered all their herds, all their flocks, and all their goods.
[Numbers] [31]:[10] They burned all the towns where the Midianites had settled, along with all their encampments.
[Numbers] [31]:[11] They carried off all the spoil and all the plunder, both people and livestock,
[Numbers] [31]:[12] and brought the captives, the plunder, and the spoil to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the assembly of the Israelites at the camp on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.
[Numbers] [31]:[13] Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the assembly went out to meet them outside the camp.
[Numbers] [31]:[14] But Moses was angry with the officers of the army—the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds—who were returning from the campaign.
[Numbers] [31]:[15] "Have you let all the women live?" he said to them.
[Numbers] [31]:[16] "These were the very ones who followed Balaam's advice and enticed the Israelites to be unfaithful to the LORD in the affair at Peor, so that a plague struck the LORD's assembly.
[Numbers] [31]:[17] Now kill every male among the children, and kill every woman who has slept with a man.
[Numbers] [31]:[18] But keep alive for yourselves every girl who has never slept with a man.
[Numbers] [31]:[19] As for you, stay outside the camp for seven days. Everyone who has killed a person or touched a dead body must purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, both you and your captives.
[Numbers] [31]:[20] Purify every garment, everything made of leather, everything woven of goat hair, and every wooden object."
[Numbers] [31]:[21] Then Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had gone into battle, "This is the requirement of the law that the LORD gave Moses:
[Numbers] [31]:[22] the gold, the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin, and the lead—
[Numbers] [31]:[23] anything that can withstand fire you must put through the fire, and it will be clean. But it must also be purified with the water of cleansing. And whatever cannot withstand fire you must pass through the water.
[Numbers] [31]:[24] On the seventh day wash your clothes, and you will be clean. Then you may come into the camp."
[Numbers] [31]:[25] The LORD said to Moses,
[Numbers] [31]:[26] "You, Eleazar the priest, and the family heads of the assembly are to count all that was captured, both people and livestock.
[Numbers] [31]:[27] Divide the plunder between the fighting men who went into battle and the rest of the assembly.
[Numbers] [31]:[28] From the soldiers who went into battle, set apart as a tribute for the LORD one out of every five hundred—of the people, the cattle, the donkeys, and the sheep and goats.
[Numbers] [31]:[29] Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the LORD's portion.
[Numbers] [31]:[30] From the Israelites' half, take one out of every fifty—of the people, the cattle, the donkeys, the sheep and goats, all the livestock—and give them to the Levites, who are charged with the care of the LORD's tabernacle."
[Numbers] [31]:[31] So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [31]:[32] The plunder remaining from the spoil taken by the fighting men was 675,000 sheep and goats,
[Numbers] [31]:[33] 72,000 cattle,
[Numbers] [31]:[34] 61,000 donkeys,
[Numbers] [31]:[35] and 32,000 women who had never slept with a man.
[Numbers] [31]:[36] The half belonging to those who had gone to war came to 337,500 sheep and goats,
[Numbers] [31]:[37] of which the tribute for the LORD was 675;
[Numbers] [31]:[38] 36,000 cattle, of which the tribute for the LORD was 72;
[Numbers] [31]:[39] 30,500 donkeys, of which the tribute for the LORD was 61;
[Numbers] [31]:[40] and 16,000 people, of whom the tribute for the LORD was 32.
[Numbers] [31]:[41] Moses gave the tribute, the LORD's portion, to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD had commanded him.
[Numbers] [31]:[42] Then there was the Israelites' half, which Moses had divided off from the share of the fighting men:
[Numbers] [31]:[43] The assembly's half came to 337,500 sheep and goats,
[Numbers] [31]:[44] 36,000 cattle,
[Numbers] [31]:[45] 30,500 donkeys,
[Numbers] [31]:[46] and 16,000 people.
[Numbers] [31]:[47] From the Israelites' half Moses took one out of every fifty, both of the people and of the livestock, and gave them to the Levites, who were charged with the care of the LORD's tabernacle, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [31]:[48] Then the officers over the units of the army—the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds—came to Moses
[Numbers] [31]:[49] and said to him, "Your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one man is missing.
[Numbers] [31]:[50] So we have brought as an offering to the LORD the gold articles each of us found—armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and pendants—to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD."
[Numbers] [31]:[51] Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, all the crafted articles.
[Numbers] [31]:[52] All the gold that the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds presented to the LORD came to sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels.
[Numbers] [31]:[53] Each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself.
[Numbers] [31]:[54] Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD.
[Numbers] [32]:[1] The Reubenites and the Gadites had very large herds and flocks. When they saw that the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead was ideal country for livestock,
[Numbers] [32]:[2] they came to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the leaders of the community, and said:
[Numbers] [32]:[3] "Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo and Beon—
[Numbers] [32]:[4] the land the LORD struck down before the community of Israel—is land for livestock, and your servants have livestock."
[Numbers] [32]:[5] They said, "If we have found favor in your eyes, let this land be given to your servants as a possession. Do not make us cross the Jordan."
[Numbers] [32]:[6] Moses said to the Gadites and the Reubenites, "Shall your brothers go to war while you sit here?
[Numbers] [32]:[7] Why would you discourage the Israelites from crossing over into the land the LORD has given them?
[Numbers] [32]:[8] This is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh Barnea to look over the land.
[Numbers] [32]:[9] They went up as far as the Valley of Eshcol, saw the land, and discouraged the Israelites from entering the land the LORD had given them.
[Numbers] [32]:[10] The LORD's anger burned that day, and he swore this oath:
[Numbers] [32]:[11] 'Not one of the men who came up out of Egypt, twenty years old or more, will see the land I promised on oath to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, because they have not followed me wholeheartedly—
[Numbers] [32]:[12] not one except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, for they followed the LORD wholeheartedly.'
[Numbers] [32]:[13] The LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil in his sight was gone.
[Numbers] [32]:[14] And now here you stand, in place of your fathers—a brood of sinners, adding still more to the LORD's fierce anger against Israel.
[Numbers] [32]:[15] If you turn away from following him, he will again leave this people in the wilderness, and you will be the ruin of them all."
[Numbers] [32]:[16] Then they came up to him and said, "We would like to build pens here for our livestock and cities for our little ones.
[Numbers] [32]:[17] But we will take up arms at once and go ahead of the Israelites until we have brought them to their place. Meanwhile our little ones will live in fortified cities, safe from the inhabitants of the land.
[Numbers] [32]:[18] We will not return to our homes until every Israelite has received his inheritance.
[Numbers] [32]:[19] We will not inherit any land with them on the other side of the Jordan or beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on the east side of the Jordan."
[Numbers] [32]:[20] Then Moses said to them, "If you will do this—if you will arm yourselves before the LORD for battle,
[Numbers] [32]:[21] and if every armed man among you crosses the Jordan before the LORD until he has driven out his enemies before him,
[Numbers] [32]:[22] and the land is subdued before the LORD—then afterward you may return, free of obligation to the LORD and to Israel. And this land will be your possession before the LORD.
[Numbers] [32]:[23] But if you fail to do this, you will be sinning against the LORD; and be sure your sin will find you out.
[Numbers] [32]:[24] Build cities for your little ones and pens for your flocks—but do what you have promised."
[Numbers] [32]:[25] The Gadites and the Reubenites said to Moses, "Your servants will do as our lord commands.
[Numbers] [32]:[26] Our little ones, our wives, our flocks and all our livestock will remain here in the cities of Gilead.
[Numbers] [32]:[27] But your servants, every man armed for war, will cross over to fight before the LORD, just as our lord says."
[Numbers] [32]:[28] Then Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the family heads of the Israelite tribes.
[Numbers] [32]:[29] He said to them, "If the Gadites and the Reubenites, every man armed for battle, cross the Jordan with you before the LORD, then when the land is subdued before you, give them the land of Gilead as their possession.
[Numbers] [32]:[30] But if they do not cross over with you armed, they must accept their holding among you in the land of Canaan."
[Numbers] [32]:[31] The Gadites and the Reubenites answered, "What the LORD has said to your servants, we will do.
[Numbers] [32]:[32] We will cross over before the LORD into Canaan armed for battle, but the property we inherit will be on this side of the Jordan."
[Numbers] [32]:[33] So Moses gave to the Gadites, the Reubenites and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan—the whole land with its cities and the territory around them.
[Numbers] [32]:[34] The Gadites rebuilt Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
[Numbers] [32]:[35] Atroth Shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
[Numbers] [32]:[36] Beth Nimrah and Beth Haran as fortified cities, and they built pens for their flocks.
[Numbers] [32]:[37] And the Reubenites rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh and Kiriathaim,
[Numbers] [32]:[38] as well as Nebo and Baal Meon (these names were changed) and Sibmah. They gave new names to the cities they rebuilt.
[Numbers] [32]:[39] The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were there.
[Numbers] [32]:[40] So Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
[Numbers] [32]:[41] Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, went and captured their settlements and named them Havvoth Jair.[^1] [^1]: Havvoth Jair means "the settlements of Jair."
[Numbers] [32]:[42] Nobah went and captured Kenath and its surrounding villages, and he called it Nobah, after himself.
[Numbers] [33]:[1] These are the stages of the journey of the Israelites when they came out of Egypt by their divisions, under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
[Numbers] [33]:[2] At the LORD's command Moses wrote down the places from which they set out, stage by stage. These are their stages, from one starting point to the next:
[Numbers] [33]:[3] They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. The day after the Passover the Israelites marched out boldly, in full view of all the Egyptians,
[Numbers] [33]:[4] while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck down among them; and the LORD had also brought judgment on their gods.
[Numbers] [33]:[5] The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
[Numbers] [33]:[6] They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
[Numbers] [33]:[7] They set out from Etham, turned back to Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and camped near Migdol.
[Numbers] [33]:[8] They set out from Pi-hahiroth, passed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness, traveled three days through the wilderness of Etham, and camped at Marah.
[Numbers] [33]:[9] They set out from Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
[Numbers] [33]:[10] They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.[^1] [^1]: Hebrew *Yam Suph*, which may also be rendered Sea of Reeds.
[Numbers] [33]:[11] They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
[Numbers] [33]:[12] They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
[Numbers] [33]:[13] They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
[Numbers] [33]:[14] They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
[Numbers] [33]:[15] They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
[Numbers] [33]:[16] They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
[Numbers] [33]:[17] They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
[Numbers] [33]:[18] They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
[Numbers] [33]:[19] They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
[Numbers] [33]:[20] They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
[Numbers] [33]:[21] They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
[Numbers] [33]:[22] They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
[Numbers] [33]:[23] They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
[Numbers] [33]:[24] They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
[Numbers] [33]:[25] They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
[Numbers] [33]:[26] They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
[Numbers] [33]:[27] They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
[Numbers] [33]:[28] They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
[Numbers] [33]:[29] They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
[Numbers] [33]:[30] They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
[Numbers] [33]:[31] They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
[Numbers] [33]:[32] They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
[Numbers] [33]:[33] They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
[Numbers] [33]:[34] They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
[Numbers] [33]:[35] They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
[Numbers] [33]:[36] They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin, that is, at Kadesh.
[Numbers] [33]:[37] They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom.
[Numbers] [33]:[38] At the LORD's command Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor, and there he died, in the fortieth year after the Israelites came out of Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month.
[Numbers] [33]:[39] Aaron was a hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
[Numbers] [33]:[40] Now the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.
[Numbers] [33]:[41] They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
[Numbers] [33]:[42] They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
[Numbers] [33]:[43] They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
[Numbers] [33]:[44] They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
[Numbers] [33]:[45] They set out from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.
[Numbers] [33]:[46] They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
[Numbers] [33]:[47] They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, facing Nebo.
[Numbers] [33]:[48] They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
[Numbers] [33]:[49] There on the plains of Moab they camped along the Jordan, from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim.
[Numbers] [33]:[50] On the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho, the LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [33]:[51] "Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
[Numbers] [33]:[52] drive out before you all the inhabitants of the land. Destroy all their carved images and all their cast idols, and demolish all their high places.
[Numbers] [33]:[53] Take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to possess.
[Numbers] [33]:[54] You shall apportion the land by lot according to your clans: give a larger inheritance to a larger clan and a smaller one to a smaller clan. Whatever falls to anyone by lot shall be his. You shall divide it according to your ancestral tribes.
[Numbers] [33]:[55] But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land before you, those you allow to remain will become splinters in your eyes and thorns in your sides. They will harass you in the land where you live,
[Numbers] [33]:[56] and then I will do to you what I planned to do to them."
[Numbers] [34]:[1] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [34]:[2] Command the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land of Canaan, this is the land that will fall to you as your inheritance — the land of Canaan with its boundaries.
[Numbers] [34]:[3] Your southern side shall run from the Wilderness of Zin along the border of Edom. Your southern boundary shall begin at the end of the Salt Sea on the east,
[Numbers] [34]:[4] then turn south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, continue on to Zin, and end south of Kadesh Barnea. From there it shall go on to Hazar Addar and pass over to Azmon,
[Numbers] [34]:[5] where it shall turn from Azmon to the Wadi of Egypt and end at the Sea.
[Numbers] [34]:[6] For your western boundary you shall have the Great Sea and its coast. This shall be your western boundary.
[Numbers] [34]:[7] This shall be your northern boundary: from the Great Sea mark out a line to Mount Hor,
[Numbers] [34]:[8] and from Mount Hor mark out a line to Lebo Hamath, and the boundary shall end at Zedad.
[Numbers] [34]:[9] Then the boundary shall go on to Ziphron and end at Hazar Enan. This shall be your northern boundary.
[Numbers] [34]:[10] For your eastern boundary, mark out a line from Hazar Enan to Shepham.
[Numbers] [34]:[11] The boundary shall go down from Shepham to Riblah on the east side of Ain and continue down until it touches the eastern slope of the Sea of Kinnereth.
[Numbers] [34]:[12] Then the boundary shall go down along the Jordan and end at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land, with its boundaries on every side.
[Numbers] [34]:[13] Moses commanded the Israelites: This is the land you are to receive as your inheritance by lot, the land the LORD has commanded to be given to the nine and a half tribes.
[Numbers] [34]:[14] For the tribe of the Reubenites by their ancestral houses and the tribe of the Gadites by their ancestral houses have already received their inheritance, and the half-tribe of Manasseh has received theirs as well.
[Numbers] [34]:[15] These two and a half tribes have received their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, eastward toward the sunrise.
[Numbers] [34]:[16] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [34]:[17] These are the names of the men who shall divide the land among you as your inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
[Numbers] [34]:[18] You shall also take one leader, one leader from each tribe, to apportion the land as an inheritance.
[Numbers] [34]:[19] And these are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
[Numbers] [34]:[20] from the tribe of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
[Numbers] [34]:[21] from the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Kislon;
[Numbers] [34]:[22] the leader from the tribe of Dan, Bukki son of Jogli;
[Numbers] [34]:[23] from the sons of Joseph: the leader from the tribe of Manasseh, Hanniel son of Ephod,
[Numbers] [34]:[24] and the leader from the tribe of Ephraim, Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
[Numbers] [34]:[25] the leader from the tribe of Zebulun, Elizaphan son of Parnach;
[Numbers] [34]:[26] the leader from the tribe of Issachar, Paltiel son of Azzan;
[Numbers] [34]:[27] the leader from the tribe of Asher, Ahihud son of Shelomi;
[Numbers] [34]:[28] the leader from the tribe of Naphtali, Pedahel son of Ammihud.

[Numbers] [35]:[1] The LORD spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho:
[Numbers] [35]:[2] "Command the Israelites to give the Levites towns to live in out of the inheritance they possess, and give the Levites pastureland around those towns.
[Numbers] [35]:[3] The towns will be theirs to live in, and the pastureland will be for their livestock, their goods, and all their animals.
[Numbers] [35]:[4] The pastureland around the towns you give the Levites shall extend a thousand cubits out from the town wall on every side.
[Numbers] [35]:[5] Outside the town, measure two thousand cubits on the east side, two thousand on the south, two thousand on the west, and two thousand on the north, with the town in the center. This will be the pastureland for their towns.
[Numbers] [35]:[6] Among the towns you give the Levites there shall be six cities of refuge, to which anyone who has killed a person may flee. To these add forty-two more towns.
[Numbers] [35]:[7] In all you are to give the Levites forty-eight towns, together with their pastureland.
[Numbers] [35]:[8] The towns you give from the holdings of the Israelites shall be taken in proportion: from a larger tribe take more, from a smaller tribe take fewer. Each tribe is to give the Levites towns according to the size of its inheritance."
[Numbers] [35]:[9] The LORD said to Moses:
[Numbers] [35]:[10] "Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
[Numbers] [35]:[11] select certain towns to be your cities of refuge, to which a person who has killed someone unintentionally may flee.
[Numbers] [35]:[12] They will be your refuge from the avenger, so that the one accused of murder does not die until he has stood trial before the assembly.
[Numbers] [35]:[13] The six towns you give shall be your cities of refuge.
[Numbers] [35]:[14] Give three of them on the east side of the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan as cities of refuge.
[Numbers] [35]:[15] These six towns will be a place of refuge for the Israelites, for the foreigner, and for the stranger living among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
[Numbers] [35]:[16] If a man strikes someone with an iron object so that he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
[Numbers] [35]:[17] Or if a man has a stone in his hand that can kill, and he strikes someone so that he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
[Numbers] [35]:[18] Or if a man has a wooden object in his hand that can kill, and he strikes someone so that he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
[Numbers] [35]:[19] The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death; when he finds him, he shall kill him.
[Numbers] [35]:[20] If a man shoves another out of hatred, or deliberately throws something at him so that he dies,
[Numbers] [35]:[21] or in hostility strikes him with his hand so that he dies, the one who struck him must be put to death; he is a murderer. The avenger of blood shall kill the murderer when he meets him.
[Numbers] [35]:[22] But if he shoves him suddenly, without hostility, or throws some object at him unintentionally,
[Numbers] [35]:[23] or without seeing him drops on him a stone that can kill, and he dies—though he was not his enemy and did not intend him harm—
[Numbers] [35]:[24] then the assembly must judge between the accused and the avenger of blood according to these regulations.
[Numbers] [35]:[25] The assembly is to protect the one accused of murder from the avenger of blood and send him back to the city of refuge to which he fled. He must stay there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
[Numbers] [35]:[26] But if he ever leaves the boundary of the city of refuge to which he has fled,
[Numbers] [35]:[27] and the avenger of blood finds him outside the boundary of his city of refuge and kills him, the avenger is not guilty of bloodshed;
[Numbers] [35]:[28] for the accused must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest. Only after the death of the high priest may he return to his own property.
[Numbers] [35]:[29] These are to be legal statutes for you throughout your generations, wherever you live.
[Numbers] [35]:[30] Anyone who kills a person is to be put to death on the testimony of witnesses; no one is to be put to death on the testimony of a single witness.
[Numbers] [35]:[31] Do not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves to die; he must surely be put to death.
[Numbers] [35]:[32] Do not accept a ransom for anyone who has fled to a city of refuge, allowing him to go back and live on his own land before the death of the high priest.
[Numbers] [35]:[33] Do not pollute the land where you live. Bloodshed pollutes the land, and no atonement can be made for the land on which blood has been shed except by the blood of the one who shed it.
[Numbers] [35]:[34] Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell, for I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites."
[Numbers] [36]:[1] The heads of the fathers' houses of the clan of the sons of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, from the clans of the sons of Joseph, came forward. They spoke before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the fathers' houses of the Israelites.
[Numbers] [36]:[2] They said, "The LORD commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the Israelites, and my lord was commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.
[Numbers] [36]:[3] Now if they marry men from another of the Israelite tribes, their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our fathers and added to the inheritance of the tribe they marry into; so it will be taken from the portion allotted to us.
[Numbers] [36]:[4] And when the Jubilee comes for the Israelites, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe they have married into, and their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of our fathers' tribe."
[Numbers] [36]:[5] So at the word of the LORD, Moses commanded the Israelites: "What the tribe of the sons of Joseph says is right.
[Numbers] [36]:[6] This is what the LORD has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: They may marry whomever they please, but they must marry within a clan of their father's tribe.
[Numbers] [36]:[7] No inheritance of the Israelites shall pass from tribe to tribe, for each of the Israelites shall hold to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.
[Numbers] [36]:[8] Every daughter who inherits property in any of the Israelite tribes shall marry someone from a clan of her father's tribe, so that each of the Israelites may keep the inheritance of his fathers.
[Numbers] [36]:[9] No inheritance shall pass from one tribe to another, for each of the Israelite tribes shall hold to its own inheritance."
[Numbers] [36]:[10] The daughters of Zelophehad did just as the LORD commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [36]:[11] Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married sons of their father's brothers.
[Numbers] [36]:[12] They married within the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of their father's clan.
[Numbers] [36]:[13] These are the commandments and ordinances that the LORD gave through Moses to the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[1] These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Di-zahab.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[2] It is eleven days' journey from Horeb by way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-barnea.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[3] In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses spoke to the Israelites everything the LORD had commanded him to tell them.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[4] This was after he had defeated Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[5] There, beyond the Jordan in the land of Moab, Moses undertook to expound this law, saying:
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[6] The LORD our God said to us at Horeb: "You have stayed long enough at this mountain.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[7] Break camp and set out. Go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors—in the Arabah, in the hills, in the lowlands, in the Negev, and along the seacoast—the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[8] See, I have set the land before you. Go in and take possession of the land the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, that he would give to them and to their descendants after them."
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[9] At that time I said to you, "I cannot carry you alone.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[10] The LORD your God has multiplied you, and today you are as numerous as the stars of heaven.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[11] May the LORD, the God of your fathers, increase you a thousand times over and bless you as he has promised!
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[12] But how can I bear your troubles, your burdens, and your disputes all by myself?
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[13] Choose from each of your tribes men who are wise, discerning, and respected, and I will set them over you as leaders."
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[14] And you answered me, "What you propose to do is good."
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[15] So I took the leading men of your tribes, wise and respected men, and appointed them as heads over you: commanders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens, and officers for your tribes.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[16] And I charged your judges at that time: "Hear the cases between your brothers, and judge fairly between a man and his brother or the foreigner living with him.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[17] Show no partiality in judgment. Hear the small and the great alike. Do not be intimidated by anyone, for judgment belongs to God. Any case too hard for you, bring to me, and I will hear it."
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[18] At that time I instructed you in everything you were to do.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[19] Then we set out from Horeb and went through all that vast and dreadful wilderness you saw, on the way to the hill country of the Amorites, as the LORD our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh-barnea.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[20] And I said to you, "You have reached the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[21] See, the LORD your God has set the land before you. Go up and take possession of it, as the LORD, the God of your fathers, told you. Do not be afraid; do not be dismayed."
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[22] Then all of you came to me and said, "Let us send men ahead of us to scout out the land and bring back word about the route we should take and the cities we will come to."
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[23] The plan seemed good to me, so I chose twelve of you, one man from each tribe.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[24] They set out and went up into the hill country, and they came to the Valley of Eshcol and explored it.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[25] Taking some of the fruit of the land, they brought it down to us and reported, "It is a good land that the LORD our God is giving us."
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[26] But you were unwilling to go up; you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[27] You grumbled in your tents and said, "The LORD hates us; that is why he brought us out of Egypt—to hand us over to the Amorites for them to destroy us.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[28] Where can we go up? Our brothers have melted our hearts with their report: 'The people are greater and taller than we are; the cities are large, with walls up to the sky; and we even saw the Anakites there.'"
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[29] Then I said to you, "Do not be terrified; do not be afraid of them.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[30] The LORD your God, who goes before you, will fight for you, just as he did for you in Egypt before your very eyes,
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[31] and in the wilderness, where you saw how the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all along the way you traveled until you reached this place."
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[32] Yet for all this, you did not trust the LORD your God,
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[33] who went ahead of you on the way to find you a place to camp—in fire by night and in a cloud by day, to show you the way you should go.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[34] When the LORD heard what you said, he was angry and swore this oath:
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[35] "Not one of these men, this evil generation, shall see the good land I swore to give your fathers—
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[36] none except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He shall see it, and to him and his children I will give the land he set his foot on, because he followed the LORD wholeheartedly."
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[37] Because of you the LORD was angry with me also, and he said, "You too shall not enter there.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[38] Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, he shall enter it. Encourage him, for he will give Israel its inheritance.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[39] And your little ones, whom you said would be taken as plunder, your children who do not yet know good from bad—they shall enter it. To them I will give it, and they will take possession of it.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[40] But as for you, turn around and set out toward the wilderness by way of the Red Sea." [Footnote: Hebrew Yam Suph, also rendered "Sea of Reeds."]
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[41] Then you answered me, "We have sinned against the LORD. We will go up and fight, just as the LORD our God commanded us." And each of you strapped on his weapons, thinking it an easy thing to go up into the hill country.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[42] But the LORD said to me, "Tell them: Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not among you, or you will be struck down before your enemies."
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[43] So I told you, but you would not listen. You rebelled against the LORD's command and in your arrogance you marched into the hill country.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[44] The Amorites who lived in those hills came out against you; they chased you like a swarm of bees and beat you down in Seir, all the way to Hormah.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[45] You came back and wept before the LORD, but the LORD would not listen to your voice or pay attention to you.
[Deuteronomy] [1]:[46] So you stayed at Kadesh a long time—all those days you spent there.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[1] Then we turned back and set out for the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea, as the LORD had told me, and for many days we circled Mount Seir.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[2] Then the LORD said to me,
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[3] "You have circled this mountain long enough. Turn north.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[4] And command the people: You are about to pass through the territory of your kinsmen, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so be very careful.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[5] Do not provoke them, for I will not give you any of their land, not so much as a footstep, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his possession.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[6] You shall buy food from them with silver, so that you may eat, and you shall also buy water from them with silver, so that you may drink.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[7] For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has watched over your journey through this vast wilderness. These forty years the LORD your God has been with you, and you have lacked nothing."
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[8] So we passed by our kinsmen, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, leaving the road through the Arabah from Elath and Ezion-geber. Then we turned and went along the road toward the wilderness of Moab.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[9] And the LORD said to me, "Do not harass Moab or engage them in battle, for I will not give you any of his land as a possession, since I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their possession."
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[10] (The Emim used to live there, a people great and numerous and tall as the Anakim.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[11] Like the Anakim, they too were reckoned as Rephaim, but the Moabites called them Emim.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[12] The Horites used to live in Seir, but the descendants of Esau dispossessed them, wiped them out, and settled in their place, just as Israel did in the land the LORD gave them as their possession.)
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[13] "Now get up and cross the Zered Valley." So we crossed the Zered Valley.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[14] Thirty-eight years passed from the time we left Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Zered Valley, until the whole generation of fighting men had perished from the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[15] Indeed, the hand of the LORD was against them, to root them out from the camp until they had all perished.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[16] When all the fighting men among the people had died,
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[17] the LORD said to me,
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[18] "Today you are to cross the border of Moab at Ar.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[19] When you approach the territory of the Ammonites, do not harass them or provoke them, for I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites as a possession, since I have given it to the descendants of Lot as their possession."
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[20] (That land too was reckoned as a land of Rephaim. Rephaim used to live there, though the Ammonites called them Zamzummim—
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[21] a people great and numerous and tall as the Anakim. But the LORD destroyed them before the Ammonites, who dispossessed them and settled in their place,
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[22] just as he had done for the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, when he destroyed the Horites before them, so that they dispossessed them and have lived in their place to this day.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[23] And the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, were destroyed by the Caphtorim, who came from Caphtor and settled in their place.)
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[24] "Rise up, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley. See, I have given Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land into your hand. Begin to take possession of it, and engage him in battle.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[25] This very day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you upon all the peoples under heaven. When they hear the report of you, they will tremble and writhe in anguish because of you."
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[26] From the wilderness of Kedemoth I sent messengers to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying,
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[27] "Let me pass through your land. I will keep strictly to the road and turn aside neither to the right nor to the left.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[28] Sell me food for silver so that I may eat, and give me water for silver so that I may drink. Only let me pass through on foot,
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[29] as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land the LORD our God is giving us."
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[30] But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass through, for the LORD your God had hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, in order to give him into your hand, as he has now done.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[31] And the LORD said to me, "See, I have begun to give Sihon and his land over to you. Begin to take possession, so that you may occupy his land."
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[32] Then Sihon came out against us with all his people to do battle at Jahaz.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[33] And the LORD our God gave him over to us, and we struck him down along with his sons and all his people.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[34] At that time we captured all his cities and devoted every city to destruction—men, women, and children. We left no survivor.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[35] We took only the livestock as our plunder, along with the spoil of the cities we captured.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[36] From Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Valley, and from the city in the valley, as far as Gilead, there was no town too strong for us. The LORD our God gave them all over to us.
[Deuteronomy] [2]:[37] But you did not go near the land of the Ammonites, nor any part along the Jabbok River, nor the towns of the hill country — nothing that the LORD our God had forbidden us.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[1] Then we turned and went up the road toward Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against us with all his people to fight at Edrei.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[2] But the LORD said to me, "Do not fear him, for I have given him into your hand, along with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[3] So the LORD our God also gave Og king of Bashan and all his people into our hand, and we struck them down until not a single survivor was left.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[4] At that time we captured all his cities; there was not a town we did not take from them—sixty cities, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[5] All of these were cities fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, besides a great many unwalled villages.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[6] We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, destroying every city—men, women, and children.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[7] But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[8] So at that time we took the land from the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon—
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[9] the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, while the Amorites call it Senir—
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[10] all the cities of the plateau, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of Og's kingdom in Bashan.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[11] For only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed was a bed of iron; it is still in Rabbah of the Ammonites, nine cubits long and four cubits wide, by the common cubit.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[12] At that time we took possession of this land. I gave the Reubenites and the Gadites the territory from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, along with half the hill country of Gilead and its cities.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[13] The rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh—the whole region of Argob, all of Bashan. It used to be called the land of the Rephaim.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[14] Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and he named that part of Bashan after himself, Havvoth Jair, which it is called to this day.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[15] And to Machir I gave Gilead.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[16] To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave the territory from Gilead down to the Arnon Valley, with the middle of the valley as the border, and up to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites,
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[17] along with the Arabah, bordered by the Jordan, from Kinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, below the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[18] At that time I commanded you: "The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your fighting men are to cross over armed ahead of your brothers, the Israelites.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[19] Only your wives, your children, and your livestock—and I know you have much livestock—may remain in the cities I have given you,
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[20] until the LORD gives rest to your brothers as he has to you, and they too take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the property I have given you."
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[21] At that time I commanded Joshua: "Your own eyes have seen everything the LORD your God has done to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you are about to enter.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[22] Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God himself will fight for you."
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[23] At that time I pleaded with the LORD:
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[24] "Sovereign LORD, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your mighty hand. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do such deeds and mighty works as yours?
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[25] Let me cross over, I pray, and see the good land beyond the Jordan—that fine hill country and Lebanon."
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[26] But the LORD was angry with me because of you, and he would not listen to me. "Enough," the LORD said to me. "Do not speak to me about this matter again.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[27] Go up to the top of Pisgah and look west and north and south and east. See it with your own eyes, for you shall not cross this Jordan.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[28] But commission Joshua, and strengthen and encourage him, for he will cross over ahead of this people, and he will give them as their inheritance the land you will see.
[Deuteronomy] [3]:[29] So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth Peor.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[1] Now, Israel, listen to the statutes and the ordinances I am teaching you to keep, so that you may live and go in and take possession of the land the LORD, the God of your fathers, is giving you.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[2] Do not add to the word I am commanding you, and do not take away from it, so that you keep the commandments of the LORD your God that I am commanding you.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[3] You saw with your own eyes what the LORD did at Baal Peor: every man who followed Baal Peor was destroyed by the LORD your God from among you.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[4] But you who hold fast to the LORD your God are all alive today.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[5] See, I have taught you statutes and ordinances, as the LORD my God commanded me, so that you may follow them in the land you are entering to take as your own.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[6] Keep them and do them, for this is your wisdom and understanding in the sight of the nations. When they hear all these statutes they will say, "Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people."
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[7] For what great nation has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is to us whenever we call on him?
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[8] And what great nation has statutes and ordinances as righteous as all this law I am setting before you today?
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[9] Only be careful, and guard yourself closely, so that you do not forget the things your eyes have seen, and so that they do not slip from your heart as long as you live. Make them known to your children and to your children's children.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[10] Remember the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me, "Assemble the people before me, and I will let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days they live on the earth, and may teach them to their children."
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[11] You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain blazed with fire to the heart of the heavens—darkness, cloud, and deep gloom.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[12] Then the LORD spoke to you out of the fire. You heard the sound of words but saw no form; there was only a voice.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[13] He declared to you his covenant, which he commanded you to keep—the Ten Commandments—and he wrote them on two tablets of stone.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[14] And at that time the LORD commanded me to teach you statutes and ordinances for you to follow in the land you are crossing over to possess.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[15] Watch yourselves very carefully, since you saw no form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb out of the fire,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[16] so that you do not become corrupt and make for yourselves an idol in any form: the likeness of a male or a female,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[17] the likeness of any animal on the earth or of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[18] the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground or of any fish in the waters below the earth.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[19] And be careful, when you look up to the sky and see the sun, the moon, and the stars—all the host of heaven—that you are not drawn away to bow down to them and serve them, things the LORD your God has allotted to all the peoples under heaven.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[20] But you the LORD took and brought out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be his own people, his inheritance, as you are this day.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[21] The LORD was angry with me because of you, and he swore that I would not cross the Jordan and would not enter the good land the LORD your God is giving you as your inheritance.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[22] For I am going to die in this land; I will not cross the Jordan. But you will cross over and take possession of this good land.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[23] Be careful not to forget the covenant of the LORD your God, which he made with you, and not to make for yourselves an idol in the form of anything the LORD your God has forbidden you.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[24] For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[25] When you have children and grandchildren and have grown old in the land, if you become corrupt and make an idol in any form, doing evil in the sight of the LORD your God and provoking him to anger,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[26] I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you this day that you will quickly perish from the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not live long there, but will surely be destroyed.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[27] The LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and only a few of you will survive among the nations to which the LORD will drive you.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[28] There you will serve gods made by human hands, of wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or eat or smell.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[29] But from there you will seek the LORD your God, and you will find him if you search for him with all your heart and with all your soul.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[30] When you are in distress and all these things have come upon you, in the latter days you will return to the LORD your God and listen to his voice.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[31] For the LORD your God is a merciful God; he will not abandon you or destroy you or forget the covenant with your fathers, which he swore to them.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[32] Ask now about the days that are past, the days before your time, from the day God created man on the earth, and from one end of the heavens to the other: has anything as great as this ever happened, or has anything like it ever been heard of?
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[33] Has any people ever heard the voice of God speaking out of the fire, as you have heard, and lived?
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[34] Or has any god ever attempted to come and take for himself a nation out of the midst of another nation, by trials, by signs and wonders, by war, by a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, as the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your very eyes?
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[35] You were shown these things so that you would know that the LORD is God; there is no other besides him.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[36] From heaven he made you hear his voice to discipline you, and on earth he showed you his great fire, and you heard his words out of the fire.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[37] Because he loved your fathers and chose their descendants after them, he brought you out of Egypt by his presence and his great power,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[38] driving out before you nations greater and stronger than you, to bring you in and give you their land as your inheritance, as it is this day.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[39] Know therefore this day, and take it to heart, that the LORD is God in the heavens above and on the earth below; there is no other.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[40] Keep his statutes and his commandments, which I am giving you today, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and so that you may live long in the land the LORD your God is giving you for all time.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[41] Then Moses set apart three cities east of the Jordan,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[42] so that anyone who killed another unintentionally, without having hated him beforehand, could flee there—to one of these cities—and live.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[43] They were Bezer in the wilderness, on the plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[44] This is the law that Moses set before the Israelites.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[45] These are the testimonies, the statutes, and the ordinances that Moses spoke to the Israelites after they came out of Egypt,
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[46] east of the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses and the Israelites defeated after they came out of Egypt.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[47] They took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan—the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan—
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[48] from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Gorge as far as Mount Sion, that is, Hermon,[^1] [^1]: Mount Sion here is another name for Mount Hermon in the north; it is not the same as Mount Zion in Jerusalem.
[Deuteronomy] [4]:[49] together with the whole Arabah east of the Jordan, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, below the slopes of Pisgah.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[1] Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: Hear, Israel, the statutes and the judgments that I speak in your hearing today. Learn them, and be careful to keep them.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[2] The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[3] It was not with our fathers that the LORD made this covenant, but with us — with all of us who are alive here today.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[4] The LORD spoke with you face to face on the mountain, out of the fire.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[5] I was standing between the LORD and you at that time, to declare to you the word of the LORD, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[6] I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[7] You shall have no other gods before me.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[8] You shall not make for yourself a carved image of any form — of anything in the heavens above, or on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[9] You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, who visits the guilt of the fathers upon the children, to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me,
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[10] but who shows steadfast love to thousands of generations of those who love me and keep my commandments.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[11] You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not leave unpunished anyone who takes his name in vain.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[12] Observe the Sabbath day, keeping it holy, as the LORD your God has commanded you.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[13] Six days you shall labor and do all your work,
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[14] but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you shall do no work — neither you, nor your son or daughter, nor your male or female servant, nor your ox, your donkey, or any of your livestock, nor the foreigner within your gates — so that your male and female servants may rest as you do.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[15] Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out from there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. That is why the LORD your God has commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[16] Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God has commanded you, so that your days may be long and it may go well with you in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[17] You shall not murder.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[18] You shall not commit adultery.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[19] You shall not steal.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[20] You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[21] You shall not covet your neighbor's wife. You shall not set your desire on your neighbor's house, or his field, his male or female servant, his ox or donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[22] These words the LORD spoke to your whole assembly on the mountain, out of the fire, the cloud, and the deep darkness, with a mighty voice — and he added nothing more. He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[23] When you heard the voice out of the darkness, while the mountain was blazing with fire, all the heads of your tribes and your elders came to me,
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[24] and you said: Look, the LORD our God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the fire. Today we have seen that God can speak with a human being and that person still lives.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[25] But now, why should we die? For this great fire will consume us. If we go on hearing the voice of the LORD our God, we will die.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[26] For what mortal has ever heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the fire, as we have, and lived?
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[27] You go near and listen to everything the LORD our God says. Then tell us all that the LORD our God tells you, and we will listen and obey.
[Deuteronomy] [5]:[28] The LORD heard what you said to me, and the LORD said to me: I have heard what this people said to you. Everything they said is good.
