[Deuteronomy] [12]:[18] Instead, you shall eat them in the presence of the LORD your God at the place the LORD your God chooses—you, your son and daughter, your male and female servants, and the Levite within your gates—and you shall rejoice before the LORD your God in everything you undertake.
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[19] Take care that you do not neglect the Levite as long as you live in your land.
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[20] When the LORD your God enlarges your territory as he promised you, and you say, "I want to eat meat," because you crave it, you may eat as much meat as you desire.
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[21] If the place the LORD your God chooses to put his name is too far from you, then you may slaughter any of the herd or flock the LORD has given you, as I have commanded you, and eat within your towns as much as you desire.
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[22] Eat it as you would gazelle or deer; the unclean and the clean alike may eat it.
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[23] Only be firm in this: do not eat the blood, for the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[24] Do not eat it; pour it out on the ground like water.
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[25] Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[26] But your holy offerings and your vow offerings you shall take and bring to the place the LORD will choose.
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[27] Present your burnt offerings, both the meat and the blood, on the altar of the LORD your God. The blood of your sacrifices shall be poured out on the altar of the LORD your God, but the meat you may eat.
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[28] Be careful to obey all these words I command you, so that it may always go well with you and your children after you, because you will be doing what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[29] When the LORD your God cuts off before you the nations you are going in to dispossess, and you drive them out and settle in their land,
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[30] take care that you are not ensnared into following them after they have been destroyed before you. Do not inquire about their gods, asking, "How did these nations serve their gods? I will do the same."
[Deuteronomy] [12]:[31] You must not worship the LORD your God in that way, for in worshiping their gods they have done every abomination the LORD hates—they even burn their sons and daughters in the fire to their gods.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[1] Everything I command you, be careful to do it. Do not add to it, and do not take away from it.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[2] If a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and gives you a sign or a wonder,
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[3] and the sign or wonder he spoke of comes to pass, and he says, "Let us follow other gods"—gods you have not known—"and let us serve them,"
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[4] do not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams. For the LORD your God is testing you, to know whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[5] You shall follow the LORD your God and fear him. Keep his commandments, obey his voice, serve him, and hold fast to him.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[6] But that prophet or dreamer of dreams shall be put to death, for he has spoken rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, seeking to turn you aside from the way the LORD your God commanded you to walk. So purge the evil from your midst.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[7] If your brother, your own mother's son, or your son or your daughter, or the wife you hold close, or the friend who is like your own soul secretly entices you, saying, "Let us go and serve other gods"—gods that neither you nor your fathers have known,
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[8] gods of the peoples around you, whether near you or far away, from one end of the earth to the other—
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[9] do not give in to him or listen to him. Show him no pity; do not spare him or shield him.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[10] You shall surely put him to death. Your own hand shall be the first against him to kill him, and afterward the hand of all the people.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[11] Stone him to death, because he sought to draw you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[12] Then all Israel will hear of it and be afraid, and no one among you will do such an evil thing again.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[13] If you hear that in one of the cities the LORD your God is giving you to live in,
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[14] worthless men have gone out from among you and led the inhabitants of their city astray, saying, "Let us go and serve other gods"—gods you have not known—
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[15] then you shall inquire, investigate, and question thoroughly. And if it is true and confirmed that this abomination has been committed among you,
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[16] you shall surely strike down the inhabitants of that city with the sword. Devote it to destruction—the city, everyone in it, and its livestock—by the sword.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[17] Gather all its plunder into the middle of its square and burn the city and all its plunder with fire, a whole offering to the LORD your God. It shall be a heap of ruins forever, never to be rebuilt.
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[18] Let nothing devoted to destruction cling to your hand, so that the LORD may turn from his burning anger and show you mercy, have compassion on you and multiply you, as he swore to your fathers—
[Deuteronomy] [13]:[19] when you obey the voice of the LORD your God, keeping all his commandments that I am giving you today, and doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[1] You are the children of the LORD your God. Do not cut yourselves or shave the front of your heads for the dead,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[2] for you are a people holy to the LORD your God. Out of all the peoples on the face of the earth, the LORD has chosen you to be his treasured people.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[3] You must not eat anything detestable.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[4] These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[5] the deer, the gazelle, the roebuck, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[6] You may eat any animal that has a divided hoof, split in two, and that chews the cud.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[7] But these you must not eat, though they chew the cud or have a divided hoof: the camel, the hare, and the rock badger. They chew the cud but do not have divided hooves; they are unclean for you.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[8] The pig, too, is unclean for you, because it has a divided hoof but does not chew the cud. You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[9] Of all that lives in the water you may eat this: whatever has fins and scales you may eat.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[10] But whatever has no fins and scales you must not eat; it is unclean for you.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[11] You may eat any clean bird.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[12] But these you must not eat: the eagle, the vulture, the black vulture,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[13] the buzzard, the falcon, any kind of kite,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[14] any kind of raven,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[15] the ostrich, the nighthawk, the sea gull, any kind of hawk,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[16] the little owl, the great owl, the white owl,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[17] the pelican, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[18] the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[19] All winged insects that swarm are unclean for you; do not eat them.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[20] You may eat any clean winged creature.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[21] Do not eat anything you find already dead. You may give it to the foreigner residing in your towns, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to an outsider. But you are a people holy to the LORD your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[22] Be sure to set aside a tenth of all that your fields produce each year.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[23] Eat the tithe of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks in the presence of the LORD your God at the place he will choose as a dwelling for his Name, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God always.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[24] But if the place the LORD your God chooses to put his Name is too far away, and the journey is too great for you to carry your tithe—because the LORD your God has blessed you—
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[25] then exchange it for silver, take the silver in your hand, and go to the place the LORD your God chooses.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[26] Use the silver to buy whatever you desire: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink—whatever you wish. Then you and your household shall eat there in the presence of the LORD your God and rejoice.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[27] And do not neglect the Levite living in your towns, for he has no portion or inheritance of his own among you.
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[28] At the end of every three years, bring out all the tithe of that year's produce and store it in your towns,
[Deuteronomy] [14]:[29] so that the Levite, who has no portion or inheritance among you, and the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow who live in your towns may come and eat their fill. Then the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands that you undertake.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[1] At the end of every seven years you shall grant a release of debts.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[2] This is how the release shall work: every creditor shall release what he has lent to his neighbor. He shall not press his neighbor or his brother for payment, because the LORD's release has been proclaimed.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[3] You may press a foreigner for payment, but whatever your brother owes you, you shall release.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[4] However, there will be no poor among you, for the LORD will surely bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess—
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[5] if only you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God, taking care to follow all this commandment that I am giving you today.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[6] For the LORD your God will bless you as he has promised, and you will lend to many nations but borrow from none; you will rule over many nations, but none will rule over you.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[7] If there is a poor man among you, one of your brothers, in any of your towns in the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not harden your heart or shut your hand against your brother in his need.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[8] Rather, open your hand wide to him and lend him freely whatever he needs.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[9] Be careful that no wicked thought creeps into your heart, such as: "The seventh year, the year of release, is near"—so that you look grudgingly at your brother in need and give him nothing. Then he will cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[10] Give to him generously and without a grudging heart, for because of this the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you set your hand to.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[11] For there will always be poor people in the land. That is why I command you: open your hand wide to your brother, to the needy and the poor in your land.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[12] If one of your own people, a Hebrew man or woman, is sold to you and serves you six years, in the seventh year you shall let that person go free from you.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[13] And when you set him free, do not send him away empty-handed.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[14] Supply him generously from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress. Give to him as the LORD your God has blessed you.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[15] Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you. That is why I am giving you this command today.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[16] But if he says to you, "I will not leave you," because he loves you and your household and is content with you,
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[17] then take an awl and drive it through his ear into the door, and he will be your servant for life. Do the same for your female servant.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[18] Do not think it a hardship to set him free, for his six years of service have been worth twice the wages of a hired hand. And the LORD your God will bless you in all you do.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[19] Set apart to the LORD your God every firstborn male of your herds and flocks. Do not put the firstborn of your oxen to work, and do not shear the firstborn of your flock.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[20] Year after year you and your household shall eat it in the presence of the LORD your God at the place the LORD will choose.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[21] But if it has any defect—if it is lame or blind, or has any serious flaw—you shall not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[22] You may eat it in your own town. Both the unclean and the clean may eat it, as they would a gazelle or a deer.
[Deuteronomy] [15]:[23] Only you must not eat its blood; pour it out on the ground like water.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[1] Observe the month of Abib and keep the Passover to the LORD your God, for it was in the month of Abib that the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[2] You shall sacrifice the Passover to the LORD your God from the flock and the herd, at the place the LORD will choose as a dwelling for his name.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[3] You shall eat no leavened bread with it. For seven days you shall eat with it unleavened bread, the bread of affliction—for you came out of the land of Egypt in haste—so that all the days of your life you may remember the day you left the land of Egypt.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[4] No leaven shall be found anywhere in your territory for seven days, and none of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day shall remain until morning.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[5] You may not sacrifice the Passover in just any of your towns that the LORD your God is giving you.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[6] Only at the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name shall you sacrifice the Passover, in the evening at sunset, the appointed time when you came out of Egypt.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[7] Cook it and eat it at the place the LORD your God will choose, and in the morning you may turn back and go to your tents.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[8] For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a solemn assembly to the LORD your God; you shall do no work.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[9] Count off seven weeks; begin to count the seven weeks from the time you first put the sickle to the standing grain.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[10] Then keep the Feast of Weeks to the LORD your God with a freewill offering in proportion to the blessing the LORD your God has given you.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[11] And you shall rejoice before the LORD your God—you, your son and daughter, your male and female servants, the Levite in your towns, and the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow among you—at the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[12] Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and be careful to keep these statutes.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[13] Keep the Feast of Booths for seven days, after you have gathered in the produce of your threshing floor and your winepress.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[14] Rejoice at your feast—you, your son and daughter, your male and female servants, and the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow who live in your towns.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[15] For seven days you shall celebrate the feast to the LORD your God at the place the LORD will choose, for the LORD your God will bless you in all your harvest and in all the work of your hands, and your joy will be complete.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[16] Three times a year all your men shall appear before the LORD your God at the place he will choose: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Booths. And no one shall appear before the LORD empty-handed.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[17] Each shall give as he is able, in proportion to the blessing the LORD your God has given you.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[18] Appoint judges and officials for yourselves in all the towns the LORD your God is giving you, tribe by tribe, and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[19] Do not pervert justice or show partiality. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[20] Justice, and justice alone, you shall pursue, so that you may live and take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving you.
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[21] Do not plant any tree as a sacred pole beside the altar you build for the LORD your God,
[Deuteronomy] [16]:[22] and do not set up a sacred pillar, for such things the LORD your God hates.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[1] Do not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep that has any defect or serious flaw, for that is detestable to the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[2] If a man or woman among you, in one of the towns the LORD your God is giving you, is found doing what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, violating his covenant,
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[3] and has gone and served other gods and bowed down to them, or to the sun or the moon or any of the host of heaven—something I never commanded—
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[4] and if it is reported to you and you hear of it, then investigate the matter thoroughly. If it is true and confirmed that such a detestable thing has been done in Israel,
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[5] then bring out to your gates the man or the woman who has done this evil thing, and stone that man or woman to death.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[6] On the testimony of two or three witnesses a person shall be put to death; no one shall be put to death on the testimony of only one witness.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[7] The hands of the witnesses shall be the first raised against him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. So you shall purge the evil from among you.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[8] If a case is too difficult for you to judge—cases of bloodshed, of legal rights, or of bodily injury—any dispute within your towns, then rise and go up to the place the LORD your God will choose.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[9] Go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who is in office at that time. Bring your inquiry to them, and they will give you the verdict.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[10] You must act according to the decision they give you from that place the LORD will choose. Be careful to do everything they instruct you.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[11] Act according to the instruction they give you and the judgment they declare to you. Do not turn aside from what they tell you, to the right or to the left.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[12] Anyone who acts arrogantly and refuses to listen to the priest who ministers there before the LORD your God, or to the judge, must die. So you shall purge the evil from Israel.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[13] Then all the people will hear and be afraid, and will not act arrogantly again.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[14] When you enter the land the LORD your God is giving you and take possession of it and settle in it, and you say, "Let us set a king over us like all the nations around us,"
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[15] be sure to set over you the king the LORD your God chooses. He must come from among your own brothers. You may not place a foreigner over you, one who is not your brother.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[16] He must not acquire great numbers of horses for himself, or send the people back to Egypt to get more of them, for the LORD has told you, "You are never to return that way again."
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[17] He must not take many wives, or his heart will be led astray. And he must not accumulate great amounts of silver and gold.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[18] When he takes the throne of his kingdom, he is to write for himself on a scroll a copy of this law, copied from the scroll kept by the Levitical priests.
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[19] He is to keep it with him and read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God and keep all the words of this law and these statutes, and do them—
[Deuteronomy] [17]:[20] so that his heart may not be lifted up above his brothers, and he may not turn from the commandment to the right or to the left, and so that he and his descendants may reign long over his kingdom in Israel.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[1] The Levitical priests—indeed, the whole tribe of Levi—shall have no portion or inheritance with Israel. They shall eat the offerings made by fire to the LORD and the dues that belong to him.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[2] Levi shall have no inheritance among his brothers; the LORD himself is his inheritance, as he promised him.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[3] This is what the priests are due from the people: from everyone who offers a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep, the priest is to be given the shoulder, the two cheeks, and the stomach.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[4] You shall give him the first of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, and the first wool shorn from your flock,
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[5] for the LORD your God has chosen him and his sons out of all your tribes to stand and serve in the name of the LORD for all time.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[6] If a Levite comes from any of your towns anywhere in Israel where he has been living, and he comes with all his heart's desire to the place the LORD will choose,
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[7] he may serve in the name of the LORD his God like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[8] He shall have an equal share of the food, apart from whatever he receives from the sale of his family property.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[9] When you enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, do not learn to imitate the detestable practices of the nations there.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[10] Let no one among you be found who makes his son or daughter pass through the fire, who practices divination or interprets omens, who reads signs or works sorcery,
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[11] who casts spells, or who consults ghosts or spirits, or seeks answers from the dead.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[12] Anyone who does such things is detestable to the LORD, and it is because of these detestable practices that the LORD your God is driving out these nations before you.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[13] You are to be wholehearted in your loyalty to the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[14] The nations you are about to dispossess listen to those who read signs and practice divination. But you—the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[15] The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among you, from your own brothers. You must listen to him.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[16] For this is what you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb, on the day of the assembly, when you said, "Let me not hear the voice of the LORD my God again or see this great fire anymore, or I will die."
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[17] And the LORD said to me, "What they have spoken is good.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[18] I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their brothers. I will put my words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[19] And if anyone refuses to listen to my words, which that prophet speaks in my name, I myself will hold him accountable.
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[20] But any prophet who presumes to speak in my name something I have not commanded him to say, or who speaks in the name of other gods—that prophet must die."
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[21] You may say in your heart, "How can we recognize a word that the LORD has not spoken?"
[Deuteronomy] [18]:[22] If what a prophet proclaims in the name of the LORD does not take place or come true, then that is a word the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously; do not be afraid of him.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[1] When the LORD your God cuts off the nations whose land he is giving you, and you drive them out and settle in their cities and their houses,
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[2] you shall set apart three cities for yourself in the land the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[3] Build roads to them, and divide into three regions the territory that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance, so that anyone who kills another may flee there.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[4] This is the rule for the one who kills another and flees there to save his life: anyone who strikes down his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him in the past.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[5] Suppose a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and as his hand swings the axe to fell a tree, the head slips off the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies. Such a man may flee to one of these cities and live.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[6] Otherwise the avenger of blood might pursue the killer in the heat of his anger, overtake him because the way is long, and take his life—though he did not deserve to die, since he had not hated his neighbor in the past.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[7] That is why I command you: set apart three cities for yourself.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[8] And if the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as he swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land he promised to give them—
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[9] if you carefully keep all this commandment that I give you today, loving the LORD your God and walking in his ways always—then you shall add three more cities to these three,
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[10] so that innocent blood is not shed in the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and bloodguilt does not come upon you.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[11] But if a man hates his neighbor, lies in wait for him, attacks him and takes his life, and then flees to one of these cities,
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[12] the elders of his own city shall send for him and bring him back from there, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to die.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[13] Show him no pity. Purge from Israel the guilt of shedding innocent blood, and it will go well with you.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[14] Do not move your neighbor's boundary marker, set up by those who came before you, in the inheritance you receive in the land the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[15] A single witness is not enough to convict anyone of any crime or offense he may have committed. A matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[16] If a malicious witness comes forward against someone, accusing him of wrongdoing,
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[17] the two parties to the dispute shall stand before the LORD, before the priests and the judges who are in office at that time.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[18] The judges shall investigate the matter thoroughly, and if the witness proves to be a liar, giving false testimony against his brother,
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[19] then do to him what he intended to do to his brother. So you shall purge the evil from among you.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[20] The rest will hear of it and be afraid, and never again will such an evil thing be done among you.
[Deuteronomy] [19]:[21] Show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[1] When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots and an army greater than your own, do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, is with you.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[2] When you are about to join battle, the priest shall come forward and speak to the troops.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[3] He shall say to them: Hear, O Israel, today you are going into battle against your enemies. Do not lose heart. Do not be afraid, do not panic, and do not tremble before them,
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[4] for the LORD your God goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies and to save you.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[5] Then the officers shall say to the troops: Is there a man who has built a new house and not yet dedicated it? Let him go back home, or he may die in the battle and another man dedicate it.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[6] Is there a man who has planted a vineyard and not yet enjoyed its fruit? Let him go back home, or he may die in the battle and another man enjoy it.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[7] Is there a man who is engaged to a woman and has not yet married her? Let him go back home, or he may die in the battle and another man marry her.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[8] The officers shall speak to the troops again and say: Is there a man who is afraid and faint of heart? Let him go back home, so that he does not make his brothers' hearts melt like his own.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[9] When the officers have finished speaking to the troops, they shall appoint army commanders at the head of the people.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[10] When you advance on a city to attack it, first offer it terms of peace.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[11] If it accepts your offer of peace and opens its gates to you, then all the people found in it shall serve you as forced laborers.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[12] But if it refuses peace and makes war against you, then lay siege to it.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[13] When the LORD your God gives it into your hand, put every male in it to the sword.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[14] But the women, the children, the livestock, and everything else in the city—all its spoil—you may take as plunder for yourself, and you may use the spoil of your enemies that the LORD your God has given you.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[15] This is how you shall treat all the cities that lie very far from you, cities that are not among the cities of these nations.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[16] But in the cities of these peoples that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you shall leave nothing alive that breathes.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[17] You shall devote them to destruction—the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites—just as the LORD your God has commanded you,
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[18] so that they may not teach you to imitate all the detestable things they do for their gods, and so you sin against the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[19] When you besiege a city for a long time, waging war against it in order to capture it, do not destroy its trees by taking an axe to them; you may eat from them, but you shall not cut them down. Are the trees of the field human, that you should besiege them too?
[Deuteronomy] [20]:[20] Only trees that you know are not fruit trees may you destroy and cut down, to build siegeworks against the city that is waging war with you, until it falls.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[1] If someone is found slain, lying in the open field in the land the LORD your God is giving you to possess, and no one knows who struck him down,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[2] then your elders and judges shall go out and measure the distance to the towns around the body.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[3] The elders of the town nearest the body shall take a heifer that has never been worked and has never worn a yoke,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[4] and they shall bring the heifer down to a valley with a running stream, where the ground has never been plowed or sown, and there in the valley they shall break the heifer's neck.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[5] Then the priests, the sons of Levi, shall come forward, for the LORD your God has chosen them to serve him and to pronounce blessings in the name of the LORD, and by their word every dispute and every case of assault is to be settled.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[6] And all the elders of the town nearest the body shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[7] and they shall declare: "Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it happen.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[8] Make atonement for your people Israel, whom you have redeemed, O LORD, and do not hold the guilt of innocent blood against your people Israel." And the blood will be atoned for on their behalf.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[9] So you shall purge from among you the guilt of innocent blood, for you will have done what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[10] When you go out to war against your enemies and the LORD your God hands them over to you and you take captives,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[11] and you see among the captives a beautiful woman and are drawn to her and would take her as your wife,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[12] then you shall bring her into your house. She must shave her head, trim her nails,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[13] and put aside the clothes she was captured in. She shall live in your house and mourn her father and mother a full month. After that you may go to her and be her husband, and she will be your wife.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[14] But if you are not pleased with her, you shall let her go wherever she wishes. You must not sell her for money or treat her as a slave, since you have humiliated her.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[15] If a man has two wives, one loved and the other unloved, and both bear him sons, but the firstborn is the son of the unloved wife,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[16] then when he divides his property among his sons, he may not treat the son of the wife he loves as the firstborn in place of the actual firstborn, the son of the wife he does not love.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[17] He must acknowledge the firstborn, the son of the unloved wife, by giving him a double share of everything he owns, for that son is the firstfruits of his strength; the right of the firstborn belongs to him.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[18] If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey his father and mother and does not listen to them even when they discipline him,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[19] his father and mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his town, to the gate where they gather,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[20] and they shall say to the elders of his town, "This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He will not obey us. He is a glutton and a drunkard."
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[21] Then all the men of his town shall stone him to death. So you shall purge the evil from among you, and all Israel will hear of it and be afraid.
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[22] If a man commits a crime punishable by death and is executed, and you hang his body on a tree,
[Deuteronomy] [21]:[23] you must not leave his body hanging on the tree overnight. Be sure to bury him that same day, for anyone who is hanged is under God's curse. Do not defile the land the LORD your God is giving you as your inheritance.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[1] If you see your brother's ox or his sheep straying, do not ignore it; be sure to take it back to him.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[2] If your brother does not live near you, or you do not know who he is, take the animal home with you and keep it until he comes looking for it; then give it back to him.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[3] Do the same with his donkey, and the same with his cloak, and the same with anything else your brother loses and you find. You must not ignore it.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[4] If you see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen on the road, do not ignore it; help him get the animal back on its feet.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[5] A woman must not put on a man's clothing, and a man must not wear a woman's garment, for whoever does such things is detestable to the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[6] If you come upon a bird's nest along the road, in a tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs and the mother sitting on them, do not take the mother along with the young.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[7] You must let the mother go and take only the young, so that it may go well with you and you may live long.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[8] When you build a new house, put a railing around your roof, so that you do not bring bloodguilt on your house if someone should fall from it.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[9] Do not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, or the whole yield will be forfeit—both the crop you have sown and the fruit of the vineyard.[^1] [^1]: Literally "become holy," that is, set apart so that the owner may no longer use it.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[10] Do not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[11] Do not wear cloth of mixed fibers, wool and linen woven together.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[12] Make tassels for the four corners of the cloak you wrap around yourself.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[13] If a man marries a woman, and after sleeping with her comes to hate her,
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[14] and he makes up charges against her and gives her a bad name, saying, "I married this woman, but when I came to her I did not find proof of her virginity,"
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[15] then the young woman's father and mother shall bring the proof of her virginity to the elders of the city at the gate.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[16] The young woman's father shall say to the elders, "I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, and he has come to hate her.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[17] Now he has made up charges against her, saying, 'I did not find proof of your daughter's virginity.' But here is the proof of my daughter's virginity." Then her parents shall spread out the cloth before the elders of the city.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[18] The elders of that city shall take the man and punish him.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[19] They shall fine him a hundred pieces of silver and give them to the young woman's father, because he has given an Israelite virgin a bad name. She shall remain his wife, and he may never divorce her as long as he lives.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[20] But if the charge is true, and no proof of the young woman's virginity is found,
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[21] she shall be brought to the door of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her to death, because she has done a disgraceful thing in Israel by acting like a prostitute while in her father's house. So you shall purge the evil from among you.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[22] If a man is found sleeping with another man's wife, both of them shall die, the man who slept with her and the woman as well. So you shall purge the evil from Israel.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[23] If a man comes upon a virgin in the city who is engaged to another man, and he sleeps with her,
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[24] you shall bring them both out to the gate of that city and stone them to death—the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he violated his neighbor's wife. So you shall purge the evil from among you.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[25] But if the man meets the engaged young woman out in the open country, and he forces her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[26] Do nothing to the young woman; she has committed no sin deserving death. This case is like that of a man who attacks his neighbor and murders him.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[27] For he found her out in the country, and though the engaged young woman cried out, there was no one to rescue her.
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[28] If a man meets a virgin who is not engaged, and he seizes her and lies with her, and they are discovered,
[Deuteronomy] [22]:[29] the man who lay with her shall give her father fifty pieces of silver, and she shall become his wife, because he has violated her. He may never divorce her as long as he lives.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[1] No man shall take his father's wife, nor uncover his father's skirt.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[2] No man whose testicles are crushed or whose organ is cut off shall enter the assembly of the LORD.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[3] No one born of a forbidden union shall enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation none of his descendants shall enter the assembly of the LORD.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[4] No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the assembly of the LORD; even to the tenth generation none of them shall ever enter the assembly of the LORD,
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[5] because they did not come to meet you with bread and water on your journey when you came out of Egypt, and because they hired Balaam son of Beor from Pethor in Mesopotamia to curse you.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[6] But the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam; instead, the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loves you.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[7] You shall never seek their welfare or their good, as long as you live.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[8] Do not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother. Do not despise an Egyptian, for you were a stranger in his land.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[9] The children born to them in the third generation may enter the assembly of the LORD.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[10] When you march out to camp against your enemies, keep yourself from everything evil.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[11] If any man among you becomes unclean from an emission in the night, he shall go outside the camp; he must not come back inside it.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[12] Toward evening he shall wash himself with water, and at sunset he may return to the camp.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[13] You shall have a place outside the camp where you may go to relieve yourself.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[14] And you shall keep a spade among your equipment; when you squat outside, dig a hole with it, and afterward cover up your excrement.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[15] For the LORD your God walks about in your camp to keep you safe and to deliver your enemies to you. Therefore your camp must be holy, so that he does not see anything indecent among you and turn away from you.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[16] You shall not hand a slave back to his master when he has escaped to you from that master.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[17] He shall live with you, among you, in whatever place he chooses in one of your towns, wherever it suits him. You shall not mistreat him.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[18] No daughter of Israel shall be a cult prostitute, and no son of Israel shall be a cult prostitute.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[19] You shall not bring the wages of a prostitute or the earnings of a dog into the house of the LORD your God to pay any vow, for both are detestable to the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[20] You shall not charge your brother interest—interest on money, interest on food, interest on anything that may be lent at interest.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[21] You may charge a foreigner interest, but not your brother, so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything you set your hand to in the land you are entering to possess.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[22] If you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not be slow to fulfill it, for the LORD your God will surely require it of you, and you would be guilty of sin.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[23] But if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[24] Be careful to do what your lips have promised: the freewill offering you vowed to the LORD your God with your own mouth.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[25] When you enter your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat your fill of grapes, but you shall not put any into your basket.
[Deuteronomy] [23]:[26] When you walk into your neighbor's standing grain, you may pluck ears with your hand, but you shall not put a sickle to your neighbor's grain.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[1] If a man marries a woman and then finds her displeasing because he has discovered something offensive about her, he may write her a certificate of divorce, hand it to her, and send her away from his house.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[2] And if, after leaving his house, she goes and becomes another man's wife,
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[3] and this second husband also turns against her, writes her a certificate of divorce, hands it to her, and sends her away from his house—or if the second husband dies—
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[4] then her first husband, who divorced her, may not take her back as his wife, since she has been defiled. That would be detestable in the LORD's sight. You must not bring sin upon the land the LORD your God is giving you as your inheritance.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[5] When a man has just married, he is not to go out with the army or be assigned any other duty. He shall be free to stay at home for one year, to bring joy to the wife he has married.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[6] No one is to take a pair of millstones—or even the upper stone—as security for a debt, for that would be taking a life as security.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[7] If a man is caught kidnapping one of his brothers, an Israelite, and treats him as a slave and sells him, that kidnapper must die. You are to purge the evil from among you.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[8] In cases of skin disease, be careful to do exactly as the Levitical priests instruct you. Take care to follow what I have commanded them.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[9] Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam along the way after you came out of Egypt.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[10] When you make a loan of any kind to your neighbor, do not go into his house to collect what he offers as security.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[11] Stay outside, and let the man to whom you are making the loan bring the pledge out to you.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[12] If he is poor, do not go to sleep holding his pledge.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[13] Be sure to return the pledge to him by sunset, so that he may sleep in his own cloak and bless you. This will be counted as righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[14] Do not exploit a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether he is one of your brothers or a foreigner living in one of your towns.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[15] Pay him his wages the same day, before the sun goes down, because he is poor and his life depends on it. Otherwise he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[16] Fathers are not to be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[17] Do not deny justice to the foreigner or the orphan, and do not take a widow's garment as security.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[18] Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you to do this.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[19] When you are harvesting in your field and overlook a sheaf, do not go back for it. Leave it for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[20] When you beat the olives from your trees, do not go over the branches again. What is left is for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[21] When you harvest the grapes in your vineyard, do not go back over the vines. What is left is for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
[Deuteronomy] [24]:[22] Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[1] When two men have a dispute, they shall come before the court, and the judges shall decide between them, acquitting the innocent and condemning the guilty.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[2] If the guilty man deserves to be beaten, the judge shall have him lie down and be flogged in his presence with the number of lashes his crime deserves.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[3] He may be given forty lashes, but no more; otherwise, if he is beaten beyond this with many blows, your brother will be degraded in your sight.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[4] You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[5] If brothers live together and one of them dies without a son, the widow of the dead man shall not marry outside the family. Her husband's brother shall take her as his wife and fulfill the duty of a brother-in-law to her.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[6] The first son she bears shall carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name is not blotted out of Israel.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[7] But if the man refuses to take his brother's widow, she shall go up to the elders at the city gate and say, "My husband's brother refuses to preserve his brother's name in Israel; he will not do his duty as a brother-in-law to me."
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[8] Then the elders of his city shall summon him and speak with him. If he stands his ground and says, "I do not want to take her,"
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[9] his brother's widow shall step up to him in the presence of the elders, pull his sandal off his foot, spit in his face, and declare, "So shall it be done to the man who will not build up his brother's house."
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[10] And his family shall be known in Israel as "the house of the man whose sandal was pulled off."
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[11] If two men are fighting with each other, a man and his countryman, and the wife of one comes to rescue her husband from the man who is beating him, and she reaches out her hand and seizes him by his private parts,
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[12] you shall cut off her hand; show her no pity.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[13] You shall not have two differing weights in your bag, one large and one small.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[14] You shall not have two differing measures in your house, one large and one small.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[15] You shall have an accurate and honest weight, and an accurate and honest measure, so that you may live long in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[16] For everyone who does such things, everyone who deals dishonestly, is detestable to the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[17] Remember what the Amalekites did to you along the way when you came out of Egypt:
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[18] how they met you on the road and cut down all who were straggling behind, when you were weary and worn out; they had no fear of God.
[Deuteronomy] [25]:[19] Therefore, when the LORD your God gives you rest from all the enemies around you in the land he is giving you as an inheritance to possess, you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget!
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[1] When you come into the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you take possession of it and settle there,
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[2] take some of the first of all the produce of the soil that you harvest from the land the LORD your God is giving you, put it in a basket, and go to the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[3] Go to the priest who is serving at that time and say to him, "Today I declare before the LORD your God that I have come into the land the LORD swore to our fathers he would give us."
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[4] The priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it down before the altar of the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[5] Then you shall declare before the LORD your God: "My father was a wandering Aramean. He went down to Egypt and lived there as a stranger, few in number, and there he became a great nation, mighty and many.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[6] But the Egyptians mistreated us and oppressed us, and imposed hard labor on us.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[7] So we cried out to the LORD, the God of our fathers, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our misery, our toil, and our oppression.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[8] The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, with signs and wonders.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[9] He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[10] And now, see, I have brought the first of the produce of the soil that you, LORD, have given me." Then set it down before the LORD your God and bow low before the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[11] And you shall rejoice in all the good things the LORD your God has given you and your household—you, the Levite, and the foreigner living among you.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[12] When you have finished setting aside the full tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, give it to the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, so that they may eat their fill in your towns.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[13] Then say before the LORD your God: "I have cleared the sacred portion out of my house and given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, just as you commanded me. I have not violated your commandments, nor have I forgotten them.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[14] I have not eaten any of it while in mourning, nor removed any of it while unclean, nor offered any of it to the dead. I have obeyed the voice of the LORD my God; I have done everything you commanded me.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[15] Look down from your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the land you have given us, as you swore to our fathers—a land flowing with milk and honey."
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[16] Today the LORD your God commands you to follow these statutes and ordinances. Keep them and do them with all your heart and with all your soul.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[17] Today you have declared that the LORD is your God, that you will walk in his ways, keep his statutes, his commandments, and his ordinances, and obey his voice.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[18] And today the LORD has declared that you are his people, his treasured possession, as he promised you, and that you are to keep all his commandments.
[Deuteronomy] [26]:[19] He will set you high above all the nations he has made, for praise, renown, and honor, and you will be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he has promised.
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[1] Then Moses and the elders of Israel charged the people: "Keep the whole commandment that I am giving you today.
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[2] On the day you cross the Jordan into the land the LORD your God is giving you, set up large stones and coat them with plaster.
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[3] Write on them all the words of this law when you cross over, so that you may enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the LORD, the God of your fathers, promised you.
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[4] And when you have crossed the Jordan, set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I am commanding you today, and coat them with plaster.
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[5] Build there an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones; do not use any iron tool on them.
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[6] Build the altar of the LORD your God with uncut stones, and offer on it burnt offerings to the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[7] Sacrifice fellowship offerings there, eat them, and rejoice before the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[8] And you shall write very clearly on the stones all the words of this law."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[9] Then Moses and the Levitical priests said to all Israel: "Be silent, Israel, and listen! This day you have become the people of the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[10] So obey the voice of the LORD your God and follow his commandments and statutes, which I am giving you today."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[11] That same day Moses charged the people:

[Deuteronomy] [27]:[13] And these shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[14] Then the Levites shall respond, calling out in a loud voice to every man of Israel:"
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[15] "Cursed is anyone who makes a carved or cast image—a thing detestable to the LORD, the work of a craftsman's hands—and sets it up in secret." And all the people shall answer, "Amen."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[16] "Cursed is anyone who dishonors his father or his mother." And all the people shall say, "Amen."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[17] "Cursed is anyone who moves his neighbor's boundary marker." And all the people shall say, "Amen."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[18] "Cursed is anyone who leads the blind astray on the road." And all the people shall say, "Amen."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[19] "Cursed is anyone who denies justice to the foreigner, the fatherless, or the widow." And all the people shall say, "Amen."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[20] "Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his father's wife, for he has dishonored his father's bed." And all the people shall say, "Amen."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[21] "Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with any animal." And all the people shall say, "Amen."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[22] "Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother." And all the people shall say, "Amen."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[23] "Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his mother-in-law." And all the people shall say, "Amen."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[24] "Cursed is anyone who strikes down his neighbor in secret." And all the people shall say, "Amen."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[25] "Cursed is anyone who takes a bribe to kill an innocent person." And all the people shall say, "Amen."
[Deuteronomy] [27]:[26] "Cursed is anyone who does not uphold the words of this law by doing them." And all the people shall say, "Amen."
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[1] If you listen faithfully to the voice of the LORD your God, keeping and doing all his commandments that I give you today, the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[2] All these blessings will come upon you and overtake you, because you listen to the voice of the LORD your God:
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[3] Blessed will you be in the city, and blessed in the field.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[4] Blessed will be the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your soil, and the fruit of your livestock—the calves of your herds and the young of your flocks.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[5] Blessed will be your basket and your kneading trough.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[6] Blessed will you be when you come in, and blessed when you go out.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[7] The LORD will cause the enemies who rise against you to be struck down before you. They will march out against you by one road and flee from you by seven.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[8] The LORD will command his blessing upon you—on your barns and on everything you set your hand to—and he will bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[9] The LORD will establish you as his holy people, just as he swore to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and walk in his ways.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[10] Then all the peoples of the earth will see that the name of the LORD is called over you, and they will stand in awe of you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[11] The LORD will give you abundant prosperity—in the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock, and the fruit of your soil—in the land the LORD swore to your fathers to give you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[12] The LORD will open his good storehouse, the heavens, to give rain to your land in its season and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations but borrow from none.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[13] The LORD will make you the head and not the tail; you will be only at the top and never at the bottom—if you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I give you today, keeping them and doing them,
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[14] and if you do not turn aside from any of the words I command you today, to the right or to the left, going after other gods to serve them.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[15] But if you do not listen to the voice of the LORD your God, if you are not careful to do all his commandments and statutes that I give you today, then all these curses will come upon you and overtake you:
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[16] Cursed will you be in the city, and cursed in the field.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[17] Cursed will be your basket and your kneading trough.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[18] Cursed will be the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your soil, the calves of your herds and the young of your flocks.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[19] Cursed will you be when you come in, and cursed when you go out.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[20] The LORD will send upon you cursing, confusion, and frustration in everything you set your hand to do, until you are destroyed and quickly perish, because of the evil of your deeds in forsaking me.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[21] The LORD will make the plague cling to you until it has wiped you off the land you are entering to take possession of.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[22] The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, with fever and inflammation, with scorching heat and drought,* with blight and mildew, and they will pursue you until you perish. [*Footnote: The Hebrew word here can be read as "sword"; a closely related form means "drought."]
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[23] The sky above you will be bronze, and the ground beneath you iron.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[24] The LORD will turn the rain of your land into dust and powder; it will come down on you from the sky until you are destroyed.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[25] The LORD will cause you to be struck down before your enemies. You will march out against them by one road and flee from them by seven, and you will become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[26] Your corpses will be food for every bird of the sky and every beast of the earth, and no one will drive them away.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[27] The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, scabs, and itch, and there will be no healing for you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[28] The LORD will strike you with madness, with blindness, and with confusion of mind.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[29] You will grope at midday like a blind man groping in the dark, and you will not succeed in your ways. You will be nothing but oppressed and robbed all your days, with no one to save you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[30] You will be engaged to a woman, and another man will lie with her. You will build a house but not live in it. You will plant a vineyard but never enjoy its fruit.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[31] Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, but you will not eat of it. Your donkey will be seized from you and never returned. Your sheep will be handed over to your enemies, and no one will come to your rescue.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[32] Your sons and daughters will be handed over to another people while you watch, and you will strain your eyes for them day after day, powerless to lift a hand.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[33] A people you do not know will eat the fruit of your soil and all the produce of your labor, and you will be nothing but oppressed and crushed all your days.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[34] You will go mad at the sight of what your eyes must see.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[35] The LORD will strike you with painful boils on your knees and legs, from the soles of your feet to the top of your head, and there will be no healing for you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[36] The LORD will drive you and the king you set over yourself to a nation you and your fathers have never known, and there you will serve other gods of wood and stone.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[37] You will become an object of horror, a byword and a taunt among all the peoples where the LORD drives you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[38] You will sow much seed in the field but harvest little, for the locust will devour it.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[39] You will plant vineyards and tend them, but you will drink no wine and gather nothing, for the worm will consume them.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[40] You will have olive trees throughout your territory, but you will have no oil to anoint yourself, for your olives will drop off.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[41] You will father sons and daughters, but they will not remain yours, for they will go into captivity.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[42] Swarming locusts will take over all your trees and the fruit of your soil.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[43] The foreigner living among you will rise higher and higher, while you sink lower and lower.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[44] He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[45] All these curses will come upon you; they will pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God or keep the commandments and statutes he gave you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[46] They will be a sign and a portent against you and your descendants forever.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[47] Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and a glad heart in the midst of all your abundance,
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[48] you will serve your enemies, whom the LORD sends against you—in hunger and thirst, in nakedness and utter want. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until he has destroyed you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[49] The LORD will bring against you a nation from far away, from the ends of the earth, swooping down like an eagle—a nation whose language you do not understand,
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[50] a ruthless nation that shows no respect to the old and no mercy to the young.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[51] They will devour the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your soil until you are destroyed. They will leave you no grain, no new wine, no oil, no calves of your herds or young of your flocks, until they have brought you to ruin.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[52] They will besiege you in all your towns until the high, fortified walls you trust in have fallen throughout your land. They will besiege you in every town in all the land the LORD your God has given you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[53] Then you will eat the fruit of your own womb—the flesh of the sons and daughters the LORD your God gave you—in the siege and distress your enemy inflicts on you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[54] Even the most refined and delicate man among you will begrudge his brother, the wife he embraces, and the children who are left to him,
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[55] refusing to share with any of them the flesh of his children that he eats, because nothing else is left him in the siege and distress your enemy inflicts on you in all your towns.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[56] The most refined and delicate woman among you, so pampered and soft that she would never set the sole of her foot on the ground, will begrudge the husband she embraces, and her son and her daughter,
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[57] even the afterbirth from between her legs and the children she bears; for in utter want she will secretly eat them in the siege and distress your enemy inflicts on you in your towns.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[58] If you are not careful to do all the words of this law, written in this book, and to fear this glorious and awesome name, the LORD your God,
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[59] then the LORD will bring extraordinary plagues on you and your descendants—severe and lasting plagues, and grievous, lingering diseases.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[60] He will bring back upon you all the diseases of Egypt that you dreaded, and they will cling to you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[61] The LORD will also bring on you every sickness and plague not recorded in this book of the law, until you are destroyed.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[62] You who were as numerous as the stars of the sky will be left few in number, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[63] Just as it pleased the LORD to make you prosper and multiply, so it will please the LORD to bring you to ruin and destroy you, and you will be uprooted from the land you are entering to take possession of.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[64] The LORD will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other, and there you will serve other gods of wood and stone, which neither you nor your fathers have known.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[65] Among those nations you will find no rest, no resting place for the sole of your foot. There the LORD will give you a trembling heart, failing eyes, and a despairing soul.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[66] Your life will hang in the balance before you; night and day you will be filled with dread, never sure of your life.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[67] In the morning you will say, "If only it were evening!" and in the evening, "If only it were morning!"—because of the terror in your heart and the sights your eyes must see.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[68] The LORD will send you back to Egypt in ships, along the road I said you would never see again. There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one will buy you.
[Deuteronomy] [28]:[69] These are the words of the covenant that the LORD commanded Moses to make with the Israelites in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant he had made with them at Horeb.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[1] Moses summoned all Israel and said to them: You have seen everything the LORD did before your eyes in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, to all his servants, and to all his land—
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[2] the great trials your eyes witnessed, those great signs and wonders.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[3] Yet to this day the LORD has not given you a heart to understand, eyes to see, or ears to hear.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[4] I led you forty years in the wilderness. Your clothes did not wear out on you, and the sandals on your feet did not wear out.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[5] You ate no bread and drank no wine or strong drink, so that you would know that I am the LORD your God.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[6] When you came to this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan marched out to meet us in battle, and we defeated them.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[7] We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[8] So keep the words of this covenant and carry them out, that you may prosper in everything you do.

[Deuteronomy] [29]:[12] so that he may establish you today as his people and be your God, as he promised you and as he swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[13] It is not with you alone that I am making this covenant with its oath,
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[14] but with everyone standing here with us today before the LORD our God, and also with those who are not here with us today.

[Deuteronomy] [29]:[16] You saw their detestable things and their idols of wood and stone, of silver and gold, that they kept among them.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[17] Make sure there is no man or woman, no clan or tribe among you whose heart turns away today from the LORD our God to go and serve the gods of those nations—make sure there is no root among you bearing poison and bitterness.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[18] When such a person hears the words of this oath, he congratulates himself in his heart and says, "I will be safe, even though I walk in the stubbornness of my own heart." This would sweep away the watered land along with the dry.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[19] The LORD will never be willing to forgive him. Instead, the LORD's anger and jealousy will smolder against that man, every curse written in this book will settle on him, and the LORD will blot out his name from under heaven.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[20] The LORD will single him out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, in keeping with all the curses of the covenant written in this Book of the Law.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[21] The next generation, your children who come after you, and the foreigner who arrives from a distant land, will see the plagues of that land and the diseases the LORD has inflicted on it—
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[22] the whole land a burning waste of sulfur and salt, unsown, yielding nothing, with not a blade of grass growing on it, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in his anger and wrath.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[23] All the nations will ask, "Why has the LORD done this to this land? Why this great outburst of anger?"
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[24] And the answer will be: "Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their fathers, the covenant he made with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[25] They went and served other gods and bowed down to them, gods they had not known, gods he had not assigned to them.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[26] So the LORD's anger burned against that land, bringing upon it every curse written in this book.
[Deuteronomy] [29]:[27] The LORD uprooted them from their soil in anger and wrath and great fury, and cast them into another land, as it is today."

[Deuteronomy] [30]:[12] It is not in heaven, that you should say, "Who will go up to heaven for us and bring it down to us, so that we may hear it and do it?"
[Deuteronomy] [30]:[13] Nor is it beyond the sea, that you should say, "Who will cross the sea for us and bring it to us, so that we may hear it and do it?"
[Deuteronomy] [30]:[14] No, the word is very near you: it is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can do it.
[Deuteronomy] [30]:[15] See, today I have set before you life and good, death and evil.
[Deuteronomy] [30]:[16] For I command you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his ordinances, so that you may live and multiply, and the LORD your God may bless you in the land you are entering to possess.
[Deuteronomy] [30]:[17] But if your heart turns away and you will not listen, and you are drawn aside to bow down to other gods and serve them,
[Deuteronomy] [30]:[18] I declare to you today that you will surely perish. You will not live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess.

[Deuteronomy] [31]:[1] Then Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[2] He said to them: "I am a hundred and twenty years old today. I can no longer go out and come in, and the LORD has told me, 'You shall not cross this Jordan.'
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[3] The LORD your God himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will take possession of their land. Joshua will cross over ahead of you, as the LORD has said.
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[4] The LORD will do to them what he did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when he destroyed them.
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[5] The LORD will hand them over to you, and you are to deal with them according to every command I have given you.
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[6] Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid, do not be terrified before them, for the LORD your God goes with you; he will never fail you or forsake you."
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[7] Then Moses summoned Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel, "Be strong and courageous, for you will go with this people into the land the LORD swore to their fathers to give them, and you will give it to them as their inheritance.
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[8] The LORD himself goes before you; he will be with you. He will never fail you or forsake you. Do not be afraid; do not be dismayed."
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[9] So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.

[Deuteronomy] [31]:[13] Then their children, who do not know it, will hear it and learn to fear the LORD your God as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."

[Deuteronomy] [31]:[15] Then the LORD appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood over the entrance of the tent.
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[16] And the LORD said to Moses: "You are about to lie down with your fathers, and this people will rise up and prostitute themselves to the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will forsake me and break the covenant I made with them.
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[17] On that day my anger will burn against them. I will forsake them and hide my face from them, and they will be devoured. Many disasters and calamities will come upon them, and on that day they will say, 'Have not these disasters come upon us because our God is no longer among us?'
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[18] And on that day I will surely hide my face because of all the evil they have done in turning to other gods.
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[19] Now write down this song for yourselves and teach it to the Israelites; put it in their mouths, so that it may be a witness for me against them.
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[20] When I bring them into the land I promised on oath to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey, and when they have eaten their fill and grown fat, they will turn to other gods and serve them; they will despise me and break my covenant.
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[21] And when many disasters and calamities come upon them, this song will testify against them, for it will not be lost from the lips of their descendants. For I know what they are inclined to do even now, before I bring them into the land I promised them on oath.

[Deuteronomy] [31]:[26] "Take this Book of the Law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God. There it will remain as a witness against you.
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[27] For I know how rebellious and stiff-necked you are. Even now, while I am still alive and with you, you have rebelled against the LORD; how much more after I die!
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[28] Assemble before me all the elders of your tribes and all your officials, so that I can speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth to testify against them.
[Deuteronomy] [31]:[29] For I know that after my death you are sure to become utterly corrupt and to turn from the way I have commanded you. In days to come disaster will overtake you, because you will do evil in the sight of the LORD and provoke him to anger by what your hands have made."

[Deuteronomy] [32]:[39] See now that I, I am he, and there is no god besides me. I put to death and I give life; I wound and I heal, and no one can deliver from my hand.
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[40] For I lift my hand to heaven and declare: As surely as I live forever,
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[41] when I sharpen my flashing sword and my hand takes hold of judgment, I will bring vengeance on my adversaries and repay those who hate me.
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[42] I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh—the blood of the slain and the captives, the heads of the enemy's leaders.
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[43] Rejoice, you nations, with his people! For he will avenge the blood of his servants; he will bring vengeance on his adversaries and make atonement for his land and his people.
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[44] Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Joshua son of Nun.
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[45] When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[46] he said to them, "Take to heart all the words I am solemnly declaring to you this day, so that you may command your children to be careful to do all the words of this law.
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[47] They are not empty words for you—they are your life. By them you will live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[48] That very same day the LORD said to Moses,
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[49] "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range, Mount Nebo in the land of Moab, opposite Jericho, and view the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites as their possession.
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[50] There on the mountain you are about to climb, you will die and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[51] This is because both of you broke faith with me among the Israelites at the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin, and because you did not uphold my holiness among the Israelites.
[Deuteronomy] [32]:[52] You will see the land from a distance, but you will not enter it—the land I am giving to the Israelites.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[1] This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the Israelites before his death.
