[Deuteronomy] [33]:[2] He said: The LORD came from Sinai and dawned upon them from Seir; he shone forth from Mount Paran and came with ten thousands of holy ones, with flaming fire at his right hand, a law for them.[^1] [^1]: The last line of the Hebrew is uncertain; it may be read "fire of law" or "a fiery law."
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[3] Truly he loves the peoples; all his holy ones are in your hand. They sat down at your feet; each receives your words.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[4] Moses commanded us a law, a possession for the assembly of Jacob.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[5] So he became king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people gathered, the tribes of Israel together.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[6] Let Reuben live and not die; let his men be few no longer.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[7] And this he said of Judah: Hear, O LORD, the cry of Judah, and bring him back to his people. With his own hands he contends for himself; be his help against his foes.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[8] Of Levi he said: Your Thummim and your Urim belong to your faithful one, whom you tested at Massah and contended with at the waters of Meribah.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[9] He said of his father and mother, "I have no regard for them." He did not acknowledge his brothers or recognize his own children, for the Levites kept your word and guarded your covenant.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[10] They teach your judgments to Jacob and your law to Israel. They offer incense before you and whole burnt offerings on your altar.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[11] Bless his strength, O LORD, and accept the work of his hands. Strike down those who rise against him, and let his enemies never rise again.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[12] Of Benjamin he said: The beloved of the LORD dwells in safety beside him; the LORD shelters him all day long, and Benjamin rests between his shoulders.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[13] Of Joseph he said: May the LORD bless his land with the best gifts of heaven above, with the dew, and with the deep waters that lie below;
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[14] with the finest the sun brings forth and the best the moons yield;
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[15] with the choicest fruits of the ancient mountains and the abundance of the everlasting hills;
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[16] with the best gifts of the earth and its fullness, and the favor of him who dwelt in the burning bush. Let all this rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the prince among his brothers.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[17] In majesty he is like a firstborn bull; his horns are the horns of a wild ox. With them he will gore the nations, even those at the ends of the earth. Such are the ten thousands of Ephraim; such are the thousands of Manasseh.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[18] Of Zebulun he said: Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[19] They summon peoples to the mountain; there they offer the sacrifices of righteousness. They feast on the abundance of the seas and on the treasures hidden in the sand.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[20] Of Gad he said: Blessed is he who enlarges Gad! He lies down like a lion, tearing off the arm and the head.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[21] He chose the best land for himself; the leader's portion was kept for him. When the heads of the people assembled, he carried out the LORD's righteous will and his judgments concerning Israel.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[22] Of Dan he said: Dan is a lion's cub, leaping out from Bashan.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[23] Of Naphtali he said: Naphtali is rich in favor and full of the LORD's blessing; he shall take possession of the sea and the south.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[24] Of Asher he said: Most blessed of sons is Asher; may he be favored by his brothers and bathe his feet in oil.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[25] Your gates will have bars of iron and bronze, and your strength will match your days.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[26] There is none like God, O Jeshurun, who rides the heavens to help you, who rides the clouds in his majesty.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[27] The eternal God is your refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms. He drove out the enemy before you and said, "Destroy them!"
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[28] So Israel dwells in safety, set apart, Jacob's fountain secure, in a land of grain and new wine, where his heavens drop their dew.
[Deuteronomy] [33]:[29] Blessed are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD? He is the shield that helps you and the sword of your triumph. Your enemies will cringe before you, and you will tread on their high places.
[Deuteronomy] [34]:[1] Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, across from Jericho. And the LORD showed him the whole land: Gilead as far as Dan,
[Deuteronomy] [34]:[2] all of Naphtali, the territory of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the Western Sea,
[Deuteronomy] [34]:[3] the Negev, and the whole plain—the valley of Jericho, the City of Palms—as far as Zoar.
[Deuteronomy] [34]:[4] Then the LORD said to him, "This is the land I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob when I said, 'I will give it to your descendants.' I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross over into it."
[Deuteronomy] [34]:[5] So Moses, the servant of the LORD, died there in the land of Moab, as the LORD had said.
[Deuteronomy] [34]:[6] He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth Peor, but to this day no one knows where his grave is.<note>The Hebrew verb is singular with an unstated subject; the implied subject is understood to be the LORD, though it may also be read impersonally, "he was buried."</note>
[Deuteronomy] [34]:[7] Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died, yet his eyes were not weak nor his strength gone.
[Deuteronomy] [34]:[8] The Israelites mourned for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days, until the time of weeping and mourning for Moses was over.
[Deuteronomy] [34]:[9] Now Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands on him. So the Israelites listened to him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Deuteronomy] [34]:[10] Never again has a prophet risen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,
[Deuteronomy] [34]:[11] who performed all those signs and wonders the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt—to Pharaoh, to all his servants, and to his whole land—
[Deuteronomy] [34]:[12] and who displayed all that mighty power and all those great and terrifying deeds that Moses did in the sight of all Israel.
[Joshua] [1]:[1] After the death of Moses, the servant of the LORD, the LORD said to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' assistant:
[Joshua] [1]:[2] "Moses my servant is dead. Now get up and cross this Jordan, you and all this people, into the land I am giving to them, to the Israelites.
[Joshua] [1]:[3] Every place where the sole of your foot treads I have given you, just as I promised Moses.
[Joshua] [1]:[4] From the wilderness and this Lebanon to the great river, the Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and on to the Great Sea where the sun sets—all this shall be your territory.
[Joshua] [1]:[5] No one will be able to stand against you as long as you live. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will not fail you or forsake you.
[Joshua] [1]:[6] Be strong and courageous, for you will give this people possession of the land I swore to their fathers to give them.
[Joshua] [1]:[7] Only be strong and very courageous, taking care to act in accordance with all the law that Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may succeed wherever you go.
[Joshua] [1]:[8] This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth; meditate on it day and night, so that you may take care to act in accordance with all that is written in it. Then you will make your way prosperous, and then you will succeed.
[Joshua] [1]:[9] Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be terrified or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go."
[Joshua] [1]:[10] Then Joshua gave this order to the officers of the people:
[Joshua] [1]:[11] "Go through the camp and command the people: 'Prepare provisions for yourselves, for in three days you will cross this Jordan to go in and take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving you to possess.'"
[Joshua] [1]:[12] To the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joshua said:
[Joshua] [1]:[13] "Remember the word that Moses, the servant of the LORD, commanded you: 'The LORD your God is giving you rest and has granted you this land.'
[Joshua] [1]:[14] Your wives, your children, and your livestock may remain in the land Moses gave you east of the Jordan. But all your fighting men, armed for battle, must cross over ahead of your brothers and help them,
[Joshua] [1]:[15] until the LORD gives your brothers rest, as he has given you, and they too have taken possession of the land the LORD your God is giving them. Then you may return to the land of your possession and take it as your own, the land Moses, the servant of the LORD, gave you east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise."
[Joshua] [1]:[16] They answered Joshua: "Everything you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.
[Joshua] [1]:[17] Just as we obeyed Moses in everything, so we will obey you. Only may the LORD your God be with you, as he was with Moses.
[Joshua] [1]:[18] Anyone who rebels against your command and does not obey your words, whatever you order, shall be put to death. Only be strong and courageous!"
[Joshua] [2]:[1] Then Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two men out from Shittim as spies, saying, "Go, look over the land, especially Jericho." So they went and came to the house of a prostitute named Rahab, and they stayed there.
[Joshua] [2]:[2] The king of Jericho was told, "Look, men have come here tonight from the Israelites to search out the land."
[Joshua] [2]:[3] So the king of Jericho sent word to Rahab: "Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house, for they have come to search out the whole land."
[Joshua] [2]:[4] But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.
[Joshua] [2]:[5] At dark, when it was time to shut the gate, the men left. I don't know where they went. Go after them quickly—you may overtake them."
[Joshua] [2]:[6] But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them under the stalks of flax she had laid out there.
[Joshua] [2]:[7] So the pursuers went after them along the road toward the Jordan, as far as the fords; and the gate was shut as soon as they had gone out.
[Joshua] [2]:[8] Before the spies lay down for the night, she came up to them on the roof
[Joshua] [2]:[9] and said to them, "I know that the LORD has given you this land, that dread of you has fallen upon us, and that all who live in this land are melting away before you.
[Joshua] [2]:[10] For we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites east of the Jordan, whom you utterly destroyed.
[Joshua] [2]:[11] When we heard it, our hearts melted, and no courage was left in anyone because of you; for the LORD your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below.
[Joshua] [2]:[12] Now then, swear to me by the LORD that, since I have shown you kindness, you will also show kindness to my father's house. Give me a sure sign
[Joshua] [2]:[13] that you will spare the lives of my father and mother, my brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them, and deliver us from death."
[Joshua] [2]:[14] The men said to her, "Our lives for yours! If you do not report this business of ours, then when the LORD gives us the land we will deal kindly and faithfully with you."
[Joshua] [2]:[15] Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was built into the city wall, and she lived in the wall itself.
[Joshua] [2]:[16] She said to them, "Go into the hill country, so the pursuers will not come upon you. Hide there three days until they return; after that you can go on your way."
[Joshua] [2]:[17] The men said to her, "We will be released from this oath you have made us swear
[Joshua] [2]:[18] unless, when we enter the land, you tie this cord of scarlet thread in the window through which you let us down, and gather your father and mother, your brothers, and all your father's household into your house.
[Joshua] [2]:[19] If anyone goes out the doors of your house into the street, his blood will be on his own head, and we will be innocent. But if a hand is laid on anyone who is with you in the house, his blood will be on our heads.
[Joshua] [2]:[20] And if you report this business of ours, we will be released from the oath you made us swear."
[Joshua] [2]:[21] "Let it be as you say," she replied. She sent them away, and they departed; and she tied the scarlet cord in the window.
[Joshua] [2]:[22] They left and went into the hill country and stayed there three days, until the pursuers returned. The pursuers had searched all along the road but did not find them.
[Joshua] [2]:[23] Then the two men started back. They came down from the hills, crossed over, and came to Joshua son of Nun, and told him everything that had happened to them.
[Joshua] [2]:[24] They said to Joshua, "The LORD has surely given the whole land into our hands; all who live in the land are melting away before us."
[Joshua] [3]:[1] Joshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the Israelites. There they camped before crossing over.
[Joshua] [3]:[2] At the end of three days the officers went through the camp
[Joshua] [3]:[3] and gave the people this command: "When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, carried by the Levitical priests, break camp and follow it.
[Joshua] [3]:[4] But keep a distance of about two thousand cubits between you and it; do not come near it. This way you will know the road to take, since you have never traveled it before."
[Joshua] [3]:[5] Joshua said to the people, "Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you."
[Joshua] [3]:[6] Then Joshua said to the priests, "Lift the ark of the covenant and cross over ahead of the people." So they lifted the ark of the covenant and went on before them.
[Joshua] [3]:[7] The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to exalt you in the sight of all Israel, so they may know that I am with you as I was with Moses.
[Joshua] [3]:[8] Command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant: 'When you reach the edge of the Jordan's waters, stand still in the Jordan.'"
[Joshua] [3]:[9] Then Joshua said to the Israelites, "Come here and listen to the words of the LORD your God."
[Joshua] [3]:[10] And Joshua said, "By this you will know that the living God is among you and that he will surely drive out before you the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites.
[Joshua] [3]:[11] Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is going to cross the Jordan ahead of you.
[Joshua] [3]:[12] Now choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one from each tribe.
[Joshua] [3]:[13] And when the feet of the priests who carry the ark of the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, come to rest in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan will be cut off—the waters flowing down from upstream—and they will stand in a single heap.
[Joshua] [3]:[14] So the people broke camp to cross the Jordan, with the priests carrying the ark of the covenant ahead of them.
[Joshua] [3]:[15] Now the Jordan was overflowing all its banks, as it does all through the harvest season. But as soon as those carrying the ark reached the Jordan and the feet of the priests carrying it touched the water's edge,
[Joshua] [3]:[16] the water flowing down from upstream stopped and stood in a single heap a great distance away, at Adam, the town near Zarethan, while the water flowing down toward the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, was completely cut off. So the people crossed over opposite Jericho.
[Joshua] [3]:[17] The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel crossed over on dry ground, until the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan.
[Joshua] [4]:[1] When the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, the LORD said to Joshua:
[Joshua] [4]:[2] "Choose twelve men from among the people, one man from each tribe,
[Joshua] [4]:[3] and command them: 'Lift up twelve stones from here, from the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the priests' feet stood, and carry them over with you and set them down at the camp where you stay tonight.'"
[Joshua] [4]:[4] So Joshua called the twelve men he had appointed from the Israelites, one from each tribe,
[Joshua] [4]:[5] and he said to them, "Go over ahead of the ark of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you take up a stone on his shoulder, one for each of the tribes of Israel,
[Joshua] [4]:[6] so that this may be a sign among you. In days to come, when your children ask you, 'What do these stones mean to you?'
[Joshua] [4]:[7] tell them that the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD. When it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. These stones are to be a memorial for the Israelites forever."
[Joshua] [4]:[8] The Israelites did just as Joshua commanded. They took up twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, as the LORD had told Joshua, one for each of the tribes of Israel, and carried them over with them to the camp, where they set them down.
[Joshua] [4]:[9] Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, at the place where the feet of the priests who carried the ark of the covenant had stood. And they are there to this day.
[Joshua] [4]:[10] The priests who carried the ark remained standing in the middle of the Jordan until everything was done that the LORD had commanded Joshua to tell the people, just as Moses had commanded Joshua. And the people hurried across.
[Joshua] [4]:[11] When all the people had finished crossing, the ark of the LORD and the priests crossed over in the sight of the people.
[Joshua] [4]:[12] The Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed for battle ahead of the Israelites, as Moses had told them.
[Joshua] [4]:[13] About forty thousand men armed for battle crossed over before the LORD to the plains of Jericho, ready for war.
[Joshua] [4]:[14] That day the LORD exalted Joshua in the sight of all Israel, and they revered him all his life, as they had revered Moses.
[Joshua] [4]:[15] Then the LORD said to Joshua:
[Joshua] [4]:[16] "Command the priests who carry the ark of the testimony to come up out of the Jordan."
[Joshua] [4]:[17] So Joshua commanded the priests, "Come up out of the Jordan."
[Joshua] [4]:[18] And when the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up out of the middle of the Jordan, no sooner had their feet touched dry ground than the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and ran over all its banks as before.
[Joshua] [4]:[19] The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month and camped at Gilgal, on the eastern border of Jericho.
[Joshua] [4]:[20] And Joshua set up at Gilgal the twelve stones they had taken from the Jordan.
[Joshua] [4]:[21] He said to the Israelites, "In days to come, when your children ask their fathers, 'What do these stones mean?'
[Joshua] [4]:[22] tell your children, 'Israel crossed this Jordan on dry ground.'
[Joshua] [4]:[23] For the LORD your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed over, just as the LORD your God did to the Red Sea,* which he dried up before us until we had crossed over, *Hebrew: Sea of Reeds
[Joshua] [4]:[24] so that all the peoples of the earth might know that the hand of the LORD is mighty, and so that you might always fear the LORD your God."
[Joshua] [5]:[1] When all the Amorite kings west of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings along the sea heard how the LORD had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the Israelites until they had crossed over, their hearts melted, and no courage was left in any of them because of the Israelites.
[Joshua] [5]:[2] At that time the LORD said to Joshua, "Make yourself flint knives and circumcise the Israelites again."
[Joshua] [5]:[3] So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at Gibeath-haaraloth.^[Gibeath-haaraloth means "the hill of the foreskins."]
[Joshua] [5]:[4] This was the reason Joshua circumcised them: all the males who came out of Egypt, all the fighting men, had died in the wilderness along the way after they left Egypt.
[Joshua] [5]:[5] All the people who came out had been circumcised, but none of those born in the wilderness along the way after they left Egypt had been circumcised.
[Joshua] [5]:[6] The Israelites had walked forty years in the wilderness until the whole nation—the fighting men who came out of Egypt—had perished, because they had not obeyed the voice of the LORD. To them the LORD had sworn that they would never see the land he had promised on oath to their fathers to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
[Joshua] [5]:[7] So he raised up their sons in their place, and these were the ones Joshua circumcised. They were still uncircumcised, since they had not been circumcised along the way.
[Joshua] [5]:[8] When the whole nation had been circumcised, they stayed where they were in the camp until they had healed.
[Joshua] [5]:[9] Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the disgrace of Egypt from you." So that place has been called Gilgal to this day.
[Joshua] [5]:[10] While the Israelites were camped at Gilgal, they kept the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, on the plains of Jericho.
[Joshua] [5]:[11] The day after the Passover, on that very day, they ate the produce of the land: unleavened bread and roasted grain.
[Joshua] [5]:[12] The manna stopped the day after they ate the produce of the land. The Israelites had no more manna, but ate the crops of the land of Canaan that year.
[Joshua] [5]:[13] Now while Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua went up to him and asked, "Are you for us or for our enemies?"
[Joshua] [5]:[14] "Neither," he replied. "I am the commander of the LORD's army. Now I have come." Then Joshua fell facedown to the ground in worship and said to him, "What does my lord have to say to his servant?"
[Joshua] [5]:[15] The commander of the LORD's army answered, "Take off your sandal from your foot, for the place where you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so.
[Joshua] [6]:[1] Now Jericho was shut up tight because of the Israelites. No one went out, and no one came in.
[Joshua] [6]:[2] And the LORD said to Joshua, "See, I have delivered Jericho into your hand, along with its king and its fighting men.
[Joshua] [6]:[3] March around the city with all your soldiers, circling it once. Do this for six days.
[Joshua] [6]:[4] Seven priests shall carry seven ram's-horn trumpets before the ark. On the seventh day march around the city seven times, with the priests blowing the trumpets.
[Joshua] [6]:[5] When they sound a long blast on the ram's horn and you hear the trumpet, all the people are to give a great shout. Then the city wall will collapse, and the people shall charge straight in, each man where he stands."
[Joshua] [6]:[6] So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven ram's-horn trumpets before the ark of the LORD."
[Joshua] [6]:[7] And he said to the people, "Move out and march around the city, and let the armed men go ahead of the ark of the LORD."
[Joshua] [6]:[8] When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven ram's-horn trumpets before the LORD moved forward, blowing the trumpets, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD followed behind them.
[Joshua] [6]:[9] The armed men marched ahead of the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard followed the ark, while the trumpets sounded on and on.
[Joshua] [6]:[10] But Joshua had commanded the people, "Do not shout, do not let your voice be heard, do not let a single word leave your mouth until the day I tell you to shout. Then shout!"
[Joshua] [6]:[11] So he had the ark of the LORD carried around the city, circling it once. Then they returned to the camp and spent the night there.
[Joshua] [6]:[12] Joshua rose early the next morning, and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.
[Joshua] [6]:[13] The seven priests carrying the seven ram's-horn trumpets before the ark of the LORD went on, blowing the trumpets as they marched. The armed men went ahead of them, and the rear guard followed the ark of the LORD, while the trumpets sounded on and on.
[Joshua] [6]:[14] On the second day they marched around the city once and returned to the camp. They did this for six days.
[Joshua] [6]:[15] On the seventh day they rose at daybreak and marched around the city in the same way, seven times. Only on that day did they circle the city seven times.
[Joshua] [6]:[16] On the seventh time around, when the priests sounded the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, "Shout! For the LORD has given you the city.
[Joshua] [6]:[17] The city and everything in it are devoted to the LORD for destruction. Only Rahab the prostitute shall live, she and all who are with her in her house, because she hid the messengers we sent.
[Joshua] [6]:[18] But keep away from what is devoted to destruction, or you will bring destruction on yourselves by taking any of it. You would make the camp of Israel liable to destruction and bring disaster upon it.
[Joshua] [6]:[19] All the silver and gold and the articles of bronze and iron are holy to the LORD; they must go into the LORD's treasury."
[Joshua] [6]:[20] So the people shouted, and the trumpets sounded. When the people heard the blast of the trumpet, they raised a great shout, and the wall fell down flat. The people charged into the city, each man where he stood, and they captured it.
[Joshua] [6]:[21] They devoted to destruction everything in the city, putting to the sword man and woman, young and old, ox, sheep, and donkey.
[Joshua] [6]:[22] To the two men who had scouted the land Joshua said, "Go into the prostitute's house and bring her out, along with everyone belonging to her, as you swore to her."
[Joshua] [6]:[23] So the young men who had been spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father and mother, her brothers, and everyone belonging to her. They brought out her whole family and left them outside the camp of Israel.
[Joshua] [6]:[24] Then they burned the city and everything in it, but the silver and gold and the articles of bronze and iron they placed in the treasury of the LORD's house.
[Joshua] [6]:[25] Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, her father's household, and all who belonged to her, and she has lived among Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers Joshua had sent to spy out Jericho.
[Joshua] [6]:[26] At that time Joshua pronounced this oath: "Cursed before the LORD is the man who undertakes to rebuild this city, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he will lay its foundation; at the cost of his youngest he will set up its gates."
[Joshua] [6]:[27] So the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame spread throughout the land.
[Joshua] [7]:[1] But the Israelites broke faith concerning the things devoted to destruction. Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was devoted, and the LORD's anger burned against the Israelites.
[Joshua] [7]:[2] Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which lies near Beth Aven, east of Bethel, and told them, "Go up and scout out the land." So the men went up and scouted Ai.
[Joshua] [7]:[3] When they returned to Joshua they said, "There is no need for the whole army to go up. Send about two or three thousand men to attack Ai. Do not wear out the whole army there, for the people of Ai are few."
[Joshua] [7]:[4] So about three thousand men went up—and they fled before the men of Ai.
[Joshua] [7]:[5] The men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them, chasing them from the gate as far as Shebarim and cutting them down on the slope. At this the hearts of the people melted and turned to water.
[Joshua] [7]:[6] Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown on the ground before the ark of the LORD until evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they threw dust on their heads.
[Joshua] [7]:[7] And Joshua said, "Alas, Lord GOD, why did you ever bring this people across the Jordan—only to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!
[Joshua] [7]:[8] O Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned its back before its enemies?
[Joshua] [7]:[9] The Canaanites and all who live in the land will hear of it. They will surround us and wipe our name from the earth. And then what will you do for your great name?"
[Joshua] [7]:[10] The LORD said to Joshua, "Stand up! Why are you lying facedown?
[Joshua] [7]:[11] Israel has sinned. They have violated my covenant, which I commanded them to keep. They have taken some of what was devoted to destruction; they have stolen, they have lied, they have put it among their own possessions.
[Joshua] [7]:[12] That is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies. They turn their backs and run, because they themselves have now become devoted to destruction. I will not be with you any longer unless you destroy whatever among you is devoted to destruction.
[Joshua] [7]:[13] Get up! Consecrate the people. Say to them, 'Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, because this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: There is devoted property among you, Israel. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove it from your midst.'
[Joshua] [7]:[14] In the morning you shall come forward tribe by tribe. The tribe the LORD singles out shall come forward clan by clan; the clan the LORD singles out shall come forward household by household; and the household the LORD singles out shall come forward man by man.
[Joshua] [7]:[15] The one who is caught with the devoted things shall be burned with fire, he and all that belongs to him, because he has violated the covenant of the LORD and has done an outrageous thing in Israel."
[Joshua] [7]:[16] Early the next morning Joshua had Israel come forward by tribes, and the tribe of Judah was singled out.
[Joshua] [7]:[17] He brought forward the clans of Judah, and the clan of the Zerahites was singled out. He brought the clan of the Zerahites forward man by man, and Zabdi was singled out.
[Joshua] [7]:[18] Joshua brought his household forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was singled out.
[Joshua] [7]:[19] Then Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and make confession to him. Tell me what you have done; do not hide it from me."
[Joshua] [7]:[20] Achan answered Joshua, "It is true. I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did:
[Joshua] [7]:[21] Among the spoil I saw a beautiful robe from Babylonia, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels. I coveted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath."
[Joshua] [7]:[22] Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. There it was, hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.
[Joshua] [7]:[23] They took the things from the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and spread them out before the LORD.
[Joshua] [7]:[24] Then Joshua, together with all Israel, took Achan son of Zerah, along with the silver, the robe, and the bar of gold, his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys and sheep, his tent and everything he had, and brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
[Joshua] [7]:[25] Joshua said, "Why have you brought this disaster on us? Today the LORD brings disaster on you." Then all Israel pelted him with stones, and they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.
[Joshua] [7]:[26] Over him they piled a great heap of stones, which remains to this day. Then the LORD turned from his fierce anger. That is why the place has been called the Valley of Achor ever since.
[Joshua] [8]:[1] Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid or dismayed. Take the whole army with you and go up against Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.
[Joshua] [8]:[2] Do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that you may take its spoil and its livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city."
[Joshua] [8]:[3] So Joshua and the whole army set out to go up against Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty warriors and sent them out by night,
[Joshua] [8]:[4] giving them these orders: "Listen carefully. You are to lie in ambush behind the city. Do not go far from it, and all of you stay ready.
[Joshua] [8]:[5] I and all the men with me will approach the city, and when they come out against us as they did before, we will flee from them.
[Joshua] [8]:[6] They will pursue us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, 'They are running from us as they did before.' So we will flee from them.
[Joshua] [8]:[7] Then you will rise up from the ambush and take possession of the city, for the LORD your God will give it into your hand.
[Joshua] [8]:[8] When you have captured the city, set it on fire. Do as the LORD has commanded. See, these are my orders to you."
[Joshua] [8]:[9] So Joshua sent them off, and they went to the place of ambush and took up position between Bethel and Ai, to the west of Ai. But Joshua spent that night among the people.
[Joshua] [8]:[10] Early the next morning Joshua mustered the people, and he and the elders of Israel went up ahead of them to Ai.
[Joshua] [8]:[11] The whole army that was with him marched up, drew near, and took up position opposite the city. They camped north of Ai, with the valley between them and the city.
[Joshua] [8]:[12] Joshua had taken about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
[Joshua] [8]:[13] So the forces took their positions—the main camp north of the city and the rear guard west of it—and that night Joshua went out into the middle of the valley.
[Joshua] [8]:[14] When the king of Ai saw this, he and all his people hurried out early to meet Israel in battle at the appointed place facing the Arabah. But he did not know that an ambush had been set against him behind the city.
[Joshua] [8]:[15] Joshua and all Israel let themselves be driven back before them and fled toward the wilderness.
[Joshua] [8]:[16] All the men of Ai were summoned to give chase, and as they pursued Joshua they were drawn far from the city.
[Joshua] [8]:[17] Not a man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city wide open and pursued Israel.
[Joshua] [8]:[18] Then the LORD said to Joshua, "Stretch out toward Ai the javelin in your hand, for I will give the city into your hand." So Joshua stretched out the javelin in his hand toward the city.
[Joshua] [8]:[19] The moment he stretched out his hand, the men in ambush rose quickly from their position and ran. They entered the city, captured it, and set it on fire at once.
[Joshua] [8]:[20] When the men of Ai looked back, they saw the smoke of the city rising to the sky, and they had no strength to flee in any direction, for the Israelites who had been fleeing toward the wilderness now turned on their pursuers.
[Joshua] [8]:[21] For when Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city and that smoke was rising from it, they turned around and struck down the men of Ai.
[Joshua] [8]:[22] The others came out of the city against them, so that the men of Ai were caught in the middle, with Israelites on this side and on that. Israel cut them down, leaving no survivor and none who escaped.
[Joshua] [8]:[23] But the king of Ai they took alive and brought to Joshua.
[Joshua] [8]:[24] When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the open country and in the wilderness where they had chased them, and every one of them had fallen by the sword until none were left, all Israel returned to Ai and put it to the sword.
[Joshua] [8]:[25] Twelve thousand fell that day, men and women alike—all the people of Ai.
[Joshua] [8]:[26] Joshua did not draw back the hand that held out the javelin until he had devoted to destruction all who lived in Ai.
[Joshua] [8]:[27] Only the livestock and the spoil of that city did Israel take for themselves, just as the LORD had commanded Joshua.
[Joshua] [8]:[28] So Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanent heap of ruins, a desolate place to this day.
[Joshua] [8]:[29] He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening, and at sunset Joshua ordered that his body be taken down from the tree and thrown at the entrance of the city gate. Over it they raised a great heap of stones, which is there to this day.
[Joshua] [8]:[30] Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,
[Joshua] [8]:[31] just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites—an altar of uncut stones, on which no iron tool had been used, as it is written in the Book of the Law of Moses. On it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD and sacrificed fellowship offerings.
[Joshua] [8]:[32] There, in the presence of the Israelites, Joshua wrote on the stones a copy of the law that Moses had written.
[Joshua] [8]:[33] All Israel—foreigners and native-born alike—with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD, facing the Levitical priests who carried it. Half the people stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded, so that the people of Israel would be blessed first.
[Joshua] [8]:[34] Afterward Joshua read aloud all the words of the law—the blessing and the curse—just as it is written in the Book of the Law.
[Joshua] [8]:[35] There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded which Joshua did not read before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who traveled among them.
[Joshua] [9]:[1] When all the kings west of the Jordan heard the news — those in the hill country, in the lowlands, and along the whole coast of the Great Sea toward Lebanon: the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites —
[Joshua] [9]:[2] they banded together to make war on Joshua and Israel, with one accord.
[Joshua] [9]:[3] But when the people of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai,
[Joshua] [9]:[4] they resorted to a ruse of their own. They set out disguised as envoys, with worn-out sacks on their donkeys and old wineskins, cracked and patched together.
[Joshua] [9]:[5] They wore worn-out sandals, mended, on their feet, and threadbare clothes, and all the bread they carried was dry and crumbling.
[Joshua] [9]:[6] They came to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal and said to him and to the men of Israel, "We have come from a distant land; now make a treaty with us."
[Joshua] [9]:[7] But the men of Israel said to the Hivites, "Perhaps you live right among us. How then can we make a treaty with you?"
[Joshua] [9]:[8] "We are your servants," they said to Joshua. And Joshua asked them, "Who are you, and where do you come from?"
[Joshua] [9]:[9] They answered, "Your servants have come from a very distant land, because of the name of the LORD your God. For we have heard the report of him and of everything he did in Egypt,
[Joshua] [9]:[10] and everything he did to the two kings of the Amorites east of the Jordan — Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth.
[Joshua] [9]:[11] So our elders and all the people of our land said to us, 'Take provisions for the journey and go to meet them. Say to them: We are your servants; now make a treaty with us.'
[Joshua] [9]:[12] This bread of ours was still warm when we packed it at home on the day we left to come to you. Now look at it — dry and crumbling.
[Joshua] [9]:[13] These wineskins were new when we filled them, and now they are split open. And our clothes and sandals are worn out from the great length of the journey."
[Joshua] [9]:[14] The men took some of their provisions, but they did not inquire of the LORD.
[Joshua] [9]:[15] So Joshua made peace with them and entered into a covenant to let them live, and the leaders of the assembly confirmed it with an oath.
[Joshua] [9]:[16] Three days after they had made the treaty with them, Israel learned that these people were their neighbors, living right among them.
[Joshua] [9]:[17] So the Israelites set out and on the third day came to their towns: Gibeon, Kephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath Jearim.
[Joshua] [9]:[18] But the Israelites did not attack them, because the leaders of the assembly had sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. And the whole assembly grumbled against the leaders.
[Joshua] [9]:[19] But all the leaders answered the whole assembly, "We have sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel; now we cannot touch them.
[Joshua] [9]:[20] This is what we will do with them: we will let them live, so that no wrath comes upon us for breaking the oath we swore to them."
[Joshua] [9]:[21] And the leaders said to them, "Let them live." So they became woodcutters and water carriers for the whole assembly, just as the leaders had promised them.
[Joshua] [9]:[22] Then Joshua summoned them and said, "Why did you deceive us by saying, 'We live far away from you,' while in fact you live right among us?
[Joshua] [9]:[23] Now therefore you are under a curse: you will never cease to serve as woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God."
[Joshua] [9]:[24] They answered Joshua, "Your servants were clearly told how the LORD your God had commanded his servant Moses to give you the whole land and to destroy all its inhabitants before you. So we feared for our lives because of you, and that is why we did this.
[Joshua] [9]:[25] We are now in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you."
[Joshua] [9]:[26] So Joshua dealt with them accordingly: he saved them from the hand of the Israelites, and they did not kill them.
[Joshua] [9]:[27] That day Joshua made them woodcutters and water carriers for the assembly and for the altar of the LORD — as they still are to this day — at whatever place the LORD would choose.
[Joshua] [10]:[1] When Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction, doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them,
[Joshua] [10]:[2] Adoni-zedek and his people were terrified, for Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities—larger than Ai—and all its men were warriors.
[Joshua] [10]:[3] So Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon:
[Joshua] [10]:[4] "Come up to me and help me, and let us attack Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and the Israelites."
[Joshua] [10]:[5] Then the five kings of the Amorites—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon—joined forces and marched up with all their armies. They took up positions against Gibeon and attacked it.
[Joshua] [10]:[6] The men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal: "Do not abandon your servants. Come up to us quickly, save us, and help us, for all the Amorite kings of the hill country have joined forces against us."
[Joshua] [10]:[7] So Joshua marched up from Gilgal with his whole army, all his best fighting men.
[Joshua] [10]:[8] And the LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, for I have given them into your hand. Not one of them will be able to stand against you."
[Joshua] [10]:[9] Joshua came upon them suddenly, having marched all night from Gilgal.
[Joshua] [10]:[10] The LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, who struck them down in a great slaughter at Gibeon, pursued them along the road up to Beth-horon, and cut them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.
[Joshua] [10]:[11] As they fled before Israel down the descent of Beth-horon, the LORD hurled great hailstones on them from the sky all the way to Azekah, and they died. More of them died from the hailstones than from the swords of the Israelites.
[Joshua] [10]:[12] On the day the LORD gave the Amorites over to the Israelites, Joshua spoke to the LORD, and in the sight of Israel he said: "Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and moon, over the Valley of Aijalon."
[Joshua] [10]:[13] So the sun stood still and the moon halted until the nation had taken vengeance on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar?* The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and delayed its setting for about a full day. [*Footnote: Jashar means "the upright one"; the book is an ancient collection of songs no longer preserved.]
[Joshua] [10]:[14] There has never been a day like it before or since, a day when the LORD listened to the voice of a man—because the LORD was fighting for Israel.
[Joshua] [10]:[15] Then Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.
[Joshua] [10]:[16] Now the five kings had fled and hidden in the cave at Makkedah.
[Joshua] [10]:[17] When Joshua was told, "The five kings have been found, hiding in the cave at Makkedah,"
[Joshua] [10]:[18] he said, "Roll large stones up to the mouth of the cave, and post men there to guard them.
[Joshua] [10]:[19] But you—do not stop. Pursue your enemies and attack them from behind. Do not let them reach their cities, for the LORD your God has given them into your hand."
[Joshua] [10]:[20] When Joshua and the Israelites had finished inflicting a crushing defeat on them, until they were wiped out—though a few survivors escaped to the fortified cities—
[Joshua] [10]:[21] the whole army returned safely to Joshua at the camp in Makkedah, and no one dared say a word against the Israelites.
[Joshua] [10]:[22] Then Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out to me."
[Joshua] [10]:[23] So they did, bringing the five kings out of the cave to him—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
[Joshua] [10]:[24] When they had brought these kings to Joshua, he summoned all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the troops who had gone with him, "Come here, put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came forward and put their feet on their necks.
[Joshua] [10]:[25] Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid or dismayed. Be strong and courageous, for this is what the LORD will do to all the enemies you fight."
[Joshua] [10]:[26] Then Joshua struck the kings down and killed them, and hung them on five trees, where they remained until evening.
[Joshua] [10]:[27] At sunset Joshua gave the order, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had been hiding. Then they placed large stones over the mouth of the cave, and those stones remain there to this very day.
[Joshua] [10]:[28] That day Joshua captured Makkedah and put it and its king to the sword. He devoted the city and everyone in it to destruction, leaving no survivor, and he did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
[Joshua] [10]:[29] Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and attacked it.
[Joshua] [10]:[30] The LORD gave that city and its king into Israel's hand as well. Joshua put it to the sword along with everyone in it, leaving no survivor there, and he did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.
[Joshua] [10]:[31] Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Libnah to Lachish. He laid siege to it and attacked it.
[Joshua] [10]:[32] The LORD gave Lachish into Israel's hand, and Joshua captured it on the second day. He put it to the sword along with everyone in it, just as he had done to Libnah.
[Joshua] [10]:[33] Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, but Joshua struck him down along with his people, until no survivor was left.
[Joshua] [10]:[34] Then Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Lachish to Eglon. They laid siege to it and attacked it.
[Joshua] [10]:[35] They captured it that very day and put it to the sword, devoting to destruction everyone in it, just as they had done to Lachish.
[Joshua] [10]:[36] Then Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and attacked it.
[Joshua] [10]:[37] They captured it and put it to the sword, along with its king, all its towns, and everyone in it. They left no survivor, just as they had done to Eglon; they devoted the city and everyone in it to destruction.
[Joshua] [10]:[38] Then Joshua and all Israel with him turned back to Debir and attacked it.
[Joshua] [10]:[39] They captured it, its king, and all its villages, and put them to the sword. They devoted everyone in it to destruction, leaving no survivor. Joshua did to Debir and its king as he had done to Hebron and to Libnah and its king.
[Joshua] [10]:[40] So Joshua struck down the whole land—the hill country, the Negev, the western foothills, and the slopes—together with all their kings. He left no survivor but devoted everything that breathed to destruction, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
[Joshua] [10]:[41] Joshua conquered them from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and the whole region of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
[Joshua] [10]:[42] All these kings and their lands Joshua captured in one campaign, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
[Joshua] [10]:[43] Then Joshua returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal.
[Joshua] [11]:[1] When Jabin king of Hazor heard of it, he sent word to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,
[Joshua] [11]:[2] and to the kings in the north—in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Kinneroth, in the lowlands, and in the heights of Dor to the west,
[Joshua] [11]:[3] to the Canaanites in the east and the west, to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Jebusites in the hill country, and to the Hivites at the foot of Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
[Joshua] [11]:[4] They marched out with all their armies, a vast host, as numerous as the sand on the seashore, with a great many horses and chariots.
[Joshua] [11]:[5] All these kings joined forces, and they came and camped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
[Joshua] [11]:[6] The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, for tomorrow at this time I will give them all up, slain before Israel. You are to hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire."
[Joshua] [11]:[7] So Joshua and all his fighting men came upon them suddenly at the waters of Merom and fell upon them.
[Joshua] [11]:[8] The LORD gave them into the hand of Israel, who struck them down and pursued them as far as Greater Sidon, as far as Misrephoth Maim, and eastward as far as the Valley of Mizpeh. They struck them down until no survivor was left.
[Joshua] [11]:[9] Joshua did to them as the LORD had told him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
[Joshua] [11]:[10] At that time Joshua turned back, captured Hazor, and put its king to the sword, for Hazor had formerly been the head of all these kingdoms.
[Joshua] [11]:[11] They struck down every person in it with the sword, devoting them to destruction; nothing that breathed was left alive. And Hazor he burned with fire.
[Joshua] [11]:[12] Joshua captured all the cities of these kings, along with their kings, and put them to the sword. He devoted them to destruction, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.
[Joshua] [11]:[13] But Israel did not burn any of the cities that stood on their mounds—only Hazor did Joshua burn.
[Joshua] [11]:[14] The Israelites took all the spoil of these cities and the livestock as their own plunder, but they put every person to the sword until they had destroyed them; they left nothing alive that breathed.
[Joshua] [11]:[15] As the LORD had commanded his servant Moses, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did. He left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Joshua] [11]:[16] So Joshua took all that land: the hill country, all the Negev, all the land of Goshen, the lowlands, the Arabah, and the hill country of Israel with its lowlands—
[Joshua] [11]:[17] from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, as far as Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings, struck them down, and put them to death.
[Joshua] [11]:[18] Joshua waged war against all these kings for a long time.
[Joshua] [11]:[19] Not one city made peace with the Israelites except the Hivites who lived in Gibeon; all the rest they took in battle.
[Joshua] [11]:[20] For it was the LORD's doing to harden their hearts, so that they came against Israel in battle, in order that they might be devoted to destruction and receive no mercy, but be wiped out, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
[Joshua] [11]:[21] At that time Joshua went and cut off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and all the hill country of Israel. Joshua devoted them to destruction along with their cities.
[Joshua] [11]:[22] No Anakim were left in the land of the Israelites; only in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod did any remain.
[Joshua] [11]:[23] So Joshua took the whole land, just as the LORD had told Moses, and he gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to the allotments of their tribes. And the land had rest from war.
[Joshua] [12]:[1] These are the kings of the land whom the Israelites defeated, taking possession of their territory east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Gorge to Mount Hermon, including all the eastern Arabah:
[Joshua] [12]:[2] Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon. His rule extended from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Gorge—from the middle of the gorge—over half of Gilead as far as the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites,
[Joshua] [12]:[3] and over the Arabah as far as the Sea of Kinnereth on the east, and to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, on the east toward Beth Jeshimoth, and southward below the slopes of Pisgah.
[Joshua] [12]:[4] Next was the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the last of the Rephaim, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
[Joshua] [12]:[5] He ruled over Mount Hermon, Salecah, and all of Bashan up to the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and over half of Gilead as far as the territory of Sihon king of Heshbon.
[Joshua] [12]:[6] Moses, the servant of the LORD, and the Israelites defeated them, and Moses gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
[Joshua] [12]:[7] These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the Israelites defeated west of the Jordan, from Baal Gad in the Valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir. Joshua gave their land to the tribes of Israel as a possession, according to their allotted portions:
[Joshua] [12]:[8] the hill country, the western foothills, the Arabah, the mountain slopes, the wilderness, and the Negev—the lands of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
[Joshua] [12]:[9] The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, near Bethel, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[10] the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[11] the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[12] the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[13] the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[14] the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[15] the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[16] the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[17] the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[18] the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[19] the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[20] the king of Shimron Meron, one; the king of Akshaph, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[21] the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[22] the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[23] the king of Dor in Naphath Dor, one; the king of Goyim in Gilgal, one;
[Joshua] [12]:[24] the king of Tirzah, one. Thirty-one kings in all.
[Joshua] [13]:[1] Now Joshua was old, well advanced in years, and the LORD said to him: "You are old and advanced in years, and very much of the land still remains to be taken.
[Joshua] [13]:[2] This is the land that remains: all the districts of the Philistines and all the territory of the Geshurites,
[Joshua] [13]:[3] from the Shihor east of Egypt north to the border of Ekron—all of it counted as Canaanite—the five Philistine rulers of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron, along with the Avvites
[Joshua] [13]:[4] in the south; all the land of the Canaanites; and Mearah, which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;
[Joshua] [13]:[5] also the land of the Gebalites, and all of Lebanon to the east, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath.
[Joshua] [13]:[6] All the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians—I myself will drive them out before the Israelites. Only allot the land to Israel as an inheritance, as I have commanded you.
[Joshua] [13]:[7] Now divide this land as an inheritance among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."
[Joshua] [13]:[8] The other half of Manasseh, together with the Reubenites and the Gadites, had already received the inheritance Moses gave them east of the Jordan, just as Moses the servant of the LORD had assigned it:
[Joshua] [13]:[9] from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Gorge, including the town in the middle of the gorge, and the whole plateau from Medeba to Dibon;
[Joshua] [13]:[10] all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the Ammonites;
[Joshua] [13]:[11] Gilead, the territory of the Geshurites and Maacathites, all of Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;
[Joshua] [13]:[12] all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei—he was one of the last of the Rephaim. Moses defeated them and drove them out.
[Joshua] [13]:[13] But the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites and the Maacathites, so Geshur and Maacath have lived among the Israelites to this day.
[Joshua] [13]:[14] To the tribe of Levi alone Moses gave no inheritance; the offerings made by fire to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, as he promised them.
[Joshua] [13]:[15] This is what Moses gave to the tribe of Reuben, clan by clan:
[Joshua] [13]:[16] Their territory reached from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Gorge, including the town in the middle of the gorge, and the whole plateau by Medeba;
[Joshua] [13]:[17] Heshbon and all its towns on the plateau—Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,
[Joshua] [13]:[18] Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,
[Joshua] [13]:[19] Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill in the valley,
[Joshua] [13]:[20] Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth—
[Joshua] [13]:[21] all the towns of the plateau and the entire kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon. Moses had defeated him and the chiefs of Midian—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—princes allied with Sihon who lived in that land.
[Joshua] [13]:[22] The Israelites also put Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, to the sword along with the others they killed.
[Joshua] [13]:[23] The border of the Reubenites was the Jordan. These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the Reubenites, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [13]:[24] This is what Moses gave to the tribe of Gad, to the Gadites, clan by clan:
[Joshua] [13]:[25] Their territory was Jazer, all the towns of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Aroer, near Rabbah;
[Joshua] [13]:[26] and from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the territory of Debir;
[Joshua] [13]:[27] and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon. Their border was the Jordan, up to the southern end of the Sea of Kinnereth, on the east side of the Jordan.
[Joshua] [13]:[28] These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the Gadites, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [13]:[29] This is what Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh, that is, to half the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh, clan by clan:
[Joshua] [13]:[30] Their territory extended from Mahanaim and included all Bashan, the entire kingdom of Og king of Bashan—all the settlements of Jair in Bashan, sixty towns—
[Joshua] [13]:[31] half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the royal cities of Og in Bashan. This was for the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh—for half of the sons of Machir, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [13]:[32] These are the inheritances Moses assigned in the plains of Moab, across the Jordan east of Jericho.
[Joshua] [13]:[33] But to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance; the LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he promised them.
[Joshua] [14]:[1] These are the inheritances the Israelites received in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of Israel allotted to them.
[Joshua] [14]:[2] Their inheritance was assigned by lot, as the LORD had commanded through Moses, for the nine and a half tribes.
[Joshua] [14]:[3] For Moses had given the inheritance of the two and a half tribes beyond the Jordan, but to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.
[Joshua] [14]:[4] For the sons of Joseph had become two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim; and the Levites were given no share of the land, only towns to live in, with pasturelands for their livestock and their possessions.
[Joshua] [14]:[5] The Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they divided the land.
[Joshua] [14]:[6] Then the people of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him: "You know what the LORD said to Moses, the man of God, at Kadesh-barnea concerning you and me.
[Joshua] [14]:[7] I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to scout out the land, and I brought him back a report just as I saw it in my heart.
[Joshua] [14]:[8] My brothers who went up with me made the heart of the people melt, but I followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly.
[Joshua] [14]:[9] On that day Moses swore this oath: 'The land where you have set your foot will surely be your inheritance and your children's forever, because you have followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly.'
[Joshua] [14]:[10] And now, look: the LORD has kept me alive, just as he promised, these forty-five years since he spoke this word to Moses, while Israel journeyed through the wilderness. Here I am today, eighty-five years old.
[Joshua] [14]:[11] I am still as strong today as I was the day Moses sent me out; my strength now is the same as it was then, for war and for going out and coming in.
[Joshua] [14]:[12] So give me this hill country the LORD spoke of that day, for you yourself heard then that the Anakites are there, with large fortified cities. It may be that the LORD will be with me, and I will drive them out, just as the LORD said."
[Joshua] [14]:[13] Then Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as his inheritance.
[Joshua] [14]:[14] So Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite as an inheritance to this day, because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, wholeheartedly.
[Joshua] [14]:[15] Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba, after the greatest man among the Anakites. And the land had rest from war.
[Joshua] [15]:[1] The allotment for the tribe of Judah, clan by clan, reached to the border of Edom, to the Wilderness of Zin in the far south.
[Joshua] [15]:[2] Their southern boundary began at the end of the Salt Sea, from the bay that faces south,
[Joshua] [15]:[3] ran south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, continued on to Zin, went up south of Kadesh Barnea, passed by Hezron up to Addar, and curved around to Karka.
[Joshua] [15]:[4] From there it passed on to Azmon and came out at the Wadi of Egypt, ending at the sea. This shall be your southern boundary.
[Joshua] [15]:[5] The eastern boundary was the Salt Sea as far as the mouth of the Jordan. The northern boundary began at the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Jordan,
[Joshua] [15]:[6] went up to Beth Hoglah, passed north of Beth Arabah, and went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
[Joshua] [15]:[7] Then it climbed to Debir from the Valley of Achor, turned north to Gilgal, which faces the Ascent of Adummim south of the ravine, and continued on to the waters of En Shemesh, coming out at En Rogel.
[Joshua] [15]:[8] From there it ran up the Valley of Ben Hinnom along the southern slope of the Jebusite city—that is, Jerusalem—and on to the top of the hill west of the Hinnom Valley, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim.
[Joshua] [15]:[9] From the hilltop the boundary bent toward the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, ran out to the towns of Mount Ephron, and bent toward Baalah, that is, Kiriath Jearim.
[Joshua] [15]:[10] Then it curved west from Baalah to Mount Seir, ran along the northern slope of Mount Jearim—that is, Kesalon—went down to Beth Shemesh and crossed to Timnah.
[Joshua] [15]:[11] It went on to the northern slope of Ekron, bent toward Shikkeron, passed along to Mount Baalah, and came out at Jabneel, ending at the sea.
[Joshua] [15]:[12] The western boundary was the coastline of the Great Sea. These were the boundaries around the people of Judah, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [15]:[13] To Caleb son of Jephunneh, Joshua gave a portion among the people of Judah, as the LORD had commanded him: Kiriath Arba, that is, Hebron—Arba being the ancestor of Anak.
[Joshua] [15]:[14] Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai, the descendants of Anak.
[Joshua] [15]:[15] From there he went up against the inhabitants of Debir, formerly called Kiriath Sepher.
[Joshua] [15]:[16] And Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Aksah in marriage to the man who attacks and captures Kiriath Sepher."
[Joshua] [15]:[17] Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, captured it, so Caleb gave him his daughter Aksah in marriage.
[Joshua] [15]:[18] When she came to Othniel, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What can I do for you?"
[Joshua] [15]:[19] She answered, "Grant me a favor. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well." So he gave her the upper and lower springs.
[Joshua] [15]:[20] This is the inheritance of the tribe of Judah, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [15]:[21] The southernmost towns of the tribe of Judah, toward the border of Edom in the Negev, were: Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,
[Joshua] [15]:[22] Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,
[Joshua] [15]:[23] Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan,
[Joshua] [15]:[24] Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,
[Joshua] [15]:[25] Hazor Hadattah, Kerioth Hezron (that is, Hazor),
[Joshua] [15]:[26] Amam, Shema, Moladah,
[Joshua] [15]:[27] Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth Pelet,
[Joshua] [15]:[28] Hazar Shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah,
[Joshua] [15]:[29] Baalah, Iyim, Ezem,
[Joshua] [15]:[30] Eltolad, Kesil, Hormah,
[Joshua] [15]:[31] Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,
[Joshua] [15]:[32] Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain and Rimmon—twenty-nine towns in all, with their villages.
[Joshua] [15]:[33] In the western foothills: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,
[Joshua] [15]:[34] Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, Enam,
[Joshua] [15]:[35] Jarmuth, Adullam, Sokoh, Azekah,
[Joshua] [15]:[36] Shaaraim, Adithaim and Gederah (or Gederothaim)—fourteen towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [15]:[37] Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal Gad,
[Joshua] [15]:[38] Dilean, Mizpah, Joktheel,
[Joshua] [15]:[39] Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,
[Joshua] [15]:[40] Kabbon, Lahmas, Kitlish,
[Joshua] [15]:[41] Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah and Makkedah—sixteen towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [15]:[42] Libnah, Ether, Ashan,
[Joshua] [15]:[43] Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,
[Joshua] [15]:[44] Keilah, Akzib and Mareshah—nine towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [15]:[45] Ekron, with its surrounding settlements and villages;
[Joshua] [15]:[46] from Ekron to the sea, all the territory near Ashdod, with their villages;
[Joshua] [15]:[47] Ashdod with its surrounding settlements and villages; and Gaza with its settlements and villages, as far as the Wadi of Egypt and the coastline of the Great Sea.
[Joshua] [15]:[48] In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Sokoh,
[Joshua] [15]:[49] Dannah, Kiriath Sannah (that is, Debir),
[Joshua] [15]:[50] Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,
[Joshua] [15]:[51] Goshen, Holon and Giloh—eleven towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [15]:[52] Arab, Rumah, Eshan,
[Joshua] [15]:[53] Janum, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah,
[Joshua] [15]:[54] Humtah, Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron) and Zior—nine towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [15]:[55] Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,
[Joshua] [15]:[56] Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,
[Joshua] [15]:[57] Kain, Gibeah and Timnah—ten towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [15]:[58] Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor,
[Joshua] [15]:[59] Maarath, Beth Anoth and Eltekon—six towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [15]:[60] Kiriath Baal (that is, Kiriath Jearim) and Rabbah—two towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [15]:[61] In the wilderness: Beth Arabah, Middin, Sekakah,
[Joshua] [15]:[62] Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi—six towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [15]:[63] The people of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, who were living in Jerusalem; so to this day the Jebusites live there alongside the people of Judah.
[Joshua] [16]:[1] The lot for the descendants of Joseph ran from the Jordan at Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho, through the wilderness that climbs from Jericho into the hill country of Bethel.
[Joshua] [16]:[2] From Bethel it went on to Luz and crossed over to the territory of the Archites at Ataroth.
[Joshua] [16]:[3] Then it went down westward to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the territory of Lower Beth-horon and on to Gezer, and it ended at the Great Sea.
[Joshua] [16]:[4] So the descendants of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
[Joshua] [16]:[5] This was the territory of the Ephraimites, clan by clan: the boundary of their inheritance ran from Ataroth-addar on the east to Upper Beth-horon,
[Joshua] [16]:[6] From there the boundary ran westward, with Michmethath on the north, and it turned eastward to Taanath-shiloh and passed by it on the east of Janoah.
[Joshua] [16]:[7] Then it went down from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah, touched Jericho, and came out at the Jordan.
[Joshua] [16]:[8] From Tappuah the boundary ran west to the Kanah Ravine and ended at the sea. This was the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim, clan by clan,
[Joshua] [16]:[9] together with all the towns and their villages that were set apart for the Ephraimites within the inheritance of the Manassites.
[Joshua] [16]:[10] But they did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer. So the Canaanites have lived among the Ephraimites to this day, subjected to forced labor.
[Joshua] [17]:[1] A lot also fell to the tribe of Manasseh, since he was Joseph's firstborn. Machir, Manasseh's firstborn and the father of Gilead, received Gilead and Bashan, because he was a man of war.
[Joshua] [17]:[2] The rest of the descendants of Manasseh received land by their clans: the sons of Abiezer, the sons of Helek, the sons of Asriel, the sons of Shechem, the sons of Hepher, and the sons of Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, by their clans.
[Joshua] [17]:[3] Now Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
[Joshua] [17]:[4] They came before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua son of Nun, and before the leaders, and said, "The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." So, at the LORD's command, he gave them an inheritance among the brothers of their father.
[Joshua] [17]:[5] Thus ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan,
[Joshua] [17]:[6] because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance along with his sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of Manasseh's descendants.
[Joshua] [17]:[7] The border of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethath, which lies east of Shechem; then the border went south to the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
[Joshua] [17]:[8] The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on Manasseh's border, belonged to the sons of Ephraim.
[Joshua] [17]:[9] Then the border went down to the Wadi Kanah. South of the wadi these towns belonged to Ephraim, among the towns of Manasseh; Manasseh's territory lay north of the wadi, and it ended at the sea.
[Joshua] [17]:[10] The land to the south belonged to Ephraim and the land to the north to Manasseh, with the sea as its border. On the north they bordered Asher, and on the east Issachar.
[Joshua] [17]:[11] Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh also held Beth-shean with its villages, Ibleam with its villages, Dor and its villages, En-dor and its villages, Taanach and its villages, and Megiddo and its villages—the three heights.[^1] [^1]: The meaning of the Hebrew phrase rendered "the three heights" is uncertain; it may refer to three hill districts or high regions associated with these towns.
[Joshua] [17]:[12] But the descendants of Manasseh could not dispossess these towns, for the Canaanites were determined to go on living in this land.
[Joshua] [17]:[13] When the Israelites grew stronger, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they did not drive them out completely.
[Joshua] [17]:[14] The descendants of Joseph said to Joshua, "Why have you given us only one lot and one portion as our inheritance, when we are a numerous people, for the LORD has blessed us so richly until now?"
[Joshua] [17]:[15] Joshua answered them, "If you are such a numerous people, go up into the forest and clear ground for yourselves there in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too cramped for you."
[Joshua] [17]:[16] But the descendants of Joseph said, "The hill country is not enough for us, and all the Canaanites living in the valley country have iron chariots—both those in Beth-shean with its villages and those in the Valley of Jezreel."
[Joshua] [17]:[17] Then Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh, "You are a numerous people and you have great strength. You shall not have only one lot,
[Joshua] [17]:[18] for the hill country shall be yours. Though it is forest, you will clear it, and it shall be yours to its farthest limits. You will drive out the Canaanites, even though they have iron chariots and are strong."
[Joshua] [18]:[1] The whole congregation of the Israelites gathered at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there, and the land lay subdued before them.
[Joshua] [18]:[2] But seven tribes of Israel still remained without an allotted inheritance.
[Joshua] [18]:[3] So Joshua said to the Israelites, "How long will you hold back from going in to take possession of the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you?
[Joshua] [18]:[4] Choose three men from each tribe, and I will send them out to travel through the land and map it according to their inheritance; then let them come back to me.
[Joshua] [18]:[5] They are to divide it into seven portions. Judah is to keep its territory in the south, and the house of Joseph its territory in the north.
[Joshua] [18]:[6] You are to map out the land in seven portions and bring the record to me here, and I will cast lots for you here before the LORD our God.
[Joshua] [18]:[7] The Levites, however, have no portion among you, for the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance. And Gad, Reuben, and half the tribe of Manasseh have already received their inheritance beyond the Jordan to the east, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave them."
[Joshua] [18]:[8] So the men set out on their way. Joshua charged those who went to map the land: "Go, travel through the land, map it, and return to me. Then I will cast lots for you here before the LORD at Shiloh."
[Joshua] [18]:[9] The men went and passed through the land, recording it in a scroll, town by town, in seven portions; then they returned to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh.
[Joshua] [18]:[10] And Joshua cast lots for them at Shiloh before the LORD, and there he divided the land among the Israelites according to their divisions.
[Joshua] [18]:[11] The lot came up for the tribe of Benjamin by its clans, and the territory allotted to them lay between the descendants of Judah and the descendants of Joseph.
[Joshua] [18]:[12] On the north side their boundary began at the Jordan, went up the slope north of Jericho, then up into the hill country westward, and came out at the wilderness of Beth Aven.
[Joshua] [18]:[13] From there the boundary passed on to Luz, to the southern slope of Luz—that is, Bethel—and went down to Ataroth Addar, on the mountain south of Lower Beth Horon.
[Joshua] [18]:[14] On the west side the boundary turned and bent southward from the mountain facing Beth Horon on the south, and it came out at Kiriath Baal—that is, Kiriath Jearim—a town of Judah. This was the western side.
[Joshua] [18]:[15] The southern side began at the edge of Kiriath Jearim, and the boundary ran west and came out at the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.
[Joshua] [18]:[16] Then it went down to the foot of the mountain that faces the Valley of Ben Hinnom, at the north end of the Valley of Rephaim, and continued down the Valley of Hinnom along the southern slope of the Jebusite city, and on down to En Rogel.
[Joshua] [18]:[17] It bent northward and went out to En Shemesh, then on to Geliloth, which faces the Ascent of Adummim, and down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
[Joshua] [18]:[18] It passed along to the northern slope facing the Arabah and went down into the Arabah.
[Joshua] [18]:[19] Then the boundary passed along to the northern slope of Beth Hoglah and came out at the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the southern end of the Jordan. This was the southern boundary.
[Joshua] [18]:[20] The Jordan formed the boundary on the eastern side. This was the inheritance of the Benjaminites, with its boundaries on every side, according to their clans.
[Joshua] [18]:[21] The towns of the tribe of Benjamin, according to their clans, were: Jericho, Beth Hoglah, Emek Keziz,
[Joshua] [18]:[22] Beth Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel,
[Joshua] [18]:[23] Avvim, Parah, Ophrah,
[Joshua] [18]:[24] Kephar Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba—twelve towns with their villages;
[Joshua] [18]:[25] Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,
[Joshua] [18]:[26] Mizpeh, Kephirah, Mozah,
[Joshua] [18]:[27] Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,
[Joshua] [18]:[28] Zelah, Haeleph, the Jebusite city—that is, Jerusalem—Gibeah, and Kiriath—fourteen towns with their villages. This was the inheritance of the Benjaminites according to their clans.
[Joshua] [19]:[1] The second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the Simeonites, clan by clan. Their inheritance lay within the inheritance of Judah.
