[Joshua] [19]:[2] Their inheritance included Beersheba, also called Sheba, then Moladah,
[Joshua] [19]:[3] Hazar Shual, Balah, Ezem,
[Joshua] [19]:[4] Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,
[Joshua] [19]:[5] Ziklag, Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susah,
[Joshua] [19]:[6] Beth Lebaoth, and Sharuhen—thirteen towns with their villages;
[Joshua] [19]:[7] Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan—four towns with their villages;
[Joshua] [19]:[8] together with all the villages surrounding these towns as far as Baalath Beer, that is, Ramah of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the Simeonites, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [19]:[9] The inheritance of the Simeonites was taken from the territory of Judah, because Judah's share was more than they needed. So the Simeonites received their inheritance within Judah's territory.
[Joshua] [19]:[10] The third lot came up for Zebulun, clan by clan. The border of their inheritance ran as far as Sarid.
[Joshua] [19]:[11] From there it went west to Maralah, touched Dabbesheth, and reached the ravine near Jokneam.
[Joshua] [19]:[12] From Sarid it turned east toward the sunrise, to the border of Kisloth Tabor, then went on to Daberath and up to Japhia.
[Joshua] [19]:[13] From there it continued eastward to Gath Hepher and Eth Kazin, came out at Rimmon, and turned toward Neah.
[Joshua] [19]:[14] From there the border curved north of Hannathon and ended at the Valley of Iphtah El.
[Joshua] [19]:[15] Included were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem—twelve towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [19]:[16] These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the Zebulunites, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [19]:[17] The fourth lot came out for Issachar, for the Issacharites, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [19]:[18] Their territory included Jezreel, Kesulloth, Shunem,
[Joshua] [19]:[19] Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath,
[Joshua] [19]:[20] Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez,
[Joshua] [19]:[21] Remeth, En Gannim, En Haddah, and Beth Pazzez.
[Joshua] [19]:[22] The border touched Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth Shemesh, and ended at the Jordan—sixteen towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [19]:[23] These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the tribe of Issachar, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [19]:[24] The fifth lot came out for the tribe of Asher, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [19]:[25] Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Acshaph,
[Joshua] [19]:[26] Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal. On the west the border touched Carmel and Shihor Libnath.
[Joshua] [19]:[27] It then turned east toward Beth Dagon, touched Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah El, and went north to Beth Emek and Neiel, passing Cabul on the left.
[Joshua] [19]:[28] It went on to Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon.
[Joshua] [19]:[29] The border then turned back toward Ramah and went to the fortified city of Tyre, turned toward Hosah, and came out at the sea in the region of Aczib,
[Joshua] [19]:[30] along with Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob—twenty-two towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [19]:[31] These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the tribe of Asher, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [19]:[32] The sixth lot came out for Naphtali, for the Naphtalites, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [19]:[33] Their border ran from Heleph and the great tree in Zaanannim, past Adami Nekeb and Jabneel to Lakkum, and ended at the Jordan.
[Joshua] [19]:[34] The border then turned west through Aznoth Tabor and came out at Hukkok. It touched Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan on the east.
[Joshua] [19]:[35] The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Kinnereth,
[Joshua] [19]:[36] Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,
[Joshua] [19]:[37] Kedesh, Edrei, En Hazor,
[Joshua] [19]:[38] Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath, and Beth Shemesh—nineteen towns with their villages.
[Joshua] [19]:[39] These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the tribe of Naphtali, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [19]:[40] The seventh lot came out for the tribe of Dan, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [19]:[41] The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir Shemesh,
[Joshua] [19]:[42] Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah,
[Joshua] [19]:[43] Elon, Timnah, Ekron,
[Joshua] [19]:[44] Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,
[Joshua] [19]:[45] Jehud, Bene Berak, Gath Rimmon,
[Joshua] [19]:[46] Me Jarkon, and Rakkon, with the border facing Joppa.
[Joshua] [19]:[47] But the territory of the Danites proved too small for them, so they marched up and attacked Leshem. They captured it, put it to the sword, took possession of it, and settled there. They named Leshem Dan, after their ancestor Dan.
[Joshua] [19]:[48] These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the tribe of Dan, clan by clan.
[Joshua] [19]:[49] When they had finished apportioning the land according to its boundaries, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.
[Joshua] [19]:[50] At the LORD's command they gave him the town he had asked for—Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He rebuilt the town and settled there.
[Joshua] [19]:[51] These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the families of the tribes of Israel assigned by lot at Shiloh, before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting. And so they finished dividing the land.
[Joshua] [20]:[1] The LORD said to Joshua:
[Joshua] [20]:[2] "Tell the Israelites: Designate the cities of refuge, as I instructed you through Moses,
[Joshua] [20]:[3] so that anyone who kills a person accidentally, without intent, may flee there. They will be your refuge from the avenger of blood.
[Joshua] [20]:[4] When someone flees to one of these cities, he is to stand at the entrance of the city gate and state his case before the elders of that city. Then they are to take him into the city and give him a place to live among them.
[Joshua] [20]:[5] If the avenger of blood pursues him, they must not hand the killer over to him, since he struck down his neighbor unintentionally and had borne him no hatred before.
[Joshua] [20]:[6] He is to stay in that city until he has stood trial before the assembly and until the death of the high priest serving at that time. Then he may go back to his own town and his own home, the town he fled from."
[Joshua] [20]:[7] So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath Arba, that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.
[Joshua] [20]:[8] And east of the Jordan, across from Jericho, they designated Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.
[Joshua] [20]:[9] These were the cities appointed for all the Israelites and for any foreigner living among them, so that anyone who killed a person accidentally could flee there and not die at the hand of the avenger of blood until he had stood before the assembly.
[Joshua] [21]:[1] The heads of the Levite families came to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the heads of the families of the tribes of Israel.
[Joshua] [21]:[2] At Shiloh in the land of Canaan they said to them, "The LORD commanded through Moses that we be given cities to live in, with pastureland for our livestock."
[Joshua] [21]:[3] So, at the LORD's command, the Israelites gave the Levites these cities with their pasturelands out of their own inheritance.
[Joshua] [21]:[4] The lot came out for the clans of the Kohathites. The descendants of Aaron the priest, who were Levites, received thirteen cities by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
[Joshua] [21]:[5] The rest of the Kohathites received ten cities by lot from the clans of the tribes of Ephraim and Dan and from the half-tribe of Manasseh.
[Joshua] [21]:[6] The descendants of Gershon received thirteen cities by lot from the clans of the tribes of Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali, and from the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
[Joshua] [21]:[7] The descendants of Merari, clan by clan, received twelve cities from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
[Joshua] [21]:[8] So the Israelites gave the Levites these cities with their pasturelands by lot, as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
[Joshua] [21]:[9] From the tribes of Judah and Simeon they assigned the following cities, here listed by name:
[Joshua] [21]:[10] These cities went to the descendants of Aaron from the Kohathite clans of the Levites, since the first lot fell to them.
[Joshua] [21]:[11] They were given Kiriath Arba, that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah—Arba being the ancestor of Anak—along with the pastureland around it.
[Joshua] [21]:[12] But the fields and villages belonging to the city they gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his possession.
[Joshua] [21]:[13] So to the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron, a city of refuge for anyone accused of murder, with its pastureland, and Libnah with its pastureland,
[Joshua] [21]:[14] Jattir with its pastureland, Eshtemoa with its pastureland,
[Joshua] [21]:[15] Holon with its pastureland, Debir with its pastureland,
[Joshua] [21]:[16] Ain with its pastureland, Juttah with its pastureland, and Beth Shemesh with its pastureland—nine cities from these two tribes.
[Joshua] [21]:[17] From the tribe of Benjamin they gave them Gibeon with its pastureland, Geba with its pastureland,
[Joshua] [21]:[18] Anathoth with its pastureland, and Almon with its pastureland—four cities.
[Joshua] [21]:[19] In all, the cities of the priests, the descendants of Aaron, numbered thirteen, together with their pasturelands.
[Joshua] [21]:[20] The rest of the Kohathite clans of the Levites received their cities by lot from the tribe of Ephraim.
[Joshua] [21]:[21] They were given Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, a city of refuge for anyone accused of murder, with its pastureland, and Gezer with its pastureland,
[Joshua] [21]:[22] Kibzaim with its pastureland, and Beth Horon with its pastureland—four cities.
[Joshua] [21]:[23] From the tribe of Dan they received Eltekeh with its pastureland, Gibbethon with its pastureland,
[Joshua] [21]:[24] Aijalon with its pastureland, and Gath Rimmon with its pastureland—four cities.
[Joshua] [21]:[25] From the half-tribe of Manasseh they received Taanach with its pastureland and Gath Rimmon with its pastureland—two cities.
[Joshua] [21]:[26] All these ten cities with their pasturelands went to the rest of the Kohathite clans.
[Joshua] [21]:[27] To the Gershonites, one of the Levite clans, they gave from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan, a city of refuge for anyone accused of murder, with its pastureland, and Be Eshterah with its pastureland—two cities.
[Joshua] [21]:[28] From the tribe of Issachar: Kishion with its pastureland, Daberath with its pastureland,
[Joshua] [21]:[29] Jarmuth with its pastureland, and En Gannim with its pastureland—four cities.
[Joshua] [21]:[30] From the tribe of Asher: Mishal with its pastureland, Abdon with its pastureland,
[Joshua] [21]:[31] Helkath with its pastureland, and Rehob with its pastureland—four cities.
[Joshua] [21]:[32] From the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee, a city of refuge for anyone accused of murder, with its pastureland, Hammoth Dor with its pastureland, and Kartan with its pastureland—three cities.
[Joshua] [21]:[33] The cities of the Gershonite clans came to thirteen in all, together with their pasturelands.
[Joshua] [21]:[34] To the Merarite clans, the rest of the Levites, they gave from the tribe of Zebulun: Jokneam with its pastureland, Kartah with its pastureland,
[Joshua] [21]:[35] Dimnah with its pastureland, and Nahalal with its pastureland—four cities.
[Joshua] [21]:[36] From the tribe of Reuben: Bezer with its pastureland, Jahzah with its pastureland,
[Joshua] [21]:[37] Kedemoth with its pastureland, and Mephaath with its pastureland—four cities.
[Joshua] [21]:[38] From the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead, a city of refuge for anyone accused of murder, with its pastureland, Mahanaim with its pastureland,
[Joshua] [21]:[39] Heshbon with its pastureland, and Jazer with its pastureland—four cities in all.
[Joshua] [21]:[40] The cities allotted to the Merarite clans, the last of the Levite clans, came to twelve.
[Joshua] [21]:[41] In all, the cities of the Levites within the holdings of the Israelites came to forty-eight cities, together with their pasturelands.
[Joshua] [21]:[42] Each of these cities had its own pastureland surrounding it; this was true of them all.
[Joshua] [21]:[43] So the LORD gave Israel all the land he had sworn to give their fathers, and they took possession of it and settled there.
[Joshua] [21]:[44] The LORD gave them rest on every side, just as he had sworn to their fathers. Not one of their enemies could stand against them; the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hands.
[Joshua] [21]:[45] Not one word failed of all the good things the LORD had promised the house of Israel; every one of them came true.
[Joshua] [22]:[1] Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh
[Joshua] [22]:[2] and said to them: "You have kept everything Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and you have obeyed my voice in all that I commanded you.
[Joshua] [22]:[3] You have not deserted your brothers through all this long time, down to this very day, but have faithfully kept the charge laid on you by the LORD your God.
[Joshua] [22]:[4] Now the LORD your God has given rest to your brothers, as he promised them. So turn back and go to your tents, to the land you hold as your own, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave you beyond the Jordan.
[Joshua] [22]:[5] Only be very careful to keep the commandment and the law that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to hold fast to him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul."
[Joshua] [22]:[6] Then Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their tents.
[Joshua] [22]:[7] To one half of the tribe of Manasseh Moses had given land in Bashan, and to the other half Joshua gave land alongside their brothers west of the Jordan. And when Joshua sent them away to their tents, he blessed them
[Joshua] [22]:[8] and said to them: "Return to your tents with great wealth—with vast herds, with silver and gold, bronze and iron, and with a great quantity of clothing. Divide the spoil taken from your enemies with your brothers."
[Joshua] [22]:[9] So the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh left the Israelites at Shiloh in the land of Canaan and set out for the land of Gilead, the land they held as their own, where they had settled according to the command of the LORD through Moses.
[Joshua] [22]:[10] When they came to the region of the Jordan that lies in the land of Canaan, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there by the Jordan—a great altar, imposing to see.
[Joshua] [22]:[11] And the Israelites heard it said: "Look, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar facing the land of Canaan, in the region of the Jordan, on the Israelite side."
[Joshua] [22]:[12] When the Israelites heard this, the whole assembly of Israel gathered at Shiloh to go up and wage war against them.
[Joshua] [22]:[13] The Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead,
[Joshua] [22]:[14] and with him ten leaders, one from each ancestral house of every tribe of Israel; each was the head of an ancestral house among the clans of Israel.
[Joshua] [22]:[15] They came to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead and said to them:
[Joshua] [22]:[16] "This is what the whole assembly of the LORD says: What is this treachery you have committed against the God of Israel, turning away this day from the LORD by building yourselves an altar and rebelling against the LORD today?
[Joshua] [22]:[17] Was the sin at Peor not enough for us? To this day we have not cleansed ourselves of it, and a plague came upon the assembly of the LORD.
[Joshua] [22]:[18] And now you turn away from the LORD! If you rebel against the LORD today, tomorrow he will be angry with the whole assembly of Israel.
[Joshua] [22]:[19] If the land you hold is unclean, then cross over to the land the LORD holds as his own, where the LORD's tabernacle stands, and take your possession among us. But do not rebel against the LORD, and do not rebel against us by building yourselves an altar other than the altar of the LORD our God.
[Joshua] [22]:[20] When Achan son of Zerah broke faith concerning what was devoted to destruction, did not wrath fall upon the whole assembly of Israel? And he was only one man—yet he was not the only one who died for his sin."
[Joshua] [22]:[21] Then the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the heads of the clans of Israel:
[Joshua] [22]:[22] "The Mighty One, God, the LORD! The Mighty One, God, the LORD—he knows, and let Israel itself know! If this was done in rebellion or treachery against the LORD, then do not spare us this day.
[Joshua] [22]:[23] If we built an altar to turn away from the LORD, or to offer burnt offerings and grain offerings on it, or to present fellowship offerings on it, may the LORD himself call us to account.
[Joshua] [22]:[24] No—we did this out of concern, for we thought: In time to come your children might say to our children, 'What have you to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?
[Joshua] [22]:[25] The LORD has set the Jordan as a boundary between us and you Reubenites and Gadites. You have no share in the LORD.' So your children might make our children stop fearing the LORD.
[Joshua] [22]:[26] That is why we said, 'Let us now build this altar—not for burnt offerings or sacrifices,
[Joshua] [22]:[27] but as a witness between us and you and the generations after us, that we too perform the service of the LORD before him with our burnt offerings, our sacrifices, and our fellowship offerings.' Then in time to come your children will not say to our children, 'You have no share in the LORD.'
[Joshua] [22]:[28] And we said: If in time to come they say this to us or to our descendants, we will answer, 'Look at the replica of the LORD's altar that our fathers built—not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you.'
[Joshua] [22]:[29] Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD and turn away from him today by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, or sacrifices, other than the altar of the LORD our God that stands before his tabernacle."
[Joshua] [22]:[30] When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the assembly and the heads of the clans of Israel who were with him heard what the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the Manassites said, they were satisfied.
[Joshua] [22]:[31] And Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the Manassites, "Today we know that the LORD is among us, because you have not committed this treachery against the LORD. Now you have delivered the Israelites from the hand of the LORD."
[Joshua] [22]:[32] Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders left the Reubenites and the Gadites in the land of Gilead and returned to the land of Canaan, to the Israelites, and reported to them.
[Joshua] [22]:[33] The Israelites were satisfied with the report and praised God; they spoke no more of going up to wage war against them and ravaging the land where the Reubenites and Gadites lived.
[Joshua] [22]:[34] And the Reubenites and the Gadites gave the altar this name: "A Witness Between Us That the LORD Is God."[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew text does not state the name itself; it reads simply "they named the altar, for it is a witness between us that the LORD is God." The name given here is drawn from the words that follow.
[Joshua] [23]:[1] A long time later, after the LORD had given Israel rest from all their enemies around them, Joshua was old, well advanced in years.
[Joshua] [23]:[2] So Joshua summoned all Israel—its elders, its leaders, its judges, and its officers—and said to them: "I am old, well advanced in years.
[Joshua] [23]:[3] You yourselves have seen everything the LORD your God did to all these nations for your sake, for the LORD your God is the one who fights for you.
[Joshua] [23]:[4] See, I have allotted to you these nations that remain as an inheritance for your tribes, from the Jordan, along with all the nations I have cut off, as far as the Great Sea in the west.
[Joshua] [23]:[5] The LORD your God himself will drive them out before you and dispossess them, and you will take possession of their land, just as the LORD your God promised you.
[Joshua] [23]:[6] So be very strong to keep and to do everything written in the Book of the Law of Moses, turning aside from it neither to the right nor to the left.
[Joshua] [23]:[7] Do not associate with these nations that remain among you. Do not invoke the names of their gods or swear by them; do not serve them or bow down to them.
[Joshua] [23]:[8] Rather, hold fast to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.
[Joshua] [23]:[9] The LORD has driven out great and mighty nations before you; to this day no one has been able to stand against you.
[Joshua] [23]:[10] One of you routs a thousand, because the LORD your God himself fights for you, just as he promised.
[Joshua] [23]:[11] So watch yourselves very carefully, and love the LORD your God.
[Joshua] [23]:[12] But if you turn away and bind yourselves to the rest of these nations that remain among you, intermarrying with them and mingling with them,
[Joshua] [23]:[13] then know for certain that the LORD your God will no longer drive out these nations before you. Instead they will become a snare and a trap for you, a whip on your backs and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land the LORD your God has given you.
[Joshua] [23]:[14] Now today I am going the way of all the earth. You know with all your heart and all your soul that not one of all the good promises the LORD your God made concerning you has failed. Every one has come true; not one of them has failed.
[Joshua] [23]:[15] But just as every good thing the LORD your God promised you has come to you, so the LORD will bring upon you every evil thing, until he has destroyed you from this good land he has given you.
[Joshua] [23]:[16] If you violate the covenant of the LORD your God, which he commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them, then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and you will quickly perish from the good land he has given you."
[Joshua] [24]:[1] Then Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He summoned the elders of Israel, their leaders, their judges, and their officers, and they presented themselves before God.
[Joshua] [24]:[2] And Joshua said to all the people, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Long ago your ancestors lived beyond the River—Terah, the father of Abraham and of Nahor—and they served other gods.
[Joshua] [24]:[3] But I took your father Abraham from beyond the River and led him through all the land of Canaan. I multiplied his offspring and gave him Isaac,
[Joshua] [24]:[4] and to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. To Esau I gave the hill country of Seir as his possession, while Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
[Joshua] [24]:[5] Then I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt with plagues by all that I did there; and afterward I brought you out.
[Joshua] [24]:[6] I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, and you came to the sea. The Egyptians pursued your ancestors with chariots and horsemen as far as the Red Sea.
[Joshua] [24]:[7] They cried out to the LORD, and he put darkness between you and the Egyptians; he brought the sea over them and covered them. Your own eyes saw what I did in Egypt. Then you lived in the wilderness a long time.
[Joshua] [24]:[8] I brought you to the land of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan. They fought against you, but I gave them into your hands; you took possession of their land, and I destroyed them before you.
[Joshua] [24]:[9] Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel. He sent and called for Balaam son of Beor to curse you,
[Joshua] [24]:[10] but I would not listen to Balaam. Instead he blessed you again and again, and I rescued you from his hand.
[Joshua] [24]:[11] You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The citizens of Jericho fought against you, as did the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites; but I gave them into your hands.
[Joshua] [24]:[12] I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it drove them out before you—the two kings of the Amorites. It was not by your sword or your bow.
[Joshua] [24]:[13] I gave you a land you had not labored for and cities you had not built, and you have settled in them; you eat from vineyards and olive groves you did not plant.
[Joshua] [24]:[14] "Now therefore, fear the LORD and serve him with integrity and faithfulness. Put away the gods your ancestors served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.
[Joshua] [24]:[15] But if serving the LORD seems wrong in your eyes, then choose today whom you will serve—whether the gods your ancestors served beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are living. As for me and my household, we will serve the LORD."
[Joshua] [24]:[16] The people answered, "Far be it from us to forsake the LORD and serve other gods!
[Joshua] [24]:[17] For the LORD our God is the one who brought us and our ancestors up out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and who performed those great signs before our eyes. He protected us on the whole journey we traveled and among all the peoples through whose midst we passed.
[Joshua] [24]:[18] And the LORD drove out before us all the peoples, including the Amorites who lived in the land. We too will serve the LORD, for he is our God."
[Joshua] [24]:[19] But Joshua said to the people, "You are not able to serve the LORD, for he is a holy God. He is a jealous God; he will not forgive your rebellion and your sins.
[Joshua] [24]:[20] If you forsake the LORD and serve foreign gods, he will turn and bring disaster on you and make an end of you, after he has done you good."
[Joshua] [24]:[21] But the people said to Joshua, "No! We will serve the LORD."
[Joshua] [24]:[22] Then Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the LORD, to serve him." And they said, "We are witnesses."
[Joshua] [24]:[23] "Now then, put away the foreign gods that are among you, and turn your hearts to the LORD, the God of Israel."
[Joshua] [24]:[24] And the people said to Joshua, "We will serve the LORD our God, and we will obey his voice."
[Joshua] [24]:[25] So on that day Joshua made a covenant for the people, and there at Shechem he established for them a statute and an ordinance.
[Joshua] [24]:[26] Joshua recorded these words in the Book of the Law of God. Then he took a large stone and set it up there under the oak that stood by the sanctuary of the LORD.
[Joshua] [24]:[27] And Joshua said to all the people, "Look, this stone will be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words the LORD spoke to us. It will be a witness against you, so that you do not deny your God."
[Joshua] [24]:[28] Then Joshua sent the people away, each to his own inheritance.
[Joshua] [24]:[29] After these things, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of one hundred and ten.
[Joshua] [24]:[30] They buried him within the territory of his inheritance at Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
[Joshua] [24]:[31] Israel served the LORD throughout the lifetime of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him and who had known all that the LORD had done for Israel.
[Joshua] [24]:[32] The bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, were buried at Shechem in the plot of ground Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred pieces of silver. It became the inheritance of Joseph's descendants.
[Joshua] [24]:[33] Eleazar son of Aaron also died, and they buried him at Gibeah, which belonged to his son Phinehas and had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.
[Judges] [1]:[1] After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the LORD, "Which of us is to go up first against the Canaanites to fight them?"
[Judges] [1]:[2] The LORD answered, "Judah is to go up. I have handed the land over to him."
[Judges] [1]:[3] Then Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Come up with me into the territory allotted to me, and let us fight the Canaanites together; then I will go with you into your territory." So Simeon went with him.
[Judges] [1]:[4] Judah went up, and the LORD handed the Canaanites and the Perizzites over to them; they struck down ten thousand men at Bezek.
[Judges] [1]:[5] At Bezek they came upon Adoni-bezek and fought him, and they defeated the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
[Judges] [1]:[6] Adoni-bezek fled, but they pursued him, captured him, and cut off his thumbs and big toes.
[Judges] [1]:[7] Then Adoni-bezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to pick up scraps under my table. As I have done, so God has repaid me." They brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died.
[Judges] [1]:[8] The men of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They put its people to the sword and set the city on fire.
[Judges] [1]:[9] After that, the men of Judah went down to fight the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, in the Negev, and in the foothills.
[Judges] [1]:[10] Judah marched against the Canaanites living in Hebron—Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba—and they defeated Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
[Judges] [1]:[11] From there they advanced against the inhabitants of Debir, which was formerly called Kiriath-sepher.
[Judges] [1]:[12] Caleb said, "Whoever attacks Kiriath-sepher and takes it, I will give him my daughter Achsah in marriage."
[Judges] [1]:[13] Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it, so Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah in marriage.
[Judges] [1]:[14] When she came to Othniel, she urged him to ask her father for a field. As she got down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, "What do you want?"
[Judges] [1]:[15] She answered, "Grant me a favor. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well." So Caleb gave her the upper and lower springs.
[Judges] [1]:[16] The descendants of Moses' father-in-law, the Kenite, went up with the people of Judah from the City of Palms to the wilderness of Judah, which lies in the Negev near Arad, and they went and settled among the people there.
[Judges] [1]:[17] Judah went with his brother Simeon, and together they defeated the Canaanites living in Zephath. They devoted the city to destruction, and so it was named Hormah.<note>Hormah sounds like the Hebrew word for "destruction."</note>
[Judges] [1]:[18] Judah also took Gaza with its territory, Ashkelon with its territory, and Ekron with its territory.
[Judges] [1]:[19] The LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country, but they could not drive out the people of the plain, because they had iron chariots.
[Judges] [1]:[20] Hebron was given to Caleb, as Moses had promised, and he drove out from there the three sons of Anak.
[Judges] [1]:[21] But the Benjaminites did not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem; so the Jebusites have lived there among the Benjaminites to this day.
[Judges] [1]:[22] The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
[Judges] [1]:[23] They sent men to scout out Bethel, which was formerly called Luz.
[Judges] [1]:[24] The scouts saw a man coming out of the city and said to him, "Show us the way into the city, and we will treat you kindly."
[Judges] [1]:[25] So he showed them the way in, and they put the city to the sword, but they let the man and his whole family go.
[Judges] [1]:[26] The man went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a city and named it Luz; that is its name to this day.
[Judges] [1]:[27] Manasseh did not drive out the people of Beth-shean and its villages, or Taanach and its villages, or the people of Dor and its villages, or the people of Ibleam and its villages, or the people of Megiddo and its villages; the Canaanites were determined to remain in that land.
[Judges] [1]:[28] When Israel grew strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.
[Judges] [1]:[29] Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, so the Canaanites went on living there among them.
[Judges] [1]:[30] Zebulun did not drive out the people of Kitron or the people of Nahalol, so the Canaanites lived among them, but they were put to forced labor.
[Judges] [1]:[31] Asher did not drive out the people of Acco or Sidon, or of Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.
[Judges] [1]:[32] So the Asherites lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, because they did not drive them out.
[Judges] [1]:[33] Naphtali did not drive out the people of Beth-shemesh or of Beth-anath, so they lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land; but the people of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath were put to forced labor for them.
[Judges] [1]:[34] The Amorites pressed the Danites back into the hill country and would not let them come down into the plain.
[Judges] [1]:[35] The Amorites were determined to remain in Mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim, but as the house of Joseph grew stronger, they too were put to forced labor.
[Judges] [1]:[36] The border of the Amorites ran from the Ascent of Akrabbim and from Sela on upward.
[Judges] [2]:[1] The angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said: "I brought you up out of Egypt and led you into the land I swore to give your fathers. I said, 'I will never break my covenant with you,
[Judges] [2]:[2] and you shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land; you shall tear down their altars.' But you have not obeyed my voice. What is this you have done?
[Judges] [2]:[3] So now I say: I will not drive them out before you; they will be thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you."
[Judges] [2]:[4] When the angel of the LORD had spoken these words to all the Israelites, the people lifted up their voices and wept.
[Judges] [2]:[5] So they named that place Bochim, and there they sacrificed to the LORD.
[Judges] [2]:[6] When Joshua dismissed the people, the Israelites went out, each to his own inheritance, to take possession of the land.
[Judges] [2]:[7] The people served the LORD throughout the lifetime of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him, men who had seen all the great work the LORD had done for Israel.
[Judges] [2]:[8] Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of a hundred and ten.
[Judges] [2]:[9] They buried him within the borders of his inheritance, at Timnath-heres in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
[Judges] [2]:[10] That whole generation, too, was gathered to their fathers, and another generation arose after them who did not know the LORD or what he had done for Israel.
[Judges] [2]:[11] Then the Israelites did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and served the Baals.
[Judges] [2]:[12] They abandoned the LORD, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt, and followed other gods, the gods of the peoples around them. They bowed down to them and provoked the LORD to anger.
[Judges] [2]:[13] They abandoned the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtoreths.
[Judges] [2]:[14] So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel. He handed them over to raiders who plundered them, and he sold them into the power of the enemies around them, so that they could no longer stand before their enemies.
[Judges] [2]:[15] Wherever they marched out, the hand of the LORD was against them for harm, just as the LORD had said and sworn to them. They were in great distress.
[Judges] [2]:[16] Then the LORD raised up judges, who saved them from the hand of those who plundered them.
[Judges] [2]:[17] Yet they would not listen to their judges either, but prostituted themselves to other gods and bowed down to them. They quickly turned from the way their fathers had walked in obedience to the LORD's commands; they did not do as their fathers had done.
[Judges] [2]:[18] Whenever the LORD raised up a judge for them, the LORD was with the judge and saved them from the hand of their enemies as long as the judge lived; for the LORD was moved to pity by their groaning under those who oppressed and afflicted them.
[Judges] [2]:[19] But when the judge died, they would turn back and become more corrupt than their fathers, following other gods to serve them and bow down to them. They would not give up their practices or their stubborn ways.
[Judges] [2]:[20] So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he said, "Because this nation has violated the covenant I laid down for their fathers and has not listened to my voice,
[Judges] [2]:[21] I in turn will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died.
[Judges] [2]:[22] I will use them to test Israel, to see whether they will keep the way of the LORD and walk in it as their fathers did, or not."
[Judges] [2]:[23] So the LORD let those nations remain; he did not drive them out at once or hand them over to Joshua.
[Judges] [3]:[1] These are the nations the LORD left in place to test Israel through them—all those Israelites who had not known any of the wars of Canaan.
[Judges] [3]:[2] He did this only so that the generations of Israel might learn warfare—those, at least, who had known nothing of it before.
[Judges] [3]:[3] The nations were these: the five rulers of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived in the mountains of Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.
[Judges] [3]:[4] They were left to test Israel, to find out whether they would obey the commandments the LORD had given their fathers through Moses.
[Judges] [3]:[5] So the Israelites lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
[Judges] [3]:[6] They took their daughters as wives and gave their own daughters to their sons, and they served their gods.
[Judges] [3]:[7] The Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD. They forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
[Judges] [3]:[8] So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim, and the Israelites served Cushan-rishathaim for eight years.
[Judges] [3]:[9] Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for them, who saved them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
[Judges] [3]:[10] The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.
[Judges] [3]:[11] So the land had rest for forty years. Then Othniel son of Kenaz died.
[Judges] [3]:[12] Again the Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD gave Eglon king of Moab power over Israel, because they had done what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
[Judges] [3]:[13] Eglon gathered to himself the Ammonites and the Amalekites, and he went and struck Israel down, and they took possession of the City of Palms.
[Judges] [3]:[14] So the Israelites served Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years.
[Judges] [3]:[15] Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for them: Ehud son of Gera, a Benjaminite, a left-handed man. The Israelites sent tribute by his hand to Eglon king of Moab.
[Judges] [3]:[16] Ehud had made himself a double-edged sword about a cubit long, and he strapped it under his clothing on his right thigh.
[Judges] [3]:[17] He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
[Judges] [3]:[18] When Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the men who had carried it.
[Judges] [3]:[19] But he himself turned back at the carved stones near Gilgal and said, "I have a secret message for you, O king." The king said, "Silence!" and all who were standing by him withdrew from his presence.
[Judges] [3]:[20] Ehud came to him while he was sitting alone in his cool upper chamber, and Ehud said, "I have a message from God for you." And the king rose from his seat.
[Judges] [3]:[21] Ehud reached with his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and drove it into Eglon's belly.
[Judges] [3]:[22] Even the hilt went in after the blade, and the fat closed over it, for he did not pull the sword out of his belly; and the filth came out.
[Judges] [3]:[23] Then Ehud went out to the porch, closing the doors of the upper chamber behind him and locking them.
[Judges] [3]:[24] After he had gone, the king's servants came and saw that the doors of the upper chamber were locked. They said, "He must be relieving himself in the cool inner room."
[Judges] [3]:[25] They waited until they were embarrassed, and still he did not open the doors of the upper chamber. So they took the key and opened them—and there lay their lord, fallen dead on the floor.
[Judges] [3]:[26] Ehud had escaped while they delayed. He passed the carved stones and got away to Seirah.
[Judges] [3]:[27] When he arrived, he sounded the trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites went down with him from the hills, with him at their head.
[Judges] [3]:[28] He said to them, "Follow me, for the LORD has given your enemies, the Moabites, into your hand." So they followed him down and seized the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, letting no one cross over.
[Judges] [3]:[29] At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites, all robust and valiant men; not one escaped.
[Judges] [3]:[30] That day Moab was subdued under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest for eighty years.
[Judges] [3]:[31] After him came Shamgar son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad. He too delivered Israel.
[Judges] [4]:[1] After Ehud was dead, the Israelites again did what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
[Judges] [4]:[2] So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.
[Judges] [4]:[3] Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, for Sisera had nine hundred iron chariots, and for twenty years he had cruelly oppressed the Israelites.
[Judges] [4]:[4] Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.
[Judges] [4]:[5] She used to sit under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came up to her for judgment.
[Judges] [4]:[6] She sent for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, "Has not the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded you: 'Go, march to Mount Tabor and take with you ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun.
[Judges] [4]:[7] I will draw out Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, to meet you at the Kishon River with his chariots and his troops, and I will give him into your hand.'"
[Judges] [4]:[8] Barak said to her, "If you go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go."
[Judges] [4]:[9] "I will surely go with you," she said, "but the honor will not be yours on the road you are taking, for the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman." So Deborah rose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
[Judges] [4]:[10] Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and ten thousand men marched up behind him. Deborah went up with him as well.
[Judges] [4]:[11] Now Heber the Kenite had separated from the other Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, and had pitched his tent by the oak at Zaanannim, near Kedesh.
[Judges] [4]:[12] When Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up Mount Tabor,
[Judges] [4]:[13] he summoned all his chariots, nine hundred iron chariots, and all the troops with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the Kishon River.
[Judges] [4]:[14] Then Deborah said to Barak, "Up! This is the day the LORD has given Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone out before you?" So Barak charged down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men behind him.
[Judges] [4]:[15] And the LORD routed Sisera and all the chariots and all the army by the edge of the sword before Barak. Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.
[Judges] [4]:[16] Barak pursued the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth-hagoyim, and Sisera's whole army fell by the sword; not one man was left.
[Judges] [4]:[17] Meanwhile Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
[Judges] [4]:[18] Jael came out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me. Do not be afraid." So he turned aside to her in the tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
[Judges] [4]:[19] He said to her, "Please give me a little water to drink; I am thirsty." She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him again.
[Judges] [4]:[20] "Stand at the entrance of the tent," he told her, "and if anyone comes and asks you, 'Is there a man here?' say, 'No.'"
[Judges] [4]:[21] But Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg and a hammer in her hand, went quietly to him, and drove the peg through his temple into the ground while he lay fast asleep, exhausted. So he died.
[Judges] [4]:[22] Just then Barak came by in pursuit of Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. "Come," she said, "I will show you the man you are looking for." He went in with her, and there lay Sisera, dead, with the tent peg through his temple.
[Judges] [4]:[23] On that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites.
[Judges] [4]:[24] And the hand of the Israelites pressed harder and harder against Jabin king of Canaan until they destroyed him.
[Judges] [5]:[1] On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang this song:
[Judges] [5]:[2] When the leaders took the lead in Israel, when the people willingly offered themselves — bless the LORD!
[Judges] [5]:[3] Hear this, you kings; listen, you rulers! I will sing to the LORD, I myself will sing; I will make music to the LORD, the God of Israel.
[Judges] [5]:[4] LORD, when you went out from Seir, when you marched from the fields of Edom, the earth shook, the heavens poured, the clouds poured down water.
[Judges] [5]:[5] The mountains melted before the LORD, even Sinai, before the LORD, the God of Israel.
[Judges] [5]:[6] In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways lay empty, and travelers kept to the winding trails.
[Judges] [5]:[7] Village life in Israel ceased — it ceased — until I, Deborah, arose, until I arose, a mother in Israel.
[Judges] [5]:[8] They chose new gods; then war came to the gates. Was a shield to be seen, or a spear, among forty thousand in Israel?
[Judges] [5]:[9] My heart goes out to the commanders of Israel, to the people who willingly offered themselves — bless the LORD!
[Judges] [5]:[10] You who ride on white donkeys, you who sit on saddle blankets, you who walk the roads — tell of it!
[Judges] [5]:[11] To the sound of singing at the watering places, there they recount the righteous deeds of the LORD, the righteous deeds of his villagers in Israel. Then the people of the LORD marched down to the gates.
[Judges] [5]:[12] Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, break into song! Rise up, Barak, and lead away your captives, son of Abinoam!
[Judges] [5]:[13] Then those who were left came down against the nobles; the people of the LORD came down for me against the mighty.
[Judges] [5]:[14] From Ephraim they came, whose roots are in Amalek; behind you, Benjamin, with your kinsmen. From Machir the commanders came down, and from Zebulun those who bear the marshal's staff.
[Judges] [5]:[15] The princes of Issachar were with Deborah; Issachar followed Barak, rushing into the valley at his heels. But among the clans of Reuben there was deep searching of heart.
[Judges] [5]:[16] Why did you linger among the sheepfolds, listening to the whistling for the flocks? Among the clans of Reuben there was deep searching of heart.
[Judges] [5]:[17] Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan. And Dan — why did he linger by the ships? Asher sat still on the seacoast and remained in his harbors.
[Judges] [5]:[18] But Zebulun was a people who risked their lives to the death, and Naphtali too, on the heights of the field.
[Judges] [5]:[19] Kings came and fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo — but they carried off no silver, no plunder.
[Judges] [5]:[20] From the heavens they fought; the stars from their courses fought against Sisera.
[Judges] [5]:[21] The river Kishon swept them away, that ancient river, the river Kishon. March on, my soul, in strength!
[Judges] [5]:[22] Then the hooves of the horses hammered the ground — the galloping, galloping of his stallions.
[Judges] [5]:[23] "Curse Meroz," said the angel of the LORD, "bitterly curse its people, because they did not come to help the LORD, to help the LORD against the mighty."
[Judges] [5]:[24] Most blessed of women be Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite; most blessed of women who dwell in tents.
[Judges] [5]:[25] He asked for water; she gave him milk. In a bowl fit for a prince she brought him curds.
[Judges] [5]:[26] Her hand reached for the tent peg, her right hand for the workman's hammer. She struck Sisera, she crushed his head; she shattered and pierced his temple.
[Judges] [5]:[27] At her feet he sank, he fell, he lay still. At her feet he sank, he fell; where he sank, there he fell — dead.
[Judges] [5]:[28] Through the window Sisera's mother looked out; behind the lattice she wailed: "Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why is the clatter of his chariots delayed?"
[Judges] [5]:[29] The wisest of her ladies answer her; she keeps repeating the words to herself:
[Judges] [5]:[30] "Surely they are finding and dividing the spoil — a girl or two for every man, dyed cloth as spoil for Sisera, dyed cloth richly embroidered, two embroidered pieces for the neck of the plunderer."
[Judges] [5]:[31] So may all your enemies perish, O LORD! But may those who love you be like the sun when it rises in its strength. And the land had rest for forty years.
[Judges] [6]:[1] The Israelites did what was evil in the LORD's sight, and the LORD handed them over to Midian for seven years.
[Judges] [6]:[2] Midian's grip on Israel grew so harsh that, to escape them, the Israelites made hiding places for themselves in the mountains, along with caves and strongholds.
[Judges] [6]:[3] Whenever Israel sowed its crops, the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the peoples of the east would come up and attack Israel.
[Judges] [6]:[4] They camped against them and destroyed the produce of the land as far as Gaza, leaving Israel nothing to live on—no sheep, no ox, no donkey.
[Judges] [6]:[5] They came up with their livestock and their tents, swarming in like locusts; they and their camels were beyond counting. They invaded the land to ravage it.
[Judges] [6]:[6] So Israel was brought very low because of Midian, and the Israelites cried out to the LORD.
[Judges] [6]:[7] When the Israelites cried out to the LORD on account of Midian,
[Judges] [6]:[8] the LORD sent them a prophet, who said to them: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I brought you up out of Egypt and led you out of the house of slavery.
[Judges] [6]:[9] I rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all who oppressed you. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.
[Judges] [6]:[10] And I said to you, 'I am the LORD your God; do not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you live.' But you have not listened to my voice."
[Judges] [6]:[11] Then the angel of the LORD came and sat under the oak at Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, while his son Gideon was threshing wheat in the winepress to hide it from the Midianites.
[Judges] [6]:[12] The angel of the LORD appeared to him and said, "The LORD is with you, mighty warrior."
[Judges] [6]:[13] Gideon replied, "Please, my lord, if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us? Where are all his wonders that our fathers told us about, saying, 'Did not the LORD bring us up out of Egypt?' But now the LORD has abandoned us and handed us over to Midian."
[Judges] [6]:[14] The LORD turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Am I not sending you?"
[Judges] [6]:[15] But he said to him, "Please, my Lord, how can I save Israel? Look, my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."
[Judges] [6]:[16] The LORD said to him, "I will be with you, and you will strike down Midian as though they were one man."
[Judges] [6]:[17] Gideon said to him, "If I have found favor in your eyes, give me a sign that it is really you speaking with me.
[Judges] [6]:[18] Please do not leave this place until I come back to you and bring out my offering and set it before you." And he said, "I will stay until you return."
[Judges] [6]:[19] Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened bread from an ephah of flour. He put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, brought them out to him under the oak, and presented them.
[Judges] [6]:[20] The angel of God said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened bread, set them on this rock, and pour out the broth." And he did so.
[Judges] [6]:[21] Then the angel of the LORD reached out the tip of the staff in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread. Fire flared up from the rock and consumed the meat and the bread, and the angel of the LORD vanished from his sight.
[Judges] [6]:[22] When Gideon realized that it was the angel of the LORD, he said, "Oh no, Lord GOD! I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face!"
[Judges] [6]:[23] But the LORD said to him, "Peace to you. Do not be afraid; you will not die."
[Judges] [6]:[24] So Gideon built an altar to the LORD there and called it "The LORD Is Peace." To this day it still stands in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
[Judges] [6]:[25] That same night the LORD said to him, "Take your father's bull, the second bull, seven years old. Tear down your father's altar to Baal and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.
[Judges] [6]:[26] Then build a proper altar to the LORD your God on top of this stronghold. Take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah pole you cut down."
[Judges] [6]:[27] So Gideon took ten of his servants and did as the LORD had told him. But because he was afraid of his father's household and the men of the town, he did it at night rather than by day.
[Judges] [6]:[28] When the men of the town got up early in the morning, there was the altar of Baal, torn down, the Asherah pole beside it cut down, and the second bull offered up on the newly built altar.
[Judges] [6]:[29] They said to one another, "Who did this thing?" And after they investigated and searched, they said, "Gideon son of Joash did it."
[Judges] [6]:[30] So the men of the town said to Joash, "Bring out your son. He must die, because he has torn down Baal's altar and cut down the Asherah pole beside it."
[Judges] [6]:[31] But Joash said to all who stood against him, "Will you plead Baal's case? Will you rescue him? Whoever argues for him shall be put to death by morning. If Baal is a god, let him defend himself, since it was his altar that was torn down."
[Judges] [6]:[32] So that day Gideon was called Jerubbaal, meaning, "Let Baal contend with him," because he tore down Baal's altar.
[Judges] [6]:[33] Now all the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the peoples of the east joined forces, crossed over, and camped in the Valley of Jezreel.
[Judges] [6]:[34] Then the Spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon. He sounded the ram's horn, and the men of Abiezer rallied behind him.
[Judges] [6]:[35] He sent messengers throughout Manasseh, and they too were called out to follow him. He also sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they came up to meet them.
[Judges] [6]:[36] Then Gideon said to God, "If you really are going to save Israel by my hand, as you have said—
[Judges] [6]:[37] look, I am placing a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew only on the fleece and all the ground is dry, then I will know that you will save Israel by my hand, as you have said."
[Judges] [6]:[38] And so it was. He rose early the next morning and wrung out the fleece, and he squeezed from it enough dew to fill a bowl with water.
[Judges] [6]:[39] Then Gideon said to God, "Do not be angry with me; let me speak just once more. Let me make one more test with the fleece: let the fleece alone be dry, and let there be dew on all the ground."
[Judges] [6]:[40] That night God did so: the fleece alone was dry, and there was dew on all the ground.
[Judges] [7]:[1] Jerubbaal—that is, Gideon—rose early, and all the people with him, and they camped beside the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian lay to the north of them, by the hill of Moreh in the valley.
[Judges] [7]:[2] The LORD said to Gideon, "You have too many people with you for me to give Midian into their hands. Israel might boast against me and say, 'My own hand saved me.'
[Judges] [7]:[3] Now then, announce to the people: 'Whoever is afraid and trembling may turn back and leave Mount Gilead.'" Twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.
[Judges] [7]:[4] Then the LORD said to Gideon, "There are still too many. Take them down to the water, and I will sift them for you there. The one I tell you shall go with you, he shall go; and anyone I tell you shall not go with you, he shall not go."
[Judges] [7]:[5] So he took the people down to the water, and the LORD said to Gideon, "Everyone who laps up the water with his tongue as a dog laps, set him apart on one side; and everyone who kneels down to drink, set him on the other."
[Judges] [7]:[6] The number of those who lapped, hand to mouth, was three hundred men. All the rest of the people knelt down to drink the water.
[Judges] [7]:[7] The LORD said to Gideon, "With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you and give Midian into your hand. Let all the others go, each to his own place."
[Judges] [7]:[8] So the three hundred took the people's provisions and their trumpets, and Gideon sent all the other Israelites home to their tents, keeping only the three hundred men. Now the camp of Midian lay below him in the valley.
[Judges] [7]:[9] That same night the LORD said to him, "Get up, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.
[Judges] [7]:[10] But if you are afraid to go down, take your servant Purah with you to the camp,
[Judges] [7]:[11] and listen to what they are saying. Afterward your hands will be strengthened, and you will go down against the camp." So he went down with his servant Purah to the outposts of the armed men in the camp.
[Judges] [7]:[12] The Midianites, the Amalekites, and all the people of the east lay sprawled across the valley, as thick as locusts, and their camels were beyond counting, like the sand on the seashore.
[Judges] [7]:[13] When Gideon arrived, a man was telling his comrade a dream. "Listen," he said, "I had a dream: a round loaf of barley bread came tumbling into the camp of Midian. It struck a tent, and the tent turned over and collapsed."
[Judges] [7]:[14] His comrade answered, "That can be nothing but the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite. God has given Midian and the whole camp into his hand."
[Judges] [7]:[15] When Gideon heard the dream and its interpretation, he bowed down in worship. He returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Get up! The LORD has given the camp of Midian into your hands."
[Judges] [7]:[16] He divided the three hundred men into three companies and put a trumpet in every man's hand, along with an empty jar and a torch inside the jar.
[Judges] [7]:[17] He told them, "Watch me and do the same. When I reach the edge of the camp, do exactly as I do.
[Judges] [7]:[18] When I and all who are with me blow our trumpets, then you blow yours all around the camp and shout, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"
[Judges] [7]:[19] Gideon and the hundred men with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just after the guard had been changed. They blew their trumpets and smashed the jars in their hands.
[Judges] [7]:[20] The three companies blew their trumpets and shattered their jars. Holding the torches in their left hands and the trumpets in their right hands to blow, they shouted, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"
[Judges] [7]:[21] Each man held his position around the camp, while the whole camp ran, crying out and fleeing.
[Judges] [7]:[22] As the three hundred trumpets sounded, the LORD set every man's sword against his comrade throughout the camp, and the army fled as far as Beth Shittah toward Zererah, to the edge of Abel Meholah near Tabbath.
[Judges] [7]:[23] The Israelites were called out from Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh, and they pursued the Midianites.
[Judges] [7]:[24] Gideon also sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down against Midian and seize the waters ahead of them as far as Beth Barah, and the Jordan as well." So all the men of Ephraim were called out, and they seized the waters as far as Beth Barah, and the Jordan.
[Judges] [7]:[25] They captured the two Midianite commanders, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb, and they pursued the Midianites. Then they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan.
[Judges] [8]:[1] The men of Ephraim said to Gideon, "Why have you treated us like this? Why didn't you call us when you went to fight against Midian?" And they quarreled with him bitterly.
[Judges] [8]:[2] But he answered them, "What have I accomplished compared to you? Aren't Ephraim's gleanings better than Abiezer's whole harvest?
[Judges] [8]:[3] God gave the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, into your hands. What was I able to do compared to you?" When he said this, their anger against him subsided.
[Judges] [8]:[4] Gideon came to the Jordan and crossed over, he and the three hundred men with him, exhausted yet still in pursuit.
[Judges] [8]:[5] He said to the men of Succoth, "Please give some loaves of bread to the men who are following me, for they are exhausted, and I am pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."
[Judges] [8]:[6] But the officials of Succoth said, "Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your grasp, that we should give bread to your army?"
[Judges] [8]:[7] Gideon replied, "Very well. When the LORD has given Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will thresh your flesh with desert thorns and briers."
[Judges] [8]:[8] From there he went up to Penuel and made the same request of them, and the men of Penuel answered him just as the men of Succoth had.
[Judges] [8]:[9] So he said to the men of Penuel as well, "When I return in peace, I will tear down this tower."
[Judges] [8]:[10] Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their armies, about fifteen thousand men, all who were left of the entire army of the people of the East; a hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had already fallen.
[Judges] [8]:[11] Gideon went up by the route of the tent dwellers east of Nobah and Jogbehah and attacked the army, catching it off guard.
[Judges] [8]:[12] Zebah and Zalmunna fled, but he pursued them and captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, throwing their whole army into panic.
[Judges] [8]:[13] Then Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle by the Pass of Heres.
[Judges] [8]:[14] He caught a young man from Succoth and questioned him, and the young man wrote down for him the names of the seventy-seven officials and elders of Succoth.
[Judges] [8]:[15] Then Gideon came to the men of Succoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, 'Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your grasp, that we should give bread to your exhausted men?'"
[Judges] [8]:[16] So he took the elders of the city, and with desert thorns and briers he punished the men of Succoth.
[Judges] [8]:[17] He also tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.
[Judges] [8]:[18] Then he asked Zebah and Zalmunna, "What sort of men did you kill at Tabor?" "Men like you," they answered, "each one with the bearing of a king's son."
[Judges] [8]:[19] He said, "They were my brothers, the sons of my own mother. As surely as the LORD lives, if you had spared them, I would not kill you."
[Judges] [8]:[20] Turning to Jether, his firstborn, he said, "Get up and kill them!" But the boy did not draw his sword; he was afraid, because he was still only a boy.
[Judges] [8]:[21] Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Get up and strike us down yourself. As the man is, so is his strength." So Gideon stood up and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments from their camels' necks.
[Judges] [8]:[22] The Israelites said to Gideon, "Rule over us—you, your son, and your grandson—for you have saved us from the hand of Midian."
[Judges] [8]:[23] But Gideon answered them, "I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you. The LORD will rule over you."
[Judges] [8]:[24] Then Gideon said, "I do have one request: that each of you give me an earring from your share of the plunder." (It was the custom of the Ishmaelites to wear gold earrings.)
[Judges] [8]:[25] "We will gladly give them," they answered. So they spread out a garment, and each man threw an earring from his plunder onto it.
[Judges] [8]:[26] The weight of the gold earrings he had asked for came to seventeen hundred shekels, not counting the crescent ornaments, the pendants, and the purple garments worn by the kings of Midian, or the chains that were on their camels' necks.
[Judges] [8]:[27] Gideon made the gold into an ephod, which he set up in his town, in Ophrah. And all Israel prostituted themselves by worshiping it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his household.
[Judges] [8]:[28] So Midian was subdued before the Israelites and lifted its head no more. And the land had peace for forty years, during the days of Gideon.
[Judges] [8]:[29] Jerubbaal son of Joash went back home and settled there.
[Judges] [8]:[30] Gideon had seventy sons of his own, for he had many wives.
[Judges] [8]:[31] His concubine, who lived in Shechem, also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.
[Judges] [8]:[32] Gideon son of Joash died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
[Judges] [8]:[33] No sooner had Gideon died than the Israelites turned back and prostituted themselves with the Baals, setting up Baal-Berith as their god.
[Judges] [8]:[34] They did not remember the LORD their God, who had rescued them from the hands of all their enemies on every side.
[Judges] [8]:[35] Nor did they show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal—Gideon—in keeping with all the good he had done for Israel.
[Judges] [9]:[1] Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem, to his mother's brothers, and said to them and to the whole clan of his mother's family,
[Judges] [9]:[2] "Ask all the leaders of Shechem this: Which is better for you—that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or that one man rule over you? Remember, I am your own flesh and blood."
[Judges] [9]:[3] When his mother's brothers repeated all this on his behalf to all the leaders of Shechem, their hearts inclined toward Abimelech, for they said, "He is our brother."
[Judges] [9]:[4] They gave him seventy pieces of silver from the temple of Baal-berith, and with it Abimelech hired worthless and reckless men, who followed him.
[Judges] [9]:[5] He went to his father's house at Ophrah and murdered his brothers, the seventy sons of Jerubbaal, on a single stone. Only Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, survived, because he hid himself.
[Judges] [9]:[6] Then all the leaders of Shechem and all Beth-millo gathered together and went and made Abimelech king by the oak of the pillar at Shechem.
[Judges] [9]:[7] When Jotham was told of it, he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim, raised his voice, and called out to them: "Listen to me, you leaders of Shechem, that God may listen to you!
[Judges] [9]:[8] Once the trees set out to anoint a king over themselves. They said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us.'
[Judges] [9]:[9] But the olive tree answered them, 'Should I give up my rich oil, by which God and men are honored, to go and sway over the trees?'
[Judges] [9]:[10] So the trees said to the fig tree, 'Come, you reign over us.'
[Judges] [9]:[11] But the fig tree answered them, 'Should I give up my sweetness and my good fruit, to go and sway over the trees?'
[Judges] [9]:[12] Then the trees said to the vine, 'Come, you reign over us.'
[Judges] [9]:[13] But the vine answered them, 'Should I give up my new wine, which gladdens God and men, to go and sway over the trees?'
[Judges] [9]:[14] Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, 'Come, you reign over us.'
[Judges] [9]:[15] And the thornbush said to the trees, 'If you are truly anointing me king over you, then come and take refuge in my shade; but if not, let fire come out of the thornbush and devour the cedars of Lebanon.'
[Judges] [9]:[16] Now then, if you have acted in good faith and with integrity in making Abimelech king, if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house and treated him as his deeds deserved—
[Judges] [9]:[17] for my father fought for you, risked his life, and rescued you from the hand of Midian,
[Judges] [9]:[18] but today you have risen against my father's house, murdered his sons, seventy men, on a single stone, and made Abimelech, the son of his slave woman, king over the leaders of Shechem because he is your brother—
[Judges] [9]:[19] if, then, you have acted in good faith and with integrity toward Jerubbaal and his house this day, may you rejoice in Abimelech, and may he rejoice in you too.
[Judges] [9]:[20] But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and devour the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo, and let fire come out from the leaders of Shechem and from Beth-millo and devour Abimelech."
[Judges] [9]:[21] Then Jotham slipped away and fled to Beer, and he settled there, out of reach of his brother Abimelech.
[Judges] [9]:[22] Abimelech held sway over Israel for three years.
[Judges] [9]:[23] Then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech.
[Judges] [9]:[24] This happened so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might be avenged, and their blood laid on their brother Abimelech, who had killed them, and on the leaders of Shechem, who had strengthened his hands to murder his brothers.
[Judges] [9]:[25] The leaders of Shechem set men in ambush against him on the mountaintops, and they robbed everyone who passed by them on the road. And Abimelech was told of it.
[Judges] [9]:[26] Now Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers and moved into Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem put their trust in him.
[Judges] [9]:[27] They went out into the fields, gathered the grapes from their vineyards, trod them, and held a festival. Then they entered the temple of their god, ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.
[Judges] [9]:[28] And Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, with Zebul as his deputy? Serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem! Why should we serve him?
[Judges] [9]:[29] If only this people were under my command, I would get rid of Abimelech!" And he said to Abimelech, "Muster your army and come out!"
[Judges] [9]:[30] When Zebul, the ruler of the city, heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, his anger burned.
[Judges] [9]:[31] He sent messengers secretly to Abimelech, saying, "Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem, and they are stirring up the city against you.
[Judges] [9]:[32] Now then, set out by night, you and the troops with you, and lie in wait in the fields.
[Judges] [9]:[33] In the morning, at sunrise, set out early and sweep down on the city. And when Gaal and the men with him come out against you, do to him whatever your hand finds to do.
[Judges] [9]:[34] So Abimelech and all the troops with him set out by night, and they lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.
[Judges] [9]:[35] When Gaal son of Ebed came out and stood at the entrance of the city gate, Abimelech and the troops with him rose from the ambush.
[Judges] [9]:[36] Gaal saw the troops and said to Zebul, "Look, troops are coming down from the mountaintops!" But Zebul said to him, "You are seeing the shadows of the mountains as if they were men."
[Judges] [9]:[37] Gaal spoke up again, "Look, men are coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming by way of the Diviners' Oak."
[Judges] [9]:[38] Then Zebul said to him, "Where is your big talk now? You said, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?' Are these not the men you despised? Go out now and fight them!"
[Judges] [9]:[39] So Gaal went out at the head of the leaders of Shechem and fought against Abimelech.
[Judges] [9]:[40] Abimelech chased him, and he fled before him, and many fell slain all the way to the entrance of the gate.
[Judges] [9]:[41] Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers so they could not live in Shechem.
[Judges] [9]:[42] The next day the people went out into the fields, and Abimelech was told of it.
[Judges] [9]:[43] He took his men, divided them into three companies, and lay in wait in the fields. When he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose against them and struck them down.
[Judges] [9]:[44] Abimelech and the company with him rushed forward and took their stand at the entrance of the city gate, while the other two companies charged all who were in the fields and struck them down.
[Judges] [9]:[45] All that day Abimelech fought against the city. He captured it and killed the people in it; he tore the city down and sowed it with salt.
[Judges] [9]:[46] When all the leaders of the Tower of Shechem heard of it, they went into the stronghold of the temple of El-berith.
[Judges] [9]:[47] Abimelech was told that all the leaders of the Tower of Shechem had gathered there.
[Judges] [9]:[48] So Abimelech went up Mount Zalmon with all his men. He took an axe in his hand, cut off a branch from the trees, lifted it, and laid it on his shoulder. Then he said to the men with him, "Hurry and do what you have seen me do!"
[Judges] [9]:[49] So each of them cut a branch too and followed Abimelech. They piled the branches against the stronghold and set it on fire over those inside, so that all the people of the Tower of Shechem died as well—about a thousand men and women.
[Judges] [9]:[50] Then Abimelech went to Thebez, laid siege to it, and captured it.
[Judges] [9]:[51] But there was a strong tower inside the city, and all the men and women, all the leading citizens, fled to it. They shut themselves in and went up on the roof of the tower.
[Judges] [9]:[52] Abimelech came to the tower and attacked it, and he approached the entrance of the tower to set it on fire.
[Judges] [9]:[53] But a woman threw an upper millstone down on Abimelech's head and crushed his skull.
[Judges] [9]:[54] He quickly called his young armor-bearer and said to him, "Draw your sword and kill me, so they cannot say of me, 'A woman killed him.'" So the young man ran him through, and he died.
[Judges] [9]:[55] When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they all went home.
[Judges] [9]:[56] So God repaid the evil that Abimelech had done to his father in murdering his seventy brothers,
[Judges] [9]:[57] and God brought all the evil of the men of Shechem back on their own heads. The curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.
[Judges] [10]:[1] After Abimelech, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, rose up to deliver Israel. He lived in Shamir, in the hill country of Ephraim.
[Judges] [10]:[2] He judged Israel twenty-three years, and then he died and was buried in Shamir.
[Judges] [10]:[3] After him rose Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel twenty-two years.
[Judges] [10]:[4] He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty towns in the land of Gilead, which to this day are called Havvoth-jair.*
[Judges] [10]:[5] Then Jair died and was buried in Kamon.
[Judges] [10]:[6] Again the Israelites did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. They served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the Ammonites, and the gods of the Philistines. They abandoned the LORD and no longer served him.
[Judges] [10]:[7] So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hands of the Philistines and the Ammonites.
[Judges] [10]:[8] That year they shattered and crushed the Israelites, and for eighteen years they oppressed all the Israelites beyond the Jordan, in the land of the Amorites in Gilead.
[Judges] [10]:[9] The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to make war on Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, and Israel was in dire distress.
[Judges] [10]:[10] Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD: "We have sinned against you. We have abandoned our God and served the Baals."
[Judges] [10]:[11] And the LORD said to the Israelites: "Did I not save you from Egypt, from the Amorites, from the Ammonites, and from the Philistines?
[Judges] [10]:[12] When the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites oppressed you, and you cried out to me, I saved you from their hand.
[Judges] [10]:[13] But you have abandoned me and served other gods. Therefore I will deliver you no more.
[Judges] [10]:[14] Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen. Let them save you in your time of distress."
[Judges] [10]:[15] But the Israelites said to the LORD, "We have sinned. Do to us whatever seems good to you—only deliver us this day, we beg you."
[Judges] [10]:[16] So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD, and he could no longer bear Israel's misery.
[Judges] [10]:[17] The Ammonites were called to arms and camped in Gilead, and the Israelites assembled and camped at Mizpah.
[Judges] [10]:[18] The people, the leaders of Gilead, said to one another, "Whoever takes the lead in fighting the Ammonites will be head over all who live in Gilead."
[Judges] [11]:[1] Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty warrior, but he was the son of a prostitute. Gilead was his father.
[Judges] [11]:[2] Gilead's wife also bore him sons, and when her sons grew up, they drove Jephthah out. "You will inherit nothing in our father's house," they told him, "for you are the son of another woman."
[Judges] [11]:[3] So Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob. There worthless men gathered around him and went out with him.
[Judges] [11]:[4] Some time later the Ammonites made war against Israel.
[Judges] [11]:[5] When the Ammonites attacked Israel, the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah back from the land of Tob.
[Judges] [11]:[6] "Come," they said to him, "be our commander, so we can fight the Ammonites."
