[Judges] [11]:[7] But Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "Weren't you the ones who hated me and drove me out of my father's house? Why do you come to me now, when you are in trouble?"
[Judges] [11]:[8] The elders of Gilead answered, "That is why we have turned to you now. Come with us and fight the Ammonites, and you shall be head over all of us who live in Gilead."
[Judges] [11]:[9] Jephthah said to them, "If you bring me back to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gives them over to me, then I will be your head."
[Judges] [11]:[10] The elders of Gilead replied, "The LORD is our witness: we will surely do as you say."
[Judges] [11]:[11] So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him their head and commander. And Jephthah repeated all his words before the LORD at Mizpah.
[Judges] [11]:[12] Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites, asking, "What do you have against me, that you have come to make war in my land?"
[Judges] [11]:[13] The king of the Ammonites answered Jephthah's messengers, "When Israel came up out of Egypt, they took my land from the Arnon to the Jabbok and to the Jordan. Now give those lands back peaceably."
[Judges] [11]:[14] Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites once again,
[Judges] [11]:[15] saying to him: "This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.
[Judges] [11]:[16] When they came up from Egypt, Israel traveled through the wilderness to the Red Sea and came to Kadesh.
[Judges] [11]:[17] Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Please let us pass through your land.' But the king of Edom would not listen. They also sent to the king of Moab, and he refused. So Israel stayed at Kadesh.
[Judges] [11]:[18] Then they journeyed through the wilderness, went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and came to the east side of the land of Moab, where they camped on the far side of the Arnon. They did not enter the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was Moab's border.
[Judges] [11]:[19] Israel then sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, 'Please let us pass through your land to our own place.'
[Judges] [11]:[20] But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory. He mustered all his troops, camped at Jahaz, and fought against Israel.
[Judges] [11]:[21] And the LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his troops into Israel's hand, and they struck them down. So Israel took possession of the whole land of the Amorites who lived in that country.
[Judges] [11]:[22] They took possession of all Amorite territory, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness to the Jordan.
[Judges] [11]:[23] Now then, the LORD, the God of Israel, drove out the Amorites before his people Israel—and you would take possession of it?
[Judges] [11]:[24] Will you not take possession of whatever Chemosh your god gives you? So we will take possession of whatever the LORD our God has driven out before us.
[Judges] [11]:[25] Are you any better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever quarrel with Israel or go to war against them?
[Judges] [11]:[26] For three hundred years Israel has lived in Heshbon and its villages, in Aroer and its villages, and in all the towns along the Arnon. Why did you not reclaim them in all that time?
[Judges] [11]:[27] I have not wronged you, but you are doing me wrong by making war on me. Let the LORD, the Judge, decide today between the Israelites and the Ammonites."
[Judges] [11]:[28] But the king of the Ammonites paid no attention to the message Jephthah sent him.
[Judges] [11]:[29] Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah. He crossed through Gilead and Manasseh, passed by Mizpah of Gilead, and from there advanced against the Ammonites.
[Judges] [11]:[30] And Jephthah made a vow to the LORD: "If you give the Ammonites into my hand,
[Judges] [11]:[31] then whoever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me when I return safely from the Ammonites shall belong to the LORD, and I will offer him up as a burnt offering.
[Judges] [11]:[32] So Jephthah crossed over to fight the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them into his hand.
[Judges] [11]:[33] He struck them down from Aroer to the outskirts of Minnith—twenty towns—and as far as Abel Keramim. It was a crushing blow, and the Ammonites were subdued before the Israelites.
[Judges] [11]:[34] When Jephthah came home to Mizpah, there was his daughter, coming out to meet him with tambourines and dancing. She was his only child; he had no other son or daughter.
[Judges] [11]:[35] When he saw her, he tore his clothes and cried, "Oh, my daughter! You have brought me to my knees; you have become the cause of my ruin. I have opened my mouth to the LORD and I cannot take it back."
[Judges] [11]:[36] She said to him, "My father, you have opened your mouth to the LORD. Do to me as you have vowed, now that the LORD has avenged you on your enemies, the Ammonites.
[Judges] [11]:[37] She said to her father, "Grant me this one request: give me two months to go and wander the hills with my friends and weep, because I will never marry."
[Judges] [11]:[38] "Go," he said, and he let her go for two months. She and her friends went into the hills and wept because she would never marry.
[Judges] [11]:[39] After the two months she returned to her father, and he did to her as he had vowed. She had never known a man. And so it became a custom in Israel
[Judges] [11]:[40] that year after year the young women of Israel go out for four days to commemorate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite.[^1] [^1]: Or "to lament for"; the Hebrew verb is rare and may mean either to recount or to mourn.
[Judges] [12]:[1] The men of Ephraim were mustered, and they crossed over to Zaphon and said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We will burn your house down over your head!"
[Judges] [12]:[2] Jephthah answered them, "I and my people were locked in a bitter struggle with the Ammonites. I called you, but you did not rescue me from their hand.
[Judges] [12]:[3] When I saw that you would not save me, I took my life in my own hands and crossed over against the Ammonites, and the LORD gave them into my hand. So why have you come up against me today to fight me?"
[Judges] [12]:[4] Then Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought Ephraim, and the men of Gilead struck Ephraim down, because they had said, "You Gileadites are nothing but fugitives from Ephraim, living in the midst of Ephraim and Manasseh."
[Judges] [12]:[5] The Gileadites seized the fords of the Jordan against Ephraim, and whenever an Ephraimite fugitive said, "Let me cross over," the men of Gilead would ask him, "Are you an Ephraimite?" If he said, "No,"
[Judges] [12]:[6] they would say to him, "Then say 'Shibboleth.'" And he would say, "Sibboleth," for he could not pronounce it correctly. Then they would seize him and kill him at the fords of the Jordan. Forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell at that time.
[Judges] [12]:[7] Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in one of the towns of Gilead.
[Judges] [12]:[8] After him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.
[Judges] [12]:[9] He had thirty sons, and thirty daughters whom he gave in marriage, and he brought in thirty daughters for his sons from elsewhere. He judged Israel seven years.
[Judges] [12]:[10] Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
[Judges] [12]:[11] After him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel, and he judged Israel ten years.
[Judges] [12]:[12] Then Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried at Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
[Judges] [12]:[13] After him Abdon son of Hillel, from Pirathon, judged Israel.
[Judges] [12]:[14] He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys. He judged Israel eight years.
[Judges] [12]:[15] Then Abdon son of Hillel, from Pirathon, died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.
[Judges] [13]:[1] Again the Israelites did what was evil in the LORD's sight, and the LORD handed them over to the Philistines for forty years.
[Judges] [13]:[2] There was a man from Zorah, of the clan of Dan, whose name was Manoah. His wife was barren and had borne no children.
[Judges] [13]:[3] The angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, "You are barren and have borne no children, but now you will conceive and give birth to a son.
[Judges] [13]:[4] So be careful: drink no wine or strong drink, and eat nothing unclean,
[Judges] [13]:[5] for you are going to conceive and give birth to a son. No razor is to touch his head, for the boy will be a Nazirite of God from birth, and he will begin to deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines."
[Judges] [13]:[6] The woman went and told her husband, "A man of God came to me. He looked like an angel of God—awesome to behold. I did not ask him where he came from, and he did not tell me his name.
[Judges] [13]:[7] But he said to me, 'You are going to conceive and give birth to a son. Now drink no wine or strong drink, and eat nothing unclean, for the boy will be a Nazirite of God from birth until the day he dies.'"
[Judges] [13]:[8] Then Manoah pleaded with the LORD: "Please, Lord, let the man of God you sent come to us again and teach us what we are to do for the boy who will be born."
[Judges] [13]:[9] God listened to Manoah, and the angel of God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field. Her husband Manoah was not with her.
[Judges] [13]:[10] The woman hurried and ran to tell her husband, "Look, the man who came to me the other day has appeared to me again!"
[Judges] [13]:[11] Manoah got up and followed his wife. When he came to the man, he asked him, "Are you the man who spoke to my wife?" "I am," he said.
[Judges] [13]:[12] Then Manoah said, "When your words come true, how are we to raise the boy? What is he to do?"
[Judges] [13]:[13] The angel of the LORD answered Manoah, "Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her.
[Judges] [13]:[14] She is to eat nothing that comes from the grapevine, and she must drink no wine or strong drink and eat nothing unclean. She must observe everything I commanded her."
[Judges] [13]:[15] Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "Please stay while we prepare a young goat for you."
[Judges] [13]:[16] The angel of the LORD replied, "Even if I stay, I will not eat your food. But if you want to prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD." Manoah did not know that he was the angel of the LORD.
[Judges] [13]:[17] Then Manoah asked the angel of the LORD, "What is your name, so that we may honor you when your word comes true?"
[Judges] [13]:[18] The angel of the LORD said to him, "Why do you ask my name? It is too wonderful for you to know."
[Judges] [13]:[19] So Manoah took the young goat and the grain offering and offered them on the rock to the LORD. And the LORD did a wondrous thing while Manoah and his wife looked on.
[Judges] [13]:[20] As the flame rose from the altar toward heaven, the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar. When Manoah and his wife saw it, they fell facedown to the ground.
[Judges] [13]:[21] The angel of the LORD did not appear again to Manoah and his wife. Then Manoah realized that it had been the angel of the LORD.
[Judges] [13]:[22] "We are surely going to die," he said to his wife, "for we have seen God!"
[Judges] [13]:[23] But his wife answered, "If the LORD had wanted to kill us, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and a grain offering from our hands, nor would he have shown us all this or told us such things now."
[Judges] [13]:[24] The woman gave birth to a son and named him Samson. The boy grew, and the LORD blessed him.
[Judges] [13]:[25] And the Spirit of the LORD began to stir in him at Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
[Judges] [14]:[1] Samson went down to Timnah, and there he saw a woman, one of the Philistine daughters.
[Judges] [14]:[2] He came back up and told his father and mother, "I have seen a woman in Timnah, one of the Philistine daughters. Now get her for me as my wife."
[Judges] [14]:[3] But his father and mother said to him, "Is there no woman among the daughters of your own kin or among all my people, that you must go and take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?" Samson answered his father, "Get her for me, for she is the right one in my eyes."
[Judges] [14]:[4] His father and mother did not know that this was from the LORD, who was seeking an occasion against the Philistines; for at that time the Philistines ruled over Israel.
[Judges] [14]:[5] So Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother. When they came to the vineyards of Timnah, a young lion came roaring toward him.
[Judges] [14]:[6] The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him, and he tore the lion apart with his bare hands as one tears apart a young goat. But he did not tell his father or mother what he had done.
[Judges] [14]:[7] Then he went on down and spoke with the woman, and she pleased Samson.
[Judges] [14]:[8] Some time later, when he went back to marry her, he turned aside to look at the carcass of the lion, and there in it was a swarm of bees and honey.
[Judges] [14]:[9] He scooped the honey into his hands and ate as he went along. When he came to his father and mother, he gave them some, and they ate it too; but he did not tell them that he had taken the honey from the carcass of the lion.
[Judges] [14]:[10] His father went down to the woman, and Samson gave a feast there, as the young men customarily did.
[Judges] [14]:[11] When the people saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him.
[Judges] [14]:[12] Samson said to them, "Let me put a riddle to you. If you can solve it and tell me the answer within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.
[Judges] [14]:[13] But if you cannot tell me the answer, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes." "Tell us your riddle," they said. "Let us hear it."
[Judges] [14]:[14] So he said to them: "Out of the eater came something to eat; out of the strong came something sweet." For three days they could not solve it.
[Judges] [14]:[15] On the seventh day they said to Samson's wife, "Coax your husband into explaining the riddle to us, or we will burn you and your father's household to death. Did you invite us here to rob us? Is that not so?"
[Judges] [14]:[16] So Samson's wife wept before him and said, "You only hate me; you do not love me. You have put a riddle to my people, but you have not told me the answer." "Look," he replied, "I have not told my own father or mother—why should I tell you?"
[Judges] [14]:[17] She wept before him all seven days of the feast, and on the seventh day he finally told her, because she kept pressing him. Then she told the riddle to her people.
[Judges] [14]:[18] Before sunset on the seventh day the men of the town said to him: "What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?" And he said to them, "If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have solved my riddle."
[Judges] [14]:[19] Then the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him. He went down to Ashkelon, struck down thirty of their men, stripped them of their garments, and gave the clothes to those who had explained the riddle. Burning with anger, he went up to his father's house.
[Judges] [14]:[20] And Samson's wife was given to the companion who had attended him.
[Judges] [15]:[1] Some time later, during the wheat harvest, Samson went to visit his wife, bringing a young goat. He said, "I'm going in to my wife, into her room." But her father would not let him in.
[Judges] [15]:[2] "I was sure you hated her," her father said, "so I gave her to your best man. Isn't her younger sister better than she is? Take her instead."
[Judges] [15]:[3] But Samson said to them, "This time I have a right to get even with the Philistines. I am going to do them real harm."
[Judges] [15]:[4] So Samson went out and caught three hundred foxes. He took torches, tied the foxes tail to tail, and fastened a torch between each pair of tails.
[Judges] [15]:[5] Then he lit the torches and turned the foxes loose in the standing grain of the Philistines. He burned the stacked sheaves and the standing grain, and the vineyards and olive groves as well.
[Judges] [15]:[6] The Philistines asked, "Who did this?" And they were told, "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because his wife was taken from him and given to his best man." So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death.
[Judges] [15]:[7] Samson said to them, "Since you have acted like this, I swear I will not stop until I have taken my revenge on you."
[Judges] [15]:[8] He struck them down, hip and thigh, with great slaughter. Then he went down and stayed in the cleft of the rock of Etam.
[Judges] [15]:[9] The Philistines came up and camped in Judah, spreading out near Lehi.
[Judges] [15]:[10] The men of Judah asked, "Why have you come up against us?" They answered, "We have come to take Samson prisoner, to do to him as he did to us."
[Judges] [15]:[11] Then three thousand men of Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam and said to Samson, "Don't you know that the Philistines rule over us? What is this you have done to us?" He answered, "I did to them what they did to me."
[Judges] [15]:[12] They said, "We have come down to tie you up and hand you over to the Philistines." Samson said, "Swear to me that you yourselves will not kill me."
[Judges] [15]:[13] "We will not," they said. "We will only tie you up and hand you over to them. We will certainly not kill you." So they bound him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock.
[Judges] [15]:[14] As he came to Lehi, the Philistines came shouting to meet him. Then the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him. The ropes on his arms became like flax that has burned in the fire, and the bonds fell away from his hands.
[Judges] [15]:[15] Finding a fresh jawbone of a donkey, he reached out, took it, and struck down a thousand men.
[Judges] [15]:[16] Then Samson said: "With the jawbone of a donkey, heaps upon heaps! With the jawbone of a donkey I have struck down a thousand men." [Footnote: In Hebrew the word for "donkey" and the word for "heap" sound alike, making a play on words.]
[Judges] [15]:[17] When he had finished speaking, he threw the jawbone from his hand, and the place was called Ramath Lehi.
[Judges] [15]:[18] He was very thirsty, so he called out to the LORD: "You have given your servant this great victory. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?"
[Judges] [15]:[19] Then God split open the hollow place at Lehi, and water came out of it. Samson drank, his strength returned, and he revived. That is why the spring is called En Hakkore, and it is at Lehi to this day.
[Judges] [15]:[20] Samson judged Israel for twenty years in the days of the Philistines.
[Judges] [16]:[1] Samson went to Gaza, and there he saw a prostitute and went in to her.
[Judges] [16]:[2] Word came to the men of Gaza: "Samson is here!" So they surrounded the place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate. All night they kept still, saying, "At dawn we will kill him."
[Judges] [16]:[3] But Samson lay there only until midnight. At midnight he got up, took hold of the doors of the city gate and the two posts, tore them loose along with the bar, hoisted them onto his shoulders, and carried them to the top of the hill that faces Hebron.
[Judges] [16]:[4] Some time later he fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.
[Judges] [16]:[5] The rulers of the Philistines came to her and said, "Coax him and find out where his great strength comes from and how we can overpower him, so we can tie him up and subdue him. Each of us will give you eleven hundred pieces of silver."
[Judges] [16]:[6] So Delilah said to Samson, "Tell me, where does your great strength come from, and how could you be tied up and subdued?"
[Judges] [16]:[7] Samson answered her, "If they tie me with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, I will become weak and be like any other man."
[Judges] [16]:[8] So the rulers of the Philistines brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she tied him with them.
[Judges] [16]:[9] With men lying in wait in the inner room, she called out to him, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" But he snapped the bowstrings as easily as a strand of yarn snaps when it touches fire. So the secret of his strength was not discovered.
[Judges] [16]:[10] Then Delilah said to Samson, "Look, you have made a fool of me and told me lies. Now tell me how you can be tied up."
[Judges] [16]:[11] He said to her, "If they tie me tight with new ropes that have never been used, I will become weak and be like any other man."
[Judges] [16]:[12] So Delilah took new ropes and tied him with them, and with men lying in wait in the inner room she called out to him, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" But he snapped the ropes off his arms like thread.
[Judges] [16]:[13] He said to her, "If you weave the seven braids of my head into the fabric on the loom." [Footnote: The Hebrew sentence breaks off here; ancient versions continue, "then I will become weak and be like any other man."]
[Judges] [16]:[14] So she fastened them with the pin and called out to him, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" He woke from his sleep and tore away the loom pin along with the woven fabric.
[Judges] [16]:[15] Then she said to him, "How can you say, 'I love you,' when your heart is not with me? Three times now you have made a fool of me and have not told me where your great strength comes from."
[Judges] [16]:[16] She pressed him with her words day after day until he was worn out to the point of death.
[Judges] [16]:[17] So he told her everything in his heart: "No razor has ever touched my head, for I have been a Nazirite dedicated to God from my mother's womb. If I were shaved, my strength would leave me, and I would become weak and be like any other man."
[Judges] [16]:[18] When Delilah saw that he had told her everything in his heart, she sent word to the rulers of the Philistines: "Come up once more, for he has told me everything in his heart." So the rulers of the Philistines came to her, bringing the silver with them.
[Judges] [16]:[19] She lulled him to sleep on her lap, then called for a man, and she herself shaved off the seven braids of his head. Then she began to torment him, and his strength left him.
[Judges] [16]:[20] Then she called, "Samson, the Philistines are upon you!" He woke from his sleep and thought, "I will go out as before and shake myself free." But he did not know that the LORD had left him.
[Judges] [16]:[21] The Philistines seized him, gouged out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza. They bound him with bronze shackles and set him to grinding grain in the prison.
[Judges] [16]:[22] But the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved.
[Judges] [16]:[23] Now the rulers of the Philistines gathered to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon and to celebrate, saying, "Our god has delivered Samson our enemy into our hands."
[Judges] [16]:[24] When the people saw him, they praised their god, saying, "Our god has delivered into our hands our enemy, the one who ravaged our land and multiplied our dead."
[Judges] [16]:[25] And when their hearts were merry, they said, "Bring out Samson to entertain us." So they called Samson from the prison, and he performed for them. They stood him between the pillars.
[Judges] [16]:[26] Samson said to the boy who was holding his hand, "Let go of me and let me feel the pillars that hold up the temple, so I can lean against them."
[Judges] [16]:[27] The temple was crowded with men and women; all the rulers of the Philistines were there, and on the roof were about three thousand men and women watching Samson perform.
[Judges] [16]:[28] Then Samson called out to the LORD: "Sovereign LORD, remember me. Please, God, strengthen me just once more, and let me with one blow take revenge on the Philistines for my two eyes."
[Judges] [16]:[29] Then Samson braced himself against the two central pillars on which the temple stood, his right hand on one and his left hand on the other,
[Judges] [16]:[30] And Samson said, "Let me die with the Philistines!" He pushed with all his might, and the temple came down on the rulers and all the people in it. So he killed many more when he died than while he lived.
[Judges] [16]:[31] Then his brothers and his father's whole family came down, took him up, and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. He had judged Israel twenty years.
[Judges] [17]:[1] There was a man from the hill country of Ephraim whose name was Micah.
[Judges] [17]:[2] He said to his mother, "The eleven hundred pieces of silver that were taken from you—about which you uttered a curse and spoke it in my hearing—look, the silver is with me; I took it." His mother said, "May the LORD bless you, my son."
[Judges] [17]:[3] He returned the eleven hundred pieces of silver to his mother, and she said, "I solemnly dedicate this silver to the LORD, from my own hand, for my son, to make a carved image and a cast idol. Now I give it back to you."
[Judges] [17]:[4] So he returned the silver to his mother, and she took two hundred pieces of it and gave them to a silversmith, who made them into a carved image and a cast idol. And it was placed in Micah's house.
[Judges] [17]:[5] This man Micah had a shrine,* and he made an ephod and household idols, and he installed one of his sons to serve him as priest. [*Footnote: Hebrew "a house of God" (or "of gods").]
[Judges] [17]:[6] In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did as he saw fit.
[Judges] [17]:[7] Now there was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah, of the clan of Judah. He was a Levite, and he was staying there.
[Judges] [17]:[8] This man left the town of Bethlehem in Judah to find some other place to live. On his way he came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah.
[Judges] [17]:[9] Micah asked him, "Where do you come from?" He answered, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am looking for a place to live."
[Judges] [17]:[10] Then Micah said to him, "Stay with me and be my father and priest, and I will give you ten pieces of silver a year, along with a set of clothes and your food." So the Levite went in.
[Judges] [17]:[11] The Levite agreed to stay with the man, and the young man became like one of his own sons to him.
[Judges] [17]:[12] Micah installed the Levite, and the young man became his priest and lived in his house.
[Judges] [17]:[13] Then Micah said, "Now I know that the LORD will prosper me, since I have a Levite as my priest."
[Judges] [18]:[1] In those days there was no king in Israel. And in those days the tribe of the Danites was looking for an inheritance to settle in, because down to that day no inheritance had fallen to them among the tribes of Israel.
[Judges] [18]:[2] So the Danites sent out five men from their clan, chosen from among them all, capable men from Zorah and Eshtaol, to scout the land and explore it. They told them, "Go, explore the land." The men came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and spent the night there.
[Judges] [18]:[3] While they were near Micah's house, they recognized the voice of the young Levite. They turned aside there and asked him, "Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? What is your business here?"
[Judges] [18]:[4] He told them, "Micah has done such and such for me. He hired me, and I have become his priest."
[Judges] [18]:[5] Then they said to him, "Please inquire of God, so we may know whether the journey we are making will succeed."
[Judges] [18]:[6] The priest answered them, "Go in peace. The journey you are making is under the LORD's eye."
[Judges] [18]:[7] So the five men went on and came to Laish. They saw that the people there lived in safety, in the manner of the Sidonians, quiet and unsuspecting; there was no one in the land who held power to harass them. They were far from the Sidonians and had no dealings with anyone.
[Judges] [18]:[8] When they came back to their kinsmen at Zorah and Eshtaol, their kinsmen asked them, "What do you report?"
[Judges] [18]:[9] They said, "Get up, let us attack them! We have seen the land, and it is very good. Are you going to sit still? Do not hesitate to go and take possession of the land.
[Judges] [18]:[10] When you get there, you will come to an unsuspecting people, and the land is wide open. God has given it into your hands—a place where nothing on earth is lacking."
[Judges] [18]:[11] So six hundred men from the clan of the Danites, armed with weapons of war, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol.
[Judges] [18]:[12] They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. That is why the place is called Mahaneh-dan to this day; it lies west of Kiriath-jearim.
[Judges] [18]:[13] From there they passed on to the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah's house.
[Judges] [18]:[14] Then the five men who had gone to scout out the land of Laish spoke up and said to their kinsmen, "Do you know that in these houses there is an ephod, household gods, a carved image, and a cast idol? Now consider what you should do."
[Judges] [18]:[15] So they turned aside there and came to the house of the young Levite at Micah's place, and greeted him.
[Judges] [18]:[16] Meanwhile the six hundred Danites, armed with their weapons of war, stood at the entrance of the gate.
[Judges] [18]:[17] The five men who had gone to scout out the land went up, entered the house, and took the carved image, the ephod, the household gods, and the cast idol, while the priest stood at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men armed with weapons of war.
[Judges] [18]:[18] When these men went into Micah's house and took the carved image, the ephod, the household gods, and the cast idol, the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"
[Judges] [18]:[19] They said to him, "Be quiet. Put your hand over your mouth and come with us. Be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be priest to the household of one man, or to be priest to a tribe and a clan in Israel?"
[Judges] [18]:[20] This pleased the priest. He took the ephod, the household gods, and the carved image, and went along with the people.
[Judges] [18]:[21] They turned and set out, placing the children, the livestock, and their goods ahead of them.
[Judges] [18]:[22] When they were some distance from Micah's house, the men in the houses near Micah's house were called together, and they overtook the Danites.
[Judges] [18]:[23] They shouted after them, and the Danites turned and said to Micah, "What is the matter with you, that you have called out your men?"
[Judges] [18]:[24] He answered, "You took the gods I made, and my priest, and went away. What do I have left? How can you ask me, 'What is the matter with you?'"
[Judges] [18]:[25] The Danites said to him, "Don't raise your voice against us, or angry men will attack you, and you will lose your life and the lives of your household."
[Judges] [18]:[26] So the Danites went on their way, and Micah, seeing that they were too strong for him, turned and went back home.
[Judges] [18]:[27] They took what Micah had made, along with his priest, and came to Laish, to a people quiet and unsuspecting. They struck them down with the sword and burned the city.
[Judges] [18]:[28] There was no one to rescue them, for the city was far from Sidon and they had no dealings with anyone. It lay in the valley near Beth-rehob. The Danites rebuilt the city and settled there.
[Judges] [18]:[29] They named it Dan, after their ancestor Dan, who was born to Israel; but the city's name had formerly been Laish.
[Judges] [18]:[30] The Danites set up the carved image for themselves, and Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Manasseh,[^1] and his sons were priests to the tribe of Dan until the day the land went into exile. [^1]: In the Hebrew text the name is written with a raised letter, and many ancient witnesses read "Moses" here.
[Judges] [18]:[31] So they set up for themselves Micah's carved image, the one he had made, and it stood there as long as the house of God was at Shiloh.
[Judges] [19]:[1] In those days, when there was no king in Israel, a certain Levite living in the remote hill country of Ephraim took for himself a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.
[Judges] [19]:[2] But his concubine was unfaithful to him and left him for her father's house in Bethlehem of Judah, and she stayed there four whole months.
[Judges] [19]:[3] Then her husband set out after her to speak tenderly to her and bring her back. He had his servant with him and a pair of donkeys. She brought him into her father's house, and when the young woman's father saw him, he welcomed him gladly.
[Judges] [19]:[4] His father-in-law, the young woman's father, pressed him to stay, so he remained with him three days; they ate and drank and spent the nights there.
[Judges] [19]:[5] On the fourth day they rose early in the morning, and the man got up to go. But the young woman's father said to his son-in-law, "Have a bite of bread to strengthen yourself, and then you can go."
[Judges] [19]:[6] So the two of them sat down and ate and drank together. Then the young woman's father said to the man, "Please, stay the night and enjoy yourself."
[Judges] [19]:[7] When the man got up to leave, his father-in-law urged him again, so he stayed the night there.
[Judges] [19]:[8] He rose early on the fifth morning to go, but the young woman's father said, "Strengthen yourself first, and wait until the day declines." So the two of them ate.
[Judges] [19]:[9] Then the man got up to go, he and his concubine and his servant, but his father-in-law, the young woman's father, said to him, "Look, the day is fading toward evening. Stay the night. See, the day is nearly over. Spend the night here and enjoy yourself. Tomorrow you can rise early for your journey and go home."
[Judges] [19]:[10] But the man would not stay the night. He got up and left, and came to a point opposite Jebus—that is, Jerusalem—with his pair of saddled donkeys and his concubine.
[Judges] [19]:[11] As they neared Jebus, the day was almost gone, and the servant said to his master, "Come, let us turn aside to this city of the Jebusites and spend the night there."
[Judges] [19]:[12] But his master said to him, "We will not turn aside into a foreign city where there are no Israelites. We will go on to Gibeah."
[Judges] [19]:[13] He said to his servant, "Come, let us reach one of these places and spend the night in Gibeah or Ramah."
[Judges] [19]:[14] So they went on their way, and the sun set on them as they came near Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.
[Judges] [19]:[15] They turned aside there to spend the night in Gibeah. He went in and sat down in the city square, but no one took them into his house for the night.
[Judges] [19]:[16] Then an old man came in from his work in the field at evening. He was from the hill country of Ephraim and was living in Gibeah, though the men of the place were Benjaminites.
[Judges] [19]:[17] He looked up and saw the traveler in the city square, and the old man asked, "Where are you going, and where do you come from?"
[Judges] [19]:[18] He answered him, "We are traveling from Bethlehem in Judah to the remote hill country of Ephraim. That is where I am from. I went to Bethlehem in Judah, and now I am going to the house of the LORD,* but no one has taken me into his house. [*Footnote: Some ancient witnesses read "to my house."]
[Judges] [19]:[19] We have straw and fodder for our donkeys, and bread and wine for myself, for your servant woman, and for the young man who is with your servants. We lack nothing."
[Judges] [19]:[20] "Peace to you," said the old man. "Let me take care of whatever you need—only do not spend the night in the square."
[Judges] [19]:[21] So he brought him into his house and fed the donkeys. Then they washed their feet and ate and drank.
[Judges] [19]:[22] While they were enjoying themselves, the men of the city—worthless men—surrounded the house, pounding on the door. They shouted to the old man who owned the house, "Bring out the man who came into your house, so we can have our way with him!"
[Judges] [19]:[23] The owner of the house went out to them and said, "No, my brothers, do not do such an evil thing. This man is a guest in my house; do not commit this outrage.
[Judges] [19]:[24] Here is my virgin daughter and his concubine. Let me bring them out. Violate them and do to them whatever you please, but do not commit such an outrage against this man."
[Judges] [19]:[25] But the men would not listen to him. So the man seized his concubine and pushed her out to them. They raped her and abused her all night until morning, and let her go as dawn was breaking.
[Judges] [19]:[26] At daybreak the woman came and collapsed at the door of the man's house where her master was, and lay there until it was light.
[Judges] [19]:[27] When her master got up in the morning and opened the doors of the house to go on his way, there lay his concubine at the doorway of the house, her hands on the threshold.
[Judges] [19]:[28] He said to her, "Get up, let us go," but there was no answer. So he put her on his donkey and set out for home.
[Judges] [19]:[29] When he reached his house, he took a knife, took hold of his concubine, cut her limb by limb into twelve pieces, and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel.
[Judges] [19]:[30] Everyone who saw it said, "Nothing like this has ever happened or been seen from the day the Israelites came up out of the land of Egypt until this day. Think about it, take counsel, and speak!"
[Judges] [20]:[1] Then all the Israelites came out, and the whole assembly gathered as one man before the LORD at Mizpah, from Dan to Beersheba, including the land of Gilead.
[Judges] [20]:[2] The leaders of all the people, of all the tribes of Israel, took their places in the assembly of the people of God—four hundred thousand men on foot, armed with swords.
[Judges] [20]:[3] Now the Benjaminites heard that the Israelites had gone up to Mizpah. And the Israelites said, "Tell us how this evil thing happened."
[Judges] [20]:[4] So the Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered: "I came to Gibeah in Benjamin with my concubine to spend the night.
[Judges] [20]:[5] During the night the citizens of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house, intending to kill me. They raped my concubine, and she died.
[Judges] [20]:[6] So I took my concubine, cut her in pieces, and sent her through every part of Israel's inheritance, because they had committed this outrage and disgrace in Israel.
[Judges] [20]:[7] Now then, all of you Israelites, speak up and give your verdict here and now."
[Judges] [20]:[8] All the people rose as one man and said, "None of us will go home to his tent; none of us will return to his house.
[Judges] [20]:[9] This is what we will do to Gibeah: we will go up against it as the lot directs.
[Judges] [20]:[10] We will take ten men out of every hundred from all the tribes of Israel, a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand, to gather provisions for the army. Then, when the army arrives at Gibeah in Benjamin, it can give them what they deserve for this outrage committed in Israel."
[Judges] [20]:[11] So all the men of Israel gathered against the city, united as one man.
[Judges] [20]:[12] The tribes of Israel sent men throughout all the clans of Benjamin, saying, "What is this evil that has been done among you?
[Judges] [20]:[13] Now hand over those worthless men of Gibeah so we can put them to death and purge this evil from Israel." But the Benjaminites would not listen to their fellow Israelites.
[Judges] [20]:[14] Instead, the Benjaminites came together from their towns to Gibeah to go to war against the Israelites.
[Judges] [20]:[15] That day the Benjaminites mustered from their towns twenty-six thousand swordsmen, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah, who mustered seven hundred choice men.
[Judges] [20]:[16] Among all these troops were seven hundred choice men who were left-handed, each of whom could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.
[Judges] [20]:[17] The Israelites, apart from Benjamin, mustered four hundred thousand swordsmen, all of them fighting men.
[Judges] [20]:[18] They set out and went up to Bethel and inquired of God. The Israelites asked, "Who of us is to go up first to fight against the Benjaminites?" The LORD replied, "Judah first."
[Judges] [20]:[19] The Israelites rose early the next morning and camped near Gibeah.
[Judges] [20]:[20] The men of Israel went out to fight Benjamin and drew up their battle lines against Gibeah.
[Judges] [20]:[21] The Benjaminites came out of Gibeah, and that day they laid twenty-two thousand men of Israel dead on the ground.
[Judges] [20]:[22] But the men of Israel encouraged one another and again took up their positions where they had stationed themselves the first day.
[Judges] [20]:[23] The Israelites went up and wept before the LORD until evening, and they inquired of the LORD, "Shall we go up again to fight against the Benjaminites, our brothers?" The LORD answered, "Go up against them."
[Judges] [20]:[24] So the Israelites advanced against Benjamin on the second day.
[Judges] [20]:[25] That second day, when Benjamin came out from Gibeah to meet them, they cut down another eighteen thousand Israelites, all of them armed with swords.
[Judges] [20]:[26] Then all the Israelites, the whole army, went up to Bethel, and there they sat weeping before the LORD. They fasted that day until evening and presented burnt offerings and fellowship offerings to the LORD.
[Judges] [20]:[27] And the Israelites inquired of the LORD—for in those days the ark of the covenant of God was there,
[Judges] [20]:[28] with Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, ministering before it—and they asked, "Shall we go out again to fight against the Benjaminites, our brothers, or shall we stop?" The LORD answered, "Go, for tomorrow I will give them into your hands."
[Judges] [20]:[29] Then Israel set an ambush around Gibeah.
[Judges] [20]:[30] On the third day the Israelites went up against the Benjaminites and took up positions against Gibeah as they had done before.
[Judges] [20]:[31] The Benjaminites came out to meet them and were drawn away from the city. They began to strike down the Israelites as before, killing about thirty of them out in the open, along the roads—one leading up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah.
[Judges] [20]:[32] The Benjaminites said, "We are defeating them as before." But the Israelites were saying, "Let us retreat and draw them away from the city to the roads."
[Judges] [20]:[33] All the men of Israel moved from their places and took up positions at Baal Tamar, and the Israelite ambush charged out from its place west of Geba.[^1] [^1]: The meaning of the Hebrew phrase is uncertain; it may read "from the clearing" or "from the meadows of Geba."
[Judges] [20]:[34] Ten thousand of the finest men from all Israel came up opposite Gibeah. The fighting was fierce, and Benjamin did not realize how close disaster was.
[Judges] [20]:[35] The LORD defeated Benjamin before Israel, and on that day the Israelites struck down twenty-five thousand one hundred Benjaminites, all armed with swords.
[Judges] [20]:[36] Then the Benjaminites saw that they were beaten. Now the men of Israel had given way before Benjamin, because they were relying on the ambush they had set near Gibeah.
[Judges] [20]:[37] The men in ambush rushed forward and swept into Gibeah; they spread out and put the whole city to the sword.
[Judges] [20]:[38] The men of Israel had agreed on a signal with the men in ambush: they would send up a great cloud of smoke from the city.
[Judges] [20]:[39] Then the men of Israel turned in the battle. Benjamin had begun to strike down the Israelites, killing about thirty of them, for they said, "Surely Israel is being beaten before us, as in the first battle!"
[Judges] [20]:[40] But when the column of smoke began to rise from the city, the Benjaminites turned and saw the whole city going up in smoke to the sky.
[Judges] [20]:[41] Then the men of Israel turned on them, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, for they realized that disaster had come upon them.
[Judges] [20]:[42] So they fled before the Israelites toward the wilderness, but the battle overtook them, and those coming out of the towns cut them down there.
[Judges] [20]:[43] They surrounded the Benjaminites and pursued them without rest, cutting them down all the way to a point east of Gibeah.
[Judges] [20]:[44] Eighteen thousand Benjaminites fell, all of them valiant fighters.
[Judges] [20]:[45] As they turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, the Israelites cut down five thousand men along the roads. They pressed after them as far as Gidom and struck down two thousand more.
[Judges] [20]:[46] In all, twenty-five thousand Benjaminite swordsmen fell that day, all of them valiant fighters.
[Judges] [20]:[47] But six hundred men turned and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, where they stayed four months.
[Judges] [20]:[48] The men of Israel turned back against the Benjaminites and put them to the sword—the people of every town, along with the animals and everything else they found. And all the towns they came upon they set on fire.
[Judges] [21]:[1] The men of Israel had sworn an oath at Mizpah: "None of us will give his daughter in marriage to a Benjaminite."
[Judges] [21]:[2] So the people came to Bethel and sat there before God until evening, and they lifted up their voices and wept bitterly.
[Judges] [21]:[3] They said, "Why, LORD, God of Israel, has this happened in Israel, that today one tribe should be missing from Israel?"
[Judges] [21]:[4] Early the next morning the people built an altar there and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings.
[Judges] [21]:[5] Then the Israelites asked, "Which of all the tribes of Israel failed to come up to the LORD with the assembly?" For they had bound themselves with a solemn oath that anyone who did not come up to the LORD at Mizpah should be put to death.
[Judges] [21]:[6] The Israelites grieved for their brother Benjamin and said, "Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel.
[Judges] [21]:[7] What shall we do about wives for those who are left, since we have sworn by the LORD not to give them any of our daughters in marriage?"
[Judges] [21]:[8] Then they asked, "Which one of the tribes of Israel did not come up to the LORD at Mizpah?" And it turned out that no one from Jabesh Gilead had come to the camp, to the assembly.
[Judges] [21]:[9] For when the people were counted, not one of the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead was there.
[Judges] [21]:[10] So the assembly sent twelve thousand fighting men there with these orders: "Go and put the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead to the sword, including the women and children.
[Judges] [21]:[11] This is what you are to do: devote to destruction every male, and every woman who has slept with a man."
[Judges] [21]:[12] Among the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead they found four hundred young virgins who had never slept with a man, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan.
[Judges] [21]:[13] Then the whole assembly sent word to the Benjaminites at the rock of Rimmon, offering them peace.
[Judges] [21]:[14] So the Benjaminites returned at that time, and they were given the women of Jabesh Gilead who had been spared. But there were not enough for them all.
[Judges] [21]:[15] The people grieved for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a gap in the tribes of Israel.
[Judges] [21]:[16] And the elders of the assembly said, "What shall we do about wives for those who are left, since the women of Benjamin have been wiped out?"
[Judges] [21]:[17] They said, "The survivors of Benjamin must have heirs, so that a tribe of Israel will not be blotted out.
[Judges] [21]:[18] Yet we cannot give them our own daughters as wives, for the Israelites have sworn: 'Cursed be anyone who gives a wife to Benjamin.'"
[Judges] [21]:[19] Then they said, "Look, there is the yearly festival of the LORD at Shiloh, which lies north of Bethel, east of the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah."
[Judges] [21]:[20] So they instructed the Benjaminites: "Go and hide in the vineyards
[Judges] [21]:[21] and watch. When the young women of Shiloh come out to join in the dancing, rush from the vineyards, and each of you seize a wife from the young women of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.
[Judges] [21]:[22] When their fathers or brothers come to us with a complaint, we will say to them, 'Be kind to us and let them keep these young women, since we did not capture a wife for each man in the war. And you are not guilty, for you yourselves did not give your daughters to them.'"
[Judges] [21]:[23] So that is what the Benjaminites did. They carried off as many wives as they needed from the dancers, and they went back to their own inheritance, rebuilt the towns, and settled in them.
[Judges] [21]:[24] At that time the Israelites left that place, each going to his own tribe and clan; each one set out for his own inheritance.
[Judges] [21]:[25] In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did as he saw fit.
[Ruth] [1]:[1] In the days when the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land, and a man from Bethlehem in Judah went to live for a time in the country of Moab, he and his wife and his two sons.
[Ruth] [1]:[2] The man's name was Elimelech, his wife's name was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They came to the country of Moab and settled there.
[Ruth] [1]:[3] Then Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, and she was left with her two sons.
[Ruth] [1]:[4] The sons married Moabite women, one named Orpah and the other Ruth. They lived there about ten years,
[Ruth] [1]:[5] and then both Mahlon and Chilion died as well, so the woman was left without her two children and without her husband.
[Ruth] [1]:[6] Then she set out with her daughters-in-law to return from the country of Moab, for she had heard there that the LORD had come to the aid of his people and given them food.
[Ruth] [1]:[7] So she left the place where she had been living, and her two daughters-in-law with her, and they set out on the road back to the land of Judah.
[Ruth] [1]:[8] But Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, "Go back, each of you, to your mother's house. May the LORD show you kindness, as you have shown to the dead and to me.
[Ruth] [1]:[9] May the LORD grant that each of you find rest in the home of a husband." Then she kissed them, and they wept aloud.
[Ruth] [1]:[10] They said to her, "No, we will go back with you to your people."
[Ruth] [1]:[11] But Naomi said, "Turn back, my daughters. Why would you come with me? Can I still bear sons who could become your husbands?
[Ruth] [1]:[12] Turn back, my daughters. Go. I am too old to have a husband. And even if I thought there was hope for me—even if I had a husband tonight and bore sons—
[Ruth] [1]:[13] would you wait for them until they grew up? Would you keep yourselves from marrying for their sake? No, my daughters. It is more bitter for me than for you, for the LORD's hand has gone out against me."
[Ruth] [1]:[14] At this they wept aloud again. Then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.
[Ruth] [1]:[15] "Look," said Naomi, "your sister-in-law is going back to her people and her gods. Go back with her."
[Ruth] [1]:[16] But Ruth said, "Do not urge me to leave you or to turn back from following you. Where you go I will go, and where you stay I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.
[Ruth] [1]:[17] Where you die I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD deal with me ever so severely if anything but death separates you and me."
[Ruth] [1]:[18] When Naomi saw that she was determined to go with her, she said no more.
[Ruth] [1]:[19] So the two of them went on until they came to Bethlehem. And when they arrived in Bethlehem, the whole town was stirred, and the women said, "Can this be Naomi?"
[Ruth] [1]:[20] "Do not call me Naomi," she told them. "Call me Mara,* because the Almighty has made my life very bitter. *Footnote: Naomi means "pleasant"; Mara means "bitter."
[Ruth] [1]:[21] I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi? The LORD has afflicted me;* the Almighty has brought misfortune upon me." *Footnote: Or "the LORD has testified against me."
[Ruth] [1]:[22] So Naomi returned, and with her was Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, who came back with her from the country of Moab. They arrived in Bethlehem as the barley harvest was beginning.
[Ruth] [2]:[1] Now Naomi had a relative on her husband's side, a man of standing from the clan of Elimelech, whose name was Boaz.
[Ruth] [2]:[2] Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, "Let me go out to the fields and gather the leftover grain behind anyone who will show me kindness." Naomi said to her, "Go ahead, my daughter."
[Ruth] [2]:[3] So she went out and began to gather in the fields behind the harvesters. As it happened, she came to the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the clan of Elimelech.
[Ruth] [2]:[4] Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and said to the harvesters, "The LORD be with you." "The LORD bless you," they answered.
[Ruth] [2]:[5] Boaz asked his servant in charge of the harvesters, "Whose young woman is this?"
[Ruth] [2]:[6] The servant in charge of the harvesters answered, "She is the Moabite woman who came back with Naomi from the country of Moab.
[Ruth] [2]:[7] She said, 'Please let me gather and glean among the sheaves behind the harvesters.' She came and has been on her feet from early this morning until now, resting only a little in the shelter."
[Ruth] [2]:[8] So Boaz said to Ruth, "Listen to me, my daughter. Don't go to glean in any other field, and don't go away from here. Stay close to my young women.
[Ruth] [2]:[9] Keep your eyes on the field where they are harvesting, and follow along behind my young women. I have ordered the men not to touch you. And when you are thirsty, go to the jars and drink the water the men have drawn.
[Ruth] [2]:[10] At this she fell on her face, bowing to the ground, and said to him, "Why have I found such favor in your eyes that you notice me—a foreigner?"
[Ruth] [2]:[11] Boaz answered her, "I have been told all about what you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband—how you left your father and mother and the land of your birth and came to a people you did not know before.
[Ruth] [2]:[12] May the LORD repay you for what you have done, and may you be richly rewarded by the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge."
[Ruth] [2]:[13] "May I continue to find favor in your eyes, my lord," she said, "for you have comforted me and spoken kindly to your servant—though I am not even equal to one of your servant girls."
[Ruth] [2]:[14] At mealtime Boaz said to her, "Come over here. Have some bread and dip your piece in the wine vinegar." So she sat down beside the harvesters, and he offered her roasted grain. She ate all she wanted and had some left over.
[Ruth] [2]:[15] As she got up to glean, Boaz gave orders to his men: "Let her gather even among the sheaves, and don't shame her.
[Ruth] [2]:[16] Even pull out some stalks from the bundles for her and leave them for her to gather, and don't rebuke her."
[Ruth] [2]:[17] So she gleaned in the field until evening. Then she threshed what she had gathered, and it came to about an ephah of barley.[^1] [^1]: An ephah was roughly twenty-two liters, or about thirty pounds of grain—an unusually large amount for a day's gleaning.
[Ruth] [2]:[18] She carried it back to town, and her mother-in-law saw how much she had gathered. Ruth also brought out and gave her what she had left over from her meal.
[Ruth] [2]:[19] Her mother-in-law asked her, "Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the man who took notice of you!" Then Ruth told her mother-in-law about the one she had worked with. "The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz," she said.
[Ruth] [2]:[20] "Blessed be he by the LORD," Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, "who has not stopped showing his kindness to the living and the dead." And she added, "That man is a close relative of ours; he is one of our family redeemers."[^1] [^1]: A family redeemer was a near relative responsible for buying back a poor relative's land, and for protecting and providing for the family in need.
[Ruth] [2]:[21] Then Ruth the Moabite said, "He even told me, 'Stay close to my young men until they have finished all my harvest.'"
[Ruth] [2]:[22] Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, "It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, so that no one may harm you in another field."
[Ruth] [2]:[23] So she stayed close to the young women of Boaz, gleaning until the barley harvest and the wheat harvest were finished. And she lived with her mother-in-law.
[Ruth] [3]:[1] Then Naomi, her mother-in-law, said to her, "My daughter, should I not look for a home for you, where you will be well provided for?
[Ruth] [3]:[2] Now Boaz, whose young women you have worked with, is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be winnowing barley at the threshing floor.
[Ruth] [3]:[3] So wash and anoint yourself, put on your best clothes, and go down to the threshing floor. But do not let him know you are there until he has finished eating and drinking.
[Ruth] [3]:[4] When he lies down, note the place where he lies. Then go, uncover his feet, and lie down. He will tell you what to do."
[Ruth] [3]:[5] "I will do everything you say," Ruth answered.
[Ruth] [3]:[6] So she went down to the threshing floor and did everything her mother-in-law had told her.
[Ruth] [3]:[7] When Boaz had finished eating and drinking and his heart was content, he went to lie down at the far end of the grain pile. Ruth came quietly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
[Ruth] [3]:[8] In the middle of the night the man was startled. He turned over, and there was a woman lying at his feet.
[Ruth] [3]:[9] "Who are you?" he asked. "I am your servant Ruth," she said. "Spread the corner of your garment over your servant, for you are a redeemer."
[Ruth] [3]:[10] Then he said, "The LORD bless you, my daughter. This last kindness of yours is greater than the first, for you have not gone after the young men, whether poor or rich.
[Ruth] [3]:[11] And now, my daughter, do not be afraid. I will do for you all that you ask, for the whole town knows that you are a woman of noble character.
[Ruth] [3]:[12] Now it is true that I am a redeemer, yet there is another redeemer more closely related than I.
[Ruth] [3]:[13] Stay here tonight. In the morning, if he will redeem you, good—let him redeem you. But if he is not willing, then as surely as the LORD lives, I will redeem you. Lie down until morning."
[Ruth] [3]:[14] So she lay at his feet until morning, but she rose while it was still too dark for anyone to be recognized, for he had said, "No one must know that a woman came to the threshing floor."
[Ruth] [3]:[15] He also said, "Bring the cloak you are wearing and hold it out." When she did, he measured out six measures of barley and lifted it onto her. Then he went into the town.
[Ruth] [3]:[16] When Ruth came to her mother-in-law, Naomi asked, "How did it go, my daughter?" [footnote: Hebrew, "Who are you, my daughter?"] And she told her everything the man had done for her.
[Ruth] [3]:[17] She added, "He gave me these six measures of barley and said, 'Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty-handed.'"
[Ruth] [3]:[18] Then Naomi said, "Wait, my daughter, until you learn how the matter turns out, for the man will not rest until he has settled it today."
[Ruth] [4]:[1] Meanwhile Boaz went up to the town gate and sat down there. Just then the redeemer he had spoken of came by, and Boaz said, "Come over here, friend, and sit down." So he turned aside and sat down.
[Ruth] [4]:[2] Boaz then took ten of the elders of the town and said, "Sit down here," and they sat down.
[Ruth] [4]:[3] He said to the redeemer, "Naomi, who has come back from the country of Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.
[Ruth] [4]:[4] I thought I should bring the matter to your attention and say: Buy it in the presence of those sitting here and of the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, redeem it. But if you will not, tell me, so that I may know—for there is no one to redeem it but you, and I come after you." And he said, "I will redeem it."
[Ruth] [4]:[5] Then Boaz said, "On the day you buy the field from Naomi, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, the widow of the dead man, in order to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance."
[Ruth] [4]:[6] At that the redeemer said, "Then I cannot redeem it for myself, or I would ruin my own inheritance. Take over my right of redemption yourself, for I cannot redeem it."
[Ruth] [4]:[7] Now in earlier times in Israel, this was the custom concerning redemption and exchange, to confirm any transaction: a man would take off his sandal and hand it to the other party. This was the way of attesting a matter in Israel.
[Ruth] [4]:[8] So the redeemer said to Boaz, "Buy it yourself," and he took off his sandal.
[Ruth] [4]:[9] Then Boaz said to the elders and to all the people, "You are witnesses today that I have bought from Naomi everything that belonged to Elimelech and everything that belonged to Kilion and Mahlon.
[Ruth] [4]:[10] And I have also acquired Ruth the Moabite, Mahlon's widow, as my wife, in order to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance, so that his name will not be cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his town. You are witnesses today."
[Ruth] [4]:[11] All the people at the gate and the elders said, "We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman who is entering your house like Rachel and Leah, who together built up the house of Israel. May you prosper in Ephrathah and be renowned in Bethlehem.
[Ruth] [4]:[12] And through the offspring the LORD gives you by this young woman, may your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah."
[Ruth] [4]:[13] So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife. He went to her, and the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she bore a son.
[Ruth] [4]:[14] Then the women said to Naomi, "Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you this day without a redeemer! May his name be renowned in Israel.
[Ruth] [4]:[15] He will renew your life and sustain you in your old age. For your daughter-in-law, who loves you and who is worth more to you than seven sons, has given him birth."
[Ruth] [4]:[16] Naomi took the child, laid him on her lap, and became his nurse.
[Ruth] [4]:[17] The women of the neighborhood gave him a name, saying, "A son has been born to Naomi." And they named him Obed. He was the father of Jesse, the father of David.
[Ruth] [4]:[18] This is the line of Perez: Perez was the father of Hezron,
[Ruth] [4]:[19] Hezron the father of Ram, Ram the father of Amminadab,
[Ruth] [4]:[20] Amminadab the father of Nahshon, Nahshon the father of Salmon,
[Ruth] [4]:[21] Salmon the father of Boaz, Boaz the father of Obed,
[Ruth] [4]:[22] Obed the father of Jesse, and Jesse the father of David.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[1] There was a man from Ramathaim-zophim, in the hill country of Ephraim, whose name was Elkanah son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[2] He had two wives; one was named Hannah, the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[3] Year after year this man would go up from his town to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of hosts at Shiloh, where Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests of the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[4] Whenever the day came for Elkanah to sacrifice, he would give portions to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[5] But to Hannah he would give a double portion, for he loved Hannah, though the LORD had closed her womb.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[6] Her rival taunted her bitterly, provoking her because the LORD had closed her womb.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[7] So it went year after year: every time Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, Peninnah would provoke her, and Hannah would weep and refuse to eat.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[8] Her husband Elkanah said to her, "Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why is your heart so heavy? Am I not more to you than ten sons?"
[1 Samuel] [1]:[9] After they had eaten and drunk at Shiloh, Hannah got up. Now Eli the priest was sitting on his seat by the doorpost of the LORD's temple.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[10] In deep anguish Hannah prayed to the LORD, weeping bitterly.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[11] And she made a vow: "LORD of hosts, if you will only look on the misery of your servant and remember me, if you will not forget your servant but give her a son, then I will give him to the LORD for all the days of his life, and no razor shall ever touch his head."
[1 Samuel] [1]:[12] As she kept on praying before the LORD, Eli watched her mouth.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[13] Hannah was praying in her heart; her lips were moving, but no sound came out. So Eli thought she was drunk
[1 Samuel] [1]:[14] and said to her, "How long will you go on drinking? Put your wine away."
[1 Samuel] [1]:[15] "No, my lord," Hannah answered. "I am a woman in deep distress. I have not been drinking wine or strong drink; I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[16] Do not take your servant for a worthless woman; it is out of my great anguish and grief that I have been speaking all this time.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[17] Then Eli answered, "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant what you have asked of him."
[1 Samuel] [1]:[18] She said, "May your servant find favor in your eyes." Then she went on her way, and she ate, and her face was no longer downcast.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[19] Early the next morning they rose and worshiped before the LORD, and then returned home to Ramah. Elkanah made love to his wife Hannah, and the LORD remembered her.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[20] In the course of time Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, "I asked the LORD for him."
[1 Samuel] [1]:[21] When Elkanah went up with all his household to offer the yearly sacrifice to the LORD and to fulfill his vow,
[1 Samuel] [1]:[22] Hannah did not go. She said to her husband, "Once the boy is weaned, I will take him and present him before the LORD, and he will stay there for good."
[1 Samuel] [1]:[23] "Do what seems best to you," her husband Elkanah told her. "Stay here until you have weaned him; only may the LORD make good his word." So the woman stayed and nursed her son until she had weaned him.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[24] When he was weaned, she took him up with her, along with three bulls, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, and brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh, though he was still a small child. [Footnote: Hebrew tradition reads "three bulls"; other ancient witnesses read "a three-year-old bull," which agrees with the single bull slaughtered in verse 25.]
[1 Samuel] [1]:[25] When they had slaughtered the bull, they brought the boy to Eli,
[1 Samuel] [1]:[26] and she said, "Pardon me, my lord. As surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[27] I prayed for this child, and the LORD has granted me what I asked of him.
[1 Samuel] [1]:[28] So now I give him to the LORD. For his whole life he will be given over to the LORD." And there he worshiped the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[1] Then Hannah prayed: "My heart exults in the LORD; in the LORD my horn is lifted high. My mouth speaks boldly against my enemies, for I rejoice in your salvation.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[2] No one is holy like the LORD; there is none besides you, and no rock like our God.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[3] Speak no more so proudly; let no arrogance come from your mouth, for the LORD is a God who knows, and by him every deed is weighed.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[4] The bows of the mighty are broken, but the weak are armed with strength.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[5] Those who were full now hire themselves out for bread, but the hungry go hungry no more. Even the barren woman has borne seven, but she who had many sons is left desolate.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[6] The LORD brings death and gives life; he brings down to Sheol and raises up.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[7] The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he humbles and he exalts.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[8] He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap, seating them among princes and giving them a throne of honor. For the foundations of the earth are the LORD's, and on them he has set the world.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[9] He guards the steps of his faithful ones, but the wicked are silenced in darkness— for no one prevails by his own strength.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[10] Those who oppose the LORD will be shattered; he will thunder against them from heaven. The LORD will judge the ends of the earth; he will give strength to his king and lift high the horn of his anointed."
[1 Samuel] [2]:[11] Then Elkanah went home to Ramah, but the boy remained to serve the LORD under Eli the priest.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[12] Eli's sons were worthless men; they had no regard for the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[13] This was their practice with the people: whenever anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come with a three-pronged fork in his hand while the meat was boiling.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[14] He would thrust it into the pan or kettle or cauldron or pot, and whatever the fork brought up the priest took for himself. This is how they treated all the Israelites who came to Shiloh.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[15] Even before the fat was burned, the priest's servant would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, "Give the priest meat to roast. He will not take boiled meat from you—only raw."
[1 Samuel] [2]:[16] If the man said to him, "Let the fat be burned first, then take whatever you want," the servant would answer, "No, hand it over now; if you won't, I'll take it by force."
[1 Samuel] [2]:[17] So the sin of these young men was very great in the LORD's sight, for they treated the offering of the LORD with contempt.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[18] But Samuel served before the LORD, a boy wearing a linen ephod.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[19] Each year his mother made him a little robe and brought it to him when she went up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[20] Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, saying, "May the LORD give you children by this woman in place of the one asked for and given to the LORD." Then they would return home.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[21] And the LORD showed his care for Hannah: she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. Meanwhile the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[22] Now Eli was very old, and he kept hearing about everything his sons were doing to all Israel and how they slept with the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[23] So he said to them, "Why do you do such things? I hear about your evil deeds from all these people.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[24] No, my sons; the report I hear is not good. You are leading the LORD's people into sin.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[25] If one person sins against another, God may mediate for him; but if someone sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?" His sons, however, would not listen to their father, for it was the LORD's will to put them to death.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[26] And the boy Samuel continued to grow, and he was pleasing both to the LORD and to the people.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[27] A man of God came to Eli and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: Did I not reveal myself plainly to your father's house when they were in Egypt under Pharaoh?
[1 Samuel] [2]:[28] Out of all the tribes of Israel I chose your father to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, and to wear the ephod before me. And I gave your father's house all the offerings made by fire by the Israelites.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[29] Why then do you trample on my sacrifice and my offering, which I commanded for my dwelling? You honor your sons above me, fattening yourselves on the choicest part of every offering my people Israel bring.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[30] Therefore the LORD, the God of Israel, declares: I did indeed promise that your house and your father's house would minister before me forever. But now the LORD declares: Far be it from me! Those who honor me I will honor, but those who despise me will be treated with contempt.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[31] The days are coming when I will cut off your strength and the strength of your father's house, and no one in your family will live to old age.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[32] You will look on in distress at my dwelling. Though good will be done for Israel, never again will there be an old man in your house.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[33] Every one of your line whom I do not cut off from my altar will be spared only to wear out your eyes with weeping and to grieve your heart, and all your descendants will die in the prime of life.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[34] And this will be the sign to you: what happens to your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas—both of them will die on the same day.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[35] Then I will raise up for myself a faithful priest, who will do what is in my heart and mind. I will build him an enduring house, and he will walk before my anointed one all his days.
[1 Samuel] [2]:[36] And everyone left in your house will come and bow down before him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and will say, 'Please attach me to one of the priestly offices, so I may eat a morsel of bread.'"
[1 Samuel] [3]:[1] The boy Samuel served the LORD under Eli. In those days the word of the LORD was rare; visions were not widespread.
[1 Samuel] [3]:[2] One night Eli was lying down in his usual place. His eyes had grown so weak that he could no longer see.
[1 Samuel] [3]:[3] The lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was.
[1 Samuel] [3]:[4] Then the LORD called to Samuel, and he answered, "Here I am."
[1 Samuel] [3]:[5] He ran to Eli and said, "Here I am; you called me." But Eli said, "I did not call. Go back and lie down." So he went and lay down.
[1 Samuel] [3]:[6] Again the LORD called, "Samuel!" Samuel got up, went to Eli, and said, "Here I am; you called me." "I did not call, my son," he said. "Go back and lie down."
[1 Samuel] [3]:[7] Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, and the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.
[1 Samuel] [3]:[8] A third time the LORD called Samuel. He got up, went to Eli, and said, "Here I am; you called me." Then Eli understood that it was the LORD who was calling the boy.
[1 Samuel] [3]:[9] So Eli said to Samuel, "Go and lie down, and if he calls you, say, 'Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening.'" So Samuel went and lay down in his place.
[1 Samuel] [3]:[10] Then the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, "Samuel! Samuel!" And Samuel said, "Speak, for your servant is listening."
[1 Samuel] [3]:[11] The LORD said to Samuel: "See, I am about to do something in Israel that will make the ears of everyone who hears of it ring.
[1 Samuel] [3]:[12] On that day I will carry out against Eli everything I have spoken against his house, from beginning to end.
[1 Samuel] [3]:[13] I have told him that I am judging his house forever because of the sin he knew about: his sons were bringing a curse on themselves, and he did not restrain them.
[1 Samuel] [3]:[14] Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the guilt of Eli's house will never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering."
[1 Samuel] [3]:[15] Samuel lay down until morning, and then he opened the doors of the house of the LORD. He was afraid to tell Eli the vision,
[1 Samuel] [3]:[16] but Eli called him and said, "Samuel, my son." And he answered, "Here I am."
[1 Samuel] [3]:[17] "What did he say to you?" Eli asked. "Do not hide it from me. May God deal with you, and deal with you all the more, if you hide from me a single word of all that he said to you."
[1 Samuel] [3]:[18] So Samuel told him everything and hid nothing from him. Then Eli said, "He is the LORD; let him do what seems good to him."
[1 Samuel] [3]:[19] Samuel grew up, and the LORD was with him, and he let none of his words fall to the ground.
[1 Samuel] [3]:[20] And all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, knew that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [3]:[21] The LORD continued to appear at Shiloh, for there he revealed himself to Samuel through his word.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[1] Samuel's word came to all Israel. Now Israel marched out to meet the Philistines in battle. They camped at Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[2] The Philistines drew up their lines against Israel, and when the battle was joined, Israel was defeated before the Philistines, who struck down about four thousand men on the field of battle.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[3] When the troops came back to the camp, the elders of Israel asked, "Why has the LORD let us be defeated today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the LORD's covenant here from Shiloh, so that it may come among us and save us from the hand of our enemies."
[1 Samuel] [4]:[4] So the people sent to Shiloh, and they carried from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned between the cherubim. And Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[5] When the ark of the LORD's covenant came into the camp, all Israel raised such a great shout that the earth shook.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[6] Hearing the noise of the shouting, the Philistines asked, "What is this sound of great shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?" Then they learned that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[7] The Philistines were afraid, for they said, "A god has come into their camp!" And they said, "We are lost! Nothing like this has ever happened before.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[8] We are lost! Who can deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with every kind of plague in the wilderness.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[9] Be strong, Philistines, and be men, or you will become slaves to the Hebrews as they were slaves to you. Be men, and fight!"
[1 Samuel] [4]:[10] So the Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated. Every man fled to his tent, and the slaughter was very great: thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[11] The ark of God was captured, and Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[12] That same day a man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh, his clothes torn and dirt on his head.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[13] When he arrived, there was Eli, sitting on his seat beside the road, watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of God. The man came into the city to tell the news, and the whole city cried out.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[14] When Eli heard the sound of the outcry, he asked, "What is this uproar?" Then the man hurried and came and told Eli.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[15] Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes had grown dim, so that he could not see.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[16] The man said to Eli, "I am the one who has come from the battle line; I fled from the battle today." Eli asked, "What happened, my son?"
