[1 Samuel] [4]:[17] The messenger answered, "Israel fled before the Philistines. There was a great slaughter among the troops. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God has been captured."
[1 Samuel] [4]:[18] When he mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell backward off his seat beside the gate. His neck was broken and he died, for he was old and heavy. He had led Israel forty years.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[19] His daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and near the time of birth. When she heard the news that the ark of God had been captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she went into labor and gave birth, for her pains came upon her.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[20] As she was dying, the women attending her said, "Do not be afraid; you have given birth to a son." But she did not answer or take it to heart.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[21] She named the boy Ichabod, saying, "The glory has departed from Israel"—because the ark of God had been captured and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
[1 Samuel] [4]:[22] She said, "The glory has departed from Israel, for the ark of God has been captured."
[1 Samuel] [5]:[1] When the Philistines had captured the ark of God, they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
[1 Samuel] [5]:[2] Then the Philistines took the ark of God, carried it into the temple of Dagon, and set it up beside Dagon.
[1 Samuel] [5]:[3] When the people of Ashdod rose early the next morning, there was Dagon, fallen face down on the ground before the ark of the LORD. So they took Dagon and put him back in his place.
[1 Samuel] [5]:[4] But when they rose early the following morning, there was Dagon again, fallen face down on the ground before the ark of the LORD, with his head and the palms of both his hands cut off, lying on the threshold. Only his body was left.
[1 Samuel] [5]:[5] That is why to this day the priests of Dagon and all who enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod do not step on the threshold.
[1 Samuel] [5]:[6] The hand of the LORD lay heavy on the people of Ashdod. He devastated them and struck them with tumors,<fn>The Hebrew term refers to painful swellings; the affliction may have been an outbreak of plague.</fn> both Ashdod and its territory.
[1 Samuel] [5]:[7] When the men of Ashdod saw what was happening, they said, "The ark of the God of Israel must not stay here with us, for his hand is harsh against us and against Dagon our god."
[1 Samuel] [5]:[8] So they sent word and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines and asked, "What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" They answered, "Let the ark of the God of Israel be moved to Gath." So they moved the ark of the God of Israel.
[1 Samuel] [5]:[9] But after they had moved it, the hand of the LORD was against that city, throwing it into a very great panic. He struck the men of the city, young and old, and tumors broke out on them.
[1 Samuel] [5]:[10] So they sent the ark of God to Ekron. But as the ark of God entered Ekron, the people of Ekron cried out, "They have brought the ark of the God of Israel around to us to kill us and our people!"
[1 Samuel] [5]:[11] They sent word and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines and said, "Send the ark of the God of Israel away. Let it return to its own place, so that it will not kill us and our people." For a deadly panic had fallen on the whole city; the hand of God lay very heavy there.
[1 Samuel] [5]:[12] Those who did not die were struck with tumors, and the outcry of the city went up to heaven.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[1] The ark of the LORD was in Philistine territory seven months.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[2] Then the Philistines summoned the priests and the diviners and said, "What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Tell us how to send it back to its own place."
[1 Samuel] [6]:[3] They answered, "If you send the ark of the God of Israel away, do not send it empty. By all means return a guilt offering to him. Then you will be healed, and you will know why his hand has not turned away from you."
[1 Samuel] [6]:[4] "What guilt offering should we return to him?" they asked. They answered, "Five gold tumors and five gold mice, matching the number of the Philistine rulers, since the same plague struck all of you and your rulers.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[5] Make images of your tumors and images of your mice that are ravaging the land, and give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps he will lighten his hand upon you, upon your gods, and upon your land.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[6] Why harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened theirs? When he dealt harshly with them, did they not let the people go, and they went?
[1 Samuel] [6]:[7] Now then, get a new cart ready, with two milk cows that have never worn a yoke. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take their calves away from them and shut them up at home.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[8] Take the ark of the LORD and set it on the cart, and place beside it in a box the gold objects you are returning to him as a guilt offering. Then send it on its way,
[1 Samuel] [6]:[9] and watch: if it goes up the road toward its own territory, toward Beth Shemesh, then it is the LORD who has brought this great disaster on us. But if it does not, then we will know it was not his hand that struck us; it happened to us by chance."
[1 Samuel] [6]:[10] So the men did this. They took two milk cows and hitched them to the cart and shut their calves up at home.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[11] They set the ark of the LORD on the cart, along with the box containing the gold mice and the images of their tumors.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[12] Then the cows went straight up the road toward Beth Shemesh. They kept to the one highway, lowing as they went, and turned neither to the right nor to the left. The rulers of the Philistines followed them as far as the border of Beth Shemesh.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[13] Now the people of Beth Shemesh were harvesting wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the ark, they rejoiced at the sight.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[14] The cart came to the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh and stopped there beside a large stone. The people chopped up the wood of the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[15] The Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the box that was with it, containing the gold objects, and set them on the large stone. That day the men of Beth Shemesh offered burnt offerings and made sacrifices to the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[16] The five rulers of the Philistines saw all this and returned that same day to Ekron.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[17] These are the gold tumors the Philistines sent back as a guilt offering to the LORD: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, and one for Ekron.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[18] And the gold mice matched the number of all the Philistine towns belonging to the five rulers—both the fortified cities and the outlying villages. The large stone on which they set the ark of the LORD is a witness to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew text here reads "Abel the great"; the reading "the large stone" follows other ancient witnesses and matches verses 14–15.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[19] But the LORD struck down some of the men of Beth Shemesh because they looked into the ark of the LORD. He struck down seventy men out of fifty thousand, and the people mourned because the LORD had struck them with such a great blow.
[1 Samuel] [6]:[20] The men of Beth Shemesh said, "Who can stand before the LORD, this holy God? To whom shall the ark go up from here?"
[1 Samuel] [6]:[21] So they sent messengers to the people of Kiriath Jearim, saying, "The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up to your place."
[1 Samuel] [7]:[1] So the men of Kiriath-jearim came and took up the ark of the LORD and brought it to the house of Abinadab on the hill, and they consecrated his son Eleazar to keep watch over the ark of the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [7]:[2] From the day the ark came to rest at Kiriath-jearim a long time passed—twenty years—and the whole house of Israel lamented and longed after the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [7]:[3] Then Samuel said to the whole house of Israel, "If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, get rid of the foreign gods among you, and the Ashtaroth as well. Set your hearts on the LORD and serve him alone, and he will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines."
[1 Samuel] [7]:[4] So the Israelites got rid of the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and they served the LORD alone.
[1 Samuel] [7]:[5] Then Samuel said, "Gather all Israel at Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD for you."
[1 Samuel] [7]:[6] So they gathered at Mizpah and drew water and poured it out before the LORD. They fasted that day, and there they confessed, "We have sinned against the LORD." And Samuel judged the Israelites at Mizpah.
[1 Samuel] [7]:[7] When the Philistines heard that the Israelites had gathered at Mizpah, the Philistine rulers marched up against Israel. And when the Israelites heard of it, they were afraid of the Philistines.
[1 Samuel] [7]:[8] They said to Samuel, "Do not stop crying out to the LORD our God for us, that he may save us from the hand of the Philistines."
[1 Samuel] [7]:[9] So Samuel took a suckling lamb and offered it whole as a burnt offering to the LORD. He cried out to the LORD on Israel's behalf, and the LORD answered him.
[1 Samuel] [7]:[10] As Samuel was offering the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to fight against Israel. But that day the LORD thundered against the Philistines with a mighty voice and threw them into panic, and they were routed before Israel.
[1 Samuel] [7]:[11] The men of Israel charged out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, striking them down as far as below Beth-car.
[1 Samuel] [7]:[12] Then Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen, and he named it Ebenezer, saying, "Thus far the LORD has helped us." [Footnote: Ebenezer means "stone of help."]
[1 Samuel] [7]:[13] So the Philistines were subdued and did not invade the territory of Israel again. The hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
[1 Samuel] [7]:[14] The towns the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron to Gath, and Israel also recovered the territory around them from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
[1 Samuel] [7]:[15] Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
[1 Samuel] [7]:[16] Year after year he would travel a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, judging Israel in all these places.
[1 Samuel] [7]:[17] Then he would return to Ramah, for his home was there, and there too he judged Israel. And there he built an altar to the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[1] When Samuel had grown old, he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[2] His firstborn son was named Joel and his second Abijah; they served as judges in Beersheba.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[3] But his sons did not walk in his ways. They turned aside after dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[4] So all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[5] They said to him, "You are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint a king to judge us, like all the other nations."
[1 Samuel] [8]:[6] But it displeased Samuel when they said, "Give us a king to judge us," and Samuel prayed to the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[7] And the LORD said to Samuel, "Listen to the people in all that they say to you. It is not you they have rejected; they have rejected me as their king.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[8] Just as they have done from the day I brought them up out of Egypt until this day—forsaking me and serving other gods—so they are doing to you as well.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[9] Now then, listen to them. But warn them solemnly and make known to them the ways of the king who will reign over them.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[10] So Samuel reported all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[11] He said, "These will be the ways of the king who will reign over you: He will take your sons and assign them to his chariots and his horsemen, and they will run before his chariot.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[12] He will appoint them as commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, to plow his ground and reap his harvest, and to make his weapons of war and the equipment for his chariots.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[13] He will take your daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[14] He will take the best of your fields, your vineyards, and your olive groves and give them to his servants.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[15] He will take a tenth of your grain and your vintage and give it to his officials and his servants.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[16] He will take your male and female servants, the best of your young men, and your donkeys, and put them to his own work.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[17] He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his slaves.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[18] When that day comes, you will cry out because of the king you have chosen for yourselves, but the LORD will not answer you on that day."
[1 Samuel] [8]:[19] But the people refused to listen to Samuel. "No," they said, "there shall be a king over us!
[1 Samuel] [8]:[20] Then we too will be like all the other nations, with a king to judge us, to go out before us and fight our battles."
[1 Samuel] [8]:[21] Samuel listened to all that the people said and repeated it in the ears of the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [8]:[22] And the LORD said to Samuel, "Listen to them and give them a king." Then Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Each of you, go back to your own town."
[1 Samuel] [9]:[1] There was a man from Benjamin whose name was Kish son of Abiel, son of Zeror, son of Becorath, son of Aphiah, son of a Benjaminite; he was a man of standing.
[1 Samuel] [9]:[2] He had a son named Saul, young and handsome. There was no one among the Israelites more handsome than he; he stood head and shoulders above all the people.
[1 Samuel] [9]:[3] Now the donkeys belonging to Kish, Saul's father, had strayed off, and Kish said to his son Saul, "Take one of the servants with you and go look for the donkeys."
[1 Samuel] [9]:[4] So he passed through the hill country of Ephraim and through the region of Shalishah, but they did not find them. They went on through the region of Shaalim, and they were not there. They passed through the territory of Benjamin, and still did not find them.
[1 Samuel] [9]:[5] When they came to the region of Zuph, Saul said to the servant who was with him, "Come, let us go back, or my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us."
[1 Samuel] [9]:[6] But the servant said to him, "Listen, there is a man of God in this town, and he is highly respected; everything he says comes true. Let us go there now. Perhaps he will tell us which way to take."
[1 Samuel] [9]:[7] Saul said to his servant, "If we go, what can we bring the man? The bread in our bags is gone, and we have no gift to bring the man of God. What do we have?"
[1 Samuel] [9]:[8] The servant answered Saul again, "Look, I have a quarter shekel of silver here. I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way."
[1 Samuel] [9]:[9] (Formerly in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, he would say, "Come, let us go to the seer," for the one now called a prophet was formerly called a seer.)
[1 Samuel] [9]:[10] Saul said to his servant, "Well said. Come, let us go." So they set out for the town where the man of God was.
[1 Samuel] [9]:[11] As they were climbing the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to draw water and asked them, "Is the seer here?"
[1 Samuel] [9]:[12] "He is," they answered. "He is just ahead of you. Hurry now, for he has come to town today, since the people have a sacrifice at the high place.
[1 Samuel] [9]:[13] As soon as you enter the town you will find him, before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not eat until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice; only then will the guests eat. Go up now, for you will find him today.
[1 Samuel] [9]:[14] So they went up to the town. As they were entering it, there was Samuel, coming toward them on his way up to the high place.
[1 Samuel] [9]:[15] Now the day before Saul came, the LORD had revealed this to Samuel:
[1 Samuel] [9]:[16] "About this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin. Anoint him ruler over my people Israel; he will deliver my people from the hand of the Philistines. For I have looked upon my people, because their cry has come to me."
[1 Samuel] [9]:[17] When Samuel caught sight of Saul, the LORD said to him, "Here is the man I spoke to you about; this one will govern my people."
[1 Samuel] [9]:[18] Saul approached Samuel in the gateway and said, "Tell me, please, where is the seer's house?"
[1 Samuel] [9]:[19] "I am the seer," Samuel answered. "Go up ahead of me to the high place, for today you are to eat with me. In the morning I will send you on your way and tell you all that is on your mind.
[1 Samuel] [9]:[20] As for the donkeys you lost three days ago, do not give them another thought; they have been found. And to whom does all that Israel desires belong, if not to you and to all your father's house?"
[1 Samuel] [9]:[21] Saul answered, "Am I not a Benjaminite, from the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and is not my clan the least of all the clans of the tribe of Benjamin? Why do you speak to me like this?"
[1 Samuel] [9]:[22] Then Samuel took Saul and his servant, brought them into the hall, and seated them at the head of the guests, who numbered about thirty.
[1 Samuel] [9]:[23] Samuel said to the cook, "Bring the portion I gave you, the one I told you to set aside."
[1 Samuel] [9]:[24] So the cook took up the thigh with what was on it and set it before Saul. Samuel said, "Here is what was kept back. Set it before you and eat, for it was reserved for you for this occasion, when I said, 'I have invited the people.'" And Saul ate with Samuel that day.
[1 Samuel] [9]:[25] After they came down from the high place into the town, Samuel talked with Saul on the roof.
[1 Samuel] [9]:[26] They rose early, and at daybreak Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, "Get ready, and I will send you on your way." Saul got up, and the two of them, he and Samuel, went outside together.
[1 Samuel] [9]:[27] As they were going down to the edge of the town, Samuel said to Saul, "Tell the servant to go on ahead of us"—and he went on—"but you stay here a moment, so that I may make known to you the word of God."
[1 Samuel] [10]:[1] Then Samuel took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul's head, and kissed him. He said, "Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over his inheritance?
[1 Samuel] [10]:[2] When you leave me today, you will meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They will say to you, 'The donkeys you went to look for have been found. Your father has stopped worrying about the donkeys and is anxious about you, asking, "What shall I do about my son?"'
[1 Samuel] [10]:[3] Then you will go on from there until you come to the oak of Tabor. Three men will meet you there, on their way up to God at Bethel: one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a skin of wine.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[4] They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you are to accept from them.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[5] After that you will come to Gibeah of God, where the Philistine garrison is. As you enter the town, you will meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place, with harp, tambourine, flute, and lyre going before them, and they will be prophesying.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[6] Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them, and you will be changed into a different man.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[7] When these signs come to you, do whatever your hand finds to do, for God is with you.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[8] Go down ahead of me to Gilgal. I will come down to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice fellowship offerings. Wait seven days until I come to you and tell you what you are to do."
[1 Samuel] [10]:[9] As Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed his heart, and all these signs came to pass that day.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[10] When they came to Gibeah, a band of prophets met him. The Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied among them.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[11] All who had known him before saw him prophesying with the prophets, and the people said to one another, "What has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?"
[1 Samuel] [10]:[12] And a man from there answered, "And who is their father?" So it became a proverb: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
[1 Samuel] [10]:[13] When he had finished prophesying, he went to the high place.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[14] Saul's uncle asked him and his servant, "Where did you go?" "To look for the donkeys," Saul said. "When we saw they were nowhere to be found, we went to Samuel."
[1 Samuel] [10]:[15] "Tell me," his uncle said, "what did Samuel say to you?"
[1 Samuel] [10]:[16] Saul answered his uncle, "He told us plainly that the donkeys had been found." But he said nothing to him about what Samuel had said concerning the kingship.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[17] Samuel summoned the people to the LORD at Mizpah
[1 Samuel] [10]:[18] and said to the Israelites, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I brought Israel up out of Egypt, and I rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.'
[1 Samuel] [10]:[19] But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your troubles and distresses, and you have said to him, 'No—set a king over us.' So now present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and clans."
[1 Samuel] [10]:[20] When Samuel brought all the tribes of Israel forward, the tribe of Benjamin was chosen.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[21] Then he brought the tribe of Benjamin forward by its clans, and the clan of Matri was chosen; and Saul son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was not to be found.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[22] So they inquired further of the LORD, "Has the man come here yet?" And the LORD said, "Yes, he has hidden himself among the baggage."
[1 Samuel] [10]:[23] They ran and brought him out, and when he stood among the people he was a head taller than any of them.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[24] Samuel said to all the people, "Do you see the man the LORD has chosen? There is no one like him among all the people." And all the people shouted, "Long live the king!"
[1 Samuel] [10]:[25] Samuel explained to the people the regulations of the kingship. He wrote them in a book and laid it before the LORD. Then Samuel sent all the people away, each to his own home.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[26] Saul also went home to Gibeah, accompanied by the men of valor whose hearts God had touched.
[1 Samuel] [10]:[27] But some worthless men said, "How can this man save us?" They despised him and brought him no gift. But Saul kept silent.
[1 Samuel] [11]:[1] Nahash the Ammonite came up and laid siege to Jabesh Gilead. All the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, "Make a treaty with us, and we will serve you."
[1 Samuel] [11]:[2] But Nahash the Ammonite answered them, "I will make a treaty with you on one condition: that I gouge out the right eye of every one of you and so bring disgrace on all Israel."
[1 Samuel] [11]:[3] The elders of Jabesh said to him, "Give us seven days, so we can send messengers throughout the territory of Israel. If no one comes to save us, we will surrender to you."
[1 Samuel] [11]:[4] When the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and reported these things in the hearing of the people, all the people wept aloud.
[1 Samuel] [11]:[5] Just then Saul was coming in from the field, behind his oxen. "What is wrong with the people?" he asked. "Why are they weeping?" And they told him what the men of Jabesh had said.
[1 Samuel] [11]:[6] When Saul heard their words, the Spirit of God came powerfully upon him, and his anger burned fiercely.
[1 Samuel] [11]:[7] He took a pair of oxen, cut them in pieces, and sent them by messengers throughout the territory of Israel with this message: "This is what will be done to the oxen of anyone who does not follow Saul and Samuel." Then the terror of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out as one man.
[1 Samuel] [11]:[8] When Saul mustered them at Bezek, the men of Israel numbered three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.
[1 Samuel] [11]:[9] They told the messengers who had come, "Say this to the men of Jabesh Gilead: 'By the time the sun is hot tomorrow, you will be delivered.'" When the messengers brought this word to the men of Jabesh, they were overjoyed.
[1 Samuel] [11]:[10] So the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, "Tomorrow we will surrender to you, and you may do to us whatever seems good to you."
[1 Samuel] [11]:[11] The next day Saul divided his men into three companies. During the last watch of the night they broke into the enemy camp and struck down the Ammonites until the heat of the day. Those who survived were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.
[1 Samuel] [11]:[12] Then the people said to Samuel, "Who was it that asked, 'Shall Saul reign over us?' Hand these men over, and we will put them to death."
[1 Samuel] [11]:[13] But Saul said, "No one will be put to death today, for this is the day the LORD has brought deliverance to Israel."
[1 Samuel] [11]:[14] Then Samuel said to the people, "Come, let us go to Gilgal and there renew the kingship."
[1 Samuel] [11]:[15] So all the people went to Gilgal, and there before the LORD they made Saul king. There they sacrificed fellowship offerings before the LORD, and Saul and all the Israelites celebrated with great joy.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[1] Then Samuel said to all Israel: "I have listened to your voice in everything you asked of me, and I have set a king over you.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[2] Now here is the king, walking before you. As for me, I am old and gray, and my sons are here with you. I have walked before you from my youth until this day.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[3] Here I stand. Testify against me before the LORD and before his anointed: Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I cheated? Whom have I oppressed? From whose hand have I accepted a bribe to blind my eyes? Tell me, and I will make it right."
[1 Samuel] [12]:[4] They answered, "You have not cheated us or oppressed us, and you have taken nothing from anyone's hand."
[1 Samuel] [12]:[5] He said to them, "The LORD is witness against you, and his anointed is witness this day, that you have found nothing in my hand." And they said, "He is witness."
[1 Samuel] [12]:[6] Then Samuel said to the people: "It is the LORD who appointed Moses and Aaron and who brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[7] Now take your stand, and I will bring my case against you before the LORD, recounting all the righteous acts the LORD has done for you and for your fathers.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[8] When Jacob went to Egypt and your fathers cried out to the LORD, the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, who brought your fathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[9] But they forgot the LORD their God, so he sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab, and they fought against them.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[10] Then they cried out to the LORD and said, 'We have sinned, for we have forsaken the LORD and served the Baals and the Ashtoreths. But now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve you.'
[1 Samuel] [12]:[11] So the LORD sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel, and he rescued you from the hand of the enemies all around you, and you lived in safety.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[12] But when you saw that Nahash king of the Ammonites was coming against you, you said to me, 'No, a king must reign over us'—though the LORD your God was your king.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[13] Now here is the king you have chosen, the one you asked for. See, the LORD has set a king over you.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[14] If you fear the LORD and serve him and listen to his voice, and do not rebel against the LORD's command, and if both you and the king who reigns over you follow the LORD your God—well and good.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[15] But if you do not listen to the voice of the LORD and you rebel against his command, then the hand of the LORD will be against you as it was against your fathers.[^1] [^1]: Hebrew reads literally "against you and against your fathers"; some ancient witnesses read "against you and your king."
[1 Samuel] [12]:[16] Now then, stand still and see this great thing the LORD is about to do before your eyes.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[17] Is it not the wheat harvest today? I will call on the LORD, and he will send thunder and rain. Then you will know and see how great is the evil you have done in the eyes of the LORD in asking for a king."
[1 Samuel] [12]:[18] Then Samuel called on the LORD, and that same day the LORD sent thunder and rain. And all the people stood in great fear of the LORD and of Samuel.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[19] Then all the people said to Samuel, "Pray to the LORD your God for your servants, so that we do not die; for to all our sins we have added this evil of asking for a king."
[1 Samuel] [12]:[20] Samuel answered the people, "Do not be afraid. You have done all this evil; yet do not turn away from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[21] Do not turn aside after empty things that cannot profit or deliver, for they are empty.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[22] For the sake of his great name the LORD will not abandon his people, because it pleased the LORD to make you his own people.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[23] As for me, far be it from me to sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you. I will teach you the good and right way.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[24] Only fear the LORD and serve him faithfully with all your heart; consider what great things he has done for you.
[1 Samuel] [12]:[25] But if you persist in doing evil, both you and your king will be swept away."
[1 Samuel] [13]:[1] Saul was [thirty] years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel [forty-]two years.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew text reads literally "Saul was a year old when he became king, and he reigned two years over Israel." A number appears to have dropped out in the copying of the text; the bracketed numbers are supplied from ancient witnesses and the wider account.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[2] Saul chose three thousand men out of Israel: two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah in Benjamin. The rest of the people he sent home, each to his own tent.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[3] Jonathan struck down the Philistine garrison at Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. Then Saul had the ram's horn sounded throughout the land, saying, "Let the Hebrews hear!"
[1 Samuel] [13]:[4] And all Israel heard the news: "Saul has struck down the Philistine garrison, and now Israel has become a stench to the Philistines." So the people were called out to join Saul at Gilgal.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[5] The Philistines gathered to fight against Israel: thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They came up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[6] When the men of Israel saw that they were in trouble, for the army was hard pressed, the people hid themselves in caves and thickets, among rocks, in vaults and cisterns.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[7] Some Hebrews even crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. Saul was still at Gilgal, and all the people who followed him were trembling.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[8] He waited seven days, the time Samuel had set, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people began to slip away from him.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[9] So Saul said, "Bring me the burnt offering and the fellowship offerings." And he offered up the burnt offering.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[10] Just as he finished offering the burnt offering, Samuel arrived, and Saul went out to meet him and greet him.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[11] Samuel said, "What have you done?" Saul answered, "When I saw that the people were slipping away from me, and that you did not come at the appointed time, and that the Philistines were massing at Michmash,
[1 Samuel] [13]:[12] I thought, 'Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the LORD's favor.' So I forced myself and offered the burnt offering."
[1 Samuel] [13]:[13] Samuel said to Saul, "You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the command the LORD your God gave you. If you had, the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[14] But now your kingdom will not endure. The LORD has sought out a man after his own heart and appointed him ruler over his people, because you have not kept what the LORD commanded you."
[1 Samuel] [13]:[15] Then Samuel set out and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah in Benjamin. Saul mustered the troops who were with him, about six hundred men.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[16] Saul, his son Jonathan, and the troops with them were stationed at Geba in Benjamin, while the Philistines camped at Michmash.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[17] Raiders went out from the Philistine camp in three companies. One turned toward Ophrah, in the land of Shual;
[1 Samuel] [13]:[18] another turned toward Beth-horon; and the third turned toward the border overlooking the Valley of Zeboim, facing the wilderness.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[19] No blacksmith could be found anywhere in the land of Israel, for the Philistines had said, "The Hebrews must not be allowed to make swords or spears!"
[1 Samuel] [13]:[20] So all Israel had to go down to the Philistines to have their plowshares, mattocks, axes, and sickles sharpened.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[21] The charge was two-thirds of a shekel for sharpening plowshares and mattocks, and a third of a shekel for pitchforks and axes, and for resetting a goad.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew names a weight called a *pim*, about two-thirds of a shekel. This verse is difficult, and the weights given are estimates.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[22] So on the day of battle not a sword or spear could be found in the hand of any of the men with Saul and Jonathan; only Saul and his son Jonathan had them.
[1 Samuel] [13]:[23] And a detachment of Philistines went out to the pass at Michmash.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[1] One day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man who carried his armor, "Come, let's cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side." But he did not tell his father.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[2] Saul was staying on the outskirts of Gibeah, under the pomegranate tree at Migron, and the troops with him numbered about six hundred men.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[3] Among them was Ahijah son of Ahitub, the brother of Ichabod son of Phinehas son of Eli, the LORD's priest at Shiloh; he was wearing the ephod. No one knew that Jonathan had gone.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[4] In the pass that Jonathan meant to cross to reach the Philistine outpost there was a rocky crag on one side and a rocky crag on the other. The name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[5] One crag rose up on the north, facing Michmash, and the other on the south, facing Geba.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[6] Jonathan said to the young man who carried his armor, "Come, let's cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the LORD will act for us, for nothing can keep the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few."
[1 Samuel] [14]:[7] His armor-bearer answered him, "Do everything that is in your heart. Go ahead—I am with you, heart and soul."
[1 Samuel] [14]:[8] Jonathan said, "Here is what we will do: we will cross over to those men and let them see us.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[9] If they say to us, 'Wait until we come to you,' then we will stay where we are and not go up to them.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[10] But if they say, 'Come up to us,' then we will climb up, for the LORD has given them into our hand. That will be our sign."
[1 Samuel] [14]:[11] So the two of them showed themselves to the Philistine outpost, and the Philistines said, "Look, the Hebrews are crawling out of the holes where they've been hiding!"
[1 Samuel] [14]:[12] The men of the outpost called out to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, "Come up to us, and we'll teach you a lesson!" Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, "Climb up behind me, for the LORD has given them into the hand of Israel."
[1 Samuel] [14]:[13] Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armor-bearer behind him. The Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer came behind and finished them off.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[14] In that first attack Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men within an area of about half an acre.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[15] Then panic spread through the camp, the field, and all the troops. The outpost and the raiding parties trembled too; the earth shook, and it became a terror from God.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[16] Saul's lookouts at Gibeah in Benjamin saw the multitude melting away and scattering in every direction.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[17] Saul said to the troops with him, "Call the roll and find out who has left us." When they had counted, Jonathan and his armor-bearer were missing.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[18] Saul said to Ahijah, "Bring the ark of God here"—for at that time the ark of God was with the Israelites. [Footnote: Some ancient witnesses read "ephod" instead of "ark of God," which fits the reference to Ahijah's ephod in verse 3 and Saul's words in verse 19.]
[1 Samuel] [14]:[19] But while Saul was still speaking to the priest, the tumult in the Philistine camp grew louder and louder. So Saul said to the priest, "Withdraw your hand."
[1 Samuel] [14]:[20] Then Saul and all his men rallied and went into the battle, and there they found the Philistines turning their swords against each other in utter confusion.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[21] The Hebrews who had earlier been with the Philistines and had gone up with them into their camp now went over to the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[22] And when all the men of Israel who had hidden in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were fleeing, they too joined the pursuit in the battle.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[23] So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the fighting moved on beyond Beth Aven.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[24] The men of Israel were hard pressed that day, because Saul had bound the troops with an oath: "Cursed be anyone who eats food before evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies." So none of the troops tasted any food.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[25] The whole army came into a forest, and there was honey on the ground.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[26] When the men entered the forest, they saw the honey flowing, yet no one put his hand to his mouth, because they feared the oath.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[27] But Jonathan had not heard his father bind the people with the oath. He reached out the tip of the staff in his hand, dipped it into the honeycomb, and raised his hand to his mouth—and his eyes brightened.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[28] Then one of the soldiers spoke up: "Your father bound the troops with a solemn oath, saying, 'Cursed be anyone who eats food today.'" And the men were exhausted.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[29] Jonathan said, "My father has brought trouble on the land. See how my eyes brightened when I tasted a little of this honey.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[30] How much better it would have been if the men had eaten freely today from the plunder they took from their enemies! Would not the slaughter of the Philistines have been even greater?"
[1 Samuel] [14]:[31] That day they struck down the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon, and the men were utterly worn out.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[32] They pounced on the plunder, taking sheep, cattle, and calves; they slaughtered them on the ground and ate the meat with the blood still in it.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[33] Then Saul was told, "Look, the men are sinning against the LORD by eating meat with the blood in it." He said, "You have broken faith. Roll a large stone over to me at once."
[1 Samuel] [14]:[34] Then Saul said, "Go among the troops and tell them, 'Each of you bring me your ox or your sheep, and slaughter it here and eat it. Do not sin against the LORD by eating meat with the blood in it.'" So that night everyone brought his ox and slaughtered it there.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[35] Then Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first altar he built to the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[36] Saul said, "Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until dawn, and let us not leave one of them alive." "Do whatever seems best to you," they answered. But the priest said, "Let us inquire of God here."
[1 Samuel] [14]:[37] So Saul asked God, "Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will you give them into Israel's hand?" But God did not answer him that day.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[38] Saul said, "Come here, all you leaders of the army; look into it and see how this sin came about today.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[39] As surely as the LORD lives, who saves Israel—even if it lies with my son Jonathan, he must die." But not one of the men said a word.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[40] Then he said to all Israel, "You stand on one side, and I and my son Jonathan will stand on the other." "Do what seems best to you," the men replied.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[41] Then Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, "Give a perfect answer." Jonathan and Saul were taken, and the troops went free.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[42] Saul said, "Cast the lot between me and my son Jonathan." And Jonathan was taken.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[43] Then Saul said to Jonathan, "Tell me what you have done." So Jonathan told him, "I merely tasted a little honey with the tip of the staff in my hand. And now I must die."
[1 Samuel] [14]:[44] Saul said, "May God deal with me, be it ever so severely, if you do not die, Jonathan."
[1 Samuel] [14]:[45] But the men said to Saul, "Shall Jonathan die—he who has brought about this great deliverance in Israel? Never! As surely as the LORD lives, not a hair of his head shall fall to the ground, for he has done this today with God's help." So the men rescued Jonathan, and he did not die.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[46] Then Saul broke off the pursuit of the Philistines, and the Philistines returned to their own land.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[47] After Saul had taken the kingship over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side: Moab, the Ammonites, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he inflicted punishment.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[48] He fought valiantly, struck down the Amalekites, and delivered Israel from the hands of those who had plundered them.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[49] Saul's sons were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchishua. The name of his older daughter was Merab, and the name of the younger was Michal.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[50] His wife's name was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. The commander of his army was Abner son of Ner, Saul's uncle.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[51] Kish, Saul's father, and Ner, Abner's father, were sons of Abiel.
[1 Samuel] [14]:[52] All the days of Saul there was bitter war with the Philistines, and whenever Saul saw a mighty or valiant man, he took him into his service.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[1] Samuel said to Saul, "The LORD sent me to anoint you king over his people, over Israel. Now listen to the words of the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[2] This is what the LORD of hosts says: 'I have taken account of what Amalek did to Israel, how they waylaid them on the road when they came up from Egypt.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[3] Now go and strike Amalek. Devote to destruction everything they have. Do not spare them; put to death man and woman, child and infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.'"
[1 Samuel] [15]:[4] So Saul summoned the people and mustered them at Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers, and ten thousand men of Judah.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[5] Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the valley.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[6] And Saul said to the Kenites, "Go, withdraw, get away from among the Amalekites, or I will sweep you away with them. For you showed kindness to all the Israelites when they came up from Egypt." So the Kenites withdrew from among the Amalekites.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[7] Saul struck down the Amalekites from Havilah as far as Shur, which lies east of Egypt.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[8] He took Agag king of Amalek alive, but all the people he devoted to destruction by the edge of the sword.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[9] Saul and the army spared Agag, along with the best of the sheep and cattle, the fattened animals and the lambs—everything of value. These they were unwilling to destroy; but everything despised and worthless they devoted to destruction.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[10] Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel:
[1 Samuel] [15]:[11] "I regret that I made Saul king, for he has turned away from me and has not carried out my commands." Samuel was angered, and he cried out to the LORD all night.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[12] Early in the morning Samuel rose to meet Saul, but he was told, "Saul has gone to Carmel, where he set up a monument in his own honor; then he turned and went on down to Gilgal."
[1 Samuel] [15]:[13] When Samuel reached him, Saul said, "The LORD bless you! I have carried out the LORD's command."
[1 Samuel] [15]:[14] But Samuel said, "Then what is this bleating of sheep in my ears? What is this lowing of cattle that I hear?"
[1 Samuel] [15]:[15] Saul answered, "They were brought from the Amalekites; the troops spared the best of the sheep and cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God. The rest we devoted to destruction."
[1 Samuel] [15]:[16] "Enough!" Samuel said to Saul. "Let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night." "Speak," Saul replied.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[17] Samuel said, "Though you were small in your own eyes, did you not become the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel,
[1 Samuel] [15]:[18] and he sent you on a mission, saying, 'Go and devote to destruction those sinners, the Amalekites; wage war against them until you have wiped them out.'
[1 Samuel] [15]:[19] Why then did you not obey the LORD? Why did you pounce on the plunder and do what is evil in the LORD's sight?"
[1 Samuel] [15]:[20] "But I did obey the LORD," Saul said. "I went on the mission the LORD gave me. I brought back Agag king of Amalek, and I devoted the Amalekites to destruction.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[21] The troops took sheep and cattle from the plunder, the best of what was devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[22] But Samuel said: "Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obeying the voice of the LORD? To obey is better than sacrifice, and to heed is better than the fat of rams.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[23] For rebellion is like the sin of divination, and defiance like the evil of idolatry. Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, he has rejected you as king."
[1 Samuel] [15]:[24] Then Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned. I violated the LORD's command and your instructions, because I was afraid of the people and gave in to them.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[25] Now I beg you, forgive my sin and come back with me, so that I may worship the LORD."
[1 Samuel] [15]:[26] But Samuel said to him, "I will not go back with you. You have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you as king over Israel!"
[1 Samuel] [15]:[27] As Samuel turned to leave, Saul caught hold of the hem of his robe, and it tore.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[28] Samuel said to him, "The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to one of your neighbors—to one better than you.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[29] Moreover, the Glory of Israel does not lie or change his mind; for he is not a man, that he should change his mind.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[30] Saul said, "I have sinned. But please honor me before the elders of my people and before Israel; come back with me, so that I may worship the LORD your God."
[1 Samuel] [15]:[31] So Samuel went back with Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[32] Then Samuel said, "Bring me Agag king of Amalek." Agag came to him confidently, thinking, "Surely the bitterness of death is past."
[1 Samuel] [15]:[33] But Samuel said, "As your sword has made women childless, so will your mother be childless among women." And Samuel cut Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[34] Then Samuel left for Ramah, and Saul went up to his home in Gibeah of Saul.
[1 Samuel] [15]:[35] Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, for Samuel grieved over Saul. And the LORD regretted that he had made Saul king over Israel.
[1 Samuel] [16]:[1] The LORD said to Samuel, "How long will you mourn for Saul, when I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem, for I have chosen one of his sons to be king."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[2] But Samuel said, "How can I go? If Saul hears of it, he will kill me." The LORD said, "Take a heifer with you and say, 'I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.'
[1 Samuel] [16]:[3] Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what to do. You are to anoint for me the one I point out to you."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[4] So Samuel did what the LORD said and went to Bethlehem. The elders of the town came trembling to meet him and asked, "Do you come in peace?"
[1 Samuel] [16]:[5] "In peace," he answered. "I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice." Then he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.
[1 Samuel] [16]:[6] When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and thought, "Surely here before the LORD stands his anointed one."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[7] But the LORD said to Samuel, "Do not look at his appearance or his height, for I have rejected him. The LORD does not see as man sees: man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[8] Then Jesse called Abinadab and had him pass before Samuel. But Samuel said, "The LORD has not chosen this one either."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[9] Jesse then had Shammah pass by, but Samuel said, "The LORD has not chosen this one either."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[10] Jesse had seven of his sons pass before Samuel, but Samuel said to him, "The LORD has not chosen these."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[11] So he asked Jesse, "Are these all the young men you have?" "There is still the youngest," Jesse answered. "He is out tending the sheep." Samuel said, "Send for him. We will not sit down until he comes here."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[12] So he sent for him and brought him in. He had a ruddy complexion, fine eyes, and a handsome face. And the LORD said, "Rise and anoint him; this is the one."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[13] So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and from that day on the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon David. Then Samuel set out and returned to Ramah.
[1 Samuel] [16]:[14] Now the Spirit of the LORD had departed from Saul, and a harmful spirit from the LORD tormented him.
[1 Samuel] [16]:[15] Saul's servants said to him, "Look, an evil spirit from God is tormenting you.
[1 Samuel] [16]:[16] Let our lord give the word, and your servants here will look for someone who knows how to play the lyre. When the evil spirit from God comes upon you, he will play, and you will feel better."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[17] So Saul said to his servants, "Find me someone who plays well and bring him to me."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[18] One of the young men answered, "I have seen a son of Jesse of Bethlehem who knows how to play. He is a brave man and a warrior, wise in speech and handsome, and the LORD is with him."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[19] Then Saul sent messengers to Jesse with this word: "Send me your son David, who is with the sheep."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[20] So Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine, and a young goat, and sent them to Saul with his son David.
[1 Samuel] [16]:[21] David came to Saul and entered his service. Saul loved him dearly, and David became one of his armor-bearers.
[1 Samuel] [16]:[22] Then Saul sent word to Jesse: "Let David remain in my service, for I am pleased with him."
[1 Samuel] [16]:[23] Whenever the spirit from God came upon Saul, David would take his lyre and play, and Saul would find relief and feel better, and the evil spirit would leave him.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[1] The Philistines gathered their forces for war. They assembled at Socoh in Judah and camped between Socoh and Azekah, at Ephes Dammim.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[2] Saul and the men of Israel gathered as well; they camped in the Valley of Elah and drew up their lines to meet the Philistines.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[3] The Philistines held one hill and the Israelites another, with the valley between them.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[4] Then a champion came out from the Philistine camp. His name was Goliath, from Gath, and he stood six cubits and a span tall.[fn]
[1 Samuel] [17]:[5] He wore a bronze helmet on his head and a coat of scale armor weighing five thousand shekels of bronze.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[6] He had bronze greaves on his legs and a bronze javelin slung across his shoulders.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[7] The shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam, and its iron point weighed six hundred shekels. A shield bearer went ahead of him.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[8] He stood and shouted to the ranks of Israel, "Why have you come out to draw up for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and are you not the servants of Saul? Choose a man and send him down to me.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[9] If he can fight me and kill me, we will become your servants. But if I overcome him and kill him, you will become our servants and serve us."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[10] And the Philistine said, "This day I defy the ranks of Israel! Give me a man, and let the two of us fight."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[11] When Saul and all Israel heard the Philistine's words, they were shaken and terrified.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[12] Now David was the son of an Ephrathite from Bethlehem in Judah named Jesse, who had eight sons. In Saul's day Jesse was old, well advanced in years.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[13] Jesse's three oldest sons had gone with Saul to the war. The names of the three who went to battle were Eliab the firstborn, Abinadab the second, and Shammah the third.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[14] David was the youngest. The three oldest had followed Saul,
[1 Samuel] [17]:[15] but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father's sheep at Bethlehem.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[16] For forty days the Philistine came forward morning and evening and took his stand.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[17] Jesse said to his son David, "Take this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers, and hurry to their camp.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[18] Take these ten cuts of cheese to the commander of their thousand. See how your brothers are and bring back some token from them.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[19] Saul and your brothers and all the men of Israel are in the Valley of Elah, fighting the Philistines."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[20] Early the next morning David left the flock with a keeper, loaded up, and set out as Jesse had told him. He reached the camp just as the army was moving into position, shouting the battle cry.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[21] Israel and the Philistines drew up their lines facing each other.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[22] David left his supplies with the keeper of the baggage, ran to the battle line, and greeted his brothers.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[23] As he was talking with them, the champion stepped out from the Philistine ranks—Goliath the Philistine from Gath—and shouted his usual challenge, and David heard it.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[24] When the men of Israel saw the man, they all fled from him in great fear.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[25] The Israelites had been saying, "Do you see this man who keeps coming out? He comes out to defy Israel. The king will give great wealth to the man who kills him. He will also give him his daughter in marriage and exempt his father's family from taxes in Israel."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[26] David asked the men standing near him, "What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and removes this disgrace from Israel? Who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the ranks of the living God?"
[1 Samuel] [17]:[27] They repeated to him what they had been saying: "This is what will be done for the man who kills him."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[28] When Eliab, his oldest brother, heard him speaking with the men, he burned with anger at David and said, "Why have you come down here? And who did you leave those few sheep with in the wilderness? I know how conceited you are and how wicked your heart is; you came down only to watch the battle."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[29] "What have I done now?" said David. "Can't I even ask a question?"
[1 Samuel] [17]:[30] He turned away to someone else and asked the same thing, and the men gave him the same answer as before.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[31] What David had said was repeated and reported to Saul, and Saul sent for him.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[32] David said to Saul, "Let no one lose heart on account of this Philistine. Your servant will go and fight him."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[33] Saul replied, "You cannot go out against this Philistine and fight him. You are only a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[34] But David said to Saul, "Your servant has been tending his father's sheep. When a lion or a bear came and carried off a lamb from the flock,
[1 Samuel] [17]:[35] I went after it, struck it down, and rescued the lamb from its mouth. When it turned on me, I seized it by the mane, struck it, and killed it.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[36] Your servant has killed both lion and bear, and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, because he has defied the armies of the living God.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[37] David went on, "The LORD, who rescued me from the paw of the lion and the paw of the bear, will rescue me from the hand of this Philistine." Saul said to David, "Go, and may the LORD be with you."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[38] Then Saul dressed David in his own tunic, put a bronze helmet on his head, and clothed him with a coat of armor.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[39] David strapped Saul's sword over the tunic and tried to walk, but he was not used to it. "I cannot go in these," he said to Saul, "I'm not used to them." So he took them off.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[40] He took his staff in his hand, chose five smooth stones from the stream, put them in the pouch of his shepherd's bag, and with his sling in his hand approached the Philistine.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[41] The Philistine came steadily closer to David, with his shield bearer ahead of him.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[42] When the Philistine looked and saw David, he despised him, for he was only a boy, ruddy and handsome.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[43] He said to David, "Am I a dog, that you come at me with sticks?" And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[44] "Come here," he said, "and I'll give your flesh to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the field."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[45] David answered, "You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[46] This very day the LORD will hand you over to me. I will strike you down and cut off your head, and this day I will give the corpses of the Philistine army to the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth. Then the whole earth will know that Israel has a God,
[1 Samuel] [17]:[47] and all who are gathered here will know that the LORD does not save with sword or spear. The battle belongs to the LORD, and he will hand you over to us."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[48] When the Philistine rose and came forward to meet David, David hurried and ran toward the battle line to face the Philistine.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[49] Reaching into his bag, David took out a stone, slung it, and struck the Philistine on the forehead. The stone sank into his forehead, and he fell facedown on the ground.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[50] So David triumphed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone; he struck him down and killed him, though he had no sword in his hand.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[51] David ran and stood over him, took hold of the Philistine's sword and drew it from its sheath, finished him off, and cut off his head with it. When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they fled.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[52] Then the men of Israel and Judah surged forward with a shout and pursued the Philistines to the entrance of Gath* and to the gates of Ekron. *The Hebrew text reads "Gai"; some ancient witnesses read "Gath."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[53] When the Israelites returned from chasing the Philistines, they plundered their camp.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[54] David took the Philistine's head and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put the man's weapons in his own tent.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[55] As Saul watched David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner, the commander of the army, "Abner, whose son is that young man?" Abner answered, "As surely as you live, my king, I do not know."
[1 Samuel] [17]:[56] "Find out whose son this young man is," the king said.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[57] As soon as David returned from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with the Philistine's head still in his hand.
[1 Samuel] [17]:[58] "Whose son are you, young man?" Saul asked him. David answered, "I am the son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem."
[1 Samuel] [18]:[1] When David had finished speaking with Saul, Jonathan's soul was bound to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[2] From that day on Saul kept David with him and would not let him return to his father's house.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[3] Jonathan made a covenant with David, because he loved him as his own soul.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[4] Jonathan took off the robe he was wearing and gave it to David, along with his armor, his sword, his bow, and his belt.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[5] David went out wherever Saul sent him, and he succeeded. So Saul put him in command of the fighting men, and this pleased all the people, and Saul's officers as well.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[6] As they were coming home, when David returned from killing the Philistine, the women came out of all the towns of Israel to meet King Saul with singing and dancing, with tambourines and rejoicing and three-stringed instruments.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[7] And the women sang to one another as they celebrated: "Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his tens of thousands."
[1 Samuel] [18]:[8] Saul was furious; this saying displeased him deeply. "They have credited David with tens of thousands," he said, "but me with only thousands. What more can he have but the kingdom?"
[1 Samuel] [18]:[9] And from that day on Saul kept a jealous eye on David.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[10] The next day an evil spirit from God came powerfully upon Saul, and he raved inside the house while David was playing the lyre, as he did day after day. Saul had a spear in his hand,
[1 Samuel] [18]:[11] and he hurled it, saying to himself, "I will pin David to the wall." But David eluded him twice.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[12] Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with him but had departed from Saul.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[13] So Saul sent him away from his presence and made him a commander over a thousand, and David led the troops out and brought them back.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[14] In everything he did David had great success, for the LORD was with him.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[15] When Saul saw how successful he was, he was afraid of him.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[16] But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he led them out and brought them back.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[17] Saul said to David, "Here is my older daughter Merab. I will give her to you as your wife; only serve me bravely and fight the LORD's battles." For Saul thought, "I will not lay a hand on him; let the hand of the Philistines be on him."
[1 Samuel] [18]:[18] But David said to Saul, "Who am I, and what is my family, my father's clan in Israel, that I should become the king's son-in-law?"
[1 Samuel] [18]:[19] So when the time came for Merab, Saul's daughter, to be given to David, she was given in marriage to Adriel of Meholah instead.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[20] Now Saul's daughter Michal was in love with David, and when Saul was told of it, he was pleased.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[21] "I will give her to him," Saul thought, "so that she may be a snare to him and the hand of the Philistines may be against him." So Saul said to David, "Now you have a second chance to become my son-in-law."
[1 Samuel] [18]:[22] Then Saul ordered his servants, "Speak to David privately and say, 'Look, the king is pleased with you, and all his servants love you. Now become his son-in-law.'"
[1 Samuel] [18]:[23] They repeated these words to David, but David said, "Do you think it is a small thing to become the king's son-in-law? I am a poor man, and little known."
[1 Samuel] [18]:[24] When Saul's servants reported to him what David had said,
[1 Samuel] [18]:[25] Saul replied, "Say this to David: 'The king wants no other bride-price than a hundred Philistine foreskins, to take revenge on the king's enemies.'" Saul's plan was to have David fall by the hands of the Philistines.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[26] When the servants told David these things, he was pleased to become the king's son-in-law. Before the time had expired,
[1 Samuel] [18]:[27] David went out with his men and killed two hundred Philistines. He brought their foreskins and counted them out in full before the king, so that he might become the king's son-in-law. Then Saul gave him his daughter Michal as his wife.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[28] When Saul saw and knew that the LORD was with David, and that his daughter Michal loved him,
[1 Samuel] [18]:[29] Saul feared David all the more, and he remained David's enemy the rest of his days.
[1 Samuel] [18]:[30] Whenever the Philistine commanders came out to fight, David was more successful than all the rest of Saul's officers, and his name became highly honored.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[1] Saul told his son Jonathan and all his servants to kill David. But Jonathan, Saul's son, was very fond of David,
[1 Samuel] [19]:[2] so he warned him: "My father Saul is looking for a chance to kill you. Be on your guard tomorrow morning; find a hiding place and stay out of sight.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[3] I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are, and I will speak to him about you. Whatever I find out, I will tell you.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[4] So Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul. He said to him, "Let the king not sin against his servant David, for he has not sinned against you. What he has done has been of great benefit to you.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[5] He took his life in his hands when he struck down the Philistine, and the LORD brought about a great victory for all Israel. You saw it, and you rejoiced. Why then would you sin against innocent blood by killing David without cause?"
[1 Samuel] [19]:[6] Saul listened to Jonathan and swore, "As the LORD lives, he will not be put to death."
[1 Samuel] [19]:[7] Then Jonathan called David and told him everything that had been said. He brought David to Saul, and David served him as before.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[8] War broke out again. David went out to fight the Philistines and struck them such a heavy blow that they fled before him.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[9] But an evil spirit from the LORD came over Saul as he sat in his house with his spear in his hand, while David was playing the lyre.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[10] Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David slipped away from him, and the spear drove into the wall. David fled and escaped that night.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[11] Saul sent messengers to David's house to watch it and to kill him in the morning. But Michal, David's wife, warned him, "If you don't get away tonight, tomorrow you will be dead."
[1 Samuel] [19]:[12] So Michal let David down through a window, and he ran away and escaped.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[13] Then Michal took the household idol, laid it on the bed, put a quilt of goats' hair at its head, and covered it with a garment.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[14] When Saul sent messengers to seize David, she said, "He is sick."
[1 Samuel] [19]:[15] Saul sent the messengers back to see David, saying, "Bring him up to me in his bed so I can kill him."
[1 Samuel] [19]:[16] But when the messengers came in, there was the household idol in the bed with the quilt of goats' hair at its head.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[17] Saul said to Michal, "Why have you deceived me like this and let my enemy get away?" Michal answered, "He said to me, 'Let me go. Why should I kill you?'"
[1 Samuel] [19]:[18] David fled and escaped. He came to Samuel at Ramah and told him everything Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel went to Naioth and stayed there.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[19] Saul was told, "David is at Naioth in Ramah."
[1 Samuel] [19]:[20] So Saul sent messengers to seize David. But when they saw the company of prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing there as their leader, the Spirit of God came upon Saul's messengers, and they also prophesied.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[21] When Saul was told, he sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. Saul sent messengers a third time, and they also prophesied.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[22] Finally he went to Ramah himself. When he came to the great cistern at Secu, he asked, "Where are Samuel and David?" "At Naioth in Ramah," someone said.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[23] So he went on toward Naioth in Ramah. But the Spirit of God came upon him too, and he walked along prophesying until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
[1 Samuel] [19]:[24] He too stripped off his clothes and prophesied before Samuel, and he lay naked all that day and all that night. That is why people say, "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
[1 Samuel] [20]:[1] David fled from Naioth in Ramah. He came to Jonathan and said, "What have I done? What is my guilt, and what is my sin against your father, that he is trying to take my life?"
[1 Samuel] [20]:[2] Jonathan said to him, "Never! You will not die. Look, my father does nothing, great or small, without telling me. Why would he hide this from me? It isn't so."
[1 Samuel] [20]:[3] But David swore again and said, "Your father knows perfectly well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he has said, 'Jonathan must not know this, or he will be grieved.' Yet as surely as the LORD lives and as you live, there is only a step between me and death."
[1 Samuel] [20]:[4] Jonathan said to David, "Whatever you want, I will do for you."
[1 Samuel] [20]:[5] David said to Jonathan, "Tomorrow is the new moon, and I am supposed to sit and eat with the king. Let me go, and I will hide in the field until the evening of the third day.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[6] If your father misses me at all, say, 'David urgently begged my permission to hurry to Bethlehem, his hometown, because his whole clan is holding its yearly sacrifice there.'
[1 Samuel] [20]:[7] If he says, 'Fine,' then your servant is safe. But if he flares up in anger, you will know he is set on doing me harm.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[8] So show kindness to your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant with you before the LORD. If I am guilty of anything, then kill me yourself—why bring me to your father?"
[1 Samuel] [20]:[9] Jonathan said, "Never! If I learn that my father is determined to harm you, I will surely tell you."
[1 Samuel] [20]:[10] David asked Jonathan, "Who will let me know if your father answers you harshly?"
[1 Samuel] [20]:[11] Jonathan said to David, "Come, let's go out to the field." So the two of them went out to the field.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[12] Then Jonathan said to David, "By the LORD, the God of Israel: when I have sounded out my father, by this time tomorrow or the day after, if he is favorable toward you, I will surely send word and let you know.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[13] But if my father intends to harm you, may the LORD deal with me severely if I do not let you know and send you safely on your way. May the LORD be with you as he has been with my father.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[14] And as long as I live, show me the LORD's own faithful love; and if I die,
[1 Samuel] [20]:[15] never cut off your kindness from my family—not even when the LORD has cut off every one of David's enemies from the face of the earth."
[1 Samuel] [20]:[16] So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, "May the LORD call David's enemies to account."
[1 Samuel] [20]:[17] And Jonathan had David swear again, out of his love for him, for he loved him as he loved his own life.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[18] Then Jonathan said to him, "Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed, because your place will be empty.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[19] The day after tomorrow, go to the place where you hid before, and wait there by the stone Ezel.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[20] I will shoot three arrows off to the side, as though I were shooting at a target.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[21] Then I will send the boy: 'Go, find the arrows.' If I say to him, 'The arrows are on this side of you; bring them here,' then come, for it is safe for you—as surely as the LORD lives, there is no danger.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[22] But if I say to the young man, 'The arrows are beyond you,' then go, for the LORD has sent you away.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[23] And about the matter you and I have spoken of—the LORD is witness between you and me forever."
[1 Samuel] [20]:[24] So David hid in the field. When the new moon came, the king sat down to eat.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[25] He sat in his usual place by the wall. Jonathan rose, and Abner sat down beside Saul; but David's place was empty.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[26] Saul said nothing that day, for he thought, "Something has happened to make him unclean—surely he is unclean."
[1 Samuel] [20]:[27] But the next day, the second day of the month, David's place was empty again. So Saul asked his son Jonathan, "Why hasn't the son of Jesse come to the meal, either yesterday or today?"
[1 Samuel] [20]:[28] Jonathan answered Saul, "David earnestly asked my permission to go to Bethlehem.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[29] He said, 'Please let me go, because our family is holding a sacrifice in the town and my brother has ordered me to be there. If I have found favor in your eyes, let me get away to see my brothers.' That is why he has not come to the king's table."
[1 Samuel] [20]:[30] Then Saul's anger flared up against Jonathan, and he said to him, "You son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Don't I know that you have sided with the son of Jesse, to your own shame and to the shame of the mother who bore you?
[1 Samuel] [20]:[31] As long as the son of Jesse lives on this earth, neither you nor your kingdom will be secure. Now send for him and bring him to me, for he must die!"
[1 Samuel] [20]:[32] Jonathan answered his father Saul, "Why should he be put to death? What has he done?"
[1 Samuel] [20]:[33] At that Saul hurled his spear at him to strike him down—and Jonathan knew that his father was determined to kill David.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[34] Jonathan got up from the table in fierce anger. He ate no food that second day of the month, for he was grieved over David and over the way his father had disgraced him.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[35] In the morning Jonathan went out to the field to meet David, and a young boy was with him.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[36] He said to the boy, "Run and find the arrows I shoot." As the boy ran, he shot an arrow beyond him.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[37] When the boy came to the place where Jonathan's arrow had fallen, Jonathan called after him, "Isn't the arrow beyond you?"
[1 Samuel] [20]:[38] Then Jonathan called after the boy, "Hurry! Be quick! Don't stop!" And the boy picked up the arrows and came back to his master.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[39] The boy knew nothing of all this; only Jonathan and David knew the matter.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[40] Then Jonathan handed his weapons to the boy and told him, "Go, take them back to town."
[1 Samuel] [20]:[41] When the boy had gone, David rose from his hiding place to the south, fell facedown on the ground, and bowed three times. Then they kissed each other and wept together—David wept the longest.
[1 Samuel] [20]:[42] Jonathan said to David, "Go in peace. We have both sworn in the name of the LORD, saying, 'The LORD be between you and me, and between your descendants and mine, forever.'"
[1 Samuel] [21]:[1] Then David rose and went, and Jonathan went back into the city.
[1 Samuel] [21]:[2] David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech came trembling to meet him and asked, "Why are you alone? Why is no one with you?"
[1 Samuel] [21]:[3] David answered Ahimelech the priest, "The king has given me a commission and told me, 'No one is to know anything about the mission I am sending you on, or about my orders.' As for my men, I have arranged to meet them at a certain place.
[1 Samuel] [21]:[4] Now then, what do you have on hand? Give me five loaves of bread, or whatever you can find."
[1 Samuel] [21]:[5] The priest answered David, "I have no ordinary bread on hand—only holy bread, provided the men have kept themselves from women."
[1 Samuel] [21]:[6] David answered the priest, "Truly, women have been kept from us, as always when I set out. The men's gear is holy even on an ordinary journey; how much more today will it be holy!"
[1 Samuel] [21]:[7] So the priest gave him the holy bread, since there was none there but the bread of the Presence, which had been removed from before the LORD and replaced with fresh, warm bread on the day it was taken away.
[1 Samuel] [21]:[8] Now one of Saul's servants was there that day, detained before the LORD. His name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief of Saul's shepherds.
[1 Samuel] [21]:[9] David asked Ahimelech, "Do you have a spear or a sword here on hand? I brought neither my sword nor my weapons with me, because the king's business was urgent."
[1 Samuel] [21]:[10] The priest said, "The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the Valley of Elah, is here, wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. Take it, if you want it—there is no other here but that one." David said, "There is none like it. Give it to me."
[1 Samuel] [21]:[11] That day David rose and fled from Saul, and he came to Achish king of Gath.
[1 Samuel] [21]:[12] But the servants of Achish said to him, "Isn't this David, the king of the land? Isn't he the one they sang of in their dances: 'Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"
[1 Samuel] [21]:[13] David took these words to heart and became very afraid of Achish king of Gath.
[1 Samuel] [21]:[14] So he pretended to be out of his mind in their presence and acted like a madman among them, making marks on the doors of the gate and letting his spittle run down his beard.
[1 Samuel] [21]:[15] Achish said to his servants, "Look at him—the man is insane! Why bring him to me?
[1 Samuel] [21]:[16] Am I short of madmen, that you bring this one to rave in my presence? Is he to come into my house?"
[1 Samuel] [22]:[1] David left there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and his father's whole household heard of it, they went down to him there.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[2] Everyone in distress, everyone in debt, everyone bitter in spirit gathered to him, and he became their commander. About four hundred men were with him.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[3] From there David went to Mizpeh in Moab and said to the king of Moab, "Please let my father and mother come and stay with you until I know what God will do for me."
[1 Samuel] [22]:[4] So he left them with the king of Moab, and they stayed with him the whole time David was in the stronghold.
