[1 Samuel] [22]:[5] But the prophet Gad said to David, "Do not stay in the stronghold. Go to the land of Judah." So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[6] Saul heard that David and the men with him had been discovered. Saul was sitting at Gibeah under the tamarisk tree on the height, spear in hand, with all his servants standing around him.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[7] Saul said to the servants standing around him, "Listen now, men of Benjamin! Will the son of Jesse give all of you fields and vineyards? Will he make all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?
[1 Samuel] [22]:[8] Yet all of you have conspired against me, and no one told me when my own son made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Not one of you is concerned for me or tells me that my son has stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as he does today."
[1 Samuel] [22]:[9] Then Doeg the Edomite, who was standing with Saul's servants, answered, "I saw the son of Jesse come to Nob, to Ahimelech son of Ahitub.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[10] Ahimelech inquired of the LORD for him, gave him provisions, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine."
[1 Samuel] [22]:[11] The king sent for Ahimelech the priest, son of Ahitub, and for his father's whole household, the priests at Nob, and they all came to the king.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[12] Saul said, "Listen now, son of Ahitub." He answered, "Here I am, my lord."
[1 Samuel] [22]:[13] Saul said to him, "Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse—giving him bread and a sword and inquiring of God for him, so that he could rise against me and lie in wait, as he does today?"
[1 Samuel] [22]:[14] Ahimelech answered the king, "Who among all your servants is as trustworthy as David? He is the king's son-in-law, he obeys your every command, and he is honored in your house.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[15] Is today the first time I have inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let the king not charge his servant or anyone in my father's household with anything, for your servant knew nothing of all this, small or great.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[16] But the king said, "You shall surely die, Ahimelech—you and your father's whole household."
[1 Samuel] [22]:[17] And the king ordered the guards standing beside him, "Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too have sided with David. They knew he was fleeing and did not tell me." But the king's servants would not raise a hand to strike down the priests of the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[18] Then the king said to Doeg, "You turn and strike down the priests." So Doeg the Edomite turned and struck them down. That day he killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[19] He also put Nob, the town of the priests, to the sword—men and women, children and infants, oxen, donkeys, and sheep.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[20] But one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped and fled to David.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[21] Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[22] Then David said to Abiathar, "That day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, I knew he would be sure to tell Saul. I am responsible for every life in your father's household.
[1 Samuel] [22]:[23] Stay with me; do not be afraid. The one who seeks my life seeks yours as well. With me you will be safe."
[1 Samuel] [23]:[1] They told David, "The Philistines are attacking Keilah and looting the threshing floors."

[1 Samuel] [23]:[3] But David's men said to him, "Look, even here in Judah we live in fear. How much worse if we go to Keilah against the Philistine battle lines!"

[1 Samuel] [24]:[1] David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En-gedi.

[1 Samuel] [24]:[6] Afterward David's conscience struck him because he had cut off the corner of Saul's robe.
[1 Samuel] [24]:[7] He said to his men, "The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my lord, the LORD's anointed, or lift my hand against him; for he is the LORD's anointed."
[1 Samuel] [24]:[8] With these words David held his men back and would not let them attack Saul. And Saul left the cave and went on his way.
[1 Samuel] [24]:[9] Then David got up, went out of the cave, and called after Saul, "My lord the king!" When Saul looked behind him, David bowed with his face to the ground and paid him homage.
[1 Samuel] [24]:[10] David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to men who say, 'David is out to harm you'?
[1 Samuel] [24]:[11] This very day your own eyes have seen how the LORD gave you into my hand in the cave. I was urged to kill you, but I spared you. I said, 'I will not lift my hand against my lord, for he is the LORD's anointed.'
[1 Samuel] [24]:[12] See, my father—yes, see the corner of your robe in my hand! For I cut off the corner of your robe and did not kill you. Know and see that there is no evil or rebellion in my hand. I have not sinned against you, yet you are hunting me down to take my life.
[1 Samuel] [24]:[13] May the LORD judge between me and you, and may the LORD avenge me on you; but my own hand will not touch you.
[1 Samuel] [24]:[14] As the old proverb says, 'From the wicked comes wickedness.' But my hand will not touch you.
[1 Samuel] [24]:[15] Against whom has the king of Israel marched out? Whom are you chasing? A dead dog! A single flea!
[1 Samuel] [24]:[16] May the LORD be the judge and decide between me and you. May he look into it, take up my cause, and vindicate me against your hand."
[1 Samuel] [24]:[17] When David had finished saying this to Saul, Saul asked, "Is that your voice, my son David?" And Saul wept aloud.
[1 Samuel] [24]:[18] He said to David, "You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me with good, while I have repaid you with evil.
[1 Samuel] [24]:[19] You have shown today how well you have dealt with me: the LORD handed me over to you, and you did not kill me.
[1 Samuel] [24]:[20] When a man finds his enemy, does he let him go unharmed? May the LORD reward you with good for what you have done for me today.

[1 Samuel] [25]:[1] Samuel died, and all Israel gathered to mourn for him, and they buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David went down to the wilderness of Paran.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[2] There was a man in Maon whose holdings were in Carmel. He was a very wealthy man, with three thousand sheep and a thousand goats, and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[3] The man's name was Nabal, and his wife's name was Abigail. She was intelligent and beautiful, but her husband was harsh and mean in all his dealings. He was a Calebite.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[4] While David was in the wilderness, he heard that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[5] So David sent ten young men and said to them, "Go up to Carmel, and when you come to Nabal, greet him in my name.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[6] Say to him: 'Long life to you! Peace to you, peace to your household, and peace to all that is yours!
[1 Samuel] [25]:[7] I have heard that you are shearing. Now, your shepherds have been with us, and we did them no harm; nothing of theirs went missing the whole time they were in Carmel.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[8] Ask your own servants and they will tell you. So look kindly on my young men, since we have come at a festive time. Please give whatever you can spare to your servants and to your son David.'"
[1 Samuel] [25]:[9] David's young men came and delivered all this to Nabal in David's name, and then they waited.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[10] But Nabal answered David's servants, "Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse? These days there are plenty of servants running away from their masters.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[11] Am I to take my bread and my water and the meat I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men who come from who knows where?"
[1 Samuel] [25]:[12] So David's young men turned back the way they had come, and when they arrived they reported to him everything Nabal had said.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[13] David said to his men, "Strap on your swords!" So each man strapped on his sword, and David strapped on his as well. About four hundred men went up with David, while two hundred stayed behind with the baggage.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[14] Meanwhile, one of the servants told Abigail, Nabal's wife, "David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, and he insulted them.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[15] But those men were very good to us. They did us no harm, and we lost nothing the whole time we moved about with them out in the fields.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[16] They were a wall around us night and day, the whole time we were with them herding the sheep.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[17] Now think carefully about what you should do, because disaster is closing in on our master and his whole household. He is such a scoundrel that no one can reason with him."
[1 Samuel] [25]:[18] Abigail acted quickly. She took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five dressed sheep, five measures of roasted grain, a hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of pressed figs, and loaded them on donkeys.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[19] Then she said to her servants, "Go on ahead of me; I am coming behind you." But she said nothing to her husband Nabal.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[20] As she rode her donkey down under the cover of the hill, David and his men were coming down toward her, and she met them.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[21] Now David had been saying, "It was all for nothing that I protected everything this fellow owns in the wilderness, so that nothing of his went missing. He has repaid me evil for good.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[22] May God deal harshly with David's enemies, and worse still, if by morning I leave even one male alive of all who belong to him!
[1 Samuel] [25]:[23] When Abigail saw David, she quickly got down from her donkey, fell before him with her face to the ground, and bowed low.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[24] She fell at his feet and said, "On me alone, my lord, let the blame fall. Please let your servant speak to you; hear the words of your servant.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[25] Let my lord pay no attention to that worthless man Nabal. He is just what his name says: Nabal, "Fool"—and folly goes with him. But I, your servant, did not see the young men my lord sent.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[26] And now, my lord, as surely as the LORD lives and as you live, the LORD has kept you from shedding blood and from taking vengeance with your own hand. May your enemies and all who seek to harm my lord end up like Nabal.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[27] Let this gift, which your servant has brought to my lord, be given to the young men who follow my lord.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[28] Please forgive your servant's offense. The LORD will surely establish a lasting house for my lord, because my lord fights the battles of the LORD, and no wrong will be found in you as long as you live.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[29] Though someone rises up to pursue you and seek your life, the life of my lord will be bound securely in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God. But the lives of your enemies he will hurl away as from the pocket of a sling.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[30] And when the LORD has done for my lord all the good he has promised, and has appointed you ruler over Israel,
[1 Samuel] [25]:[31] then my lord will have no cause for grief or remorse over having shed blood without cause and having taken vengeance himself. And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, remember your servant.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[32] David said to Abigail, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me today!
[1 Samuel] [25]:[33] Blessed be your good judgment, and blessed be you, for keeping me this day from shedding blood and from avenging myself with my own hand.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[34] As surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives—he has kept me from harming you—if you had not hurried to meet me, not one male of Nabal's household would have been left alive by daybreak." [Footnote: Hebrew idiom, literally "one who urinates against a wall," a blunt expression for a male.]
[1 Samuel] [25]:[35] Then David accepted from her hand what she had brought him and said, "Go home in peace. I have listened to you and granted your request."
[1 Samuel] [25]:[36] When Abigail came to Nabal, he was holding a banquet in his house like a king's feast. He was in high spirits and very drunk, so she told him nothing at all until daybreak.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[37] In the morning, when the wine had left him, his wife told him everything, and his heart failed within him; he became like stone.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[38] About ten days later, the LORD struck Nabal, and he died.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[39] When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, "Blessed be the LORD, who has taken up my cause against the insult I suffered from Nabal, and who has kept his servant from doing wrong. The LORD has brought Nabal's evil down on his own head." Then David sent word to Abigail, asking her to become his wife.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[40] David's servants went to Abigail at Carmel and said to her, "David has sent us to you to take you to him as his wife."
[1 Samuel] [25]:[41] She rose, bowed with her face to the ground, and said, "Here is your servant, ready to be a slave and to wash the feet of my lord's servants."
[1 Samuel] [25]:[42] Abigail quickly got up and mounted her donkey, and with her five maids attending her she followed David's messengers and became his wife.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[43] David had also married Ahinoam of Jezreel, so both of them were his wives.
[1 Samuel] [25]:[44] But Saul had given his daughter Michal, David's wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[1] The Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah and said, "Isn't David hiding on the hill of Hachilah, facing the wasteland?"
[1 Samuel] [26]:[2] So Saul set out and went down to the Wilderness of Ziph with three thousand picked men of Israel, to search for David in the Wilderness of Ziph.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[3] Saul camped on the hill of Hachilah, which faces the wasteland, beside the road. David was staying in the wilderness, and he saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[4] So David sent out scouts and learned that Saul had indeed come.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[5] Then David set out and came to the place where Saul had camped. He saw the spot where Saul was lying, along with Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army. Saul was lying inside the camp's circle, with the troops camped around him.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[6] David turned to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and asked, "Who will go down with me to Saul, into the camp?" Abishai said, "I will go down with you."
[1 Samuel] [26]:[7] So David and Abishai came to the troops by night, and there was Saul, lying asleep inside the camp's circle, his spear stuck in the ground by his head, with Abner and the troops lying around him.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[8] Abishai said to David, "Today God has handed your enemy over to you. Now let me pin him to the ground with the spear—one stroke; I won't need a second."
[1 Samuel] [26]:[9] But David said to Abishai, "Don't destroy him! Who can lift a hand against the LORD's anointed and be innocent?"
[1 Samuel] [26]:[10] And David said, "As surely as the LORD lives, the LORD himself will strike him down—either his day will come and he will die, or he will go into battle and be swept away.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[11] The LORD forbid that I should lift my hand against the LORD's anointed. Now take the spear by his head and the water jug, and let's go."
[1 Samuel] [26]:[12] So David took the spear and the water jug from beside Saul's head, and they left. No one saw, no one knew, no one woke up; they were all asleep, for a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[13] Then David crossed over to the other side and stood on top of the hill at a distance, with a wide gap between them.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[14] David shouted to the troops and to Abner son of Ner, "Aren't you going to answer, Abner?" Abner replied, "Who are you, shouting to the king?"
[1 Samuel] [26]:[15] David said to Abner, "Aren't you a man? Who is like you in Israel? Why, then, didn't you keep watch over your lord the king? Someone came to destroy the king, your lord.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[16] What you have done is not good. As surely as the LORD lives, you all deserve to die, because you did not guard your lord, the LORD's anointed. Now look around—where are the king's spear and the water jug that were by his head?"
[1 Samuel] [26]:[17] Saul recognized David's voice and said, "Is that your voice, my son David?" David answered, "It is my voice, my lord the king."
[1 Samuel] [26]:[18] And he said, "Why is my lord pursuing his servant? What have I done? What wrong am I guilty of?
[1 Samuel] [26]:[19] Now let my lord the king listen to his servant's words: If the LORD has incited you against me, then let him accept an offering. But if it is men who have done it, may they be cursed before the LORD, for they have driven me out today from sharing in the LORD's inheritance, saying, 'Go, serve other gods.'
[1 Samuel] [26]:[20] Now, do not let my blood fall to the ground far from the presence of the LORD. For the king of Israel has come out to hunt a single flea, as one hunts a partridge in the mountains."
[1 Samuel] [26]:[21] Then Saul said, "I have sinned. Come back, my son David. I will never harm you again, because my life was precious in your eyes today. I have acted like a fool and gone terribly wrong."
[1 Samuel] [26]:[22] David answered, "Here is the king's spear. Let one of your young men come over and get it.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[23] The LORD repays every man for his righteousness and faithfulness. The LORD handed you over to me today, but I would not lift my hand against the LORD's anointed.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[24] Just as your life was precious in my eyes today, so may my life be precious in the LORD's eyes, and may he deliver me from every trouble."
[1 Samuel] [26]:[25] Then Saul said to David, "Blessed are you, my son David. You will surely do great things and surely prevail." So David went on his way, and Saul returned home.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[1] David said to himself, "Now, one of these days, I will be swept away by Saul's hand. There is nothing better for me than to escape to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will give up searching for me anywhere in the territory of Israel, and I will slip out of his hand."
[1 Samuel] [27]:[2] So David set out and crossed over, he and the six hundred men with him, to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[3] David settled with Achish in Gath, he and his men, each with his household — David with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, Nabal's widow.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[4] When Saul was told that David had fled to Gath, he searched for him no longer.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[5] David said to Achish, "If I have found favor in your eyes, let me be given a place in one of the outlying towns, so I may live there. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?"
[1 Samuel] [27]:[6] That day Achish gave him Ziklag; and so Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[7] David lived in Philistine territory a year and four months.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[8] David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites — for these were the peoples who from ancient times had inhabited the land stretching toward Shur as far as Egypt.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[9] Whenever David attacked a region, he left neither man nor woman alive; he took sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and clothing, and then returned to Achish.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[10] When Achish asked, "Where did you raid today?" David would answer, "Against the Negev of Judah," or "Against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites," or "Against the Negev of the Kenites."
[1 Samuel] [27]:[11] David would leave neither man nor woman alive to bring back to Gath, for he thought, "They might report on us and say, 'This is what David did.'" Such was his practice the whole time he lived in Philistine territory.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[12] So Achish trusted David, thinking, "He has made himself utterly detestable to his own people Israel; he will be my servant for life."
[1 Samuel] [28]:[1] In those days the Philistines gathered their forces for war against Israel. Achish said to David, "You know, of course, that you and your men are to march out with me in the army."
[1 Samuel] [28]:[2] David answered Achish, "Then you will see for yourself what your servant can do." Achish said to David, "Very well, I will make you my bodyguard for life."
[1 Samuel] [28]:[3] Now Samuel was dead. All Israel had mourned for him and buried him in Ramah, his own town. And Saul had driven the mediums and spiritists out of the land.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[4] The Philistines assembled and came and camped at Shunem, while Saul gathered all Israel and camped at Gilboa.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[5] When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid; terror gripped his heart.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[6] Saul inquired of the LORD, but the LORD gave him no answer—not by dreams, not by Urim, not by prophets.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[7] So Saul said to his servants, "Find me a woman who is a medium, so I can go and consult her." His servants told him, "There is a woman at Endor who is a medium."
[1 Samuel] [28]:[8] So Saul disguised himself, putting on other clothes, and went with two men. They came to the woman at night, and Saul said, "Consult a spirit for me and bring up the one I name."
[1 Samuel] [28]:[9] But the woman said to him, "Surely you know what Saul has done—how he has cut off the mediums and spiritists from the land. Why are you setting a trap for my life, to have me killed?"
[1 Samuel] [28]:[10] Saul swore to her by the LORD, "As surely as the LORD lives, you will not be punished for this."
[1 Samuel] [28]:[11] Then the woman asked, "Whom shall I bring up for you?" "Bring up Samuel," he said.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[12] When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out at the top of her voice and said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!"
[1 Samuel] [28]:[13] The woman answered, "I see a divine being coming up out of the ground." [Footnote: The Hebrew word can mean God, gods, or a spirit being, and the verb here is plural.]
[1 Samuel] [28]:[14] "What does he look like?" he asked. "An old man wrapped in a robe is coming up," she said. Then Saul knew it was Samuel, and he bowed low with his face to the ground.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[15] Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?" "I am in great distress," Saul answered. "The Philistines are attacking me, and God has turned away from me. He no longer answers me, either by prophets or by dreams. So I have called on you to tell me what to do."
[1 Samuel] [28]:[16] Samuel said, "Why ask me, now that the LORD has turned away from you and become your enemy?
[1 Samuel] [28]:[17] The LORD has done to you just as he spoke through me: he has torn the kingdom out of your hand and given it to your neighbor, to David.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[18] Because you did not obey the voice of the LORD and did not carry out his burning anger against Amalek, the LORD has done this to you today.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[19] The LORD will hand both you and Israel over to the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will also hand Israel's army over to the Philistines."
[1 Samuel] [28]:[20] Instantly Saul fell full length on the ground, terrified by Samuel's words. His strength was gone, for he had eaten nothing all that day and all that night.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[21] The woman came to Saul and saw how deeply shaken he was. She said to him, "Look, your servant obeyed you. I took my life in my hands and did what you asked of me.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[22] Now please listen to your servant and let me set a piece of bread before you. Eat, so you will have strength for the journey."
[1 Samuel] [28]:[23] He refused and said, "I will not eat." But his servants joined the woman in urging him, and he listened to them. He got up from the ground and sat on the bed.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[24] The woman had a fattened calf at the house, and she quickly slaughtered it. She took flour, kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[25] Then she set it before Saul and his servants, and they ate. That same night they got up and left.
[1 Samuel] [29]:[1] The Philistines gathered all their forces at Aphek, while Israel camped by the spring in Jezreel.
[1 Samuel] [29]:[2] As the Philistine rulers marched past with their units of hundreds and thousands, David and his men came at the rear with Achish.
[1 Samuel] [29]:[3] The Philistine commanders asked, "What are these Hebrews doing here?" Achish answered them, "This is David, the servant of Saul king of Israel. He has been with me now for days, even years, and from the day he deserted to me until now I have found no fault in him.
[1 Samuel] [29]:[4] But the Philistine commanders were angry with him and said, "Send the man back. Let him return to the place you assigned him. He must not go into battle with us, or he will turn against us in the fighting. How better could he win back his master's favor than with the heads of these men of ours?"
[1 Samuel] [29]:[5] Isn't this the David they sang about in their dances: 'Saul has slain his thousands, and David his tens of thousands'?"
[1 Samuel] [29]:[6] So Achish called David and said to him, "As surely as the LORD lives, you have been honest, and it would please me to have you march out and back with me in the army, for I have found no wrong in you from the day you came to me until now. But the rulers do not approve of you.
[1 Samuel] [29]:[7] Now go back, and go in peace; do nothing to displease the Philistine rulers."
[1 Samuel] [29]:[8] "But what have I done?" David asked. "What have you found against your servant from the day I came to you until now, that I should not go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?"
[1 Samuel] [29]:[9] Achish answered, "I know you are as pleasing to me as an angel of God. But the Philistine commanders have said, 'He must not go up with us into battle.'
[1 Samuel] [29]:[10] So get up early in the morning, you and your master's servants who came with you; set out at daybreak, as soon as it is light, and go."
[1 Samuel] [29]:[11] So David and his men got up early in the morning to return to the land of the Philistines, and the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[1] When David and his men reached Ziklag on the third day, they found that the Amalekites had raided the Negev and Ziklag. They had struck Ziklag and burned it down.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[2] They had taken captive the women who were there, young and old alike, but had killed no one; they drove them off and went on their way.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[3] When David and his men came to the town, there it was, burned to the ground, and their wives, sons, and daughters taken captive.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[4] Then David and the men with him wept aloud until they had no strength left to weep.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[5] David's two wives had also been taken captive—Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal of Carmel.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[6] David was in great distress, for the men were talking of stoning him; every one of them was bitter in spirit over his sons and daughters. But David found strength in the LORD his God.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[7] David said to Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, "Bring me the ephod." So Abiathar brought it to him,
[1 Samuel] [30]:[8] and David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I pursue this raiding party? Will I overtake them?" "Pursue them," he answered. "You will surely overtake them and surely rescue the captives."
[1 Samuel] [30]:[9] So David set out with the six hundred men who were with him, and they came to the Besor Valley, where the rest stayed behind.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[10] David pressed on with four hundred men, while two hundred were too exhausted to cross the Besor Valley and stayed there.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[11] They came across an Egyptian in the open country and brought him to David. They gave him bread to eat and water to drink,
[1 Samuel] [30]:[12] along with a piece of pressed figs and two cakes of raisins. He ate, and his strength returned to him, for he had not eaten bread or drunk water for three days and three nights.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[13] David asked him, "Who do you belong to, and where are you from?" He answered, "I am a young Egyptian, the slave of an Amalekite. My master abandoned me three days ago because I fell ill.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[14] We raided the Negev of the Kerethites, the territory of Judah, and the Negev of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag."
[1 Samuel] [30]:[15] David asked him, "Can you lead me down to this raiding party?" He said, "Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or hand me over to my master, and I will lead you down to them."
[1 Samuel] [30]:[16] So he led him down, and there they were, sprawled all over the countryside, eating, drinking, and celebrating because of the great spoil they had taken from the land of the Philistines and the land of Judah.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[17] David struck them down from dusk until the evening of the next day, and not one of them escaped except four hundred young men who mounted camels and fled.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[18] David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, and he rescued his two wives.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[19] Nothing was missing—young or old, sons or daughters, plunder or anything else they had carried off. David brought it all back.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[20] He also took all the flocks and herds, and his men drove them ahead of the other livestock, saying, "This is David's spoil."
[1 Samuel] [30]:[21] Then David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow him and had been left behind at the Besor Valley. They came out to meet David and the men with him, and as David approached, he greeted them.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[22] But all the worthless scoundrels among the men who had gone with David said, "Since they did not go with us, we will not share with them any of the spoil we recovered—except that each man may take his wife and children and go."
[1 Samuel] [30]:[23] David replied, "No, my brothers, you must not do that with what the LORD has given us. He protected us and handed over to us the raiders who came against us.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[24] Who would listen to such a thing? The share of the man who goes into battle and the share of the man who stays with the supplies shall be the same; they shall share alike."
[1 Samuel] [30]:[25] From that day on David made this a statute and an ordinance for Israel, and it remains so to this day.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[26] When David reached Ziklag, he sent some of the spoil to his friends, the elders of Judah, with the message: "Here is a gift for you from the spoil of the LORD's enemies."
[1 Samuel] [30]:[27] He sent it to those in Bethel, Ramoth of the Negev, and Jattir;
[1 Samuel] [30]:[28] to those in Aroer, Siphmoth, and Eshtemoa;
[1 Samuel] [30]:[29] to those in Racal, in the towns of the Jerahmeelites and the towns of the Kenites;
[1 Samuel] [30]:[30] to those in Hormah, Bor Ashan, and Athach;
[1 Samuel] [30]:[31] to those in Hebron; and to all the other places where David and his men had roamed.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[1] Meanwhile the Philistines were fighting against Israel. The men of Israel fled before them, and many fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[2] The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[3] The fighting pressed hard against Saul. The archers found him, and he was badly wounded by them.[^1] [^1]: Or "and he was in great anguish because of the archers."
[1 Samuel] [31]:[4] Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through, or these uncircumcised men will come and run me through and make sport of me." But his armor-bearer would not do it, for he was terrified. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[5] When the armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his sword and died with him.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[6] So Saul died that day, together with his three sons, his armor-bearer, and all his men.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[7] When the men of Israel across the valley and beyond the Jordan saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and fled. Then the Philistines came and settled in them.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[8] The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[9] They cut off his head and stripped off his armor, and they sent word throughout the land of the Philistines, carrying the news to the temples of their idols and to the people.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[10] They put his armor in the temple of the Ashtoreths and fastened his body to the wall of Beth-shan.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[11] But when the people of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
[1 Samuel] [31]:[12] all their fighting men set out and marched through the night. They took the bodies of Saul and his sons down from the wall of Beth-shan, brought them to Jabesh, and burned them there.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[13] Then they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree at Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[1] After the death of Saul, when David had returned from defeating the Amalekites, he stayed in Ziklag two days.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[2] On the third day a man came from Saul's camp, his clothes torn and dirt on his head. When he came to David, he fell to the ground and bowed low.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[3] David asked him, "Where have you come from?" He answered, "I escaped from the camp of Israel."
[2 Samuel] [1]:[4] "Tell me what happened," David said. He replied, "The army fled from the battle. Many of the men fell and died. Saul and his son Jonathan are dead too."
[2 Samuel] [1]:[5] Then David said to the young man who brought the report, "How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?"
[2 Samuel] [1]:[6] The young man said, "I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and there was Saul, leaning on his spear, with the chariots and horsemen closing in on him.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[7] He turned around and saw me, and he called out to me. I said, 'Here I am.'
[2 Samuel] [1]:[8] He asked me, 'Who are you?' I answered, 'I am an Amalekite.'
[2 Samuel] [1]:[9] Then he said to me, 'Stand over me and kill me. The agony has gripped me, but I am still alive.'
[2 Samuel] [1]:[10] So I stood over him and killed him, for I knew he could not survive after he had fallen. Then I took the crown from his head and the band from his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord."
[2 Samuel] [1]:[11] Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them, and so did all the men with him.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[12] They mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, for the people of the LORD and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[13] David said to the young man who had brought him the report, "Where are you from?" He answered, "I am the son of a foreigner, an Amalekite."
[2 Samuel] [1]:[14] David said to him, "How is it you were not afraid to lift your hand to destroy the LORD's anointed?"
[2 Samuel] [1]:[15] Then David called one of his men and said, "Go, strike him down!" So he struck him, and he died.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[16] For David had said to him, "Your blood is on your own head, for your own mouth testified against you when you said, 'I killed the LORD's anointed.'"
[2 Samuel] [1]:[17] Then David sang this lament for Saul and his son Jonathan,
[2 Samuel] [1]:[18] and he ordered that the people of Judah be taught this song, called The Bow. It is written in the Book of Jashar:
[2 Samuel] [1]:[19] Your glory, O Israel, lies slain on your heights. How the mighty have fallen!
[2 Samuel] [1]:[20] Tell it not in Gath, proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, or the daughters of the Philistines will rejoice, the daughters of the uncircumcised will exult.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[21] Mountains of Gilboa, may you have no dew or rain, nor fields that yield offerings. For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, the shield of Saul, no longer anointed with oil.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[22] From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan did not turn back, the sword of Saul did not return empty.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[23] Saul and Jonathan—beloved and gracious in life, in death they were not parted. They were swifter than eagles, stronger than lions.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[24] Daughters of Israel, weep for Saul, who clothed you in scarlet and finery, who adorned your garments with gold.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[25] How the mighty have fallen in the midst of battle! Jonathan lies slain on your heights.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[26] I grieve for you, Jonathan, my brother. You were very dear to me. Your love for me was wonderful, surpassing the love of women.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[27] How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!
[2 Samuel] [2]:[1] Some time later David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I go up to one of the cities of Judah?" The LORD said to him, "Go up." David asked, "Where shall I go?" He answered, "To Hebron."
[2 Samuel] [2]:[2] So David went up there, along with his two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the wife of Nabal of Carmel.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[3] David also brought up the men who were with him, each with his household, and they settled in the towns around Hebron.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[4] Then the men of Judah came and there anointed David king over the house of Judah. When David was told that it was the men of Jabesh-gilead who had buried Saul,
[2 Samuel] [2]:[5] he sent messengers to them with this word: "May you be blessed by the LORD, because you showed this kindness to your lord, to Saul, and buried him.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[6] Now may the LORD show you steadfast love and faithfulness, and I too will do good to you because you have done this.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[7] Now then, let your hands be strong, and be valiant men, for Saul your lord is dead, and the house of Judah has anointed me king over them."
[2 Samuel] [2]:[8] Meanwhile Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, had taken Ish-bosheth son of Saul and brought him over to Mahanaim,
[2 Samuel] [2]:[9] and made him king over Gilead, the Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin—over all Israel.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[10] Ish-bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[11] The length of time David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[12] Abner son of Ner set out from Mahanaim to Gibeon with the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[13] Joab son of Zeruiah and David's servants also set out, and they met them at the pool of Gibeon. One company sat down on one side of the pool, the other on the opposite side.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[14] Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men get up and fight before us." Joab said, "Let them get up."
[2 Samuel] [2]:[15] So they got up and were counted off: twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve of David's servants.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[16] Each man seized his opponent by the head and drove his sword into his side, and they fell together. That is why the place at Gibeon is called Helkath-hazzurim.^[The name means "field of sword edges," or "field of flints."]
[2 Samuel] [2]:[17] The fighting that day was fierce beyond measure, and Abner and the men of Israel were beaten by David's servants.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[18] The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel was as fleet of foot as a wild gazelle.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[19] Asahel chased after Abner, swerving neither right nor left as he pursued him.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[20] Abner looked back and said, "Is that you, Asahel?" "It is," he answered.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[21] Abner said to him, "Turn aside to your right or your left; take on one of the young men and strip him of his gear." But Asahel would not stop chasing him.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[22] Again Abner said to Asahel, "Stop chasing me! Why should I strike you to the ground? How could I ever look your brother Joab in the face?"
[2 Samuel] [2]:[23] But he refused to turn aside, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the butt of his spear, and the spear came out through his back. He fell there and died on the spot. And everyone who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died stopped there.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[24] But Joab and Abishai kept up the pursuit of Abner. As the sun was going down, they came to the hill of Ammah, which lies opposite Giah on the road to the wilderness of Gibeon.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[25] The Benjaminites rallied behind Abner, formed a single band, and took their stand on the top of a hill.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[26] Then Abner called out to Joab, "Must the sword devour forever? Don't you know that this will end in bitterness? How long before you order your men to stop pursuing their brothers?"
[2 Samuel] [2]:[27] Joab answered, "As God lives, if you had not spoken, the men would not have given up the pursuit of their brothers until morning."
[2 Samuel] [2]:[28] So Joab blew the ram's horn, and all the troops halted; they no longer pursued Israel or continued the fight.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[29] Abner and his men marched through the Arabah all that night. They crossed the Jordan, went on through the whole Bithron, and came to Mahanaim.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[30] When Joab turned back from pursuing Abner, he gathered all the troops. Nineteen of David's servants were missing, besides Asahel.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[31] But David's servants had struck down three hundred and sixty men of Benjamin, from among Abner's forces; all of them died.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[32] They carried Asahel away and buried him in his father's tomb at Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched all night, and daybreak found them at Hebron.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[1] The war between the house of Saul and the house of David dragged on a long time. David grew steadily stronger, while the house of Saul grew steadily weaker.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[2] Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel;
[2 Samuel] [3]:[3] his second, Kileab, by Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel; the third, Absalom, son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
[2 Samuel] [3]:[4] the fourth, Adonijah, son of Haggith; the fifth, Shephatiah, son of Abital;
[2 Samuel] [3]:[5] and the sixth, Ithream, by David's wife Eglah. These were born to David in Hebron.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[6] While the war between the house of Saul and the house of David went on, Abner kept strengthening his position in the house of Saul.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[7] Now Saul had a concubine named Rizpah daughter of Aiah. And Ish-bosheth said to Abner, "Why have you slept with my father's concubine?"
[2 Samuel] [3]:[8] Abner was furious at Ish-bosheth's words and said, "Am I a dog's head from Judah? To this very day I have shown loyalty to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers and his friends, and I have not handed you over to David—and now you charge me with an offense over this woman!
[2 Samuel] [3]:[9] May God do so to Abner, and more, if I do not bring about for David exactly what the LORD swore to him:
[2 Samuel] [3]:[10] to take the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish David's throne over Israel and over Judah, from Dan to Beersheba."
[2 Samuel] [3]:[11] Ish-bosheth could not say another word to Abner, because he was afraid of him.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[12] Then Abner sent messengers on his own behalf to David, saying, "To whom does the land belong? Make a covenant with me, and look, my hand is with you to bring all Israel over to you."
[2 Samuel] [3]:[13] David answered, "Good. I will make a covenant with you. But I ask one thing of you: do not come into my presence unless you bring Michal daughter of Saul when you come to see me."
[2 Samuel] [3]:[14] Then David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth son of Saul with this demand: "Give me my wife Michal, whom I won for myself with a hundred Philistine foreskins."
[2 Samuel] [3]:[15] So Ish-bosheth sent and took her from her husband, Paltiel son of Laish.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[16] Her husband went with her, weeping as he followed her all the way to Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go back home." And he went back.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[17] Abner had also conferred with the elders of Israel, saying, "For some time now you have wanted David as your king.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[18] Now act, for the LORD has said to David, 'By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and from the hand of all their enemies.'"
[2 Samuel] [3]:[19] Abner spoke to the Benjaminites as well. Then he went to Hebron to tell David everything that Israel and the whole house of Benjamin had agreed to.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[20] When Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men, David gave a feast for him and his men.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[21] Abner said to David, "Let me go at once and gather all Israel to my lord the king, so that they may make a covenant with you and you may rule over everything your heart desires." So David sent Abner away, and he went in peace.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[22] Just then David's men returned with Joab from a raid, bringing much plunder with them. Abner was no longer with David in Hebron, for David had sent him away, and he had gone in peace.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[23] When Joab and all his troops arrived, he was told, "Abner son of Ner came to the king, and the king sent him away, and he has gone in peace."
[2 Samuel] [3]:[24] So Joab went to the king and said, "What have you done? Abner came to you—why did you let him go? Now he has gotten clean away!
[2 Samuel] [3]:[25] You know Abner son of Ner. He came to deceive you, to learn your movements and everything you are doing."
[2 Samuel] [3]:[26] Then Joab left David and sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Sirah. But David knew nothing about it.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[27] When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the gateway as though to speak with him privately, and there he struck him in the stomach, and he died—in revenge for the blood of Joab's brother Asahel.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[28] Later, when David heard of it, he said, "I and my kingdom are forever innocent before the LORD of the blood of Abner son of Ner.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[29] May it fall on the head of Joab and on all his father's house! May the house of Joab never be without someone with a running sore or a skin disease, or a man who leans on a staff, or who falls by the sword, or who lacks food."
[2 Samuel] [3]:[30] So Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner, because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[31] Then David said to Joab and to all the people with him, "Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, and walk in mourning before Abner." And King David himself walked behind the bier.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[32] They buried Abner in Hebron, and the king wept aloud at Abner's grave, and all the people wept.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[33] The king sang this lament for Abner: "Should Abner die the death of a fool?
[2 Samuel] [3]:[34] Your hands were not bound, your feet were not put in irons. You fell as one who falls before treacherous men." And all the people wept over him again.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[35] Then all the people came to urge David to eat something while it was still day, but David swore, "May God do so to me, and more, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun sets!"
[2 Samuel] [3]:[36] All the people noticed this, and it pleased them; indeed, whatever the king did seemed good to all the people.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[37] So on that day all the people and all Israel knew that it had not been the king's will to put Abner son of Ner to death.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[38] And the king said to his servants, "Do you not realize that a prince and a great man has fallen in Israel this day?
[2 Samuel] [3]:[39] Today I am weak, though anointed king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too strong for me. May the LORD repay the evildoer according to his evil!"
[2 Samuel] [4]:[1] When Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, heard that Abner had died at Hebron, his hands went limp, and all Israel was shaken.
[2 Samuel] [4]:[2] Saul's son had two men who were commanders of raiding bands. One was named Baanah and the other Rechab; they were sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, of the tribe of Benjamin—for Beeroth too was reckoned as belonging to Benjamin.
[2 Samuel] [4]:[3] The people of Beeroth had fled to Gittaim, and they have lived there as foreigners to this day.
[2 Samuel] [4]:[4] Now Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son who was crippled in both feet. He was five years old when the news about Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse picked him up and fled, but as she hurried away, he fell and was left lame. His name was Mephibosheth.
[2 Samuel] [4]:[5] Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon of Beeroth, set out and came to the house of Ish-bosheth in the heat of the day, while he was taking his midday rest.
[2 Samuel] [4]:[6] They came right inside the house while the wheat was being taken in, and they struck him in the belly. Then Rechab and his brother Baanah slipped away.
[2 Samuel] [4]:[7] They had entered the house while he lay on his bed in his bedroom, and they struck him down and killed him. They cut off his head, took it with them, and traveled all night by way of the Arabah.
[2 Samuel] [4]:[8] They brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron and said to the king, "Here is the head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life. Today the LORD has avenged my lord the king on Saul and his offspring."
[2 Samuel] [4]:[9] But David answered Rechab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon of Beeroth: "As surely as the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from every distress—
[2 Samuel] [4]:[10] when a man told me, 'Saul is dead,' thinking he was bringing good news, I seized him and killed him at Ziklag. That was the reward I gave him for his news!
[2 Samuel] [4]:[11] How much more, when wicked men have murdered an innocent man in his own house, on his own bed—shall I not now require his blood from your hands and rid the land of you?"
[2 Samuel] [4]:[12] So David gave the order to his men, and they killed them. They cut off their hands and feet and hung the bodies beside the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in Abner's tomb at Hebron.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[1] Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, "Here we are—we are your own flesh and blood.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[2] "Even before now, while Saul was king over us, it was you who led Israel out and brought them home. And the LORD said to you, 'You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be ruler over Israel.'"
[2 Samuel] [5]:[3] So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD; and they anointed David king over Israel.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[4] David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[5] In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[6] The king and his men marched on Jerusalem against the Jebusites who lived there. They said to David, "You will never get in here. Even the blind and the lame could drive you off"—meaning, "David will never get in here."
[2 Samuel] [5]:[7] But David captured the stronghold of Zion—that is, the City of David.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[8] That day David said, "Whoever attacks the Jebusites must go up through the water shaft to reach the lame and the blind, those whom David hates." That is why they say, "The blind and the lame shall not enter the house."
[2 Samuel] [5]:[9] David took up residence in the stronghold and called it the City of David, and he built up the area around it, from the Millo inward.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[10] And David went on and grew greater and greater, for the LORD God of hosts was with him.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[11] Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar logs, carpenters, and stonemasons, and they built a palace for David.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[12] Then David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and had exalted his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[13] After he came from Hebron, David took more concubines and wives in Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to him.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[14] These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
[2 Samuel] [5]:[15] Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
[2 Samuel] [5]:[16] Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[17] When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, they all came up to search for him; and when David heard of it, he went down to the stronghold.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[18] The Philistines came and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[19] So David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?" The LORD answered him, "Go up, for I will surely deliver the Philistines into your hand."
[2 Samuel] [5]:[20] So David went to Baal-perazim and defeated them there. He said, "The LORD has broken through my enemies before me like a bursting flood." That is why he named that place Baal-perazim.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[21] The Philistines abandoned their idols there, and David and his men carried them off.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[22] Once again the Philistines came up and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[23] So David inquired of the LORD, and he answered, "Do not go straight up. Circle around behind them and attack them opposite the balsam trees.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[24] As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move quickly, for then the LORD has gone out ahead of you to strike the camp of the Philistines."
[2 Samuel] [5]:[25] David did as the LORD commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines all the way from Geba to Gezer.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[1] David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand in all.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[2] Then David and all the people with him set out from Baale-judah to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the Name, the name of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned above the cherubim.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[3] They set the ark of God on a new cart and carried it from the house of Abinadab on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were guiding the new cart,
[2 Samuel] [6]:[4] bringing it with the ark of God from the house of Abinadab on the hill, and Ahio walked ahead of the ark.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[5] David and the whole house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all kinds of instruments of cypress wood—with lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles, and cymbals.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[6] When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out to the ark of God and took hold of it, because the oxen had stumbled.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[7] The anger of the LORD blazed against Uzzah, and God struck him down there for his irreverence, and he died there beside the ark of God.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[8] David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah, so he named that place Perez-uzzah, and it is called so to this day.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[9] David was afraid of the LORD that day, and he said, "How can the ark of the LORD ever come to me?"
[2 Samuel] [6]:[10] So David was unwilling to bring the ark of the LORD up to himself in the City of David; instead he turned it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[11] The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and his entire household.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[12] King David was told, "The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him because of the ark of God." So David went and brought the ark of God up from the house of Obed-edom to the City of David with rejoicing.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[13] When those carrying the ark of the LORD had taken six steps, David sacrificed a bull and a fattened calf.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[14] And David danced before the LORD with all his might, wearing a linen ephod.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[15] So David and the whole house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting and the sound of the ram's horn.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[16] As the ark of the LORD entered the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked down through the window, and when she saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, she despised him in her heart.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[17] They brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent David had pitched for it, and David offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings before the LORD.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[18] When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the fellowship offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[19] He distributed to all the people, to the whole multitude of Israel, both men and women, a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins to each one. Then all the people went home.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[20] When David returned to bless his household, Michal daughter of Saul came out to meet him and said, "How the king of Israel has distinguished himself today, exposing himself before the eyes of his servants' slave girls as one of the vulgar might shamelessly expose himself!"
[2 Samuel] [6]:[21] David said to Michal, "It was before the LORD, who chose me over your father and all his house and appointed me ruler over the LORD's people, over Israel—before the LORD I will celebrate.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[22] I will make myself even more contemptible than this, and I will be humbled in my own eyes. But by the slave girls you spoke of, by them I will be held in honor."
[2 Samuel] [6]:[23] And Michal daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[1] Once the king was settled in his palace and the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies around him,
[2 Samuel] [7]:[2] the king said to Nathan the prophet, "Look, I am living in a house of cedar, while the ark of God stays in a tent."
[2 Samuel] [7]:[3] Nathan answered the king, "Go and do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you."
[2 Samuel] [7]:[4] But that night the word of the LORD came to Nathan:
[2 Samuel] [7]:[5] "Go and say to my servant David, 'This is what the LORD says: Are you the one to build me a house to dwell in?
[2 Samuel] [7]:[6] I have not lived in a house from the day I brought the Israelites up out of Egypt until this day; I have moved from place to place with a tent for my dwelling.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[7] Wherever I moved among all the Israelites, did I ever say a word to any of the tribes of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people Israel: Why have you not built me a house of cedar?'
[2 Samuel] [7]:[8] Now then, say this to my servant David: 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over my people Israel.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[9] I have been with you wherever you went, and I have cut off all your enemies before you. Now I will make your name great, like the names of the greatest men on earth.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[10] And I will provide a place for my people Israel and plant them, so that they may dwell secure and be disturbed no more. Violent men will no longer oppress them as they did at the beginning,
[2 Samuel] [7]:[11] as they have done ever since the day I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies. The LORD declares to you that the LORD himself will build a house for you:
[2 Samuel] [7]:[12] When your days are done and you rest with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, who will come from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[13] He is the one who will build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[14] I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me. When he does wrong, I will discipline him with the rod of men, with blows inflicted by human hands.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[15] But my steadfast love will never depart from him, as I took it from Saul, whom I removed from before you.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[16] Your house and your kingdom will endure forever before you; your throne will be established forever.'"
[2 Samuel] [7]:[17] Nathan reported to David all these words and this entire vision.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[18] Then King David went in and sat before the LORD, and he said: "Who am I, Lord GOD, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
[2 Samuel] [7]:[19] And as if this were not enough in your sight, Lord GOD, you have also spoken about the future of your servant's house. Is this your way with man, Lord GOD?
[2 Samuel] [7]:[20] What more can David say to you? You know your servant, Lord GOD.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[21] For the sake of your word and according to your own heart, you have done this great thing and made it known to your servant.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[22] How great you are, Lord GOD! There is no one like you, and there is no God but you, as we have heard with our own ears.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[23] And who is like your people Israel—the one nation on earth that God went out to redeem as a people for himself? You made a name for yourself and did great and awesome deeds, driving out nations and their gods before your people, whom you redeemed for yourself from Egypt.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[24] You established your people Israel as your very own forever, and you, LORD, became their God.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[25] And now, LORD God, keep forever the promise you have made concerning your servant and his house. Do as you have said,
[2 Samuel] [7]:[26] so that your name will be great forever, and men will say, 'The LORD of hosts is God over Israel!' And may the house of your servant David be established before you.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[27] For you, LORD of hosts, God of Israel, have revealed this to your servant, saying, 'I will build a house for you.' That is why your servant has found the courage to pray this prayer to you.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[28] And now, Lord GOD, you are God, and your words are truth. You have promised this good thing to your servant.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[29] Now be pleased to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you. For you, Lord GOD, have spoken, and with your blessing the house of your servant will be blessed forever."
[2 Samuel] [8]:[1] Some time later David struck down the Philistines and subdued them, and he took Metheg-ammah out of the hands of the Philistines.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[2] He also defeated Moab. He made them lie down on the ground and measured them off with a cord: two lengths he measured out for death and one full length for life. So the Moabites became David's servants and brought him tribute.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[3] David also struck down Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to restore his control at the Euphrates River.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[4] David captured from him seventeen hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He hamstrung all the chariot horses, but he left enough for a hundred chariots.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[5] When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of them.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[6] Then David stationed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became his servants and brought him tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[7] David took the gold shields carried by Hadadezer's servants and brought them to Jerusalem.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[8] And from Betah and Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a great quantity of bronze.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[9] When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer,
[2 Samuel] [8]:[10] he sent his son Joram to King David to greet him and to congratulate him on his victory in battle over Hadadezer, for Hadadezer had been at war with Toi. Joram brought with him articles of silver, gold, and bronze.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[11] King David dedicated these also to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had dedicated from all the nations he had subdued:
[2 Samuel] [8]:[12] from Aram, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and Amalek, and from the plunder of Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[13] David made a name for himself when he returned from striking down eighteen thousand Arameans in the Valley of Salt.[^1] [^1]: Some ancient witnesses and the parallel account read "Edomites" here, which fits the Valley of Salt and the account of Edom that follows.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[14] He stationed garrisons throughout Edom—garrisons in all of Edom—and all the Edomites became David's servants. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[15] So David reigned over all Israel, administering justice and righteousness for all his people.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[16] Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
[2 Samuel] [8]:[17] Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Seraiah was secretary;
[2 Samuel] [8]:[18] Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and Pelethites; and David's sons were priests.[^1] [^1]: David's sons were not Levites; the term here likely denotes chief officials or royal advisers serving at the king's side.
[2 Samuel] [9]:[1] David asked, "Is there anyone still left of the house of Saul, so that I may show him kindness for Jonathan's sake?"
[2 Samuel] [9]:[2] Now there was a servant of Saul's household named Ziba, and they summoned him to David. The king said to him, "Are you Ziba?" "At your service," he answered.
[2 Samuel] [9]:[3] The king asked, "Is there no one at all left of Saul's house to whom I may show God's own kindness?" Ziba answered the king, "There is still a son of Jonathan; he is crippled in both feet."
[2 Samuel] [9]:[4] "Where is he?" the king asked. Ziba answered, "He is in the house of Machir son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar."
[2 Samuel] [9]:[5] So King David sent and had him brought from the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo Debar.
[2 Samuel] [9]:[6] When Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell facedown and bowed low. David said, "Mephibosheth!" "I am your servant," he answered.
[2 Samuel] [9]:[7] "Do not be afraid," David said to him, "for I will surely show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land that belonged to Saul your grandfather, and you will always eat at my table."
[2 Samuel] [9]:[8] Mephibosheth bowed down and said, "What is your servant, that you should notice a dead dog like me?"
[2 Samuel] [9]:[9] Then the king summoned Ziba, Saul's steward, and said to him, "I have given to your master's grandson everything that belonged to Saul and his whole house.
[2 Samuel] [9]:[10] You and your sons and your servants are to farm the land for him and bring in the harvest, so that your master's grandson may have food to eat. And Mephibosheth, your master's grandson, will always eat at my table." (Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.)
[2 Samuel] [9]:[11] Ziba said to the king, "Whatever my lord the king commands his servant, your servant will do." So Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's sons. [Footnote: Hebrew reads "my table"; the sense is the king's table.]
[2 Samuel] [9]:[12] Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and all the members of Ziba's household were servants of Mephibosheth.
[2 Samuel] [9]:[13] So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, and he always ate at the king's table. He was lame in both feet.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[1] Some time later the king of the Ammonites died, and his son Hanun became king in his place.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[2] David said, "I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me." So David sent a delegation of his servants to console him over his father. But when David's servants arrived in the land of the Ammonites,
[2 Samuel] [10]:[3] the Ammonite commanders said to Hanun their lord, "Do you really think David is honoring your father by sending you men to console you? Hasn't David sent his servants to you to explore the city, to spy it out and overthrow it?"
[2 Samuel] [10]:[4] So Hanun seized David's servants, shaved off half of each man's beard, cut their garments in half at the buttocks, and sent them away.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[5] When David was told, he sent men to meet them, for the men were deeply humiliated. The king said, "Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return."
[2 Samuel] [10]:[6] When the Ammonites realized they had made themselves odious to David, they sent and hired the Arameans of Beth Rehob and the Arameans of Zobah—twenty thousand foot soldiers—along with the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and twelve thousand men from Tob.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[7] When David heard of it, he sent out Joab with the whole army of fighting men.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[8] The Ammonites marched out and took up battle positions at the entrance of the gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open field.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[9] When Joab saw that he faced battle lines both in front of him and behind him, he chose some of the best troops in Israel and drew them up against the Arameans.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[10] The rest of the men he put under the command of his brother Abishai, who drew them up against the Ammonites.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[11] Joab said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you are to come to my rescue; but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come and rescue you.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[12] Be strong, and let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. And may the LORD do what is good in his sight."
[2 Samuel] [10]:[13] Then Joab and the troops with him advanced to fight the Arameans, and they fled before him.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[14] When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans were fleeing, they fled before Abishai and withdrew into the city. So Joab broke off the attack against the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[15] When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they regrouped.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[16] Hadadezer sent messengers and brought out the Arameans from beyond the River, and they came to Helam, with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer's army leading them.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[17] When David was told of it, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and came to Helam. The Arameans drew up their lines to meet David and fought against him.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[18] But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven hundred of their charioteers and forty thousand of their horsemen. He also struck down Shobach the commander of their army, and he died there.
[2 Samuel] [10]:[19] When all the kings who were vassals of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with the Israelites and became subject to them. So the Arameans were afraid to help the Ammonites anymore.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[1] In the spring of the year, at the time when kings march out to war, David sent Joab out with his servants and all Israel, and they ravaged the Ammonites and laid siege to Rabbah. But David stayed behind in Jerusalem.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[2] One evening David got up from his bed and walked about on the roof of the king's house. From the roof he saw a woman bathing, and the woman was very beautiful.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[3] David sent someone to inquire about her, and he was told, "That is Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam and the wife of Uriah the Hittite."
[2 Samuel] [11]:[4] So David sent messengers and had her brought to him, and he slept with her—she had just purified herself from her uncleanness—and then she returned to her house.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[5] The woman conceived, and she sent word to David: "I am pregnant."
[2 Samuel] [11]:[6] Then David sent word to Joab: "Send me Uriah the Hittite." And Joab sent Uriah to David.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[7] When Uriah came to him, David asked how Joab was, how the troops were, and how the war was going.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[8] Then David said to Uriah, "Go down to your house and wash your feet." So Uriah left the king's house, and a gift from the king was sent after him.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[9] But Uriah slept at the entrance of the king's house with all his master's servants and did not go down to his own house.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[10] When David was told, "Uriah did not go down to his house," he said to Uriah, "Haven't you just come from a journey? Why didn't you go down to your house?"
[2 Samuel] [11]:[11] Uriah answered David, "The ark and Israel and Judah are staying in shelters, and my lord Joab and my lord's servants are camped in the open field. Should I then go to my house to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? As you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do such a thing."
[2 Samuel] [11]:[12] So David said to Uriah, "Stay here today as well, and tomorrow I will send you back." So Uriah remained in Jerusalem that day and the next.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[13] David invited him to eat and drink in his presence, and he got him drunk. But in the evening Uriah went out to lie down on his bed among his master's servants; he did not go down to his own house.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[14] In the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it with Uriah.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[15] In the letter he wrote: "Put Uriah at the front, where the fighting is fiercest, then pull back from him so that he is struck down and dies."
[2 Samuel] [11]:[16] So as Joab kept watch on the city, he stationed Uriah at the place where he knew the strongest defenders were.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[17] The men of the city came out and fought against Joab, and some of the troops, David's own servants, fell. Uriah the Hittite also died.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[18] Then Joab sent David a full report of the battle.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[19] He instructed the messenger: "When you have finished giving the king the whole account of the battle,
[2 Samuel] [11]:[20] if the king's anger flares up and he asks you, 'Why did you go so close to the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot from the wall?
[2 Samuel] [11]:[21] Who struck down Abimelech son of Jerubbesheth? Wasn't it a woman who threw an upper millstone down on him from the wall, so that he died at Thebez? Why did you go so near the wall?'—then say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well.'"
[2 Samuel] [11]:[22] The messenger set out, and when he arrived he told David everything Joab had sent him to say.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[23] The messenger said to David, "The men prevailed against us and came out at us into the open field, but we drove them back to the entrance of the gate.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[24] Then the archers shot at your servants from the wall, and some of the king's servants died. Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead as well."
[2 Samuel] [11]:[25] David said to the messenger, "Tell Joab this: 'Do not let this matter trouble you, for the sword devours now one and now another. Press your attack on the city and tear it down.' And encourage him."
[2 Samuel] [11]:[26] When Uriah's wife heard that her husband Uriah was dead, she mourned for him.
[2 Samuel] [11]:[27] When the mourning was over, David sent for her and brought her into his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But what David had done was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[1] So the LORD sent Nathan to David. He came to him and said: "There were two men in a certain city, one rich and one poor.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[2] The rich man had flocks and herds in great number,
[2 Samuel] [12]:[3] but the poor man had nothing at all except one little ewe lamb that he had bought. He raised her, and she grew up with him and with his children. She ate from his own morsel and drank from his own cup and slept in his arms; she was like a daughter to him.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[4] Then a traveler came to the rich man, and he was unwilling to take one of his own sheep or cattle to prepare for the guest who had come to him. So he took the poor man's lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him."
[2 Samuel] [12]:[5] David burned with anger against the man and said to Nathan, "As the LORD lives, the man who did this deserves to die!
[2 Samuel] [12]:[6] He must repay for the lamb four times over, because he did such a thing and had no pity."
[2 Samuel] [12]:[7] Then Nathan said to David, "You are the man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I anointed you king over Israel, and I rescued you from the hand of Saul.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[8] I gave you your master's house and your master's wives into your arms, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah. And if that had been too little, I would have added much more for you.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[9] Why then did you despise the word of the LORD and do what is evil in my sight? You struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword and took his wife to be your own wife. You killed him with the sword of the Ammonites.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[10] Now therefore the sword will never depart from your house, because you despised me and took the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your own wife.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[11] This is what the LORD says: I am going to raise up disaster against you out of your own house. I will take your wives before your very eyes and give them to your own neighbor, and he will lie with your wives in broad daylight.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[12] You acted in secret, but I will do this thing before all Israel and in broad daylight."
[2 Samuel] [12]:[13] Then David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against the LORD." And Nathan said to David, "The LORD has also taken away your sin; you will not die.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[14] Nevertheless, because by this deed you have shown utter contempt for the LORD, the son born to you will surely die.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew text reads "you have shown utter contempt for the enemies of the LORD"; the word "enemies" is widely understood as an early scribal softening of a statement that seemed too harsh.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[15] Then Nathan went home. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah's wife had borne to David, and he became gravely ill.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[16] David pleaded with God for the boy. He fasted, and he went in and lay all night on the ground.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[17] The elders of his household stood beside him to raise him from the ground, but he refused and would not eat any food with them.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[18] On the seventh day the child died. David's servants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, "While the child was still alive, we spoke to him and he would not listen to us. How can we tell him the child is dead? He may do something terrible."
[2 Samuel] [12]:[19] But David saw his servants whispering to one another, and he understood that the child was dead. "Is the child dead?" he asked them. "He is dead," they answered.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[20] Then David got up from the ground. He washed, anointed himself, and changed his clothes; then he went into the house of the LORD and worshiped. He returned to his own house and asked for food, and they set it before him, and he ate.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[21] His servants said to him, "What is this you have done? While the child was alive you fasted and wept, but now that the child is dead you got up and ate food."
[2 Samuel] [12]:[22] He answered, "While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept, for I thought, 'Who knows? The LORD may be gracious to me and let the child live.'
[2 Samuel] [12]:[23] But now he is dead. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me."
