[2 Samuel] [12]:[24] Then David comforted his wife Bathsheba, and he went to her and lay with her. She gave birth to a son, and she named him Solomon. The LORD loved him,
[2 Samuel] [12]:[25] and he sent word through Nathan the prophet to name him Jedidiah, for the LORD's sake.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[26] Meanwhile Joab fought against Rabbah of the Ammonites and captured the royal city.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[27] Then Joab sent messengers to David and said, "I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the water supply of the city.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[28] Now gather the rest of the troops, lay siege to the city, and take it—otherwise I will take the city myself, and it will be named after me."
[2 Samuel] [12]:[29] So David gathered all the troops, went to Rabbah, attacked it, and captured it.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[30] He took the crown from the head of their king. It weighed a talent of gold and was set with precious stones, and it was placed on David's head. He also brought out great quantities of plunder from the city.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[31] He brought out the people who were there and put them to labor with saws and iron picks and iron axes, and he set them to work at the brick kilns. He did this to all the Ammonite cities. Then David and all the troops returned to Jerusalem.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[1] Some time later, Absalom son of David had a beautiful sister named Tamar, and Amnon son of David fell in love with her.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[2] Amnon was so tormented over his sister Tamar that he made himself ill, for she was a virgin, and it seemed impossible to him to do anything to her.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[3] Now Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of David's brother Shimeah, and Jonadab was a very shrewd man.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[4] He said to him, "Why are you, the king's son, so haggard morning after morning? Won't you tell me?" Amnon answered, "I am in love with Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom."
[2 Samuel] [13]:[5] Jonadab said to him, "Lie down on your bed and pretend to be ill. When your father comes to see you, say to him, 'Please let my sister Tamar come and give me something to eat. Let her prepare the food where I can see it, so that I may watch and eat from her hand.'"
[2 Samuel] [13]:[6] So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to him, "Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes here in front of me, so that I may eat from her hand."
[2 Samuel] [13]:[7] David sent word to Tamar at the palace: "Go to the house of your brother Amnon and prepare food for him."
[2 Samuel] [13]:[8] So Tamar went to the house of her brother Amnon, where he lay in bed. She took dough, kneaded it, shaped the cakes in his sight, and baked them.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[9] Then she took the pan and served him, but he refused to eat. "Send everyone out of here," Amnon said, and they all left him.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[10] Then Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the bedroom, so that I may eat from your hand." Tamar took the cakes she had made and brought them to her brother Amnon in the bedroom.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[11] But when she brought them to him to eat, he seized her and said, "Come, lie with me, my sister."
[2 Samuel] [13]:[12] "No, my brother!" she said. "Do not violate me. Such a thing is not done in Israel. Do not commit this outrage.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[13] And I—where could I carry my disgrace? And you would be like one of the depraved fools in Israel. Speak to the king; he will not keep me from you."
[2 Samuel] [13]:[14] But he would not listen to her, and being stronger than she was, he overpowered her and raped her.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[15] Then Amnon was seized with a violent hatred for her; the hatred he felt for her was greater than the love he had felt. "Get up and get out!" he said to her.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[16] "No," she said, "sending me away is a greater wrong than what you have already done to me." But he would not listen to her.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[17] He called the young man who served him and said, "Get this woman out of my sight, and bolt the door behind her."
[2 Samuel] [13]:[18] She was wearing an ornamented robe, for this is how the virgin daughters of the king were dressed. So his servant put her out and bolted the door behind her.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[19] Tamar put ashes on her head, tore the ornamented robe she was wearing, laid her hand on her head, and went away, crying aloud as she went.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[20] Her brother Absalom said to her, "Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now, my sister, keep quiet. He is your brother; do not take this thing to heart." So Tamar lived in her brother Absalom's house, a desolate woman.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[21] When King David heard all about it, he was furious.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[22] But Absalom said nothing to Amnon, good or bad; he hated Amnon for violating his sister Tamar.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[23] Two years later, when Absalom's sheepshearers were at Baal Hazor near Ephraim, Absalom invited all the king's sons.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[24] Absalom went to the king and said, "Your servant is shearing sheep. Will the king and his servants please come with your servant?"
[2 Samuel] [13]:[25] "No, my son," the king replied. "We should not all go; we would only be a burden to you." Although Absalom pressed him, he still refused to go, but he gave him his blessing.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[26] Then Absalom said, "If not, please let my brother Amnon come with us." "Why should he go with you?" the king asked.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[27] But Absalom pressed him, so he sent Amnon along with all the king's sons.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[28] Absalom ordered his men, "Watch closely. When Amnon is in high spirits from the wine and I say to you, 'Strike Amnon down,' then kill him. Have no fear. Have I not given you the order myself? Be strong and courageous."
[2 Samuel] [13]:[29] So Absalom's men did to Amnon exactly as Absalom had ordered. Then all the king's sons got up, each mounted his mule, and fled.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[30] While they were still on the way, this report reached David: "Absalom has struck down all the king's sons; not one of them is left."
[2 Samuel] [13]:[31] The king stood up, tore his garments, and lay down on the ground, and all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[32] But Jonadab son of Shimeah, David's brother, said, "My lord must not think that they have killed all the young men, the king's sons. Only Amnon is dead. This has been Absalom's fixed purpose from the day Amnon violated his sister Tamar.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[33] So now, let my lord the king not take it to heart, thinking that all the king's sons are dead. Only Amnon is dead."
[2 Samuel] [13]:[34] Meanwhile, Absalom had fled. When the young man on watch looked up, he saw many people coming along the road behind him, on the side of the hill.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[35] Jonadab said to the king, "Look, the king's sons have come. It has happened just as your servant said."
[2 Samuel] [13]:[36] As he finished speaking, the king's sons arrived, weeping loudly. And the king and all his servants also wept very bitterly.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[37] Absalom, however, had fled to Talmai son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. And the king mourned for his son day after day.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[38] After Absalom had fled to Geshur, he stayed there three years.
[2 Samuel] [13]:[39] And King David longed to go out to Absalom, for he had been consoled over Amnon's death.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[1] Joab son of Zeruiah knew that the king's heart went out to Absalom.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[2] So Joab sent to Tekoa and brought back a wise woman from there, and he said to her, "Pretend to be in mourning. Put on mourning clothes and use no oil, and act like a woman who has grieved many days for the dead.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[3] Then go to the king and speak to him in this way." And Joab put the words in her mouth.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[4] The woman from Tekoa came to the king, fell on her face to the ground in homage, and said, "Help me, O king!" [Footnote: The Hebrew text reads "said" here; the reading "came" follows the sense required by the context and is supported by ancient versions.]
[2 Samuel] [14]:[5] The king said to her, "What is your trouble?" She answered, "Truly, I am a widow; my husband is dead.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[6] Your servant had two sons. They quarreled out in the field, and there was no one to part them. One struck the other and killed him.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[7] Now the whole clan has risen against your servant. They say, 'Hand over the one who struck his brother, so we may put him to death for the life of the brother he murdered, and destroy the heir as well.' So they would snuff out the last ember I have left, leaving my husband neither name nor survivor on the face of the earth."
[2 Samuel] [14]:[8] The king said to the woman, "Go home. I will issue orders on your behalf."
[2 Samuel] [14]:[9] But the woman from Tekoa said to the king, "My lord the king, let the guilt be on me and on my father's house; the king and his throne are innocent."
[2 Samuel] [14]:[10] The king replied, "If anyone says anything to you, bring him to me, and he will never trouble you again."
[2 Samuel] [14]:[11] She said, "Then let the king swear by the LORD your God to keep the avenger of blood from doing any more destruction, so they will not destroy my son." He said, "As the LORD lives, not one hair of your son's head shall fall to the ground."
[2 Samuel] [14]:[12] Then the woman said, "Please let your servant speak a word to my lord the king." "Speak," he said.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[13] The woman said, "Then why have you devised such a thing against the people of God? In saying this, the king convicts himself, for he has not brought back his own banished son.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[14] We must all die; we are like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again. Yet God does not take away life; instead he devises ways so that the banished one is not cast off from him.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[15] Now I have come to speak this word to my lord the king because the people made me afraid. Your servant thought, 'Let me speak to the king; perhaps he will do what his servant asks.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[16] Surely the king will listen and rescue his servant from the hand of the man who would destroy both me and my son from the inheritance of God.'
[2 Samuel] [14]:[17] And your servant thought, 'May the word of my lord the king bring me peace,' for my lord the king is like the angel of God in discerning good and evil. May the LORD your God be with you."
[2 Samuel] [14]:[18] Then the king said to the woman, "Do not hide from me what I am about to ask you." "Let my lord the king speak," the woman said.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[19] The king asked, "Is not the hand of Joab in all of this?" The woman answered, "As surely as you live, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or the left from anything my lord the king has said. Yes, it was your servant Joab who instructed me; he put all these words in the mouth of your servant.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[20] Your servant Joab did this to change the course of things. But my lord has wisdom like the wisdom of the angel of God—he knows everything that happens in the land."
[2 Samuel] [14]:[21] The king said to Joab, "Very well, I grant it. Go, bring back the young man Absalom."
[2 Samuel] [14]:[22] Joab fell with his face to the ground in homage and blessed the king. "Today," Joab said, "your servant knows that I have found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because the king has granted his servant's request."
[2 Samuel] [14]:[23] Then Joab set out for Geshur and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[24] But the king said, "He must go to his own house; he is not to see my face." So Absalom went to his own house and did not see the king's face.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[25] In all Israel there was no man so highly praised for his beauty as Absalom; from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no flaw in him.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[26] Whenever he cut the hair of his head—he cut it once a year, when it grew too heavy for him—he would weigh it, and it came to two hundred shekels by the royal weight.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[27] Three sons were born to Absalom, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar; she was a beautiful woman.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[28] Absalom lived in Jerusalem two full years without seeing the king's face.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[29] Then Absalom sent word to Joab, asking him to go to the king on his behalf, but Joab would not come to him. He sent a second time, and still Joab would not come.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[30] So Absalom said to his servants, "Look, Joab's field is next to mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire." And Absalom's servants set the field on fire.
[2 Samuel] [14]:[31] Then Joab got up and came to Absalom's house and said to him, "Why have your servants set my field on fire?"
[2 Samuel] [14]:[32] Absalom answered Joab, "Look, I sent word to you and said, 'Come here, so I can send you to the king to ask why I have come home from Geshur. It would be better for me if I were still there.' Now let me see the king's face, and if there is guilt in me, let him put me to death."
[2 Samuel] [14]:[33] So Joab went to the king and told him. Then the king summoned Absalom, and he came in and bowed with his face to the ground before the king; and the king kissed Absalom.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[1] Some time later Absalom acquired a chariot and horses, along with fifty men to run ahead of him.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[2] He would rise early and stand beside the road leading to the city gate. Whenever anyone came with a case to bring before the king for judgment, Absalom would call out to him and ask, "What town are you from?" And when the man answered, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel,"
[2 Samuel] [15]:[3] Absalom would say to him, "Look, your claims are good and right, but the king has appointed no one to hear you."
[2 Samuel] [15]:[4] And Absalom would add, "If only I were made judge in this land! Then everyone with a case or a claim could come to me, and I would see that he got justice."
[2 Samuel] [15]:[5] And whenever a man approached to bow down before him, Absalom would reach out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[6] This is how Absalom treated every Israelite who came to the king for judgment, and so he stole the hearts of the people of Israel.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[7] At the end of four years Absalom said to the king, "Let me go to Hebron and fulfill the vow I made to the LORD.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[8] For while your servant was living in Geshur in Aram, I made this vow: 'If the LORD brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the LORD.'"
[2 Samuel] [15]:[9] The king said to him, "Go in peace." So he set out for Hebron.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[10] Then Absalom sent messengers secretly throughout all the tribes of Israel with this word: "As soon as you hear the sound of the ram's horn, say, 'Absalom is king in Hebron!'"
[2 Samuel] [15]:[11] Two hundred men from Jerusalem went with Absalom. They had been invited as guests and went in all innocence, knowing nothing of the matter.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[12] Absalom also sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, to come from his town of Giloh. And while Absalom was offering the sacrifices, the conspiracy gained strength, and his following kept growing.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[13] A messenger came to David and reported, "The hearts of the men of Israel have gone over to Absalom."
[2 Samuel] [15]:[14] Then David said to all his officials who were with him in Jerusalem, "Come, we must flee, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Go quickly, or he will overtake us, bring disaster down on us, and put the city to the sword."
[2 Samuel] [15]:[15] The king's servants answered him, "Whatever our lord the king decides, your servants are ready."
[2 Samuel] [15]:[16] So the king set out on foot, and his whole household with him, but he left behind ten concubines to look after the palace.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[17] The king went out on foot with all the people following him, and they stopped at the last house.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[18] All his servants passed by him, along with all the Kerethites and Pelethites, and all six hundred Gittites who had come with him from Gath marched past the king.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[19] The king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why should you come along with us? Go back and stay with the king. You are a foreigner, an exile from your own land.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[20] You came only yesterday. Should I make you wander with us today, when I am going wherever I can? Go back, and take your countrymen with you, and may steadfast love and faithfulness go with you.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[21] But Ittai answered the king, "As surely as the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there your servant will be."
[2 Samuel] [15]:[22] David said to Ittai, "Very well, march on." So Ittai the Gittite marched on with all his men and all the children who were with him.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[23] The whole countryside wept aloud as all the people passed by. The king crossed the Kidron Valley, and all the people moved on toward the wilderness.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[24] Zadok was also there, and with him all the Levites, carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar offered sacrifices until all the people had finished leaving the city.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[25] Then the king said to Zadok, "Take the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the LORD's eyes, he will bring me back and let me see both it and his dwelling place again.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[26] But if he says, 'I am not pleased with you,' then here I am; let him do to me whatever seems good to him."
[2 Samuel] [15]:[27] The king also said to Zadok the priest, "Listen: go back to the city in peace, and take with you your son Ahimaaz and Jonathan son of Abiathar—your two sons.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[28] I will wait at the fords in the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me."
[2 Samuel] [15]:[29] So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed there.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[30] But David went on up the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went, his head covered and his feet bare. And all the people with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[31] When David was told that Ahithophel was among the conspirators with Absalom, he prayed, "LORD, turn Ahithophel's counsel into folly."
[2 Samuel] [15]:[32] When David reached the summit, where people used to worship God, Hushai the Arkite was there to meet him, his robe torn and dust on his head.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[33] David said to him, "If you go with me, you will only be a burden to me.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[34] But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, O king; as I was your father's servant in the past, so now I will be your servant,' then you can frustrate Ahithophel's counsel for me.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[35] Won't the priests Zadok and Abiathar be there with you? Report to them everything you hear in the king's palace.
[2 Samuel] [15]:[36] Their two sons are with them, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar. Send me word through them of everything you hear."
[2 Samuel] [15]:[37] So Hushai, David's friend, arrived in the city just as Absalom was entering Jerusalem.
[2 Samuel] [16]:[1] When David had gone a little beyond the summit, there was Ziba, Mephibosheth's servant, coming to meet him with a pair of saddled donkeys loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.
[2 Samuel] [16]:[2] The king asked Ziba, "What are these for?" Ziba answered, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride on, the bread and the summer fruits are for the young men to eat, and the wine is for those who grow faint in the wilderness to drink."
[2 Samuel] [16]:[3] "And where is your master's son?" the king asked. Ziba said to the king, "He is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will restore my father's kingdom to me.'"
[2 Samuel] [16]:[4] Then the king said to Ziba, "Everything that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours." Ziba said, "I bow before you. May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king."
[2 Samuel] [16]:[5] As King David approached Bahurim, a man came out from there, from the clan of the house of Saul. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and he came out cursing as he went.
[2 Samuel] [16]:[6] He pelted David and all King David's servants with stones, though all the troops and all the warriors were on his right and on his left.
[2 Samuel] [16]:[7] This is what Shimei said as he cursed: "Get out, get out, you man of blood, you worthless man!
[2 Samuel] [16]:[8] The LORD has brought back upon you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the LORD has handed the kingdom over to your son Absalom. See, disaster has overtaken you, because you are a man of blood!"
[2 Samuel] [16]:[9] Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and take off his head."
[2 Samuel] [16]:[10] But the king said, "What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse, for the LORD has told him, 'Curse David.' Who then can ask, 'Why have you done this?'"
[2 Samuel] [16]:[11] And David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "Look, my own son, my own flesh and blood, is seeking my life. How much more, then, this Benjaminite! Leave him alone and let him curse, for the LORD has told him to.
[2 Samuel] [16]:[12] Perhaps the LORD will look on my affliction and repay me with good for the cursing I receive today."
[2 Samuel] [16]:[13] So David and his men went on their way, while Shimei kept pace with him along the hillside opposite, cursing as he went, throwing stones at him and flinging dust.
[2 Samuel] [16]:[14] The king and all the people with him arrived exhausted, and there he refreshed himself.
[2 Samuel] [16]:[15] Meanwhile Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.
[2 Samuel] [16]:[16] When Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom, he said to him, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"
[2 Samuel] [16]:[17] Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your loyalty to your friend? Why didn't you go with your friend?"
[2 Samuel] [16]:[18] Hushai answered Absalom, "No. The one chosen by the LORD, by this people, and by all the men of Israel—his I will be, and with him I will stay.
[2 Samuel] [16]:[19] And furthermore, whom should I serve? Should it not be his son? As I served your father, so I will serve you."
[2 Samuel] [16]:[20] Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give us your counsel. What should we do?"
[2 Samuel] [16]:[21] Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, whom he left to keep the house. Then all Israel will hear that you have made yourself odious to your father, and the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened."
[2 Samuel] [16]:[22] So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.
[2 Samuel] [16]:[23] Now in those days the counsel Ahithophel gave was regarded as though one had inquired of the word of God—so was all Ahithophel's counsel esteemed by both David and Absalom.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[1] Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight in pursuit of David.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[2] I will come upon him while he is weary and his hands are weak, and I will throw him into panic. All the people with him will flee, and I will strike down the king alone.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[3] Then I will bring all the people back to you. The return of them all depends on the one man you are seeking; then the whole people will be at peace."
[2 Samuel] [17]:[4] The plan seemed right to Absalom and to all the elders of Israel.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[5] But Absalom said, "Call Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he has to say too."
[2 Samuel] [17]:[6] When Hushai came to Absalom, Absalom said to him, "This is what Ahithophel has proposed. Shall we act on his word? If not, speak up."
[2 Samuel] [17]:[7] Hushai answered Absalom, "This time the advice Ahithophel has given is not good."
[2 Samuel] [17]:[8] Hushai went on, "You know your father and his men: they are warriors, and they are as fierce as a bear in the field robbed of her cubs. Your father is a man of war; he will not spend the night with the troops.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[9] Even now he is hiding in one of the ravines or somewhere else. If some of your men fall at the first attack, whoever hears of it will say, 'There has been a slaughter among the troops who follow Absalom.'
[2 Samuel] [17]:[10] Then even the bravest man, with a heart like the heart of a lion, will melt with fear, for all Israel knows that your father is a warrior and that those with him are men of valor.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[11] So this is my advice: Let all Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, be gathered to you, as numerous as the sand on the seashore, and go yourself into battle at their head.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[12] Then we will come upon him wherever he may be found, and we will settle on him as the dew settles on the ground. Neither he nor any of the men with him will be left alive—not one.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[13] And if he withdraws into a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down into the valley until not even a pebble of it can be found."
[2 Samuel] [17]:[14] Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than the advice of Ahithophel." For the LORD had ordained that Ahithophel's good counsel be frustrated, so that the LORD might bring disaster on Absalom.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[15] Then Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, "This is the advice Ahithophel gave Absalom and the elders of Israel, and this is what I advised.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[16] Now send word quickly and tell David: 'Do not spend the night in the plains of the wilderness, but cross over at once, or the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.'"
[2 Samuel] [17]:[17] Jonathan and Ahimaaz were waiting at En-rogel, and a servant girl would go and bring them word, and they would go and report to King David, for they could not risk being seen entering the city.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[18] But a young man saw them and told Absalom. So the two of them hurried away and came to the house of a man in Bahurim who had a well in his courtyard, and they climbed down into it.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[19] The woman took a covering, spread it over the mouth of the well, and scattered grain on top of it, so that nothing was noticed.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[20] When Absalom's servants came to the woman at the house, they asked, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman answered, "They have crossed the stream." The men searched but found no one, so they returned to Jerusalem.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[21] After they had gone, the two climbed out of the well and went and reported to King David. They said to him, "Get up and cross the water quickly, for this is what Ahithophel has advised against you."
[2 Samuel] [17]:[22] So David and all the people with him set out and crossed the Jordan. By daybreak not one was left who had not crossed the Jordan.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[23] When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and set out for his home in his own town. He put his household in order and hanged himself. So he died and was buried in his father's tomb.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[24] David came to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan with all the men of Israel.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[25] Absalom had put Amasa in command of the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra the Israelite, who had married Abigail daughter of Nahash, the sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[26] Israel and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.
[2 Samuel] [17]:[27] When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim
[2 Samuel] [17]:[28] brought bedding, bowls, and pottery, along with wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils,
[2 Samuel] [17]:[29] honey, curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd. They set it before David and the people with him to eat, for they said, "The people have grown hungry, weary, and thirsty in the wilderness."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[1] David mustered the troops who were with him and appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[2] He sent the army out in three divisions: a third under Joab, a third under Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the troops, "I myself will surely march out with you."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[3] But the men said, "You must not go out. If we are put to flight, no one will care about us; even if half of us die, no one will care. But you are worth ten thousand of us. It is better now that you stand ready to help us from the city."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[4] The king said to them, "I will do whatever seems best to you." So the king stood beside the gate while all the troops marched out by hundreds and by thousands.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[5] The king ordered Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, "Deal gently for my sake with the young man Absalom." And all the troops heard the king give this order to all the commanders concerning Absalom.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[6] So the army marched into the field against Israel, and the battle was fought in the forest of Ephraim.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[7] There the army of Israel was routed before the servants of David, and the slaughter there was great that day—twenty thousand men.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[8] The battle spread out over the whole countryside, and the forest devoured more men that day than the sword.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[9] Absalom happened to meet David's men. He was riding on his mule, and as the mule passed under the thick branches of a great oak, Absalom's head caught fast in the tree. He was left hanging between heaven and earth while the mule beneath him went on.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[10] A certain man saw it and reported to Joab, "I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[11] Joab said to the man who told him, "You saw him? Then why didn't you strike him to the ground right there? I would gladly have given you ten pieces of silver and a belt."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[12] But the man replied to Joab, "Even if a thousand pieces of silver were weighed into my hands, I would not lift my hand against the king's son. In our hearing the king commanded you and Abishai and Ittai, 'Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.'
[2 Samuel] [18]:[13] "Or if I had dealt treacherously against my own life—and nothing is hidden from the king—you yourself would have stood aloof."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[14] Joab said, "I will not waste time with you like this." He took three javelins in his hand and thrust them into Absalom's heart while he was still alive in the heart of the oak.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[15] Then ten young men, Joab's armor-bearers, surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[16] Joab sounded the ram's horn, and the troops broke off their pursuit of Israel, for Joab held them back.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[17] They took Absalom, threw him into a deep pit in the forest, and piled a very great heap of stones over him. Meanwhile all Israel fled, each to his own home.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[18] During his lifetime Absalom had taken a pillar and set it up for himself in the King's Valley, for he said, "I have no son to keep my name in remembrance." He named the pillar after himself, and to this day it is called Absalom's Monument.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[19] Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run and bring the king the news that the LORD has vindicated him against his enemies."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[20] But Joab said to him, "You are not the man to carry news today. You may carry news another day, but not today, because the king's son is dead."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[21] Then Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed to Joab and ran off.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[22] Ahimaaz son of Zadok pressed Joab again: "Come what may, let me also run after the Cushite." Joab said, "Why do you want to run, my son? You have no news that will bring you a reward."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[23] "Come what may, I want to run," he said. So Joab told him, "Run." Then Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[24] David was sitting between the two gates. The watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall, looked out, and saw a man running alone.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[25] The watchman called out and told the king. The king said, "If he is alone, he has news to report." And the man came steadily closer.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[26] Then the watchman saw another man running, and he called down to the gatekeeper, "Look, another man is running alone!" The king said, "He too is bringing news."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[27] The watchman said, "It seems to me the first man runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok." "He is a good man," said the king. "He comes with good news."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[28] Ahimaaz called out to the king, "All is well!" He bowed before the king with his face to the ground and said, "Blessed be the LORD your God, who has handed over the men who raised their hands against my lord the king."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[29] The king asked, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" Ahimaaz answered, "I saw a great commotion when the king's servant Joab sent me, your servant, but I do not know what it was."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[30] The king said, "Step aside and stand here." So he stepped aside and stood there.
[2 Samuel] [18]:[31] Then the Cushite arrived and said, "Let my lord the king hear the good news: today the LORD has vindicated you and freed you from the hand of all who rose up against you."
[2 Samuel] [18]:[32] The king asked the Cushite, "Is the young man Absalom safe?" The Cushite answered, "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rose up against you to do you harm, be like that young man."
[2 Samuel] [19]:[1] The king was shaken. He went up to the chamber over the gate and wept, and as he went he cried out, "My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you—Absalom, my son, my son!"
[2 Samuel] [19]:[2] Joab was told, "Look, the king is weeping and mourning for Absalom."
[2 Samuel] [19]:[3] So the victory that day was turned into mourning for all the troops, because that day they heard it said, "The king is grieving over his son."
[2 Samuel] [19]:[4] The troops slipped into the city that day like men who steal away in shame after fleeing from battle.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[5] The king had covered his face, and he cried out at the top of his voice, "My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!"
[2 Samuel] [19]:[6] Then Joab came to the king in the house and said, "Today you have shamed all your servants, who this very day saved your life, and the lives of your sons and daughters, your wives and your concubines.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[7] You love those who hate you and hate those who love you. Today you have made it plain that your commanders and your servants mean nothing to you. I see clearly that if Absalom were alive and all of us dead today, that would suit you well.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[8] Now get up, go out, and speak kindly to your servants. For I swear by the LORD, if you do not go out, not a single man will stay with you tonight, and that will be worse for you than every disaster that has come upon you from your youth until now."
[2 Samuel] [19]:[9] So the king got up and took his seat in the gateway, and word was passed to all the troops: "The king is sitting in the gate." Then all the troops came before the king. Meanwhile Israel had fled, every man to his tent.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[10] Throughout all the tribes of Israel the people were arguing with one another: "The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies; he delivered us from the hand of the Philistines. But now he has fled the land because of Absalom,
[2 Samuel] [19]:[11] and Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about bringing the king back?"
[2 Samuel] [19]:[12] King David sent word to Zadok and Abiathar the priests: "Speak to the elders of Judah and say, 'Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his house, when the talk of all Israel has already reached the king where he is staying?
[2 Samuel] [19]:[13] You are my brothers; you are my own bone and flesh. Why then should you be the last to bring the king back?'
[2 Samuel] [19]:[14] And say to Amasa, 'Are you not my own bone and flesh? So may God do to me, and more also, if you do not become commander of my army for all time, in place of Joab.'"
[2 Samuel] [19]:[15] So he won over the hearts of all the men of Judah as though they were one man, and they sent word to the king: "Come back, you and all your servants."
[2 Samuel] [19]:[16] So the king set out on his return and came to the Jordan, and Judah came to Gilgal to meet the king and bring him across the Jordan.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[17] Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[18] With him were a thousand men from Benjamin, and Ziba, the steward of Saul's household, with his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed down to the Jordan ahead of the king
[2 Samuel] [19]:[19] and crossed at the ford to bring the king's household over and to do whatever he thought best. Shimei son of Gera threw himself down before the king as he was about to cross the Jordan
[2 Samuel] [19]:[20] and said to him, "Let my lord not hold me guilty. Do not remember the wrong your servant did on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem; may the king not take it to heart.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[21] For your servant knows that I have sinned. But see, today I have come, the first of all the house of Joseph, to come down and meet my lord the king."
[2 Samuel] [19]:[22] Then Abishai son of Zeruiah spoke up: "Should Shimei not be put to death for this? He cursed the LORD's anointed!"
[2 Samuel] [19]:[23] But David said, "What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah, that you should turn against me today? Shall a single man be put to death in Israel today? Do I not know that today I am king over Israel?"
[2 Samuel] [19]:[24] So the king said to Shimei, "You shall not die," and the king gave him his oath.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[25] Mephibosheth son of Saul also came down to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet or trimmed his mustache or washed his clothes from the day the king left until the day the king came home safely.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[26] When he came to meet the king in Jerusalem, the king asked him, "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"
[2 Samuel] [19]:[27] He answered, "My lord the king, my servant deceived me. Your servant said, 'I will saddle my donkey and ride it and go with the king'—for your servant is lame.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[28] But he slandered your servant to my lord the king. Still, my lord the king is like an angel of God; do whatever seems good to you.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[29] My father's whole house deserved nothing but death from my lord the king, yet you set your servant among those who eat at your table. What further claim do I have, and what right to appeal to the king?"
[2 Samuel] [19]:[30] The king said to him, "Why go on talking? I have said it: you and Ziba shall divide the land."
[2 Samuel] [19]:[31] And Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take it all, now that my lord the king has come home in peace."
[2 Samuel] [19]:[32] Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim and crossed the Jordan with the king, to escort him across the river.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[33] Barzillai was very old, eighty years of age. He had provided the king with food during his stay at Mahanaim, for he was a very wealthy man.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[34] The king said to Barzillai, "Cross over with me, and I will provide for you at my side in Jerusalem."
[2 Samuel] [19]:[35] But Barzillai answered the king, "How many years of life are left to me, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?
[2 Samuel] [19]:[36] I am eighty years old today. Can I still tell good from bad? Can your servant taste what he eats or drinks? Can I still hear the voices of men and women singing? Why should your servant be one more burden to my lord the king?
[2 Samuel] [19]:[37] Your servant will only cross the Jordan with the king a little way. Why should the king reward me like this?
[2 Samuel] [19]:[38] Please let your servant turn back, so that I may die in my own town, near the grave of my father and mother. But here is your servant Kimham; let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him whatever seems good to you."
[2 Samuel] [19]:[39] The king said, "Kimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him whatever seems good to you; and anything you ask of me I will do for you."
[2 Samuel] [19]:[40] So all the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed too. Then the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and Barzillai returned home.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[41] The king went on to Gilgal, and Kimham went with him. All the men of Judah escorted the king across, and half the men of Israel as well.
[2 Samuel] [19]:[42] Then all the men of Israel came to the king and said to him, "Why did our brothers, the men of Judah, steal you away and bring the king and his household across the Jordan, along with all the men of David?"
[2 Samuel] [19]:[43] The men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king is our close relative. Why does this make you angry? Have we eaten anything at the king's expense? Has he given us any gift?"
[2 Samuel] [19]:[44] The men of Israel answered the men of Judah, "We have ten shares in the king, so we have a greater claim on David than you do. Why then did you treat us with contempt? Were we not the first to speak of bringing back our king?" But the men of Judah spoke even more fiercely than the men of Israel.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[1] Now there happened to be there a scoundrel named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. He sounded the ram's horn and cried out: "We have no share in David, no inheritance in the son of Jesse! To your tents, Israel!"
[2 Samuel] [20]:[2] So all the men of Israel deserted David and followed Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed loyal to their king, all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[3] When David came to his house in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to keep the house and put them under guard. He provided for them, but he did not go in to them. So they were shut away until the day they died, living as widows.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[4] Then the king said to Amasa, "Summon the men of Judah to me within three days, and be here yourself."
[2 Samuel] [20]:[5] So Amasa went to summon Judah, but he took longer than the time appointed for him.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[6] David said to Abishai, "Sheba son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom did. Take your lord's servants and pursue him, or he will find fortified cities for himself and escape us."
[2 Samuel] [20]:[7] So Joab's men went out after him, along with the Kerethites and the Pelethites and all the warriors. They left Jerusalem in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[8] When they reached the great stone at Gibeon, Amasa came to meet them. Joab was wearing his military tunic, and strapped over it at his waist was a belt with a sword in its sheath. As he stepped forward, the sword fell out.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[9] Joab said to Amasa, "Are you well, my brother?" And with his right hand Joab took hold of Amasa's beard to kiss him.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[10] Amasa was not on guard against the sword in Joab's hand, and Joab struck him in the belly with it, spilling his entrails on the ground. He needed no second blow, and Amasa died. Then Joab and his brother Abishai pursued Sheba son of Bichri.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[11] One of Joab's young men stood over Amasa and called out, "Whoever favors Joab and whoever is for David—follow Joab!"
[2 Samuel] [20]:[12] But Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road. When the man saw that all the troops were stopping there, he dragged Amasa off the road into a field and threw a garment over him, for everyone who came upon him stopped at the sight.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[13] Once he had been removed from the road, all the men went on after Joab in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[14] Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel Beth Maacah, and all the Berites gathered together and followed him in.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[15] Joab's forces came and besieged him in Abel Beth Maacah. They threw up a siege ramp against the city, and it stood level with the outer wall, and all the troops with Joab were battering the wall to bring it down.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[16] Then a wise woman called out from the city, "Listen! Listen! Tell Joab to come here so I may speak with him."
[2 Samuel] [20]:[17] He came near, and the woman asked, "Are you Joab?" "I am," he answered. She said to him, "Listen to the words of your servant." "I am listening," he said.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[18] Then she said, "There was a saying in the old days: 'Let them inquire at Abel'—and so the matter was settled.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[19] I am one of the peaceable and faithful in Israel. Yet you are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up the LORD's inheritance?"
[2 Samuel] [20]:[20] Joab answered, "Far be it, far be it from me to swallow up or destroy!
[2 Samuel] [20]:[21] That is not the case. But a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bichri by name, has lifted his hand against the king, against David. Hand over that one man, and I will withdraw from the city." The woman said to Joab, "His head will be thrown to you over the wall."
[2 Samuel] [20]:[22] Then the woman went to all the people with her wise counsel, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it out to Joab. He sounded the ram's horn, and his men dispersed from the city, each to his own tent. And Joab returned to the king in Jerusalem.
[2 Samuel] [20]:[23] Joab was over the whole army of Israel; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and the Pelethites;
[2 Samuel] [20]:[24] Adoram was in charge of forced labor; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the record keeper;
[2 Samuel] [20]:[25] Sheva was secretary; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
[2 Samuel] [20]:[26] and Ira the Jairite was also a priest to David.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[1] In the days of David there was a famine that lasted three years, year after year, and David sought the face of the LORD. The LORD said, "It is because of Saul and his bloodstained house, because he put the Gibeonites to death."
[2 Samuel] [21]:[2] So the king summoned the Gibeonites and spoke to them. Now the Gibeonites were not Israelites but a remnant of the Amorites, and the Israelites had sworn an oath to spare them; yet Saul had sought to strike them down in his zeal for Israel and Judah.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[3] David said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you? How can I make atonement, so that you will bless the inheritance of the LORD?"
[2 Samuel] [21]:[4] The Gibeonites answered him, "It is not a matter of silver or gold between us and Saul or his house, nor is it for us to put any man in Israel to death." David said, "Then what do you say I should do for you?"
[2 Samuel] [21]:[5] They said to the king, "As for the man who consumed us and plotted to destroy us, so that we would not survive anywhere in the territory of Israel—
[2 Samuel] [21]:[6] let seven of his sons be handed over to us, and we will hang them before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of the LORD." The king said, "I will hand them over."
[2 Samuel] [21]:[7] But the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, because of the oath before the LORD that was between them, between David and Jonathan son of Saul.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[8] So the king took the two sons of Rizpah daughter of Aiah, whom she had borne to Saul—Armoni and Mephibosheth—and the five sons of Michal daughter of Saul, whom she had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite. [^1] [^1]: The Hebrew text reads *Michal*; since Adriel married Saul's daughter Merab (1 Samuel 18:19) and Michal had no children (2 Samuel 6:23), some ancient manuscripts and many interpreters read *Merab* here.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[9] He handed them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged them on the hill before the LORD. All seven of them fell together; they were put to death in the first days of the harvest, at the beginning of the barley harvest.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[10] Then Rizpah daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on the rock. From the beginning of the harvest until the rain poured down on the bodies from the heavens, she did not let the birds of the sky settle on them by day or the wild animals by night.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[11] When David was told what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, Saul's concubine, had done,
[2 Samuel] [21]:[12] he went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of his son Jonathan from the citizens of Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen them from the public square of Beth Shan, where the Philistines had hung them on the day they struck Saul down at Gilboa.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[13] He brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of his son Jonathan, and they also gathered the bones of those who had been hanged.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[14] They buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in the land of Benjamin, at Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father, and they did everything the king commanded. After that, God answered prayer on behalf of the land.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[15] Once again there was war between the Philistines and Israel. David went down with his servants, and they fought the Philistines; and David grew weary.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[16] Then Ishbi-Benob, one of the descendants of the Rapha, whose bronze spearhead weighed three hundred shekels and who was armed with a new sword, intended to kill David.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[17] But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to his aid, struck the Philistine down, and killed him. Then David's men swore to him, "Never again will you go out with us to battle, so that the lamp of Israel may not be extinguished."
[2 Samuel] [21]:[18] Some time later there was another battle with the Philistines, at Gob. At that time Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, one of the descendants of the Rapha.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[19] In yet another battle with the Philistines at Gob, Elhanan son of Jaare-Oregim the Bethlehemite struck down Goliath the Gittite, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[20] And there was another battle, at Gath, where there was a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—twenty-four in all. He too was descended from the Rapha.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[21] When he taunted Israel, Jonathan son of Shimeah, David's brother, struck him down.
[2 Samuel] [21]:[22] These four were descendants of the Rapha in Gath, and they fell at the hands of David and his servants.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[1] David spoke to the LORD the words of this song on the day the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[2] He said: The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer,
[2 Samuel] [22]:[3] my God, my rock in whom I take refuge, my shield and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold and my refuge, my savior—you save me from violence.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[4] I call on the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and I am saved from my enemies.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[5] The waves of death engulfed me; the torrents of destruction terrified me.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[6] The cords of the grave coiled around me; the snares of death confronted me.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[7] In my distress I called on the LORD; I called out to my God. From his temple he heard my voice, and my cry reached his ears.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[8] Then the earth reeled and quaked; the foundations of the heavens trembled and shook, because he was angry.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[9] Smoke rose from his nostrils; consuming fire came from his mouth, and burning coals blazed out of it.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[10] He parted the heavens and came down, with dark clouds beneath his feet.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[11] He mounted a cherub and flew; he appeared on the wings of the wind.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[12] He made darkness his canopy around him—a mass of water, thick clouds of the sky.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[13] Out of the brightness before him blazed coals of fire.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[14] The LORD thundered from heaven; the Most High let his voice resound.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[15] He shot his arrows and scattered them, sent lightning and routed them.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[16] The channels of the sea were laid bare, the foundations of the world uncovered, at the rebuke of the LORD, at the blast of breath from his nostrils.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[17] He reached down from on high and took hold of me; he drew me out of deep waters.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[18] He rescued me from my powerful enemy, from my foes, who were too strong for me.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[19] They confronted me in the day of my calamity, but the LORD was my support.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[20] He brought me out into a spacious place; he rescued me because he delighted in me.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[21] The LORD dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he rewarded me.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[22] For I have kept the ways of the LORD; I have not done evil by turning from my God.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[23] All his judgments are before me; I have not turned away from his statutes.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[24] I have been blameless before him and have kept myself from sin.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[25] The LORD has repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness in his sight.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[26] To the faithful you show yourself faithful, to the blameless warrior you show yourself blameless,
[2 Samuel] [22]:[27] to the pure you show yourself pure, but to the crooked you show yourself shrewd.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[28] You save an afflicted people, but your eyes are on the haughty, and you bring them low.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[29] You are my lamp, O LORD; the LORD turns my darkness into light.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[30] With you I can charge a troop; with my God I can scale a wall.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[31] As for God, his way is perfect; the word of the LORD is flawless. He is a shield to all who take refuge in him.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[32] For who is God besides the LORD? And who is a rock except our God?
[2 Samuel] [22]:[33] God is my strong fortress; he makes my way perfect.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[34] He makes my feet like the feet of a deer; he sets me secure on the heights.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[35] He trains my hands for battle; my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[36] You have given me the shield of your salvation; your help has made me great.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[37] You widen the path beneath me, so that my ankles do not give way.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[38] I pursued my enemies and destroyed them; I did not turn back until they were wiped out.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[39] I consumed them and crushed them; they could not rise—they fell beneath my feet.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[40] You armed me with strength for battle; you made my adversaries bow beneath me.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[41] You made my enemies turn their backs in flight, and I destroyed those who hated me.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[42] They looked for help, but no one saved them—to the LORD, but he did not answer.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[43] I ground them fine as the dust of the earth; I crushed and trampled them like mud in the streets.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[44] You delivered me from the strife of my people; you kept me as the head of nations. A people I did not know now serves me.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[45] Foreigners cower before me; as soon as they hear of me, they obey me.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[46] Foreigners lose heart; they come trembling from their strongholds.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[47] The LORD lives! Blessed be my Rock! Exalted be God, the Rock of my salvation—
[2 Samuel] [22]:[48] the God who avenges me, who brings peoples down under me,
[2 Samuel] [22]:[49] who sets me free from my enemies. You lift me above my adversaries; you rescue me from violent men.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[50] Therefore I will praise you, O LORD, among the nations; I will sing praises to your name.
[2 Samuel] [22]:[51] He gives his king great victories; he shows unfailing love to his anointed, to David and his descendants forever.[^1] [^1]: The written Hebrew form here can also be read "He is a tower of salvation for his king."
[2 Samuel] [23]:[1] These are the last words of David: The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, the sweet singer of Israel:
[2 Samuel] [23]:[2] The Spirit of the LORD has spoken through me; his word was on my tongue.
[2 Samuel] [23]:[3] The God of Israel has spoken; the Rock of Israel said to me: One who rules over men in righteousness, who rules in the fear of God,
[2 Samuel] [23]:[4] is like the light of morning at sunrise, a cloudless dawn, like the gleam after rain that brings grass from the earth.
[2 Samuel] [23]:[5] Is not my house so with God? For he has made an everlasting covenant with me, ordered in every detail and secure. Will he not bring to flower all my salvation and every desire?
[2 Samuel] [23]:[6] But the worthless are all like thorns swept aside; they cannot be gathered by hand.
[2 Samuel] [23]:[7] Anyone who touches them must arm himself with iron or the shaft of a spear; they are burned up completely on the spot.

[2 Samuel] [23]:[9] Next to him was Eleazar son of Dodo son of Ahohi, one of the three mighty men with David when they defied the Philistines who had gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel withdrew.

[2 Samuel] [23]:[11] Next to him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines had massed at Lehi, where there was a field full of lentils, and the troops fled from the Philistines.

[2 Samuel] [23]:[13] Three of the thirty chief men went down at harvest time to David at the cave of Adullam, while a band of Philistines was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
[2 Samuel] [23]:[14] David was then in the stronghold, and a Philistine garrison held Bethlehem.
[2 Samuel] [23]:[15] David said longingly, "If only someone would give me a drink of water from the well at the gate of Bethlehem!"
[2 Samuel] [23]:[16] So the three mighty men broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well at the gate of Bethlehem, and carried it back to David. But he would not drink it; he poured it out to the LORD.
[2 Samuel] [23]:[17] "Far be it from me, LORD, to do this," he said. "Is this not the blood of men who went at the risk of their lives?" And he refused to drink it. Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.

[2 Samuel] [23]:[19] Was he not the most honored of the thirty? He became their commander, but he never attained to the three.
[2 Samuel] [23]:[20] Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man from Kabzeel, was a doer of great deeds. He struck down the two champions of Moab, and he went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.
[2 Samuel] [23]:[21] He also struck down an imposing Egyptian. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but Benaiah went against him with a club, wrenched the spear from the Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear.
[2 Samuel] [23]:[22] Such were the deeds of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he won a name among the three mighty men.
[2 Samuel] [23]:[23] He was honored above the thirty, but he did not belong to the three. And David put him in charge of his bodyguard.

[2 Samuel] [24]:[1] Again the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, "Go, count Israel and Judah."
[2 Samuel] [24]:[2] So the king said to Joab, the commander of the army who was with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and register the people, so that I may know how many there are."
[2 Samuel] [24]:[3] But Joab said to the king, "May the LORD your God multiply the people a hundred times over, and may the eyes of my lord the king live to see it. But why does my lord the king desire such a thing?"
[2 Samuel] [24]:[4] The king's word, however, prevailed against Joab and the commanders of the army, so Joab and the commanders went out from the king's presence to register the people of Israel.
[2 Samuel] [24]:[5] They crossed the Jordan and camped at Aroer, south of the town that lies in the middle of the valley of Gad, and then went on to Jazer.
[2 Samuel] [24]:[6] They came to Gilead and to the region of Tahtim Hodshi, and on to Dan Jaan and around to Sidon.
[2 Samuel] [24]:[7] Then they came to the fortress of Tyre and all the towns of the Hivites and Canaanites, and finally they went on to Beersheba in the Negev of Judah.
[2 Samuel] [24]:[8] After going through the whole land, they came back to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
[2 Samuel] [24]:[9] Joab reported the number of the people to the king: in Israel there were eight hundred thousand able-bodied men who could handle a sword, and in Judah five hundred thousand.
[2 Samuel] [24]:[10] But afterward David's heart struck him for having counted the people, and he said to the LORD, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, LORD, take away the guilt of your servant, for I have acted like a fool."
[2 Samuel] [24]:[11] Before David got up the next morning, the word of the LORD had come to Gad the prophet, David's seer:
[2 Samuel] [24]:[12] "Go and say to David, 'This is what the LORD says: I am offering you three things. Choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you.'"
[2 Samuel] [24]:[13] So Gad went to David and told him, "Shall seven years of famine come upon your land? Or three months of fleeing from your enemies while they pursue you? Or three days of plague in your land? Now think it over and decide what answer I should give to the one who sent me."
[2 Samuel] [24]:[14] David said to Gad, "I am in deep distress. Let us fall into the hands of the LORD, for his mercy is great; but do not let me fall into human hands."
[2 Samuel] [24]:[15] So the LORD sent a plague upon Israel from that morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand of the people died, from Dan to Beersheba.
[2 Samuel] [24]:[16] When the angel stretched out his hand to destroy Jerusalem, the LORD relented from the disaster and said to the angel who was destroying the people, "Enough! Stay your hand now." The angel of the LORD was then at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
[2 Samuel] [24]:[17] When David saw the angel who was striking down the people, he said to the LORD, "I am the one who has sinned; I am the one who has done wrong. But these sheep—what have they done? Let your hand fall on me and on my father's house."
[2 Samuel] [24]:[18] That day Gad came to David and said to him, "Go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."
[2 Samuel] [24]:[19] So David went up, as the LORD had commanded through the word of Gad.
[2 Samuel] [24]:[20] When Araunah looked out and saw the king and his men coming toward him, he went out and bowed down before the king with his face to the ground.
[2 Samuel] [24]:[21] Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" David answered, "To buy your threshing floor, so that I can build an altar to the LORD and the plague on the people may be stopped."
[2 Samuel] [24]:[22] Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take whatever pleases him and offer it up. Here are oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and the ox yokes for the wood.
[2 Samuel] [24]:[23] All this Araunah gives to the king." And he added, "May the LORD your God accept you."
[2 Samuel] [24]:[24] But the king said to Araunah, "No, I insist on paying you for it. I will not offer to the LORD my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
[2 Samuel] [24]:[25] David built an altar to the LORD there and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. Then the LORD answered his prayer for the land, and the plague on Israel was stopped.
[1 Kings] [1]:[1] King David was now old, advanced in years, and though they covered him with clothes, he could not get warm.
[1 Kings] [1]:[2] So his servants said to him, "Let a search be made for a young virgin for my lord the king. Let her attend the king and care for him; let her lie in your arms, and my lord the king will be warm."
[1 Kings] [1]:[3] They searched throughout the territory of Israel for a beautiful young woman, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
[1 Kings] [1]:[4] The young woman was very beautiful. She cared for the king and served him, but the king did not have relations with her.
[1 Kings] [1]:[5] Now Adonijah son of Haggith put himself forward, saying, "I will be king." He provided himself with chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run ahead of him.
[1 Kings] [1]:[6] His father had never rebuked him or asked, "Why have you done this?" He was also very handsome, and he was born next after Absalom.
[1 Kings] [1]:[7] He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they gave their support to Adonijah.
[1 Kings] [1]:[8] But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's own warriors did not side with Adonijah.
[1 Kings] [1]:[9] Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fattened calves at the Stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En Rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah who were royal officials,
[1 Kings] [1]:[10] but he did not invite Nathan the prophet, or Benaiah, or the warriors, or his brother Solomon.
[1 Kings] [1]:[11] Then Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord David knows nothing about it?
[1 Kings] [1]:[12] Come now, let me advise you how to save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.
[1 Kings] [1]:[13] Go in to King David and say to him, 'My lord the king, did you not swear to your servant, "Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne"? Why then has Adonijah become king?'
[1 Kings] [1]:[14] While you are still speaking with the king, I will come in after you and confirm what you have said."
[1 Kings] [1]:[15] So Bathsheba went in to the king in his chamber. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was attending him.
[1 Kings] [1]:[16] Bathsheba bowed low and paid homage to the king. "What do you want?" the king asked.
[1 Kings] [1]:[17] She said to him, "My lord, you yourself swore to your servant by the LORD your God: 'Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne.'
[1 Kings] [1]:[18] But now Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, know nothing about it.
[1 Kings] [1]:[19] He has sacrificed great numbers of cattle, fattened calves, and sheep, and has invited all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army, but he has not invited your servant Solomon.
[1 Kings] [1]:[20] My lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, waiting for you to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
[1 Kings] [1]:[21] Otherwise, as soon as my lord the king rests with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be treated as criminals."
[1 Kings] [1]:[22] While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
[1 Kings] [1]:[23] They told the king, "Nathan the prophet is here." So he came before the king and bowed with his face to the ground.
[1 Kings] [1]:[24] Nathan said, "My lord the king, have you declared that Adonijah shall be king after you and shall sit on your throne?
[1 Kings] [1]:[25] For today he has gone down and sacrificed great numbers of cattle, fattened calves, and sheep. He has invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest, and right now they are eating and drinking in his presence and shouting, 'Long live King Adonijah!'
[1 Kings] [1]:[26] But he did not invite me, your servant, or Zadok the priest, or Benaiah son of Jehoiada, or your servant Solomon.
[1 Kings] [1]:[27] Has this been done by my lord the king without letting your servant know who is to sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?"
[1 Kings] [1]:[28] Then King David said, "Call Bathsheba in to me." She came into the king's presence and stood before him.
[1 Kings] [1]:[29] And the king swore an oath: "As surely as the LORD lives, who has delivered me out of every trouble,
[1 Kings] [1]:[30] I will carry out this very day what I swore to you by the LORD, the God of Israel: Solomon your son shall be king after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place."
[1 Kings] [1]:[31] Then Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground, knelt before the king, and said, "May my lord King David live forever!"
[1 Kings] [1]:[32] King David said, "Call in Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada." When they came before the king,
[1 Kings] [1]:[33] he said to them, "Take your lord's servants with you, set my son Solomon on my own mule, and escort him down to Gihon.
[1 Kings] [1]:[34] There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him king over Israel. Then blow the trumpet and shout, 'Long live King Solomon!'
[1 Kings] [1]:[35] Then come back up after him, and let him come and sit on my throne and reign in my place. I have appointed him ruler over Israel and Judah."
[1 Kings] [1]:[36] Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, "Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, so declare it.
[1 Kings] [1]:[37] As the LORD was with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he make his throne even greater than the throne of my lord King David."
[1 Kings] [1]:[38] So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Kerethites and the Pelethites went down, set Solomon on King David's mule, and brought him to Gihon.
[1 Kings] [1]:[39] Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. Then they sounded the trumpet, and all the people shouted, "Long live King Solomon!"
[1 Kings] [1]:[40] And all the people went up after him, playing flutes and rejoicing with such great joy that the earth resounded with their noise.
[1 Kings] [1]:[41] Adonijah and all his guests heard it just as they were finishing their feast. When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he said, "Why is the city in such an uproar?"
[1 Kings] [1]:[42] Even as he spoke, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrived. Adonijah said, "Come in. You are a man of standing; surely you bring good news."
[1 Kings] [1]:[43] "Not at all," Jonathan answered. "Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
[1 Kings] [1]:[44] The king sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Kerethites and the Pelethites, and they set him on the king's mule.
[1 Kings] [1]:[45] Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king at Gihon. They came up from there rejoicing, and the city rang with it. That is the noise you heard.
[1 Kings] [1]:[46] What is more, Solomon has taken his seat on the royal throne.
[1 Kings] [1]:[47] And the king's servants have come to congratulate our lord King David, saying, 'May your God make Solomon's name greater than yours, and his throne greater than yours!' And the king bowed in worship on his bed.
[1 Kings] [1]:[48] The king also said, 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has today granted one to sit on my throne while my own eyes look on.'"
[1 Kings] [1]:[49] At this all Adonijah's guests rose in alarm, and each went his own way.
[1 Kings] [1]:[50] But Adonijah, in fear of Solomon, got up and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.
[1 Kings] [1]:[51] Then Solomon was told, "Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon and has taken hold of the horns of the altar. He says, 'Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put his servant to the sword.'"
[1 Kings] [1]:[52] Solomon replied, "If he proves himself a man of honor, not a hair of his head will fall to the ground; but if evil is found in him, he will die."
[1 Kings] [1]:[53] Then King Solomon sent men, and they brought him down from the altar. Adonijah came and bowed before King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, "Go to your house."
[1 Kings] [2]:[1] When David's time to die drew near, he charged his son Solomon:
[1 Kings] [2]:[2] "I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, and show yourself a man.
[1 Kings] [2]:[3] Keep the charge of the LORD your God: walk in his ways, and keep his statutes, his commandments, his ordinances, and his testimonies, as it is written in the Law of Moses, so that you may prosper in everything you do and everywhere you turn.
[1 Kings] [2]:[4] Do this so that the LORD may fulfill the promise he made concerning me: 'If your sons watch their way and walk faithfully before me with all their heart and with all their soul, you will never lack a man on the throne of Israel.'
[1 Kings] [2]:[5] You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me—what he did to the two commanders of Israel's armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them, shedding the blood of war in a time of peace, and he put the blood of war on the belt around his waist and on the sandals on his feet.
[1 Kings] [2]:[6] Act with the wisdom you have, and do not let his gray head go down to the grave in peace.
[1 Kings] [2]:[7] But show kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for they stood by me when I fled from your brother Absalom.
[1 Kings] [2]:[8] And there is with you Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim. He cursed me with a bitter curse the day I went to Mahanaim. But when he came down to meet me at the Jordan, I swore to him by the LORD, 'I will not put you to death by the sword.'
[1 Kings] [2]:[9] Now do not let him go unpunished. You are a wise man; you will know what to do to him. Bring his gray head down to the grave in blood."
[1 Kings] [2]:[10] Then David slept with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.
[1 Kings] [2]:[11] David reigned over Israel forty years: seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
[1 Kings] [2]:[12] So Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was firmly established.
[1 Kings] [2]:[13] Now Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. She asked, "Do you come in peace?" "In peace," he said.
[1 Kings] [2]:[14] Then he added, "I have something to say to you." "Speak," she said.
[1 Kings] [2]:[15] He said, "You know that the kingdom was mine, and that all Israel looked to me as king. But the kingdom has turned about and gone to my brother, for it came to him from the LORD.
[1 Kings] [2]:[16] Now I have one request to make of you; do not refuse me." "Speak," she said.
[1 Kings] [2]:[17] He said, "Please ask King Solomon—he will not refuse you—to give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife."
[1 Kings] [2]:[18] "Very well," Bathsheba said, "I will speak to the king for you."
[1 Kings] [2]:[19] So Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king rose to meet her and bowed to her; then he sat down on his throne and had a throne brought for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand.
[1 Kings] [2]:[20] She said, "I have one small request to make of you; do not refuse me." The king answered, "Ask, my mother; I will not refuse you."
[1 Kings] [2]:[21] So she said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife."
[1 Kings] [2]:[22] King Solomon answered his mother, "And why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask the kingdom for him as well—he is my older brother—yes, for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah!"
[1 Kings] [2]:[23] Then King Solomon swore by the LORD: "May God do so to me and more also, if Adonijah has not spoken this word at the cost of his life!
[1 Kings] [2]:[24] Now therefore, as the LORD lives, who has established me and seated me on the throne of my father David and who has made me a house as he promised—today Adonijah shall be put to death!"
[1 Kings] [2]:[25] So King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who struck Adonijah down, and he died.
[1 Kings] [2]:[26] To Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go to Anathoth, to your own fields. You deserve to die, but I will not put you to death now, because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD before my father David and shared in all my father's hardships."
[1 Kings] [2]:[27] So Solomon removed Abiathar from serving as priest to the LORD, fulfilling the word the LORD had spoken at Shiloh concerning the house of Eli.
[1 Kings] [2]:[28] When the news reached Joab—who had sided with Adonijah, though he had not sided with Absalom—he fled to the tent of the LORD and took hold of the horns of the altar.
[1 Kings] [2]:[29] King Solomon was told that Joab had fled to the tent of the LORD and was there beside the altar. So Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada with the order, "Go, strike him down."
[1 Kings] [2]:[30] Benaiah came to the tent of the LORD and said to Joab, "The king says, 'Come out!'" But he answered, "No, I will die here." Benaiah brought word back to the king: "This is what Joab said, and this is how he answered me."
[1 Kings] [2]:[31] The king said to him, "Do as he says. Strike him down and bury him, and so remove from me and from my father's house the innocent blood that Joab shed.
[1 Kings] [2]:[32] The LORD will bring Joab's blood back on his own head, because he struck down two men more righteous and better than himself and killed them with the sword, without my father David's knowledge: Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel's army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah's army.
[1 Kings] [2]:[33] Their blood will come back on the head of Joab and on the head of his descendants forever; but for David and his descendants, his house and his throne, there will be peace from the LORD forevermore."
[1 Kings] [2]:[34] So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up, struck Joab down, and put him to death; and he was buried at his own house in the wilderness.
[1 Kings] [2]:[35] The king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada over the army in his place, and he put Zadok the priest in the place of Abiathar.
[1 Kings] [2]:[36] Then the king summoned Shimei and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there; do not go out from there to anywhere at all.
[1 Kings] [2]:[37] On the day you leave and cross the Kidron Valley, know for certain that you will die; your blood will be on your own head."
[1 Kings] [2]:[38] Shimei answered the king, "The sentence is fair. As my lord the king has said, so your servant will do." And Shimei lived in Jerusalem a long time.
[1 Kings] [2]:[39] But at the end of three years, two of Shimei's slaves ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath, and Shimei was told, "Your slaves are in Gath."
[1 Kings] [2]:[40] So Shimei got up, saddled his donkey, and went to Achish at Gath to look for his slaves; he went and brought them back from Gath.
[1 Kings] [2]:[41] When Solomon was told that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and returned,
[1 Kings] [2]:[42] the king summoned Shimei and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by the LORD and warn you, 'On the day you leave and go anywhere at all, know for certain that you will die'? And you said to me, 'The sentence is fair; I will obey.'
[1 Kings] [2]:[43] Why then have you not kept your oath to the LORD and the command I laid on you?"
