[1 Kings] [2]:[44] The king also said to Shimei, "You know—your own heart knows—all the evil you did to my father David. So the LORD will bring your evil back on your own head.
[1 Kings] [2]:[45] But King Solomon will be blessed, and David's throne will be established before the LORD forever."
[1 Kings] [2]:[46] Then the king gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who went out and struck Shimei down, and he died. So the kingdom was firmly established in Solomon's hand.
[1 Kings] [3]:[1] Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt. He took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her to the City of David until he had finished building his own house, the house of the LORD, and the wall around Jerusalem.
[1 Kings] [3]:[2] The people, however, were still sacrificing at the high places, because no house had yet been built for the name of the LORD.
[1 Kings] [3]:[3] Solomon loved the LORD, walking in the statutes of his father David—except that he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
[1 Kings] [3]:[4] The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place; Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
[1 Kings] [3]:[5] At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, and God said, "Ask what I should give you."
[1 Kings] [3]:[6] Solomon answered, "You showed great kindness to your servant David, my father, because he walked before you in faithfulness and righteousness and uprightness of heart toward you. You have kept for him this great kindness and have given him a son to sit on his throne this very day.
[1 Kings] [3]:[7] And now, LORD my God, you have made your servant king in place of my father David, but I am only a young man; I do not know how to go out or come in.
[1 Kings] [3]:[8] Your servant is among your people whom you have chosen, a people so numerous they cannot be counted or numbered.
[1 Kings] [3]:[9] So give your servant a listening heart to judge your people, to discern between good and evil—for who is able to judge this great people of yours?"
[1 Kings] [3]:[10] It pleased the LORD that Solomon had asked for this.
[1 Kings] [3]:[11] God said to him, "Because you have asked for this and have not asked for long life for yourself, or riches, or the death of your enemies, but have asked for discernment to hear a case rightly,
[1 Kings] [3]:[12] I now do as you have asked. I give you a heart so wise and discerning that no one like you has ever lived before you, and no one like you will arise after you.
[1 Kings] [3]:[13] I also give you what you did not ask for: both riches and honor, so that among kings there will be no one like you all your days.
[1 Kings] [3]:[14] And if you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and my commandments, as your father David walked, I will lengthen your days."
[1 Kings] [3]:[15] Then Solomon awoke—and it had been a dream. He went to Jerusalem, stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, and gave a banquet for all his servants.
[1 Kings] [3]:[16] Then two women who were prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.
[1 Kings] [3]:[17] One of the women said, "Please, my lord, this woman and I live in the same house, and I gave birth while she was there in the house.
[1 Kings] [3]:[18] On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also had a child. We were alone; there was no stranger with us in the house—only the two of us.
[1 Kings] [3]:[19] During the night this woman's son died, because she lay on him.
[1 Kings] [3]:[20] So she got up in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your servant was asleep. She laid him at her breast and laid her dead son at mine.
[1 Kings] [3]:[21] When I got up in the morning to nurse my son, there he was—dead. But when I looked at him closely in the morning, I saw that he was not the son I had borne."
[1 Kings] [3]:[22] The other woman said, "No! The living one is my son; the dead one is yours." But the first insisted, "No! The dead one is yours; the living one is mine." So they argued before the king.
[1 Kings] [3]:[23] Then the king said, "One says, 'This is my son who is alive, and your son is dead,' and the other says, 'No! Your son is dead, and my son is alive.'"
[1 Kings] [3]:[24] So the king said, "Bring me a sword." And they brought a sword before the king.
[1 Kings] [3]:[25] Then the king ordered, "Cut the living child in two, and give half to one and half to the other."
[1 Kings] [3]:[26] But the woman whose son was alive was moved with deep compassion for her son and said to the king, "Please, my lord, give her the living child—only do not kill him!" The other said, "He shall be neither mine nor yours. Cut him in two!"
[1 Kings] [3]:[27] Then the king gave his ruling: "Give the living child to her; do not kill him. She is his mother."
[1 Kings] [3]:[28] When all Israel heard the verdict the king had given, they stood in awe of him, for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to administer justice.
[1 Kings] [4]:[1] So King Solomon ruled over all Israel.
[1 Kings] [4]:[2] These were his high officials: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest;
[1 Kings] [4]:[3] Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, secretaries; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, the record keeper;
[1 Kings] [4]:[4] Benaiah son of Jehoiada, commander of the army; Zadok and Abiathar, priests;
[1 Kings] [4]:[5] Azariah son of Nathan, in charge of the district governors; Zabud son of Nathan, priest and friend of the king;
[1 Kings] [4]:[6] Ahishar, in charge of the palace; and Adoniram son of Abda, in charge of the forced labor.
[1 Kings] [4]:[7] Solomon had twelve district governors over all Israel, who supplied provisions for the king and his household. Each one was responsible for one month of the year.
[1 Kings] [4]:[8] These are their names: Ben-Hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;
[1 Kings] [4]:[9] Ben-Deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, and Elon Beth Hanan;
[1 Kings] [4]:[10] Ben-Hesed, in Arubboth—Socoh and all the land of Hepher were his;
[1 Kings] [4]:[11] Ben-Abinadab, in all of Naphath Dor—he had Solomon's daughter Taphath as his wife;
[1 Kings] [4]:[12] Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo, and all of Beth Shan, which lies beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth Shan to Abel Meholah and over as far as Jokmeam;
[1 Kings] [4]:[13] Ben-Geber, in Ramoth Gilead—the settlements of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead were his, as well as the region of Argob in Bashan, sixty large cities with walls and bronze bars on their gates;
[1 Kings] [4]:[14] Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
[1 Kings] [4]:[15] Ahimaaz, in Naphtali—he too had married a daughter of Solomon, Basemath;
[1 Kings] [4]:[16] Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
[1 Kings] [4]:[17] Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;
[1 Kings] [4]:[18] Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;
[1 Kings] [4]:[19] Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the country of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan. He was the one governor over that land.
[1 Kings] [4]:[20] The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore; they ate and drank and rejoiced.
[1 Kings] [5]:[1] Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines and on to the border of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.
[1 Kings] [5]:[2] Solomon's provisions for a single day were thirty kors of fine flour and sixty kors of meal,
[1 Kings] [5]:[3] ten fattened oxen, twenty pasture-fed cattle, and a hundred sheep and goats, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened fowl.
[1 Kings] [5]:[4] For he held sway over the whole region west of the Euphrates, from Tiphsah to Gaza, and over all its kings, and he had peace on every side.
[1 Kings] [5]:[5] So Judah and Israel lived in safety, everyone under his own vine and his own fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
[1 Kings] [5]:[6] Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots and twelve thousand horsemen.
[1 Kings] [5]:[7] Those officers supplied provisions for King Solomon and for all who came to King Solomon's table, each in his appointed month; they let nothing be lacking.
[1 Kings] [5]:[8] They also brought barley and straw for the horses and the swift steeds to the place where they were needed, each according to his assigned duty.
[1 Kings] [5]:[9] God gave Solomon wisdom and very great insight, and a breadth of understanding as measureless as the sand on the seashore.
[1 Kings] [5]:[10] Solomon's wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the peoples of the East and all the wisdom of Egypt.
[1 Kings] [5]:[11] He was wiser than anyone else—wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and than Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol—and his fame spread through all the surrounding nations.
[1 Kings] [5]:[12] He composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.
[1 Kings] [5]:[13] He spoke about trees, from the cedar of Lebanon to the hyssop that grows out of a wall; and he spoke about animals and birds, creeping things and fish.
[1 Kings] [5]:[14] People came from every nation to hear Solomon's wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth who had heard how wise he was.
[1 Kings] [5]:[15] When Hiram king of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed king in place of his father, he sent his servants to him, for Hiram had always been a friend of David.
[1 Kings] [5]:[16] And Solomon sent this message to Hiram:
[1 Kings] [5]:[17] "You know that my father David could not build a house for the name of the LORD his God because of the wars that surrounded him on every side, until the LORD put his enemies under the soles of my feet.
[1 Kings] [5]:[18] But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side; there is no adversary, no disaster.
[1 Kings] [5]:[19] So I intend to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, just as the LORD told my father David: 'Your son, whom I will set on your throne in your place, he shall build the house for my name.'
[1 Kings] [5]:[20] Now then, give orders that cedars of Lebanon be cut for me. My servants will work alongside your servants, and I will pay you whatever wages you set for your servants. For you know that we have no one who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians."
[1 Kings] [5]:[21] When Hiram heard Solomon's message, he was overjoyed and said, "Blessed be the LORD this day, who has given David a wise son to rule this great people."
[1 Kings] [5]:[22] So Hiram sent word to Solomon: "I have received your message. I will do everything you desire with the cedar and cypress timber.
[1 Kings] [5]:[23] My servants will bring the logs down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will float them in rafts by sea to the place you designate. There I will have them broken apart, and you can take them away. And you, in turn, will meet my need by supplying food for my household."
[1 Kings] [5]:[24] So Hiram kept Solomon supplied with all the cedar and cypress timber he wanted,
[1 Kings] [5]:[25] and Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand kors of wheat as food for his household and twenty kors of pressed oil. This Solomon gave to Hiram year after year.
[1 Kings] [5]:[26] The LORD gave Solomon wisdom, just as he had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a treaty.
[1 Kings] [5]:[27] King Solomon conscripted laborers from all Israel—thirty thousand men in all.
[1 Kings] [5]:[28] He sent them to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand a month, so that they spent one month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor.
[1 Kings] [5]:[29] Solomon also had seventy thousand men to carry loads and eighty thousand to quarry stone in the hills,
[1 Kings] [5]:[30] besides his three thousand three hundred foremen who were in charge of the project and supervised the workers.
[1 Kings] [5]:[31] At the king's command they quarried huge, costly blocks of dressed stone to lay the foundation of the temple.
[1 Kings] [5]:[32] Solomon's builders and Hiram's builders, together with the men of Gebal, cut and shaped them, and they prepared the timber and the stone for building the temple.
[1 Kings] [6]:[1] In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites came out of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, which is the second month, he began to build the house of the LORD.
[1 Kings] [6]:[2] The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
[1 Kings] [6]:[3] The portico in front of the main hall of the house was twenty cubits long, matching the width of the house, and it projected ten cubits out from the front of the house.
[1 Kings] [6]:[4] He made windows for the house, recessed and latticed.
[1 Kings] [6]:[5] Against the wall of the house he built a structure running all around it, enclosing the walls of the house on every side, both the main hall and the inner sanctuary; and he made side chambers all around.
[1 Kings] [6]:[6] The lowest story was five cubits wide, the middle one six cubits, and the third seven cubits, for he set recesses in the outside wall of the house all around, so that the beams would not be inserted into the walls of the house.
[1 Kings] [6]:[7] When the house was built, it was built of stone finished at the quarry, so that no hammer or ax or any iron tool was heard in the house while it was being built.
[1 Kings] [6]:[8] The entrance to the lowest story was on the south side of the house; a winding stairway led up to the middle story, and from the middle story to the third.[^ The Hebrew text reads "middle story"; "lowest" follows the ancient versions.]
[1 Kings] [6]:[9] So he built the house and finished it, and he roofed the house with beams and planks of cedar.
[1 Kings] [6]:[10] He built the side structure against the whole house, each story five cubits high, and it was joined to the house with timbers of cedar.
[1 Kings] [6]:[11] Then the word of the LORD came to Solomon:
[1 Kings] [6]:[12] "Concerning this house you are building: if you walk in my statutes and carry out my judgments and keep all my commandments by walking in them, then I will establish with you the word I spoke to David your father.
[1 Kings] [6]:[13] I will dwell among the Israelites, and I will not forsake my people Israel."
[1 Kings] [6]:[14] So Solomon built the house and finished it.
[1 Kings] [6]:[15] He lined the inner walls of the house with cedar boards, paneling them with wood from the floor of the house to the rafters of the ceiling, and he covered the floor of the house with cypress boards.
[1 Kings] [6]:[16] He partitioned off twenty cubits at the rear of the house with cedar boards from floor to ceiling, and within he built the inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
[1 Kings] [6]:[17] The main hall in front of the inner sanctuary was forty cubits long.
[1 Kings] [6]:[18] The cedar within the house was carved with gourds and open flowers; everything was cedar, and no stone could be seen.
[1 Kings] [6]:[19] He prepared the inner sanctuary within the house, to place there the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
[1 Kings] [6]:[20] The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high, and he overlaid it with pure gold; and he overlaid the altar of cedar.
[1 Kings] [6]:[21] Solomon overlaid the interior of the house with pure gold, and he stretched gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which he had overlaid with gold.
[1 Kings] [6]:[22] He overlaid the whole house with gold, until the entire house was finished, and he also overlaid with gold the altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary.
[1 Kings] [6]:[23] In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olive wood, each ten cubits high.
[1 Kings] [6]:[24] One wing of the cherub was five cubits and the other wing five cubits—ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other.
[1 Kings] [6]:[25] The second cherub also measured ten cubits; both cherubim had the same measurements and the same form.
[1 Kings] [6]:[26] The height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and so was the other.
[1 Kings] [6]:[27] He placed the cherubim inside the innermost room. Their wings were spread out, so that the wing of the one touched one wall and the wing of the other touched the other wall, while in the middle of the room their wings touched wing to wing.
[1 Kings] [6]:[28] And he overlaid the cherubim with gold.
[1 Kings] [6]:[29] On all the walls of the house, all around, both in the inner and the outer room, he carved figures of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.
[1 Kings] [6]:[30] He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, in both the inner and the outer room.
[1 Kings] [6]:[31] For the entrance to the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive wood, with a lintel and five-sided doorposts.
[1 Kings] [6]:[32] On the two olive-wood doors he carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and he overlaid them with gold, hammering the gold over the cherubim and the palm trees.
[1 Kings] [6]:[33] In the same way he made doorposts of olive wood, four-sided, for the entrance to the main hall,
[1 Kings] [6]:[34] and two doors of cypress wood, each door having two leaves that turned on their hinges.
[1 Kings] [6]:[35] He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers on them, and overlaid them with gold, evenly applied over the carving.
[1 Kings] [6]:[36] He built the inner court with three courses of dressed stone and one course of trimmed cedar beams.
[1 Kings] [6]:[37] The foundation of the house of the LORD was laid in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv.
[1 Kings] [6]:[38] And in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul—that is, the eighth month—the house was finished, down to every detail and every specification. So he built it in seven years.
[1 Kings] [7]:[1] Solomon spent thirteen years building his own palace, until the whole of it was finished.
[1 Kings] [7]:[2] He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high, resting on four rows of cedar pillars with cedar beams laid across the pillars.
[1 Kings] [7]:[3] It was roofed with cedar above the beams that rested on the pillars—forty-five of them, fifteen to a row.
[1 Kings] [7]:[4] There were three rows of window frames, window facing window in three tiers.
[1 Kings] [7]:[5] All the doorways and their frames were squared, and window faced window in three tiers.
[1 Kings] [7]:[6] He made the Hall of Pillars fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide, with a porch in front of it, and pillars with a canopy in front of them.
[1 Kings] [7]:[7] He made the Hall of the Throne, where he would give judgment—the Hall of Judgment—and it was paneled with cedar from floor to rafters.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew reads "from floor to floor."
[1 Kings] [7]:[8] His own residence, where he lived, was in the other court behind the hall, built in the same manner. He also built a house like this hall for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had married.
[1 Kings] [7]:[9] All of these were of costly stones, cut to measure and trimmed with the saw on the inside and the outside, from the foundation up to the coping, and outside as far as the great court.
[1 Kings] [7]:[10] The foundation was of costly stones, great stones, some ten cubits and some eight cubits long.
[1 Kings] [7]:[11] Above these were costly stones, cut to measure, and cedar.
[1 Kings] [7]:[12] The great court had all around it three courses of dressed stone and one course of cedar beams, as did the inner court of the LORD's house and the vestibule of the house.
[1 Kings] [7]:[13] King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre.
[1 Kings] [7]:[14] He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father had been a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze. He was filled with skill, understanding, and knowledge to do every kind of work in bronze. He came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.
[1 Kings] [7]:[15] He cast the two bronze pillars. One pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a line of twelve cubits measured its circumference; so also the second pillar.
[1 Kings] [7]:[16] He made two capitals of cast bronze to set on the tops of the pillars; each capital was five cubits high.
[1 Kings] [7]:[17] Lattices of woven mesh and wreaths of chainwork covered the capitals on the tops of the pillars—seven wreaths for each capital.
[1 Kings] [7]:[18] He made the pomegranates in two rows all around on the one network, to cover the capital at the top of the pillar, and he did the same for the other capital.
[1 Kings] [7]:[19] The capitals on the tops of the pillars in the vestibule were shaped like lilies, four cubits high.
[1 Kings] [7]:[20] On the capitals of the two pillars, above the rounded part next to the network, were two hundred pomegranates in rows all around, on the second capital as well.
[1 Kings] [7]:[21] He set up the pillars at the vestibule of the temple. He set up the pillar on the south and named it Jachin, and he set up the pillar on the north and named it Boaz.
[1 Kings] [7]:[22] On the tops of the pillars was lily-work. So the work of the pillars was finished.
[1 Kings] [7]:[23] He made the sea of cast bronze, ten cubits from rim to rim, perfectly round, five cubits high, and thirty cubits in circumference.
[1 Kings] [7]:[24] Under its rim, encircling it all around, were gourds, ten to a cubit, going all the way around the sea; the gourds were in two rows, cast together with it.
[1 Kings] [7]:[25] It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The sea rested on them, and all their hindquarters were turned inward.
[1 Kings] [7]:[26] It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was shaped like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held two thousand baths.
[1 Kings] [7]:[27] He also made ten bronze stands; each stand was four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.
[1 Kings] [7]:[28] This was the construction of the stands: they had side panels set within frames,
[1 Kings] [7]:[29] and on the panels between the frames were lions, oxen, and cherubim, and on the frames likewise above; beneath the lions and oxen were wreaths of hanging work.
[1 Kings] [7]:[30] Each stand had four bronze wheels with bronze axles, and its four feet had supports; these supports were cast beneath the basin, and each had wreaths at the side.
[1 Kings] [7]:[31] Its opening, inside the crown at the top, was a cubit across; the opening was round, made like a pedestal, a cubit and a half wide. On the opening too there were carvings, and its panels were square, not round.
[1 Kings] [7]:[32] The four wheels were underneath the panels, and the axles of the wheels were attached to the stand. Each wheel was a cubit and a half high.
[1 Kings] [7]:[33] The wheels were made like chariot wheels; their axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were all cast.
[1 Kings] [7]:[34] There were four supports at the four corners of each stand, the supports being of one piece with the stand.
[1 Kings] [7]:[35] At the top of the stand was a round band half a cubit high, and on the top of the stand its stays and panels were of one piece with it.
[1 Kings] [7]:[36] On the plates of its stays and on its panels he engraved cherubim, lions, and palm trees, wherever there was room, with wreaths all around.
[1 Kings] [7]:[37] This is how he made the ten stands: all of them cast alike, the same measure and the same form.
[1 Kings] [7]:[38] He made ten bronze basins, each holding forty baths—about eight hundred liters—and measuring four cubits across, one basin for each of the ten stands.
[1 Kings] [7]:[39] He set five of the stands on the south side of the house and five on the north side, and he placed the sea at the southeast corner of the house.
[1 Kings] [7]:[40] Hiram also made the pots, the shovels, and the sprinkling bowls. So Hiram finished all the work he did for King Solomon on the house of the LORD:
[1 Kings] [7]:[41] the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two networks covering the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;
[1 Kings] [7]:[42] the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;
[1 Kings] [7]:[43] the ten stands and the ten basins on the stands;
[1 Kings] [7]:[44] the one sea and the twelve oxen beneath it;
[1 Kings] [7]:[45] the pots, the shovels, and the basins. All these objects that Hiram made for King Solomon for the house of the LORD were of burnished bronze.
[1 Kings] [7]:[46] The king had them cast in the plain of the Jordan, in clay molds, between Succoth and Zarethan.
[1 Kings] [7]:[47] Solomon left all these vessels unweighed, for they were so many; the weight of the bronze could not be determined.
[1 Kings] [7]:[48] Solomon also made all the furnishings for the house of the LORD: the golden altar; the golden table on which the bread of the Presence was set;
[1 Kings] [7]:[49] the lampstands of pure gold, five on the south side and five on the north, in front of the inner sanctuary; the gold flowers, lamps, and tongs;
[1 Kings] [7]:[50] the cups, snuffers, sprinkling bowls, dishes, and firepans of pure gold; and the gold sockets for the doors of the innermost room, the Most Holy Place, and for the doors of the main hall of the temple.
[1 Kings] [7]:[51] When all the work that King Solomon did on the house of the LORD was finished, he brought in the sacred gifts of his father David—the silver, the gold, and the vessels—and placed them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
[1 Kings] [8]:[1] Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the Israelites, to King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the LORD's covenant from the City of David, that is, Zion.
[1 Kings] [8]:[2] All the men of Israel gathered to King Solomon at the festival in the month of Ethanim, that is, the seventh month.
[1 Kings] [8]:[3] When all the elders of Israel had come, the priests took up the ark.
[1 Kings] [8]:[4] They brought up the ark of the LORD, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent; the priests and the Levites carried them up.
[1 Kings] [8]:[5] King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel, who had assembled before him, were with him in front of the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle beyond counting or numbering.
[1 Kings] [8]:[6] Then the priests brought the ark of the LORD's covenant to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
[1 Kings] [8]:[7] For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, overshadowing the ark and its poles from above.
[1 Kings] [8]:[8] The poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the Holy Place in front of the inner sanctuary, though they could not be seen from outside; and they are there to this day.
[1 Kings] [8]:[9] There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses had placed there at Horeb, when the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites as they came out of the land of Egypt.
[1 Kings] [8]:[10] When the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house of the LORD,
[1 Kings] [8]:[11] and the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
[1 Kings] [8]:[12] Then Solomon said: "The LORD has said that he would dwell in thick darkness.
[1 Kings] [8]:[13] I have surely built you a lofty house, a place for you to dwell forever."
[1 Kings] [8]:[14] Then the king turned around and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood.
[1 Kings] [8]:[15] He said: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with his own mouth to my father David and has fulfilled it with his own hand. He said,
[1 Kings] [8]:[16] 'From the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house, that my name might be there; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.'
[1 Kings] [8]:[17] Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
[1 Kings] [8]:[18] But the LORD said to my father David, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart.
[1 Kings] [8]:[19] Nevertheless, you shall not build the house; your son, who will come from your own body, he shall build the house for my name.'
[1 Kings] [8]:[20] The LORD has kept the promise he made: I have succeeded my father David and sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
[1 Kings] [8]:[21] There I have made a place for the ark, which holds the covenant of the LORD that he made with our fathers when he brought them out of the land of Egypt."
[1 Kings] [8]:[22] Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in the presence of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward heaven.
[1 Kings] [8]:[23] He said: "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above or on earth below, keeping covenant and steadfast love with your servants who walk before you with all their heart.
[1 Kings] [8]:[24] You have kept what you promised your servant, my father David; with your mouth you spoke it, and with your hand you have fulfilled it, as it is this day.
[1 Kings] [8]:[25] Now therefore, LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant, my father David, what you promised him when you said, 'You shall never fail to have a man before me to sit on the throne of Israel, if only your sons watch their way and walk before me as you have walked before me.'
[1 Kings] [8]:[26] And now, God of Israel, let your word be confirmed, the word you spoke to your servant, my father David.
[1 Kings] [8]:[27] But will God really dwell on the earth? Look, the heavens, even the highest heaven, cannot contain you—how much less this house that I have built!
[1 Kings] [8]:[28] Yet turn to the prayer of your servant and to his plea, LORD my God; hear the cry and the prayer that your servant prays before you this day,
[1 Kings] [8]:[29] that your eyes may be open night and day toward this house, the place of which you said, 'My name shall be there,' to hear the prayer that your servant prays toward this place.
[1 Kings] [8]:[30] Hear the plea of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, the place where you dwell; hear and forgive.
[1 Kings] [8]:[31] When someone wrongs his neighbor and is required to take an oath, and he comes and swears the oath before your altar in this house,
[1 Kings] [8]:[32] then hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants: condemn the guilty, bringing his conduct down on his own head, and vindicate the innocent, rewarding him according to his righteousness.
[1 Kings] [8]:[33] When your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against you, and they turn back to you, confess your name, and pray and plead with you in this house,
[1 Kings] [8]:[34] then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave to their fathers.
[1 Kings] [8]:[35] When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, and they pray toward this place, confess your name, and turn from their sin because you have afflicted them,
[1 Kings] [8]:[36] then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel; teach them the good way in which they should walk, and send rain on your land, which you gave your people as an inheritance.
[1 Kings] [8]:[37] If there is famine in the land, or plague, blight or mildew, locusts or grasshoppers; if an enemy besieges them in any of their cities—whatever the affliction or sickness—
[1 Kings] [8]:[38] then whatever prayer or plea is made by anyone among all your people Israel, each one knowing the affliction of his own heart and spreading out his hands toward this house,
[1 Kings] [8]:[39] hear from heaven, the place where you dwell; forgive and act. Deal with everyone according to all that he does, since you know his heart—for you alone know the hearts of all human beings—
[1 Kings] [8]:[40] so that they may fear you all the days they live in the land you gave to our fathers.
[1 Kings] [8]:[41] Also concerning the foreigner, who is not of your people Israel but has come from a distant land for the sake of your name—
[1 Kings] [8]:[42] for they will hear of your great name, your mighty hand, and your outstretched arm—and when such a one comes and prays toward this house,
[1 Kings] [8]:[43] hear from heaven, the place where you dwell, and do whatever the foreigner asks of you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as your people Israel do, and may know that this house I have built bears your name.
[1 Kings] [8]:[44] When your people go out to battle against their enemy, wherever you send them, and they pray to the LORD toward the city you have chosen and the house I have built for your name,
[1 Kings] [8]:[45] then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause.
[1 Kings] [8]:[46] When they sin against you—for there is no one who does not sin—and you are angry with them and hand them over to an enemy who takes them captive to a land far off or near,
[1 Kings] [8]:[47] and if they come to their senses in the land where they are held captive, and repent and plead with you in the land of their captors, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly,'
[1 Kings] [8]:[48] and if they return to you with all their heart and all their soul in the land of the enemies who took them captive, and pray to you toward their land, which you gave to their fathers, toward the city you have chosen and the house I have built for your name,
[1 Kings] [8]:[49] then hear from heaven, the place where you dwell, their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause.
[1 Kings] [8]:[50] Forgive your people who have sinned against you, forgive all the transgressions they have committed against you, and grant them compassion in the sight of their captors, so that they will show them mercy;
[1 Kings] [8]:[51] for they are your people, your inheritance, whom you brought out of Egypt, out of the iron furnace.
[1 Kings] [8]:[52] May your eyes be open to the plea of your servant and to the plea of your people Israel, and may you listen to them whenever they call to you.
[1 Kings] [8]:[53] For you set them apart from all the peoples of the earth to be your own inheritance, just as you declared through your servant Moses when you brought our fathers out of Egypt, Sovereign LORD."
[1 Kings] [8]:[54] When Solomon had finished praying this whole prayer and plea to the LORD, he rose from before the altar of the LORD, where he had been kneeling with his hands spread out toward heaven.
[1 Kings] [8]:[55] He stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice, saying:
[1 Kings] [8]:[56] "Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to his people Israel, just as he promised. Not one word has failed of all the good promises he made through his servant Moses.
[1 Kings] [8]:[57] May the LORD our God be with us as he was with our fathers; may he never leave us or forsake us.
[1 Kings] [8]:[58] May he turn our hearts to himself, so that we walk in all his ways and keep the commandments, statutes, and ordinances he gave our fathers.
[1 Kings] [8]:[59] And may these words of mine, with which I have pleaded before the LORD, be near to the LORD our God day and night, that he may uphold the cause of his servant and the cause of his people Israel, as each day requires,
[1 Kings] [8]:[60] so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God and there is no other.
[1 Kings] [8]:[61] And may your hearts be wholly devoted to the LORD our God, to walk in his statutes and keep his commandments, as at this day."
[1 Kings] [8]:[62] Then the king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices before the LORD.
[1 Kings] [8]:[63] Solomon offered as fellowship offerings to the LORD twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the LORD.
[1 Kings] [8]:[64] That same day the king consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat of the fellowship offerings, because the bronze altar before the LORD was too small to hold the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat of the fellowship offerings.
[1 Kings] [8]:[65] So at that time Solomon held the festival, and all Israel with him—a vast assembly, from Lebo Hamath to the Wadi of Egypt—before the LORD our God, for seven days and seven days more, fourteen days in all.
[1 Kings] [8]:[66] On the eighth day he sent the people away. They blessed the king and went to their homes joyful and glad in heart for all the good the LORD had done for his servant David and for his people Israel.
[1 Kings] [9]:[1] When Solomon had finished building the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and everything else he had set his heart on making,
[1 Kings] [9]:[2] the LORD appeared to Solomon a second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.
[1 Kings] [9]:[3] The LORD said to him: "I have heard your prayer and your plea that you have made before me. I have consecrated this house you have built, to put my name there forever; my eyes and my heart will be there for all time.
[1 Kings] [9]:[4] As for you, if you walk before me as your father David walked, with integrity of heart and uprightness, doing all that I have commanded you, keeping my statutes and my ordinances,
[1 Kings] [9]:[5] then I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever, as I promised your father David when I said, 'You will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.'
[1 Kings] [9]:[6] But if you and your children turn away from me and do not keep the commands and statutes I have set before you, and go off to serve other gods and bow down to them,
[1 Kings] [9]:[7] then I will cut Israel off from the land I have given them, and I will cast out of my sight this house that I have consecrated for my name. Israel will become a byword and an object of scorn among all peoples.
[1 Kings] [9]:[8] And though this house now stands so high, everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will hiss, saying, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this house?'
[1 Kings] [9]:[9] And the answer will be, 'Because they abandoned the LORD their God, who brought their ancestors out of the land of Egypt, and embraced other gods, bowing down to them and serving them—that is why the LORD has brought all this disaster on them.'"
[1 Kings] [9]:[10] At the end of the twenty years during which Solomon built these two buildings—the house of the LORD and the royal palace—
[1 Kings] [9]:[11] King Solomon gave twenty towns in Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, because Hiram had supplied him with all the cedar and cypress timber and gold he desired.
[1 Kings] [9]:[12] But when Hiram came from Tyre to inspect the towns Solomon had given him, he was not pleased with them.
[1 Kings] [9]:[13] "What are these towns you have given me, my brother?" he said. And he named them the Land of Cabul,* a name they bear to this day. *Cabul sounds like a Hebrew expression meaning "good for nothing."
[1 Kings] [9]:[14] Now Hiram had sent the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold.
[1 Kings] [9]:[15] This is the account of the forced labor King Solomon conscripted to build the house of the LORD, his own palace, the Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
[1 Kings] [9]:[16] (Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer. He set it on fire, killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and gave it as a wedding gift to his daughter, Solomon's wife.)
[1 Kings] [9]:[17] So Solomon rebuilt Gezer. He also built up Lower Beth Horon,
[1 Kings] [9]:[18] Baalath, and Tadmor* in the wilderness, in the land, *The written Hebrew text reads Tamar; the traditional reading is Tadmor.
[1 Kings] [9]:[19] as well as all his store cities and the cities for his chariots and for his cavalry—whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout the territory he ruled.
[1 Kings] [9]:[20] As for all the people who were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—those who were not Israelites—
[1 Kings] [9]:[21] that is, their descendants remaining in the land, whom the Israelites had not been able to destroy—these Solomon conscripted for his slave labor force, as it is to this day.
[1 Kings] [9]:[22] But Solomon did not make slaves of any of the Israelites; they were his fighting men, his officials, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
[1 Kings] [9]:[23] These were the chief officers in charge of Solomon's projects—five hundred and fifty of them—who supervised the men doing the work.
[1 Kings] [9]:[24] After Pharaoh's daughter had come up from the City of David to the palace Solomon had built for her, he built the Millo.
[1 Kings] [9]:[25] Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD, burning incense before the LORD along with them. So he completed the temple.
[1 Kings] [9]:[26] King Solomon also built a fleet of ships at Ezion Geber, near Elath on the shore of the Red Sea,* in the land of Edom. *Hebrew: Sea of Reeds.
[1 Kings] [9]:[27] And Hiram sent his servants—sailors who knew the sea—to serve in the fleet with Solomon's men.
[1 Kings] [9]:[28] They sailed to Ophir and brought back four hundred and twenty talents of gold, which they delivered to King Solomon.
[1 Kings] [10]:[1] When the queen of Sheba heard how famous Solomon was—a fame bound up with the name of the LORD—she came to test him with hard questions.
[1 Kings] [10]:[2] She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large retinue—camels loaded with spices, a great quantity of gold, and precious stones. She came to Solomon and spoke with him about everything that was on her mind,
[1 Kings] [10]:[3] and Solomon answered all her questions. Nothing was too obscure for the king to explain to her.
[1 Kings] [10]:[4] When the queen of Sheba had seen all of Solomon's wisdom, and the palace he had built,
[1 Kings] [10]:[5] the food on his table, the seating of his officials, the attending servants in their robes, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the house of the LORD, it left her breathless.
[1 Kings] [10]:[6] She said to the king, "The report I heard in my own country about your accomplishments and your wisdom was true."
[1 Kings] [10]:[7] "But I did not believe it until I came and saw it with my own eyes. And in fact, I was not told the half of it! Your wisdom and your prosperity go far beyond the report I heard."
[1 Kings] [10]:[8] "How fortunate are your people! How fortunate these servants of yours, who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom!"
[1 Kings] [10]:[9] "Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and set you on the throne of Israel. Because the LORD loves Israel forever, he has made you king to administer justice and righteousness."
[1 Kings] [10]:[10] Then she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again did such an abundance of spices come as the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
[1 Kings] [10]:[11] Hiram's fleet, which had carried gold from Ophir, also brought from there a great supply of almug wood and precious stones.
[1 Kings] [10]:[12] The king used the almug wood to make supports for the house of the LORD and for the royal palace, and to make lyres and harps for the singers. Never again has such almug wood been imported or seen, down to this day.
[1 Kings] [10]:[13] King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she asked for, besides what he gave her out of his royal bounty. Then she and her servants returned to her own country.
[1 Kings] [10]:[14] The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in a single year was six hundred sixty-six talents,
[1 Kings] [10]:[15] not counting the revenue from the traveling merchants, the traders, all the kings of Arabia, and the governors of the land.
[1 Kings] [10]:[16] King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold, six hundred shekels of gold went into each shield,[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew reads simply "six hundred of gold"; the unit of weight is not stated but is most likely shekels.
[1 Kings] [10]:[17] and three hundred small shields of hammered gold, three minas of gold in each. The king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
[1 Kings] [10]:[18] The king also made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with refined gold.
[1 Kings] [10]:[19] The throne had six steps, and its back was rounded at the top. On both sides of the seat were armrests, with a lion standing beside each armrest,
[1 Kings] [10]:[20] and twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like it had ever been made for any kingdom.
[1 Kings] [10]:[21] All King Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. Silver was not used, for in Solomon's days it counted for nothing.
[1 Kings] [10]:[22] The king had a fleet of Tarshish ships at sea along with Hiram's fleet. Once every three years the fleet would come in, carrying gold and silver, ivory, apes, and baboons.[^1] [^1]: "Tarshish ships" refers to large ocean-going trading vessels. The final item in the list is uncertain; it may mean baboons or peacocks.
[1 Kings] [10]:[23] So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in wealth and in wisdom.
[1 Kings] [10]:[24] The whole world sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart,
[1 Kings] [10]:[25] and each one brought a gift—articles of silver and gold, robes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules—year after year.
[1 Kings] [10]:[26] Solomon accumulated chariots and horses. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.
[1 Kings] [10]:[27] The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as plentiful as the sycamore fig trees of the foothills.
[1 Kings] [10]:[28] Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and from Kue; the king's traders bought them from Kue at the going price.
[1 Kings] [10]:[29] A chariot was imported from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred fifty. They also exported them to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
[1 Kings] [11]:[1] King Solomon loved many foreign women. Besides Pharaoh's daughter, there were Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites—
[1 Kings] [11]:[2] women from the nations about which the LORD had told the Israelites, "You shall not intermarry with them, and they shall not intermarry with you, for they will surely turn your hearts after their gods." Yet Solomon clung to them in love.
[1 Kings] [11]:[3] He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned his heart away.
[1 Kings] [11]:[4] So it was that when Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart after other gods, and his heart was no longer wholly true to the LORD his God, as the heart of David his father had been.
[1 Kings] [11]:[5] Solomon followed Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Milcom, the abomination of the Ammonites.
[1 Kings] [11]:[6] Solomon did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; he did not follow the LORD wholeheartedly, as David his father had done.
[1 Kings] [11]:[7] Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, on the hill facing Jerusalem, and one for Molech, the abomination of the Ammonites.
[1 Kings] [11]:[8] He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods.
[1 Kings] [11]:[9] The LORD grew angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice
[1 Kings] [11]:[10] and had commanded him about this very thing, that he should not follow other gods. But Solomon did not keep what the LORD had commanded.
[1 Kings] [11]:[11] So the LORD said to Solomon, "Since this has been your way, and you have not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom away from you and give it to your servant.
[1 Kings] [11]:[12] Yet for the sake of David your father I will not do it in your lifetime; I will tear it out of the hand of your son.
[1 Kings] [11]:[13] Still, I will not tear away the whole kingdom. I will give one tribe to your son, for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen."
[1 Kings] [11]:[14] Then the LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite, of the royal line of Edom.
[1 Kings] [11]:[15] Earlier, when David was at war with Edom, Joab the commander of the army had gone up to bury the dead, and he struck down every male in Edom.
[1 Kings] [11]:[16] Joab and all Israel stayed there six months, until he had killed every male in Edom.
[1 Kings] [11]:[17] But Hadad fled to Egypt, along with some Edomites who had served his father. Hadad was only a small boy at the time.
[1 Kings] [11]:[18] They set out from Midian and came to Paran; there they took men with them and went on to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave Hadad a house, provided for his food, and granted him land.
[1 Kings] [11]:[19] Hadad found such great favor with Pharaoh that Pharaoh gave him in marriage the sister of his own wife, the sister of Queen Tahpenes.
[1 Kings] [11]:[20] Tahpenes' sister bore him a son, Genubath, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh's palace; and Genubath lived there among Pharaoh's own children.
[1 Kings] [11]:[21] While Hadad was in Egypt, he heard that David had gone to rest with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army was dead. So Hadad said to Pharaoh, "Let me go, that I may return to my own country."
[1 Kings] [11]:[22] Pharaoh said to him, "What have you lacked with me, that now you want to go back to your own country?" "Nothing," Hadad answered, "only let me go."
[1 Kings] [11]:[23] God also raised up against Solomon another adversary: Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah.
[1 Kings] [11]:[24] He gathered men around him and became the leader of a raiding band after David struck them down. They went to Damascus, settled there, and made him king in Damascus.
[1 Kings] [11]:[25] He was an adversary to Israel as long as Solomon lived, adding to the trouble caused by Hadad. He loathed Israel and reigned over Aram.
[1 Kings] [11]:[26] Jeroboam son of Nebat also rebelled against the king. He was an Ephraimite from Zeredah, and his mother was a widow named Zeruah; he was one of Solomon's officials.
[1 Kings] [11]:[27] This is how he came to rebel against the king: Solomon had built the Millo and closed the breach in the wall of the city of David his father.
[1 Kings] [11]:[28] Now Jeroboam was a capable man, and when Solomon saw how well the young man did his work, he put him in charge of all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.
[1 Kings] [11]:[29] About that time, when Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah of Shiloh met him on the road. Ahijah was wearing a new cloak, and the two of them were alone out in the open country.
[1 Kings] [11]:[30] Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.
[1 Kings] [11]:[31] Then he said to Jeroboam, "Take ten pieces for yourself, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'See, I am about to tear the kingdom out of Solomon's hand, and I will give you ten tribes.
[1 Kings] [11]:[32] But one tribe will remain his, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.
[1 Kings] [11]:[33] For they have forsaken me and bowed down to Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, to Chemosh the god of Moab, and to Milcom the god of the Ammonites. They have not walked in my ways, doing what is right in my eyes and keeping my statutes and my judgments, as David his father did.
[1 Kings] [11]:[34] Yet I will not take the whole kingdom out of Solomon's hand; I will let him rule as prince all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant, whom I chose and who kept my commandments and my statutes.
[1 Kings] [11]:[35] But I will take the kingship from the hand of his son and give you ten tribes.
[1 Kings] [11]:[36] To his son I will give one tribe, so that David my servant may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city I have chosen for myself, to put my name there.
[1 Kings] [11]:[37] As for you, I will take you, and you will reign over all that your heart desires; you will be king over Israel.
[1 Kings] [11]:[38] And if you listen to all I command you, and walk in my ways, and do what is right in my eyes by keeping my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did, then I will be with you. I will build you a lasting dynasty, as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.
[1 Kings] [11]:[39] I will humble the descendants of David because of this, but not forever.'"
[1 Kings] [11]:[40] Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam got up and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and stayed there until Solomon's death.
[1 Kings] [11]:[41] The rest of the acts of Solomon, all that he did and his wisdom—are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?
[1 Kings] [11]:[42] Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.
[1 Kings] [11]:[43] Then Solomon went to rest with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
[1 Kings] [12]:[1] Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
[1 Kings] [12]:[2] Now Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it while he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon; and Jeroboam stayed on in Egypt.
[1 Kings] [12]:[3] So they sent for him and called him, and Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel came and said to Rehoboam:
[1 Kings] [12]:[4] "Your father made our yoke harsh. Now lighten the hard labor your father imposed and the heavy yoke he laid on us, and we will serve you."
[1 Kings] [12]:[5] He said to them, "Go away for three days, then come back to me." So the people went away.
[1 Kings] [12]:[6] King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served in the presence of his father Solomon while he was alive. "What do you advise?" he asked. "How shall I answer these people?"
[1 Kings] [12]:[7] They said to him, "If today you will be a servant to these people, serve them, answer them, and speak kind words to them, they will be your servants forever."
[1 Kings] [12]:[8] But he rejected the advice the elders gave him and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and who served him.
[1 Kings] [12]:[9] He asked them, "What do you advise? How shall we answer these people who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke your father laid on us'?"
[1 Kings] [12]:[10] The young men who had grown up with him replied, "Tell these people who said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy; now lighten it for us'—tell them this: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.'
[1 Kings] [12]:[11] Now then, my father loaded you with a heavy yoke; I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips; I will discipline you with scorpions."
[1 Kings] [12]:[12] Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had said: "Come back to me on the third day."
[1 Kings] [12]:[13] The king answered the people harshly. He rejected the advice the elders had given him
[1 Kings] [12]:[14] and spoke to them according to the advice of the young men: "My father made your yoke heavy; I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips; I will discipline you with scorpions."
[1 Kings] [12]:[15] So the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events came from the LORD, to fulfill the word the LORD had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
[1 Kings] [12]:[16] When all Israel saw that the king would not listen to them, the people answered the king: "What share do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, Israel! Look to your own house now, David!" So Israel went off to their tents.
[1 Kings] [12]:[17] But Rehoboam ruled over the Israelites who were living in the towns of Judah.
[1 Kings] [12]:[18] Then King Rehoboam sent out Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam managed to get into his chariot and escape to Jerusalem.
[1 Kings] [12]:[19] So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
[1 Kings] [12]:[20] When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they sent for him and called him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. No one followed the house of David except the tribe of Judah alone.
[1 Kings] [12]:[21] When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he mustered the whole house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin—a hundred and eighty thousand able young warriors—to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
[1 Kings] [12]:[22] But the word of God came to Shemaiah, the man of God:
[1 Kings] [12]:[23] "Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, to the whole house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people:
[1 Kings] [12]:[24] This is what the LORD says: Do not march up to fight against your brothers, the Israelites. Every one of you go home, for this thing is from me." So they obeyed the word of the LORD and turned back, as the LORD had commanded.
[1 Kings] [12]:[25] Jeroboam fortified Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. From there he went out and fortified Penuel.
[1 Kings] [12]:[26] Jeroboam said to himself, "Now the kingdom is likely to revert to the house of David.
[1 Kings] [12]:[27] If these people go up to offer sacrifices at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, their hearts will turn back to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah. They will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah."
[1 Kings] [12]:[28] So the king took counsel and made two golden calves. He said to the people, "It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem. Here are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt."
[1 Kings] [12]:[29] He set up one in Bethel, and the other he put in Dan.
[1 Kings] [12]:[30] And this thing became a sin, for the people went before the one calf even as far as Dan.
[1 Kings] [12]:[31] Jeroboam also built shrines on the high places and appointed priests from all sorts of people, though they were not Levites.
[1 Kings] [12]:[32] Jeroboam instituted a festival on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the festival held in Judah, and he went up to the altar. This he did in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves he had made, and in Bethel he installed the priests of the high places he had made.
[1 Kings] [12]:[33] On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a month he had devised in his own heart, he went up to the altar he had built in Bethel. So he instituted a festival for the Israelites and went up to the altar to make offerings.
[1 Kings] [13]:[1] Now a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the word of the LORD, while Jeroboam was standing at the altar to burn incense.
[1 Kings] [13]:[2] He cried out against the altar by the word of the LORD: "Altar, altar, this is what the LORD says: A son will be born to the house of David; Josiah will be his name. He will sacrifice on you the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and human bones will be burned on you."
[1 Kings] [13]:[3] That same day he gave a sign: "This is the sign that the LORD has spoken: the altar will be split apart, and the ashes on it will spill out."
[1 Kings] [13]:[4] When the king heard the word that the man of God had cried out against the altar at Bethel, Jeroboam stretched out his hand from the altar and said, "Seize him!" But the hand he had stretched out against him withered, and he could not draw it back.
[1 Kings] [13]:[5] The altar also split apart, and the ashes spilled out from it, according to the sign the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.
[1 Kings] [13]:[6] Then the king said to the man of God, "Please plead with the LORD your God and pray for me, that my hand may be restored to me." So the man of God pleaded with the LORD, and the king's hand was restored to him and became as it was before.
[1 Kings] [13]:[7] The king said to the man of God, "Come home with me and have something to eat, and I will give you a gift."
[1 Kings] [13]:[8] But the man of God said to the king, "Even if you gave me half your house, I would not go with you, nor would I eat bread or drink water in this place.
[1 Kings] [13]:[9] For this is what I was commanded by the word of the LORD: 'You shall not eat bread or drink water, and you shall not return by the way you came.'"
[1 Kings] [13]:[10] So he went another way and did not return by the road on which he had come to Bethel.
[1 Kings] [13]:[11] Now an old prophet was living in Bethel. One of his sons came and told him everything the man of God had done that day in Bethel; then they all told their father the words he had spoken to the king.
[1 Kings] [13]:[12] Their father asked them, "Which way did he go?" And his sons showed him the road the man of God from Judah had taken.
[1 Kings] [13]:[13] Then he said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." So they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it
[1 Kings] [13]:[14] and rode after the man of God. He found him sitting under an oak and said to him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" "I am," he answered.
[1 Kings] [13]:[15] Then he said to him, "Come home with me and eat some bread."
[1 Kings] [13]:[16] But he replied, "I cannot turn back and go with you, nor can I eat bread or drink water with you in this place,
[1 Kings] [13]:[17] for I was told by the word of the LORD: 'You shall not eat bread or drink water there, nor return by the way you came.'"
[1 Kings] [13]:[18] The old man said to him, "I too am a prophet, like you. An angel spoke to me by the word of the LORD: 'Bring him back with you to your house, that he may eat bread and drink water.'" But he was lying to him.
[1 Kings] [13]:[19] So the man of God went back with him and ate bread and drank water in his house.
[1 Kings] [13]:[20] While they were sitting at the table, the word of the LORD came to the prophet who had brought him back,
[1 Kings] [13]:[21] and he cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah, "This is what the LORD says: Because you have defied the word of the LORD and have not kept the command the LORD your God gave you,
[1 Kings] [13]:[22] and you went back and ate bread and drank water in the place where he told you, 'Eat no bread and drink no water' — therefore your body will not be buried in the tomb of your fathers."
[1 Kings] [13]:[23] After he had finished eating and drinking, the prophet who had brought him back saddled the donkey for him.
[1 Kings] [13]:[24] As he went on his way, a lion met him on the road and killed him. His body lay thrown down on the road, with the donkey standing beside it and the lion standing beside the body.
[1 Kings] [13]:[25] Some men passing by saw the body lying on the road and the lion standing beside it, and they went and reported it in the town where the old prophet lived.
[1 Kings] [13]:[26] When the prophet who had brought him back from his journey heard of it, he said, "It is the man of God who defied the word of the LORD. The LORD has given him over to the lion, which has mauled him and killed him, just as the LORD said he would."
[1 Kings] [13]:[27] Then he said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me," and they saddled it.
[1 Kings] [13]:[28] He went out and found the body lying on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it. The lion had neither eaten the body nor mauled the donkey.
[1 Kings] [13]:[29] So the prophet lifted up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey, and brought it back to his own town to mourn for him and bury him.
[1 Kings] [13]:[30] He laid the body in his own tomb, and they mourned over him, saying, "Alas, my brother!"
[1 Kings] [13]:[31] After burying him, he said to his sons, "When I die, bury me in the tomb where the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones.
[1 Kings] [13]:[32] For what he cried out by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel, and against all the shrines on the high places in the towns of Samaria, will surely come to pass."
[1 Kings] [13]:[33] Even after this, Jeroboam did not turn from his evil way, but went on appointing priests for the high places from among the common people. Anyone who wanted it he ordained, and that man became one of the priests of the high places.
[1 Kings] [13]:[34] By this thing the house of Jeroboam fell into sin, so that it was cut off and destroyed from the face of the earth.
[1 Kings] [14]:[1] At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam fell ill.
[1 Kings] [14]:[2] Jeroboam said to his wife, "Get up, disguise yourself so no one will recognize you as Jeroboam's wife, and go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet is there—the one who told me I would be king over this people.
[1 Kings] [14]:[3] Take with you ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will happen to the boy."
[1 Kings] [14]:[4] So Jeroboam's wife did as he said. She went to Shiloh and came to the house of Ahijah. Now Ahijah could not see; his eyes had failed because of his age.
[1 Kings] [14]:[5] But the LORD had said to Ahijah, "Jeroboam's wife is coming to ask you about her son, for he is ill. Say such and such to her. When she arrives, she will be pretending to be someone else."
[1 Kings] [14]:[6] So when Ahijah heard the sound of her footsteps at the door, he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why pretend to be someone else? I have been sent to you with heavy news.
[1 Kings] [14]:[7] Go, tell Jeroboam: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I raised you up from among the people and made you ruler over my people Israel.
[1 Kings] [14]:[8] I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you, but you have not been like my servant David, who kept my commandments and followed me with all his heart, doing only what was right in my eyes.
[1 Kings] [14]:[9] You have done more evil than all who came before you. You went and made yourself other gods and cast images, provoking me to anger, and you have thrust me behind your back.
[1 Kings] [14]:[10] Therefore I am bringing disaster on the house of Jeroboam. I will cut off from Jeroboam every last male in Israel, slave or free. I will burn up the house of Jeroboam as a man burns dung, until it is gone.
[1 Kings] [14]:[11] Those of Jeroboam's house who die in the city the dogs will eat, and those who die in the open country the birds of the sky will eat—for the LORD has spoken.
[1 Kings] [14]:[12] Now get up and go home. The moment you set foot in the city, the child will die.
[1 Kings] [14]:[13] All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He alone of Jeroboam's house will be laid in a grave, because in him, of all the house of Jeroboam, something good toward the LORD, the God of Israel, was found.
[1 Kings] [14]:[14] Moreover, the LORD will raise up for himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam—this very day, yes, even now.
[1 Kings] [14]:[15] And the LORD will strike Israel so that it sways like a reed in the water. He will uproot Israel from this good land he gave to their fathers and scatter them beyond the Euphrates, because they made their Asherah poles and provoked the LORD to anger.
[1 Kings] [14]:[16] He will give Israel up because of the sins Jeroboam committed and made Israel commit."
[1 Kings] [14]:[17] Then Jeroboam's wife got up and went away to Tirzah. As she stepped over the threshold of the house, the boy died.
[1 Kings] [14]:[18] They buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, just as the LORD had said through his servant Ahijah the prophet.
[1 Kings] [14]:[19] The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he fought and how he reigned, are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.
[1 Kings] [14]:[20] Jeroboam reigned twenty-two years, and then he lay down with his fathers, and his son Nadab succeeded him as king.
[1 Kings] [14]:[21] Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel as the place for his name. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
[1 Kings] [14]:[22] Judah did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. With the sins they committed they provoked him to jealousy more than all their fathers had done.
[1 Kings] [14]:[23] They too built for themselves high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
[1 Kings] [14]:[24] There were even male cult prostitutes in the land. They committed all the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
[1 Kings] [14]:[25] In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt marched against Jerusalem.
[1 Kings] [14]:[26] He carried off the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the royal palace. He took everything, including all the gold shields Solomon had made.
[1 Kings] [14]:[27] So King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them and entrusted them to the commanders of the guard who kept watch at the entrance of the royal palace.
[1 Kings] [14]:[28] Whenever the king went to the house of the LORD, the guards carried the shields, and afterward they returned them to the guardroom.
[1 Kings] [14]:[29] As for the rest of the acts of Rehoboam and all he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
[1 Kings] [14]:[30] There was continual war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.
[1 Kings] [14]:[31] Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite, and his son Abijam succeeded him as king.
[1 Kings] [15]:[1] In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam became king over Judah.
[1 Kings] [15]:[2] He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
[1 Kings] [15]:[3] He walked in all the sins his father had committed before him, and his heart was not wholly devoted to the LORD his God, as the heart of David his forefather had been.
[1 Kings] [15]:[4] Yet for David's sake the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, raising up his son after him and keeping Jerusalem standing—
[1 Kings] [15]:[5] because David had done what was right in the eyes of the LORD and had not turned aside from anything he commanded him all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
[1 Kings] [15]:[6] There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam as long as he lived.[^1] [^1]: Rehoboam, Abijam's father, had already died (14:31); the note looks back over his whole reign. A few Hebrew manuscripts read *Abijam* here.
[1 Kings] [15]:[7] The rest of the acts of Abijam and all he did are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah. There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam as well.
[1 Kings] [15]:[8] Abijam rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David, and Asa his son reigned in his place.
[1 Kings] [15]:[9] In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king of Judah.
[1 Kings] [15]:[10] He reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem. His grandmother's name was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.[^1] [^1]: Hebrew reads *his mother*; the term can denote a grandmother or other female ancestor. Maacah was also the mother of Abijam (v. 2).
[1 Kings] [15]:[11] Asa did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as David his forefather had done.
[1 Kings] [15]:[12] He drove the cult prostitutes out of the land and swept away all the idols his fathers had made.
[1 Kings] [15]:[13] He even removed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother, because she had made an obscene image of Asherah. Asa cut down her image and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
[1 Kings] [15]:[14] The high places, however, were not removed; even so, Asa's heart was wholly devoted to the LORD all his life.
[1 Kings] [15]:[15] He brought into the house of the LORD the gifts he and his father had dedicated—silver, gold, and vessels.
[1 Kings] [15]:[16] There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their days.
[1 Kings] [15]:[17] Baasha king of Israel marched against Judah and fortified Ramah, to cut off all traffic to and from Asa king of Judah.
[1 Kings] [15]:[18] So Asa took all the silver and gold left in the treasuries of the house of the LORD, along with the treasuries of the royal palace, and handed it over to his officials. King Asa sent them to Ben-Hadad son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion, king of Aram, who ruled in Damascus, with this message:
[1 Kings] [15]:[19] "Let there be a treaty between you and me, as there was between my father and your father. See, I am sending you a gift of silver and gold. Go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."
[1 Kings] [15]:[20] Ben-Hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his forces against the cities of Israel. He struck down Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maacah, and all Kinneroth, along with all the land of Naphtali.
[1 Kings] [15]:[21] When Baasha heard of it, he stopped fortifying Ramah and withdrew to Tirzah.
[1 Kings] [15]:[22] Then King Asa summoned all Judah—no one was exempt—and they carried away from Ramah the stones and timber Baasha had been building with. With them King Asa built up Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.
[1 Kings] [15]:[23] As for all the rest of the acts of Asa, all his achievements, everything he did, and the cities he built, they are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah. In his old age, however, he suffered from a disease in his feet.
[1 Kings] [15]:[24] Asa rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of David his forefather, and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.
[1 Kings] [15]:[25] Nadab son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.
[1 Kings] [15]:[26] He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, walking in the way of his father and in the sin he had led Israel to commit.
[1 Kings] [15]:[27] Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him and struck him down at Gibbethon, a Philistine town, while Nadab and all Israel were besieging it.
[1 Kings] [15]:[28] Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa king of Judah and reigned in his place.
[1 Kings] [15]:[29] As soon as he was king, he struck down the entire house of Jeroboam. He left Jeroboam no one that breathed, until he had destroyed them all, according to the word the LORD had spoken through his servant Ahijah the Shilonite—
[1 Kings] [15]:[30] because of the sins Jeroboam had committed and had led Israel to commit, and because he provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger.
[1 Kings] [15]:[31] The rest of the acts of Nadab and all he did are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.
[1 Kings] [15]:[32] There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel throughout their days.
[1 Kings] [15]:[33] In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned twenty-four years.
[1 Kings] [15]:[34] He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin he had led Israel to commit.
[1 Kings] [16]:[1] The word of the LORD came to Jehu son of Hanani against Baasha:
[1 Kings] [16]:[2] "I lifted you out of the dust and made you ruler over my people Israel, but you walked in the way of Jeroboam and led my people Israel into sin, provoking me to anger with their sins.
[1 Kings] [16]:[3] So now I will sweep away Baasha and his house, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
[1 Kings] [16]:[4] Anyone belonging to Baasha who dies in the city the dogs will eat, and anyone of his who dies in the open country the birds of the sky will eat."
[1 Kings] [16]:[5] The rest of the acts of Baasha, what he did and his exploits—are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
[1 Kings] [16]:[6] Baasha rested with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king in his place.
[1 Kings] [16]:[7] Moreover, through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani the word of the LORD had come against Baasha and his house, both because of all the evil he had done in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger by the work of his hands and becoming like the house of Jeroboam, and because he had struck down Jeroboam's house.
[1 Kings] [16]:[8] In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king over Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned two years.
[1 Kings] [16]:[9] His servant Zimri, commander of half the chariots, conspired against him while Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk in the house of Arza, who was in charge of the palace at Tirzah.
[1 Kings] [16]:[10] Zimri came in, struck him down, and killed him, in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and he became king in his place.
[1 Kings] [16]:[11] As soon as he began to reign and was seated on his throne, he struck down the whole house of Baasha. He did not leave him a single male, neither kinsman nor friend.
[1 Kings] [16]:[12] So Zimri destroyed the entire house of Baasha, according to the word of the LORD spoken against Baasha through the prophet Jehu—
[1 Kings] [16]:[13] because of all the sins of Baasha and the sins of his son Elah, which they committed and led Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
[1 Kings] [16]:[14] The rest of the acts of Elah and all that he did—are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
[1 Kings] [16]:[15] In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days in Tirzah. The troops were encamped against Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines.
[1 Kings] [16]:[16] When the encamped troops heard that Zimri had conspired and had struck down the king, all Israel in the camp made Omri, the commander of the army, king over Israel that very day.
[1 Kings] [16]:[17] Then Omri and all Israel with him went up from Gibbethon and laid siege to Tirzah.
[1 Kings] [16]:[18] When Zimri saw that the city had been taken, he went into the citadel of the royal palace, set the palace on fire around him, and died—
[1 Kings] [16]:[19] because of the sins he had committed, doing evil in the eyes of the LORD, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin he committed, leading Israel into sin.
[1 Kings] [16]:[20] The rest of the acts of Zimri and the conspiracy he carried out—are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
[1 Kings] [16]:[21] Then the people of Israel were split in two: half the people followed Tibni son of Ginath to make him king, and half followed Omri.
[1 Kings] [16]:[22] But the people who followed Omri proved stronger than those who followed Tibni son of Ginath. So Tibni died, and Omri became king.
[1 Kings] [16]:[23] In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel, and he reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.
