[1 Kings] [16]:[24] He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, and he built up the hill and named the city he built Samaria, after Shemer, the owner of the hill.
[1 Kings] [16]:[25] Omri did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and he acted more wickedly than all who were before him.
[1 Kings] [16]:[26] He followed the whole way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and his sin, which he had led Israel to commit, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger with their worthless idols.
[1 Kings] [16]:[27] The rest of the acts of Omri, what he did and the exploits he performed—are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
[1 Kings] [16]:[28] Omri rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king in his place.
[1 Kings] [16]:[29] Ahab son of Omri became king over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years.
[1 Kings] [16]:[30] Ahab son of Omri did evil in the eyes of the LORD, more than all who were before him.
[1 Kings] [16]:[31] As if it were a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he took as his wife Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and he went and served Baal and worshiped him.
[1 Kings] [16]:[32] He set up an altar for Baal in the temple of Baal that he built in Samaria.
[1 Kings] [16]:[33] Ahab also made an Asherah pole. He did more to provoke the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel before him.
[1 Kings] [16]:[34] In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho. He laid its foundation at the cost of Abiram his firstborn and set up its gates at the cost of Segub his youngest, according to the word the LORD had spoken through Joshua son of Nun.[^1] [^1]: See Joshua 6:26, where Joshua pronounced this curse on anyone who would rebuild Jericho.
[1 Kings] [17]:[1] Elijah the Tishbite, one of the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, "As the LORD lives, the God of Israel in whose presence I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain these coming years except at my word."
[1 Kings] [17]:[2] Then the word of the LORD came to him:
[1 Kings] [17]:[3] "Leave this place, turn eastward, and hide yourself by the Wadi Cherith, east of the Jordan.
[1 Kings] [17]:[4] You shall drink from the wadi, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there."
[1 Kings] [17]:[5] So he went and did as the LORD had said. He went and settled by the Wadi Cherith, east of the Jordan.
[1 Kings] [17]:[6] The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the wadi.
[1 Kings] [17]:[7] But after a while the wadi dried up, for there had been no rain in the land.
[1 Kings] [17]:[8] Then the word of the LORD came to him:
[1 Kings] [17]:[9] "Get up and go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and stay there. I have commanded a widow there to feed you."
[1 Kings] [17]:[10] So he got up and went to Zarephath. When he came to the entrance of the town, there was a widow gathering sticks. He called to her and said, "Please bring me a little water in a jar, so I may drink."
[1 Kings] [17]:[11] As she went to get it, he called after her and said, "Please bring me a piece of bread as well."
[1 Kings] [17]:[12] But she answered, "As the LORD your God lives, I have nothing baked—only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. I am gathering a couple of sticks now, and I will go in and prepare it for myself and my son, and we will eat it and die."
[1 Kings] [17]:[13] Elijah said to her, "Do not be afraid. Go and do as you have said, but first make me a small loaf from what you have and bring it out to me. Then make something for yourself and your son,
[1 Kings] [17]:[14] for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'The jar of flour will not run out, and the jug of oil will not run dry, until the day the LORD sends rain on the face of the ground.'"
[1 Kings] [17]:[15] She went and did as Elijah had said, and she and Elijah and her household ate for many days.
[1 Kings] [17]:[16] The jar of flour did not run out, and the jug of oil did not run dry, just as the LORD had spoken through Elijah.
[1 Kings] [17]:[17] Some time later the son of the woman who owned the house fell ill. His illness grew so severe that there was no breath left in him.
[1 Kings] [17]:[18] She said to Elijah, "What have I to do with you, man of God? Have you come to me to bring my sin to mind and to kill my son?"
[1 Kings] [17]:[19] He said to her, "Give me your son." He took him from her arms, carried him up to the upper room where he was staying, and laid him on his own bed.
[1 Kings] [17]:[20] Then he cried out to the LORD, "LORD my God, have you brought disaster even on the widow I am staying with, by killing her son?"
[1 Kings] [17]:[21] He stretched himself out over the boy three times and cried out to the LORD, "LORD my God, let this boy's life return to him."
[1 Kings] [17]:[22] The LORD heard Elijah's voice, and the boy's life returned to him, and he lived.
[1 Kings] [17]:[23] Elijah took the boy, brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother. "Look," Elijah said, "your son is alive."
[1 Kings] [17]:[24] Then the woman said to Elijah, "Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the LORD in your mouth is truth."
[1 Kings] [18]:[1] A long time passed, and in the third year the word of the LORD came to Elijah: "Go, present yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain on the land."
[1 Kings] [18]:[2] So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab. The famine was severe in Samaria.
[1 Kings] [18]:[3] Ahab summoned Obadiah, who was in charge of the palace. Now Obadiah revered the LORD deeply.
[1 Kings] [18]:[4] When Jezebel was killing off the prophets of the LORD, Obadiah had taken a hundred prophets and hidden them, fifty to a cave, and supplied them with bread and water.
[1 Kings] [18]:[5] Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go through the land to all the springs and all the streams. Perhaps we will find grass to keep the horses and mules alive, so we will not have to destroy any of the livestock."
[1 Kings] [18]:[6] They divided the land between them to search it: Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.
[1 Kings] [18]:[7] As Obadiah was on his way, Elijah suddenly met him. Obadiah recognized him, fell facedown, and said, "Is it really you, my lord Elijah?"
[1 Kings] [18]:[8] "It is I," he answered. "Go and tell your master, 'Elijah is here.'"
[1 Kings] [18]:[9] But Obadiah said, "What wrong have I done, that you are handing your servant over to Ahab to be put to death?
[1 Kings] [18]:[10] As surely as the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my master has not sent someone to look for you. And whenever they said, 'He is not here,' he made that kingdom or nation swear that they could not find you.
[1 Kings] [18]:[11] And now you say, 'Go and tell your master, "Elijah is here."'
[1 Kings] [18]:[12] The moment I leave you, the Spirit of the LORD will carry you off to who knows where. Then I will come and tell Ahab, and when he cannot find you, he will kill me—though I, your servant, have revered the LORD from my youth.
[1 Kings] [18]:[13] Has my lord not been told what I did when Jezebel was killing the prophets of the LORD—how I hid a hundred of the LORD's prophets, fifty to a cave, and supplied them with bread and water?
[1 Kings] [18]:[14] And now you say, 'Go and tell your master, "Elijah is here"'—he will kill me!"
[1 Kings] [18]:[15] Elijah said, "As surely as the LORD of hosts lives, before whom I stand, today I will present myself to him."
[1 Kings] [18]:[16] So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him, and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
[1 Kings] [18]:[17] When Ahab saw Elijah, he said to him, "So it's you—the troubler of Israel!"
[1 Kings] [18]:[18] "I have not troubled Israel," Elijah replied, "but you and your father's house have, by abandoning the LORD's commandments and following the Baals.
[1 Kings] [18]:[19] Now send word and gather all Israel to me at Mount Carmel, along with the four hundred fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel's table."
[1 Kings] [18]:[20] So Ahab sent word throughout all Israel and gathered the prophets at Mount Carmel.
[1 Kings] [18]:[21] Elijah came before all the people and said, "How long will you keep limping between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow him; but if Baal is God, follow him." The people said nothing.
[1 Kings] [18]:[22] Then Elijah said to the people, "I am the only prophet of the LORD left, while Baal has four hundred fifty prophets.
[1 Kings] [18]:[23] Let two bulls be given to us. Let them choose one bull for themselves, cut it in pieces, and lay it on the wood, but put no fire to it. I will prepare the other bull and lay it on the wood, and I will put no fire to it either.
[1 Kings] [18]:[24] Then you call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the LORD. The god who answers with fire—he is God." And all the people answered, "That is a good plan."
[1 Kings] [18]:[25] Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "Choose one bull for yourselves and prepare it first, since there are so many of you. Then call on the name of your god, but put no fire to it."
[1 Kings] [18]:[26] So they took the bull that was given them and prepared it, and they called on the name of Baal from morning until noon: "Baal, answer us!" But there was no sound and no answer. And they danced around the altar they had made.
[1 Kings] [18]:[27] At noon Elijah began to mock them. "Shout louder!" he said. "Surely he is a god. Perhaps he is lost in thought, or has stepped aside, or is away on a journey. Perhaps he is asleep and must be awakened."
[1 Kings] [18]:[28] So they shouted louder and slashed themselves with swords and spears, as was their custom, until the blood flowed over them.
[1 Kings] [18]:[29] Midday passed, and they went on with their frenzied prophesying until the time for the evening offering. But there was no sound, no answer, no response.
[1 Kings] [18]:[30] Then Elijah said to all the people, "Come here to me." They all came to him, and he repaired the altar of the LORD, which had been torn down.
[1 Kings] [18]:[31] Elijah took twelve stones, one for each of the tribes descended from Jacob, to whom the word of the LORD had come, saying, "Israel shall be your name."
[1 Kings] [18]:[32] With the stones he built an altar in the name of the LORD, and around it he dug a trench large enough to hold two measures of seed.
[1 Kings] [18]:[33] He arranged the wood, cut the bull in pieces, and laid it on the wood.
[1 Kings] [18]:[34] Then he said, "Fill four jars with water and pour it on the offering and on the wood." "Do it again," he said, and they did it again. "Do it a third time," he said, and they did it a third time.
[1 Kings] [18]:[35] The water ran down around the altar and even filled the trench.
[1 Kings] [18]:[36] At the time of the evening offering, Elijah the prophet stepped forward and prayed: "LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known today that you are God in Israel, that I am your servant, and that I have done all these things at your word.
[1 Kings] [18]:[37] Answer me, LORD, answer me, so that this people may know that you, LORD, are God, and that you have turned their hearts back again."
[1 Kings] [18]:[38] Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the burnt offering, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and it licked up the water in the trench.
[1 Kings] [18]:[39] When all the people saw it, they fell facedown and cried, "The LORD—he is God! The LORD—he is God!"
[1 Kings] [18]:[40] Elijah ordered them, "Seize the prophets of Baal! Don't let a single one escape." They seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the Kishon Valley and slaughtered them there.
[1 Kings] [18]:[41] Then Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of a heavy rain."
[1 Kings] [18]:[42] So Ahab went up to eat and drink, but Elijah climbed to the top of Mount Carmel, bent down to the ground, and put his face between his knees.
[1 Kings] [18]:[43] "Go up and look toward the sea," he told his servant. The servant went up and looked. "There is nothing," he said. Elijah told him, "Go back seven times."
[1 Kings] [18]:[44] The seventh time he reported, "Look, a cloud as small as a man's hand is rising from the sea." Elijah said, "Go and tell Ahab, 'Harness your chariot and go down before the rain stops you.'"
[1 Kings] [18]:[45] Before long the sky grew black with clouds, the wind rose, and a heavy rain came on. Ahab mounted his chariot and rode to Jezreel.
[1 Kings] [18]:[46] The hand of the LORD came upon Elijah; he tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel.
[1 Kings] [19]:[1] Ahab told Jezebel everything Elijah had done, and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
[1 Kings] [19]:[2] Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah with this word: "May the gods do so to me, and more also, if by this time tomorrow I have not made your life like the life of one of them."
[1 Kings] [19]:[3] Elijah was afraid, and he got up and fled for his life. He came to Beersheba in Judah and left his servant there,[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew consonants can also be read "he saw," that is, he saw what had happened.
[1 Kings] [19]:[4] while he himself went a day's journey into the wilderness. He came to a broom bush, sat down under it, and prayed that he might die. "Enough, LORD," he said. "Take my life; I am no better than my fathers."
[1 Kings] [19]:[5] Then he lay down under the broom bush and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel touched him and said, "Get up and eat."
[1 Kings] [19]:[6] He looked around, and there by his head was a loaf baked on hot stones and a jar of water. He ate and drank, and lay down again.
[1 Kings] [19]:[7] The angel of the LORD came back a second time, touched him, and said, "Get up and eat, for the journey is too much for you."
[1 Kings] [19]:[8] So he got up and ate and drank, and strengthened by that food he traveled forty days and forty nights until he reached Horeb, the mountain of God.
[1 Kings] [19]:[9] There he came to the cave and spent the night there. And the word of the LORD came to him: "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
[1 Kings] [19]:[10] He answered, "I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. The Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I alone am left, and now they are seeking my life to take it away."
[1 Kings] [19]:[11] The LORD said, "Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD, for the LORD is about to pass by." Then a great and powerful wind tore into the mountains and shattered the rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind came an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.
[1 Kings] [19]:[12] After the earthquake came a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire came the sound of a low whisper.
[1 Kings] [19]:[13] When Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak, went out, and stood at the mouth of the cave. And a voice came to him: "What are you doing here, Elijah?"
[1 Kings] [19]:[14] He answered, "I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of hosts. The Israelites have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I alone am left, and now they are seeking my life to take it away."
[1 Kings] [19]:[15] The LORD said to him, "Go back the way you came, to the wilderness of Damascus. When you arrive, anoint Hazael king over Aram.
[1 Kings] [19]:[16] Anoint Jehu son of Nimshi king over Israel, and anoint Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel Meholah to succeed you as prophet.
[1 Kings] [19]:[17] Whoever escapes the sword of Hazael, Jehu will put to death; and whoever escapes the sword of Jehu, Elisha will put to death.
[1 Kings] [19]:[18] Yet I will leave seven thousand in Israel—every knee that has not bowed to Baal and every mouth that has not kissed him."
[1 Kings] [19]:[19] So Elijah went from there and found Elisha son of Shaphat. He was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen, and he himself was driving the twelfth pair. Elijah passed by him and threw his cloak over him.
[1 Kings] [19]:[20] Elisha left the oxen and ran after Elijah. "Let me kiss my father and mother goodbye," he said, "and then I will follow you." "Go back," Elijah replied. "What have I done to you?"
[1 Kings] [19]:[21] So he turned back from him, took his yoke of oxen and slaughtered them. He cooked the meat using the plowing equipment for fuel, gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he set out to follow Elijah and became his servant.
[1 Kings] [20]:[1] Ben-hadad king of Aram mustered his entire army. Thirty-two kings were with him, along with horses and chariots. He marched up, laid siege to Samaria, and attacked it.
[1 Kings] [20]:[2] He sent messengers into the city to Ahab king of Israel with this word:
[1 Kings] [20]:[3] "This is what Ben-hadad says: Your silver and your gold are mine, and the best of your wives and children are mine."
[1 Kings] [20]:[4] The king of Israel answered, "As you say, my lord the king: I am yours, and all that I have."
[1 Kings] [20]:[5] The messengers came back and said, "This is what Ben-hadad says: I sent you word that you must hand over your silver and gold, your wives and your children.
[1 Kings] [20]:[6] But about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you, and they will search your house and the houses of your servants. Whatever is precious in your eyes they will seize and carry off.
[1 Kings] [20]:[7] Then the king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said, "See for yourselves how this man is bent on trouble. He sent to me for my wives and children, my silver and gold, and I did not refuse him."
[1 Kings] [20]:[8] All the elders and all the people said to him, "Do not listen to him; do not give in."
[1 Kings] [20]:[9] So he said to Ben-hadad's messengers, "Tell my lord the king: Everything you demanded of your servant the first time I will do, but this I cannot do." The messengers left and brought back his reply.
[1 Kings] [20]:[10] Then Ben-hadad sent word to him: "May the gods do so to me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria will supply a handful for each of the troops who follow me."
[1 Kings] [20]:[11] The king of Israel answered, "Tell him: The one who straps on his armor should not boast like the one who takes it off."
[1 Kings] [20]:[12] Ben-hadad heard this message while he and the kings were drinking in their shelters, and he ordered his men, "Take your positions!" So they took up positions against the city.
[1 Kings] [20]:[13] Meanwhile a prophet came up to Ahab king of Israel and said, "This is what the LORD says: Do you see this vast horde? Today I am giving it into your hand, and you will know that I am the LORD."
[1 Kings] [20]:[14] "By whom?" Ahab asked. He answered, "This is what the LORD says: By the young officers of the provincial commanders." "And who will begin the battle?" he asked. "You will," he replied.
[1 Kings] [20]:[15] So Ahab mustered the young officers of the provincial commanders—two hundred and thirty-two of them—and after them he mustered all the troops, all the Israelites: seven thousand.
[1 Kings] [20]:[16] They marched out at noon, while Ben-hadad and the thirty-two kings allied with him were in their shelters, drinking themselves drunk.
[1 Kings] [20]:[17] The young officers of the provincial commanders went out first. Ben-hadad had sent out scouts, and they reported to him, "Men are coming out of Samaria."
[1 Kings] [20]:[18] He said, "If they have come out for peace, take them alive; if they have come out for war, take them alive."
[1 Kings] [20]:[19] The young officers of the provincial commanders marched out of the city with the army behind them,
[1 Kings] [20]:[20] and each one struck down his man. The Arameans fled, with Israel in pursuit, but Ben-hadad king of Aram escaped on horseback with some of his cavalry.
[1 Kings] [20]:[21] Then the king of Israel advanced and struck down the horses and chariots, inflicting a heavy defeat on Aram.
[1 Kings] [20]:[22] Afterward the prophet came to the king of Israel and said, "Go, strengthen your position and consider carefully what you must do, for in the spring the king of Aram will march against you again."
[1 Kings] [20]:[23] Meanwhile the officials of the king of Aram said to him, "Their gods are gods of the hills; that is why they were too strong for us. But if we fight them on level ground, we will surely be stronger than they are.
[1 Kings] [20]:[24] Do this: remove each of the kings from his command and replace them with governors.
[1 Kings] [20]:[25] Then raise an army like the one you lost—horse for horse and chariot for chariot—so we can fight Israel on level ground. Surely then we will be stronger than they are." He listened to their advice and did so.
[1 Kings] [20]:[26] In the spring Ben-hadad mustered the Arameans and marched up to Aphek to fight against Israel.
[1 Kings] [20]:[27] The Israelites were mustered and provisioned, and they went out to meet them. The Israelites camped opposite them like two small flocks of goats, while the Arameans covered the countryside.
[1 Kings] [20]:[28] The man of God came and said to the king of Israel, "This is what the LORD says: Because the Arameans have said, 'The LORD is a god of the hills and not a god of the valleys,' I will give this vast horde into your hand, and you will all know that I am the LORD."
[1 Kings] [20]:[29] For seven days they camped facing each other, and on the seventh day the battle was joined. The Israelites struck down a hundred thousand Aramean foot soldiers in one day.
[1 Kings] [20]:[30] The rest fled to the city of Aphek, and the wall collapsed on twenty-seven thousand of them. Ben-hadad also fled to the city and hid in an inner room.
[1 Kings] [20]:[31] His officials said to him, "Look, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful kings. Let us go to the king of Israel with sackcloth around our waists and ropes around our heads. Perhaps he will spare your life."
[1 Kings] [20]:[32] So they put on sackcloth around their waists and ropes around their heads, went to the king of Israel, and said, "Your servant Ben-hadad says: Please let me live." The king answered, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."
[1 Kings] [20]:[33] The men took this as a good omen and quickly seized on his word: "Yes, your brother Ben-hadad!" "Go and bring him," the king said. When Ben-hadad came out, Ahab had him come up into his chariot.
[1 Kings] [20]:[34] Ben-hadad said, "I will return the cities my father took from your father, and you may set up your own market districts in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria." Ahab said, "On the basis of a treaty I will let you go." So he made a treaty with him and let him go.
[1 Kings] [20]:[35] By the word of the LORD one of the company of the prophets said to his companion, "Strike me, please." But the man refused.
[1 Kings] [20]:[36] So the prophet said, "Because you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD, the moment you leave me a lion will kill you." And when the man went off, a lion found him and killed him.
[1 Kings] [20]:[37] The prophet found another man and said, "Strike me, please." So the man struck him and wounded him.
[1 Kings] [20]:[38] Then the prophet went and stood by the road waiting for the king, disguising himself with a bandage over his eyes.
[1 Kings] [20]:[39] As the king passed by, he called out to him: "Your servant went into the thick of the battle, and a man turned aside and brought me a prisoner and said, 'Guard this man. If he goes missing, your life will be given for his life, or you will pay a talent of silver.'
[1 Kings] [20]:[40] But while your servant was busy here and there, the man disappeared." "That is your sentence," the king of Israel said. "You have pronounced it yourself."
[1 Kings] [20]:[41] Then the prophet quickly pulled the bandage away from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him as one of the prophets.
[1 Kings] [20]:[42] He said to the king, "This is what the LORD says: Because you set free from your hand the man I had devoted to destruction, your life shall stand in place of his life, and your people in place of his people."
[1 Kings] [20]:[43] Sullen and angry, the king of Israel went home to Samaria.
[1 Kings] [21]:[1] Now after these things, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel, right beside the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.
[1 Kings] [21]:[2] Ahab said to Naboth, "Give me your vineyard. I want it for a vegetable garden, since it lies so close to my house. In exchange I will give you a better vineyard than this one—or, if you prefer, I will pay you its full value in silver."
[1 Kings] [21]:[3] But Naboth said to Ahab, "The LORD forbid that I should hand over to you the inheritance of my fathers."
[1 Kings] [21]:[4] So Ahab went home sullen and angry over what Naboth the Jezreelite had told him: "I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers." He lay down on his bed, turned his face to the wall, and refused to eat.
[1 Kings] [21]:[5] His wife Jezebel came in to him and asked, "Why are you so sullen that you will not eat?"
[1 Kings] [21]:[6] He answered her, "Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said, 'Sell me your vineyard for silver, or, if you like, I will give you another vineyard in its place.' And he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"
[1 Kings] [21]:[7] Then his wife Jezebel said to him, "Is this how you exercise your kingship over Israel? Get up, eat something, and cheer up. I will get you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."
[1 Kings] [21]:[8] So she wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and sent them to the elders and nobles of Naboth's city, who sat in council with him.
[1 Kings] [21]:[9] In the letters she wrote: "Proclaim a fast and seat Naboth at the head of the people.
[1 Kings] [21]:[10] Seat two scoundrels opposite him, and have them testify against him: 'You have cursed God and the king.' Then take him out and stone him to death.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew word here literally means 'blessed,' used as a reverent substitute to avoid writing the words 'cursed God.'
[1 Kings] [21]:[11] The men of his city, the elders and nobles who lived there, did just as Jezebel had directed them, exactly as it was written in the letters she had sent them.
[1 Kings] [21]:[12] They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.
[1 Kings] [21]:[13] Then the two scoundrels came in and sat down opposite him, and they testified against Naboth in front of the people: "Naboth has cursed God and the king." So they took him outside the city and stoned him to death.
[1 Kings] [21]:[14] Then they sent word to Jezebel: "Naboth has been stoned; he is dead."
[1 Kings] [21]:[15] As soon as Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned to death, she said to Ahab, "Get up and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to sell you for silver. Naboth is no longer alive; he is dead."
[1 Kings] [21]:[16] When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he got up and went down to take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.
[1 Kings] [21]:[17] Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:
[1 Kings] [21]:[18] "Get up and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who rules in Samaria. He is now in Naboth's vineyard, where he has gone to take possession of it.
[1 Kings] [21]:[19] Say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: Have you murdered, and also taken possession?' Then say to him, 'This is what the LORD says: In the place where the dogs licked up Naboth's blood, the dogs will lick up your blood—yes, yours.'"
[1 Kings] [21]:[20] Ahab said to Elijah, "So you have found me, my enemy!" "I have found you," he answered, "because you have sold yourself to do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD.
[1 Kings] [21]:[21] I am bringing disaster upon you. I will wipe out your descendants and cut off from Ahab every male in Israel, both slave and free.
[1 Kings] [21]:[22] I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because you have provoked me to anger and have led Israel into sin.
[1 Kings] [21]:[23] And concerning Jezebel the LORD also says: 'The dogs will devour Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.'
[1 Kings] [21]:[24] Anyone belonging to Ahab who dies in the city the dogs will eat, and anyone who dies in the open country the birds of the sky will eat."
[1 Kings] [21]:[25] There was never anyone like Ahab, who sold himself to do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD, urged on by Jezebel his wife.
[1 Kings] [21]:[26] He acted most abominably in following idols, just as the Amorites had done, whom the LORD drove out before the Israelites.
[1 Kings] [21]:[27] When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put sackcloth on his body, and fasted. He slept in sackcloth and walked about subdued.
[1 Kings] [21]:[28] Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite:
[1 Kings] [21]:[29] "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the disaster in his days; I will bring it on his house in the days of his son."
[1 Kings] [22]:[1] For three years there was no war between Aram and Israel.
[1 Kings] [22]:[2] But in the third year Jehoshaphat king of Judah came down to the king of Israel.
[1 Kings] [22]:[3] The king of Israel said to his servants, "You know that Ramoth Gilead belongs to us, yet we do nothing to take it back from the hand of the king of Aram."
[1 Kings] [22]:[4] So he said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you go with me to fight for Ramoth Gilead?" Jehoshaphat answered the king of Israel, "I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."
[1 Kings] [22]:[5] Then Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please seek the word of the LORD first."
[1 Kings] [22]:[6] So the king of Israel gathered the prophets together, about four hundred men, and asked them, "Shall I go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or shall I hold back?" They answered, "Go up, and the Lord will give it into the king's hand."
[1 Kings] [22]:[7] But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there no prophet of the LORD here besides these, that we may inquire of him?"
[1 Kings] [22]:[8] The king of Israel answered Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we may inquire of the LORD, Micaiah son of Imlah, but I hate him, because he never prophesies anything good about me, only evil." Jehoshaphat said, "The king should not say that."
[1 Kings] [22]:[9] So the king of Israel called one of his officials and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once."
[1 Kings] [22]:[10] Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting on their thrones, robed in their royal garments, at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
[1 Kings] [22]:[11] Zedekiah son of Kenaanah had made iron horns for himself, and he declared, "This is what the LORD says: With these you will gore the Arameans until they are destroyed."
[1 Kings] [22]:[12] All the other prophets were prophesying the same: "Go up to Ramoth Gilead and you will succeed, for the LORD will give it into the king's hand."
[1 Kings] [22]:[13] Meanwhile the messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah said to him, "Look, the prophets speak with one voice, and it is favorable to the king. Let your word agree with theirs, and speak favorably."
[1 Kings] [22]:[14] But Micaiah said, "As surely as the LORD lives, I will speak only what the LORD tells me."
[1 Kings] [22]:[15] When he came to the king, the king asked him, "Micaiah, shall we go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or shall we hold back?" He answered, "Go up and you will succeed, for the LORD will give it into the king's hand."
[1 Kings] [22]:[16] The king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear to tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"
[1 Kings] [22]:[17] Then Micaiah said, "I saw all Israel scattered over the hills like sheep without a shepherd, and the LORD said, 'These have no master. Let each one go home in peace.'"
[1 Kings] [22]:[18] The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you that he never prophesies anything good about me, only evil?"
[1 Kings] [22]:[19] Micaiah continued, "Then hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD seated on his throne, with all the host of heaven standing around him, on his right and on his left.
[1 Kings] [22]:[20] And the LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab to go up and fall at Ramoth Gilead?' One suggested this, another that.
[1 Kings] [22]:[21] Finally a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, 'I will entice him.' 'How?' the LORD asked.
[1 Kings] [22]:[22] He answered, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.' The LORD said, 'You will succeed in enticing him. Go and do it.'
[1 Kings] [22]:[23] So now the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of yours. The LORD has decreed disaster for you."
[1 Kings] [22]:[24] Then Zedekiah son of Kenaanah came up to Micaiah and struck him on the cheek and demanded, "Which way did the spirit of the LORD go when he left me to speak to you?"
[1 Kings] [22]:[25] Micaiah answered, "You will find out on the day you go hiding from room to room."
[1 Kings] [22]:[26] The king of Israel then ordered, "Take Micaiah and hand him over to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son,
[1 Kings] [22]:[27] and say, 'This is what the king says: Put this man in prison and give him only meager rations of bread and water until I return safely.'"
[1 Kings] [22]:[28] Micaiah said, "If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me." And he added, "Hear this, all you peoples!"
[1 Kings] [22]:[29] So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth Gilead.
[1 Kings] [22]:[30] The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will go into battle in disguise, but you wear your royal robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself and went into battle.
[1 Kings] [22]:[31] Now the king of Aram had ordered his thirty-two chariot commanders, "Do not fight with anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel."
[1 Kings] [22]:[32] When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they thought, "Surely this is the king of Israel," and they turned to attack him. But Jehoshaphat cried out,
[1 Kings] [22]:[33] and when the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.
[1 Kings] [22]:[34] But someone drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the sections of his armor. The king said to his charioteer, "Turn around and get me out of the fighting, for I am wounded."
[1 Kings] [22]:[35] The battle grew fierce that day, and the king was propped up in his chariot facing the Arameans. That evening he died, and the blood from his wound ran onto the floor of the chariot.
[1 Kings] [22]:[36] As the sun was setting, a cry spread through the army: "Every man to his own city, every man to his own land!"
[1 Kings] [22]:[37] So the king died and was brought to Samaria, and they buried him there.
[1 Kings] [22]:[38] They washed the chariot at the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood, where the prostitutes bathed—just as the LORD had declared.
[1 Kings] [22]:[39] The rest of the acts of Ahab, all that he did, the palace he built and inlaid with ivory, and all the cities he built—are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
[1 Kings] [22]:[40] So Ahab rested with his fathers, and his son Ahaziah became king in his place.
[1 Kings] [22]:[41] Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
[1 Kings] [22]:[42] Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-five years. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
[1 Kings] [22]:[43] He walked in all the ways of his father Asa and did not turn aside from them; he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
[1 Kings] [22]:[44] The high places, however, were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense there.
[1 Kings] [22]:[45] Jehoshaphat was also at peace with the king of Israel.
[1 Kings] [22]:[46] The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, the might he showed and the wars he fought—are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
[1 Kings] [22]:[47] He rid the land of the rest of the male shrine prostitutes who were left from the days of his father Asa.
[1 Kings] [22]:[48] There was then no king in Edom; a deputy ruled there.
[1 Kings] [22]:[49] Jehoshaphat built a fleet of trading ships to sail to Ophir for gold, but they never sailed, for the ships were wrecked at Ezion Geber.
[1 Kings] [22]:[50] At that time Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, "Let my men sail with your men," but Jehoshaphat refused.
[1 Kings] [22]:[51] Then Jehoshaphat rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of David his father. And Jehoram his son became king in his place.
[1 Kings] [22]:[52] Ahaziah son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel two years.
[1 Kings] [22]:[53] He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, walking in the ways of his father and his mother and in the ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin.
[1 Kings] [22]:[54] He served Baal and worshiped him, provoking the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger, just as his father had done.
[2 Kings] [1]:[1] After Ahab's death, Moab rebelled against Israel.
[2 Kings] [1]:[2] Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and was injured. So he sent messengers with these orders: "Go and inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will recover from this illness."
[2 Kings] [1]:[3] But the angel of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, "Get up and go to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and ask them: 'Is there no God in Israel, that you are going to inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron?'
[2 Kings] [1]:[4] Therefore this is what the LORD says: 'You will not get up from the bed you are lying on. You will surely die.'" So Elijah went.
[2 Kings] [1]:[5] When the messengers returned to the king, he asked them, "Why have you come back?"
[2 Kings] [1]:[6] They answered, "A man came up to meet us and said, 'Go back to the king who sent you and tell him: This is what the LORD says: Is there no God in Israel, that you are sending men to inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you will not get up from the bed you are lying on. You will surely die.'"
[2 Kings] [1]:[7] The king asked them, "What did this man look like who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?"
[2 Kings] [1]:[8] They replied, "He had a garment of hair and a leather belt around his waist." The king said, "That was Elijah the Tishbite."
[2 Kings] [1]:[9] Then he sent a captain with his fifty men to Elijah. The captain went up to him, and there he was, sitting on top of the mountain, and he said, "Man of God, the king commands you: Come down!"
[2 Kings] [1]:[10] Elijah answered the captain, "If I am a man of God, may fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men!" Then fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.
[2 Kings] [1]:[11] The king sent another captain with his fifty men to him. He said to Elijah, "Man of God, this is what the king says: Come down at once!"
[2 Kings] [1]:[12] Elijah answered, "If I am a man of God, may fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men!" Then the fire of God came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.
[2 Kings] [1]:[13] So the king sent a third captain with his fifty men. This third captain went up, fell on his knees before Elijah, and pleaded with him: "Man of God, please let my life and the lives of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your sight.
[2 Kings] [1]:[14] Fire has come down from heaven and consumed the first two captains with all their men. But now let my life be precious in your sight."
[2 Kings] [1]:[15] The angel of the LORD said to Elijah, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of him." So Elijah got up and went down with him to the king.
[2 Kings] [1]:[16] He said to the king, "This is what the LORD says: Because you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron—is there no God in Israel whose word you might seek?—therefore you will not get up from the bed you are lying on. You will surely die."
[2 Kings] [1]:[17] So he died, according to the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken. Since he had no son, Joram succeeded him as king in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
[2 Kings] [1]:[18] As for all the other things Ahaziah did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
[2 Kings] [2]:[1] When the time came for the LORD to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha were on their way from Gilgal.
[2 Kings] [2]:[2] Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here; the LORD has sent me to Bethel." But Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel.
[2 Kings] [2]:[3] The company of the prophets at Bethel came out to Elisha and asked, "Do you know that today the LORD is going to take your master away from you?" "Yes, I know," he said. "Be still."
[2 Kings] [2]:[4] Then Elijah said to him, "Elisha, stay here; the LORD has sent me to Jericho." But he answered, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So they went on to Jericho.
[2 Kings] [2]:[5] The company of the prophets at Jericho came up to Elisha and asked, "Do you know that today the LORD is going to take your master away from you?" "Yes, I know," he said. "Be still."
[2 Kings] [2]:[6] Then Elijah said to him, "Stay here; the LORD has sent me to the Jordan." But he answered, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you live, I will not leave you." So the two of them went on together.
[2 Kings] [2]:[7] Fifty men from the company of the prophets followed and stood at a distance, facing them, while the two of them stood at the Jordan.
[2 Kings] [2]:[8] Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the water. The water divided to the right and to the left, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
[2 Kings] [2]:[9] As they were crossing, Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I may do for you before I am taken from you." Elisha answered, "Let me receive a double portion of your spirit."
[2 Kings] [2]:[10] "You have asked a hard thing," Elijah said. "Yet if you see me as I am taken from you, it will be yours. If not, it will not."
[2 Kings] [2]:[11] As they walked on, talking together, suddenly a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared and separated the two of them, and Elijah went up to heaven in a whirlwind.
[2 Kings] [2]:[12] Elisha saw it and cried out, "My father! My father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!" And he saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two.
[2 Kings] [2]:[13] He picked up Elijah's cloak, which had fallen from him, and went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.
[2 Kings] [2]:[14] Taking the cloak that had fallen from Elijah, he struck the water and said, "Where now is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" When he had struck the water, it divided to the right and to the left, and he crossed over.
[2 Kings] [2]:[15] The company of the prophets from Jericho saw him from across the river and said, "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha." They came to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.
[2 Kings] [2]:[16] "Look," they said, "we your servants have fifty able men. Let them go and search for your master. Perhaps the Spirit of the LORD has carried him off and set him down on some mountain or in some valley." "No," Elisha replied, "do not send them."
[2 Kings] [2]:[17] But they pressed him until he was too embarrassed to refuse, and he said, "Send them." So they sent fifty men, who searched for three days without finding him.
[2 Kings] [2]:[18] They returned to Elisha, who was staying in Jericho, and he said to them, "Didn't I tell you not to go?"
[2 Kings] [2]:[19] The men of the city said to Elisha, "Look, our lord can see that this city is well situated, but the water is bad and the land is barren."
[2 Kings] [2]:[20] "Bring me a new bowl," he said, "and put salt in it." So they brought it to him.
[2 Kings] [2]:[21] Then he went out to the spring, threw the salt into it, and said, "This is what the LORD says: I have healed this water. Never again will it cause death or make the land unfruitful."
[2 Kings] [2]:[22] And the water has been wholesome to this day, just as Elisha had said.
[2 Kings] [2]:[23] From there Elisha went up to Bethel. As he was walking along the road, some young boys came out of the city and jeered at him, "Go on up, baldhead! Go on up, baldhead!"
[2 Kings] [2]:[24] He turned around, looked at them, and called down a curse on them in the name of the LORD. Then two bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of them.
[2 Kings] [2]:[25] From there he went to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
[2 Kings] [3]:[1] Joram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
[2 Kings] [3]:[2] He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, though not as his father and mother had done; he removed the sacred pillar of Baal that his father had made.
[2 Kings] [3]:[3] Still, he clung to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin; he did not turn away from them.
[2 Kings] [3]:[4] Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he used to pay the king of Israel a tribute of a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.
[2 Kings] [3]:[5] But when Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
[2 Kings] [3]:[6] So King Joram marched out from Samaria at that time and mustered all Israel.
[2 Kings] [3]:[7] Then he set out, sending word to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to fight against Moab?" He answered, "I will go up with you. I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."
[2 Kings] [3]:[8] Then he asked, "By which route shall we march?" Joram answered, "By the way of the Desert of Edom."
[2 Kings] [3]:[9] So the king of Israel set out with the king of Judah and the king of Edom. After they had marched a roundabout route for seven days, there was no water left for the army or for the animals with them.
[2 Kings] [3]:[10] The king of Israel cried out, "Alas! The LORD has summoned these three kings only to hand them over to Moab!"
[2 Kings] [3]:[11] But Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there no prophet of the LORD here, that we may inquire of the LORD through him?" One of the servants of the king of Israel answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here—the man who poured water on the hands of Elijah."
[2 Kings] [3]:[12] "The word of the LORD is with him," said Jehoshaphat. So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom went down to him.
[2 Kings] [3]:[13] Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What do I have to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and the prophets of your mother." But the king of Israel said to him, "No—for the LORD has called these three kings together to hand them over to Moab."
[2 Kings] [3]:[14] Elisha said, "As surely as the LORD of hosts lives, whom I serve, were it not for my regard for Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not so much as look at you or notice you.
[2 Kings] [3]:[15] But now bring me a musician." And while the musician played, the hand of the LORD came upon Elisha,
[2 Kings] [3]:[16] and he said, "This is what the LORD says: Make this valley full of ditches.
[2 Kings] [3]:[17] For this is what the LORD says: You will see neither wind nor rain, yet this valley will be filled with water, and you will drink—you, your herds, and your other animals.
[2 Kings] [3]:[18] This is a small thing in the sight of the LORD; he will also hand Moab over to you.
[2 Kings] [3]:[19] You will strike down every fortified city and every major town. You will cut down every good tree, stop up every spring, and ruin every good field with stones."
[2 Kings] [3]:[20] The next morning, about the time of the morning offering, water suddenly came flowing from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
[2 Kings] [3]:[21] Now when all the Moabites heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, everyone old enough to bear arms was called out and stationed at the border.
[2 Kings] [3]:[22] When they got up early in the morning, the sun was shining on the water, and to the Moabites across the way the water looked as red as blood.
[2 Kings] [3]:[23] "That's blood!" they said. "Those kings must have fought and slaughtered each other. Now to the plunder, Moab!"
[2 Kings] [3]:[24] But when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and struck them down, and the Moabites fled before them. The Israelites invaded the land and went on striking down Moab.
[2 Kings] [3]:[25] They tore down the cities; every man threw a stone on each good field until it was covered. They stopped up every spring and cut down every good tree. Only Kir Hareseth was left with its stones in place, but the slingers surrounded it and attacked it as well.
[2 Kings] [3]:[26] When the king of Moab saw that the battle was going against him, he took seven hundred swordsmen with him to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not.
[2 Kings] [3]:[27] Then he took his firstborn son, who was to succeed him as king, and offered him as a burnt offering on the city wall. Great wrath came upon Israel, so they withdrew from him and returned to their own land.
[2 Kings] [4]:[1] A certain woman, the wife of one of the sons of the prophets, cried out to Elisha, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. Now the creditor has come to take my two boys as his slaves."
[2 Kings] [4]:[2] Elisha said to her, "What can I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" She answered, "Your servant has nothing at all in the house except a jar of oil."
[2 Kings] [4]:[3] Then he said, "Go out and borrow vessels from all your neighbors—empty vessels, and don't ask for just a few.
[2 Kings] [4]:[4] Then go inside, shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour oil into all these vessels, setting aside each one as it is filled."
[2 Kings] [4]:[5] So she left him and shut the door behind her and her sons, and while they kept bringing the vessels to her, she kept pouring.
[2 Kings] [4]:[6] When the vessels were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." But he said to her, "There are no more." Then the oil stopped.
[2 Kings] [4]:[7] She came and told the man of God, and he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debt; you and your sons can live on what is left."
[2 Kings] [4]:[8] One day Elisha was passing through Shunem, where a wealthy woman lived, and she urged him to stay for a meal. So whenever he passed by, he would stop there to eat.
[2 Kings] [4]:[9] She said to her husband, "I know that this man who so often comes our way is a holy man of God.
[2 Kings] [4]:[10] Let's build a small room on the roof and put a bed there for him, with a table, a chair, and a lamp, so that whenever he comes to us he can stay there."
[2 Kings] [4]:[11] One day when he came, he went up to the room and lay down there.
[2 Kings] [4]:[12] He said to Gehazi, his servant, "Call this Shunammite woman." So he called her, and she stood before him.
[2 Kings] [4]:[13] Elisha said to him, "Tell her, 'You have gone to all this trouble for us. What can be done for you? Should a word be spoken on your behalf to the king or to the commander of the army?'" She answered, "I live among my own people."
[2 Kings] [4]:[14] "What then can be done for her?" he asked. Gehazi said, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is old."
[2 Kings] [4]:[15] Then he said, "Call her." So he called her, and she stood in the doorway.
[2 Kings] [4]:[16] And Elisha said, "About this time next year you will hold a son in your arms." "No, my lord, man of God," she said, "do not deceive your servant."
[2 Kings] [4]:[17] But the woman conceived, and at that time the next year she bore a son, just as Elisha had told her.
[2 Kings] [4]:[18] The child grew, and one day he went out to his father, who was with the harvesters.
[2 Kings] [4]:[19] He said to his father, "My head! My head!" His father said to a servant, "Carry him to his mother."
[2 Kings] [4]:[20] The servant lifted him up and brought him to his mother. He sat on her lap until noon, and then he died.
[2 Kings] [4]:[21] She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door behind her, and went out.
[2 Kings] [4]:[22] She called to her husband and said, "Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, so I can hurry to the man of God and come back."
[2 Kings] [4]:[23] "Why go to him today?" he asked. "It is neither new moon nor Sabbath." "It is all right," she said.
[2 Kings] [4]:[24] She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Drive on; don't slow down for me unless I tell you."
[2 Kings] [4]:[25] So she set out and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her in the distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, "Look, there is the Shunammite.
[2 Kings] [4]:[26] Run out to meet her and ask her, 'Are you all right? Is your husband all right? Is the child all right?'" "Everything is all right," she said.
[2 Kings] [4]:[27] When she came to the man of God at the mountain, she took hold of his feet. Gehazi came to push her away, but the man of God said, "Leave her alone; she is in bitter distress, and the LORD has hidden it from me and not told me."
[2 Kings] [4]:[28] Then she said, "Did I ask my lord for a son? Didn't I say, 'Do not raise my hopes'?"
[2 Kings] [4]:[29] Elisha said to Gehazi, "Tuck your cloak into your belt, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer. Lay my staff on the boy's face."
[2 Kings] [4]:[30] But the boy's mother said, "As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So he got up and followed her.
[2 Kings] [4]:[31] Gehazi went on ahead and laid the staff on the boy's face, but there was no sound, no response. So he went back to meet Elisha and told him, "The boy has not awakened."
[2 Kings] [4]:[32] When Elisha reached the house, there was the boy, dead, lying on his bed.
[2 Kings] [4]:[33] He went in, shut the door on the two of them, and prayed to the LORD.
[2 Kings] [4]:[34] Then he got on the bed and lay on the boy, mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, hands to hands. As he stretched himself out over him, the boy's body grew warm.
[2 Kings] [4]:[35] Elisha turned away and walked back and forth in the room, then got on the bed and stretched out over him once more. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
[2 Kings] [4]:[36] Elisha called Gehazi and said, "Call the Shunammite." He called her, and when she came, Elisha said, "Take your son."
[2 Kings] [4]:[37] She came in, fell at his feet, and bowed to the ground. Then she took her son and went out.
[2 Kings] [4]:[38] Elisha returned to Gilgal, and there was a famine in the land. While the sons of the prophets were sitting before him, he said to his servant, "Put the large pot on the fire and cook some stew for these sons of the prophets."
[2 Kings] [4]:[39] One of them went out into the field to gather herbs and found a wild vine. He gathered some of its gourds and filled the fold of his cloak. When he came back, he cut them up into the pot of stew, though no one knew what they were.
[2 Kings] [4]:[40] They poured it out for the men to eat, but as they were eating the stew they cried out, "Man of God, there is death in the pot!" And they could not eat it.
[2 Kings] [4]:[41] Elisha said, "Bring some flour." He threw it into the pot and said, "Pour it out for the people to eat." And there was no longer anything harmful in the pot.
[2 Kings] [4]:[42] A man came from Baal Shalishah, bringing the man of God twenty loaves of barley bread from the first ripe grain, along with some fresh heads of grain in his sack. "Give it to the people to eat," Elisha said.
[2 Kings] [4]:[43] But his attendant said, "How can I set this before a hundred men?" Elisha answered, "Give it to the people to eat, for this is what the LORD says: 'They will eat, and there will be some left over.'"
[2 Kings] [4]:[44] So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, just as the LORD had said.
[2 Kings] [5]:[1] Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man in his master's eyes and highly regarded, because through him the LORD had given victory to Aram. He was a mighty warrior, but he had leprosy.
[2 Kings] [5]:[2] Now raiding parties had gone out from Aram, and they had carried off a young girl from the land of Israel, and she waited on Naaman's wife.
[2 Kings] [5]:[3] She said to her mistress, "If only my master would go to the prophet who is in Samaria! He would cure him of his leprosy."
[2 Kings] [5]:[4] So Naaman went to his master and told him, "This is what the girl from the land of Israel said."
[2 Kings] [5]:[5] "Go, then," said the king of Aram, "and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So Naaman set out, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten sets of clothing.
[2 Kings] [5]:[6] He brought the letter to the king of Israel, and it read: "With this letter I am sending you my servant Naaman, so that you may cure him of his leprosy."
[2 Kings] [5]:[7] When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends word to me to cure someone of his leprosy? Only see now, and mark how he is looking for a quarrel with me!"
[2 Kings] [5]:[8] When Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent word to the king: "Why have you torn your clothes? Let the man come to me, and he will learn that there is a prophet in Israel."
[2 Kings] [5]:[9] So Naaman came with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
[2 Kings] [5]:[10] Elisha sent a messenger out to him with this word: "Go and wash seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will be restored and you will be clean."
[2 Kings] [5]:[11] But Naaman went away angry. "I thought," he said, "that he would surely come out to me and stand there and call on the name of the LORD his God, that he would wave his hand over the place and cure the leprosy.
[2 Kings] [5]:[12] Are not the Abana and the Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?" So he turned and went off in a rage.
[2 Kings] [5]:[13] But his servants came up to him and said, "My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he simply says to you, 'Wash and be clean'?"
[2 Kings] [5]:[14] So he went down and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, as the man of God had said, and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.
[2 Kings] [5]:[15] Then he returned to the man of God with his whole company. He came and stood before him and said, "Now I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. So please accept a gift from your servant."
[2 Kings] [5]:[16] But Elisha answered, "As the LORD lives, whom I serve, I will accept nothing." And though Naaman pressed him to take it, he refused.
[2 Kings] [5]:[17] "If you will not," said Naaman, "then please let your servant be given as much earth as a pair of mules can carry, for your servant will never again offer burnt offering or sacrifice to any other god but the LORD.
[2 Kings] [5]:[18] But may the LORD forgive your servant this one thing: when my master goes into the temple of Rimmon to bow down there, leaning on my arm, and I bow down in the temple of Rimmon—when I bow down there, may the LORD forgive your servant for this."
[2 Kings] [5]:[19] "Go in peace," Elisha said. And Naaman left him and traveled some distance.
[2 Kings] [5]:[20] Then Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said to himself, "My master has let this Aramean Naaman off too easily by not accepting what he brought. As the LORD lives, I will run after him and get something from him."
[2 Kings] [5]:[21] So Gehazi hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw him running toward him, he got down from his chariot to meet him and asked, "Is everything all right?"
[2 Kings] [5]:[22] "Everything is all right," Gehazi said. "My master sent me to say, 'Two young men from the company of the prophets have just now come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two sets of clothing.'"
[2 Kings] [5]:[23] "By all means, take two talents," said Naaman. He pressed Gehazi until he agreed, then tied up two talents of silver in two bags along with two sets of clothing, and gave them to two of his servants, who carried them ahead of Gehazi.
[2 Kings] [5]:[24] When Gehazi came to the hill, he took the things from the servants and stored them away in the house. Then he sent the men off, and they left.
[2 Kings] [5]:[25] When he went in and stood before his master, Elisha asked him, "Where have you been, Gehazi?" "Your servant went nowhere at all," he said.
[2 Kings] [5]:[26] But Elisha said to him, "Was not my spirit with you when the man got down from his chariot to meet you? Is this a time to accept silver, or to accept clothing, olive groves and vineyards, flocks and herds, male and female servants?
[2 Kings] [5]:[27] Naaman's leprosy will cling to you and to your descendants forever." And Gehazi went out from his presence, leprous, white as snow.
[2 Kings] [6]:[1] The company of the prophets said to Elisha, "Look, the place where we meet with you is too cramped for us.
[2 Kings] [6]:[2] Let us go to the Jordan, where each of us can cut a beam, and let us build a place there to live." "Go," he said.
[2 Kings] [6]:[3] Then one of them said, "Please come along with your servants." "I will come," he answered.
[2 Kings] [6]:[4] So he went with them. They came to the Jordan and began cutting down trees.
[2 Kings] [6]:[5] As one of them was felling a tree, the iron axhead fell into the water. "Oh no, my lord!" he cried out. "It was borrowed!"
[2 Kings] [6]:[6] The man of God asked, "Where did it fall?" When he showed him the place, Elisha cut a stick, threw it in there, and made the iron float.
[2 Kings] [6]:[7] "Lift it out," he said. So the man reached out his hand and took it.
[2 Kings] [6]:[8] Now the king of Aram was at war with Israel. He conferred with his officers and said, "I will set up my camp in such and such a place."
[2 Kings] [6]:[9] But the man of God sent word to the king of Israel: "Be careful not to pass by that place, for the Arameans are moving down there."
[2 Kings] [6]:[10] So the king of Israel sent word to the place the man of God had named. Time and again Elisha warned him, and he was on his guard there.
[2 Kings] [6]:[11] This enraged the king of Aram. He summoned his officers and demanded, "Tell me! Which of us is for the king of Israel?"
[2 Kings] [6]:[12] "None of us, my lord the king," said one of his officers. "It is Elisha, the prophet in Israel, who tells the king of Israel the very words you speak in your bedroom."
[2 Kings] [6]:[13] "Go and find out where he is," the king ordered, "so I can send men and capture him." The report came back: "He is in Dothan."
[2 Kings] [6]:[14] So he sent horses and chariots and a strong force there. They came by night and surrounded the city.
[2 Kings] [6]:[15] When the servant of the man of God got up early and went out, there was an army with horses and chariots surrounding the city. "Oh, my lord, what shall we do?" he cried to Elisha.
[2 Kings] [6]:[16] "Don't be afraid," the prophet answered. "Those who are with us are more than those who are with them."
[2 Kings] [6]:[17] Then Elisha prayed, "LORD, open his eyes so he may see." The LORD opened the servant's eyes, and he looked, and there was the mountain, full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
[2 Kings] [6]:[18] As the Arameans came down toward him, Elisha prayed to the LORD, "Strike this army with blindness." So he struck them with blindness, as Elisha had asked.
[2 Kings] [6]:[19] Elisha told them, "This is not the road, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will lead you to the man you are looking for." And he led them to Samaria.
[2 Kings] [6]:[20] When they had entered the city, Elisha said, "LORD, open the eyes of these men so they may see." The LORD opened their eyes, and they looked, and there they were, inside Samaria.
[2 Kings] [6]:[21] When the king of Israel saw them, he asked Elisha, "Shall I kill them, my father? Shall I kill them?"
[2 Kings] [6]:[22] "Do not kill them," he answered. "Would you kill men you have captured with your own sword and bow? Set food and water before them so they may eat and drink and then go back to their master."
[2 Kings] [6]:[23] So he prepared a great feast for them, and after they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they returned to their master. And the raiding bands from Aram stopped invading Israel's territory.
[2 Kings] [6]:[24] Some time later, Ben-Hadad king of Aram mobilized his entire army, marched up, and laid siege to Samaria.
[2 Kings] [6]:[25] There was a great famine in the city; the siege lasted so long that a donkey's head sold for eighty shekels of silver, and a quarter of a kab of seed pods for five shekels. [Footnote: Hebrew literally "dove's dung," probably a term for a cheap wild plant or seed pod.]
[2 Kings] [6]:[26] As the king of Israel was passing along the wall, a woman cried out to him, "Help me, my lord the king!"
[2 Kings] [6]:[27] The king replied, "May the LORD not help you! Where could I get help for you? From the threshing floor? From the winepress?"
[2 Kings] [6]:[28] Then he asked her, "What is the matter?" She answered, "This woman said to me, 'Give up your son so we may eat him today, and tomorrow we'll eat my son.'
[2 Kings] [6]:[29] So we cooked my son and ate him. The next day I said to her, 'Give up your son so we may eat him,' but she had hidden him."
[2 Kings] [6]:[30] When the king heard the woman's words, he tore his robes. As he went along the wall, the people saw that he had sackcloth under his clothes, next to his skin.
[2 Kings] [6]:[31] He said, "May God deal with me ever so severely if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on his shoulders today!"
[2 Kings] [6]:[32] Now Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. The king sent a messenger ahead, but before he arrived, Elisha said to the elders, "Don't you see how this murderer's son has sent someone to cut off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold it shut against him. Is not the sound of his master's footsteps right behind him?"
[2 Kings] [6]:[33] While he was still speaking to them, the messenger came down to him. And the king said, "This disaster is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?"
[2 Kings] [7]:[1] Then Elisha said, "Hear the word of the LORD. This is what the LORD says: By this time tomorrow a measure of fine flour will sell for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria." [Footnote: A measure (Hebrew seah) was about seven liters of dry goods; a shekel was a weight of silver, roughly a laborer's wages for several days.]
[2 Kings] [7]:[2] The officer on whose arm the king leaned answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD were to open windows in the heavens, could such a thing happen?" Elisha replied, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."
[2 Kings] [7]:[3] Now there were four men with leprosy at the entrance of the gate, and they said to one another, "Why should we sit here until we die?
[2 Kings] [7]:[4] If we say, 'Let us go into the city,' the famine is in the city and we will die there. And if we stay here, we will die too. So come, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they spare us, we live; if they kill us, we die.
[2 Kings] [7]:[5] So they set out at dusk for the Aramean camp. But when they reached the edge of the camp, no one was there.
[2 Kings] [7]:[6] For the Lord had caused the Aramean army to hear the sound of chariots and horses and a great army, and they had said to one another, "Look, the king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to attack us!"
[2 Kings] [7]:[7] So they had fled at dusk, abandoning their tents, their horses, and their donkeys. They left the camp just as it was and ran for their lives.
[2 Kings] [7]:[8] When the men with leprosy came to the edge of the camp, they entered one of the tents, ate and drank, and carried off silver and gold and clothing, and went and hid it. Then they came back, entered another tent, took what was there, and hid that too.
[2 Kings] [7]:[9] Then they said to one another, "What we are doing is not right. This is a day of good news, and we are keeping it to ourselves. If we wait until morning light, we will be held guilty. Come, let us go and report this to the king's household."
[2 Kings] [7]:[10] So they went and called out to the gatekeeper of the city and told him, "We went to the Aramean camp, and there was no one there—not a sound of anyone—only the horses and donkeys tied up, and the tents left just as they were."
[2 Kings] [7]:[11] The gatekeepers shouted the news, and it was reported inside the palace.
[2 Kings] [7]:[12] The king got up in the night and said to his servants, "Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know we are starving, so they have left the camp to hide in the countryside, thinking, 'They will come out, and then we will take them alive and get into the city.'"
[2 Kings] [7]:[13] One of his servants answered, "Have some men take five of the horses that are left in the city. They will fare no worse than all the multitude of Israel left here—no worse than all the multitude of Israel who have already perished. Let us send them and see."
[2 Kings] [7]:[14] So they took two chariots with their horses, and the king sent them after the Aramean army with the order, "Go and see."
[2 Kings] [7]:[15] They followed them as far as the Jordan, and found the whole road strewn with clothing and equipment that the Arameans had thrown away in their headlong flight. So the messengers returned and reported to the king.
[2 Kings] [7]:[16] Then the people went out and plundered the camp of the Arameans. So a measure of fine flour sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, just as the LORD had said.
[2 Kings] [7]:[17] Now the king had put the officer on whose arm he leaned in charge of the gate, and the people trampled him in the gateway, and he died—just as the man of God had said when the king came down to him.
[2 Kings] [7]:[18] It happened exactly as the man of God had told the king: "Two measures of barley will sell for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel, by this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria."
[2 Kings] [7]:[19] The officer had answered the man of God, "Even if the LORD were to open windows in the heavens, could such a thing happen?" And Elisha had replied, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."
[2 Kings] [7]:[20] And that is exactly what happened to him: the people trampled him in the gateway, and he died.
[2 Kings] [8]:[1] Elisha had said to the woman whose son he had restored to life, "Get up and go, you and your household, and settle wherever you can, for the LORD has called for a famine, and it will come upon the land for seven years."
[2 Kings] [8]:[2] So the woman got up and did as the man of God had said. She went with her household and settled in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
[2 Kings] [8]:[3] At the end of the seven years the woman returned from the land of the Philistines, and she went to appeal to the king for her house and her land.
[2 Kings] [8]:[4] Now the king was speaking with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, and said, "Tell me all the great things Elisha has done."
[2 Kings] [8]:[5] Just as Gehazi was telling the king how Elisha had restored the dead to life, the very woman whose son he had restored came in to appeal to the king for her house and her land. And Gehazi said, "My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life."
[2 Kings] [8]:[6] The king questioned the woman, and she told him her story. Then the king assigned an official to her, saying, "Restore everything that belongs to her, along with all the income from her land from the day she left the country until now."
[2 Kings] [8]:[7] Elisha came to Damascus while Ben-hadad king of Aram was ill. When he was told, "The man of God has come here,"
[2 Kings] [8]:[8] the king said to Hazael, "Take a gift with you and go to meet the man of God. Inquire of the LORD through him: Will I recover from this illness?"
[2 Kings] [8]:[9] So Hazael went to meet him, taking with him a gift—the finest goods of Damascus, a load for forty camels. He came and stood before him and said, "Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to ask you: Will I recover from this illness?"
[2 Kings] [8]:[10] Elisha said to him, "Go and tell him, 'You will certainly recover.'[^1] Yet the LORD has shown me that he will surely die." [^1]: The written Hebrew consonants here can be read as "tell him" or as "you will not certainly recover"; the traditional reading is "tell him."
[2 Kings] [8]:[11] Then he fixed his gaze on him and stared until Hazael was ashamed, and the man of God wept.
[2 Kings] [8]:[12] "Why is my lord weeping?" Hazael asked. He answered, "Because I know the harm you will do to the people of Israel. You will set their fortresses on fire, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little ones to pieces, and rip open their pregnant women."
[2 Kings] [8]:[13] Hazael said, "But what is your servant—a mere dog—that he should do such a great thing?" Elisha answered, "The LORD has shown me that you will become king over Aram."
[2 Kings] [8]:[14] Then Hazael left Elisha and went to his master, who asked him, "What did Elisha say to you?" He answered, "He told me that you would certainly recover."
[2 Kings] [8]:[15] But the next day he took a blanket, soaked it in water, and spread it over the king's face, and he died. And Hazael became king in his place.
[2 Kings] [8]:[16] In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah.
[2 Kings] [8]:[17] He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eight years.
[2 Kings] [8]:[18] He followed the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for he had married a daughter of Ahab. And he did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [8]:[19] Yet the LORD was unwilling to destroy Judah, for the sake of his servant David, since he had promised to give him a lamp for his descendants forever.
[2 Kings] [8]:[20] In his days Edom rebelled against the rule of Judah and set up a king of its own.
[2 Kings] [8]:[21] So Joram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots. He set out by night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him, along with their chariot commanders, but his troops fled to their tents.
[2 Kings] [8]:[22] So Edom has been in rebellion against the rule of Judah to this day. Libnah also rebelled at that same time.
[2 Kings] [8]:[23] As for the rest of the acts of Joram and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
[2 Kings] [8]:[24] Joram rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David. And his son Ahaziah became king in his place.
[2 Kings] [8]:[25] In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah.
[2 Kings] [8]:[26] Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem one year. His mother's name was Athaliah, a granddaughter of Omri king of Israel.[^1] [^1]: Hebrew: "daughter of Omri"; the Hebrew word can also mean a more distant female descendant. Athaliah was the daughter of Ahab, Omri's son.
[2 Kings] [8]:[27] He followed the ways of the house of Ahab and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as the house of Ahab had done, for he was related by marriage to the house of Ahab.
[2 Kings] [8]:[28] He went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth Gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.
[2 Kings] [8]:[29] So King Joram returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Arameans had inflicted on him at Ramah in his battle with Hazael king of Aram. And Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to Jezreel to visit Joram son of Ahab, because he was ill.
[2 Kings] [9]:[1] Then Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, "Tuck in your cloak, take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
[2 Kings] [9]:[2] When you get there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi. Go in, get him up from among his companions, and take him into an inner room.
[2 Kings] [9]:[3] Then take the flask of oil, pour it on his head, and say, 'This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.' Then open the door and run; do not wait."
[2 Kings] [9]:[4] So the young man, the young prophet, went to Ramoth-gilead.
[2 Kings] [9]:[5] When he arrived, the commanders of the army were sitting together. He said, "I have a word for you, commander." "For which of us?" Jehu asked. "For you, commander," he said.
[2 Kings] [9]:[6] So Jehu got up and went into the house, and the young man poured the oil on his head and said to him, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I anoint you king over the LORD's people, over Israel.
[2 Kings] [9]:[7] You are to strike down the house of Ahab your master, so that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the LORD's servants, shed by Jezebel's hand.
[2 Kings] [9]:[8] The whole house of Ahab shall perish. I will cut off from Ahab every male in Israel, both bond and free.
[2 Kings] [9]:[9] I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
[2 Kings] [9]:[10] As for Jezebel, dogs will devour her on the plot of ground at Jezreel, and no one will bury her." Then he opened the door and fled.
[2 Kings] [9]:[11] When Jehu came out to his master's officers, they asked, "Is everything all right? Why did this madman come to you?" "You know the sort of man," he answered, "and what he had to say."
[2 Kings] [9]:[12] "That's not true!" they said. "Tell us." So he said, "He told me this and that. He said, 'This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.'"
[2 Kings] [9]:[13] At once each man took his cloak and spread it under him on the bare steps. They blew the trumpet and shouted, "Jehu is king!"
[2 Kings] [9]:[14] So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, conspired against Joram. Now Joram and all Israel had been defending Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of Aram,
[2 Kings] [9]:[15] but King Joram had returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Arameans had inflicted on him in the battle with Hazael king of Aram. Jehu said, "If this is truly your will, let no one slip out of the city to carry the news to Jezreel."
