[2 Kings] [9]:[16] Then Jehu mounted his chariot and rode to Jezreel, because Joram was lying there and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to visit him.
[2 Kings] [9]:[17] The watchman standing on the tower in Jezreel saw Jehu's company approaching and called out, "I see a company of men." Joram ordered, "Get a horseman and send him out to meet them and ask, 'Do you come in peace?'"
[2 Kings] [9]:[18] The horseman rode out to meet him and said, "This is what the king says: 'Do you come in peace?'" "What do you know of peace?" Jehu answered. "Fall in behind me." The watchman reported, "The messenger has reached them, but he isn't coming back."
[2 Kings] [9]:[19] So the king sent out a second horseman. When he came to them he said, "This is what the king says: 'Do you come in peace?'" Jehu answered, "What do you know of peace? Fall in behind me."
[2 Kings] [9]:[20] The watchman reported, "He has reached them, but he isn't coming back either. And the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi—he drives like a madman."
[2 Kings] [9]:[21] "Hitch up my chariot," Joram ordered. And when it was hitched up, Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah rode out, each in his own chariot, to meet Jehu. They met him at the plot of ground that had belonged to Naboth the Jezreelite.
[2 Kings] [9]:[22] When Joram saw Jehu he asked, "Do you come in peace, Jehu?" "How can there be peace," Jehu replied, "as long as all the idolatry and witchcraft of your mother Jezebel go on?"
[2 Kings] [9]:[23] Joram wheeled around and fled, calling out to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
[2 Kings] [9]:[24] Then Jehu drew his bow and shot Joram between the shoulders. The arrow pierced his heart, and he slumped down in his chariot.
[2 Kings] [9]:[25] Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, "Pick him up and throw him on the plot of ground that belonged to Naboth the Jezreelite. Remember how you and I were riding together behind his father Ahab when the LORD pronounced this oracle against him:
[2 Kings] [9]:[26] 'As surely as I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons yesterday, declares the LORD, I will repay you on this plot of ground, declares the LORD.' Now then, pick him up and throw him on that plot, in keeping with the word of the LORD."
[2 Kings] [9]:[27] When Ahaziah king of Judah saw what was happening, he fled up the road toward Beth Haggan. Jehu chased him, shouting, "Shoot him down too!" They wounded him in his chariot on the way up to Gur near Ibleam. He fled to Megiddo and died there.
[2 Kings] [9]:[28] His servants took him by chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in the City of David.
[2 Kings] [9]:[29] Ahaziah had become king over Judah in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab.
[2 Kings] [9]:[30] When Jehu came to Jezreel, Jezebel heard of it. She painted her eyes, arranged her hair, and looked out of the window.
[2 Kings] [9]:[31] As Jehu entered the gate, she called out, "Is it peace, you Zimri, murderer of your master?"
[2 Kings] [9]:[32] He looked up at the window and called, "Who is on my side? Who?" Two or three eunuchs looked down at him.
[2 Kings] [9]:[33] "Throw her down!" he said. So they threw her down, and some of her blood spattered the wall and the horses, and he trampled her underfoot.
[2 Kings] [9]:[34] Then he went in and ate and drank. "See to that cursed woman," he said, "and bury her, for she was a king's daughter."
[2 Kings] [9]:[35] But when they went out to bury her, they found nothing of her but the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands.
[2 Kings] [9]:[36] They went back and told Jehu, who said, "This is the word of the LORD that he spoke through his servant Elijah the Tishbite: 'On the plot of ground at Jezreel dogs will devour Jezebel's flesh.'
[2 Kings] [9]:[37] "Jezebel's corpse will lie like dung on the open field in the plot at Jezreel, so that no one can say, 'This is Jezebel.'"
[2 Kings] [10]:[1] Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. So Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the officials of Jezreel, to the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab's sons. He wrote:
[2 Kings] [10]:[2] "Your master's sons are with you, and you have chariots and horses, a fortified city and weapons. So now, as soon as this letter reaches you,
[2 Kings] [10]:[3] choose the best and most capable of your master's sons, set him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's house."
[2 Kings] [10]:[4] But they were terrified and said, "If two kings could not stand against him, how can we?"
[2 Kings] [10]:[5] So the palace administrator, the governor of the city, the elders, and the guardians sent word to Jehu: "We are your servants, and we will do whatever you tell us. We will not make anyone king. Do whatever you think best."
[2 Kings] [10]:[6] Then Jehu wrote them a second letter: "If you are on my side and will obey me, take the heads of your master's sons and come to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow." Now the king's sons, seventy of them, were with the leading men of the city, who were raising them.
[2 Kings] [10]:[7] When the letter reached them, they took the king's sons and slaughtered all seventy. They put their heads in baskets and sent them to Jehu at Jezreel.
[2 Kings] [10]:[8] When the messenger came and told him, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons," Jehu said, "Pile them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning."
[2 Kings] [10]:[9] In the morning he went out, stood before all the people, and said, "You are innocent. It was I who conspired against my master and killed him—but who struck down all these?
[2 Kings] [10]:[10] Know then that not one word the LORD spoke against the house of Ahab will fall to the ground. The LORD has done what he promised through his servant Elijah."
[2 Kings] [10]:[11] Then Jehu struck down everyone left of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, along with all his leading men, his close friends, and his priests, leaving him no survivor.
[2 Kings] [10]:[12] Then he set out for Samaria. On the way, at Beth Eked of the Shepherds,
[2 Kings] [10]:[13] Jehu came upon the relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah and asked, "Who are you?" They answered, "We are relatives of Ahaziah, and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother."
[2 Kings] [10]:[14] "Take them alive," he ordered. So they took them alive and slaughtered them at the cistern of Beth Eked—forty-two men. He left none of them alive.
[2 Kings] [10]:[15] When he left there, he met Jehonadab son of Rechab, who was coming to meet him. Jehu greeted him and said, "Is your heart as true to me as mine is to you?" "It is indeed," Jehonadab answered. "Then give me your hand," said Jehu. So he gave him his hand, and Jehu helped him up into the chariot
[2 Kings] [10]:[16] and said, "Come with me and see my zeal for the LORD." So he rode along with him in his chariot.
[2 Kings] [10]:[17] When Jehu came to Samaria, he struck down all who were left of Ahab's family there, wiping them out, just as the LORD had said to Elijah.
[2 Kings] [10]:[18] Then Jehu gathered all the people together and said to them, "Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.
[2 Kings] [10]:[19] Now summon to me all the prophets of Baal, all his servants and all his priests. Let no one be missing, for I am holding a great sacrifice for Baal. Whoever is missing will not live." But Jehu was acting deceitfully, in order to destroy the servants of Baal.
[2 Kings] [10]:[20] Jehu said, "Proclaim a solemn assembly for Baal." And they announced it.
[2 Kings] [10]:[21] Then Jehu sent word throughout Israel, and all the servants of Baal came; not one stayed away. They crowded into the temple of Baal until it was filled from wall to wall.
[2 Kings] [10]:[22] Jehu said to the keeper of the wardrobe, "Bring out robes for all the servants of Baal." So he brought out robes for them.
[2 Kings] [10]:[23] Then Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab entered the temple of Baal, and Jehu said to the servants of Baal, "Search and make sure that no servant of the LORD is here among you—only servants of Baal."
[2 Kings] [10]:[24] So they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed eighty men outside, and he had told them, "If any man lets one of these escape whom I am placing in your hands, his own life will be forfeit."
[2 Kings] [10]:[25] As soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu ordered the guards and the officers, "Go in and strike them down; let no one escape." So they cut them down with the sword. Then the guards and officers threw the bodies out and went on into the inner shrine of the temple of Baal.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew word here normally means "city"; the sense of the phrase is uncertain, and it may refer to an inner room or citadel of the temple.
[2 Kings] [10]:[26] They brought out the sacred pillars of the temple of Baal and burned them.
[2 Kings] [10]:[27] They tore down the sacred pillar of Baal, demolished the temple of Baal, and made it into a latrine—and so it remains to this day.
[2 Kings] [10]:[28] So Jehu wiped out Baal worship from Israel.
[2 Kings] [10]:[29] But he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, into which he had led Israel—the golden calves at Bethel and at Dan.
[2 Kings] [10]:[30] The LORD said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in carrying out what is right in my eyes and have done to the house of Ahab all that I had in mind, your descendants to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel."
[2 Kings] [10]:[31] Yet Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, who had led Israel into sin.
[2 Kings] [10]:[32] In those days the LORD began to reduce the territory of Israel. Hazael struck them down throughout the territory of Israel,
[2 Kings] [10]:[33] east of the Jordan: all the land of Gilead—the region of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh—from Aroer by the Arnon Valley through Gilead to Bashan.
[2 Kings] [10]:[34] As for the rest of the acts of Jehu, all that he did and all his mighty deeds, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
[2 Kings] [10]:[35] Jehu rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria. And Jehoahaz his son succeeded him as king.
[2 Kings] [10]:[36] Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty-eight years.
[2 Kings] [11]:[1] When Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, she rose up and destroyed the whole royal family.
[2 Kings] [11]:[2] But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death. She hid him and his nurse in a bedroom, out of Athaliah's sight, and so he was not killed.
[2 Kings] [11]:[3] He remained hidden with her in the house of the LORD for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.
[2 Kings] [11]:[4] In the seventh year Jehoiada sent for the commanders of hundreds, of the royal guard and of the palace guards, and brought them to himself in the house of the LORD. He made a covenant with them and put them under oath there in the house of the LORD, and then he showed them the king's son.
[2 Kings] [11]:[5] He gave them these orders: "This is what you are to do. A third of you who come on duty on the Sabbath are to keep watch over the royal palace;
[2 Kings] [11]:[6] a third are to be at the Sur Gate, and a third at the gate behind the guards. You are to stand guard over the house, taking your turns.
[2 Kings] [11]:[7] The two remaining divisions of you, all who go off duty on the Sabbath, are to keep watch over the house of the LORD for the king.
[2 Kings] [11]:[8] Surround the king on every side, each man with his weapon in his hand. Whoever breaks through the ranks is to be put to death. Stay with the king wherever he goes."
[2 Kings] [11]:[9] The commanders of hundreds did everything Jehoiada the priest had ordered. Each took his men, both those coming on duty on the Sabbath and those going off duty, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
[2 Kings] [11]:[10] Then the priest handed out to the commanders the spears and the shields that had belonged to King David and were kept in the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [11]:[11] The guards took up their positions, each man with his weapon in his hand, surrounding the king from the south side of the temple to the north side, by the altar and the temple.
[2 Kings] [11]:[12] Jehoiada brought out the king's son, placed the crown on him and gave him the covenant scroll. They proclaimed him king and anointed him, and the people clapped their hands and shouted, "Long live the king!"
[2 Kings] [11]:[13] When Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the people, she went to the people at the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [11]:[14] There she saw the king standing by the pillar, as the custom was, with the officers and the trumpeters beside him, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried out, "Treason! Treason!"
[2 Kings] [11]:[15] Jehoiada the priest ordered the commanders of hundreds who were in charge of the troops, "Bring her out between the ranks, and put to the sword anyone who follows her." For the priest had said, "She must not be put to death in the house of the LORD."
[2 Kings] [11]:[16] So they seized her, and she was taken by the way the horses enter the palace, and there she was put to death.
[2 Kings] [11]:[17] Then Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, that they would be the LORD's people; and also between the king and the people.
[2 Kings] [11]:[18] All the people of the land went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed its altars and its images to pieces and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars. Then Jehoiada the priest appointed officers to oversee the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [11]:[19] He took the commanders of hundreds, the royal guard, the palace guards and all the people of the land, and together they brought the king down from the house of the LORD. They entered the palace through the gate of the guards, and the king took his place on the royal throne.
[2 Kings] [11]:[20] All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, now that Athaliah had been put to the sword at the royal palace.
[2 Kings] [12]:[1] Jehoash was seven years old when he became king.
[2 Kings] [12]:[2] In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah, from Beersheba.
[2 Kings] [12]:[3] Jehoash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all his days, because Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
[2 Kings] [12]:[4] Yet the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
[2 Kings] [12]:[5] Jehoash said to the priests, "All the money from the sacred gifts brought into the house of the LORD—the money each man is assessed, the money paid as the valuation for persons, and all the money that anyone freely decides to bring to the house of the LORD—
[2 Kings] [12]:[6] let the priests take it for themselves, each from his own acquaintance, and let them repair whatever damage is found in the house.
[2 Kings] [12]:[7] But by the twenty-third year of King Jehoash the priests still had not repaired the damage to the temple.
[2 Kings] [12]:[8] So King Jehoash summoned Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and said to them, "Why are you not repairing the damage to the temple? From now on, take no more money from those who deal with you; hand it over instead for the repair of the temple."
[2 Kings] [12]:[9] The priests agreed that they would take no more money from the people and would no longer carry out the repairs of the temple themselves.
[2 Kings] [12]:[10] Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the altar, on the right as one enters the house of the LORD. There the priests who guarded the threshold put all the money that was brought into the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [12]:[11] Whenever they saw that there was a large amount of money in the chest, the king's secretary and the high priest would come up, tie it in bags, and count the money found in the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [12]:[12] They handed over the money that had been counted to the workmen appointed over the house of the LORD, and these paid it out to the carpenters and builders who worked on the house of the LORD,
[2 Kings] [12]:[13] and to the masons and stonecutters, and for buying timber and dressed stone to repair the damage to the house of the LORD, and for every other expense of the repairs.
[2 Kings] [12]:[14] But none of the money brought into the house of the LORD was used to make silver basins, snuffers, bowls, trumpets, or any other vessel of gold or silver for the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [12]:[15] It was given to the workmen, and with it they repaired the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [12]:[16] No accounting was demanded from the men into whose hands the money was placed to pay the workers, for they acted in good faith.
[2 Kings] [12]:[17] The money from the guilt offerings and the sin offerings was not brought into the house of the LORD; it belonged to the priests.
[2 Kings] [12]:[18] At that time Hazael king of Aram marched up, attacked Gath, and captured it. Then he set his sights on marching against Jerusalem.

[2 Kings] [12]:[20] As for the rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did, they are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah.

[2 Kings] [13]:[1] In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned seventeen years.
[2 Kings] [13]:[2] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin; he never turned away from them.
[2 Kings] [13]:[3] So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he handed them over to Hazael king of Aram and to Ben-hadad son of Hazael throughout those days.
[2 Kings] [13]:[4] Then Jehoahaz pleaded with the LORD, and the LORD listened to him, for he saw how Israel was oppressed—how the king of Aram was crushing them.
[2 Kings] [13]:[5] The LORD gave Israel a deliverer, and they escaped from the grip of Aram, so that the Israelites lived in their own homes as they had before.
[2 Kings] [13]:[6] But they did not turn away from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, who had led Israel into sin; they kept walking in them. And the Asherah pole also remained standing in Samaria.
[2 Kings] [13]:[7] Nothing was left of Jehoahaz's army but fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers, for the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like the dust at threshing.
[2 Kings] [13]:[8] The rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, all that he did and his mighty deeds, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
[2 Kings] [13]:[9] Jehoahaz slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria, and his son Joash became king in his place.
[2 Kings] [13]:[10] In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.
[2 Kings] [13]:[11] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin, but kept walking in them.
[2 Kings] [13]:[12] The rest of the acts of Joash, all that he did, and his valor in his war against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
[2 Kings] [13]:[13] Joash slept with his fathers, and Jeroboam took his place on the throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
[2 Kings] [13]:[14] Now Elisha had fallen sick with the illness from which he would die. Joash king of Israel went down to him and wept over him, saying, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!"
[2 Kings] [13]:[15] Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows," and he took a bow and arrows.
[2 Kings] [13]:[16] Then he said to the king of Israel, "Set your hand to the bow." When he had set his hand to it, Elisha laid his own hands on the king's hands.
[2 Kings] [13]:[17] "Open the window toward the east," he said, and the king opened it. Then Elisha said, "Shoot!" and he shot. And Elisha said, "The LORD's arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram! You will strike down Aram at Aphek until you have finished them off."
[2 Kings] [13]:[18] Then he said, "Take the arrows," and he took them. He said to the king of Israel, "Strike the ground," and he struck it three times and stopped.
[2 Kings] [13]:[19] The man of God was angry with him and said, "You should have struck five or six times—then you would have struck Aram down until you had finished them off. But now you will defeat Aram only three times."
[2 Kings] [13]:[20] Then Elisha died and was buried. Now Moabite raiders used to invade the land each spring.
[2 Kings] [13]:[21] Once, while some men were burying a man, they suddenly caught sight of a raiding party. They threw the man into Elisha's grave, and as soon as he touched Elisha's bones, the man came to life and rose to his feet.
[2 Kings] [13]:[22] Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel throughout the days of Jehoahaz.
[2 Kings] [13]:[23] But the LORD was gracious to them, had compassion on them, and turned toward them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He was unwilling to destroy them, and he did not cast them out from his presence—not to this day.
[2 Kings] [13]:[24] When Hazael king of Aram died, his son Ben-hadad became king in his place.
[2 Kings] [13]:[25] Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from Ben-hadad son of Hazael the towns Ben-hadad had captured in battle from his father Jehoahaz. Three times Joash defeated him, and so he recovered the towns of Israel.
[2 Kings] [14]:[1] In the second year of Joash son of Joahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah.
[2 Kings] [14]:[2] He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan, of Jerusalem.
[2 Kings] [14]:[3] He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, yet not like David his father; he did everything as his father Joash had done.
[2 Kings] [14]:[4] Only the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
[2 Kings] [14]:[5] As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his hand, he struck down the servants who had killed the king his father.
[2 Kings] [14]:[6] But he did not put the children of the murderers to death, as it is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, where the LORD commanded: "Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers; each one shall be put to death for his own sin."
[2 Kings] [14]:[7] He struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and captured Sela in battle, and he named it Joktheel, as it is called to this day.
[2 Kings] [14]:[8] Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us face each other in battle."
[2 Kings] [14]:[9] But Jehoash king of Israel sent back word to Amaziah king of Judah: "The thistle in Lebanon sent word to the cedar in Lebanon, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' But a wild beast of the field in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle underfoot.
[2 Kings] [14]:[10] You have indeed struck down Edom, and your heart has grown proud. Enjoy your glory, but stay at home. Why provoke disaster and bring yourself down, and Judah with you?"
[2 Kings] [14]:[11] But Amaziah would not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel marched out, and he and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other at Beth Shemesh in Judah.
[2 Kings] [14]:[12] Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his tent.
[2 Kings] [14]:[13] Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash, son of Ahaziah, at Beth Shemesh. Then he came to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
[2 Kings] [14]:[14] He took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the royal palace, along with hostages, and returned to Samaria.
[2 Kings] [14]:[15] As for the rest of the acts of Jehoash, what he accomplished and his valor, and how he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
[2 Kings] [14]:[16] Jehoash rested with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and his son Jeroboam succeeded him as king.
[2 Kings] [14]:[17] Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived on fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
[2 Kings] [14]:[18] As for the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
[2 Kings] [14]:[19] A conspiracy was formed against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent men after him to Lachish and killed him there.
[2 Kings] [14]:[20] They brought him back on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the City of David.
[2 Kings] [14]:[21] Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
[2 Kings] [14]:[22] He rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king had rested with his fathers.
[2 Kings] [14]:[23] In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash became king of Israel in Samaria, and he reigned forty-one years.
[2 Kings] [14]:[24] He did what was evil in the LORD's eyes and did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had led Israel into sin.
[2 Kings] [14]:[25] He restored the borders of Israel from Lebo Hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the LORD, the God of Israel, which he had spoken through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath Hepher.
[2 Kings] [14]:[26] For the LORD had seen how bitterly Israel suffered—no one was left, neither slave nor free, and there was no one to help Israel.
[2 Kings] [14]:[27] And the LORD had not said that he would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven, so he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.
[2 Kings] [14]:[28] As for the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, all that he did and his valor in battle, and how he recovered Damascus and Hamath for Israel,* are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel? [*Footnote: The Hebrew of this clause is difficult; it reads literally "which had belonged to Judah, for Israel."]
