[2 Kings] [15]:[1] In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah.
[2 Kings] [15]:[2] He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah, of Jerusalem.
[2 Kings] [15]:[3] He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done.
[2 Kings] [15]:[4] Yet the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense there.
[2 Kings] [15]:[5] The LORD struck the king, and he had a defiling skin disease until the day of his death. He lived in a separate house, while Jotham the king's son was in charge of the palace and governed the people of the land.
[2 Kings] [15]:[6] The rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
[2 Kings] [15]:[7] Azariah rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David, and his son Jotham became king in his place.
[2 Kings] [15]:[8] In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned six months.
[2 Kings] [15]:[9] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his fathers had done. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin.
[2 Kings] [15]:[10] Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him, struck him down in front of the people, killed him, and became king in his place.
[2 Kings] [15]:[11] The rest of the acts of Zechariah are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
[2 Kings] [15]:[12] This fulfilled the word the LORD had spoken to Jehu: "Your descendants to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel." And so it was.
[2 Kings] [15]:[13] Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned a full month in Samaria.
[2 Kings] [15]:[14] Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah to Samaria, struck down Shallum son of Jabesh there, killed him, and became king in his place.
[2 Kings] [15]:[15] The rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy he led, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
[2 Kings] [15]:[16] At that time Menahem marched from Tirzah and attacked Tiphsah, everyone in it, and its surrounding territory, because the city refused to open its gates to him. He struck it down and ripped open all its pregnant women.
[2 Kings] [15]:[17] In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel, and he reigned ten years in Samaria.
[2 Kings] [15]:[18] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. As long as he lived he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin.
[2 Kings] [15]:[19] Pul king of Assyria invaded the land, and Menahem gave him a thousand talents of silver to gain his support and secure his own hold on the kingdom.
[2 Kings] [15]:[20] Menahem raised the silver from Israel, exacting fifty shekels of silver from every wealthy man, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria withdrew and did not remain in the land.
[2 Kings] [15]:[21] The rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
[2 Kings] [15]:[22] Menahem rested with his fathers, and his son Pekahiah became king in his place.
[2 Kings] [15]:[23] In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned two years.
[2 Kings] [15]:[24] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin.
[2 Kings] [15]:[25] Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him. With fifty men of Gilead he struck him down in Samaria, in the citadel of the royal palace, together with Argob and Arieh. He killed him and became king in his place.
[2 Kings] [15]:[26] The rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
[2 Kings] [15]:[27] In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned twenty years.
[2 Kings] [15]:[28] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin.
[2 Kings] [15]:[29] In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria came and captured Ijon, Abel Beth Maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee—all the land of Naphtali—and he deported the people to Assyria.
[2 Kings] [15]:[30] Then Hoshea son of Elah led a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah. He struck him down and killed him, and became king in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
[2 Kings] [15]:[31] The rest of the acts of Pekah, and all that he did, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
[2 Kings] [15]:[32] In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah became king of Judah.
[2 Kings] [15]:[33] He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.
[2 Kings] [15]:[34] He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, following the example of his father Uzziah.
[2 Kings] [15]:[35] Yet the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense there. He built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [15]:[36] The rest of the acts of Jotham, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
[2 Kings] [15]:[37] In those days the LORD began to send Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.
[2 Kings] [15]:[38] Jotham rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David his forefather, and his son Ahaz became king in his place.
[2 Kings] [16]:[1] In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah.
[2 Kings] [16]:[2] Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God, as his father David had done.
[2 Kings] [16]:[3] Instead he followed the ways of the kings of Israel. He even made his own son pass through the fire, following the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
[2 Kings] [16]:[4] He sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.
[2 Kings] [16]:[5] Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel marched up to attack Jerusalem. They laid siege to Ahaz but could not overpower him.
[2 Kings] [16]:[6] At that time Rezin king of Aram recovered Elath for Aram and drove the Judeans out of Elath. Then the Edomites came to Elath and have lived there to this day.
[2 Kings] [16]:[7] So Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria with this message: "I am your servant and your son. Come up and rescue me from the hand of the king of Aram and the hand of the king of Israel, who are attacking me."
[2 Kings] [16]:[8] Ahaz took the silver and gold found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the royal palace and sent it as a bribe to the king of Assyria.
[2 Kings] [16]:[9] The king of Assyria listened to him. He marched against Damascus, captured it, deported its people to Kir, and put Rezin to death.
[2 Kings] [16]:[10] Then King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria. When he saw the altar that was in Damascus, King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest a sketch of the altar and a detailed plan of its construction.
[2 Kings] [16]:[11] So Uriah the priest built an altar according to all the instructions King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, and he finished it before King Ahaz returned from Damascus.
[2 Kings] [16]:[12] When the king came back from Damascus and saw the altar, he approached it and offered sacrifices on it.
[2 Kings] [16]:[13] He burned his whole offering and his grain offering, poured out his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his fellowship offerings on the altar.
[2 Kings] [16]:[14] As for the bronze altar that stood before the LORD, he moved it from the front of the temple—from between the new altar and the house of the LORD—and set it on the north side of the new altar.
[2 Kings] [16]:[15] Then King Ahaz gave this command to Uriah the priest: "On the great altar burn the morning whole offering and the evening grain offering, the king's whole offering and his grain offering, and the whole offering of all the people of the land, with their grain offerings and their drink offerings. Sprinkle on it all the blood of the whole offerings and all the blood of the sacrifices. But the bronze altar I will use for seeking guidance."
[2 Kings] [16]:[16] And Uriah the priest did everything King Ahaz commanded.
[2 Kings] [16]:[17] King Ahaz cut off the side panels of the movable stands and removed the basin from each of them. He took the Sea down from the bronze oxen that supported it and set it on a stone base.
[2 Kings] [16]:[18] He also removed from the house of the LORD the covered Sabbath walkway that had been built there, and the king's outer entryway—all because of the king of Assyria.
[2 Kings] [16]:[19] The rest of the acts of Ahaz—what he did—are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
[2 Kings] [16]:[20] Ahaz rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David. And Hezekiah his son succeeded him as king.
[2 Kings] [17]:[1] In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned nine years.
[2 Kings] [17]:[2] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, though not like the kings of Israel who came before him.
[2 Kings] [17]:[3] Shalmaneser king of Assyria marched against him, and Hoshea became his vassal and paid him tribute.
[2 Kings] [17]:[4] But the king of Assyria uncovered a conspiracy: Hoshea had sent messengers to So, king of Egypt, and had not paid the tribute to the king of Assyria as he had done year by year. So the king of Assyria seized him and bound him in prison.
[2 Kings] [17]:[5] Then the king of Assyria invaded the whole land, marched against Samaria, and besieged it for three years.
[2 Kings] [17]:[6] In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria captured Samaria and deported Israel to Assyria, settling them in Halah, on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
[2 Kings] [17]:[7] All this happened because the Israelites had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, out from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt. They feared other gods
[2 Kings] [17]:[8] and followed the customs of the nations the LORD had driven out before them, and the practices the kings of Israel had introduced.
[2 Kings] [17]:[9] The Israelites secretly did things against the LORD their God that were not right. They built themselves high places in all their towns, from watchtower to fortified city.
[2 Kings] [17]:[10] They set up sacred pillars and Asherah poles for themselves on every high hill and under every green tree.
[2 Kings] [17]:[11] There, on every high place, they burned incense, just like the nations whom the LORD had carried into exile before them. They did wicked things that provoked the LORD to anger.
[2 Kings] [17]:[12] They served idols, though the LORD had said to them, "You shall not do this."
[2 Kings] [17]:[13] The LORD warned Israel and Judah through every prophet and every seer: "Turn back from your evil ways. Keep my commandments and my statutes, according to the whole law that I commanded your fathers and that I sent to you through my servants the prophets."
[2 Kings] [17]:[14] But they would not listen. They stiffened their necks like their fathers, who did not trust in the LORD their God.
[2 Kings] [17]:[15] They rejected his statutes and the covenant he had made with their fathers, and the warnings he had given them. They pursued worthless idols and became worthless themselves. They followed the nations around them, though the LORD had commanded them not to imitate them.
[2 Kings] [17]:[16] They abandoned all the commandments of the LORD their God. They made for themselves two cast metal calves, made an Asherah pole, bowed down to all the host of heaven, and served Baal.
[2 Kings] [17]:[17] They made their sons and daughters pass through the fire, practiced divination and sorcery, and sold themselves to do what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger.
[2 Kings] [17]:[18] So the LORD was furious with Israel and removed them from his presence. Only the tribe of Judah was left.
[2 Kings] [17]:[19] But even Judah did not keep the commandments of the LORD their God; they followed the customs Israel had introduced.
[2 Kings] [17]:[20] So the LORD rejected all the descendants of Israel. He afflicted them and handed them over to plunderers, until at last he cast them out of his presence.
[2 Kings] [17]:[21] For when he tore Israel away from the house of David, they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king, and Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the LORD and led them into great sin.
[2 Kings] [17]:[22] The Israelites persisted in all the sins Jeroboam had committed; they did not turn away from them,
[2 Kings] [17]:[23] until the LORD removed Israel from his presence, just as he had said through all his servants the prophets. So Israel was exiled from their own land to Assyria, where they remain to this day.
[2 Kings] [17]:[24] The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim and settled them in the towns of Samaria in place of the Israelites. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its towns.
[2 Kings] [17]:[25] When they first settled there, they did not fear the LORD, so the LORD sent lions among them, and the lions killed some of them.
[2 Kings] [17]:[26] Word was sent to the king of Assyria: "The nations you deported and settled in the towns of Samaria do not know the practice of the God of the land. He has sent lions among them, and they are killing them off, because the people do not know the practice of the God of the land."
[2 Kings] [17]:[27] Then the king of Assyria gave this order: "Send back one of the priests you deported from there. Let him go and live there and teach them the practice of the God of the land."
[2 Kings] [17]:[28] So one of the priests who had been deported from Samaria came and settled in Bethel, and he taught them how to fear the LORD.
[2 Kings] [17]:[29] Yet each nation went on making its own gods, and they set them up in the shrines the Samaritans had built at the high places, each nation in the towns where they lived.
[2 Kings] [17]:[30] The men of Babylon made Succoth Benoth, the men of Cuth made Nergal, the men of Hamath made Ashima,
[2 Kings] [17]:[31] The Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burned their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
[2 Kings] [17]:[32] They feared the LORD, but they also appointed men from their own ranks as priests of the high places, and these officiated for them in the shrines of the high places.
[2 Kings] [17]:[33] They feared the LORD, yet they served their own gods according to the customs of the nations from which they had been deported.
[2 Kings] [17]:[34] To this day they persist in their former customs. They do not fear the LORD, nor do they follow the statutes and ordinances, the law and the commandment that the LORD gave the children of Jacob, whom he named Israel.
[2 Kings] [17]:[35] For the LORD had made a covenant with them and commanded them: "Do not fear other gods or bow down to them, do not serve them or sacrifice to them.
[2 Kings] [17]:[36] But the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm—him you shall fear, to him you shall bow down, and to him you shall sacrifice.
[2 Kings] [17]:[37] You shall always be careful to keep the statutes and ordinances, the law and the commandment that he wrote for you. Do not fear other gods.
[2 Kings] [17]:[38] Do not forget the covenant I made with you, and do not fear other gods.
[2 Kings] [17]:[39] Rather, fear the LORD your God, and he will deliver you from the hand of all your enemies."
[2 Kings] [17]:[40] But they would not listen; they kept following their former customs.
[2 Kings] [17]:[41] So these nations feared the LORD, yet they served their carved images; and their children and their children's children continue to this day to do just as their fathers did.
[2 Kings] [18]:[1] In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz began to reign over Judah.
[2 Kings] [18]:[2] He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abi, the daughter of Zechariah.
[2 Kings] [18]:[3] He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as David his father had done.
[2 Kings] [18]:[4] He removed the high places, smashed the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah. He also broke in pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made, for down to that time the Israelites had been burning incense to it; it was called Nehushtan.[Nehushtan sounds like the Hebrew words for "bronze" and "serpent"; the name may be understood as "the bronze thing."]
[2 Kings] [18]:[5] He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel. Among all the kings of Judah there was no one like him, either before him or after him.
[2 Kings] [18]:[6] He held fast to the LORD and did not turn away from following him; he kept the commandments the LORD had given Moses.
[2 Kings] [18]:[7] And the LORD was with him; he succeeded in everything he undertook. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and would not serve him.
[2 Kings] [18]:[8] He struck down the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territory, from watchtower to fortified city.
[2 Kings] [18]:[9] In the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria marched against Samaria and laid siege to it.
[2 Kings] [18]:[10] At the end of three years they captured it. In Hezekiah's sixth year, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was taken.
[2 Kings] [18]:[11] The king of Assyria deported Israel to Assyria and settled them in Halah, on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
[2 Kings] [18]:[12] This happened because they had not obeyed the voice of the LORD their God but had violated his covenant—all that Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded. They neither listened nor obeyed.
[2 Kings] [18]:[13] In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
[2 Kings] [18]:[14] So Hezekiah king of Judah sent word to the king of Assyria at Lachish: "I have sinned. Withdraw from me, and I will pay whatever you demand of me." The king of Assyria imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
[2 Kings] [18]:[15] Hezekiah gave him all the silver found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the royal palace.
[2 Kings] [18]:[16] At that time Hezekiah king of Judah stripped the doors of the temple of the LORD and the doorposts he himself had overlaid, and gave them to the king of Assyria.
[2 Kings] [18]:[17] The king of Assyria sent the Tartan, the Rab-saris, and the Rabshakeh with a large army from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. They came up to Jerusalem and took their stand by the aqueduct of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field.
[2 Kings] [18]:[18] They called for the king, and Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebnah the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came out to them.
[2 Kings] [18]:[19] The Rabshakeh said to them: "Tell Hezekiah: This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is this confidence of yours?
[2 Kings] [18]:[20] You talk of strategy and strength for war, but these are empty words. In whom, then, are you trusting, that you rebel against me?
[2 Kings] [18]:[21] Look now, you are trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff, which pierces the hand of anyone who leans on it. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is to all who trust in him.
[2 Kings] [18]:[22] And if you say, 'We trust in the LORD our God'—is he not the very one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, telling Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship before this altar in Jerusalem'?
[2 Kings] [18]:[23] Come now, make a bargain with my lord, the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses—if you can find riders for them!
[2 Kings] [18]:[24] How then can you turn back even one officer among the least of my lord's servants, while you rely on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
[2 Kings] [18]:[25] Besides, have I come up to destroy this place without the LORD? The LORD himself said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"
[2 Kings] [18]:[26] Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, along with Shebnah and Joah, said to the Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew in the hearing of the people on the wall."
[2 Kings] [18]:[27] But the Rabshakeh answered, "Was it only to your master and to you that my lord sent me to say these things? Was it not also to the men sitting on the wall, who will have to eat their own dung and drink their own urine along with you?"
[2 Kings] [18]:[28] Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out loudly in Hebrew: "Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!
[2 Kings] [18]:[29] This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you. He cannot deliver you from my hand.
[2 Kings] [18]:[30] Do not let Hezekiah persuade you to trust in the LORD when he says, 'The LORD will surely deliver us; this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.'
[2 Kings] [18]:[31] "Do not listen to Hezekiah. This is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from your own vine and your own fig tree and drink water from your own cistern,
[2 Kings] [18]:[32] until I come and take you away to a land like your own—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive oil and honey. Live, and do not die! Do not listen to Hezekiah when he misleads you by saying, 'The LORD will deliver us.'
[2 Kings] [18]:[33] Has any god of any nation ever delivered his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
[2 Kings] [18]:[34] Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Did they deliver Samaria from my hand?
[2 Kings] [18]:[35] Who among all the gods of the lands has delivered his land from my hand? How then can the LORD deliver Jerusalem from my hand?"
[2 Kings] [18]:[36] But the people remained silent and said nothing in reply, for the king had commanded, "Do not answer him."
[2 Kings] [18]:[37] Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder went to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and reported to him what the Rabshakeh had said.
[2 Kings] [19]:[1] When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [19]:[2] He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the scribe, and the senior priests, all of them covered in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
[2 Kings] [19]:[3] They said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, of rebuke and disgrace. Children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them.
[2 Kings] [19]:[4] Perhaps the LORD your God will hear all the words of the field commander, whom his master the king of Assyria sent to mock the living God, and will rebuke him for the words the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that still survives."
[2 Kings] [19]:[5] So King Hezekiah's servants came to Isaiah.
[2 Kings] [19]:[6] And Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master this: The LORD says, Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
[2 Kings] [19]:[7] Look, I am about to put a spirit in him, so that he hears a report and returns to his own land, and there in his own land I will make him fall by the sword."
[2 Kings] [19]:[8] When the field commander heard that the king of Assyria had left Lachish, he went back and found him fighting against Libnah.
[2 Kings] [19]:[9] Now the king received a report about Tirhakah, king of Cush: "He has set out to fight against you." So he sent messengers again to Hezekiah with this message:
[2 Kings] [19]:[10] "Say this to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you when he says, 'Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.'
[2 Kings] [19]:[11] You yourself have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, destroying them completely. And will you be delivered?
[2 Kings] [19]:[12] Did the gods of the nations my fathers destroyed rescue them—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
[2 Kings] [19]:[13] Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, or of Hena and Ivvah?"
[2 Kings] [19]:[14] Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them. Then he went up to the house of the LORD and spread it out before the LORD.
[2 Kings] [19]:[15] And Hezekiah prayed before the LORD: "LORD, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
[2 Kings] [19]:[16] Turn your ear, LORD, and hear; open your eyes, LORD, and see. Listen to the words Sennacherib has sent to mock the living God.
[2 Kings] [19]:[17] It is true, LORD, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste these nations and their lands.
[2 Kings] [19]:[18] They have thrown their gods into the fire and destroyed them, for they were not gods at all but only wood and stone, the work of human hands.
[2 Kings] [19]:[19] Now, LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone, LORD, are God."
[2 Kings] [19]:[20] Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I have heard your prayer concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria.
[2 Kings] [19]:[21] This is the word the LORD has spoken against him: "The virgin daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head as you flee.
[2 Kings] [19]:[22] Whom have you mocked and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!
[2 Kings] [19]:[23] By your messengers you have mocked the Lord, saying, 'With my many chariots I have gone up to the heights of the mountains, to the far reaches of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest cypresses. I have reached its farthest lodging place, its densest forest.
[2 Kings] [19]:[24] I have dug wells and drunk foreign waters; with the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.'
[2 Kings] [19]:[25] Have you not heard? Long ago I determined it; from days of old I planned it, and now I have brought it about—that you should turn fortified cities into heaps of rubble.
[2 Kings] [19]:[26] Their inhabitants are stripped of strength, dismayed and put to shame. They are like grass in the field, like tender green shoots, like grass sprouting on the roof, scorched before it can grow.
[2 Kings] [19]:[27] But I know when you sit and when you go out and when you come in, and how you rage against me.
[2 Kings] [19]:[28] Because you rage against me and your arrogance has reached my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth, and I will make you return by the way you came.
[2 Kings] [19]:[29] "And this will be the sign for you: This year you will eat what grows by itself, and the second year what springs from that. But in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
[2 Kings] [19]:[30] Once more the surviving remnant of the house of Judah will take root below and bear fruit above.
[2 Kings] [19]:[31] For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go forth, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will accomplish this.
[2 Kings] [19]:[32] Therefore this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: "He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow here. He will not come before it with a shield or build a siege ramp against it.
[2 Kings] [19]:[33] By the way he came he will return; he will not enter this city, declares the LORD.
[2 Kings] [19]:[34] I will defend this city and save it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant."
[2 Kings] [19]:[35] That night the angel of the LORD went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the Assyrian camp. When men rose early in the morning, there they were—all of them dead bodies.
[2 Kings] [19]:[36] So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.
[2 Kings] [19]:[37] While he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer cut him down with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son became king in his place.
[2 Kings] [20]:[1] In those days Hezekiah fell mortally ill. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, "This is what the LORD says: Put your house in order, for you are going to die; you will not recover."
[2 Kings] [20]:[2] Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD:
[2 Kings] [20]:[3] "Please, LORD, remember how I have walked before you faithfully and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in your eyes." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
[2 Kings] [20]:[4] Isaiah had not yet gone out of the middle court when the word of the LORD came to him:
[2 Kings] [20]:[5] "Go back and say to Hezekiah, the leader of my people: This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. I am going to heal you; on the third day you will go up to the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [20]:[6] I will add fifteen years to your life, and I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria. I will defend this city for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David."
[2 Kings] [20]:[7] Then Isaiah said, "Bring a cake of figs." They brought it and applied it to the boil, and he recovered.
[2 Kings] [20]:[8] Hezekiah had asked Isaiah, "What will be the sign that the LORD will heal me and that I will go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?"
[2 Kings] [20]:[9] Isaiah answered, "This is the sign for you from the LORD that the LORD will do what he has promised: shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or shall it go back ten steps?"
[2 Kings] [20]:[10] Hezekiah said, "It is a small thing for the shadow to move forward ten steps. No, let it go back ten steps."
[2 Kings] [20]:[11] Then the prophet Isaiah called out to the LORD, and he made the shadow go back the ten steps it had gone down on the stairway of Ahaz.
[2 Kings] [20]:[12] At that time Berodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been ill.
[2 Kings] [20]:[13] Hezekiah listened to them and showed them his entire treasury—the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine oil, his armory, and everything found among his treasures. There was nothing in his palace or in all his realm that he did not show them.
[2 Kings] [20]:[14] Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and asked him, "What did those men say, and where did they come from?" "They came from a distant land," Hezekiah said, "from Babylon."
[2 Kings] [20]:[15] "What did they see in your palace?" the prophet asked. "They saw everything in my palace," Hezekiah said. "There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them."
[2 Kings] [20]:[16] Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD:
[2 Kings] [20]:[17] The days are coming when everything in your palace, and all that your fathers have stored up until this day, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
[2 Kings] [20]:[18] And some of your own sons, who will come from you, whom you yourself will father, will be taken away to serve as eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
[2 Kings] [20]:[19] Hezekiah answered, "The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good." For he thought, "Will there not be peace and security in my lifetime?"
[2 Kings] [20]:[20] The rest of the acts of Hezekiah, all his achievements, and how he made the pool and the conduit and brought water into the city, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
[2 Kings] [20]:[21] Hezekiah rested with his fathers, and his son Manasseh succeeded him as king.
[2 Kings] [21]:[1] Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hephzibah.
[2 Kings] [21]:[2] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, following the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
[2 Kings] [21]:[3] He rebuilt the high places his father Hezekiah had destroyed, raised altars to Baal, and made an Asherah pole, just as Ahab king of Israel had done. He bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.
[2 Kings] [21]:[4] He built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, "In Jerusalem I will put my name."
[2 Kings] [21]:[5] He built altars to all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [21]:[6] He made his own son pass through the fire, practiced sorcery and divination, and dealt with mediums and spiritists. He did much evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger.
[2 Kings] [21]:[7] He placed the carved image of Asherah that he had made in the house of which the LORD had said to David and to his son Solomon, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.
[2 Kings] [21]:[8] I will never again make the feet of Israel wander from the land I gave to their fathers—if only they will be careful to do everything I have commanded them and keep the whole law that my servant Moses gave them."
[2 Kings] [21]:[9] But they did not listen. Manasseh led them astray, so that they did more evil than the nations the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites.
[2 Kings] [21]:[10] So the LORD spoke through his servants the prophets:
[2 Kings] [21]:[11] "Because Manasseh king of Judah has committed these detestable acts—doing more evil than the Amorites who were before him—and has led Judah into sin with his idols,
[2 Kings] [21]:[12] this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Look, I am bringing such disaster on Jerusalem and Judah that the ears of everyone who hears of it will ring.
[2 Kings] [21]:[13] I will stretch out over Jerusalem the measuring line I used on Samaria and the plumb line I used on the house of Ahab. I will wipe out Jerusalem as one wipes a dish, wiping it clean and turning it upside down.
[2 Kings] [21]:[14] I will abandon the remnant of my inheritance and hand them over to their enemies; they will become plunder and spoil for all their enemies,
[2 Kings] [21]:[15] because they have done what is evil in my eyes and have provoked me to anger from the day their fathers came out of Egypt until this day."
[2 Kings] [21]:[16] Manasseh also shed so much innocent blood that he filled Jerusalem from end to end—besides the sin by which he led Judah to do what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [21]:[17] As for the rest of the acts of Manasseh, all that he did and the sin he committed, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
[2 Kings] [21]:[18] Manasseh rested with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his palace, the garden of Uzza. His son Amon succeeded him as king.
[2 Kings] [21]:[19] Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz, from Jotbah.
[2 Kings] [21]:[20] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done.
[2 Kings] [21]:[21] He walked in all the ways of his father, serving the idols his father had served and bowing down to them.
[2 Kings] [21]:[22] He forsook the LORD, the God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [21]:[23] Then Amon's officials conspired against him and killed the king in his own house.
[2 Kings] [21]:[24] But the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king in his place.
[2 Kings] [21]:[25] As for the rest of the acts of Amon and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
[2 Kings] [21]:[26] He was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and his son Josiah succeeded him as king.
[2 Kings] [22]:[1] Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jedidah daughter of Adaiah, from Bozkath.
[2 Kings] [22]:[2] He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and walked in all the ways of his father David, turning aside neither to the right nor to the left.
[2 Kings] [22]:[3] In the eighteenth year of his reign, King Josiah sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, the secretary, to the house of the LORD with these orders:
[2 Kings] [22]:[4] "Go up to Hilkiah the high priest and have him count the money that has been brought into the house of the LORD, which the doorkeepers have collected from the people.
[2 Kings] [22]:[5] Let it be handed over to the supervisors appointed over the house of the LORD, and let them pay it out to those working on the house of the LORD, to repair its damage—
[2 Kings] [22]:[6] to the carpenters, the builders, and the masons, and for buying timber and quarried stone to repair the house.
[2 Kings] [22]:[7] But no accounting is to be required of them for the money handed over to them, because they deal honestly."
[2 Kings] [22]:[8] Then Hilkiah the high priest said to Shaphan the secretary, "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD." Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it.
[2 Kings] [22]:[9] Shaphan the secretary went to the king and reported to him: "Your servants have emptied out the money that was found in the house and handed it over to the workmen appointed to oversee the house of the LORD."
[2 Kings] [22]:[10] Then Shaphan the secretary told the king, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." And Shaphan read it aloud before the king.
[2 Kings] [22]:[11] When the king heard the words of the Book of the Law, he tore his clothes.
[2 Kings] [22]:[12] He gave this command to Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, Shaphan the secretary, and Asaiah the king's servant:
[2 Kings] [22]:[13] "Go and inquire of the LORD for me, for the people, and for all Judah about the words of this book that has been found. Great is the wrath of the LORD that burns against us, because our fathers did not obey the words of this book by doing all that is written concerning us."
[2 Kings] [22]:[14] So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem, in the Second District, and they spoke with her.
[2 Kings] [22]:[15] She said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the man who sent you to me:
[2 Kings] [22]:[16] This is what the LORD says: I am about to bring disaster on this place and on its inhabitants—everything written in the book that the king of Judah has read—
[2 Kings] [22]:[17] because they have abandoned me and burned incense to other gods, provoking me to anger with all the work of their hands. My wrath burns against this place, and it will not be quenched.
[2 Kings] [22]:[18] But tell the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the LORD: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning the words you have heard:
[2 Kings] [22]:[19] Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I spoke against this place and its inhabitants—that they would become a desolation and a curse—and because you tore your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you, declares the LORD.
[2 Kings] [22]:[20] Therefore I will gather you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace. Your eyes will not see all the disaster I am going to bring on this place." So they brought back word to the king.
[2 Kings] [23]:[1] Then the king sent word, and they gathered to him all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
[2 Kings] [23]:[2] The king went up to the house of the LORD, and with him every man of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests and the prophets, and all the people, from the least to the greatest. And he read in their hearing every word of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [23]:[3] The king stood by the pillar and made the covenant before the LORD: to follow the LORD and keep his commandments, his testimonies, and his statutes with all his heart and all his soul, carrying out the words of this covenant written in this book. And all the people joined in the covenant.
[2 Kings] [23]:[4] Then the king ordered Hilkiah the high priest, the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the threshold to remove from the temple of the LORD all the vessels made for Baal, for Asherah, and for all the host of heaven. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron and carried their ashes to Bethel.
[2 Kings] [23]:[5] He deposed the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense at the high places in the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, along with those who burned incense to Baal, to the sun and the moon, to the constellations, and to all the host of heaven.
[2 Kings] [23]:[6] He brought the Asherah pole out of the house of the LORD to the Kidron Valley outside Jerusalem, burned it there, ground it to dust, and threw its dust on the graves of the common people.
[2 Kings] [23]:[7] He tore down the quarters of the male cult prostitutes that were in the house of the LORD, where the women wove hangings for Asherah.
[2 Kings] [23]:[8] He brought all the priests in from the cities of Judah and defiled the high places where the priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba. He tore down the high places at the gates—the one at the entrance of the gate of Joshua, the governor of the city, on the left as one enters the city gate.
[2 Kings] [23]:[9] However, the priests of the high places did not come up to the altar of the LORD in Jerusalem; they only ate unleavened bread among their brothers.
[2 Kings] [23]:[10] He defiled Topheth in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, so that no one could make his son or daughter pass through the fire to Molech.
[2 Kings] [23]:[11] He removed the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun at the entrance to the house of the LORD, near the chamber of Nathan-melech the official, which was in the precincts; and he burned the chariots of the sun with fire.
[2 Kings] [23]:[12] The king tore down the altars on the roof of the upper chamber of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah had made, and the altars Manasseh had made in the two courts of the house of the LORD. He smashed them there and threw their rubble into the Kidron Valley.
[2 Kings] [23]:[13] The king also defiled the high places east of Jerusalem, south of the Mount of Corruption, which Solomon king of Israel had built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Sidonians, for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, and for Milcom the detestable god of the Ammonites.
[2 Kings] [23]:[14] He shattered the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and filled their places with human bones.
[2 Kings] [23]:[15] He also tore down the altar at Bethel—the high place made by Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel into sin—that altar and that high place. He burned the high place, ground it to dust, and burned the Asherah pole.
[2 Kings] [23]:[16] Then Josiah turned and saw the tombs there on the hill. He sent men to take the bones from the tombs, and he burned them on the altar and defiled it, in keeping with the word of the LORD proclaimed by the man of God who had foretold these things.
[2 Kings] [23]:[17] He asked, "What is that monument I see?" The men of the city told him, "It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and foretold these very things you have done to the altar at Bethel."
[2 Kings] [23]:[18] "Leave it alone," he said. "Let no one disturb his bones." So they spared his bones, along with the bones of the prophet who had come from Samaria.
[2 Kings] [23]:[19] Josiah also removed all the shrines at the high places in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had built to provoke the LORD to anger, and he did to them just as he had done at Bethel.
[2 Kings] [23]:[20] He slaughtered on the altars all the priests of the high places who were there, and burned human bones on them. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
[2 Kings] [23]:[21] The king commanded all the people: "Keep the Passover to the LORD your God, as it is written in this Book of the Covenant."
[2 Kings] [23]:[22] No such Passover had been kept since the days of the judges who ruled Israel, nor throughout all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.
[2 Kings] [23]:[23] But in the eighteenth year of King Josiah this Passover was kept to the LORD in Jerusalem.
[2 Kings] [23]:[24] Josiah also swept away the mediums and spiritists, the household gods, the idols, and all the detestable things that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, in order to fulfill the words of the law written in the book that Hilkiah the priest had found in the house of the LORD.
[2 Kings] [23]:[25] Before him there was no king like him, who turned to the LORD with all his heart, with all his soul, and with all his strength, according to all the law of Moses; nor did any like him arise after him.
[2 Kings] [23]:[26] Even so, the LORD did not turn from the fierce heat of his great anger, which burned against Judah because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked him.
[2 Kings] [23]:[27] The LORD said, "I will remove Judah also from my presence, as I removed Israel. I will reject this city Jerusalem, which I chose, and the house of which I said, 'My Name shall be there.'"
[2 Kings] [23]:[28] As for the rest of the acts of Josiah, and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
[2 Kings] [23]:[29] In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt marched up to the king of Assyria at the Euphrates River. King Josiah went out to meet him, and Neco killed him at Megiddo as soon as he saw him.
[2 Kings] [23]:[30] His servants carried his body in a chariot from Megiddo, brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own tomb. Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him, and made him king in place of his father.
[2 Kings] [23]:[31] Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
[2 Kings] [23]:[32] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his fathers had done.
[2 Kings] [23]:[33] Pharaoh Neco imprisoned him at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so that he could not reign in Jerusalem, and imposed on the land a fine of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
[2 Kings] [23]:[34] Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of his father Josiah, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But he took Jehoahaz away to Egypt, and there he died.
[2 Kings] [23]:[35] Jehoiakim paid the silver and gold to Pharaoh, but he taxed the land to raise the money Pharaoh demanded. He exacted the silver and gold from the people of the land, each according to his assessment, to give it to Pharaoh Neco.
[2 Kings] [23]:[36] Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zebidah daughter of Pedaiah, from Rumah.
[2 Kings] [23]:[37] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his fathers had done.
[2 Kings] [24]:[1] During his reign Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon invaded the land, and Jehoiakim was his vassal for three years. Then he turned and rebelled against him.
[2 Kings] [24]:[2] The LORD sent raiding bands against him—Chaldeans, Arameans, Moabites, and Ammonites. He sent them against Judah to destroy it, in keeping with the word the LORD had spoken through his servants the prophets.
[2 Kings] [24]:[3] Surely this came upon Judah at the LORD's command, to remove them from his presence because of the sins of Manasseh and all that he had done,
[2 Kings] [24]:[4] and also because of the innocent blood he had shed—he had filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the LORD was not willing to forgive.
[2 Kings] [24]:[5] As for the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and all that he did—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
[2 Kings] [24]:[6] Jehoiakim rested with his fathers, and his son Jehoiachin became king in his place.
[2 Kings] [24]:[7] The king of Egypt did not march out from his own land again, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to him, from the Wadi of Egypt to the Euphrates River.
[2 Kings] [24]:[8] Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. His mother's name was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan, from Jerusalem.
[2 Kings] [24]:[9] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father had done.
[2 Kings] [24]:[10] At that time the officers of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against Jerusalem and laid siege to the city.
[2 Kings] [24]:[11] Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon himself came against the city while his officers had it under siege.
[2 Kings] [24]:[12] Jehoiachin king of Judah surrendered to the king of Babylon, along with his mother, his servants, his officials, and his court attendants. The king of Babylon took him captive in the eighth year of his own reign.
[2 Kings] [24]:[13] He carried off from there all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the royal palace, and he stripped away all the gold objects that Solomon king of Israel had made for the temple of the LORD—just as the LORD had said.
[2 Kings] [24]:[14] He carried all Jerusalem into exile: all the officials and all the fighting men, ten thousand captives in all, and every craftsman and metalworker. No one was left except the poorest people of the land.
[2 Kings] [24]:[15] He deported Jehoiachin to Babylon, along with the king's mother, the king's wives, his court attendants, and the leading men of the land; he led them into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon.
[2 Kings] [24]:[16] The king of Babylon also brought into exile in Babylon all seven thousand fighting men and a thousand craftsmen and metalworkers—all of them strong and fit for war.
[2 Kings] [24]:[17] The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
[2 Kings] [24]:[18] Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eleven years. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
[2 Kings] [24]:[19] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.
[2 Kings] [24]:[20] It was because of the LORD's anger that all this happened to Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them out of his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
[2 Kings] [25]:[1] In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with his whole army against Jerusalem. He laid siege to it and built siege works all around it.
[2 Kings] [25]:[2] The city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
[2 Kings] [25]:[3] By the ninth day of the month the famine in the city had become so severe that there was no food for the people of the land.
[2 Kings] [25]:[4] Then the city wall was breached. All the soldiers fled by night through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden, though the Chaldeans surrounded the city, and the king went toward the Arabah.
[2 Kings] [25]:[5] But the Chaldean army pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and his whole army was scattered from him.
[2 Kings] [25]:[6] They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where sentence was passed on him.
[2 Kings] [25]:[7] They slaughtered Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, then put out his eyes, bound him in bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon.
[2 Kings] [25]:[8] On the seventh day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard and servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
[2 Kings] [25]:[9] He burned down the house of the LORD, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem; every great house he burned with fire.
[2 Kings] [25]:[10] And the whole Chaldean army under the commander of the guard tore down the walls surrounding Jerusalem.
[2 Kings] [25]:[11] Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard carried into exile the rest of the people who were left in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.
[2 Kings] [25]:[12] But the commander of the guard left behind some of the poorest of the land to work the vineyards and the fields.
[2 Kings] [25]:[13] The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars of the house of the LORD, along with the stands and the bronze Sea that were in the house of the LORD, and carried the bronze to Babylon.
[2 Kings] [25]:[14] They also took the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the dishes, and all the bronze articles used in the temple service.
[2 Kings] [25]:[15] The commander of the guard took the firepans and the basins, everything made of gold and everything made of silver.
[2 Kings] [25]:[16] The bronze from the two pillars, the Sea, and the stands, which Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, was too heavy to be weighed.
[2 Kings] [25]:[17] Each pillar was eighteen cubits high. The bronze capital on top of it was three cubits high, with a network and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze. The second pillar, with its network, was the same.
[2 Kings] [25]:[18] The commander of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank, and the three doorkeepers.
[2 Kings] [25]:[19] From the city he took a court official who was in charge of the fighting men, five of the king's personal advisers who were found in the city, the secretary of the army commander who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
[2 Kings] [25]:[20] Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard took them all and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
[2 Kings] [25]:[21] There at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death. So Judah was carried away from its land.
[2 Kings] [25]:[22] Over the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left behind, he appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan.
[2 Kings] [25]:[23] When all the army commanders and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, they came to him at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, together with their men.
[2 Kings] [25]:[24] Gedaliah gave them and their men his oath: "Do not be afraid of the Chaldean officials. Settle down in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you."
[2 Kings] [25]:[25] But in the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, who was of royal blood, came with ten men and struck Gedaliah down, killing him along with the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
[2 Kings] [25]:[26] Then all the people, from the least to the greatest, together with the army commanders, set out and fled to Egypt, for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.
[2 Kings] [25]:[27] In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, released Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison.
[2 Kings] [25]:[28] He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat of honor above those of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
[2 Kings] [25]:[29] So Jehoiachin put aside his prison clothes and for the rest of his life ate regularly at the king's table.
[2 Kings] [25]:[30] Day by day the king gave him a regular allowance as long as he lived.

[1 Chronicles] [1]:[45] When Jobab died, Husham, from the land of the Temanites, reigned in his place.

[1 Chronicles] [2]:[3] The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, and Shelah. These three were born to him by Bath-shua the Canaanite. Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the LORD's sight, and the LORD put him to death.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[4] Tamar, his daughter-in-law, bore him Perez and Zerah. Judah had five sons in all.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[5] The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[6] The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara—five in all.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[7] The son of Carmi: Achar, who brought trouble on Israel by taking what was devoted to destruction.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[8] The son of Ethan: Azariah.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[9] The sons born to Hezron: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[10] Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, the leader of the people of Judah.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[11] Nahshon fathered Salma, and Salma fathered Boaz.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[12] Boaz fathered Obed, and Obed fathered Jesse.

[1 Chronicles] [2]:[14] Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[15] Ozem the sixth, and David the seventh.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[16] Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel—three.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[17] Abigail bore Amasa, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[18] Caleb son of Hezron had children by Azubah his wife, and by Jerioth. These were Azubah's sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[19] When Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, and she bore him Hur.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[20] Hur fathered Uri, and Uri fathered Bezalel.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[21] Later Hezron married the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead, when he was sixty years old, and she bore him Segub.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[22] Segub fathered Jair, who had twenty-three towns in the land of Gilead.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[23] But Geshur and Aram captured the settlements of Jair from them, along with Kenath and its surrounding villages—sixty towns. All these were descendants of Machir, the father of Gilead.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[24] After Hezron died in Caleb Ephrathah, his wife Abijah bore him Ashhur, the father of Tekoa.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[25] The sons of Jerahmeel, Hezron's firstborn: Ram his firstborn, then Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[26] Jerahmeel had another wife, whose name was Atarah; she was the mother of Onam.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[27] The sons of Ram, Jerahmeel's firstborn: Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[28] The sons of Onam: Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[29] Abishur's wife was named Abihail, and she bore him Ahban and Molid.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[30] The sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim. Seled died without children.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[31] The son of Appaim: Ishi. The son of Ishi: Sheshan. The son of Sheshan: Ahlai.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[32] The sons of Jada, Shammai's brother: Jether and Jonathan. Jether died without children.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[33] The sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were the descendants of Jerahmeel.
[1 Chronicles] [2]:[34] Now Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. He had an Egyptian servant named Jarha,

[1 Chronicles] [4]:[8] Koz fathered Anub and Zobebah, and the clans of Aharhel son of Harum.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[9] Jabez was more honored than his brothers. His mother had named him Jabez, saying, "I gave birth to him in pain."[^1] [^1]: The name Jabez echoes the Hebrew word for pain or sorrow.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[10] Jabez called on the God of Israel: "Oh, that you would bless me indeed and enlarge my territory, that your hand would be with me, and that you would keep me from harm, so that I suffer no pain." And God granted what he asked.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[11] Chelub, the brother of Shuhah, fathered Mehir, who was the father of Eshton.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[12] Eshton fathered Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of Ir-nahash. These were the men of Recah.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[13] The sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah. The sons of Othniel: Hathath.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[14] Meonothai fathered Ophrah, and Seraiah fathered Joab, the father of Ge-harashim,[^1] so called because its people were craftsmen. [^1]: Ge-harashim means "Valley of Craftsmen."
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[15] The sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh: Iru, Elah, and Naam. The sons of Elah: Kenaz.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[16] The sons of Jehallelel: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[17] The sons of Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. And she conceived and bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[18] Mered's Judahite wife bore Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. These were the sons of Bithiah, Pharaoh's daughter, whom Mered had married.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[19] The sons of Hodiah's wife, the sister of Naham: the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[20] The sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon. The sons of Ishi: Zoheth and Ben-zoheth.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[21] The sons of Shelah son of Judah: Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the clans of the linen workers' guild at Beth-ashbea;
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[22] also Jokim, the men of Cozeba, and Joash and Saraph, who ruled in Moab, and Jashubi-lehem. These are ancient records.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[23] They were the potters who lived at Netaim and Gederah; they lived there in the king's service.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[24] The sons of Simeon: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul;
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[25] Shallum was his son, Mibsam his son, Mishma his son.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[26] The descendants of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimei his son.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[27] Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers did not have many sons, so their whole clan did not become as numerous as the people of Judah.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[28] They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual,
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[29] Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[30] Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[31] Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susim, Beth-biri, and Shaaraim. These were their towns until David became king.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[32] Their villages were Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan—five towns—
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[33] together with all the villages around these towns as far as Baal. These were their settlements, and they kept a genealogical record.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[34] Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[35] Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah, the son of Seraiah, the son of Asiel,
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[36] Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[37] and Ziza son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah, the son of Shimri, the son of Shemaiah—
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[38] these are the men listed by name, leaders in their clans; and their families increased greatly.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[39] They went to the entrance of Gedor, to the east side of the valley, to look for pasture for their flocks.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[40] They found rich, good pasture, and the land was broad, quiet, and peaceful, for the people who had lived there before were Hamites.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[41] These men, recorded by name, came in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah and attacked their tents and the Meunites who were found there. They destroyed them completely, and so it remains to this day, and they settled in their place, because there was pasture for their flocks.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[42] Five hundred of these Simeonites went to Mount Seir, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.
[1 Chronicles] [4]:[43] They struck down the remnant of the Amalekites who had survived, and they have lived there to this day.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[1] The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel—he was indeed the firstborn, but when he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel, so that he is not enrolled in the genealogy as the firstborn.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[2] For Judah grew strong among his brothers, and a ruler came from him, yet the birthright belonged to Joseph.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[3] The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[4] The descendants of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[5] Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[6] Beerah his son, whom Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria carried into exile. He was a chief of the Reubenites.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[7] His kinsmen, by their clans, as they were enrolled in the genealogy of their generations: Jeiel the chief, Zechariah,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[8] and Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel. He lived in Aroer and as far as Nebo and Baal-meon,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[9] and eastward he settled as far as the edge of the wilderness that reaches from the Euphrates River, for their livestock had increased greatly in the land of Gilead.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[10] In the days of Saul they went to war against the Hagrites, who fell by their hand, and they settled in their tents throughout the whole region east of Gilead.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[11] The sons of Gad lived opposite them in the land of Bashan as far as Salecah:
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[12] Joel the chief, Shapham the second, then Janai and Shaphat in Bashan.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[13] Their kinsmen, by their fathers' houses, were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber—seven in all.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[14] These were the sons of Abihail son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz;
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[15] Ahi son of Abdiel, son of Guni, was head of their fathers' houses.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[16] They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its villages, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon to their farthest limits.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[17] All of them were enrolled by genealogy in the days of Jotham king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[18] The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had valiant men who carried shield and sword and drew the bow, trained for battle: forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty ready for military service.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[19] They waged war against the Hagrites, and against Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[20] They were given help against them, and the Hagrites and all their allies were handed over to them, for they cried out to God in the battle, and he answered their plea because they trusted in him.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[21] They carried off the livestock of the Hagrites: fifty thousand camels, two hundred fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys, and a hundred thousand captives.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[22] Many fell slain, because the battle was God's. And they lived in their place until the exile.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[23] The people of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon; they were numerous.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[24] These were the heads of their fathers' houses: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel—mighty warriors, men of renown, heads of their fathers' houses.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[25] But they were unfaithful to the God of their fathers and prostituted themselves to the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[26] So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria and the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried them away—the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh—bringing them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river Gozan, where they remain to this day.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[27] The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[28] The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[29] The children of Amram: Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[30] Eleazar fathered Phinehas, Phinehas fathered Abishua,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[31] Abishua fathered Bukki, Bukki fathered Uzzi,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[32] Uzzi fathered Zerahiah, Zerahiah fathered Meraioth,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[33] Meraioth fathered Amariah, Amariah fathered Ahitub,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[34] Ahitub fathered Zadok, Zadok fathered Ahimaaz,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[35] Ahimaaz fathered Azariah, Azariah fathered Johanan,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[36] and Johanan fathered Azariah—he was the one who served as priest in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[37] Azariah fathered Amariah, Amariah fathered Ahitub,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[38] Ahitub fathered Zadok, Zadok fathered Shallum,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[39] Shallum fathered Hilkiah, Hilkiah fathered Azariah,
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[40] Azariah fathered Seraiah, and Seraiah fathered Jehozadak.
[1 Chronicles] [5]:[41] Jehozadak went into exile when the LORD carried Judah and Jerusalem away into exile by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[1] The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[2] These are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[3] The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[4] The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of the Levites, listed by their fathers.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[5] Of Gershom: Libni his son, Jahath his son, Zimmah his son,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[6] Joah his son, Iddo his son, Zerah his son, Jeatherai his son.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[7] The sons of Kohath: Amminadab his son, Korah his son, Assir his son,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[8] Elkanah his son, Ebiasaph his son, Assir his son,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[9] Tahath his son, Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, and Shaul his son.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[10] The sons of Elkanah: Amasai and Ahimoth.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[11] As for Elkanah, the sons of Elkanah were Zophai his son, Nahath his son,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[12] Eliab his son, Jeroham his son, Elkanah his son.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[13] The sons of Samuel: Joel the firstborn, and Abijah the second. [Footnote: The Hebrew here reads "the firstborn, Vashni, and Abijah"; the name Joel is supplied from other lists of Samuel's sons, and "Vashni" is understood as "and the second."]
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[14] The sons of Merari: Mahli, Libni his son, Shimei his son, Uzzah his son,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[15] Shimea his son, Haggiah his son, Asaiah his son.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[16] These are the men whom David put in charge of the music in the house of the LORD, after the ark came to rest there.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[17] They ministered with music before the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, and they carried out their service according to the order laid down for them.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[18] These are the men who served, together with their sons. From the Kohathites: Heman the singer, the son of Joel, the son of Samuel,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[19] the son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Eliel, the son of Toah,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[20] the son of Zuph, the son of Elkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[21] the son of Elkanah, the son of Joel, the son of Azariah, the son of Zephaniah,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[22] the son of Tahath, the son of Assir, the son of Ebiasaph, the son of Korah,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[23] the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[24] His brother Asaph, who stood at his right hand: Asaph the son of Berechiah, the son of Shimea,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[25] the son of Michael, the son of Baaseiah, the son of Malchijah,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[26] the son of Ethni, the son of Zerah, the son of Adaiah,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[27] the son of Ethan, the son of Zimmah, the son of Shimei,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[28] the son of Jahath, the son of Gershom, the son of Levi.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[29] On the left stood their kinsmen, the sons of Merari: Ethan the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[30] the son of Hashabiah, the son of Amaziah, the son of Hilkiah,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[31] the son of Amzi, the son of Bani, the son of Shemer,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[32] the son of Mahli, the son of Mushi, the son of Merari, the son of Levi.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[33] Their kinsmen the Levites were assigned to all the other service of the tabernacle, the house of God.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[34] But Aaron and his sons made the offerings on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense, doing all the work of the Most Holy Place and making atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[35] These are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[36] Bukki his son, Uzzi his son, Zerahiah his son,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[37] Meraioth his son, Amariah his son, Ahitub his son,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[38] Zadok his son, Ahimaaz his son.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[39] These are their dwelling places, the settlements within their territories. To the sons of Aaron, of the clan of the Kohathites, since the lot fell to them,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[40] they gave Hebron in the land of Judah, with the pasturelands around it.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[41] But the open country of the city and its villages they gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[42] To the sons of Aaron they gave the cities of refuge: Hebron, Libnah with its pasturelands, Jattir, Eshtemoa with its pasturelands,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[43] Hilez with its pasturelands, Debir with its pasturelands,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[44] Ashan with its pasturelands, and Beth-shemesh with its pasturelands.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[45] From the tribe of Benjamin: Geba with its pasturelands, Alemeth with its pasturelands, and Anathoth with its pasturelands. In all, their cities numbered thirteen, distributed among their clans.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[46] To the rest of the Kohathites were given by lot ten cities from the clans of the half-tribe of Manasseh.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[47] To the sons of Gershom, clan by clan, were given thirteen cities from the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali, and the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[48] To the sons of Merari, clan by clan, were allotted twelve cities from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the tribe of Zebulun.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[49] So the Israelites gave the Levites these cities with their pasturelands.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[50] From the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin they assigned by lot the cities named above.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[51] Some of the clans of the Kohathites received the cities of their territory from the tribe of Ephraim.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[52] They were given the cities of refuge: Shechem with its pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, Gezer with its pasturelands,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[53] Jokmeam with its pasturelands, Beth-horon with its pasturelands,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[54] Aijalon with its pasturelands, and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[55] From the half-tribe of Manasseh: Aner with its pasturelands and Bileam with its pasturelands—these for the rest of the clans of the Kohathites.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[56] To the sons of Gershom were given, from the clan of the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands and Ashtaroth with its pasturelands;
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[57] from the tribe of Issachar: Kedesh with its pasturelands, Daberath with its pasturelands,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[58] Ramoth with its pasturelands, and Anem with its pasturelands;
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[59] from the tribe of Asher: Mashal with its pasturelands, Abdon with its pasturelands,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[60] Hukok with its pasturelands, and Rehob with its pasturelands;
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[61] and from the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee with its pasturelands, Hammon with its pasturelands, and Kiriathaim with its pasturelands.
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[62] To the rest of the Merarites were given, from the tribe of Zebulun: Rimmono with its pasturelands and Tabor with its pasturelands;
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[63] and beyond the Jordan at Jericho, on the east side of the Jordan, from the tribe of Reuben: Bezer in the wilderness with its pasturelands, Jahzah with its pasturelands,
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[64] Kedemoth with its pasturelands, and Mephaath with its pasturelands;
[1 Chronicles] [6]:[65] and from the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead with its pasturelands, Mahanaim with its pasturelands,
