[1 Chronicles] [7]:[1] The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron — four in all.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[2] The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Samuel — heads of their fathers' houses. Of the line of Tola they were mighty warriors in their generations; in the days of David their number was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[3] The son of Uzzi: Izrahiah. The sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah — five, all of them chiefs.* [*Footnote: Only four names are listed here; the total of five may include Izrahiah himself.]
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[4] Along with them, by their generations and by their fathers' houses, were fighting units of the army, thirty-six thousand strong, for they had many wives and sons.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[5] Their kinsmen among all the clans of Issachar were mighty warriors, eighty-seven thousand in all, as recorded in their genealogies.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[6] The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael — three.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[7] The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri — five, heads of their fathers' houses, mighty warriors. Their genealogical record numbered twenty-two thousand thirty-four.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[8] The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth — all of these were the sons of Becher.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[9] Their genealogical record, by their generations, listed the heads of their fathers' houses, mighty warriors: twenty thousand two hundred.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[10] The son of Jediael: Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[11] All these were the sons of Jediael, listed as heads of their fathers' houses, mighty warriors — seventeen thousand two hundred ready to march out to war.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[12] Shuppim and Huppim were the sons of Ir; Hushim was the son of Aher.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[13] The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum — the descendants of Bilhah.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[14] The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his Aramean concubine bore; she also bore Machir, the father of Gilead.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[15] Machir took a wife from among the Huppites and Shuppites;* his sister's name was Maacah. The name of the second was Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had only daughters. [*Footnote: Or "Machir took a wife for Huppim and for Shuppim."]
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[16] Maacah, Machir's wife, bore a son and named him Peresh; his brother was named Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[17] The son of Ulam: Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[18] His sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[19] The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[20] The descendants of Ephraim: Shuthelah, Bered his son, Tahath his son, Eleadah his son, Tahath his son,
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[21] Zabad his son, Shuthelah his son, and also Ezer and Elead, whom the men of Gath, born in that land, killed, for they had gone down to seize their livestock.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[22] Their father Ephraim mourned for many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[23] Then he went in to his wife, and she conceived and bore a son. He named him Beriah,* because disaster had struck his house. [*Footnote: The name Beriah sounds like the Hebrew phrase meaning "in misfortune."]
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[24] His daughter was Sheerah, who built Lower and Upper Beth-horon, as well as Uzzen-sheerah.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[25] Rephah was his son, and Resheph; Telah his son, Tahan his son,
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[26] Ladan his son, Ammihud his son, Elishama his son,
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[27] Nun his son, Joshua his son.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[28] Their holdings and settlements were Bethel and its villages, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its villages to the west, and Shechem and its villages as far as Ayyah and its villages.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[29] Along the borders of the Manassites lay Beth-shean and its villages, Taanach and its villages, Megiddo and its villages, and Dor and its villages. In these the descendants of Joseph, the son of Israel, made their home.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[30] The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, with their sister Serah.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[31] The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[32] Heber fathered Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham, and their sister Shua.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[33] The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were the sons of Japhlet.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[34] The sons of Shemer: Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[35] The sons of his brother Helem: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[36] The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[37] Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[38] The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispah, and Ara.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[39] The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
[1 Chronicles] [7]:[40] All these were the descendants of Asher, heads of their fathers' houses, chosen men, mighty warriors, and chief among the leaders. The number enrolled for service in war was twenty-six thousand men.

[1 Chronicles] [8]:[29] In Gibeon lived Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, whose wife's name was Maacah.[^1] [^1]: The name Jeiel is supplied from the parallel list later in this book; the Hebrew here reads simply "the father of Gibeon."
[1 Chronicles] [8]:[30] His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
[1 Chronicles] [8]:[31] Gedor, Ahio, and Zecher.
[1 Chronicles] [8]:[32] Mikloth fathered Shimeah. These also lived opposite their kinsmen in Jerusalem, along with their kinsmen.
[1 Chronicles] [8]:[33] Ner fathered Kish, Kish fathered Saul, and Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.[^1] [^1]: Eshbaal is called Ish-bosheth in the books of Samuel.
[1 Chronicles] [8]:[34] The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal fathered Micah.[^1] [^1]: Merib-baal is called Mephibosheth in the books of Samuel.
[1 Chronicles] [8]:[35] The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
[1 Chronicles] [8]:[36] Ahaz fathered Jehoaddah; Jehoaddah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri fathered Moza.
[1 Chronicles] [8]:[37] Moza fathered Binea; Raphah was his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
[1 Chronicles] [8]:[38] Azel had six sons, and these are their names: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were the sons of Azel.
[1 Chronicles] [8]:[39] The sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam his firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.
[1 Chronicles] [8]:[40] The sons of Ulam were mighty warriors, archers who drew the bow, and they had many sons and grandsons, one hundred and fifty in all. All these were among the sons of Benjamin.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[1] So all Israel was registered by genealogy, and these are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel. And Judah was carried away into exile to Babylon because of their unfaithfulness.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[2] The first to resettle on their own property in their own towns were Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[3] In Jerusalem there lived some of the descendants of Judah, of Benjamin, and of Ephraim and Manasseh:
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[4] Uthai son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani, from the descendants of Perez son of Judah.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[5] From the Shilonites: Asaiah the firstborn, and his sons.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[6] From the descendants of Zerah: Jeuel. Their kinsmen numbered 690.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[7] From the descendants of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah;
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[8] Ibneiah son of Jeroham; Elah son of Uzzi, son of Michri; and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[9] Their kinsmen, according to their genealogies, numbered 956. All these men were heads of their ancestral houses.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[10] From the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin;
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[11] and Azariah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the chief officer of the house of God;
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[12] Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah; and Maasai son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[13] Their kinsmen, heads of their ancestral houses, numbered 1,760 — capable men, skilled in the work of the service of the house of God.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[14] From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, of the descendants of Merari;
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[15] Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zichri, son of Asaph;
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[16] Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[17] The gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, and Ahiman; their kinsman Shallum was the chief.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[18] To this day he is stationed at the King's Gate on the east side. These were the gatekeepers belonging to the camps of the Levites.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[19] Shallum son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his kinsmen of his ancestral house, the Korahites, were in charge of the work of the service, guarding the thresholds of the tent, just as their fathers had guarded the entrance to the camp of the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[20] In earlier times Phinehas son of Eleazar was the chief officer over them, and the LORD was with him.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[21] Zechariah son of Meshelemiah was the gatekeeper at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[22] All those chosen as gatekeepers at the thresholds numbered 212. They were registered by genealogy in their villages. David and Samuel the seer had appointed them to their trusted office.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[23] So they and their sons were in charge of the gates of the house of the LORD, the house of the tent, keeping watch.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[24] The gatekeepers were stationed on all four sides — east, west, north, and south.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[25] Their kinsmen in their villages had to come in from time to time to serve with them for seven-day terms,
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[26] for the four chief gatekeepers, who were Levites, held a position of trust and were in charge of the chambers and the treasuries of the house of God.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[27] They spent the night around the house of God, because the watch was their responsibility, and they had charge of the key to open it morning by morning.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[28] Some of them were in charge of the utensils used in the service; they counted them when they brought them in and when they took them out.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[29] Others were appointed over the furnishings and all the holy vessels, and over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the frankincense, and the spices.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[30] Some of the priests' sons prepared the mixture of the spices.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[31] Mattithiah, one of the Levites, the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was entrusted with baking the flat cakes.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[32] And some of their kinsmen, the Kohathites, were in charge of preparing the bread of the Presence every Sabbath.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[33] These were the singers, heads of Levite families, living in the temple chambers and free from other duties, because they were on duty day and night.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[34] These were the heads of the Levite families, chiefs according to their genealogies, and they lived in Jerusalem.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[35] Jeiel the father of Gibeon lived in Gibeon; his wife's name was Maacah.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[36] His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[37] Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[38] Mikloth was the father of Shimeam. They too lived near their kinsmen in Jerusalem, along with their relatives.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[39] Ner was the father of Kish, Kish the father of Saul, and Saul the father of Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[40] The son of Jonathan was Merib-baal, and Merib-baal was the father of Micah.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[41] The sons of Micah were Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz. [Footnote: The Hebrew text here lists only three sons; the name Ahaz is supplied from the parallel list in chapter 8 and from ancient versions, since verse 42 continues with Ahaz.]
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[42] Ahaz was the father of Jarah; Jarah was the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; and Zimri was the father of Moza.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[43] Moza was the father of Binea; Rephaiah was his son, Eleasah his son, and Azel his son.
[1 Chronicles] [9]:[44] Azel had six sons, and these were their names: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[1] Now the Philistines fought against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before them and fell slain on Mount Gilboa.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[2] The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and they struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[3] The fighting closed in on Saul; the archers found him, and he was gravely wounded by them.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[4] Then Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through, or these uncircumcised men will come and abuse me." But his armor-bearer would not; he was terrified. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[5] When the armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his sword and died.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[6] So Saul died with his three sons, and all his household perished together.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[7] When all the Israelites in the valley saw that their men had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and fled. Then the Philistines came and settled in them.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[8] The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[9] They stripped him, carried off his head and his armor, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news to their idols and to the people.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[10] They put his armor in the temple of their gods and fastened his skull in the temple of Dagon.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[11] When all the people of Jabesh Gilead heard everything the Philistines had done to Saul,
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[12] all their brave men set out, took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons, and brought them to Jabesh. They buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh, and they fasted seven days.
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[13] So Saul died for his unfaithfulness to the LORD: he did not keep the word of the LORD, and he even consulted a medium for guidance,
[1 Chronicles] [10]:[14] instead of seeking guidance from the LORD. So the LORD put him to death and turned the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[1] Then all Israel gathered to David at Hebron and said, "Look, we are your own flesh and blood.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[2] Even in the past, while Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out and brought them home. And the LORD your God said to you, 'You shall shepherd my people Israel, and you shall be ruler over my people Israel.'"
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[3] So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them at Hebron before the LORD. Then they anointed David king over Israel, as the LORD had spoken through Samuel.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[4] David and all Israel marched to Jerusalem, that is, Jebus, where the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, were living.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[5] The people of Jebus said to David, "You will never get in here." But David captured the stronghold of Zion, that is, the City of David.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[6] David had said, "Whoever strikes down a Jebusite first shall become chief and commander." Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, and so he became chief.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[7] David took up residence in the stronghold; that is why it was called the City of David.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[8] He built up the city all around, from the Millo to the surrounding wall, and Joab restored the rest of the city.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[9] And David grew greater and greater, for the LORD of hosts was with him.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[10] These are the chiefs of David's mighty men, who together with all Israel gave his kingship strong support to make him king, as the LORD had promised concerning Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[11] This is the list of David's mighty men: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of the officers. He wielded his spear against three hundred men, killing them in a single encounter.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[12] Next to him was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[13] He was with David at Pas Dammim when the Philistines gathered there for battle. There was a plot of ground full of barley, and the troops fled before the Philistines.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[14] But they took their stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck the Philistines down; and the LORD brought about a great victory.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[15] Three of the thirty chiefs went down to David at the rock, to the cave of Adullam, while a Philistine army was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[16] At that time David was in the stronghold, and a Philistine garrison was at Bethlehem.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[17] David was seized with longing and said, "If only someone would give me a drink of water from the well by the gate of Bethlehem!"
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[18] So the three broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well by the gate of Bethlehem, and carried it back to David. But David refused to drink it; instead he poured it out to the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[19] "God forbid that I should do such a thing!" he said. "Shall I drink the blood of these men who went at the risk of their lives? For they brought it at the risk of their lives." And he would not drink it. Such were the deeds of the three mighty men.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[20] Abishai the brother of Joab was chief of the three. He wielded his spear against three hundred men and killed them, and he won a name alongside the three.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[21] Of the second group of three he was the most honored, and he became their commander, though he never equaled the first three.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[22] Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a valiant fighter from Kabzeel, a man of many exploits. He struck down the two mightiest warriors of Moab, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[23] He also struck down an Egyptian, a man about seven and a half feet tall. The Egyptian had a spear like a weaver's beam in his hand, but Benaiah went against him with a club. He wrenched the spear out of the Egyptian's hand and killed him with that very spear.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[24] Such were the deeds of Benaiah son of Jehoiada; he too won a name alongside the three mighty men.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[25] He was held in greater honor than any of the thirty, but he was not counted among the three. And David put him in charge of his bodyguard.
[1 Chronicles] [11]:[26] The mighty warriors were: Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,

[1 Chronicles] [12]:[1] These are the men who came to David at Ziklag, while he was still confined because of Saul son of Kish. They were among the mighty men who helped him in battle,
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[2] armed with bows and able to shoot arrows or sling stones with either the right hand or the left. They were kinsmen of Saul, from Benjamin.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[3] Ahiezer was their chief, then Joash, both sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth; Berachah; Jehu of Anathoth;
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[4] Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty and over the thirty;
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[5] Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, Jozabad of Gederah;

[1 Chronicles] [12]:[7] Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites;
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[8] and Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham of Gedor.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[9] From the Gadites there went over to David at the stronghold in the wilderness mighty warriors, men trained for war, who could handle shield and spear. Their faces were like the faces of lions, and they were as swift as gazelles on the mountains.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[10] Ezer was the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[11] Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[12] Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[13] Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[14] Jeremiah the tenth, Machbannai the eleventh.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[15] These were the commanders of the army from the sons of Gad; the least of them was a match for a hundred, and the greatest for a thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[16] These were the men who crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it was overflowing all its banks, and they drove off everyone living in the valleys, both east and west.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[17] Some of the men of Benjamin and Judah also came to David at the stronghold.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[18] David went out to meet them and said to them, "If you have come to me in peace, to help me, my heart will be joined to yours. But if you have come to betray me to my enemies, though there is no wrong in my hands, may the God of our fathers see it and judge."
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[19] Then the Spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the thirty, and he said: "We are yours, David! We are with you, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to those who help you, for your God helps you." So David received them and made them officers over his troops.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[20] Some men of Manasseh also went over to David when he marched with the Philistines against Saul—though they did not help the Philistines, for the Philistine rulers, after taking counsel, sent David away, saying, "He may go over to his master Saul at the cost of our heads."
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[21] As he was going to Ziklag, these men of Manasseh went over to him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, chiefs of thousands in Manasseh.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[22] They helped David against the raiding bands, for they were all mighty warriors, and they became commanders in his army.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[23] Day after day men kept coming to David to help him, until there was a great army, like the army of God.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[24] These are the numbers of the armed troops who came to David at Hebron to turn the kingdom of Saul over to him, as the LORD had said:
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[25] From Judah, bearing shield and spear: 6,800 armed for war.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[26] From Simeon, mighty warriors ready for battle: 7,100.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[27] From Levi: 4,600,
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[28] along with Jehoiada, leader of the house of Aaron, and with him 3,700,
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[29] and Zadok, a young man and a mighty warrior, with twenty-two commanders from his father's house.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[30] From Benjamin, the kinsmen of Saul: 3,000; until then most of them had remained loyal to the house of Saul.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[31] From Ephraim: 20,800 mighty warriors, men of renown in their clans.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[32] From the half-tribe of Manasseh: 18,000, designated by name to come and make David king.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[33] From Issachar, men who understood the times and knew what Israel should do: 200 chiefs, with all their kinsmen under their command.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[34] From Zebulun: 50,000 seasoned troops, equipped for battle with every kind of weapon, ready to help with undivided loyalty.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[35] From Naphtali: 1,000 officers, and with them 37,000 men with shield and spear.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[36] From Dan: 28,600 men ready for battle.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[37] From Asher: 40,000 seasoned troops, prepared for battle.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[38] And from beyond the Jordan, from Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh: 120,000 men armed with every kind of weapon of war.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[39] All these were fighting men who could hold their place in the ranks. They came to Hebron with a whole heart to make David king over all Israel, and all the rest of Israel were of one mind to make David king.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[40] They spent three days there with David, eating and drinking, for their kinsmen had provided for them.
[1 Chronicles] [12]:[41] Their neighbors as well, from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought food on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen: flour, cakes of figs, clusters of raisins, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep in abundance—for there was joy in Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[1] David consulted with the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with every leader.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[2] Then David said to the whole assembly of Israel, "If it seems good to you, and if it is the will of the LORD our God, let us send word far and wide to the rest of our brothers in all the territories of Israel, and also to the priests and Levites in the cities where they have their pasturelands, that they should gather to us,
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[3] and let us bring back the ark of our God, for we did not seek it in the days of Saul."
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[4] The whole assembly agreed to do this, for the plan seemed right in the eyes of all the people.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[5] So David assembled all Israel, from the Shihor Brook in Egypt to Lebo Hamath, to bring the ark of God up from Kiriath Jearim.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[6] David and all Israel went up to Baalah, that is, to Kiriath Jearim in Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, the LORD who is enthroned above the cherubim, the ark that bears his name.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[7] They moved the ark of God from the house of Abinadab on a new cart, with Uzzah and Ahio guiding it.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[8] David and all Israel were celebrating before God with all their strength, with songs and lyres and harps, with tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[9] When they came to the threshing floor of Kidon, Uzzah reached out his hand to steady the ark, because the oxen had stumbled.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[10] Then the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and he struck him down because he had put out his hand to the ark, and he died there before God.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[11] David was angry because the LORD had broken out against Uzzah, so he named that place Perez Uzzah, and it is called that to this day.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[12] David was afraid of God that day, and he said, "How can I ever bring the ark of God home to me?"
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[13] So David did not take the ark with him to the City of David, but had it turned aside to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.
[1 Chronicles] [13]:[14] The ark of God remained with the household of Obed-Edom in his house for three months, and the LORD blessed the house of Obed-Edom and all that he had.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[1] Huram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar logs, masons, and carpenters to build him a palace.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[2] So David knew that the LORD had established him as king over Israel, for his kingdom was highly exalted for the sake of his people Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[3] In Jerusalem David took more wives, and he fathered more sons and daughters.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[4] These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[5] Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet,
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[6] Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[7] Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[8] When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, they all marched up to search him out. David heard of it and went out to face them.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[9] The Philistines came and raided the Valley of Rephaim.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[10] So David inquired of God, "Shall I attack the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?" The LORD answered him, "Attack. I will hand them over to you."
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[11] So they went up to Baal-perazim, and there David struck them down. David said, "God has broken through my enemies by my hand like a bursting flood." That is why they named the place Baal-perazim, which means "the lord of breakthroughs."
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[12] The Philistines had abandoned their gods there, and at David's command they were burned in the fire.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[13] Once again the Philistines raided the valley.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[14] David inquired of God again, and God told him, "Do not go up after them. Circle around them and come at them in front of the balsam trees.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[15] As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, go out to battle, for God has gone out ahead of you to strike down the Philistine army."
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[16] David did as God commanded him, and they struck down the Philistine army from Gibeon all the way to Gezer.
[1 Chronicles] [14]:[17] So David's fame spread through every land, and the LORD put the dread of David on all the nations.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[1] David built houses for himself in the City of David, and he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[2] Then David said, "No one is to carry the ark of God except the Levites, for the LORD chose them to carry the ark of the LORD and to serve him forever."
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[3] David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the LORD to the place he had prepared for it.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[4] David gathered together the sons of Aaron and the Levites:
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[5] of the sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief and one hundred twenty of his relatives;
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[6] of the sons of Merari, Asaiah the chief and two hundred twenty of his relatives;
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[7] of the sons of Gershom, Joel the chief and one hundred thirty of his relatives;
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[8] of the sons of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief and two hundred of his relatives;
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[9] of the sons of Hebron, Eliel the chief and eighty of his relatives;
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[10] of the sons of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief and one hundred twelve of his relatives.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[11] Then David summoned the priests Zadok and Abiathar, and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[12] He said to them, "You are the heads of the Levite families. Consecrate yourselves, you and your relatives, so that you may bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel, to the place I have prepared for it.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[13] Because you were not there the first time, the LORD our God broke out against us, for we did not seek him according to the ordinance."
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[14] So the priests and the Levites consecrated themselves to bring up the ark of the LORD, the God of Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[15] And the Levites carried the ark of God on their shoulders with the poles, as Moses had commanded according to the word of the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[16] David told the chiefs of the Levites to appoint their relatives as singers, to sound aloud with instruments of music—harps, lyres, and cymbals—lifting their voices in joy.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[17] So the Levites appointed Heman son of Joel; from among his relatives, Asaph son of Berechiah; and from the sons of Merari, their relatives, Ethan son of Kushaiah;
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[18] and with them their relatives of the second rank: Zechariah, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, and Obed-Edom and Jeiel, the gatekeepers.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[19] The singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were to sound the bronze cymbals;
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[20] Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah were to play harps set to alamoth;
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[21] and Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were to lead with lyres set to sheminith.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[22] Chenaniah, the chief of the Levites, was in charge of the singing; he directed it, because he was skillful.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[23] Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers for the ark.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[24] Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer, the priests, blew the trumpets before the ark of God. Obed-Edom and Jehiah were also gatekeepers for the ark.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[25] So David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands went with rejoicing to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the house of Obed-Edom.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[26] Because God helped the Levites who were carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[27] David was clothed in a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who were carrying the ark, and the singers, and Chenaniah the director of the singing. David also wore a linen ephod.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[28] So all Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the LORD with shouts, with the sound of the ram's horn, with trumpets and cymbals, and with harps and lyres sounding out.
[1 Chronicles] [15]:[29] As the ark of the covenant of the LORD came to the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul looked down from the window, and when she saw King David dancing and celebrating, she despised him in her heart.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[1] So they brought in the ark of God and set it inside the tent that David had pitched for it, and they offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings before God.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[2] When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the fellowship offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[3] Then he distributed to everyone in Israel, both men and women, a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[4] He appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, to make petition, to give thanks, and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel:
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[5] Asaph was the chief, Zechariah second to him, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, with harps and lyres; and Asaph sounded the cymbals.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[6] The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel were to blow the trumpets regularly before the ark of the covenant of God.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[7] That day David first appointed Asaph and his brothers to give thanks to the LORD in this way:
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[8] Give thanks to the LORD, call on his name; make known among the nations what he has done.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[9] Sing to him, sing praise to him; tell of all his wonderful works.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[10] Glory in his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[11] Look to the LORD and to his strength; seek his face always.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[12] Remember the wonders he has done, his miracles and the judgments he pronounced,
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[13] you offspring of Israel his servant, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[14] He is the LORD our God; his judgments fill the whole earth.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[15] Remember his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[16] the covenant he made with Abraham, the oath he swore to Isaac.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[17] He confirmed it to Jacob as a decree, to Israel as an everlasting covenant:
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[18] "To you I will give the land of Canaan as the portion you inherit."
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[19] When they were few in number, few indeed, and strangers in it,<f>The Hebrew here reads "when you were few in number"; the third person is used to match the surrounding lines.</f>
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[20] wandering from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people,
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[21] he let no one oppress them; for their sake he rebuked kings:
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[22] "Do not touch my anointed ones; do my prophets no harm."
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[23] Sing to the LORD, all the earth; proclaim his salvation day after day.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[24] Declare his glory among the nations, his wonderful deeds among all peoples.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[25] For great is the LORD and most worthy of praise; he is to be feared above all gods.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[26] For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[27] Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and joy are in his dwelling place.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[28] Ascribe to the LORD, you families of the nations, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[29] Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name; bring an offering and come before him. Worship the LORD in the splendor of his holiness.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[30] Tremble before him, all the earth! Surely the world stands firm; it cannot be shaken.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[31] Let the heavens rejoice, let the earth be glad; let them say among the nations, "The LORD reigns!"
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[32] Let the sea resound, and all that fills it; let the fields be jubilant, and everything in them.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[33] Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[34] Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his mercy endures forever.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[35] Cry out, "Save us, God our Savior; gather us and deliver us from the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise."
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[36] Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Then all the people said, "Amen," and "Praise the LORD."
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[37] David left Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to minister before the ark regularly, according to each day's requirements.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[38] He also left Obed-Edom and his sixty-eight associates; Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun, and also Hosah, were gatekeepers.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[39] David left Zadok the priest and his fellow priests before the tabernacle of the LORD at the high place in Gibeon,
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[40] to present burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, in accordance with everything written in the Law of the LORD, which he had commanded Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[41] With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of those chosen and designated by name to give thanks to the LORD, "for his mercy endures forever."
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[42] Heman and Jeduthun were responsible for the trumpets and cymbals and for the other instruments for sacred song. The sons of Jeduthun were stationed at the gate.
[1 Chronicles] [16]:[43] Then all the people left, each for their own home, and David returned home to bless his household.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[1] Once David was settled in his palace, he said to Nathan the prophet, "Here I am, living in a house of cedar, while the ark of the LORD's covenant stays under tent curtains."
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[2] Nathan said to David, "Do whatever is in your heart, for God is with you."
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[3] But that night the word of God came to Nathan:
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[4] "Go and tell David my servant: This is what the LORD says: You are not the one to build me a house to dwell in.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[5] I have never lived in a house from the day I brought Israel up until this day; I have gone from tent to tent, from one dwelling place to another.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[6] Wherever I have journeyed with all Israel, did I ever say a word to any of Israel's judges, whom I commanded to shepherd my people, asking, 'Why have you not built me a house of cedar?'
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[7] Now then, say this to my servant David: This is what the LORD of hosts says: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be ruler over my people Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[8] I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies before you. Now I will make your name like the names of the greatest men on earth.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[9] I will provide a place for my people Israel and plant them there, so that they may dwell in their own home and be disturbed no more. Wicked men will no longer wear them down, as they did at the beginning,
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[10] from the days when I appointed judges over my people Israel. And I will subdue all your enemies. I also declare to you that the LORD will build you a house.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[11] When your days are done and you go to be with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, one of your own sons, and I will establish his kingdom.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[12] He is the one who will build me a house, and I will establish his throne forever.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[13] I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me. I will never withdraw my steadfast love from him, as I withdrew it from the one who came before you.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[14] I will set him firmly in my house and in my kingdom forever; his throne will be established forever."
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[15] Nathan reported to David all these words and this entire vision.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[16] Then King David went in and sat before the LORD, and he said: "Who am I, LORD God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[17] And as if this were not enough in your sight, my God, you have spoken about the future of your servant's house. You have looked on me as though I were the most highly honored of men, LORD God.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[18] What more can David say to you for honoring your servant? For you know your servant.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[19] LORD, for the sake of your servant and according to your own heart, you have done this great thing and made known all these great promises.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[20] LORD, there is no one like you, and there is no God but you, as we have heard with our own ears.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[21] And who is like your people Israel—the one nation on earth whom God went out to redeem as a people for himself, making a name for yourself by great and awesome deeds, driving out nations before your people, whom you redeemed from Egypt?
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[22] You made your people Israel your very own forever, and you, LORD, became their God.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[23] And now, LORD, let the word you have spoken concerning your servant and his house be established forever. Do as you have promised,
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[24] so that it may stand and your name may be magnified forever, and people will say, 'The LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, is God to Israel, and the house of your servant David stands firm before you.'
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[25] You, my God, have revealed to your servant that you will build him a house. That is why your servant has found the courage to pray before you.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[26] And now, LORD, you are God, and you have promised this good thing to your servant.
[1 Chronicles] [17]:[27] Now you have been pleased to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you. For you, LORD, have blessed it, and it is blessed forever."
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[1] Some time later David defeated the Philistines and subdued them, taking Gath and its surrounding villages out of Philistine hands.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[2] He also defeated Moab, and the Moabites became David's subjects and paid him tribute.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[3] David defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah, as far as Hamath, when Hadadezer marched out to establish his power along the Euphrates River.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[4] David captured from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers. He hamstrung all the chariot horses, but kept a hundred chariots for himself.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[5] When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down twenty-two thousand of them.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[6] He stationed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became his subjects and paid him tribute. So the LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[7] David took the gold shields carried by Hadadezer's officers and brought them to Jerusalem.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[8] From Tibhath and Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David took a great quantity of bronze, which Solomon later used to make the bronze Sea, the pillars, and the bronze vessels.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[9] When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the entire army of Hadadezer king of Zobah,
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[10] he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and congratulate him on his victory over Hadadezer, who had been at war with Tou. Hadoram brought all kinds of articles of gold, silver, and bronze.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[11] King David dedicated these to the LORD, along with the silver and gold he had carried off from all the nations—from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines, and the Amalekites.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[12] Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[13] David stationed garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became his subjects. So the LORD gave David victory wherever he went.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[14] David reigned over all Israel, governing his whole people with justice and righteousness.
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[15] Joab son of Zeruiah commanded the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder;
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[16] Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Shavsha was secretary;
[1 Chronicles] [18]:[17] Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Kerethites and Pelethites; and David's sons were the chief officials at the king's side.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[1] Some time later Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son became king in his place.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[2] David said, "I will show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me." So David sent messengers to console him over his father. But when David's servants came to Hanun in the land of the Ammonites to console him,
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[3] the Ammonite commanders said to Hanun, "Do you really think David is honoring your father by sending you men to console you? Haven't his servants come to you to explore the land, to overthrow it, and to spy it out?"
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[4] So Hanun seized David's servants, shaved them, cut their garments in two at the hips, and sent them away.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[5] When word came to David about the men, he sent messengers to meet them, for the men were deeply humiliated. The king said, "Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return."
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[6] When the Ammonites saw that they had made themselves odious to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram Naharaim, Aram Maacah, and Zobah.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[7] They hired thirty-two thousand chariots, along with the king of Maacah and his troops, who came and camped near Medeba. The Ammonites also mustered from their cities and came out to fight.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[8] When David heard of it, he sent Joab out with the whole army of fighting men.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[9] The Ammonites marched out and drew up in battle formation at the entrance to the city, while the kings who had come took up positions by themselves in the open field.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[10] Joab saw that he faced battle lines both in front of him and behind, so he chose some of the best troops in Israel and deployed them against the Arameans.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[11] The rest of the men he put under the command of his brother Abishai, and they were deployed against the Ammonites.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[12] Joab said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you are to come to my rescue; but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will rescue you.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[13] Be strong, and let us fight bravely for our people and for the cities of our God. And may the LORD do what is good in his sight."
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[14] Then Joab and the troops with him advanced to attack the Arameans, and they fled before him.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[15] When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans were fleeing, they too fled before his brother Abishai and withdrew into the city. So Joab returned to Jerusalem.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[16] When the Arameans saw that they had been routed by Israel, they sent messengers and brought out the Arameans from beyond the Euphrates, with Shophach the commander of Hadadezer's army at their head.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[17] When David was told of it, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, advanced against them, and drew up his lines to meet them. David formed his battle line against the Arameans, and they fought against him.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[18] But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed seven thousand of their charioteers and forty thousand foot soldiers. He also killed Shophach the commander of their army.
[1 Chronicles] [19]:[19] When the vassals of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with David and became subject to him. And the Arameans were no longer willing to help the Ammonites.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[1] In the spring of the year, at the time when kings march out to war, Joab led out the armed forces and ravaged the land of the Ammonites. He came and laid siege to Rabbah, while David remained in Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabbah down and destroyed it.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[2] David took the crown from the head of their king. He found that it weighed a talent of gold and was set with a precious stone, and he placed it on his own head. He also carried off a great quantity of plunder from the city. [Footnote: The Hebrew word rendered "their king" (malkam) may also be read as the name of the Ammonite god Milcom.]
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[3] He brought out the people who were in it and set them to labor with saws, iron picks, and axes. David did the same to all the cities of the Ammonites. Then David and all the troops returned to Jerusalem. [Footnote: The Hebrew verb is uncertain; it may also mean that David cut or sawed the captives, that is, subjected them to harsh punishment.]
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[4] Some time later war broke out with the Philistines at Gezer. It was then that Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Sippai, one of the descendants of the Rephaim, and the Philistines were subdued.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[5] There was war with the Philistines again, and Elhanan son of Jair struck down Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[6] There was war at Gath once more. A man of enormous size was there, with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—twenty-four in all. He too was descended from the Rephaim.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[7] When he taunted Israel, Jonathan son of Shimea, David's brother, struck him down.
[1 Chronicles] [20]:[8] These were descendants of the Rephaim in Gath, and they fell at the hands of David and his men.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[1] Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to number Israel.[^1] [^1]: Hebrew *satan* can also mean "an adversary" or "an accuser."
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[2] So David said to Joab and the commanders of the troops, "Go, count Israel from Beersheba to Dan, and bring me the report, so that I may know their number."
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[3] But Joab replied, "May the LORD multiply his people a hundred times over! My lord the king, are they not all my lord's servants? Why should my lord want this? Why should it bring guilt on Israel?"
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[4] But the king's word prevailed over Joab. So Joab set out, went throughout all Israel, and returned to Jerusalem.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[5] Joab gave David the total of the people: in all Israel there were one million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and in Judah four hundred seventy thousand men who drew the sword.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[6] But he did not include Levi and Benjamin in the count, for the king's command was repugnant to him.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[7] This thing was evil in God's sight, so he struck Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[8] Then David said to God, "I have sinned greatly by doing this. Now take away the guilt of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[9] And the LORD spoke to Gad, David's seer:
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[10] "Go and say to David: Thus says the LORD: I am holding out three things to you. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you."
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[11] So Gad came to David and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: Take your choice—
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[12] either three years of famine, or three months of being swept away before your foes while the sword of your enemies overtakes you, or three days of the sword of the LORD—plague in the land, with the angel of the LORD ravaging every part of Israel. Now decide what answer I am to bring back to him who sent me."
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[13] David said to Gad, "I am in deep distress. Let me fall into the hand of the LORD, for his mercy is very great; but do not let me fall into human hands."
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[14] So the LORD sent a plague on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[15] And God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. But as he was destroying, the LORD saw and relented concerning the disaster, and said to the destroying angel, "Enough! Now stay your hand." The angel of the LORD was standing at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[16] David looked up and saw the angel of the LORD standing between earth and heaven, with a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell facedown.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[17] David said to God, "Was it not I who ordered the people to be counted? I am the one who sinned and did this evil. But these sheep—what have they done? LORD my God, let your hand fall on me and on my father's house, but do not let this plague remain on your people."
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[18] Then the angel of the LORD told Gad to say to David that David should go up and build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[19] So David went up at the word Gad had spoken in the name of the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[20] Ornan turned and saw the angel; his four sons who were with him hid themselves. Now Ornan was threshing wheat.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[21] As David approached, Ornan looked up and saw him. He left the threshing floor and bowed before David with his face to the ground.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[22] David said to Ornan, "Give me the site of this threshing floor, so I can build an altar to the LORD on it. Sell it to me for the full price, so that the plague on the people may be stopped."
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[23] Ornan said to David, "Take it. Let my lord the king do whatever seems good to him. See, I give you the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for wood, and the wheat for the grain offering. I give it all."
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[24] But King David said to Ornan, "No, I insist on paying the full price. I will not take for the LORD what is yours, or offer a burnt offering that costs me nothing."
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[25] So David paid Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the site.[^1] [^1]: About 15 pounds or 6.9 kilograms of gold.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[26] David built an altar to the LORD there and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. He called on the LORD, and the LORD answered him with fire from heaven on the altar of burnt offering.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[27] Then the LORD spoke to the angel, and he returned his sword to its sheath.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[28] At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he sacrificed there.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[29] For the tabernacle of the LORD, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering were at that time at the high place in Gibeon.
[1 Chronicles] [21]:[30] But David could not go before it to inquire of God, because he was terrified of the sword of the angel of the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[1] Then David said, "This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel."
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[2] David gave orders to gather the foreigners living in the land of Israel, and he appointed stonecutters to dress stone for building the house of God.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[3] He provided iron in abundance for the nails of the gate doors and for the clamps, and more bronze than could be weighed,
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[4] and cedar logs beyond counting, for the Sidonians and the Tyrians brought David cedar logs in abundance.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[5] David said, "My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD must be exceedingly great, a name and a glory throughout all lands. So I will make preparations for it." And David made abundant preparations before his death.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[6] Then he called for his son Solomon and charged him to build a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[7] David said to Solomon, "My son, it was my own heart's desire to build a house for the name of the LORD my God.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[8] But the word of the LORD came to me: 'You have shed much blood and waged great wars. You shall not build a house for my name, because you have shed so much blood on the earth in my sight.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[9] Look, a son will be born to you who will be a man of rest, and I will give him rest from all his enemies on every side. Solomon will be his name, and I will grant peace and quiet to Israel in his days.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[10] He is the one who will build a house for my name. He will be my son, and I will be his father, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.'
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[11] Now, my son, may the LORD be with you, so that you may succeed and build the house of the LORD your God, as he said you would.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[12] Only may the LORD give you insight and understanding, and may he give you charge over Israel, so that you keep the law of the LORD your God.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[13] Then you will succeed, if you are careful to keep the statutes and judgments that the LORD commanded Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or dismayed.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[14] See, by hard labor I have provided for the house of the LORD a hundred thousand talents of gold and a million talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weighing, for there is so much of it. I have also provided timber and stone, and you may add to them.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[15] You have many workers at your disposal: stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and craftsmen skilled in every kind of work.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[16] Of the gold, the silver, the bronze, and the iron there is no limit. Now rise and do the work, and may the LORD be with you."
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[17] David also commanded all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon:
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[18] "Is not the LORD your God with you? Has he not given you rest on every side? For he has handed the inhabitants of the land over to me, and the land is subdued before the LORD and before his people.
[1 Chronicles] [22]:[19] Now devote your heart and soul to seeking the LORD your God. Rise and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the holy vessels of God may be brought into the house built for the name of the LORD."
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[1] When David was old and full of days, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[2] He gathered together all the leaders of Israel, along with the priests and the Levites.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[3] The Levites thirty years old and older were counted, and the number of men, head by head, was thirty-eight thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[4] Of these, twenty-four thousand were to oversee the work of the house of the LORD, six thousand were officers and judges,
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[5] four thousand were gatekeepers, and four thousand were to praise the LORD with the instruments I have made for praise." [footnote: The sudden first person reflects David's own words, quoted here from his arrangements.]
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[6] David divided them into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[7] Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[8] The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, then Zetham and Joel—three in all.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[9] The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran—three in all. These were the heads of the families of Ladan.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[10] The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These four were the sons of Shimei.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[11] Jahath was the chief and Zizah the second, but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so they were counted as one family with one assignment. [footnote: Zizah is called Zina in the preceding verse; both spellings occur in the Hebrew text.]
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[12] The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel—four in all.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[13] The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart, he and his sons forever, to be consecrated as most holy, to burn incense before the LORD, to minister to him, and to pronounce blessings in his name forever.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[14] As for Moses the man of God, his sons were counted as part of the tribe of Levi.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[15] The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[16] The sons of Gershom: Shebuel was the chief.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[17] The sons of Eliezer: Rehabiah was the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[18] The sons of Izhar: Shelomith was the chief.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[19] The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[20] The sons of Uzziel: Micah the first and Isshiah the second.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[21] The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[22] Eleazar died leaving no sons, only daughters; their cousins, the sons of Kish, married them.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[23] The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth—three in all.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[24] These were the sons of Levi by their families—the heads of families as they were registered, listed by name, head by head—those twenty years old and older who did the work of the service of the house of the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[25] For David had said, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people, and he has come to dwell in Jerusalem forever.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[26] So the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the articles used in its service."
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[27] For by David's final instructions, the sons of Levi were counted from twenty years old and older.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[28] Their duty was to assist the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD: to care for the courts and the side rooms, for the purification of all the holy things, and for the work of the service of the house of God—
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[29] for the bread of the Presence, the fine flour for the grain offering, the wafers of unleavened bread, what is baked on the griddle and what is well mixed with oil, and for all measures of quantity and size.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[30] They were also to stand every morning to thank and praise the LORD, and likewise in the evening,
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[31] and whenever burnt offerings were presented to the LORD on the Sabbaths, at the New Moons, and at the appointed feasts—according to the number prescribed for them, continually before the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [23]:[32] So they were to keep charge of the tent of meeting and of the sanctuary, and to assist their kinsmen the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[1] These were the divisions of the sons of Aaron. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[2] Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and they had no sons, so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[3] With the help of Zadok from the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech from the sons of Ithamar, David divided them into their appointed order of service.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[4] Since the sons of Eleazar had more men at the head of their families than the sons of Ithamar, they were divided accordingly: sixteen heads of ancestral houses from the sons of Eleazar, and eight from the sons of Ithamar.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[5] They divided them by lot, one group with the other, for there were officers of the sanctuary and officers of God among both the sons of Eleazar and the sons of Ithamar.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[6] Shemaiah son of Nethanel, a scribe from the Levites, recorded their names in the presence of the king, the officials, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the priests and the Levites—one ancestral house drawn for Eleazar, and one drawn for Ithamar.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[7] The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[8] the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[9] the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin,
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[10] the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[11] the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[12] the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[13] the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[14] the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[15] the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[16] the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[17] the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[18] the twenty-third to Delaiah, the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[19] This was their appointed order of service when they entered the house of the LORD, according to the rule handed down to them by Aaron their father, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[20] As for the rest of the sons of Levi: from the sons of Amram, Shubael; from the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[21] As for Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah was the first.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[22] From the Izharites, Shelomoth; from the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[23] The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth. [^fn] [^fn]: The Hebrew text here reads simply "and the sons of, Jeriah..."; the name Hebron is supplied from the parallel list of Levite families.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[24] The sons of Uzziel: Micah; from the sons of Micah, Shamir.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[25] The brother of Micah was Isshiah; from the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[26] The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi, and the sons of Jaaziah his son. [^fn] [^fn]: Or "The sons of Jaaziah: Beno"; the Hebrew word beno can be read either as a personal name or as "his son."
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[27] The sons of Merari through Jaaziah his son: Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[28] From Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[29] From Kish: from the sons of Kish, Jerahmeel.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[30] The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites, listed by their ancestral houses.
[1 Chronicles] [24]:[31] They also cast lots, just as their relatives the sons of Aaron had done, in the presence of King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the priests and the Levites—the head of each family treated the same as his youngest brother.
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[1] David and the commanders of the army set apart for service the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, who were to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals. This was the number of the men who did this work according to their service:
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[2] Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, sons of Asaph, under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied at the king's command.
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[3] Of Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah — six in all — under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the lyre, giving thanks and praise to the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[4] Of Heman, the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[5] All these were sons of Heman, the king's seer, according to God's promise to raise up his strength. God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[6] All of them were under the direction of their father for the music in the house of the LORD, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, for the service of the house of God. Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman served under the king's direction.
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[7] Their number, together with their kinsmen trained in singing to the LORD — all of them skilled — was two hundred eighty-eight.
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[8] They cast lots for their duties, small and great alike, teacher along with pupil.
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[9] The first lot fell to Joseph of the family of Asaph; the second to Gedaliah, with his brothers and his sons — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[10] the third to Zaccur, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[11] the fourth to Izri, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[12] the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[13] the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[14] the seventh to Jesarelah, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[15] the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[16] the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[17] the tenth to Shimei, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[18] the eleventh to Azarel, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[19] the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[20] the thirteenth to Shubael, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[21] the fourteenth to Mattithiah, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[22] the fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[23] the sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[24] the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
