[1 Chronicles] [25]:[30] the twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and his brothers — twelve;
[1 Chronicles] [25]:[31] the twenty-fourth to Romamti-ezer, his sons and his brothers — twelve.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[1] The divisions of the gatekeepers: From the Korahites: Meshelemiah son of Kore, one of the sons of Asaph.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[2] Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[3] Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Eliehoenai the seventh.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[4] Obed-edom also had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sachar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[5] Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth—for God had blessed him.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[6] To Shemaiah his son were born sons who ruled over their father's house, for they were men of great ability.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[7] The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad, whose relatives Elihu and Semachiah were capable men as well.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[8] All these were descendants of Obed-edom—they, their sons, and their relatives—men of ability with strength for the work: sixty-two in all belonging to Obed-edom.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[9] Meshelemiah had sons and relatives, capable men—eighteen in all.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[10] Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (though he was not the firstborn, his father made him chief),
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[11] Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth. The sons and relatives of Hosah numbered thirteen in all.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[12] These were the divisions of the gatekeepers: the chief men held guard duties, like their brothers, to serve in the house of the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[13] They cast lots, small and great alike, according to their fathers' houses, for each gate.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[14] The lot for the east fell to Shelemiah. Then lots were cast for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and his lot came out for the north.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[15] To Obed-edom fell the south, and to his sons the storehouse.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[16] To Shuppim and Hosah fell the west, with the Shalleketh Gate on the ascending road—one watch corresponding to another.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[17] On the east there were six Levites each day, on the north four each day, on the south four each day, and at the storehouse two at a time.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[18] At the colonnade on the west there were four at the road and two at the colonnade itself.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[19] These were the divisions of the gatekeepers among the sons of Korah and the sons of Merari.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[20] Among the Levites, Ahijah was in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the holy gifts.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[21] The sons of Ladan, the Gershonites who belonged to Ladan, heads of the families of Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[22] The sons of Jehieli: Zetham and his brother Joel, who were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[23] From the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites:
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[24] Shebuel son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was chief officer over the treasuries.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[25] His relatives through Eliezer: Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, and Shelomoth his son.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[26] This Shelomoth and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the holy gifts dedicated by King David, by the heads of the families, by the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and by the commanders of the army.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[27] They had dedicated part of the spoils of war for the upkeep of the house of the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[28] Everything that Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah had dedicated—all these dedicated gifts were under the care of Shelomoth and his brothers.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[29] Of the Izharites: Chenaniah and his sons were assigned to duties outside the temple, as officials and judges over Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[30] Of the Hebronites: Hashabiah and his relatives—one thousand seven hundred capable men—had charge of the affairs of Israel west of the Jordan, for all the work of the LORD and the service of the king.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[31] Of the Hebronites: Jerijah was chief, according to the genealogies of the Hebronites by their families. In the fortieth year of David's reign a search was made, and men of great ability were found among them at Jazer in Gilead.
[1 Chronicles] [26]:[32] His relatives, capable men, numbered two thousand seven hundred heads of families. King David put them in charge of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh for every matter concerning God and for the affairs of the king.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[1] This is the list of the Israelites—heads of families, commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who served the king in all matters concerning the divisions that came and went month by month throughout the year. Each division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[2] Over the first division, for the first month, was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[3] He was a descendant of Perez and chief of all the army commanders for the first month.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[4] Over the division for the second month was Dodai the Ahohite, with Mikloth as chief officer of his division; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[5] The third army commander, for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, who was chief; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[6] This was the Benaiah who was a mighty man among the Thirty and over the Thirty; his son Ammizabad was in charge of his division.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[7] The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and after him his son Zebadiah; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[8] The fifth, for the fifth month, was the commander Shamhuth the Izrahite; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[9] The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[10] The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, from the descendants of Ephraim; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[11] The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[12] The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer of Anathoth, a Benjaminite; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[13] The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai of Netophah, of the Zerahites; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[14] The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah of Pirathon, from the descendants of Ephraim; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[15] The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai of Netophah, of the family of Othniel; his division numbered twenty-four thousand.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[16] Over the tribes of Israel: for the Reubenites, Eliezer son of Zichri was the chief officer; for the Simeonites, Shephatiah son of Maacah;
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[17] for Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[18] for Judah, Elihu, one of David's brothers; for Issachar, Omri son of Michael;
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[19] for Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel;
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[20] for the Ephraimites, Hoshea son of Azaziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[21] for the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner;
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[22] for Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the officers over the tribes of Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[23] David did not count those twenty years old or younger, because the LORD had promised to make Israel as numerous as the stars of heaven.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[24] Joab son of Zeruiah began the count but did not finish it. Wrath came upon Israel because of this, and the number was not entered in the chronicles of King David.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[25] Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the king's storehouses. Jonathan son of Uzziah was in charge of the storehouses in the countryside, in the towns, the villages, and the watchtowers.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[26] Ezri son of Chelub was in charge of the field workers who tilled the soil.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[27] Shimei of Ramah was in charge of the vineyards; Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the produce of the vineyards for the wine cellars.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[28] Baal-Hanan of Geder was in charge of the olive and sycamore-fig trees in the western foothills; Joash was in charge of the stores of olive oil.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[29] Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the herds grazing in Sharon; Shaphat son of Adlai was in charge of the herds in the valleys.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[30] Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels; Jehdeiah of Meronoth was in charge of the she-donkeys.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[31] Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the flocks. All these were the officials in charge of King David's property.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[32] Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counselor, a man of insight and a scribe. Jehiel son of Hachmoni attended the king's sons.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[33] Ahithophel was the king's counselor, and Hushai the Arkite was the king's friend.
[1 Chronicles] [27]:[34] Ahithophel was succeeded by Jehoiada son of Benaiah and by Abiathar. Joab was the commander of the king's army.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[1] David assembled at Jerusalem all the leaders of Israel: the heads of the tribes, the commanders of the divisions serving the king, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, the stewards of all the property and livestock belonging to the king and his sons, together with the court officials, the mighty men, and all the warriors.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[2] Then King David rose to his feet and said: "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. It was my heart's desire to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the LORD, for the footstool of our God, and I made preparations to build.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[3] But God said to me, 'You shall not build a house for my name, for you are a man of war and have shed blood.'
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[4] Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me out of all my father's house to be king over Israel forever. For he chose Judah as leader, and within the house of Judah, my father's house, and among my father's sons he was pleased to make me king over all Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[5] And of all my sons—for the LORD has given me many sons—he has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[6] He said to me, 'Solomon your son is the one who shall build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[7] I will establish his kingdom forever, if he holds firm in keeping my commandments and my judgments, as he is doing this day.'
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[8] So now, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God: keep and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God, so that you may possess this good land and leave it as an inheritance to your children after you forever.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[9] And you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and a willing mind, for the LORD searches every heart and understands every intention of the thoughts. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[10] See now that the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and act!"
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[11] Then David gave Solomon his son the plan of the vestibule and its buildings, its storehouses, its upper rooms, its inner chambers, and the room for the mercy seat;
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[12] and the plan of all that he had in mind by the Spirit: the courts of the house of the LORD and all the surrounding chambers, the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries for the dedicated gifts;
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[13] the divisions of the priests and the Levites, all the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and all the vessels for the service of the house of the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[14] He assigned the weight of gold for all the gold vessels for each kind of service, and the weight of silver for all the silver vessels for each kind of service:
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[15] the weight of the golden lampstands and their golden lamps, the weight of each lampstand and its lamps; and for the silver lampstands, the weight of each lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand;
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[16] the weight of gold for each table of the showbread, and the silver for the silver tables;
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[17] the forks, the basins, and the pitchers of pure gold; the weight for each golden bowl, and the weight for each silver bowl;
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[18] and the weight of refined gold for the altar of incense. He also gave him the plan for the chariot—the golden cherubim that spread their wings and cover the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[19] "All this," said David, "the LORD made clear to me in writing from his hand—all the work to be done according to the plan."
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[20] Then David said to Solomon his son, "Be strong and courageous, and do the work. Do not be afraid or dismayed, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not fail you or forsake you until all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished.
[1 Chronicles] [28]:[21] See, here are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of the house of God; and with you in all the work will be every willing man skilled in any kind of service, and the officials and all the people are at your command."
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[1] Then King David said to the whole assembly: "My son Solomon, the one whom God has chosen, is young and inexperienced, and the work is great; for this palace is not for man but for the LORD God.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[2] With all my strength I have made provision for the house of my God: gold for the gold work, silver for the silver, bronze for the bronze, iron for the iron, and wood for the wood; also onyx stones and stones for settings, stones of antimony and of many colors, every kind of precious stone, and marble in abundance.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[3] Moreover, because of my delight in the house of my God, I now give for the house of my God my own treasure of gold and silver, over and above all that I have provided for the holy house:
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[4] three thousand talents of gold, gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, for overlaying the walls of the buildings,
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[5] gold for the gold work and silver for the silver, and for all the work to be done by the craftsmen. Now who will offer himself willingly, consecrating himself today to the LORD?"
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[6] Then the leaders of the families, the officers of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials in charge of the king's work gave willingly.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[7] For the service of the house of God they gave five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and a hundred thousand talents of iron.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[8] Whoever had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD, into the care of Jehiel the Gershonite.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[9] The people rejoiced at their willing response, for they had given freely and wholeheartedly to the LORD. King David also rejoiced greatly.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[10] Then David blessed the LORD in the sight of the whole assembly, saying: "Blessed are you, LORD, God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[11] Yours, LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the victory and the majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth is yours. Yours, LORD, is the kingdom, and you are exalted as head over all.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[12] Riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all. In your hand are strength and might, and it is in your power to make great and to give strength to all.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[13] And now, our God, we give you thanks and praise your glorious name.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[14] But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give so willingly as this? For everything comes from you, and from your hand we have given to you.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[15] We are strangers before you, and sojourners, as all our fathers were. Our days on earth are like a shadow, and there is no hope of remaining.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[16] LORD our God, all this abundance that we have provided for building you a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and all of it is yours.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[17] I know, my God, that you test the heart and delight in what is right. With an upright heart I have freely offered all these things, and now I have seen with joy how your people who are here have given willingly to you.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[18] LORD, God of our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, keep this desire in the hearts of your people forever, and direct their hearts to you.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[19] And give my son Solomon a whole heart to keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your statutes, to carry out everything, and to build the palace for which I have made provision."
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[20] Then David said to the whole assembly, "Praise the LORD your God!" And the whole assembly praised the LORD, the God of their fathers, and they bowed their heads and prostrated themselves before the LORD and before the king.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[21] The next day they sacrificed to the LORD and offered burnt offerings to him: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[22] They ate and drank before the LORD that day with great joy. Then they made Solomon son of David king a second time; they anointed him before the LORD as ruler, and Zadok as priest.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[23] So Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king in place of his father David. He prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[24] All the officials and the mighty men, and all the sons of King David as well, pledged their allegiance to King Solomon.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[25] The LORD exalted Solomon greatly in the sight of all Israel and bestowed on him such royal majesty as no king over Israel had ever had before him.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[26] David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[27] He reigned over Israel forty years: seven years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[28] He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor, and his son Solomon reigned in his place.
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[29] The acts of King David, from first to last, are written in the records of Samuel the seer, the records of Nathan the prophet, and the records of Gad the seer,
[1 Chronicles] [29]:[30] together with all the details of his reign and his power, and the events that came upon him and upon Israel and upon all the kingdoms of the other lands.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[1] Solomon son of David established himself firmly over his kingdom, for the LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[2] Solomon spoke to all Israel—to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to every leader in all Israel, the heads of the families.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[3] Then Solomon and the whole assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon, for God's tent of meeting was there, the one Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[4] David, however, had brought up the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[5] But the bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made was there before the tabernacle of the LORD, and Solomon and the assembly sought the LORD there.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[6] Solomon went up to the bronze altar before the LORD at the tent of meeting and offered a thousand burnt offerings on it.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[7] That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what I should give you."
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[8] Solomon answered God, "You showed great faithful love to my father David, and you have made me king in his place.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[9] Now, LORD God, let your promise to my father David be confirmed, for you have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[10] Give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may lead this people, for who can govern this great people of yours?"
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[11] God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for riches, wealth, or honor, nor for the death of your enemies, and because you did not ask for long life, but asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern my people over whom I have made you king—
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[12] wisdom and knowledge are granted to you. And I will also give you riches, wealth, and honor such as no king before you has had and none after you will have."
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[13] So Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, to Jerusalem, and he reigned over Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[14] Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, which he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[15] The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as plentiful as the sycamores of the foothills.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[16] Solomon's horses were imported from Egypt and from Kue; the king's traders acquired them from Kue at the going price. [Footnote: Kue was a region in Cilicia, in what is now southern Turkey, known for its horses.]
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[17] They imported a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty. And through these same traders they were exported to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
[2 Chronicles] [1]:[18] Then Solomon resolved to build a house for the name of the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[1] Solomon conscripted seventy thousand men as burden-bearers and eighty thousand to quarry stone in the hills, with three thousand six hundred to supervise them.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[2] Then Solomon sent word to Huram king of Tyre: "Deal with me as you dealt with my father David, when you sent him cedar to build himself a house to live in.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[3] I am about to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, to consecrate it to him for burning fragrant incense before him, for the regular setting out of the bread, and for burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the appointed feasts of the LORD our God. This is an everlasting ordinance for Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[4] The house I am building will be great, for our God is greater than all gods.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[5] Yet who is able to build him a house, when heaven and the highest heavens cannot contain him? And who am I to build him a house—except as a place to burn incense before him?
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[6] So send me a man skilled in working with gold and silver, bronze and iron, and with purple, crimson, and violet yarn, a man trained in engraving, to work with the skilled craftsmen I have here in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[7] Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants are skilled at cutting the timber of Lebanon. My servants will work alongside yours
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[8] to provide me with timber in abundance, for the house I am building must be great and wonderful.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[9] And for your servants, the woodsmen who cut the timber, I will supply twenty thousand kors of crushed wheat, twenty thousand kors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil."
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[10] Huram king of Tyre answered in a letter that he sent to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you king over them."
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[11] And Huram added: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth! He has given King David a wise son, endowed with insight and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[12] I am sending you Huram-abi, a skilled man of great understanding,
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[13] the son of a woman of the tribe of Dan, his father a man of Tyre. He is trained to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, and in purple, violet, and crimson yarn and in fine linen. He is skilled in every kind of engraving and can carry out any design given to him. He will work with your craftsmen and with those of my lord David, your father.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[14] Now then, let my lord send his servants the wheat and barley, the oil and wine that he spoke of.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[15] We will cut all the timber from Lebanon that you need and float it in rafts by sea to Joppa, and you can haul it up to Jerusalem."
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[16] Solomon took a census of all the foreigners residing in the land of Israel, following the census his father David had taken, and they numbered a hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.
[2 Chronicles] [2]:[17] He assigned seventy thousand of them as burden-bearers, eighty thousand as stonecutters in the hills, and three thousand six hundred as foremen to keep the people at work.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[1] Then Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David, at the place David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[2] He began to build on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[3] These are the foundations Solomon laid for building the house of God: the length, in cubits of the old standard, was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[4] The portico in front, running the full width of the house, measured twenty cubits across, and its height was a hundred and twenty cubits; and he overlaid the inside with pure gold.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[5] The great hall he paneled with cypress wood, overlaid it with fine gold, and decorated it with palm trees and chains.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[6] He adorned the house with precious stones for beauty, and the gold was gold of Parvaim.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[7] He overlaid the house—its beams, thresholds, walls, and doors—with gold, and he carved cherubim on the walls.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[8] He made the Most Holy Place: its length, corresponding to the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits. He overlaid it with six hundred talents of fine gold.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[9] The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He also overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[10] In the Most Holy Place he made two sculptured cherubim and overlaid them with gold.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[11] The total wingspan of the cherubim was twenty cubits: one wing of the first cherub was five cubits and touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, also five cubits, touched the wing of the other cherub.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[12] Likewise one wing of the second cherub was five cubits and touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, five cubits, met the wing of the first cherub.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[13] The wings of these cherubim spread out twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, facing the main hall.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[14] He made the curtain of blue, purple, and crimson yarn and fine linen, and worked cherubim into it.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[15] In front of the house he made two pillars, thirty-five cubits high, each with a capital of five cubits on top.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[16] He made chainwork in the inner sanctuary and placed it on top of the pillars; he made a hundred pomegranates and fastened them into the chains.
[2 Chronicles] [3]:[17] He set up the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and one on the left. The one on the right he named Jachin, and the one on the left Boaz.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[1] He made a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[2] He made the cast metal Sea, ten cubits from rim to rim, perfectly round, five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[3] Beneath it, figures of oxen encircled it all the way around, ten to a cubit, surrounding the Sea on every side. The oxen were in two rows, cast as one piece with the Sea.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[4] It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The Sea rested on top of them, and all their hindquarters were turned inward.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[5] It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was shaped like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held three thousand baths.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[6] He made ten basins, setting five on the right and five on the left, for washing. In them they rinsed what was used for the burnt offering, but the Sea was for the priests to wash in.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[7] He made ten gold lampstands according to the specifications for them, and set them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[8] He made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. He also made a hundred gold bowls.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[9] He made the court of the priests and the great courtyard with its doors, and he overlaid the doors with bronze.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[10] He set the Sea on the south side, at the southeast corner.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[11] Huram also made the pots, the shovels, and the bowls. So Huram finished the work he had undertaken for King Solomon in the house of God:
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[12] the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two networks to cover the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[13] the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, covering the two bowl-shaped capitals on the front of the pillars;
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[14] the stands, and the basins on the stands;
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[15] the one Sea, and the twelve oxen beneath it;
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[16] and the pots, the shovels, the forks, and all their utensils. Huram-abi made all these things of polished bronze for King Solomon, for the house of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[17] The king cast them in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[18] Solomon made all these articles in such great quantity that the weight of the bronze could not be determined.
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[19] Solomon also made all the furnishings for the house of God: the golden altar; the tables on which the bread of the Presence was set;
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[20] the lampstands of pure gold with their lamps, to burn as prescribed in front of the inner sanctuary;
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[21] the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs, all of purest gold;
[2 Chronicles] [4]:[22] the wick trimmers, the bowls, the dishes, and the censers, of pure gold; and the doorway of the temple—its inner doors to the Most Holy Place and the doors of the main hall—overlaid with gold.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[1] So all the work that Solomon did for the house of the LORD was finished. Then Solomon brought in the gifts his father David had dedicated—the silver, the gold, and all the vessels—and placed them in the treasuries of the house of God.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[2] Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral houses of the Israelites, at Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the City of David, that is, Zion.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[3] All the men of Israel gathered to the king at the festival in the seventh month.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[4] When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the Levites took up the ark.

[2 Chronicles] [5]:[7] The priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.

[2 Chronicles] [5]:[9] The poles were so long that their ends could be seen extending from the ark in front of the inner sanctuary, though they were not visible from outside. And there they remain to this day.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[10] There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets that Moses had placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.

[2 Chronicles] [5]:[12] and all the Levitical singers—Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and kinsmen—stood on the east side of the altar, dressed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres, and with them a hundred and twenty priests sounding trumpets.
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[13] The trumpeters and singers joined as one, making a single sound of praise and thanksgiving to the LORD. As they lifted up their voices with trumpets, cymbals, and instruments of music, they praised the LORD: "He is good; his mercy endures forever." Then the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud,
[2 Chronicles] [5]:[14] and the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[1] Then Solomon said: "The LORD has said that he would dwell in thick darkness.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[2] And I have built for you a lofty house, a place for you to dwell in forever."

[2 Chronicles] [6]:[4] He said: "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who with his own mouth spoke to my father David and with his own hand has fulfilled it, saying:
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[5] 'From the day I brought my people out of the land of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house for my name to be there, and I chose no man to be ruler over my people Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[6] But I have chosen Jerusalem for my name to be there, and I have chosen David to be over my people Israel.'
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[7] Now it was in the heart of my father David to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[8] But the LORD said to my father David, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[9] Nevertheless, you are not the one to build the house; your son, who will come from your own body, he shall build the house for my name.'
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[10] Now the LORD has kept the promise he made: I have succeeded my father David and taken my seat on the throne of Israel, just as the LORD promised, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[11] There I have placed the ark, which contains the covenant of the LORD that he made with the people of Israel."
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[12] Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in front of the whole assembly of Israel and spread out his hands.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[13] He had made a bronze platform five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high, and had set it in the middle of the court. He stood on it, knelt down before the whole assembly of Israel, spread out his hands toward heaven,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[14] and said: "LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth, keeping covenant and showing steadfast love to your servants who walk before you with all their heart.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[15] You have kept your promise to your servant, my father David; what you spoke with your mouth you have fulfilled with your hand this very day.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[16] Now therefore, LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant, my father David, what you promised him when you said, 'You shall never fail to have a man to sit before me on the throne of Israel, if only your sons guard their way and walk in my law as you have walked before me.'
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[17] And now, LORD, God of Israel, let your word that you spoke to your servant David be confirmed.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[18] But will God really dwell with man on the earth? Look, the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain you—how much less this house that I have built!
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[19] Yet turn toward the prayer of your servant and his plea for mercy, LORD my God; hear the cry and the prayer that your servant prays before you.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[20] May your eyes be open toward this house day and night, toward the place where you said you would put your name, to hear the prayer that your servant prays toward this place.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[21] Hear the pleas of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from heaven, the place where you dwell—hear and forgive.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[22] If someone sins against his neighbor and is required to swear an oath, and he comes and swears before your altar in this house,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[23] then hear from heaven and act. Judge your servants: condemn the guilty by bringing his conduct down on his own head, and vindicate the righteous by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[24] If your people Israel are defeated before an enemy because they have sinned against you, and they turn back and confess your name and pray and plead with you in this house,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[25] then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave to them and to their fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[26] If the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, and they pray toward this place and confess your name and turn from their sin because you have afflicted them,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[27] then hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel, teaching them the good way in which they should walk, and send rain on your land, which you gave to your people as an inheritance.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[28] When famine or plague comes to the land, or blight or mildew, locusts or grasshoppers, or when their enemies besiege them in any of their cities—whatever disaster or disease may come—
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[29] and when any prayer or plea is made by any person or by all your people Israel, each one knowing his own affliction and pain, and spreading out his hands toward this house,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[30] then hear from heaven, the place where you dwell, and forgive. Deal with each person, whose heart you know, according to all his ways—for you alone know the hearts of all people.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[31] so that they may fear you and walk in your ways all the days they live in the land you gave to our fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[32] And as for the foreigner who does not belong to your people Israel but comes from a distant land because of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm—when he comes and prays toward this house,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[33] then hear from heaven, the place where you dwell, and do whatever the foreigner asks of you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you as your people Israel do, and may know that this house I have built bears your name.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[34] When your people go out to war against their enemies, wherever you send them, and they pray to you toward this city that you have chosen and the house I have built for your name,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[35] then hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[36] When they sin against you—for there is no one who does not sin—and you become angry with them and hand them over to an enemy who takes them captive to a land far or near,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[37] and if they come to their senses in the land of their captivity and repent and plead with you there, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly,'
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[38] and if they turn back to you with all their heart and all their soul in the land of their captivity where they were taken, and pray toward their land that you gave to their fathers, toward the city you have chosen and the house I have built for your name,
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[39] then hear from heaven, the place where you dwell, their prayer and their pleas, and uphold their cause; and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[40] Now, my God, let your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[41] And now arise, LORD God, and come to your resting place, you and the ark of your might. May your priests, LORD God, be clothed with salvation, and may your faithful ones rejoice in what is good.
[2 Chronicles] [6]:[42] LORD God, do not reject your anointed one. Remember your steadfast love for David your servant."
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[1] When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the house.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[2] The priests could not enter the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[3] All the Israelites saw the fire come down and the glory of the LORD upon the house, and they knelt with their faces to the ground on the pavement, worshiped, and gave thanks to the LORD: "He is good; his mercy endures forever."
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[4] Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[5] King Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand cattle and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[6] The priests stood at their posts, and so did the Levites with the instruments for the LORD's music, which King David had made for giving thanks to the LORD—"for his mercy endures forever"—whenever David offered praise through them. Opposite them the priests sounded trumpets, while all Israel stood.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[7] Solomon consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar Solomon had made could not hold the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the fat portions.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[8] At that time Solomon kept the festival for seven days, and all Israel with him—an immense assembly, from Lebo Hamath to the Brook of Egypt.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[9] On the eighth day they held a closing assembly, for they had celebrated the dedication of the altar for seven days and the festival for seven days.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[10] On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, joyful and glad of heart for the goodness the LORD had shown to David, to Solomon, and to his people Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[11] So Solomon finished the house of the LORD and the royal palace. Everything he had set his heart on doing in the house of the LORD and in his own house he carried through successfully.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[12] Then the LORD appeared to Solomon by night and said to him: "I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[13] If I shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, or command the locust to devour the land, or send a plague among my people,
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[14] and if my people, who are called by my name, humble themselves and pray and seek my face and turn from their evil ways, then I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[15] Now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[16] And now I have chosen and consecrated this house, so that my name may be there forever; my eyes and my heart will be there for all time.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[17] As for you, if you walk before me as your father David walked, doing all that I have commanded you, and if you keep my statutes and my judgments,
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[18] then I will establish your royal throne, as I covenanted with your father David when I said, 'You shall never lack a man to rule over Israel.'
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[19] But if you turn away and forsake the statutes and commandments I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and worship them,
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[20] then I will uproot you from my land, which I gave you, and I will cast this house, which I have consecrated for my name, out of my sight, and make it a byword and an object of scorn among all peoples.
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[21] And this house, now so exalted, will appall everyone who passes by, and they will ask, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this house?'
[2 Chronicles] [7]:[22] And the answer will be: 'Because they abandoned the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and embraced other gods, worshiping and serving them. That is why he has brought all this disaster upon them.'"
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[1] At the end of the twenty years during which Solomon had built the house of the LORD and his own palace,
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[2] Solomon rebuilt the towns that Huram had given him, and he settled Israelites in them.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[3] Solomon then marched against Hamath-zobah and overpowered it.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[4] He built Tadmor in the wilderness, along with all the storage towns he built in Hamath.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[5] He built up Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon as fortified cities, with walls, gates, and bars,
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[6] as well as Baalath and all the storage towns that belonged to him, and all the towns for his chariots and for his cavalry—whatever he desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout the land under his rule.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[7] As for all the people who were left of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, who were not Israelites—
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[8] that is, their descendants who remained in the land after them, whom the Israelites had not wiped out—Solomon conscripted them for forced labor, as they are to this day.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[9] But Solomon did not make slaves of any of the Israelites for his work; they were his fighting men, his officers and captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[10] These were King Solomon's chief officials—two hundred fifty of them—who supervised the people.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[11] Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the City of David to the house he had built for her, for he said, "No wife of mine shall live in the house of David king of Israel, because the places the ark of the LORD has entered are holy."
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[12] Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of the LORD that he had built in front of the portico,
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[13] presenting each day's offering as Moses had commanded, for the Sabbaths, the New Moons, and the three annual festivals—the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Booths.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[14] Following the instructions of his father David, he appointed the divisions of the priests for their service and the Levites for their duties, to offer praise and to assist the priests according to each day's requirement, and the gatekeepers by their divisions at the various gates; for this was what David, the man of God, had commanded.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[15] They did not depart from the king's command concerning the priests and the Levites in any matter, including the treasuries.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[16] So all of Solomon's work was carried out, from the day the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid until its completion. The house of the LORD was finished.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[17] Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Eloth on the seacoast in the land of Edom.
[2 Chronicles] [8]:[18] And Huram sent him ships with his own servants, men who knew the sea. They sailed with Solomon's servants to Ophir, took on four hundred fifty talents of gold, and brought it back to King Solomon.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[1] When the queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame, she came to Jerusalem to test him with hard questions. She arrived with a very large retinue, with camels carrying spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones. She came to Solomon and spoke with him about everything on her mind,
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[2] and Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too obscure for him to explain to her.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[3] When the queen of Sheba had seen Solomon's wisdom, the palace he had built,
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[4] the food on his table, the seating of his officials, the attending servants in their robes, his cupbearers in their robes, and the stairway by which he went up to the house of the LORD, it took her breath away.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[5] She said to the king, "The report I heard in my own country about your achievements and your wisdom is true.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[6] I did not believe what they said until I came and saw it with my own eyes. And in fact, I was not told the half of the greatness of your wisdom; you far surpass the report I heard.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[7] How fortunate are your people! How fortunate these servants of yours, who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom!
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[8] Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and set you on his throne as king for the LORD your God. Because your God loves Israel and would establish them forever, he has made you king over them, to administer justice and righteousness."
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[9] Then she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, spices in great abundance, and precious stones. There has never been spice like that which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[10] The servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum wood and precious stones.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[11] The king used the algum wood to make steps for the house of the LORD and for the royal palace, and lyres and harps for the singers. Nothing like them had ever been seen before in the land of Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[12] King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she asked for, besides all that she had brought to the king. Then she departed and returned to her own land with her servants.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[13] The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in a single year was six hundred and sixty-six talents,
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[14] not counting what the traveling merchants and traders brought in. All the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land also brought gold and silver to Solomon.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[15] King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold, six hundred shekels of hammered gold going into each one, [footnote: The Hebrew does not state the unit of weight; "shekels" is supplied.]
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[16] and three hundred small shields of hammered gold, three hundred shekels of gold going into each one. The king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[17] The king also made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[18] The throne had six steps, with a footstool of gold attached to it. On both sides of the seat were armrests, with a lion standing beside each of them,
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[19] and twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like it had ever been made for any kingdom.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[20] All King Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. Silver was reckoned as nothing in the days of Solomon,
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[21] for the king had a fleet of ships that sailed to Tarshish with Huram's servants. Once every three years the ships of Tarshish would return, bringing gold and silver, ivory, apes, and baboons. [footnote: The meaning of the Hebrew word rendered "baboons" is uncertain; it may refer to peacocks.]
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[22] So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[23] All the kings of the earth sought an audience with Solomon, to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[24] Each of them brought a gift: articles of silver and gold, robes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules — year after year.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[25] Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, which he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[26] He ruled over all the kings from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt. [footnote: Hebrew "the River," a standard designation for the Euphrates.]
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[27] The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as plentiful as the sycamore-figs of the foothills.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[28] Horses were imported for Solomon from Egypt and from all other lands.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[29] As for the rest of the acts of Solomon, from beginning to end, are they not written in the records of Nathan the prophet, in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[30] Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.
[2 Chronicles] [9]:[31] Then Solomon rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father, and Rehoboam his son succeeded him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[1] Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[2] When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it—he was in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon—he returned from Egypt.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[3] They sent for him, and Jeroboam came with all Israel and said to Rehoboam:
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[4] "Your father made our yoke harsh. Now lighten the hard labor your father imposed and the heavy yoke he laid on us, and we will serve you."
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[5] He answered them, "Come back to me in three days." So the people went away.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[6] King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. He asked, "How do you advise me to answer this people?"
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[7] They said to him, "If you are good to this people and please them, and speak kindly to them, they will be your servants forever."
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[8] But he rejected the advice the elders gave him and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and who were in his service.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[9] He asked them, "What is your advice? How shall we answer this people who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke your father laid on us'?"
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[10] The young men who had grown up with him replied, "This is what you should say to the people who told you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy; now lighten it for us.' Tell them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.'
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[11] Now, my father laid a heavy yoke on you; I will make it heavier still. My father disciplined you with whips; I will use scorpions."
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[12] Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had ordered when he said, "Come back to me on the third day."
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[13] The king answered them harshly; King Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[14] He spoke to them as the young men had advised: "I will make your yoke heavy; I will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips; I will use scorpions."
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[15] So the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events was from God, to fulfill the word the LORD had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[16] When all Israel saw that the king refused to listen to them, they answered him: "What share do we have in David? What part in the son of Jesse? To your tents, Israel! Look after your own house, David!" And all Israel went home to their tents.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[17] But Rehoboam ruled over the Israelites living in the towns of Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[18] King Rehoboam sent out Hadoram, who was in charge of forced labor, but the Israelites stoned him to death. King Rehoboam barely managed to get into his chariot and escape to Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [10]:[19] So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[1] When Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he mustered the house of Judah and Benjamin—a hundred and eighty thousand picked troops—to fight against Israel and win the kingdom back for himself.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[2] But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, the man of God:
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[3] "Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin:
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[4] Thus says the LORD: You shall not march out and fight against your brothers. Every one of you, go home, for this thing is from me." So they listened to the words of the LORD and turned back from marching against Jeroboam.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[5] Rehoboam settled in Jerusalem and built up cities for defense in Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[6] He built Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[7] Beth Zur, Soco, Adullam,
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[8] Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[9] Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[10] Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron—fortified cities in Judah and Benjamin.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[11] He strengthened the fortresses, appointed commanders over them, and stocked them with stores of food, oil, and wine.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[12] In every city he placed shields and spears, making the cities exceedingly strong. So Judah and Benjamin were his.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[13] The priests and Levites from all their districts throughout Israel sided with him,
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[14] for the Levites left their pasturelands and their holdings and came to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had rejected them from serving as priests of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[15] Jeroboam appointed his own priests for the high places, for the goat idols, and for the calves he had made.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[16] And those from every tribe of Israel who set their hearts on seeking the LORD, the God of Israel, followed the Levites to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[17] So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah and supported Rehoboam son of Solomon for three years, for during those three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[18] Rehoboam took as his wife Mahalath, the daughter of Jerimoth son of David, whose mother was Abihail, the daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[19] She bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[20] After her he took Maacah, the daughter of Absalom, and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[21] Rehoboam loved Maacah, the daughter of Absalom, more than all his other wives and concubines; he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[22] Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as chief prince among his brothers, intending to make him king.
[2 Chronicles] [11]:[23] He acted wisely, dispersing his sons throughout all the territories of Judah and Benjamin, to all the fortified cities, and he gave them abundant provisions and sought many wives for them.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[1] When Rehoboam's rule was firmly established and he had grown strong, he abandoned the law of the LORD, and all Israel with him.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[2] In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt marched against Jerusalem, because they had been unfaithful to the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[3] He came with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen, and troops beyond counting who came with him from Egypt: Libyans, Sukkites, and Cushites.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[4] He captured the fortified cities of Judah and advanced as far as Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[5] Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and to the officials of Judah who had gathered in Jerusalem because of Shishak, and he said to them, "This is what the LORD says: You have abandoned me, so I in turn have abandoned you to the hand of Shishak."
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[6] Then the officials of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is righteous."
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[7] When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them. I will grant them a measure of deliverance, and my wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[8] Yet they will become his servants, so that they may learn the difference between serving me and serving the kingdoms of other lands."
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[9] So Shishak king of Egypt marched against Jerusalem and carried off the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the royal palace. He took everything, including the gold shields that Solomon had made.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[10] King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them and entrusted them to the officers of the guard who kept watch at the entrance of the royal palace.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[11] Whenever the king went to the house of the LORD, the guards would carry the shields, and afterward they would return them to the guardroom.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[12] Because he humbled himself, the LORD's anger turned away from him, and he was not destroyed completely. Indeed, there was still some good in Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[13] King Rehoboam established himself firmly in Jerusalem and continued to reign. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel in which to put his name. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[14] He did what was evil, for he did not set his heart to seek the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[15] The events of Rehoboam's reign, from beginning to end, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, along with the genealogies? There was continual warfare between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.
[2 Chronicles] [12]:[16] Rehoboam rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David, and his son Abijah succeeded him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[1] In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[2] He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel, from Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[3] Abijah went into battle with an army of seasoned warriors, four hundred thousand chosen men, while Jeroboam drew up his lines against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, mighty warriors.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[4] Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim, in the hill country of Ephraim, and called out: "Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel!
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[5] Do you not know that the LORD, the God of Israel, gave the kingship over Israel to David forever—to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[6] Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[7] Worthless men, scoundrels, gathered around him and defied Rehoboam son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and irresolute and could not stand up to them.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[8] And now you intend to stand up against the kingdom of the LORD, which is in the hands of David's sons. You are a vast horde, and you have with you the golden calves that Jeroboam made for you as gods.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[9] Have you not driven out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made your own priests, like the peoples of other lands? Anyone who comes to be ordained with a young bull and seven rams becomes a priest of what are not gods at all.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[10] But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not forsaken him. The priests who serve the LORD are the sons of Aaron, and the Levites do their appointed work.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[11] Morning after morning and evening after evening they offer burnt offerings and fragrant incense to the LORD; they set out the rows of bread on the pure table and tend the lamps of the golden lampstand every evening. We keep the charge of the LORD our God, but you have forsaken him.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[12] See, God himself is with us at our head, and his priests with their trumpets are ready to sound the battle cry against you. Men of Israel, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your fathers, for you cannot succeed."
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[13] Meanwhile Jeroboam had sent troops around to ambush them from the rear, so that his forces were in front of Judah and the ambush behind them.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[14] When Judah turned and saw that they were under attack from both front and rear, they cried out to the LORD, and the priests blew the trumpets.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[15] Then the men of Judah raised the battle cry, and at the sound of their cry God struck down Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[16] The Israelites fled before Judah, and God gave them into the hands of Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[17] Abijah and his troops inflicted a crushing defeat on them: five hundred thousand of Israel's chosen men fell slain.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[18] So the Israelites were subdued at that time, and the men of Judah prevailed, because they relied on the LORD, the God of their fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[19] Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured from him the towns of Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, with their surrounding villages.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[20] Jeroboam never regained his power during the days of Abijah, and the LORD struck him down, and he died.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[21] But Abijah grew strong. He took fourteen wives and had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[22] The rest of Abijah's acts, his ways and his sayings, are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.
[2 Chronicles] [13]:[23] Abijah rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David, and his son Asa became king in his place. In Asa's days the land was at peace for ten years.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[1] Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[2] He removed the foreign altars and the high places, smashed the sacred pillars, and cut down the Asherah poles.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[3] He commanded Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, and to keep the law and the commandment.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[4] He removed the high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Judah, and the kingdom was at peace under him.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[5] He built fortified cities in Judah, for the land was at peace. No one made war against him in those years, because the LORD had given him rest.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[6] He said to Judah, "Let us build up these cities and surround them with walls and towers, with gates and bars. The land is still ours, because we have sought the LORD our God. We sought him, and he has given us rest on every side." So they built, and they prospered.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[7] Asa had an army of three hundred thousand men from Judah, armed with large shields and spears, and two hundred and eighty thousand from Benjamin, carrying small shields and drawing bows. All of them were mighty warriors.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[8] Then Zerah the Cushite marched out against them with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and he advanced as far as Mareshah.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[9] Asa went out to meet him, and they drew up their battle lines in the Valley of Zephathah near Mareshah.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[10] Asa called out to the LORD his God: "LORD, there is no one besides you to help the powerless against the mighty. Help us, LORD our God, for we rely on you, and in your name we have come against this vast horde. LORD, you are our God; do not let mere mortals prevail against you."
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[11] So the LORD struck down the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[12] Asa and the troops with him pursued them as far as Gerar. The Cushites fell until not one of them was left alive, for they were shattered before the LORD and before his army. And they carried off a very great amount of plunder.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[13] They struck down all the cities around Gerar, for the terror of the LORD had fallen on them. They plundered all those cities, for there was much plunder in them.
[2 Chronicles] [14]:[14] They attacked the camps of the herdsmen as well and carried off great numbers of sheep and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[1] The Spirit of God came upon Azariah son of Oded.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[2] He went out to meet Asa and said to him: "Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin: The LORD is with you when you are with him. If you seek him, he will let you find him; but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[3] For a long time Israel was without the true God, without a priest to teach, and without the Law.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[4] But in their distress they turned to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought him, and he let them find him.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[5] In those times there was no safety for anyone coming or going, for great turmoil gripped all the inhabitants of the lands.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[6] Nation was crushed by nation and city by city, for God troubled them with every kind of distress.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[7] But you, be strong; do not let your hands grow slack, for your work will be rewarded."
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[8] When Asa heard these words, the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage. He removed the detestable idols from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the towns he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim, and he restored the altar of the LORD that stood in front of the portico of the LORD's house.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[9] Then he gathered all Judah and Benjamin, along with those from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who were living among them—for great numbers had come over to him from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[10] They assembled at Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[11] That day they sacrificed to the LORD from the plunder they had brought back: seven hundred head of cattle and seven thousand sheep and goats.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[12] They entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and all their soul.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[13] Whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, whether small or great, man or woman.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[14] They swore their oath to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, with trumpets, and with rams' horns.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[15] All Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn it with all their heart and had sought him with wholehearted desire, and he let them find him. And the LORD gave them rest on every side.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[16] King Asa even removed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother, because she had made a repulsive image for Asherah. Asa cut down her image, crushed it, and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[17] The high places were not removed from Israel, yet Asa's heart was fully committed all his days.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[18] He brought into the house of God the silver and gold and the vessels that his father had dedicated and that he himself had dedicated.
[2 Chronicles] [15]:[19] And there was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[1] In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha king of Israel marched against Judah and fortified Ramah to cut off all traffic in and out for Asa king of Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[2] Then Asa took silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the king's house and sent it to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who ruled in Damascus, with this message:
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[3] "Let there be a treaty between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. See, I have sent you silver and gold. Go, break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[4] Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his forces against the cities of Israel. They struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the storage cities of Naphtali.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[5] When Baasha heard of it, he stopped building Ramah and abandoned the work.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[6] Then King Asa took all Judah, and they carried away the stones and timber of Ramah with which Baasha had been building, and with them he fortified Geba and Mizpah.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[7] At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you relied on the king of Aram and not on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped your hand.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[8] Were not the Cushites and the Libyans a mighty army with vast numbers of chariots and horsemen? But when you relied on the LORD, he gave them into your hand.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[9] For the eyes of the LORD range through the whole earth to strengthen those whose hearts are wholly his. In this you have acted foolishly, and from now on you will have wars."
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[10] Asa was angry with the seer and put him in the stocks, for he was enraged at him over this. At that same time Asa also cruelly oppressed some of the people.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[11] The acts of Asa, from first to last, are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[12] In the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa became diseased in his feet, and his illness grew severe. Yet even in his illness he did not seek the LORD, but turned to physicians.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[13] So Asa rested with his fathers; he died in the forty-first year of his reign.
[2 Chronicles] [16]:[14] They buried him in the tomb he had cut out for himself in the city of David. They laid him on a bier filled with spices and all kinds of blended perfumes, and they made an enormous fire in his honor.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[1] Jehoshaphat his son became king in his place, and he grew strong against Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[2] He stationed troops in all the fortified cities of Judah and set garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[3] The LORD was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the earlier ways of his father David and did not seek the Baals.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[4] Instead he sought the God of his father and walked in his commandments, not following the practices of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[5] So the LORD established the kingdom in his hand. All Judah brought tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he had great wealth and honor.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[6] His heart took courage in the ways of the LORD, and he went on to remove the high places and the Asherah poles from Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[7] In the third year of his reign he sent his officials—Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah—to teach in the cities of Judah,
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[8] and with them the Levites Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah; and with them the priests Elishama and Jehoram.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[9] They taught in Judah, having with them the Book of the Law of the LORD. They went around through all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[10] The terror of the LORD was upon all the kingdoms of the lands surrounding Judah, so that they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[11] Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute, and the Arabs brought him flocks: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred goats.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[12] Jehoshaphat kept growing greater and greater. He built fortresses and storage cities in Judah,
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[13] He had much property in the cities of Judah, and in Jerusalem fighting men, mighty warriors.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[14] This was their muster by their fathers' houses: from Judah, commanders of thousands—Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand mighty warriors;
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[15] next to him Jehohanan the commander, and with him two hundred eighty thousand;
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[16] next to him Amasiah son of Zichri, who volunteered himself to the LORD, and with him two hundred thousand mighty warriors.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[17] From Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty warrior, and with him two hundred thousand armed with bow and shield;
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[18] next to him Jehozabad, and with him one hundred eighty thousand equipped for war.
[2 Chronicles] [17]:[19] These were the men who served the king, besides those the king had stationed in the fortified cities throughout Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[1] Jehoshaphat had great riches and honor, and he allied himself with Ahab by marriage.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[2] Some years later he went down to visit Ahab in Samaria, and Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle in abundance for him and for the people who were with him, and he urged him to march against Ramoth-gilead.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[3] Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead?" He answered him, "I am as you are, and my people as your people; we will join you in the battle."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[4] But Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please seek the word of the LORD first."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[5] So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and asked them, "Shall we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I hold back?" They said, "Go up, and God will give it into the king's hand."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[6] But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no other prophet of the LORD here, that we may inquire of him?"
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[7] The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we may inquire of the LORD, but I hate him, because he never prophesies anything good about me, only trouble, all his days. He is Micaiah son of Imlah." Jehoshaphat said, "The king should not say such a thing."
