[2 Chronicles] [18]:[8] So the king of Israel summoned one of his officers and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[9] Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting on their thrones, dressed in their robes, at the threshing floor by the entrance of the gate of Samaria, with all the prophets prophesying before them.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[10] Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had made himself horns of iron, and he declared, "Thus says the LORD: With these you shall gore the Arameans until they are destroyed."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[11] And all the prophets prophesied the same thing: "March up to Ramoth-gilead and triumph; the LORD will give it into the king's hand."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[12] The messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah said to him, "Listen, the prophets are unanimous in speaking favorably to the king. Let your word be like theirs; speak favorably."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[13] But Micaiah said, "As the LORD lives, I will speak whatever my God tells me."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[14] When he came to the king, the king said to him, "Micaiah, shall we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I hold back?" He answered, "Go up and triumph! They will be given into your hand."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[15] The king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear to tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[16] Then Micaiah said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep without a shepherd. And the LORD said, 'These have no master; let each one go home in peace.'"
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[17] The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you? He never prophesies anything good about me, only trouble."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[18] Micaiah went on, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD seated on his throne, with all the host of heaven standing on his right and on his left.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[19] And the LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab king of Israel to march up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' One said this, another said that,
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[20] until a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, 'I will entice him.' The LORD asked him, 'How?'
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[21] He answered, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.' The LORD said, 'You will entice him, and you will succeed. Go and do it.'
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[22] So now the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of these prophets of yours; the LORD has decreed disaster for you."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[23] Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came up and struck Micaiah on the cheek, saying, "Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go when he left me to speak to you?"
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[24] Micaiah answered, "You will find out on the day you go into an inner room to hide."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[25] The king of Israel ordered, "Take Micaiah and hand him over to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son,
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[26] and say, 'Thus says the king: Put this man in prison and feed him a meager ration of bread and water until I return safely.'"
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[27] Micaiah said, "If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me." And he added, "Hear it, all you peoples!"
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[28] So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah marched up to Ramoth-gilead.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[29] The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your royal robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into battle.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[30] Now the king of Aram had ordered his chariot commanders, "Do not fight with anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[31] When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "That is the king of Israel," and they turned to attack him. But Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him; God drew them away from him.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[32] For when the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[33] But someone drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. The king said to his charioteer, "Turn around and get me out of the battle, for I am wounded."
[2 Chronicles] [18]:[34] The fighting raged all that day, and the king of Israel was propped up in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening. At sunset he died.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[1] Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned safely to his house in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[2] Jehu son of Hanani, the seer, went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? Because of this, wrath rests upon you from the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[3] Yet some good is found in you, for you have swept the Asherah poles out of the land and have set your heart to seek God."
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[4] So Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem. Then he went out again among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[5] He appointed judges in the land, in each of the fortified cities of Judah, city by city,
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[6] and he said to the judges, "Consider carefully what you do, for you judge not for man but for the LORD, who is with you when you render judgment.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[7] Now then, let the fear of the LORD be upon you. Be careful in what you do, for with the LORD our God there is no injustice, no partiality, and no taking of bribes."
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[8] In Jerusalem too, Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites, the priests, and the heads of the families of Israel to administer the law of the LORD and to settle disputes. And they returned to Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[9] He charged them: "This is how you are to act: in the fear of the LORD, faithfully, and with a whole heart.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[10] Whenever a case comes before you from your brothers who live in their cities—whether bloodshed or questions of law, commandment, statutes, or ordinances—you are to warn them, so that they do not become guilty before the LORD and wrath come upon you and your brothers. Do this, and you will not incur guilt.
[2 Chronicles] [19]:[11] See, Amariah the chief priest is over you in every matter of the LORD, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, in every matter of the king; and the Levites serve as officers before you. Be strong and act, and may the LORD be with those who do what is right."
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[1] Some time later the Moabites and the Ammonites, together with some of the Meunites, came to make war on Jehoshaphat.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[2] Messengers came and reported to Jehoshaphat: "A vast army is coming against you from beyond the Sea, from Edom. They are already at Hazazon Tamar"—that is, En Gedi.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[3] Jehoshaphat was afraid, and he set himself to seek the LORD; he proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[4] So Judah gathered to seek help from the LORD; from every town of Judah they came to seek him.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[5] Then Jehoshaphat stood up in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, at the house of the LORD, in front of the new courtyard,
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[6] and said: "LORD, God of our fathers, are you not the God who is in heaven? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. Power and might are in your hand, and no one can withstand you.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[7] Our God, did you not drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel and give it forever to the descendants of Abraham your friend?
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[8] They have lived in it and have built you a sanctuary in it for your Name, saying,
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[9] 'If disaster comes upon us—the sword of judgment, or plague, or famine—we will stand before this house and before you, for your Name is in this house. We will cry out to you in our distress, and you will hear and save.'
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[10] But now here are the men of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whose land you would not let Israel invade when they came out of Egypt, so they turned aside from them and did not destroy them.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[11] See how they repay us—coming to drive us out of the possession you gave us as our inheritance.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[12] Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no power to face this vast horde attacking us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you."
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[13] All the men of Judah stood there before the LORD, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[14] Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, as he stood in the assembly.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[15] He said: "Listen, all Judah and you who live in Jerusalem, and you, King Jehoshaphat! This is what the LORD says to you: Do not be afraid or dismayed because of this vast horde, for the battle is not yours, but God's.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[16] Tomorrow march down against them. They will be coming up by the Pass of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the valley, facing the wilderness of Jeruel.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[17] You will not have to fight this battle. Take your positions, stand firm, and see the deliverance the LORD will give you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid, do not be dismayed. Go out to face them tomorrow, and the LORD will be with you."
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[18] Jehoshaphat bowed with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the people of Jerusalem fell down in worship before the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[19] Then the Levites from the Kohathites and the Korahites stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, with a very loud voice.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[20] Early in the morning they set out for the Desert of Tekoa. As they started out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Listen to me, Judah and you who live in Jerusalem! Trust in the LORD your God, and you will stand firm; trust in his prophets, and you will succeed."
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[21] After consulting the people, he appointed men to sing to the LORD and to praise him in the splendor of holiness as they went out ahead of the army, saying: "Give thanks to the LORD, for his mercy endures forever."
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[22] As they began to sing and praise, the LORD set ambushes against the men of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir who were invading Judah, and they were defeated.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[23] The Ammonites and Moabites turned on the men from Mount Seir to destroy and annihilate them; and when they had finished off the men of Seir, they helped to destroy one another.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[24] When the men of Judah came to the place overlooking the wilderness and looked toward the vast army, they saw only corpses lying on the ground; no one had escaped.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[25] So Jehoshaphat and his men went to carry off the plunder, and they found among them a great amount of goods, clothing, and articles of value—more than they could take away. There was so much plunder that it took them three days to collect it.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[26] On the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Berakah, where they praised the LORD. That is why it is called the Valley of Berakah to this day.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[27] Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat at their head, returned joyfully to Jerusalem, for the LORD had given them cause to rejoice over their enemies.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[28] They entered Jerusalem and went to the house of the LORD with harps and lyres and trumpets.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[29] The fear of God came upon all the kingdoms of the surrounding lands when they heard how the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[30] And the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was at peace, for his God had given him rest on every side.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[31] So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem twenty-five years. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[32] He walked in the way of his father Asa and did not turn from it; he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[33] The high places, however, were not removed, and the people still had not set their hearts on the God of their fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[34] The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from beginning to end, are written in the annals of Jehu son of Hanani, which are recorded in the book of the kings of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[35] Later, Jehoshaphat king of Judah made an alliance with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[36] He joined with him to build ships to go to Tarshish, and they built the ships at Ezion-geber.
[2 Chronicles] [20]:[37] Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD will break apart what you have made." So the ships were wrecked and could not sail to Tarshish.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[1] Then Jehoshaphat rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David, and his son Jehoram became king in his place.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[2] He had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael, and Shephatiah. All of these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.[^1] [^1]: Jehoshaphat ruled Judah; here the writer calls him king of Israel, using that name for the whole covenant people.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[3] Their father had given them many gifts of silver and gold and precious things, along with fortified cities in Judah, but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[4] When Jehoram had taken hold of his father's kingdom and made himself secure, he put all his brothers to the sword, and some of the officials of Israel as well.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[5] Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[6] He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for he had married a daughter of Ahab. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[7] Yet the LORD was unwilling to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant he had made with David, and because he had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons forever.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[8] In his days Edom rebelled against the rule of Judah and set up a king of their own.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[9] So Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all his chariots. He rose by night and struck down the Edomites who had surrounded him, along with their chariot commanders.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[10] So Edom has been in rebellion against the rule of Judah to this day. At the same time Libnah also revolted against his rule, because he had forsaken the LORD, the God of his fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[11] He also built high places in the hills of Judah, led the people of Jerusalem into unfaithfulness, and drew Judah astray.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[12] Then a letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, which said: "This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: Because you have not walked in the ways of your father Jehoshaphat or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[13] but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel and have led Judah and the people of Jerusalem into unfaithfulness, just as the house of Ahab led Israel astray, and because you have murdered your own brothers, your father's house, men better than yourself—
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[14] the LORD is about to strike your people, your sons, your wives, and all your possessions with a heavy blow.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[15] And you yourself will suffer a severe illness, a disease of the bowels, until your bowels come out because of the disease, day after day."
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[16] The LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabs who lived near the Cushites.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[17] They came up against Judah, broke into it, and carried off all the possessions found in the king's palace, together with his sons and his wives. Not a son was left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[18] After all this, the LORD struck him with an incurable disease of the bowels.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[19] In the course of time, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of the disease, and he died in terrible agony. His people made no fire in his honor, as they had done for his fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [21]:[20] He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He passed away, to no one's regret, and they buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[1] The people of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, Jehoram's youngest son, king in his place, since the raiding band that came with the Arabs against the camp had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[2] Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah, granddaughter of Omri. [Footnote: The parallel account and some ancient witnesses read twenty-two years old.]
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[3] He too walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor in doing wrong.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[4] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as the house of Ahab had done, for after his father's death they were his advisers, to his ruin.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[5] He followed their counsel and went with Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, to make war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[6] So he returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds they had inflicted on him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. And Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to Jezreel to visit Joram son of Ahab, because he was ill.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[7] Ahaziah's downfall came from God through this visit to Joram. For when he arrived, he went out with Jehoram to meet Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[8] While Jehu was executing judgment on the house of Ahab, he came upon the officials of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers, who served Ahaziah, and he killed them.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[9] Then he searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria. They brought him to Jehu and put him to death, but they buried him, for they said, "He is the grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart." And the house of Ahaziah had no one strong enough to hold the kingdom.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[10] When Athaliah, Ahaziah's mother, saw that her son was dead, she set about destroying the whole royal line of the house of Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[11] But Jehoshabeath, the king's daughter, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death, and she put him and his nurse in a bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, daughter of King Jehoram and wife of Jehoiada the priest—she was Ahaziah's sister—hid him from Athaliah, and Athaliah did not put him to death.
[2 Chronicles] [22]:[12] He remained hidden with them in the house of God for six years, while Athaliah ruled the land.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[1] In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage and brought the commanders of hundreds into a covenant with him: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[2] They traveled throughout Judah and gathered the Levites from all the towns of Judah, along with the heads of the families of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[3] Then the whole assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. Jehoiada said to them, "Here is the king's son! He shall reign, just as the LORD promised concerning the sons of David.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[4] This is what you are to do: a third of you priests and Levites who come on duty on the Sabbath are to guard the doors,
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[5] a third are to be at the royal palace, and a third at the Foundation Gate, while all the people are to be in the courts of the house of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[6] No one is to enter the house of the LORD except the priests and the Levites who minister there; they may enter, for they are consecrated. But all the people are to keep the watch of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[7] The Levites are to surround the king, each man with his weapons in his hand, and anyone who enters the temple is to be put to death. Stay close to the king wherever he goes."
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[8] The Levites and all Judah did everything Jehoiada the priest had commanded. Each of them took his men—those coming on duty on the Sabbath and those going off duty—for Jehoiada the priest had not released any of the divisions.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[9] Jehoiada the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and the large and small shields that had belonged to King David and were kept in the house of God.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[10] He stationed all the people, each man with his weapon in his hand, around the king—from the right side of the temple to the left, near the altar and the temple.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[11] Then they brought out the king's son, put the crown on him, gave him the testimony, and proclaimed him king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and they shouted, "Long live the king!"
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[12] When Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to them at the house of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[13] She looked, and there was the king, standing by his pillar at the entrance, with the officers and the trumpeters beside him. All the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers were leading the praise with their instruments. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and cried out, "Treason! Treason!"
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[14] Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds who were in charge of the troops and said to them, "Take her out between the ranks, and put to the sword anyone who follows her." For the priest had said, "Do not put her to death in the house of the LORD."
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[15] So they seized her, and when she reached the entrance of the Horse Gate at the royal palace, they put her to death there.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[16] Then Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they would be the LORD's people.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[17] All the people went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed its altars and its images, and they killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, in front of the altars.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[18] Then Jehoiada placed the oversight of the house of the LORD in the hands of the priests, who were Levites, whom David had assigned to the house of the LORD, to offer the burnt offerings of the LORD as written in the Law of Moses, with rejoicing and song, as David had directed.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[19] He also stationed gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD, so that no one who was unclean in any way could enter.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[20] Then he took the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers of the people, and all the people of the land, and brought the king down from the house of the LORD. They went through the Upper Gate into the palace and seated the king on the royal throne.
[2 Chronicles] [23]:[21] All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, for they had put Athaliah to death with the sword.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[1] Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah, from Beersheba.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[2] Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD as long as Jehoiada the priest lived.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[3] Jehoiada found two wives for him, and he had sons and daughters.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[4] Some time later Joash resolved to restore the house of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[5] He gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the towns of Judah and collect money from all Israel, year by year, to repair the house of your God. See that you act quickly in this matter." But the Levites did not act quickly.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[6] So the king summoned Jehoiada the chief priest and said to him, "Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the tax laid down by Moses, the servant of the LORD, and by the assembly of Israel for the tent of the testimony?"
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[7] For the sons of that wicked woman Athaliah had broken into the house of God and had even used all its sacred objects for the Baals.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[8] At the king's command they made a chest and placed it outside, at the gate of the house of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[9] Then a proclamation was made throughout Judah and Jerusalem that the tax imposed on Israel in the wilderness by Moses, the servant of God, should be brought to the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[10] All the officials and all the people rejoiced; they brought their contributions and dropped them into the chest until it was full.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[11] Whenever the chest was carried by the Levites to the king's officers and they saw that there was a great deal of money in it, the king's secretary and the chief priest's officer would come, empty the chest, and carry it back to its place. This they did day after day, and they collected a large amount of money.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[12] The king and Jehoiada handed it over to those who carried out the work of the house of the LORD, and they hired stonecutters and carpenters to restore the house of the LORD, and also workers in iron and bronze to repair it.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[13] The workmen labored, and under their hands the work of repair went forward. They restored the house of God according to its original design and reinforced it.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[14] When they had finished, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Jehoiada, and it was used to make utensils for the house of the LORD: vessels for the service and for the burnt offerings, dishes, and articles of gold and silver. And throughout Jehoiada's lifetime burnt offerings were presented continually in the house of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[15] Jehoiada grew old and full of years, and he died at the age of a hundred and thirty.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[16] They buried him in the City of David with the kings, because he had done good in Israel, both toward God and toward his house.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[17] After the death of Jehoiada, the officials of Judah came and bowed before the king, and he listened to them.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[18] They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and served the Asherah poles and the idols. Because of this guilt of theirs, wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[19] The LORD sent prophets among them to bring them back to himself; they testified against them, but the people would not listen.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[20] Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood above the people and said to them, "This is what God says: Why do you break the commandments of the LORD, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have forsaken the LORD, he has forsaken you."
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[21] But they conspired against him, and at the king's command they stoned him to death in the courtyard of the house of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[22] King Joash did not remember the kindness that Jehoiada his father had shown him, but killed Jehoiada's son. As he lay dying he said, "May the LORD see this and call you to account."
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[23] At the turn of the year the army of Aram marched against Joash. They invaded Judah and Jerusalem, destroyed all the leaders of the people, and sent all the plunder to the king of Damascus.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[24] Though the army of Aram had come with only a few men, the LORD delivered into their hands a very great army, because Judah had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers. So they carried out judgment on Joash.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[25] When the Arameans withdrew, they left him severely wounded. His own servants conspired against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him on his bed. So he died, and they buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[26] Those who conspired against him were Zabad, son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad, son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.
[2 Chronicles] [24]:[27] The account of his sons, the many prophecies against him, and the restoration of the house of God are written in the commentary on the Book of the Kings. And Amaziah his son succeeded him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[1] Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan, of Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[2] He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, yet not with a whole heart.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[3] Once the kingdom was firmly in his grasp, he executed the officials who had murdered his father the king.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[4] But he did not put their children to death, for he acted according to what is written in the Law, in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded: "Fathers shall not die for their children, nor children for their fathers; each one shall die for his own sin."
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[5] Amaziah assembled Judah and organized them by their fathers' households under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, for all of Judah and Benjamin. He mustered those twenty years old and upward and found there were three hundred thousand choice men fit for military service, able to handle spear and shield.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[6] He also hired a hundred thousand seasoned warriors from Israel for a hundred talents of silver.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[7] But a man of God came to him and said: "Your Majesty, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel—not with any of the Ephraimites.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[8] Even if you go and fight ever so bravely, God will bring you down before the enemy, for God has power to help and power to overthrow."
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[9] Amaziah said to the man of God, "But what about the hundred talents I paid to the troops of Israel?" The man of God answered, "The LORD can give you far more than that."
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[10] So Amaziah dismissed the troops that had come to him from Ephraim and sent them back to their own place. They were furious with Judah and went home in a blazing rage.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[11] Amaziah then took courage, led out his people, and marched to the Valley of Salt, where he struck down ten thousand men of Seir.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[12] The men of Judah also captured ten thousand alive; they brought them to the top of the cliff and threw them down from the top of the cliff, so that all of them were dashed to pieces.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[13] Meanwhile the troops Amaziah had sent back, refusing to let them go with him into battle, raided the towns of Judah from Samaria to Beth Horon. They killed three thousand people and carried off a great deal of plunder.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[14] When Amaziah returned from slaughtering the Edomites, he brought back the gods of the people of Seir, set them up as his own gods, bowed down before them, and burned offerings to them.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[15] The anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and he sent a prophet to him, who said, "Why have you sought the gods of this people, gods that could not deliver their own people from your hand?"
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[16] While the prophet was still speaking, the king said to him, "Have we appointed you counselor to the king? Stop! Why should you be struck down?" So the prophet stopped, but he said, "I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel."
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[17] After taking counsel, Amaziah king of Judah sent word to Joash son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu, king of Israel: "Come, let us meet face to face."
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[18] But Joash king of Israel sent back this reply to Amaziah king of Judah: "A thistle in Lebanon sent word to a cedar in Lebanon, 'Give your daughter to my son in marriage.' But a wild beast of Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle underfoot.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[19] You say to yourself, 'Look, I have defeated Edom,' and your heart has grown proud and boastful. Now stay home! Why provoke disaster and bring yourself down, and Judah with you?"
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[20] But Amaziah would not listen, for this was from God, so that he might hand them over to their enemies—because they had sought the gods of Edom.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[21] So Joash king of Israel marched out, and he and Amaziah king of Judah met face to face at Beth Shemesh in Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[22] Judah was routed before Israel, and every man fled to his home.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[23] Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash, the son of Jehoahaz, at Beth Shemesh. He brought him to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate—four hundred cubits.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[24] He took all the gold and silver and all the articles found in the house of God, which had been in the care of Obed-Edom, together with the treasures of the royal palace and the hostages, and returned to Samaria.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[25] Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[26] As for the rest of the acts of Amaziah, from beginning to end, are they not written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel?
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[27] From the time that Amaziah turned away from following the LORD, they conspired against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent men after him to Lachish and killed him there.
[2 Chronicles] [25]:[28] They brought him back on horses and buried him with his fathers in the City of Judah.[^1] [^1]: Some ancient manuscripts and versions read "City of David."
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[1] Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[2] He rebuilt Eloth and restored it to Judah after the king had rested with his fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[3] Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah, of Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[4] He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[5] He set himself to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God; and as long as he sought the LORD, God gave him success.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[6] He went out and made war against the Philistines, and he broke down the walls of Gath, the walls of Jabneh, and the walls of Ashdod. Then he built cities in the territory of Ashdod and among the Philistines.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[7] God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and against the Meunites.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[8] The Ammonites paid tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread as far as the border of Egypt, for he had grown very strong.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[9] Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate, and at the angle of the wall, and he fortified them.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[10] He also built towers in the wilderness and dug many cisterns, for he had large herds both in the foothills and on the plain. He had farmers and vinedressers in the hills and in the fertile fields, for he loved the soil.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[11] Uzziah had an army trained for war, ready to go out in companies according to the number mustered by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[12] The total number of the heads of families, mighty warriors all, was 2,600.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[13] Under their command was an army of 307,500 trained for war, a powerful force to support the king against his enemies.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[14] Uzziah supplied the entire army with shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and slingstones.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[15] In Jerusalem he made machines, designed by skilled men, to be placed on the towers and the corners, to shoot arrows and hurl large stones. His fame spread far and wide, for he was marvelously helped until he became strong.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[16] But when he had become strong, his heart grew proud, to his own destruction. He was unfaithful to the LORD his God and entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[17] Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of the LORD, courageous men.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[18] They confronted King Uzziah and said to him, "It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have been unfaithful, and you will have no honor from the LORD God."
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[19] Then Uzziah, who had a censer in his hand to burn incense, became enraged. And while he raged at the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead before the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the altar of incense.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[20] When Azariah the chief priest and all the priests turned toward him and saw the leprosy on his forehead, they rushed him out of there. He himself hurried to leave, because the LORD had struck him.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[21] King Uzziah remained a leper until the day of his death. He lived in a separate house, a leper, cut off from the house of the LORD, while his son Jotham was in charge of the palace and governed the people of the land.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[22] The rest of the acts of Uzziah, from beginning to end, were recorded by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
[2 Chronicles] [26]:[23] Uzziah rested with his fathers, and they buried him near his fathers in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, "He was a leper." And his son Jotham became king in his place.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[1] Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerushah, the daughter of Zadok.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[2] He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Uzziah had done—except that he did not enter the temple of the LORD. But the people continued in their corrupt ways.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[3] He rebuilt the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, and he did extensive building on the wall of Ophel.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[4] He also built cities in the hill country of Judah, and forts and towers in the wooded areas.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[5] He went to war against the king of the Ammonites and defeated them. That year the Ammonites paid him a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat, and ten thousand cors of barley. The Ammonites brought him the same tribute in the second and third years as well.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[6] So Jotham grew powerful, because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[7] The rest of the acts of Jotham, all his wars and all his ways, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[8] He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [27]:[9] Then Jotham rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. And his son Ahaz became king in his place.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[1] Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father David had done.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[2] Instead he followed the ways of the kings of Israel, and he even made cast images for the Baals.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[3] He burned incense in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom and burned his sons in the fire, following the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[4] He sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[5] So the LORD his God handed him over to the king of Aram, who defeated him, took a great many of his people captive, and brought them to Damascus. He was also handed over to the king of Israel, who struck him a heavy blow.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[6] In a single day Pekah son of Remaliah killed a hundred and twenty thousand men in Judah, all of them seasoned soldiers, because they had abandoned the LORD, the God of their fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[7] Zichri, a warrior of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the officer in charge of the palace, and Elkanah, second in command to the king.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[8] The Israelites took two hundred thousand of their own kindred captive—women, sons, and daughters. They also carried off a great deal of plunder and brought it to Samaria.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[9] But a prophet of the LORD named Oded was there. He went out to meet the army as it came to Samaria and said to them: "Look, because the LORD, the God of your fathers, was angry with Judah, he handed them over to you. But you have slaughtered them in a rage that reaches to heaven.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[10] And now you intend to subjugate the people of Judah and Jerusalem as your slaves, male and female. But are you not yourselves guilty of sins against the LORD your God?
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[11] Now listen to me: send back the captives you have taken from your own kindred, for the fierce anger of the LORD rests on you."
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[12] Then some of the leaders of Ephraim—Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai—confronted those who were returning from the war.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[13] "Do not bring the captives here," they said, "or we will be guilty before the LORD. Do you intend to add to our sins and our guilt? Our guilt is already great, and his fierce anger rests on Israel."
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[14] So the soldiers gave up the captives and the plunder before the officials and the whole assembly.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[15] Then the men designated by name took charge of the captives. From the plunder they clothed all who were naked; they gave them clothes and sandals, fed them and gave them drink, and anointed their wounds. They put all the weak ones on donkeys and brought them to their kindred at Jericho, the City of Palms. Then they returned to Samaria.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[16] At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria for help.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[17] The Edomites had also come and attacked Judah and carried off captives,
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[18] while the Philistines raided the towns of the foothills and the Negev of Judah. They captured Beth Shemesh, Aijalon, and Gederoth, as well as Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo with their surrounding villages, and settled there.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[19] The LORD humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had promoted lawlessness in Judah and been utterly unfaithful to the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[20] Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria came against him and oppressed him instead of strengthening him.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[21] For Ahaz took treasures from the temple of the LORD, from the royal palace, and from the officials, and gave them to the king of Assyria—but it did him no good.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[22] In the time of his distress, King Ahaz became still more unfaithful to the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[23] He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, who had defeated him, thinking, "Since the gods of the kings of Aram have helped them, I will sacrifice to them so they will help me too." But they were the ruin of him and of all Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[24] Ahaz gathered up the furnishings of the house of God, cut them to pieces, and shut the doors of the LORD's temple. He set up altars at every street corner in Jerusalem,
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[25] and in every town in Judah he built high places to burn incense to other gods, provoking the LORD, the God of his fathers, to anger.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[26] The rest of his acts and all his ways, from beginning to end, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [28]:[27] Ahaz rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of Jerusalem, but he was not brought to the tombs of the kings of Israel. And Hezekiah his son succeeded him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[1] Hezekiah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[2] He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his forefather David had done.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[3] In the first month of the first year of his reign he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[4] He brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them in the square on the east side,
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[5] and he said to them: "Listen to me, Levites! Consecrate yourselves now, and consecrate the house of the LORD, the God of your fathers. Carry the filth out of the sanctuary.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[6] For our fathers were unfaithful; they did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD our God and abandoned him. They turned their faces away from the dwelling place of the LORD and turned their backs on him.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[7] They even shut the doors of the portico and put out the lamps. They burned no incense and offered no burnt offerings in the sanctuary to the God of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[8] So the wrath of the LORD fell on Judah and Jerusalem, and he made them an object of horror, of dismay, and of scorn, as you see with your own eyes.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[9] This is why our fathers have fallen by the sword and our sons and daughters and wives are in captivity.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[10] Now I intend to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, so that his burning anger may turn away from us.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[11] My sons, do not be negligent now, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before him and serve him, to be his ministers and to burn incense."
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[12] Then these Levites stepped forward: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah from the Kohathites; from the Merarites, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; from the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[13] from the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeiel; from the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[14] from the sons of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; and from the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[15] They gathered their brothers and consecrated themselves, and then they went in to purify the house of the LORD, as the king had commanded according to the words of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[16] The priests went into the inner part of the house of the LORD to purify it. Everything unclean that they found in the temple of the LORD they brought out to the courtyard of the house of the LORD, and the Levites took it and carried it out to the Kidron Valley.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[17] They began the consecration on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they came to the portico of the LORD. For eight more days they consecrated the house of the LORD, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[18] Then they went in to King Hezekiah and reported: "We have purified the entire house of the LORD, the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the table for the rows of bread with all its utensils.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[19] We have also prepared and consecrated all the articles that King Ahaz cast aside in his unfaithfulness during his reign. They are now in front of the altar of the LORD."
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[20] Early the next morning King Hezekiah gathered the officials of the city and went up to the house of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[21] They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. And the king ordered the priests, the descendants of Aaron, to offer them on the altar of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[22] So they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests took the blood and sprinkled it against the altar. Then they slaughtered the rams and sprinkled the blood against the altar, and they slaughtered the lambs and sprinkled the blood against the altar.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[23] The goats for the sin offering were brought before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[24] The priests slaughtered them and presented their blood on the altar as a sin offering, to make atonement for all Israel; for the king had ordered the burnt offering and the sin offering for all Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[25] He stationed the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps, and lyres, according to the command of David, of Gad the king's seer, and of Nathan the prophet; for this command came from the LORD through his prophets.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[26] So the Levites stood ready with David's instruments, and the priests with their trumpets.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[27] Then Hezekiah gave the order to offer the burnt offering on the altar. As the offering began, the song to the LORD began as well, with the trumpets and the instruments of David king of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[28] The whole assembly bowed in worship while the singers sang and the trumpeters sounded their trumpets. All this continued until the burnt offering was finished.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[29] When the offering was completed, the king and everyone with him knelt down and worshiped.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[30] King Hezekiah and the officials ordered the Levites to praise the LORD with the words of David and of Asaph the seer. So they sang praises with gladness and bowed their heads and worshiped.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[31] Then Hezekiah said, "Now that you have consecrated yourselves to the LORD, come forward and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the LORD." So the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and all whose hearts were willing brought burnt offerings.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[32] The number of burnt offerings the assembly brought was seventy bulls, a hundred rams, and two hundred lambs—all of them as a burnt offering to the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[33] The animals consecrated as sacrifices amounted to six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep and goats.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[34] But the priests were too few to skin all the burnt offerings, so their brothers the Levites helped them until the work was finished and until the priests had consecrated themselves; for the Levites had been more conscientious in consecrating themselves than the priests.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[35] There were also many burnt offerings, along with the fat of the fellowship offerings and the drink offerings that accompanied the burnt offerings. So the service of the house of the LORD was reestablished.
[2 Chronicles] [29]:[36] Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced over what God had done for the people, for it had all come about so suddenly.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[1] Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah, and he also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, inviting them to come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to keep the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[2] The king and his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem had decided to keep the Passover in the second month,
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[3] since they could not keep it at the proper time: not enough priests had consecrated themselves, and the people had not gathered in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[4] The plan seemed right to the king and to the whole assembly,
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[5] so they resolved to send a proclamation throughout Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, calling the people to come to Jerusalem and keep the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel; for they had not kept it in great numbers as it is written.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[6] So the couriers went throughout Israel and Judah with letters from the hand of the king and his officials, and by the king's command they said: "People of Israel, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, that he may return to the remnant of you who have escaped the hand of the kings of Assyria.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[7] Do not be like your fathers and your brothers, who were unfaithful to the LORD, the God of their fathers, so that he made them an object of horror, as you yourselves see.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[8] Now do not stiffen your necks as your fathers did. Give your hand to the LORD and come to his sanctuary, which he has consecrated forever, and serve the LORD your God, so that his fierce anger may turn away from you.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[9] For if you return to the LORD, your brothers and your children will find compassion with their captors and will come back to this land. For the LORD your God is gracious and merciful, and he will not turn his face from you if you return to him."
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[10] The couriers went from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and as far as Zebulun, but the people laughed at them and mocked them.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[11] Yet some from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[12] In Judah too the hand of God was at work, giving them one heart to carry out what the king and the officials had commanded by the word of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[13] A great crowd gathered in Jerusalem to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month—a very large assembly.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[14] They set to work and removed the altars in Jerusalem, and they took away all the incense altars and threw them into the Kidron Valley.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[15] They slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and Levites, put to shame, consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings into the house of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[16] They took their accustomed places as prescribed in the Law of Moses, the man of God, the priests sprinkling the blood they received from the hand of the Levites.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[17] For many in the assembly had not consecrated themselves; so the Levites had to slaughter the Passover lambs for everyone who was not clean, to consecrate them to the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[18] For a great many of the people—many from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun—had not purified themselves, yet they ate the Passover contrary to what is written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May the LORD, who is good, make atonement for everyone
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[19] who sets his heart to seek God, the LORD, the God of his fathers, even if he is not clean according to the purity of the sanctuary."
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[20] And the LORD listened to Hezekiah and healed the people.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[21] The people of Israel who were present in Jerusalem kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with great joy, and day after day the Levites and the priests praised the LORD with loud instruments.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[22] Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed skill in the service of the LORD. So they ate the festal meal for the seven days, sacrificing fellowship offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[23] Then the whole assembly agreed to keep the feast another seven days, and they kept those seven days with joy.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[24] For Hezekiah king of Judah contributed a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep to the assembly, and the officials contributed a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep. And a great number of priests consecrated themselves.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[25] The whole assembly of Judah rejoiced, along with the priests and the Levites, and all the assembly that had come from Israel, and the foreigners who had come from the land of Israel or lived in Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[26] There was great joy in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon son of David, king of Israel, there had been nothing like it in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [30]:[27] Then the priests and the Levites stood and blessed the people, and their voice was heard; their prayer came to his holy dwelling place, to heaven.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[1] When all this was finished, all the Israelites who were present went out to the towns of Judah and smashed the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and tore down the high places and the altars throughout Judah and Benjamin and in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had destroyed them all. Then all the Israelites returned to their own towns, each to his own property.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[2] Hezekiah assigned the priests and Levites to their divisions, each according to his duty, whether priest or Levite, for burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, to minister, to give thanks, and to sing praises at the gates of the LORD's camps.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[3] From his own possessions the king set aside a portion for the burnt offerings: the morning and evening burnt offerings and those for the Sabbaths, the New Moons, and the appointed feasts, as it is written in the Law of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[4] He ordered the people living in Jerusalem to give the portion due the priests and Levites, so that they could devote themselves to the Law of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[5] As soon as the order went out, the Israelites brought a generous supply of the firstfruits of their grain, new wine, olive oil, and honey, and all the produce of the fields; and they brought in tithes of everything in abundance.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[6] The people of Israel and Judah who lived in the towns of Judah also brought a tithe of their herds and flocks, and a tithe of the holy things dedicated to the LORD their God, and they piled them up in heap after heap.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[7] They began building the heaps in the third month and finished in the seventh month.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[8] When Hezekiah and his officials came and saw the heaps, they blessed the LORD and his people Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[9] Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites about the heaps,
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[10] and Azariah the chief priest, from the house of Zadok, answered him: "Since the people began bringing their contributions to the house of the LORD, we have had enough to eat and plenty to spare, for the LORD has blessed his people, and this great amount is what is left over."
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[11] Then Hezekiah gave orders to prepare storerooms in the house of the LORD, and they were prepared.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[12] They faithfully brought in the contributions, the tithes, and the dedicated gifts. Conaniah the Levite was in charge of them, and his brother Shimei was second in command.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[13] Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah served as supervisors under Conaniah and his brother Shimei, by appointment of King Hezekiah and of Azariah the official in charge of the house of God.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[14] Kore son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper at the East Gate, was in charge of the freewill offerings given to God, distributing the contributions made to the LORD and also the consecrated gifts.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[15] Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah assisted him faithfully in the towns of the priests, distributing to their fellow Levites and priests according to their divisions, to old and young alike.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[16] In addition, they distributed to the males three years old and upward who were listed in the genealogical records—all who entered the house of the LORD to perform the daily duties of their service, according to their responsibilities and their divisions.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[17] The priests were enrolled by their families, and the Levites twenty years old and upward according to their duties and their divisions.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[18] They were enrolled along with all their little ones, their wives, their sons, and their daughters—the whole company—for they had faithfully consecrated themselves.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[19] As for the priests, the descendants of Aaron, who lived on the farmlands around their towns, men were designated by name in each of those towns to distribute portions to every male among the priests and to all the Levites listed in the genealogies.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[20] This is what Hezekiah did throughout Judah. He did what was good and right and faithful before the LORD his God.
[2 Chronicles] [31]:[21] In everything he undertook—in the service of the house of God and in obedience to the law and the commandments—he sought his God and worked wholeheartedly, and so he prospered.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[1] After all this faithful work, Sennacherib king of Assyria came and invaded Judah. He laid siege to the fortified cities, intending to take them for himself.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[2] When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and was set on attacking Jerusalem,
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[3] he consulted with his officers and his warriors about stopping up the springs outside the city, and they supported him.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[4] A large force was mustered, and they stopped up all the springs and the stream that flowed through the land. "Why should the kings of Assyria come and find plenty of water?" they said.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[5] Then Hezekiah set to work with resolve. He rebuilt every broken section of the wall, raised towers on it, built another wall outside it, and reinforced the Millo in the City of David. He also produced weapons and shields in quantity.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[6] He appointed commanders over the people, gathered them to himself in the square at the city gate, and encouraged them with these words:
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[7] "Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or dismayed before the king of Assyria and the whole horde with him, for there is a greater power with us than with him.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[8] With him is only human strength, but with us is the LORD our God, to help us and to fight our battles." And the people took confidence from the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[9] Afterward, while Sennacherib king of Assyria was still at Lachish with all his forces, he sent his servants to Jerusalem, to Hezekiah king of Judah and to all the people of Judah who were in Jerusalem, with this message:
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[10] "This is what Sennacherib king of Assyria says: On what are you relying, that you sit under siege in Jerusalem?
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[11] Is not Hezekiah misleading you, handing you over to die of hunger and thirst, when he says, 'The LORD our God will rescue us from the hand of the king of Assyria'?
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[12] Was it not this same Hezekiah who removed his God's high places and altars and told Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship at one altar and burn your offerings there'?
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[13] Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of other lands? Were the gods of the nations of those lands ever able to save their land from my hand?
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[14] Among all the gods of those nations that my fathers destroyed, which one could save his people from my hand? How then can your God save you from my hand?
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[15] So do not let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you like this, and do not believe him. For no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to save his people from my hand or from the hand of my fathers. How much less will your God save you from my hand!"
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[16] His servants said still more against the LORD God and against his servant Hezekiah.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[17] Sennacherib also wrote letters mocking the LORD, the God of Israel, and speaking against him: "Just as the gods of the nations of other lands did not save their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not save his people from my hand."
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[18] Then they shouted loudly in Hebrew to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to frighten and terrify them, so that they might capture the city.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[19] They spoke of the God of Jerusalem as if he were like the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[20] Then King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz prayed about this and cried out to heaven.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[21] And the LORD sent an angel, who cut down every mighty warrior, every commander and officer, in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he went back to his own land in disgrace. And when he entered the temple of his god, his own sons struck him down there with the sword.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[22] So the LORD saved Hezekiah and the people of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria and from every other hand, and he gave them rest on every side.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[23] Many brought offerings to the LORD in Jerusalem and costly gifts to Hezekiah king of Judah. From then on he was highly regarded by all the nations.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[24] In those days Hezekiah fell sick and was near death. He prayed to the LORD, who answered him and gave him a sign.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[25] But Hezekiah did not respond in keeping with the kindness shown him, for his heart grew proud. So wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[26] Then Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, he and the people of Jerusalem with him, and the LORD's wrath did not come upon them during Hezekiah's lifetime.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[27] Hezekiah had very great wealth and honor. He made treasuries for his silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of valuables,
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[28] as well as storehouses for the harvest of grain, new wine, and oil, and stalls for every kind of livestock, and flocks in the pens.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[29] He built towns for himself and acquired great numbers of sheep and cattle, for God had given him very great possessions.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[30] It was this same Hezekiah who blocked the upper outlet of the Gihon spring and channeled the water down to the west side of the City of David. He succeeded in everything he undertook.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[31] And so it was with the envoys of the rulers of Babylon, who were sent to him to inquire about the sign that had occurred in the land: God left him to himself, to test him and to know everything that was in his heart.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[32] The rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his faithful deeds are written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz, in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [32]:[33] Hezekiah rested with his fathers and was buried on the ascent to the tombs of David's descendants. All Judah and the people of Jerusalem honored him at his death. And his son Manasseh succeeded him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[1] Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[2] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, following the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before the people of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[3] He rebuilt the high places his father Hezekiah had torn down, raised altars to the Baals, made Asherah poles, and bowed down to all the host of heaven and served them.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[4] He built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, "My name will be in Jerusalem forever."
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[5] In both courts of the house of the LORD he built altars to all the host of heaven.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[6] He made his own sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben Hinnom; he practiced soothsaying and divination and witchcraft, and consulted mediums and spiritists. He did a great deal of evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[7] He took the carved image he had made and set it up in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to his son Solomon, "In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will put my name forever.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[8] I will never again remove Israel from the land I assigned to your fathers, if only they are careful to do all that I commanded them—the whole law, the statutes, and the ordinances given through Moses."
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[9] But Manasseh led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray, so that they did more evil than the nations the LORD had destroyed before the people of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[10] The LORD spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they paid no attention.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[11] So the LORD brought against them the army commanders of the king of Assyria, who took Manasseh captive with hooks, bound him with bronze shackles, and carried him off to Babylon.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[12] In his distress he sought the favor of the LORD his God and humbled himself deeply before the God of his fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[13] He prayed to him, and the LORD was moved by his plea and heard his petition. He brought him back to Jerusalem and to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[14] Afterward he rebuilt the outer wall of the City of David, west of the Gihon spring in the valley, as far as the entrance of the Fish Gate, and around the Ophel, and he made it very high. He also stationed military commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[15] He removed the foreign gods and the image from the house of the LORD, along with all the altars he had built on the temple hill and in Jerusalem, and he threw them outside the city.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[16] Then he restored the altar of the LORD and sacrificed fellowship offerings and thank offerings on it, and he told Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[17] The people, however, still sacrificed at the high places, though only to the LORD their God.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[18] The rest of the acts of Manasseh, his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, are recorded in the annals of the kings of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[19] His prayer and how God was moved by his plea, all his sins and unfaithfulness, and the sites where he built high places and set up the Asherah poles and the idols before he humbled himself—all these are written in the records of the seers.[^1] [^1]: Or *in the records of Hozai*; the Hebrew word can be read as a personal name.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[20] Manasseh rested with his fathers and was buried at his palace. And his son Amon succeeded him as king.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[21] Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[22] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done. Amon sacrificed to all the idols his father Manasseh had made, and he served them.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[23] But he did not humble himself before the LORD as his father Manasseh had done; instead, Amon only multiplied his guilt.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[24] His servants conspired against him and killed him in his own house.
[2 Chronicles] [33]:[25] But the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king in his place.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[1] Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[2] He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, walking in the ways of David his father and turning aside neither to the right nor to the left.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[3] In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still a boy, he began to seek the God of David his father, and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherah poles, the carved images, and the cast idols.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[4] Under his direction they tore down the altars of the Baals; he cut to pieces the incense altars that stood above them, and he shattered the Asherah poles, the carved images, and the cast idols, ground them to dust, and scattered it over the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[5] He burned the bones of the priests on their altars, and so he cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[6] He did the same in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, and in the ruins that lay around them.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[7] He tore down the altars, beat the Asherah poles and the carved images into powder, and cut to pieces all the incense altars throughout the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[8] In the eighteenth year of his reign, in order to cleanse the land and the temple, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder to repair the house of the LORD his God.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[9] They went to Hilkiah the high priest and handed over the money that had been brought into the house of God, which the Levites who guarded the thresholds had collected from Manasseh and Ephraim and from all the remnant of Israel, and from all Judah and Benjamin and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.[^1] [^1]: The written Hebrew text reads "the inhabitants of Jerusalem"; the traditional reading is "and they returned to Jerusalem."
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[10] They handed it over to those doing the work, the men appointed over the house of the LORD, and those who were doing the work in the house of the LORD used it to restore and repair the temple.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[11] They gave it to the carpenters and builders to buy dressed stone and timber for couplings and beams for the buildings that the kings of Judah had allowed to fall into ruin.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[12] The men did the work faithfully. Over them were appointed Jahath and Obadiah, Levites of the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam of the sons of the Kohathites, to direct them, along with the Levites who were all skilled with musical instruments.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[13] They were also over the laborers and directed all the workmen in every kind of task. Some of the Levites served as scribes, officials, and gatekeepers.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[14] While they were bringing out the money that had been brought into the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest found the Book of the Law of the LORD given through Moses.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[15] Hilkiah said to Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD," and he gave the book to Shaphan.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[16] Shaphan brought the book to the king and reported to him as well, "Your servants are doing everything that was entrusted to them.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[17] They have emptied out the money that was found in the house of the LORD and handed it over to the supervisors and the workmen."
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[18] Then Shaphan the scribe told the king, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." And Shaphan read from it in the presence of the king.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[19] When the king heard the words of the Law, he tore his clothes.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[20] He gave this command to Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king's servant:
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[21] "Go, inquire of the LORD for me and for those who remain in Israel and Judah concerning the words of the book that has been found. For great is the wrath of the LORD that has been poured out on us, because our fathers did not keep the word of the LORD by doing everything written in this book.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[22] So Hilkiah and those the king had sent went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem, in the Second District, and they spoke with her about this.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[23] She said to them: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the man who sent you to me,
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[24] this is what the LORD says: I am about to bring disaster on this place and on its inhabitants—all the curses written in the book that was read before the king of Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[25] Because they have forsaken me and burned incense to other gods, provoking me to anger with all the works of their hands, my wrath will be poured out on this place, and it will not be quenched.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[26] But say this to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of the LORD: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning the words you have heard:
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[27] Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and its inhabitants, and because you humbled yourself before me, tore your clothes, and wept before me, I also have heard you, declares the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[28] Behold, I will gather you to your fathers, and you will be laid in your grave in peace. Your eyes will not see all the disaster I am bringing on this place and on its inhabitants." So they brought back word to the king.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[29] Then the king sent word and gathered together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[30] He went up to the house of the LORD with all the men of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, the Levites, and all the people, from the greatest to the least, and he read in their hearing all the words of the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the house of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[31] The king stood in his place and made a covenant before the LORD to follow the LORD and to keep his commandments, his testimonies, and his statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, carrying out the words of the covenant written in this book.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[32] Then he had everyone present in Jerusalem and Benjamin pledge themselves to it, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem acted in accordance with the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [34]:[33] Josiah removed all the detestable things from all the lands belonging to the Israelites, and he made all who were in Israel serve the LORD their God. As long as he lived, they did not turn away from following the LORD, the God of their fathers.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[1] Josiah kept the Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and they slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the first month.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[2] He appointed the priests to their duties and encouraged them in the service of the house of the LORD.
