[2 Chronicles] [35]:[3] He said to the Levites who taught all Israel and were holy to the LORD: "Put the holy ark in the house that Solomon son of David, king of Israel, built. You need no longer carry it on your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and his people Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[4] Prepare yourselves by your ancestral houses, according to your divisions, as prescribed in the writing of David king of Israel and in the document of his son Solomon.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[5] Stand in the holy place, arranged to serve the ancestral houses of your kinsmen, the lay people, with one Levite family group assigned to each.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[6] Slaughter the Passover lamb, consecrate yourselves, and make preparations for your kinsmen, so that everything may be done according to the word of the LORD given through Moses."
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[7] Josiah contributed to the lay people, to all who were present, flocks of lambs and young goats for the Passover offerings, thirty thousand in number, along with three thousand cattle. These came from the king's own possessions.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[8] His officials also made a freewill contribution to the people, to the priests, and to the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, the chief officers of the house of God, gave the priests twenty-six hundred Passover offerings and three hundred cattle.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[9] Conaniah, along with Shemaiah and Nethanel his brothers, and Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, the officers of the Levites, contributed to the Levites five thousand Passover offerings and five hundred cattle.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[10] So the service was arranged: the priests stood at their posts and the Levites in their divisions, according to the king's command.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[11] They slaughtered the Passover lambs, and the priests sprinkled the blood handed to them, while the Levites skinned the animals.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[12] They set aside the burnt offerings to distribute them to the groupings of the ancestral houses of the lay people, to present them to the LORD as it is written in the book of Moses; and they did the same with the cattle.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[13] They roasted the Passover lamb over the fire, as prescribed, and boiled the holy offerings in pots, kettles, and pans, and served them quickly to all the people.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[14] Afterward they made preparations for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the sons of Aaron, were occupied until nightfall offering the burnt offerings and the fat portions. So the Levites made preparations for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[15] The singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their stations according to the command of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's seer; and the gatekeepers were at each gate. They did not need to leave their service, for their kinsmen the Levites made preparations for them.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[16] So the whole service of the LORD was arranged that day, to keep the Passover and to offer burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD, according to the command of King Josiah.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[17] The Israelites who were present kept the Passover at that time, along with the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[18] No Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet; none of the kings of Israel had kept such a Passover as Josiah kept, with the priests, the Levites, all Judah, the Israelites who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[19] This Passover was kept in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[20] After all this, when Josiah had put the temple in order, Neco king of Egypt marched up to fight at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[21] But Neco sent messengers to him, saying: "What quarrel is there between you and me, king of Judah? I am not coming against you today, but against the house with which I am at war, and God has told me to hurry. Stop opposing God, who is with me, or he will destroy you."
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[22] Josiah, however, would not turn away from him; instead he disguised himself to fight him. He would not listen to the words of Neco, which came from the mouth of God, and he went to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[23] The archers shot King Josiah, and the king said to his servants, "Take me away, for I am badly wounded."
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[24] So his servants took him out of his chariot, put him in his second chariot, and brought him to Jerusalem, where he died. He was buried in the tombs of his fathers, and all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[25] Jeremiah composed a lament for Josiah, and to this day all the male and female singers sing of Josiah in their laments. They made these a custom in Israel, and they are written in the Laments.
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[26] Now the rest of the acts of Josiah, and his deeds of faithful love, done in accordance with what is written in the law of the LORD —
[2 Chronicles] [35]:[27] his acts from first to last, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[1] Then the people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and made him king in Jerusalem in place of his father.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[2] Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[3] The king of Egypt deposed him in Jerusalem and imposed a fine on the land of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold. [Footnote: A talent weighed roughly 34 kilograms (75 pounds).]
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[4] The king of Egypt made Eliakim, his brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But Neco took Jehoahaz his brother and carried him off to Egypt.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[5] Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[6] Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched against him and bound him in bronze shackles to take him to Babylon.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[7] Nebuchadnezzar also carried off to Babylon some of the vessels of the house of the LORD, and he put them in his palace in Babylon.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[8] The rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, the detestable things he did, and all that was found against him are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. And Jehoiachin his son became king in his place.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[9] Jehoiachin was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. [Footnote: The Hebrew text reads "eight years"; the parallel account and some ancient witnesses read "eighteen years."]
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[10] In the spring King Nebuchadnezzar sent and had him brought to Babylon, along with the precious vessels of the house of the LORD, and he made Zedekiah, Jehoiachin's brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem. [Footnote: Hebrew "his brother"; the term can denote a close male relative — Zedekiah was Jehoiachin's uncle.]
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[11] Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[12] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD his God, and he did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke from the mouth of the LORD.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[13] He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear an oath by God. He stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning back to the LORD, the God of Israel.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[14] And all the leaders of the priests and the people multiplied their treachery, following all the detestable practices of the nations, and they defiled the house of the LORD, which he had made holy in Jerusalem.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[15] The LORD, the God of their fathers, sent word to them again and again through his messengers, because he had compassion on his people and on his dwelling place.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[16] But they mocked the messengers of God, despised his words, and scoffed at his prophets, until the wrath of the LORD against his people burned beyond remedy.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[17] So he brought up against them the king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in their own sanctuary. He spared neither young man nor young woman, neither the elderly nor the aged; God gave them all into his hand.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[18] All the vessels of the house of God, great and small, the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king and his officials—all of it he carried off to Babylon.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[19] They burned the house of God, tore down the wall of Jerusalem, set fire to all its palaces, and destroyed all its precious vessels.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[20] Those who survived the sword he carried into exile in Babylon, and they became servants to him and to his sons until the kingdom of Persia came to power—
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[21] to fulfill the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed its sabbaths. All the days it lay desolate it kept sabbath, until seventy years were complete.
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[22] In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, so that the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah might be accomplished, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent a proclamation throughout his kingdom, and also put it in writing:
[2 Chronicles] [36]:[23] "This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has appointed me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Any of you who are of his people—may the LORD his God be with him, and let him go up."
[Ezra] [1]:[1] In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, so that the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah might be fulfilled, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, and he sent a proclamation throughout his whole kingdom, and also put it in writing:
[Ezra] [1]:[2] "This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has charged me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
[Ezra] [1]:[3] Whoever among you belongs to his people—may his God be with him—let him go up to Jerusalem in Judah and build the house of the LORD, the God of Israel, the God who is in Jerusalem.
[Ezra] [1]:[4] And everyone who remains, wherever he lives, let the people of that place support him with silver and gold, with goods and livestock, along with a freewill offering for the house of God in Jerusalem."
[Ezra] [1]:[5] Then the heads of the families of Judah and Benjamin, along with the priests and the Levites—everyone whose spirit God had stirred—set out to go up and build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.
[Ezra] [1]:[6] And all their neighbors strengthened their hands with articles of silver and gold, with goods and livestock and valuable gifts, besides all the freewill offerings.
[Ezra] [1]:[7] King Cyrus also brought out the articles of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had carried off from Jerusalem and placed in the temple of his own god.
[Ezra] [1]:[8] Cyrus king of Persia had them brought out by Mithredath the treasurer, who counted them out to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.
[Ezra] [1]:[9] This was the inventory: thirty gold basins, a thousand silver basins, twenty-nine knives,*
[Ezra] [1]:[10] thirty gold bowls, four hundred and ten silver bowls of a second kind, and a thousand other articles.
[Ezra] [1]:[11] In all there were five thousand four hundred articles of gold and silver. Sheshbazzar brought all of these up with the exiles when they came from Babylon to Jerusalem.

[Ezra] [2]:[62] These searched for their entry in the genealogical records, but it could not be found, so they were excluded from the priesthood as unclean.
[Ezra] [2]:[63] The governor told them not to eat any of the most holy food until a priest should arise to consult the Urim and Thummim.

[Ezra] [2]:[65] besides their male and female servants, of whom there were 7,337; and they had 200 male and female singers.
[Ezra] [2]:[66] Their horses numbered 736, their mules 245,
[Ezra] [2]:[67] their camels 435, and their donkeys 6,720.
[Ezra] [2]:[68] When they arrived at the house of the LORD in Jerusalem, some of the heads of families made freewill offerings toward the house of God, to rebuild it on its site.
[Ezra] [2]:[69] According to their ability they gave to the treasury for the work 61,000 darics of gold, 5,000 minas of silver, and 100 priestly garments.
[Ezra] [2]:[70] So the priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants settled in their towns, and all Israel in their towns.
[Ezra] [3]:[1] When the seventh month came, and the Israelites were settled in their towns, the people gathered as one in Jerusalem.
[Ezra] [3]:[2] Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, together with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his kinsmen, set to work and rebuilt the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it as prescribed in the Law of Moses, the man of God.
[Ezra] [3]:[3] They set the altar on its foundations, for they were in dread of the peoples of the surrounding lands, and they offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD, both morning and evening offerings.
[Ezra] [3]:[4] They celebrated the Festival of Booths as it is written, offering the daily burnt offerings by number, as the ordinance required for each day,
[Ezra] [3]:[5] and after that the regular daily offerings, the offerings for the new moons and for all the appointed festivals of the LORD, as well as the freewill offerings brought to the LORD.
[Ezra] [3]:[6] From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, though the foundation of the LORD's temple had not yet been laid.
[Ezra] [3]:[7] They gave money to the masons and carpenters, and food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre, so that they would ship cedar logs from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, as authorized by Cyrus king of Persia.
[Ezra] [3]:[8] In the second month of the second year after their arrival at the house of God in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak, along with the rest of their kinsmen—the priests and the Levites and all who had come back from captivity to Jerusalem—began the work, and they appointed Levites twenty years old and upward to supervise the building of the house of the LORD.
[Ezra] [3]:[9] So Jeshua with his sons and kinsmen, and Kadmiel with his sons, the descendants of Judah, stood together to oversee those working on the house of God, along with the sons of Henadad with their sons and kinsmen, the Levites.
[Ezra] [3]:[10] When the builders had laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, the priests took their places in their vestments with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD according to the directions of David king of Israel.
[Ezra] [3]:[11] And they sang responsively, praising and giving thanks to the LORD: "He is good; his steadfast love toward Israel endures forever." Then all the people raised a great shout of praise to the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid.
[Ezra] [3]:[12] But many of the priests and Levites and heads of families, the old men who had seen the first house, wept aloud when they saw the foundation of this house being laid, while many others shouted for joy.
[Ezra] [3]:[13] No one could distinguish the sound of the shouts of joy from the sound of weeping, for the people raised such a great shout that the noise was heard far away.
[Ezra] [4]:[1] When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returned exiles were building a temple for the LORD, the God of Israel,
[Ezra] [4]:[2] they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of the families and said to them, "Let us build with you, for we seek your God as you do, and we have been sacrificing to him ever since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us here."
[Ezra] [4]:[3] But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of Israel's families answered them, "You have nothing to do with us in building a house for our God. We ourselves will build for the LORD, the God of Israel, just as King Cyrus, king of Persia, commanded us."
[Ezra] [4]:[4] Then the people of the land kept weakening the hands of the people of Judah and making them afraid to build.
[Ezra] [4]:[5] They bribed officials to work against them and frustrate their plans throughout the reign of Cyrus king of Persia and on into the reign of Darius king of Persia.
[Ezra] [4]:[6] In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
[Ezra] [4]:[7] And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of their associates wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia. The letter was written in Aramaic script and set out in the Aramaic language.
[Ezra] [4]:[8] Rehum the commanding officer and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes as follows:
[Ezra] [4]:[9] From Rehum the commanding officer, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates—the judges, the envoys, the officials, the Persians, the men of Erech, the Babylonians, the men of Susa, that is, the Elamites,
[Ezra] [4]:[10] together with the rest of the peoples whom the great and honorable Osnappar deported and settled in the city of Samaria and elsewhere in the province Beyond the River. And now:
[Ezra] [4]:[11] This is a copy of the letter they sent him: To King Artaxerxes, from your servants, the men of the province Beyond the River. And now:
[Ezra] [4]:[12] Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from you to us have arrived at Jerusalem. They are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city; they are finishing its walls and repairing its foundations.
[Ezra] [4]:[13] Now let it be known to the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, they will pay no tribute, tax, or toll, and the royal revenue will suffer.
[Ezra] [4]:[14] Now because we eat the salt of the palace, and it is not right for us to watch the king be dishonored, we send this word to inform the king,
[Ezra] [4]:[15] so that a search may be made in the record books of your fathers. In those records you will find and learn that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and that from ancient times revolt has been stirred up within it. That is why this city was laid waste.
[Ezra] [4]:[16] We inform the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are finished, you will no longer have any holding in the province Beyond the River.
[Ezra] [4]:[17] The king sent this reply: To Rehum the commanding officer, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their associates who live in Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River: Greetings. And now:
[Ezra] [4]:[18] The letter you sent us has been read out clearly in my presence.
[Ezra] [4]:[19] I gave the order, and a search was made, and it was found that this city has risen against kings from ancient times, and that rebellion and revolt have been carried on in it.
[Ezra] [4]:[20] Mighty kings have ruled in Jerusalem and governed the whole province Beyond the River, and tribute, tax, and toll were paid to them.
[Ezra] [4]:[21] Now give the order to make these men stop, so that this city is not rebuilt until I issue a further decree.
[Ezra] [4]:[22] See that you are not negligent in this matter. Why should the damage grow and the kings be harmed?
[Ezra] [4]:[23] As soon as the copy of the letter of King Artaxerxes was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their associates, they hurried to the Jews in Jerusalem and forced them to stop by force of arms.
[Ezra] [4]:[24] So the work on the house of God in Jerusalem came to a halt, and it stood still until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.
[Ezra] [5]:[1] Now Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, the prophets, prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.
[Ezra] [5]:[2] Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak set to work and began to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem, and the prophets of God were with them, supporting them.
[Ezra] [5]:[3] At that time Tattenai, the governor of the province Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and their associates came to them and said, "Who gave you authority to build this house and to complete this structure?"
[Ezra] [5]:[4] Then we said to them, "What are the names of the men who are constructing this building?"
[Ezra] [5]:[5] But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, and they were not stopped until a report could go to Darius and an answer be sent back concerning it.
[Ezra] [5]:[6] This is a copy of the letter that Tattenai, the governor of the province Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and his associates, the officials of the province Beyond the River, sent to King Darius.
[Ezra] [5]:[7] They sent him a report, and this is what was written in it: To King Darius, all peace.
[Ezra] [5]:[8] Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. It is being built with massive stones, and timber is being set into the walls. The work is being done with diligence and is prospering in their hands.
[Ezra] [5]:[9] Then we questioned those elders and said to them, "Who gave you authority to build this house and to complete this structure?"
[Ezra] [5]:[10] We also asked them their names, so that we could inform you by writing down the names of the men who lead them.
[Ezra] [5]:[11] And this is the answer they gave us: "We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the house that was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel built and finished.
[Ezra] [5]:[12] But because our fathers provoked the God of heaven to anger, he handed them over to Nebuchadnezzar the Chaldean, king of Babylon, who tore down this house and carried the people away to Babylon.
[Ezra] [5]:[13] Yet in the first year of Cyrus, king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued a decree that this house of God be rebuilt.
[Ezra] [5]:[14] Moreover, the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to the temple in Babylon—these King Cyrus took out of the temple in Babylon and handed over to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he had appointed governor.
[Ezra] [5]:[15] He said to him, "Take these vessels, go and deposit them in the temple in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be rebuilt on its site."
[Ezra] [5]:[16] So this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem, and from that time until now it has been under construction, and it is not yet finished."
[Ezra] [5]:[17] Now then, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the royal archives there in Babylon, to see whether a decree was in fact issued by King Cyrus for the rebuilding of this house of God in Jerusalem. And let the king send us his decision in this matter.
[Ezra] [6]:[1] Then King Darius issued an order, and a search was made in the archives where the treasures were stored in Babylon.
[Ezra] [6]:[2] And at Ecbatana, in the fortress in the province of Media, a scroll was found, and this is what was written in it:
[Ezra] [6]:[3] "In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus issued this order concerning the house of God in Jerusalem: Let the house be rebuilt as a place for offering sacrifices, and let its foundations be laid. Its height shall be sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits,
[Ezra] [6]:[4] with three courses of dressed stone and one course of timber. The cost is to be paid from the royal treasury.
[Ezra] [6]:[5] Moreover, the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, are to be returned. They shall be brought back to their place in the temple in Jerusalem and deposited in the house of God."
[Ezra] [6]:[6] Now then, Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates, the officials of Beyond the River: keep far away from there.
[Ezra] [6]:[7] Leave the work on this house of God alone. Let the governor of the Jews and the elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God on its site.
[Ezra] [6]:[8] I also issue this decree concerning what you are to do for these elders of the Jews in the building of this house of God: the cost is to be paid in full to these men from the royal treasury, out of the tribute of Beyond the River, so that the work is not halted.
[Ezra] [6]:[9] Whatever is needed—young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, along with wheat, salt, wine, and oil—is to be given to them daily without fail, according to the word of the priests in Jerusalem,
[Ezra] [6]:[10] so that they may offer pleasing sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.
[Ezra] [6]:[11] I further decree that if anyone alters this order, a beam shall be pulled from his house, and he shall be impaled on it, and his house shall be made a ruin because of this.
[Ezra] [6]:[12] And may the God who has caused his name to dwell there overthrow any king or people who lifts a hand to alter this or to destroy this house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued this decree; let it be carried out with all diligence.
[Ezra] [6]:[13] Then Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates carried out with all diligence exactly what King Darius had sent word to do.
[Ezra] [6]:[14] So the elders of the Jews went on building and prospering through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished the building according to the command of the God of Israel and the decree of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
[Ezra] [6]:[15] This house was completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
[Ezra] [6]:[16] Then the people of Israel—the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the returned exiles—celebrated the dedication of this house of God with joy.
[Ezra] [6]:[17] For the dedication of this house of God they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs, and as a sin offering for all Israel twelve male goats, one for each of the tribes of Israel.
[Ezra] [6]:[18] They installed the priests in their groups and the Levites in their divisions for the service of God in Jerusalem, as prescribed in the book of Moses.
[Ezra] [6]:[19] On the fourteenth day of the first month the returned exiles kept the Passover.
[Ezra] [6]:[20] For the priests and the Levites had purified themselves together; all of them were clean. They slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the returned exiles, for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.
[Ezra] [6]:[21] So the Israelites who had returned from exile ate it, together with all who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the peoples of the land to seek the LORD, the God of Israel.
[Ezra] [6]:[22] For seven days they kept the Festival of Unleavened Bread with joy, because the LORD had filled them with joy and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, so that he supported them in the work on the house of God, the God of Israel.
[Ezra] [7]:[1] After all this, during the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, there came Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
[Ezra] [7]:[2] son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
[Ezra] [7]:[3] son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
[Ezra] [7]:[4] son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
[Ezra] [7]:[5] son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest.
[Ezra] [7]:[6] This Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given; and because the hand of the LORD his God was upon him, the king granted him everything he asked.
[Ezra] [7]:[7] Some of the Israelites, along with priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants, went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
[Ezra] [7]:[8] Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of that seventh year of the king.
[Ezra] [7]:[9] He had set out from Babylon on the first day of the first month, and he came to Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, for the good hand of his God was upon him.
[Ezra] [7]:[10] For Ezra had set his heart to study the Law of the LORD, to do it, and to teach its statutes and judgments in Israel.
[Ezra] [7]:[11] This is a copy of the letter King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest and scribe, a scholar in matters concerning the commandments and statutes of the LORD for Israel:
[Ezra] [7]:[12] Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest, scribe of the Law of the God of heaven: Greetings.
[Ezra] [7]:[13] I hereby decree that any of the people of Israel in my kingdom, including their priests and Levites, who freely choose to go up to Jerusalem, may go with you.
[Ezra] [7]:[14] For you are sent by the king and his seven counselors to inquire about Judah and Jerusalem according to the Law of your God, which is in your hand,
[Ezra] [7]:[15] and to bring the silver and gold that the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,
[Ezra] [7]:[16] together with all the silver and gold you may obtain throughout the province of Babylon, along with the freewill offerings of the people and the priests for the house of their God in Jerusalem.
[Ezra] [7]:[17] Therefore with this money you are to buy without delay bulls, rams, and lambs, with their grain offerings and drink offerings, and offer them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
[Ezra] [7]:[18] Whatever seems best to you and your brothers to do with the rest of the silver and gold, do it according to the will of your God.
[Ezra] [7]:[19] And the vessels entrusted to you for the service of the house of your God, deliver them before the God of Jerusalem.
[Ezra] [7]:[20] Whatever else is needed for the house of your God, whatever you must provide, pay for it from the royal treasury.
[Ezra] [7]:[21] I, King Artaxerxes, further decree to all the treasurers of the province Beyond the River: whatever Ezra the priest, scribe of the Law of the God of heaven, asks of you, it shall be done with all diligence —
[Ezra] [7]:[22] up to a hundred talents of silver, a hundred cors of wheat, a hundred baths of wine, a hundred baths of oil, and salt without limit.
[Ezra] [7]:[23] Whatever the God of heaven has commanded, let it be done with care for the house of the God of heaven, so that no wrath may come upon the realm of the king and his sons.
[Ezra] [7]:[24] Be it also known to you that no tax, tribute, or toll may be imposed on any of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, or other servants of this house of God.
[Ezra] [7]:[25] And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God that is in your hand, appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people in the province Beyond the River — all who know the laws of your God; and teach those who do not know them.
[Ezra] [7]:[26] And whoever will not obey the Law of your God and the law of the king, let judgment be executed on him with all diligence: death, banishment, confiscation of property, or imprisonment.
[Ezra] [7]:[27] Blessed be the LORD, the God of our fathers, who put it into the king's heart to glorify the house of the LORD in Jerusalem,
[Ezra] [7]:[28] and who extended his steadfast love to me before the king, his counselors, and all the king's mighty officials. And I took courage, for the hand of the LORD my God was upon me, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
[Ezra] [8]:[1] These are the heads of their families, and this is the genealogical record of those who came up with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes:
[Ezra] [8]:[2] Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; of the sons of David, Hattush;
[Ezra] [8]:[3] of the sons of Shecaniah; of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him 150 men registered by genealogy;
[Ezra] [8]:[4] of the sons of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him 200 men;
[Ezra] [8]:[5] of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel, and with him 300 men;
[Ezra] [8]:[6] of the sons of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him 50 men;
[Ezra] [8]:[7] of the sons of Elam, Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him 70 men;
[Ezra] [8]:[8] of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him 80 men;
[Ezra] [8]:[9] of the sons of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him 218 men;
[Ezra] [8]:[10] of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him 160 men;
[Ezra] [8]:[11] of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him 28 men;
[Ezra] [8]:[12] of the sons of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him 110 men;
[Ezra] [8]:[13] of the sons of Adonikam, the last ones, whose names were Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, and with them 60 men;
[Ezra] [8]:[14] and of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zaccur, and with him 70 men.
[Ezra] [8]:[15] I assembled them at the river that flows toward Ahava, and we camped there three days. When I reviewed the people and the priests, I found no Levites among them.
[Ezra] [8]:[16] So I summoned Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, who were leaders, and Joiarib and Elnathan, who were men of insight.
[Ezra] [8]:[17] I sent them to Iddo, the leader at the place called Casiphia, and I told them what to say to Iddo and his kinsmen, the temple servants at Casiphia—that they should bring us ministers for the house of our God.
[Ezra] [8]:[18] Since the gracious hand of our God was upon us, they brought us a capable man from the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi, the son of Israel—Sherebiah—along with his sons and brothers, eighteen men;
[Ezra] [8]:[19] also Hashabiah, and with him Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari, with his brothers and their sons, twenty men;
[Ezra] [8]:[20] and 220 of the temple servants, whom David and his officials had appointed to assist the Levites. All of them were registered by name.
[Ezra] [8]:[21] There by the Ahava River I proclaimed a fast, that we might humble ourselves before our God and ask him for a safe journey for ourselves, our children, and all our possessions.
[Ezra] [8]:[22] I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from enemies along the way, since we had told him, "The hand of our God is upon all who seek him, for good; but his power and his anger are against all who forsake him."
[Ezra] [8]:[23] So we fasted and pleaded with our God about this, and he answered our prayer.
[Ezra] [8]:[24] Then I set apart twelve of the leading priests, together with Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers,
[Ezra] [8]:[25] and I weighed out to them the silver, the gold, and the vessels—the offering for the house of our God that the king, his counselors, his officials, and all Israel who were present had donated.
[Ezra] [8]:[26] I weighed out into their hands 650 talents of silver, silver vessels weighing 100 talents, 100 talents of gold,
[Ezra] [8]:[27] twenty golden bowls worth a thousand darics, and two vessels of fine polished bronze, as precious as gold.
[Ezra] [8]:[28] And I said to them, "You are holy to the LORD, and these vessels are holy. The silver and the gold are a freewill offering to the LORD, the God of your fathers.
[Ezra] [8]:[29] Guard them carefully until you weigh them out in Jerusalem, in the chambers of the house of the LORD, before the leading priests, the Levites, and the heads of the families of Israel."
[Ezra] [8]:[30] So the priests and the Levites took charge of the silver, the gold, and the vessels that had been weighed out, to bring them to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.
[Ezra] [8]:[31] On the twelfth day of the first month we set out from the Ahava River to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was upon us, and he protected us from enemies and from bandits along the way.
[Ezra] [8]:[32] We arrived in Jerusalem and stayed there three days.
[Ezra] [8]:[33] On the fourth day the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed out in the house of our God into the hands of Meremoth son of Uriah the priest, and with him Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
[Ezra] [8]:[34] Everything was counted and weighed, and the entire weight was recorded at that time.
[Ezra] [8]:[35] Then those who had come back from exile, the returning captives, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve goats as a sin offering—all of it a burnt offering to the LORD.
[Ezra] [8]:[36] They also delivered the king's decrees to the royal satraps and to the governors of the province Beyond the River, and they gave their support to the people and to the house of God.
[Ezra] [9]:[1] When all this had been done, the officials came to me and said: "The people of Israel, along with the priests and the Levites, have not kept themselves separate from the peoples of the lands and their detestable practices—from the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.
[Ezra] [9]:[2] They have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and for their sons, so that the holy seed has been mingled with the peoples of the lands. And the officials and leaders have led the way in this unfaithfulness."
[Ezra] [9]:[3] When I heard this, I tore my garment and my robe, pulled hair from my head and my beard, and sat down appalled.
[Ezra] [9]:[4] Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles, while I sat appalled until the evening offering.
[Ezra] [9]:[5] At the evening offering I rose from my fasting, and having torn my garment and my robe, I fell on my knees and spread out my hands to the LORD my God.
[Ezra] [9]:[6] I prayed: "My God, I am ashamed and disgraced to lift up my face to you, my God, for our iniquities have risen higher than our heads, and our guilt has grown up to the heavens.
[Ezra] [9]:[7] From the days of our fathers to this day our guilt has been great. Because of our iniquities we, our kings, and our priests have been handed over to the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to open shame, as it is today.
[Ezra] [9]:[8] But now, for a brief moment, the LORD our God has shown us grace by leaving us a remnant and giving us a stake in his holy place, so that our God may brighten our eyes and grant us a little relief in our bondage.
[Ezra] [9]:[9] For we are slaves; yet in our bondage our God has not forsaken us. He has extended to us his steadfast love before the kings of Persia, giving us new life to raise up the house of our God and restore its ruins, and granting us a wall of protection in Judah and Jerusalem.
[Ezra] [9]:[10] And now, our God, what can we say after this? For we have abandoned your commandments,
[Ezra] [9]:[11] which you gave through your servants the prophets when you said: 'The land you are entering to possess is a land defiled by the impurity of its peoples, by their detestable practices, which have filled it with their uncleanness from one end to the other.
[Ezra] [9]:[12] Therefore do not give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters for your sons, and never seek their peace or their prosperity, so that you may be strong and eat the good of the land and leave it as an inheritance to your children forever.'
[Ezra] [9]:[13] After all that has come upon us because of our evil deeds and our great guilt—and you, our God, have punished us less than our iniquities deserve and have given us such a remnant as this—
[Ezra] [9]:[14] shall we again break your commandments and intermarry with the peoples who practice these abominations? Would you not be angry enough with us to destroy us, leaving no remnant, no survivor?
[Ezra] [9]:[15] LORD, God of Israel, you are righteous, for we are left as a remnant, as we are this day. Here we are before you in our guilt, for because of it no one can stand in your presence."
[Ezra] [10]:[1] While Ezra was praying and making this confession, weeping and lying prostrate before the house of God, a very large assembly of Israel gathered around him—men, women, and children—for the people were weeping bitterly.
[Ezra] [10]:[2] Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, one of the descendants of Elam, spoke up and said to Ezra: "We have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women from the peoples of the land. Yet even now there is hope for Israel in spite of this.
[Ezra] [10]:[3] So let us now make a covenant with our God to send away all these women along with their children, according to the counsel of the Lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God. Let it be done according to the Law.
[Ezra] [10]:[4] Rise up, for this matter rests on you, and we stand with you. Take courage and act."
[Ezra] [10]:[5] So Ezra rose and made the leading priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to do as had been said—and they took the oath.
[Ezra] [10]:[6] Then Ezra withdrew from before the house of God and went to the chamber of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. There he spent the night, eating no bread and drinking no water, for he was mourning over the unfaithfulness of those who had returned from exile.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew text reads "and he went there"; "spent the night" follows an ancient reading supported by early versions.
[Ezra] [10]:[7] A proclamation was then issued throughout Judah and Jerusalem, calling all the returned exiles to assemble in Jerusalem.
[Ezra] [10]:[8] Anyone who failed to appear within three days would, by decision of the leaders and the elders, forfeit all his property and be excluded from the assembly of the exiles.
[Ezra] [10]:[9] So all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered in Jerusalem within the three days. It was the twentieth day of the ninth month. All the people sat in the open square before the house of God, trembling because of this matter and because of the heavy rain.
[Ezra] [10]:[10] Then Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, "You have been unfaithful. You have married foreign women and so added to the guilt of Israel.
[Ezra] [10]:[11] Now then, make confession to the LORD, the God of your fathers, and do his will: separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from your foreign wives."
[Ezra] [10]:[12] The whole assembly answered with a loud voice: "Yes! It is our duty to do as you say.
[Ezra] [10]:[13] But the people are many, and it is the rainy season; we cannot stand out in the open. Besides, this is not the work of one day or two, for we have sinned greatly in this matter.
[Ezra] [10]:[14] Let our leaders act for the whole assembly. Then let everyone in our towns who has married a foreign woman come at appointed times, together with the elders and judges of each town, until the fierce anger of our God over this matter is turned away from us."
[Ezra] [10]:[15] Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah opposed this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite supported them.
[Ezra] [10]:[16] So the returned exiles did as had been proposed. Ezra the priest selected men who were heads of families, each designated by name according to his father's house. On the first day of the tenth month they sat down to examine the matter,
[Ezra] [10]:[17] and by the first day of the first month they had finished dealing with all the men who had married foreign women.
[Ezra] [10]:[18] Among the descendants of the priests, these were found to have married foreign women: from the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and his brothers—Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.
[Ezra] [10]:[19] They pledged themselves to send away their wives, and being guilty, they presented a ram from the flock as their guilt offering.
[Ezra] [10]:[20] From the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
[Ezra] [10]:[21] From the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
[Ezra] [10]:[22] From the sons of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
[Ezra] [10]:[23] Among the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
[Ezra] [10]:[24] Among the singers: Eliashib. Among the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
[Ezra] [10]:[25] And among the rest of Israel: from the sons of Parosh—Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
[Ezra] [10]:[26] From the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
[Ezra] [10]:[27] From the sons of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
[Ezra] [10]:[28] From the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
[Ezra] [10]:[29] From the sons of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Ramoth.
[Ezra] [10]:[30] From the sons of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
[Ezra] [10]:[31] From the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Ishijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,
[Ezra] [10]:[32] Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah.
[Ezra] [10]:[33] From the sons of Hashum: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
[Ezra] [10]:[34] From the sons of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel,
[Ezra] [10]:[35] Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhi,
[Ezra] [10]:[36] Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,
[Ezra] [10]:[37] Mattaniah, Mattenai, Jaasu,
[Ezra] [10]:[38] Bani, Binnui, Shimei,
[Ezra] [10]:[39] Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah,
[Ezra] [10]:[40] Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,
[Ezra] [10]:[41] Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,
[Ezra] [10]:[42] Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.
[Ezra] [10]:[43] From the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.
[Ezra] [10]:[44] All of these had married foreign women, and some of these wives had borne children.
[Nehemiah] [1]:[1] The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, I was in the citadel of Susa.
[Nehemiah] [1]:[2] Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some men from Judah, and I questioned them about the Jews who had survived, those left from the exile, and about Jerusalem.
[Nehemiah] [1]:[3] They told me, "Those who survived the exile and remain in the province are in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned with fire."
[Nehemiah] [1]:[4] When I heard these words, I sat down and wept. For days I mourned, fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
[Nehemiah] [1]:[5] I said: "LORD, God of heaven, the great and awesome God, who keeps his covenant of steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments,
[Nehemiah] [1]:[6] let your ear be attentive and your eyes open to hear the prayer of your servant, which I pray before you today, day and night, for your servants, the people of Israel. I confess the sins we Israelites have committed against you. Both I and my father's house have sinned.
[Nehemiah] [1]:[7] We have acted corruptly toward you and have not kept the commandments, statutes, and ordinances you gave your servant Moses.
[Nehemiah] [1]:[8] Remember, I pray, the word you commanded your servant Moses: 'If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations;
[Nehemiah] [1]:[9] but if you return to me and keep my commandments and do them, then even if your exiles are at the farthest horizon, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place I have chosen as a dwelling for my name.'
[Nehemiah] [1]:[10] They are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your great power and your mighty hand.
[Nehemiah] [1]:[11] Lord, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant and to the prayer of your servants who delight in revering your name. Grant your servant success today, and give him compassion in the presence of this man." I was the king's cupbearer.
[Nehemiah] [2]:[1] In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, when wine was set before him, I took the wine and handed it to the king. I had never been downcast in his presence before,
[Nehemiah] [2]:[2] so the king said to me, "Why does your face look so sad, when you are not ill? This can be nothing but sadness of heart." Then I was very much afraid,
[Nehemiah] [2]:[3] and I said to the king, "May the king live forever! Why should my face not be sad, when the city where my ancestors are buried lies in ruins and its gates have been consumed by fire?"
[Nehemiah] [2]:[4] The king said to me, "What is it you want?" So I prayed to the God of heaven,
[Nehemiah] [2]:[5] and then answered the king, "If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor with you, send me to Judah, to the city where my ancestors are buried, so that I may rebuild it."
[Nehemiah] [2]:[6] Then the king, with the queen sitting beside him, asked me, "How long will your journey take, and when will you return?" It pleased the king to send me, and I set him a time.
[Nehemiah] [2]:[7] I also said to the king, "If it pleases the king, let letters be given me for the governors of the province Beyond the River, so that they will grant me passage until I reach Judah;
[Nehemiah] [2]:[8] and a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king's forest, so that he will give me timber to make beams for the gates of the citadel by the temple, for the city wall, and for the house I will occupy." And the king granted my requests, for the gracious hand of my God was upon me.
[Nehemiah] [2]:[9] So I came to the governors of the province Beyond the River and gave them the king's letters. The king had also sent army officers and cavalry with me.
[Nehemiah] [2]:[10] When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard of this, they were deeply disturbed that someone had come to seek the welfare of the Israelites.
[Nehemiah] [2]:[11] I came to Jerusalem, and after I had been there three days,
[Nehemiah] [2]:[12] I set out at night with a few men. I had told no one what my God had laid on my heart to do for Jerusalem. There was no animal with me except the one I was riding.
[Nehemiah] [2]:[13] By night I went out through the Valley Gate toward the Dragon Spring and the Dung Gate, inspecting the walls of Jerusalem, which had been broken down, and its gates, which had been consumed by fire.
[Nehemiah] [2]:[14] Then I went on to the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, but there was no room for my mount to get through.
[Nehemiah] [2]:[15] So I went up the valley by night, inspecting the wall. Then I turned back and came in again through the Valley Gate, and so returned.
[Nehemiah] [2]:[16] The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was doing, for as yet I had said nothing to the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials, or any of the others who would be doing the work.
[Nehemiah] [2]:[17] Then I said to them, "You see the trouble we are in: Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned with fire. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, and we will no longer be a disgrace."
[Nehemiah] [2]:[18] I told them how the gracious hand of my God had been upon me, and what the king had said to me. They replied, "Let us start rebuilding." So they set their hands to the good work.
[Nehemiah] [2]:[19] But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard about it, they mocked and ridiculed us. "What is this you are doing?" they said. "Are you rebelling against the king?"
[Nehemiah] [2]:[20] I answered them, "The God of heaven will give us success. We his servants will start rebuilding, but as for you, you have no share, no claim, and no historic right in Jerusalem."
[Nehemiah] [3]:[1] Then Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests set to work and rebuilt the Sheep Gate. They consecrated it and set its doors in place, and they consecrated the wall as far as the Tower of the Hundred, all the way to the Tower of Hananel.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[2] Next to him the men of Jericho built, and next to them Zaccur son of Imri.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[3] The Fish Gate was rebuilt by the sons of Hassenaah. They laid its beams and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[4] Next to them Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, made repairs. Next to them Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, made repairs, and next to them Zadok son of Baana.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[5] Next to them the men of Tekoa made repairs, but their nobles would not put their shoulders to the work of their Lord.[fn: The Hebrew word can mean either their Lord (God) or their lords, that is, their supervisors.]
[Nehemiah] [3]:[6] The Old Gate was repaired by Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah. They laid its beams and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[7] Next to them Melatiah of Gibeon and Jadon of Meronoth made repairs, along with the men of Gibeon and Mizpah, which was under the authority of the governor of the province Beyond the River.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[8] Next to him Uzziel son of Harhaiah, a goldsmith, made repairs, and next to him Hananiah, a perfumer. They restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[9] Next to them Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[10] Next to them Jedaiah son of Harumaph made repairs opposite his own house, and next to him Hattush son of Hashabniah.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[11] Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-Moab repaired another section, along with the Tower of the Ovens.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[12] Next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of the other half of the district of Jerusalem, made repairs, he and his daughters.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[13] The Valley Gate was repaired by Hanun and the residents of Zanoah. They rebuilt it and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place, and they repaired a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the Dung Gate.[fn: About 450 metres or 1,500 feet.]
[Nehemiah] [3]:[14] The Dung Gate was repaired by Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth Haccherem. He rebuilt it and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[15] The Fountain Gate was repaired by Shallun son of Col-Hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah. He rebuilt it, roofed it over, and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place. He also repaired the wall of the Pool of Shelah by the King's Garden, as far as the steps that go down from the City of David.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[16] After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth Zur, made repairs to a point opposite the tombs of David, as far as the pool that was made and the House of the Warriors.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[17] Next to him the Levites made repairs under Rehum son of Bani. Beside him Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his own district.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[18] Next to him their fellow Levites made repairs under Binnui son of Henadad, ruler of the other half of the district of Keilah.[fn: The Hebrew text reads Bavvai here; he is probably the same man called Binnui in verse 24.]
[Nehemiah] [3]:[19] Next to him Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section, from a point facing the ascent to the armory as far as the angle in the wall.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[20] Next to him Baruch son of Zabbai worked with zeal, repairing another section from the angle to the entrance of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[21] Next to him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the entrance of Eliashib's house to the far end of it.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[22] Next to him the priests from the surrounding countryside made repairs.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[23] Next to them Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs in front of their house, and next to them Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, made repairs beside his house.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[24] Next to him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the angle and the corner,
[Nehemiah] [3]:[25] and Palal son of Uzai worked opposite the angle and the tower projecting from the upper palace of the king, beside the court of the guard. Next to him was Pedaiah son of Parosh.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[26] The temple servants were living on Ophel, and they made repairs up to a point opposite the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[27] Next to them the men of Tekoa repaired another section, from the great projecting tower to the wall of Ophel.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[28] Above the Horse Gate the priests made repairs, each in front of his own house.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[29] Next to them Zadok son of Immer made repairs opposite his house, and next to him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the East Gate.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[30] Next to him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. Next to them Meshullam son of Berechiah made repairs opposite his living quarters.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[31] Next to him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and the merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate, and on to the upper room at the corner.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[32] And between the upper room at the corner and the Sheep Gate the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[33] When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he flew into a rage and, seething with anger, ridiculed the Jews.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[34] In the presence of his associates and the army of Samaria he said, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore things for themselves? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Can they bring stones back to life out of heaps of rubble, burned as they are?"
[Nehemiah] [3]:[35] Tobiah the Ammonite, standing beside him, said, "Whatever they build—if even a fox climbed up on it, it would break down their wall of stones!"
[Nehemiah] [3]:[36] Hear us, our God, for we are despised. Turn their taunts back on their own heads, and hand them over as plunder in a land of captivity.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[37] Do not cover over their guilt, and do not let their sin be blotted out from before you, for they have provoked you to anger in the presence of the builders.
[Nehemiah] [3]:[38] So we rebuilt the wall, and it was joined together all the way around to half its height, for the people had a heart to work.
[Nehemiah] [4]:[1] When Sanballat and Tobiah, along with the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the men of Ashdod, heard that the repair of the walls of Jerusalem was moving ahead and that the gaps were being closed, they were furious.
[Nehemiah] [4]:[2] They all conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem and throw it into confusion.
[Nehemiah] [4]:[3] But we prayed to our God, and because of the threat we posted a guard against them day and night.
[Nehemiah] [4]:[4] Meanwhile the people of Judah said, "The strength of the laborers is failing, and there is far too much rubble; we cannot rebuild the wall."
[Nehemiah] [4]:[5] And our enemies said, "Before they know it or see a thing, we will be in among them. We will kill them and put an end to the work."
[Nehemiah] [4]:[6] Then the Jews who lived near them came and warned us ten times over, "Wherever you turn, they will come against us."
[Nehemiah] [4]:[7] So I stationed men in the lowest places behind the wall, at the exposed points, positioning them by families with their swords, their spears, and their bows.
[Nehemiah] [4]:[8] I looked things over, then rose and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people: "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your homes."
[Nehemiah] [4]:[9] When our enemies heard that we knew of their scheme and that God had frustrated it, we all returned to the wall, each to his own work.
[Nehemiah] [4]:[10] From that day on, half of my men did the work while the other half stood ready with spears, shields, bows, and armor; and the officers took their place behind all the people of Judah
[Nehemiah] [4]:[11] who were building the wall. Those who carried loads worked with one hand and held a weapon in the other,
[Nehemiah] [4]:[12] and each of the builders worked with his sword strapped to his waist. The man who sounded the trumpet stayed beside me.
[Nehemiah] [4]:[13] I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, "The work is vast and spread out, and we are far apart from one another along the wall.
[Nehemiah] [4]:[14] Wherever you hear the trumpet sound, rally to us there. Our God will fight for us!"
[Nehemiah] [4]:[15] So we carried on the work, half of the men holding spears, from the first light of dawn until the stars came out.
[Nehemiah] [4]:[16] At that time I also told the people, "Let every man and his servant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they may stand guard for us by night and work by day."
[Nehemiah] [4]:[17] Neither I nor my brothers nor my men nor the guards with me ever took off our clothes; each of us kept his weapon at hand, even when going for water.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[1] Then a great outcry arose from the people and their wives against their fellow Jews.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[2] Some were saying, "With our sons and daughters we are many; we must get grain so we can eat and stay alive."
[Nehemiah] [5]:[3] Others were saying, "We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards, and our houses to get grain during the famine."
[Nehemiah] [5]:[4] And still others were saying, "We have borrowed money against our fields and vineyards to pay the king's tax.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[5] Now our flesh is the same as the flesh of our brothers, our children the same as theirs, yet here we are forcing our sons and daughters into slavery. Some of our daughters have already been enslaved, and we are powerless to act, for our fields and vineyards belong to others.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[6] When I heard their outcry and these complaints, I was furious.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[7] After thinking it over, I brought charges against the nobles and officials. I told them, "You are exacting interest from your own brothers!" And I called a great assembly to deal with them.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[8] I said to them, "As far as we were able, we have bought back our fellow Jews who had been sold to the nations. And now you are selling your own brothers, only for them to be sold back to us!" They said nothing, for they could find no answer.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[9] So I continued, "What you are doing is not right. Should you not walk in the fear of our God to avoid the taunts of the nations, our enemies?
[Nehemiah] [5]:[10] I myself, along with my brothers and my men, have been lending the people money and grain. Let us stop charging interest!
[Nehemiah] [5]:[11] Give back to them this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves, and their houses, and also the hundredth part of the money, the grain, the new wine, and the oil that you have exacted from them."
[Nehemiah] [5]:[12] They answered, "We will give it back, and we will demand nothing more from them. We will do just as you say." Then I summoned the priests and made them take an oath to keep this promise.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[13] I also shook out the fold of my robe and said, "So may God shake out of his house and his property every man who does not keep this promise. May he be shaken out and left empty!" The whole assembly said, "Amen," and praised the LORD. And the people did as they had promised.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[14] Moreover, from the day I was appointed governor in the land of Judah—from the twentieth year until the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, twelve years in all—neither I nor my brothers ate the food allotted to the governor.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[15] The earlier governors, my predecessors, had laid a heavy burden on the people, taking food and wine from them, besides forty shekels of silver. Their assistants also lorded it over the people. But I did not act that way, because I feared God.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[16] What is more, I devoted myself to the work on this wall. We bought no land, and all my men were gathered there for the work.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[17] Furthermore, a hundred and fifty Jews and officials ate at my table, along with those who came to us from the surrounding nations.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[18] Each day one ox, six choice sheep, and poultry were prepared for me, and every ten days an abundant supply of wine. Yet in spite of all this, I never demanded the food allotted to the governor, because the burden on this people was heavy.
[Nehemiah] [5]:[19] Remember me with favor, my God, for all I have done for this people.
[Nehemiah] [6]:[1] When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and that not a single gap was left in it—though at that time I had not yet set the doors in the gates—
[Nehemiah] [6]:[2] Sanballat and Geshem sent me this message: "Come, let us meet together at Hakkephirim^ in the plain of Ono." But they were plotting to do me harm. ^ Or "in one of the villages"; the Hebrew word can be read either as a place name or as a common noun.
[Nehemiah] [6]:[3] So I sent messengers to them with this reply: "I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and come down to you?"
[Nehemiah] [6]:[4] Four times they sent me the same message, and each time I gave them the same answer.
[Nehemiah] [6]:[5] The fifth time, Sanballat sent his servant to me with the same message, and in his hand was an open letter.
[Nehemiah] [6]:[6] In it was written: "It is reported among the nations—and Geshem says it too—that you and the Jews are planning to revolt, and that this is why you are building the wall. They say you intend to make yourself their king,
[Nehemiah] [6]:[7] and that you have even set up prophets to proclaim about you in Jerusalem, 'There is a king in Judah!' Now this report will reach the king. So come, let us confer together."
[Nehemiah] [6]:[8] Then I sent him this reply: "Nothing of what you say has happened. You are inventing it all out of your own head."
[Nehemiah] [6]:[9] They were all trying to frighten us, thinking, "Their hands will drop from the work, and it will never be finished." But now, my God,^ strengthen my hands. ^ The words "my God" are not in the Hebrew, which reads simply "But now, strengthen my hands"; they are supplied because the line is a prayer.
[Nehemiah] [6]:[10] Then I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabel, who was shut in there. He said, "Let us meet in the house of God, inside the temple, and let us bar the temple doors, for they are coming to kill you—tonight they are coming to kill you."
[Nehemiah] [6]:[11] But I said, "Should a man like me run away? And who like me could enter the temple and live? I will not go!"
[Nehemiah] [6]:[12] I realized that God had not sent him; he had spoken this prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
[Nehemiah] [6]:[13] He was hired to make me afraid, so that I would do this and sin, and they would have an evil report to spread and could hold me in contempt.
[Nehemiah] [6]:[14] Remember, my God, what Tobiah and Sanballat have done—and Noadiah the prophetess as well, and the rest of the prophets who tried to frighten me.
[Nehemiah] [6]:[15] So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of Elul, in fifty-two days.
[Nehemiah] [6]:[16] When all our enemies heard of it, all the nations around us were afraid, and their confidence sank low, for they knew that this work had been accomplished by our God.
[Nehemiah] [6]:[17] In those days, too, the nobles of Judah were sending many letters to Tobiah, and letters from Tobiah kept coming to them,
[Nehemiah] [6]:[18] for many in Judah were bound to him by oath, since he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
[Nehemiah] [6]:[19] They kept praising his good deeds in my presence and reporting my words back to him. And Tobiah sent letters to intimidate me.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[1] When the wall had been rebuilt and I had set up the doors, the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Levites were appointed.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[2] I put my brother Hanani, together with Hananiah the commander of the citadel, in charge of Jerusalem, for he was a trustworthy man who feared God more than most.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[3] I said to them, "The gates of Jerusalem are not to be opened until the sun is hot, and while the gatekeepers are still on duty the doors are to be shut and barred. Appoint guards from among the residents of Jerusalem, each at his post, each in front of his own house."
[Nehemiah] [7]:[4] The city was large and spacious, but the people in it were few, and no houses had been rebuilt.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[5] Then my God put it into my heart to assemble the nobles, the officials, and the people to be registered by families. I found the genealogical record of those who had come up first, and I found written in it:
[Nehemiah] [7]:[6] These are the people of the province who came up from the captivity of the exiles, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away, and who returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[7] They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
[Nehemiah] [7]:[8] the descendants of Parosh, 2,172;

[Nehemiah] [7]:[40] of Immer, 1,052;
[Nehemiah] [7]:[41] of Pashhur, 1,247;
[Nehemiah] [7]:[42] of Harim, 1,017.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[43] The Levites: the descendants of Jeshua, through Kadmiel, of the line of Hodevah, 74.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[44] The singers: the descendants of Asaph, 148.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[45] The gatekeepers: the descendants of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai, 138.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[46] The temple servants: the descendants of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,
[Nehemiah] [7]:[47] Keros, Sia, Padon,
[Nehemiah] [7]:[48] Lebana, Hagaba, Shalmai,
