[Nehemiah] [7]:[55] Barkos, Sisera, Temah,
[Nehemiah] [7]:[56] Neziah, and Hatipha.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[57] The descendants of Solomon's servants: the descendants of Sotai, Sophereth, Perida,
[Nehemiah] [7]:[58] Jaala, Darkon, Giddel,
[Nehemiah] [7]:[59] Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth-hazzebaim, and Amon.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[60] All the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants numbered 392.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[61] The following came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, but they could not prove that their families and their descent were from Israel:
[Nehemiah] [7]:[62] the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, 642.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[63] And among the priests: the descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai — the one who had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and took his family name.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[64] These searched for their family records, but they could not be found, so they were excluded from the priesthood as unclean.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[65] The governor ordered them not to eat any of the most holy food until a priest should arise to consult the Urim and Thummim.[^1] [^1]: Urim and Thummim: sacred objects kept by the high priest and used to seek God's decision.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[66] The whole assembly together numbered 42,360,
[Nehemiah] [7]:[67] besides their male and female servants, of whom there were 7,337. They also had 245 male and female singers.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[68] There were 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[69] The governor gave to the treasury 1,000 gold darics, 50 bowls, and 530 priestly garments.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew title here is *Tirshatha*, a Persian term for a provincial governor. A daric was a Persian gold coin; a mina was a weight of silver.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[70] Others among the heads of families gave to the treasury for the work 20,000 gold darics and 2,200 minas of silver.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[71] And what the rest of the people gave was 20,000 gold darics, 2,000 minas of silver, and 67 priestly garments.
[Nehemiah] [7]:[72] So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel settled in their towns. When the seventh month came, the Israelites were in their towns.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[1] Then all the people gathered as one to the square in front of the Water Gate, and they asked Ezra the scribe to bring the Book of the Law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded Israel.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[2] So on the first day of the seventh month Ezra the priest brought the Law before the assembly—men and women and all who could understand what they heard.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[3] He read from it, facing the square before the Water Gate, from daybreak until midday, to the men and the women and all who could understand; and the ears of all the people were attentive to the Book of the Law.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[4] Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform built for the occasion. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah; and on his left, Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[5] Ezra opened the book in full view of all the people, for he stood above them; and as he opened it, all the people stood up.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[6] Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people lifted their hands and answered, "Amen! Amen!" Then they bowed down and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[7] And Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah—the Levites—explained the Law to the people while they remained in their places.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[8] They read from the book, from the Law of God, making it clear and giving the sense, so that the people understood the reading.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[9] Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were teaching the people said to them all, "This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not mourn or weep." For all the people had been weeping as they heard the words of the Law.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[10] He said to them, "Go, eat what is rich and drink what is sweet, and send portions to those who have nothing prepared, for this day is holy to our Lord. Do not grieve, for the joy of the LORD is your strength."
[Nehemiah] [8]:[11] The Levites calmed all the people, saying, "Be still, for this day is holy. Do not grieve."
[Nehemiah] [8]:[12] So all the people went away to eat and drink, to send portions, and to celebrate with great joy, because they had understood the words that had been made known to them.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[13] On the second day the heads of the families of all the people, along with the priests and the Levites, gathered around Ezra the scribe to study the words of the Law.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[14] They found written in the Law, which the LORD had commanded through Moses, that the Israelites were to live in booths during the festival of the seventh month,
[Nehemiah] [8]:[15] and that they should proclaim this word and spread it through all their towns and in Jerusalem: "Go out to the hills and bring back branches of olive and wild olive, myrtle, palm, and other leafy trees, to make booths, as it is written."
[Nehemiah] [8]:[16] So the people went out and brought them back and made booths for themselves, each on his own roof, in their courtyards, in the courts of the house of God, in the square by the Water Gate, and in the square by the Gate of Ephraim.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[17] The whole assembly of those who had returned from exile made booths and lived in them. From the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day the Israelites had not done so, and their joy was very great.
[Nehemiah] [8]:[18] Day after day, from the first day to the last, he read from the Book of the Law of God. They kept the festival seven days, and on the eighth day there was a solemn assembly, according to the ordinance.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[1] On the twenty-fourth day of that same month the Israelites gathered together, fasting and dressed in sackcloth, with dust on them.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[2] Those of Israelite descent separated themselves from all foreigners, and they stood and confessed their sins and the guilt of their fathers.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[3] They stood in their places, and for a quarter of the day they read aloud from the Book of the Law of the LORD their God, and for another quarter they confessed and bowed down before the LORD their God.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[4] On the platform of the Levites stood Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Kenani, and they cried out with a loud voice to the LORD their God.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[5] Then the Levites—Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah—said: "Stand up and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting." "Blessed be your glorious name, which is exalted above every blessing and praise.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[6] You alone are the LORD. You made the heavens, the highest heavens and all their host, the earth and everything on it, the seas and everything in them. You give life to them all, and the host of heaven bows down before you.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[7] You are the LORD God, who chose Abram and brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and gave him the name Abraham.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[8] You found his heart faithful before you, and you made a covenant with him to give him the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites—to give it to his descendants. And you have kept your word, for you are righteous.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[9] You saw the misery of our fathers in Egypt; you heard their cry at the Red Sea.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[10] You sent signs and wonders against Pharaoh, against all his servants and all the people of his land, for you knew how arrogantly they treated them. And you made a name for yourself that endures to this day.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[11] You split the sea before them, and they passed through it on dry ground; but their pursuers you hurled into the depths like a stone into raging waters.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[12] By a pillar of cloud you led them by day, and by a pillar of fire at night, to light the way they were to travel.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[13] You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven. You gave them just decrees and true laws, good statutes and commandments.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[14] You made known to them your holy Sabbath, and through your servant Moses you gave them commandments, statutes, and law.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[15] For their hunger you gave them bread from heaven, and for their thirst you brought water out of the rock. You told them to go in and take possession of the land you had sworn with uplifted hand to give them.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[16] But they and our fathers acted arrogantly; they stiffened their necks and did not obey your commandments.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[17] They refused to listen and forgot the wonders you had done among them. They became stiff-necked, and in their rebellion they appointed a leader to return to their slavery. But you are a forgiving God, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love; you did not abandon them.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[18] Even when they cast for themselves an image of a calf and said, 'This is your god who brought you up out of Egypt,' committing terrible blasphemies,
[Nehemiah] [9]:[19] you in your great mercy did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not depart from over them by day to lead them on their way, nor the pillar of fire by night to give them light on the road they were to travel.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[20] You gave your good Spirit to instruct them. You did not withhold your manna from their mouths, and you gave them water for their thirst.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[21] For forty years you sustained them in the wilderness; they lacked nothing. Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[22] You gave them kingdoms and peoples and allotted to them the lands on every side. They took possession of the land of Sihon, the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[23] You made their children as numerous as the stars in the sky, and you brought them into the land you had told their fathers to enter and possess.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[24] So their children went in and took possession of the land. You subdued before them the Canaanites who lived there and handed them over to them, with their kings and the peoples of the land, to do with them as they pleased.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[25] They captured fortified cities and fertile land. They took over houses full of every good thing, cisterns already hewn, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. They ate and were satisfied; they grew fat and delighted themselves in your great goodness.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[26] But they were defiant and rebelled against you. They cast your law behind their backs and killed your prophets, who had warned them to turn back to you; and they committed terrible blasphemies.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[27] So you handed them over to their enemies, who oppressed them. But when they were oppressed and cried out to you, you heard from heaven, and in your great mercy you gave them deliverers, who rescued them from the hand of their enemies.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[28] But as soon as they were at rest, they again did what was evil in your sight. Then you abandoned them to the hand of their enemies, who ruled over them. And when they turned back and cried out to you, you heard from heaven, and time after time you rescued them in your mercy.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[29] You warned them to return to your law, but they became arrogant and did not obey your commandments. They sinned against your decrees, by which a person will live if he keeps them. They turned a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their necks, and would not listen.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[30] For many years you were patient with them. By your Spirit you warned them through your prophets, yet they would not listen. So you handed them over to the peoples of the lands.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[31] But in your great mercy you did not put an end to them or abandon them, for you are a gracious and compassionate God.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[32] Now therefore, our God—the great, mighty, and awesome God, who keeps covenant and steadfast love—do not treat lightly all the hardship that has come upon us, upon our kings and leaders, our priests and prophets, our fathers and all your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until today.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[33] In all that has happened to us, you have been just; you have acted faithfully, while we have acted wickedly.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[34] Our kings, our leaders, our priests, and our fathers did not keep your law; they did not heed your commandments or the warnings you gave them.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[35] Even while they were in their kingdom, enjoying the great goodness you gave them in the spacious and fertile land you set before them, they did not serve you or turn from their evil ways.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[36] See, we are slaves today—slaves in the very land you gave our fathers so they could enjoy its fruit and its good things.
[Nehemiah] [9]:[37] Because of our sins, its abundant harvest goes to the kings you have set over us. They rule over our bodies and our livestock as they please. We are in great distress."
[Nehemiah] [10]:[1] In view of all this, we are entering into a binding agreement, put in writing; and on the sealed document are the names of our officials, our Levites, and our priests.

[Nehemiah] [10]:[29] The rest of the people—the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands in order to follow the Law of God, together with their wives, their sons, and their daughters, all who had the knowledge to understand—
[Nehemiah] [10]:[30] joined with their brothers, the nobles, and bound themselves with a curse and an oath to walk in the Law of God, given through Moses the servant of God, and to keep and carry out all the commandments of the LORD our Lord, with his judgments and his statutes:
[Nehemiah] [10]:[31] We will not give our daughters to the peoples of the land, nor take their daughters for our sons.
[Nehemiah] [10]:[32] When the peoples of the land bring their wares or any grain to sell on the Sabbath day, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on any holy day. Every seventh year we will let the land rest and cancel every debt.
[Nehemiah] [10]:[33] We take upon ourselves the obligation to give a third of a shekel each year for the service of the house of our God:
[Nehemiah] [10]:[34] for the rows of bread set out in the sanctuary, for the daily grain offering and the daily burnt offering, for the Sabbaths, the new moons, and the appointed feasts, for the holy offerings and the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for all the work of the house of our God.
[Nehemiah] [10]:[35] We—the priests, the Levites, and the people—have also cast lots for the wood offering, to bring it to the house of our God, family by family, at the appointed times year by year, to be burned on the altar of the LORD our God, as it is written in the Law.
[Nehemiah] [10]:[36] We will also bring to the house of the LORD, year by year, the firstfruits of our soil and the firstfruits of the fruit of every tree,
[Nehemiah] [10]:[37] and the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as it is written in the Law, bringing the firstborn of our herds and flocks to the house of our God, to the priests who minister there.
[Nehemiah] [10]:[38] We will bring the first of our ground meal, our contributions, the fruit of every tree, and the new wine and oil to the priests, to the storerooms of the house of our God, and the tithe of our soil to the Levites, for it is the Levites who collect the tithes in all the towns where we work.
[Nehemiah] [10]:[39] A priest, a descendant of Aaron, is to accompany the Levites when they receive the tithes, and the Levites are to bring up a tenth of the tithes to the house of our God, to the storerooms of the treasury.
[Nehemiah] [10]:[40] For the people of Israel and the Levites are to bring their contributions of grain, new wine, and oil to those storerooms, where the vessels of the sanctuary are kept and where the ministering priests, the gatekeepers, and the singers are. We will not neglect the house of our God.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[1] The leaders of the people settled in Jerusalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of every ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, while the other nine remained in the towns.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[2] And the people blessed all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[3] These are the heads of the province who settled in Jerusalem, while in the towns of Judah everyone lived on his own property in his own town — Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants, and the descendants of Solomon's servants.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[4] In Jerusalem there settled some of the people of Judah and some of the people of Benjamin. From the people of Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, of the descendants of Perez;
[Nehemiah] [11]:[5] and Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, of the Shilonites.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[6] All the descendants of Perez living in Jerusalem numbered 468 able men.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[7] These are the Benjaminites: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah;
[Nehemiah] [11]:[8] and after him Gabbai and Sallai — 928 in all.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[9] Joel son of Zichri was their overseer, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in charge of the city.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[10] From the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib; Jachin;
[Nehemiah] [11]:[11] Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the chief officer of the house of God,
[Nehemiah] [11]:[12] and their kinsmen who did the work of the house of God — 822; and Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah,
[Nehemiah] [11]:[13] and his kinsmen, heads of families — 242; and Amashsai son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer,
[Nehemiah] [11]:[14] and their kinsmen, able warriors — 128. Their overseer was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[15] From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni;
[Nehemiah] [11]:[16] Shabbethai and Jozabad, two of the heads of the Levites, who were in charge of the outside work of the house of God;
[Nehemiah] [11]:[17] Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, who led the thanksgiving in prayer; Bakbukiah, second among his kinsmen; and Abda son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[18] All the Levites in the holy city numbered 284.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[19] The gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon, and their kinsmen who kept watch at the gates — 172.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[20] The rest of Israel, with the priests and the Levites, lived in all the towns of Judah, each on his own inheritance.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[21] The temple servants lived on Ophel, and Ziha and Gishpa were in charge of them.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[22] The overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Mica, one of the descendants of Asaph, the singers who served in the work of the house of God.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[23] For there was a command from the king concerning them, a fixed provision for the singers, as each day required.
[Nehemiah] [11]:[24] Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, of the descendants of Zerah son of Judah, was at the king's side in all matters concerning the people.

[Nehemiah] [11]:[27] in Hazar-shual, in Beersheba and its settlements,
[Nehemiah] [11]:[28] in Ziklag, in Meconah and its settlements,

[Nehemiah] [12]:[23] The sons of Levi who were heads of the fathers' houses were recorded in the Book of the Chronicles until the days of Johanan son of Eliashib.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[24] The leaders of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel, with their kinsmen standing opposite them, to praise and give thanks according to the command of David the man of God, watch answering watch.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[25] Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers, standing guard at the storerooms by the gates.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[26] These served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra the priest and scribe.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[27] At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, the Levites were sought out from all their settlements and brought to Jerusalem to celebrate the dedication with rejoicing, with thanksgivings and singing, with cymbals, harps, and lyres.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[28] So the sons of the singers gathered from the district around Jerusalem, from the villages of the Netophathites,
[Nehemiah] [12]:[29] from Beth-gilgal, and from the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, for the singers had built themselves villages around Jerusalem.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[30] The priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people, the gates, and the wall.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[31] Then I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and appointed two great choirs of thanksgiving. One went to the right along the top of the wall toward the Dung Gate,
[Nehemiah] [12]:[32] and behind them went Hoshaiah and half the leaders of Judah,
[Nehemiah] [12]:[33] along with Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
[Nehemiah] [12]:[34] Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah,
[Nehemiah] [12]:[35] and some of the priests' sons with trumpets: Zechariah son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph,
[Nehemiah] [12]:[36] and his kinsmen Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God; and Ezra the scribe went before them.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[37] At the Fountain Gate they went straight up the steps of the city of David, by the ascent of the wall, and passed above the house of David to the Water Gate on the east.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[38] The second choir of thanksgiving went to the left, and I followed it with half the people, along the top of the wall above the Tower of the Ovens to the Broad Wall,
[Nehemiah] [12]:[39] then above the Gate of Ephraim, past the Old Gate and the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel and the Tower of the Hundred, to the Sheep Gate; and they came to a halt at the Gate of the Guard.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[40] So the two choirs of thanksgiving took their places in the house of God, and I with them, along with half the officials,
[Nehemiah] [12]:[41] and the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets,
[Nehemiah] [12]:[42] and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. The singers sang out, with Jezrahiah as their director.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[43] That day they offered great sacrifices and rejoiced, for God had given them great joy. The women and the children rejoiced as well, and the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[44] On that day men were appointed over the storerooms that served as treasuries for the contributions, the firstfruits, and the tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the towns the portions prescribed by the law for the priests and the Levites; for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who were serving.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[45] They kept the charge of their God and the charge of purification, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and of Solomon his son.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[46] For long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, there were directors of the singers, and there were songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.
[Nehemiah] [12]:[47] And in the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah, all Israel gave the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers. They set apart what was due to the Levites, and the Levites set apart what was due to the sons of Aaron.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[1] On that day the Book of Moses was read aloud to the people, and there it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God,
[Nehemiah] [13]:[2] because they had not met the Israelites with bread and water, but had hired Balaam against them to curse them—though our God turned the curse into a blessing.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[3] When the people heard the Law, they separated from Israel everyone of foreign descent.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[4] Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who had been put in charge of the storerooms of the house of our God and was closely associated with Tobiah,
[Nehemiah] [13]:[5] had provided him with a large room where they had formerly stored the grain offerings, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of grain, new wine, and oil prescribed for the Levites, the singers, and the gatekeepers, along with the contributions for the priests.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[6] While all this was going on I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had gone to the king. Some time later I asked the king for leave,
[Nehemiah] [13]:[7] and I came back to Jerusalem. Then I learned of the evil Eliashib had done for Tobiah in providing him a room in the courts of the house of God.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[8] I was deeply grieved, and I threw all of Tobiah's household goods out of the room.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[9] Then I gave orders, and they purified the rooms; and I brought back there the vessels of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[10] I also learned that the portions due the Levites had not been given, so that the Levites and the singers who did the work had each gone back to his own field.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[11] So I confronted the officials and said, "Why has the house of God been neglected?" Then I gathered them together and stationed them at their posts.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[12] And all Judah brought the tithe of grain, new wine, and oil into the storerooms.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[13] I put Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites in charge of the storerooms, with Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, as their assistant, for these men were considered trustworthy. Their duty was to distribute the supplies to their brothers.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[14] Remember me for this, my God, and do not blot out the good I have done for the house of my God and its services.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[15] In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath, bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, along with wine, grapes, figs, and every kind of load, and hauling it all into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. So I warned them against selling food on that day.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[16] Men from Tyre who lived there were bringing in fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling it on the Sabbath to the people of Judah, and in Jerusalem itself.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[17] Then I confronted the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day?
[Nehemiah] [13]:[18] Did not your fathers do the same, so that our God brought all this disaster on us and on this city? Now you are stirring up more wrath against Israel by profaning the Sabbath."
[Nehemiah] [13]:[19] So when the gates of Jerusalem began to grow dark before the Sabbath, I ordered the doors to be shut and commanded that they not be opened until after the Sabbath. And I stationed some of my own men at the gates, so that no load could be brought in on the Sabbath day.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[20] Once or twice the merchants and sellers of all kinds of goods spent the night outside Jerusalem.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[21] But I warned them and said, "Why are you spending the night by the wall? If you do it again, I will lay hands on you." From that time on they did not come on the Sabbath.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[22] Then I ordered the Levites to purify themselves and come and guard the gates, in order to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember me for this also, my God, and spare me according to your great mercy.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[23] In those days I also saw Jews who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[24] Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod or the language of one of the other peoples, and did not know how to speak the language of Judah.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[25] I confronted them and called down curses on them. I beat some of the men and pulled out their hair, and I made them swear by God: "You shall not give your daughters in marriage to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[26] Was it not because of such marriages that Solomon king of Israel sinned? Among the many nations there was no king like him. He was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel—yet even he was led into sin by foreign women.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[27] Must we then hear of you doing all this great evil, acting unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign women?"
[Nehemiah] [13]:[28] One of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite; I drove him away from me.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[29] Remember them, my God, because they defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.
[Nehemiah] [13]:[30] So I purified them from everything foreign, and I assigned duties to the priests and Levites, each to his own task,
[Nehemiah] [13]:[31] and I provided for the wood offering at appointed times, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, my God, for good.
[Esther] [1]:[1] This happened in the days of Ahasuerus—the Ahasuerus who ruled over a hundred and twenty-seven provinces, from India to Ethiopia.
[Esther] [1]:[2] In those days, while King Ahasuerus was seated on his royal throne in the citadel of Susa,
[Esther] [1]:[3] in the third year of his reign he gave a banquet for all his officials and servants—the army of Persia and Media, the nobles, and the governors of the provinces were there before him—
[Esther] [1]:[4] and for many days, a hundred and eighty in all, he displayed the vast wealth of his kingdom and the splendid glory of his greatness.
[Esther] [1]:[5] When those days were over, the king held a seven-day banquet in the garden court of the royal palace for all the people who were in the citadel of Susa, from the greatest to the least.
[Esther] [1]:[6] There were hangings of white linen and violet cloth, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings on pillars of marble. Couches of gold and silver stood on a pavement of porphyry, marble, mother-of-pearl, and precious stone.
[Esther] [1]:[7] Drinks were served in golden vessels, no two of them alike, and the royal wine flowed freely, as befitted the king's bounty.
[Esther] [1]:[8] The rule for the drinking was that no one should be compelled, for the king had instructed every steward of his household to serve each man just as he wished.
[Esther] [1]:[9] Queen Vashti also gave a banquet for the women in the royal palace of King Ahasuerus.
[Esther] [1]:[10] On the seventh day, when the king's heart was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas—the seven eunuchs who served in the presence of King Ahasuerus—
[Esther] [1]:[11] to bring Queen Vashti before him wearing her royal crown, so that he might display her beauty to the peoples and the officials; for she was lovely to look at.
[Esther] [1]:[12] But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command delivered by the eunuchs. Then the king became furious, and his anger burned within him.
[Esther] [1]:[13] So the king consulted the wise men who understood the times—for it was the king's custom to lay matters before all who knew law and judgment—
[Esther] [1]:[14] those closest to him being Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven officials of Persia and Media who had access to the king and held the highest rank in the kingdom.
[Esther] [1]:[15] "According to the law," he asked, "what is to be done with Queen Vashti, since she has not obeyed the command of King Ahasuerus delivered by the eunuchs?"
[Esther] [1]:[16] Memucan answered before the king and the officials: "Queen Vashti has not wronged the king alone, but all the officials and all the peoples in every province of King Ahasuerus.
[Esther] [1]:[17] For what the queen has done will become known to all the women, and they will despise their husbands, saying, 'King Ahasuerus commanded that Queen Vashti be brought before him, and she would not come.'
[Esther] [1]:[18] This very day the noble women of Persia and Media who have heard what the queen did will speak the same way to all the king's officials, and there will be no end of contempt and anger.
[Esther] [1]:[19] So if it pleases the king, let a royal decree go out from him and be written into the laws of Persia and Media, never to be revoked, that Vashti shall never again come before King Ahasuerus, and that the king give her royal position to another woman who is better than she.
[Esther] [1]:[20] When the king's edict is proclaimed throughout his vast realm, all the women will honor their husbands, from the greatest to the least."
[Esther] [1]:[21] This advice pleased the king and his officials, and the king did as Memucan proposed.
[Esther] [1]:[22] He sent letters to all the king's provinces, to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language, declaring that every man should be master of his own household, and that each should speak the language of his own people.
[Esther] [2]:[1] After these things, when King Ahasuerus' rage had subsided, he remembered Vashti — what she had done, and what had been decreed against her.
[Esther] [2]:[2] Then the king's attendants who served him said, "Let a search be made for beautiful young virgins for the king.
[Esther] [2]:[3] Let the king appoint officers in every province of his kingdom to gather every beautiful young virgin to the citadel of Susa, to the harem, under the care of Hegai, the king's eunuch who keeps the women, and let their beauty treatments be provided.
[Esther] [2]:[4] And let the young woman who pleases the king become queen in place of Vashti." The proposal pleased the king, and he acted on it.
[Esther] [2]:[5] Now there was a Jew in the citadel of Susa named Mordecai son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjaminite,
[Esther] [2]:[6] who had been carried away from Jerusalem among the exiles taken with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried into exile.
[Esther] [2]:[7] He was raising Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle's daughter, for she had neither father nor mother. The young woman was lovely in form and beautiful to look at, and when her father and mother died, Mordecai took her as his own daughter.
[Esther] [2]:[8] So when the king's order and decree were proclaimed and many young women were gathered to the citadel of Susa under Hegai's care, Esther too was taken to the king's palace, into the care of Hegai, keeper of the women.
[Esther] [2]:[9] The young woman pleased him and won his favor, so he quickly provided her with her beauty treatments and her portions of food, along with seven chosen maids from the king's palace, and he moved her and her maids to the best place in the harem.
[Esther] [2]:[10] Esther had not disclosed her people or her family background, for Mordecai had ordered her not to tell.
[Esther] [2]:[11] Day after day Mordecai walked back and forth in front of the courtyard of the harem, to learn how Esther was and what was happening to her.
[Esther] [2]:[12] Now when the turn came for each young woman to go in to King Ahasuerus, she had first completed the twelve months prescribed for the women — for so their time of beautifying was filled: six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with perfumes and women's cosmetics.
[Esther] [2]:[13] When the young woman went in to the king in this way, whatever she asked for was given her to take with her from the harem to the king's palace.
[Esther] [2]:[14] In the evening she would go in, and in the morning she would return to the second harem, under the care of Shaashgaz, the king's eunuch who kept the concubines. She would not go in to the king again unless he delighted in her and summoned her by name.
[Esther] [2]:[15] When the turn came for Esther, the daughter of Abihail, the uncle of Mordecai who had taken her as his own daughter, to go in to the king, she asked for nothing except what Hegai, the king's eunuch who kept the women, advised. And Esther won the admiration of everyone who saw her.
[Esther] [2]:[16] Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus, into his royal residence, in the tenth month, the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
[Esther] [2]:[17] The king loved Esther more than all the other women, and she won his favor and devotion more than all the other virgins. So he set the royal crown on her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.
[Esther] [2]:[18] Then the king gave a great banquet for all his officials and servants — Esther's banquet. He granted the provinces a remission of taxes and distributed gifts with royal generosity.
[Esther] [2]:[19] When the virgins were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.
[Esther] [2]:[20] Esther still had not disclosed her family background or her people, just as Mordecai had ordered her; she did what Mordecai told her, as she had done when he was raising her.
[Esther] [2]:[21] In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the threshold, grew angry and plotted to lay hands on King Ahasuerus.
[Esther] [2]:[22] But the plot became known to Mordecai, and he told Queen Esther, and Esther reported it to the king in Mordecai's name.
[Esther] [2]:[23] The matter was investigated and confirmed, and the two men were hanged on a pole.[^1] [^1]: Or "impaled on a stake"; the Hebrew word means "tree" or "wood."
[Esther] [3]:[1] After these events King Ahasuerus promoted Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, advancing him and setting his seat above all the officials who were with him.
[Esther] [3]:[2] All the king's servants at the King's Gate knelt and bowed down to Haman, for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai would not kneel or bow down.
[Esther] [3]:[3] So the king's servants at the King's Gate said to Mordecai, "Why do you disobey the king's command?"
[Esther] [3]:[4] Day after day they spoke to him, but he would not listen to them. So they reported it to Haman, to see whether Mordecai's words would stand, for he had told them that he was a Jew.
[Esther] [3]:[5] When Haman saw that Mordecai would neither kneel nor bow down to him, he was filled with rage.
[Esther] [3]:[6] Yet he thought it beneath him to lay hands on Mordecai alone, for they had told him who Mordecai's people were. So Haman sought to destroy all the Jews, the people of Mordecai, throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus.
[Esther] [3]:[7] In the first month, the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, they cast the pur—that is, the lot—before Haman, from day to day and from month to month, and the lot fell on the twelfth month, the month of Adar.
[Esther] [3]:[8] Then Haman said to King Ahasuerus, "There is a certain people scattered and dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom. Their laws differ from those of every other people, and they do not keep the king's laws, so it is not in the king's interest to tolerate them.
[Esther] [3]:[9] If it pleases the king, let an order be written that they be destroyed, and I will weigh out ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who administer the king's affairs, to be brought into the royal treasury."
[Esther] [3]:[10] So the king took the signet ring from his hand and gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.
[Esther] [3]:[11] And the king said to Haman, "The silver is yours to keep, and the people as well—do with them as you see fit."
[Esther] [3]:[12] On the thirteenth day of the first month the king's scribes were summoned, and everything Haman commanded was written to the king's satraps, to the governors over each province, and to the officials of each people—to every province in its own script and to every people in its own language. It was written in the name of King Ahasuerus and sealed with the king's signet ring.
[Esther] [3]:[13] Letters were sent by couriers to all the king's provinces, ordering that all the Jews—young and old, women and children—be destroyed, killed, and annihilated in a single day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, and their possessions plundered.
[Esther] [3]:[14] A copy of the document was to be issued as law in every province and published to all the peoples, so that they would be ready for that day.
[Esther] [3]:[15] The couriers went out in haste at the king's command, and the decree was issued in the citadel of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Susa was thrown into confusion.
[Esther] [4]:[1] When Mordecai learned all that had been done, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the middle of the city, crying out loudly and bitterly.
[Esther] [4]:[2] He came only as far as the king's gate, for no one dressed in sackcloth was allowed to enter it.
[Esther] [4]:[3] In every single province where the king's command and decree arrived, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping, and wailing, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
[Esther] [4]:[4] When Esther's maids and eunuchs came and told her, the queen was deeply shaken. She sent clothes for Mordecai to wear in place of his sackcloth, but he would not accept them.
[Esther] [4]:[5] Then Esther summoned Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs assigned to attend her, and ordered him to go to Mordecai and find out what this was about and why.
[Esther] [4]:[6] So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the king's gate,
[Esther] [4]:[7] and Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him, including the exact amount of silver Haman had promised to pay into the royal treasury for the destruction of the Jews.
[Esther] [4]:[8] He also gave him a copy of the written decree issued in Susa for their annihilation, to show Esther and explain it to her, and to charge her to go to the king to plead with him and beg him for her people.
[Esther] [4]:[9] Hathach returned and reported Mordecai's words to Esther.
[Esther] [4]:[10] Then Esther told Hathach to take this message back to Mordecai:
[Esther] [4]:[11] "All the king's servants and the people of the king's provinces know that for any man or woman who goes to the king in the inner court without being summoned, there is but one law: death — unless the king extends the golden scepter and spares that person's life. And I have not been summoned to the king for thirty days now."
[Esther] [4]:[12] When Esther's words were reported to Mordecai,
[Esther] [4]:[13] he sent back this reply: "Do not imagine that you alone of all the Jews will escape, because you are in the king's house.
[Esther] [4]:[14] For if you keep silent at a time like this, relief and deliverance will arise for the Jews from another place, but you and your father's house will perish. And who knows? Perhaps you have come to the throne for just such a time as this."
[Esther] [4]:[15] Then Esther sent this answer to Mordecai:
[Esther] [4]:[16] "Go, gather all the Jews in Susa and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my maids will fast in the same way. Then I will go to the king, even though it is against the law. And if I perish, I perish."
[Esther] [4]:[17] So Mordecai went away and did everything Esther had commanded him.
[Esther] [5]:[1] On the third day Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the palace, facing the king's hall. The king was seated on his royal throne in the hall, facing the entrance.
[Esther] [5]:[2] When the king saw Queen Esther standing in the court, she found favor in his eyes, and he held out to her the golden scepter in his hand. Esther approached and touched the tip of the scepter.
[Esther] [5]:[3] The king said to her, "What is it, Queen Esther? What is your request? Even half the kingdom, and it will be given you."
[Esther] [5]:[4] Esther answered, "If it pleases the king, let the king and Haman come today to the banquet I have prepared for him."
[Esther] [5]:[5] The king said, "Bring Haman quickly, so we may do as Esther says." So the king and Haman came to the banquet Esther had prepared.
[Esther] [5]:[6] As they were drinking wine, the king said to Esther, "What is your petition? It will be granted you. What is your request? Even half the kingdom, and it will be done."
[Esther] [5]:[7] Esther answered, "My petition and my request is this:
[Esther] [5]:[8] If I have found favor in the king's eyes, and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and fulfill my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet I will prepare for them. Tomorrow I will do as the king has said."
[Esther] [5]:[9] Haman went out that day glad and in high spirits. But when he saw Mordecai at the king's gate, and Mordecai neither rose nor stirred before him, Haman was filled with rage against him.
[Esther] [5]:[10] Still, Haman restrained himself and went home. Then he sent for his friends and for Zeresh his wife,
[Esther] [5]:[11] and he recounted to them the splendor of his wealth, his many sons, and all the ways the king had honored him and raised him above the officials and servants of the king.
[Esther] [5]:[12] "What is more," Haman said, "Queen Esther invited no one but me to accompany the king to the banquet she gave. And tomorrow I am invited by her again, along with the king.
[Esther] [5]:[13] Yet none of this means a thing to me as long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate."
[Esther] [5]:[14] His wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Have a pole set up, fifty cubits high, and in the morning ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on it. Then go with the king to the banquet in good spirits." The advice pleased Haman, and he had the pole set up.
[Esther] [6]:[1] That night the king could not sleep, so he ordered the book of records, the chronicles, to be brought and read aloud before him.
[Esther] [6]:[2] There it was found written how Mordecai had reported that Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the threshold, had plotted to lay hands on King Ahasuerus.
[Esther] [6]:[3] The king asked, "What honor or distinction has been given to Mordecai for this?" The king's attendants who served him answered, "Nothing has been done for him."
[Esther] [6]:[4] "Who is in the court?" the king asked. Now Haman had just entered the outer court of the palace to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows he had prepared for him.
[Esther] [6]:[5] The king's attendants said, "Haman is standing in the court." "Let him come in," said the king.
[Esther] [6]:[6] When Haman entered, the king asked him, "What should be done for the man whom the king wishes to honor?" Haman thought to himself, "Whom would the king wish to honor more than me?"
[Esther] [6]:[7] So Haman answered the king, "For the man whom the king wishes to honor,
[Esther] [6]:[8] let royal robes be brought that the king himself has worn, and a horse that the king himself has ridden, with a royal crown set on its head.
[Esther] [6]:[9] Let the robe and the horse be entrusted to one of the king's most noble officials, and let them clothe the man whom the king wishes to honor and lead him on horseback through the city square, proclaiming before him: 'So shall it be done for the man whom the king wishes to honor!'
[Esther] [6]:[10] "Hurry," the king said to Haman, "take the robes and the horse, just as you have said, and do this for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king's gate. Leave out nothing of all you have spoken."
[Esther] [6]:[11] So Haman took the robe and the horse, clothed Mordecai, and led him on horseback through the city square, proclaiming before him, "So shall it be done for the man whom the king wishes to honor!"
[Esther] [6]:[12] Then Mordecai returned to the king's gate, but Haman rushed home, mourning, with his head covered.
[Esther] [6]:[13] Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had happened to him. Then his advisers and his wife Zeresh said to him, "If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of Jewish descent, you cannot prevail against him; you will surely fall before him."
[Esther] [6]:[14] While they were still speaking with him, the king's eunuchs arrived and hurried Haman off to the banquet Esther had prepared.
[Esther] [7]:[1] So the king and Haman came to feast with Queen Esther.
[Esther] [7]:[2] And again on this second day, as they drank their wine, the king said to Esther, "What is your petition, Queen Esther? It shall be granted you. What is your request? Up to half the kingdom, and it shall be done."
[Esther] [7]:[3] Queen Esther answered, "If I have found favor in your eyes, O king, and if it pleases the king, let my life be granted me as my petition, and my people as my request.
[Esther] [7]:[4] For we have been sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, killed, and annihilated. If we had merely been sold as slaves and servant girls, I would have kept silent, for such trouble would not be worth disturbing the king."
[Esther] [7]:[5] Then King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther, "Who is he? Where is the man who has dared to do such a thing?"
[Esther] [7]:[6] Esther said, "The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman!" And Haman stood terrified before the king and queen.
[Esther] [7]:[7] In his fury the king rose from the wine banquet and went out into the palace garden, while Haman stayed behind to beg Queen Esther for his life, for he saw that the king had already determined his ruin.
[Esther] [7]:[8] When the king returned from the palace garden to the banquet hall, Haman had thrown himself on the couch where Esther was reclining. The king exclaimed, "Will he even assault the queen while she is with me in my own house?" As the words left the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.
[Esther] [7]:[9] Then Harbona, one of the eunuchs attending the king, said, "Look, the gallows Haman made for Mordecai, who spoke up for the king's good, is standing at Haman's house, fifty cubits high."[fn] The king said, "Hang him on it."
[Esther] [7]:[10] So they hanged Haman on the gallows he had prepared for Mordecai, and the king's fury subsided.
[Esther] [8]:[1] That same day King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the estate of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. And Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had told him how he was related to her.
[Esther] [8]:[2] The king took off his signet ring, which he had taken back from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai; and Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's estate.
[Esther] [8]:[3] Then Esther spoke to the king again. She fell at his feet, weeping and pleading with him to undo the evil plot of Haman the Agagite and the scheme he had devised against the Jews.
[Esther] [8]:[4] The king extended the golden scepter to Esther, and Esther rose and stood before him.
[Esther] [8]:[5] She said, "If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor with him, and if the king thinks it right and I am pleasing in his eyes, let an order be written to revoke the letters devised by Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews in all the king's provinces.
[Esther] [8]:[6] For how can I bear to watch the disaster that is to fall on my people? How can I bear to watch the destruction of my kindred?"
[Esther] [8]:[7] King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther and to Mordecai the Jew, "See, I have given Haman's estate to Esther, and he himself has been hanged on the gallows because he raised his hand against the Jews.
[Esther] [8]:[8] Now you write concerning the Jews whatever seems best to you, in the king's name, and seal it with the king's signet ring; for no document written in the king's name and sealed with the king's ring can be revoked."
[Esther] [8]:[9] So the king's secretaries were summoned at that time, on the twenty-third day of the third month, the month of Sivan, and an edict was written exactly as Mordecai directed, to the Jews and to the satraps, the governors, and the officials of the hundred and twenty-seven provinces from India to Ethiopia—to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language, and to the Jews in their own script and language.
[Esther] [8]:[10] He wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, sealed it with the king's signet ring, and sent the letters by mounted couriers riding swift royal horses bred from the finest stock.
[Esther] [8]:[11] By these letters the king granted the Jews in every city the right to assemble and defend their lives—to destroy, kill, and annihilate any armed force of any people or province that might attack them, together with the women and children of those attackers, and to plunder their goods—
[Esther] [8]:[12] on a single day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar.
[Esther] [8]:[13] A copy of the document was to be issued as law in every province and published to all the peoples, so that the Jews would be ready on that day to take revenge on their enemies.
[Esther] [8]:[14] The couriers, riding the swift royal horses, went out in urgent haste at the king's command, and the decree was also issued in the citadel of Susa.
[Esther] [8]:[15] Mordecai left the king's presence wearing royal robes of blue and white, a large golden crown, and a purple cloak of fine linen. And the city of Susa shouted and rejoiced.
[Esther] [8]:[16] For the Jews there was light and gladness, joy and honor.
[Esther] [8]:[17] In every province and every city, wherever the king's command and decree arrived, there was joy and gladness among the Jews, with feasting and celebration. And many of the peoples of the land professed themselves Jews, because the fear of the Jews had fallen upon them.
[Esther] [9]:[1] In the twelfth month, the month of Adar, on the thirteenth day, when the king's command and decree were to be carried out—on the very day when the enemies of the Jews had hoped to overpower them—the reverse took place: the Jews overpowered those who hated them.
[Esther] [9]:[2] The Jews gathered in their cities throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus to strike down those who sought their harm, and no one could stand against them, for the fear of them had fallen on all the peoples.
[Esther] [9]:[3] All the officials of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and the king's administrators supported the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai had fallen on them.
[Esther] [9]:[4] For Mordecai was great in the king's house, and his fame spread through all the provinces, for the man Mordecai kept growing greater and greater.
[Esther] [9]:[5] So the Jews struck down all their enemies with the sword, killing and destroying, and they did as they pleased with those who hated them.
[Esther] [9]:[6] In the citadel of Susa the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men,
[Esther] [9]:[7] and they killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,
[Esther] [9]:[8] Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,
[Esther] [9]:[9] Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha—
[Esther] [9]:[10] the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. But they laid no hand on the plunder.
[Esther] [9]:[11] That same day the number of those killed in the citadel of Susa was reported to the king.
[Esther] [9]:[12] The king said to Queen Esther, "In the citadel of Susa the Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men, along with the ten sons of Haman. What must they have done in the rest of the king's provinces! Now what is your petition? It shall be granted you. What more do you request? It shall be done."
[Esther] [9]:[13] Esther answered, "If it pleases the king, let the Jews in Susa be allowed to act tomorrow as well, according to today's decree, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged on the gallows."
[Esther] [9]:[14] The king ordered that it be done. The decree was issued in Susa, and they hanged the ten sons of Haman.
[Esther] [9]:[15] The Jews in Susa gathered again on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and killed three hundred men in Susa, but they laid no hand on the plunder.
[Esther] [9]:[16] The rest of the Jews throughout the king's provinces also gathered to defend their lives and gain relief from their enemies. They killed seventy-five thousand of those who hated them, but they laid no hand on the plunder.
[Esther] [9]:[17] This was on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, and on the fourteenth they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
[Esther] [9]:[18] But the Jews in Susa had gathered on the thirteenth and the fourteenth, and they rested on the fifteenth and made it a day of feasting and gladness.
[Esther] [9]:[19] This is why the Jews of the countryside, who live in the unwalled towns, keep the fourteenth day of the month of Adar as a day of gladness and feasting, a holiday on which they send portions of food to one another.
[Esther] [9]:[20] Mordecai recorded these things and sent letters to all the Jews in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, both near and far,
[Esther] [9]:[21] binding them to observe the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar year after year,
[Esther] [9]:[22] as the days on which the Jews gained relief from their enemies, and as the month in which their sorrow was turned into gladness and their mourning into a holiday. They were to keep them as days of feasting and gladness, sending portions of food to one another and gifts to the poor.
[Esther] [9]:[23] So the Jews took upon themselves what they had already begun to do and what Mordecai had written to them.
[Esther] [9]:[24] For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast the pur—that is, the lot—to crush and destroy them.
[Esther] [9]:[25] But when Esther came before the king, he ordered in writing that the evil scheme Haman had devised against the Jews should fall back on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.
[Esther] [9]:[26] Therefore these days are called Purim, after the name Pur. And so, because of everything written in this letter, and because of what they had seen and what had happened to them,
[Esther] [9]:[27] the Jews established and took upon themselves and their descendants and all who joined them that they would never fail to observe these two days as prescribed and at the appointed time, year after year.
[Esther] [9]:[28] These days are remembered and kept in every generation, in every family, in every province and every city, and these days of Purim will never cease among the Jews, nor will their memory die out among their descendants.
[Esther] [9]:[29] Then Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, along with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter about Purim.
[Esther] [9]:[30] Letters were sent to all the Jews in the hundred and twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus—words of peace and truth—
[Esther] [9]:[31] to confirm these days of Purim at their appointed times, just as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had established for them, and just as they had taken upon themselves and upon their descendants the matters of the fasts and their cries of lament.
[Esther] [9]:[32] So Queen Esther's decree confirmed these matters of Purim, and it was written down in the record.
[Esther] [10]:[1] King Ahasuerus imposed tribute on the land and on the islands of the sea.
[Esther] [10]:[2] And all his acts of power and might, together with the full account of how the king had raised Mordecai to greatness—are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?
[Esther] [10]:[3] For Mordecai the Jew was second to King Ahasuerus, great among the Jews and esteemed by the multitude of his brothers, for he sought the good of his people and spoke peace to all his people's descendants.
[Job] [1]:[1] There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright; he feared God and turned away from evil.
[Job] [1]:[2] Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.
[Job] [1]:[3] He owned seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred donkeys, and he had a great many servants. He was the greatest of all the people of the East.
[Job] [1]:[4] His sons used to go and hold a feast, each in his own house on his appointed day, and they would send word and invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
[Job] [1]:[5] When the days of feasting had run their course, Job would send for them and consecrate them. He would rise early in the morning and offer burnt offerings, one for each of them, for Job thought, "Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts." This is what Job always did.
[Job] [1]:[6] One day the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came among them.
[Job] [1]:[7] The LORD said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered the LORD, "From roaming the earth and walking back and forth on it."
[Job] [1]:[8] The LORD said to Satan, "Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth—a blameless and upright man, who fears God and turns away from evil."
[Job] [1]:[9] Satan answered the LORD, "Is it for nothing that Job fears God?
[Job] [1]:[10] Have you not put a hedge around him and his house and everything he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his livestock have spread out across the land.
[Job] [1]:[11] But stretch out your hand now and touch everything he has, and he will surely curse you to your face." [Footnote: The Hebrew verb here is literally "bless," used as a reverent substitute for "curse."]
[Job] [1]:[12] The LORD said to Satan, "Very well, everything he has is in your hands. Only do not lay a hand on the man himself." Then Satan went out from the presence of the LORD.
[Job] [1]:[13] One day, while Job's sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house,
[Job] [1]:[14] a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing nearby,
[Job] [1]:[15] when the Sabeans attacked and carried them off. They put the servants to the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
[Job] [1]:[16] He was still speaking when another came and said, "The fire of God fell from heaven and burned among the sheep and the servants and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
[Job] [1]:[17] He was still speaking when another came and said, "The Chaldeans formed three raiding parties, swept down on the camels and carried them off. They put the servants to the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
[Job] [1]:[18] He was still speaking when yet another came and said, "Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house,
[Job] [1]:[19] when suddenly a mighty wind swept in from the desert and struck the four corners of the house. It collapsed on the young people, and they are dead, and I alone have escaped to tell you."
[Job] [1]:[20] Then Job stood up, tore his robe, and shaved his head. He fell to the ground in worship
[Job] [1]:[21] and said: "Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I will return. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD."
[Job] [1]:[22] Through all this Job did not sin or charge God with wrongdoing.
[Job] [2]:[1] Again there came a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan also came among them to present himself before the LORD.
[Job] [2]:[2] The LORD said to Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan answered the LORD, "From roaming the earth and walking back and forth across it."
[Job] [2]:[3] The LORD said to Satan, "Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth: a man blameless and upright, who fears God and turns away from evil. He still holds fast to his integrity, though you incited me against him to ruin him without cause."
[Job] [2]:[4] Satan answered the LORD, "Skin for skin! A man will give up all he has to save his own life.
[Job] [2]:[5] But just stretch out your hand and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will surely curse you to your face.
[Job] [2]:[6] The LORD said to Satan, "Very well, he is in your hands, but spare his life."
[Job] [2]:[7] So Satan went out from the presence of the LORD and struck Job with painful sores from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head.
[Job] [2]:[8] And Job took a piece of broken pottery to scrape himself while he sat among the ashes.
[Job] [2]:[9] His wife said to him, "Are you still holding on to your integrity? Curse God and die!"
[Job] [2]:[10] He answered her, "You are talking like a foolish woman. Shall we accept good from God and not accept trouble?" In all this Job did not sin with his lips.
[Job] [2]:[11] When Job's three friends heard of all the trouble that had come upon him, each of them set out from his own place—Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They agreed to go together to show him sympathy and comfort him.
[Job] [2]:[12] When they looked up from a distance, they could not recognize him. They wept aloud, tore their robes, and tossed dust into the air over their heads.
[Job] [2]:[13] Then they sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw how great his suffering was.
[Job] [3]:[1] After this Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
[Job] [3]:[2] Then Job spoke up and said:
[Job] [3]:[3] Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night that said, "A boy is conceived."
[Job] [3]:[4] That day—let it be darkness. Let God above not seek it out; let no light shine upon it.
[Job] [3]:[5] Let darkness and deep shadow claim it back; let a cloud settle over it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.
[Job] [3]:[6] That night—let thick darkness seize it. Let it not be counted among the days of the year; let it not enter the number of the months.
[Job] [3]:[7] Yes, let that night be barren; let no glad cry come into it.
[Job] [3]:[8] Let those who curse the day put a curse on it, those ready to rouse Leviathan.
[Job] [3]:[9] Let the stars of its twilight go dark; let it hope for light and find none, and never see the first rays of dawn—
[Job] [3]:[10] because it did not shut the doors of the womb that bore me, and hide trouble from my eyes.
[Job] [3]:[11] Why did I not die at birth, come out of the womb and breathe my last?
[Job] [3]:[12] Why were there knees to receive me, or breasts for me to nurse?
[Job] [3]:[13] For now I would be lying down in quiet; I would be asleep and at rest,
[Job] [3]:[14] with kings and counselors of the earth who built for themselves what now lies in ruins,
[Job] [3]:[15] or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.
[Job] [3]:[16] Or why was I not buried like a stillborn child, like an infant who never saw the light?
[Job] [3]:[17] There the wicked cease from raging, and there the weary are at rest.
[Job] [3]:[18] Together the prisoners are at ease; they no longer hear the slave driver's voice.
[Job] [3]:[19] Small and great are there alike, and the slave is free from his master.
[Job] [3]:[20] Why is light given to the one in misery, and life to the bitter in soul—
[Job] [3]:[21] to those who long for death that does not come, who dig for it more than for hidden treasure,
[Job] [3]:[22] who rejoice with delight and are glad when they find the grave?
[Job] [3]:[23] Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?
[Job] [3]:[24] For my sighing comes instead of my food, and my groans pour out like water.
[Job] [3]:[25] For the thing I dreaded has overtaken me, and what I feared has come upon me.
[Job] [3]:[26] I have no ease, no quiet, no rest—only turmoil.
[Job] [4]:[1] Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
[Job] [4]:[2] If someone ventures a word with you, will you be weary of it? Yet who can hold back from speaking?
[Job] [4]:[3] Think how you have instructed many, how you strengthened failing hands.
[Job] [4]:[4] Your words held up the one who stumbled; you braced the buckling knees.
[Job] [4]:[5] But now trouble comes to you, and you are worn out; it strikes you, and you are dismayed.
[Job] [4]:[6] Is not your reverence your confidence, and the integrity of your ways your hope?
[Job] [4]:[7] Consider now: who ever perished being innocent? Where were the upright ever destroyed?
[Job] [4]:[8] As I have seen, those who plow iniquity and sow trouble reap it themselves.
[Job] [4]:[9] By the breath of God they perish; by the blast of his anger they are consumed.
[Job] [4]:[10] The lion roars, the fierce lion growls, yet the teeth of the young lions are broken.
[Job] [4]:[11] The old lion dies for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness are scattered.
[Job] [4]:[12] A word was brought to me in secret; my ear caught a whisper of it.
[Job] [4]:[13] Amid troubling thoughts from visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on people,
[Job] [4]:[14] dread and trembling came over me, and terror filled all my bones.
[Job] [4]:[15] A spirit glided past my face, and the hair of my flesh stood on end.
[Job] [4]:[16] It stood still, but I could not recognize its appearance; a form was before my eyes. There was silence, and then I heard a voice:
[Job] [4]:[17] "Can a mortal be righteous before God? Can anyone be pure before his Maker?
[Job] [4]:[18] If he puts no trust in his servants and charges his angels with error,
[Job] [4]:[19] how much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed like a moth!
[Job] [4]:[20] Between morning and evening they are shattered; unnoticed, they perish forever.
[Job] [4]:[21] Is not their tent cord pulled up within them? They die, and not with wisdom.
[Job] [5]:[1] Call out, then—is there anyone to answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?
[Job] [5]:[2] For resentment kills the fool, and envy slays the simple.
[Job] [5]:[3] I myself have seen a fool taking root, but suddenly I cursed his dwelling.
[Job] [5]:[4] His children are far from safety; they are crushed in the gate, with no one to rescue them.
[Job] [5]:[5] The hungry eat up his harvest, taking it even from among the thorns, and the thirsty pant after his wealth.
[Job] [5]:[6] For trouble does not come out of the dust, nor does hardship sprout from the ground.
[Job] [5]:[7] Yet man is born to trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
[Job] [5]:[8] But as for me, I would seek God, and to God I would commit my cause—
[Job] [5]:[9] who does great things beyond searching out, wonders beyond number.
[Job] [5]:[10] He sends rain upon the earth and pours water on the open fields.
[Job] [5]:[11] He lifts the lowly on high, and those who mourn are raised to safety.
[Job] [5]:[12] He frustrates the schemes of the crafty, so that their hands achieve nothing lasting.
[Job] [5]:[13] He catches the wise in their own cunning, and the plans of the devious are brought to a quick end.
[Job] [5]:[14] By day they meet with darkness and grope at noon as though it were night.
[Job] [5]:[15] But he saves the needy from the sword of their mouth, from the grip of the strong.
[Job] [5]:[16] So the poor have hope, and injustice shuts its mouth.
[Job] [5]:[17] Blessed indeed is the one whom God corrects; do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.
[Job] [5]:[18] For he wounds, but he binds up; he strikes, but his hands also heal.
[Job] [5]:[19] From six troubles he will deliver you; in seven no harm will touch you.
[Job] [5]:[20] In famine he will ransom you from death, and in battle from the power of the sword.
[Job] [5]:[21] You will be hidden from the lash of the tongue, and you will not fear destruction when it comes.
[Job] [5]:[22] At destruction and famine you will laugh, and you will not fear the beasts of the earth.
[Job] [5]:[23] For you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you.
[Job] [5]:[24] You will know that your tent is secure; you will inspect your home and find nothing missing.
[Job] [5]:[25] You will know that your offspring are many, your descendants like the grass of the earth.
[Job] [5]:[26] You will come to the grave in full vigor, like a sheaf gathered in its season.
[Job] [5]:[27] See, we have examined this, and it is true. Hear it, and know it for yourself.
[Job] [6]:[1] Then Job answered:
[Job] [6]:[2] If only my anguish could be weighed, and all my ruin laid on the scales together!
[Job] [6]:[3] It would outweigh the sand of the seas — that is why my words have been rash.
[Job] [6]:[4] For the arrows of the Almighty are in me; my spirit drinks their poison. God's terrors are arrayed against me.
[Job] [6]:[5] Does the wild donkey bray over fresh grass, or the ox bellow over its fodder?
[Job] [6]:[6] Is tasteless food eaten without salt? Is there any flavor in the white of an egg?
[Job] [6]:[7] I refuse to touch such things; they are like food that makes me sick.
[Job] [6]:[8] Oh, that I might have my request, that God would grant what I long for —
[Job] [6]:[9] that God would be willing to crush me, to let loose his hand and cut me off!
[Job] [6]:[10] Then I would still have this comfort, this joy amid relentless pain: that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
[Job] [6]:[11] What strength do I have, that I should still hope? What is my end, that I should be patient?
[Job] [6]:[12] Is my strength the strength of stone? Is my flesh bronze?
[Job] [6]:[13] Is there any help left in me, now that success has been driven from me?
[Job] [6]:[14] A despairing man should have the loyalty of his friend, even if that man forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
[Job] [6]:[15] But my brothers are as treacherous as a wadi, as the streambeds that run dry,
[Job] [6]:[16] dark with melting ice, swollen with thawing snow,
[Job] [6]:[17] but ceasing to flow in the dry season, vanishing from their place in the heat.
[Job] [6]:[18] Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go up into the wasteland and perish.
[Job] [6]:[19] The caravans of Tema look for water, the traveling merchants of Sheba hope for it,
[Job] [6]:[20] but they are put to shame for their confidence; they arrive there only to be disappointed.
[Job] [6]:[21] Now you have become like that to me: you see something dreadful and are afraid.
[Job] [6]:[22] Have I ever said, 'Give me something,' or 'Pay a ransom for me out of your wealth,'
[Job] [6]:[23] or 'Rescue me from the hand of the enemy,' or 'Redeem me from the grip of the ruthless'?
[Job] [6]:[24] Teach me, and I will be silent; show me where I have gone wrong.
[Job] [6]:[25] How painful are honest words! But what does your arguing prove?
[Job] [6]:[26] Do you think you can correct what I say and treat the words of a desperate man as wind?
[Job] [6]:[27] You would even cast lots for an orphan and barter away your friend.
[Job] [6]:[28] But now, be so kind as to look at me. Would I lie to your face?
[Job] [6]:[29] Relent; let there be no injustice. Reconsider, for my cause is still just.
[Job] [6]:[30] Is there any wrong on my tongue? Can my mouth not discern what is malicious?
[Job] [7]:[1] Is not the life of a mortal on earth a hard service? Are not his days like the days of a hired laborer?
[Job] [7]:[2] Like a slave longing for the shade, like a hired hand waiting for his wages,
[Job] [7]:[3] so I have been allotted months of emptiness, and nights of misery have been assigned to me.
[Job] [7]:[4] When I lie down I ask, "When will I get up?" But the night drags on, and I am filled with tossing until dawn.
[Job] [7]:[5] My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin scabs over and oozes.
[Job] [7]:[6] My days pass more swiftly than a weaver's shuttle, and they come to an end without hope.
[Job] [7]:[7] Remember that my life is but a breath; my eye will never again see anything good.
[Job] [7]:[8] The eye that now sees me will see me no more; your eyes will turn toward me, but I will be gone.
[Job] [7]:[9] As a cloud fades and vanishes, so the one who goes down to the grave does not come up again.
[Job] [7]:[10] He never returns to his house; his place knows him no more.
[Job] [7]:[11] So I, for my part, will not restrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit, I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
[Job] [7]:[12] Am I the sea, or a sea monster, that you set a guard over me?
[Job] [7]:[13] When I think my bed will comfort me and my couch will ease my complaint,
[Job] [7]:[14] then you terrify me with dreams and horrify me with visions,
[Job] [7]:[15] so that I would choose strangling and death rather than this body of mine.
[Job] [7]:[16] I despise my life; I would not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are a breath.
[Job] [7]:[17] What is a mortal, that you make so much of him, that you set your heart upon him,
[Job] [7]:[18] that you examine him every morning and test him every moment?
[Job] [7]:[19] Will you never look away from me, or let me alone long enough to swallow my spit?
[Job] [7]:[20] If I have sinned, what can I do to you, you watcher of mankind? Why have you made me your target, so that I have become a burden to myself?
[Job] [7]:[21] Why do you not pardon my offense and take away my guilt? For soon I will lie down in the dust; you will search for me, and I will be no more.
[Job] [8]:[1] Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
[Job] [8]:[2] How long will you go on talking like this? The words of your mouth are a driving wind.
[Job] [8]:[3] Does God pervert justice? Does the Almighty pervert what is right?
[Job] [8]:[4] If your children sinned against him, he handed them over to their own rebellion.
[Job] [8]:[5] But if you will seek God and plead with the Almighty for mercy,
[Job] [8]:[6] if you are pure and upright, then surely he will rouse himself for you and restore your rightful home.
[Job] [8]:[7] Then your beginnings will seem small, so great will your future be.
[Job] [8]:[8] Ask the generations that came before; consider what their fathers discovered.
[Job] [8]:[9] For we were born only yesterday and know nothing; our days on earth are a shadow.
[Job] [8]:[10] Will they not teach you and tell you, and bring forth words out of their hearts?
[Job] [8]:[11] Can papyrus grow tall where there is no marsh? Can reeds flourish without water?
[Job] [8]:[12] Still in bloom and uncut, they wither faster than any grass.
[Job] [8]:[13] So are the paths of all who forget God; the hope of the godless perishes.
[Job] [8]:[14] His confidence is fragile, his trust a spider's web.
[Job] [8]:[15] He leans on his house, but it does not stand; he clings to it, but it does not hold.
[Job] [8]:[16] He is like a well-watered plant in the sunshine, spreading its shoots over the garden;
[Job] [8]:[17] its roots wrap around a pile of rocks and cling to a house of stones.
[Job] [8]:[18] But when it is torn from its place, that place disowns it: 'I never saw you.'
[Job] [8]:[19] See, such is the joy of his way, and from the soil others spring up.
[Job] [8]:[20] Surely God does not reject a blameless man, nor does he uphold the hand of evildoers.
