[Job] [8]:[21] He will yet fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouts of joy.
[Job] [8]:[22] Those who hate you will be clothed in shame, and the tent of the wicked will be no more.
[Job] [9]:[1] Then Job answered:
[Job] [9]:[2] "Yes, I know it is so. But how can a mortal be right before God?
[Job] [9]:[3] If one wished to contend with him, he could not answer him once in a thousand times.
[Job] [9]:[4] He is wise in heart and mighty in strength—who has ever defied him and come away whole?
[Job] [9]:[5] He moves mountains, and they never know it; he overturns them in his anger.
[Job] [9]:[6] He shakes the earth from its place, and its pillars tremble.
[Job] [9]:[7] He commands the sun, and it does not rise; he seals up the stars.
[Job] [9]:[8] He alone stretches out the heavens and treads on the heights of the sea.
[Job] [9]:[9] He made the Bear and Orion, the Pleiades and the chambers of the south.
[Job] [9]:[10] He does great things beyond searching out, wonders beyond number.
[Job] [9]:[11] If he passes by me, I do not see him; if he moves on, I do not perceive him.
[Job] [9]:[12] If he snatches away, who can turn him back? Who can say to him, 'What are you doing?'
[Job] [9]:[13] God does not turn back his anger; beneath him the helpers of Rahab bow low.
[Job] [9]:[14] How then could I answer him, or choose my words to argue with him?
[Job] [9]:[15] Though I were in the right, I could not answer; I could only plead with my judge for mercy.
[Job] [9]:[16] If I called and he answered me, I could not believe that he was listening to my voice.
[Job] [9]:[17] For he crushes me with a tempest and multiplies my wounds without cause.
[Job] [9]:[18] He will not let me catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
[Job] [9]:[19] If it is a matter of strength—he is mighty! If of justice—who can summon him?
[Job] [9]:[20] Though I were righteous, my own mouth would condemn me; though I were blameless, it would prove me perverse.
[Job] [9]:[21] I am blameless—yet I do not know myself; I despise my life.
[Job] [9]:[22] It is all the same; therefore I say: he destroys both the blameless and the wicked.
[Job] [9]:[23] When a scourge brings sudden death, he mocks the despair of the innocent.
[Job] [9]:[24] The earth is handed over to the wicked; he covers the faces of its judges. If it is not he, then who?
[Job] [9]:[25] My days are swifter than a runner; they flee away, they see no good.
[Job] [9]:[26] They skim past like boats of reed, like an eagle swooping on its prey.
[Job] [9]:[27] If I say, 'I will forget my complaint, I will change my expression and smile,'
[Job] [9]:[28] I still dread all my sufferings, for I know you will not hold me innocent.
[Job] [9]:[29] I will be held guilty—why then should I labor in vain?
[Job] [9]:[30] If I washed myself with snow water and cleansed my hands with lye,
[Job] [9]:[31] you would plunge me into the pit, and even my own clothes would loathe me.
[Job] [9]:[32] For he is not a man like me, that I could answer him, that we could come together in court.
[Job] [9]:[33] There is no arbiter between us who could lay his hand on us both,
[Job] [9]:[34] who could remove God's rod from me, so that his terror would no longer frighten me.
[Job] [9]:[35] Then I would speak without fear of him—but as it is, I am not so within myself.
[Job] [10]:[1] I am sick of my life. I will let my complaint run free; I will speak out of the bitterness of my soul.
[Job] [10]:[2] I will say to God: Do not condemn me. Tell me what charge you bring against me.
[Job] [10]:[3] Does it please you to oppress me, to spurn the work of your own hands while you smile on the schemes of the wicked?
[Job] [10]:[4] Do you have eyes of flesh? Do you see as a mortal sees?
[Job] [10]:[5] Are your days like the days of a mortal, your years like the years of a man,
[Job] [10]:[6] that you must search out my guilt and hunt for my sin—
[Job] [10]:[7] though you know that I am not guilty, and no one can rescue me from your hand?
[Job] [10]:[8] Your hands shaped me and made me, every part of me; will you now turn and destroy me?
[Job] [10]:[9] Remember, I pray, that you molded me like clay. Will you return me to the dust?
[Job] [10]:[10] Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese,
[Job] [10]:[11] clothe me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with bones and sinews?
[Job] [10]:[12] You granted me life and showed me mercy, and your care watched over my spirit.
[Job] [10]:[13] Yet this is what you hid in your heart; now I know what you had in mind.
[Job] [10]:[14] If I sinned, you were watching me, and you would not let my guilt go unpunished.
[Job] [10]:[15] If I am guilty—woe to me! And even if I am innocent, I cannot lift up my head, for I am filled with shame and see nothing but my affliction.
[Job] [10]:[16] If I hold my head high, you hunt me like a lion and display your power against me again and again.
[Job] [10]:[17] You bring fresh witnesses against me and pour out your anger on me; wave after wave assaults me.
[Job] [10]:[18] Why then did you bring me out of the womb? I wish I had died before any eye saw me,
[Job] [10]:[19] that I had never come to be—carried straight from the womb to the grave.
[Job] [10]:[20] Are not my days few? Let me alone, turn away from me, so I may have a moment's comfort
[Job] [10]:[21] before I go, never to return, to the land of darkness and deepest shadow,
[Job] [10]:[22] to a land of gloom, dark as night itself, of deathly shadow and no order, where even the light is like darkness.
[Job] [11]:[1] Then Zophar the Naamathite answered:
[Job] [11]:[2] "Should such a flood of words go unanswered? Is a man proved right just because he talks?
[Job] [11]:[3] Should your empty talk silence others? Are you to mock with no one to rebuke you?
[Job] [11]:[4] You say, 'My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your sight.'
[Job] [11]:[5] But oh, that God himself would speak, that he would open his lips against you,
[Job] [11]:[6] and disclose to you the secrets of wisdom—for sound understanding has two sides. Then you would know that God has overlooked much of your guilt.
[Job] [11]:[7] Can you fathom the depths of God? Can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
[Job] [11]:[8] Higher than the heavens—what can you do? Deeper than the grave—what can you know?
[Job] [11]:[9] Its measure is longer than the earth and wider than the sea.
[Job] [11]:[10] If he sweeps through and imprisons, if he convenes the court, who can turn him back?
[Job] [11]:[11] For he knows those who are worthless; he sees their wickedness—should he not take note of it?
[Job] [11]:[12] But a hollow man will gain understanding about as soon as a wild donkey is born human.
[Job] [11]:[13] If you would set your heart right and stretch out your hands to him,
[Job] [11]:[14] if you put away the sin that is in your hand and let no wrongdoing dwell in your tents,
[Job] [11]:[15] then you could lift up your face without shame; you would stand firm and be unafraid.
[Job] [11]:[16] You would forget your misery, remembering it like waters that have flowed away.
[Job] [11]:[17] Your life would be brighter than noon, and darkness would become like morning.
[Job] [11]:[18] You would rest secure, for there is hope; you would look around and lie down in safety.
[Job] [11]:[19] You would rest with no one to make you afraid, and many would seek your favor.
[Job] [11]:[20] But the eyes of the wicked will fail; every escape will be cut off from them, and their hope will be the last gasp of breath."
[Job] [12]:[1] Then Job answered:
[Job] [12]:[2] No doubt you are the people, and wisdom will die with you!
[Job] [12]:[3] But I too have a mind like yours; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know such things as these?
[Job] [12]:[4] I have become a laughingstock to my friends — I, who called on God and he answered me; the just and blameless man is a laughingstock.
[Job] [12]:[5] Contempt for misfortune — that is the thought of the man at ease; it waits for those whose feet are slipping.
[Job] [12]:[6] The tents of raiders are left in peace, and those who provoke God are secure — those who carry their god in their own hand.
[Job] [12]:[7] But ask the animals, and they will teach you; the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.
[Job] [12]:[8] Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; let the fish of the sea declare it to you.
[Job] [12]:[9] Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
[Job] [12]:[10] In his hand is the life of every living thing and the breath of all mankind.
[Job] [12]:[11] Does not the ear test words as the palate tastes food?
[Job] [12]:[12] Wisdom is with the aged, and understanding comes with length of days.
[Job] [12]:[13] With God are wisdom and might; his are counsel and understanding.
[Job] [12]:[14] See, what he tears down cannot be rebuilt; the man he shuts in cannot be released.
[Job] [12]:[15] If he holds back the waters, there is drought; if he lets them loose, they overwhelm the land.
[Job] [12]:[16] With him are strength and sound wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver are both his.
[Job] [12]:[17] He leads counselors away stripped and makes fools of judges.
[Job] [12]:[18] He loosens the fetters put on by kings and binds a loincloth around their waists.
[Job] [12]:[19] He leads priests away stripped and overthrows the long established.
[Job] [12]:[20] He silences the lips of trusted advisers and takes away the discernment of elders.
[Job] [12]:[21] He pours contempt on nobles and loosens the belt of the mighty.
[Job] [12]:[22] He uncovers the deep things of darkness and brings deep shadow into the light.
[Job] [12]:[23] He makes nations great, and destroys them; he spreads nations abroad, and leads them away.
[Job] [12]:[24] He takes away the understanding of the leaders of the people of the earth, and sends them wandering in a trackless waste.
[Job] [12]:[25] They grope in darkness with no light; he makes them stagger like drunkards.
[Job] [13]:[1] All this my eye has seen; my ear has heard and understood it.
[Job] [13]:[2] What you know, I know as well; I am not inferior to you.
[Job] [13]:[3] But I would speak to the Almighty; I want to argue my case with God.
[Job] [13]:[4] You, however, are plasterers of lies; every one of you is a worthless healer.
[Job] [13]:[5] If only you would keep completely silent! That would be your wisdom.
[Job] [13]:[6] Hear now my argument; listen to the pleading of my lips.
[Job] [13]:[7] Will you speak falsely on God's behalf? Will you tell lies for him?
[Job] [13]:[8] Will you show him partiality? Will you argue the case for God?
[Job] [13]:[9] Would it go well when he examines you? Can you deceive him as one deceives a man?
[Job] [13]:[10] He would surely rebuke you if you secretly showed partiality.
[Job] [13]:[11] Would not his majesty terrify you, and the dread of him fall upon you?
[Job] [13]:[12] Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are walls of clay.
[Job] [13]:[13] Be silent and let me speak; then let come upon me what may.
[Job] [13]:[14] Why should I take my flesh in my teeth and hold my life in my hands?
[Job] [13]:[15] Though he slay me, yet will I hope in him; still I will argue my case to his face.
[Job] [13]:[16] This itself will be my salvation, for no godless man may come before him.
[Job] [13]:[17] Listen carefully to my words; let my declaration reach your ears.
[Job] [13]:[18] See, I have prepared my case; I know that I will be vindicated.
[Job] [13]:[19] Who is there to contend with me? If there is, then let me be silent and die.
[Job] [13]:[20] Only two things do not do to me, and then I will not hide from your face:
[Job] [13]:[21] Withdraw your hand from me, and do not let your terror frighten me.
[Job] [13]:[22] Then summon me, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you reply to me.
[Job] [13]:[23] How many are my iniquities and sins? Show me my offense and my sin.
[Job] [13]:[24] Why do you hide your face and treat me as your enemy?
[Job] [13]:[25] Would you terrify a windblown leaf? Would you chase after dry stubble?
[Job] [13]:[26] For you write down bitter charges against me and make me inherit the sins of my youth.
[Job] [13]:[27] You put my feet in the stocks and watch all my paths; you mark the very soles of my feet.
[Job] [13]:[28] So man wastes away like something rotten, like a garment eaten by moths.
[Job] [14]:[1] Man, born of woman, is short of days and full of trouble.
[Job] [14]:[2] He comes up like a flower and withers; he flees like a shadow and does not last.
[Job] [14]:[3] And on such a one you fix your eye? Do you bring me into judgment with you?
[Job] [14]:[4] Who can bring what is clean out of what is unclean? No one.
[Job] [14]:[5] Since his days are determined, the number of his months is with you; you have set his limit, and he cannot pass beyond it.
[Job] [14]:[6] Look away from him and let him be, until he has served out his day like a hired hand.
[Job] [14]:[7] For a tree there is hope: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its shoots will not fail.
[Job] [14]:[8] Though its root grows old in the ground and its stump dies in the dust,
[Job] [14]:[9] at the scent of water it will bud and put out branches like a young plant.
[Job] [14]:[10] But a man dies and is laid low; a mortal breathes his last, and where is he?
[Job] [14]:[11] As water disappears from the sea, and a river runs dry and is parched,
[Job] [14]:[12] so a man lies down and does not rise. Till the heavens are no more he will not awake, nor be roused from his sleep.
[Job] [14]:[13] If only you would hide me in the grave, conceal me until your anger passes, set me a fixed time and then remember me!
[Job] [14]:[14] If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I would wait, until my relief should come.
[Job] [14]:[15] You would call, and I would answer you; you would long for the work of your hands.
[Job] [14]:[16] For then you would count my steps, but not keep watch over my sin.
[Job] [14]:[17] My offense would be sealed up in a bag, and you would cover over my guilt.
[Job] [14]:[18] But as a mountain crumbles away and a rock is moved from its place,
[Job] [14]:[19] as water wears away the stones and torrents wash away the soil of the earth, so you destroy the hope of mortals.
[Job] [14]:[20] You overpower him once and for all, and he is gone; you change his face and send him away.
[Job] [14]:[21] If his children are honored, he does not know it; if they are brought low, he never perceives it.
[Job] [14]:[22] He feels only the pain of his own flesh; his own soul mourns within him.
[Job] [15]:[1] Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
[Job] [15]:[2] "Should a wise man answer with empty wind, filling his belly with the east wind?
[Job] [15]:[3] Should he argue with words that accomplish nothing, with speeches that serve no purpose?
[Job] [15]:[4] But you—you undermine the fear of God and hinder devotion before him.
[Job] [15]:[5] Your own guilt is teaching your mouth; you choose the tongue of the crafty.
[Job] [15]:[6] Your own mouth condemns you, not I; your own lips testify against you.
[Job] [15]:[7] Were you the first man ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
[Job] [15]:[8] Have you listened in on God's council? Do you keep wisdom to yourself alone?
[Job] [15]:[9] What do you know that we do not know? What insight have you that we lack?
[Job] [15]:[10] Among us are the gray-haired and the aged, men older than your father.
[Job] [15]:[11] Are God's consolations too small for you, a word spoken gently to you?
[Job] [15]:[12] Why does your heart carry you away? Why do your eyes flash,
[Job] [15]:[13] that you turn your spirit against God and let such words pour from your mouth?
[Job] [15]:[14] What is man, that he should be pure, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?
[Job] [15]:[15] If God puts no trust in his holy ones, and even the heavens are not clean in his eyes,
[Job] [15]:[16] how much less man, loathsome and corrupt, who drinks in wickedness like water!
[Job] [15]:[17] Listen to me and I will explain; what I have seen, I will declare—
[Job] [15]:[18] what wise men have handed down, hiding nothing they received from their fathers,
[Job] [15]:[19] who alone possessed the land, with no stranger passing among them.
[Job] [15]:[20] All his days the wicked man writhes in torment; the years are numbered for the ruthless.
[Job] [15]:[21] Terrifying sounds fill his ears; in the midst of peace the destroyer comes for him.
[Job] [15]:[22] He has no hope of escaping the darkness; the sword lies in wait for him.
[Job] [15]:[23] He wanders in search of bread: "Where is it?" He knows the day of darkness is close at hand.
[Job] [15]:[24] Distress and anguish terrify him; they overwhelm him like a king poised for the assault.
[Job] [15]:[25] For he stretched out his hand against God and defied the Almighty,
[Job] [15]:[26] charging at him with stiff neck, behind the thick bosses of his shield.
[Job] [15]:[27] His face is padded with fat, his waist swollen with flesh.
[Job] [15]:[28] He will live in ruined towns, in houses where no one dwells, houses crumbling into rubble.
[Job] [15]:[29] He will not grow rich; his wealth will not endure, nor will his possessions spread over the land.
[Job] [15]:[30] He will not escape the darkness; a flame will wither his shoots, and the breath of God's mouth will carry him away.
[Job] [15]:[31] Let him not trust in what is worthless and be deceived, for emptiness will be all he gains.
[Job] [15]:[32] Before his time he will be paid in full, and his branch will never turn green.
[Job] [15]:[33] Like a vine he will shake off his unripe grapes, like an olive tree he will cast off his blossoms.
[Job] [15]:[34] For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of those who take bribes.
[Job] [15]:[35] They conceive trouble and give birth to evil; their womb fashions deceit."
[Job] [16]:[1] Then Job answered:
[Job] [16]:[2] I have heard many things like these. Miserable comforters are you all!
[Job] [16]:[3] Is there no end to your windy words? What provokes you to keep answering?
[Job] [16]:[4] I too could speak as you do, if you were in my place. I could string together fine words against you and shake my head at you.
[Job] [16]:[5] But I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the comfort of my lips would ease your pain.
[Job] [16]:[6] If I speak, my pain is not eased; and if I hold back, what relief goes from me?
[Job] [16]:[7] Surely now he has worn me out. You have laid waste all my company.
[Job] [16]:[8] You have shriveled me up, and it stands as a witness; my gauntness rises against me and testifies to my face.
[Job] [16]:[9] His anger has torn me and hunted me down; he has gnashed his teeth at me. My adversary fixes his glaring eyes on me.
[Job] [16]:[10] Men gape at me with open mouths; they strike my cheeks in scorn; they mass themselves together against me.
[Job] [16]:[11] God hands me over to the ungodly and flings me into the grip of the wicked.
[Job] [16]:[12] I was at ease, and he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and dashed me to pieces. He has set me up as his target;
[Job] [16]:[13] his archers surround me. He pierces my kidneys without pity and pours my gall on the ground.
[Job] [16]:[14] He breaks through me, breach upon breach; he rushes at me like a warrior.
[Job] [16]:[15] I have sewn sackcloth over my skin and thrust my horn into the dust.
[Job] [16]:[16] My face is flushed with weeping, and deep shadow lies on my eyelids,
[Job] [16]:[17] though there is no violence in my hands and my prayer is pure.
[Job] [16]:[18] O earth, do not cover my blood; let my cry find no resting place.
[Job] [16]:[19] Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven; the one who vouches for me is on high.
[Job] [16]:[20] My friends are my mockers; to God my eye pours out its tears,
[Job] [16]:[21] that he might plead a man's case with God, as one pleads for a friend.
[Job] [16]:[22] For only a few years will pass, and then I will walk the road from which I shall not return.
[Job] [17]:[1] My spirit is broken, my days are snuffed out, the graves are ready for me.
[Job] [17]:[2] Surely mockers surround me, and my eyes must dwell on their hostility.
[Job] [17]:[3] Give me, I pray, the pledge you require; who else will shake hands as my guarantor?
[Job] [17]:[4] You have closed their minds to understanding; therefore you will not let them triumph.
[Job] [17]:[5] Whoever betrays his friends for a share of the spoil, the eyes of his children will fail.
[Job] [17]:[6] He has made me a byword among the peoples, a man in whose face they spit.
[Job] [17]:[7] My eyes have grown dim with grief, and all my limbs are but a shadow.
[Job] [17]:[8] The upright are appalled at this, and the innocent are stirred up against the godless.
[Job] [17]:[9] Yet the righteous holds to his way, and he whose hands are clean grows stronger.
[Job] [17]:[10] But turn, all of you, and come again, I beg you! Yet I will find no wise man among you.
[Job] [17]:[11] My days are past, my plans are shattered, and so are the desires of my heart.
[Job] [17]:[12] These men turn night into day; in the face of darkness they say, 'Light is near.'
[Job] [17]:[13] If the only home I hope for is the grave, if I spread out my bed in darkness,
[Job] [17]:[14] if I say to the pit, 'You are my father,' and to the worm, 'My mother' or 'My sister,'
[Job] [17]:[15] where then is my hope? Who can see any hope for me?
[Job] [17]:[16] Will it go down with me to the bars of the grave? Shall we rest together in the dust?
[Job] [18]:[1] Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
[Job] [18]:[2] How long will you go on hunting for words? Think it through, and then we can talk.
[Job] [18]:[3] Why are we counted as cattle, reckoned unclean in your eyes?
[Job] [18]:[4] You who tear yourself to pieces in your anger — shall the earth be abandoned for your sake, or the rock be moved from its place?
[Job] [18]:[5] Indeed, the light of the wicked is extinguished; the flame of his fire no longer shines.
[Job] [18]:[6] The light in his tent grows dark, and the lamp above him is snuffed out.
[Job] [18]:[7] His vigorous stride is cut short, and his own schemes throw him down.
[Job] [18]:[8] For by his own feet he is thrust into a net; he walks about upon the netting.
[Job] [18]:[9] A trap seizes him by the heel; a snare holds him fast.
[Job] [18]:[10] A rope lies hidden for him in the ground, a snare across his path.
[Job] [18]:[11] Terrors startle him on every side and chase him at his heels.
[Job] [18]:[12] Hunger wastes away his strength; ruin waits ready for his fall.
[Job] [18]:[13] Disease eats away his skin; the firstborn of death devours his limbs.
[Job] [18]:[14] He is torn from the safety of his tent and marched off to the king of terrors.
[Job] [18]:[15] Strangers settle in his tent, for nothing of his remains; burning sulfur is scattered over his dwelling.
[Job] [18]:[16] Below, his roots dry up; above, his branches wither.
[Job] [18]:[17] His memory perishes from the earth; he has no name in the streets.
[Job] [18]:[18] He is driven from light into darkness and banished from the world.
[Job] [18]:[19] He leaves no offspring or descendant among his people, no survivor where he once lived.
[Job] [18]:[20] Those who come after are appalled at his day; those who went before are seized with horror.
[Job] [18]:[21] Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked, and this is the place of the one who does not know God.
[Job] [19]:[1] Then Job answered:
[Job] [19]:[2] How long will you torment me and crush me with words?
[Job] [19]:[3] Ten times now you have insulted me; you are not ashamed to abuse me.
[Job] [19]:[4] And even if I have gone astray, my error is my own concern.
[Job] [19]:[5] If indeed you would exalt yourselves over me and use my disgrace against me,
[Job] [19]:[6] then know this: it is God who has wronged me and closed his net around me.
[Job] [19]:[7] I cry out, "Violence!" but there is no answer; I call for help, but there is no justice.
[Job] [19]:[8] He has walled up my way so I cannot pass, and he has draped my paths in darkness.
[Job] [19]:[9] He has stripped me of my honor and taken the crown from my head.
[Job] [19]:[10] He tears me down on every side until I am gone; he uproots my hope like a tree.
[Job] [19]:[11] His anger burns against me; he counts me among his enemies.
[Job] [19]:[12] His troops advance together; they build a siege ramp against me and camp around my tent.
[Job] [19]:[13] He has driven my brothers far from me; my acquaintances have become total strangers.
[Job] [19]:[14] My relatives have failed me; my close friends have forgotten me.
[Job] [19]:[15] Those who live in my house and my serving women count me a stranger; I have become a foreigner in their eyes.
[Job] [19]:[16] I call my servant, and he does not answer; I have to plead with him myself.
[Job] [19]:[17] My breath is repulsive to my wife; I am loathsome to my own children.
[Job] [19]:[18] Even young boys despise me; when I stand up, they speak against me.
[Job] [19]:[19] All my closest friends detest me; those I loved have turned against me.
[Job] [19]:[20] My bones cling to my skin and my flesh; I have escaped with nothing but the skin of my teeth.
[Job] [19]:[21] Have pity on me, my friends, have pity, for the hand of God has struck me.
[Job] [19]:[22] Why do you hound me as God does? Will you never have your fill of my flesh?
[Job] [19]:[23] Oh, that my words were written down! Oh, that they were inscribed in a scroll,
[Job] [19]:[24] cut with an iron stylus and filled with lead, carved in rock forever!
[Job] [19]:[25] But I know that my Redeemer lives, and in the end he will stand upon the dust.
[Job] [19]:[26] And after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God.
[Job] [19]:[27] I myself will see him; my own eyes will behold him, and not another. My heart faints with longing within me.
[Job] [19]:[28] If you say, "How we will hound him!" and, "The root of the trouble lies in him,"
[Job] [19]:[29] then fear the sword yourselves, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword; then you will know that there is judgment.
[Job] [20]:[1] Then Zophar the Naamathite answered:
[Job] [20]:[2] "My thoughts compel me to reply; that is why the agitation rises in me.
[Job] [20]:[3] I have heard a rebuke that shames me, but the spirit of my understanding gives me my answer.
[Job] [20]:[4] Surely you know this from of old, ever since man was set upon the earth:
[Job] [20]:[5] the triumph of the wicked is brief, and the joy of the godless lasts only a moment.
[Job] [20]:[6] Though his pride climbs to the heavens and his head reaches the clouds,
[Job] [20]:[7] he will perish forever like his own dung; those who saw him will ask, 'Where is he?'
[Job] [20]:[8] Like a dream he flies away, and no one finds him; he is driven off like a vision of the night.
[Job] [20]:[9] The eye that glimpsed him will see him no more; his place will never behold him again.
[Job] [20]:[10] His children must make amends to the poor; his own hands must give back his wealth.
[Job] [20]:[11] His bones may be full of youthful vigor, but it lies down with him in the dust.
[Job] [20]:[12] Though evil tastes sweet in his mouth and he hides it under his tongue,
[Job] [20]:[13] though he savors it and will not let it go, holding it against his palate,
[Job] [20]:[14] yet his food turns sour in his stomach; it becomes the venom of vipers within him.
[Job] [20]:[15] He swallows down riches and vomits them up again; God drives them out of his belly.
[Job] [20]:[16] He sucks the poison of vipers; the tongue of the adder kills him.
[Job] [20]:[17] He will never see the streams, the rivers running with honey and cream.
[Job] [20]:[18] He must give back his gain and never swallow it; he cannot enjoy the profit of his trading.
[Job] [20]:[19] For he crushed the poor and left them destitute; he seized a house he did not build.
[Job] [20]:[20] His greed knew no peace; nothing he treasured can save him.
[Job] [20]:[21] Nothing escaped his devouring; therefore his prosperity will not last.
[Job] [20]:[22] In the fullness of his plenty, distress will overtake him; every hand of the wretched will come against him.
[Job] [20]:[23] When he has filled his belly, God will unleash his burning anger against him and rain it down upon him as his food.
[Job] [20]:[24] Though he flees from an iron weapon, an arrow from a bow of bronze will pierce him through.
[Job] [20]:[25] It is drawn out and comes through his back, the gleaming point out of his gall; terrors close in on him.
[Job] [20]:[26] Utter darkness lies in wait for his treasures; a fire that no breath has fanned will consume him, and it will go badly for whoever is left in his tent.
[Job] [20]:[27] The heavens will expose his guilt, and the earth will rise up against him.
[Job] [20]:[28] The produce of his house will be carried away, poured out in torrents on the day of God's wrath.
[Job] [20]:[29] This is the portion God assigns the wicked, the inheritance decreed for him by God."
[Job] [21]:[1] Then Job answered:
[Job] [21]:[2] "Listen closely to what I say; let this be the comfort you offer me.
[Job] [21]:[3] Bear with me while I speak, and after I have spoken, mock if you must.
[Job] [21]:[4] Is my complaint against a mere man? Why then should I not lose patience?
[Job] [21]:[5] Look at me and be appalled; clap your hand over your mouth.
[Job] [21]:[6] When I remember, I am terrified, and shuddering seizes my flesh.
[Job] [21]:[7] Why do the wicked go on living, growing old and increasing in power?
[Job] [21]:[8] Their children are secure around them, their offspring before their eyes.
[Job] [21]:[9] Their homes are safe and free from fear; the rod of God does not fall on them.
[Job] [21]:[10] Their bull breeds and never fails; their cow calves and does not miscarry.
[Job] [21]:[11] They send out their little ones like a flock; their children dance about.
[Job] [21]:[12] They lift their voices with tambourine and lyre, and rejoice at the sound of the pipe.
[Job] [21]:[13] They spend their days in prosperity and in a moment go down to the grave.
[Job] [21]:[14] Yet they say to God, 'Leave us alone! We have no desire to know your ways.
[Job] [21]:[15] Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What would we gain by praying to him?'
[Job] [21]:[16] But their prosperity is not in their own hands; the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
[Job] [21]:[17] How often is the lamp of the wicked snuffed out? How often does disaster overtake them, and God in his anger deal out their portion of pain?
[Job] [21]:[18] How often are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?
[Job] [21]:[19] You say, 'God stores up a man's punishment for his children.' Let him repay the man himself, so that he knows it!
[Job] [21]:[20] Let his own eyes see his ruin; let him drink the wrath of the Almighty.
[Job] [21]:[21] For what does he care about the household he leaves behind, when the number of his months is cut off?
[Job] [21]:[22] Can anyone teach knowledge to God, who judges even those on high?
[Job] [21]:[23] One man dies in full vigor, wholly at ease and secure;
[Job] [21]:[24] his sides are filled with fat, and the marrow of his bones is moist.
[Job] [21]:[25] Another dies with a bitter soul, having never tasted anything good.
[Job] [21]:[26] Side by side they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them both.
[Job] [21]:[27] I know full well what you are thinking, the schemes by which you would wrong me.
[Job] [21]:[28] For you ask, 'Where now is the nobleman's house? Where are the tents the wicked lived in?'
[Job] [21]:[29] Have you never asked those who travel the roads? Do you not recognize the signs they give—
[Job] [21]:[30] that the evil man is spared in the day of calamity, led away safe on the day of wrath?
[Job] [21]:[31] Who confronts him to his face with his conduct? Who repays him for what he has done?
[Job] [21]:[32] He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.
[Job] [21]:[33] The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows in his train, and those who went before him are beyond number.
[Job] [21]:[34] So how can you comfort me with empty words? Of your answers, nothing remains but falsehood."
[Job] [22]:[1] Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered:
[Job] [22]:[2] "Can a man be of use to God? Can even the wisest be of profit to him?
[Job] [22]:[3] Does it delight the Almighty that you are righteous? Does he gain anything if your ways are blameless?
[Job] [22]:[4] Is it for your reverence that he rebukes you and brings you to judgment?
[Job] [22]:[5] Is not your wickedness great, and your sins beyond counting?
[Job] [22]:[6] For you took pledges from your brothers without cause and stripped the naked of their clothing.
[Job] [22]:[7] You gave no water to the weary and withheld bread from the hungry.
[Job] [22]:[8] The land belonged to the man of power, and the favored one lived on it.
[Job] [22]:[9] You sent widows away empty-handed and crushed the strength of orphans.
[Job] [22]:[10] That is why snares surround you and sudden terror overwhelms you,
[Job] [22]:[11] why darkness blinds you and a flood of water covers you over.
[Job] [22]:[12] Is not God in the heights of heaven? Look how high the loftiest stars are!
[Job] [22]:[13] Yet you say, 'What does God know? Can he judge through the thick darkness?
[Job] [22]:[14] Thick clouds veil him, so he cannot see, as he walks the vault of heaven.'
[Job] [22]:[15] Will you keep to the ancient path that wicked men have trodden?
[Job] [22]:[16] They were snatched away before their time, their foundations washed out by a flood.
[Job] [22]:[17] They said to God, "Leave us alone! What can the Almighty do to us?"
[Job] [22]:[18] Yet it was he who filled their houses with good things. So the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
[Job] [22]:[19] The righteous see their ruin and rejoice; the innocent mock them:
[Job] [22]:[20] "Surely our adversaries are wiped out, and fire has devoured what they left behind."
[Job] [22]:[21] Come to terms with God and be at peace with him; then good will come to you.
[Job] [22]:[22] Receive instruction from his mouth and store up his words in your heart.
[Job] [22]:[23] If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored; put wrongdoing far from your tent,
[Job] [22]:[24] and lay your gold in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the stones of the streambeds.
[Job] [22]:[25] Then the Almighty himself will be your gold, your treasure of silver.
[Job] [22]:[26] Then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
[Job] [22]:[27] You will pray to him, and he will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
[Job] [22]:[28] What you decide will be done, and light will shine on your ways.
[Job] [22]:[29] When others are brought low, you will say, "Lift them up!" and he will save the downcast.
[Job] [22]:[30] He will deliver even the guilty; by the cleanness of your hands he will be set free.
[Job] [23]:[1] Then Job answered:
[Job] [23]:[2] Even today my complaint is bitter; his hand lies heavy in spite of my groaning.
[Job] [23]:[3] If only I knew where to find him, if only I could come to his dwelling!
[Job] [23]:[4] I would lay my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
[Job] [23]:[5] I would learn what he would answer me and understand what he would say.
[Job] [23]:[6] Would he contend against me with his great power? No, he would surely listen to me.
[Job] [23]:[7] There an upright man could reason with him, and I would be acquitted forever by my judge.
[Job] [23]:[8] But if I go east, he is not there; if west, I cannot perceive him.
[Job] [23]:[9] When he is at work in the north, I cannot see him; when he turns to the south, I catch no glimpse of him.
[Job] [23]:[10] Yet he knows the way I take; when he has tested me, I will come out as gold.
[Job] [23]:[11] My feet have held fast to his steps; I have kept to his way and not turned aside.
[Job] [23]:[12] I have not departed from the command of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my own desire.
[Job] [23]:[13] But he stands alone, and who can turn him back? What he desires, that he does.
[Job] [23]:[14] He will carry out what he has decreed for me, and many such plans are still with him.
[Job] [23]:[15] That is why I am terrified before him; when I consider it, I am afraid of him.
[Job] [23]:[16] God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has filled me with terror.
[Job] [23]:[17] Yet I am not silenced by the darkness, by the thick gloom that covers my face.
[Job] [24]:[1] Why does the Almighty not set times for judgment? Why do those who know him never see his days?
[Job] [24]:[2] Men move boundary stones; they steal flocks and pasture them as their own.
[Job] [24]:[3] They drive off the orphan's donkey and take the widow's ox as a pledge.
[Job] [24]:[4] They shove the needy off the road, and the poor of the land are driven into hiding.
[Job] [24]:[5] Like wild donkeys in the wilderness, the poor go out to their labor, scavenging for food; the wasteland must yield bread for their children.
[Job] [24]:[6] They gather fodder in the fields and glean the vineyards of the wicked.
[Job] [24]:[7] They spend the night naked, without clothing, with nothing to cover them in the cold.
[Job] [24]:[8] Drenched by the mountain rains, they huddle against the rock for want of shelter.
[Job] [24]:[9] They tear the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge from the poor.
[Job] [24]:[10] Naked they go about, without clothing; starving, they carry the sheaves.
[Job] [24]:[11] They press out oil between the terraces; they tread the winepresses, yet go thirsty.
[Job] [24]:[12] From the city the dying groan, and the throats of the wounded cry out for help—yet God charges no one with wrong.
[Job] [24]:[13] These are among those who rebel against the light, who do not know its ways or remain in its paths.
[Job] [24]:[14] At first light the murderer rises to kill the poor and needy, and in the night he prowls like a thief.
[Job] [24]:[15] The eye of the adulterer watches for dusk, thinking, "No eye will see me," and he keeps his face hidden.
[Job] [24]:[16] In the darkness they break into houses; by day they shut themselves in—they want nothing to do with the light.
[Job] [24]:[17] For deep darkness is morning to them all; they are at home with the terrors of the dark.
[Job] [24]:[18] Yet they are swept away like foam on the water; their portion of the land is cursed, and no one turns toward their vineyards.
[Job] [24]:[19] As drought and heat snatch away the melted snow, so the grave snatches away those who have sinned.
[Job] [24]:[20] The womb that bore him forgets him; the worm finds him sweet; he is remembered no more, and wickedness is shattered like a tree.
[Job] [24]:[21] He preys on the barren woman who bears no child and shows no kindness to the widow.
[Job] [24]:[22] Yet he drags away the mighty by his power; when he rises up, no one is sure of his life.
[Job] [24]:[23] He may let them rest in false security, but his eyes are on their ways.
[Job] [24]:[24] For a little while they are exalted, and then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all the rest, cut off like heads of grain.
[Job] [24]:[25] If this is not so, who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?
[Job] [25]:[1] Then Bildad the Shuhite answered:
[Job] [25]:[2] "Dominion and dread belong to him; he makes peace in his heights.
[Job] [25]:[3] Can his armies be numbered? And on whom does his light not rise?
[Job] [25]:[4] How then can a mortal be righteous before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
[Job] [25]:[5] If even the moon is not bright and the stars are not clean in his eyes,
[Job] [25]:[6] how much less a mortal, who is a maggot, a human being, who is a worm!"
[Job] [26]:[1] Then Job answered:
[Job] [26]:[2] "What help you have given to the powerless! What mighty deliverance for the arm without strength!
[Job] [26]:[3] What counsel you have offered to one without wisdom! And what abundance of insight you have displayed!
[Job] [26]:[4] With whose help have you spoken these words? And whose breath was it that came out of you?
[Job] [26]:[5] The shades below writhe in terror—the waters and all who dwell in them.
[Job] [26]:[6] Sheol lies naked before him, and Destruction has no covering.
[Job] [26]:[7] He stretches out the north over the void and hangs the earth upon nothing.
[Job] [26]:[8] He binds up the waters in his clouds, yet the clouds do not burst beneath their weight.
[Job] [26]:[9] He covers the face of the full moon, spreading his cloud across it.
[Job] [26]:[10] He has drawn a circle on the face of the waters, at the boundary between light and darkness.
[Job] [26]:[11] The pillars of heaven shudder, astonished at his rebuke.
[Job] [26]:[12] By his power he stilled the sea; by his understanding he shattered Rahab.
[Job] [26]:[13] By his breath the heavens were made fair; his hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
[Job] [26]:[14] And these are but the fringes of his ways—only a whisper of a word do we hear of him. Who then could comprehend the thunder of his mighty deeds?
[Job] [27]:[1] And Job took up his discourse again and said:
[Job] [27]:[2] As God lives, who has denied me justice, as the Almighty lives, who has made my soul bitter—
[Job] [27]:[3] as long as there is breath in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils,
[Job] [27]:[4] my lips will speak no wrong, and my tongue will utter no deceit.
[Job] [27]:[5] Far be it from me to say that you are right; till my last breath I will not let go of my integrity.
[Job] [27]:[6] I hold fast to my righteousness and will not release it; my heart does not reproach me for any of my days.
[Job] [27]:[7] Let my enemy be counted as the wicked, and the one who rises against me as the unjust.
[Job] [27]:[8] For what hope has the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
[Job] [27]:[9] Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?
[Job] [27]:[10] Will he take delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?
[Job] [27]:[11] I will teach you about the hand of God; what is with the Almighty I will not conceal.
[Job] [27]:[12] Look, all of you have seen it for yourselves; why then do you go on with such empty talk?
[Job] [27]:[13] This is the portion a wicked man receives from God, the inheritance that tyrants get from the Almighty:
[Job] [27]:[14] If his children increase, it is for the sword, and his offspring will never have bread enough.
[Job] [27]:[15] Those he leaves behind are buried by the plague, and his widows do not weep for him.
[Job] [27]:[16] Though he piles up silver like dust and heaps up clothing like clay,
[Job] [27]:[17] what he heaps up the righteous will wear, and the innocent will divide his silver.
[Job] [27]:[18] He builds his house like a moth's cocoon, like a shelter a watchman throws together.
[Job] [27]:[19] He lies down rich, but he will not be gathered; he opens his eyes, and it is gone.
[Job] [27]:[20] Terrors overtake him like rushing waters; in the night a whirlwind steals him away.
[Job] [27]:[21] The east wind lifts him up, and he is gone; it hurls him from his place.
[Job] [27]:[22] It flings itself against him without mercy; he flees headlong from its grip.
[Job] [27]:[23] It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.
[Job] [28]:[1] Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place where gold is refined.
[Job] [28]:[2] Iron is taken from the dust, and copper is smelted from stone.
[Job] [28]:[3] Man puts an end to the darkness; he searches to the farthest limit for ore in gloom and deep shadow.
[Job] [28]:[4] He sinks a shaft far from where anyone lives, in places forgotten by the foot of man; there the miners dangle and sway, far from human company.
[Job] [28]:[5] As for the earth, out of it comes food, yet underneath it is turned up as by fire.
[Job] [28]:[6] Its stones are the place of sapphires, and its dust holds gold.
[Job] [28]:[7] No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon's eye has seen it.
[Job] [28]:[8] The proud beasts have not trodden it; no lion has passed that way.
[Job] [28]:[9] Man lays his hand on the flinty rock and overturns mountains at their roots.
[Job] [28]:[10] He cuts channels through the rock, and his eye sees every precious thing.
[Job] [28]:[11] He dams up the sources of the streams and brings hidden things to light.
[Job] [28]:[12] But where can wisdom be found? And where is the place of understanding?
[Job] [28]:[13] No one knows its worth, and it is not found in the land of the living.
[Job] [28]:[14] The deep says, "It is not in me"; the sea says, "It is not with me."
[Job] [28]:[15] It cannot be bought with gold, nor can its price be weighed out in silver.
[Job] [28]:[16] It cannot be valued against the gold of Ophir, against precious onyx or sapphire.
[Job] [28]:[17] Neither gold nor crystal can equal it, nor can it be exchanged for vessels of fine gold.
[Job] [28]:[18] Coral and quartz are not worth mentioning; the price of wisdom is beyond pearls.
[Job] [28]:[19] The topaz of Cush cannot equal it, nor can it be valued against pure gold.
[Job] [28]:[20] From where, then, does wisdom come? And where is the place of understanding?
[Job] [28]:[21] It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing, concealed even from the birds of the sky.
[Job] [28]:[22] Abaddon and Death say, "We have only heard a report of it with our ears."
[Job] [28]:[23] God understands the way to it, and he knows its place.
[Job] [28]:[24] For he looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.
[Job] [28]:[25] When he gave the wind its weight and measured out the waters,
[Job] [28]:[26] when he set a decree for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
[Job] [28]:[27] then he saw wisdom and declared it; he established it and searched it out.
[Job] [28]:[28] And he said to man, "Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding."
[Job] [29]:[1] Job took up his discourse again and said:
[Job] [29]:[2] Oh, that I were as in the months gone by, in the days when God watched over me,
[Job] [29]:[3] when his lamp shone above my head, and by his light I walked through darkness;
[Job] [29]:[4] as I was in the days of my prime, when God's friendship rested on my tent,
[Job] [29]:[5] when the Almighty was still with me and my children were all around me,
[Job] [29]:[6] when my steps were bathed in cream and the rock poured out streams of oil for me.
[Job] [29]:[7] When I went out to the gate of the city and took my seat in the public square,
[Job] [29]:[8] the young men saw me and stepped aside, and the aged rose and stood.
[Job] [29]:[9] The princes held back their words and laid a hand over their mouths.
[Job] [29]:[10] The voices of the nobles fell silent, and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.
[Job] [29]:[11] Whoever heard me called me blessed, and whoever saw me bore witness in my favor,
[Job] [29]:[12] because I rescued the poor who cried for help, and the orphan who had no one to assist him.
[Job] [29]:[13] The blessing of the dying came upon me, and I made the widow's heart sing for joy.
[Job] [29]:[14] I clothed myself in righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my turban.
[Job] [29]:[15] I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
[Job] [29]:[16] I was a father to the needy, and I searched out the case of the one I did not know.
[Job] [29]:[17] I broke the fangs of the wicked and tore the prey from his teeth.
[Job] [29]:[18] I thought: I will die in my own nest, and my days will be as many as the sand.
[Job] [29]:[19] My roots reach down to the water, and the dew lies all night on my branches.
[Job] [29]:[20] My glory stays fresh within me, and my bow is ever new in my hand.
[Job] [29]:[21] Men listened to me and waited; they kept silent for my counsel.
[Job] [29]:[22] After I had spoken, they said no more; my words fell gently on them.
[Job] [29]:[23] They waited for me as for the rain, and opened their mouths wide for the showers of spring.
[Job] [29]:[24] When I smiled at them, they could scarcely believe it; the light of my face they never let fall.
[Job] [29]:[25] I chose the way for them and sat as their chief; I dwelt like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners.
[Job] [30]:[1] But now they laugh at me, men younger than I, whose fathers I would have refused to put with the dogs of my flock.
[Job] [30]:[2] What use to me was the strength of their hands? All their vigor had perished.
[Job] [30]:[3] Gaunt from want and hunger, they gnawed the parched ground, in the gloom of waste and desolation.
[Job] [30]:[4] They picked saltwort among the bushes, and the roots of the broom tree were their bread.
[Job] [30]:[5] They were driven out from among people, shouted at as if they were thieves,
[Job] [30]:[6] forced to live in dry riverbeds, in holes in the ground and among the rocks.
[Job] [30]:[7] Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they huddled together.
[Job] [30]:[8] A senseless brood, sons of nobodies, they were whipped out of the land.
[Job] [30]:[9] And now I am their taunting song; I have become a byword among them.
[Job] [30]:[10] They loathe me and keep their distance; they do not hold back from spitting in my face.
[Job] [30]:[11] Because God has loosed my bowstring and afflicted me, they cast off the bridle before me.
[Job] [30]:[12] On my right the rabble rises up; they trip my feet and throw up their siege ramps against me.
[Job] [30]:[13] They tear up my path; they further my ruin, and no one need help them.
[Job] [30]:[14] They come on as through a wide breach; amid the crash they roll in upon me.
[Job] [30]:[15] Terrors are turned loose against me; my dignity is driven off like the wind, and my deliverance passes by like a cloud.
[Job] [30]:[16] And now my life is poured out within me; days of affliction have taken hold of me.
[Job] [30]:[17] Night pierces my bones; the pains that gnaw me never rest.
[Job] [30]:[18] With great force my garment is disfigured; it binds me tight like the collar of my tunic.
[Job] [30]:[19] He has thrown me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
[Job] [30]:[20] I cry out to you, and you do not answer; I stand before you, and you only look at me.
[Job] [30]:[21] You have turned cruel toward me; with the strength of your hand you assail me.
[Job] [30]:[22] You lift me up to the wind and make me ride it; you melt me away in the roar of the storm.
[Job] [30]:[23] For I know you will bring me down to death, to the house appointed for all the living.
[Job] [30]:[24] Yet surely no one lays a hand on a man in ruins, when in his disaster he cries for help.
[Job] [30]:[25] Did I not weep for the one whose days were hard? Was not my soul grieved for the poor?
[Job] [30]:[26] But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I waited for light, darkness fell.
[Job] [30]:[27] My insides churn and will not be still; days of affliction confront me.
[Job] [30]:[28] I go about blackened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
[Job] [30]:[29] I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of ostriches.
[Job] [30]:[30] My skin turns black and peels away, and my bones burn with fever.
[Job] [30]:[31] My lyre is tuned to mourning, and my flute to the sound of weeping.
[Job] [31]:[1] I made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I gaze at a young woman?
[Job] [31]:[2] For what portion would I have from God above, what inheritance from the Almighty on high?
[Job] [31]:[3] Is it not ruin for the wicked, disaster for those who do evil?
[Job] [31]:[4] Does he not see my ways and count my every step?
[Job] [31]:[5] If I have walked with falsehood, or my foot has hurried after deceit—
[Job] [31]:[6] let God weigh me on honest scales; then he will know my integrity.
[Job] [31]:[7] If my steps have turned aside from the way, if my heart has followed my eyes, or my hands have been stained with wrong,
[Job] [31]:[8] then let another eat what I sow, and let my crops be uprooted.
[Job] [31]:[9] If my heart has been enticed by a woman, or I have lurked at my neighbor's door,
[Job] [31]:[10] then let my wife grind grain for another, and let other men lie with her.
[Job] [31]:[11] For that would be a shameful act, a sin to be judged by the courts.
[Job] [31]:[12] It is a fire that burns all the way to destruction, tearing up all my harvest by the roots.
[Job] [31]:[13] If I have denied justice to my servant, whether man or woman, when they had a grievance against me,
[Job] [31]:[14] what would I do when God confronts me? What would I answer when he calls me to account?
[Job] [31]:[15] Did not he who made me in the womb make them? Did not the same One form us both there?
[Job] [31]:[16] If I have withheld from the poor what they needed, or let the eyes of the widow grow weary,
[Job] [31]:[17] if I have eaten my bread alone and shared none of it with the fatherless—
[Job] [31]:[18] but from my youth I reared him as a father would, and from my birth I guided the widow—
[Job] [31]:[19] if I have seen anyone perishing for lack of clothing, or the needy without a garment,
[Job] [31]:[20] and his body did not bless me for warming him with the fleece of my sheep,
[Job] [31]:[21] if I have raised my hand against the fatherless, knowing I had influence in the gate,
[Job] [31]:[22] then let my arm fall from the shoulder, let it be broken off at the joint.
[Job] [31]:[23] For I lived in dread of calamity from God, and before his majesty I could not have stood.
[Job] [31]:[24] If I have put my trust in gold, or said to pure gold, 'You are my security,'
[Job] [31]:[25] if I have gloried in my great wealth, in the fortune my hands had gained,
[Job] [31]:[26] if I have looked at the sun in its brilliance, or the moon moving in splendor,
[Job] [31]:[27] so that my heart was secretly enticed and my hand blew them a kiss,
[Job] [31]:[28] that too would be a sin to be judged, for I would have been unfaithful to God above.
[Job] [31]:[29] If I have rejoiced at my enemy's ruin, or gloated over the trouble that found him—
[Job] [31]:[30] no, I never let my mouth sin by calling down a curse on his life.
[Job] [31]:[31] Have the men of my household not said, 'Who has not been filled with Job's meat?'
[Job] [31]:[32] No stranger ever spent the night in the street, for my door was always open to the traveler.
[Job] [31]:[33] If I have concealed my sin as others do, hiding my guilt in my heart [footnote: Or 'as Adam did'; the Hebrew term can mean either 'humankind' or the name Adam.]
[Job] [31]:[34] because I feared the crowd and dreaded the contempt of the clans, so that I kept silent and would not go outside—
[Job] [31]:[35] Oh, that someone would hear me! Here is my signature—let the Almighty answer me. Let my accuser write out his indictment.
[Job] [31]:[36] Surely I would wear it on my shoulder; I would bind it on me like a crown.
[Job] [31]:[37] I would give him an account of my every step; like a prince I would approach him.
[Job] [31]:[38] If my land has cried out against me and its furrows have wept together,
[Job] [31]:[39] if I have consumed its yield without payment and broken the spirit of its tenants,
[Job] [31]:[40] then let thorns come up instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
[Job] [32]:[1] So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
[Job] [32]:[2] Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, burned with anger. His anger burned against Job for justifying himself rather than God,
[Job] [32]:[3] and it burned against his three friends, because they had found no answer, yet had condemned Job.
[Job] [32]:[4] Now Elihu had waited before speaking to Job, because the others were older than he was.
[Job] [32]:[5] But when Elihu saw that the three men had no answer left in their mouths, his anger burned.
[Job] [32]:[6] So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite spoke up and said: I am young in years, and you are old; that is why I held back, afraid to tell you what I know.
[Job] [32]:[7] I thought, Let age speak; let many years teach wisdom.
[Job] [32]:[8] But it is the spirit in a person, the breath of the Almighty, that gives understanding.
[Job] [32]:[9] It is not the many who are wise, nor the aged who understand what is right.
[Job] [32]:[10] So I say: Listen to me; I too will tell you what I know.
[Job] [32]:[11] I waited while you spoke, I listened to your reasoning as you searched for words.
[Job] [32]:[12] I gave you my full attention, and look—not one of you refuted Job or answered his arguments.
[Job] [32]:[13] So do not say, We have found wisdom; let God refute him, not man.
[Job] [32]:[14] He has not marshaled his words against me, so I will not answer him with speeches like yours.
[Job] [32]:[15] They are dismayed and have no more to say; words have failed them.
[Job] [32]:[16] Am I to wait, now that they are silent, now that they stand there with no answer?
[Job] [32]:[17] I too will have my say; I too will tell what I know.
[Job] [32]:[18] For I am full of words; the spirit within me compels me.
[Job] [32]:[19] Inside I am like wine that has no vent, like new wineskins ready to burst.
[Job] [32]:[20] I must speak and find relief; I must open my lips and answer.
[Job] [32]:[21] I will show no partiality to anyone, nor will I flatter any man.
[Job] [32]:[22] For I do not know how to flatter—my Maker would soon carry me off.
[Job] [33]:[1] But now, Job, hear my speech, and listen to all my words.
[Job] [33]:[2] Look, I have opened my mouth; my tongue forms words on my palate.
[Job] [33]:[3] My words come from an upright heart; my lips speak sincerely what I know.
[Job] [33]:[4] The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
[Job] [33]:[5] Answer me, if you can; marshal your case before me and take your stand.
[Job] [33]:[6] Before God I am just what you are; I too was pinched off from clay.
[Job] [33]:[7] No dread of me should terrify you; no pressure from me should weigh you down.
[Job] [33]:[8] Surely you have said in my hearing—I heard the very sound of your words—
[Job] [33]:[9] "I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there is no guilt in me.
[Job] [33]:[10] Yet he finds occasions against me; he counts me as his enemy.
[Job] [33]:[11] He puts my feet in the stocks; he watches all my paths."
[Job] [33]:[12] But in this you are not right, and I will answer you: God is greater than any mortal.
[Job] [33]:[13] Why do you contend against him, complaining that he gives no account of any of his doings?
[Job] [33]:[14] For God speaks in one way, and in two, though no one perceives it.
[Job] [33]:[15] In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people as they slumber on their beds,
[Job] [33]:[16] then he opens their ears and seals his instruction upon them,
[Job] [33]:[17] to turn a person from his deeds and to cut off pride from a man,
[Job] [33]:[18] to hold his soul back from the pit, his life from perishing by the sword.
[Job] [33]:[19] A person is also chastened with pain on his bed, with unrelenting aching in his bones,
[Job] [33]:[20] so that his life loathes bread and his appetite refuses the choicest food.
[Job] [33]:[21] His flesh wastes away out of sight, and his bones, once hidden, stick out.
[Job] [33]:[22] His soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the messengers of death.
[Job] [33]:[23] If there is an angel at his side, a mediator, one out of a thousand, to declare to a man what is right for him,
[Job] [33]:[24] and he is gracious to him and says, "Spare him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom"—
[Job] [33]:[25] then his flesh grows fresher than a child's; he returns to the days of his youth.
[Job] [33]:[26] He prays to God, and God accepts him; he sees God's face with shouts of joy, for God restores his righteousness to him.
[Job] [33]:[27] He sings before others and says, "I sinned and perverted what was right, yet it was not repaid to me.
[Job] [33]:[28] He redeemed my soul from going down to the pit, and my life shall see the light."
[Job] [33]:[29] Truly, God does all these things, twice, even three times, with a man,
[Job] [33]:[30] to bring back his soul from the pit, that the light of life may shine on him.
[Job] [33]:[31] Pay attention, Job; listen to me. Be silent, and I will speak.
[Job] [33]:[32] If you have anything to say, answer me; speak, for I would gladly declare you right.
[Job] [33]:[33] If not, then listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.
[Job] [34]:[1] Then Elihu spoke again:
[Job] [34]:[2] Hear my words, you who are wise; listen to me, you who have knowledge.
[Job] [34]:[3] For the ear weighs words as the palate tastes food.
[Job] [34]:[4] Let us choose for ourselves what is right; let us learn together what is good.
[Job] [34]:[5] For Job has said, "I am innocent, yet God has denied me justice."
[Job] [34]:[6] "Though I am in the right, I am called a liar; though I am without transgression, my wound will not heal."
[Job] [34]:[7] What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water,
[Job] [34]:[8] who keeps company with evildoers and walks with the wicked?
[Job] [34]:[9] For he says, "A man gains nothing by taking delight in God."
[Job] [34]:[10] So listen to me, you men of understanding: Far be it from God to do wrong, from the Almighty to act unjustly.
[Job] [34]:[11] He repays a man for what he does and brings upon him what his ways deserve.
[Job] [34]:[12] Truly, God will never act wickedly; the Almighty will never pervert justice.
[Job] [34]:[13] Who put him in charge of the earth? Who entrusted to him the whole world?
[Job] [34]:[14] If he were to set his heart on it and withdraw his spirit and breath,
[Job] [34]:[15] all flesh would perish together, and man would return to the dust.
[Job] [34]:[16] If you have understanding, hear this; listen to what I have to say.
[Job] [34]:[17] Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the Righteous One, the Mighty One,
[Job] [34]:[18] who says to a king, "You are worthless," and to nobles, "You are wicked";
[Job] [34]:[19] who shows no partiality to princes and no preference for the rich over the poor, for they are all the work of his hands?
[Job] [34]:[20] In a moment they die; in the middle of the night a people is shaken and passes away; the mighty are removed by no human hand.
[Job] [34]:[21] For his eyes are on the ways of a man; he sees his every step.
[Job] [34]:[22] There is no darkness, no deep shadow, where evildoers can hide.
[Job] [34]:[23] God has no need to examine a man further, or bring him before him for judgment.
[Job] [34]:[24] He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets up others in their place.
[Job] [34]:[25] Because he takes note of their deeds, he overturns them in the night, and they are crushed.
[Job] [34]:[26] He strikes them down for their wickedness where everyone can see,
[Job] [34]:[27] because they turned away from following him and had no regard for any of his ways.
[Job] [34]:[28] They caused the cry of the poor to come before him, and he heard the cry of the afflicted.
[Job] [34]:[29] But if he keeps silent, who can condemn? If he hides his face, who can behold him? Yet he is over nation and man alike,
[Job] [34]:[30] to keep the godless from ruling and from laying snares for the people.
[Job] [34]:[31] Suppose a man says to God, "I have borne my punishment; I will offend no more.
[Job] [34]:[32] Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will not do it again."
[Job] [34]:[33] Should God then repay you on your own terms, since you refuse to repent? For you must choose, not I; so tell me what you know.
[Job] [34]:[34] Men of understanding will say to me, and any wise man who hears me will agree:
[Job] [34]:[35] "Job speaks without knowledge; his words show no insight."
[Job] [34]:[36] If only Job were tested to the limit for answering like a wicked man!
[Job] [34]:[37] For to his sin he adds rebellion; he claps his hands in scorn among us and multiplies his words against God.
[Job] [35]:[1] Then Elihu continued and said:
[Job] [35]:[2] Do you think this is justice, when you say, "I am in the right, not God"?
[Job] [35]:[3] For you ask, "What good does it do me? What do I gain by not sinning?"* [*Or "What advantage is it to you?"—the Hebrew has "to you," which may address God.]
[Job] [35]:[4] I will answer you—you and your friends with you.
[Job] [35]:[5] Look up at the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds so high above you.
[Job] [35]:[6] If you sin, how does that harm him? If your offenses pile up, what does it do to him?
[Job] [35]:[7] If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?
[Job] [35]:[8] Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself, and your righteousness only a human being.
[Job] [35]:[9] People cry out under the weight of oppression; they plead for relief from the arm of the mighty.
[Job] [35]:[10] But no one asks, "Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
[Job] [35]:[11] who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?"
[Job] [35]:[12] There they cry out, but he gives no answer, because of the arrogance of the wicked.
[Job] [35]:[13] Surely God does not listen to empty talk; the Almighty pays it no regard.
[Job] [35]:[14] How much less, then, when you say he takes no notice! Yet your case lies before him—so wait for him.
[Job] [35]:[15] And now, because his anger has not brought punishment, and he takes little note of wrongdoing,
[Job] [35]:[16] Job opens his mouth with empty words and multiplies talk without knowledge.
[Job] [36]:[1] Elihu continued and said:
[Job] [36]:[2] Bear with me a little, and I will show you, for I still have something to say on God's behalf.
[Job] [36]:[3] I will bring my knowledge from far away and ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
[Job] [36]:[4] For truly, my words are no lie; one perfect in knowledge stands before you.
[Job] [36]:[5] Look, God is mighty, yet he despises no one; he is mighty in strength of understanding.
[Job] [36]:[6] He does not let the wicked live, but grants justice to the afflicted.
[Job] [36]:[7] He does not turn his eyes from the righteous; he seats them with kings on the throne forever, and they are lifted high.
[Job] [36]:[8] But if they are bound in chains, held fast in cords of affliction,
[Job] [36]:[9] then he declares to them what they have done—their transgressions, how they have grown proud.
[Job] [36]:[10] He opens their ears to discipline and commands them to turn from wrongdoing.
[Job] [36]:[11] If they listen and serve him, they will finish their days in prosperity and their years in pleasant things.
[Job] [36]:[12] But if they do not listen, they will perish by the sword and die without knowledge.
[Job] [36]:[13] The godless in heart nurse their anger; they do not cry for help when he binds them.
[Job] [36]:[14] They die in their youth, and their life ends among the temple prostitutes.
[Job] [36]:[15] But he rescues the afflicted through their affliction and opens their ears through oppression.
[Job] [36]:[16] He would also draw you out of distress into a broad place with no constraint, and your table would be spread with rich food.
[Job] [36]:[17] But you are full of the judgment due the wicked; judgment and justice have taken hold of you.
[Job] [36]:[18] Beware that wrath does not lure you into scoffing, and let no great ransom turn you aside.
[Job] [36]:[19] Will your cry for help avail you in distress, or all your mustered strength?
[Job] [36]:[20] Do not long for the night, when peoples are swept away in their place.
[Job] [36]:[21] Take care, do not turn to wrongdoing, for you have chosen this rather than affliction.
[Job] [36]:[22] Look, God is exalted in his power; who is a teacher like him?
[Job] [36]:[23] Who has prescribed his way for him, or who has said, "You have done wrong"?
[Job] [36]:[24] Remember to magnify his work, which people have praised in song.
[Job] [36]:[25] All humanity has looked upon it; mortals gaze on it from afar.
[Job] [36]:[26] Look, God is great beyond our knowing; the number of his years is past all searching.
[Job] [36]:[27] He draws up the drops of water; they filter down as rain from his mist,
[Job] [36]:[28] which the clouds pour down, showering abundantly on all mankind.
[Job] [36]:[29] Who can understand the spreading of the clouds, the thunder of his pavilion?
[Job] [36]:[30] See how he spreads his lightning around him and covers the roots of the sea.
[Job] [36]:[31] By these he judges the peoples and gives food in abundance.
[Job] [36]:[32] He covers his hands with the lightning and commands it to strike the mark.
[Job] [36]:[33] His thunder announces his coming; even the cattle sense the rising storm.
[Job] [37]:[1] At this my heart pounds too, and leaps from its place.
[Job] [37]:[2] Listen closely to the rumble of his voice, to the thunder that goes out from his mouth.
[Job] [37]:[3] He unleashes it under the whole sky, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.
[Job] [37]:[4] After it his voice roars; he thunders with the voice of his majesty, and he holds nothing back once his voice is heard.
[Job] [37]:[5] God thunders wondrously with his voice; he does great things beyond our understanding.
[Job] [37]:[6] He says to the snow, "Fall to the earth," and to the rain shower and the mighty downpour, "Pour down."
[Job] [37]:[7] He seals up the hand of everyone, so that all people may know his work.
[Job] [37]:[8] Then the wild animals slip into their lairs and stay in their dens.
[Job] [37]:[9] Out of its chamber comes the whirlwind, and cold from the scattering winds.
[Job] [37]:[10] By the breath of God the ice is formed, and the broad waters freeze solid.
[Job] [37]:[11] He loads the thundercloud with moisture; he scatters the clouds heavy with his lightning.
[Job] [37]:[12] They wheel about, turning wherever he guides them, to carry out all that he commands them across the face of the inhabited world.
[Job] [37]:[13] Whether for punishment, or for the good of his land, or in mercy, he sends them where he wills.
[Job] [37]:[14] Listen to this, Job; stand still and consider the wonders of God.
[Job] [37]:[15] Do you know how God gives them their orders, how he makes the lightning of his cloud flash out?
[Job] [37]:[16] Do you know how the clouds are poised, the wonders of him who is perfect in knowledge?
[Job] [37]:[17] You, whose clothes are stifling when the earth lies still beneath the south wind—
[Job] [37]:[18] can you spread out the skies with him, hard as a mirror of cast metal?
[Job] [37]:[19] Teach us, then, what we should say to him; we cannot set our case in order, for we are in the dark.
[Job] [37]:[20] Should he be told that I want to speak? Would anyone ask to be swallowed up?
[Job] [37]:[21] Now no one can look at the light, blazing in the skies, once the wind has swept past and swept them clean.
[Job] [37]:[22] Out of the north comes a golden splendor; around God is awesome majesty.
[Job] [37]:[23] The Almighty—we cannot fathom him. He is great in power, yet in justice and abundant righteousness he does no violence.
[Job] [37]:[24] Therefore people fear him; he has no regard for any who are wise in heart.
[Job] [38]:[1] Then the LORD answered Job out of the storm:
[Job] [38]:[2] Who is this that darkens counsel with words empty of knowledge?
[Job] [38]:[3] Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall inform me.
[Job] [38]:[4] Where were you when I laid the earth's foundation? Tell me, if you have understanding.
[Job] [38]:[5] Who set its measurements? Surely you know. Who stretched the measuring line across it?
[Job] [38]:[6] On what were its footings sunk, or who laid its cornerstone,
[Job] [38]:[7] while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
[Job] [38]:[8] Who shut the sea behind doors when it burst forth from the womb,
[Job] [38]:[9] when I made the clouds its garment and thick darkness its swaddling band,
[Job] [38]:[10] when I fixed my limit for it and set its bars and doors in place,
[Job] [38]:[11] when I said, 'This far you may come and no farther; here your proud waves must halt'?
[Job] [38]:[12] Have you ever commanded the morning or shown the dawn its place,
[Job] [38]:[13] that it might seize the edges of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
[Job] [38]:[14] The earth takes shape like clay under a seal; its features stand out like a garment.
[Job] [38]:[15] The wicked are denied their light, and the upraised arm is broken.
[Job] [38]:[16] Have you journeyed to the springs of the sea or walked in the recesses of the deep?
[Job] [38]:[17] Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of deepest darkness?
[Job] [38]:[18] Have you grasped the vast expanse of the earth? Tell me, if you know it all.
[Job] [38]:[19] Which is the way to the home of light, and where does darkness reside,
[Job] [38]:[20] that you might take them to their own territory and know the paths to their dwellings?
[Job] [38]:[21] Surely you know, for you were already born! The number of your days is so great!
[Job] [38]:[22] Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or seen the storehouses of the hail,
[Job] [38]:[23] which I have reserved for times of trouble, for days of battle and war?
[Job] [38]:[24] What is the way to the place where light is parceled out, or where the east wind is scattered over the earth?
[Job] [38]:[25] Who cuts a channel for the torrents of rain, and a path for the thunderbolt,
[Job] [38]:[26] to water a land where no one lives, a desert with no human in it,
[Job] [38]:[27] to satisfy the waste and desolate ground and make the grass sprout there?
[Job] [38]:[28] Does the rain have a father? Who fathered the drops of dew?
[Job] [38]:[29] From whose womb comes the ice? Who gives birth to the frost of heaven,
[Job] [38]:[30] when the waters harden like stone and the surface of the deep is frozen fast?
[Job] [38]:[31] Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loosen the cords of Orion?
[Job] [38]:[32] Can you bring out the constellations in their season or lead out the Bear with her cubs?
[Job] [38]:[33] Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you set up their rule over the earth?
[Job] [38]:[34] Can you raise your voice to the clouds and cover yourself with a flood of water?
[Job] [38]:[35] Do you send the lightning bolts on their way? Do they report to you, 'Here we are'?
[Job] [38]:[36] Who put wisdom in the hidden parts, or gave understanding to the mind?[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew words rendered *hidden parts* and *mind* are uncertain; they may instead refer to birds, as in "the ibis" and "the rooster."
[Job] [38]:[37] Who has the wisdom to number the clouds? Who can tip over the water jars of the heavens,
[Job] [38]:[38] when the dust hardens into a mass and the clods stick together?
[Job] [38]:[39] Do you hunt the prey for the lioness and satisfy the hunger of the young lions,
[Job] [38]:[40] when they crouch in their dens or lie in wait in the thicket?
[Job] [38]:[41] Who provides food for the raven when its young cry out to God and wander about for lack of food?
[Job] [39]:[1] Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch over the doe in her labor?
[Job] [39]:[2] Can you count the months they carry their young? Do you know the time of their delivery,
[Job] [39]:[3] when they crouch down and bring forth their offspring, and their labor pains are past?
[Job] [39]:[4] Their young grow strong and thrive in the open; they leave and do not return.
[Job] [39]:[5] Who set the wild donkey free? Who untied his ropes?
[Job] [39]:[6] I gave him the wasteland as his home, the salt flats as his dwelling place.
[Job] [39]:[7] He laughs at the noise of the town; he never hears the driver's shouts.
[Job] [39]:[8] He roams the hills for pasture, searching out every green thing.
[Job] [39]:[9] Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Will he spend the night beside your stall?
[Job] [39]:[10] Can you tie him with ropes to the furrow? Will he break up the valleys behind you?
[Job] [39]:[11] Can you trust him because his strength is great? Will you leave your labor to him?
[Job] [39]:[12] Can you count on him to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
[Job] [39]:[13] The ostrich flaps her wings in joy, but they are no match for the pinions and plumage of the stork.
[Job] [39]:[14] She leaves her eggs on the ground and lets the dust keep them warm,
[Job] [39]:[15] forgetting that a foot may crush them, that a wild animal may trample them.
[Job] [39]:[16] She is hard on her young, as if they were not hers; her labor is wasted, and she has no fear,
[Job] [39]:[17] for God made her forget wisdom and gave her no share of understanding.
[Job] [39]:[18] Yet when she rises up to run, she laughs at the horse and its rider.
[Job] [39]:[19] Do you give the horse his strength? Do you clothe his neck with a flowing mane?
[Job] [39]:[20] Do you make him leap like a locust, striking terror with his proud snorting?
[Job] [39]:[21] He paws the valley floor, exulting in his power, and charges out to meet the weapons.
[Job] [39]:[22] He laughs at fear and is not dismayed; he does not turn back from the sword.
[Job] [39]:[23] The quiver rattles against his side, along with the flashing spear and lance.
[Job] [39]:[24] Trembling with fury, he devours the ground; he cannot stand still when the trumpet sounds.
[Job] [39]:[25] At the blast of the horn he cries, "Aha!" He catches the scent of battle far off, the thunder of commanders and the war cry.
[Job] [39]:[26] Does the hawk take flight by your understanding, spreading his wings toward the south?
[Job] [39]:[27] Is it at your command that the eagle soars and builds his nest on high?
[Job] [39]:[28] He dwells on the cliff and lodges there; the rocky crag is his fortress.
[Job] [39]:[29] From there he spies out his prey; his eyes see it far away.
[Job] [39]:[30] His young ones feast on blood, and wherever the slain are, there he is.
[Job] [40]:[1] Then the LORD answered Job:
[Job] [40]:[2] Will the one who argues with the Almighty accept correction? Let him who accuses God give an answer.
[Job] [40]:[3] Then Job answered the LORD:
[Job] [40]:[4] See, I am of little worth—what can I reply to you? I lay my hand over my mouth.
[Job] [40]:[5] I have spoken once, and I will not answer again; twice, and I will say no more.
[Job] [40]:[6] Then the LORD answered Job out of the storm:
[Job] [40]:[7] Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you will inform me.
[Job] [40]:[8] Would you really annul my justice? Would you condemn me to justify yourself?
[Job] [40]:[9] Do you have an arm like God's? Can you thunder with a voice like his?
[Job] [40]:[10] Then deck yourself with majesty and grandeur; clothe yourself in glory and splendor.
[Job] [40]:[11] Pour out the fury of your anger; look on every proud man and bring him low.
[Job] [40]:[12] Look on every proud man and humble him; crush the wicked where they stand.
[Job] [40]:[13] Bury them in the dust together; shroud their faces in the hidden place.
[Job] [40]:[14] Then even I would praise you, that your own right hand can save you.
[Job] [40]:[15] Look now at Behemoth, which I made along with you; he eats grass like an ox.
[Job] [40]:[16] Look at the strength in his loins, the power in the muscles of his belly.
[Job] [40]:[17] He stiffens his tail like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are woven tight.
[Job] [40]:[18] His bones are tubes of bronze, his limbs like bars of iron.
[Job] [40]:[19] He is the first of God's works; only his Maker can bring a sword against him.
[Job] [40]:[20] For the mountains yield him their produce, and all the wild animals play there.
[Job] [40]:[21] He lies down under the lotus trees, hidden among the reeds of the marsh.
