[Job] [40]:[22] The lotus trees cover him with their shade; the willows of the stream surround him.
[Job] [40]:[23] Though the river rages, he is not alarmed; he is unshaken though the Jordan surges against his mouth.
[Job] [40]:[24] Can anyone capture him while he watches, or pierce his nose with a snare?
[Job] [40]:[25] Can you haul in Leviathan with a hook, or tie down his tongue with a rope?
[Job] [40]:[26] Can you run a cord through his nose, or pierce his jaw with a barb?
[Job] [40]:[27] Will he plead with you again and again? Will he speak soft words to you?
[Job] [40]:[28] Will he make a covenant with you, so you can take him as a slave for life?
[Job] [40]:[29] Will you play with him as with a bird, or leash him for your servant girls?
[Job] [40]:[30] Will traders haggle over him? Will they divide him among the merchants?
[Job] [40]:[31] Can you fill his hide with harpoons, or his head with fishing spears?
[Job] [40]:[32] Lay a hand on him—remember the battle; you will never try again!
[Job] [41]:[1] Look, any hope of taking him is false; the mere sight of him lays a man low.
[Job] [41]:[2] No one is fierce enough to rouse him. Who then can stand before me?
[Job] [41]:[3] Who has ever given me anything first, that I should repay him? Whatever is under all the heavens is mine.
[Job] [41]:[4] I will not keep silent about his limbs, his mighty strength, his graceful frame.
[Job] [41]:[5] Who can strip off his outer coat? Who can approach him within his double armor?* *Or 'within his double bridle'; the Hebrew word means 'bridle,' often understood here as the creature's jaws or double row of scales.
[Job] [41]:[6] Who can pry open the doors of his face? His teeth are ringed with terror.
[Job] [41]:[7] His pride is his rows of shields, shut up tight as with a seal.
[Job] [41]:[8] Each one presses against the next; not even air can pass between them.
[Job] [41]:[9] They cling to one another, locked so fast they cannot be pulled apart.
[Job] [41]:[10] His snorting flashes out light; his eyes are like the first rays of dawn.
[Job] [41]:[11] Out of his mouth go blazing torches; sparks of fire shoot from him.
[Job] [41]:[12] Smoke streams from his nostrils, as from a pot boiling over a fire of reeds.
[Job] [41]:[13] His breath sets coals ablaze, and flame leaps from his mouth.
[Job] [41]:[14] Strength has its lair in his neck, and dismay dances before him.
[Job] [41]:[15] The folds of his flesh cling together, cast solid, immovable.
[Job] [41]:[16] His heart is hard as stone, hard as a lower millstone.
[Job] [41]:[17] When he rises up, the mighty are terrified; at the crashing they shrink back.
[Job] [41]:[18] The sword that reaches him accomplishes nothing, nor does spear or dart or javelin.
[Job] [41]:[19] He counts iron as straw, and bronze as rotten wood.
[Job] [41]:[20] The arrow cannot drive him off; sling stones are nothing but chaff to him.
[Job] [41]:[21] He reckons the club as stubble, and laughs at the whir of the spear.
[Job] [41]:[22] His underside is jagged potsherds; he leaves the mud furrowed like a threshing sledge.
[Job] [41]:[23] He makes the deep boil like a pot; he churns the sea into a jar of ointment.
[Job] [41]:[24] Behind him he leaves a shining wake; you would think the deep had turned white with age.
[Job] [41]:[25] Nothing on earth is his equal, a creature made without fear.
[Job] [41]:[26] He surveys all that is lofty; he is king over every proud beast.
[Job] [42]:[1] Then Job answered the LORD:
[Job] [42]:[2] "I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be thwarted.
[Job] [42]:[3] 'Who is this that obscures counsel without knowledge?' Surely I spoke of things I did not understand, wonders beyond me that I did not know.
[Job] [42]:[4] 'Listen now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you shall inform me.'
[Job] [42]:[5] I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye has seen you.
[Job] [42]:[6] Therefore I despise myself, and I repent in dust and ashes."[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew verb has no stated object; it may also be rendered "I take back my words" or "I yield."
[Job] [42]:[7] After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite: "My anger burns against you and your two friends, for you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has.
[Job] [42]:[8] Now take seven bulls and seven rams, go to my servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly, for you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has."
[Job] [42]:[9] So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them, and the LORD accepted Job's prayer.
[Job] [42]:[10] And when Job prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his fortunes; indeed, the LORD gave him twice as much as he had before.
[Job] [42]:[11] Then all his brothers and sisters and everyone who had known him before came and ate with him in his house. They consoled and comforted him over all the trouble the LORD had brought upon him, and each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring.[^1] [^1]: Hebrew *qesitah*, an ancient unit of money of unknown weight.
[Job] [42]:[12] The LORD blessed the latter part of Job's life more than the first. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand donkeys.
[Job] [42]:[13] He also had seven sons and three daughters.
[Job] [42]:[14] He named the first Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
[Job] [42]:[15] Nowhere in all the land were there women as beautiful as Job's daughters, and their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers.
[Job] [42]:[16] After this Job lived a hundred and forty years, and he saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.
[Job] [42]:[17] And so Job died, old and full of days.
[Psalms] [1]:[1] Blessed is the one who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, who does not stand in the way of sinners, who does not sit in the seat of mockers,

[Psalms] [13]:[5] and my enemy will say, "I have overcome him," and my foes will rejoice when I fall.
[Psalms] [13]:[6] But I trust in your steadfast love; my heart rejoices in your salvation. I will sing to the LORD, for he has dealt bountifully with me.
[Psalms] [14]:[1] For the choir director. Of David. The fool says in his heart, "There is no God." They are corrupt, their deeds are vile; there is no one who does good.
[Psalms] [14]:[2] The LORD looks down from heaven on the children of man to see if there are any who understand, any who seek God.
[Psalms] [14]:[3] All have turned away, together they have become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
[Psalms] [14]:[4] Do they know nothing, all these evildoers, who devour my people as they devour bread and never call on the LORD?
[Psalms] [14]:[5] There they were seized with terror, for God is with the generation of the righteous.
[Psalms] [14]:[6] You would frustrate the plans of the poor, but the LORD is their refuge.
[Psalms] [14]:[7] Oh, that salvation for Israel would come out of Zion! When the LORD restores the fortunes of his people, let Jacob rejoice and Israel be glad.
[Psalms] [15]:[1] A psalm of David. LORD, who may dwell in your tent? Who may live on your holy mountain?
[Psalms] [15]:[2] The one who walks blamelessly and does what is right, who speaks the truth from the heart;
[Psalms] [15]:[3] who spreads no slander with his tongue, who does his neighbor no harm and casts no reproach on his kinsman;
[Psalms] [15]:[4] who looks with contempt on a vile person but honors those who fear the LORD; who keeps his oath even when it costs him, and does not go back on it;
[Psalms] [15]:[5] who lends his money without interest and takes no bribe against the innocent. Whoever does these things will never be shaken.
[Psalms] [16]:[1] A miktam of David. Keep me safe, O God, for in you I take refuge.
[Psalms] [16]:[2] I say to the LORD, "You are my Lord; apart from you I have nothing good."
[Psalms] [16]:[3] As for the holy ones in the land, they are the noble ones in whom is all my delight.
[Psalms] [16]:[4] Those who run after another god multiply their sorrows; I will not pour out their drink offerings of blood, nor take their names upon my lips.
[Psalms] [16]:[5] The LORD is my portion and my cup; you hold my lot secure.
[Psalms] [16]:[6] The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; surely I have a beautiful inheritance.
[Psalms] [16]:[7] I will bless the LORD, who counsels me; even at night my inmost being instructs me.
[Psalms] [16]:[8] I have set the LORD always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
[Psalms] [16]:[9] Therefore my heart is glad and my glory rejoices; my body also rests secure.
[Psalms] [16]:[10] For you will not abandon my soul to the grave, nor let your faithful one see decay.
[Psalms] [16]:[11] You make known to me the path of life; in your presence there is fullness of joy, at your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
[Psalms] [17]:[1] A prayer of David. Hear my just cause, LORD; listen to my cry; give ear to my prayer— it comes from lips without deceit.
[Psalms] [17]:[2] Let my vindication come from your presence; let your eyes see what is right.
[Psalms] [17]:[3] You have tested my heart and examined me by night; you have refined me and found nothing wrong. I have resolved that my mouth will not sin.
[Psalms] [17]:[4] As for the deeds of men, by the word of your lips I have kept myself from the ways of the violent.
[Psalms] [17]:[5] Hold my steps steady on your paths, that my feet may not slip.
[Psalms] [17]:[6] I call on you, O God, for you answer me; turn your ear to me and hear my words.
[Psalms] [17]:[7] Show the wonder of your faithful love, Savior of all who take refuge in you, saving them by your right hand from those who rise against them.
[Psalms] [17]:[8] Guard me as the apple of your eye; hide me in the shadow of your wings
[Psalms] [17]:[9] from the wicked who assault me, from my deadly enemies who close in on me.
[Psalms] [17]:[10] Their hearts are sealed in fat; their mouths speak with arrogance.
[Psalms] [17]:[11] Now they have closed in around us, dogging our every step, their eyes fixed to bring us to the ground.
[Psalms] [17]:[12] He is like a lion hungry for prey, like a young lion crouching in hiding.
[Psalms] [17]:[13] Rise up, LORD! Confront him, bring him down; rescue my life from the wicked by your sword.
[Psalms] [17]:[14] Deliver me by your hand, LORD, from men of this world whose portion is in this life. You fill their bellies with what you have stored up; their children have their fill, and they leave the rest to their little ones.
[Psalms] [17]:[15] But I, in righteousness, will see your face; when I awake, I will be satisfied with your likeness.
[Psalms] [18]:[1] For the choirmaster. Of David, the servant of the LORD, who sang to the LORD the words of this song on the day the LORD rescued him from the grasp of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
[Psalms] [18]:[2] He said: I love you, LORD, my strength.
[Psalms] [18]:[3] The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my crag where I take refuge, my shield, the horn of my salvation, my stronghold.
[Psalms] [18]:[4] I call on the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and I am saved from my enemies.
[Psalms] [18]:[5] The cords of death wound around me; the torrents of destruction terrified me.
[Psalms] [18]:[6] The cords of the grave coiled about me; the snares of death confronted me.
[Psalms] [18]:[7] In my distress I called on the LORD; I cried to my God for help. From his temple he heard my voice, and my cry before him reached his ears.
[Psalms] [18]:[8] Then the earth reeled and shook; the foundations of the mountains trembled and quaked, because he was angry.
[Psalms] [18]:[9] Smoke rose from his nostrils, and consuming fire came from his mouth; burning coals blazed out of him.
[Psalms] [18]:[10] He bent the heavens low and came down, thick darkness beneath his feet.
[Psalms] [18]:[11] He mounted a cherub and flew; he soared on the wings of the wind.
[Psalms] [18]:[12] He made darkness his covering, his canopy around him—the dark rain clouds of the skies.
[Psalms] [18]:[13] Out of the brightness before him his clouds swept on, with hail and coals of fire.
[Psalms] [18]:[14] The LORD thundered from heaven; the Most High raised his voice, with hail and coals of fire.
[Psalms] [18]:[15] He shot his arrows and scattered them; he hurled lightning and routed them.
[Psalms] [18]:[16] The channels of the waters were laid bare, and the foundations of the world uncovered at your rebuke, LORD, at the blast of breath from your nostrils.
[Psalms] [18]:[17] He reached down from on high and took hold of me; he drew me out of deep waters.
[Psalms] [18]:[18] He rescued me from my powerful enemy, from my foes, who were too strong for me.
[Psalms] [18]:[19] They confronted me in the day of my calamity, but the LORD was my support.
[Psalms] [18]:[20] He brought me out into open ground; he delivered me, because he delighted in me.
[Psalms] [18]:[21] The LORD dealt with me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he repaid me.
[Psalms] [18]:[22] For I have kept the ways of the LORD; I have not turned wickedly from my God.
[Psalms] [18]:[23] All his judgments are before me; I have not put his statutes away from me.
[Psalms] [18]:[24] I was blameless before him and kept myself from guilt.
[Psalms] [18]:[25] So the LORD repaid me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands in his sight.
[Psalms] [18]:[26] With the faithful you show yourself faithful; with the blameless you show yourself blameless.
[Psalms] [18]:[27] With the pure you show yourself pure, but with the crooked you show yourself shrewd.
[Psalms] [18]:[28] You save a humble people, but you bring down eyes that are haughty.
[Psalms] [18]:[29] You light my lamp; the LORD my God turns my darkness into light.
[Psalms] [18]:[30] With you I can charge a raiding party; with my God I can scale a wall.
[Psalms] [18]:[31] As for God, his way is perfect; the word of the LORD is proven true. He is a shield to all who take refuge in him.
[Psalms] [18]:[32] For who is God besides the LORD? And who is a rock except our God?
[Psalms] [18]:[33] It is God who arms me with strength and makes my way perfect.
[Psalms] [18]:[34] He makes my feet like the feet of a deer and sets me secure on the heights.
[Psalms] [18]:[35] He trains my hands for battle, so that my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
[Psalms] [18]:[36] You have given me the shield of your salvation; your right hand upholds me, and your gentleness has made me great.
[Psalms] [18]:[37] You make a wide path for my steps, and my ankles do not give way.
[Psalms] [18]:[38] I pursued my enemies and overtook them; I did not turn back until they were destroyed.
[Psalms] [18]:[39] I struck them down, and they could not rise; they fell beneath my feet.
[Psalms] [18]:[40] You armed me with strength for the battle; you made my adversaries bow beneath me.
[Psalms] [18]:[41] You made my enemies turn their backs in flight, and I destroyed those who hated me.
[Psalms] [18]:[42] They cried for help, but no one saved them; they cried to the LORD, but he did not answer.
[Psalms] [18]:[43] I ground them fine as dust before the wind; I poured them out like mud in the streets.
[Psalms] [18]:[44] You delivered me from the strife of the people; you made me head of nations. A people I did not know now serve me.
[Psalms] [18]:[45] As soon as they hear of me, they obey me; foreigners come cringing to me.
[Psalms] [18]:[46] Foreigners lose heart; they come trembling from their strongholds.
[Psalms] [18]:[47] The LORD lives! Blessed be my rock! Exalted be the God of my salvation—
[Psalms] [18]:[48] the God who avenges me and subdues nations under me,
[Psalms] [18]:[49] who delivers me from my enemies. You lifted me above my adversaries; you rescued me from violent men.
[Psalms] [18]:[50] Therefore I will praise you among the nations, LORD; I will sing praise to your name.
[Psalms] [18]:[51] He gives his king great victories; he shows steadfast love to his anointed, to David and his descendants forever.
[Psalms] [19]:[1] For the choirmaster. A psalm of David.
[Psalms] [19]:[2] The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands.
[Psalms] [19]:[3] Day after day they pour forth speech; night after night they reveal knowledge.
[Psalms] [19]:[4] There is no speech, there are no words, no sound of their voice is heard.
[Psalms] [19]:[5] Yet their line goes out through all the earth, their words to the ends of the world. In them he has pitched a tent for the sun,
[Psalms] [19]:[6] which comes out like a bridegroom from his chamber, rejoicing like a champion to run its course.
[Psalms] [19]:[7] It rises at one end of the heavens and circles to the other; nothing is hidden from its heat.
[Psalms] [19]:[8] The law of the LORD is perfect, reviving the soul. The testimony of the LORD is sure, making wise the simple.
[Psalms] [19]:[9] The precepts of the LORD are right, giving joy to the heart. The commandment of the LORD is radiant, giving light to the eyes.
[Psalms] [19]:[10] The fear of the LORD is pure, enduring forever. The judgments of the LORD are true, and altogether righteous.
[Psalms] [19]:[11] They are more desirable than gold, than much pure gold; sweeter than honey, than honey from the comb.
[Psalms] [19]:[12] Moreover, by them your servant is warned; in keeping them there is great reward.
[Psalms] [19]:[13] Who can discern his own errors? Cleanse me from my hidden faults.
[Psalms] [19]:[14] Keep your servant also from willful sins; do not let them rule over me. Then I will be blameless, innocent of great transgression.
[Psalms] [19]:[15] May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be pleasing in your sight, O LORD, my rock and my redeemer.

[Psalms] [28]:[1] Of David. To you, LORD, I call; my rock, do not be deaf to me. For if you stay silent toward me, I will be like those who go down to the pit.
[Psalms] [28]:[2] Hear the sound of my pleading when I cry to you for help, when I lift up my hands toward your most holy place.
[Psalms] [28]:[3] Do not drag me away with the wicked, with those who do evil, who speak peace to their neighbors while malice fills their hearts.
[Psalms] [28]:[4] Repay them for what they have done, for the evil of their deeds; give them what their hands have earned, and bring back on them what they deserve.
[Psalms] [28]:[5] For they have no regard for the works of the LORD or for what his hands have made; so he will tear them down and never build them up again.
[Psalms] [28]:[6] Blessed be the LORD, for he has heard the sound of my pleading.
[Psalms] [28]:[7] The LORD is my strength and my shield; in him my heart trusted, and I was helped, so my heart leaped for joy, and with my song I will thank him.
[Psalms] [28]:[8] The LORD is their strength, and he is the saving stronghold of his anointed.
[Psalms] [28]:[9] Save your people and bless your inheritance; be their shepherd and carry them forever.
[Psalms] [29]:[1] A psalm of David. Ascribe to the LORD, you heavenly beings, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
[Psalms] [29]:[2] Ascribe to the LORD the glory of his name; worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness.
[Psalms] [29]:[3] The voice of the LORD is over the waters; the God of glory thunders, the LORD over the mighty waters.
[Psalms] [29]:[4] The voice of the LORD is powerful; the voice of the LORD is full of majesty.
[Psalms] [29]:[5] The voice of the LORD shatters the cedars; the LORD shatters the cedars of Lebanon.
[Psalms] [29]:[6] He makes them skip like a calf, Lebanon and Sirion like a young wild ox.
[Psalms] [29]:[7] The voice of the LORD flashes forth flames of fire.
[Psalms] [29]:[8] The voice of the LORD makes the wilderness tremble; the LORD makes the wilderness of Kadesh tremble.
[Psalms] [29]:[9] The voice of the LORD makes the deer give birth and strips the forests bare. And in his temple all cry, "Glory!"
[Psalms] [29]:[10] The LORD sits enthroned above the flood; the LORD sits enthroned as king forever.
[Psalms] [29]:[11] The LORD gives strength to his people; the LORD blesses his people with peace.
[Psalms] [30]:[1] A psalm. A song for the dedication of the house. Of David.
[Psalms] [30]:[2] I will exalt you, LORD, for you lifted me out of the depths and did not let my enemies gloat over me.
[Psalms] [30]:[3] LORD my God, I cried to you for help, and you healed me.
[Psalms] [30]:[4] LORD, you brought me up from the realm of the dead; you kept me alive so I would not go down to the pit.
[Psalms] [30]:[5] Sing to the LORD, you his faithful ones; give thanks to his holy name.
[Psalms] [30]:[6] For his anger lasts only a moment, but his favor a lifetime. Weeping may spend the night, but joy comes in the morning.
[Psalms] [30]:[7] When I felt secure, I said, "I will never be shaken."
[Psalms] [30]:[8] LORD, in your favor you made my mountain stand firm; but when you hid your face, I was terrified.
[Psalms] [30]:[9] To you, LORD, I called; to the Lord I pleaded for mercy:
[Psalms] [30]:[10] "What is gained by my blood, if I go down to the pit? Can dust praise you? Can it proclaim your faithfulness?
[Psalms] [30]:[11] Hear me, LORD, and have mercy on me; LORD, be my helper."
[Psalms] [30]:[12] You turned my mourning into dancing; you stripped off my sackcloth and clothed me with joy,
[Psalms] [30]:[13] so that my glory may sing your praise and not be silent. LORD my God, I will thank you forever.

[Psalms] [31]:[14] For I hear the whispering of many; terror surrounds me as they conspire against me and plot to take my life.
[Psalms] [31]:[15] But I trust in you, LORD; I say, "You are my God."
[Psalms] [31]:[16] My times are in your hand; deliver me from the grip of my enemies and from those who pursue me.
[Psalms] [31]:[17] Let your face shine upon your servant; save me in your mercy.
[Psalms] [31]:[18] LORD, let me not be put to shame, for I have called on you. Let the wicked be put to shame; let them be silenced in the grave.
[Psalms] [31]:[19] Let lying lips be struck dumb, that speak arrogantly against the righteous with pride and contempt.
[Psalms] [31]:[20] How great is your goodness, which you have stored up for those who fear you and shown to those who take refuge in you, in the sight of everyone.
[Psalms] [31]:[21] In the shelter of your presence you hide them from human plots; you keep them safe in your tent from quarreling tongues.
[Psalms] [31]:[22] Blessed be the LORD, for he has shown me the wonder of his mercy in a city under siege.
[Psalms] [31]:[23] In my alarm I said, "I am cut off from your sight." Yet you heard my cry for mercy when I called to you for help.
[Psalms] [31]:[24] Love the LORD, all you his faithful ones. The LORD preserves those who are true, but he repays in full the one who acts in pride.
[Psalms] [31]:[25] Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who wait for the LORD.

[Psalms] [35]:[5] Let them be like chaff before the wind, with the angel of the LORD driving them away.
[Psalms] [35]:[6] Let their way be dark and slippery, with the angel of the LORD pursuing them.
[Psalms] [35]:[7] For without cause they hid their net for me; without cause they dug a pit for my life.
[Psalms] [35]:[8] Let ruin overtake them unawares; let the net they hid catch them, and into that ruin let them fall.
[Psalms] [35]:[9] Then my soul will rejoice in the LORD and delight in his salvation.
[Psalms] [35]:[10] All my bones will say, "LORD, who is like you? You rescue the poor from those too strong for them, the poor and needy from the one who robs them."
[Psalms] [35]:[11] Malicious witnesses come forward; they question me about things I know nothing of.
[Psalms] [35]:[12] They repay me evil for good, leaving my soul bereaved.
[Psalms] [35]:[13] Yet when they were ill, I wore sackcloth; I humbled myself with fasting, and my prayer kept returning to my own heart.
[Psalms] [35]:[14] I went about grieving as though for a friend or a brother; I bowed down in sorrow, as one mourning a mother.
[Psalms] [35]:[15] But when I stumbled, they gathered in glee; attackers I did not even know gathered against me, tearing at me without ceasing.
[Psalms] [35]:[16] Like godless mockers at a feast, they gnashed their teeth at me.

[Psalms] [35]:[20] They do not speak peace, but against those who live quietly in the land they devise words of deceit.

[Psalms] [35]:[22] You have seen it, LORD; do not be silent. Lord, do not be far from me.

[Psalms] [35]:[24] Judge me according to your righteousness, LORD my God, and do not let them gloat over me.

[Psalms] [39]:[1] For the choirmaster. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David.
[Psalms] [39]:[2] I said, "I will watch my ways so I do not sin with my tongue; I will keep a muzzle on my mouth as long as the wicked are before me."
[Psalms] [39]:[3] I was mute in silence; I kept still, even from good, and my pain grew worse.
[Psalms] [39]:[4] My heart grew hot within me; as I mused, the fire burned. Then I spoke with my tongue:
[Psalms] [39]:[5] "Show me, LORD, my end and what the measure of my days is; let me know how fleeting I am.
[Psalms] [39]:[6] You have made my days mere handbreadths; my lifetime is as nothing before you. Surely everyone stands as a breath. Selah
[Psalms] [39]:[7] Surely everyone walks about as a mere shadow; surely for nothing they bustle about; they heap up wealth and do not know who will gather it.
[Psalms] [39]:[8] And now, Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in you.
[Psalms] [39]:[9] Deliver me from all my transgressions; do not make me the scorn of fools.
[Psalms] [39]:[10] I am silent; I do not open my mouth, for you are the one who has done it.
[Psalms] [39]:[11] Remove your plague from me; I am consumed by the hostility of your hand.
[Psalms] [39]:[12] When you discipline a man with rebukes for sin, you consume like a moth what he treasures. Surely everyone is but a breath. Selah
[Psalms] [39]:[13] Hear my prayer, LORD, and listen to my cry for help; do not be silent at my tears. For I am a stranger with you, a sojourner, like all my fathers.
[Psalms] [39]:[14] Look away from me, that I may find relief, before I depart and am no more."

[Psalms] [80]:[3] Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, stir up your might; come and save us.
[Psalms] [80]:[4] Restore us, O God; let your face shine on us, that we may be saved.
[Psalms] [80]:[5] LORD God of hosts, how long will your anger smolder against the prayer of your people?
[Psalms] [80]:[6] You have fed them the bread of tears and made them drink tears by the measure.
[Psalms] [80]:[7] You have made us a cause of strife to our neighbors, and our enemies laugh among themselves.
[Psalms] [80]:[8] Restore us, O God of hosts; let your face shine on us, that we may be saved.
[Psalms] [80]:[9] You brought a vine out of Egypt; you drove out the nations and planted it.
[Psalms] [80]:[10] You cleared the ground before it; it took root and filled the land.
[Psalms] [80]:[11] The mountains were covered with its shade, the mighty cedars with its branches.
[Psalms] [80]:[12] It sent out its branches to the Sea, its shoots as far as the River.
[Psalms] [80]:[13] Why have you broken down its walls, so that all who pass by pick its fruit?
[Psalms] [80]:[14] The boar from the forest ravages it, and whatever moves in the field feeds on it.
[Psalms] [80]:[15] Return to us, O God of hosts! Look down from heaven and see; watch over this vine,
[Psalms] [80]:[16] the stock your right hand has planted, the son you raised up for yourself.
[Psalms] [80]:[17] It is burned with fire, it is cut down; they perish at the rebuke of your face.
[Psalms] [80]:[18] Let your hand rest on the man at your right hand, on the son of man you have raised up for yourself.
[Psalms] [80]:[19] Then we will not turn away from you; revive us, and we will call on your name.
[Psalms] [80]:[20] Restore us, LORD God of hosts; let your face shine on us, that we may be saved.
[Psalms] [81]:[1] For the director of music. According to the gittith.<fn>The gittith is an unknown musical term, possibly an instrument or a tune.</fn> Of Asaph.
[Psalms] [81]:[2] Sing for joy to God, our strength; shout aloud to the God of Jacob!
[Psalms] [81]:[3] Raise a song, strike the tambourine, sound the sweet lyre and the harp.
[Psalms] [81]:[4] Blow the ram's horn at the new moon, and at the full moon, on the day of our feast.
[Psalms] [81]:[5] For this is a decree for Israel, an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
[Psalms] [81]:[6] He set it up as a testimony for Joseph when he went out against the land of Egypt. I heard a language I did not know:
[Psalms] [81]:[7] "I lifted the burden from his shoulder; his hands were freed from the basket.
[Psalms] [81]:[8] In your distress you called, and I rescued you; I answered you from the thundercloud; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah
[Psalms] [81]:[9] Hear, my people, and I will warn you—Israel, if only you would listen to me!
[Psalms] [81]:[10] You shall have no foreign god among you; you shall not bow down to any strange god.
[Psalms] [81]:[11] I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. Open wide your mouth, and I will fill it.
[Psalms] [81]:[12] But my people would not listen to my voice; Israel would have none of me.
[Psalms] [81]:[13] So I gave them over to their stubborn hearts, to follow their own devices.
[Psalms] [81]:[14] If only my people would listen to me, if Israel would walk in my ways,
[Psalms] [81]:[15] how quickly I would subdue their enemies and turn my hand against their foes!
[Psalms] [81]:[16] Those who hate the LORD would cringe before him, and their punishment would last forever.
[Psalms] [81]:[17] But you I would feed with the finest wheat<fn>Hebrew: he would feed him.</fn>; with honey from the rock I would satisfy you."
[Psalms] [82]:[1] A psalm of Asaph. God takes his stand in the assembly of God; in the midst of the gods he renders judgment:
[Psalms] [82]:[2] "How long will you judge unjustly and lift up the face of the wicked? Selah
[Psalms] [82]:[3] Give justice to the weak and the fatherless; uphold the cause of the afflicted and the destitute.
[Psalms] [82]:[4] Rescue the poor and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked."
[Psalms] [82]:[5] They neither know nor understand; they walk about in darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.
[Psalms] [82]:[6] I said, "You are gods, sons of the Most High, all of you.
[Psalms] [82]:[7] Yet you will die like mere men; you will fall like any prince."
[Psalms] [82]:[8] Rise up, O God, and judge the earth, for you shall inherit all the nations.
[Psalms] [83]:[1] A song. A psalm of Asaph.
[Psalms] [83]:[2] O God, do not keep quiet; do not be silent, do not be still, O God.
[Psalms] [83]:[3] See how your enemies are in an uproar, how those who hate you lift their heads.
[Psalms] [83]:[4] Against your people they lay crafty plans; they conspire against those you treasure.
[Psalms] [83]:[5] They say, "Come, let us wipe them out as a nation, so that the name of Israel is remembered no more."
[Psalms] [83]:[6] With one mind they scheme together; against you they make a covenant—
[Psalms] [83]:[7] the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
[Psalms] [83]:[8] Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, Philistia with the people of Tyre.
[Psalms] [83]:[9] Even Assyria has joined them; they are the strong arm of Lot's descendants. Selah
[Psalms] [83]:[10] Do to them as you did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the brook Kishon,
[Psalms] [83]:[11] who were destroyed at En-dor and became dung on the ground.
[Psalms] [83]:[12] Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
[Psalms] [83]:[13] who said, "Let us take the pastures of God for our own possession."
[Psalms] [83]:[14] My God, make them like whirling dust, like chaff before the wind.
[Psalms] [83]:[15] As fire burns through a forest, as flames set the mountains ablaze,
[Psalms] [83]:[16] so pursue them with your tempest and terrify them with your storm.
[Psalms] [83]:[17] Cover their faces with shame, that they may seek your name, O LORD.
[Psalms] [83]:[18] Let them be disgraced and dismayed forever; let them perish in humiliation.
[Psalms] [83]:[19] Then they will know that you alone, whose name is the LORD, are the Most High over all the earth.
[Psalms] [84]:[1] For the choirmaster. On the gittith. A psalm of the sons of Korah.<note>Gittith: probably a musical term, perhaps a tune or an instrument; the meaning is uncertain.</note>
[Psalms] [84]:[2] How lovely are your dwelling places, LORD of hosts!
[Psalms] [84]:[3] My soul longs, yes, faints for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh cry out for joy to the living God.
[Psalms] [84]:[4] Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young — at your altars, LORD of hosts, my King and my God.
[Psalms] [84]:[5] Blessed are those who dwell in your house; they are always praising you. Selah
[Psalms] [84]:[6] Blessed are those whose strength is in you, in whose hearts are the pilgrim highways.<note>Hebrew reads simply "highways in their hearts"; the image is of roads leading up to the sanctuary, hence the sense of a pilgrim's journey.</note>
[Psalms] [84]:[7] As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; the early rain covers it with blessings.
[Psalms] [84]:[8] They go from strength to strength, till each appears before God in Zion.
[Psalms] [84]:[9] LORD God of hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob. Selah
[Psalms] [84]:[10] Look upon our shield, O God; look with favor on the face of your anointed.
[Psalms] [84]:[11] Better is one day in your courts than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather stand at the threshold of the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.
[Psalms] [84]:[12] For the LORD God is a sun and shield; the LORD bestows favor and honor. No good thing does he withhold from those who walk uprightly.
[Psalms] [84]:[13] LORD of hosts, blessed is the one who trusts in you.

[Psalms] [86]:[1] A prayer of David. Turn your ear, LORD, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.
[Psalms] [86]:[2] Guard my life, for I am devoted to you; save your servant who trusts in you—you are my God.
[Psalms] [86]:[3] Be gracious to me, Lord, for I call to you all day long.
[Psalms] [86]:[4] Bring joy to your servant's soul, for to you, Lord, I lift up my soul.
[Psalms] [86]:[5] You, Lord, are good and forgiving, rich in mercy to all who call on you.
[Psalms] [86]:[6] Hear my prayer, LORD; listen to the voice of my pleading.
[Psalms] [86]:[7] In the day of my distress I call on you, for you will answer me.
[Psalms] [86]:[8] Among the gods there is none like you, Lord, and no deeds compare with yours.
[Psalms] [86]:[9] All the nations you have made will come and bow before you, Lord, and give glory to your name.
[Psalms] [86]:[10] For you are great and do wondrous things; you alone are God.
[Psalms] [86]:[11] Teach me your way, LORD, that I may walk in your truth; give me an undivided heart, that I may fear your name.
[Psalms] [86]:[12] I will praise you, Lord my God, with all my heart, and glorify your name forever.
[Psalms] [86]:[13] For great is your steadfast love toward me; you have delivered my soul from the depths of Sheol.
[Psalms] [86]:[14] O God, the arrogant have risen against me; a band of ruthless men seeks my life, and they give no thought to you.
[Psalms] [86]:[15] But you, Lord, are a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in love and faithfulness.
[Psalms] [86]:[16] Turn to me and have mercy on me; grant your strength to your servant and save the son of your handmaid.
[Psalms] [86]:[17] Give me a sign of your goodness, so that those who hate me may see it and be put to shame, for you, LORD, have helped me and comforted me.

[Psalms] [88]:[1] A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the choirmaster: according to Mahalath Leannoth. A maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.
[Psalms] [88]:[2] LORD, God of my salvation, by day I cry out, by night I come before you.
[Psalms] [88]:[3] Let my prayer reach your presence; turn your ear to my cry.
[Psalms] [88]:[4] For my soul is full of troubles, and my life has come to the edge of Sheol.* [*Sheol: the realm of the dead]
[Psalms] [88]:[5] I am counted among those who go down to the pit; I have become like a man with no strength left,
[Psalms] [88]:[6] set loose among the dead, like the slain who lie in the tomb, whom you remember no more, cut off from your hand.
[Psalms] [88]:[7] You have laid me in the lowest pit, in dark places, in the depths.
[Psalms] [88]:[8] Your wrath lies heavy upon me; you have overwhelmed me with all your waves. Selah
[Psalms] [88]:[9] You have driven my friends far from me; you have made me a horror to them. I am shut in and cannot escape.
[Psalms] [88]:[10] My eyes are worn out from affliction. I call to you, LORD, every day; I spread out my hands to you.
[Psalms] [88]:[11] Do you work wonders for the dead? Do the departed rise up to praise you? Selah
[Psalms] [88]:[12] Is your mercy declared in the grave, your faithfulness in the place of ruin?
[Psalms] [88]:[13] Are your wonders known in the darkness, your righteousness in the land of oblivion?
[Psalms] [88]:[14] But I cry to you for help, LORD; in the morning my prayer comes before you.
[Psalms] [88]:[15] Why, LORD, do you reject me? Why do you hide your face from me?
[Psalms] [88]:[16] From my youth I have been afflicted and close to death; I have borne your terrors, and I am at my wits' end.
[Psalms] [88]:[17] Your burning anger has swept over me; your terrors have destroyed me.
[Psalms] [88]:[18] All day long they surround me like water; together they close in on me.
[Psalms] [88]:[19] You have taken from me friend and neighbor; darkness is my only companion.
[Psalms] [89]:[1] A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.
[Psalms] [89]:[2] I will sing of the LORD's steadfast love forever; with my mouth I will make your faithfulness known to every generation.
[Psalms] [89]:[3] For I have said, "Steadfast love is built to last forever; in the heavens you establish your faithfulness."
[Psalms] [89]:[4] "I have made a covenant with my chosen one; I have sworn to David my servant:
[Psalms] [89]:[5] I will establish your offspring forever and build your throne for all generations." Selah
[Psalms] [89]:[6] The heavens praise your wonders, LORD, and your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones.
[Psalms] [89]:[7] For who in the skies can compare with the LORD? Who among the heavenly beings is like him?
[Psalms] [89]:[8] God is feared in the great council of the holy ones, awesome above all who surround him.
[Psalms] [89]:[9] LORD God of hosts, who is like you? Mighty are you, LORD, and your faithfulness surrounds you.
[Psalms] [89]:[10] You rule over the raging of the sea; when its waves rise up, you still them.
[Psalms] [89]:[11] You crushed Rahab like a corpse; with your mighty arm you scattered your enemies.
[Psalms] [89]:[12] The heavens are yours, and yours the earth; you founded the world and all that fills it.
[Psalms] [89]:[13] North and south you created; Tabor and Hermon sing for joy at your name.
[Psalms] [89]:[14] Yours is an arm of power; your hand is strong, your right hand lifted high.
[Psalms] [89]:[15] Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne; love and faithfulness go before you.
[Psalms] [89]:[16] Blessed are the people who know the festal shout, who walk, LORD, in the light of your face.
[Psalms] [89]:[17] They rejoice in your name all day long; in your righteousness they are lifted up.
[Psalms] [89]:[18] For you are the glory of their strength, and by your favor you raise our horn high.
[Psalms] [89]:[19] For our shield belongs to the LORD, our king to the Holy One of Israel.
[Psalms] [89]:[20] Once you spoke in a vision to your faithful ones and said: "I have granted help to a warrior; I have raised up a chosen one from the people.
[Psalms] [89]:[21] I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him.
[Psalms] [89]:[22] My hand will steady him; my arm will give him strength.
[Psalms] [89]:[23] No enemy will outwit him, no wicked man oppress him.
[Psalms] [89]:[24] I will crush his foes before him and strike down those who hate him.
[Psalms] [89]:[25] My faithfulness and my love will be with him, and through my name his horn will be lifted high.
[Psalms] [89]:[26] I will set his hand upon the sea, his right hand upon the rivers.
[Psalms] [89]:[27] He will call to me, 'You are my Father, my God, the rock of my salvation.'
[Psalms] [89]:[28] And I will make him the firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
[Psalms] [89]:[29] Forever I will keep my love for him, and my covenant with him will stand firm.
[Psalms] [89]:[30] I will establish his offspring forever, his throne as long as the heavens endure.
[Psalms] [89]:[31] If his sons forsake my law and do not walk in my judgments,
[Psalms] [89]:[32] if they violate my statutes and fail to keep my commandments,
[Psalms] [89]:[33] I will punish their rebellion with the rod and their guilt with blows;
[Psalms] [89]:[34] but I will not withdraw my love from him, nor will I betray my faithfulness.
[Psalms] [89]:[35] I will not violate my covenant or alter what my lips have spoken.
[Psalms] [89]:[36] Once and for all I have sworn by my holiness: I will not lie to David.
[Psalms] [89]:[37] His offspring will endure forever, his throne as long as the sun before me;
[Psalms] [89]:[38] like the moon it will stand firm forever, a faithful witness in the sky." Selah
[Psalms] [89]:[39] But now you have cast off and rejected; you have raged against your anointed.
[Psalms] [89]:[40] You have renounced the covenant with your servant and defiled his crown in the dust.
[Psalms] [89]:[41] You have broken down all his walls and reduced his strongholds to ruins.
[Psalms] [89]:[42] All who pass by have plundered him; he has become the scorn of his neighbors.
[Psalms] [89]:[43] You have raised the right hand of his foes; you have made all his enemies rejoice.
[Psalms] [89]:[44] You have turned back the edge of his sword and have not upheld him in battle.
[Psalms] [89]:[45] You have put an end to his splendor and hurled his throne to the ground.
[Psalms] [89]:[46] You have cut short the days of his youth; you have covered him with shame. Selah
[Psalms] [89]:[47] How long, LORD? Will you hide yourself forever? How long will your wrath burn like fire?
[Psalms] [89]:[48] Remember how fleeting my life is. For what emptiness have you created all humankind?
[Psalms] [89]:[49] Who can live and never see death? Who can save his soul from the grip of the grave? Selah
[Psalms] [89]:[50] Lord, where is your love of old, which in your faithfulness you swore to David?
[Psalms] [89]:[51] Remember, Lord, how your servants are mocked, how I bear in my heart the insults of all the many peoples,
[Psalms] [89]:[52] how your enemies have mocked, LORD, how they have mocked every step of your anointed.

[Psalms] [90]:[1] A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, you have been our dwelling place through all generations.
[Psalms] [90]:[2] Before the mountains were born, before you brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting you are God.
[Psalms] [90]:[3] You return mortals to dust, saying, "Return, you children of man."
[Psalms] [90]:[4] For a thousand years in your sight are like a day that has just gone by, like a watch in the night.
[Psalms] [90]:[5] You sweep them away like a flood; they are like sleep, like grass that springs up in the morning—
[Psalms] [90]:[6] in the morning it blooms and flourishes; by evening it withers and dries up.
[Psalms] [90]:[7] We are consumed by your anger, terrified by your wrath.
[Psalms] [90]:[8] You set our sins before you, our secret faults in the light of your presence.
[Psalms] [90]:[9] All our days pass away under your fury; we finish our years with a sigh.
[Psalms] [90]:[10] Seventy years—that is the span of our life, or eighty, if we have the strength; yet even the best of them is toil and sorrow, for they pass quickly, and we fly away.
[Psalms] [90]:[11] Who knows the power of your anger? Your wrath is as great as the fear you are due.
[Psalms] [90]:[12] Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
[Psalms] [90]:[13] Turn back, LORD! How long? Have compassion on your servants.
[Psalms] [90]:[14] Satisfy us in the morning with your steadfast love, that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.
[Psalms] [90]:[15] Give us joy for as many days as you have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen trouble.
[Psalms] [90]:[16] Let your work be seen by your servants, and your splendor by their children.
[Psalms] [90]:[17] May the favor of the Lord our God rest upon us; establish the work of our hands—yes, establish the work of our hands.

[Psalms] [92]:[4] on the ten-stringed lute and on the harp, to the melody of the lyre.
[Psalms] [92]:[5] For you have made me glad by your work, O LORD; at the deeds of your hands I sing for joy.

[Psalms] [92]:[8] though the wicked spring up like grass and all evildoers blossom, they are doomed to destruction forever.
[Psalms] [92]:[9] But you, O LORD, are on high forever.

[Psalms] [92]:[11] But you have lifted up my horn like that of a wild ox; I am anointed with fresh oil.

[Psalms] [92]:[15] They will still bear fruit in old age; they will stay fresh and green,

[Psalms] [136]:[3] Give thanks to the Lord of lords; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[4] To him who alone does great wonders; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[5] To him who made the heavens with understanding; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[6] To him who spread out the earth upon the waters; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[7] To him who made the great lights; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[8] The sun to rule over the day; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[9] The moon and stars to rule over the night; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[10] To him who struck down Egypt's firstborn; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[11] And brought Israel out from among them; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[12] With a strong hand and an outstretched arm; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[13] To him who split the Red Sea in two; his steadfast love endures forever. [footnote: Hebrew: Sea of Reeds]
[Psalms] [136]:[14] And led Israel through the midst of it; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[15] But swept Pharaoh and his army into the Red Sea; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[16] To him who led his people through the wilderness; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[17] To him who struck down great kings; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[18] And killed mighty kings; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[19] Sihon, king of the Amorites; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[20] And Og, king of Bashan; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[21] And gave their land as an inheritance; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[22] An inheritance for Israel his servant; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[23] Who remembered us when we were brought low; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[24] And broke us free from our foes; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[25] Who gives food to all flesh; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [136]:[26] Give thanks to the God of heaven; his steadfast love endures forever.
[Psalms] [137]:[1] By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion.
[Psalms] [137]:[2] On the willows there we hung up our harps,
[Psalms] [137]:[3] for there our captors demanded songs of us, our tormentors called for songs of joy: "Sing us one of the songs of Zion!"
[Psalms] [137]:[4] How can we sing the LORD's song on foreign soil?
[Psalms] [137]:[5] If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand forget how to play.[^1] [^1]: Hebrew simply reads "may my right hand forget," leaving the object unstated; the context of harp playing (verse 2) is supplied.
[Psalms] [137]:[6] Let my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy.
[Psalms] [137]:[7] Remember, LORD, against the Edomites the day of Jerusalem, how they said, "Tear it down! Tear it down to its foundations!"[^1] [^1]: "The day of Jerusalem" refers to the day the city fell to its enemies.
[Psalms] [137]:[8] Daughter of Babylon, you destroyer,[^1] blessed is the one who repays you for what you did to us, [^1]: Or "you who are doomed to be destroyed."
[Psalms] [137]:[9] blessed is the one who seizes your infants and dashes them against the rock.

[Psalms] [138]:[4] All the kings of the earth will thank you, LORD, for they have heard the words of your mouth.
[Psalms] [138]:[5] They will sing of the ways of the LORD, for the glory of the LORD is great.
[Psalms] [138]:[6] For the LORD is exalted, yet he sees the lowly; the proud he knows from afar.
[Psalms] [138]:[7] Though I walk in the midst of trouble, you keep me alive; you stretch out your hand against the wrath of my enemies, and your right hand saves me.

[Psalms] [139]:[1] For the choirmaster. A psalm of David. LORD, you have searched me and you know me.
[Psalms] [139]:[2] You know when I sit down and when I rise; you discern my thoughts from far away.
[Psalms] [139]:[3] You mark my going out and my lying down; you are familiar with all my ways.
[Psalms] [139]:[4] Not a word is on my tongue, LORD, but you know it completely.
[Psalms] [139]:[5] You hem me in, behind and before; you lay your hand upon me.
[Psalms] [139]:[6] Such knowledge is too wonderful for me, too high for me to reach.
[Psalms] [139]:[7] Where can I go from your Spirit? Where can I flee from your presence?
[Psalms] [139]:[8] If I climb to the heavens, you are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, you are there.
[Psalms] [139]:[9] If I rise on the wings of the dawn and settle at the farthest edge of the sea,
[Psalms] [139]:[10] even there your hand will guide me, your right hand will hold me fast.
[Psalms] [139]:[11] If I say, "Surely the darkness will hide me, and the light around me turn to night,"
[Psalms] [139]:[12] even the darkness is not dark to you; the night shines like the day, for darkness is as light to you.
[Psalms] [139]:[13] For you created my inmost being; you knit me together in my mother's womb.
[Psalms] [139]:[14] I praise you, for I am awesomely and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful; my soul knows it well.
[Psalms] [139]:[15] My frame was not hidden from you when I was made in secret, woven together in the depths of the earth.
[Psalms] [139]:[16] Your eyes saw my unformed body; all my days were written in your book, ordained before a single one of them had come to be.
[Psalms] [139]:[17] How precious to me are your thoughts, O God! How vast is their number!
[Psalms] [139]:[18] If I could count them, they would outnumber the grains of sand. When I awake, I am still with you.
[Psalms] [139]:[19] If only you would slay the wicked, O God! Away from me, you men of blood!
[Psalms] [139]:[20] They speak of you with malice; your enemies misuse your name.
[Psalms] [139]:[21] Do I not hate those who hate you, LORD, and loathe those who rise against you?
[Psalms] [139]:[22] I hate them with a perfect hatred; I count them my enemies.
[Psalms] [139]:[23] Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts.
[Psalms] [139]:[24] See if there is any offensive way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
[Psalms] [140]:[1] For the choir director. A psalm of David.
[Psalms] [140]:[2] Rescue me, LORD, from evil men; protect me from the violent,
[Psalms] [140]:[3] who plot evil in their hearts and stir up war every day.
[Psalms] [140]:[4] They sharpen their tongues like a serpent; the venom of a viper is under their lips. Selah
[Psalms] [140]:[5] Guard me, LORD, from the hands of the wicked; protect me from the violent, who plot to trip up my feet.
[Psalms] [140]:[6] The arrogant have hidden a trap for me; with cords they have spread a net beside the path and set snares for me. Selah
[Psalms] [140]:[7] I say to the LORD: You are my God. Listen, LORD, to my cry for mercy.
[Psalms] [140]:[8] LORD God, my mighty savior, you shield my head on the day of battle.
[Psalms] [140]:[9] Do not grant the wicked their desires, LORD; do not let their schemes succeed, or they will exalt themselves. Selah
[Psalms] [140]:[10] As for the head of those who surround me—let the malice of their own lips cover them.
[Psalms] [140]:[11] Let burning coals rain down on them; let them be thrown into the fire, into watery pits, never to rise again.
[Psalms] [140]:[12] Let the slanderer find no footing in the land; let disaster hunt down the man of violence.
[Psalms] [140]:[13] I know that the LORD secures justice for the poor and upholds the cause of the needy.
[Psalms] [140]:[14] Surely the righteous will praise your name, and the upright will dwell in your presence.
[Psalms] [141]:[1] A psalm of David. LORD, I call to you; hurry to me. Listen to my voice when I call to you.
[Psalms] [141]:[2] Let my prayer rise before you like incense, the lifting of my hands like the evening sacrifice.
[Psalms] [141]:[3] Set a guard, LORD, over my mouth; keep watch at the door of my lips.
[Psalms] [141]:[4] Do not let my heart turn to any evil thing, to take part in wicked deeds with those who do wrong; let me not taste their delicacies.
[Psalms] [141]:[5] Let the righteous strike me—it is a kindness; let him rebuke me—it is oil on my head; let my head never refuse it. But my prayer is still against the deeds of the wicked.
[Psalms] [141]:[6] When their judges are thrown down from the cliffs, then they will hear my words, for they are pleasant.
[Psalms] [141]:[7] Like ground broken and split open by the plow, our bones are scattered at the mouth of Sheol.
[Psalms] [141]:[8] But my eyes are on you, LORD God; in you I take refuge—do not leave me defenseless.
[Psalms] [141]:[9] Keep me from the snares they have set for me, from the traps of those who do wrong.
[Psalms] [141]:[10] Let the wicked fall into their own nets, all of them together, while I pass by in safety.

[Psalms] [142]:[3] I pour out my complaint before him; before him I tell my trouble.
[Psalms] [142]:[4] When my spirit grows faint within me, you know my path. On the road where I walk they have hidden a trap for me.
[Psalms] [142]:[5] Look to my right and see: no one recognizes me. Refuge has perished from me; no one cares for my life.
[Psalms] [142]:[6] I cry out to you, LORD; I say, "You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living."

[Psalms] [142]:[8] Bring my soul out of prison, that I may give thanks to your name. The righteous will gather around me, for you will deal bountifully with me.
[Psalms] [143]:[1] A psalm of David. LORD, hear my prayer; listen to my plea for mercy. In your faithfulness answer me, in your righteousness.
[Psalms] [143]:[2] Do not bring your servant to judgment, for no one alive is righteous before you.
[Psalms] [143]:[3] For the enemy hunts me down; he crushes my life to the ground. He makes me dwell in darkness, like those long dead.
[Psalms] [143]:[4] So my spirit fails within me; my heart is numb inside me.
[Psalms] [143]:[5] I remember the days of old; I meditate on all you have done; I ponder the work of your hands.
[Psalms] [143]:[6] I stretch out my hands to you; my soul thirsts for you like a parched land. Selah
[Psalms] [143]:[7] Answer me quickly, LORD; my spirit is spent. Do not hide your face from me, or I will be like those who go down to the pit.
[Psalms] [143]:[8] Let me hear of your steadfast love in the morning, for I trust in you. Show me the way I should walk, for to you I lift up my soul.
[Psalms] [143]:[9] Deliver me from my enemies, LORD; to you I flee for cover.
[Psalms] [143]:[10] Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Let your good Spirit lead me on level ground.

[Psalms] [143]:[12] In your steadfast love cut off my enemies; destroy all who oppress my soul, for I am your servant.

[Proverbs] [1]:[1] The proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel:
[Proverbs] [1]:[2] For gaining wisdom and discipline, for understanding words of insight;
[Proverbs] [1]:[3] for receiving instruction in wise dealing, in righteousness, justice, and integrity;
[Proverbs] [1]:[4] for giving prudence to the simple, knowledge and discretion to the young.
[Proverbs] [1]:[5] Let the wise listen and add to their learning, and let the discerning gain guidance—
[Proverbs] [1]:[6] for understanding a proverb and a riddle-saying, the words of the wise and their riddles.
[Proverbs] [1]:[7] The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge; fools despise wisdom and discipline.
[Proverbs] [1]:[8] Listen, my son, to your father's instruction, and do not forsake your mother's teaching.
[Proverbs] [1]:[9] They are a graceful wreath for your head, a necklace to adorn your neck.
[Proverbs] [1]:[10] My son, if sinners entice you, do not give in.
[Proverbs] [1]:[11] If they say, "Come along with us; let's lie in wait for blood, let's ambush some innocent soul for no reason;
[Proverbs] [1]:[12] let's swallow them alive like the grave, whole like those who go down to the pit;
[Proverbs] [1]:[13] we'll find all kinds of costly wealth and fill our houses with plunder;
[Proverbs] [1]:[14] throw in your lot with us, and we'll all share one purse"—
[Proverbs] [1]:[15] my son, do not walk in the way with them; keep your foot from their path.
[Proverbs] [1]:[16] For their feet run to evil; they hurry to shed blood.
[Proverbs] [1]:[17] How useless to spread the net where every bird can see it!
[Proverbs] [1]:[18] Yet these men lie in wait for their own blood; they ambush their own lives.
[Proverbs] [1]:[19] Such are the ways of all who are greedy for gain; it takes away the life of those who have it.
[Proverbs] [1]:[20] Wisdom calls aloud in the street; she raises her voice in the public squares.
[Proverbs] [1]:[21] At the head of the noisy streets she cries out; at the entrance of the city gates she speaks her words:
[Proverbs] [1]:[22] "How long, you simple ones, will you love your simple ways? How long will mockers delight in mockery and fools hate knowledge?
[Proverbs] [1]:[23] Turn at my reproof! Then I will pour out my spirit on you; I will make my words known to you.
[Proverbs] [1]:[24] But since you refused when I called and no one paid attention when I stretched out my hand,
[Proverbs] [1]:[25] since you ignored all my counsel and would have none of my correction,
[Proverbs] [1]:[26] I in turn will laugh at your disaster; I will mock when terror overtakes you—
[Proverbs] [1]:[27] when terror strikes you like a storm and your disaster sweeps in like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish come upon you.
[Proverbs] [1]:[28] Then they will call to me, but I will not answer; they will look for me, but will not find me,
[Proverbs] [1]:[29] since they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of the LORD,
[Proverbs] [1]:[30] since they would have none of my counsel and despised all my correction.
[Proverbs] [1]:[31] So they will eat the fruit of their own way and have their fill of their own schemes.
[Proverbs] [1]:[32] For the waywardness of the simple kills them, and the complacency of fools destroys them;
[Proverbs] [1]:[33] but whoever listens to me will dwell in safety, secure, with no fear of harm."
[Proverbs] [2]:[1] My son, if you accept my words and treasure up my commands within you,
[Proverbs] [2]:[2] turning your ear toward wisdom and inclining your heart to understanding—
[Proverbs] [2]:[3] yes, if you call out for insight and raise your voice for understanding,
[Proverbs] [2]:[4] if you seek it like silver and search for it as for hidden treasure,
[Proverbs] [2]:[5] then you will understand the fear of the LORD and find the knowledge of God.
[Proverbs] [2]:[6] For the LORD gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding.
[Proverbs] [2]:[7] He stores up sound wisdom for the upright; he is a shield to those who walk in integrity,
[Proverbs] [2]:[8] guarding the paths of justice and watching over the way of his faithful ones.

[Proverbs] [2]:[10] For wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul.

[Proverbs] [2]:[13] from those who abandon the straight paths to walk in ways of darkness,

[Proverbs] [2]:[17] who forsakes the companion of her youth and forgets the covenant of her God.

[Proverbs] [3]:[1] My son, do not forget my teaching; let your heart keep my commands.

[Proverbs] [30]:[1] The words of Agur son of Jakeh—an oracle. This is what the man declared to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
[Proverbs] [30]:[2] Surely I am more like a brute than a man; I do not have human understanding.
[Proverbs] [30]:[3] I have not learned wisdom, nor have I gained knowledge of the Holy One.
[Proverbs] [30]:[4] Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has gathered the wind in the hollow of his hands? Who has wrapped up the waters in a garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son's name? Surely you know!
[Proverbs] [30]:[5] Every word of God is refined; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.
[Proverbs] [30]:[6] Do not add to his words, or he will rebuke you and expose you as a liar.
[Proverbs] [30]:[7] Two things I ask of you; do not withhold them from me before I die:
[Proverbs] [30]:[8] Keep falsehood and lying far from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the bread I need,
[Proverbs] [30]:[9] or I may have too much and deny you, saying, "Who is the LORD?" Or I may become poor and steal, and so dishonor the name of my God.
[Proverbs] [30]:[10] Do not slander a servant to his master, or he will curse you, and you will bear the guilt.
[Proverbs] [30]:[11] There is a generation that curses its father and refuses to bless its mother.

[Proverbs] [30]:[14] There is a generation whose teeth are swords, whose jaws are knives, devouring the poor from the earth and the needy from among mankind.
[Proverbs] [30]:[15] The leech has two daughters: "Give!" and "Give!" Three things are never satisfied, four never say, "Enough!":
[Proverbs] [30]:[16] the grave, the barren womb, land that never has enough water, and fire, which never says, "Enough!"
[Proverbs] [30]:[17] The eye that mocks a father and scorns obedience to a mother will be picked out by the ravens of the valley and eaten by the young vultures.
[Proverbs] [30]:[18] Three things are too wonderful for me, four I cannot understand:
[Proverbs] [30]:[19] the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship on the open sea, and the way of a man with a young woman.
[Proverbs] [30]:[20] This is the way of an adulteress: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says, "I have done nothing wrong."
[Proverbs] [30]:[21] Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot bear up:
[Proverbs] [30]:[22] a servant who becomes king, a fool who is filled with food,
[Proverbs] [30]:[23] an unloved woman who finally marries, and a maidservant who displaces her mistress.
[Proverbs] [30]:[24] Four things on earth are small, yet they are wise beyond wisdom:
[Proverbs] [30]:[25] Ants are a people without strength, yet they store up their food in the summer.
[Proverbs] [30]:[26] Rock badgers are a people without power, yet they make their home in the crags.
[Proverbs] [30]:[27] Locusts have no king, yet they advance in ranks together.
[Proverbs] [30]:[28] A lizard you can catch with your hand, yet it lives in kings' palaces.
