[Song of Solomon] [6]:[9] but she is the only one, my dove, my perfect one, the only child of her mother, the favorite of the one who bore her. The daughters saw her and called her blessed; the queens and concubines praised her.
[Song of Solomon] [6]:[10] Who is this that shines forth like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun, awesome as an army with banners?
[Song of Solomon] [6]:[11] I went down to the nut orchard to see the new growth of the valley, to see whether the vine had budded, whether the pomegranates were in bloom.
[Song of Solomon] [6]:[12] Before I knew it, my desire had set me among the chariots of my princely people.
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[1] Turn, turn, O Shulammite; turn, turn, that we may gaze on you. Why should you gaze on the Shulammite, as at the dance of two camps?
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[2] How beautiful are your feet in sandals, O noble daughter! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the work of a master's hands.
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[3] Your navel is a rounded bowl—may it never lack blended wine. Your belly is a heap of wheat encircled with lilies.
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[4] Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[5] Your neck is like a tower of ivory. Your eyes are the pools of Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, looking out toward Damascus.
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[6] Your head crowns you like Carmel, and the flowing hair of your head is like purple; a king is held captive in its tresses.
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[7] How beautiful you are, how pleasant, O love, with all your delights!
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[8] Your stature is like a palm tree, and your breasts are its clusters.
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[9] I said, "I will climb the palm tree and take hold of its clusters." May your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the fragrance of your breath like apples,
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[10] and your mouth like the finest wine, flowing smoothly to my beloved, stirring the lips of sleepers.
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[11] I am my beloved's, and his desire is for me.
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[12] Come, my beloved, let us go out to the countryside; let us spend the night among the villages.
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[13] Let us rise early for the vineyards and see whether the vine has budded, whether its blossoms have opened, whether the pomegranates are in bloom. There I will give you my love.
[Song of Solomon] [7]:[14] The mandrakes give off their fragrance, and at our doors is every choice fruit, new as well as old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[1] If only you were my brother, nursed at my mother's breast! Then I could kiss you when I found you in the street, and no one would despise me for it.
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[2] I would lead you and bring you to my mother's house — she would teach me — and I would give you spiced wine to drink, the juice of my pomegranates.
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[3] His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[4] I charge you, daughters of Jerusalem: do not stir up, do not awaken love until it desires.
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[5] Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on the one she loves? Under the apple tree I awakened you; there your mother travailed with you, there she travailed who gave you birth.
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[6] Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm; for love is as strong as death, its passion as unyielding as the grave. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a flame of the LORD.
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[7] Many waters cannot quench love, nor can rivers wash it away. If a man offered all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[8] We have a little sister, and her breasts are not yet grown. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[9] If she is a wall, we will build turrets of silver upon her; if she is a door, we will enclose her with panels of cedar.
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[10] I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. So in his eyes I have become as one who finds peace.
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[11] Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon. He leased the vineyard to caretakers; each was to bring for its fruit a thousand pieces of silver.
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[12] My own vineyard is before me. The thousand is yours, Solomon, and two hundred for those who tend its fruit.
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[13] You who dwell in the gardens, companions are listening for your voice — let me hear it!
[Song of Solomon] [8]:[14] Hurry away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young stag upon the mountains of spices.
[Isaiah] [1]:[1] The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
[Isaiah] [1]:[2] Hear, O heavens! Listen, O earth! For the LORD has spoken: "I reared children and raised them up, and they have rebelled against me.
[Isaiah] [1]:[3] The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's stall, but Israel does not know, my people do not understand."
[Isaiah] [1]:[4] Woe to a sinful nation, a people weighed down with guilt, offspring of evildoers, children who bring ruin! They have abandoned the LORD, spurned the Holy One of Israel, turned their backs on him.
[Isaiah] [1]:[5] Why go on being beaten? Why keep adding rebellion? The whole head is sick, the whole heart is faint.
[Isaiah] [1]:[6] From the sole of the foot to the head there is nothing sound in it—only wounds and welts and raw sores, not cleaned, not bandaged, not soothed with oil.
[Isaiah] [1]:[7] Your land is desolate, your cities burned with fire. Before your very eyes strangers devour your soil, and it lies desolate, like a land overthrown by strangers.
[Isaiah] [1]:[8] The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field, like a city under siege.
[Isaiah] [1]:[9] Had the LORD of hosts not left us a few survivors, we would have been like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.
[Isaiah] [1]:[10] Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the teaching of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
[Isaiah] [1]:[11] "What to me is the multitude of your sacrifices?" says the LORD. "I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened beasts; I take no delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and male goats.
[Isaiah] [1]:[12] When you come to appear before me, who asked you to trample my courts?
[Isaiah] [1]:[13] Stop bringing meaningless offerings! Your incense is detestable to me. New moon and Sabbath, the calling of assemblies—I cannot endure iniquity together with solemn gathering.
[Isaiah] [1]:[14] Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hates. They have become a burden to me; I am weary of bearing them.
[Isaiah] [1]:[15] When you spread out your hands, I will hide my eyes from you. Even when you multiply your prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are full of blood.
[Isaiah] [1]:[16] Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean. Remove your evil deeds from my sight. Stop doing wrong;
[Isaiah] [1]:[17] learn to do good. Seek justice, bring relief to the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead the widow's cause.
[Isaiah] [1]:[18] "Come now, let us settle the matter," says the LORD. "Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be white as snow; though they are red as crimson, they shall be like wool.
[Isaiah] [1]:[19] If you are willing and obey, you will eat the good of the land;
[Isaiah] [1]:[20] but if you refuse and rebel, you will be devoured by the sword." For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
[Isaiah] [1]:[21] How the faithful city has become a whore! She was filled with justice; righteousness once dwelt in her—but now murderers.
[Isaiah] [1]:[22] Your silver has become dross, your wine is watered down.
[Isaiah] [1]:[23] Your rulers are rebels, companions of thieves. Every one of them loves a bribe and chases after gifts. They do not defend the orphan, and the widow's cause never reaches them.
[Isaiah] [1]:[24] Therefore this is the declaration of the Lord, the LORD of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: "Ah, I will vent my wrath on my foes and take vengeance on my enemies.
[Isaiah] [1]:[25] I will turn my hand against you; I will smelt away your dross as with lye and remove all your impurities.
[Isaiah] [1]:[26] I will restore your judges as at the first, your counselors as at the beginning. Then you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City."
[Isaiah] [1]:[27] Zion will be redeemed by justice, and those in her who repent by righteousness.
[Isaiah] [1]:[28] But rebels and sinners will be shattered together, and those who forsake the LORD will perish.
[Isaiah] [1]:[29] You will be ashamed of the sacred oaks you have desired, and disgraced by the gardens you have chosen.
[Isaiah] [1]:[30] You will be like an oak whose leaves wither, like a garden without water.
[Isaiah] [1]:[31] The strong man will become tinder and his work a spark; both will burn together, with no one to quench the fire.
[Isaiah] [2]:[1] The word that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
[Isaiah] [2]:[2] In the last days the mountain of the LORD's house will stand firm as the highest of the mountains, raised above the hills, and all the nations will stream to it.
[Isaiah] [2]:[3] Many peoples will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, that he may teach us his ways, so that we may walk in his paths." For out of Zion goes forth instruction, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
[Isaiah] [2]:[4] He will judge between the nations and settle disputes for many peoples. They will hammer their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, and they will train for war no more.
[Isaiah] [2]:[5] House of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the LORD.
[Isaiah] [2]:[6] For you have abandoned your people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled with practices from the East and with soothsayers like the Philistines, and they strike hands with the children of foreigners.
[Isaiah] [2]:[7] Their land is full of silver and gold, and their treasures have no end; their land is full of horses, and their chariots have no end.
[Isaiah] [2]:[8] Their land is full of idols; they bow down to the work of their hands, to what their own fingers have made.
[Isaiah] [2]:[9] So humanity is brought low, and everyone is humbled — do not forgive them.
[Isaiah] [2]:[10] Go into the rock, hide yourself in the dust, before the terror of the LORD and the splendor of his majesty.
[Isaiah] [2]:[11] The proud eyes of man will be brought low, and human arrogance will be humbled; the LORD alone will be exalted on that day.
[Isaiah] [2]:[12] For the LORD of hosts has a day against all that is proud and lofty, against all that is lifted up — and it will be brought low:
[Isaiah] [2]:[13] against all the cedars of Lebanon, lofty and lifted up, and against all the oaks of Bashan;
[Isaiah] [2]:[14] against all the towering mountains and all the lofty hills;
[Isaiah] [2]:[15] against every high tower and every fortified wall;
[Isaiah] [2]:[16] against all the ships of Tarshish and all the splendid vessels.
[Isaiah] [2]:[17] Human pride will be humbled, and human arrogance brought low; the LORD alone will be exalted on that day,
[Isaiah] [2]:[18] and the idols will vanish completely.
[Isaiah] [2]:[19] People will go into the caves of the rocks and into holes in the ground, before the terror of the LORD and the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to shake the earth.
[Isaiah] [2]:[20] On that day people will throw away their idols of silver and their idols of gold, which they made for themselves to worship, and cast them to the moles and the bats.
[Isaiah] [2]:[21] They will go into the crevices of the rocks and the clefts of the cliffs, before the terror of the LORD and the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to shake the earth.
[Isaiah] [2]:[22] Stop relying on man, who has but breath in his nostrils. Of what account is he?
[Isaiah] [3]:[1] Look: the Lord, the LORD of hosts, is about to strip Jerusalem and Judah of every support and supply — every reserve of bread, every reserve of water —
[Isaiah] [3]:[2] the warrior and the soldier, the judge and the prophet, the diviner and the elder,
[Isaiah] [3]:[3] the commander of fifty and the man of rank, the counselor, the skilled craftsman, and the expert in charms.
[Isaiah] [3]:[4] I will make boys their officials; mere children will rule over them.
[Isaiah] [3]:[5] The people will oppress one another, each man his neighbor. The young will bully the old, and the base will insult the honored.
[Isaiah] [3]:[6] A man will seize his brother in his father's house and say: "You have a cloak — you be our leader; take this heap of ruins under your hand."
[Isaiah] [3]:[7] But on that day he will protest: "I will not be your healer. In my house there is no bread and no cloak. Do not make me leader of the people."
[Isaiah] [3]:[8] For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, because their words and their deeds are against the LORD, defying the gaze of his glory.
[Isaiah] [3]:[9] The look on their faces testifies against them; they flaunt their sin like Sodom, they do not hide it. Woe to them! They have brought disaster on themselves.
[Isaiah] [3]:[10] Tell the righteous it will go well with them, for they will enjoy the fruit of their deeds.
[Isaiah] [3]:[11] Woe to the wicked! Disaster is upon them, for what their hands have done will be done to them.
[Isaiah] [3]:[12] My people — children oppress them, and women rule over them. My people, your guides lead you astray; they have swallowed up the path you should walk.
[Isaiah] [3]:[13] The LORD takes his place in court; he rises to judge the peoples.
[Isaiah] [3]:[14] The LORD enters into judgment against the elders and officials of his people: "It is you who have devoured the vineyard; the plunder of the poor is in your houses.
[Isaiah] [3]:[15] What do you mean by crushing my people and grinding the faces of the poor?" declares the Lord, the LORD of hosts.
[Isaiah] [3]:[16] The LORD says: Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, walking with outstretched necks and flirting eyes, mincing along with tinkling steps and ornaments jingling at their feet —
[Isaiah] [3]:[17] the Lord will bring sores on the heads of the daughters of Zion; the LORD will lay bare their scalps.* *Footnote: Or "will expose their nakedness"; the meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
[Isaiah] [3]:[18] On that day the Lord will strip away their finery: the anklets and headbands and crescent necklaces,
[Isaiah] [3]:[19] the pendants, the bracelets, and the veils,
[Isaiah] [3]:[20] the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the perfume bottles, and the amulets,
[Isaiah] [3]:[21] the signet rings and the nose rings,
[Isaiah] [3]:[22] the fine robes, the capes, the cloaks, and the purses,
[Isaiah] [3]:[23] the mirrors, the linen garments, the turbans, and the shawls.
[Isaiah] [3]:[24] Instead of perfume there will be a stench; instead of a sash, a rope; instead of well-set hair, baldness; instead of fine clothing, sackcloth; instead of beauty, branding.* *Footnote: The Hebrew line breaks off after "instead of beauty"; the final word ("branding" or "shame") is supplied for sense.
[Isaiah] [3]:[25] Your men will fall by the sword, your warriors in battle.
[Isaiah] [3]:[26] The gates of Zion will lament and mourn; stripped bare, she will sit on the ground.
[Isaiah] [4]:[1] On that day seven women will seize a single man and say, "We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothes—only let us be called by your name. Take away our disgrace."
[Isaiah] [4]:[2] On that day the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and splendor of those in Israel who survive.
[Isaiah] [4]:[3] And everyone who is left in Zion, who remains in Jerusalem, will be called holy—everyone recorded for life in Jerusalem.
[Isaiah] [4]:[4] When the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and rinsed away the bloodstains from the midst of Jerusalem by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning,
[Isaiah] [4]:[5] Then the LORD will create over all of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day and smoke, and the brightness of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory there will be a canopy.
[Isaiah] [4]:[6] And there will be a shelter, a shade by day from the heat, a refuge and a hiding place from storm and rain.
[Isaiah] [5]:[1] Let me sing for the one I love a song about his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hillside.
[Isaiah] [5]:[2] He broke up the soil and cleared it of stones and planted it with choice vines. He built a watchtower in the middle of it and hewed out a winepress as well. Then he waited for it to yield grapes, but it yielded only sour ones.
[Isaiah] [5]:[3] So now, you who live in Jerusalem, you people of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.
[Isaiah] [5]:[4] What more could have been done for my vineyard that I did not do for it? Why, when I waited for it to yield grapes, did it yield only sour ones?
[Isaiah] [5]:[5] Now let me tell you what I am going to do to my vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be devoured; I will break down its wall, and it will be trampled.
[Isaiah] [5]:[6] I will make it a wasteland. It will not be pruned or hoed, and briers and thorns will grow up in it. I will command the clouds not to rain on it.
[Isaiah] [5]:[7] The vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are the planting he delighted in. He waited for justice, but look—bloodshed; for righteousness, but listen—a cry of distress.
[Isaiah] [5]:[8] Woe to you who add house to house and join field to field until no space is left, and you are the only ones living in the land.
[Isaiah] [5]:[9] The LORD of Hosts has declared in my hearing: Surely the many houses will lie desolate, the great and fine ones left without a resident.
[Isaiah] [5]:[10] Ten acres of vineyard will produce only one bath of wine, and a homer of seed only an ephah of grain.
[Isaiah] [5]:[11] Woe to those who rise early in the morning to chase after strong drink, who linger into the night until wine inflames them.
[Isaiah] [5]:[12] They have harp and lyre, tambourine and flute and wine at their feasts, but they pay no attention to the work of the LORD and take no notice of what his hands have done.
[Isaiah] [5]:[13] Therefore my people will go into exile for lack of knowledge; their nobles will go hungry and their multitudes will be parched with thirst.
[Isaiah] [5]:[14] Therefore the grave has opened wide its throat and gaped with mouth beyond measure; down go the city's splendor and her multitude, her uproar and all who revel in her.
[Isaiah] [5]:[15] Humanity will be brought low, everyone humbled, and the eyes of the arrogant lowered.
[Isaiah] [5]:[16] But the LORD of Hosts will be exalted by his justice, and the holy God will show himself holy by his righteousness.
[Isaiah] [5]:[17] Then lambs will graze as in their own pasture, and among the ruins of the rich strangers will feed.
[Isaiah] [5]:[18] Woe to those who drag iniquity along with cords of falsehood and sin with cart ropes,
[Isaiah] [5]:[19] who say, "Let him hurry, let him speed his work along, so we may see it. Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come near and arrive, so we may know it."
[Isaiah] [5]:[20] Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who turn darkness into light and light into darkness, who make bitter sweet and sweet bitter.
[Isaiah] [5]:[21] Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight.
[Isaiah] [5]:[22] Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine and champions at mixing strong drink,
[Isaiah] [5]:[23] who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deny justice to the one who is in the right.
[Isaiah] [5]:[24] Therefore, as fire consumes stubble and flame devours dry grass, so their root will rot and their blossom blow away like dust; for they have rejected the law of the LORD of Hosts and spurned the word of the Holy One of Israel.
[Isaiah] [5]:[25] That is why the anger of the LORD burns against his people; he has raised his hand against them and struck them down. The mountains shook, and their corpses lay like refuse in the streets. Yet his anger is not turned away; his hand is still raised.
[Isaiah] [5]:[26] He lifts up a banner to the nations far away; he whistles for those at the ends of the earth. Here they come, swiftly and speedily!
[Isaiah] [5]:[27] Not one of them grows weary or stumbles; not one slumbers or sleeps. No belt is loosened at the waist, no sandal strap is broken.
[Isaiah] [5]:[28] Their arrows are sharpened, all their bows are strung; their horses' hooves are like flint, their chariot wheels like a whirlwind.
[Isaiah] [5]:[29] Their roar is like a lion's; they roar like young lions. They growl as they seize their prey and carry it off, and no one can rescue it.
[Isaiah] [5]:[30] On that day they will roar over it like the roaring of the sea. And if one looks at the land, there is only darkness and distress; even the light is darkened by clouds.
[Isaiah] [6]:[1] In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a high and lofty throne, and the train of his robe filled the temple.
[Isaiah] [6]:[2] Above him stood seraphim, each with six wings: with two they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
[Isaiah] [6]:[3] And they called out to one another: "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory."
[Isaiah] [6]:[4] At the sound of the voice that called, the doorposts of the thresholds shook, and the house was filled with smoke.
[Isaiah] [6]:[5] Then I said, "Woe to me! I am ruined! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people of unclean lips—and my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts!"
[Isaiah] [6]:[6] Then one of the seraphim flew to me, holding a glowing coal that he had taken from the altar with tongs.
[Isaiah] [6]:[7] He touched my mouth with it and said, "See, this has touched your lips; your guilt is taken away, and your sin is atoned for."
[Isaiah] [6]:[8] Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?" And I said, "Here I am. Send me!"
[Isaiah] [6]:[9] And he said, "Go and say to this people: 'Hear, but never understand; look, but never perceive.'
[Isaiah] [6]:[10] Make the heart of this people dull, their ears heavy, and their eyes blind—so that they cannot see with their eyes, or hear with their ears, or understand with their hearts, and so turn and be healed.
[Isaiah] [6]:[11] Then I said, "How long, Lord?" And he answered, "Until the cities lie in ruins with no one living in them, the houses are empty of people, and the land is left a desolate waste;
[Isaiah] [6]:[12] The LORD will drive the people far away, and great will be the abandonment in the midst of the land.
[Isaiah] [6]:[13] And though a tenth remains in it, it too will be burned again—like a terebinth or an oak, which leaves a stump when it is felled. That stump is a holy seed."
[Isaiah] [7]:[1] In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel marched up against Jerusalem to make war on it, but they could not prevail against it.
[Isaiah] [7]:[2] When word came to the house of David, "Aram has joined forces with Ephraim," the heart of the king and the heart of his people shook like the trees of the forest before the wind.
[Isaiah] [7]:[3] Then the LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-Jashub,* at the end of the aqueduct of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field,
[Isaiah] [7]:[4] and say to him: Be careful, keep calm, and do not be afraid. Do not lose heart over these two smoldering stubs of firewood—over the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.
[Isaiah] [7]:[5] Because Aram, together with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted evil against you, saying,
[Isaiah] [7]:[6] "Let us march against Judah, tear it apart, and divide it among ourselves, and set the son of Tabeel on its throne"—
[Isaiah] [7]:[7] this is what the Lord GOD says: It will not happen; it will not take place.
[Isaiah] [7]:[8] For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered beyond being a people.
[Isaiah] [7]:[9] The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in faith, you will not stand at all.
[Isaiah] [7]:[10] Again the LORD spoke to Ahaz:
[Isaiah] [7]:[11] "Ask the LORD your God for a sign—as deep as the realm of the dead or as high as the heavens."
[Isaiah] [7]:[12] But Ahaz said, "I will not ask; I will not put the LORD to the test."
[Isaiah] [7]:[13] Then Isaiah said, "Listen now, house of David! Is it not enough for you to wear out human patience? Must you weary my God as well?
[Isaiah] [7]:[14] Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: See, the virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and she will call him Immanuel.*
[Isaiah] [7]:[15] He will eat curds and honey by the time he knows enough to reject the wrong and choose the right.
[Isaiah] [7]:[16] For before the boy knows enough to reject the wrong and choose the right, the land of the two kings you dread will be laid waste.
[Isaiah] [7]:[17] The LORD will bring on you and on your people and on your father's house such days as have not come since Ephraim broke away from Judah—he will bring the king of Assyria.
[Isaiah] [7]:[18] On that day the LORD will whistle for the flies from the distant streams of Egypt and for the bees from the land of Assyria.
[Isaiah] [7]:[19] They will all come and settle in the steep ravines and in the clefts of the rocks, on all the thornbushes and at all the watering holes.
[Isaiah] [7]:[20] On that day the Lord will use a razor hired from beyond the River—the king of Assyria—to shave your head and the hair of your legs, and to take off your beard as well.
[Isaiah] [7]:[21] On that day a man will keep alive only a young cow and two sheep.
[Isaiah] [7]:[22] And because of the abundance of milk they give, he will have curds to eat. All who remain in the land will live on curds and honey.
[Isaiah] [7]:[23] On that day, every place where there were a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels of silver will be given over to briers and thorns.
[Isaiah] [7]:[24] Men will go there with bow and arrow, for the whole land will be covered with briers and thorns.
[Isaiah] [7]:[25] As for all the hills once cultivated with the hoe, you will no longer go there for fear of the briers and thorns; they will become places where cattle are turned loose and sheep run free.
[Isaiah] [8]:[1] The LORD said to me: Take a large tablet and write on it with an ordinary stylus: "Belonging to Maher-shalal-hash-baz."
[Isaiah] [8]:[2] And I took reliable witnesses for myself: Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.
[Isaiah] [8]:[3] Then I went to the prophetess, and she conceived and bore a son. And the LORD said to me: Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
[Isaiah] [8]:[4] For before the boy knows how to say "My father" or "My mother," the wealth of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria will be carried off before the king of Assyria.
[Isaiah] [8]:[5] The LORD spoke to me again, saying:
[Isaiah] [8]:[6] Because this people has rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah and has taken delight in Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
[Isaiah] [8]:[7] therefore the Lord is about to bring up against them the mighty, abundant waters of the River — the king of Assyria in all his glory. It will rise over all its channels and overflow all its banks.
[Isaiah] [8]:[8] It will sweep on into Judah, flooding and passing through, reaching up to the neck; and its outspread wings will cover the whole breadth of your land, O Immanuel.
[Isaiah] [8]:[9] Rage, you peoples, and be shattered! Listen, all you far corners of the earth! Arm yourselves and be shattered; arm yourselves and be shattered!
[Isaiah] [8]:[10] Devise your plan — it will be thwarted. Speak your word — it will not stand. For God is with us.
[Isaiah] [8]:[11] For thus the LORD spoke to me, his hand strong upon me, warning me not to walk in the way of this people:
[Isaiah] [8]:[12] Do not call conspiracy everything this people calls conspiracy; do not fear what they fear, and do not be terrified.
[Isaiah] [8]:[13] The LORD of hosts — him you shall regard as holy; he shall be your fear, he shall be your dread.
[Isaiah] [8]:[14] He will become a sanctuary, but also a stone that makes people stumble and a rock that trips them up — for both houses of Israel — a trap and a snare for the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
[Isaiah] [8]:[15] Many will stumble over them; they will fall and be broken, they will be snared and captured.
[Isaiah] [8]:[16] Bind up the testimony; seal the teaching among my disciples.
[Isaiah] [8]:[17] I will wait for the LORD, who hides his face from the house of Jacob; in him I will hope.
[Isaiah] [8]:[18] Here I am, and the children the LORD has given me — we are signs and portents in Israel from the LORD of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
[Isaiah] [8]:[19] And when they tell you to consult the mediums and the spiritists who chirp and mutter — should not a people consult its God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living?
[Isaiah] [8]:[20] To the teaching and to the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, there is no dawn for them.
[Isaiah] [8]:[21] They will pass through the land, hard-pressed and hungry; and when they are famished they will rage and curse their king and their god. They will turn their faces upward,
[Isaiah] [8]:[22] and they will look to the earth — but there is only distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish, and they will be thrust into thick darkness.
[Isaiah] [8]:[23] But there will be no gloom for the land that was in anguish. In the past he humbled the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the future he will bring glory to the way of the sea, the land beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
[Isaiah] [9]:[1] The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; on those who lived in a land of deep shadow, light has dawned.
[Isaiah] [9]:[2] You have multiplied the nation; you have made its joy great. They rejoice before you as people rejoice at harvest, as they exult when dividing the spoil.
[Isaiah] [9]:[3] For the yoke that burdened them, the bar across their shoulders, the rod of their oppressor—you have shattered them, as on the day of Midian.
[Isaiah] [9]:[4] For every boot that tramped in the tumult, every cloak rolled in blood, will be burned, fuel for the fire.
[Isaiah] [9]:[5] For to us a child is born, to us a son is given; and the government will rest on his shoulders. And his name shall be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
[Isaiah] [9]:[6] Of the increase of his government and of peace there will be no end. He will reign on David's throne and over his kingdom, establishing and upholding it with justice and righteousness from now on and forever. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will accomplish this.
[Isaiah] [9]:[7] The Lord has sent a word against Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel.
[Isaiah] [9]:[8] All the people will know it—Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria—who say in pride and arrogance of heart:
[Isaiah] [9]:[9] "The bricks have fallen, but we will rebuild with dressed stone; the sycamores have been felled, but we will put cedars in their place."
[Isaiah] [9]:[10] So the LORD raised up against him the adversaries of Rezin and stirred up his enemies:
[Isaiah] [9]:[11] Aram from the east and the Philistines from the west, and they devoured Israel with open mouths. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
[Isaiah] [9]:[12] Still the people did not return to him who struck them, and they did not seek the LORD of hosts.
[Isaiah] [9]:[13] So the LORD cut off from Israel both head and tail, both palm branch and reed, in a single day.
[Isaiah] [9]:[14] The elder and the man of rank are the head; the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
[Isaiah] [9]:[15] Those who guide this people have led them astray, and those they guide are swallowed up.
[Isaiah] [9]:[16] Therefore the Lord takes no delight in their young men, and he has no compassion on their orphans and widows; for everyone is godless and does evil, and every mouth speaks folly. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
[Isaiah] [9]:[17] For wickedness burns like a fire; it consumes briers and thorns. It sets the thickets of the forest ablaze, and they roll upward in a column of smoke.
[Isaiah] [9]:[18] By the fury of the LORD of hosts the land is scorched, and the people have become fuel for the fire; no one spares his brother.
[Isaiah] [9]:[19] They tear at what is on the right, but remain hungry; they devour what is on the left, but are not satisfied. Each one devours the flesh of his own arm:
[Isaiah] [9]:[20] Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they turn against Judah. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
[Isaiah] [10]:[1] Woe to those who enact unjust decrees, to the scribes who keep writing oppression,
[Isaiah] [10]:[2] to turn the needy away from justice and rob the poor of my people of their rights, making widows their plunder and preying on the fatherless.
[Isaiah] [10]:[3] What will you do on the day of reckoning, when the storm comes from far away? To whom will you flee for help, and where will you leave your wealth?
[Isaiah] [10]:[4] Nothing remains but to crouch among the captives or fall among the slain. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
[Isaiah] [10]:[5] Woe to Assyria, the rod of my anger — the club in their hand is my fury!
[Isaiah] [10]:[6] I send him against a godless nation; I charge him against the people of my wrath, to seize spoil and carry off plunder, to trample them down like mud in the streets.
[Isaiah] [10]:[7] But this is not what he intends; this is not what his heart plans. His heart is set on destruction, on cutting off nations — and not a few.
[Isaiah] [10]:[8] For he says, "Are not my commanders all kings?
[Isaiah] [10]:[9] Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?
[Isaiah] [10]:[10] As my hand reached the kingdoms of idols, whose images outnumbered those of Jerusalem and Samaria —
[Isaiah] [10]:[11] shall I not do to Jerusalem and her images what I have done to Samaria and her idols?"
[Isaiah] [10]:[12] When the Lord has finished all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, he will punish the fruit of the arrogant heart of the king of Assyria and the haughty pride of his eyes.
[Isaiah] [10]:[13] For he says: "By the strength of my own hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I have understanding. I removed the boundaries of peoples and plundered their treasures; like a bull I brought down those who sat enthroned.
[Isaiah] [10]:[14] My hand found the wealth of the peoples as one finds a nest; as one gathers abandoned eggs, I gathered all the earth. Not a wing fluttered, not a beak opened to chirp."
[Isaiah] [10]:[15] Does the axe boast over the one who swings it, or the saw exalt itself above the one who wields it? As if a rod could brandish the one who lifts it, or a club could lift the one who is not wood!
[Isaiah] [10]:[16] Therefore the Lord, the LORD of hosts, will send a wasting sickness among his stout warriors, and beneath his glory a burning will be kindled, like the burning of fire.
[Isaiah] [10]:[17] The Light of Israel will become a fire, and his Holy One a flame; in a single day it will burn and devour his thorns and briers.
[Isaiah] [10]:[18] The glory of his forest and his fruitful land it will consume, soul and body alike, and it will be as when a sick man wastes away.
[Isaiah] [10]:[19] The remaining trees of his forest will be so few that a child could write them down.
[Isaiah] [10]:[20] On that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob will no longer lean on the one who struck them, but will lean in truth on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
[Isaiah] [10]:[21] A remnant will return, the remnant of Jacob, to the Mighty God.
[Isaiah] [10]:[22] For though your people Israel be like the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them will return. Destruction is decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
[Isaiah] [10]:[23] For the Lord, the LORD of hosts, will carry out the destruction that is decreed in the midst of all the earth.
[Isaiah] [10]:[24] Therefore the Lord, the LORD of hosts, says this: "My people who dwell in Zion, do not be afraid of Assyria, though he strikes you with the rod and lifts up his club against you as Egypt did.
[Isaiah] [10]:[25] For in a very little while my fury will be spent, and my anger will turn to their destruction.
[Isaiah] [10]:[26] The LORD of hosts will raise a whip against him, as when he struck Midian at the rock of Oreb; he will lift his staff over the sea as he did in Egypt.
[Isaiah] [10]:[27] On that day his burden will be lifted from your shoulder and his yoke from your neck, and the yoke will be broken because of the fat.^[The Hebrew of this last clause is obscure; literally "because of fatness" — probably the neck grown too strong and full for the yoke.]
[Isaiah] [10]:[28] He comes against Aiath, passes through Migron, stores his equipment at Michmash.
[Isaiah] [10]:[29] They cross the pass: "We will camp for the night at Geba." Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul has fled.
[Isaiah] [10]:[30] Cry aloud, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Poor Anathoth!
[Isaiah] [10]:[31] Madmenah is in flight; the people of Gebim take cover.
[Isaiah] [10]:[32] This very day he will halt at Nob; he shakes his fist at the mount of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
[Isaiah] [10]:[33] Look: the Lord, the LORD of hosts, will lop off the branches with terrifying power. The tallest trees will be cut down, and the lofty ones brought low.
[Isaiah] [10]:[34] He will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One.
[Isaiah] [11]:[1] A shoot will come up from the stump of Jesse, and from his roots a branch will bear fruit.
[Isaiah] [11]:[2] The Spirit of the LORD will rest on him—the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
[Isaiah] [11]:[3] His delight will be in the fear of the LORD. He will not judge by what his eyes see, nor decide by what his ears hear.
[Isaiah] [11]:[4] With righteousness he will judge the poor, and with justice he will decide for the lowly of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he will slay the wicked.
[Isaiah] [11]:[5] Righteousness will be the belt around his waist, and faithfulness the sash around his hips.
[Isaiah] [11]:[6] The wolf will live with the lamb, the leopard will lie down with the young goat; the calf and the young lion and the fatling together, and a little child will lead them.
[Isaiah] [11]:[7] The cow and the bear will graze, their young will lie down together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox.
[Isaiah] [11]:[8] The nursing infant will play near the cobra's hole, and the weaned child will reach his hand over the viper's nest.
[Isaiah] [11]:[9] They will neither harm nor destroy on all my holy mountain, for the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
[Isaiah] [11]:[10] On that day the root of Jesse will stand as a banner for the peoples; the nations will seek him, and his resting place will be glorious.
[Isaiah] [11]:[11] On that day the Lord will reach out his hand a second time to reclaim the remnant of his people—those left in Assyria and Egypt, in Pathros and Cush, in Elam and Shinar, in Hamath and the coastlands of the sea.
[Isaiah] [11]:[12] He will raise a banner for the nations and gather the outcasts of Israel; he will assemble the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
[Isaiah] [11]:[13] Ephraim's jealousy will vanish, and Judah's enemies will be cut off. Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not harass Ephraim.
[Isaiah] [11]:[14] They will swoop down on the slopes of Philistia to the west; together they will plunder the people of the east. They will lay hands on Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites will be subject to them.
[Isaiah] [11]:[15] The LORD will dry up the gulf of the Egyptian sea; with a scorching wind he will sweep his hand over the Euphrates. He will break it into seven streams, so that people can cross over in sandals.
[Isaiah] [11]:[16] There will be a highway for the remnant of his people left in Assyria, as there was for Israel on the day they came up from the land of Egypt.
[Isaiah] [12]:[1] On that day you will say: "I thank you, LORD. Though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away, and you have comforted me.
[Isaiah] [12]:[2] See, God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid. For the LORD, the LORD himself, is my strength and my song; he has become my salvation."
[Isaiah] [12]:[3] With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation.
[Isaiah] [12]:[4] On that day you will say: "Give thanks to the LORD, call on his name; make known among the peoples what he has done, proclaim that his name is exalted.
[Isaiah] [12]:[5] Sing to the LORD, for he has done glorious things; let this be known in all the earth.
[Isaiah] [12]:[6] Shout aloud and sing for joy, you who dwell in Zion, for the Holy One of Israel is great in your midst."
[Isaiah] [13]:[1] An oracle concerning Babylon, which Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
[Isaiah] [13]:[2] Raise a banner on a bare mountain, lift your voice to them, wave them on to enter the gates of the nobles.
[Isaiah] [13]:[3] I myself have given the command; I have summoned my consecrated ones, my warriors, to carry out my anger—those who exult in my triumph.
[Isaiah] [13]:[4] Listen: an uproar on the mountains, like that of a vast multitude! Listen: the roar of kingdoms, of nations gathering! The LORD of hosts is mustering an army for battle.
[Isaiah] [13]:[5] They come from a distant land, from the ends of the heavens—the LORD and the weapons of his wrath—to destroy the whole earth.
[Isaiah] [13]:[6] Wail, for the day of the LORD is near; it comes like devastation from the Almighty.
[Isaiah] [13]:[7] Therefore every hand goes limp, and every human heart melts away.
[Isaiah] [13]:[8] They are terrified; pangs and pains seize them, they writhe like a woman in labor. They stare at one another aghast, their faces aflame.
[Isaiah] [13]:[9] See, the day of the LORD is coming—cruel, with fury and burning anger—to make the earth a desolation and to destroy the sinners within it.
[Isaiah] [13]:[10] The stars of heaven and their constellations will not give their light. The rising sun will be darkened, and the moon will not shed its light.
[Isaiah] [13]:[11] I will punish the world for its evil, the wicked for their guilt. I will put an end to the arrogance of the proud and humble the pride of tyrants.
[Isaiah] [13]:[12] I will make people scarcer than fine gold, humankind rarer than the gold of Ophir.
[Isaiah] [13]:[13] Therefore I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth will be shaken from its place at the fury of the LORD of hosts, on the day of his burning anger.
[Isaiah] [13]:[14] Like a hunted gazelle, like sheep with no one to gather them, each will turn back to his own people, each will flee to his own land.
[Isaiah] [13]:[15] Whoever is found will be run through, and whoever is caught will fall by the sword.
[Isaiah] [13]:[16] Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses will be plundered and their wives violated.
[Isaiah] [13]:[17] See, I am stirring up against them the Medes, who have no regard for silver and take no delight in gold.
[Isaiah] [13]:[18] Their bows will strike down the young men; they will show no mercy to the fruit of the womb, and their eyes will not spare the children.
[Isaiah] [13]:[19] Babylon, the jewel of kingdoms, the glory and pride of the Chaldeans, will be overthrown by God like Sodom and Gomorrah.
[Isaiah] [13]:[20] It will never be inhabited again or lived in through all generations. No Arab will pitch his tent there, no shepherd will let his flock rest there.
[Isaiah] [13]:[21] But desert creatures will lie down there, and its houses will be full of howling beasts; there ostriches will dwell, and there wild goats will leap about.
[Isaiah] [13]:[22] Hyenas will cry out in its strongholds, jackals in its luxurious palaces. Its time is close at hand, and its days will not be prolonged.
[Isaiah] [14]:[1] For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob; once again he will choose Israel and settle them in their own land. Foreigners will join them and attach themselves to the house of Jacob.
[Isaiah] [14]:[2] Nations will take them and bring them to their own place, and the house of Israel will possess them in the LORD's land as male and female servants. They will take their captors captive and rule over their oppressors.
[Isaiah] [14]:[3] On the day the LORD gives you rest from your pain and turmoil, and from the harsh labor forced upon you,
[Isaiah] [14]:[4] you will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon: How the oppressor has ceased! How his fury has ended!
[Isaiah] [14]:[5] The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of rulers,
[Isaiah] [14]:[6] which struck the peoples in wrath with unceasing blows, which subdued nations in anger with relentless persecution.
[Isaiah] [14]:[7] The whole earth is at rest and quiet; all break out in singing.
[Isaiah] [14]:[8] Even the cypresses rejoice over you, and the cedars of Lebanon: "Now that you lie fallen, no woodsman comes up against us."
[Isaiah] [14]:[9] The realm of the dead below stirs to meet you at your coming; it rouses the shades to greet you, all who were leaders of the earth. It makes all who were kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
[Isaiah] [14]:[10] They all speak up and say to you: "So you too have become weak as we are; you have become like us."
[Isaiah] [14]:[11] Your pomp has been brought down to the realm of the dead, along with the music of your harps. Maggots are spread out as your bed beneath you, and worms are your covering.
[Isaiah] [14]:[12] How you have fallen from heaven, O shining one, son of the dawn! You have been cut down to the earth, you who laid the nations low.
[Isaiah] [14]:[13] You said in your heart: "I will ascend to the heavens; above the stars of God I will raise my throne. I will sit enthroned on the mount of assembly, on the utmost heights of the north.
[Isaiah] [14]:[14] I will ascend above the tops of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High."
[Isaiah] [14]:[15] But you will be brought down to the realm of the dead, to the depths of the pit.
[Isaiah] [14]:[16] Those who see you stare at you; they ponder your fate: "Is this the man who shook the earth and made kingdoms tremble,
[Isaiah] [14]:[17] who made the world a wilderness and tore down its cities, who would not let his captives go home?"
[Isaiah] [14]:[18] All the kings of the nations lie in glory, each in his own tomb.
[Isaiah] [14]:[19] But you are cast out of your grave like a rejected branch, covered with the slain, with those pierced by the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit—like a trampled corpse.
[Isaiah] [14]:[20] You will not be joined with them in burial, for you destroyed your land and killed your people. Let the offspring of evildoers never be named again.
[Isaiah] [14]:[21] Prepare a place to slaughter his sons for the guilt of their fathers, so they may not rise to inherit the earth and cover the face of the world with cities.
[Isaiah] [14]:[22] "I will rise up against them," declares the LORD of hosts. "I will cut off from Babylon her name and her remnant, her offspring and her descendants," declares the LORD.
[Isaiah] [14]:[23] "I will make her a possession of owls and a swampland; I will sweep her away with the broom of destruction," declares the LORD of hosts.
[Isaiah] [14]:[24] The LORD of hosts has sworn: "Surely, as I have planned, so it shall be; as I have purposed, so it shall stand:
[Isaiah] [14]:[25] I will break Assyria in my land; on my mountains I will trample him down. His yoke will be lifted from my people, and his burden removed from their shoulders."
[Isaiah] [14]:[26] This is the plan determined for the whole earth; this is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
[Isaiah] [14]:[27] For the LORD of hosts has purposed, and who can thwart him? His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?
[Isaiah] [14]:[28] In the year King Ahaz died, this oracle came:
[Isaiah] [14]:[29] Do not rejoice, all you Philistines, that the rod that struck you is broken; for from the root of the snake will come a viper, and its fruit will be a darting, fiery serpent.
[Isaiah] [14]:[30] The poorest of the poor will find pasture, and the needy will lie down in safety. But your root I will kill with famine, and it will slay your remnant.
[Isaiah] [14]:[31] Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Melt away, all you Philistines! For smoke is coming from the north, and no one straggles from the ranks.
[Isaiah] [14]:[32] What answer will be given to the envoys of that nation? "The LORD has established Zion, and in her the afflicted of his people find refuge."
[Isaiah] [15]:[1] An oracle concerning Moab: In one night Ar of Moab is laid waste and left in ruins; in one night Kir of Moab is laid waste and left in ruins.
[Isaiah] [15]:[2] Bayith and Dibon have gone up to the high places to weep. Over Nebo and over Medeba Moab wails. Every head is shaved, every beard cut off.
[Isaiah] [15]:[3] In the streets they are wrapped in sackcloth; on the rooftops and in the squares everyone wails and melts into tears.
[Isaiah] [15]:[4] Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voices are heard as far as Jahaz. So the armed men of Moab cry aloud, and their souls tremble within them.
[Isaiah] [15]:[5] My heart cries out for Moab; her fugitives flee as far as Zoar, as far as Eglath-shelishiyah. Up the ascent of Luhith they climb, weeping as they go; on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of ruin.
[Isaiah] [15]:[6] For the waters of Nimrim will become a wasteland, since the grass is withered, the new growth is gone, and nothing green is left.
[Isaiah] [15]:[7] So the wealth they have gathered, and all they have stored up, they carry away over the Ravine of the Poplars.
[Isaiah] [15]:[8] For the cry has gone all around the border of Moab; her wailing reaches Eglaim, her wailing reaches Beer-elim.
[Isaiah] [15]:[9] The waters of Dimon are full of blood, and still I will bring more upon Dimon: a lion against the survivors of Moab, against those who remain in the land.
[Isaiah] [16]:[1] Send lambs to the ruler of the land, from Sela through the wilderness to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.
[Isaiah] [16]:[2] Like fluttering birds driven from the nest, so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon.
[Isaiah] [16]:[3] "Give counsel, render judgment; make your shadow like night at high noon. Hide the outcasts; do not betray the fugitive.
[Isaiah] [16]:[4] Let my outcasts dwell among you, Moab; be a shelter for them from the destroyer. When the oppressor is no more, when destruction has ceased and the one who tramples has vanished from the land,
[Isaiah] [16]:[5] then a throne will be established in steadfast love, and on it will sit in faithfulness, in the tent of David, one who judges and seeks justice and is swift to do righteousness."
[Isaiah] [16]:[6] We have heard of the pride of Moab—how great it is—of his arrogance, his pride, and his fury; but his boasting is empty.
[Isaiah] [16]:[7] Therefore Moab wails for Moab; all of them wail. For the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth they moan, utterly stricken.
[Isaiah] [16]:[8] For the fields of Heshbon have withered, and the vine of Sibmah. The lords of the nations have trampled down its choice branches, which reached as far as Jazer and strayed into the wilderness; its shoots spread abroad and crossed over the sea.
[Isaiah] [16]:[9] Therefore I weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah; I drench you with my tears, O Heshbon and Elealeh, for over your summer fruit and your harvest the shout of the enemy has fallen.
[Isaiah] [16]:[10] Joy and gladness are taken away from the orchard; no one sings or shouts in the vineyards. No one treads out wine in the presses; I have silenced the shouting.
[Isaiah] [16]:[11] Therefore my inmost parts moan like a harp for Moab, and my heart for Kir-heres.
[Isaiah] [16]:[12] And when Moab appears, when he wears himself out on the high place and comes to his sanctuary to pray, it will do him no good.
[Isaiah] [16]:[13] This is the word that the LORD spoke concerning Moab in time past.
[Isaiah] [16]:[14] But now the LORD has spoken, saying: "Within three years, as a hired worker counts them, the glory of Moab will be brought into contempt, despite all its vast multitude; and the remnant will be very small and feeble."
[Isaiah] [17]:[1] An oracle concerning Damascus: Look, Damascus will cease to be a city; it will become a heap of ruins.
[Isaiah] [17]:[2] The cities of Aroer are abandoned. They will be left to the flocks, which will lie down there with no one to frighten them.
[Isaiah] [17]:[3] The fortress will vanish from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus. What is left of Aram will fare like the glory of the Israelites, declares the LORD of hosts.
[Isaiah] [17]:[4] On that day the glory of Jacob will fade, and the fat of his body will waste away.
[Isaiah] [17]:[5] It will be as when a reaper gathers the standing grain and his arm harvests the ears; it will be as when someone gleans ears of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.
[Isaiah] [17]:[6] Yet gleanings will be left in it, as when an olive tree is beaten: two or three olives at the very top, four or five on the fruitful branches, declares the LORD, the God of Israel.
[Isaiah] [17]:[7] On that day people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will turn to the Holy One of Israel.
[Isaiah] [17]:[8] They will no longer look to the altars, the work of their own hands, nor gaze at what their fingers have made, the Asherah poles and the incense altars.
[Isaiah] [17]:[9] On that day their fortified cities will be like the abandoned places of the thicket and the topmost bough, left empty before the Israelites; and all will be desolation.
[Isaiah] [17]:[10] For you have forgotten the God of your salvation; you have not remembered the Rock, your refuge. That is why you plant your lovely gardens and set out cuttings from a foreign vine.
[Isaiah] [17]:[11] The day you plant them, you make them grow; the morning you sow, you bring them into bloom — but the harvest vanishes on the day of sickness and incurable pain.
[Isaiah] [17]:[12] Ah, the din of many peoples — they rage like the raging of the seas! The uproar of nations — they roar like the roar of mighty waters!
[Isaiah] [17]:[13] The nations roar like the roar of great waters, but he rebukes them, and they flee far away, driven like chaff on the mountains before the wind, like whirling dust before a gale.
[Isaiah] [17]:[14] At evening, sudden terror! Before morning, they are gone. This is the portion of those who plunder us, the lot of those who rob us.
[Isaiah] [18]:[1] Woe to the land of whirring wings, beyond the rivers of Cush,
[Isaiah] [18]:[2] which sends its envoys by sea, in vessels of papyrus over the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth-skinned, to a people feared far and wide, a nation mighty and conquering, whose land the rivers divide.
[Isaiah] [18]:[3] All you inhabitants of the world, all who dwell on the earth: when a banner is raised on the mountains, look; when the trumpet sounds, listen.
[Isaiah] [18]:[4] For this is what the LORD said to me: I will stay quiet and watch from my dwelling place, like shimmering heat in the blaze of noon, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
[Isaiah] [18]:[5] For before the harvest, when the blossom is over and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will cut off the shoots with pruning knives and strip away the spreading branches.
[Isaiah] [18]:[6] They will all be left to the mountain birds of prey and to the wild beasts of the land; the birds of prey will summer on them, and all the wild beasts will winter on them.
[Isaiah] [18]:[7] At that time gifts will be brought to the LORD of hosts by a people tall and smooth-skinned, from a people feared far and wide, a nation mighty and conquering, whose land the rivers divide — brought to the place of the name of the LORD of hosts, to Mount Zion.
[Isaiah] [19]:[1] An oracle concerning Egypt: See, the LORD rides on a swift cloud and comes to Egypt. The idols of Egypt tremble before him, and the heart of Egypt melts within it.
[Isaiah] [19]:[2] I will stir up Egypt against Egypt; they will fight, brother against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
[Isaiah] [19]:[3] Egypt's spirit will drain away within it, and I will swallow up its counsel. They will turn to idols and charmers, to mediums and spiritists.
[Isaiah] [19]:[4] I will hand Egypt over to a cruel master, and a fierce king will rule over them, declares the Lord, the LORD of hosts.
[Isaiah] [19]:[5] The waters of the sea will fail, and the river will dry up and be parched.
[Isaiah] [19]:[6] The canals will stink; the streams of Egypt will dwindle and dry up. Reed and rush will wither away.
[Isaiah] [19]:[7] The meadows along the Nile, at the very mouth of the Nile, and every sown field beside it will dry up, blow away, and be no more.
[Isaiah] [19]:[8] The fishermen will groan and mourn, all who cast a hook into the Nile; those who spread nets on the water will waste away.
[Isaiah] [19]:[9] The workers in combed flax will be dismayed, and the weavers of white cloth.
[Isaiah] [19]:[10] Her pillars will be crushed, and all who work for wages will be sick at heart.
[Isaiah] [19]:[11] The officials of Zoan are nothing but fools; Pharaoh's wise counselors give senseless advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am a son of the wise, a son of ancient kings"?
[Isaiah] [19]:[12] Where, then, are your wise men? Let them tell you and make known what the LORD of hosts has planned against Egypt.
[Isaiah] [19]:[13] The officials of Zoan have become fools, the officials of Memphis are deceived; the cornerstones of her tribes have led Egypt astray.
[Isaiah] [19]:[14] The LORD has poured into her a spirit of confusion; they make Egypt stagger in all she does, like a drunkard staggering in his vomit.
[Isaiah] [19]:[15] There will be nothing Egypt can do—neither head nor tail, neither palm branch nor reed.
[Isaiah] [19]:[16] On that day the Egyptians will be like women, trembling with fear before the raised hand of the LORD of hosts, which he lifts against them.
[Isaiah] [19]:[17] And the land of Judah will bring terror to Egypt; everyone who hears its name will be afraid, because of what the LORD of hosts has planned against them.
[Isaiah] [19]:[18] On that day five cities in the land of Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the LORD of hosts. One of them will be called the City of Destruction.
[Isaiah] [19]:[19] On that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the heart of Egypt, and a pillar to the LORD at her border.
[Isaiah] [19]:[20] It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of their oppressors, he will send them a savior and defender, and he will rescue them.
[Isaiah] [19]:[21] So the LORD will make himself known to Egypt, and on that day the Egyptians will know the LORD. They will worship with sacrifice and offering; they will make vows to the LORD and fulfill them.
[Isaiah] [19]:[22] The LORD will strike Egypt—striking and healing. They will turn to the LORD, and he will listen to their pleas and heal them.
[Isaiah] [19]:[23] On that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will go to Egypt and the Egyptians to Assyria, and the Egyptians and Assyrians will worship together.
[Isaiah] [19]:[24] On that day Israel will be the third with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the earth,
[Isaiah] [19]:[25] whom the LORD of hosts has blessed, saying, "Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance."
[Isaiah] [20]:[1] In the year that the commander in chief came to Ashdod, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, he fought against Ashdod and captured it.[^1] [^1]: "Commander in chief" renders an Assyrian military title (Tartan), the second-in-command of the army.
[Isaiah] [20]:[2] At that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz: "Go, take off the sackcloth from your waist and remove the sandals from your feet." And he did so, going stripped and barefoot.
[Isaiah] [20]:[3] Then the LORD said, "Just as my servant Isaiah has gone stripped and barefoot for three years as a sign and a portent against Egypt and Cush,
[Isaiah] [20]:[4] so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old alike, stripped and barefoot, with buttocks bared—the shame of Egypt.
[Isaiah] [20]:[5] Then they will be dismayed and put to shame because of Cush, their hope, and Egypt, their boast.
[Isaiah] [20]:[6] And in that day the inhabitants of this coastland will say, "Look what has become of our hope, the one we fled to for help and rescue from the king of Assyria! How then can we escape?"
[Isaiah] [21]:[1] An oracle concerning the wilderness by the sea: Like storm winds sweeping through the Negev, it comes from the desert, from a land of terror.
[Isaiah] [21]:[2] A harsh vision has been told to me: the traitor betrays, the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam! Lay siege, Media! I have put an end to all her groaning.
[Isaiah] [21]:[3] Therefore my body is racked with anguish; pangs have seized me, like the pangs of a woman in labor. I am doubled over by what I hear; I am terrified by what I see.
[Isaiah] [21]:[4] My heart staggers, horror overwhelms me; the twilight I longed for has become my dread.
[Isaiah] [21]:[5] Set the table! Post the lookout! Eat, drink! Get up, you officers! Oil the shields!
[Isaiah] [21]:[6] For this is what the Lord said to me: "Go, post a watchman, and let him report what he sees.
[Isaiah] [21]:[7] When he sees a chariot, a pair of horsemen, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, let him listen closely, very closely."
[Isaiah] [21]:[8] Then the lookout called out like a lion: "On the watchtower, my Lord, I stand all day long, and at my post I keep guard through every night.
[Isaiah] [21]:[9] Look—here comes a chariot of men, a pair of horsemen!" And he answered and said: "Fallen, fallen is Babylon! All the images of her gods lie shattered on the ground."
[Isaiah] [21]:[10] O my threshed people, my child of the threshing floor, what I have heard from the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, I have declared to you.
[Isaiah] [21]:[11] An oracle concerning Dumah: Someone calls to me from Seir, "Watchman, what is left of the night? Watchman, what is left of the night?"
[Isaiah] [21]:[12] The watchman answers, "Morning is coming, and night as well. If you must inquire, then inquire; come back again."
[Isaiah] [21]:[13] An oracle concerning Arabia: In the thickets of Arabia you must camp for the night, you caravans of Dedan.
[Isaiah] [21]:[14] Bring water to the thirsty, you who live in the land of Tema; meet the fugitive with bread.
[Isaiah] [21]:[15] For they flee from the swords—from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, from the weight of battle.
[Isaiah] [21]:[16] For this is what the Lord said to me: "Within one year, as a hired worker counts the years, all the splendor of Kedar will come to an end.
[Isaiah] [21]:[17] And the remnant of the bowmen, the warriors of the sons of Kedar, will be few." For the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
[Isaiah] [22]:[1] An oracle concerning the Valley of Vision: What is the matter with you now, that you have all gone up to the rooftops,
[Isaiah] [22]:[2] you town full of uproar, city of tumult, exultant town? Your slain were not slain by the sword, nor did they die in battle.
[Isaiah] [22]:[3] All your commanders fled together; without a bow they were captured. All who were found in you were taken prisoner together, though they had fled far away.
[Isaiah] [22]:[4] Therefore I said: Look away from me; let me weep bitterly. Do not press to comfort me over the ruin of the daughter of my people.
[Isaiah] [22]:[5] For the Lord GOD of hosts has a day of panic, of trampling and confusion in the Valley of Vision—walls broken down and a cry for help echoing to the mountain.
[Isaiah] [22]:[6] Elam took up the quiver with chariots and horsemen, and Kir uncovered the shield.
[Isaiah] [22]:[7] Your choicest valleys were filled with chariots, and the horsemen took their stand at the gate.
[Isaiah] [22]:[8] He stripped away the defenses of Judah. On that day you looked to the weapons in the House of the Forest.
[Isaiah] [22]:[9] You saw that the breaches in the city of David were many, and you collected the water of the lower pool.
[Isaiah] [22]:[10] You counted the houses of Jerusalem, and you tore houses down to fortify the wall.
[Isaiah] [22]:[11] You built a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But you did not look to him who made it, nor did you see the one who shaped it long ago.
[Isaiah] [22]:[12] On that day the Lord GOD of hosts called you to weeping and mourning, to shaving your heads and putting on sackcloth.
[Isaiah] [22]:[13] But look—joy and celebration! Killing cattle, slaughtering sheep, eating meat and drinking wine: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"
[Isaiah] [22]:[14] The LORD of hosts has revealed this in my hearing: "Surely this sin will not be atoned for you until you die," says the Lord GOD of hosts.
[Isaiah] [22]:[15] Thus says the Lord GOD of hosts: Go, present yourself to this steward, to Shebna, who is over the household:
[Isaiah] [22]:[16] What are you doing here, and who gave you the right, that you have cut out a tomb for yourself here—carving your grave on the height, chiseling a resting place for yourself in the rock?
[Isaiah] [22]:[17] Look, the LORD is about to hurl you away violently, strong man; he will grip you tight,
[Isaiah] [22]:[18] wind you up like a ball and fling you into a vast land. There you will die, and there your splendid chariots will lie—you disgrace to your master's house!
[Isaiah] [22]:[19] I will thrust you from your office, and you will be pulled down from your post.
[Isaiah] [22]:[20] On that day I will summon my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
[Isaiah] [22]:[21] I will clothe him with your robe and fasten your sash around him. I will hand your authority over to him, and he will be a father to those who live in Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
[Isaiah] [22]:[22] I will place the key of the house of David on his shoulder; what he opens no one will shut, and what he shuts no one will open.
[Isaiah] [22]:[23] I will drive him in like a peg in a firm place, and he will become a throne of honor for his father's house.
[Isaiah] [22]:[24] On him they will hang all the glory of his father's house—the offspring and the offshoots, every small vessel, from the bowls to all the jars.
[Isaiah] [22]:[25] On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, the peg driven into the firm place will give way; it will be cut down and fall, and the load hanging on it will be destroyed. For the LORD has spoken.
[Isaiah] [23]:[1] An oracle concerning Tyre: Wail, you ships of Tarshish, for Tyre is laid waste, without house, without harbor. From the land of Cyprus the word came to them.
[Isaiah] [23]:[2] Be silent, you who live on the coast—you whom the merchants of Sidon, crossing the sea, once filled.
[Isaiah] [23]:[3] On the great waters came the grain of Shihor, the harvest of the Nile was her revenue, and she became the marketplace of the nations.
[Isaiah] [23]:[4] Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the fortress of the sea, saying: "I have never been in labor or given birth; I have reared no young men, brought up no young women."
[Isaiah] [23]:[5] When the report reaches Egypt, they will writhe at the news of Tyre.
[Isaiah] [23]:[6] Cross over to Tarshish; wail, you who live on the coast.
[Isaiah] [23]:[7] Is this your jubilant city, whose origin is from ancient days, whose feet carried her to settle in far-off lands?
[Isaiah] [23]:[8] Who planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose merchants were princes, whose traders were the honored of the earth?
[Isaiah] [23]:[9] The LORD of hosts planned it, to defile the pride of all splendor, to humble all who are honored on the earth.

[Isaiah] [23]:[11] He has stretched out his hand over the sea; he has made kingdoms tremble. The LORD has given the command concerning Canaan, to destroy her strongholds.
[Isaiah] [23]:[12] He said, "You will revel no more, violated virgin daughter of Sidon. Rise, cross over to Cyprus—even there you will find no rest."
[Isaiah] [23]:[13] Look at the land of the Chaldeans—that people who came to nothing! Assyria made it a place for desert creatures; they raised siege towers against it, stripped its palaces bare, and left it a heap of ruins.
[Isaiah] [23]:[14] Wail, you ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is destroyed.
[Isaiah] [23]:[15] In that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the span of a single king's life. But at the end of seventy years it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:
[Isaiah] [23]:[16] "Take up a harp, walk through the city, forgotten prostitute; play skillfully, sing song after song, so that you may be remembered."
[Isaiah] [23]:[17] At the end of seventy years the LORD will turn his attention to Tyre. She will return to her hire and prostitute herself with all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.
[Isaiah] [23]:[18] Yet her profit and her hire will be set apart as holy to the LORD. It will not be stored up or hoarded; her earnings will go to those who dwell before the LORD, for abundant food and fine clothing.

[Isaiah] [24]:[3] The earth will be utterly laid waste, utterly plundered, for the LORD has spoken this word.
[Isaiah] [24]:[4] The earth mourns and withers; the world languishes and fades; the exalted of the earth's people languish.

[Isaiah] [24]:[10] The city of chaos lies shattered; every house is shut, no one can enter.

[Isaiah] [24]:[12] Desolation is all that is left in the city; the gate is battered into ruins.

[Isaiah] [24]:[17] Terror, pit, and snare are upon you, you who live on the earth!

[Isaiah] [24]:[19] The earth is utterly broken, the earth is split apart, the earth totters and reels.
[Isaiah] [24]:[20] The earth staggers like a drunkard, it sways like a hut. Its rebellion weighs heavy upon it; it falls, never to rise again.
