[Isaiah] [28]:[12] he who once said to them, "This is the resting place; give rest to the weary. This is the place of repose." But they would not listen.
[Isaiah] [28]:[13] So the word of the LORD will be to them: order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line, a little here, a little there — so that they will go and stumble backward, be broken, ensnared, and captured.
[Isaiah] [28]:[14] Therefore hear the word of the LORD, you scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem.
[Isaiah] [28]:[15] You say, "We have made a covenant with death; with the grave we have an agreement. When the raging flood sweeps by, it will not touch us, for we have made falsehood our refuge and taken shelter in a lie."
[Isaiah] [28]:[16] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: See, I am laying in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone for a sure foundation. Whoever believes will not be shaken.
[Isaiah] [28]:[17] I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb line. Hail will sweep away your refuge of lies, and water will flood your hiding place.
[Isaiah] [28]:[18] Your covenant with death will be annulled; your agreement with the grave will not stand. When the raging flood sweeps by, it will beat you down.
[Isaiah] [28]:[19] As often as it passes through, it will carry you off; morning after morning it will pass through, by day and by night. And the understanding of this message will bring nothing but terror.
[Isaiah] [28]:[20] For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too narrow to wrap yourself in.
[Isaiah] [28]:[21] The LORD will rise up as he did at Mount Perazim; he will rouse himself as he did in the Valley of Gibeon — to do his work, his strange work, to perform his task, his alien task.
[Isaiah] [28]:[22] So now, stop your scoffing, or your chains will be made heavier; for I have heard from the Lord, the LORD of Hosts, of destruction decreed against the whole land.
[Isaiah] [28]:[23] Listen and hear my voice; pay attention and hear what I say.
[Isaiah] [28]:[24] Does the plowman plow all day long before he sows? Does he keep breaking up and harrowing his ground?
[Isaiah] [28]:[25] No — once he has leveled its surface, he scatters caraway and sows cumin; he plants wheat in rows and barley in its place, and spelt along the edge.
[Isaiah] [28]:[26] He is instructed in the right way, for his God teaches him.
[Isaiah] [28]:[27] Caraway is not threshed with a sledge, nor is a cartwheel rolled over cumin; caraway is beaten out with a rod, and cumin with a stick.
[Isaiah] [28]:[28] Grain must be ground for bread, but no one threshes it endlessly. Though he drives the wheels of his cart over it, his horses do not crush it to powder.
[Isaiah] [28]:[29] All this too comes from the LORD of Hosts: wonderful is his counsel, and great his wisdom.
[Isaiah] [29]:[1] Woe to you, Ariel, Ariel, the city where David camped! Add year to year, let the festivals run their round—
[Isaiah] [29]:[2] then I will lay siege to Ariel, and there will be mourning and lament; she will become to me like an altar hearth.
[Isaiah] [29]:[3] I will encamp against you all around, I will ring you with towers and raise siege works against you.
[Isaiah] [29]:[4] Brought low, you will speak from the ground; your words will come muffled out of the dust. Your voice will rise like a ghost's from the earth, and out of the dust your speech will whisper.
[Isaiah] [29]:[5] But the horde of your enemies will become like fine dust, the multitude of the ruthless like blowing chaff. And it will happen in an instant, suddenly:
[Isaiah] [29]:[6] She will be visited in judgment by the LORD of hosts—with thunder and earthquake and a great roar, with whirlwind and tempest and the flame of a devouring fire.
[Isaiah] [29]:[7] Then the horde of all the nations that fight against Ariel—all who war against her, who besiege her and press her hard—will be like a dream, a vision in the night.
[Isaiah] [29]:[8] As a hungry man dreams he is eating, but wakes with his hunger unsatisfied; as a thirsty man dreams he is drinking, but wakes faint, his thirst unquenched—so it will be with the horde of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion.
[Isaiah] [29]:[9] Be dazed and dumbfounded! Blind yourselves and be blind! You are drunk, but not from wine; you stagger, but not from strong drink.
[Isaiah] [29]:[10] For the LORD has poured over you a spirit of deep sleep; he has shut your eyes—the prophets—and covered your heads—the seers.
[Isaiah] [29]:[11] For you this whole vision is like the words of a sealed scroll. Give it to someone who can read and say, "Please read this," and he will answer, "I cannot; it is sealed."
[Isaiah] [29]:[12] Or give the scroll to someone who cannot read and say, "Please read this," and he will answer, "I do not know how to read."
[Isaiah] [29]:[13] The Lord says: "Because these people come near me with their mouths and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me, and their worship of me is nothing but rules taught by men—
[Isaiah] [29]:[14] Therefore I will astound this people once more with wonder upon wonder. The wisdom of their wise will perish, and the understanding of their clever ones will vanish."
[Isaiah] [29]:[15] Woe to those who go to great depths to hide their plans from the LORD, who do their work in darkness and say, "Who sees us? Who knows?"
[Isaiah] [29]:[16] You have turned things upside down! Is the clay the equal of the potter? Shall what is made say of its maker, "He did not make me"? Shall the pot say of the potter, "He knows nothing"?
[Isaiah] [29]:[17] In just a little while, Lebanon will become an orchard, and the orchard will seem like a forest.
[Isaiah] [29]:[18] On that day the deaf will hear the words of the scroll, and out of gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind will see.
[Isaiah] [29]:[19] Once more the humble will rejoice in the LORD, and the poor among men will exult in the Holy One of Israel.
[Isaiah] [29]:[20] For the ruthless will be no more, the mocker will vanish, and all who lie in wait to do evil will be cut down—
[Isaiah] [29]:[21] those who with a word make a man out to be guilty, who ensnare the one who testifies in court, and with empty charges deny justice to the innocent.
[Isaiah] [29]:[22] Therefore this is what the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, says to the house of Jacob: "No longer will Jacob be ashamed; no longer will their faces grow pale.
[Isaiah] [29]:[23] When they see their children, the work of my hands among them, they will keep my name holy; they will acknowledge the holiness of the Holy One of Jacob and stand in awe of the God of Israel.
[Isaiah] [29]:[24] Those who have gone astray in spirit will gain understanding, and those who grumble will learn wisdom."
[Isaiah] [30]:[1] Woe to the rebellious children, declares the LORD, who carry out plans that are not mine, who forge alliances without my Spirit, heaping sin upon sin.
[Isaiah] [30]:[2] They go down to Egypt without asking my counsel, seeking refuge in Pharaoh's stronghold, shelter in Egypt's shadow.
[Isaiah] [30]:[3] But Pharaoh's stronghold will bring you shame, and Egypt's shadow nothing but disgrace.
[Isaiah] [30]:[4] Though his officials are in Zoan and his envoys reach as far as Hanes,
[Isaiah] [30]:[5] they will all be put to shame because of a people who cannot help them, who bring no aid and no advantage, only shame and reproach.
[Isaiah] [30]:[6] An oracle concerning the beasts of the Negev: Through a land of trouble and distress, where lioness and lion prowl, where viper and darting serpent dwell, they carry their wealth on the shoulders of young donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people who cannot help.
[Isaiah] [30]:[7] Egypt's help is worthless and empty. That is why I have called her Rahab who sits idle.
[Isaiah] [30]:[8] Now go, write it on a tablet before them, inscribe it in a book, that it may stand for the days to come, a witness forever.
[Isaiah] [30]:[9] For they are a defiant people, lying children, children unwilling to hear the instruction of the LORD.
[Isaiah] [30]:[10] They say to the seers, "See nothing," and to the prophets, "Do not tell us what is right. Speak to us smooth words; prophesy illusions.
[Isaiah] [30]:[11] "Get out of the way, turn aside from the path, and let us hear no more of the Holy One of Israel."
[Isaiah] [30]:[12] Therefore this is what the Holy One of Israel says: Because you have rejected this word and trusted instead in oppression and deceit, leaning on them for support,
[Isaiah] [30]:[13] this guilt of yours will be like a bulging crack in a high wall, ready to fall, whose collapse comes suddenly, in an instant.
[Isaiah] [30]:[14] It will shatter like a potter's jar, smashed so ruthlessly that no fragment is left big enough to carry coals from a hearth or to scoop water from a cistern.
[Isaiah] [30]:[15] For this is what the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, says: In returning and rest you will be saved; in quietness and trust will be your strength. But you were not willing.
[Isaiah] [30]:[16] You said, "No, we will flee on horses" — therefore you will flee! — "we will ride swift steeds" — therefore your pursuers will be swift!
[Isaiah] [30]:[17] A thousand of you will run from the threat of one; at the threat of five you will all take flight, until you are left like a flagpole on a mountaintop, like a banner on a hill.
[Isaiah] [30]:[18] Yet the LORD waits to show you grace; he rises up to have mercy on you. For the LORD is a God of justice. Blessed are all who wait for him.
[Isaiah] [30]:[19] People of Zion, who dwell in Jerusalem, you will weep no longer. He will surely be gracious to you when you cry for help; the moment he hears, he will answer you.
[Isaiah] [30]:[20] Though the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, your Teacher will hide himself no longer; with your own eyes you will see your Teacher.
[Isaiah] [30]:[21] And your ears will hear a voice behind you saying, "This is the way; walk in it," whenever you turn to the right or to the left.
[Isaiah] [30]:[22] Then you will treat as filth your silver-plated idols and your gold-covered images. You will throw them away like a defiled rag and say, "Be gone!"
[Isaiah] [30]:[23] He will send rain for the seed you sow in the ground, and bread from the yield of the soil, rich and abundant. On that day your cattle will graze in broad pastures.
[Isaiah] [30]:[24] The oxen and donkeys that work the ground will eat seasoned fodder, winnowed with shovel and fork.
[Isaiah] [30]:[25] On every high mountain and every lofty hill there will be streams of running water, on the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall.
[Isaiah] [30]:[26] The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, on the day the LORD binds up the wounds of his people and heals the bruises he has inflicted.
[Isaiah] [30]:[27] See, the name of the LORD comes from far away, his anger burning, his burden heavy. His lips are full of fury, and his tongue is a devouring fire.
[Isaiah] [30]:[28] His breath is like a raging torrent that rises to the neck, sifting the nations in the sieve of destruction, setting in the jaws of the peoples a bridle that leads them astray.
[Isaiah] [30]:[29] But you will sing as on the night of a holy festival, and your hearts will be glad, like those who march to the music of the flute up to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
[Isaiah] [30]:[30] The LORD will make his majestic voice heard and show his arm coming down — with raging anger and devouring flame, with cloudburst and downpour and hailstones.
[Isaiah] [30]:[31] At the voice of the LORD, Assyria will be shattered; he will strike her down with his rod.
[Isaiah] [30]:[32] Every stroke of the punishing staff that the LORD lays upon her will come to the beat of tambourines and lyres; with brandished arm he will fight against them.
[Isaiah] [30]:[33] For Topheth has long been prepared, made ready for the king, deep and wide, its fire pit piled high with fire and wood. The breath of the LORD, like a stream of burning sulfur, will set it ablaze. [Isaiah] [31]:[1] Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on horses, who trust in chariots because they are many and in horsemen because they are strong — but who do not look to the Holy One of Israel or seek the LORD.
[Isaiah] [31]:[2] Yet he too is wise, and he brings disaster; he does not take back his words. He will rise against the house of evildoers and against the help of those who do wrong.
[Isaiah] [31]:[3] The Egyptians are only human, not God; their horses are flesh, not spirit. When the LORD stretches out his hand, the helper will stumble and the one helped will fall, and both will perish together.
[Isaiah] [31]:[4] For this is what the LORD has said to me: As a lion, a young lion, growls over its prey — and though a whole band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not frightened by their shouting or dismayed by their uproar — so the LORD of hosts will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its hill.
[Isaiah] [31]:[5] Like birds hovering overhead, so the LORD of hosts will shield Jerusalem; he will shield and deliver it, he will pass over it and rescue it.
[Isaiah] [31]:[6] Return, people of Israel, to the one against whom you have so deeply rebelled.
[Isaiah] [31]:[7] For on that day everyone will reject his own idols of silver and idols of gold, which your hands have made for you as a sin.
[Isaiah] [31]:[8] Then Assyria will fall by a sword not of man; a sword not wielded by mortals will devour them. They will flee before the sword, and their young men will be put to forced labor.
[Isaiah] [31]:[9] Their stronghold will pass away in terror, and their officers will be shattered at the sight of the battle standard, declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
[Isaiah] [32]:[1] Look—a king will reign in righteousness, and rulers will govern with justice.
[Isaiah] [32]:[2] Each will be like a shelter from the wind, a hiding place from the storm, like streams of water in a dry land, like the shade of a great rock in a weary country.
[Isaiah] [32]:[3] Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed, and the ears of those who hear will listen.
[Isaiah] [32]:[4] The reckless heart will gain understanding, and the stammering tongue will speak clearly and readily.
[Isaiah] [32]:[5] No longer will the fool be called noble, nor the scoundrel be spoken of as generous.

[Isaiah] [32]:[7] The scoundrel's methods are wicked; he devises schemes to destroy the poor with lying words, and to deny justice to the needy.
[Isaiah] [32]:[8] But the noble man devises noble things, and he stands by what is noble.
[Isaiah] [32]:[9] You women who are at ease, rise up and hear my voice; you complacent daughters, listen to what I say.
[Isaiah] [32]:[10] In a year and some days you will tremble, you who feel secure, for the grape harvest will fail and the ingathering will not come.
[Isaiah] [32]:[11] Shudder, you women at ease; tremble, you who feel secure. Strip yourselves bare and put on sackcloth around your waists.
[Isaiah] [32]:[12] Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine,
[Isaiah] [32]:[13] for the soil of my people, overgrown with thorns and briers—yes, for all the joyful houses and the jubilant city.
[Isaiah] [32]:[14] For the palace is abandoned, the bustling city deserted; citadel and watchtower have become dens forever, the delight of wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks—
[Isaiah] [32]:[15] until the Spirit is poured out on us from on high, and the desert becomes a fertile field, and the fertile field seems like a forest.
[Isaiah] [32]:[16] Then justice will dwell in the desert, and righteousness will make its home in the fertile field.
[Isaiah] [32]:[17] The fruit of righteousness will be peace; the work of righteousness will be quietness and confidence forever.
[Isaiah] [32]:[18] My people will live in peaceful dwellings, in secure homes, in undisturbed places of rest.
[Isaiah] [32]:[19] Though hail comes down and the forest falls, and the city is leveled to the ground,
[Isaiah] [32]:[20] blessed are you who sow beside all the waters, who let the ox and the donkey range free.
[Isaiah] [33]:[1] Woe to you, destroyer, who have not been destroyed; you traitor, whom no one has betrayed! When you finish destroying, you will be destroyed; when you stop betraying, you will be betrayed.
[Isaiah] [33]:[2] LORD, be gracious to us; we long for you. Be their arm every morning, our salvation in time of distress.
[Isaiah] [33]:[3] At the sound of the tumult the peoples flee; when you rise up, the nations scatter.
[Isaiah] [33]:[4] Your plunder is gathered as young locusts gather; like a swarm of locusts they rush upon it.
[Isaiah] [33]:[5] The LORD is exalted, for he dwells on high; he has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
[Isaiah] [33]:[6] He will be the sure foundation of your times, a wealth of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge; the fear of the LORD is Zion's treasure.
[Isaiah] [33]:[7] Look, their heroes cry aloud in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
[Isaiah] [33]:[8] The highways lie deserted; no traveler is on the road. The treaty is broken, the cities are despised, and no one is held in regard.
[Isaiah] [33]:[9] The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and withers away. Sharon has become like the desert, and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
[Isaiah] [33]:[10] "Now I will arise," says the LORD. "Now I will lift myself up; now I will be exalted.
[Isaiah] [33]:[11] You conceive chaff, you give birth to straw; your breath is a fire that will devour you.
[Isaiah] [33]:[12] The peoples will be burned to lime, like thornbushes cut down and set ablaze.
[Isaiah] [33]:[13] Hear, you who are far off, what I have done; and you who are near, acknowledge my might.
[Isaiah] [33]:[14] The sinners in Zion are terrified; trembling grips the godless: "Who among us can dwell with a devouring fire? Who among us can dwell with everlasting flames?"
[Isaiah] [33]:[15] The one who walks righteously and speaks what is right, who rejects gain from extortion and keeps his hands from taking bribes, who stops his ears against plots of murder and shuts his eyes against looking on evil—
[Isaiah] [33]:[16] he will dwell on the heights; his refuge will be a fortress of rock. His bread will be given him, and his water will not fail.
[Isaiah] [33]:[17] Your eyes will see the king in his beauty and behold a land that stretches far away.
[Isaiah] [33]:[18] Your heart will ponder the former terror: "Where is the scribe? Where is the one who weighed the tribute? Where is the officer who counted the towers?"
[Isaiah] [33]:[19] You will no longer see that insolent people, that people of obscure speech beyond understanding, stammering in a tongue you cannot grasp.
[Isaiah] [33]:[20] Look on Zion, the city of our appointed feasts; your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful home, a tent that will not be moved. Its stakes will never be pulled up, nor any of its ropes broken.
[Isaiah] [33]:[21] But there the LORD in his majesty will be for us a place of broad rivers and streams, where no galley with oars will travel and no mighty ship will pass.
[Isaiah] [33]:[22] For the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our king; he will save us.
[Isaiah] [33]:[23] Your rigging hangs slack: the mast is not held firm, the sail is not spread. Then an abundance of spoil will be divided, and even the lame will carry off plunder.
[Isaiah] [33]:[24] And no one living there will say, "I am sick"; the people who dwell in her will be forgiven their sin.
[Isaiah] [34]:[1] Come near, you nations, and listen; pay attention, you peoples! Let the earth hear, and all that fills it, the world and everything it brings forth.
[Isaiah] [34]:[2] For the LORD is enraged at all the nations, furious with all their armies. He has doomed them to destruction, handed them over to the slaughter.
[Isaiah] [34]:[3] Their slain will be thrown out, and the stench of their corpses will rise; the mountains will dissolve with their blood.
[Isaiah] [34]:[4] All the host of heaven will waste away, and the sky will be rolled up like a scroll. All their host will wither, as a leaf withers on the vine, as fruit shrivels on the fig tree.
[Isaiah] [34]:[5] For my sword has drunk its fill in the heavens. Look, it descends on Edom, on the people I have doomed, to bring judgment.
[Isaiah] [34]:[6] The sword of the LORD is soaked with blood, gorged with fat—the blood of lambs and goats, the fat of the kidneys of rams. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
[Isaiah] [34]:[7] Wild oxen will go down with them, young bulls along with the mighty. Their land will drink its fill of blood, and their dust will be soaked with fat.
[Isaiah] [34]:[8] For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of retribution, to take up Zion's cause.
[Isaiah] [34]:[9] Edom's streams will turn to pitch, her dust to sulfur; her land will become burning tar.
[Isaiah] [34]:[10] Night and day it will not be quenched; its smoke will rise forever. From generation to generation it will lie waste; no one will ever pass through it again.
[Isaiah] [34]:[11] The desert owl and the screech owl will possess it; the great owl and the raven will make their home there. The LORD will stretch out over it the measuring line of chaos and the plumb line of desolation.
[Isaiah] [34]:[12] Her nobles will have nothing left to call a kingdom; all her princes will come to nothing.
[Isaiah] [34]:[13] Thorns will overrun her palaces, nettles and brambles her fortresses. She will become a haunt for jackals, a home for ostriches.
[Isaiah] [34]:[14] Desert creatures will meet with hyenas, and wild goats will call to one another. There too the night creature will settle and find herself a resting place.
[Isaiah] [34]:[15] There the owl will nest and lay her eggs, hatch them and gather her brood under her shadow. There too the falcons will gather, each with her mate.
[Isaiah] [34]:[16] Search the scroll of the LORD and read: not one of these will be missing, not one will lack her mate. For his own mouth has commanded it, and his breath has gathered them.
[Isaiah] [34]:[17] He has cast the lot for them; his hand has measured out their portions. They will possess it forever and dwell there from generation to generation.
[Isaiah] [35]:[1] The wilderness and the parched land will be glad; the desert will rejoice and blossom like the crocus.

[Isaiah] [35]:[3] Strengthen the weak hands, steady the buckling knees.

[Isaiah] [35]:[5] Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
[Isaiah] [35]:[6] Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will shout for joy. For water will break forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
[Isaiah] [35]:[7] The burning sand will become a pool, and the thirsty ground bubbling springs. In the haunt where jackals lie down, there will be grass, with reeds and rushes.
[Isaiah] [35]:[8] And a highway will be there, a road, and it will be called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel it; it is for those who walk the way, and fools will not go astray.
[Isaiah] [35]:[9] No lion will be there, no ravenous beast will go up on it; none will be found there. But the redeemed will walk it.

[Isaiah] [36]:[1] In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria marched against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
[Isaiah] [36]:[2] The king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh* from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a large army. He took his stand by the aqueduct of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field. [*Footnote: Rabshakeh is an Assyrian title for a high-ranking royal official, not a personal name.]
[Isaiah] [36]:[3] Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, went out to him, along with Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder.
[Isaiah] [36]:[4] The Rabshakeh said to them: "Tell Hezekiah this: Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: What is this confidence of yours?
[Isaiah] [36]:[5] I say your strategy and your strength for war are nothing but empty words. Now, in whom are you trusting, that you have rebelled against me?
[Isaiah] [36]:[6] Look, you are trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff, which pierces the hand of anyone who leans on it. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is to all who trust in him.
[Isaiah] [36]:[7] And if you say to me, 'We trust in the LORD our God'—is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship before this altar'?
[Isaiah] [36]:[8] Come now, make a bargain with my lord the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses—if you can put riders on them!
[Isaiah] [36]:[9] How then can you turn back even one of the least of my lord's officers, when you rely on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
[Isaiah] [36]:[10] And now, was it apart from the LORD that I came up against this land to destroy it? The LORD himself said to me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"
[Isaiah] [36]:[11] Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in Hebrew in the hearing of the people on the wall."
[Isaiah] [36]:[12] But the Rabshakeh said, "Was it to your master and to you that my lord sent me to say these things? Was it not to the men sitting on the wall, who will have to eat their own dung and drink their own urine along with you?"
[Isaiah] [36]:[13] Then the Rabshakeh stood and shouted in a loud voice in Hebrew: "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!"
[Isaiah] [36]:[14] Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he cannot rescue you.
[Isaiah] [36]:[15] Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD by saying, 'The LORD will surely rescue us; this city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.'
[Isaiah] [36]:[16] Do not listen to Hezekiah! For thus says the king of Assyria: Make your peace with me and come out to me,* and every one of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree and drink water from his own cistern, [*Footnote: Literally "make a blessing with me," an idiom for accepting terms of surrender.]
[Isaiah] [36]:[17] until I come and take you away to a land like your own—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
[Isaiah] [36]:[18] Do not let Hezekiah mislead you by saying, 'The LORD will rescue us.' Has any god of any nation ever rescued his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
[Isaiah] [36]:[19] Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they rescue Samaria from my hand?
[Isaiah] [36]:[20] Which of all the gods of these lands has rescued his land from my hand, that the LORD should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?"
[Isaiah] [36]:[21] But the people were silent and answered him not a word, for the king had commanded, "Do not answer him."
[Isaiah] [36]:[22] Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and reported to him the words of the Rabshakeh.
[Isaiah] [37]:[1] When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into the house of the LORD.
[Isaiah] [37]:[2] He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and the senior priests, all covered in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
[Isaiah] [37]:[3] They said to him: "This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace; children have come to the point of birth, and there is no strength to deliver them.
[Isaiah] [37]:[4] Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the field commander, whom his master the king of Assyria sent to mock the living God, and will rebuke him for the words the LORD your God has heard. Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that still survives."
[Isaiah] [37]:[5] So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah,
[Isaiah] [37]:[6] and Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master this: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
[Isaiah] [37]:[7] I am going to put a spirit in him, so that when he hears a report he will return to his own land, and there in his own land I will make him fall by the sword.'"
[Isaiah] [37]:[8] When the field commander returned, he found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.
[Isaiah] [37]:[9] Now the king of Assyria received a report about Tirhakah, king of Cush: "He has marched out to fight against you." So he sent messengers again to Hezekiah with this word:
[Isaiah] [37]:[10] "Say this to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying, 'Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.'
[Isaiah] [37]:[11] You have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, devoting them to destruction. And will you be delivered?
[Isaiah] [37]:[12] Did the gods of the nations my fathers destroyed rescue them—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
[Isaiah] [37]:[13] Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena and Ivvah?"
[Isaiah] [37]:[14] Hezekiah took the letters from the hand of the messengers and read them. Then he went up to the house of the LORD and spread them out before the LORD.
[Isaiah] [37]:[15] And Hezekiah prayed to the LORD:
[Isaiah] [37]:[16] "LORD of hosts, God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth.
[Isaiah] [37]:[17] Incline your ear, LORD, and hear; open your eyes, LORD, and see. Listen to all the words Sennacherib has sent to mock the living God.
[Isaiah] [37]:[18] It is true, LORD, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the lands, and every land of theirs,
[Isaiah] [37]:[19] and have thrown their gods into the fire. But they were no gods at all, only the work of human hands, wood and stone—so they destroyed them.
[Isaiah] [37]:[20] Now, LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are the LORD."
[Isaiah] [37]:[21] Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you have prayed to me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria,
[Isaiah] [37]:[22] this is the word the LORD has spoken against him: The Virgin Daughter Zion despises you and mocks you; the Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head as you flee.
[Isaiah] [37]:[23] Whom have you mocked and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!
[Isaiah] [37]:[24] By your servants you have mocked the Lord, and you have said: 'With my many chariots I have climbed the mountain heights, the far recesses of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest cypresses. I have reached its remotest heights, its densest forest.
[Isaiah] [37]:[25] I have dug wells and drunk water; with the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.'
[Isaiah] [37]:[26] Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained it; in days of old I planned it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you should turn fortified cities into heaps of rubble.
[Isaiah] [37]:[27] Their people, drained of power, were dismayed and put to shame. They were like plants in the field, like tender green shoots, like grass sprouting on the roof, scorched before it grows up.
[Isaiah] [37]:[28] But I know where you dwell, when you come and when you go, and how you rage against me.
[Isaiah] [37]:[29] Because you rage against me, and because your arrogance has reached my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth, and I will make you return by the way you came.
[Isaiah] [37]:[30] And this will be the sign for you: This year you will eat what grows by itself, and the second year what springs from that. But in the third year sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
[Isaiah] [37]:[31] Once more the surviving remnant of the house of Judah will take root below and bear fruit above.
[Isaiah] [37]:[32] For out of Jerusalem will come a remnant, and out of Mount Zion a band of survivors. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will accomplish this.
[Isaiah] [37]:[33] Therefore this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow here. He will not come before it with a shield or build a siege ramp against it.
[Isaiah] [37]:[34] By the way he came he will return; he will not enter this city, declares the LORD.
[Isaiah] [37]:[35] I will defend this city and save it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant.
[Isaiah] [37]:[36] Then the angel of the LORD went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the Assyrian camp. When the people rose early the next morning — there they all lay, dead bodies.
[Isaiah] [37]:[37] So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.
[Isaiah] [37]:[38] One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer cut him down with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And Esarhaddon his son succeeded him as king.
[Isaiah] [38]:[1] In those days Hezekiah fell sick and was near death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, "This is what the LORD says: Put your house in order, for you are going to die; you will not recover."
[Isaiah] [38]:[2] Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD:
[Isaiah] [38]:[3] "Remember, LORD, I beg you, how I have walked before you faithfully and with a whole heart, and have done what is good in your eyes." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
[Isaiah] [38]:[4] Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah:
[Isaiah] [38]:[5] "Go and say to Hezekiah: This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. I am going to add fifteen years to your life.
[Isaiah] [38]:[6] And I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria; I will defend this city.
[Isaiah] [38]:[7] This will be the sign to you from the LORD that the LORD will do what he has promised:
[Isaiah] [38]:[8] I will make the shadow cast by the sun go back the ten steps it has gone down on the stairway of Ahaz." So the sunlight went back the ten steps it had descended.
[Isaiah] [38]:[9] A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, after his illness and recovery:
[Isaiah] [38]:[10] I said, "In the prime of my life I must pass through the gates of the grave; I am robbed of the rest of my years."
[Isaiah] [38]:[11] I said, "I will not see the LORD, the LORD, in the land of the living; never again will I look on my fellow man, or be with those who dwell in this world."
[Isaiah] [38]:[12] My dwelling is pulled up and carried off like a shepherd's tent. Like a weaver I have rolled up my life, and he has cut me from the loom. Day and night you bring me to an end.
[Isaiah] [38]:[13] I waited patiently till dawn, but like a lion he broke all my bones. Day and night you bring me to an end.
[Isaiah] [38]:[14] I cried like a swift or a swallow, I moaned like a dove. My eyes grew weak as I looked to the heavens. I am oppressed, Lord; come to my aid!
[Isaiah] [38]:[15] But what can I say? He has spoken to me, and he himself has done this. I will walk humbly all my years because of this anguish of my soul.
[Isaiah] [38]:[16] Lord, by such things people live, and my spirit finds life in them too. Restore me to health; let me live!
[Isaiah] [38]:[17] Surely it was for my benefit that I suffered such anguish. In your love you kept me from the pit of destruction; you have hurled all my sins behind your back.
[Isaiah] [38]:[18] For the grave cannot praise you, death cannot sing your praise; those who go down to the pit cannot hope for your faithfulness.
[Isaiah] [38]:[19] The living, the living—they praise you, as I am doing today; a father tells his children about your faithfulness.
[Isaiah] [38]:[20] The LORD will save me, and we will make music on stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the LORD.
[Isaiah] [38]:[21] Isaiah had said, "Let them bring a poultice of figs and apply it to the boil, and he will recover."
[Isaiah] [38]:[22] And Hezekiah had asked, "What will be the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?"
[Isaiah] [39]:[1] At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that Hezekiah had been ill and had recovered.
[Isaiah] [39]:[2] Hezekiah welcomed the envoys gladly and showed them his treasure house—the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine oil, his whole armory, and everything found among his treasures. There was nothing in his palace or in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them.
[Isaiah] [39]:[3] Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and asked him, "What did these men say, and where did they come from?" Hezekiah answered, "They came to me from a distant land, from Babylon."
[Isaiah] [39]:[4] "What did they see in your palace?" Isaiah asked. "They saw everything in my palace," Hezekiah said. "There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them."

[Isaiah] [39]:[6] "Look, the days are coming when everything in your palace, and all that your fathers have stored up until this day, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
[Isaiah] [39]:[7] And some of your own sons, your own flesh and blood, whom you will father, will be taken away to serve as eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon." [Footnote: The Hebrew word can also mean court officials or royal stewards.]

[Isaiah] [40]:[1] Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.
[Isaiah] [40]:[2] Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and call out to her that her hard service is over, that her guilt is paid for, that she has received from the LORD's hand double for all her sins.
[Isaiah] [40]:[3] A voice cries out: In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
[Isaiah] [40]:[4] Every valley shall be lifted up, every mountain and hill made low; the rugged ground shall become level, and the rough places a plain.
[Isaiah] [40]:[5] And the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all flesh together will see it, for the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
[Isaiah] [40]:[6] A voice says, "Cry out!" And I said, "What shall I cry?" All flesh is grass, and all its beauty like the flower of the field.
[Isaiah] [40]:[7] The grass withers, the flower fades, for the breath of the LORD blows on it; surely the people are grass.
[Isaiah] [40]:[8] The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever.
[Isaiah] [40]:[9] Go up on a high mountain, you who bring good news to Zion. Lift up your voice with strength, you who bring good news to Jerusalem. Lift it up, do not be afraid; say to the cities of Judah, "Here is your God!"
[Isaiah] [40]:[10] See, the Lord GOD comes with power, and his arm rules for him. See, his reward is with him, and his recompense goes before him.
[Isaiah] [40]:[11] He tends his flock like a shepherd: he gathers the lambs in his arms and carries them close to his heart; he gently leads the nursing ewes.
[Isaiah] [40]:[12] Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, or marked off the heavens with the span of his fingers? Who has held the dust of the earth in a measure, weighed the mountains on a scale and the hills in a balance?
[Isaiah] [40]:[13] Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or instructed him as his counselor?
[Isaiah] [40]:[14] Whom did he consult to gain understanding? Who taught him the path of justice, or taught him knowledge, or showed him the way of insight?
[Isaiah] [40]:[15] See, the nations are like a drop from a bucket; they count as the dust on the scales. See, he lifts up the islands like fine powder.
[Isaiah] [40]:[16] Lebanon is not enough for the fire, nor its animals enough for a burnt offering.
[Isaiah] [40]:[17] Before him all the nations are as nothing; he regards them as less than nothing, as emptiness.
[Isaiah] [40]:[18] To whom, then, will you compare God? What likeness will you set beside him?
[Isaiah] [40]:[19] The craftsman casts an idol; the goldsmith overlays it with gold and fashions silver chains for it.
[Isaiah] [40]:[20] The one too poor for such an offering chooses wood that will not rot; he looks for a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple.
[Isaiah] [40]:[21] Do you not know? Have you not heard? Was it not told you from the beginning? Have you not understood since the earth was founded?
[Isaiah] [40]:[22] He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain and spreads them out like a tent to live in.
[Isaiah] [40]:[23] He reduces rulers to nothing and makes the judges of the earth into emptiness.
[Isaiah] [40]:[24] No sooner are they planted, no sooner are they sown, no sooner do they take root in the ground, than he breathes on them and they wither, and a whirlwind sweeps them away like straw.
[Isaiah] [40]:[25] "To whom will you compare me? Who is my equal?" says the Holy One.
[Isaiah] [40]:[26] Lift your eyes on high and see: who created all these? He brings out their host by number and calls them each by name. Because of his great might and the strength of his power, not one of them is missing.
[Isaiah] [40]:[27] Why do you say, Jacob, and complain, Israel, "My way is hidden from the LORD; my cause is ignored by my God"?
[Isaiah] [40]:[28] Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not grow tired or weary, and his understanding no one can fathom.
[Isaiah] [40]:[29] He gives strength to the weary and increases the power of the weak.
[Isaiah] [40]:[30] Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall;
[Isaiah] [40]:[31] but those who hope in the LORD will renew their strength. They will rise on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not be faint.
[Isaiah] [41]:[1] Be silent before me, you coastlands; let the nations renew their strength. Let them come forward and speak; let us meet together for judgment.

[Isaiah] [41]:[3] He pursues them and passes on unharmed, by a path his feet have never walked.

[Isaiah] [41]:[12] You will look for those who quarreled with you and not find them; those who made war on you will be as nothing at all.
[Isaiah] [41]:[13] For I am the LORD your God, who takes hold of your right hand and says to you, "Do not fear; I am your help."
[Isaiah] [41]:[14] Do not fear, you worm Jacob, you few men of Israel. I am your help, declares the LORD; your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
[Isaiah] [41]:[15] Look, I am making you a threshing sledge, new and sharp, with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and reduce the hills to chaff.
[Isaiah] [41]:[16] You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them off; a gale will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the LORD; in the Holy One of Israel you will glory.
[Isaiah] [41]:[17] When the poor and needy search for water and there is none, and their tongues are parched with thirst, I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not abandon them.
[Isaiah] [41]:[18] I will open rivers on the barren heights and springs in the valleys; I will turn the desert into pools of water, and the parched land into flowing springs.
[Isaiah] [41]:[19] In the wilderness I will plant the cedar and the acacia, the myrtle and the olive; in the wasteland I will set the cypress, the plane, and the pine together,
[Isaiah] [41]:[20] so that all may see and know, consider and understand together, that the hand of the LORD has done this, that the Holy One of Israel has created it.
[Isaiah] [41]:[21] Present your case, says the LORD; bring forward your arguments, says the King of Jacob.
[Isaiah] [41]:[22] Let them come and tell us what is going to happen. Tell us what the former things were, so that we may consider them and know how they turned out; or announce to us the things that are coming.
[Isaiah] [41]:[23] Declare what is to come hereafter, so that we may know you are gods. Do something, good or evil, so that we may see it together and be filled with dread.
[Isaiah] [41]:[24] Look, you are nothing, and your work is worthless; whoever chooses you is detestable.
[Isaiah] [41]:[25] I stirred up one from the north, and he comes; from the rising of the sun he calls on my name. He tramples rulers like mortar, like a potter treading clay.
[Isaiah] [41]:[26] Who announced this from the beginning, so that we might know, or foretold it, so that we might say, "He was right"? No one announced it, no one proclaimed it, no one heard a word from you.

[Isaiah] [41]:[29] Look, they are all a delusion; their deeds amount to nothing. Their idols are wind and emptiness.

[Isaiah] [43]:[28] So I disgraced the officials of the sanctuary; I consigned Jacob to destruction and Israel to scorn.
[Isaiah] [44]:[1] But now listen, Jacob my servant, Israel whom I have chosen.
[Isaiah] [44]:[2] This is what the LORD says—he who made you, who formed you in the womb and will help you: Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, Jeshurun whom I have chosen.
[Isaiah] [44]:[3] For I will pour water on the thirsty ground and streams on the dry land; I will pour out my Spirit on your offspring and my blessing on your descendants.
[Isaiah] [44]:[4] They will spring up like grass in a meadow, like poplars by flowing streams.
[Isaiah] [44]:[5] One will say, "I belong to the LORD," another will take the name of Jacob, and another will write on his hand, "The LORD's," and take the name of Israel as his own.
[Isaiah] [44]:[6] This is what the LORD says—Israel's King and Redeemer, the LORD of hosts: I am the first and I am the last; apart from me there is no God.
[Isaiah] [44]:[7] Who is like me? Let him proclaim it, let him declare and lay it out before me—who has announced from of old what was to come, since I established an ancient people. Let them tell what is yet to be.
[Isaiah] [44]:[8] Do not tremble, do not be afraid. Did I not announce it and declare it to you long ago? You are my witnesses. Is there any God besides me? There is no other Rock; I know of none.
[Isaiah] [44]:[9] All who fashion idols are nothing, and the things they treasure are worthless. Their witnesses see nothing and know nothing, so they will be put to shame.
[Isaiah] [44]:[10] Who shapes a god and casts an idol that can do him no good?
[Isaiah] [44]:[11] Look, all its devotees will be disgraced; its craftsmen are only human. Let them all assemble and take their stand; they will be terrified and put to shame together.
[Isaiah] [44]:[12] The blacksmith takes his tool and works over the coals; he shapes the idol with hammers and forges it with the strength of his arm. He grows hungry and his strength fails; he drinks no water and faints.
[Isaiah] [44]:[13] The carpenter stretches out his measuring line and marks the shape with a stylus; he works it with chisels and traces it with a compass. He carves it in human form, in the glorious likeness of a man, to sit in a shrine.
[Isaiah] [44]:[14] He cuts down cedars, or takes a cypress or an oak; he lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest. Or he plants a laurel, and the rain makes it grow.
[Isaiah] [44]:[15] Then it becomes fuel for a man: he takes some of it and warms himself, he kindles a fire and bakes bread. But he also makes a god of it and worships it; he makes an idol and bows down to it.
[Isaiah] [44]:[16] Half of the wood he burns in the fire; over it he roasts his meat and eats his fill. He warms himself and says, "Ah, I am warm; I can see the fire."
[Isaiah] [44]:[17] From the rest he makes a god, his idol; he bows down to it and worships. He prays to it and says, "Save me, for you are my god."
[Isaiah] [44]:[18] They know nothing, they understand nothing; their eyes are plastered over so they cannot see, and their minds are closed so they cannot comprehend.
[Isaiah] [44]:[19] No one stops to think, no one has the knowledge or the understanding to say, "Half of it I burned in the fire; over its coals I baked bread, I roasted meat and ate. Shall I make the rest into a detestable thing? Shall I bow down to a block of wood?"
[Isaiah] [44]:[20] He feeds on ashes; his deluded heart has led him astray. He cannot save himself, nor say, "Is not this thing in my right hand a lie?"
[Isaiah] [44]:[21] Remember these things, Jacob, for you are my servant, Israel. I formed you; you are my servant. Israel, I will not forget you.
[Isaiah] [44]:[22] I have swept away your transgressions like a cloud, your sins like the morning mist. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.
[Isaiah] [44]:[23] Sing, you heavens, for the LORD has done it! Shout aloud, you depths of the earth! Break into song, you mountains, you forest and every tree in it! For the LORD has redeemed Jacob; he displays his glory in Israel.
[Isaiah] [44]:[24] This is what the LORD says—your Redeemer, who formed you in the womb: I am the LORD, the Maker of all things, who stretched out the heavens alone, who spread out the earth with none beside me;
[Isaiah] [44]:[25] who overturns the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners; who turns the wise back and reduces their knowledge to nonsense;
[Isaiah] [44]:[26] who confirms the word of his servant and fulfills the counsel of his messengers; who says of Jerusalem, "It shall be inhabited," and of the towns of Judah, "They shall be rebuilt," and of her ruins, "I will raise them up";
[Isaiah] [44]:[27] who says to the deep, "Be dry! I will dry up your streams";
[Isaiah] [44]:[28] who says of Cyrus, "He is my shepherd, and he will accomplish all that I please"; who says of Jerusalem, "It shall be rebuilt," and of the temple, "Its foundation shall be laid."
[Isaiah] [45]:[1] This is what the LORD says to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped, to subdue nations before him and strip kings of their armor, to open doors before him so that no gate stays shut:
[Isaiah] [45]:[2] I will go before you and level the mountains; I will shatter doors of bronze and cut through bars of iron.
[Isaiah] [45]:[3] I will give you the treasures of darkness and riches hidden away, so that you may know that I am the LORD, the God of Israel, who calls you by name.
[Isaiah] [45]:[4] For the sake of my servant Jacob, of Israel my chosen, I have called you by name; I have given you a title of honor, though you do not know me.
[Isaiah] [45]:[5] I am the LORD, and there is no other; apart from me there is no God. I arm you for battle, though you do not know me,
[Isaiah] [45]:[6] so that from the rising of the sun to its setting people may know there is none but me. I am the LORD, and there is no other.
[Isaiah] [45]:[7] I form the light and create the darkness; I make peace and create disaster. I, the LORD, do all these things.
[Isaiah] [45]:[8] Rain down, you heavens above; let the clouds pour out righteousness. Let the earth open wide, let salvation spring up, and let righteousness blossom with it. I, the LORD, have created it.
[Isaiah] [45]:[9] Woe to the one who quarrels with his Maker, a mere shard among the shards of the earth! Does the clay say to the potter, "What are you making?" or, "Your work has no hands"?
[Isaiah] [45]:[10] Woe to the one who says to a father, "What are you fathering?" or to a woman, "What are you laboring to bear?"
[Isaiah] [45]:[11] This is what the LORD says, the Holy One of Israel, the one who formed him: Ask me about the things to come! Concerning my children and the work of my hands, would you give me orders?
[Isaiah] [45]:[12] I made the earth, and I created humankind upon it. It was my hands that stretched out the heavens, and I command all their host.
[Isaiah] [45]:[13] I have stirred him up in righteousness, and I will make all his ways straight. He will rebuild my city and set my exiles free, without payment and without bribe, says the LORD of hosts.
[Isaiah] [45]:[14] This is what the LORD says: The wealth of Egypt, the merchandise of Cush, and the tall Sabeans will come over to you and be yours. They will walk behind you; they will come over in chains. They will bow down to you and plead with you: "Surely God is with you, and there is no other; there is no other God."
[Isaiah] [45]:[15] Truly you are a God who hides himself, O God of Israel, the Savior.
[Isaiah] [45]:[16] They will all be ashamed and disgraced; the makers of idols will go off together in humiliation.
[Isaiah] [45]:[17] But Israel is saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation; you will never be ashamed or disgraced, to all eternity.
[Isaiah] [45]:[18] For this is what the LORD says—he who created the heavens, he is God; he formed the earth and made it, he established it. He did not create it to be empty, but formed it to be inhabited: I am the LORD, and there is no other.
[Isaiah] [45]:[19] I have not spoken in secret, from somewhere in a land of darkness. I have not said to Jacob's descendants, "Seek me in vain." I, the LORD, speak the truth; I declare what is right.
[Isaiah] [45]:[20] Gather together and come; draw near, you survivors of the nations. They know nothing, those who carry about idols of wood and pray to a god that cannot save.
[Isaiah] [45]:[21] Speak up and present your case; take counsel together. Who foretold this long ago, who declared it from of old? Was it not I, the LORD? And there is no God besides me, a righteous God and a Savior; there is none but me.
[Isaiah] [45]:[22] Turn to me and be saved, all you ends of the earth, for I am God, and there is no other.
[Isaiah] [45]:[23] By myself I have sworn; from my mouth has gone forth in righteousness a word that will not return: Before me every knee will bow, and every tongue will swear allegiance.
[Isaiah] [45]:[24] "In the LORD alone," it will be said of me, "are righteousness and strength." All who rage against him will come to him and be put to shame.
[Isaiah] [45]:[25] In the LORD all the descendants of Israel will be justified, and in him they will glory.
[Isaiah] [46]:[1] Bel bows down, Nebo stoops low; their idols are loaded on beasts and cattle. The things you carry in procession are a burden, a load for the weary.
[Isaiah] [46]:[2] They stoop and bow down together; they cannot save the load, and they themselves go off into captivity.
[Isaiah] [46]:[3] Listen to me, house of Jacob, all you who remain of the house of Israel—you whom I have carried since birth, whom I have borne since the womb.
[Isaiah] [46]:[4] Even to your old age I am the same, and to your gray hairs I will carry you. I have made you, and I will bear you; I will sustain you and I will rescue you.
[Isaiah] [46]:[5] To whom will you compare me, or count me equal? To whom will you liken me, that we should be alike?
[Isaiah] [46]:[6] They pour out gold from the purse and weigh silver on the scales; they hire a goldsmith to make it into a god, and then they kneel and bow down to it.
[Isaiah] [46]:[7] They lift it to their shoulders and haul it; they set it in its place, and there it stands—it cannot move from its spot. Someone cries out to it, and it does not answer; it cannot save him from his distress.
[Isaiah] [46]:[8] Remember this and stand firm; take it to heart, you rebels.
[Isaiah] [46]:[9] Remember the former things, those of long ago: I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like me.
[Isaiah] [46]:[10] I declare the end from the beginning, from ancient times what is still to come. I say: My purpose will stand, and I will do all that I please.
[Isaiah] [46]:[11] I summon a bird of prey from the east, from a distant land a man to fulfill my purpose. What I have said, I will bring about; what I have planned, I will do.
[Isaiah] [46]:[12] Listen to me, you stubborn of heart, you who are far from righteousness.
[Isaiah] [46]:[13] I am bringing my righteousness near—it is not far off; my salvation will not be delayed. I will grant salvation in Zion, and my splendor to Israel.
[Isaiah] [47]:[1] Come down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon; sit on the ground, unthroned daughter of the Chaldeans. No longer will they call you tender and delicate.
[Isaiah] [47]:[2] Take the millstones and grind flour. Remove your veil, strip off your skirt, bare your legs, wade through the rivers.
[Isaiah] [47]:[3] Your nakedness will be uncovered, your shame exposed. I will take vengeance, and I will spare no one.
[Isaiah] [47]:[4] Our Redeemer—the LORD of hosts is his name, the Holy One of Israel.
[Isaiah] [47]:[5] Sit in silence, go into the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans. No longer will they call you queen of kingdoms.
[Isaiah] [47]:[6] I was angry with my people; I profaned my inheritance and handed them over to you. You showed them no mercy; even on the aged you laid your yoke most heavily.
[Isaiah] [47]:[7] You said, "I will be queen forever." You never took these things to heart or considered how it would end.
[Isaiah] [47]:[8] Now then, listen, you pampered one, lounging in your security, saying to yourself, "I am, and there is no one besides me. I will never sit as a widow or know the loss of children."
[Isaiah] [47]:[9] Both of these will come upon you in an instant, on a single day: loss of children and widowhood. They will come upon you in full measure, despite your many sorceries and all the power of your spells.
[Isaiah] [47]:[10] You trusted in your wickedness and said, "No one sees me." Your wisdom and knowledge have led you astray, and you said in your heart, "I am, and there is no one besides me."
[Isaiah] [47]:[11] But disaster will come upon you, and you will not know how to charm it away. Ruin will fall on you that you cannot ward off; devastation will come upon you suddenly, before you know it.
[Isaiah] [47]:[12] Keep on, then, with your spells and your many sorceries, at which you have labored since your youth. Perhaps you will find some benefit; perhaps you will inspire terror.
[Isaiah] [47]:[13] You are worn out with all your schemes. Let them stand up and save you—those who map the heavens, who study the stars, who announce month by month what is coming upon you.
[Isaiah] [47]:[14] See, they are all like stubble; the fire consumes them. They cannot save themselves from the power of the flame. These are no coals for warming, no fire to sit beside.
[Isaiah] [47]:[15] So it is with those you labored for, your traders from your youth. Each one has wandered off to his own place; there is no one to save you.
[Isaiah] [48]:[1] Hear this, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel and who came from the loins of Judah, you who swear by the name of the LORD and invoke the God of Israel—but not in truth or righteousness.
[Isaiah] [48]:[2] For they call themselves after the holy city and lean on the God of Israel—the LORD of hosts is his name.
[Isaiah] [48]:[3] The former things I declared long ago; they went out from my mouth, and I made them heard. Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.
[Isaiah] [48]:[4] Because I knew how stubborn you are—your neck an iron sinew, your forehead bronze—
[Isaiah] [48]:[5] I told you long ago; before it happened I made you hear it, so you could not say, "My idol did this; my carved image and my cast figure ordained it."
[Isaiah] [48]:[6] You have heard it—look at it all. Will you not admit it? From now on I make you hear new things, hidden things you have not known.
[Isaiah] [48]:[7] They are created now, not long ago; before today you never heard of them, so you cannot say, "Look, I knew them already."
[Isaiah] [48]:[8] You have not heard, you have not known, and long ago your ear was not opened. For I knew how treacherous you are; you have been called a rebel from birth.
[Isaiah] [48]:[9] For my name's sake I hold back my anger; for the sake of my praise I restrain myself toward you, so as not to destroy you.
[Isaiah] [48]:[10] See, I have refined you, but not with silver; I have tested you in the furnace of affliction.
[Isaiah] [48]:[11] For my own sake, for my own sake I act—why should my name be profaned? I will not give my glory to another.
[Isaiah] [48]:[12] Listen to me, Jacob, and Israel, whom I have called: I am he. I am the first, and I am the last.
[Isaiah] [48]:[13] My own hand laid the foundations of the earth, and my right hand spread out the heavens. When I summon them, they stand forth together.
[Isaiah] [48]:[14] Gather together, all of you, and listen: which of them ever foretold these things? The LORD loves him; he will carry out his purpose against Babylon, and his arm will be against the Chaldeans.
[Isaiah] [48]:[15] I, I myself have spoken; yes, I have called him. I have brought him, and he will succeed in his way.
[Isaiah] [48]:[16] Come near to me and hear this: from the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the moment it came to be, I was there. And now the Lord GOD has sent me, and his Spirit.
[Isaiah] [48]:[17] This is what the LORD says—your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your good, who leads you in the way you should go.
[Isaiah] [48]:[18] If only you had listened to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
[Isaiah] [48]:[19] Your offspring would have been like the sand, the children of your body like its grains; their name would never be cut off or wiped out from before me.
[Isaiah] [48]:[20] Go out from Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! With a shout of joy declare it, proclaim it, send it out to the ends of the earth. Say, "The LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob."
[Isaiah] [48]:[21] They did not thirst when he led them through the deserts; he made water flow from the rock for them—he split the rock, and water gushed out.
[Isaiah] [48]:[22] There is no peace, says the LORD, for the wicked.
[Isaiah] [49]:[1] Listen to me, you coastlands; pay attention, you distant peoples. The LORD called me from the womb; while I was still in my mother's body he spoke my name.
[Isaiah] [49]:[2] He made my mouth like a sharpened sword; in the shadow of his hand he hid me. He made me a polished arrow and concealed me in his quiver.
[Isaiah] [49]:[3] He said to me, "You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will show my glory."
[Isaiah] [49]:[4] But I said, "I have labored in vain; I have spent my strength for nothing, for emptiness. Yet surely my cause rests with the LORD, and my reward with my God."
[Isaiah] [49]:[5] And now the LORD speaks—he who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him, so that Israel might be gathered to him; and I am honored in the eyes of the LORD, for my God has been my strength—
[Isaiah] [49]:[6] he says: "It is too small a thing for you to be my servant, only to restore the tribes of Jacob and bring back those of Israel who are preserved. I will make you a light for the nations, that my salvation may reach to the ends of the earth."
[Isaiah] [49]:[7] This is what the LORD says—the Redeemer of Israel, his Holy One—to him who is despised, abhorred by the nation, the servant of rulers: "Kings will see and rise, princes will see and bow down, because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you."
[Isaiah] [49]:[8] This is what the LORD says: "In the time of my favor I answered you; on the day of salvation I helped you. I will keep you and make you a covenant for the people, to restore the land and apportion its desolate inheritances,
[Isaiah] [49]:[9] to say to the captives, 'Come out,' and to those in darkness, 'Show yourselves!' They will graze along the roads and find pasture on every barren height.
[Isaiah] [49]:[10] They will not hunger or thirst, nor will scorching heat or sun strike them down. For he who has compassion on them will guide them and lead them to springs of water.
[Isaiah] [49]:[11] I will turn all my mountains into a road, and my highways will be raised up.
[Isaiah] [49]:[12] See, they come from far away—these from the north, these from the west, and these from the land of Syene.[^1] [^1]: Hebrew "the land of Sinim," likely Syene (Aswan) in the far south of Egypt.
[Isaiah] [49]:[13] Sing for joy, you heavens; rejoice, you earth; break into song, you mountains! For the LORD has comforted his people and will have compassion on his afflicted ones.
[Isaiah] [49]:[14] But Zion said, "The LORD has abandoned me; the Lord has forgotten me."
[Isaiah] [49]:[15] Can a woman forget the child at her breast, or have no compassion on the son she bore? Even if she could forget, I will not forget you.
[Isaiah] [49]:[16] See, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands; your walls are ever before me.
[Isaiah] [49]:[17] Your builders hurry back;[^1] those who tore you down and laid you waste depart from you. [^1]: Or "your sons"; the two words differ only in vowels, and the traditional Hebrew text reads "your sons."
[Isaiah] [49]:[18] Lift up your eyes and look around: they are all gathering, they are coming to you. As surely as I live, declares the LORD, you will wear them all like jewelry; you will put them on like a bride.
[Isaiah] [49]:[19] Though you were ruined and laid waste, your land in rubble, now you will be too small for your people, and those who devoured you will be far away.
[Isaiah] [49]:[20] The children born in your bereavement will yet say in your hearing, "This place is too cramped for me; make room for me to settle."
[Isaiah] [49]:[21] Then you will say in your heart, "Who bore me these? I was bereaved and barren, exiled and cast aside—so who raised them? I was left all alone; where have these come from?"
[Isaiah] [49]:[22] This is what the Lord GOD says: "See, I will lift up my hand to the nations and raise my banner to the peoples; they will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders.
[Isaiah] [49]:[23] Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow before you with their faces to the ground; they will lick the dust at your feet. Then you will know that I am the LORD, and that those who hope in me will not be put to shame."
[Isaiah] [49]:[24] Can plunder be taken from a warrior, or captives rescued from a tyrant?[^1] [^1]: The traditional Hebrew text reads "from a righteous one"; ancient scroll and version evidence, along with the parallel in the next verse, reads "from a tyrant."
[Isaiah] [49]:[25] But this is what the LORD says: "Yes, the warrior's captives will be taken, and the tyrant's plunder rescued. I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children.
[Isaiah] [49]:[26] I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh; they will be drunk on their own blood as with wine. Then all flesh will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob."

[Isaiah] [50]:[2] Why was there no one there when I came? Why did no one answer when I called? Is my arm too short to redeem? Do I lack the strength to rescue? Look, at my rebuke I dry up the sea; I turn rivers into desert. Their fish rot for want of water and die of thirst.
[Isaiah] [50]:[3] I clothe the heavens in darkness and wrap them in sackcloth.
[Isaiah] [50]:[4] The Lord GOD has given me a well-taught tongue, so that I know how to sustain the weary with a word. Morning by morning he wakens me, he wakens my ear to listen like one who is taught.
[Isaiah] [50]:[5] The Lord GOD has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious; I did not draw back.
[Isaiah] [50]:[6] I offered my back to those who struck me, my cheeks to those who tore out my beard. I did not hide my face from insult and spitting.
[Isaiah] [50]:[7] But the Lord GOD helps me; therefore I am not disgraced. Therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I will not be put to shame.
[Isaiah] [50]:[8] The one who vindicates me is near. Who dares to bring a charge against me? Let us confront each other. Who is my accuser? Let him come forward.
[Isaiah] [50]:[9] See, the Lord GOD helps me. Who then will condemn me? Look, they will all wear out like a garment; the moth will devour them.
[Isaiah] [50]:[10] Who among you fears the LORD and obeys the voice of his servant? Whoever walks in darkness with no light at all, let him trust in the name of the LORD and lean on his God.
[Isaiah] [50]:[11] Look, all of you who kindle a fire and arm yourselves with firebrands: walk by the light of your own fire, by the brands you have set ablaze. This is what you will receive from my hand: you will lie down in torment.
[Isaiah] [51]:[1] Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the LORD: look to the rock from which you were hewn, to the quarry from which you were dug.
[Isaiah] [51]:[2] Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who gave you birth. For he was but one when I called him, and I blessed him and made him many.
[Isaiah] [51]:[3] Surely the LORD comforts Zion; he comforts all her ruins. He makes her wilderness like Eden, her desert like the garden of the LORD. Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and the sound of song.
[Isaiah] [51]:[4] Pay attention to me, my people; give ear to me, my nation. For instruction will go out from me, and I will set my justice as a light to the peoples.
[Isaiah] [51]:[5] My righteousness draws near, my salvation has gone out, and my arms will judge the peoples. The coastlands wait for me; they hope in my arm.
[Isaiah] [51]:[6] Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look at the earth beneath. The heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment, and its inhabitants will die like gnats.[^1] [^1]: Or "will die in like manner"; the Hebrew word can mean either "gnats" or "thus, in like manner."
[Isaiah] [51]:[7] Listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law: do not fear the reproach of mortals, and do not be dismayed at their reviling.
[Isaiah] [51]:[8] For the moth will eat them like a garment, and the worm will devour them like wool. But my righteousness will last forever, and my salvation to all generations.
[Isaiah] [51]:[9] Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD! Awake as in days of old, as in generations long past. Was it not you who cut Rahab to pieces, who pierced the dragon?
[Isaiah] [51]:[10] Was it not you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of the sea a road for the redeemed to cross over?
[Isaiah] [51]:[11] So the ransomed of the LORD will return and come to Zion with singing; everlasting joy will crown their heads. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
[Isaiah] [51]:[12] I, I am he who comforts you. Who are you, that you fear a mortal who dies, a son of man who is made like grass,
[Isaiah] [51]:[13] that you forget the LORD your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth? All day long you live in constant dread of the oppressor's fury, as though he were poised to destroy. But where is the oppressor's fury now?
[Isaiah] [51]:[14] The one bowed down in chains will soon be set free; he will not die in the pit, nor will he lack bread.
[Isaiah] [51]:[15] For I am the LORD your God, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar—the LORD of hosts is his name.
[Isaiah] [51]:[16] I have put my words in your mouth and covered you with the shadow of my hand, to plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth, and to say to Zion, "You are my people."
[Isaiah] [51]:[17] Rouse yourself, rouse yourself! Stand up, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the LORD's hand the cup of his wrath, who have drained to the dregs the goblet that makes people stagger.
[Isaiah] [51]:[18] Of all the sons she bore, there is none to guide her; of all the sons she raised, there is none to take her by the hand.
[Isaiah] [51]:[19] These two things have come upon you—who will grieve for you?—ruin and destruction, famine and sword. Who will comfort you?
[Isaiah] [51]:[20] Your sons have fainted; they lie at the head of every street like an antelope caught in a net. They are filled with the wrath of the LORD, with the rebuke of your God.
[Isaiah] [51]:[21] Therefore hear this, you afflicted one, you who are drunk—but not with wine.
[Isaiah] [51]:[22] This is what your Lord says, the LORD, your God, who defends his people: See, I have taken from your hand the cup that made you stagger; from that goblet, the cup of my wrath, you will never drink again.
[Isaiah] [51]:[23] I will put it into the hands of your tormentors, who said to you, "Lie down, that we may walk over you"—and you made your back like the ground, like a street for them to cross.
[Isaiah] [52]:[1] Awake, awake! Clothe yourself with strength, Zion. Put on your garments of splendor, Jerusalem, the holy city. Never again will the uncircumcised and the unclean enter you.
[Isaiah] [52]:[2] Shake off the dust; rise up and sit enthroned, Jerusalem. Loose the chains from your neck, captive Daughter Zion.
[Isaiah] [52]:[3] For this is what the LORD says: You were sold for nothing, and without money you will be redeemed.
[Isaiah] [52]:[4] For this is what the Lord GOD says: At first my people went down to Egypt to live there as strangers, and Assyria oppressed them for no reason.
[Isaiah] [52]:[5] And now what do I have here? declares the LORD. For my people have been carried off for nothing; their rulers howl, declares the LORD, and all day long, without ceasing, my name is despised.
[Isaiah] [52]:[6] Therefore my people will know my name; on that day they will know that it is I who speak: Here I am.
[Isaiah] [52]:[7] How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the herald who proclaims peace, who brings good news of happiness, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, "Your God reigns!"
[Isaiah] [52]:[8] Listen! Your watchmen lift up their voices; together they shout for joy. For with their own eyes they will see the LORD returning to Zion.
[Isaiah] [52]:[9] Break out together into songs of joy, you ruins of Jerusalem, for the LORD has comforted his people; he has redeemed Jerusalem.
[Isaiah] [52]:[10] The LORD has bared his holy arm in the sight of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
[Isaiah] [52]:[11] Depart, depart, go out from there! Touch nothing unclean! Come out from her midst; purify yourselves, you who carry the vessels of the LORD.
[Isaiah] [52]:[12] But you will not leave in haste, nor will you go in flight; for the LORD goes before you, and the God of Israel is your rear guard.
[Isaiah] [52]:[13] See, my servant will prosper; he will be raised and lifted up and highly exalted.
[Isaiah] [52]:[14] Just as many were appalled at him—his appearance was so disfigured, beyond that of any man, and his form beyond human likeness—
[Isaiah] [52]:[15] so he will sprinkle many nations, and kings will shut their mouths because of him. For what they were never told, they will see, and what they never heard, they will understand.
[Isaiah] [53]:[1] Who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?
[Isaiah] [53]:[2] He grew up before him like a young shoot, like a root out of dry ground. He had no beauty, no majesty to draw our eyes, nothing in his appearance that we should desire him.
[Isaiah] [53]:[3] He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief. Like one from whom people hide their faces, he was despised, and we held him of no account.
[Isaiah] [53]:[4] Yet it was our griefs he bore, our sorrows he carried; but we considered him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.
[Isaiah] [53]:[5] But he was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought us peace was laid upon him, and by his wounds we are healed.
[Isaiah] [53]:[6] All of us have strayed like sheep; each one has turned to his own way. And the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
[Isaiah] [53]:[7] He was oppressed and afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth. Like a lamb led to the slaughter, like a sheep silent before its shearers, he did not open his mouth.
[Isaiah] [53]:[8] By oppression and judgment he was taken away. And who of his generation gave it a thought? For he was cut off from the land of the living, stricken for the transgression of my people.
[Isaiah] [53]:[9] They assigned him a grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death, though he had done no violence, nor was there any deceit in his mouth.
[Isaiah] [53]:[10] Yet it was the LORD's will to crush him and cause him to suffer. When he makes his life a guilt offering, he will see his offspring and prolong his days, and the will of the LORD will prosper in his hand.
[Isaiah] [53]:[11] Out of the anguish of his soul he will see and be satisfied. By his knowledge my righteous servant will justify many, and he will bear their iniquities.
[Isaiah] [53]:[12] Therefore I will give him a portion among the great, and he will divide the spoils with the strong, because he poured out his life unto death and was numbered with the transgressors. For he bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors.
[Isaiah] [54]:[1] Sing, barren woman, you who never bore a child; break into song and shout for joy, you who never went into labor. For the children of the desolate woman are more than the children of her who has a husband, says the LORD.
[Isaiah] [54]:[2] Enlarge the site of your tent, stretch out the curtains of your dwellings — do not hold back. Lengthen your ropes and drive your stakes deep.
[Isaiah] [54]:[3] For you will spread out to the right and to the left; your offspring will possess the nations and settle the desolate cities.
[Isaiah] [54]:[4] Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame; do not be dismayed, for you will not be disgraced. You will forget the shame of your youth and remember no more the reproach of your widowhood.
[Isaiah] [54]:[5] For your Maker is your husband — the LORD of hosts is his name — and your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel; he is called the God of all the earth.
[Isaiah] [54]:[6] The LORD has called you back like a wife deserted and grieved in spirit, like a wife married in youth only to be rejected, says your God.
[Isaiah] [54]:[7] For a brief moment I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will gather you back.
[Isaiah] [54]:[8] In a surge of anger I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting love I will have compassion on you, says the LORD, your Redeemer.
[Isaiah] [54]:[9] For me this is like the waters of Noah: as I swore that the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth, so I have sworn not to be angry with you, never to rebuke you again.
[Isaiah] [54]:[10] Though the mountains may depart and the hills be shaken, my steadfast love will not depart from you, nor will my covenant of peace be shaken, says the LORD, who has compassion on you.
[Isaiah] [54]:[11] Afflicted city, storm-tossed and uncomforted, I will set your stones in antimony and lay your foundations with sapphires.
[Isaiah] [54]:[12] I will make your battlements of rubies, your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.
[Isaiah] [54]:[13] All your children will be taught by the LORD, and great will be their peace.
[Isaiah] [54]:[14] You will be established in righteousness. Oppression will be far from you — you will have nothing to fear; terror will be far removed — it will not come near you.
