[Isaiah] [54]:[15] If anyone attacks you, it will not be from me; whoever attacks you will fall before you.
[Isaiah] [54]:[16] See, it is I who created the blacksmith who fans the coals into flame and forges a weapon fit for its work; and it is I who created the destroyer to wreak havoc.
[Isaiah] [54]:[17] No weapon forged against you will succeed, and you will refute every tongue that rises against you in judgment. This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their vindication from me, declares the LORD.
[Isaiah] [55]:[1] Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters! And you who have no money, come, buy and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money, without cost.
[Isaiah] [55]:[2] Why spend your silver on what is not bread, your labor on what does not satisfy? Listen carefully to me, and eat what is good; let your soul delight in the richest of fare.
[Isaiah] [55]:[3] Turn your ear and come to me; listen, and you will live. I will make an everlasting covenant with you, my faithful mercies promised to David.
[Isaiah] [55]:[4] See, I made him a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander of the nations.
[Isaiah] [55]:[5] See, you will summon a nation you do not know, and a nation that does not know you will run to you, for the sake of the LORD your God, and of the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you.
[Isaiah] [55]:[6] Seek the LORD while he may be found; call on him while he is near.
[Isaiah] [55]:[7] Let the wicked forsake his way and the evildoer his thoughts. Let him return to the LORD, and he will have mercy on him, and to our God, for he will freely pardon.
[Isaiah] [55]:[8] For my thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways my ways, declares the LORD.
[Isaiah] [55]:[9] As the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways and my thoughts than your thoughts.
[Isaiah] [55]:[10] As the rain and the snow come down from heaven and do not return there without watering the earth, making it bud and flourish, so that it yields seed for the sower and bread for the eater,
[Isaiah] [55]:[11] so is my word that goes out from my mouth: it will not return to me empty, but will accomplish what I desire and achieve the purpose for which I sent it.
[Isaiah] [55]:[12] You will go out with joy and be led forth in peace; the mountains and hills will break into song before you, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
[Isaiah] [55]:[13] Instead of the thornbush the cypress will rise, and instead of briers the myrtle will grow. This will bring renown to the LORD, an everlasting sign that will never be cut off.
[Isaiah] [56]:[1] This is what the LORD says: Keep justice and do what is right, for my salvation is close at hand and my righteousness is about to be revealed.
[Isaiah] [56]:[2] Blessed is the one who does this, the man who holds fast to it — who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.
[Isaiah] [56]:[3] Let no foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say, "The LORD will surely exclude me from his people." And let no eunuch say, "I am nothing but a withered tree."
[Isaiah] [56]:[4] For this is what the LORD says: To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, who choose what pleases me and hold fast to my covenant —
[Isaiah] [56]:[5] to them I will give, within my house and within my walls, a memorial and a name better than sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will never be cut off.
[Isaiah] [56]:[6] And the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD to serve him, to love the name of the LORD and to be his servants — all who keep the Sabbath without profaning it and hold fast to my covenant —
[Isaiah] [56]:[7] these I will bring to my holy mountain and give them joy in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
[Isaiah] [56]:[8] So declares the Lord GOD, who gathers the outcasts of Israel: I will gather still others to him, besides those already gathered to him.
[Isaiah] [56]:[9] All you beasts of the field, come and devour — all you beasts of the forest!
[Isaiah] [56]:[10] Israel's watchmen are blind, every one of them; they know nothing. They are all mute dogs that cannot bark, dreaming as they lie there, in love with sleep.
[Isaiah] [56]:[11] They are greedy dogs that never have enough. And they are shepherds who understand nothing; every one of them has turned to his own way, each seeking his own gain, to the last of them.
[Isaiah] [56]:[12] "Come," they say, "let me get some wine; let us drink our fill of strong drink! And tomorrow will be like today — even better, far grander!"
[Isaiah] [57]:[1] The righteous man perishes, and no one takes it to heart; the faithful are swept away, and no one understands that the righteous is taken away from the face of evil.
[Isaiah] [57]:[2] He enters into peace; they rest on their beds, all who walk in uprightness.
[Isaiah] [57]:[3] But you, come here, you children of a sorceress, offspring of an adulterer and a prostitute!
[Isaiah] [57]:[4] At whom are you sneering? At whom do you open your mouth wide and stick out your tongue? Are you not children of rebellion, offspring of lies—
[Isaiah] [57]:[5] you who burn with lust among the oaks, under every green tree, who slaughter your children in the ravines, under the clefts of the rocks?
[Isaiah] [57]:[6] Among the smooth stones of the valley is your portion; they, they are your lot. To them you poured out a drink offering, to them you brought your grain offering. Should I relent because of this?
[Isaiah] [57]:[7] On a high and lofty mountain you spread your bed, and there you went up to offer your sacrifice.
[Isaiah] [57]:[8] Behind the door and the doorpost you set up your idol. Turning away from me, you stripped yourself bare, you climbed up and made your bed wide; you struck your bargain with them, you loved their bed and gazed on their nakedness.
[Isaiah] [57]:[9] You went to the king with oil and heaped up your perfumes; you sent your envoys far away and went down as low as the grave.
[Isaiah] [57]:[10] You wore yourself out on your many roads, yet you never said, "It is hopeless." You found new strength for your hand, and so you did not grow weak.
[Isaiah] [57]:[11] Whom did you so dread and fear that you lied, and did not remember me or take it to heart? Is it not because I have kept silent, and that for so long, that you no longer fear me?
[Isaiah] [57]:[12] I myself will expose your righteousness and your deeds, and they will not help you.
[Isaiah] [57]:[13] When you cry out, let your collection of idols save you! The wind will carry them all off, a mere breath will sweep them away. But whoever takes refuge in me will inherit the land and possess my holy mountain.
[Isaiah] [57]:[14] And it will be said: Build up, build up, clear the road! Remove every obstacle from the way of my people.
[Isaiah] [57]:[15] For this is what the high and exalted One says, who lives forever, whose name is Holy: I dwell in the high and holy place, and also with the one who is crushed and humble in spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble and to revive the heart of the crushed.
[Isaiah] [57]:[16] For I will not accuse forever, nor will I always be angry; otherwise the spirit would fail before me, the very breath of life that I have made.
[Isaiah] [57]:[17] Because of his sinful greed I was angry; I struck him, I hid my face and was angry, yet he kept turning away, going his own willful way.
[Isaiah] [57]:[18] I have seen his ways, and I will heal him; I will lead him and give him comfort in full measure, him and those who mourn with him,
[Isaiah] [57]:[19] I create the word on the lips: Peace, peace to those far off and to those near, says the LORD, and I will heal him.
[Isaiah] [57]:[20] But the wicked are like the churning sea that cannot be still, whose waters toss up mire and mud.
[Isaiah] [57]:[21] "There is no peace," says my God, "for the wicked."
[Isaiah] [58]:[1] Shout it out, hold nothing back! Lift up your voice like a trumpet. Declare to my people their rebellion, to the house of Jacob their sins.
[Isaiah] [58]:[2] Day after day they seek me and delight to know my ways, like a nation that does what is right and has not forsaken the justice of its God. They ask me for righteous judgments; they delight to draw near to God.
[Isaiah] [58]:[3] "Why have we fasted, and you have not seen it? Why have we humbled ourselves, and you take no notice?" Look — on the day of your fast you pursue your own desires and drive all your laborers hard.
[Isaiah] [58]:[4] Look — you fast only to quarrel and fight and to strike with a wicked fist. Fasting as you do today will never make your voice heard on high.
[Isaiah] [58]:[5] Is this the fast I have chosen, a day for a man to humble himself? Is it to bow his head like a reed, to lie in sackcloth and ashes? Is that what you call a fast, a day acceptable to the LORD?
[Isaiah] [58]:[6] Is not this the fast I have chosen: to loosen the chains of injustice, to untie the cords of the yoke, to set the oppressed free, and to break every yoke?
[Isaiah] [58]:[7] Is it not to share your bread with the hungry and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to clothe him, and not to turn away from your own flesh and blood?
[Isaiah] [58]:[8] Then your light will break forth like the dawn, and your healing will spring up quickly. Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the LORD will be your rear guard.
[Isaiah] [58]:[9] Then you will call, and the LORD will answer; you will cry out, and he will say, "Here I am." If you rid yourself of the yoke, of the pointing finger and the malicious word,
[Isaiah] [58]:[10] if you give of yourself to the hungry and satisfy the needs of the afflicted, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your night will be like noonday.
[Isaiah] [58]:[11] The LORD will guide you continually; he will satisfy you in a sun-scorched land and strengthen your frame. You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.
[Isaiah] [58]:[12] Your people will rebuild the ancient ruins and raise up the age-old foundations; you will be called Repairer of Broken Walls, Restorer of Streets Where People Live.
[Isaiah] [58]:[13] If you keep your feet from breaking the Sabbath, from pursuing your own interests on my holy day; if you call the Sabbath a delight and the LORD's holy day honorable; if you honor it by not going your own way, not pursuing your own interests or speaking idle words —
[Isaiah] [58]:[14] then you will find your delight in the LORD, and I will make you ride on the heights of the land and feed you with the inheritance of your father Jacob. For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
[Isaiah] [59]:[1] Look, the LORD's hand is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear.
[Isaiah] [59]:[2] It is your sins that have made a separation between you and your God; your wrongdoing has hidden his face from you, so that he does not hear.
[Isaiah] [59]:[3] For your hands are defiled with blood and your fingers with guilt; your lips speak lies, your tongue mutters injustice.
[Isaiah] [59]:[4] No one calls for justice; no one pleads a case honestly. They trust in emptiness and speak worthless words; they conceive trouble and give birth to evil.
[Isaiah] [59]:[5] They hatch the eggs of vipers and weave the spider's web. Whoever eats their eggs dies, and when one is crushed, a viper breaks out.
[Isaiah] [59]:[6] Their webs will make no clothing; they cannot cover themselves with what they make. Their deeds are deeds of evil, and acts of violence fill their hands.
[Isaiah] [59]:[7] Their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are thoughts of wickedness; ruin and destruction mark their roads.
[Isaiah] [59]:[8] The way of peace they do not know, and there is no justice in their paths. They have made their roads crooked; no one who walks in them knows peace.
[Isaiah] [59]:[9] So justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us. We hope for light, but there is darkness; for brightness, but we walk in gloom.
[Isaiah] [59]:[10] We grope along the wall like the blind, we grope like those without eyes. We stumble at noon as if it were twilight; among the strong we are like the dead.
[Isaiah] [59]:[11] We all growl like bears and moan mournfully like doves. We hope for justice, but there is none; for salvation, but it stays far from us.
[Isaiah] [59]:[12] For our rebellions against you are many, and our sins testify against us. Our rebellions are with us, and we know our iniquities:
[Isaiah] [59]:[13] rebelling against the LORD and denying him, turning away from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving lies in the heart and uttering them.
[Isaiah] [59]:[14] So justice is driven back and righteousness stands at a distance; truth has stumbled in the public square, and honesty cannot enter.
[Isaiah] [59]:[15] Truth is nowhere to be found, and whoever turns from evil is plundered. The LORD saw it, and it was evil in his eyes that there was no justice.
[Isaiah] [59]:[16] He saw that there was no one, and he was appalled that no one intervened. So his own arm brought him salvation, and his righteousness sustained him.
[Isaiah] [59]:[17] He put on righteousness as armor and the helmet of salvation on his head; he clothed himself in the garments of vengeance and wrapped himself in zeal as a cloak.
[Isaiah] [59]:[18] According to their deeds he will repay: wrath to his adversaries, retribution to his enemies; to the coastlands he will render what is due.
[Isaiah] [59]:[19] for he will come like a pent-up river, driven by the breath of the LORD.[^1] [^1]: Or "when the adversary comes like a flood, the Spirit of the LORD will drive him back." The Hebrew word can mean either "narrow, pent-up" or "adversary."
[Isaiah] [59]:[20] "A Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from rebellion," declares the LORD.
[Isaiah] [59]:[21] "And as for me, this is my covenant with them," says the LORD: "My Spirit, who is upon you, and my words, which I have put in your mouth, will not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouths of your children, nor from the mouths of their descendants, from now on and forever," says the LORD.
[Isaiah] [60]:[1] Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
[Isaiah] [60]:[2] For look: darkness covers the earth, and thick darkness the peoples; but the LORD rises upon you, and his glory appears over you.
[Isaiah] [60]:[3] Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawning.
[Isaiah] [60]:[4] Lift up your eyes and look around: they all gather, they come to you. Your sons come from far away, and your daughters are carried on the hip.
[Isaiah] [60]:[5] Then you will see and be radiant, your heart will throb and swell with joy, for the riches of the sea will be turned toward you, the wealth of the nations will come to you.
[Isaiah] [60]:[6] Caravans of camels will cover you, young camels of Midian and Ephah; all of them will come from Sheba, bearing gold and frankincense, proclaiming the praises of the LORD.
[Isaiah] [60]:[7] All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you, the rams of Nebaioth will serve you; they will go up on my altar as an acceptable offering, and I will glorify my glorious house.
[Isaiah] [60]:[8] Who are these that fly like a cloud, like doves to their windows?
[Isaiah] [60]:[9] Surely the coastlands wait for me, the ships of Tarshish in the lead, to bring your sons from far away, their silver and their gold with them, for the name of the LORD your God, for the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you.
[Isaiah] [60]:[10] Foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their kings will serve you; for in my wrath I struck you, but in my favor I have shown you mercy.
[Isaiah] [60]:[11] Your gates will always stand open; day and night they will never be shut, so that the wealth of the nations may be brought to you, with their kings led in procession.
[Isaiah] [60]:[12] For the nation and kingdom that will not serve you will perish; those nations will be utterly laid waste.
[Isaiah] [60]:[13] The glory of Lebanon will come to you—cypress, plane, and pine together—to adorn the place of my sanctuary; and I will honor the place where my feet rest.
[Isaiah] [60]:[14] The children of your oppressors will come bowing before you; all who despised you will bow down at your feet. They will call you the City of the LORD, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
[Isaiah] [60]:[15] Whereas you were forsaken and hated, with no one passing through, I will make you the everlasting pride, the joy of all generations.
[Isaiah] [60]:[16] You will drink the milk of nations and nurse at the breasts of kings. Then you will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
[Isaiah] [60]:[17] Instead of bronze I will bring gold, instead of iron I will bring silver; instead of wood, bronze, and instead of stones, iron. I will make peace your governor and righteousness your ruler.
[Isaiah] [60]:[18] Violence will no longer be heard of in your land, nor ruin and destruction within your borders; you will call your walls Salvation and your gates Praise.
[Isaiah] [60]:[19] The sun will no longer be your light by day, nor will the moon shine on you with its brightness; the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.
[Isaiah] [60]:[20] Your sun will never set, and your moon will not wane; the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning will be ended.
[Isaiah] [60]:[21] Your people will all be righteous; they will possess the land forever—the shoot of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.
[Isaiah] [60]:[22] The least of them will become a thousand, the smallest a mighty nation. I am the LORD; in its time I will bring it about swiftly.
[Isaiah] [61]:[1] The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and release to those who are bound,
[Isaiah] [61]:[2] to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all who mourn,
[Isaiah] [61]:[3] to provide for those who mourn in Zion—to give them a crown instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of mourning, a garment of praise instead of a faint spirit. They will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, for his glory.
[Isaiah] [61]:[4] They will rebuild the ancient ruins and raise up what was long devastated; they will restore the ruined cities, desolate for generation after generation.
[Isaiah] [61]:[5] Strangers will stand and pasture your flocks, and foreigners will be your plowmen and vinedressers.
[Isaiah] [61]:[6] But you will be called priests of the LORD; they will speak of you as ministers of our God. You will feed on the wealth of the nations, and in their glory you will boast.
[Isaiah] [61]:[7] Instead of your shame you will have a double portion, and instead of disgrace they will shout for joy over their portion. Therefore in their land they will possess a double portion; everlasting joy will be theirs.
[Isaiah] [61]:[8] For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery and wrongdoing. I will faithfully give them their reward and make an everlasting covenant with them.
[Isaiah] [61]:[9] Their offspring will be known among the nations, their descendants among the peoples. All who see them will acknowledge that they are the offspring the LORD has blessed.
[Isaiah] [61]:[10] I will rejoice greatly in the LORD; my soul will exult in my God. For he has clothed me with the garments of salvation and wrapped me in the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom wears his priestly headdress, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
[Isaiah] [61]:[11] For as the earth brings forth its growth, and as a garden causes what is sown to spring up, so the Lord GOD will make righteousness and praise spring up before all the nations.
[Isaiah] [62]:[1] For Zion's sake I will not keep silent, for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until her righteousness breaks out like the dawn and her salvation blazes like a torch.
[Isaiah] [62]:[2] The nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory; and you will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will bestow.
[Isaiah] [62]:[3] You will be a crown of beauty in the LORD's hand, a royal diadem in the palm of your God.
[Isaiah] [62]:[4] No longer will you be called Forsaken, and no longer will your land be called Desolate; but you will be called My Delight Is in Her, and your land Married—for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
[Isaiah] [62]:[5] As a young man marries a virgin, so your sons will marry you; and as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
[Isaiah] [62]:[6] On your walls, Jerusalem, I have posted watchmen; all day and all night they will never be silent. You who remind the LORD, take no rest for yourselves,
[Isaiah] [62]:[7] and give him no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes her the praise of the earth.
[Isaiah] [62]:[8] The LORD has sworn by his right hand and by his mighty arm: "Never again will I give your grain to your enemies for food, and never again will foreigners drink the new wine for which you have labored.
[Isaiah] [62]:[9] But those who harvest the grain will eat it and praise the LORD, and those who gather the grapes will drink it in the courts of my sanctuary.
[Isaiah] [62]:[10] Pass through, pass through the gates! Clear the way for the people! Build up, build up the highway! Remove the stones! Raise a banner for the nations!
[Isaiah] [62]:[11] See, the LORD has proclaimed to the ends of the earth: Say to the daughter of Zion, "See, your salvation comes! See, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him."
[Isaiah] [62]:[12] They will be called the Holy People, the Redeemed of the LORD; and you will be called Sought After, a City No Longer Forsaken.
[Isaiah] [63]:[1] Who is this coming from Edom, from Bozrah in crimson-stained garments? Who is this, robed in splendor, striding forward in the greatness of his strength? "It is I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to save."
[Isaiah] [63]:[2] Why are your clothes red, your garments like one who treads the winepress?
[Isaiah] [63]:[3] "I have trodden the winepress alone; from the peoples no one was with me. I trod them down in my anger and trampled them in my wrath; their lifeblood spattered my garments, and I stained all my clothing.
[Isaiah] [63]:[4] For the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redemption had come.
[Isaiah] [63]:[5] I looked, but there was no one to help; I was appalled that no one gave support. So my own arm brought me victory, and my own wrath sustained me.
[Isaiah] [63]:[6] I trampled the peoples in my anger; in my wrath I made them drunk and poured out their lifeblood on the ground."
[Isaiah] [63]:[7] I will recount the steadfast love of the LORD, the praises of the LORD, for all that the LORD has done for us—the great goodness he has shown the house of Israel, according to his compassion and his abundant steadfast love.
[Isaiah] [63]:[8] He said, "Surely they are my people, children who will not act falsely." And he became their Savior.
[Isaiah] [63]:[9] In all their distress he too was distressed, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and in his pity he redeemed them; he lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.
[Isaiah] [63]:[10] But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit. So he turned and became their enemy, and he himself fought against them.
[Isaiah] [63]:[11] Then his people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses: Where is he who brought them up out of the sea, with the shepherds of his flock? Where is he who set his Holy Spirit among them,
[Isaiah] [63]:[12] who sent his glorious arm to go at the right hand of Moses, who divided the waters before them to make for himself an everlasting name,
[Isaiah] [63]:[13] who led them through the depths? Like a horse in the wilderness, they did not stumble;
[Isaiah] [63]:[14] like cattle going down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD gave them rest. So you led your people, to make for yourself a glorious name.
[Isaiah] [63]:[15] Look down from heaven and see, from your holy and glorious dwelling. Where are your zeal and your might? The stirring of your heart and your compassion are held back from me.
[Isaiah] [63]:[16] Yet you are our Father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us. You, LORD, are our Father; our Redeemer from of old is your name.
[Isaiah] [63]:[17] Why, LORD, do you let us wander from your ways and harden our hearts so we do not fear you? Return, for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your inheritance.
[Isaiah] [63]:[18] For a little while your holy people held possession; now our enemies have trampled down your sanctuary.
[Isaiah] [63]:[19] We have become like those you have never ruled, like those never called by your name. Oh, that you would tear open the heavens and come down, that the mountains would quake before you!
[Isaiah] [64]:[1] As fire sets brushwood ablaze and makes water boil, come down to make your name known to your enemies, so that the nations tremble before you.
[Isaiah] [64]:[2] When you did awesome things we did not look for, you came down, and the mountains melted away before you.
[Isaiah] [64]:[3] From ages past no one has heard, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen any God but you, who acts for the one who waits for him.
[Isaiah] [64]:[4] You come to meet those who rejoice to do what is right, who remember you in your ways. But you were angry, for we went on sinning; in our sins we have lived a long time—can we still be saved?
[Isaiah] [64]:[5] We have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteous deeds are like a filthy garment. We all wither like a leaf, and our sins sweep us away like the wind.
[Isaiah] [64]:[6] No one calls on your name or rouses himself to take hold of you, for you have hidden your face from us and made us waste away in the grip of our sins.
[Isaiah] [64]:[7] Yet, LORD, you are our Father. We are the clay, and you are the potter; we are all the work of your hand.
[Isaiah] [64]:[8] Do not be angry beyond measure, LORD; do not remember our sin forever. Look upon us, we pray: we are all your people.
[Isaiah] [64]:[9] Your holy cities have become a wilderness; Zion has become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
[Isaiah] [64]:[10] Our holy and glorious house, where our fathers praised you, has been burned with fire, and all that we treasured lies in ruins.
[Isaiah] [64]:[11] After all this, LORD, will you hold back? Will you keep silent and afflict us beyond measure?
[Isaiah] [65]:[1] I let myself be sought by those who never asked for me; I let myself be found by those who never looked for me. I said, "Here I am, here I am," to a nation that never called on my name.
[Isaiah] [65]:[2] All day long I have held out my hands to a rebellious people, who walk a path that is not good, following their own devices—
[Isaiah] [65]:[3] a people who provoke me to my face without ceasing, sacrificing in gardens and burning incense on bricks,
[Isaiah] [65]:[4] who sit among the graves and spend the night in secret places, who eat the flesh of swine, with broth of foul things in their pots,
[Isaiah] [65]:[5] who say, "Keep your distance! Do not come near me, for I am holier than you." These are smoke in my nostrils, a fire that smolders all day long.
[Isaiah] [65]:[6] See, it stands written before me: I will not keep silent, but I will repay—I will repay it into their lap,
[Isaiah] [65]:[7] your own sins together with the sins of your fathers, says the LORD. Because they burned incense on the mountains and defied me on the hills, I will measure out into their lap the wages of their former deeds.
[Isaiah] [65]:[8] This is what the LORD says: As when juice is still found in a cluster of grapes and someone says, "Do not destroy it, there is a blessing in it," so will I do for the sake of my servants: I will not destroy them all.
[Isaiah] [65]:[9] I will bring forth offspring from Jacob, and from Judah those who will possess my mountains. My chosen ones will possess it, and my servants will dwell there.
[Isaiah] [65]:[10] Sharon will become a pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a resting place for cattle, for my people who seek me.
[Isaiah] [65]:[11] But as for you who forsake the LORD and forget my holy mountain, who spread a table for Fortune and fill cups of mixed wine for Destiny—
[Isaiah] [65]:[12] I will assign you to the sword, and you will all bow down for the slaughter. For I called and you did not answer; I spoke and you did not listen. You did what is evil in my eyes and chose what displeases me.
[Isaiah] [65]:[13] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: My servants will eat, but you will go hungry; my servants will drink, but you will go thirsty; my servants will rejoice, but you will be put to shame.
[Isaiah] [65]:[14] My servants will sing out of gladness of heart, but you will cry out from anguish of heart and wail from a broken spirit.
[Isaiah] [65]:[15] You will leave your name behind as a curse to my chosen ones; the Lord GOD will put you to death, but his servants he will call by another name.
[Isaiah] [65]:[16] Whoever invokes a blessing in the land will do so by the God of truth, and whoever swears an oath in the land will swear by the God of truth. For the former troubles are forgotten, and hidden from my eyes.
[Isaiah] [65]:[17] See, I am creating new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.
[Isaiah] [65]:[18] Instead, rejoice and be glad forever in what I create; for I am about to create Jerusalem as a delight and her people as a joy.
[Isaiah] [65]:[19] I will rejoice over Jerusalem and delight in my people; the sound of weeping and crying will never be heard in her again.
[Isaiah] [65]:[20] Never again will there be an infant who lives but a few days, or an old man who does not live out his years. The one who dies at a hundred will be thought a mere youth, and the sinner who reaches only a hundred will be considered cursed.
[Isaiah] [65]:[21] They will build houses and live in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
[Isaiah] [65]:[22] They will not build for another to inhabit, nor plant for another to eat. For my people's days will be like the days of a tree, and my chosen ones will long enjoy the work of their hands.
[Isaiah] [65]:[23] They will not labor in vain, nor bear children for calamity; for they are offspring blessed by the LORD, they and their descendants with them.
[Isaiah] [65]:[24] Before they call, I will answer; while they are still speaking, I will hear.
[Isaiah] [65]:[25] The wolf and the lamb will graze together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox, but the serpent's food will be dust. They will do no harm and work no ruin on all my holy mountain, says the LORD.
[Isaiah] [66]:[1] This is what the LORD says: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. Where, then, is the house you would build for me? Where is the place of my rest?
[Isaiah] [66]:[2] My own hand made all these things, and so they all came to be, declares the LORD. But this is the one I look upon: the humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at my word.
[Isaiah] [66]:[3] Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who kills a man; whoever sacrifices a lamb, like one who breaks a dog's neck; whoever presents a grain offering, like one who offers pig's blood; whoever burns incense, like one who blesses an idol. They have chosen their own ways, and their souls delight in their abominations.
[Isaiah] [66]:[4] So I in turn will choose harsh treatment for them and bring upon them the very thing they dread. For I called, and no one answered; I spoke, and they did not listen. They did what was evil in my eyes and chose what did not please me.
[Isaiah] [66]:[5] Hear the word of the LORD, you who tremble at his word: Your own brothers, who hate you and cast you out for my name's sake, have said, "Let the LORD show his glory, so we may see your joy!" But they are the ones who will be put to shame.
[Isaiah] [66]:[6] An uproar from the city! A sound from the temple! The voice of the LORD, repaying his enemies what they deserve!
[Isaiah] [66]:[7] Before she was in labor, she gave birth; before the pains came upon her, she delivered a son.
[Isaiah] [66]:[8] Who has ever heard of such a thing? Who has ever seen the like? Can a land be born in a single day? Can a nation be brought forth in a moment? Yet no sooner was Zion in labor than she gave birth to her children.
[Isaiah] [66]:[9] Shall I bring to the point of birth and not deliver? says the LORD. Shall I who bring forth close the womb? says your God.
[Isaiah] [66]:[10] Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad for her, all you who love her. Exult with her in joy, all you who mourn over her,
[Isaiah] [66]:[11] so that you may nurse and be satisfied at her comforting breasts, so that you may drink deeply and delight in her abundant glory.
[Isaiah] [66]:[12] For this is what the LORD says: I am about to extend peace to her like a river, and the wealth of the nations like a flooding stream. You will nurse and be carried on her hip and dandled on her knees.
[Isaiah] [66]:[13] As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you; in Jerusalem you will be comforted.
[Isaiah] [66]:[14] You will see it, and your heart will rejoice; your bones will flourish like new grass. The hand of the LORD will be made known to his servants, but his fury against his enemies.
[Isaiah] [66]:[15] See, the LORD is coming with fire, and his chariots like a whirlwind, to unleash his anger in wrath and his rebuke with flames of fire.
[Isaiah] [66]:[16] For with fire and with his sword the LORD will execute judgment on all flesh, and many will be the slain of the LORD.
[Isaiah] [66]:[17] Those who consecrate and purify themselves to go into the gardens, following the one in the middle,^f who eat the flesh of pigs and vermin and mice—they will all come to an end together, declares the LORD.
[Isaiah] [66]:[18] For I know their deeds and their thoughts. The time is coming when I will gather all nations and tongues, and they will come and see my glory.
[Isaiah] [66]:[19] I will set a sign among them, and from among them I will send survivors to the nations—to Tarshish, to Put and Lud who draw the bow, to Tubal and Greece, and to the distant coastlands that have never heard my fame or seen my glory. And they will proclaim my glory among the nations.
[Isaiah] [66]:[20] They will bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the LORD—on horses and in chariots and wagons, on mules and camels—to my holy mountain, Jerusalem, says the LORD, just as the Israelites bring their grain offering in clean vessels to the house of the LORD.
[Isaiah] [66]:[21] And some of them I will take as priests and Levites, says the LORD.
[Isaiah] [66]:[22] For just as the new heavens and the new earth that I am making will endure before me, declares the LORD, so your offspring and your name will endure.
[Isaiah] [66]:[23] From new moon to new moon and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all flesh will come to bow down before me, says the LORD.
[Isaiah] [66]:[24] And they will go out and look on the corpses of those who rebelled against me. For their worm will not die, their fire will not be quenched, and they will be a horror to all flesh.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[1] The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests at Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[2] The word of the LORD came to him in the thirteenth year of the reign of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah,
[Jeremiah] [1]:[3] and it continued to come throughout the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, when Jerusalem was carried into exile in the fifth month.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[4] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Jeremiah] [1]:[5] "Before I formed you in the womb I knew you; before you were born I set you apart. I appointed you a prophet to the nations."
[Jeremiah] [1]:[6] Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! I do not know how to speak—I am only a boy."
[Jeremiah] [1]:[7] But the LORD said to me, "Do not say, 'I am only a boy.' You will go wherever I send you, and you will speak whatever I command you.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[8] Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, declares the LORD."
[Jeremiah] [1]:[9] Then the LORD reached out his hand and touched my mouth, and the LORD said to me, "See, I have put my words in your mouth.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[10] See, today I appoint you over nations and kingdoms: to uproot and tear down, to destroy and overthrow, to build and to plant.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[11] The word of the LORD came to me: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" "I see a branch of an almond tree," I answered.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew word for "almond tree" (shaqed) sounds like the word for "watching" (shoqed) in the next verse.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[12] Then the LORD said to me, "You have seen well, for I am watching over my word to carry it out."
[Jeremiah] [1]:[13] Again the word of the LORD came to me: "What do you see?" "I see a boiling pot," I answered, "tilted away from the north."
[Jeremiah] [1]:[14] Then the LORD said to me: "Out of the north disaster will break loose on all who live in the land.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[15] For I am summoning all the tribes of the kingdoms of the north, declares the LORD. They will come, and each will set up his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, against all her surrounding walls and against all the cities of Judah.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[16] I will pronounce my judgments against them for all their wickedness in forsaking me, in burning incense to other gods, and in worshiping the works of their own hands.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[17] Now brace yourself, stand up and tell them everything I command you. Do not be terrified of them, or I will terrify you before them.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[18] Today I have made you a fortified city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls against the whole land—against the kings of Judah, its officials, its priests, and the people of the land.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[19] They will fight against you but will not overcome you, for I am with you to deliver you, declares the LORD."
[Jeremiah] [2]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Jeremiah] [2]:[2] Go and proclaim in the hearing of Jerusalem: This is what the LORD says: I remember the devotion of your youth, your love as a bride, how you followed me through the wilderness, through a land not sown.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[3] Israel was holy to the LORD, the firstfruits of his harvest. All who devour him incur guilt; disaster comes upon them, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[4] Hear the word of the LORD, house of Jacob, all you clans of the house of Israel.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[5] This is what the LORD says: What fault did your fathers find in me, that they went far from me, chasing after worthless things and becoming worthless themselves?
[Jeremiah] [2]:[6] They did not ask, "Where is the LORD, who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and ravines, a land of drought and deep darkness, a land no one crosses and where no one lives?"
[Jeremiah] [2]:[7] I brought you into a fruitful land to eat its fruit and its good things. But you came and defiled my land, and made my inheritance detestable.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[8] The priests did not ask, "Where is the LORD?" Those who handle the law did not know me; the shepherds rebelled against me. The prophets prophesied by Baal and followed what has no worth.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[9] Therefore I bring my case against you again, declares the LORD, and against your children's children I will bring it.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[10] Cross over to the shores of Cyprus and look; send to Kedar and observe closely; see whether anything like this has ever happened.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[11] Has any nation ever exchanged its gods, though they are no gods at all? Yet my people have exchanged their Glory for what has no worth.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[12] Be appalled at this, you heavens; shudder and be utterly desolate, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[13] For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and dug for themselves cisterns—cracked cisterns that cannot hold water.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[14] Is Israel a slave? Was he born into servitude? Why then has he become plunder?
[Jeremiah] [2]:[15] Young lions have roared over him; they have raised their voices. They have laid his land waste; his cities are burned, left without inhabitants.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[16] Even the men of Memphis and Tahpanhes have shaved the crown of your head.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[17] Have you not brought this on yourself by forsaking the LORD your God while he was leading you along the way?
[Jeremiah] [2]:[18] And now, what do you gain by going to Egypt to drink the waters of the Nile? What do you gain by going to Assyria to drink the waters of the River?
[Jeremiah] [2]:[19] Your own wickedness will discipline you; your own backsliding will rebuke you. Consider and see how evil and bitter it is for you to forsake the LORD your God and to have no fear of me, declares the Lord, the LORD of hosts.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[20] Long ago I broke your yoke and tore off your bonds, but you said, "I will not serve." Instead, on every high hill and under every green tree you lay down as a prostitute.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[21] I planted you as a choice vine, from wholly reliable seed. How then did you turn against me, becoming a degenerate, foreign vine?
[Jeremiah] [2]:[22] Though you wash yourself with lye and use soap in abundance, the stain of your guilt remains before me, declares the Lord GOD.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[23] How can you say, "I am not defiled; I have not run after the Baals"? Look at your way in the valley; know what you have done—a restless young camel running here and there,
[Jeremiah] [2]:[24] a wild donkey at home in the wilderness, sniffing the wind in her craving—when she is in heat, who can turn her back? Any who seek her need not weary themselves; in her month they will find her.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[25] Keep your feet from going bare and your throat from thirst. But you said, "It is hopeless. No! I love strangers, and after them I will go."
[Jeremiah] [2]:[26] As a thief is disgraced when he is caught, so the house of Israel is disgraced—they, their kings and their officials, their priests and their prophets—
[Jeremiah] [2]:[27] who say to a tree, "You are my father," and to a stone, "You gave me birth." They have turned their backs to me and not their faces; yet in their time of trouble they say, "Rise up and save us!"
[Jeremiah] [2]:[28] But where are the gods you made for yourselves? Let them rise up and save you in your time of trouble, for your gods are as many as your cities, Judah.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[29] Why do you bring a case against me? You have all rebelled against me, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[30] In vain I struck your children; they accepted no correction. Your own sword devoured your prophets like a ravening lion.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[31] You of this generation, consider the word of the LORD: Have I been a wilderness to Israel, or a land of thick darkness? Why then do my people say, "We are free to roam; we will come to you no more"?
[Jeremiah] [2]:[32] Does a young woman forget her jewelry, a bride her wedding sash? Yet my people have forgotten me days without number.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[33] How skillfully you arrange your ways to seek out love! Therefore you have even taught your ways to wicked women.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[34] On your skirts is found the lifeblood of the innocent poor, though you did not catch them breaking in. Yet in spite of all this
[Jeremiah] [2]:[35] you say, "I am innocent; surely his anger has turned from me." Now I will bring you to judgment because you say, "I have not sinned."
[Jeremiah] [2]:[36] Why do you wander about so much, changing your way? You will be put to shame by Egypt too, as you were put to shame by Assyria.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[37] From this one too you will go out with your hands on your head, for the LORD has rejected those you trust, and you will not prosper through them.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[1] If a man divorces his wife and she leaves him and marries another man, can he ever go back to her? Would not that land be utterly defiled? And you have played the whore with many lovers—yet you would return to me? declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[2] Lift up your eyes to the barren heights and look: where have you not been violated? You sat waiting by the roadsides like a nomad in the desert, and you defiled the land with your whoring and your wickedness.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[3] So the showers were withheld, and no spring rain came. Yet you kept the brazen face of a prostitute; you refused to be ashamed.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[4] Have you not just now called to me, "My Father, you are the friend of my youth"?
[Jeremiah] [3]:[5] "Will he be angry forever? Will he hold his wrath to the end?" This is how you speak—while you do all the evil you can.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[6] In the days of King Josiah the LORD said to me: Have you seen what faithless Israel has done? She went up on every high hill and under every green tree, and there she played the whore.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[7] I thought that after she had done all this she would return to me, but she did not return. And her treacherous sister Judah saw it.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[8] I saw that for all the adulteries of faithless Israel I had sent her away and given her a certificate of divorce. Yet her treacherous sister Judah was not afraid; she too went and played the whore.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[9] With her reckless whoring she defiled the land, committing adultery with stone and wood.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[10] And through all of this her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with all her heart, but only in pretense, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[11] Then the LORD said to me: Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[12] Go and proclaim these words toward the north: Return, faithless Israel, declares the LORD. I will not look on you in anger, for I am merciful, declares the LORD; I will not be angry forever.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[13] Only acknowledge your guilt: you rebelled against the LORD your God, you scattered your favors among strangers under every green tree, and you did not obey my voice, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[14] Return, faithless children, declares the LORD, for I am your master. I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[15] I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will shepherd you with knowledge and understanding.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[16] And when you have increased and multiplied in the land in those days, declares the LORD, no one will say any more, "The ark of the covenant of the LORD." It will not come to mind; no one will remember it or miss it, and it will not be made again.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[17] At that time Jerusalem will be called the throne of the LORD, and all the nations will gather to it, to the name of the LORD in Jerusalem. No longer will they follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[18] In those days the house of Judah will join the house of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land I gave your fathers as an inheritance.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[19] I had said: How gladly would I set you among my children and give you a pleasant land, the most beautiful heritage of all the nations! And I thought you would call me "My Father" and never turn away from following me.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[20] But like a wife unfaithful to her husband, so you have been unfaithful to me, house of Israel, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[21] A sound is heard on the barren heights—the weeping and pleading of the people of Israel, because they have twisted their ways and forgotten the LORD their God.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[22] Return, faithless children; I will heal your faithlessness. "Here we are, we come to you, for you are the LORD our God.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[23] Surely the hills are a delusion, the uproar on the mountains is a lie. Surely in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[24] From our youth the shameful thing has devoured what our fathers toiled for—their flocks and herds, their sons and daughters.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[25] Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us. We have sinned against the LORD our God, we and our fathers, from our youth to this day, and we have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God."
[Jeremiah] [4]:[1] If you return, Israel, declares the LORD, return to me. If you remove your detestable idols from my presence and no longer stray,
[Jeremiah] [4]:[2] and if you swear, "As the LORD lives," in truth, in justice, and in righteousness, then the nations will be blessed in him, and in him they will boast.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[3] For this is what the LORD says to the people of Judah and to Jerusalem: Break up your fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[4] Circumcise yourselves to the LORD; remove the foreskin of your hearts, people of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, or my wrath will break out like fire and burn with no one to quench it, because of the evil of your deeds.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[5] Announce it in Judah, proclaim it in Jerusalem, and say: Blow the trumpet through the land! Cry aloud and say: Gather together! Let us flee to the fortified cities!
[Jeremiah] [4]:[6] Raise a signal toward Zion! Take flight, do not stand still! For I am bringing disaster from the north, and terrible destruction.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[7] A lion has come up from his thicket; a destroyer of nations has set out. He has left his place to lay your land waste; your cities will be ruins, without an inhabitant.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[8] For this, put on sackcloth, mourn and wail, for the burning anger of the LORD has not turned away from us.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[9] On that day, declares the LORD, the heart of the king will fail, and the heart of the officials; the priests will be appalled and the prophets astounded.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[10] Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! How completely you have deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, 'You will have peace,' while the sword reaches to the throat!"
[Jeremiah] [4]:[11] At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: A scorching wind from the barren heights of the desert blows toward the daughter of my people—not to winnow, not to cleanse—
[Jeremiah] [4]:[12] a wind far stronger than these comes from me. Now I will pronounce my judgments against them.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[13] Look! He comes up like clouds; his chariots are like a whirlwind, his horses swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we are ruined!
[Jeremiah] [4]:[14] Wash the evil from your heart, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will you harbor wicked schemes within you?
[Jeremiah] [4]:[15] A voice declares from Dan, proclaiming disaster from the hill country of Ephraim.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[16] Warn the nations, announce it concerning Jerusalem: Besiegers are coming from a distant land; they raise their war cry against the cities of Judah.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[17] They surround her like watchmen over a field, because she has rebelled against me, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[18] Your ways and your deeds have brought this upon you. This is your calamity—how bitter it is, how it pierces your very heart!
[Jeremiah] [4]:[19] My anguish, my anguish! I writhe in pain. Oh, the walls of my heart! My heart pounds within me; I cannot keep silent, for my very soul has heard the sound of the trumpet, the battle cry.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[20] Disaster upon disaster is announced; the whole land is laid waste. In an instant my tents are destroyed, my curtains in a moment.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[21] How long must I see the signal and hear the sound of the trumpet?
[Jeremiah] [4]:[22] For my people are foolish; they do not know me. They are senseless children with no understanding. They are skilled at doing evil, but they do not know how to do good.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[23] I looked at the earth, and it was formless and empty; and at the heavens, and their light was gone.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[24] I looked at the mountains, and they were quaking; all the hills were reeling.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[25] I looked, and there was no one at all; every bird of the sky had fled.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[26] I looked, and the fruitful land was a desert; all its cities were torn down before the LORD, before his burning anger.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[27] For this is what the LORD says: The whole land will be desolate, though I will not destroy it completely.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[28] For this the earth will mourn and the heavens above grow dark, because I have spoken and I have purposed; I will not relent, and I will not turn back.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[29] At the sound of horsemen and archers, every town takes flight. They creep into thickets and climb among the rocks. Every town is abandoned; no one lives in them.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[30] And you, devastated one—what are you doing, dressing in scarlet, adorning yourself with gold, enlarging your eyes with paint? You beautify yourself in vain. Your lovers despise you; they seek your life.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[31] For I hear a cry like a woman in labor, anguish like one giving birth to her first child—the cry of the daughter of Zion, gasping for breath, stretching out her hands: "Woe to me! I am fainting before my killers."
[Jeremiah] [5]:[1] Roam the streets of Jerusalem, look and see; search her squares. If you can find one person, if there is even one who does justice and seeks faithfulness, then I will forgive her.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[2] Even when they say, "As the LORD lives," they are swearing falsely.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[3] O LORD, do your eyes not look for faithfulness? You struck them, but they felt no pain; you consumed them, but they refused to take correction. They set their faces harder than rock; they refused to turn back.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[4] So I thought, "These are only the poor; they are foolish, for they do not know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[5] Let me go to the great ones and speak with them, for they know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God." But they, one and all, had broken the yoke and torn off the bonds.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[6] Therefore a lion from the forest will strike them down, a wolf of the desert will ravage them. A leopard lies in wait by their cities; whoever ventures out will be torn to pieces. For their rebellions are many, their turnings away are countless.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[7] Why should I forgive you? Your children have abandoned me and sworn by gods that are no gods. I fed them full, and they committed adultery; they crowded into the house of the prostitute.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[8] They were well-fed, lusty stallions, each one neighing after his neighbor's wife.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[9] Shall I not punish them for this? declares the LORD. Shall I not avenge myself on a nation such as this?
[Jeremiah] [5]:[10] Go up through her rows of vines and destroy, but do not finish them off. Strip away her branches, for they do not belong to the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[11] For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have been utterly faithless to me, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[12] They have denied the LORD and said, "It is not he! No disaster will come upon us; we will never see sword or famine.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[13] The prophets are only wind, and the word is not in them. So let it be done to them!"
[Jeremiah] [5]:[14] Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of hosts, says: Because you have spoken these words, I am making my words in your mouth a fire, and this people the wood it consumes.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[15] Listen, house of Israel: I am bringing a nation against you from far away, declares the LORD—an enduring nation, an ancient nation, a nation whose language you do not know and whose speech you cannot understand.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[16] Their quiver is an open grave; all of them are warriors.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[17] They will devour your harvest and your bread; they will devour your sons and your daughters; they will devour your flocks and herds; they will devour your vines and fig trees. With the sword they will batter down your fortified cities in which you trust.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[18] Yet even in those days, declares the LORD, I will not make an end of you.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[19] And when they ask, "Why has the LORD our God done all this to us?" you are to tell them, "Just as you abandoned me and served foreign gods in your own land, so you will serve strangers in a land that is not yours."
[Jeremiah] [5]:[20] Announce this in the house of Jacob, proclaim it in Judah:
[Jeremiah] [5]:[21] Hear this, you foolish people, without understanding—you have eyes but do not see, ears but do not hear.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[22] Do you not fear me? declares the LORD. Do you not tremble before me? I set the sand as a boundary for the sea, an everlasting limit it cannot cross. The waves rage, but they cannot prevail; they roar, but they cannot pass it.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[23] But this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart; they have turned aside and gone their own way.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[24] They do not say in their hearts, "Let us fear the LORD our God, who gives the rains in their season, the autumn rain and the spring rain, who keeps for us the appointed weeks of harvest."
[Jeremiah] [5]:[25] Your wrongdoings have turned these away; your sins have withheld the good from you.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[26] For among my people are wicked men. They lie in wait like fowlers crouching; they set a deadly snare, and it is people they catch.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[27] Like a cage full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit. That is why they have grown great and rich;
[Jeremiah] [5]:[28] they are fat and sleek. They even overflow with deeds of evil; they do not defend the cause of the fatherless, yet they prosper, and they do not uphold the rights of the needy.
[Jeremiah] [5]:[29] Shall I not punish them for this? declares the LORD. Shall I not avenge myself on a nation such as this?
[Jeremiah] [5]:[30] An appalling and horrifying thing has happened in the land:
[Jeremiah] [5]:[31] the prophets prophesy lies, the priests rule by their own authority, and my people love it so. But what will you do in the end of it all?
[Jeremiah] [6]:[1] Flee for safety, people of Benjamin, out of Jerusalem! Blow the ram's horn in Tekoa, raise a signal over Beth-haccherem, for disaster looms out of the north, a great destruction.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[2] So lovely and delicate is Daughter Zion—and I will destroy her.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[3] Shepherds and their flocks will come against her; they will pitch their tents all around her, each grazing his own portion.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[4] "Prepare for holy battle against her! Up, let us attack at noon!" "Woe to us, for the day is fading, the evening shadows stretch long."
[Jeremiah] [6]:[5] "Up, then, let us attack by night and destroy her palaces!"
[Jeremiah] [6]:[6] For this is what the LORD of hosts says: Cut down her trees, throw up a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This is the city marked for punishment; there is nothing but oppression within her.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[7] As a well keeps its water fresh, so she keeps her wickedness fresh. Violence and ruin resound in her; sickness and wounds are always before me.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[8] Take warning, Jerusalem, or I will turn away from you in disgust and make you a wasteland, a land where no one lives.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[9] This is what the LORD of hosts says: They will glean the remnant of Israel as thoroughly as a vine is stripped; reach your hand over the shoots again, like a grape-picker.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[10] To whom can I speak and give warning, so that they will listen? Their ears are closed; they cannot pay attention. The word of the LORD has become an offense to them; they take no delight in it.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[11] But I am filled with the wrath of the LORD; I am weary of holding it in. Pour it out on the children in the street, and on the gatherings of young men as well! For even husband with wife will be taken, the aged along with those full of years.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[12] Their houses will be turned over to others, their fields and their wives as well, for I will stretch out my hand against those who live in the land, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[13] From the least of them to the greatest, all are greedy for unjust gain; from prophet to priest, all practice deceit.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[14] They dress the wound of my people as though it were nothing. 'Peace, peace,' they say, when there is no peace.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[15] Were they ashamed when they committed such abominations? No, they felt no shame at all; they did not even know how to blush. So they will fall among the fallen; when I punish them, they will go down, says the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[16] This is what the LORD says: Stand at the crossroads and look; ask for the ancient paths, where the good way lies, and walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, "We will not walk in it."
[Jeremiah] [6]:[17] I appointed watchmen over you: "Listen for the sound of the horn!" But they said, "We will not listen."
[Jeremiah] [6]:[18] Therefore hear, you nations; take note, you assembly, of what will happen to them.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[19] Hear, O earth: I am bringing disaster on this people, the fruit of their own schemes, because they have not listened to my words and have rejected my law.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[20] What is frankincense from Sheba to me, or sweet cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable; your sacrifices do not please me.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[21] Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am setting stumbling blocks before this people. Fathers and sons alike will stumble over them; neighbor and friend will perish.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[22] This is what the LORD says: Look, an army is coming from the land of the north; a great nation is stirring from the ends of the earth.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[23] They grip bow and spear; they are cruel and show no mercy. Their noise roars like the sea as they ride on horses, drawn up like men for battle against you, Daughter Zion.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[24] We have heard the report of them, and our hands hang limp. Anguish has seized us, pain like a woman in labor.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[25] Do not go out into the fields, do not walk on the roads, for the enemy has a sword, and terror is on every side.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[26] Daughter of my people, put on sackcloth and roll in ashes; mourn as for an only son, with bitter lament, for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[27] I have made you an assayer among my people, a fortified wall, that you may know and test their ways.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[28] They are all hardened rebels, going about as slanderers. They are bronze and iron; all of them act corruptly.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[29] The bellows blast fiercely, the lead is consumed by the fire, but the refining goes on in vain; the wicked are not purged away.
[Jeremiah] [6]:[30] They are called rejected silver, because the LORD has rejected them.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[1] The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
[Jeremiah] [7]:[2] Stand in the gate of the LORD's house and proclaim this word there: Hear the word of the LORD, all you of Judah who enter these gates to worship the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[3] This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Mend your ways and your deeds, and I will let you dwell in this place.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[4] Do not trust in deceptive words, chanting, "The temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD!"
[Jeremiah] [7]:[5] But if you truly mend your ways and your deeds, if you truly deal justly with one another,
[Jeremiah] [7]:[6] if you do not oppress the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, if you do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow other gods to your own ruin,
[Jeremiah] [7]:[7] then I will let you dwell in this place, in the land I gave to your fathers, from age to age.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[8] But look—you are trusting in deceptive words that are worth nothing.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[9] Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal, and follow other gods you have not known,
[Jeremiah] [7]:[10] and then come and stand before me in this house that bears my name, and say, "We are safe"—only to go on doing all these detestable things?
[Jeremiah] [7]:[11] Has this house that bears my name become a den of robbers in your eyes? I myself have seen it, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[12] Go now to my place at Shiloh, where I first made my name dwell, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[13] And now, because you have done all these things, declares the LORD—I spoke to you again and again, but you would not listen; I called you, but you would not answer—
[Jeremiah] [7]:[14] therefore I will do to this house that bears my name, the house you trust in, and to the place I gave to you and your fathers, what I did to Shiloh.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[15] I will cast you out of my presence, just as I cast out all your kinsmen, all the offspring of Ephraim.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[16] As for you, do not pray for this people; raise no cry or prayer on their behalf, and do not plead with me, for I will not listen to you.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[17] Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
[Jeremiah] [7]:[18] The children gather wood, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the Queen of Heaven; and they pour out drink offerings to other gods to provoke me to anger.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[19] But is it me they are provoking? declares the LORD. Is it not themselves, to their own shame?
[Jeremiah] [7]:[20] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: My anger and my fury will be poured out on this place—on man and beast, on the trees of the field and the fruit of the ground—and it will burn and not be quenched.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[21] This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Go ahead, pile your burnt offerings on your sacrifices and eat the meat yourselves!
[Jeremiah] [7]:[22] For when I brought your fathers out of the land of Egypt, I did not speak to them or command them concerning burnt offerings and sacrifices.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[23] But this is what I commanded them: Obey my voice, and I will be your God and you will be my people; walk in every way I command you, so that it may go well with you.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[24] But they did not listen or pay attention. They followed their own counsels, the stubbornness of their evil hearts, and went backward instead of forward.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[25] From the day your fathers came out of the land of Egypt until this day, I sent you all my servants the prophets, sending them again and again, day after day, early and late.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[26] Yet they did not listen to me or pay attention. They stiffened their necks and did worse than their fathers.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[27] So you will speak all these words to them, and they will not listen to you; you will call to them, and they will not answer you.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[28] Then say to them: This is the nation that would not obey the voice of the LORD its God or accept correction. Faithfulness has perished; it has vanished from their lips.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[29] Shear off your consecrated hair and throw it away; raise a lament on the barren heights, for the LORD has rejected and abandoned the generation of his wrath.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[30] For the people of Judah have done what is evil in my eyes, declares the LORD. They have set their detestable idols in the house that bears my name, defiling it.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[31] They have built the high places of Topheth in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, to burn their sons and daughters in the fire—something I never commanded and that never entered my mind.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[32] So the days are coming, declares the LORD, when it will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter; for they will bury in Topheth until there is no room left.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[33] The corpses of this people will become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth, with no one to drive them away.
[Jeremiah] [7]:[34] And I will silence in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem the sound of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, for the land will lie in ruins.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[1] At that time, declares the LORD, they will bring out from their graves the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of Judah's officials, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[2] They will spread them out before the sun and the moon and all the host of heaven, which they loved and served, which they followed and consulted and worshiped. They will not be gathered or buried; they will be like dung on the face of the ground.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[3] Then all who remain of this evil family will choose death rather than life, in every place where I have driven them, declares the LORD of hosts.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[4] You shall say to them: Thus says the LORD: When people fall, do they not get up again? When someone turns away, does he not turn back?
[Jeremiah] [8]:[5] Why then has this people, Jerusalem, turned away in perpetual apostasy? They cling to deceit; they refuse to return.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[6] I have listened and heard: they do not speak what is right. No one repents of his wickedness, saying, "What have I done?" Every one of them turns to his own course, like a horse plunging into battle.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[7] Even the stork in the sky knows her appointed seasons, and the dove, the swift, and the crane keep the time of their coming. But my people do not know the ordinance of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[8] How can you say, "We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us," when in fact the lying pen of the scribes has turned it into a lie?
[Jeremiah] [8]:[9] The wise will be put to shame; they will be dismayed and trapped. See, they have rejected the word of the LORD—so what wisdom do they have?
[Jeremiah] [8]:[10] Therefore I will give their wives to others and their fields to new owners. From the least to the greatest, all are greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, all practice deceit.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[11] They dress the wound of my people as though it were nothing, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[12] Are they ashamed of the abomination they have committed? No, they have no shame at all; they do not even know how to blush. So they will fall among the fallen; when I punish them, they will be brought down, says the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[13] I will surely gather them in, declares the LORD. There are no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree, and the leaves are withered; what I gave them is gone from them.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[14] Why are we sitting here? Gather together! Let us flee to the fortified cities and perish there. For the LORD our God has doomed us to perish and given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[15] We hoped for peace, but no good has come; for a time of healing, but there is only terror.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[16] From Dan the snorting of his horses is heard; at the neighing of his stallions the whole land trembles. They come and devour the land and everything in it, the city and all who live there.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[17] See, I am sending venomous snakes among you, vipers that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[18] My grief is beyond healing; my heart is sick within me.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[19] Listen—the cry of my people from a distant land: "Is the LORD not in Zion? Is her King no longer there?" Why have they provoked me to anger with their carved images, with their worthless foreign idols?
[Jeremiah] [8]:[20] "The harvest is past, the summer has ended, and we are not saved."
[Jeremiah] [8]:[21] For the wound of my people I am wounded; I mourn, and horror grips me.
[Jeremiah] [8]:[22] Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Why then has no healing come for the wound of my people?
[Jeremiah] [8]:[23] Oh, that my head were a spring of water and my eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of my people!
[Jeremiah] [9]:[1] If only I had a traveler's lodge out in the wilderness, that I might leave my people and go away from them! For they are all adulterers, a pack of traitors.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[2] They bend their tongues like bows; falsehood is their weapon. It is not for truth that they grow strong in the land. For they press on from evil to evil, and me they do not know, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[3] Guard yourselves, each of you, against your neighbor, and trust no brother; for every brother is a deceiver, and every neighbor goes about slandering.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[4] They cheat one another, and no one speaks the truth. They have trained their tongues to lie; they wear themselves out doing wrong.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[5] You live in the midst of deceit; through deceit they refuse to know me, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[6] Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says: I will refine them and test them—what else can I do with the daughter of my people?
[Jeremiah] [9]:[7] Their tongue is a deadly arrow; their words are deceit. With his mouth a man speaks peace to his neighbor, but inwardly he sets an ambush for him.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[8] Shall I not punish them for such things? declares the LORD. Shall I not avenge myself on a nation like this?
[Jeremiah] [9]:[9] For the mountains I will take up weeping and wailing, and for the wilderness pastures a lament, because they are scorched and empty, with no one passing through, and the sound of the herds is heard no more. From the birds of the sky to the animals, all have fled and are gone.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[10] I will make Jerusalem a heap of rubble, a lair of jackals, and the cities of Judah I will make a wasteland, with no one living there.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[11] Who is wise enough to understand this? To whom has the mouth of the LORD spoken, that he may explain it? Why has the land been ruined, scorched like a desert where no one passes through?
[Jeremiah] [9]:[12] And the LORD said: It is because they abandoned my law, which I set before them; they did not listen to my voice or walk by it.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[13] Instead they followed their own stubborn hearts and went after the Baals, as their fathers taught them.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[14] Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am going to feed this people bitter wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[15] I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send the sword after them until I have made an end of them.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[16] This is what the LORD of hosts says: Take note—call for the women who mourn, and let them come; send for the skilled ones, and let them come.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[17] Let them hurry and raise a lament over us, till our eyes run with tears and our eyelids stream with water.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[18] For a sound of wailing is heard from Zion: "How we are ruined! We are utterly disgraced, for we have left the land, for our homes have been torn down."
[Jeremiah] [9]:[19] Hear, you women, the word of the LORD; let your ears take in the word of his mouth. Teach your daughters this lament, and each one teach her neighbor this dirge:
[Jeremiah] [9]:[20] Death has climbed in through our windows; it has entered our fortresses, cutting down the children in the streets and the young men in the squares.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[21] Say this—thus declares the LORD: The corpses of men will lie like dung on the open field, like sheaves behind the reaper, with no one to gather them.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[22] This is what the LORD says: Let not the wise boast of his wisdom, let not the strong boast of his strength, let not the rich boast of his riches.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[23] But if anyone boasts, let him boast in this: that he understands and knows me—that I am the LORD, who acts with steadfast love, justice, and righteousness on the earth; for in these I delight, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [9]:[24] The days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish all who are circumcised only in the flesh:
[Jeremiah] [9]:[25] Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all who clip the hair at their temples, who live in the desert. For all these nations are uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[1] Hear the word the LORD has spoken concerning you, house of Israel.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[2] This is what the LORD says: Do not learn the ways of the nations, and do not be terrified by signs in the heavens, though the nations are terrified by them.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[3] For the customs of the peoples are worthless. A tree is cut from the forest and shaped by a craftsman's hands with a chisel.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[4] They adorn it with silver and gold and fasten it with hammer and nails so it will not topple.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[5] Like a scarecrow in a cucumber field they stand, and they cannot speak. They must be carried, for they cannot walk. Do not fear them; they can do no harm, and they have no power to do good.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[6] There is none like you, LORD. You are great, and your name is great in power.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[7] Who would not fear you, King of the nations? Reverence belongs to you. Among all the wise men of the nations and in all their kingdoms there is none like you.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[8] They are all senseless and foolish alike; the instruction of idols is nothing but wood.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[9] Hammered silver is brought from Tarshish and gold from Uphaz, the work of a craftsman and of the goldsmith's hands. They are clothed in violet and purple, all of it the work of skilled hands.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[10] But the LORD is the true God; he is the living God and the everlasting King. When he is angry, the earth quakes, and the nations cannot endure his wrath.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[11] Tell them this: These gods, who did not make the heavens and the earth, will perish from the earth and from under the heavens.[^1] [^1]: This verse is written in Aramaic rather than Hebrew.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[12] He made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[13] When he thunders, the waters in the heavens roar; he raises mist from the ends of the earth. He sends lightning with the rain and brings out the wind from his storehouses.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[14] Everyone is senseless and without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols. His images are a fraud; there is no breath in them.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[15] They are worthless, a work of mockery; when their time of reckoning comes, they will perish.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[16] Jacob's portion is not like these, for he is the maker of all things, and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance. The LORD of hosts is his name.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[17] Gather up your bundle from the ground, you who live under siege.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[18] For this is what the LORD says: Look, this time I am about to sling out the inhabitants of the land, and I will bring distress on them so that they will feel it.
