[Jeremiah] [10]:[19] Woe to me because of my ruin! My wound is severe. Yet I said, "This is my sickness, and I must bear it."
[Jeremiah] [10]:[20] My tent is destroyed, all my ropes are snapped. My children have gone from me, and they are no more. There is no one left to pitch my tent or set up my curtains.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[21] For the shepherds are senseless and have not sought the LORD. That is why they have not prospered, and all their flock is scattered.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[22] Listen! A report is coming, a great commotion from the land of the north, to make the cities of Judah a desolation, a haunt of jackals.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[23] I know, LORD, that a person's way is not his own; no one who walks can direct his own steps.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[24] Correct me, LORD, but with justice—not in your anger, or you will reduce me to nothing.
[Jeremiah] [10]:[25] Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you, and on the peoples that do not call on your name; for they have devoured Jacob—devoured him and consumed him—and have laid waste his homeland.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[1] The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
[Jeremiah] [11]:[2] Hear the terms of this covenant, and speak them to the people of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[3] Say to them: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Cursed is the one who does not obey the terms of this covenant,
[Jeremiah] [11]:[4] which I commanded your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, saying, "Listen to my voice and do everything I command you, and you will be my people and I will be your God"—
[Jeremiah] [11]:[5] so that I might fulfill the oath I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is today. And I answered, "Amen, LORD."
[Jeremiah] [11]:[6] Then the LORD said to me: Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem: Hear the terms of this covenant and carry them out.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[7] For I solemnly warned your fathers on the day I brought them up from the land of Egypt, and I have warned them again and again to this very day, saying, "Listen to my voice."
[Jeremiah] [11]:[8] But they did not listen or pay attention; each followed the stubbornness of his own evil heart. So I brought upon them all the words of this covenant, which I had commanded them to keep but they did not keep.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[9] The LORD said to me: A conspiracy has been found among the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[10] They have gone back to the sins of their forefathers, who refused to listen to my words; they have followed other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant I made with their fathers.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[11] Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to bring on them a disaster they cannot escape. Though they cry out to me, I will not listen to them.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[12] Then the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods to whom they burn incense, but those gods will not save them at all in the time of their trouble.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[13] For your gods have become as many as your cities, Judah; and the altars you have set up to that shameful thing are as many as the streets of Jerusalem—altars for burning incense to Baal.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[14] As for you, do not pray for this people or raise up any plea or petition for them, for I will not listen when they call to me in the time of their trouble.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[15] What is my beloved doing in my house, carrying out her vile schemes with the crowd? Can consecrated flesh avert your doom? When you do evil, then you rejoice.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[16] The LORD once called you a thriving olive tree, lovely in form and fruit. But with the roar of a mighty storm he has set it on fire, and its branches are broken.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[17] The LORD of hosts, who planted you, has decreed disaster for you, because of the evil the house of Israel and the house of Judah have done, provoking me to anger by burning incense to Baal.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[18] The LORD made it known to me, and I knew; you showed me what they were doing.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[19] But I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter; I did not know that they were plotting against me, saying, "Let us destroy the tree with its fruit; let us cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name will be remembered no more."
[Jeremiah] [11]:[20] But you, LORD of hosts, who judge righteously and test the heart and mind, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have committed my cause.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[21] Therefore this is what the LORD says about the men of Anathoth who are seeking your life and saying, "Do not prophesy in the name of the LORD, or you will die by our hands"—
[Jeremiah] [11]:[22] therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says: I am about to punish them. Their young men will die by the sword, their sons and daughters by famine.
[Jeremiah] [11]:[23] Not even a remnant will be left to them, for I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth in the year of their reckoning.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[1] You are righteous, LORD, whenever I bring a case before you; yet I would argue my cause with you. Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why do all the treacherous live at ease?
[Jeremiah] [12]:[2] You planted them, and they took root; they grow and bear fruit. You are near in their mouths but far from their hearts.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[3] But you know me, LORD; you see me and test my heart toward you. Drag them off like sheep for the slaughter, set them apart for the day of killing.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[4] How long will the land mourn and the grass of every field wither? Because of the evil of those who live in it the animals and birds are swept away, for the people say, "He will not see what becomes of us."
[Jeremiah] [12]:[5] If you have raced with men on foot and they have worn you out, how will you compete with horses? If you feel safe in a land at peace, what will you do in the thickets of the Jordan?
[Jeremiah] [12]:[6] Even your brothers, your own father's house, even they have betrayed you; even they have raised the hue and cry behind you. Do not trust them, though they speak kindly to you.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[7] I have abandoned my house, forsaken my inheritance; I have handed the beloved of my soul into the grip of her enemies.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[8] My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest; she roars against me — therefore I hate her.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[9] Is my inheritance a speckled bird of prey to me, with birds of prey circling all around her? Go, gather every wild beast; bring them to devour.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[10] Many shepherds have ruined my vineyard and trampled my portion; they have turned the field I delighted in into a desolate wasteland.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[11] They have made it a wasteland; desolate, it mourns before me. The whole land is laid waste, and no one takes it to heart.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[12] Over all the bare heights of the wilderness the destroyers have come, for the sword of the LORD devours from one end of the land to the other; no one has peace.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[13] They have sown wheat and reaped thorns; they have worn themselves out for nothing. Be ashamed of your harvests, because of the burning anger of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[14] This is what the LORD says concerning all my evil neighbors who lay hands on the inheritance I gave my people Israel to possess: I am about to uproot them from their land, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[15] But after I have uprooted them, I will again have compassion on them and bring them back, each to his inheritance and each to his land.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[16] And if they truly learn the ways of my people, swearing by my name, "As the LORD lives," just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they will be built up in the midst of my people.
[Jeremiah] [12]:[17] But if any nation will not listen, I will uproot it completely and destroy it, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[1] This is what the LORD said to me: "Go and buy yourself a linen belt and put it around your waist, but do not let it touch water."
[Jeremiah] [13]:[2] So I bought the belt, as the LORD had said, and put it around my waist.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[3] Then the word of the LORD came to me a second time:
[Jeremiah] [13]:[4] "Take the belt you bought and are wearing around your waist, and go at once to the Euphrates and hide it there in a cleft of the rock."
[Jeremiah] [13]:[5] So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, as the LORD had commanded me.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[6] After many days the LORD said to me, "Get up, go to the Euphrates and take back the belt I told you to hide there."
[Jeremiah] [13]:[7] So I went to the Euphrates and dug, and I took the belt from the place where I had hidden it. But the belt was ruined—good for nothing at all.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[8] Then the word of the LORD came to me:
[Jeremiah] [13]:[9] This is what the LORD says: In the same way I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[10] These evil people, who refuse to listen to my words, who follow the stubbornness of their own hearts and go after other gods to serve them and bow down to them—they will be like this belt, good for nothing at all.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[11] For as a belt clings to a man's waist, so I bound the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah to myself, declares the LORD, to be my people, my renown, my praise, and my glory. But they would not listen.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[12] Speak this word to them: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Every jar is meant to be filled with wine. And when they say to you, "Don't we know very well that every jar is meant to be filled with wine?"—
[Jeremiah] [13]:[13] then tell them: This is what the LORD says: I am going to fill with drunkenness all who live in this land—the kings who sit on David's throne, the priests, the prophets, and all who live in Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[14] I will smash them one against another, parents and children together, declares the LORD. I will show no pity, no mercy, no compassion to keep me from destroying them.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[15] Hear and pay attention; do not be arrogant, for the LORD has spoken.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[16] Give glory to the LORD your God before he brings the darkness, before your feet stumble on the darkening hills. You hope for light, but he will turn it to deep gloom and make it thick darkness.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[17] But if you will not listen, I will weep in secret because of your pride; my eyes will weep bitterly, overflowing with tears, because the LORD's flock has been taken captive.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[18] Say to the king and the queen mother: Come down from your thrones, for your glorious crowns have fallen from your heads.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[19] The cities of the Negev are shut up, and there is no one to open them. All Judah is carried into exile, carried away completely.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[20] Lift up your eyes and see those coming from the north. Where is the flock entrusted to you, the sheep that were your glory?
[Jeremiah] [13]:[21] What will you say when he sets over you as rulers the very ones you trained to be your allies? Will not pangs seize you like a woman in labor?
[Jeremiah] [13]:[22] And if you ask yourself, "Why has this happened to me?"—it is because of your many sins that your skirts have been stripped off and your body violated.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[23] Can a Cushite change his skin, or a leopard its spots? Neither can you do good, you who are schooled in evil.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[24] I will scatter them like chaff driven off by the desert wind.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[25] This is your lot, the portion I have measured out for you, declares the LORD, because you have forgotten me and trusted in lies.
[Jeremiah] [13]:[26] So I myself will pull your skirts up over your face, and your shame will be seen—
[Jeremiah] [13]:[27] your adulteries, your lustful neighing, your shameless prostitution. On the hills and in the fields I have seen your detestable acts. Woe to you, Jerusalem! How long will you remain unclean?
[Jeremiah] [14]:[1] The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought:
[Jeremiah] [14]:[2] Judah mourns, her gates languish; they sink to the ground in mourning, and the cry of Jerusalem goes up.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[3] The nobles send their young men for water; they come to the cisterns and find none. They return with their vessels empty, ashamed and disgraced, their heads covered.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[4] The ground is cracked, for there has been no rain in the land. The farmers are ashamed; they cover their heads.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[5] Even the doe in the field gives birth and abandons her young, because there is no grass.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[6] Wild donkeys stand on the barren heights and pant for air like jackals; their eyes fail, for there is no vegetation.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[7] Though our sins testify against us, act, O LORD, for the sake of your name. Our rebellions are many; against you we have sinned.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[8] O Hope of Israel, its Savior in time of trouble, why are you like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who stops only for the night?
[Jeremiah] [14]:[9] Why are you like a man taken by surprise, like a warrior who cannot save? Yet you are among us, O LORD, and we bear your name. Do not abandon us!
[Jeremiah] [14]:[10] This is what the LORD says about this people: They love to wander; they do not restrain their feet. So the LORD does not accept them; now he will remember their guilt and punish their sins.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[11] Then the LORD said to me: Do not pray for the welfare of this people.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[12] Even if they fast, I will not listen to their cry; even if they offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. Instead, I will make an end of them by sword, famine, and plague.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[13] Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD, look: the prophets keep telling them, 'You will not see the sword, and famine will not come upon you; I will give you lasting peace in this place.'"
[Jeremiah] [14]:[14] And the LORD said to me: The prophets are prophesying lies in my name. I did not send them, I did not commission them, I did not speak to them. What they prophesy to you are lying visions, worthless divinations, and the delusions of their own minds.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[15] Therefore this is what the LORD says about the prophets who prophesy in my name though I did not send them, and who say, "No sword or famine will touch this land": by sword and famine those very prophets will meet their end.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[16] And the people to whom they prophesy will be thrown into the streets of Jerusalem, victims of famine and sword, with no one to bury them—they, their wives, their sons and their daughters. For I will pour out on them the evil they deserve.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[17] Speak this word to them: Let my eyes stream with tears night and day, without ceasing, for the virgin daughter of my people has suffered a crushing blow, a devastating wound.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[18] If I go out into the country, there lie those slain by the sword; if I enter the city, there are the ravages of famine. Both prophet and priest have gone off to a land they do not know.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[19] Have you rejected Judah completely? Do you loathe Zion? Why have you struck us so that we cannot be healed? We hoped for peace, but no good has come; we hoped for a time of healing, but there is only terror.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[20] We acknowledge our wickedness, O LORD, and the guilt of our fathers; we have sinned against you.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[21] For the sake of your name, do not despise us; do not dishonor your glorious throne. Remember your covenant with us, and do not break it.
[Jeremiah] [14]:[22] Can the worthless idols of the nations bring rain? Can the skies by themselves send showers? No, it is you, O LORD our God. So we put our hope in you, for you are the one who does all this.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[1] Then the LORD said to me: Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my heart would not turn toward this people. Send them away from my presence—let them go!
[Jeremiah] [15]:[2] And when they ask you, "Where shall we go?" tell them: This is what the LORD says: Those destined for death, to death; those for the sword, to the sword; those for famine, to famine; those for captivity, to captivity.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[3] I will appoint over them four kinds of destroyers, declares the LORD: the sword to kill, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[4] I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of what Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, did in Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[5] Who will have pity on you, Jerusalem? Who will grieve for you? Who will turn aside to ask how you are?
[Jeremiah] [15]:[6] You have rejected me, declares the LORD; you keep going backward. So I have stretched out my hand against you and destroyed you; I am weary of relenting.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[7] I winnowed them with a fork at the gates of the land; I bereaved them, I destroyed my people, for they would not turn from their ways.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[8] Their widows became more numerous before me than the sand of the seas. At midday I brought a destroyer against the mothers of young men; suddenly I brought down on them anguish and terror.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[9] The mother of seven grew faint; she gasped out her life. Her sun set while it was still day; she was disgraced and humiliated. And those of them who are left I will hand over to the sword before their enemies, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[10] Woe to me, my mother, that you gave me birth—a man of strife and contention to the whole land! I have not lent, nor have I borrowed, yet everyone curses me.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[11] The LORD said: Surely I will set you free for a good purpose; surely I will make the enemy plead with you in a time of disaster, in a time of distress.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[12] Can iron be broken—iron from the north—or bronze?
[Jeremiah] [15]:[13] Your wealth and your treasures I will give away as plunder, without price, because of all your sins throughout your territory.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[14] I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, for my anger has kindled a fire that will burn against you.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[15] You know, LORD—remember me and care for me; take vengeance for me on those who persecute me. In your patience, do not take me away; know that I bear reproach for your sake.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[16] When your words came, I ate them; your word became my joy and the delight of my heart, for I bear your name, LORD God of hosts.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[17] I never sat in the company of revelers to make merry. I sat alone because your hand was on me, for you had filled me with indignation.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[18] Why is my pain unending and my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? You have become to me like a deceptive brook, like waters that cannot be trusted.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[19] Therefore this is what the LORD says: If you turn back, I will restore you, and you shall stand before me. If you separate the precious from the worthless, you shall be as my mouth. Let them turn to you, but you must not turn to them.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[20] To this people I will make you a fortified wall of bronze; they will fight against you but will not overcome you, for I am with you to save you and deliver you, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [15]:[21] I will rescue you from the hand of the wicked and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Jeremiah] [16]:[2] You shall not take a wife, and you shall have no sons or daughters in this place.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[3] For this is what the LORD says concerning the sons and daughters born in this place, concerning the mothers who bear them and the fathers who father them in this land:
[Jeremiah] [16]:[4] They will die of deadly diseases. No one will mourn for them or bury them; they will lie like dung on the ground. They will perish by sword and famine, and their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[5] For this is what the LORD says: Do not enter a house where there is mourning; do not go to lament or console them. For I have withdrawn my peace from this people, declares the LORD—my steadfast love and my mercy.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[6] Both great and small will die in this land. They will not be buried, and no one will mourn for them or cut himself or shave his head for them.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[7] No one will break bread for the mourner to comfort him for the dead, nor give him the cup of consolation to drink for his father or his mother.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[8] And do not enter a house where there is feasting, to sit with them and eat and drink.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[9] For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Before your very eyes and in your days I will silence in this place the sound of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.

[Jeremiah] [16]:[12] And you have done worse than your fathers. Look how each of you follows the stubbornness of his evil heart instead of listening to me.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[13] So I will hurl you out of this land into a land neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you will serve other gods day and night, for I will show you no favor.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[14] Therefore the days are coming, declares the LORD, when it will no longer be said, "As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the people of Israel up out of the land of Egypt,"
[Jeremiah] [16]:[15] but rather, "As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the people of Israel up out of the land of the north and out of all the lands where he had driven them." For I will bring them back to their own land, which I gave to their fathers.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[16] Look, I am sending for many fishermen, declares the LORD, and they will catch them. After that I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them down on every mountain and hill and out of the clefts of the rocks.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[17] For my eyes are on all their ways. They are not hidden from me, and their guilt is not concealed from my sight.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[18] First I will repay them double for their guilt and their sin, because they have defiled my land with the carcasses of their vile idols and have filled my inheritance with their abominations.
[Jeremiah] [16]:[19] O LORD, my strength and my stronghold, my refuge in the day of trouble, to you the nations will come from the ends of the earth and say: "Our fathers inherited nothing but lies, worthless idols of no benefit at all."
[Jeremiah] [16]:[20] Can a man make gods for himself? Such are no gods at all!
[Jeremiah] [16]:[21] Therefore I will make them know—this time I will make them know my hand and my might—and they will know that my name is the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[1] The sin of Judah is written with an iron stylus, engraved with a diamond point on the tablet of their heart and on the horns of your altars,
[Jeremiah] [17]:[2] while their children remember their altars and their Asherah poles beside a green tree, on the high hills.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[3] My mountain in the open country: your wealth and all your treasures I will hand over as plunder, along with your high places, because of the sin committed throughout your territory.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[4] By your own doing you will let go of the inheritance I gave you, and I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, for you have kindled a fire in my anger that will burn forever.

[Jeremiah] [17]:[6] He will be like a shrub in the wasteland; he will not see when good comes. He will live in the parched places of the desert, in a salt land where no one dwells.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[7] Blessed is the one who trusts in the LORD, whose confidence is in him.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[8] He will be like a tree planted by water, sending out its roots toward the stream. It has no fear when the heat comes; its leaves stay green. It is not anxious in a year of drought, and it never stops bearing fruit.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[9] The heart is deceitful above all things and beyond cure. Who can understand it?

[Jeremiah] [17]:[11] Like a partridge that hatches eggs it did not lay is the one who gains riches unjustly. In the middle of his days they will desert him, and in the end he will prove to be a fool.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[12] A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[13] LORD, hope of Israel, all who forsake you will be put to shame. Those who turn away from you will be written in the dust, for they have abandoned the LORD, the spring of living water.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[14] Heal me, LORD, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for you are my praise.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[15] Look, they keep saying to me, "Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come now!"
[Jeremiah] [17]:[16] But I have not run away from being a shepherd in your service, nor have I longed for the day of disaster. You know it: whatever came from my lips was there before your face.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[17] Do not become a terror to me; you are my refuge in the day of trouble.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[18] Let my persecutors be put to shame, but do not let me be put to shame. Let them be terrified, but do not let me be terrified. Bring on them the day of disaster; destroy them with double destruction.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[19] This is what the LORD said to me: Go and stand in the People's Gate, where the kings of Judah enter and leave, and in all the gates of Jerusalem,
[Jeremiah] [17]:[20] and say to them: Hear the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah and all Judah and all who live in Jerusalem and come through these gates.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[21] This is what the LORD says: Guard your lives, and do not carry a load on the Sabbath day or bring it through the gates of Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[22] Do not carry a load out of your houses on the Sabbath day or do any work, but keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[23] Yet they did not listen or pay attention; they stiffened their necks so that they would not hear or accept correction.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[24] But if you listen carefully to me, declares the LORD, and bring no load through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, but keep the Sabbath day holy by doing no work on it,
[Jeremiah] [17]:[25] then kings and princes who sit on David's throne will come through the gates of this city, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their officials, the people of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem; and this city will be inhabited forever.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[26] People will come from the towns of Judah and the places around Jerusalem, from the territory of Benjamin, from the foothills, the hill country, and the Negev, bringing burnt offerings and sacrifices, grain offerings and incense, and bringing thank offerings to the house of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [17]:[27] But if you do not listen to me, to keep the Sabbath day holy, and if you carry a load and come through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will set fire to its gates, and the fire will consume the fortresses of Jerusalem and will not be quenched.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[1] The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
[Jeremiah] [18]:[2] "Get up and go down to the potter's house, and there I will let you hear my words."
[Jeremiah] [18]:[3] So I went down to the potter's house, and there he was, working at the wheel.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[4] But the vessel he was shaping from the clay was ruined in his hands, so he made it over into another vessel, whatever seemed right to him.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[5] Then the word of the LORD came to me:
[Jeremiah] [18]:[6] "House of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter does? declares the LORD. Look, like clay in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[7] If at any moment I speak against a nation or a kingdom, to uproot it, tear it down, and destroy it,
[Jeremiah] [18]:[8] and that nation against which I have spoken turns from its evil, then I will relent of the disaster I intended to bring on it.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[9] And if at any moment I speak about a nation or a kingdom, to build it up and plant it,
[Jeremiah] [18]:[10] but it does what is evil in my eyes and will not listen to my voice, then I will relent of the good I had promised to do for it.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[11] Now say to the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: This is what the LORD says: I am shaping disaster against you and devising a plan against you. Turn back, each of you, from your evil way, and make your ways and your deeds good.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[12] But they say, "It is hopeless. We will follow our own plans; each of us will act on the stubbornness of his evil heart."
[Jeremiah] [18]:[13] Therefore this is what the LORD says: Ask among the nations—who has ever heard the like? Virgin Israel has done a thing too horrible for words.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[14] Does the snow of Lebanon ever leave the rocky slopes? Do the cold waters that flow from afar ever run dry?
[Jeremiah] [18]:[15] Yet my people have forgotten me; they burn incense to worthless idols. Those idols have made them stumble in their ways, off the ancient roads, to walk on side paths, on a road never paved,
[Jeremiah] [18]:[16] making their land a desolation, an object of endless scorn. All who pass by will be appalled and shake their heads.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[17] Like a wind from the east I will scatter them before the enemy. I will show them my back, not my face, on the day of their calamity.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[18] Then they said, "Come, let us make plans against Jeremiah, for instruction will never be lost from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor a word from the prophet. Come, let us strike him down with the tongue and pay no attention to anything he says."
[Jeremiah] [18]:[19] Give heed to me, LORD; listen to what my accusers are saying!
[Jeremiah] [18]:[20] Should evil be the payment for good? Yet they have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you and spoke on their behalf, to turn your wrath away from them.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[21] So hand their children over to famine; deliver them to the power of the sword. Let their wives be left childless and widowed; let their men be struck down by death, their young men cut down by the sword in battle.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[22] Let a cry be heard from their houses when you suddenly bring raiders against them—for they have dug a pit to catch me and hidden snares for my feet.
[Jeremiah] [18]:[23] But you, LORD, know all their plots to kill me. Do not cover over their guilt or blot out their sin from your sight. Let them be overthrown before you; deal with them in the time of your anger.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[1] This is what the LORD said: Go and buy a potter's earthenware jar. Take with you some of the elders of the people and some of the senior priests,
[Jeremiah] [19]:[2] and go out to the Valley of Ben-Hinnom, at the entrance of the Potsherd Gate, and proclaim there the words I speak to you.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[3] Say: Hear the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to bring such disaster on this place that the ears of everyone who hears of it will ring.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[4] For they have forsaken me and made this place foreign to me. They have burned incense here to other gods that neither they nor their ancestors nor the kings of Judah ever knew, and they have filled this place with the blood of the innocent.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[5] They have built the high places of Baal to burn their children in the fire as offerings to Baal—something I never commanded or spoke of, something that never entered my mind.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[6] So look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when this place will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[7] In this place I will pour out and empty the plans of Judah and Jerusalem. I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies, at the hand of those who seek their lives, and I will give their corpses as food to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[8] I will make this city a horror, a thing to be hissed at; everyone who passes by will be appalled and will hiss at all its wounds.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[9] I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and they will devour one another's flesh in the siege and distress inflicted on them by their enemies and by those who seek their lives.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[10] Then break the jar before the eyes of the men who go with you,
[Jeremiah] [19]:[11] and say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts says: So will I break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter's vessel that can never be mended again. They will bury the dead in Topheth for lack of any other place to bury.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[12] This is what I will do to this place and to those who live in it, declares the LORD. I will make this city like Topheth.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[13] The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will be defiled like the place of Topheth—all the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to the whole host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[14] Then Jeremiah came back from Topheth, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of the LORD's house and said to all the people:
[Jeremiah] [19]:[15] This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am bringing on this city and on all its surrounding towns every disaster I pronounced against it, because they stiffened their necks and refused to listen to my words.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[1] Now Pashhur son of Immer, the priest who was chief officer in the house of the LORD, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[2] So Pashhur had Jeremiah the prophet beaten and put in the stocks at the Upper Benjamin Gate of the house of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[3] The next morning, when Pashhur released him from the stocks, Jeremiah said to him: "The LORD does not call you Pashhur, but Terror on Every Side." [footnote: Hebrew Magor-Missabib, 'Terror on Every Side'; the same phrase recurs in verse 10.]
[Jeremiah] [20]:[4] For this is what the LORD says: I am making you a terror to yourself and to all who love you. They will fall by the sword of their enemies while your own eyes look on. All Judah I will hand over to the king of Babylon, who will carry them off to Babylon and strike them down with the sword.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[5] I will hand over all the wealth of this city, all its earnings, all its treasures, and all the riches of the kings of Judah to their enemies. They will plunder them, seize them, and carry them off to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[6] And you, Pashhur, and all who live in your house will go into exile. You will go to Babylon, and there you will die, and there you will be buried—you and all who love you, to whom you prophesied lies."
[Jeremiah] [20]:[7] You enticed me, LORD, and I was enticed; you overpowered me and prevailed. I have become a laughingstock all day long; everyone mocks me.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[8] Whenever I speak, I have to cry out; I shout, "Violence and ruin!" So the word of the LORD has brought me nothing but insult and derision all day long.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[9] And when I say, "I will not mention him or speak any more in his name," then his word is like a fire burning in my heart, shut up in my bones. I grow weary of holding it in—I cannot.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[10] I hear many whispering, "Terror on every side! Denounce him! Let us denounce him!" All my trusted friends watch for me to stumble: "Perhaps he can be tricked; then we will prevail against him and take our revenge on him."
[Jeremiah] [20]:[11] But the LORD is with me like a mighty warrior; therefore my persecutors will stumble and not prevail. They will be utterly disgraced, for they have not succeeded; their everlasting shame will never be forgotten.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[12] LORD of hosts, who tests the righteous and sees the heart and mind, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have committed my cause.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[13] Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD! For he has rescued the life of the needy from the hand of evildoers.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[14] Cursed be the day I was born! May the day my mother bore me never be blessed.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[15] Cursed be the man who brought my father the news, who said, "A son is born to you!"—and made him glad.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[16] May that man be like the cities the LORD overthrew without relenting. May he hear screaming in the morning and the battle cry at noon,
[Jeremiah] [20]:[17] because he did not kill me in the womb, so that my mother would have been my grave and her womb forever great with child.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[18] Why did I ever come out of the womb, only to see trouble and sorrow and end my days in shame?
[Jeremiah] [21]:[1] The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, with this message:
[Jeremiah] [21]:[2] "Please inquire of the LORD on our behalf, for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is making war against us. Perhaps the LORD will deal with us according to all his wonders, and Nebuchadnezzar will withdraw from us."
[Jeremiah] [21]:[3] Then Jeremiah said to them: This is what you are to tell Zedekiah:
[Jeremiah] [21]:[4] This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I am going to turn back against you the weapons of war that are in your hands, the ones you are using to fight the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who are besieging you outside the wall. I will gather them into the center of this city.
[Jeremiah] [21]:[5] And I myself will fight against you with outstretched hand and mighty arm, in anger, in fury, and in great wrath.
[Jeremiah] [21]:[6] I will strike down those who live in this city, both man and beast; they will die of a terrible plague.
[Jeremiah] [21]:[7] After that, declares the LORD, I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, the people, and all who are left in this city after the plague, the sword, and the famine, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, into the hand of their enemies, into the hand of those who seek their lives. He will put them to the sword; he will show them no pity, no compassion, no mercy.
[Jeremiah] [21]:[8] And to this people you shall say: This is what the LORD says: See, I am setting before you the way of life and the way of death.
[Jeremiah] [21]:[9] Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, by famine, or by plague. But whoever goes out and surrenders to the Chaldeans who are besieging you will live; he will escape with his life as his only spoil.
[Jeremiah] [21]:[10] For I have set my face against this city for harm and not for good, declares the LORD. It will be handed over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it to the ground.
[Jeremiah] [21]:[11] And to the royal house of Judah: Hear the word of the LORD!
[Jeremiah] [21]:[12] House of David, this is what the LORD says: Administer justice every morning; rescue the plundered from the hand of the oppressor. Otherwise my wrath will break out like fire and burn with no one to quench it, because of the evil you have done.
[Jeremiah] [21]:[13] I am against you, you who dwell above the valley, you rock of the plateau, declares the LORD—you who say, "Who can come down against us? Who can enter our dwellings?"
[Jeremiah] [21]:[14] I will punish you as your deeds deserve, declares the LORD. I will kindle a fire in her forest, and it will consume everything around her.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[1] This is what the LORD says: Go down to the house of the king of Judah and speak this word there.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[2] Say: Hear the word of the LORD, king of Judah, you who sit on David's throne—you, your servants, and your people who come through these gates.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[3] This is what the LORD says: Do justice and righteousness. Rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of his oppressor. Do not wrong or violate the foreigner, the orphan, or the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[4] For if you truly do what I have said, then kings who sit on David's throne will come riding through the gates of this house in chariots and on horses—each king with his servants and his people.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[5] But if you will not listen to these words, I swear by myself, declares the LORD, that this house will become a ruin.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[6] For this is what the LORD says concerning the house of the king of Judah: You are like Gilead to me, like the summit of Lebanon—yet I will surely make you a wasteland, cities without inhabitants.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[7] I will appoint destroyers against you, each with his weapons; they will cut down your finest cedars and throw them on the fire.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[8] Many nations will pass by this city and ask one another, "Why has the LORD done this to such a great city?"
[Jeremiah] [22]:[9] And they will answer: "Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD their God and bowed down to other gods and served them."
[Jeremiah] [22]:[10] Do not weep for the dead or mourn for him. Weep bitterly for the one who goes away, for he will never return to see the land of his birth.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[11] For this is what the LORD says about Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who reigned in place of his father Josiah: He has gone out from this place and will never return.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[12] He will die in the place where they have taken him captive; he will never see this land again.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[13] Woe to him who builds his house by unrighteousness and his upper rooms by injustice, who makes his neighbor work for nothing and does not pay him his wages,
[Jeremiah] [22]:[14] who says, "I will build myself a spacious house with airy upper rooms," who cuts out windows for it, panels it with cedar, and paints it red with vermilion.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[15] Do you think you are a king because you compete in cedar? Did not your father eat and drink, and also do justice and righteousness? Then all went well for him.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[16] He defended the cause of the poor and needy, and it went well for him. Is that not what it means to know me? declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[17] But your eyes and your heart are set on nothing but your own gain—on shedding innocent blood, on oppression and violence.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[18] Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: They will not mourn for him, crying, "Alas, my brother! Alas, my sister!" They will not mourn for him, crying, "Alas, my lord! Alas, his majesty!"
[Jeremiah] [22]:[19] He will have the burial of a donkey—dragged away and thrown out beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[20] Go up to Lebanon and cry out; raise your voice in Bashan; cry out from Abarim, for all your lovers are crushed.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[21] I spoke to you in your prosperity, but you said, "I will not listen." This has been your way since your youth: you have never obeyed my voice.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[22] The wind will shepherd away all your shepherds, and your lovers will go into captivity. Then you will be ashamed and humiliated because of all your wickedness.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[23] You who dwell in Lebanon, nested among the cedars: how you will groan when the pains come upon you, anguish like a woman in labor!
[Jeremiah] [22]:[24] As surely as I live, declares the LORD, even if Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet ring on my right hand, I would tear you off.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[25] I will hand you over to those who seek your life, to those you dread—to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to the Chaldeans.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[26] I will hurl you and the mother who bore you into another land, where neither of you was born, and there you will die.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[27] To the land they long with all their heart to return to, they will never return.
[Jeremiah] [22]:[28] Is this man Coniah a broken pot, despised and shattered, a vessel no one wants? Why are he and his children hurled out and cast into a land they do not know?
[Jeremiah] [22]:[29] O land, land, land, hear the word of the LORD!
[Jeremiah] [22]:[30] This is what the LORD says: Record this man as childless, a man who will not prosper in his days; for none of his offspring will succeed in sitting on David's throne or ruling again in Judah.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[1] Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[2] Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says against the shepherds who tend my people: You have scattered my flock and driven them away, and you have not cared for them. So now I will deal with you for the evil of your deeds, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[3] I myself will gather the remnant of my flock from all the lands where I have driven them, and I will bring them back to their pasture, and they will be fruitful and multiply.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[4] I will raise up shepherds over them who will tend them, and they will no longer be afraid or terrified, and not one of them will be missing, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[5] Look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch. He will reign as king and act wisely, and he will do what is just and right in the land.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[6] In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will live in safety. And this is the name by which he will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[7] Therefore, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when people will no longer say, "As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the Israelites up out of the land of Egypt,"
[Jeremiah] [23]:[8] but rather, "As surely as the LORD lives, who brought up and led back the offspring of the house of Israel out of the land of the north and out of all the lands where he had driven them." Then they will live on their own soil.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[9] Concerning the prophets: My heart is broken within me; all my bones tremble. I am like a drunken man, like one overcome with wine, because of the LORD and because of his holy words.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[10] For the land is full of adulterers; because of the curse the land mourns, and the pastures of the wilderness are withered. They run to do evil, and their strength is used for what is wrong.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[11] Both prophet and priest are godless; even in my own house I have found their wickedness, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[12] Therefore their way will be like slippery ground in the dark; they will be driven on and fall in it. For I will bring disaster upon them in the year of their reckoning, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[13] Among the prophets of Samaria I have seen something offensive: they prophesied by Baal and led my people Israel astray.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[14] And among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen something horrible: they commit adultery and live a lie. They strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns from his wickedness. To me they have all become like Sodom, and the people of Jerusalem like Gomorrah.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[15] Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts says concerning the prophets: I will feed them bitter wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink, for from the prophets of Jerusalem godlessness has spread through the whole land.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[16] This is what the LORD of Hosts says: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. They are filling you with empty hopes. They speak visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[17] They keep saying to those who despise me, "The LORD says: You will have peace," and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart, "No harm will come to you."
[Jeremiah] [23]:[18] But who has stood in the council of the LORD to see and hear his word? Who has paid attention to his word and truly heard it?
[Jeremiah] [23]:[19] See, the storm of the LORD breaks out in fury, a whirling tempest; it will burst upon the heads of the wicked.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[20] The anger of the LORD will not turn back until he has carried out and fulfilled the purposes of his heart. In days to come you will understand it clearly.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[21] I did not send these prophets, yet they have run with their message. I did not speak to them, yet they have prophesied.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[22] But if they had stood in my council, they would have proclaimed my words to my people and turned them from their evil way and from their evil deeds.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[23] Am I a God who is only near, declares the LORD, and not a God far away?
[Jeremiah] [23]:[24] Can anyone hide in secret places where I cannot see him? declares the LORD. Do I not fill both heaven and earth? declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[25] I have heard what the prophets say who prophesy lies in my name, claiming, "I had a dream! I had a dream!"
[Jeremiah] [23]:[26] How long will this go on in the hearts of these prophets who prophesy lies, who prophesy the delusions of their own minds?
[Jeremiah] [23]:[27] They intend to make my people forget my name by the dreams they tell one another, just as their ancestors forgot my name for the sake of Baal.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[28] Let the prophet who has a dream tell his dream, but let the one who has my word speak my word faithfully. What has straw to do with grain? declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[29] Is not my word like fire, declares the LORD, and like a hammer that shatters rock?
[Jeremiah] [23]:[30] So I am against the prophets, declares the LORD, who steal my words from one another.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[31] Yes, I am against the prophets, declares the LORD, who wag their own tongues and then say, "The LORD declares."
[Jeremiah] [23]:[32] I am against those who prophesy false dreams, declares the LORD. They tell them and lead my people astray with their lies and reckless boasting, though I never sent them or commanded them. They are no help at all to this people, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[33] When this people, or a prophet or a priest, asks you, "What is the burden of the LORD?" say to them, "You are the burden! And I will cast you off, declares the LORD." [Footnote: The Hebrew word rendered "burden" also means "oracle," so the question means "What message has the LORD given?" The traditional Hebrew text of the reply reads "What burden?"; ancient versions read "You are the burden."]
[Jeremiah] [23]:[34] As for the prophet or the priest or anyone among the people who says, "This is the burden of the LORD"—I will punish that man and his household.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[35] Instead, each of you is to say to your neighbor and to your brother: "What has the LORD answered? What has the LORD spoken?"
[Jeremiah] [23]:[36] But you must no longer speak of "the burden of the LORD," for each man's own word becomes his burden, and so you twist the words of the living God, the LORD of Hosts, our God.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[37] This is what you are to say to a prophet: "What has the LORD answered you? What has the LORD spoken?"
[Jeremiah] [23]:[38] But if you say, "the burden of the LORD," then this is what the LORD says: Because you keep using these words, "the burden of the LORD," though I sent you word not to say it,
[Jeremiah] [23]:[39] therefore, behold, I will surely lift you up and cast you away from my presence, along with the city I gave to you and to your ancestors.
[Jeremiah] [23]:[40] And I will bring upon you everlasting disgrace and everlasting shame that will never be forgotten.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[1] The LORD showed me this: two baskets of figs set out before the temple of the LORD. This was after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away from Jerusalem Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, together with the officials of Judah, the craftsmen and the metalworkers, and had brought them to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[2] One basket held very good figs, like those that ripen first; the other held very bad figs, so bad they could not be eaten.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[3] The LORD said to me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I answered, "Figs. The good ones are very good, and the bad ones are so bad they cannot be eaten."
[Jeremiah] [24]:[4] Then the word of the LORD came to me:
[Jeremiah] [24]:[5] This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Like these good figs, so I will look with favor on the exiles of Judah, whom I sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[6] I will keep my eyes on them for their good, and I will bring them back to this land. I will build them up and not tear them down; I will plant them and not uproot them.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[7] I will give them a heart to know me, that I am the LORD. They will be my people, and I will be their God, for they will return to me with all their heart.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[8] But like the bad figs, so bad they cannot be eaten—this is what the LORD says—so will I deal with Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, and the remnant of Jerusalem, both those left in this land and those living in the land of Egypt.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[9] I will make them a horror, a thing of evil, to all the kingdoms of the earth—a disgrace and a byword, an object of ridicule and cursing, in every place where I drive them.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[10] I will send the sword, famine, and plague against them until they are destroyed from the land I gave to them and to their ancestors.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[1] The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah—that was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon—
[Jeremiah] [25]:[2] the word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem:
[Jeremiah] [25]:[3] From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until this very day—twenty-three years now—the word of the LORD has come to me, and I have spoken to you again and again, but you would not listen.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[4] The LORD sent you all his servants the prophets, again and again, but you would not listen; you would not turn your ear to hear.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[5] They said: Turn back, each of you, from your evil way and from your wicked deeds, and live on the land the LORD gave to you and to your fathers forever and ever.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[6] Do not follow other gods to serve them and bow down to them. Do not provoke me to anger with the work of your hands, and I will do you no harm.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[7] But you would not listen to me, declares the LORD; instead you provoked me to anger with the work of your hands, to your own harm.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[8] Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says: Because you have not listened to my words,
[Jeremiah] [25]:[9] I am sending for all the tribes of the north, declares the LORD, and for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will bring them against this land and its inhabitants and against all these surrounding nations. I will devote them to destruction and make them an object of horror and scorn, an everlasting ruin.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[10] I will banish from them the sound of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[11] This whole land will become a ruin and a wasteland, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[12] But when the seventy years are complete, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation for their guilt, declares the LORD, and the land of the Chaldeans too, and I will make it a desolation forever.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[13] I will bring upon that land everything I have spoken against it, all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[14] For they too will be enslaved by many nations and great kings, and I will repay them according to their deeds and the work of their hands.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[15] This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, said to me: Take this cup of the wine of wrath from my hand and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[16] They will drink and stagger and go mad because of the sword I am sending among them.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[17] So I took the cup from the LORD's hand and made all the nations to whom he sent me drink it:
[Jeremiah] [25]:[18] Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin and an object of horror, of scorn and cursing, as they are today;
[Jeremiah] [25]:[19] Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his officials and all his people;
[Jeremiah] [25]:[20] all the mixed peoples; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the land of the Philistines—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and what is left of Ashdod;
[Jeremiah] [25]:[21] Edom, Moab and the Ammonites;
[Jeremiah] [25]:[22] all the kings of Tyre and all the kings of Sidon; the kings of the coastlands across the sea;
[Jeremiah] [25]:[23] Dedan, Tema, Buz and all who clip the hair at their temples;
[Jeremiah] [25]:[24] all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed peoples who live in the desert;
[Jeremiah] [25]:[25] all the kings of Zimri, all the kings of Elam and all the kings of Media;
[Jeremiah] [25]:[26] all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another—and all the kingdoms of the world that are on the face of the earth. And after them the king of Sheshach will drink too.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[27] Then say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Drink, get drunk, vomit, and fall to rise no more, because of the sword I am sending among you.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[28] And if they refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink, say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts says: You must drink it!
[Jeremiah] [25]:[29] See, I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears my name, and will you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for I am summoning the sword against all who live on the earth, declares the LORD of hosts.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[30] So prophesy all these words against them and say to them: The LORD roars from on high; from his holy dwelling he thunders. He roars mightily against his fold; like those who tread the grapes he shouts against all who live on the earth.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[31] The uproar reaches the ends of the earth, for the LORD has a case against the nations; he brings judgment on all flesh and hands the wicked over to the sword, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[32] This is what the LORD of hosts says: Look! Disaster is spreading from nation to nation, and a mighty storm is rising from the ends of the earth.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[33] On that day those slain by the LORD will lie from one end of the earth to the other. No one will mourn them; they will not be gathered or buried, but will lie like dung on the ground.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[34] Wail, you shepherds, and cry out! Roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock! For the days of your slaughter have come; you will be scattered and fall like a choice vessel.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[35] There will be no refuge for the shepherds, no escape for the leaders of the flock.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[36] Hear the cry of the shepherds, the wailing of the leaders of the flock, for the LORD is destroying their pasture.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[37] The peaceful meadows are silenced before the burning anger of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[38] Like a lion he has left his lair, for their land has become a desolation because of the oppressor's fierce anger, because of the burning anger of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[1] At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from the LORD:
[Jeremiah] [26]:[2] This is what the LORD says: Stand in the court of the LORD's house and speak to all who come from the cities of Judah to worship in the house of the LORD. Tell them everything I command you; do not hold back a single word.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[3] Perhaps they will listen and each one turn from his evil way. Then I will relent of the disaster I intend to bring on them because of the evil of their deeds.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[4] Say to them: This is what the LORD says: If you will not listen to me and walk in my law, which I have set before you,
[Jeremiah] [26]:[5] and heed the words of my servants the prophets, whom I have sent to you again and again, though you have not listened,
[Jeremiah] [26]:[6] then I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse among all the nations of the earth.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[7] The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[8] And when Jeremiah had finished saying everything the LORD had commanded him to say to all the people, the priests, the prophets, and all the people seized him and said, "You must die!
[Jeremiah] [26]:[9] Why have you prophesied in the name of the LORD that this house will become like Shiloh and this city will be desolate, without an inhabitant?" And all the people gathered against Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[10] When the officials of Judah heard of these things, they came up from the king's palace to the house of the LORD and took their seats at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD's house.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[11] Then the priests and the prophets said to the officials and to all the people, "This man deserves a sentence of death, for he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your own ears."
[Jeremiah] [26]:[12] Then Jeremiah said to all the officials and all the people: "The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house and this city everything you have heard.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[13] Now then, reform your ways and your deeds, and obey the voice of the LORD your God, and the LORD will relent of the disaster he has pronounced against you.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[14] As for me, I am in your hands. Do with me whatever seems good and right to you.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[15] But know for certain that if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood on yourselves, on this city, and on its inhabitants; for in truth the LORD has sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing."
[Jeremiah] [26]:[16] Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, "This man does not deserve a sentence of death, for he has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God."
[Jeremiah] [26]:[17] And some of the elders of the land rose and said to the whole assembly of the people:
[Jeremiah] [26]:[18] "Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and he said to all the people of Judah: 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins, and the temple mount a wooded height.'
[Jeremiah] [26]:[19] Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did he not fear the LORD and seek his favor, so that the LORD relented of the disaster he had pronounced against them? But we would be bringing great harm on our own lives!
[Jeremiah] [26]:[20] Now there was also a man named Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim, who prophesied in the name of the LORD. He prophesied against this city and this land in words just like Jeremiah's.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[21] When King Jehoiakim and all his warriors and all the officials heard his words, the king sought to put him to death. But Uriah heard of it and was afraid, so he fled and went to Egypt.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[22] Then King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt: Elnathan son of Achbor and others with him.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[23] They brought Uriah out of Egypt and took him to King Jehoiakim, who struck him down with the sword and threw his corpse among the graves of the common people.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[24] But Ahikam son of Shaphan gave Jeremiah his support, so that he was not handed over to the people to be put to death.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[1] At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:[fn]
[Jeremiah] [27]:[2] This is what the LORD said to me: Make yourself straps and crossbars for a yoke, and put them on your neck.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[3] Then send them to the king of Edom, the king of Moab, the king of the Ammonites, the king of Tyre, and the king of Sidon, by the hand of the envoys who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[4] Give them this charge for their masters: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says—tell your masters this:
[Jeremiah] [27]:[5] By my great power and my outstretched arm I made the earth, along with the people and the animals that are on it, and I give it to whomever I please.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[6] Now I have handed all these lands over to my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; even the wild animals I have given him to serve him.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[7] All nations will serve him and his son and his grandson, until the time comes for his own land as well; then many nations and great kings will make him their servant.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[8] But any nation or kingdom that will not serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and will not bend its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon—that nation I will punish with sword, famine, and plague, declares the LORD, until I have destroyed it by his hand.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[9] So do not listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dreams, your fortune-tellers, or your sorcerers, who tell you, "You will not serve the king of Babylon."
[Jeremiah] [27]:[10] They are prophesying lies to you, and the result will be that you are carried far from your land; I will drive you out, and you will perish.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[11] But the nation that bends its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him—that nation I will leave on its own soil, declares the LORD, to work it and live there.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[12] To Zedekiah king of Judah I spoke in the same way: Bend your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon; serve him and his people, and you will live.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[13] Why should you and your people die by sword, famine, and plague, as the LORD has declared against any nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?
[Jeremiah] [27]:[14] Do not listen to the words of the prophets who tell you, "You will not serve the king of Babylon," for they are prophesying lies to you.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[15] I have not sent them, declares the LORD. They are prophesying falsely in my name, so that I will drive you out and you will perish—you and the prophets who prophesy to you.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[16] Then I said to the priests and to all this people: This is what the LORD says: Do not listen to the words of your prophets who tell you, "Look, the vessels of the LORD's house will soon be brought back from Babylon." They are prophesying lies to you.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[17] Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon, and you will live. Why should this city become a ruin?
[Jeremiah] [27]:[18] If they are prophets and the word of the LORD is with them, let them plead with the LORD of hosts that the vessels still left in the house of the LORD, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem not be carried off to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[19] For this is what the LORD of hosts says about the pillars, the bronze Sea, the stands, and the rest of the vessels still left in this city—
[Jeremiah] [27]:[20] those that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[21] Yes, this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says about the vessels still left in the house of the LORD, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem:
[Jeremiah] [27]:[22] They will be taken to Babylon and remain there until the day I attend to them, declares the LORD. Then I will bring them up and restore them to this place.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[1] That same year, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur, who was from Gibeon, said to me in the house of the LORD, in the presence of the priests and all the people:
[Jeremiah] [28]:[2] "This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[3] Within two years I will bring back to this place all the vessels of the LORD's house that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from this place and carried to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[4] And I will bring back to this place Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the exiles of Judah who went to Babylon, declares the LORD, for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon."
[Jeremiah] [28]:[5] Then the prophet Jeremiah answered the prophet Hananiah in the presence of the priests and all the people who were standing in the house of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[6] The prophet Jeremiah said, "Amen! May the LORD do so. May the LORD fulfill the words you have prophesied and bring back the vessels of the LORD's house and all the exiles from Babylon to this place.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[7] But listen now to this word I speak in your hearing and in the hearing of all the people:
[Jeremiah] [28]:[8] The prophets who came before me and before you from ancient times prophesied war, disaster, and plague against many lands and great kingdoms.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[9] As for the prophet who prophesies peace, only when his word comes true will it be known that the LORD has truly sent him."
[Jeremiah] [28]:[10] Then the prophet Hananiah took the yoke off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah and broke it,
[Jeremiah] [28]:[11] and Hananiah said in the presence of all the people, "This is what the LORD says: In just this way, within two years, I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon off the neck of all the nations." And the prophet Jeremiah went on his way.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[12] After the prophet Hananiah had broken the yoke off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
[Jeremiah] [28]:[13] "Go and tell Hananiah: This is what the LORD says: You have broken yokes of wood, but in their place you have made yokes of iron.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[14] For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I have put an iron yoke on the neck of all these nations, to make them serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and serve him they will. I have even given him the wild animals."
[Jeremiah] [28]:[15] Then the prophet Jeremiah said to the prophet Hananiah, "Listen, Hananiah! The LORD has not sent you, yet you have made this people trust in a lie.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[16] Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to remove you from the face of the earth. This very year you will die, because you have spoken rebellion against the LORD."
[Jeremiah] [28]:[17] And the prophet Hananiah died that same year, in the seventh month.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[1] These are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the surviving elders of the exile, and to the priests, the prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[2] This was after King Jehoiachin, the queen mother, the court officials, the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, and the craftsmen and metalworkers had gone out from Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[3] He sent it by the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in Babylon. It said:
[Jeremiah] [29]:[4] This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles whom I carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon:
[Jeremiah] [29]:[5] Build houses and settle down; plant gardens and eat their fruit.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[6] Take wives and have sons and daughters; find wives for your sons and give your daughters in marriage, so that they too may have sons and daughters. Multiply there; do not dwindle away.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[7] Seek the welfare of the city where I have sent you into exile, and pray to the LORD on its behalf, for in its welfare you will find your welfare.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[8] For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Do not let your prophets among you or your diviners deceive you, and do not listen to the dreams that you encourage them to dream.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[9] They are prophesying lies to you in my name. I did not send them, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[10] For this is what the LORD says: When Babylon's seventy years are complete, I will attend to you and fulfill my good promise to you, to bring you back to this place.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[11] For I know the plans I have for you, declares the LORD—plans for peace and not for harm, to give you a future and a hope.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[12] Then you will call on me and come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[13] You will seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[14] I will let myself be found by you, declares the LORD, and I will restore your fortunes. I will gather you from all the nations and all the places where I have driven you, declares the LORD, and I will bring you back to the place from which I sent you into exile.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[15] But you say, "The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon."
[Jeremiah] [29]:[16] This is what the LORD says about the king who sits on David's throne and about all the people who remain in this city, your brothers who did not go with you into exile—
[Jeremiah] [29]:[17] this is what the LORD of hosts says: I am sending sword, famine, and plague against them, and I will make them like rotten figs, too bad to be eaten.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[18] I will pursue them with sword, famine, and plague, and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth—a curse, a desolation, an object of scorn and reproach among all the nations where I have driven them.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[19] For they did not listen to my words, declares the LORD, which I sent to them again and again by my servants the prophets—and you did not listen either, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[20] So hear the word of the LORD, all you exiles whom I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[21] This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying lies to you in my name: I am handing them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will put them to death before your eyes.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[22] Because of them this curse will be used by all the exiles of Judah in Babylon: "May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon burned in the fire."
[Jeremiah] [29]:[23] For they have done an outrageous thing in Israel: they committed adultery with their neighbors' wives and spoke lying words in my name, which I did not command them. I am the one who knows, and I am witness, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[24] To Shemaiah the Nehelamite you shall say this:
[Jeremiah] [29]:[25] This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: You have sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, and to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, and to all the priests, saying,
[Jeremiah] [29]:[26] "The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to be the officer in charge of the house of the LORD, over every madman who plays the prophet, so that you should put him in the stocks and in irons.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[27] So why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who keeps playing the prophet among you?
[Jeremiah] [29]:[28] For he has even sent word to us in Babylon: 'It will be a long time. Build houses and settle down; plant gardens and eat their fruit.'"
[Jeremiah] [29]:[29] Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[30] Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
[Jeremiah] [29]:[31] Send word to all the exiles: This is what the LORD says concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you when I did not send him, and has made you trust in a lie,
[Jeremiah] [29]:[32] Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am going to punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. He will have no one left living among this people, nor will he see the good I am going to do for my people, declares the LORD, because he has spoken rebellion against the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[1] The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
[Jeremiah] [30]:[2] This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Write in a book every word I have spoken to you.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[3] For the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel and Judah, says the LORD, and bring them back to the land I gave their fathers, and they will take possession of it.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[4] These are the words the LORD spoke concerning Israel and Judah:
[Jeremiah] [30]:[5] This is what the LORD says: We have heard a cry of terror—panic, and no peace.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[6] Ask now and see: can a man give birth? Why then do I see every warrior with his hands on his belly like a woman in labor, and every face turned deathly pale?
[Jeremiah] [30]:[7] How dreadful that day will be! There has never been one like it. It is a time of distress for Jacob, yet he will be saved out of it.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[8] On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, I will break the yoke from your neck and tear off your bonds, and strangers will no longer make you their slave.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[9] They will serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[10] So do not be afraid, my servant Jacob; do not be dismayed, Israel, declares the LORD. For I will surely save you from far away, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will come back and live in quiet and safety, and no one will make him afraid.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[11] For I am with you to save you, declares the LORD. I will make an end of all the nations among which I scattered you, but you I will not destroy. I will discipline you with justice; I will by no means leave you unpunished.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[12] For this is what the LORD says: Your wound is incurable, your injury beyond healing.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[13] There is no one to plead your cause, no remedy for your sore, no cure for you.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[14] All your lovers have forgotten you; they no longer look for you. I have struck you as an enemy strikes, with the discipline of the merciless, because your guilt is so great and your sins so many.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[15] Why do you cry out over your wound, over pain that has no cure? Because your guilt is so great and your sins so many, I have done this to you.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[16] But all who devour you will be devoured; all your enemies will go into exile. Those who plunder you will be plundered; all who prey on you I will make prey.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[17] I will restore you to health and heal your wounds, declares the LORD, because you are called an outcast, Zion for whom no one cares.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[18] This is what the LORD says: I will restore the fortunes of Jacob's tents and have compassion on his dwellings. The city will be rebuilt on its ruins, and the palace will stand in its rightful place.
