[Jeremiah] [30]:[19] From them will come songs of thanksgiving and the sound of laughter. I will make them many, not few; I will bring them honor, and they will not be despised.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[20] His children will be as in days of old, and his community will stand firm before me. I will punish all who oppress him.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[21] Their leader will be one of their own; their ruler will come from among them. I will bring him near, and he will approach me—for who on his own would dare to draw near to me? declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[22] You will be my people, and I will be your God.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[23] See, the storm of the LORD bursts out in fury, a whirling tempest that breaks over the heads of the wicked.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[24] The LORD's burning anger will not turn back until he has accomplished the purpose of his heart. In days to come you will understand this.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[1] At that time, declares the LORD, I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[2] This is what the LORD says: The people who survived the sword found grace in the wilderness; Israel went out to find its rest.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[3] From far away the LORD appeared to me: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you to myself with faithful love.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[4] Again I will build you, and you shall be rebuilt, O virgin Israel. Again you will take up your tambourines and go out dancing with the joyful.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[5] Again you will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria; the planters will plant and enjoy the fruit.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[6] For there will come a day when the watchmen call out on the hills of Ephraim, "Rise up, let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God!"
[Jeremiah] [31]:[7] For this is what the LORD says: Sing with joy for Jacob; shout aloud at the head of the nations. Proclaim it, give praise, and say, "LORD, save your people, the remnant of Israel!"
[Jeremiah] [31]:[8] See, I am bringing them from the land of the north, gathering them from the ends of the earth—among them the blind and the lame, the pregnant woman and the one in labor together; a great assembly will return here.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[9] They will come with weeping, and with pleas for mercy I will lead them back. I will guide them to streams of water on a level path where they will not stumble, for I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[10] Hear the word of the LORD, you nations, and declare it in the distant coastlands: He who scattered Israel will gather him and will guard him as a shepherd guards his flock.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[11] For the LORD has ransomed Jacob and redeemed him from the hand of one stronger than he.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[12] They will come and sing for joy on the heights of Zion; they will stream to the goodness of the LORD—the grain, the new wine, and the oil, the young of the flocks and herds. Their life will be like a well-watered garden, and they will never languish again.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[13] Then the young woman will rejoice in the dance, and the young men and the old together. I will turn their mourning into gladness; I will comfort them and give them joy instead of sorrow.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[14] I will fill the priests with abundance, and my people will be satisfied with my goodness, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[15] This is what the LORD says: A voice is heard in Ramah, mourning and bitter weeping—Rachel weeping for her children, refusing to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[16] This is what the LORD says: Keep your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your labor, declares the LORD; they will return from the land of the enemy.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[17] There is hope for your future, declares the LORD; your children will return to their own land.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[18] I have surely heard Ephraim grieving: "You disciplined me, and I was disciplined, like an untrained calf. Bring me back, and I will return, for you are the LORD my God.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[19] After I turned away, I repented; after I came to understand, I struck my thigh in grief. I was ashamed and humiliated, for I bore the disgrace of my youth."
[Jeremiah] [31]:[20] Is not Ephraim my dear son, the child in whom I delight? For as often as I speak against him, I still remember him. Therefore my heart yearns for him; I will surely have mercy on him, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[21] Set up road markers for yourself; put up guideposts. Fix your mind on the highway, the road you traveled. Return, O virgin Israel, return to these cities of yours.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[22] How long will you waver, unfaithful daughter? For the LORD has created something new on the earth: a woman shall encompass a man.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[23] This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Once again they will speak these words in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes: "May the LORD bless you, O dwelling of righteousness, O holy mountain."
[Jeremiah] [31]:[24] Judah and the people of all its towns will live there together—farmers and shepherds who move about with their flocks.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[25] For I have satisfied the weary soul, and every languishing soul I have filled.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[26] At this I awoke and looked around, and my sleep had been sweet to me.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[27] The days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of people and the seed of animals.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[28] And just as I watched over them to uproot and tear down, to overthrow, destroy, and bring disaster, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[29] In those days they will no longer say, "The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge."
[Jeremiah] [31]:[30] Instead, each will die for his own guilt; whoever eats the sour grapes, his own teeth will be set on edge.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[31] The days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[32] It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt—my covenant that they broke, though I was their husband, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[33] But this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the LORD: I will put my law within them and write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[34] No longer will anyone teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, "Know the LORD," for they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares the LORD. For I will forgive their guilt and remember their sin no more.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[35] This is what the LORD says—he who gives the sun for light by day, who fixes the order of the moon and the stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so its waves roar; the LORD of hosts is his name:
[Jeremiah] [31]:[36] Only if these fixed orders depart from before me, declares the LORD, will the offspring of Israel ever cease to be a nation before me, for all time.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[37] This is what the LORD says: Only if the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below explored will I reject all the offspring of Israel for all they have done, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[38] The days are coming, declares the LORD, when this city will be rebuilt for the LORD, from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[39] The measuring line will stretch out farther, straight to the hill of Gareb, and then turn toward Goah.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[40] The whole valley of the dead bodies and the ashes, and all the terraced fields as far as the Kidron Valley, to the corner of the Horse Gate on the east, will be holy to the LORD. The city will never again be uprooted or torn down.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[1] The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[2] At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was confined in the courtyard of the guard in the palace of the king of Judah.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[3] Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up there, saying, "Why do you prophesy, 'This is what the LORD says: I am about to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[4] "'Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape the hands of the Chaldeans, but will surely be handed over to the king of Babylon. He will speak with him face to face and see him with his own eyes.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[5] He will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and there he will remain until I deal with him, declares the LORD. Though you fight against the Chaldeans, you will not succeed.'"
[Jeremiah] [32]:[6] Jeremiah said: The word of the LORD came to me:
[Jeremiah] [32]:[7] Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle is coming to you to say, "Buy my field at Anathoth, for you have the right of redemption to buy it."
[Jeremiah] [32]:[8] Then, just as the LORD had said, my cousin Hanamel came to me in the courtyard of the guard and said, "Buy my field at Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, for you have the right of inheritance and the right of redemption. Buy it for yourself." Then I knew this was the word of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[9] So I bought the field at Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel and weighed out the silver for him—seventeen shekels of silver.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[10] I signed the deed and sealed it, called in witnesses, and weighed out the silver on the scales.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[11] Then I took the deed of purchase—the sealed copy containing the terms and conditions, and the open copy—
[Jeremiah] [32]:[12] and I gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, in the presence of my cousin Hanamel, of the witnesses who had signed the deed, and of all the Judeans sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[13] In their presence I gave Baruch these instructions:
[Jeremiah] [32]:[14] "This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Take these documents—both the sealed deed of purchase and the open copy—and put them in a clay jar so that they will last a long time.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[15] For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Houses, fields, and vineyards will again be bought in this land."
[Jeremiah] [32]:[16] After I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the LORD:
[Jeremiah] [32]:[17] "Ah, Lord GOD! You made the heavens and the earth by your great power and outstretched arm. Nothing is too hard for you.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[18] You show steadfast love to thousands, but you bring the guilt of the fathers into the laps of their children after them. O great and mighty God, whose name is the LORD of hosts,
[Jeremiah] [32]:[19] great in counsel and mighty in deed: your eyes are open to all the ways of the children of men, to reward each one according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[20] You performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and you have continued them to this day, both in Israel and among all mankind, and you have made for yourself a name that endures to this day.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[21] You brought your people Israel out of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a mighty hand and outstretched arm, and with great terror.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[22] You gave them this land, which you had sworn to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[23] They came in and took possession of it, but they did not obey your voice or walk in your law. They did nothing of all you commanded them to do, and so you brought all this disaster upon them.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[24] See how the siege ramps have reached the city to take it! Because of the sword, famine, and plague, the city is being handed over to the Chaldeans who are attacking it. What you said has happened, and now you see it.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[25] And yet, Lord GOD, you said to me, 'Buy the field with silver and call in witnesses'—though the city is being handed over to the Chaldeans."
[Jeremiah] [32]:[26] Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
[Jeremiah] [32]:[27] "See, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is anything too hard for me?
[Jeremiah] [32]:[28] Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am about to hand this city over to the Chaldeans and to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will capture it.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[29] The Chaldeans who are attacking this city will come in, set it on fire, and burn it down, along with the houses where the people burned incense on the roofs to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods, provoking me to anger.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[30] From their youth the people of Israel and the people of Judah have done nothing but evil in my sight; indeed, the people of Israel have done nothing but provoke me by the work of their hands, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[31] This city has so stirred my anger and wrath, from the day it was built until now, that I must remove it from my sight—
[Jeremiah] [32]:[32] because of all the evil the people of Israel and Judah have done to provoke me: they, their kings and officials, their priests and prophets, the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[33] They turned their backs to me and not their faces; though I taught them again and again, they would not listen or accept correction.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[34] They set up their detestable idols in the house that bears my name, to defile it.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[35] They built high places to Baal in the Valley of Ben Hinnom to sacrifice their sons and daughters to Molech—something I never commanded, something that never entered my mind—committing this abomination and leading Judah into sin.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[36] Now therefore, this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about this city of which you say, 'It has been handed over to the king of Babylon by sword, famine, and plague':
[Jeremiah] [32]:[37] I will surely gather them from all the lands where I banished them in my fierce anger and great wrath. I will bring them back to this place and let them live in safety.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[38] They will be my people, and I will be their God.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[39] I will give them one heart and one way, so that they will always fear me, for their own good and the good of their children after them.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[40] I will make an everlasting covenant with them: I will never turn away from doing good to them, and I will put the fear of me in their hearts so that they will not turn away from me.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[41] I will rejoice in doing them good, and with all my heart and soul I will faithfully plant them in this land.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[42] For this is what the LORD says: Just as I brought all this great disaster on this people, so I will bring on them all the good I have promised them.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[43] Fields will again be bought in this land of which you say, 'It is a wasteland, without people or animals, handed over to the Chaldeans.'
[Jeremiah] [32]:[44] Fields will be bought with silver, deeds will be written, sealed, and witnessed—in the land of Benjamin, in the places around Jerusalem, in the towns of Judah, in the towns of the hill country, of the western foothills, and of the Negev—for I will restore their fortunes, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[1] The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still confined in the courtyard of the guard:
[Jeremiah] [33]:[2] This is what the LORD says, he who made the earth, the LORD who formed it and established it—the LORD is his name:
[Jeremiah] [33]:[3] Call to me, and I will answer you. I will tell you great and hidden things you do not know.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[4] For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the houses of this city and the houses of the kings of Judah that are torn down for use against the siege ramps and the sword:
[Jeremiah] [33]:[5] They come to fight the Chaldeans, only to fill these places with the corpses of those I strike down in my anger and my wrath—for I have hidden my face from this city because of all their evil.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[6] Yet I am going to bring it healing and restoration; I will heal my people and reveal to them abundant peace and security.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[7] I will restore the fortunes of Judah and the fortunes of Israel, and I will rebuild them as they were at first.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[8] I will cleanse them of all the guilt of their sin against me, and I will forgive all their sins against me and all their acts of rebellion against me.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[9] Then this city will bring me joyful renown, praise, and honor before all the nations of the earth, when they hear of all the good I do for my people. They will tremble in awe at all the good and all the peace I provide for it.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[10] This is what the LORD says: You say of this place, "It is a wasteland, without people or animals." Yet in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, now desolate and empty of people, inhabitants, and animals, there will be heard once more
[Jeremiah] [33]:[11] the sound of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the bride, the voices of those who bring thank offerings to the house of the LORD and sing, "Give thanks to the LORD of hosts, for the LORD is good; his mercy endures forever." For I will restore the fortunes of the land as they were at first, says the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[12] This is what the LORD of hosts says: In this place, now a wasteland without people or animals, and in all its towns, there will once again be pastures where shepherds rest their flocks.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[13] In the towns of the hill country, the towns of the lowland, and the towns of the Negev; in the land of Benjamin, the villages around Jerusalem, and the towns of Judah, flocks will again pass under the hand of the one who counts them, says the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[14] The days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will fulfill the gracious promise I made to the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[15] In those days and at that time I will make a righteous Branch sprout from David's line; he will do what is just and right in the land.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[16] In those days Judah will be saved and Jerusalem will live in safety. And this is the name by which it will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[17] For this is what the LORD says: David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel,
[Jeremiah] [33]:[18] nor will the Levitical priests ever lack a man to stand before me continually, offering burnt offerings, presenting grain offerings, and making sacrifices.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[19] The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
[Jeremiah] [33]:[20] This is what the LORD says: If you could break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night, so that day and night no longer came at their appointed time,
[Jeremiah] [33]:[21] then my covenant with David my servant could also be broken, so that he would have no descendant to reign on his throne, and so could my covenant with the Levitical priests who minister before me.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[22] As countless as the stars of heaven and as measureless as the sand on the seashore, so will I multiply the descendants of David my servant and the Levites who minister before me.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[23] The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
[Jeremiah] [33]:[24] Have you not noticed what these people are saying: "The LORD has rejected the two families he chose"? So they despise my people and no longer regard them as a nation.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[25] This is what the LORD says: As surely as I have established my covenant with day and night and the fixed order of heaven and earth,
[Jeremiah] [33]:[26] so surely I will not reject the descendants of Jacob and David my servant, nor fail to take rulers from his offspring to rule over the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For I will restore their fortunes and have compassion on them.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[1] The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD while Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army, along with all the kingdoms of the earth under his rule and all the peoples, were fighting against Jerusalem and all its towns:
[Jeremiah] [34]:[2] This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah and tell him, Thus says the LORD: I am handing this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[3] And you will not escape his hand; you will surely be captured and handed over to him. You will see the king of Babylon eye to eye, and he will speak with you face to face, and you will go to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[4] Yet hear the word of the LORD, Zedekiah king of Judah. This is what the LORD says concerning you: You will not die by the sword;
[Jeremiah] [34]:[5] you will die in peace. As spices were burned for your fathers, the kings before you, so they will burn spices for you, and they will mourn for you, "Alas, lord!" For I myself have spoken this word, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[6] So Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,
[Jeremiah] [34]:[7] while the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against the remaining cities of Judah—against Lachish and Azekah, for these were the fortified cities still left in Judah.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[8] The word came to Jeremiah from the LORD after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim liberty for them:
[Jeremiah] [34]:[9] that everyone should set free his Hebrew slaves, male and female, so that no one would hold a fellow Judean in slavery.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[10] All the officials and all the people who had entered into the covenant—that everyone would set free his male and female slaves and no longer hold them in slavery—obeyed and set them free.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[11] But afterward they changed their minds and took back the male and female slaves they had set free, forcing them into slavery again.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[12] Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
[Jeremiah] [34]:[13] This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I made a covenant with your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, saying:
[Jeremiah] [34]:[14] At the end of seven years, each of you must set free his Hebrew brother who has sold himself to you. When he has served you six years, you must let him go free. But your fathers did not listen to me or pay attention.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[15] Just now you turned back and did what is right in my eyes: each of you proclaimed liberty to his neighbor, and you made a covenant before me in the house that bears my name.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[16] But then you turned back and profaned my name; each of you took back the male and female slaves you had set free to go where they pleased, and you forced them to become your slaves again.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[17] Therefore this is what the LORD says: You have not obeyed me by proclaiming liberty, each to his brother and to his neighbor. So now I proclaim liberty for you, declares the LORD—liberty to the sword, to plague, and to famine! And I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[18] The men who violated my covenant and did not keep the terms of the covenant they made before me—I will make them like the calf they cut in two and walked between its pieces:
[Jeremiah] [34]:[19] the officials of Judah and of Jerusalem, the court officials, the priests, and all the people of the land who walked between the pieces of the calf.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[20] I will hand them over to their enemies and to those who seek their lives, and their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[21] And Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials I will hand over to their enemies, to those who seek their lives, and to the army of the king of Babylon that has withdrawn from you.
[Jeremiah] [34]:[22] I am about to give the command, declares the LORD, and I will bring them back to this city. They will fight against it, capture it, and burn it down. And I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, with no one living there.
[Jeremiah] [35]:[1] This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
[Jeremiah] [35]:[2] "Go to the house of the Rechabites and speak with them. Bring them to the house of the LORD, into one of the chambers, and offer them wine to drink."
[Jeremiah] [35]:[3] So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, the son of Habazziniah, along with his brothers and all his sons—the whole house of the Rechabites—
[Jeremiah] [35]:[4] and I brought them to the house of the LORD, into the chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God. It was next to the chamber of the officials, above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold.
[Jeremiah] [35]:[5] Then I set before the members of the house of the Rechabites bowls full of wine and cups, and I said to them, "Drink some wine."
[Jeremiah] [35]:[6] But they answered, "We drink no wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us: 'You and your children are never to drink wine.
[Jeremiah] [35]:[7] You are not to build houses, or sow seed, or plant vineyards, or own them. Instead, you are to live in tents all your days, so that you may live long in the land where you are sojourning.'
[Jeremiah] [35]:[8] We have obeyed the voice of Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, in everything he commanded us: to drink no wine all our days—neither we, nor our wives, nor our sons and daughters.
[Jeremiah] [35]:[9] We build no houses to live in, and we have no vineyard or field or seed.
[Jeremiah] [35]:[10] We have lived in tents, obeying and doing everything our father Jonadab commanded us.
[Jeremiah] [35]:[11] But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon marched into the land, we said, 'Come, let us go into Jerusalem to escape the army of the Chaldeans and the army of the Arameans.' So we have been living in Jerusalem."
[Jeremiah] [35]:[12] Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
[Jeremiah] [35]:[13] "This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Go and say to the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, Will you not accept correction and listen to my words? declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [35]:[14] The command of Jonadab son of Rechab, who ordered his sons not to drink wine, has been carried out. To this day they have drunk none, because they obeyed their father's command. But I have spoken to you again and again, and you have not listened to me.
[Jeremiah] [35]:[15] Again and again I sent you all my servants the prophets, saying, 'Turn now, each of you, from your evil way; mend your deeds and do not follow other gods to serve them, and dwell in the land I gave to you and your fathers.' But you would not incline your ear or listen to me.
[Jeremiah] [35]:[16] The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab have kept the command their father gave them, but this people has not listened to me.
[Jeremiah] [35]:[17] Therefore this is what the LORD God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to bring on Judah and on all the inhabitants of Jerusalem every disaster I have pronounced against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen; I called to them and they did not answer."
[Jeremiah] [35]:[18] Then Jeremiah said to the house of the Rechabites, "This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Because you have obeyed the command of Jonadab your father and have kept all his precepts, doing everything he commanded you,
[Jeremiah] [35]:[19] therefore this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Jonadab son of Rechab will never lack a descendant to stand before me."
[Jeremiah] [36]:[1] In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
[Jeremiah] [36]:[2] "Take a scroll and write on it all the words I have spoken to you concerning Israel and Judah and all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you in the days of Josiah until now.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[3] Perhaps when the house of Judah hears of all the disaster I intend to bring on them, they will each turn from their evil way, and I will forgive their guilt and their sin."
[Jeremiah] [36]:[4] So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and as Jeremiah dictated, Baruch wrote on the scroll all the words the LORD had spoken to him.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[5] Then Jeremiah instructed Baruch: "I am restricted; I cannot go to the house of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[6] So you go, and on a day of fasting read aloud from the scroll the words of the LORD that you wrote at my dictation. Read them in the hearing of the people at the house of the LORD, and in the hearing of all the people of Judah who come in from their towns.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[7] Perhaps their plea for mercy will come before the LORD, and each of them will turn from their evil way, for great is the anger and wrath the LORD has pronounced against this people."
[Jeremiah] [36]:[8] Baruch son of Neriah did everything Jeremiah the prophet had commanded him, reading the words of the LORD from the scroll at the house of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[9] In the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, a fast before the LORD was proclaimed for all the people of Jerusalem and for all who came in to Jerusalem from the towns of Judah.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[10] Then, in the hearing of all the people, Baruch read Jeremiah's words from the scroll at the house of the LORD, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD's house.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[11] When Micaiah son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, heard all the words of the LORD read from the scroll,
[Jeremiah] [36]:[12] he went down to the king's palace, to the chamber of the scribe, where all the officials were sitting: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the other officials.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[13] Micaiah reported to them everything he had heard when Baruch read the scroll in the hearing of the people.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[14] So all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi, to say to Baruch, "Bring the scroll you read in the hearing of the people, and come." So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[15] They said to him, "Sit down, please, and read it to us." So Baruch read it to them.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[16] When they had heard all the words, they turned to one another in fear and said to Baruch, "We must report all this to the king."
[Jeremiah] [36]:[17] Then they asked Baruch, "Tell us, please, how did you write all these words? Did they come from his own mouth?"
[Jeremiah] [36]:[18] Baruch answered, "He dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them in ink on the scroll."
[Jeremiah] [36]:[19] Then the officials said to Baruch, "Go and hide, you and Jeremiah. Let no one know where you are."
[Jeremiah] [36]:[20] After storing the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, they went to the king in the courtyard and reported everything to him.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[21] The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and he brought it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe and read it to the king and to all the officials standing beside him.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[22] It was the ninth month, and the king was sitting in his winter quarters with a fire burning in the brazier before him.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[23] Each time Jehudi finished reading three or four columns, the king would cut them off with a scribe's knife and throw them into the fire in the brazier, until the entire scroll was consumed in the fire.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[24] Yet neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words was afraid, nor did any of them tear their clothes.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[25] Even when Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[26] Instead the king ordered Jerahmeel, a son of the king, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the LORD had hidden them.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[27] After the king had burned the scroll containing the words Baruch had written at Jeremiah's dictation, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
[Jeremiah] [36]:[28] "Take another scroll and write on it all the words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[29] And say concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah: This is what the LORD says: You burned that scroll and said, 'Why did you write on it that the king of Babylon would surely come and destroy this land and wipe out both people and animals from it?'
[Jeremiah] [36]:[30] Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: "He will have no one to sit on David's throne; his body will be thrown out, exposed to the heat by day and the frost by night.
[Jeremiah] [36]:[31] I will punish him and his offspring and his servants for their guilt, and I will bring on them, on the people of Jerusalem, and on the people of Judah every disaster I pronounced against them, because they would not listen."
[Jeremiah] [36]:[32] So Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, and as Jeremiah dictated, he wrote on it all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to them.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[1] Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned as king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim, for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had made Zedekiah king in the land of Judah.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[2] But neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words the LORD had spoken through Jeremiah the prophet.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[3] Yet King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet with this message: "Please pray for us to the LORD our God."
[Jeremiah] [37]:[4] At that time Jeremiah was still moving freely among the people, for they had not yet put him in prison.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[5] Meanwhile Pharaoh's army had marched out of Egypt, and when the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the report of it, they withdrew from Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[6] Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet:
[Jeremiah] [37]:[7] This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Tell the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of me: Pharaoh's army, which marched out to help you, is going back to its own land, to Egypt.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[8] The Chaldeans will return and attack this city; they will capture it and burn it down.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[9] This is what the LORD says: Do not deceive yourselves, thinking, "The Chaldeans will surely leave us." They will not leave.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[10] Even if you struck down the whole Chaldean army that is fighting against you, and only wounded men were left in their tents, they would rise up and burn this city down.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[11] When the Chaldean army had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
[Jeremiah] [37]:[12] Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to take possession of his share of property there among the people.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[13] But when he reached the Benjamin Gate, an officer of the guard was on duty there, whose name was Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah, and he seized Jeremiah the prophet and said, "You are deserting to the Chaldeans!"
[Jeremiah] [37]:[14] "That's a lie," Jeremiah said. "I am not deserting to the Chaldeans." But Irijah would not listen to him; he arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[15] The officials were enraged at Jeremiah. They had him beaten and imprisoned in the house of Jonathan the secretary, which they had made into a prison.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[16] So Jeremiah was put into the dungeon, into the vaulted cells, and there he remained many days.
[Jeremiah] [37]:[17] Then King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought to the palace, where he questioned him in private: "Is there any word from the LORD?" "There is," Jeremiah answered. "You will be handed over to the king of Babylon."
[Jeremiah] [37]:[18] Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "What wrong have I done to you or your servants or this people, that you have put me in prison?
[Jeremiah] [37]:[19] And where are your prophets who prophesied to you, saying, 'The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land'?
[Jeremiah] [37]:[20] But now, please listen, my lord the king. Let my plea come before you: do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the secretary, or I will die there."
[Jeremiah] [37]:[21] So King Zedekiah gave orders, and Jeremiah was placed in the courtyard of the guard and given a loaf of bread each day from the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
[Jeremiah] [38]:[1] Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words Jeremiah was speaking to all the people:
[Jeremiah] [38]:[2] "This is what the LORD says: Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, by famine, or by plague, but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live; he will escape with his life and survive.
[Jeremiah] [38]:[3] This is what the LORD says: This city will surely be handed over to the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it."
[Jeremiah] [38]:[4] So the officials said to the king, "This man must be put to death. By speaking such words to them he is undermining the courage of the soldiers who are left in this city and of all the people. This man is not seeking the welfare of this people, but their ruin."
[Jeremiah] [38]:[5] King Zedekiah answered, "He is in your hands; the king can do nothing to stop you."
[Jeremiah] [38]:[6] So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah the king's son, which was in the courtyard of the guard. They lowered Jeremiah by ropes. There was no water in the cistern, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mud.
[Jeremiah] [38]:[7] But Ebed-melech the Cushite, a court official in the king's palace, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. While the king was sitting in the Benjamin Gate,
[Jeremiah] [38]:[8] Ebed-melech left the palace and said to him,
[Jeremiah] [38]:[9] "My lord the king, these men have done wrong in all they have done to Jeremiah the prophet. They have thrown him into the cistern, where he will starve to death, since there is no more bread in the city."
[Jeremiah] [38]:[10] Then the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, "Take thirty men with you from here and lift Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies."
[Jeremiah] [38]:[11] So Ebed-melech took the men with him and went to a room beneath the treasury in the palace. From there he took worn-out rags and cast-off clothing and let them down with ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern.
[Jeremiah] [38]:[12] Ebed-melech the Cushite called down to Jeremiah, "Put these rags and cast-off clothing under your armpits, to pad the ropes." Jeremiah did so,
[Jeremiah] [38]:[13] and they pulled him up by the ropes and lifted him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
[Jeremiah] [38]:[14] Then King Zedekiah sent for Jeremiah the prophet and had him brought to the third entrance of the LORD's house. "I am going to ask you something," the king said. "Hide nothing from me."
[Jeremiah] [38]:[15] Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I tell you, you will surely put me to death. And if I give you advice, you will not listen to me."
[Jeremiah] [38]:[16] But King Zedekiah swore to Jeremiah in private, "As surely as the LORD lives, who gave us breath, I will not put you to death or hand you over to those men who want to kill you."
[Jeremiah] [38]:[17] Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, says: If you will surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, your life will be spared, this city will not be burned down, and you and your household will live.
[Jeremiah] [38]:[18] But if you will not surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, this city will be handed over to the Chaldeans; they will burn it down, and you yourself will not escape their hands."
[Jeremiah] [38]:[19] King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Jews who have gone over to the Chaldeans; they may hand me over to them, and they will abuse me."
[Jeremiah] [38]:[20] "They will not hand you over," Jeremiah replied. "Obey the voice of the LORD in what I am telling you. Then it will go well with you, and your life will be spared.
[Jeremiah] [38]:[21] But if you refuse to surrender, this is what the LORD has shown me:
[Jeremiah] [38]:[22] All the women left in the palace of the king of Judah will be led out to the officers of the king of Babylon, and they will say to you: 'Your trusted friends misled you and got the better of you. Now that your feet are sunk in the mire, they have turned their backs on you.'
[Jeremiah] [38]:[23] All your wives and children will be led out to the Chaldeans, and you yourself will not escape their hands. You will be captured by the king of Babylon, and you will burn this city down with fire."
[Jeremiah] [38]:[24] Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Let no one know about this conversation, or you may die.
[Jeremiah] [38]:[25] If the officials hear that I have spoken with you and they come and say, 'Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you. Do not hide it from us, or we will kill you'—
[Jeremiah] [38]:[26] then tell them, 'I was pleading with the king not to send me back to Jonathan's house to die there.'"
[Jeremiah] [38]:[27] All the officials did come to Jeremiah and question him, and he told them exactly what the king had ordered him to say. So they said no more to him, for no one had overheard the conversation.
[Jeremiah] [38]:[28] And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured. This is how Jerusalem was taken:
[Jeremiah] [39]:[1] In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with his entire army against Jerusalem and laid siege to it.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[2] In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city was broken open.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[3] Then all the officers of the king of Babylon came in and took their seats in the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim the chief officer, Nergal-sharezer the chief adviser, and all the rest of the officers of the king of Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[4] When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the soldiers saw them, they fled, slipping out of the city by night through the king's garden, by the gate between the two walls, and headed toward the Arabah.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[5] But the Chaldean army pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They seized him and brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he passed sentence on him.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[6] At Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he slaughtered all the nobles of Judah as well.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[7] Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him in bronze shackles to take him to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[8] The Chaldeans burned down the king's palace and the houses of the people, and they tore down the walls of Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[9] Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, carried off to Babylon the rest of the people left in the city, along with those who had deserted to him, and the rest of the people who remained.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[10] But Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, left behind in the land of Judah some of the poorest of the people, who owned nothing, and on that day he gave them vineyards and fields.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[11] Now Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had given orders concerning Jeremiah through Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard:
[Jeremiah] [39]:[12] "Take him and look after him. Do him no harm, but do for him whatever he tells you."
[Jeremiah] [39]:[13] So Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, Nebushazban the chief officer, Nergal-sharezer the chief adviser, and all the chief officers of the king of Babylon sent word,
[Jeremiah] [39]:[14] and they had Jeremiah brought from the courtyard of the guard and handed him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, to take him home. So he lived among the people.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[15] While Jeremiah was still confined in the courtyard of the guard, the word of the LORD came to him:
[Jeremiah] [39]:[16] "Go and say to Ebed-melech the Cushite: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to bring my words against this city—for disaster and not for good—and on that day they will come to pass before your eyes.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[17] But I will rescue you on that day, declares the LORD, and you will not be handed over to the men you dread.
[Jeremiah] [39]:[18] I will surely deliver you; you will not fall by the sword. You will escape with your life, because you have trusted in me, declares the LORD."
[Jeremiah] [40]:[1] The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had released him from Ramah. He had taken him bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah who were being deported to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [40]:[2] The captain of the guard took Jeremiah aside and said to him, "The LORD your God pronounced this disaster against this place,
[Jeremiah] [40]:[3] and now the LORD has brought it about and done just as he said. Because you sinned against the LORD and would not obey his voice, this thing has come upon you.
[Jeremiah] [40]:[4] But now, see, I am freeing you today from the chains on your wrists. If you wish to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you. But if it seems wrong to you to come with me to Babylon, then stay. Look, the whole land lies before you; go wherever it seems good and right to you.
[Jeremiah] [40]:[5] If you choose to remain, then go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and live with him among the people; or go anywhere else you please." Then the captain of the guard gave him provisions and a gift and let him go.
[Jeremiah] [40]:[6] So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and stayed with him among the people who were left in the land.
[Jeremiah] [40]:[7] When all the commanders of the forces who were out in the open country, along with their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and had put under his charge the men, women, and children, those of the poorest of the land who had not been deported to Babylon—
[Jeremiah] [40]:[8] they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite—they and their men.
[Jeremiah] [40]:[9] Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore an oath to them and their men: "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Settle in the land, serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.
[Jeremiah] [40]:[10] As for me, I am staying at Mizpah to represent you before the Chaldeans who come to us. But you, gather in the wine, the summer fruit, and the oil; store them in your jars, and live in the towns you have taken over."
[Jeremiah] [40]:[11] And when all the Judeans in Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom, and in all the other lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan,
[Jeremiah] [40]:[12] they all returned from every place where they had been scattered and came back to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah. And they gathered in wine and summer fruit in great abundance.
[Jeremiah] [40]:[13] Now Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah
[Jeremiah] [40]:[14] and said to him, "Are you not aware that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to take your life?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.
[Jeremiah] [40]:[15] Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke privately to Gedaliah at Mizpah: "Let me go and strike down Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know. Why should he take your life and scatter all the Judeans who have gathered around you, so that the remnant of Judah perishes?"
[Jeremiah] [40]:[16] But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do this thing, for what you are saying about Ishmael is not true."
[Jeremiah] [41]:[1] In the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, who was of royal descent and one of the king's chief officers, came with ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. While they were eating together there at Mizpah,
[Jeremiah] [41]:[2] Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men with him rose up and struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, with the sword, killing the man whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
[Jeremiah] [41]:[3] Ishmael also killed all the Judeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were found there, the fighting men.
[Jeremiah] [41]:[4] On the second day after the murder of Gedaliah, before anyone knew of it,
[Jeremiah] [41]:[5] eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria, their beards shaved, their clothes torn, and their bodies gashed, carrying grain offerings and frankincense to bring to the house of the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [41]:[6] Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went. When he met them, he said, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."
[Jeremiah] [41]:[7] But when they had come into the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the men with him slaughtered them and threw them into a cistern.
[Jeremiah] [41]:[8] Ten of them, however, said to Ishmael, "Do not kill us, for we have hidden stores of wheat, barley, oil, and honey in the fields." So he held back and did not kill them with the others.
[Jeremiah] [41]:[9] The cistern where Ishmael threw all the bodies of the men he had struck down along with Gedaliah was the one King Asa had made as a defense against Baasha king of Israel; Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.
[Jeremiah] [41]:[10] Then Ishmael took captive all the rest of the people at Mizpah—the king's daughters and all the people who were left there, whom Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.
[Jeremiah] [41]:[11] When Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces with him heard of all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done,
[Jeremiah] [41]:[12] they took all their men and went to fight Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They caught up with him at the great pool in Gibeon.
[Jeremiah] [41]:[13] When all the people with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces with him, they were overjoyed.
[Jeremiah] [41]:[14] All the people Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned about and went over to Johanan son of Kareah.
[Jeremiah] [41]:[15] But Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men and fled to the Ammonites.
[Jeremiah] [41]:[16] Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces with him took charge of all the remnant of the people whom he had recovered from Ishmael son of Nethaniah at Mizpah after Ishmael had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam—soldiers, women, children, and court officials whom he brought back from Gibeon.
[Jeremiah] [41]:[17] They set out and stayed at Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem, on their way to Egypt,
[Jeremiah] [41]:[18] to escape the Chaldeans; for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
[Jeremiah] [42]:[1] Then all the commanders of the forces came forward—Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest—
[Jeremiah] [42]:[2] and said to Jeremiah the prophet, "Let our plea come before you: pray for us to the LORD your God, for all this remnant. For we are left few out of many, as your own eyes can see.
[Jeremiah] [42]:[3] Let the LORD your God tell us the way we should go and what we should do."
[Jeremiah] [42]:[4] Jeremiah the prophet answered them, "I have heard you. I will indeed pray to the LORD your God as you have asked, and whatever the LORD answers you, I will tell you; I will keep nothing back from you."
[Jeremiah] [42]:[5] Then they said to Jeremiah, "May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not act on everything the LORD your God sends you to tell us.
[Jeremiah] [42]:[6] Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may go well with us when we obey the voice of the LORD our God."
[Jeremiah] [42]:[7] Ten days later the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.
[Jeremiah] [42]:[8] So he called for Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were with him, and for all the people from the least to the greatest,
[Jeremiah] [42]:[9] and said to them: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says, the one to whom you sent me to lay your plea before him:
[Jeremiah] [42]:[10] If you will indeed remain in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, for I relent of the disaster I have brought upon you.
[Jeremiah] [42]:[11] Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you now fear. Do not be afraid of him, declares the LORD, for I am with you to save you and to deliver you from his hand.
[Jeremiah] [42]:[12] I will grant you compassion, so that he will have compassion on you and restore you to your own land.
[Jeremiah] [42]:[13] But if you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' and so disobey the voice of the LORD your God,
[Jeremiah] [42]:[14] saying, 'No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will see no war, hear no sound of the trumpet, and never go hungry for bread—there we will settle,'
[Jeremiah] [42]:[15] then hear the word of the LORD, you remnant of Judah. This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: If you are determined to go to Egypt and settle there,
[Jeremiah] [42]:[16] then the sword you fear will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine you dread will follow close behind you into Egypt, and there you will die.
[Jeremiah] [42]:[17] All the men who are determined to go to Egypt and settle there will die by the sword, by famine, and by plague. Not one of them will survive or escape the disaster I am bringing upon them.
[Jeremiah] [42]:[18] For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: As my anger and wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will become an object of cursing and horror, of condemnation and reproach, and you will never see this place again.
[Jeremiah] [42]:[19] The LORD has spoken to you, remnant of Judah: Do not go to Egypt. Be certain of this: I have warned you today
[Jeremiah] [42]:[20] that you went astray at the cost of your own lives. For you sent me to the LORD your God, saying, 'Pray for us to the LORD our God; tell us everything the LORD our God says, and we will do it.'
[Jeremiah] [42]:[21] I have told you today, but you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God in anything he sent me to tell you.
[Jeremiah] [42]:[22] So now be certain of this: you will die by the sword, by famine, and by plague in the place where you want to go and settle."
[Jeremiah] [43]:[1] When Jeremiah had finished telling all the people every word of the LORD their God—everything the LORD their God had sent him to tell them, all these words—
[Jeremiah] [43]:[2] Azariah son of Hoshaiah and Johanan son of Kareah and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, "You are lying! The LORD our God did not send you to say, 'Do not go to Egypt to settle there.'
[Jeremiah] [43]:[3] It is Baruch son of Neriah who is inciting you against us, to hand us over to the Chaldeans, so they may kill us or carry us into exile in Babylon."
[Jeremiah] [43]:[4] So Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces and all the people refused to obey the voice of the LORD, which told them to stay in the land of Judah.
[Jeremiah] [43]:[5] Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces took the whole remnant of Judah—those who had come back from all the nations where they had been scattered, to live in the land of Judah:
[Jeremiah] [43]:[6] the men, the women, the children, the king's daughters, and every person whom Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, along with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
[Jeremiah] [43]:[7] They went to the land of Egypt, for they did not obey the voice of the LORD, and they came as far as Tahpanhes.
[Jeremiah] [43]:[8] Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes:
[Jeremiah] [43]:[9] "Take some large stones in your hand and bury them in the mortar of the brick pavement at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah.
[Jeremiah] [43]:[10] Then say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am going to send for my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and I will set his throne over these stones I have buried, and he will spread his royal canopy above them.
[Jeremiah] [43]:[11] He will come and strike the land of Egypt: those destined for death, to death; those for captivity, to captivity; those for the sword, to the sword.
[Jeremiah] [43]:[12] I will set fire to the temples of Egypt's gods; he will burn them and carry the idols off captive. He will wrap up the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps up his cloak, and he will depart from there unharmed.
[Jeremiah] [43]:[13] He will shatter the sacred pillars of Heliopolis, the city of the sun, in the land of Egypt, and he will burn down the temples of Egypt's gods."
[Jeremiah] [44]:[1] The word that came to Jeremiah for all the Judeans living in the land of Egypt—those settled in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and the region of Pathros:
[Jeremiah] [44]:[2] This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: You yourselves saw all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the towns of Judah. Look at them today—ruins, with no one living in them,
[Jeremiah] [44]:[3] because of the evil they did to provoke me, going off to burn incense and serve other gods that neither they nor you nor your fathers had ever known.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[4] Again and again I sent you all my servants the prophets, saying, "Do not do this detestable thing that I hate!"
[Jeremiah] [44]:[5] But they would not listen or pay attention; they would not turn from their evil or stop burning incense to other gods.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[6] So my fury and my anger poured out and blazed through the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, and they became the desolate ruins they are today.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[7] And now, this is what the LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Why are you bringing such great harm on yourselves, cutting off from Judah man and woman, child and infant, leaving yourselves no remnant at all?
[Jeremiah] [44]:[8] Why provoke me with what your hands have made, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where you have come to live? You will destroy yourselves and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[9] Have you forgotten the evils of your fathers and the evils of the kings of Judah and their wives, and your own evils and the evils of your wives, committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
[Jeremiah] [44]:[10] To this day they have shown no remorse, no fear; they have not walked in my law and my statutes, which I set before you and before your fathers.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[11] Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am setting my face against you for disaster, to cut off all Judah.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[12] I will take the remnant of Judah who were determined to go to the land of Egypt and settle there, and they will all meet their end in Egypt. They will fall by the sword and be consumed by famine; from the least to the greatest, they will die by sword and famine, and they will become an object of cursing and horror, of scorn and reproach.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[13] I will punish those living in the land of Egypt just as I punished Jerusalem—with the sword, with famine, and with plague.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[14] None of the remnant of Judah who have gone to live in the land of Egypt will escape or survive to return to the land of Judah, though they long to return and live there. Not one will return, except a few fugitives.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[15] Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, along with all the women standing there—a great assembly—and all the people living in the land of Egypt, in the region of Pathros, answered Jeremiah:
[Jeremiah] [44]:[16] "As for the word you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD—we will not listen to you.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[17] We will most certainly do everything we said we would: we will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, just as we did—we and our fathers, our kings and our officials—in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. Then we had plenty of food, we prospered, and we saw no disaster.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[18] But ever since we stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything and have been consumed by sword and famine."
[Jeremiah] [44]:[19] And the women added, "When we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, was it without our husbands' knowledge that we made cakes shaped in her image and poured out drink offerings to her?"
[Jeremiah] [44]:[20] Then Jeremiah said to all the people—the men and the women, all who had answered him:
[Jeremiah] [44]:[21] "The incense you burned in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem—you and your fathers, your kings and your officials and the people of the land—did the LORD not remember it? Did it not rise up in his mind?
[Jeremiah] [44]:[22] When the LORD could no longer bear the evil of your deeds and the detestable things you did, your land became a desolate ruin and a curse, without inhabitant, as it is today.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[23] Because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD, because you did not obey the voice of the LORD or walk in his law, his statutes, and his decrees, this disaster has overtaken you, as it has today."
[Jeremiah] [44]:[24] Then Jeremiah said to all the people, including all the women: "Hear the word of the LORD, all you of Judah who are in the land of Egypt.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[25] This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives have said with your mouths and carried out with your hands, 'We will certainly fulfill the vows we made to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.' Very well—keep your vows! Carry them out!
[Jeremiah] [44]:[26] Therefore hear the word of the LORD, all you of Judah living in the land of Egypt: I swear by my great name, says the LORD, that never again will my name be invoked by anyone of Judah anywhere in the land of Egypt, saying, 'As the Lord GOD lives.'
[Jeremiah] [44]:[27] See, I am watching over them for harm, not for good. Every man of Judah in the land of Egypt will perish by sword and famine until they are finished.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[28] Those who escape the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, only a few in number. Then the whole remnant of Judah who came to live in Egypt will know whose word stands—mine or theirs.
[Jeremiah] [44]:[29] This will be the sign to you, declares the LORD, that I am going to punish you in this place, so you may know that my words against you will surely stand, bringing disaster:
[Jeremiah] [44]:[30] This is what the LORD says: I am going to hand Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt over to his enemies, to those who seek his life, just as I handed Zedekiah king of Judah over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.
[Jeremiah] [45]:[1] This is the word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah, when he wrote these words on a scroll at Jeremiah's dictation, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
[Jeremiah] [45]:[2] This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning you, Baruch:
[Jeremiah] [45]:[3] You have said, "How wretched I am! The LORD has added grief to my pain. I am worn out with groaning, and I find no rest."
[Jeremiah] [45]:[4] Say this to him: This is what the LORD says: Look — what I have built I am tearing down, and what I have planted I am uprooting; and so it will be throughout the whole land.
[Jeremiah] [45]:[5] And you — are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For I am about to bring disaster on all flesh, declares the LORD, but wherever you go I will grant you your life as spoil.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[1] The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[2] Concerning Egypt, against the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was at Carchemish by the Euphrates River, the army that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
[Jeremiah] [46]:[3] Ready the shields, both small and large, and advance for battle!
[Jeremiah] [46]:[4] Harness the horses; mount up, you riders! Take your stand with helmets on; polish the spears, put on the armor!
[Jeremiah] [46]:[5] Why then do I see them terrified, falling back? Their warriors are beaten down; they flee headlong and never turn, for terror is on every side, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[6] The swift cannot flee, the warrior cannot escape. In the north, by the Euphrates River, they have stumbled and fallen.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[7] Who is this rising like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge?
[Jeremiah] [46]:[8] Egypt rises like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge. He said, "I will rise and cover the land; I will destroy the city and those who live in it."
[Jeremiah] [46]:[9] Charge, you horses! Drive furiously, you chariots! Let the warriors march out—Cush and Put, who carry the shield, and the Ludim, who draw the bow.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[10] But that day belongs to the Lord GOD of hosts, a day of vengeance, to take revenge on his foes. The sword will devour till it is glutted, till it has drunk its fill of their blood. For the Lord GOD of hosts holds a sacrifice in the land of the north by the Euphrates River.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[11] Go up to Gilead and get balm, virgin daughter of Egypt. But you multiply remedies in vain; there is no healing for you.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[12] The nations have heard of your disgrace; your cry fills the earth. Warrior stumbles over warrior; the two of them have fallen together.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[13] The word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:
[Jeremiah] [46]:[14] Announce it in Egypt, proclaim it in Migdol, proclaim it in Memphis and Tahpanhes: "Take your stand and get ready, for the sword devours all around you."
[Jeremiah] [46]:[15] Why have your mighty ones been swept away? They could not stand, for the LORD thrust them down.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[16] He made many stumble; they fell over one another. They said, "Get up! Let us go back to our own people, to the land of our birth, away from the ravaging sword."
[Jeremiah] [46]:[17] There they cried: "Pharaoh king of Egypt is nothing but noise; he has let his moment pass."
[Jeremiah] [46]:[18] As surely as I live, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts, one is coming who is like Tabor among the mountains, like Carmel by the sea.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[19] Pack your bags for exile, daughter of Egypt, you who sit secure, for Memphis will become a waste, laid in ruins with no one living there.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[20] Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly from the north is coming against her.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[21] Even her hired soldiers in her midst are like fattened calves. They too have turned and fled together; they did not stand, for the day of their ruin has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[22] Egypt makes a sound like a serpent gliding away, for the enemy advances in force; they come against her with axes, like men who cut down trees.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[23] They will cut down her forest, declares the LORD, dense though it is. For they are more numerous than locusts; they cannot be counted.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[24] The daughter of Egypt is put to shame, handed over to a people from the north.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[25] The LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to punish Amon god of Thebes, and Pharaoh, and Egypt with her gods and her kings—yes, Pharaoh and all who trust in him.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[26] I will hand them over to those who seek their lives, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. But afterward Egypt will be inhabited as in days gone by, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[27] But as for you, do not be afraid, my servant Jacob; do not be dismayed, Israel. For I will surely save you from far away, and your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be at rest, secure, with no one to make him afraid.
[Jeremiah] [46]:[28] Do not be afraid, my servant Jacob, declares the LORD, for I am with you. Though I will completely destroy all the nations among which I have scattered you, I will not destroy you completely. I will discipline you with justice, but I will by no means leave you unpunished.
[Jeremiah] [47]:[1] The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.
[Jeremiah] [47]:[2] This is what the LORD says: Look, waters are rising from the north; they will become a flooding torrent, sweeping over the land and all that fills it, over the city and those who live in it. The people will cry out, and everyone living in the land will wail.
[Jeremiah] [47]:[3] At the sound of the pounding hooves of his stallions, at the roar of his chariots, the rumble of his wheels, fathers will not turn back for their children—their hands hang limp—
[Jeremiah] [47]:[4] because the day is coming to devastate all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every last ally. For the LORD is destroying the Philistines, the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor.
[Jeremiah] [47]:[5] Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon lies silenced. You who remain in the valley, how long will you gash yourself?
[Jeremiah] [47]:[6] Ah, sword of the LORD, how long until you rest? Return to your sheath; be still and quiet.
[Jeremiah] [47]:[7] How can you rest, when the LORD has given the command? Against Ashkelon and against the seacoast—there he has appointed it.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[1] Concerning Moab. This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Woe to Nebo, for it is laid waste! Kiriathaim is disgraced and captured; the stronghold is disgraced and shattered.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[2] Moab's glory is no more. In Heshbon they plotted her ruin: "Come, let us cut her off from being a nation." You too, Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will pursue you.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[3] Listen! A cry from Horonaim: devastation and great destruction!
[Jeremiah] [48]:[4] Moab is broken; her little ones have raised a cry.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[5] Up the ascent of Luhith they go, weeping bitterly as they climb; on the descent to Horonaim anguished cries of destruction are heard.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[6] Flee! Save your lives! Become like a shrub in the wilderness.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[7] Because you trusted in your works and your treasures, you too will be captured, and Chemosh will go into exile together with his priests and officials.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[8] The destroyer will come against every city, and no city will escape. The valley will perish and the plateau be devastated, as the LORD has said.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[9] Give wings to Moab, for she must fly away. Her cities will become a desolation, with no one living in them.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[10] Cursed is the one who does the LORD's work negligently, and cursed is the one who withholds his sword from blood.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[11] Moab has been at ease from his youth, settled like wine on its dregs, never poured from vessel to vessel, never gone into exile. So his taste has remained unchanged, and his aroma has not changed.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[12] Therefore the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will send him decanters who will tip him over; they will empty his vessels and smash his jars.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[13] Then Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, the object of their trust.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[14] How can you say, "We are warriors, men valiant in battle"?
[Jeremiah] [48]:[15] Moab is laid waste; her cities are stormed, and her finest young men have gone down to the slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[16] Moab's disaster is near at hand; his calamity is rushing upon him.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[17] Mourn for him, all you who live around him, all who know his name. Say, "How the mighty scepter is broken, the glorious staff!"
[Jeremiah] [48]:[18] Come down from your glory and sit in thirst, you who are enthroned, daughter of Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you; he has ruined your fortresses.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[19] Stand by the road and watch, you who live in Aroer. Ask the man fleeing, the woman escaping: "What has happened?"
[Jeremiah] [48]:[20] Moab is disgraced, for she is shattered. Wail and cry out! Announce it by the Arnon: Moab is laid waste!
[Jeremiah] [48]:[21] Judgment has come upon the plateau country—upon Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,
[Jeremiah] [48]:[22] upon Dibon, Nebo, and Beth-diblathaim,
[Jeremiah] [48]:[23] upon Kiriathaim, Beth-gamul, and Beth-meon,
[Jeremiah] [48]:[24] upon Kerioth and Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[25] Moab's horn is cut off, and his arm is broken, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[26] Make him drunk, for he exalted himself against the LORD. Let Moab wallow in his own vomit and become a laughingstock himself.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[27] Was not Israel a laughingstock to you? Was he caught among thieves, that you shake your head whenever you speak of him?
[Jeremiah] [48]:[28] Abandon the towns and live among the rocks, you inhabitants of Moab. Be like a dove that nests on the sides of a gaping gorge.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[29] We have heard of Moab's pride—how very proud he is—of his loftiness, his pride, his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[30] I know his insolence, declares the LORD, but it comes to nothing; his boasts accomplish nothing.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[31] Therefore I wail over Moab; for all Moab I cry out; I moan for the men of Kir-heres.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[32] More than for Jazer I weep for you, O vine of Sibmah. Your branches spread across the sea; they reached as far as the sea of Jazer. The destroyer has fallen on your summer fruit and your grape harvest.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[33] Joy and gladness are gone from the orchard land and from the land of Moab. I have stopped the wine flowing from the presses; no one treads them with shouting—the shouting is no shout of joy.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[34] The cry from Heshbon reaches Elealeh and Jahaz; they raise their voice from Zoar as far as Horonaim and Eglath-shelishiyah, for even the waters of Nimrim have become desolate.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[35] In Moab I will put an end, declares the LORD, to the one who offers sacrifice at the high place and burns incense to his gods.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[36] Therefore my heart moans like a flute for Moab; my heart moans like a flute for the men of Kir-heres, for the wealth they gained has perished.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[37] Every head is shaved and every beard cut off; every hand is slashed and every waist wrapped in sackcloth.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[38] On all the rooftops of Moab and in her squares there is nothing but mourning, for I have shattered Moab like a jar no one wants, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[39] How shattered she is! How they wail! How Moab turns his back in shame! Moab has become a laughingstock and a horror to all around him.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[40] For this is what the LORD says: Look, one swoops down like an eagle and spreads his wings over Moab.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[41] The towns are captured and the strongholds seized. On that day the hearts of Moab's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[42] Moab will be destroyed as a people, because he exalted himself against the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[43] Terror, pit, and snare await you, inhabitant of Moab, declares the LORD.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew words *pachad*, *pachat*, and *pach* form a striking sound-play that cannot be fully carried over into English.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[44] Whoever flees from the terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in the snare; for I will bring upon Moab the year of their punishment, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [48]:[45] In the shadow of Heshbon the fugitives stand helpless, for a fire has gone out from Heshbon, a flame from the midst of Sihon; it has consumed the forehead of Moab and the skulls of the noisy boasters.

[Jeremiah] [48]:[47] Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the latter days, declares the LORD. Here ends the judgment on Moab.

[Jeremiah] [49]:[21] At the sound of their fall the earth will quake; their cry will be heard as far as the Red Sea.
[Jeremiah] [49]:[22] Look, like an eagle he will rise and soar and spread his wings over Bozrah. On that day the hearts of Edom's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
[Jeremiah] [49]:[23] Concerning Damascus: Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard bad news. They melt away in fear; there is anguish like a restless sea that cannot be calmed.

[Jeremiah] [49]:[25] How can the city of praise be forsaken, the town that was my joy?

[Jeremiah] [49]:[35] This is what the LORD of hosts says: I am about to break the bow of Elam, the mainstay of their might.

[Jeremiah] [50]:[1] The word the LORD spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, through Jeremiah the prophet:
[Jeremiah] [50]:[2] Announce it among the nations, proclaim it, raise a signal! Proclaim it, hold nothing back! Say: Babylon is captured, Bel is put to shame, Marduk is shattered. Her images are put to shame, her idols are shattered.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[3] For a nation has come up against her from the north; it will make her land a wasteland, and no one will live there. Both people and animals have fled, they are gone.
