[Jeremiah] [50]:[4] In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, the people of Israel will come, they and the people of Judah together. They will go on their way weeping, and they will seek the LORD their God.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[5] They will ask the way to Zion, their faces turned toward it: "Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten."
[Jeremiah] [50]:[6] My people were lost sheep. Their shepherds led them astray, turning them loose on the mountains. They wandered from mountain to hill and forgot their resting place.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[7] All who found them devoured them, and their enemies said, "We are not guilty, for they sinned against the LORD, their righteous pasture, the LORD, the hope of their fathers."
[Jeremiah] [50]:[8] Flee from the midst of Babylon, go out from the land of the Chaldeans, and be like he-goats leading the flock.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[9] For look, I am stirring up and bringing against Babylon a company of great nations from the land of the north. They will line up against her, and from there she will be taken. Their arrows are like a skilled warrior's; none returns empty.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[10] Chaldea will be plundered; all who plunder her will have their fill, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[11] Though you rejoice, though you exult, you who plunder my inheritance; though you frisk like a heifer treading grain and neigh like stallions—
[Jeremiah] [50]:[12] your mother will be utterly disgraced, she who bore you will be humiliated. Look, she will be the last of the nations: a wilderness, a parched land, a desert.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[13] Because of the LORD's wrath she will not be inhabited; she will lie utterly desolate. All who pass by Babylon will be appalled and will hiss at all her wounds.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[14] Line up against Babylon on every side, all you who bend the bow. Shoot at her, spare no arrow, for she has sinned against the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[15] Raise the shout against her on every side! She surrenders; her bulwarks have fallen, her walls are torn down. Since this is the LORD's vengeance, take vengeance on her; do to her as she has done.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[16] Cut off from Babylon the sower and the one who wields the sickle at harvest. Before the sword of the oppressor each will turn back to his own people, each will flee to his own land.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[17] Israel is a scattered flock driven away by lions. First the king of Assyria devoured him; then this last one, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, crushed his bones.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[18] Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: I am about to punish the king of Babylon and his land, just as I punished the king of Assyria.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[19] I will bring Israel back to his pasture, and he will graze on Carmel and Bashan; his hunger will be satisfied in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[20] In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, Israel's guilt will be sought, and there will be none; and Judah's sins, and they will not be found; for I will forgive the remnant I spare.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[21] Go up against the land of Merathaim, and against those who live in Pekod. Pursue, kill, and devote them to destruction, declares the LORD; do everything I have commanded you.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[22] The noise of battle is in the land, and great destruction!
[Jeremiah] [50]:[23] How the hammer of the whole earth is cut down and broken! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
[Jeremiah] [50]:[24] I set a snare for you, Babylon, and you were caught before you knew it. You were found and seized, because you defied the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[25] The LORD has opened his armory and brought out the weapons of his wrath, for the Lord GOD of hosts has work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[26] Come against her from every quarter; break open her granaries. Pile her up like heaps of grain and devote her to destruction; let nothing be left of her.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[27] Kill all her young bulls; let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their punishment!
[Jeremiah] [50]:[28] Listen—fugitives and refugees from the land of Babylon, announcing in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance for his temple.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[29] Summon archers against Babylon, all who bend the bow. Encamp around her on every side; let no one escape. Repay her according to her deeds; do to her as she has done. For she has been arrogant against the LORD, against the Holy One of Israel.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[30] Therefore her young men will fall in her streets, and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[31] Look, I am against you, O arrogant one, declares the Lord GOD of hosts, for your day has come, the time when I punish you.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[32] The arrogant one will stumble and fall, and no one will lift him up. I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it will devour everything around him.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[33] This is what the LORD of hosts says: The people of Israel are oppressed, and the people of Judah with them. All their captors hold them fast; they refuse to let them go.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[34] But their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of hosts is his name. He will surely plead their cause, so that he may bring rest to the earth, but unrest to those who live in Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[35] A sword against the Chaldeans, declares the LORD, and against those who live in Babylon, against her officials and her wise men!
[Jeremiah] [50]:[36] A sword against her diviners, and they will become fools! A sword against her warriors, and they will be terrified!
[Jeremiah] [50]:[37] A sword against her horses and chariots and all the foreign troops in her midst, and they will become like women! A sword against her treasures, and they will be plundered!
[Jeremiah] [50]:[38] A drought against her waters, and they will dry up! For it is a land of idols, and they go mad over their dreadful images.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[39] Therefore desert creatures and hyenas will live there, and there the ostriches will dwell. Never again will it be inhabited, nor will it be settled through all generations.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[40] As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah along with their neighbors, declares the LORD, so no one will live there; no human being will settle in her.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[41] Look, a people is coming from the north; a great nation and many kings are stirring from the ends of the earth.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[42] They grip bow and javelin; they are cruel and show no mercy. Their sound roars like the sea as they ride on horses, arrayed as one man for battle against you, Daughter Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[43] The king of Babylon has heard the report of them, and his hands hang limp. Anguish grips him, pain like a woman in labor.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[44] Look, like a lion coming up from the thickets of the Jordan to a lasting pasture, in an instant I will chase them away from her, and I will appoint over her whomever I choose. For who is like me? Who can summon me? What shepherd can stand before me?
[Jeremiah] [50]:[45] Therefore hear the plan the LORD has made against Babylon, the purposes he has formed against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; surely their pasture will be made desolate.
[Jeremiah] [50]:[46] At the sound of Babylon's capture the earth will quake; her cry will be heard among the nations.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[1] This is what the LORD says: I am stirring up a destroying wind against Babylon and against those who live in Leb-kamai.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[2] I will send winnowers against Babylon, and they will winnow her and strip her land bare, for they will come at her from every side in the day of disaster.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[3] Let the archer not draw his bow, let him not put on his armor. Spare none of her young men; wipe out her whole army.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[4] They will fall slain in the land of the Chaldeans, run through in her streets.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[5] For Israel and Judah have not been forsaken by their God, the LORD of hosts, though their land is full of guilt against the Holy One of Israel.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[6] Flee from Babylon! Each of you, save your life! Do not be destroyed for her guilt, for this is the LORD's time of vengeance; he is paying her back what she deserves.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[7] Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD's hand, making the whole earth drunk. The nations drank her wine, and so they went mad.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[8] Suddenly Babylon has fallen and been shattered. Wail over her! Get balm for her pain; perhaps she can be healed.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[9] We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed. Leave her! Let us each go to his own land, for her judgment reaches to the heavens; it towers to the clouds.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[10] The LORD has brought forth our vindication. Come, let us tell in Zion what the LORD our God has done.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[11] Sharpen the arrows! Take up the shields! The LORD has stirred up the spirit of the kings of Media, for his purpose against Babylon is to destroy her. This is the LORD's vengeance, vengeance for his temple.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[12] Raise a banner against the walls of Babylon! Strengthen the watch, post the sentries, set the ambush! For the LORD has both planned and carried out what he spoke against the people of Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[13] You who dwell by many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your plunder is full.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[14] The LORD of hosts has sworn by himself: I will surely fill you with men like a swarm of locusts, and they will raise the shout of triumph over you.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[15] He made the earth by his power; he established the world by his wisdom and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[16] When he thunders, the waters in the heavens roar; he brings up clouds from the ends of the earth. He makes the lightning for the rain and brings out the wind from his storehouses.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[17] Everyone is senseless and without knowledge; every metalworker is put to shame by his idol, for his cast image is a fraud, and there is no breath in them.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[18] They are worthless, a work of mockery; when their reckoning comes, they will perish.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[19] Jacob's Portion is not like these, for he is the maker of all things, and of the tribe of his inheritance. The LORD of hosts is his name.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[20] You are my hammer, my weapon of war. With you I shatter nations; with you I destroy kingdoms.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[21] With you I shatter horse and rider; with you I shatter chariot and driver.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[22] With you I shatter man and woman; with you I shatter old and young; with you I shatter young man and young woman.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[23] With you I shatter shepherd and flock; with you I shatter plowman and team of oxen; with you I shatter governors and officials.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[24] I will repay Babylon and all who live in Chaldea for all the evil they did in Zion, before your very eyes, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[25] I am against you, destroying mountain, declares the LORD, you who destroy the whole earth. I will stretch out my hand against you, roll you down from the cliffs, and make you a burned-out mountain.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[26] No stone will be taken from you for a cornerstone, none for a foundation, for you will be desolate forever, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[27] Raise a banner in the land! Blow the trumpet among the nations! Prepare the nations for war against her; summon against her these kingdoms: Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a commander against her; send up horses like a swarm of locusts.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[28] Prepare the nations for war against her: the kings of Media, their governors and all their officials, and every land they rule.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[29] The earth trembles and writhes, for the LORD's purpose stands against Babylon: to make the land of Babylon a desolation, with no one living there.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[30] Babylon's warriors have stopped fighting; they sit in their strongholds. Their strength is gone; they have become like women. Her dwellings are set on fire; the bars of her gates are broken.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[31] One runner races to meet another, one messenger to meet another, to tell the king of Babylon that his city has been captured from end to end,
[Jeremiah] [51]:[32] that the river crossings have been seized, the marshes set on fire, and the fighting men are gripped with terror.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[33] For this is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time of threshing; soon her harvest time will come.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[34] "Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon devoured me, he crushed me. He left me an empty jar; he swallowed me like a serpent, filled his belly with my delicacies, and then spat me out.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[35] May the violence done to me and my people fall on Babylon," says the inhabitant of Zion. "May my blood be on those who live in Chaldea," says Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[36] Therefore this is what the LORD says: See, I will take up your cause and avenge you. I will dry up her sea and make her springs run dry.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[37] Babylon will become a heap of rubble, a haunt of jackals, an object of horror and scorn, a place where no one lives.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[38] Together they roar like young lions; they growl like lion cubs.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[39] But while they are inflamed I will set out a banquet for them and make them drunk, so that they shout with laughter—then they will sleep forever and never wake, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[40] I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams and goats.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[41] How Sheshach has been captured, the praise of all the earth seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations! [Footnote: "Sheshach" is a cipher for Babylon, formed by substituting letters of the Hebrew alphabet in reverse order.]
[Jeremiah] [51]:[42] The sea has risen over Babylon; its roaring waves have covered her.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[43] Her towns have become a desolation, a parched and barren land, a land where no one lives, where no human being passes through.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[44] I will punish Bel in Babylon and make him spew out what he swallowed. The nations will no longer stream to him, and the wall of Babylon will fall.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[45] Come out of her, my people! Each of you, save your life from the LORD's burning anger!
[Jeremiah] [51]:[46] Do not lose heart or be afraid when rumors spread through the land. One rumor comes this year, another the next—rumors of violence in the land and of ruler against ruler.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[47] Therefore the days are surely coming when I will punish the idols of Babylon. Her whole land will be put to shame, and all her slain will lie fallen within her.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[48] Then heaven and earth and all that is in them will shout for joy over Babylon, for out of the north the destroyers will come against her, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[49] Babylon must fall for the slain of Israel, just as the slain of all the earth have fallen because of Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[50] You who have escaped the sword, go! Do not linger! Remember the LORD from far away, and let Jerusalem rise in your hearts.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[51] "We are ashamed, for we have heard the insults; disgrace has covered our faces, because foreigners entered the holy places of the LORD's house."
[Jeremiah] [51]:[52] But the days are surely coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish her idols, and throughout her land the wounded will groan.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[53] Even if Babylon climbs to the heavens and fortifies her lofty stronghold, I will send destroyers against her, declares the LORD.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[54] The sound of a cry from Babylon, of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
[Jeremiah] [51]:[55] For the LORD is destroying Babylon; he will silence her mighty voice. The waves of the enemy roar like mighty waters; the din of their shouting rings out.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[56] For a destroyer has come against her, against Babylon; her warriors are captured and their bows are shattered. For the LORD is a God of retribution; he will repay in full.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[57] I will make her officials and wise men drunk, her governors, officers, and warriors; they will sleep forever and never wake, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[58] This is what the LORD of hosts says: Babylon's broad walls will be razed to the ground, and her high gates will be set on fire. The peoples labor for nothing; the nations wear themselves out only for the flames.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[59] This is the message Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the quartermaster.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[60] Jeremiah had written on a single scroll all the disaster that would come upon Babylon—all these words written against Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[61] He said to Seraiah, "When you get to Babylon, be sure to read all these words aloud.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[62] Then say, 'LORD, you have said you would destroy this place, so that no one will live in it, neither human nor animal; it will be desolate forever.'
[Jeremiah] [51]:[63] When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the Euphrates.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[64] Then say, 'So will Babylon sink, never to rise again, because of the disaster I will bring upon her. And her people will fall exhausted.'" Here end the words of Jeremiah.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[1] Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[2] He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[3] Indeed, because of the LORD's anger this came upon Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them out of his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[4] In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with his whole army against Jerusalem. They laid siege to it and built siege works all around it.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[5] So the city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[6] By the ninth day of the fourth month the famine in the city had grown so severe that there was no food for the people of the land.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[7] Then the city wall was breached, and all the soldiers fled. They left the city by night through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden, though the Chaldeans surrounded the city, and they went toward the Arabah.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[8] But the Chaldean army pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and his whole army scattered from him.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[9] They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, where he passed sentence on him.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[10] The king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and he also slaughtered all the officials of Judah at Riblah.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[11] Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes, bound him in bronze shackles, and the king of Babylon took him to Babylon and kept him in prison until the day of his death.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[12] In the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month—that is, the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, who served the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[13] He burned the house of the LORD, the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem; every great house he burned with fire.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[14] And the whole Chaldean army that was with the captain of the guard tore down all the walls surrounding Jerusalem.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[15] Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, carried into exile some of the poorest of the people, along with the rest of the people who were left in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the craftsmen.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[16] But Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, left some of the poorest of the land to work the vineyards and the fields.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[17] The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars of the house of the LORD, along with the stands and the bronze sea that were in the house of the LORD, and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[18] They also took the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the basins, the dishes, and all the bronze vessels used in the temple service.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[19] The captain of the guard took the bowls, the firepans, the basins, the pots, the lampstands, the dishes, and the libation vessels—everything made of gold and everything made of silver.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[20] As for the two pillars, the one sea, the twelve bronze bulls under the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of the LORD—the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weighing.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[21] Each pillar stood eighteen cubits high; its circumference was twelve cubits, it was four fingers thick, and hollow inside.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[22] On top of it was a bronze capital five cubits high, with lattice work and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze. The second pillar was the same, with its pomegranates.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[23] There were ninety-six pomegranates on each side; in all, the pomegranates on the lattice work all around numbered one hundred.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[24] The captain of the guard also took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[25] From the city he took one court official who was in command of the soldiers, seven men of the king's personal attendants who were found in the city, the scribe of the commander of the army who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found inside the city.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[26] Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[27] And there at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death. So Judah was carried away from its land.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[28] This is the number of the people Nebuchadnezzar carried into exile: in the seventh year, 3,023 Jews;
[Jeremiah] [52]:[29] in Nebuchadnezzar's eighteenth year, 832 persons from Jerusalem;
[Jeremiah] [52]:[30] in Nebuchadnezzar's twenty-third year, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, carried into exile 745 Jews. In all, 4,600 persons.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[31] In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, showed favor to Jehoiachin king of Judah and released him from prison.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[32] He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat above the seats of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[33] So Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes, and for the rest of his life he ate regularly at the king's table.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[34] And a regular allowance was given him by the king of Babylon, day by day, until the day of his death, all the days of his life.
[Lamentations] [1]:[1] How lonely she sits, the city once crowded with people! She has become like a widow—she who was great among the nations, a princess among the provinces, is now put to forced labor.
[Lamentations] [1]:[2] Bitterly she weeps in the night, tears on her cheeks. Among all her lovers there is none to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.
[Lamentations] [1]:[3] Judah has gone into exile out of misery and hard bondage. She dwells among the nations and finds no rest. All her pursuers have overtaken her in the midst of her distress.
[Lamentations] [1]:[4] The roads to Zion mourn, for no one comes to the appointed feasts. All her gates lie desolate, her priests groan, her young women grieve, and she herself is in bitterness.
[Lamentations] [1]:[5] Her foes have become her masters; her enemies are at ease. The LORD has brought her grief because of her many transgressions. Her children have gone away, captives before the enemy.
[Lamentations] [1]:[6] All splendor has departed from the daughter of Zion. Her princes have become like deer that find no pasture; they flee without strength before the pursuer.
[Lamentations] [1]:[7] In the days of her affliction and wandering, Jerusalem remembers all the treasures that were hers in days of old. When her people fell into the enemy's hand, there was no one to help her; her foes looked on and laughed at her ruin.
[Lamentations] [1]:[8] Jerusalem has sinned grievously, and so she has become unclean. All who honored her now despise her, for they have seen her nakedness. She herself groans and turns her face away.
[Lamentations] [1]:[9] Her filth clings to her skirts; she gave no thought to what would come. Her fall was astounding, and no one comforts her. "Look, O LORD, on my affliction, for the enemy has triumphed."
[Lamentations] [1]:[10] The enemy has laid his hand on all her treasures. She has watched the nations enter her sanctuary—those you had forbidden to come into your assembly.
[Lamentations] [1]:[11] All her people groan as they search for bread; they trade their treasures for food to keep themselves alive. "Look, O LORD, and see how worthless I have become."
[Lamentations] [1]:[12] Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by? Look and see: is there any suffering like the suffering inflicted on me, which the LORD brought upon me on the day of his burning anger?
[Lamentations] [1]:[13] From on high he sent fire down into my bones and made it prevail. He spread a net for my feet and turned me back. He left me desolate, faint all the day long.
[Lamentations] [1]:[14] My transgressions are bound into a yoke; by his hand they were woven together and laid upon my neck. He has broken my strength. The Lord has handed me over to those I cannot withstand.
[Lamentations] [1]:[15] The Lord has rejected all the warriors within me. He summoned an assembly against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trampled the virgin daughter of Judah as grapes in a winepress.
[Lamentations] [1]:[16] This is why I weep; my eyes, my eyes stream with tears. For no comforter is near me, no one to revive my spirit. My children are ruined, for the enemy has prevailed.
[Lamentations] [1]:[17] Zion stretches out her hands, but there is no one to comfort her. The LORD has commanded that Jacob's neighbors become his foes; Jerusalem has become something unclean among them.
[Lamentations] [1]:[18] The LORD is righteous, for I rebelled against his word. Listen, all you peoples, and see my suffering: my young women and my young men have gone into captivity.
[Lamentations] [1]:[19] I called to my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and my elders perished in the city while they searched for food to keep themselves alive.
[Lamentations] [1]:[20] Look, O LORD, for I am in distress. My insides churn; my heart is turned over within me, for I have rebelled bitterly. Outside the sword bereaves; inside there is death.
[Lamentations] [1]:[21] They have heard my groaning, but there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my ruin and rejoice at what you have done. May you bring the day you have announced, so that they become like me.
[Lamentations] [1]:[22] Let all their evil come before you, and deal with them as you have dealt with me for all my transgressions. My groans are many, and my heart is sick.
[Lamentations] [2]:[1] How the Lord in his anger has covered Daughter Zion with a cloud! He has hurled down from heaven to earth the splendor of Israel; he did not remember his footstool on the day of his anger.
[Lamentations] [2]:[2] Without pity the Lord has swallowed up every dwelling of Jacob; in his wrath he has torn down the strongholds of Daughter Judah and brought them to the ground; he has profaned the kingdom and its rulers.
[Lamentations] [2]:[3] In burning anger he has cut off every horn of Israel; he has withdrawn his right hand at the enemy's approach. He has blazed in Jacob like a flaming fire that devours everything around it.
[Lamentations] [2]:[4] He has bent his bow like an enemy, his right hand set like a foe, and he has slain all who were precious to the eye. On the tent of Daughter Zion he has poured out his fury like fire.
[Lamentations] [2]:[5] The Lord has become like an enemy; he has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all her palaces and destroyed her strongholds, and multiplied mourning and lament for Daughter Judah.
[Lamentations] [2]:[6] He has broken down his shelter like a garden booth, laid his meeting place in ruins. The LORD has made Zion forget appointed feast and Sabbath; in his fierce indignation he has spurned both king and priest.
[Lamentations] [2]:[7] The Lord has rejected his altar, disowned his sanctuary; he has handed the walls of her palaces over to the enemy. They raised a shout in the house of the LORD as on the day of a festival.
[Lamentations] [2]:[8] The LORD determined to destroy the wall of Daughter Zion. He stretched out the measuring line and did not withhold his hand from swallowing her up. He made rampart and wall lament; together they languish.
[Lamentations] [2]:[9] Her gates have sunk into the ground; he has ruined and shattered her bars. Her king and her princes are among the nations; the law is no more, and her prophets no longer receive a vision from the LORD.
[Lamentations] [2]:[10] The elders of Daughter Zion sit on the ground in silence; they have thrown dust on their heads and put on sackcloth. The young women of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground.
[Lamentations] [2]:[11] My eyes are worn out with weeping, my stomach churns; my heart is poured out on the ground because my people are shattered, because children and infants faint in the streets of the city.
[Lamentations] [2]:[12] They cry to their mothers, "Where are grain and wine?" as they faint like the wounded in the streets of the city, as their lives ebb away on their mothers' bosom.
[Lamentations] [2]:[13] What can I say for you? To what can I compare you, Daughter Jerusalem? What can I liken you to, that I might comfort you, Virgin Daughter Zion? Your wound is as vast as the sea. Who can heal you?
[Lamentations] [2]:[14] Your prophets saw for you visions false and empty; they did not expose your guilt to restore your fortunes. The oracles they saw for you were false and misleading.
[Lamentations] [2]:[15] All who pass along the way clap their hands at you; they hiss and shake their heads at Daughter Jerusalem: "Is this the city they called the perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth?"
[Lamentations] [2]:[16] All your enemies open their mouths against you; they hiss and grind their teeth and say, "We have swallowed her up! This is the day we longed for; we have lived to see it!"
[Lamentations] [2]:[17] The LORD has done what he planned; he has fulfilled his word, which he decreed long ago. He has torn down without pity; he has let the enemy gloat over you and exalted the horn of your foes.
[Lamentations] [2]:[18] Their hearts cry out to the Lord. Wall of Daughter Zion, let your tears run down like a torrent day and night; give yourself no rest, let your eyes have no relief.
[Lamentations] [2]:[19] Rise up, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches; pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift up your hands to him for the lives of your children, who faint from hunger at every street corner.
[Lamentations] [2]:[20] Look, LORD, and consider: whom have you ever treated like this? Should women eat their own offspring, the children they have cradled? Should priest and prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
[Lamentations] [2]:[21] Young and old lie on the ground in the streets; my young women and my young men have fallen by the sword. You slew them on the day of your anger; you slaughtered them without pity.
[Lamentations] [2]:[22] As for a day of festival you summoned terrors against me on every side, and on the day of the LORD's anger no one escaped or survived. Those I cared for and reared my enemy has destroyed.
[Lamentations] [3]:[1] I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of his wrath.
[Lamentations] [3]:[2] He has driven me away and made me walk in darkness, not in light.
[Lamentations] [3]:[3] Surely against me he turns his hand again and again, all day long.
[Lamentations] [3]:[4] He has worn away my flesh and my skin; he has broken my bones.
[Lamentations] [3]:[5] He has built siegeworks against me and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.
[Lamentations] [3]:[6] He has made me dwell in darkness, like those long dead.
[Lamentations] [3]:[7] He has walled me in so I cannot escape; he has weighed me down with chains.
[Lamentations] [3]:[8] Even when I cry out and plead for help, he shuts out my prayer.
[Lamentations] [3]:[9] He has blocked my ways with hewn stone; he has twisted my paths.
[Lamentations] [3]:[10] He is a bear lying in wait for me, a lion in hiding.
[Lamentations] [3]:[11] He turned my paths aside and tore me to pieces; he left me desolate.
[Lamentations] [3]:[12] He drew his bow and set me up as the target for his arrow.
[Lamentations] [3]:[13] He drove into my vitals the arrows of his quiver.
[Lamentations] [3]:[14] I have become the laughingstock of all my people, their taunting song all day long.
[Lamentations] [3]:[15] He has filled me with bitterness; he has made me drunk with wormwood.
[Lamentations] [3]:[16] He has broken my teeth with gravel and pressed me down into the ashes.
[Lamentations] [3]:[17] My soul is deprived of peace; I have forgotten what happiness is.
[Lamentations] [3]:[18] So I said, "My endurance is gone, and so is my hope from the LORD."
[Lamentations] [3]:[19] Remember my affliction and my wandering, the wormwood and the gall.
[Lamentations] [3]:[20] My soul remembers it well and sinks down within me.
[Lamentations] [3]:[21] Yet this I call to mind, and therefore I have hope:
[Lamentations] [3]:[22] The LORD's acts of mercy never cease; his compassions never come to an end.
[Lamentations] [3]:[23] They are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
[Lamentations] [3]:[24] "The LORD is my portion," says my soul, "therefore I will hope in him."
[Lamentations] [3]:[25] The LORD is good to those who wait for him, to the soul that seeks him.
[Lamentations] [3]:[26] It is good to wait in silence for the salvation of the LORD.
[Lamentations] [3]:[27] It is good for a man to bear the yoke while he is young.
[Lamentations] [3]:[28] Let him sit alone in silence, for the LORD has laid it on him.
[Lamentations] [3]:[29] Let him put his mouth to the dust; perhaps there is still hope.
[Lamentations] [3]:[30] Let him offer his cheek to the one who strikes him; let him be filled with disgrace.
[Lamentations] [3]:[31] For the Lord will not cast off forever.
[Lamentations] [3]:[32] Though he brings grief, he will show compassion in the abundance of his mercy.
[Lamentations] [3]:[33] For he does not willingly afflict or grieve anyone.
[Lamentations] [3]:[34] To crush underfoot all the prisoners of the earth,
[Lamentations] [3]:[35] to deny a man justice before the face of the Most High,
[Lamentations] [3]:[36] to rob a man in his lawsuit—does the Lord not see it?
[Lamentations] [3]:[37] Who can speak and have it happen unless the Lord has commanded it?
[Lamentations] [3]:[38] Do not both evil and good come from the mouth of the Most High?
[Lamentations] [3]:[39] Why should anyone alive complain when punished for his own sins?
[Lamentations] [3]:[40] Let us examine and test our ways, and return to the LORD.
[Lamentations] [3]:[41] Let us lift up our hearts, along with our hands, to God in heaven.
[Lamentations] [3]:[42] We have sinned and rebelled, and you have not forgiven.
[Lamentations] [3]:[43] You wrapped yourself in anger and pursued us; you killed without pity.
[Lamentations] [3]:[44] You wrapped yourself in a cloud so that no prayer could pass through.
[Lamentations] [3]:[45] You have made us filth and refuse among the nations.
[Lamentations] [3]:[46] All our enemies have opened their mouths wide against us.
[Lamentations] [3]:[47] Terror and the pit have come upon us, devastation and destruction.
[Lamentations] [3]:[48] Streams of tears flow from my eyes over the ruin of the daughter of my people.
[Lamentations] [3]:[49] My eyes will flow without ceasing, without relief,
[Lamentations] [3]:[50] until the LORD looks down from heaven and sees.
[Lamentations] [3]:[51] What I see brings grief to my soul—the fate of all the daughters of my city.
[Lamentations] [3]:[52] Those who were my enemies without cause hunted me like a bird.
[Lamentations] [3]:[53] They tried to end my life in a pit and threw stones at me.
[Lamentations] [3]:[54] The waters closed over my head, and I thought, "I am cut off."
[Lamentations] [3]:[55] I called on your name, O LORD, from the depths of the pit.
[Lamentations] [3]:[56] You heard my voice: do not close your ear to my cry for relief, to my plea for help.
[Lamentations] [3]:[57] You came near when I called on you; you said, "Do not be afraid."
[Lamentations] [3]:[58] You took up my case, O Lord; you redeemed my life.
[Lamentations] [3]:[59] You have seen the wrong done to me, O LORD; judge my cause.
[Lamentations] [3]:[60] You have seen all their vengeance, all their plots against me.
[Lamentations] [3]:[61] You have heard their insults, O LORD, all their plots against me—
[Lamentations] [3]:[62] the lips of my assailants and their muttering against me all day long.
[Lamentations] [3]:[63] Look at them, sitting and rising: I am the subject of their mocking songs.
[Lamentations] [3]:[64] Repay them, O LORD, as their hands deserve.
[Lamentations] [3]:[65] Put a veil over their hearts; let your curse be upon them.
[Lamentations] [3]:[66] Pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the LORD.
[Lamentations] [4]:[1] How the gold has lost its luster, the finest gold grown dull! The sacred stones lie scattered at the head of every street.
[Lamentations] [4]:[2] Zion's precious sons, once weighed against pure gold — how they are now reckoned as clay pots, the work of a potter's hands.
[Lamentations] [4]:[3] Even jackals offer the breast and nurse their young, but the daughter of my people has turned cruel, like ostriches in the wilderness.
[Lamentations] [4]:[4] The nursing infant's tongue sticks to the roof of his mouth for thirst; children beg for bread, but no one breaks off a piece for them.
[Lamentations] [4]:[5] Those who once ate delicacies lie desolate in the streets; those raised in crimson now cling to heaps of refuse.
[Lamentations] [4]:[6] The guilt of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment, with no hand laid upon her.
[Lamentations] [4]:[7] Her nobles were brighter than snow, whiter than milk; their bodies were ruddier than coral, their form like sapphire.
[Lamentations] [4]:[8] Now their appearance is darker than soot; no one recognizes them in the streets. Their skin is shriveled on their bones, dried up like wood.
[Lamentations] [4]:[9] Better off were those slain by the sword than those slain by hunger, who wasted away, pierced by the lack of the fruit of the field.
[Lamentations] [4]:[10] The hands of compassionate women cooked their own children; they became their food when the daughter of my people was shattered.
[Lamentations] [4]:[11] The LORD has spent his wrath, he has poured out his burning anger; he kindled a fire in Zion that consumed her foundations.
[Lamentations] [4]:[12] The kings of the earth did not believe, nor any who dwell in the world, that an enemy or a foe could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
[Lamentations] [4]:[13] It was for the sins of her prophets and the guilt of her priests, who shed within her the blood of the righteous.
[Lamentations] [4]:[14] They wandered blind through the streets, defiled with blood, so that no one could touch their garments.
[Lamentations] [4]:[15] "Away! Unclean!" people shouted at them. "Away, away, do not touch!" So they fled and wandered; among the nations it was said, "They shall stay here no longer."
[Lamentations] [4]:[16] The LORD himself has scattered them; he no longer looks on them. No one honored the priests or showed favor to the elders.
[Lamentations] [4]:[17] Still our eyes wasted away, looking in vain for help; we kept watch and watched for a nation that could not save.
[Lamentations] [4]:[18] They stalked our every step, so we could not walk in our streets. Our end drew near, our days were finished; our end had come.
[Lamentations] [4]:[19] Our pursuers were swifter than eagles in the sky; they chased us over the mountains and ambushed us in the wilderness.
[Lamentations] [4]:[20] The breath of our life, the LORD's anointed, was caught in their pits — he of whom we said, "In his shadow we shall live among the nations."
[Lamentations] [4]:[21] Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz; yet the cup will pass to you as well — you will drink and be stripped bare.
[Lamentations] [4]:[22] Your punishment is complete, daughter of Zion; he will exile you no more. But your guilt, daughter of Edom, he will punish; he will lay bare your sins.
[Lamentations] [5]:[1] Remember, LORD, what has happened to us; look, and see our disgrace.
[Lamentations] [5]:[2] Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our homes to foreigners.
[Lamentations] [5]:[3] We have become orphans, fatherless; our mothers are like widows.
[Lamentations] [5]:[4] We must pay silver for the water we drink; our own wood comes to us at a price.
[Lamentations] [5]:[5] Our pursuers are at our necks; we are worn out, and given no rest.
[Lamentations] [5]:[6] We held out our hand to Egypt, and to Assyria, to get enough bread.
[Lamentations] [5]:[7] Our fathers sinned and are no more, and we bear the weight of their guilt.
[Lamentations] [5]:[8] Slaves rule over us, and no one frees us from their hand.
[Lamentations] [5]:[9] We risk our lives to get our bread, because of the sword in the wilderness.
[Lamentations] [5]:[10] Our skin is hot as an oven from the burning heat of hunger.
[Lamentations] [5]:[11] Women are raped in Zion, virgins in the cities of Judah.
[Lamentations] [5]:[12] Princes are hanged by their hands; the elders are shown no respect.
[Lamentations] [5]:[13] Young men are made to grind at the mill, and boys stagger under loads of wood.
[Lamentations] [5]:[14] The elders have left the gate, the young men their music.
[Lamentations] [5]:[15] The joy of our heart has ceased; our dancing has turned to mourning.
[Lamentations] [5]:[16] The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!
[Lamentations] [5]:[17] Because of this our heart is sick; because of these things our eyes have grown dim:
[Lamentations] [5]:[18] because Mount Zion lies desolate, and foxes prowl over it.
[Lamentations] [5]:[19] But you, LORD, reign forever; your throne endures from generation to generation.
[Lamentations] [5]:[20] Why do you forget us forever, forsake us for so long a time?
[Lamentations] [5]:[21] Restore us to yourself, LORD, that we may return; renew our days as of old—
[Lamentations] [5]:[22] unless you have utterly rejected us and are angry with us beyond measure.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[1] In the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month, while I was among the exiles by the Kebar River, the heavens opened and I saw visions of God.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[2] On the fifth day of the month—it was the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's exile—
[Ezekiel] [1]:[3] the word of the LORD came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the Kebar River; and there the hand of the LORD was upon him.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[4] I looked, and there was a stormwind coming out of the north—a great cloud with fire flashing back and forth and a brilliant light all around it. At its center, out of the fire, was a gleam like burnished metal.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[5] And within it were the figures of four living creatures. This was their appearance: they had a human likeness,
[Ezekiel] [1]:[6] Each one had four faces, and each one had four wings.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[7] Their legs were straight, and their feet were like the hooves of a calf, gleaming like polished bronze.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[8] Under their wings, on all four sides, they had human hands; and all four of them had faces and wings.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[9] Their wings touched one another. They did not turn as they moved; each one went straight ahead.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[10] Their faces looked like this: each of the four had the face of a man in front, the face of a lion on the right, the face of an ox on the left, and the face of an eagle.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[11] Such were their faces. Their wings were spread out above; each had two wings touching the wings of another, and two covering its body.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[12] Each one went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit would go, they went, without turning as they moved.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[13] The living creatures looked like burning coals of fire, like blazing torches. The fire moved to and fro among the creatures; the fire was bright, and out of it lightning flashed.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[14] The creatures darted back and forth like flashes of lightning.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[15] As I looked at the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground beside them, one for each of the four.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[16] The wheels and their construction looked like sparkling topaz, and all four were alike. Each appeared to be made like a wheel within a wheel.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[17] When they moved, they went in any of their four directions; they did not turn as they went.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[18] Their rims were high and awesome, and all four rims were full of eyes all around.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[19] When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved beside them; and when the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose too.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[20] Wherever the spirit would go, they went, and the wheels rose along with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[21] When the creatures moved, they moved; when the creatures stood still, they stood still; and when the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose along with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[22] Above the heads of the living creatures was what looked like a vault, sparkling like awe-inspiring crystal, spread out above their heads.<fn>Hebrew *raqia*, the same word used for the expanse of sky in the creation account.</fn>
[Ezekiel] [1]:[23] Under the vault their wings were stretched out straight, one toward the other, and each had two wings covering its body.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[24] When they moved, I heard the sound of their wings, like the roar of rushing waters, like the voice of the Almighty, like the tumult of an army. When they stood still, they lowered their wings.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[25] Then there came a voice from above the vault over their heads as they stood with lowered wings.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[26] Above the vault over their heads was what looked like a throne of sapphire, and high above on the throne was a figure like that of a man.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[27] I saw that from what appeared to be his waist up he was like glowing metal, as if full of fire, and from there down he looked like fire; and brilliant light surrounded him.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[28] Like a rainbow in the clouds on a rainy day, so was the radiance around him. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. When I saw it, I fell facedown, and I heard the voice of one speaking.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[1] He said to me, "Son of man, stand up on your feet, and I will speak with you."
[Ezekiel] [2]:[2] As he spoke to me, the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet, and I heard him speaking to me.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[3] He said to me: "Son of man, I am sending you to the people of Israel, to rebellious nations that have rebelled against me. They and their fathers have revolted against me to this very day.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[4] Their children are defiant and hard-hearted, and I am sending you to them. You are to say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.'
[Ezekiel] [2]:[5] Whether they listen or refuse—for they are a rebellious house—they will know that a prophet has been among them.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[6] But you, son of man, do not be afraid of them, and do not fear their words, though briers and thorns surround you and you live among scorpions. Do not fear their words or be dismayed at the sight of them, for they are a rebellious house.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[7] You are to speak my words to them, whether they listen or refuse, for they are rebellious.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[8] But you, son of man, listen to what I say to you. Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I give you."
[Ezekiel] [2]:[9] Then I looked, and there was a hand stretched out to me, and in it was a written scroll.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[10] He unrolled it before me, and on both sides of it were written words of lament and mourning and woe.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[1] He said to me, "Son of man, eat what you find here. Eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel."
[Ezekiel] [3]:[2] So I opened my mouth, and he fed me the scroll.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[3] He said to me, "Son of man, feed your stomach and fill your belly with this scroll that I am giving you." So I ate it, and in my mouth it was as sweet as honey.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[4] Then he said to me, "Son of man, go now to the house of Israel and speak my words to them.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[5] You are not being sent to a people of obscure speech and difficult language, but to the house of Israel—
[Ezekiel] [3]:[6] not to many peoples of obscure speech and difficult language, whose words you cannot understand. Had I sent you to them, they would have listened to you.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[7] But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to me. The whole house of Israel is hard-browed and stubborn-hearted.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[8] See, I have made your face as hard as their faces, and your brow as hard as their brow.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[9] I have made your brow like a diamond, harder than flint. Do not fear them or be dismayed before them, for they are a rebellious house.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[10] And he said to me, "Son of man, take into your heart every word I speak to you, and listen with your ears.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[11] Go now to the exiles, to your own people, and speak to them. Say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says'—whether they listen or refuse."
[Ezekiel] [3]:[12] Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me a great rumbling sound: "Blessed be the glory of the LORD from his place!"
[Ezekiel] [3]:[13] It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them—a great rumbling sound.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[14] The Spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness and in the heat of my spirit, with the hand of the LORD strong upon me.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[15] I came to the exiles at Tel Abib, who lived by the Kebar River. There, where they were living, I sat among them for seven days, overwhelmed.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[16] At the end of the seven days the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [3]:[17] "Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, you must warn them for me.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[18] If I say to the wicked, 'You will surely die,' and you do not warn him or speak to warn the wicked man away from his wicked way so that he may live, that wicked man will die in his guilt, but I will hold you accountable for his blood.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[19] But if you do warn the wicked man and he does not turn from his wickedness or from his wicked way, he will die in his guilt, but you will have saved your life.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[20] And if a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does wrong, and I place a stumbling block before him, he will die. Because you did not warn him, he will die in his sin, and the righteous deeds he did will not be remembered—and I will hold you accountable for his blood.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[21] But if you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he does not sin, he will surely live because he took the warning, and you will have saved your life."
[Ezekiel] [3]:[22] The hand of the LORD was upon me there, and he said to me, "Get up, go out to the valley, and there I will speak with you."
[Ezekiel] [3]:[23] So I got up and went out to the valley, and there stood the glory of the LORD, like the glory I had seen by the Kebar River; and I fell facedown.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[24] Then the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me and said, "Go, shut yourself inside your house.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[25] As for you, son of man, they will put ropes on you and bind you with them, so that you cannot go out among them.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[26] I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so that you will be silent and unable to rebuke them, for they are a rebellious house.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[27] But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.' Whoever will listen, let him listen; whoever refuses, let him refuse—for they are a rebellious house."
[Ezekiel] [4]:[1] "Now you, son of man, take a brick, set it in front of you, and engrave on it a city — Jerusalem.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[2] Lay siege against it: build a siege wall, throw up a ramp, set up camps, and place battering rams around it.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[3] Then take an iron griddle and set it up as an iron wall between you and the city. Set your face toward it; it shall be under siege, and you yourself shall besiege it. This is a sign for the house of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[4] "Then lie down on your left side and lay the guilt of the house of Israel upon that side. For as many days as you lie on that side, you shall bear their guilt.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[5] I have assigned you the years of their guilt as a number of days: three hundred and ninety days. So you shall bear the guilt of the house of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[6] When you have finished these, lie down again, this time on your right side, and bear the guilt of the house of Judah forty days. I have assigned you one day for each year.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[7] Set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, with your arm bared, and prophesy against it.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[8] And see, I am putting ropes on you so that you cannot turn from one side to the other until you have completed the days of your siege.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[9] "Take wheat and barley, beans and lentils, millet and spelt; put them in a single vessel and make them into bread for yourself. You shall eat it during the number of days you lie on your side — three hundred and ninety days.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[10] The food you eat shall be weighed out, twenty shekels a day; you shall eat it at set times.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[11] And you shall drink water by measure, a sixth of a hin; you shall drink it at set times.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[12] You shall eat it as a barley cake, baking it in their sight over human excrement."
[Ezekiel] [4]:[13] And the LORD said, "This is how the people of Israel shall eat their bread — unclean — among the nations where I will drive them."
[Ezekiel] [4]:[14] Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! I have never defiled myself. From my youth until now I have never eaten anything that died of itself or was torn by beasts, and no tainted meat has ever entered my mouth."
[Ezekiel] [4]:[15] He said to me, "See, I allow you cow dung instead of human dung; you may prepare your bread over that."
[Ezekiel] [4]:[16] Then he said to me, "Son of man, I am about to break the staff of bread in Jerusalem. They shall eat bread by weight and in anxiety, and drink water by measure and in horror,
[Ezekiel] [4]:[17] so that, lacking bread and water, they will be appalled, each man with his brother, and waste away in their guilt."
[Ezekiel] [5]:[1] Now you, son of man, take a sharp sword and use it as a barber's razor: shave your head and your beard. Then take scales and weigh out the hair, and divide it.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[2] Burn a third of it in the fire inside the city when the days of the siege are ended. Take another third and strike it with the sword all around the city. Scatter the last third to the wind, and I will draw the sword after them.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[3] But take a few strands from it and bind them into the folds of your garment.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[4] And from these take some again, throw them into the fire, and burn them there. From it a fire will spread to the whole house of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[5] This is what the Lord GOD says: This is Jerusalem. I set her in the midst of the nations, with countries all around her.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[6] But she rebelled against my judgments more wickedly than the nations, and against my statutes more than the countries around her. They rejected my judgments and did not walk in my statutes.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[7] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you have been more turbulent than the nations around you, and have not walked in my statutes or kept my judgments—you have not even lived by the standards of the nations around you—
[Ezekiel] [5]:[8] therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: See, I myself am against you, and I will execute judgments in your midst before the eyes of the nations.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[9] Because of all your abominations I will do among you what I have never done before and will never do again.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[10] Therefore fathers will eat their children among you, and children will eat their fathers. I will execute judgments on you and scatter all who remain of you to every wind.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[11] Therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things and all your abominations, I myself will cut you down; my eye will not spare, and I will show no pity.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[12] A third of your people will die of plague or waste away from famine within you; a third will fall by the sword around you; and a third I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw the sword after them.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[13] Then my anger will be spent, I will vent my wrath on them and be satisfied. And when I have spent my wrath on them, they will know that I, the LORD, have spoken in my zeal.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[14] I will make you a ruin and a disgrace among the nations around you, in the sight of all who pass by.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[15] You will be an object of scorn and mockery, a warning and a horror to the nations around you, when I execute judgments on you in anger and wrath and furious rebuke. I, the LORD, have spoken.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[16] When I send the deadly arrows of famine against you—arrows that bring ruin, which I send to destroy you—I will heap famine upon you and cut off your supply of bread.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[17] I will send famine and wild beasts against you, and they will leave you childless. Plague and bloodshed will sweep through you, and I will bring the sword upon you. I, the LORD, have spoken.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [6]:[2] Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[3] Say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD! This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys: I myself am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy your high places.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[4] Your altars will be laid waste and your incense stands smashed, and I will throw down your slain before your idols.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[5] I will lay the corpses of the Israelites before their idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[6] Wherever you live, the cities will lie in ruins and the high places will be desolate, so that your altars are ruined and left guilty, your idols smashed and finished, your incense stands cut down, and everything you have made wiped away.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[7] The slain will fall in your midst, and you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[8] Yet I will leave a remnant: some of you will escape the sword among the nations, when you are scattered through the lands.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[9] Then your survivors will remember me among the nations where they have been carried captive—how I broke their adulterous heart that turned away from me and their eyes that lusted after their idols. They will loathe themselves to their own faces for the evils they have done, for all their detestable practices.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[10] And they will know that I am the LORD; I did not threaten in vain to bring this disaster upon them.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[11] This is what the Lord GOD says: Clap your hands, stamp your foot, and cry out, "Alas!" over all the wicked abominations of the house of Israel, for they will fall by sword, famine, and plague.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[12] The one far away will die of plague, the one near will fall by the sword, and whoever is left and survives will die of famine. So I will spend my fury on them.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[13] Then you will know that I am the LORD, when their slain lie among their idols around their altars—on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree and every leafy oak, wherever they offered fragrant incense to all their idols.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[14] I will stretch out my hand against them and make the land a desolate waste, from the wilderness to Diblah, wherever they live. Then they will know that I am the LORD.[fn]
[Ezekiel] [7]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [7]:[2] "Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says to the land of Israel: An end! The end has come upon the four corners of the land.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[3] Now the end is upon you. I will unleash my anger against you, judge you according to your ways, and bring all your abominations down on your head.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[4] My eye will not spare you, and I will show no pity. I will repay you for your ways, and your abominations will remain in your midst. Then you will know that I am the LORD."
[Ezekiel] [7]:[5] This is what the Lord GOD says: "Disaster! A disaster like no other—look, it is coming!
[Ezekiel] [7]:[6] An end has come; the end has come. It has awakened against you. Look, it is coming!
[Ezekiel] [7]:[7] Doom has come upon you, you who live in the land. The time has come, the day is near—panic, not shouts of joy on the mountains.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[8] Soon now I will pour out my wrath on you and spend my anger against you. I will judge you according to your ways and bring all your abominations down on your head.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[9] My eye will not spare, and I will show no pity. I will repay you according to your ways, and your abominations will remain in your midst. Then you will know that I am the LORD who strikes.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[10] "Look, the day! Look, it comes! Doom has gone out. The rod has budded; arrogance has blossomed.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[11] Violence has grown into a rod of wickedness. None of them will be left, none of their multitude, none of their wealth, nothing of value among them.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[12] The time has come, the day has arrived. Let the buyer not rejoice and the seller not mourn, for wrath is on the whole multitude.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[13] For the seller will not return to what he sold, as long as they remain among the living; the vision concerning the whole multitude will not be revoked, and no one will preserve his life by his iniquity.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[14] They have blown the trumpet and made everything ready, but no one goes out to battle, for my wrath is on the whole multitude.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[15] The sword is outside; plague and famine are within. Whoever is in the field will die by the sword, and whoever is in the city will be devoured by famine and plague.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[16] Those who escape will flee to the mountains; like doves of the valleys they will all moan, each over his own iniquity.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[17] Every hand will go limp, and every knee will turn to water.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[18] They will put on sackcloth, and terror will cover them. Shame will be on every face, and every head will be shaved.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[19] They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will be treated as filth. Their silver and gold cannot save them on the day of the LORD's fury. It cannot satisfy their hunger or fill their stomachs, for it became the stumbling block of their iniquity.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[20] They took pride in their beautiful ornaments and used them to make their detestable images, their vile idols. Therefore I will turn it all into filth for them.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[21] I will hand it over as plunder to foreigners and as loot to the wicked of the earth, and they will defile it.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[22] I will turn my face away from them, and they will defile my treasured place. Violent men will enter it and defile it.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[23] Forge the chain! For the land is full of bloodshed and the city is full of violence.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[24] I will bring in the most ruthless of nations, and they will take possession of their houses. I will put an end to the pride of the mighty, and their sanctuaries will be desecrated.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[25] Anguish is coming! They will look for peace, but there will be none.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[26] Disaster upon disaster will come, and rumor after rumor. They will seek a vision from the prophet; instruction will vanish from the priest and counsel from the elders.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[27] The king will mourn, the prince will be clothed in despair, and the hands of the people of the land will tremble. I will deal with them according to their conduct, and by their own standards I will judge them. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
[Ezekiel] [8]:[1] In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month, I was sitting in my house with the elders of Judah sitting before me, and the hand of the Lord GOD fell upon me there.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[2] I looked, and there was a figure with the appearance of fire: from what seemed to be his waist downward, fire; and from his waist upward, a radiance like the gleam of amber.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[3] He stretched out what looked like a hand and took me by a lock of my hair, and the Spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and brought me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces north, where the seat of the image of jealousy stood, the image that provokes to jealousy.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[4] And there was the glory of the God of Israel, like the vision I had seen in the valley.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[5] He said to me, "Son of man, lift up your eyes now toward the north." So I lifted up my eyes toward the north, and there, north of the altar gate, stood this image of jealousy at the entrance.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[6] And he said to me, "Son of man, do you see what they are doing—the great abominations that the house of Israel is committing here, driving me far from my sanctuary? But you will see still greater abominations."
[Ezekiel] [8]:[7] Then he brought me to the entrance of the court, and I looked, and there was a hole in the wall.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[8] He said to me, "Son of man, dig through the wall." So I dug through the wall, and there was a doorway.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[9] And he said to me, "Go in and see the vile abominations they are committing here."
[Ezekiel] [8]:[10] So I went in and looked, and there on the wall all around were carved every kind of creeping thing and detestable beast, and all the idols of the house of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[11] Seventy of the elders of the house of Israel were standing before them, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them, each with his censer in his hand, and a thick cloud of incense was rising.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[12] Then he said to me, "Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the dark, each in the chamber of his own carved images? For they say, 'The LORD does not see us; the LORD has abandoned the land.'"
[Ezekiel] [8]:[13] And he said to me, "You will see still greater abominations that they are committing."
[Ezekiel] [8]:[14] Then he brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD, and there sat women weeping for Tammuz.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[15] And he said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man? You will yet again see abominations greater than these."
[Ezekiel] [8]:[16] Then he brought me into the inner court of the house of the LORD, and there at the entrance of the temple of the LORD, between the portico and the altar, were about twenty-five men with their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east, bowing down to the sun in the east.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[17] And he said to me, "Do you see, son of man? Is it too small a thing for the house of Judah to commit the abominations they are committing here, that they should also fill the land with violence and provoke me again and again? Look how they thrust the branch to their nose!" [Footnote: The meaning of this gesture is uncertain; it apparently refers to a ritual act of contempt or idolatrous worship. An ancient scribal tradition reads "to my nose."]
[Ezekiel] [8]:[18] So I too will act in wrath. My eye will not spare, nor will I show pity. Though they cry in my ears with a loud voice, I will not listen to them.
[Ezekiel] [9]:[1] Then he cried out in my hearing with a loud voice: "Draw near, you executioners of the city, each with his weapon of destruction in his hand!"
[Ezekiel] [9]:[2] And behold, six men came from the direction of the upper gate, which faces north, each with his weapon for smashing in his hand; and among them was one man clothed in linen, with a writing case at his side. They came in and stood beside the bronze altar.
[Ezekiel] [9]:[3] Now the glory of the God of Israel had risen from above the cherub where it had rested, and moved to the threshold of the temple. And he called to the man clothed in linen, who had the writing case at his side,
[Ezekiel] [9]:[4] and the LORD said to him, "Pass through the city, through Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of those who sigh and groan over all the abominations committed within it."
[Ezekiel] [9]:[5] And to the others he said in my hearing, "Pass through the city after him and strike. Show no pity; spare no one.
[Ezekiel] [9]:[6] Slay them utterly—old men, young men and young women, children and women; but do not touch anyone who bears the mark. Begin at my sanctuary." So they began with the elders who were in front of the temple.
[Ezekiel] [9]:[7] Then he said to them, "Defile the temple and fill the courts with the slain. Go out!" So they went out and struck down people in the city.
[Ezekiel] [9]:[8] While they were striking them down, I was left alone; and I fell on my face and cried out, "Ah, Lord GOD! Will you destroy the entire remnant of Israel as you pour out your wrath on Jerusalem?"
[Ezekiel] [9]:[9] He said to me, "The guilt of the house of Israel and Judah is exceedingly great. The land is full of bloodshed and the city is full of injustice; for they say, 'The LORD has abandoned the land, and the LORD does not see.'
[Ezekiel] [9]:[10] So I too will show no pity; I will not spare. I will bring down on their own heads what they have done."
[Ezekiel] [9]:[11] And behold, the man clothed in linen, with the writing case at his side, brought back word: "I have done just as you commanded me."
[Ezekiel] [10]:[1] Then I looked, and above the vault over the heads of the cherubim appeared what looked like a sapphire stone, shaped like a throne.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[2] And he said to the man clothed in linen, "Go in among the wheels, beneath the cherubim. Fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim and scatter them over the city." And he went in as I watched.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[3] The cherubim were standing on the south side of the temple when the man entered, and the cloud filled the inner court. [^1] [^1]: Hebrew: to the right of the temple, that is, the south side.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[4] Then the glory of the LORD rose from above the cherub to the threshold of the temple. The temple was filled with the cloud, and the court was filled with the radiance of the glory of the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[5] And the sound of the cherubim's wings was heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Almighty when he speaks.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[6] When he commanded the man clothed in linen, "Take fire from among the wheels, from among the cherubim," the man went in and stood beside a wheel.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[7] Then one of the cherubim reached out his hand toward the fire that was among them, took some of it, and put it into the hands of the man clothed in linen, who took it and went out.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[8] Under the wings of the cherubim could be seen what looked like human hands.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[9] I looked, and there were four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub, and the wheels gleamed like topaz.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[10] In appearance the four of them were alike, each like a wheel within a wheel.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[11] When they moved, they went in any of the four directions without turning as they went; they followed wherever the head faced, never turning as they went.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[12] Their whole bodies—backs, hands, and wings—were covered with eyes all around, as were their four wheels.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[13] I heard the wheels being called "the whirling wheels."
[Ezekiel] [10]:[14] Each of them had four faces: the first was the face of a cherub, the second the face of a human, the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[15] Then the cherubim rose upward. These were the living creatures I had seen by the Kebar River.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[16] When the cherubim moved, the wheels beside them moved; and when the cherubim spread their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels did not leave their side.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[17] When the cherubim stood still, the wheels stood still; when they rose, the wheels rose with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in them.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[18] Then the glory of the LORD departed from the threshold of the temple and stopped above the cherubim.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[19] While I watched, the cherubim spread their wings and rose from the ground, and as they went, the wheels went with them. They stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the LORD's house, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[20] These were the living creatures I had seen beneath the God of Israel by the Kebar River, and I knew that they were cherubim.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[21] Each had four faces and four wings, and under their wings were what looked like human hands.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[22] Their faces had the same likeness as the faces I had seen by the Kebar River—their appearance and they themselves. Each one went straight ahead.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[1] Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the east gate of the LORD's house, the one that faces east. And there at the entrance of the gate were twenty-five men, and among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[2] And he said to me, "Son of man, these are the men who devise evil and give wicked counsel in this city.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[3] They say, 'The time is not near for building houses. This city is the pot, and we are the meat.'
[Ezekiel] [11]:[4] Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man!"
[Ezekiel] [11]:[5] Then the Spirit of the LORD fell upon me, and he said to me: "Say, 'Thus says the LORD: So you have said, house of Israel — and I know the thoughts that rise in your spirit.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[6] You have multiplied your slain in this city and filled its streets with the dead.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[7] Therefore, thus says the Lord GOD: Your slain, whom you have laid in the midst of the city — they are the meat, and the city is the pot; but you I will drive out of it.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[8] You fear the sword, and the sword is what I will bring upon you, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[9] I will drive you out of the city and hand you over to foreigners, and I will execute judgments on you.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[10] You will fall by the sword. At the border of Israel I will judge you, and you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[11] This city will not be a pot for you, nor will you be the meat inside it. At the border of Israel I will judge you,
[Ezekiel] [11]:[12] and you will know that I am the LORD — you who have not walked in my statutes or kept my ordinances, but have acted according to the customs of the nations around you.'"
[Ezekiel] [11]:[13] Now while I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. Then I fell facedown and cried out with a loud voice, "Ah, Lord GOD! Will you bring the remnant of Israel to a complete end?"
[Ezekiel] [11]:[14] Then the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [11]:[15] "Son of man, your brothers — your brothers, your own kin, and the whole house of Israel, all of them — are the ones to whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, 'Keep far away from the LORD! It is to us that this land has been given as a possession.'
[Ezekiel] [11]:[16] Therefore say: 'Thus says the Lord GOD: Though I sent them far away among the nations and scattered them among the countries, yet I myself have been a sanctuary for them in some measure, in the countries where they have gone.'
[Ezekiel] [11]:[17] Therefore say: 'Thus says the Lord GOD: I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you from the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[18] They will come there and remove from it all its detestable idols and all its abominations.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[19] And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
[Ezekiel] [11]:[20] so that they will walk in my statutes and keep my ordinances and do them. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[21] But as for those whose hearts are set on their detestable idols and abominations, I will bring their conduct down on their own heads, declares the Lord GOD.'"
[Ezekiel] [11]:[22] Then the cherubim lifted their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[23] And the glory of the LORD rose up from the midst of the city and came to rest on the mountain east of the city.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[24] Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me in the vision, by the Spirit of God, to the exiles in Chaldea. And the vision I had seen went up from me.
[Ezekiel] [11]:[25] And I told the exiles all the words of the LORD that he had shown me.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [12]:[2] Son of man, you are living among a rebellious house. They have eyes to see but do not see, ears to hear but do not hear, for they are a rebellious house.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[3] So you, son of man, pack a bundle for exile and set out in broad daylight, before their eyes. Go into exile from where you are to another place while they watch. Perhaps they will see, though they are a rebellious house.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[4] Bring out your belongings like an exile's pack in the daylight, before their eyes, and then go out in the evening, before their eyes, like those who go into exile.
