[Ezekiel] [12]:[5] While they watch, dig through the wall and carry your things out through it.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[6] Before their eyes, lift the pack to your shoulder and carry it out in the dark. Cover your face so you cannot see the land, for I have made you a sign to the house of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[7] I did just as I was commanded. I brought out my belongings like an exile's pack in the daylight, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my hands. In the dark I carried my things out on my shoulder, before their eyes.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[8] In the morning the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [12]:[9] Son of man, has not the house of Israel, that rebellious house, asked you, "What are you doing?"
[Ezekiel] [12]:[10] Say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: This oracle concerns the prince in Jerusalem and the whole house of Israel who are there with him.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[11] Say: I am a sign to you. As I have done, so it will be done to them; they will go into exile, into captivity.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[12] The prince who is among them will lift his pack to his shoulder in the dark and go out. They will dig through the wall to bring him out through it. He will cover his face so that he cannot see the land with his own eyes.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[13] I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, yet he will not see it, and there he will die.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[14] All those around him, his helpers and all his troops, I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw the sword after them.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[15] Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them through the lands.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[16] But I will spare a few of them from the sword, the famine, and the plague, so that among the nations where they go they may recount all their detestable practices. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[17] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [12]:[18] Son of man, eat your bread with trembling and drink your water with shuddering and dread.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[19] And say to the people of the land: This is what the Lord GOD says about those who live in Jerusalem and in the land of Israel: They will eat their bread in dread and drink their water in despair, for their land will be stripped of everything in it because of the violence of all who live there.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[20] The inhabited cities will be laid waste and the land will become a desolation. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[21] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [12]:[22] Son of man, what is this proverb you have in the land of Israel: "The days drag on, and every vision comes to nothing"?
[Ezekiel] [12]:[23] Therefore say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: I will put an end to this proverb, and they will never quote it again in Israel. Instead, say to them: The days are near, and so is the fulfillment of every vision.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[24] For there will be no more false visions or flattering divination within the house of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[25] For I am the LORD. I will speak, and what I speak will be done; it will no longer be delayed. In your own days, you rebellious house, I will speak the word and carry it out, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[26] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [12]:[27] Son of man, the house of Israel is saying, "The vision he sees is for many years from now; he prophesies about distant times."
[Ezekiel] [12]:[28] Therefore say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: None of my words will be delayed any longer. Whatever I speak will be done, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [13]:[2] Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are prophesying, and say to those who prophesy out of their own hearts: Hear the word of the LORD!
[Ezekiel] [13]:[3] This is what the Lord GOD says: Woe to the foolish prophets, who follow their own spirit and have seen nothing!
[Ezekiel] [13]:[4] Your prophets, Israel, have been like foxes among the ruins.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[5] You have not gone up into the breaches or repaired the wall around the house of Israel, so that it might stand in the battle on the day of the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[6] They see empty visions and lying divinations. They say, "Declares the LORD," when the LORD has not sent them, yet they wait for their word to be fulfilled.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[7] Have you not seen an empty vision and spoken a lying divination, when you say, "Declares the LORD," though I have not spoken?
[Ezekiel] [13]:[8] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you have spoken emptiness and seen lies, I am against you, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[9] My hand will be against the prophets who see empty visions and divine lies. They will not belong to the council of my people or be written in the register of the house of Israel, nor will they enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[10] Because, yes, because they have led my people astray, saying, "Peace," when there is no peace, and because when someone builds a flimsy wall they smear it over with whitewash—
[Ezekiel] [13]:[11] say to those who smear it with whitewash that it will fall. A flooding rain will come; and you, hailstones, will fall, and a stormwind will break loose.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[12] And when the wall falls, will you not be asked, "Where now is the whitewash you spread on it?"
[Ezekiel] [13]:[13] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: In my fury I will unleash a stormwind; in my anger a flooding rain will come, and hailstones in wrath to make an end.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[14] I will tear down the wall you whitewashed and level it to the ground, so that its foundation is laid bare. It will fall, and you will perish within it. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[15] So I will spend my wrath on the wall and on those who whitewashed it, and I will say to you: The wall is gone, and gone are those who whitewashed it—
[Ezekiel] [13]:[16] the prophets of Israel who prophesied concerning Jerusalem and saw visions of peace for her, when there was no peace, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[17] And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own hearts, and prophesy against them.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[18] Say: This is what the Lord GOD says: Woe to the women who sew magic bands for every wrist and make veils for the heads of people of every height, to hunt down souls! Will you hunt the souls of my people and keep your own souls alive?[^1] [^1]: The exact nature of the "bands" and "veils" is uncertain; they appear to be objects used in occult practice to ensnare people.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[19] You have profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and scraps of bread, killing souls who should not die and keeping alive souls who should not live, by lying to my people, who listen to lies.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[20] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am against your magic bands with which you hunt souls like birds. I will tear them from your arms and set free the souls you hunt like birds.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[21] I will tear off your veils and deliver my people from your hands, and they will no longer be prey in your grasp. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[22] Because you disheartened the righteous with lies, though I had brought him no grief, and because you strengthened the hands of the wicked so that he would not turn from his evil way and live,
[Ezekiel] [13]:[23] therefore you will no longer see empty visions or practice divination. I will deliver my people from your hands, and you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[1] Now some men from among the elders of Israel came to me and sat down before me.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[2] Then the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [14]:[3] "Son of man, these men have taken their idols into their hearts and set the stumbling block of their guilt before their faces. Should I let myself be consulted by them at all?
[Ezekiel] [14]:[4] Therefore speak to them and say: This is what the Lord GOD says: Any Israelite who takes his idols into his heart and sets the stumbling block of his guilt before his face, and then comes to the prophet—I, the LORD, will answer him myself, in keeping with his many idols,
[Ezekiel] [14]:[5] so that I may lay hold of the house of Israel by their own hearts, for they have all turned away from me through their idols.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[6] Therefore say to the house of Israel: This is what the Lord GOD says: Repent! Turn away from your idols, and turn your faces from all your abominations.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[7] For any Israelite, or any foreigner residing in Israel, who separates himself from me and takes his idols into his heart, setting the stumbling block of his guilt before his face, and then comes to the prophet to inquire of me—I, the LORD, will answer him myself.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[8] I will set my face against that man; I will make him a sign and a byword, and I will cut him off from among my people. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[9] And if the prophet is deceived and speaks a word, I, the LORD, have deceived that prophet; I will stretch out my hand against him and destroy him from among my people Israel.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[10] They will bear their guilt—the guilt of the one who inquires will be the same as the guilt of the prophet—
[Ezekiel] [14]:[11] so that the house of Israel may no longer stray from me and no longer defile themselves with all their transgressions. Then they will be my people, and I will be their God, declares the Lord GOD."
[Ezekiel] [14]:[12] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [14]:[13] "Son of man, if a land sins against me by acting unfaithfully, and I stretch out my hand against it and break its staff of bread, sending famine upon it and cutting off from it both man and beast,
[Ezekiel] [14]:[14] then even if these three men—Noah, Daniel, and Job—were in it, they would save only their own lives by their righteousness, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[15] Or if I let wild beasts pass through that land and they leave it bereft of its children, so that it becomes desolate, with no one passing through because of the beasts,
[Ezekiel] [14]:[16] then as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, even if these three men were in it, they could not save their own sons or daughters. They alone would be saved, and the land would be desolate.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[17] Or if I bring the sword against that land and say, 'Let the sword sweep through the land,' and I cut off from it both man and beast,
[Ezekiel] [14]:[18] then as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, even if these three men were in it, they could not save their own sons or daughters; they alone would be saved.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[19] Or if I send a plague into that land and pour out my wrath upon it in bloodshed, cutting off from it both man and beast,
[Ezekiel] [14]:[20] then as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, they could not save a son or a daughter; by their righteousness they would save only their own lives.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[21] For this is what the Lord GOD says: How much worse will it be when I send my four dreadful judgments against Jerusalem—sword and famine, wild beasts and plague—to cut off from it both man and beast!
[Ezekiel] [14]:[22] Yet some survivors will be left in it, sons and daughters who will be brought out. They will come out to you, and when you see their conduct and their deeds, you will be consoled concerning the disaster I have brought upon Jerusalem—everything I have brought upon it.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[23] They will console you when you see their conduct and their deeds, and you will know that I have done nothing in it without cause, declares the Lord GOD."
[Ezekiel] [15]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [15]:[2] Son of man, how is the wood of the vine better than any other wood, the branch that grows among the trees of the forest?
[Ezekiel] [15]:[3] Is any of its wood taken to make something useful? Does anyone take from it a peg to hang a vessel on?
[Ezekiel] [15]:[4] See—it is given to the fire as fuel. The fire consumes both its ends, and its middle is charred. Is it good for anything then?
[Ezekiel] [15]:[5] When it was whole, nothing could be made of it; how much less, now that the fire has consumed it and it is charred!
[Ezekiel] [15]:[6] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire as fuel, so have I given up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
[Ezekiel] [15]:[7] I will set my face against them. Though they have come out of the fire, the fire will yet consume them. And you will know that I am the LORD, when I set my face against them.
[Ezekiel] [15]:[8] I will make the land a desolation, because they have been utterly unfaithful, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [16]:[2] Son of man, confront Jerusalem with her abominations,
[Ezekiel] [16]:[3] and say: This is what the Lord GOD says to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth were in the land of the Canaanites; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[4] As for your birth, on the day you were born your cord was not cut, you were not washed clean with water, not rubbed with salt, not wrapped in cloths.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[5] No eye pitied you enough to do even one of these things for you out of compassion. You were thrown out into the open field, for you were despised on the day you were born.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[6] Then I passed by and saw you kicking about in your blood, and I said to you as you lay in your blood, "Live!" Yes, I said to you as you lay in your blood, "Live!"
[Ezekiel] [16]:[7] I made you grow like a plant of the field. You grew up and matured and came to full beauty. Your breasts were formed and your hair grew, but you were naked and bare.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[8] Then I passed by you and looked at you, and saw that you had reached the age for love. So I spread my cloak over you and covered your nakedness. I gave you my oath and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord GOD, and you became mine.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[9] Then I bathed you with water, washed the blood from you, and anointed you with oil.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[10] I clothed you in embroidered cloth and gave you sandals of fine leather; I wound fine linen around your head and covered you with silk.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[11] I adorned you with jewelry: I put bracelets on your wrists and a necklace around your neck,
[Ezekiel] [16]:[12] a ring in your nose, rings in your ears, and a crown of splendor on your head.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[13] So you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was of fine linen, silk, and embroidered cloth. You ate the finest flour, honey, and oil. You grew exceedingly beautiful and rose to royalty.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[14] Your fame spread among the nations because of your beauty, for it was perfect through the splendor I had bestowed on you, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[15] But you trusted in your beauty and used your fame to play the whore. You lavished your favors on every passerby, and your beauty became his.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[16] You took some of your garments and made for yourself gaudy shrines, and on them you played the whore—things that had never been and never will be again.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[17] You took the fine jewelry I gave you, made of my gold and my silver, and you made for yourself male images and played the whore with them.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[18] You took your embroidered garments to clothe them, and you set my oil and my incense before them.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[19] And the food I gave you—the finest flour, oil, and honey with which I fed you—you set before them as a pleasing aroma. So it was, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[20] You even took your sons and daughters, whom you bore to me, and sacrificed them to those images as food. Were your whorings not enough?
[Ezekiel] [16]:[21] You slaughtered my children and handed them over, making them pass through the fire to those idols.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[22] And in all your abominations and your whorings you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, kicking about in your blood.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[23] And after all your wickedness—woe, woe to you! declares the Lord GOD—
[Ezekiel] [16]:[24] you built yourself a mound and made yourself a lofty shrine in every public square.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[25] At the head of every street you built your shrine and degraded your beauty, spreading your legs for every passerby, multiplying your whorings.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[26] You played the whore with the Egyptians, your lustful neighbors, and multiplied your whorings to provoke me to anger.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[27] So I stretched out my hand against you and reduced your territory. I handed you over to the greed of your enemies, the daughters of the Philistines, who were appalled at your lewd conduct.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[28] You played the whore with the Assyrians too, because you were insatiable; you whored with them and still were not satisfied.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[29] You multiplied your whoring with Chaldea, the land of merchants, and even with this you were not satisfied.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[30] How weak your heart was, declares the Lord GOD, when you did all these things, the deeds of a brazen prostitute!
[Ezekiel] [16]:[31] When you built your mound at the head of every street and made your lofty shrine in every square, you were not even like a prostitute, for you scorned payment.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[32] You adulterous wife, who takes strangers in place of her own husband!
[Ezekiel] [16]:[33] Men give gifts to all prostitutes, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers, bribing them to come to you from every side for your whorings.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[34] So in your whoring you were the opposite of other women: no one solicited you; you paid the fee, and no fee was paid to you. You were the opposite.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[35] Therefore, you prostitute, hear the word of the LORD!
[Ezekiel] [16]:[36] This is what the Lord GOD says: Because you poured out your lust and exposed your nakedness in your whorings with your lovers, and because of all your detestable idols and the blood of your children whom you gave to them—
[Ezekiel] [16]:[37] therefore I am going to gather all your lovers with whom you found pleasure, all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from every side and strip you naked before them, and they will see all your nakedness.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[38] I will sentence you to the punishment of women who commit adultery and who shed blood; I will bring upon you the blood of wrath and jealousy.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[39] I will hand you over to them, and they will tear down your mound and demolish your lofty shrines. They will strip off your clothes, take your fine jewelry, and leave you naked and bare.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[40] They will bring a mob against you, and they will stone you and cut you to pieces with their swords.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[41] They will burn your houses with fire and execute judgment on you before the eyes of many women. So I will put an end to your whoring, and you will no longer pay your lovers.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[42] Then I will spend my wrath on you, and my jealousy will depart from you; I will be calm and no longer angry.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[43] Because you did not remember the days of your youth but enraged me with all these things, I in turn will bring your conduct down on your own head, declares the Lord GOD. Have you not added lewdness to all your other abominations?
[Ezekiel] [16]:[44] Look, everyone who quotes proverbs will use this proverb about you: "Like mother, like daughter."
[Ezekiel] [16]:[45] You are truly your mother's daughter, who despised her husband and her children, and you are truly the sister of your sisters, who despised their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[46] Your older sister was Samaria, who lived to the north of you with her daughters; and your younger sister, who lived to the south of you with her daughters, was Sodom.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[47] You not only walked in their ways and copied their abominations, but as if that were too small a thing, you became more corrupt than they in all your ways.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[48] As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters never did what you and your daughters have done.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[49] This was the guilt of your sister Sodom: she and her daughters were arrogant, overfed, and complacent in their ease, and they did not help the poor and needy.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[50] They grew haughty and committed abominations before me; so I swept them away when I saw it.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[51] Samaria did not commit half the sins you did. You multiplied your abominations beyond theirs and made your sisters look righteous by all the abominations you committed.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[52] So bear your own disgrace, for you have provided an excuse for your sister. Because your sins were more abominable than theirs, they appear more righteous than you. So be ashamed and bear your disgrace, for you have made your sisters look righteous.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[53] Yet I will restore the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters, and the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters, and I will restore your fortunes along with theirs,
[Ezekiel] [16]:[54] so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of everything you have done, becoming a consolation to them.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[55] Your sisters, Sodom with her daughters and Samaria with her daughters, will return to their former state, and you and your daughters will return to your former state.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[56] Was not your sister Sodom a byword in your mouth in the day of your pride,
[Ezekiel] [16]:[57] before your own wickedness was exposed? Now it is as at the time of the reproach of the daughters of Aram and all her neighbors, and of the daughters of the Philistines—all those around you who despise you.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[58] You must bear the consequences of your lewdness and your abominations, declares the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[59] For this is what the Lord GOD says: I will deal with you as you have done, you who despised the oath by breaking the covenant.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[60] Yet I will remember the covenant I made with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[61] Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your sisters, both those older and those younger than you. I will give them to you as daughters, though not by my covenant with you.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[62] So I will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am the LORD—
[Ezekiel] [16]:[63] that you may remember and be ashamed, and never again open your mouth because of your disgrace, when I make atonement for you for all that you have done, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [17]:[2] Son of man, pose a riddle and tell a parable to the house of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[3] Say: Thus says the Lord GOD: A great eagle with great wings and long pinions, rich in plumage of many colors, came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[4] He broke off its topmost shoot, carried it to a land of merchants, and set it in a city of traders.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[5] Then he took some of the seed of the land and planted it in fertile soil. He set it beside abundant water, placing it like a willow.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[6] It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height, with its branches turned toward him and its roots beneath him. So it became a vine, put out shoots, and sent out boughs.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[7] But there was another great eagle with great wings and thick plumage, and behold, this vine bent its roots toward him and stretched out its branches to him, so that he might water it, away from the bed where it was planted.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[8] It had been planted in good soil beside abundant water, that it might put out branches and bear fruit and become a noble vine.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[9] Say: Thus says the Lord GOD: Will it thrive? Will he not tear up its roots and strip off its fruit, so that it shrivels and every fresh leaf it puts out withers away? No strong arm and no great army will be needed to pull it up by the roots.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[10] Behold, it is planted; will it thrive? When the east wind strikes it, will it not wither away completely—wither on the bed where it grew?
[Ezekiel] [17]:[11] Then the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [17]:[12] Say now to the rebellious house: Do you not know what these things mean? Tell them: Behold, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took its king and its officials, and brought them back with him to Babylon.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[13] He took one of the royal offspring, made a covenant with him, and put him under oath. He also carried off the leading men of the land,
[Ezekiel] [17]:[14] so that the kingdom would be humbled, unable to lift itself up, and would keep his covenant and so survive.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[15] But he rebelled against him by sending his envoys to Egypt, to get horses and a great army. Will he succeed? Will one who does such things escape? Can he break a covenant and go free?
[Ezekiel] [17]:[16] As I live, declares the Lord GOD, he shall die in Babylon, in the land of the king who put him on the throne—the king whose oath he despised, whose covenant he broke.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[17] Pharaoh with his mighty army and vast company will be of no help to him in the war, when ramps are thrown up and siege walls built to cut off many lives.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[18] He despised the oath and broke the covenant; he gave his hand in pledge and still did all these things. He shall not escape.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[19] Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: As I live, it was my oath that he despised and my covenant that he broke, and I will bring it down on his own head.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[20] I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there for the treachery he committed against me.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[21] All his choice troops, in all his ranks, shall fall by the sword, and those who are left shall be scattered to every wind. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[22] Thus says the Lord GOD: I myself will take a sprig from the lofty top of the cedar and set it out. I will pluck a tender shoot from its topmost branches, and I myself will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[23] On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it, and it will put out branches and bear fruit and become a majestic cedar. Birds of every kind will nest under it; in the shade of its branches they will make their home.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[24] And all the trees of the field will know that I am the LORD: I bring down the high tree and lift up the low tree, I dry up the green tree and make the dry tree flourish. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [18]:[2] What do you mean by repeating this proverb about the land of Israel: "The fathers eat sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge"?
[Ezekiel] [18]:[3] As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, you shall no longer use this proverb in Israel.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[4] See, every soul belongs to me: the soul of the father as well as the soul of the son is mine. The soul who sins is the one who will die.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[5] Suppose a man is righteous and does what is just and right.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[6] He does not eat at the mountain shrines or lift up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor's wife or approach a woman during her period.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[7] He oppresses no one; he returns what he took in pledge for a debt; he commits no robbery. He gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[8] He does not lend at interest or take a profit. He holds back his hand from wrongdoing and judges fairly between one person and another.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[9] He walks in my statutes and faithfully keeps my ordinances. Such a man is righteous; he will surely live, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[10] But suppose he has a violent son, who sheds blood and does any of these things
[Ezekiel] [18]:[11] —he does none of these good things, but instead eats at the mountain shrines and defiles his neighbor's wife,
[Ezekiel] [18]:[12] oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not return a pledge, lifts up his eyes to the idols, and does what is detestable,
[Ezekiel] [18]:[13] lends at interest and takes a profit. Will he live? He will not live! Because he has done all these detestable things, he shall surely be put to death; his blood will be on his own head.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[14] But suppose this man in turn has a son who sees all the sins his father has committed, and though he sees them, he does not do the same.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[15] He does not eat at the mountain shrines or lift up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor's wife.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[16] He oppresses no one, takes no pledge, commits no robbery. He gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[17] He holds back his hand from harming the poor, takes no interest or profit, keeps my ordinances and walks in my statutes. He will not die for his father's guilt; he will surely live.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[18] But his father, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what was not good among his people—he will die for his own guilt.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[19] Yet you ask, "Why should the son not bear his father's guilt?" Since the son has done what is just and right, keeping all my statutes and carrying them out, he will surely live.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[20] The soul who sins is the one who will die. A son will not bear his father's guilt, nor will a father bear his son's guilt. The righteousness of the righteous will be his own, and the wickedness of the wicked will be his own.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[21] But if the wicked man turns from all the sins he has committed, keeps all my statutes, and does what is just and right, he will surely live; he will not die.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[22] None of the transgressions he has committed will be remembered against him. Because of the righteousness he has practiced, he will live.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[23] Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked? declares the Lord GOD. Is it not rather that he turn from his ways and live?
[Ezekiel] [18]:[24] But if a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does wrong, committing the same detestable things the wicked man does, will he live? None of the righteous deeds he has done will be remembered. Because of the treachery he is guilty of and the sin he has committed, he will die.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[25] Yet you say, "The Lord's way is not fair." Listen, house of Israel: Is my way unfair? Is it not your ways that are unfair?
[Ezekiel] [18]:[26] If a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does wrong, he will die for it; because of the wrong he has done, he will die.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[27] And if a wicked man turns from the wickedness he has committed and does what is just and right, he will save his life.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[28] Because he considered and turned away from all the transgressions he had committed, he will surely live; he will not die.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[29] Yet the house of Israel says, "The Lord's way is not fair." Are my ways unfair, house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are unfair?
[Ezekiel] [18]:[30] Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, each one according to his ways, declares the Lord GOD. Repent! Turn away from all your transgressions, so that guilt will not be your downfall.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[31] Cast away from you all the transgressions you have committed, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, house of Israel?
[Ezekiel] [18]:[32] For I take no pleasure in the death of anyone who dies, declares the Lord GOD. So turn, and live!
[Ezekiel] [19]:[1] As for you, raise a lament over the princes of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[2] Say: What a lioness was your mother! Among lions she lay down; among young lions she reared her cubs.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[3] She raised up one of her cubs; he became a young lion. He learned to tear his prey; he devoured men.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[4] The nations heard of him; he was caught in their pit, and they led him with hooks to the land of Egypt.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[5] When she saw that her waiting was in vain, that her hope was lost, she took another of her cubs and made him a young lion.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[6] He prowled among the lions; he became a young lion. He learned to tear his prey; he devoured men.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[7] He broke down their strongholds and laid waste their cities; the land and all who filled it were appalled at the sound of his roaring. [^1] [^1]: The Hebrew text here reads literally 'he knew his widows'; 'broke down their strongholds' follows a slight difference in the consonants supported by ancient versions.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[8] Then the nations closed in on him from the provinces all around. They spread their net over him; he was caught in their pit.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[9] With hooks they put him in a cage and brought him to the king of Babylon. They brought him into strongholds, so that his voice would never again be heard on the mountains of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[10] Your mother was like a vine in your blood, planted by the water, fruitful and full of branches from the abundant water. [^1] [^1]: 'In your blood' renders an obscure Hebrew phrase; it may mean 'in your vineyard' or 'in your likeness.'
[Ezekiel] [19]:[11] Its branches grew strong, fit for the scepters of rulers. It towered high above the thick foliage, conspicuous in its height and in the mass of its boughs.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[12] But it was uprooted in fury and thrown to the ground; the east wind dried up its fruit. Its strong branches were broken off and withered; fire consumed them.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[13] Now it is planted in the wilderness, in a land of drought and thirst.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[14] Fire went out from the stem of its branches and consumed its fruit, and no strong rod was left in it, no scepter for ruling. This is a lament, and a lament it shall remain.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[1] In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, certain of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the LORD, and they sat down before me.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[2] Then the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [20]:[3] Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: Have you come to inquire of me? As I live, I will not let you inquire of me, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[4] Will you judge them? Will you judge them, son of man? Then confront them with the abominations of their fathers,
[Ezekiel] [20]:[5] and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: On the day I chose Israel, I raised my hand in an oath to the offspring of the house of Jacob and made myself known to them in the land of Egypt. I raised my hand and swore to them, saying, I am the LORD your God.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[6] On that day I swore to them that I would bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land I had searched out for them, a land flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[7] And I said to them: Each of you, throw away the detestable things your eyes are set on, and do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[8] But they rebelled against me and refused to listen to me. Not one of them threw away the detestable things their eyes were set on, and they did not abandon the idols of Egypt. So I said I would pour out my wrath upon them and spend my anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[9] But I acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned in the sight of the nations among whom they lived, in whose sight I had made myself known to them by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[10] So I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them into the wilderness.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[11] I gave them my statutes and made known to them my rules, by which anyone who does them shall live.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[12] I also gave them my Sabbaths, as a sign between me and them, so they would know that I am the LORD who sanctifies them.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[13] But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness. They did not walk in my statutes; they rejected my rules, by which anyone who does them shall live; and they utterly profaned my Sabbaths. So I said I would pour out my wrath upon them in the wilderness and make an end of them.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[14] But I acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned in the sight of the nations, before whose eyes I had brought them out.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[15] Moreover, I swore to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them into the land I had given them, a land flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands—
[Ezekiel] [20]:[16] because they rejected my rules and did not walk in my statutes and profaned my Sabbaths, for their hearts went after their idols.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[17] Yet my eye spared them from destruction, and I did not make a full end of them in the wilderness.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[18] And I said to their children in the wilderness: Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, do not keep their rules, and do not defile yourselves with their idols.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[19] I am the LORD your God. Walk in my statutes, keep my rules, and do them.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[20] Keep my Sabbaths holy, and let them be a sign between me and you, so you may know that I am the LORD your God.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[21] But the children rebelled against me. They did not walk in my statutes, nor were they careful to keep my rules, by which anyone who does them shall live; they profaned my Sabbaths. So I said I would pour out my wrath upon them and spend my anger against them in the wilderness.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[22] But I held back my hand and acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned in the sight of the nations, before whose eyes I had brought them out.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[23] Moreover, I swore to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the lands,
[Ezekiel] [20]:[24] because they had not kept my rules, had rejected my statutes, had profaned my Sabbaths, and had fixed their eyes on the idols of their fathers.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[25] So I also gave them statutes that were not good and rules by which they could not live.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[26] I declared them defiled through their gifts, in that they offered up every firstborn, so that I might horrify them, so they would know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[27] Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: In this also your fathers blasphemed me, by dealing treacherously with me.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[28] For when I brought them into the land that I swore to give them, they saw every high hill and every leafy tree, and there they offered their sacrifices and presented offerings that provoked me; there they sent up their pleasing aromas and poured out their drink offerings.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[29] So I said to them: What is this high place to which you keep going? And its name is called Bamah to this day. [Footnote: "Bamah" is the Hebrew word for "high place."]
[Ezekiel] [20]:[30] Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord GOD: Will you defile yourselves after the manner of your fathers and prostitute yourselves after their detestable things?
[Ezekiel] [20]:[31] When you present your gifts, when you make your children pass through the fire, you defile yourselves with all your idols to this day. And shall I let you inquire of me, O house of Israel? As I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will not let you inquire of me.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[32] What rises up in your spirit will never come to pass—you who say, "We will be like the nations, like the clans of the lands, serving wood and stone."
[Ezekiel] [20]:[33] As I live, declares the Lord GOD, surely with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with wrath poured out I will reign over you.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[34] I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands where you were scattered, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with wrath poured out.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[35] I will bring you into the wilderness of the peoples, and there I will enter into judgment with you face to face.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[36] As I entered into judgment with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I will enter into judgment with you, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[37] I will make you pass under the shepherd's rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[38] I will purge out from among you the rebels and those who transgress against me. I will bring them out of the land where they sojourn, but they shall not enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[39] As for you, house of Israel, thus says the Lord GOD: Go and serve your idols, every one of you, if you will not listen to me; but afterward you shall no longer profane my holy name with your gifts and your idols.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[40] For on my holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, there all the house of Israel, all of them, shall serve me in the land. There I will accept them, and there I will require your contributions and the firstfruits of your offerings, with all your holy things.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[41] As a pleasing aroma I will accept you, when I bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands where you were scattered. And through you I will show myself holy in the sight of the nations.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[42] Then you will know that I am the LORD, when I bring you into the land of Israel, the land that I swore to give to your fathers.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[43] There you will remember your ways and all the deeds by which you defiled yourselves, and you will loathe yourselves for all the evils you have committed.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[44] And you will know that I am the LORD, when I deal with you for my name's sake and not according to your evil ways or your corrupt deeds, O house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [21]:[2] Son of man, set your face toward the south, preach against the southland, and prophesy against the forest of the southern field.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[3] Say to the forest of the Negev: Hear the word of the LORD. Thus says the Lord GOD: I am about to kindle a fire in you, and it will devour every tree in you, both green and dry. The blazing flame will not be quenched, and every face from south to north will be scorched by it.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[4] Then all flesh will see that I, the LORD, have kindled it; it will not be quenched.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[5] Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! They are saying of me, 'Is he not just spinning out riddles?'"
[Ezekiel] [21]:[6] And the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [21]:[7] Son of man, set your face toward Jerusalem, preach against her sanctuaries, and prophesy against the land of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[8] Say to the land of Israel: Thus says the LORD: I am against you. I will draw my sword from its sheath and cut off from you both the righteous and the wicked.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[9] Because I am cutting off from you both righteous and wicked, my sword will come out of its sheath against all flesh, from south to north.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[10] Then all flesh will know that I, the LORD, have drawn my sword from its sheath; it will not return again.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[11] And you, son of man, groan! With loins broken and in bitterness, groan before their eyes.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[12] And when they ask you, "Why are you groaning?" say: Because of the news that is coming. Every heart will melt, every hand will go limp, every spirit will faint, and every knee will turn to water. It is coming, it is here, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[13] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [21]:[14] Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord: A sword, a sword—sharpened and also polished!
[Ezekiel] [21]:[15] Sharpened for the slaughter, polished to flash like lightning. Shall we then rejoice? The scepter of my son despises every tree.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[16] He has given it to be polished, to be gripped in the hand. The sword is sharpened, it is polished, ready to be placed in the hand of the slayer.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[17] Cry out and wail, son of man, for it comes against my people, against all the princes of Israel. They are thrown to the sword along with my people; therefore strike your thigh.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[18] For the testing is here—and what then, if even the scepter that despises comes to nothing? declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[19] And you, son of man, prophesy and clap your hands together. Let the sword strike twice, yes, three times—the sword for the slain, the sword for the great slaughter, closing in on them from every side.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[20] So that hearts may melt and many may stumble, I have set the sword's flashing point at all their gates. Ah! It is made to flash like lightning, honed for the slaughter.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[21] Slash to the right, sword; then to the left—wherever your edge is turned.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[22] I too will clap my hands, and my fury will come to rest. I, the LORD, have spoken.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[23] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [21]:[24] Son of man, mark out two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to travel—both of them leading out from the same land. Set up a signpost where the road forks toward the city.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[25] Mark out one road for the sword to come against Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another against Judah, against fortified Jerusalem.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[26] For the king of Babylon will stand at the fork of the road, where the two ways part, to seek an omen: he will shake the arrows, consult the household idols, and examine the liver.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[27] Into his right hand comes the omen—Jerusalem: to set up battering rams, to open the mouth for the slaughter, to raise the voice with the battle shout, to bring the rams against her gates, to throw up siege ramps and build siege walls.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[28] To them it will seem a false omen, for they have sworn solemn oaths—but he calls their guilt to mind, so that they will be captured.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[29] Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Because you have brought your guilt to mind, so that your rebellions are laid bare and your sins are exposed in everything you do—because you have brought yourselves to remembrance, you will be taken captive by force.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[30] And you, profane and wicked prince of Israel, whose day has come, the time of your final punishment—
[Ezekiel] [21]:[31] thus says the Lord GOD: Remove the turban, take off the crown! Nothing will remain as it was: the lowly will be lifted up, and the exalted brought low.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[32] A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it! Nor will this stand until he comes to whom the judgment belongs; to him I will give it.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[33] And you, son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord GOD concerning the Ammonites and their taunting. Say: A sword, a sword, drawn for the slaughter, polished to devour, to flash like lightning—
[Ezekiel] [21]:[34] while they see false visions for you and divine lies for you—to lay it on the necks of the wicked who are doomed to die, whose day has come, the time of their final punishment.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[35] Return it to its sheath! In the place where you were created, in the land of your origin, I will judge you.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[36] I will pour out my indignation upon you; I will breathe the fire of my wrath against you and hand you over to brutal men, skilled in destruction.
[Ezekiel] [21]:[37] You will be fuel for the fire; your blood will be spilled in the land. You will not be remembered, for I, the LORD, have spoken.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [22]:[2] "Son of man, will you judge? Will you judge the city of blood? Then confront her with all her detestable deeds.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[3] Say: This is what the Lord GOD says: City that sheds blood in her midst, so bringing on her hour, city that has made idols against herself and so defiled herself—
[Ezekiel] [22]:[4] by the blood you have shed you have brought guilt upon yourself, and by the idols you have made you have defiled yourself. You have brought your days near and have come to the end of your years. Therefore I have made you an object of scorn to the nations and a mockery to every land.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[5] Those near and those far off will mock you, city of foul name, city full of turmoil.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[6] See how the princes of Israel within you, each one relying on the strength of his arm, use their power to shed blood.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[7] Within you they have treated father and mother with contempt; they have oppressed the stranger in your midst; they have wronged the orphan and the widow.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[8] You have despised what is holy to me and profaned my Sabbaths.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[9] In you there are men who slander in order to shed blood; in you they eat at the mountain shrines and commit shameless acts in your midst.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[10] In you a man uncovers his father's nakedness; in you they violate a woman during her time of impurity.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[11] One man commits an abomination with his neighbor's wife, another defiles his daughter-in-law with lewdness, and another violates his sister, his own father's daughter—all this within you.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[12] In you they take bribes to shed blood; you take interest and profit at another's expense, and you extort your neighbors by oppression. And me you have forgotten, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[13] See, I strike my hands together over the dishonest gain you have made and over the blood you have shed in your midst.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[14] Will your heart hold up? Will your hands be strong when the day comes that I deal with you? I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will act.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[15] I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you through the lands, and I will purge your uncleanness from you.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[16] Through your own doing you will be profaned in the sight of the nations, and you will know that I am the LORD."
[Ezekiel] [22]:[17] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [22]:[18] "Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me. All of them are copper, tin, iron, and lead in the furnace; they are nothing but the dross of silver.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[19] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because all of you have become dross, I am going to gather you into the middle of Jerusalem.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[20] As silver, copper, iron, lead, and tin are gathered into a furnace to have the fire blown upon them to melt them, so I will gather you in my anger and my wrath, and I will put you in and melt you down.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[21] I will collect you and blow upon you with the fire of my fury, and you will be melted within her.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[22] As silver is melted in the furnace, so you will be melted within her. And you will know that I, the LORD, have poured out my wrath upon you."
[Ezekiel] [22]:[23] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [22]:[24] "Son of man, say to her: You are a land that has not been cleansed, a land not rained upon in the day of wrath.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[25] Her prophets conspire in her midst; like a roaring lion tearing its prey they devour lives, they seize treasure and precious things, they make many widows within her.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[26] Her priests do violence to my law and profane what is holy to me. They make no distinction between the holy and the common, and they teach nothing about the difference between the unclean and the clean. They shut their eyes to my Sabbaths, so that I am profaned among them.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[27] Her officials within her are like wolves tearing their prey; they shed blood and destroy lives to make unjust gain.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[28] Her prophets whitewash it all for them with false visions and lying divinations, saying, 'This is what the Lord GOD says,' when the LORD has not spoken.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[29] The people of the land practice extortion and commit robbery. They wrong the poor and the needy and oppress the stranger, denying him justice.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[30] I searched among them for someone to repair the wall and stand before me in the breach on behalf of the land, so that I would not destroy it—but I found no one.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[31] So I have poured out my indignation upon them; I have consumed them with the fire of my fury. I have brought their conduct down on their own heads, declares the Lord GOD."
[Ezekiel] [23]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [23]:[2] Son of man, there were two women, daughters of the same mother.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[3] They played the whore in Egypt; in their youth they played the whore. There their breasts were fondled, and there their maiden breasts were handled.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[4] Their names were Oholah, the elder, and Oholibah, her sister. They became mine and bore sons and daughters. As for their names: Samaria is Oholah, and Jerusalem is Oholibah.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[5] But Oholah played the whore while she was mine. She burned with lust for her lovers, the Assyrians, her neighbors—
[Ezekiel] [23]:[6] governors and commanders dressed in blue, all of them handsome young men, cavalrymen mounted on horses.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[7] She gave herself as a whore to them, the choicest men of Assyria, every one of them; and with all whom she lusted after she defiled herself with their idols.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[8] Nor did she give up the whoring she began in Egypt, for in her youth men had slept with her, had handled her young breasts and poured out their lust on her.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[9] Therefore I handed her over to her lovers, to the Assyrians she lusted after.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[10] They stripped her naked, seized her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became a byword among women, and judgment was carried out on her.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[11] Her sister Oholibah saw all this, yet in her lust she was even more corrupt than her sister, and her whoring surpassed her sister's.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[12] She lusted after the Assyrians—governors and commanders, her neighbors, splendidly dressed, cavalrymen mounted on horses, all of them handsome young men.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[13] And I saw that she had defiled herself; both of them had gone the same way.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[14] But she carried her whoring still further. She saw men carved on the wall, figures of Chaldeans etched in vermilion,
[Ezekiel] [23]:[15] belts around their waists, flowing turbans on their heads, all of them looking like officers—the very image of Babylonians, whose native land is Chaldea.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[16] At the mere sight of them she lusted after them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[17] So the Babylonians came to her, to her bed of love, and defiled her with their lust. And when she had been defiled by them, she turned from them in disgust.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[18] When she flaunted her whoring and exposed her nakedness, I turned from her in disgust, just as I had turned from her sister.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[19] Yet she multiplied her whoring, remembering the days of her youth, when she played the whore in the land of Egypt,
[Ezekiel] [23]:[20] and she lusted after her lovers there, whose members were like those of donkeys and whose seed like that of horses.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[21] So you longed again for the lewdness of your youth, when the Egyptians handled your breasts and fondled your young body.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[22] Therefore, Oholibah, this is what the Lord GOD says: I am about to rouse your lovers against you, the very ones you turned from in disgust, and I will bring them against you from every side—
[Ezekiel] [23]:[23] the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, the men of Pekod and Shoa and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them, handsome young men, governors and commanders, officers and men of rank, all of them riding on horses.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[24] They will come against you with weapons, chariots, and wagons, and with a horde of peoples. They will surround you with shield and buckler and helmet. I will hand the judgment over to them, and they will judge you by their own laws.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[25] I will turn my jealous anger against you, and they will deal with you in fury. They will cut off your nose and your ears, and those left of you will fall by the sword. They will take away your sons and daughters, and what remains of you will be consumed by fire.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[26] They will strip you of your clothes and take your beautiful jewels.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[27] So I will put an end to your lewdness and to the whoring you began in Egypt. You will not lift your eyes to them again or remember Egypt anymore.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[28] For this is what the Lord GOD says: I am handing you over to those you hate, to those you turned from in disgust.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[29] They will deal with you in hatred and take everything you have worked for, leaving you stripped and naked. Then the shame of your whoring will be exposed—your lewdness and your promiscuity.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[30] All this will come upon you because you played the whore after the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[31] You have walked in your sister's way, so I will put her cup into your hand.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[32] This is what the Lord GOD says: You will drink your sister's cup, deep and wide; it will bring scorn and ridicule, for it holds so much.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[33] You will be filled with drunkenness and grief—a cup of horror and desolation, the cup of your sister Samaria.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[34] You will drink it and drain it dry, gnaw its broken pieces, and tear your breasts. For I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[35] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you have forgotten me and thrust me behind your back, you must bear the weight of your lewdness and your whoring.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[36] The LORD said to me: Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then confront them with their abominations.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[37] For they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They committed adultery with their idols, and they even offered up the children they had borne to me as food for them.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[38] And this too they did to me: on that same day they defiled my sanctuary and profaned my Sabbaths.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[39] On the very day they slaughtered their children for their idols, they entered my sanctuary and profaned it. That is what they did inside my house.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[40] They even sent for men who came from far away. A messenger was sent to them, and they came. And for them you bathed, painted your eyes, and put on your jewelry.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[41] You sat on a stately couch with a table spread before it, and on that table you set my incense and my oil.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[42] The noise of a carefree crowd was around her—men out of the great throng, and drunkards* brought to them from the desert—and they put bracelets on the women's wrists and crowns of splendor on their heads. *Footnote: The written Hebrew text reads "drunkards"; the traditional reading tradition points the word as "Sabeans," a people from the desert regions.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[43] Then I said of the one worn out by adultery: Now they will keep using her as a whore, for that is what she is.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[44] Men went in to her as men go in to a prostitute. So they went in to Oholah and Oholibah, those lewd women.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[45] But righteous men will pass sentence on them—the sentence for adulteresses and for women who shed blood—because they are adulteresses and blood is on their hands.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[46] For this is what the Lord GOD says: Bring up an assembly against them and hand them over to terror and plunder.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[47] The assembly will stone them and cut them down with their swords. They will kill their sons and daughters and burn their houses down.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[48] So I will put an end to lewdness in the land, and all women will take warning and will not act as you have.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[49] You will be repaid for your lewdness and will bear the guilt of your idolatry. Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[1] In the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [24]:[2] Son of man, write down the name of this day, this very day. On this very day the king of Babylon has laid siege to Jerusalem.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[3] Now speak a parable to the rebellious house and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: Set on the pot, set it on, and pour water into it.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[4] Gather the pieces into it, every good piece, thigh and shoulder; fill it with the choicest bones.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[5] Take the choicest of the flock, and pile the wood beneath it. Bring it to a boil, and cook its bones inside it as well.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[6] Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the city of blood, the pot whose corrosion is in it, whose corrosion will not come off! Empty it piece by piece; no lot has fallen on it.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[7] For the blood she shed is still within her. She poured it on the bare rock; she did not pour it on the ground, to cover it with dust.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[8] To stir up wrath and take vengeance, I have set her blood on the bare rock, so that it would not be covered.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[9] Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the city of blood! I too will make the fire blaze high.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[10] Heap on the wood, kindle the fire, cook the meat thoroughly, mix in the spices, and let the bones be burned.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[11] Then set the pot empty on its coals, so that it grows hot and its copper glows, its filth melting away inside it, its corrosion consumed.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[12] It has frustrated every effort; its heavy corrosion will not come off—into the fire with its corrosion!
[Ezekiel] [24]:[13] Your uncleanness is depravity. Because I would have cleansed you and you were not cleansed of your filth, you shall not be clean again until I have satisfied my wrath on you.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[14] I, the LORD, have spoken. It is coming, and I will act. I will not hold back, I will not spare, I will not relent. According to your ways and your deeds they will judge you, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[15] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [24]:[16] Son of man, I am about to take from you the delight of your eyes with a single blow. Yet you shall not mourn or weep, and no tears shall come.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[17] Groan in silence; make no mourning for the dead. Keep your turban on your head and your sandals on your feet. Do not cover your lips, and do not eat the bread of mourners.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[18] So I spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening my wife died. And in the morning I did as I was commanded.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[19] Then the people said to me, "Will you not tell us what these things mean for us, that you are doing this?"
[Ezekiel] [24]:[20] I said to them: The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [24]:[21] Say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord GOD: I am about to profane my sanctuary, the pride of your strength, the delight of your eyes, the yearning of your soul. And the sons and daughters you left behind will fall by the sword.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[22] Then you will do as I have done: you will not cover your mustache or eat the bread of mourners.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[23] Your turbans will stay on your heads and your sandals on your feet. You will not mourn or weep, but you will waste away in your guilt and groan to one another.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[24] Ezekiel will be a sign for you; you will do everything he has done. When it comes, you will know that I am the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[25] And you, son of man—will it not be on the day I take from them their stronghold, the joy of their glory, the delight of their eyes and the longing of their souls, their sons and their daughters—
[Ezekiel] [24]:[26] on that day a fugitive will come to you to bring the news to your ears.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[27] On that day your mouth will be opened to the fugitive; you will speak and be silent no longer. So you will be a sign for them, and they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [25]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [25]:[2] Son of man, set your face against the Ammonites and prophesy against them.
[Ezekiel] [25]:[3] Say to the Ammonites: Hear the word of the Lord GOD. This is what the Lord GOD says: Because you gloated over my sanctuary when it was profaned, over the land of Israel when it was laid waste, and over the house of Judah when they went into exile,
[Ezekiel] [25]:[4] therefore I am handing you over to the people of the east as their possession. They will set up their camps among you and pitch their tents in your midst; they will eat your fruit and drink your milk.
[Ezekiel] [25]:[5] I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels and Ammon a resting place for sheep. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [25]:[6] For this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you clapped your hands and stamped your feet, rejoicing with all the malice of your heart against the land of Israel,
[Ezekiel] [25]:[7] therefore I am stretching out my hand against you. I will hand you over as plunder to the nations. I will cut you off from the peoples and wipe you out from the lands; I will destroy you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [25]:[8] This is what the Lord GOD says: Because Moab and Seir said, "Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations,"
[Ezekiel] [25]:[9] therefore I will lay open the flank of Moab, beginning with its frontier cities, the glory of the land: Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim.
[Ezekiel] [25]:[10] I will give it, along with Ammon, to the people of the east as a possession, so that Ammon will not be remembered among the nations.
[Ezekiel] [25]:[11] I will execute judgment on Moab, and they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [25]:[12] This is what the Lord GOD says: Because Edom took revenge on the house of Judah, and by so doing incurred grievous guilt and avenged itself upon them,
[Ezekiel] [25]:[13] therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I will stretch out my hand against Edom and cut off from it both man and beast. I will make it a wasteland; from Teman to Dedan they will fall by the sword.
[Ezekiel] [25]:[14] I will take my vengeance on Edom by the hand of my people Israel. They will deal with Edom according to my anger and my wrath, and Edom will know my vengeance, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [25]:[15] This is what the Lord GOD says: Because the Philistines acted in vengeance, taking revenge with malicious hearts, destroying out of ancient hatred,
[Ezekiel] [25]:[16] therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am stretching out my hand against the Philistines. I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy those who remain along the coast.
[Ezekiel] [25]:[17] I will execute great vengeance on them with furious rebukes, and they will know that I am the LORD when I take my vengeance on them.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[1] In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [26]:[2] Son of man, because Tyre said of Jerusalem, "Aha! The gateway of the peoples is shattered; it has swung open to me. Now that she lies in ruins, I will be filled,"
[Ezekiel] [26]:[3] therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Tyre. I will raise many nations against you, as the sea raises its waves.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[4] They will destroy the walls of Tyre and tear down her towers. I will scrape away her rubble and leave her a bare rock.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[5] Out in the sea she will become a place for spreading nets, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD. She will become plunder for the nations,
[Ezekiel] [26]:[6] and her daughter villages on the mainland will be put to the sword. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[7] For this is what the Lord GOD says: I am bringing against Tyre from the north Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, with horses and chariots, with horsemen and a vast army.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[8] He will put your daughter villages on the mainland to the sword. He will set up siegeworks against you, raise a ramp against you, and lift his shields against you.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[9] He will drive his battering rams against your walls and break down your towers with his iron tools.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[10] His horses will be so many that their dust will cover you. Your walls will shake at the noise of horsemen, wheels, and chariots when he enters your gates as men enter a city whose walls are breached.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[11] With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets. He will kill your people with the sword, and your mighty pillars will topple to the ground.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[12] They will plunder your wealth and loot your merchandise. They will break down your walls and demolish your fine houses, and they will throw your stones, your timber, and your rubble into the water.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[13] I will silence the noise of your songs, and the music of your harps will be heard no more.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[14] I will make you a bare rock; you will become a place for spreading nets. You will never be rebuilt, for I the LORD have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[15] This is what the Lord GOD says to Tyre: Will not the coastlands quake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and the slaughter rages within you?
[Ezekiel] [26]:[16] Then all the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones, lay aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments. Clothed in terror, they will sit on the ground, trembling every moment, appalled at you.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[17] They will raise this lament over you: "How you have perished, city of renown, peopled by seafarers! You and your citizens were a power on the sea, spreading your terror over all who lived there.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[18] Now the coastlands tremble on the day of your fall; the islands of the sea are terrified at your passing."
[Ezekiel] [26]:[19] For this is what the Lord GOD says: When I make you a desolate city, like cities no longer inhabited, when I bring the deep up over you and the vast waters cover you,
[Ezekiel] [26]:[20] then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of long ago. I will make you dwell in the earth below, among ancient ruins, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not return or take your place in the land of the living.[^1]
[Ezekiel] [26]:[21] I will bring you to a horrible end, and you will be no more. You will be sought, but you will never be found again, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [27]:[2] Son of man, raise a lament over Tyre.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[3] Say to Tyre, who sits at the gateways to the sea, merchant of the peoples to many coastlands: This is what the Lord GOD says: Tyre, you said, "I am perfect in beauty."
[Ezekiel] [27]:[4] Your borders lay in the heart of the sea; your builders made your beauty perfect.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[5] They built all your planking of cypress from Senir; they took a cedar from Lebanon to make your mast.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[6] They made your oars of oaks from Bashan; they made your deck of pine from the coasts of Cyprus, inlaid with ivory.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[7] Your sail was embroidered linen from Egypt, and it served as your banner; your awnings were blue and purple from the coasts of Elishah.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[8] Men of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; your own skilled men, Tyre, were aboard as your pilots.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[9] The elders of Gebal and its craftsmen were with you, caulking your seams. All the ships of the sea and their sailors came to you to trade for your wares.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[10] Persia, Lud, and Put served in your army as your fighting men. They hung their shields and helmets on your walls and gave you your splendor.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[11] The men of Arvad and your own troops manned your walls all around, and men of Gammad were in your towers. They hung their shields around your walls; they made your beauty complete.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[12] Tarshish traded with you because of your great wealth of goods; they exchanged silver, iron, tin, and lead for your merchandise.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[13] Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded with you; they exchanged slaves and articles of bronze for your goods.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[14] Men of Beth Togarmah exchanged horses, warhorses, and mules for your merchandise.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[15] The men of Dedan traded with you; many coastlands were your customers. They paid you with ivory tusks and ebony.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[16] Aram traded with you because of your many products; they exchanged turquoise, purple cloth, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies for your merchandise.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[17] Judah and the land of Israel traded with you; they exchanged wheat from Minnith, confections, honey, oil, and balm for your goods.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[18] Damascus traded with you because of your many products and your great wealth of goods; they brought wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[19] Vedan and Javan from Uzal traded for your merchandise; wrought iron, cassia, and cane were part of your trade.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[20] Dedan traded with you in saddle blankets.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[21] Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your customers; they traded with you in lambs, rams, and goats.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[22] The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded with you; they exchanged the finest of all spices, precious stones of every kind, and gold for your merchandise.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[23] Haran, Canneh, and Eden, the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad traded with you.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[24] They traded with you in fine garments, in blue cloth and embroidered work, and in carpets of many colors, bound with cords and tightly wound, in your marketplace.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[25] The ships of Tarshish carried your wares. You were filled with cargo, heavy laden in the heart of the seas.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[26] Your oarsmen brought you out into the deep waters, but the east wind shattered you in the heart of the sea.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[27] Your wealth, your merchandise, your wares, your sailors and pilots, those who caulked your seams and traded for your goods, all your fighting men on board and the whole company within you—they will sink into the heart of the sea on the day you fall.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[28] At the sound of your pilots' cry, the settlements on the mainland will tremble.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[29] All who handle the oar will abandon their ships; the sailors and all the pilots of the sea will stand on the shore.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[30] They will raise their voices over you and cry out bitterly; they will throw dust on their heads and roll in ashes.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[31] They will shave their heads because of you and put on sackcloth. They will weep over you in anguish of soul, with bitter mourning.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[32] In their wailing they will raise a lament for you and sing this dirge over you: "Who was ever silenced like Tyre, out in the midst of the sea?"
[Ezekiel] [27]:[33] When your wares went out over the seas, you satisfied many nations; with your great wealth and merchandise you enriched the kings of the earth.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[34] Now you are shattered by the sea in the depths of the waters; your goods and your whole company have gone down with you.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[35] All who live in the coastlands are appalled at you; their kings shudder with horror, their faces twisted in dismay.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[36] The merchants among the nations hiss at you; you have come to a horrible end and will be no more, forever.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [28]:[2] Son of man, say to the prince of Tyre: This is what the Lord GOD says: Because your heart is proud and you have said, "I am a god; I sit enthroned as a god in the heart of the seas"—yet you are a man and not a god, though you set your mind as if it were the mind of a god.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[3] Look, you are wiser than Daniel; no secret is too dark for you.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[4] By your wisdom and understanding you have made yourself rich, gathering gold and silver into your treasuries.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[5] By your great wisdom in your trading you increased your wealth, and your heart grew proud because of your wealth.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[6] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you set your mind as if it were the mind of a god,
[Ezekiel] [28]:[7] I am bringing strangers against you, the most ruthless of nations. They will draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom and defile your splendor.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[8] They will bring you down to the pit, and you will die a violent death in the heart of the seas.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[9] Will you still say, "I am a god," in the presence of those who kill you? Yet you are a man and not a god in the hands of those who wound you.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[10] You will die the death of the uncircumcised at the hands of strangers. For I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[11] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [28]:[12] Son of man, raise a lament over the king of Tyre and say to him: This is what the Lord GOD says: You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and flawless in beauty.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[13] You were in Eden, the garden of God. Every precious stone adorned you: carnelian, topaz, and diamond, beryl, onyx, and jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emerald, all set in gold. Your settings and mountings were prepared for you on the day you were created.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[14] You were an anointed guardian cherub, for so I appointed you. You were on God's holy mountain; you walked among the stones of fire.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[15] You were blameless in your ways from the day you were created, until wickedness was found in you.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[16] Through your widespread trade you were filled with violence, and you sinned. So I drove you in disgrace from the mountain of God, and I banished you, guardian cherub, from among the stones of fire.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[17] Your heart grew proud because of your beauty; you corrupted your wisdom for the sake of your splendor. So I threw you to the ground; I made a spectacle of you before kings.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[18] By your many sins and dishonest trade you desecrated your sanctuaries. So I brought fire out from within you, and it consumed you; I reduced you to ashes on the ground in the sight of all who watched.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[19] All who knew you among the peoples are appalled at you. You have come to a horrible end and will be no more forever.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[20] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [28]:[21] Son of man, set your face toward Sidon and prophesy against her.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[22] Say: This is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Sidon, and I will display my glory within you. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I execute judgments against her and show myself holy in her.
