[Ezekiel] [28]:[23] I will send plague upon her and blood into her streets. The slain will fall within her, cut down by the sword that comes against her from every side. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[24] No longer will the house of Israel have a malicious briar or a painful thorn from any of their neighbors who treat them with contempt. Then they will know that I am the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[25] This is what the Lord GOD says: When I gather the house of Israel from the peoples among whom they have been scattered, I will show myself holy through them in the sight of the nations. Then they will live in their own land, which I gave to my servant Jacob.
[Ezekiel] [28]:[26] They will live there in safety, build houses, and plant vineyards. They will live in safety when I execute judgments against all their neighbors who treat them with contempt. Then they will know that I am the LORD their God.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[1] In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [29]:[2] Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all of Egypt.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[3] Speak and say: Thus says the Lord GOD: Look, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, you great monster sprawling in the midst of your channels, who says, "The Nile is mine; I made it for myself."
[Ezekiel] [29]:[4] I will put hooks in your jaws and make the fish of your channels cling to your scales. I will haul you up out of your channels with all the fish of your channels clinging to your scales.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[5] I will fling you out into the wilderness, you and all the fish of your channels. You will fall on the open field and not be gathered or picked up. I give you as food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the sky.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[6] Then all who live in Egypt will know that I am the LORD, because they have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[7] When they grasped you in their hand, you splintered and tore up their shoulders; when they leaned on you, you broke and left their backs wrenched.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[8] Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I am bringing a sword against you, and I will cut off from you both man and beast.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[9] The land of Egypt will become a desolate ruin, and they will know that I am the LORD—because he said, "The Nile is mine, and I made it."
[Ezekiel] [29]:[10] Therefore I am against you and against your channels, and I will make the land of Egypt an utter waste and desolation, from Migdol to Syene, as far as the border of Cush.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[11] No human foot will pass through it, and no animal's foot will pass through it; it will be uninhabited for forty years.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[12] I will make the land of Egypt a desolation among desolate lands, and her cities will lie desolate for forty years among ruined cities. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[13] For thus says the Lord GOD: At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples where they were scattered.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[14] I will restore the fortunes of Egypt and bring them back to the land of Pathros, the land of their origin, and there they will be a lowly kingdom.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[15] It will be the lowliest of the kingdoms and will never again raise itself above the nations. I will make them so small that they will never again rule over the nations.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[16] Egypt will no longer be a source of confidence for the house of Israel, a reminder of their guilt whenever they turned to her for help. Then they will know that I am the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[17] In the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [29]:[18] Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has made his army labor hard against Tyre. Every head was rubbed bare and every shoulder chafed raw, yet neither he nor his army got any wages from Tyre for the labor he expended against it.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[19] Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: I am giving the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will carry off her wealth, seize her spoil, and take her plunder; that will be the wages for his army.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[20] As the payment for his labor, I have given him the land of Egypt, because they worked for me, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [29]:[21] On that day I will make a horn sprout for the house of Israel, and I will open your mouth among them. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [30]:[2] Son of man, prophesy and say: This is what the Lord GOD says: Wail—"Alas for the day!"
[Ezekiel] [30]:[3] For the day is near—the day of the LORD is near—a day of dark clouds, a time of doom for the nations.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[4] A sword will come against Egypt, and anguish will grip Cush. When the slain fall in Egypt, her hordes will be carried off and her foundations torn down.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[5] Cush, Put, and Lud, all the mixed peoples, Kub, and the sons of the land of the covenant will fall by the sword along with them.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[6] This is what the LORD says: Egypt's supporters will fall, and her proud strength will collapse. From Migdol to Syene they will fall by the sword within her, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[7] They will be made desolate among desolate lands, and her cities will lie among ruined cities.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[8] Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I set fire to Egypt and all who help her are shattered.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[9] On that day messengers will go out from me in ships to terrify Cush in her complacency. Anguish will seize them on the day of Egypt's doom—for it is surely coming.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[10] This is what the Lord GOD says: I will put an end to the hordes of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[11] He and his army with him, the most ruthless of nations, will be brought in to destroy the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[12] I will dry up the Nile channels and sell the land into the hands of evil men; by the hand of foreigners I will lay waste the land and everything in it. I, the LORD, have spoken.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[13] This is what the Lord GOD says: I will destroy the idols and put an end to the images in Memphis. No longer will there be a prince in the land of Egypt, and I will spread fear throughout the land.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[14] I will lay waste Pathros, set fire to Zoan, and execute judgment on Thebes.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[15] I will pour out my wrath on Pelusium, the stronghold of Egypt, and wipe out the hordes of Thebes.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[16] I will set fire to Egypt. Pelusium will writhe in agony, Thebes will be breached, and Memphis will face distress by day.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[17] The young men of Heliopolis and Bubastis will fall by the sword, and the women will go into captivity.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[18] At Tahpanhes the day will turn dark when I break the yoke of Egypt there, and her proud strength comes to an end. A cloud will cover her, and her daughters will go into captivity.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[19] So I will execute judgment on Egypt, and they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[20] In the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh day, the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [30]:[21] Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. It has not been bound up for healing or wrapped in a bandage to make it strong enough to grasp a sword.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[22] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will break both his arms, the strong one and the one already broken, and I will make the sword fall from his hand.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[23] I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[24] I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put my sword in his hand, but I will break the arms of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh will groan before him like a man mortally wounded.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[25] I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but the arms of Pharaoh will fall. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I put my sword in the hand of the king of Babylon and he stretches it out against the land of Egypt.
[Ezekiel] [30]:[26] I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[1] In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [31]:[2] Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his horde: Whom are you like in your greatness?
[Ezekiel] [31]:[3] Look at Assyria: a cedar in Lebanon, beautiful in its branches, shading the forest, towering high, its top among the clouds.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[4] The waters made it grow; the deep made it tower high, its rivers flowing around the place where it was planted, sending its streams to every tree of the field.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[5] So it rose higher than all the trees of the field. Its boughs multiplied, its branches spread long, because of the abundant water that fed it.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[6] All the birds of the sky nested in its boughs, all the wild animals gave birth beneath its branches, and all the many nations lived in its shade.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[7] It was beautiful in its greatness, in the length of its limbs, for its roots reached down to abundant water.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[8] The cedars in the garden of God could not rival it, the junipers could not match its boughs, the plane trees were nothing beside its branches. No tree in the garden of God compared with it in beauty.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[9] I made it beautiful with its mass of limbs, and all the trees of Eden, those in the garden of God, envied it.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[10] Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: Because it grew so tall, lifting its top among the clouds, and its heart grew proud of its height,
[Ezekiel] [31]:[11] I handed it over to the mightiest of the nations, who dealt with it as its wickedness deserved. I cast it out.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[12] Strangers, the most ruthless of nations, cut it down and left it lying. Its limbs fell on the mountains and in every valley; its branches lay broken in every ravine of the land. All the peoples of the earth went out from its shade and abandoned it.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[13] On its fallen trunk all the birds of the sky settle, and among its branches are all the wild animals.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[14] This happened so that no tree by the waters would grow proud of its height or lift its top among the clouds, and no well-watered tree would rise up against them in its height. For all of them are given over to death, to the earth below, among mortals, with those who go down to the pit.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[15] This is what the Lord GOD says: On the day it went down to the grave, I brought mourning; I covered the deep over it, I held back its rivers, and the abundant waters were stopped. I draped Lebanon in gloom for it, and all the trees of the field fainted because of it.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[16] I made the nations shudder at the sound of its fall, when I brought it down to the grave with those who go down to the pit. Then all the trees of Eden were consoled in the earth below—the choicest and best of Lebanon, all the well-watered trees.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[17] They too went down with it to the grave, to those slain by the sword—those who were its strength, who lived in its shade among the nations.
[Ezekiel] [31]:[18] Which of the trees of Eden was your equal in glory and greatness? Yet you will be brought down to the earth below with the trees of Eden; you will lie among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his horde, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[1] In the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [32]:[2] Son of man, raise a lament over Pharaoh king of Egypt and say to him: You thought yourself a lion among the nations, but you are like a monster in the seas. You thrashed about in your streams, muddied the water with your feet, and fouled their channels.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[3] Thus says the Lord GOD: I will spread my net over you before an assembly of many peoples, and they will haul you up in my dragnet.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[4] I will fling you down on the land, hurl you out on the open field. I will make every bird of the sky settle on you, and I will glut the beasts of the whole earth with you.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[5] I will strew your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your remains.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[6] I will drench the land with your flowing blood, all the way to the mountains, and the ravines will be filled with you.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[7] When you are snuffed out, I will cover the heavens and darken their stars. I will veil the sun with a cloud, and the moon will not give its light.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[8] All the shining lights of the heavens I will darken over you, and I will bring darkness upon your land, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[9] I will trouble the hearts of many peoples when I carry the news of your ruin among the nations, into lands you have never known.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[10] I will make many peoples appalled at you, and their kings will shudder with horror because of you when I brandish my sword before their faces. Again and again they will tremble, each for his own life, on the day of your downfall.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[11] For thus says the Lord GOD: The sword of the king of Babylon will come upon you.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[12] By the swords of warriors—the most ruthless of nations, all of them—I will bring down your hordes. They will ravage the pride of Egypt, and all her hordes will be destroyed.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[13] I will wipe out all her cattle beside the abundant waters. No human foot will stir them again, and no hoof of cattle will muddy them.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[14] Then I will let their waters settle and make their streams flow like oil, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[15] When I make the land of Egypt a desolation, a land stripped of all that filled it, when I strike down all who live in it, then they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[16] This is a lament, and it shall be chanted; the daughters of the nations shall chant it. Over Egypt and all her hordes they shall chant it, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[17] In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [32]:[18] Son of man, wail over the hordes of Egypt and send them down—her and the daughters of mighty nations—to the world below, to those who have gone down to the pit.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[19] Whom do you surpass in splendor? Go down and be laid among the uncircumcised!
[Ezekiel] [32]:[20] They will fall among those slain by the sword. The sword is drawn; she and all her hordes are dragged away.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[21] From the depths of Sheol the mighty chiefs will speak to him and his allies: They have come down; they lie there, the uncircumcised, slain by the sword.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[22] Assyria is there with all her company, her graves all around her—all of them slain, fallen by the sword.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[23] Her graves are set in the far reaches of the pit, and her company lies around her grave—all of them slain, fallen by the sword, they who once spread terror through the land of the living.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[24] Elam is there with all her hordes around her grave—all of them slain, fallen by the sword, who went down uncircumcised to the world below, who spread their terror through the land of the living and now bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[25] Among the slain they made her a bed with all her hordes, her graves all around her—all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword. Because their terror was spread through the land of the living, they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit; they are laid among the slain.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[26] Meshech and Tubal are there with all their hordes, their graves all around them—all of them uncircumcised, pierced by the sword, because they spread their terror through the land of the living.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[27] They do not lie with the warriors who fell in ages past, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, their swords laid beneath their heads and their guilt resting on their bones—for the terror of these warriors once filled the land of the living.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[28] And you too will be broken among the uncircumcised and will lie with those slain by the sword.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[29] Edom is there, her kings and all her princes, who for all their might are laid with those slain by the sword. They lie with the uncircumcised, with those who go down to the pit.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[30] There are the princes of the north, all of them, and all the Sidonians, who went down with the slain, disgraced for all the terror of their strength. They lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword and bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[31] Pharaoh will see them and be consoled over all his hordes—Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [32]:[32] For I spread my terror through the land of the living, and Pharaoh with all his hordes will be laid among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [33]:[2] Son of man, speak to your people and say to them: When I bring the sword against a land, and the people of that land choose one of their own and make him their watchman,
[Ezekiel] [33]:[3] and he sees the sword coming against the land and blows the trumpet to warn the people,
[Ezekiel] [33]:[4] then if anyone hears the sound of the trumpet and does not heed the warning, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood is on his own head.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[5] He heard the sound of the trumpet and paid no attention; his blood is on himself. Had he taken warning, he would have saved his life.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[6] But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the trumpet, so that the people are not warned, and the sword comes and takes one of them away, that man is taken away in his own guilt, but I will hold the watchman accountable for his blood.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[7] And you, son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, you shall warn them from me.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[8] If I say to the wicked, "You wicked one, you shall surely die," and you do not speak to warn the wicked to turn from his way, that wicked man will die in his guilt, but I will hold you accountable for his blood.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[9] But if you warn the wicked to turn from his way, and he does not turn from it, he will die in his guilt, but you will have saved your life.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[10] Son of man, say to the house of Israel: This is what you keep saying: "Our transgressions and our sins weigh us down, and we are wasting away because of them. How then can we live?"
[Ezekiel] [33]:[11] Say to them: As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked turn from his way and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why should you die, O house of Israel?
[Ezekiel] [33]:[12] And you, son of man, say to your people: The righteousness of the righteous will not save him on the day he transgresses, and the wickedness of the wicked will not bring him down on the day he turns from his wickedness. The righteous cannot live by his righteousness on the day he sins.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[13] If I say to the righteous, "You shall surely live," and he trusts in his own righteousness and does what is wrong, none of his righteous deeds will be remembered; he will die for the wrong he has done.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[14] And if I say to the wicked, "You shall surely die," and he turns from his sin and does what is just and right—
[Ezekiel] [33]:[15] if he returns what he took in pledge, repays what he stole, and walks in the statutes of life, doing no wrong—he shall surely live; he shall not die.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[16] None of the sins he has committed will be remembered against him. He has done what is just and right; he shall surely live.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[17] Yet your people say, "The way of the Lord is not just," when it is their own way that is not just.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[18] If a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does what is wrong, he will die for it.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[19] And if a wicked man turns from his wickedness and does what is just and right, he will live because of it.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[20] Yet you say, "The way of the Lord is not just." I will judge each of you according to his ways, O house of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[21] In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month, a fugitive from Jerusalem came to me and said, "The city has fallen."
[Ezekiel] [33]:[22] Now the hand of the LORD had been upon me the evening before the fugitive arrived, and he had opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning. So my mouth was opened, and I was no longer silent.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[23] Then the word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [33]:[24] Son of man, those living in these ruins in the land of Israel are saying, "Abraham was only one man, yet he took possession of the land. We are many; surely the land has been given to us as our possession."
[Ezekiel] [33]:[25] Therefore say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: You eat meat with the blood still in it, you lift up your eyes to your idols, and you shed blood—and you expect to possess the land?
[Ezekiel] [33]:[26] You rely on your swords, you commit abominations, and each of you defiles his neighbor's wife—and you expect to possess the land?
[Ezekiel] [33]:[27] Say this to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: As surely as I live, those who are in the ruins will fall by the sword; those out in the open field I will give to the wild animals to devour; and those in the strongholds and caves will die of plague.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[28] I will make the land a desolate waste, and her proud strength will come to an end. The mountains of Israel will lie desolate, with no one passing through.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[29] Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I have made the land a desolate waste because of all the abominations they have committed.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[30] As for you, son of man, your people are talking about you beside the walls and in the doorways of their houses, saying to one another, each to his brother, "Come and hear what word has come from the LORD."
[Ezekiel] [33]:[31] They come to you as people do, and they sit before you as my people and listen to your words—but they do not put them into practice. With their mouths they express devotion, but their hearts chase after unjust gain.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[32] To them you are nothing more than a singer of love songs with a beautiful voice who plays well on an instrument. They hear your words, but they do not act on them.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[33] When it comes—and come it will—then they will know that a prophet has been among them.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [34]:[2] Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Prophesy, and say to them, to the shepherds: Thus says the Lord GOD: Woe to the shepherds of Israel who have been feeding themselves! Should not shepherds feed the flock?
[Ezekiel] [34]:[3] You eat the fat, you clothe yourselves with the wool, you slaughter the fattened animals, but you do not feed the flock.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[4] You have not strengthened the weak, healed the sick, or bound up the injured. You have not brought back the strays or searched for the lost. Instead you have ruled them with force and harshness.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[5] So they were scattered for lack of a shepherd, and they became food for every wild animal. They were scattered,
[Ezekiel] [34]:[6] and my sheep wandered over all the mountains and every high hill. My sheep were scattered over the whole face of the earth, with no one to search or seek for them.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[7] Therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD:
[Ezekiel] [34]:[8] As I live, declares the Lord GOD, because my flock has become plunder and food for every wild animal, since there was no shepherd, and because my shepherds did not search for my flock but fed themselves instead of my flock—
[Ezekiel] [34]:[9] therefore, you shepherds, hear the word of the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[10] Thus says the Lord GOD: I am against the shepherds, and I will require my flock from their hand. I will stop them from tending the flock, and the shepherds will no longer tend them. I will rescue my sheep from their mouths, so that they will no longer be food for them.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[11] For thus says the Lord GOD: I myself will search for my sheep and look after them.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[12] As a shepherd looks after his flock when he is among his scattered sheep, so I will look after my sheep. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on a day of clouds and thick darkness.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[13] I will bring them out from the peoples and gather them from the countries, and I will bring them into their own land. I will pasture them on the mountains of Israel, by the ravines, and in all the inhabited places of the land.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[14] I will feed them in good pasture, and their grazing land will be on the high mountains of Israel. There they will lie down in good grazing land, and there they will feed in rich pasture on the mountains of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[15] I myself will tend my sheep, and I myself will make them lie down, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[16] I will search for the lost and bring back the strays. I will bind up the injured and strengthen the weak, but the fat and the strong I will destroy. I will shepherd them with justice.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[17] As for you, my flock, thus says the Lord GOD: I am going to judge between one sheep and another, between the rams and the goats.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[18] Is it not enough for you to feed on the good pasture? Must you also trample the rest of the pasture with your feet? Is it not enough for you to drink the clear water? Must you also muddy the rest with your feet?
[Ezekiel] [34]:[19] And must my flock feed on what your feet have trampled and drink what your feet have muddied?
[Ezekiel] [34]:[20] Therefore thus says the Lord GOD to them: I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[21] Because you shove with side and shoulder and butt all the weak ones with your horns until you have scattered them abroad,
[Ezekiel] [34]:[22] I will save my flock; they will no longer be plunder. And I will judge between one sheep and another.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[23] I will set over them one shepherd, my servant David, and he will tend them; he himself will feed them, and he will be their shepherd.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[24] I, the LORD, will be their God, and my servant David will be prince among them. I, the LORD, have spoken.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[25] I will make a covenant of peace with them and rid the land of wild beasts, so that they may live safely in the wilderness and sleep in the forests.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[26] I will make them and the places around my hill a blessing. I will send down the rain in its season; there will be showers of blessing.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[27] The trees of the field will yield their fruit, the ground will yield its produce, and they will live securely on their land. Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hand of those who enslaved them.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[28] They will no longer be plunder for the nations, nor will the wild animals devour them. They will live in safety, and no one will make them afraid.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[29] I will make for them a planting of renown, and they will no longer be consumed by famine in the land or bear the scorn of the nations.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[30] Then they will know that I, the LORD their God, am with them, and that they, the house of Israel, are my people, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[31] You are my sheep, the sheep of my pasture; you are only human, and I am your God, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [35]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [35]:[2] Son of man, set your face against Mount Seir and prophesy against it.
[Ezekiel] [35]:[3] Say to it: This is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Mount Seir. I will stretch out my hand against you and make you a desolate waste.
[Ezekiel] [35]:[4] I will turn your cities into ruins, and you will be desolate. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [35]:[5] Because you harbored a hatred that never ends and handed the Israelites over to the sword in the time of their disaster, at the time of their final punishment,
[Ezekiel] [35]:[6] therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will give you over to bloodshed, and bloodshed will pursue you. Since you did not hate bloodshed, bloodshed will pursue you.
[Ezekiel] [35]:[7] I will make Mount Seir a desolate waste and cut off from it all who come and go.
[Ezekiel] [35]:[8] I will fill its mountains with the slain; those killed by the sword will fall on your hills, in your valleys, and in all your ravines.
[Ezekiel] [35]:[9] I will make you a wasteland forever; your cities will not be inhabited. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [35]:[10] Because you said, "The two nations and the two lands will be mine, and we will take possession of them"—though the LORD was there—
[Ezekiel] [35]:[11] therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will deal with you according to the anger and jealousy you showed in your hatred of them, and I will make myself known among them when I judge you.
[Ezekiel] [35]:[12] Then you will know that I, the LORD, have heard every contemptuous word you spoke against the mountains of Israel, saying, "They are laid waste; they have been handed over to us to devour."
[Ezekiel] [35]:[13] You boasted against me with your mouth and multiplied your words against me. I heard it.
[Ezekiel] [35]:[14] This is what the Lord GOD says: While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate.
[Ezekiel] [35]:[15] Just as you rejoiced when the inheritance of the house of Israel was laid waste, so I will do to you. You will be desolate, Mount Seir, you and all Edom, every bit of it. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[1] And you, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel and say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[2] This is what the Lord GOD says: Because the enemy said of you, "Aha! The ancient heights have become ours to possess,"
[Ezekiel] [36]:[3] therefore prophesy and say: This is what the Lord GOD says: Because they made you desolate and swallowed you up from every side, so that you became the possession of the rest of the nations, and because you were made the object of gossip and slander among the people,
[Ezekiel] [36]:[4] therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD. This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys, to the desolate ruins and the abandoned cities that have become plunder and mockery to the rest of the nations all around.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[5] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Surely in the fire of my zeal I have spoken against the rest of the nations and against all of Edom, who with wholehearted joy and utter contempt claimed my land as their own possession, to plunder its pastureland.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[6] Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel and say to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys: This is what the Lord GOD says: See, I have spoken in my zeal and my wrath, because you have borne the insults of the nations.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[7] Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I have raised my hand and sworn that the nations around you shall themselves bear their own disgrace.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[8] But you, mountains of Israel, will put out your branches and yield your fruit for my people Israel, for they are soon to come home.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[9] For I am for you; I will turn toward you, and you will be tilled and sown.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[10] I will multiply people upon you, the whole house of Israel, all of it. The cities will be inhabited and the ruins rebuilt.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[11] I will multiply people and animals upon you; they will increase and be fruitful. I will settle you as you were before and will do you more good than at the beginning. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[12] I will cause people to walk upon you—my people Israel. They will possess you, and you will be their inheritance; never again will you rob them of their children.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[13] This is what the Lord GOD says: Because people say to you, "You devour human beings and rob your own nation of its children,"
[Ezekiel] [36]:[14] therefore you will devour people no more and never again bereave your nation of its children, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[15] I will not let you hear the insults of the nations any longer; you will no longer bear the scorn of the peoples, and you will never again cause your nation to stumble, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[16] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [36]:[17] Son of man, when the house of Israel lived in their own land, they defiled it by their ways and their deeds. Their conduct before me was like the uncleanness of a woman in her impurity.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[18] So I poured out my wrath on them because of the blood they had shed on the land and because they had defiled it with their idols.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[19] I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the lands. I judged them according to their ways and their deeds.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[20] But when they came among the nations, wherever they went, they profaned my holy name, for it was said of them, "These are the LORD's people, yet they had to leave his land."
[Ezekiel] [36]:[21] So I had concern for my holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations where they had gone.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[22] Therefore say to the house of Israel: This is what the Lord GOD says: It is not for your sake that I am about to act, house of Israel, but for the sake of my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations where you have gone.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[23] I will vindicate the holiness of my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, which you profaned in their midst. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Lord GOD, when I show myself holy through you before their eyes.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[24] I will take you from the nations and gather you out of all the lands, and I will bring you into your own land.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[25] I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean; I will cleanse you from all your impurities and from all your idols.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[26] I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you. I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[27] I will put my Spirit within you and cause you to walk in my statutes and to keep my ordinances and do them.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[28] You will live in the land I gave your fathers; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[29] I will save you from all your uncleanness. I will summon the grain and make it plentiful, and I will not bring famine upon you.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[30] I will make the fruit of the trees and the produce of the field abundant, so that you will never again suffer the disgrace of famine among the nations.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[31] Then you will remember your evil ways and your wicked deeds, and you will loathe yourselves for your sins and your abominations.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[32] It is not for your sake that I am acting, declares the Lord GOD—know this well. Be ashamed and humiliated because of your ways, house of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[33] This is what the Lord GOD says: On the day I cleanse you from all your sins, I will resettle the cities, and the ruins will be rebuilt.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[34] The desolate land will be cultivated again, in place of the wasteland it once was before the eyes of all who passed by.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[35] They will say, "This land that lay desolate has become like the garden of Eden, and the cities that were ruined, wasted, and torn down are now fortified and inhabited."
[Ezekiel] [36]:[36] Then the nations that remain around you will know that I, the LORD, have rebuilt what was torn down and replanted what was desolate. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[37] This is what the Lord GOD says: Once again I will let myself be sought by the house of Israel, and this I will do for them: I will multiply them like a flock — a flock of people.
[Ezekiel] [36]:[38] Like the flocks set apart for sacrifice, like the flocks in Jerusalem at her appointed feasts, so the ruined cities will be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[1] The hand of the LORD came upon me, and he brought me out by the Spirit of the LORD and set me down in the middle of the valley; and it was full of bones.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[2] He led me all around them, and I saw that there were very many of them on the floor of the valley, and they were very dry.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[3] He said to me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" And I answered, "O Lord GOD, you know."
[Ezekiel] [37]:[4] Then he said to me, "Prophesy over these bones and say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the LORD!
[Ezekiel] [37]:[5] Thus says the Lord GOD to these bones: I am going to put breath in you, and you will live.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[6] I will fasten sinews on you, make flesh grow over you, cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and you will live. Then you will know that I am the LORD."
[Ezekiel] [37]:[7] So I prophesied as I was commanded. And as I prophesied there was a sound, a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to bone.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[8] I looked, and there were sinews on them; flesh had grown, and skin had covered them over. But there was no breath in them.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[9] Then he said to me, "Prophesy to the breath. Prophesy, son of man, and say to the breath: Thus says the Lord GOD: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe into these slain, that they may live."
[Ezekiel] [37]:[10] So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them. They came to life and stood on their feet—an army, vast beyond measure.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[11] Then he said to me, "Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. See how they say, 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is gone; we are cut off.'
[Ezekiel] [37]:[12] Therefore prophesy and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: I am going to open your graves and bring you up out of them, my people, and I will bring you home to the land of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[13] And you will know that I am the LORD, when I open your graves and bring you up out of them, my people.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[14] I will put my Spirit in you, and you will live; and I will settle you in your own land. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken and have done it, declares the LORD."
[Ezekiel] [37]:[15] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [37]:[16] "Son of man, take a stick and write on it, 'For Judah and the Israelites associated with him.' Then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph—the stick of Ephraim—and all the house of Israel associated with him.'
[Ezekiel] [37]:[17] Join them together, one to the other, into a single stick, so that they become one in your hand.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[18] And when your people ask you, 'Won't you tell us what you mean by this?'
[Ezekiel] [37]:[19] say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which is in Ephraim's hand, together with the tribes of Israel associated with him, and I will join them to the stick of Judah, making them one stick, so that they become one in my hand.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[20] Hold the sticks on which you have written where they can see them,
[Ezekiel] [37]:[21] and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: I am going to take the Israelites out of the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from every side and bring them into their own land.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[22] I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king will rule over all of them. Never again will they be two nations or be divided into two kingdoms.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[23] They will no longer defile themselves with their idols and detestable images and all their transgressions. I will save them from all the places where they have sinned, and I will cleanse them. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[24] My servant David will be king over them, and they will all have one shepherd. They will follow my judgments and keep my statutes and carry them out.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[25] They will live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob, where your fathers lived. They and their children and their children's children will live there forever, and David my servant will be their prince forever.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[26] I will make a covenant of peace with them, an everlasting covenant. I will establish them and multiply them, and I will set my sanctuary among them forever.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[27] My dwelling place will be with them; I will be their God, and they will be my people.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[28] Then the nations will know that I, the LORD, make Israel holy, when my sanctuary stands among them forever."
[Ezekiel] [38]:[1] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Ezekiel] [38]:[2] Son of man, set your face against Gog, of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[3] Say: This is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[4] I will turn you around, put hooks in your jaws, and bring you out with your whole army—horses and horsemen, all of them splendidly clothed, a vast company with shields large and small, every one of them wielding a sword.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[5] Persia, Cush, and Put are with them, all with shield and helmet;
[Ezekiel] [38]:[6] Gomer with all its troops, and Beth Togarmah from the far north with all its troops—many peoples are with you.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[7] Be ready; prepare yourself, you and all the hordes gathered around you, and take command of them.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[8] After many days you will be summoned. In the latter years you will invade a land that has recovered from war, whose people were gathered from many nations to the mountains of Israel, long left in ruins. They were brought out from the nations, and now all of them live in safety.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[9] You will advance, coming on like a storm; you will be like a cloud covering the land—you and all your troops, and many peoples with you.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[10] This is what the Lord GOD says: On that day thoughts will arise in your heart, and you will devise an evil scheme.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[11] You will say, "I will march against a land of unwalled villages; I will attack a peaceful people who live in safety—all of them living without walls, without bars or gates—
[Ezekiel] [38]:[12] to seize spoil and carry off plunder, to turn my hand against the ruins now inhabited and against a people gathered from the nations, rich in livestock and goods, living at the center of the earth."
[Ezekiel] [38]:[13] Sheba and Dedan, the merchants of Tarshish and all its leaders will say to you, "Have you come to seize spoil? Have you gathered your horde to carry off plunder, to make off with silver and gold, to take livestock and goods, to seize great spoil?"
[Ezekiel] [38]:[14] Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog: This is what the Lord GOD says: On that day, when my people Israel are living in safety, will you not take notice?
[Ezekiel] [38]:[15] You will come from your place in the far north, you and many peoples with you, all of them riding horses, a great horde, a mighty army.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[16] You will advance against my people Israel like a cloud covering the land. In the latter days it will happen: I will bring you against my land, so that the nations may know me, when through you, Gog, I show myself holy before their eyes.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[17] This is what the Lord GOD says: Are you not the one I spoke of in days long past through my servants the prophets of Israel? For years they prophesied in those days that I would bring you against them.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[18] On that day, when Gog comes against the land of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, my hot anger will flare up.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[19] In my zeal and my burning fury I have spoken: Surely on that day there will be a great earthquake in the land of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[20] The fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the beasts of the field, every creature that crawls on the ground, and every human being on the face of the earth will tremble before me. The mountains will be torn down, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will fall to the ground.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[21] I will summon the sword against him on all my mountains, declares the Lord GOD, and every man's sword will be against his brother.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[22] I will execute judgment on him with plague and bloodshed; I will pour down torrents of rain, hailstones, fire, and sulfur on him and on his troops and on the many peoples with him.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[23] So I will show my greatness and my holiness, and make myself known in the sight of many nations. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[1] And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog and say: Thus says the Lord GOD: I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[2] I will turn you around and drive you on, bring you up from the far reaches of the north and lead you against the mountains of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[3] Then I will strike the bow from your left hand and make the arrows fall from your right.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[4] On the mountains of Israel you will fall, you and all your troops and the peoples with you. I will give you as food to every kind of bird of prey and to the wild animals.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[5] You will fall in the open field, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[6] I will send fire on Magog and on those who live in safety along the coasts, and they will know that I am the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[7] I will make my holy name known among my people Israel, and I will no longer let my holy name be profaned. Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, the Holy One in Israel.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[8] It is coming, and it will be done, declares the Lord GOD. This is the day of which I have spoken.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[9] Then those who live in the cities of Israel will go out and make fires with the weapons—the small shields and the large, the bows and arrows, the clubs and spears—and they will burn them as fuel for seven years.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[10] They will not gather wood from the fields or cut it from the forests, for they will make their fires with the weapons. They will plunder those who plundered them and loot those who looted them, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[11] On that day I will give Gog a burial place in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers, east of the Sea. It will block the way of those who pass by, for there Gog and all his horde will be buried, and it will be called the Valley of Gog's Horde.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[12] For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them in order to cleanse the land.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[13] All the people of the land will bury them, and it will bring them renown on the day I display my glory, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[14] Men will be set apart for this continual task: to go through the land and bury those who passed through, the bodies left lying on the ground, so as to cleanse it. At the end of the seven months they will make a search.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[15] As they go through the land, whenever one of them sees a human bone, he will set up a marker beside it until the gravediggers have buried it in the Valley of Gog's Horde.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[16] And a city called Hamonah will be there as well. So they will cleanse the land.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[17] And you, son of man, thus says the Lord GOD: Say to every kind of bird and to every wild animal: Gather and come, assemble from every side for the sacrifice I am preparing for you, a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel. There you will eat flesh and drink blood.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[18] You will eat the flesh of warriors and drink the blood of the princes of the earth as though they were rams and lambs, goats and bulls—all of them fattened animals of Bashan.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[19] At the sacrifice I am preparing for you, you will eat fat until you are glutted and drink blood until you are drunk.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[20] At my table you will eat your fill of horses and charioteers, of warriors and fighting men of every kind, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[21] I will display my glory among the nations, and all the nations will see the judgment I execute and the hand I lay upon them.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[22] From that day forward the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[23] And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile for their guilt, because they were unfaithful to me. So I hid my face from them and handed them over to their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[24] I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and their transgressions, and I hid my face from them.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[25] Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and I will be jealous for my holy name.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[26] They will forget their disgrace and all the unfaithfulness they showed toward me, when they live in safety in their own land with no one to make them afraid. [Footnote: Or "they will bear their disgrace"; the Hebrew verb can be read either way.]
[Ezekiel] [39]:[27] When I bring them back from the peoples and gather them from the lands of their enemies, I will show myself holy through them in the sight of many nations.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[28] Then they will know that I am the LORD their God, for though I sent them into exile among the nations, I gathered them again to their own land and left none of them behind.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[29] I will no longer hide my face from them, for I will pour out my Spirit on the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[1] In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck down—on that very day the hand of the LORD came upon me, and he brought me there.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[2] In visions of God he brought me to the land of Israel and set me down on a very high mountain, and on it, to the south, there was what looked like the structure of a city.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[3] He brought me there, and there stood a man whose appearance was like bronze. In his hand were a linen cord and a measuring rod, and he was standing in the gateway.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[4] The man said to me, "Son of man, look with your eyes and listen with your ears, and fix your mind on everything I show you, for you have been brought here so that it may be shown to you. Tell the house of Israel all that you see."
[Ezekiel] [40]:[5] And there was a wall surrounding the temple area on the outside. In the man's hand was a measuring rod six cubits long, each cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth. He measured the thickness of the wall: one rod; and its height: one rod.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[6] Then he went to the gate that faces east and climbed its steps. He measured the threshold of the gate: one rod deep; and the other threshold: one rod deep.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[7] Each guardroom was one rod long and one rod wide, and between the guardrooms was a span of five cubits. The threshold of the gate, next to the vestibule of the gate on the inner side, was one rod.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[8] He measured the vestibule of the gate on the inner side: one rod.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[9] Then he measured the vestibule of the gate: eight cubits; and its jambs: two cubits. The vestibule of the gate was at the inner end.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[10] The guardrooms of the east gate were three on one side and three on the other, all three of the same measure; and the jambs on either side had the same measure.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[11] He measured the width of the gate's entrance: ten cubits; and the length of the gateway: thirteen cubits.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[12] In front of the guardrooms was a barrier one cubit high on one side and a barrier one cubit high on the other, and each guardroom was six cubits on one side and six cubits on the other.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[13] Then he measured the gateway from the roof of one guardroom to the roof of the opposite one: twenty-five cubits wide, doorway facing doorway.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[14] He made the jambs sixty cubits high, and the court reached to the jambs all around the gateway.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[15] From the front of the outer entrance of the gate to the front of the vestibule of the inner gate was fifty cubits.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[16] The guardrooms and their jambs had recessed windows all around the inside of the gateway, and so did the vestibules. There were windows all around on the inside, and palm trees were carved on the jambs.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[17] Then he brought me into the outer court, and there were chambers and a pavement laid out all around the court; thirty chambers faced the pavement.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[18] The pavement ran alongside the gateways, corresponding to their length; this was the lower pavement.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[19] He measured the distance from the front of the lower gate to the outer front of the inner court: a hundred cubits, on the east and on the north.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[20] He also measured the length and width of the gate of the outer court that faces north.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[21] Its guardrooms were three on one side and three on the other, and its jambs and its porch had the same measurements as the first gate: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[22] Its windows, its porch, and its palm trees had the same measurements as those of the gate facing east. Seven steps led up to it, and its porch was at the inner end.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[23] Opposite the north gate, as with the east gate, there was a gate to the inner court; he measured from gate to gate: a hundred cubits.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[24] Then he led me toward the south, and there was a gate facing south. He measured its jambs and its porch; they had the same measurements as the others.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[25] It and its porch had windows all around, like the other windows: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[26] Seven steps led up to it, and its porch was at the inner end; it had palm trees on its jambs, one on each side.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[27] The inner court also had a gate facing south, and he measured from gate to gate toward the south: a hundred cubits.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[28] Then he brought me into the inner court through the south gate, and he measured the south gate; it had the same measurements as the others.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[29] Its guardrooms, its jambs, and its porch had the same measurements, and it and its porch had windows all around: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[30] There were porches all around, twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[31] Its porch faced the outer court, and palm trees were carved on its jambs; eight steps led up to it.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[32] Then he brought me to the inner court on the east side, and he measured the gate; it had the same measurements as the others.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[33] Its guardrooms, its jambs, and its vestibule had the same measurements, and it and its vestibule had windows all around: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[34] Its porch faced the outer court, and palm trees were carved on its jambs, on both sides; eight steps led up to it.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[35] Then he brought me to the north gate and measured it; it had the same measurements as the others,
[Ezekiel] [40]:[36] with its guardrooms, its jambs, and its porch, and it had windows all around: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[37] Its vestibule faced the outer court, and palm trees were carved on its jambs, on both sides; eight steps led up to it.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[38] There was a chamber with its doorway by the jambs of the gateways; there the burnt offering was rinsed.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[39] In the vestibule of the gateway there were two tables on one side and two tables on the other, on which the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering were slaughtered.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[40] Outside, on the side wall as one goes up to the entrance of the north gateway, were two tables; and on the other side wall, by the vestibule of the gateway, were two more tables.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[41] So there were four tables on one side of the gateway and four tables on the other—eight tables in all, on which the sacrifices were slaughtered.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[42] There were also four tables of dressed stone for the burnt offering, each a cubit and a half long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit high; on them were laid the instruments used to slaughter the burnt offering and the other sacrifices.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[43] Double hooks, a handbreadth long, were fastened all around inside, and the flesh of the offering was laid on the tables.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[44] Outside the inner gate, in the inner court, were chambers for the singers: one beside the north gate, facing south, and one beside the east gate, facing north.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[45] He said to me, "This chamber that faces south is for the priests who keep charge of the temple,
[Ezekiel] [40]:[46] and the chamber that faces north is for the priests who keep charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who alone of the sons of Levi may draw near to the LORD to serve him."
[Ezekiel] [40]:[47] Then he measured the court: a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide, a perfect square; and the altar stood in front of the temple.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[48] He brought me to the vestibule of the temple and measured the jambs of the vestibule: five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other; and the width of the gateway was three cubits on one side and three cubits on the other.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[49] The vestibule was twenty cubits long and eleven cubits wide, and it was reached by steps; and there were pillars by the jambs, one on each side.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[1] Then he brought me to the nave and measured the pilasters: six cubits wide on one side and six cubits wide on the other — the width of the tent.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[2] The entrance was ten cubits wide, and the walls flanking the entrance were five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other. He measured the length of the nave: forty cubits, and its width: twenty cubits.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[3] Then he went farther in and measured the pilaster of the doorway: two cubits; the doorway itself: six cubits; and the width of the doorway: seven cubits.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[4] He measured its length: twenty cubits, and its width: twenty cubits, across from the nave. And he said to me, "This is the Most Holy Place."
[Ezekiel] [41]:[5] Then he measured the wall of the temple: six cubits thick. The width of each side chamber all around the temple was four cubits.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[6] The side chambers were arranged one above another, three tiers with thirty chambers in each. There were ledges in the temple wall all around, on which the side chambers rested, so they were not fastened into the wall of the temple itself.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[7] The side chambers grew wider as they rose from story to story, because the surrounding structure of the temple ascended stage by stage all around it; therefore the width of the building increased as it went up. So one climbed from the lowest story to the highest by way of the middle one.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[8] I also saw that the temple had a raised platform all around it, the foundations of the side chambers: a full rod, six long cubits.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[9] The outer wall of the side chambers was five cubits thick. The open area between the side chambers of the temple
[Ezekiel] [41]:[10] and the outer chambers was twenty cubits wide, all around the temple on every side.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[11] The side chambers opened onto the open area: one entrance on the north and one on the south. The open area was five cubits wide all around.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[12] The building facing the restricted area on the west side was seventy cubits wide; the wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[13] Then he measured the temple: a hundred cubits long. The courtyard, together with the building and its walls, was also a hundred cubits long.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[14] The width of the temple front, including the courtyard on the east, was a hundred cubits.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[15] He measured the length of the building facing the courtyard at the rear of the temple, along with its galleries on either side: a hundred cubits. He measured the inner nave and the vestibules of the court,
[Ezekiel] [41]:[16] the thresholds, the recessed windows, and the galleries all around the three of them. From the threshold up, everything was paneled with wood all around, and from the floor to the windows — the windows being covered —
[Ezekiel] [41]:[17] The paneling reached above the entrance, as far as the inner room, and outside as well. On every wall all around, inside and out, there were carvings by measure:
[Ezekiel] [41]:[18] cherubim and palm trees, a palm tree between each pair of cherubim. Each cherub had two faces:
[Ezekiel] [41]:[19] the face of a man toward the palm tree on one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other. They were carved throughout the temple, all around.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[20] From the floor to the space above the entrance, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the nave.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[21] The doorposts of the nave were square. In front of the sanctuary stood something that looked like
[Ezekiel] [41]:[22] an altar of wood, three cubits high and two cubits long, with its corners, its base, and its sides all of wood.* And he said to me, "This is the table that stands before the LORD." [*Footnote: The Hebrew here reads "its length and its walls were wood"; "its base" follows the ancient Greek reading.]
[Ezekiel] [41]:[23] The nave and the sanctuary each had a double door,
[Ezekiel] [41]:[24] and each door had two swinging leaves — two leaves for the one door and two for the other.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[25] On the doors of the nave were carved cherubim and palm trees, like those carved on the walls. And there was a wooden canopy over the front of the vestibule, on the outside.
[Ezekiel] [41]:[26] There were recessed windows and palm trees on either side, on the sidewalls of the vestibule; and so also on the side chambers of the temple and on the canopies.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[1] Then he led me out to the outer court, toward the north, and brought me to the chambers that face the open area and the building on the north side.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[2] Along the north side its length was a hundred cubits, where the entrance was, and its width fifty cubits.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[3] Opposite the twenty cubits belonging to the inner court, and facing the pavement of the outer court, there was gallery upon gallery in three tiers.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[4] In front of the chambers ran a walkway ten cubits wide, leading inward by a passage one cubit wide, and their entrances faced north.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[5] The upper chambers were shorter, because the galleries took space from them, more than from the lower and middle stories of the building.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[6] For they were in three tiers and had no pillars like the pillars of the courts; therefore the upper chambers were set back from the ground more than the lower and middle ones.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[7] There was an outer wall running alongside the chambers, toward the outer court, in front of the chambers; its length was fifty cubits.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[8] For the chambers on the outer court were fifty cubits long, while those facing the temple were a hundred cubits.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[9] Below these chambers was the entryway from the east, where one enters them from the outer court.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[10] Along the thickness of the wall of the court toward the east, facing the open area and the building, there were chambers,
[Ezekiel] [42]:[11] with a walkway in front of them. They looked like the chambers on the north side: the same length and width, the same exits, the same arrangements, and the same doorways.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[12] Like the doorways of the chambers on the south, there was a doorway at the head of the walkway—the walkway in front of the corresponding wall—on the east side, where one enters them.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[13] Then he said to me, "The north chambers and the south chambers that face the open area are the holy chambers, where the priests who draw near to the LORD shall eat the most holy offerings. There they shall lay the most holy offerings—the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering—for the place is holy.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[14] When the priests enter, they shall not go out from the holy place into the outer court without leaving there the garments in which they minister, for these are holy. They shall put on other garments before approaching the area open to the people."
[Ezekiel] [42]:[15] When he had finished measuring the interior of the temple area, he led me out by the gate that faces east and measured the whole area all around.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[16] He measured the east side with the measuring rod: five hundred rods by the measuring rod.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[17] He measured the north side: five hundred rods by the measuring rod.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[18] He measured the south side: five hundred rods by the measuring rod.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[19] Then he turned to the west side and measured five hundred rods by the measuring rod.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[20] So he measured it on all four sides. It had a wall all around it, five hundred rods long and five hundred wide, to separate the holy from the common.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[1] Then he brought me to the gate, the gate facing east.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[2] And there was the glory of the God of Israel, coming from the east. His voice was like the roar of mighty waters, and the earth shone with his glory.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[3] The appearance of the vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when I came to destroy the city, and the visions were like the vision I had seen by the Kebar River. And I fell on my face.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[4] Then the glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate that faces east.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[5] The Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and there the glory of the LORD filled the temple.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[6] I heard someone speaking to me out of the temple, while the man stood beside me.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[7] He said to me: Son of man, this is the place of my throne and the place for the soles of my feet, where I will dwell among the people of Israel forever. The house of Israel shall no longer defile my holy name—neither they nor their kings—by their whoring and by the corpses of their kings at their death,
[Ezekiel] [43]:[8] setting their threshold next to my threshold and their doorposts beside my doorposts, with only a wall between me and them. They defiled my holy name by the detestable things they did, and so I consumed them in my anger.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[9] Now let them put away their whoring and the corpses of their kings far from me, and I will dwell among them forever.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[10] You, son of man, describe the temple to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their sins. Let them measure its design,
[Ezekiel] [43]:[11] and if they are ashamed of all they have done, make known to them the form of the temple and its arrangement, its exits and its entrances—its whole design—along with all its statutes, all its forms, and all its laws. Write them down before their eyes, so that they may keep its whole design and all its statutes and carry them out.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[12] This is the law of the temple: on the top of the mountain, its entire area all around shall be most holy. This is the law of the temple.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[13] These are the measurements of the altar in cubits, each cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth: its base shall be a cubit high and a cubit wide, with a rim of a span around its edge. This shall be the base of the altar.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[14] From the base on the ground to the lower ledge is two cubits, with a width of one cubit; and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge is four cubits, with a width of a cubit.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[15] The altar hearth shall be four cubits high, and four horns shall project upward from the hearth.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[16] The altar hearth shall be square, twelve cubits long by twelve cubits wide, on all four sides.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[17] The ledge shall be fourteen cubits long by fourteen cubits wide on all four sides, with a rim of half a cubit around it and a base of one cubit all around; and its steps shall face east.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[18] Then he said to me: Son of man, thus says the Lord GOD: These are the statutes for the altar on the day it is built, for offering burnt offerings on it and for sprinkling blood on it.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[19] You shall give a young bull for a sin offering to the Levitical priests who are of the offspring of Zadok, who draw near to me to minister to me, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[20] You shall take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge, and on the rim all around; so you shall cleanse the altar and make atonement for it.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[21] Then you shall take the bull of the sin offering and burn it in the appointed place of the temple, outside the sanctuary.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[22] On the second day you shall offer a male goat without blemish for a sin offering, and the altar shall be cleansed as it was cleansed with the bull.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[23] When you have finished cleansing it, you shall offer a young bull without blemish and a ram from the flock without blemish.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[24] You shall present them before the LORD, and the priests shall throw salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[25] For seven days you shall provide a goat daily for a sin offering; they shall also provide a young bull and a ram from the flock, both without blemish.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[26] For seven days they shall make atonement for the altar and purify it; so they shall consecrate it.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[27] When they have completed these days, then from the eighth day onward the priests shall offer your burnt offerings and your peace offerings on the altar, and I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[1] Then he brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east, and it was shut.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[2] And the LORD said to me: This gate shall remain shut. It shall not be opened, and no one shall enter through it, for the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it. Therefore it shall remain shut.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[3] Only the prince, because he is the prince, may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD. He shall enter by way of the gate's vestibule and go out the same way.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[4] Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the temple. I looked, and there was the glory of the LORD filling the house of the LORD, and I fell on my face.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[5] And the LORD said to me: Son of man, mark well, look with your eyes and listen with your ears to everything I tell you concerning all the statutes of the house of the LORD and all its laws. Mark well the entrance of the temple and all the exits of the sanctuary.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[6] Say to the rebellious house of Israel: This is what the Lord GOD says: Enough of all your abominations, house of Israel!
[Ezekiel] [44]:[7] You brought in foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary, profaning my house, while you offered my food—the fat and the blood. So you broke my covenant with all your abominations.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[8] You did not keep charge of my holy things, but appointed others to keep charge of my sanctuary for you.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[9] This is what the Lord GOD says: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter my sanctuary—none of the foreigners who live among the people of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[10] But the Levites who went far from me when Israel went astray, wandering from me after their idols, shall bear their guilt.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[11] They shall serve in my sanctuary as guards at the gates of the temple and as servants in the temple. They shall slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they shall stand before them to serve them.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[12] Because they served them before their idols and became a stumbling block of guilt to the house of Israel, therefore I have raised my hand against them, declares the Lord GOD, and they shall bear their guilt.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[13] They shall not come near me to serve me as priests, nor come near any of my holy things or the most holy things. They shall bear their disgrace and the abominations they committed.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[14] Yet I will appoint them to keep charge of the temple, to do all its work and everything that must be done in it.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[15] But the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept charge of my sanctuary when the people of Israel went astray from me—they shall come near me to serve me. They shall stand before me to offer me the fat and the blood, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[16] They shall enter my sanctuary, and they shall come near my table to serve me, and they shall keep my charge.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[17] When they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall wear linen garments. No wool shall be on them while they minister at the gates of the inner court and inside.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[18] Linen turbans shall be on their heads and linen undergarments around their waists. They shall not wear anything that makes them sweat.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[19] When they go out to the outer court, to the people, they shall take off the garments in which they ministered and leave them in the holy chambers. They shall put on other garments, so that they do not transmit holiness to the people with their garments.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[20] They shall not shave their heads or let their hair grow long; they shall keep the hair of their heads trimmed.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[21] No priest shall drink wine when he enters the inner court.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[22] They shall not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but only virgins of the offspring of the house of Israel, or a widow who is the widow of a priest.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[23] They shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and show them how to distinguish between the unclean and the clean.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[24] In a dispute they shall serve as judges, and they shall judge it according to my ordinances. They shall keep my laws and my statutes at all my appointed feasts, and they shall keep my Sabbaths holy.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[25] They shall not go near a dead person and defile themselves; only for father or mother, son or daughter, brother or unmarried sister may they defile themselves.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[26] After he has been cleansed, they shall count seven days for him.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[27] And on the day he enters the sanctuary, into the inner court, to minister in the sanctuary, he shall offer his sin offering, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[28] This shall be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. You shall give them no possession in Israel; I am their possession.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[29] They shall eat the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, and every devoted thing in Israel shall be theirs.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[30] The best of all the firstfruits of everything, and every contribution of every kind from all your contributions, shall belong to the priests. You shall also give the priest the first of your dough, so that a blessing may rest on your house.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[31] The priests shall not eat anything, bird or animal, that has died of itself or been torn by beasts.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[1] When you divide the land by lot as an inheritance, you shall set apart a portion for the LORD as a holy district out of the land: twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew does not state the unit of measure; cubits are commonly assumed. Some ancient witnesses read twenty thousand for the width.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[2] Of this, a square of five hundred by five hundred shall be for the sanctuary, with fifty cubits of open land around it.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[3] From this district you shall measure off a section twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide, and in it shall stand the sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[4] It is the holy portion of the land; it shall belong to the priests who minister in the sanctuary, who draw near to serve the LORD. It shall be the place for their houses and a holy place for the sanctuary.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[5] Another section, twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide, shall belong to the Levites who minister in the temple, as their possession, with twenty chambers.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[6] As the possession of the city you shall assign an area five thousand wide and twenty-five thousand long, alongside the holy district. It shall belong to the whole house of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[7] The prince shall have the land on both sides of the holy district and the city's possession, bordering the holy district and the city's possession, extending westward on the west side and eastward on the east side, its length running alongside one of the tribal portions, from the western boundary to the eastern boundary.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[8] This land shall be his possession in Israel. My princes shall no longer oppress my people, but shall give the house of Israel the land according to their tribes.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[9] Thus says the Lord GOD: Enough, you princes of Israel! Put away violence and plundering, and do what is just and right. Stop dispossessing my people, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[10] You shall have honest scales, an honest ephah, and an honest bath.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[11] The ephah and the bath shall be of the same measure: the bath a tenth of a homer, and the ephah a tenth of a homer. The homer shall be the standard for both.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[12] The shekel shall be twenty gerahs; twenty shekels plus twenty-five shekels plus fifteen shekels shall be your mina.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[13] This is the offering you shall present: a sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat, and a sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[14] The required portion of oil, measured by the bath: a tenth of a bath from each kor—a kor is ten baths, that is, a homer, for ten baths make a homer.
