[Ezekiel] [45]:[15] And one sheep from every flock of two hundred from the well-watered pastures of Israel, for a grain offering, a burnt offering, and peace offerings, to make atonement for them, declares the Lord GOD.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[16] All the people of the land shall be bound to bring this offering to the prince in Israel.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[17] It shall be the prince's duty to provide the burnt offerings, the grain offering, and the drink offering at the festivals, the new moons, and the Sabbaths—at all the appointed feasts of the house of Israel. He shall provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[18] Thus says the Lord GOD: In the first month, on the first day of the month, you shall take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[19] The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the posts of the gate of the inner court.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[20] You shall do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who has sinned unintentionally or in ignorance. So you shall make atonement for the temple.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[21] In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall observe the Passover, a feast of seven days, during which unleavened bread shall be eaten.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[22] On that day the prince shall provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[23] During the seven days of the feast he shall provide as a burnt offering to the LORD seven bulls and seven rams without blemish, daily for the seven days, and a male goat each day as a sin offering.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[24] As a grain offering he shall provide an ephah with each bull and an ephah with each ram, along with a hin of oil for every ephah.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[25] In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the feast, he shall provide the same for seven days: the same sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering, and oil.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[1] This is what the Lord GOD says: The gate of the inner court that faces east shall stay shut on the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened.

The priests shall offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he shall bow down at the threshold of the gate and then go out; but the gate shall not be shut until evening.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[3] The people of the land shall also bow down before the LORD at the entrance of that gate on the Sabbaths and at the new moons.

[Ezekiel] [46]:[5] The grain offering shall be an ephah with the ram, and with the lambs whatever he is able to give, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[6] On the day of the new moon it shall be a young bull without blemish, along with six lambs and a ram; they shall be without blemish.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[7] As a grain offering he shall provide an ephah with the bull and an ephah with the ram, and with the lambs as much as he can afford, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[8] When the prince enters, he shall come in by way of the vestibule of the gate, and he shall go out the same way.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[9] When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed feasts, whoever enters by the north gate to worship shall go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate shall go out by the north gate. No one shall return through the gate by which he entered, but each shall go out straight ahead.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[10] The prince shall be among them: when they go in, he shall go in, and when they go out, he shall go out.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[11] At the festivals and the appointed feasts the grain offering shall be an ephah with a bull and an ephah with a ram, and with the lambs whatever he is able to give, along with a hin of oil for each ephah.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[12] When the prince brings a freewill offering to the LORD, whether a burnt offering or peace offerings as a freewill offering, the gate facing east shall be opened for him. He shall offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings as he does on the Sabbath day; then he shall go out, and after he has gone out the gate shall be shut.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[13] Each day you shall offer a year-old lamb without blemish as a burnt offering to the LORD; morning by morning you shall offer it.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[14] And with it, morning by morning, you shall offer a grain offering: a sixth of an ephah, with a third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour—a grain offering to the LORD, a perpetual statute for all time.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[15] So the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil shall be offered morning by morning, a continual burnt offering.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[16] This is what the Lord GOD says: If the prince makes a gift to any of his sons out of his inheritance, it shall belong to his sons; it is their possession by inheritance.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[17] But if he makes a gift out of his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall be his until the year of liberty, and then it shall revert to the prince. His inheritance belongs only to his sons; it shall remain theirs.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[18] The prince shall not take any of the people's inheritance, driving them out of their holdings. He shall provide his sons an inheritance from his own holding, so that none of my people is scattered from his own property.

[Ezekiel] [46]:[20] He said to me, "This is the place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they shall bake the grain offering, so that they need not carry them out into the outer court and transmit holiness to the people."

[Ezekiel] [47]:[1] Then he brought me back to the entrance of the temple, and there was water flowing out from under the threshold of the temple toward the east, for the temple faced east. The water was running down from under the south side of the temple, south of the altar.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[2] He led me out through the north gate and brought me around the outside to the outer gate that faces east, and I saw water trickling out on the south side.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[3] As the man went eastward with a measuring line in his hand, he measured off a thousand cubits and led me through the water, and it came up to my ankles.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[4] He measured another thousand and led me through the water, and it came up to my knees. He measured another thousand and led me through, and it came up to my waist.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[5] He measured another thousand, and now it was a river I could not cross, for the water had risen deep enough to swim in—a river that could not be crossed.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[6] He said to me, "Son of man, do you see this?" Then he led me back to the bank of the river.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[7] When I came back, I saw a great many trees along both banks of the river.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[8] He said to me, "This water flows out toward the eastern region and goes down into the Arabah, and where it enters the sea, the sea of stagnant water, the water is made fresh.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[9] Every living creature that swarms wherever the river flows will live. There will be great numbers of fish, because this water reaches there and makes the waters fresh; wherever the river flows, everything will live.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[10] Fishermen will stand along its shore; from En-gedi to En-eglaim there will be places for spreading nets. Its fish will be of many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, exceedingly many.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[11] But its swamps and marshes will not be made fresh; they are left for salt.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[12] Along the river, on both banks, all kinds of fruit trees will grow. Their leaves will not wither, and their fruit will never fail. Every month they will bear fresh fruit, because its waters flow from the sanctuary. Their fruit will be for food and their leaves for healing."

It shall extend eastward from the twenty-five thousand cubits of the offering to the eastern border, and westward from the twenty-five thousand to the western border, running alongside the tribal portions; this shall belong to the prince. The holy offering and the sanctuary of the temple shall be in the middle of it.
[Ezekiel] [48]:[22] Thus the property of the Levites and the property of the city shall lie in the middle of what belongs to the prince. The area between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin shall belong to the prince.
