[Daniel] [1]:[1] In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against Jerusalem and laid siege to it.
[Daniel] [1]:[2] And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, along with some of the vessels of the house of God. He carried them off to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and placed the vessels in the treasury of his god.
[Daniel] [1]:[3] Then the king ordered Ashpenaz, the chief of his court officials, to bring in some of the Israelites, both from the royal family and from the nobility—
[Daniel] [1]:[4] young men without any physical defect, handsome, skilled in all wisdom, endowed with knowledge and quick to understand, and fit to serve in the king's palace. He was to teach them the writing and the language of the Chaldeans.
[Daniel] [1]:[5] The king assigned them a daily portion of the royal food and of the wine he drank. They were to be trained for three years, and at the end of that time they were to enter the king's service.
[Daniel] [1]:[6] Among them were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, from the tribe of Judah.
[Daniel] [1]:[7] The chief official gave them new names: Daniel he called Belteshazzar, Hananiah he called Shadrach, Mishael he called Meshach, and Azariah he called Abednego.
[Daniel] [1]:[8] But Daniel resolved in his heart not to defile himself with the king's food and wine, and he asked the chief official for permission to avoid it.
[Daniel] [1]:[9] Now God had granted Daniel favor and compassion in the sight of the chief official,
[Daniel] [1]:[10] but the official said to Daniel, "I am afraid of my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink. Why should he see you looking worse than the other young men your age? You would cost me my head before the king."
[Daniel] [1]:[11] So Daniel said to the steward whom the chief official had put in charge of Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
[Daniel] [1]:[12] "Please test your servants for ten days. Give us nothing but vegetables to eat and water to drink.
[Daniel] [1]:[13] Then compare our appearance with that of the young men who eat the royal food, and deal with your servants according to what you see."
[Daniel] [1]:[14] He agreed to this and tested them for ten days.
[Daniel] [1]:[15] At the end of the ten days they looked healthier and better nourished than any of the young men who ate the royal food.
[Daniel] [1]:[16] So the steward took away their food and wine and gave them vegetables instead.
[Daniel] [1]:[17] To these four young men God gave knowledge and understanding of every kind of writing and wisdom, and Daniel also had insight into visions and dreams of every kind.
[Daniel] [1]:[18] At the end of the time set by the king for them to be brought in, the chief official presented them to Nebuchadnezzar.
[Daniel] [1]:[19] The king spoke with them, and among them all none was found equal to Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah; so they entered the king's service.
[Daniel] [1]:[20] In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.
[Daniel] [1]:[21] And Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.
[Daniel] [2]:[1] In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign, the king had dreams. His spirit was troubled, and sleep left him.
[Daniel] [2]:[2] So the king gave orders to summon the magicians, the enchanters, the sorcerers, and the Chaldeans to tell him what he had dreamed. They came and stood before the king,
[Daniel] [2]:[3] and the king said to them, "I have had a dream, and my spirit is troubled; I must know what the dream was."
[Daniel] [2]:[4] Then the Chaldeans answered the king in Aramaic, "May the king live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will give the interpretation."
[Daniel] [2]:[5] The king replied to the Chaldeans, "My decision stands firm: if you do not tell me both the dream and its interpretation, you will be torn limb from limb and your houses reduced to rubble.
[Daniel] [2]:[6] But if you declare the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts and rewards and great honor. So tell me the dream and its interpretation."
[Daniel] [2]:[7] They answered again, "Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will give the interpretation."
[Daniel] [2]:[8] The king said, "I know for certain that you are stalling for time, because you see that my decision stands firm:
[Daniel] [2]:[9] if you do not tell me the dream, there is one sentence for you all. You have agreed together to speak lying and misleading words to me, hoping the situation will change. So tell me the dream, and then I will know that you can give me its interpretation.
[Daniel] [2]:[10] The Chaldeans answered the king, "There is no one on earth who can tell the king what he demands. No king, however great and mighty, has ever asked such a thing of any magician or enchanter or Chaldean.
[Daniel] [2]:[11] What the king asks is too hard. No one can reveal it to the king except the gods, and they do not dwell among mortals."
[Daniel] [2]:[12] At this the king flew into a rage and gave orders to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
[Daniel] [2]:[13] So the decree went out that the wise men were to be put to death, and men were sent to find Daniel and his companions and kill them.
[Daniel] [2]:[14] Then Daniel spoke with prudence and discretion to Arioch, the commander of the king's guard, who had gone out to execute the wise men of Babylon.
[Daniel] [2]:[15] He asked Arioch, the king's officer, "Why is the king's decree so harsh?" Then Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
[Daniel] [2]:[16] So Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, so that he might show the king the interpretation.
[Daniel] [2]:[17] Then Daniel went to his house and told the matter to his companions Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
[Daniel] [2]:[18] urging them to plead for mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his companions would not be destroyed with the rest of Babylon's wise men.
[Daniel] [2]:[19] During the night the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision, and Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
[Daniel] [2]:[20] Daniel said: "Blessed be the name of God from age to age, for wisdom and power are his.
[Daniel] [2]:[21] He changes times and seasons; he removes kings and sets up kings. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who have understanding.
[Daniel] [2]:[22] He reveals deep and hidden things; he knows what lies in darkness, and light dwells with him.
[Daniel] [2]:[23] To you, God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, for you have given me wisdom and power. Now you have made known to me what we asked of you; you have made known to us the king's matter."
[Daniel] [2]:[24] Then Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, "Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me before the king, and I will give him the interpretation."
[Daniel] [2]:[25] Arioch hurried Daniel into the king's presence and said, "I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who can make known to the king the interpretation."
[Daniel] [2]:[26] The king said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, "Are you able to tell me the dream I saw and its interpretation?"
[Daniel] [2]:[27] Daniel answered the king: "No wise man, enchanter, magician, or diviner can reveal to the king the mystery he asks about.
[Daniel] [2]:[28] But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and he has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the last days. Your dream and the visions that passed through your mind as you lay in bed were these:
[Daniel] [2]:[29] As you lay there, O king, your thoughts turned to what would come to pass hereafter, and the Revealer of mysteries made known to you what is to be.
[Daniel] [2]:[30] As for me, this mystery has not been revealed to me because I have greater wisdom than anyone else alive, but so that the king may know the interpretation and understand what went through his mind.
[Daniel] [2]:[31] You looked, O king, and there before you stood a great statue—an enormous statue, dazzling in its brilliance, and terrifying in appearance.
[Daniel] [2]:[32] The head of the statue was of fine gold, its chest and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze,
[Daniel] [2]:[33] its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of clay.
[Daniel] [2]:[34] As you watched, a stone was cut out, but not by human hands. It struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and smashed them.
[Daniel] [2]:[35] Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were all broken to pieces together and became like chaff on a summer threshing floor. The wind carried them away, and no place was found for them anywhere. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
[Daniel] [2]:[36] This was the dream; now we will tell the king its interpretation.
[Daniel] [2]:[37] You, O king, are the king of kings. The God of heaven has given you the kingdom, the power, the might, and the glory;
[Daniel] [2]:[38] wherever human beings dwell, he has given into your hand the beasts of the field and the birds of the air, and made you ruler over them all. You are that head of gold.
[Daniel] [2]:[39] After you another kingdom will arise, inferior to yours; then a third kingdom, one of bronze, which will rule over the whole earth.
[Daniel] [2]:[40] Finally there will be a fourth kingdom, strong as iron—for iron shatters and crushes everything—and as iron breaks all things to pieces, so it will crush and shatter all the others.
[Daniel] [2]:[41] As you saw, the feet and toes were partly of potter's clay and partly of iron; this will be a divided kingdom, yet with some of the strength of iron in it, since you saw the iron mixed with soft, wet clay.
[Daniel] [2]:[42] And as the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, so this kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.
[Daniel] [2]:[43] As you saw the iron mixed with the common clay, so the people will mix with one another in marriage, but they will not hold together, any more than iron mixes with clay.
[Daniel] [2]:[44] In the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, nor will it be left to another people. It will crush all those kingdoms and bring them to an end, but it will stand forever.
[Daniel] [2]:[45] This is the meaning of the stone you saw cut from the mountain, not by human hands, which broke to pieces the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold. The great God has shown the king what will happen hereafter. The dream is true, and its interpretation is trustworthy."
[Daniel] [2]:[46] Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and paid homage to Daniel, and he commanded that an offering and incense be presented to him.
[Daniel] [2]:[47] The king said to Daniel, "Truly your God is the God of gods and the Lord of kings, the revealer of mysteries, for you were able to reveal this mystery."
[Daniel] [2]:[48] Then the king promoted Daniel to high office, gave him many rich gifts, and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon and chief over all its wise men.
[Daniel] [2]:[49] At Daniel's request the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to administer the province of Babylon, while Daniel himself remained at the king's court.
[Daniel] [3]:[1] King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.
[Daniel] [3]:[2] Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent word to gather the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the officials of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
[Daniel] [3]:[3] So the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the officials of the provinces gathered for the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
[Daniel] [3]:[4] Then the herald proclaimed with a loud voice: "This is the command to you, O peoples and nations and speakers of every language:
[Daniel] [3]:[5] When you hear the sound of the horn, pipe, zither, lyre, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, you are to fall down and worship the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
[Daniel] [3]:[6] Whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace."
[Daniel] [3]:[7] Therefore, as soon as all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, pipe, zither, lyre, harp, and every kind of music, all the peoples, nations, and languages fell down and worshiped the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
[Daniel] [3]:[8] At that very time certain Chaldeans came forward and maliciously accused the Jews.
[Daniel] [3]:[9] They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, "O king, live forever!
[Daniel] [3]:[10] You, O king, have issued a decree that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, pipe, zither, lyre, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music must fall down and worship the golden image,
[Daniel] [3]:[11] and that whoever does not fall down and worship shall be thrown into a blazing furnace.
[Daniel] [3]:[12] There are certain Jews whom you appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men pay no attention to you, O king. They do not serve your gods, and they do not worship the golden image you have set up."
[Daniel] [3]:[13] Then Nebuchadnezzar, in rage and fury, ordered that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought in. So these men were brought before the king.
[Daniel] [3]:[14] Nebuchadnezzar said to them, "Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods or worship the golden image I have set up?
[Daniel] [3]:[15] Now if you are ready, when you hear the sound of the horn, pipe, zither, lyre, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, to fall down and worship the image I have made, well and good. But if you will not worship, you will immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace. And who is the god who can rescue you from my hand?"
[Daniel] [3]:[16] Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered the king, "Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you in this matter.
[Daniel] [3]:[17] If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the blazing furnace, and he will deliver us from your hand, O king.
[Daniel] [3]:[18] But if not, know this, O king: we will not serve your gods, and we will not worship the golden image you have set up."
[Daniel] [3]:[19] Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the look on his face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He ordered that the furnace be heated seven times hotter than usual,
[Daniel] [3]:[20] and he commanded the strongest soldiers of his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the blazing furnace.
[Daniel] [3]:[21] So these men were bound in their robes, trousers, turbans, and other garments, and thrown into the blazing furnace.
[Daniel] [3]:[22] Because the king's command was so urgent and the furnace so exceedingly hot, the flames of the fire killed the men who carried Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego up to it.
[Daniel] [3]:[23] And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell bound into the blazing furnace.
[Daniel] [3]:[24] Then King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished. He rose up in alarm and said to his counselors, "Did we not throw three men, bound, into the fire?" They answered the king, "Certainly, O king."
[Daniel] [3]:[25] "But look," he said, "I see four men, unbound, walking around in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed—and the fourth looks like a son of the gods!"
[Daniel] [3]:[26] Then Nebuchadnezzar came near the door of the blazing furnace and called out, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out! Come here!" So Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the fire.
[Daniel] [3]:[27] The satraps, prefects, governors, and the king's counselors crowded around and saw these men: the fire had no power over their bodies, not a hair of their heads was singed, their robes were unharmed, and no smell of fire clung to them.
[Daniel] [3]:[28] Then Nebuchadnezzar declared, "Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his angel and rescued his servants who trusted in him! They set aside the king's command and yielded up their bodies rather than serve or worship any god except their own God.
[Daniel] [3]:[29] Therefore I decree that any people, nation, or language that speaks offensively against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego shall be torn limb from limb and their houses reduced to rubble, for there is no other god who can rescue like this."
[Daniel] [3]:[30] Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
[Daniel] [3]:[31] King Nebuchadnezzar, to all the peoples, nations, and languages who dwell in all the earth: May your peace abound!
[Daniel] [3]:[32] It has pleased me to declare the signs and wonders that the Most High God has done for me.
[Daniel] [3]:[33] How great are his signs, how mighty his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his dominion endures from generation to generation.
[Daniel] [4]:[1] I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and flourishing in my palace.
[Daniel] [4]:[2] I saw a dream that frightened me; as I lay on my bed, the thoughts and the visions that passed through my head terrified me.
[Daniel] [4]:[3] So I issued a decree that all the wise men of Babylon be brought before me to make known to me the interpretation of the dream.
[Daniel] [4]:[4] Then the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the diviners came in, and I told them the dream, but they could not make its interpretation known to me.
[Daniel] [4]:[5] At last Daniel came in before me—he who is called Belteshazzar after the name of my god, and in whom is the spirit of the holy gods—and I told him the dream:
[Daniel] [4]:[6] "Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and that no mystery is too difficult for you. Tell me the visions I saw in my dream, and give me their interpretation.
[Daniel] [4]:[7] These were the visions that passed through my head as I lay on my bed: I looked, and there stood a tree at the center of the earth, and its height was great.
[Daniel] [4]:[8] The tree grew large and strong; its top reached to heaven, and it could be seen to the ends of all the earth.
[Daniel] [4]:[9] Its foliage was beautiful and its fruit abundant, and in it was food for all. Under it the beasts of the field found shade, in its branches the birds of the sky nested, and from it every living thing was fed.
[Daniel] [4]:[10] As I lay on my bed I looked at the visions passing through my head, and there was a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven.
[Daniel] [4]:[11] He called out with power and said: 'Cut down the tree and lop off its branches; strip away its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the beasts flee from beneath it and the birds from its branches.
[Daniel] [4]:[12] But leave the stump with its roots in the ground, bound with iron and bronze, in the grass of the field. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let his portion be with the beasts among the plants of the earth.
[Daniel] [4]:[13] Let his mind be changed from that of a man, and let the mind of a beast be given to him, and let seven times pass over him.
[Daniel] [4]:[14] This sentence stands by decree of the watchers, this verdict by the word of the holy ones, so that the living may know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of men, and gives it to whomever he wills, and sets over it the lowliest of men.'
[Daniel] [4]:[15] This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Now you, Belteshazzar, tell me its interpretation, since none of the wise men of my kingdom is able to make it known to me. But you are able, for the spirit of the holy gods is in you."
[Daniel] [4]:[16] Then Daniel, who was called Belteshazzar, was stunned for a while, and his thoughts alarmed him. The king said, "Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its interpretation alarm you." Belteshazzar answered, "My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies!
[Daniel] [4]:[17] The tree you saw, which grew large and strong, whose top reached to heaven and which was visible to all the earth,
[Daniel] [4]:[18] whose foliage was beautiful and whose fruit was abundant, in which was food for all, under which the beasts of the field lived and in whose branches the birds of the sky made their home—
[Daniel] [4]:[19] that tree is you, O king. You have grown great and strong; your greatness has grown until it reaches to heaven, and your dominion to the ends of the earth.
[Daniel] [4]:[20] And as for what the king saw—a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven and saying, 'Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump with its roots in the ground, bound with iron and bronze, in the grass of the field; let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let his portion be with the beasts of the field until seven times pass over him'—
[Daniel] [4]:[21] this is the interpretation, O king; it is a decree of the Most High that has come upon my lord the king.
[Daniel] [4]:[22] You will be driven away from human society, and your dwelling will be with the beasts of the field. You will be made to eat grass like an ox and will be drenched with the dew of heaven, and seven times will pass over you, until you acknowledge that the Most High rules over the kingdom of men and gives it to whomever he wills.
[Daniel] [4]:[23] And as for the command to leave the stump with the roots of the tree: your kingdom will be kept secure for you, from the time you acknowledge that Heaven rules.
[Daniel] [4]:[24] Therefore, O king, may my counsel please you: break with your sins by doing what is right, and with your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor; perhaps then your prosperity will continue."
[Daniel] [4]:[25] All of this came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.
[Daniel] [4]:[26] Twelve months later, as he was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon,
[Daniel] [4]:[27] the king said, "Is this not the great Babylon that I have built as a royal residence by my mighty power and for the glory of my majesty?"
[Daniel] [4]:[28] The words were still in the king's mouth when a voice fell from heaven: "To you it is declared, King Nebuchadnezzar: the kingdom has departed from you.
[Daniel] [4]:[29] You will be driven away from human society, and your dwelling will be with the beasts of the field. You will be made to eat grass like an ox, and seven times will pass over you, until you acknowledge that the Most High rules over the kingdom of men and gives it to whomever he wills."
[Daniel] [4]:[30] At that very moment the word was fulfilled against Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven away from human society and ate grass like an ox. His body was drenched with the dew of heaven until his hair grew long like eagles' feathers and his nails like birds' claws.
[Daniel] [4]:[31] When the days were completed, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my reason returned to me. I blessed the Most High; I praised and honored him who lives forever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion and whose kingdom endures from generation to generation.
[Daniel] [4]:[32] All who dwell on the earth are counted as nothing. He does as he pleases with the host of heaven and with those who dwell on the earth. No one can stay his hand or say to him, "What have you done?"
[Daniel] [4]:[33] At that same time my reason returned to me, and for the glory of my kingdom my majesty and splendor returned to me. My counselors and my nobles sought me out, I was restored to my kingdom, and still more greatness was added to me.
[Daniel] [4]:[34] Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and honor the King of heaven, for all his works are truth and his ways are just, and those who walk in pride he is able to humble.
[Daniel] [5]:[1] King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand of his nobles, and he drank wine in the presence of the thousand.
[Daniel] [5]:[2] Under the influence of the wine, Belshazzar gave orders to bring in the vessels of gold and silver that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken from the temple in Jerusalem, so that the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines might drink from them.
[Daniel] [5]:[3] So they brought in the gold vessels that had been taken from the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem, and the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines drank from them.
[Daniel] [5]:[4] They drank wine and praised the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
[Daniel] [5]:[5] At that very moment the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall of the king's palace, opposite the lampstand. The king watched the hand as it wrote.
[Daniel] [5]:[6] Then the color drained from the king's face, and his thoughts terrified him. His limbs went limp, and his knees knocked together.
[Daniel] [5]:[7] The king called out loudly to bring in the enchanters, the Chaldeans, and the diviners. He said to the wise men of Babylon, "Whoever reads this writing and tells me its meaning will be clothed in purple, will wear a gold chain around his neck, and will rule as third in the kingdom."
[Daniel] [5]:[8] Then all the king's wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or make its meaning known to the king.
[Daniel] [5]:[9] So King Belshazzar grew even more terrified, the color drained from his face, and his nobles were at a loss.
[Daniel] [5]:[10] Because of the words of the king and his nobles, the queen came into the banquet hall. She said, "O king, live forever! Do not let your thoughts terrify you, and do not let your face grow pale.
[Daniel] [5]:[11] There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. In the days of your father he was found to have insight, understanding, and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods. King Nebuchadnezzar your father appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners—your own father the king did this—
[Daniel] [5]:[12] because an extraordinary spirit, knowledge, and understanding were found in him, along with the ability to interpret dreams, explain riddles, and unravel difficult problems—in this Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be summoned, and he will give the interpretation."
[Daniel] [5]:[13] So Daniel was brought before the king, and the king said to him, "Are you that Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah whom my father the king brought from Judah?
[Daniel] [5]:[14] I have heard that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that insight, understanding, and extraordinary wisdom are found in you.
[Daniel] [5]:[15] The wise men and enchanters were just brought before me to read this writing and tell me its meaning, but they could not explain what it means.
[Daniel] [5]:[16] But I have heard that you are able to give interpretations and unravel difficult problems. Now if you can read the writing and tell me its meaning, you will be clothed in purple, you will wear a gold chain around your neck, and you will rule as third in the kingdom."
[Daniel] [5]:[17] Then Daniel answered the king, "Keep your gifts for yourself and give your rewards to someone else. Even so, I will read the writing for the king and make its meaning known to him.
[Daniel] [5]:[18] O king, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar kingship and greatness, glory and majesty.
[Daniel] [5]:[19] Because of the greatness he gave him, all peoples, nations, and languages trembled in fear before him. He killed whomever he wished and kept alive whomever he wished; he raised up whomever he wished and brought low whomever he wished.
[Daniel] [5]:[20] But when his heart grew proud and his spirit hardened with arrogance, he was brought down from his royal throne and stripped of his glory.
[Daniel] [5]:[21] He was driven away from human company, his mind became like that of an animal, and he lived among the wild donkeys. He ate grass like cattle, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until he acknowledged that the Most High God rules over the kingdoms of men and sets over them whomever he wishes.
[Daniel] [5]:[22] But you, Belshazzar, his son, have not humbled your heart, though you knew all this.
[Daniel] [5]:[23] You have exalted yourself against the Lord of heaven. The vessels from his house were brought before you, and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines drank wine from them. You praised gods of silver and gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which cannot see or hear or know anything. But the God who holds your very breath in his hand and governs all your ways—him you did not honor.
[Daniel] [5]:[24] So the hand was sent from his presence, and this writing was inscribed.
[Daniel] [5]:[25] This is the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, and PARSIN.
[Daniel] [5]:[26] And this is what it means: MENE—God has numbered the days of your kingdom and brought it to an end.
[Daniel] [5]:[27] TEKEL—you have been weighed on the scales and found too light. [Footnote: TEKEL sounds like the Aramaic words for 'weighed' and 'light of weight.']
[Daniel] [5]:[28] PERES—your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and Persians." [Footnote: PERES sounds like the Aramaic word for 'divided' and also like the name 'Persia.']
[Daniel] [5]:[29] Then Belshazzar gave the command. They clothed Daniel in purple, placed a gold chain around his neck, and proclaimed him third ruler in the kingdom.
[Daniel] [5]:[30] That very night Belshazzar, the Chaldean king, was killed.
[Daniel] [6]:[1] So Darius the Mede received the kingdom, at about the age of sixty-two.
[Daniel] [6]:[2] It pleased Darius to appoint over the kingdom a hundred and twenty satraps, stationed throughout the realm,
[Daniel] [6]:[3] and over them three administrators, one of whom was Daniel. The satraps were accountable to them, so that the king would suffer no loss.
[Daniel] [6]:[4] Then this Daniel so distinguished himself above the administrators and satraps by his extraordinary spirit that the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.
[Daniel] [6]:[5] At this the administrators and satraps tried to find grounds for a charge against Daniel in his conduct of the kingdom's affairs, but they could find no charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy; no negligence or corruption was found in him.
[Daniel] [6]:[6] So these men said, "We will never find any charge against this Daniel unless we find it in connection with the law of his God."
[Daniel] [6]:[7] Then these administrators and satraps came as a body to the king and said to him: "King Darius, live forever!
[Daniel] [6]:[8] All the royal administrators, prefects, satraps, counselors, and governors have agreed that the king should issue a decree and enforce a ban: that anyone who prays to any god or human being during the next thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be thrown into the lions' den.
[Daniel] [6]:[9] Now, O king, issue the ban and sign the document, so that it cannot be altered—in accordance with the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed."
[Daniel] [6]:[10] So King Darius signed the document containing the ban.
[Daniel] [6]:[11] Now when Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went home to his upper room, where the windows opened toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he got down on his knees and prayed, giving thanks to his God, just as he had always done.
[Daniel] [6]:[12] Then these men came as a body and found Daniel praying and pleading before his God.
[Daniel] [6]:[13] So they went to the king and spoke to him about his royal ban: "Did you not sign a ban that during the next thirty days anyone who prays to any god or human being except to you, O king, would be thrown into the lions' den?" The king answered, "The matter stands firm, in accordance with the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed."
[Daniel] [6]:[14] Then they said to the king, "Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah, pays no attention to you, O king, or to the ban you have signed. Three times a day he makes his petition."
[Daniel] [6]:[15] When the king heard this, he was deeply distressed; he set his mind on rescuing Daniel and labored until sundown to save him.
[Daniel] [6]:[16] Then these men crowded in on the king and said to him, "Know, O king, that by the law of the Medes and Persians no ban or decree the king issues can be changed."
[Daniel] [6]:[17] So the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the lions' den. The king said to Daniel, "May your God, whom you serve continually, rescue you!"
[Daniel] [6]:[18] A stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the rings of his nobles, so that nothing concerning Daniel could be changed.
[Daniel] [6]:[19] Then the king returned to his palace and spent the night fasting; no entertainment was brought before him, and sleep fled from him.
[Daniel] [6]:[20] At the first light of dawn the king got up and hurried to the lions' den.
[Daniel] [6]:[21] When he came near the den, he called out to Daniel in an anguished voice, "Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to rescue you from the lions?"
[Daniel] [6]:[22] Daniel answered, "O king, live forever!
[Daniel] [6]:[23] My God sent his angel and shut the mouths of the lions, and they have not harmed me, because I was found innocent before him. And before you too, O king, I have done no wrong."
[Daniel] [6]:[24] The king was overjoyed and gave orders to lift Daniel out of the den. So Daniel was lifted out, and no wound was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.
[Daniel] [6]:[25] Then at the king's command the men who had accused Daniel were brought in and thrown into the lions' den, along with their children and their wives. And before they reached the floor of the den, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
[Daniel] [6]:[26] Then King Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations, and languages who dwell in all the earth: "May your peace abound!
[Daniel] [6]:[27] I hereby decree that in every part of my kingdom people are to tremble and stand in awe before the God of Daniel. For he is the living God, enduring forever; his kingdom will never be destroyed, and his dominion has no end.
[Daniel] [6]:[28] He rescues and he saves; he works signs and wonders in the heavens and on the earth. He has rescued Daniel from the power of the lions."
[Daniel] [6]:[29] So this Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
[Daniel] [7]:[1] In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel had a dream and visions passed through his mind as he lay on his bed. He wrote the dream down, and this is the account of it:
[Daniel] [7]:[2] Daniel said: In my vision at night I saw the four winds of heaven churning up the great sea,
[Daniel] [7]:[3] and four huge beasts came up out of the sea, each different from the others.
[Daniel] [7]:[4] The first was like a lion, and it had the wings of an eagle. I watched until its wings were torn off, and it was lifted from the ground and made to stand on two feet like a man, and the mind of a man was given to it.
[Daniel] [7]:[5] Then I saw a second beast, which looked like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and it had three ribs in its mouth, between its teeth. It was told, "Get up, devour much flesh!"
[Daniel] [7]:[6] After that I looked, and there before me was another beast, like a leopard. On its back it had four wings like those of a bird, and it had four heads. And it was given authority to rule.
[Daniel] [7]:[7] After that, in my vision at night, I saw a fourth beast—terrifying and dreadful and immensely strong. It had great iron teeth; it devoured and crushed and trampled underfoot whatever was left. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.
[Daniel] [7]:[8] While I was studying the horns, another horn came up among them, a small one, and three of the first horns were torn out before it. This horn had eyes like the eyes of a man and a mouth that spoke arrogantly.
[Daniel] [7]:[9] I watched until thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took his seat. His clothing was white as snow, the hair of his head like pure wool. His throne was flaming with fire, and its wheels were all ablaze.
[Daniel] [7]:[10] A river of fire flowed out from before him. Thousands upon thousands attended him; ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The court was seated, and the books were opened.
[Daniel] [7]:[11] I kept watching because of the arrogant words the horn was speaking. I watched until the beast was killed and its body destroyed and thrown into the blazing fire.
[Daniel] [7]:[12] The other beasts had already been stripped of their authority, but they were allowed to live on for a season and a time.
[Daniel] [7]:[13] In my vision at night I saw one like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into his presence.
[Daniel] [7]:[14] To him was given authority, glory, and a kingdom; all peoples, nations, and languages will serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom will never be destroyed.
[Daniel] [7]:[15] I, Daniel, was troubled in spirit within me, and the visions that passed through my mind alarmed me.
[Daniel] [7]:[16] So I approached one of those standing there and asked him for the truth about all this. He answered me and made known to me the meaning of these things:
[Daniel] [7]:[17] "These four great beasts are four kings that will arise from the earth.
[Daniel] [7]:[18] But the holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom and will possess it forever—yes, for ever and ever.
[Daniel] [7]:[19] Then I wanted to know the truth about the fourth beast, which was different from all the others—most terrifying, with its iron teeth and bronze claws, devouring and crushing and trampling underfoot whatever was left;
[Daniel] [7]:[20] and about the ten horns on its head, and about the other horn that came up, before which three of them fell—the horn that had eyes and a mouth that spoke arrogantly, and that looked more imposing than the others.
[Daniel] [7]:[21] As I watched, this horn was waging war against the holy ones and defeating them,
[Daniel] [7]:[22] until the Ancient of Days came and judgment was given in favor of the holy ones of the Most High, and the time came when they took possession of the kingdom.
[Daniel] [7]:[23] He said: "The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom that will appear on earth. It will be different from all the other kingdoms and will devour the whole earth, trampling it down and crushing it.
[Daniel] [7]:[24] The ten horns are ten kings who will rise from this kingdom. After them another king will arise, different from the earlier ones, and he will bring down three kings.
[Daniel] [7]:[25] He will speak against the Most High and wear down the holy ones of the Most High and try to change the appointed times and the law. They will be handed over to him for a time, times, and half a time.
[Daniel] [7]:[26] But the court will sit, and his dominion will be taken away, destroyed and utterly abolished.
[Daniel] [7]:[27] Then the kingship, the dominion, and the greatness of all the kingdoms under heaven will be given to the people of the holy ones of the Most High. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all rulers will serve and obey him."
[Daniel] [7]:[28] Here the account ends. I, Daniel, was deeply disturbed by my thoughts, and my face turned pale, but I kept the matter to myself.
[Daniel] [8]:[1] In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the one that had appeared to me earlier.
[Daniel] [8]:[2] In the vision I saw myself in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam; and in the vision I was beside the Ulai Canal.
[Daniel] [8]:[3] I looked up, and there before me stood a ram beside the canal. It had two horns, both of them long, but one was longer than the other, and the longer one came up last.
[Daniel] [8]:[4] I watched the ram charging west and north and south. No animal could stand against it, and none could rescue from its power. It did as it pleased and became great.
[Daniel] [8]:[5] While I was considering this, suddenly a male goat came from the west, crossing the whole earth without touching the ground, and the goat had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.
[Daniel] [8]:[6] It came toward the two-horned ram I had seen standing beside the canal and rushed at it in furious power.
[Daniel] [8]:[7] I saw it reach the ram and, enraged against it, strike the ram and shatter its two horns. The ram had no strength to stand against it; the goat threw it to the ground and trampled it, and there was no one to rescue the ram from its power.
[Daniel] [8]:[8] The male goat became very great, but at the height of its power the large horn was broken off, and in its place four conspicuous horns came up toward the four winds of heaven.
[Daniel] [8]:[9] Out of one of them came another horn, small at first, but it grew exceedingly great toward the south, toward the east, and toward the Beautiful Land.
[Daniel] [8]:[10] It grew until it reached the host of heaven, and it threw some of the host and some of the stars down to the earth and trampled them.
[Daniel] [8]:[11] It set itself up to be as great as the Prince of the host; from him the daily sacrifice was taken away, and the place of his sanctuary was cast down.
[Daniel] [8]:[12] Because of rebellion, the host was given over to it together with the daily sacrifice. It flung truth to the ground, and whatever it did, it prospered.
[Daniel] [8]:[13] Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to the one who was speaking, "How long will it take for the vision to be fulfilled—the vision concerning the daily sacrifice, the rebellion that causes desolation, and the surrender of the sanctuary and of the host to be trampled underfoot?"
[Daniel] [8]:[14] He said to me, "It will take 2,300 evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be restored to its rightful state."
[Daniel] [8]:[15] While I, Daniel, was watching the vision and trying to understand it, there before me stood one who looked like a man.
[Daniel] [8]:[16] And I heard a human voice from the Ulai calling out, "Gabriel, explain the vision to this man."
[Daniel] [8]:[17] He came to where I was standing, and when he came I was terrified and fell facedown. "Son of man," he said to me, "understand that the vision concerns the time of the end."
[Daniel] [8]:[18] While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep, my face to the ground. Then he touched me and raised me to my feet.
[Daniel] [8]:[19] He said, "I am going to tell you what will happen at the end of the time of wrath, for the vision concerns the appointed time of the end.
[Daniel] [8]:[20] The two-horned ram that you saw represents the kings of Media and Persia.
[Daniel] [8]:[21] The shaggy goat is the king of Greece, and the large horn between its eyes is the first king.
[Daniel] [8]:[22] The four horns that replaced the one that was broken off are four kingdoms that will arise from his nation, but they will not have his power.
[Daniel] [8]:[23] In the latter part of their reign, when rebels have become completely wicked, a fierce-looking king, a master of intrigue, will arise.
[Daniel] [8]:[24] He will become very strong, but not by his own power. He will cause astounding devastation and will succeed in whatever he does. He will destroy the mighty and the holy people.
[Daniel] [8]:[25] Through his cunning he will make deceit prosper under his hand, and in his own heart he will exalt himself. When they feel secure, he will destroy many; he will even take his stand against the Prince of princes. Yet he will be broken, but not by human hand.
[Daniel] [8]:[26] The vision of the evenings and mornings that has been told is true, but seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future."
[Daniel] [8]:[27] I, Daniel, was worn out and lay ill for days. Then I got up and went about the king's business. I was appalled by the vision, and no one could explain it.
[Daniel] [9]:[1] In the first year of Darius son of Xerxes, a Mede by descent, who was made king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans—
[Daniel] [9]:[2] in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of years that must pass before the desolations of Jerusalem would be completed—seventy years, as the word of the LORD had come to Jeremiah the prophet.
[Daniel] [9]:[3] So I turned my face to the Lord God, to seek him in prayer and pleading, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
[Daniel] [9]:[4] I prayed to the LORD my God and made confession: "Lord, great and awesome God, who keeps the covenant and mercy for those who love him and keep his commandments,
[Daniel] [9]:[5] we have sinned and done wrong. We have acted wickedly and rebelled, turning aside from your commandments and your rulings.
[Daniel] [9]:[6] We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our princes, our fathers, and all the people of the land.
[Daniel] [9]:[7] Righteousness belongs to you, Lord, but to us shame of face—to this very day—to the people of Judah, to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to all Israel, near and far, in every land where you have driven them because of the treachery they committed against you.
[Daniel] [9]:[8] LORD, to us belongs shame of face—to our kings, our princes, and our fathers—because we have sinned against you.
[Daniel] [9]:[9] To the Lord our God belong mercy and forgiveness, though we have rebelled against him,
[Daniel] [9]:[10] and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God by walking in his laws, which he set before us through his servants the prophets.
[Daniel] [9]:[11] All Israel has transgressed your law and turned aside, refusing to obey your voice. So the curse and the oath written in the law of Moses, the servant of God, have been poured out upon us, because we have sinned against him.
[Daniel] [9]:[12] He has carried out the word he spoke against us and against our judges who judged us, bringing on us so great a disaster that nothing like what has been done to Jerusalem has ever been done under all heaven.
[Daniel] [9]:[13] Just as it is written in the law of Moses, all this disaster has come upon us. Yet we did not entreat the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our iniquity and gaining insight into your truth.
[Daniel] [9]:[14] So the LORD kept the disaster ready and brought it upon us, for the LORD our God is righteous in everything he does; but we have not obeyed his voice.
[Daniel] [9]:[15] And now, Lord our God, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made a name for yourself that endures to this day: we have sinned, we have done wrong.
[Daniel] [9]:[16] Lord, in keeping with all your righteous acts, let your anger and your wrath turn away from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain. Because of our sins and the guilt of our fathers, Jerusalem and your people have become an object of scorn to all who surround us.
[Daniel] [9]:[17] Now therefore, our God, hear the prayer and the pleading of your servant. For your own sake, Lord, let your face shine upon your desolate sanctuary.
[Daniel] [9]:[18] Incline your ear, my God, and hear. Open your eyes and see our desolation and the city that bears your name. We do not lay our pleas before you because we are righteous, but because of your great mercy.
[Daniel] [9]:[19] Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, listen and act! For your own sake, my God, do not delay, for your city and your people bear your name."
[Daniel] [9]:[20] While I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and laying my plea before the LORD my God for his holy mountain—
[Daniel] [9]:[21] while I was still speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight at the time of the evening sacrifice.
[Daniel] [9]:[22] He instructed me and said, "Daniel, I have come now to give you insight and understanding.
[Daniel] [9]:[23] As soon as you began to pray, a word went out, and I have come to tell you, for you are greatly loved. So consider the word and understand the vision.
[Daniel] [9]:[24] Seventy weeks are decreed for your people and your holy city: to finish transgression, to put an end to sin, to atone for guilt, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophecy, and to anoint a most holy place.
[Daniel] [9]:[25] Know this and understand: from the going out of the word to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed one, a prince, there will be seven weeks; then for sixty-two weeks it will be rebuilt with streets and moat, but in times of distress.
[Daniel] [9]:[26] After the sixty-two weeks an anointed one will be cut off and have nothing. The people of a prince who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end will come like a flood, and until the end there will be war; desolations are decreed.
[Daniel] [9]:[27] He will confirm a covenant with many for one week; and in the middle of the week he will put an end to sacrifice and offering. On the wing of the temple will be abominations that bring desolation, until the decreed destruction is poured out on the desolator."
[Daniel] [10]:[1] In the third year of Cyrus, king of Persia, a word was revealed to Daniel, who was called Belteshazzar. The word was true, and it spoke of a great conflict. He understood the word, and understanding came to him in the vision.
[Daniel] [10]:[2] In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three full weeks.
[Daniel] [10]:[3] I ate no fine food; no meat or wine passed my lips, and I used no oil at all until the three weeks were over.
[Daniel] [10]:[4] On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing on the bank of the great river, the Tigris.
[Daniel] [10]:[5] I lifted my eyes and looked, and there before me stood a man dressed in linen, with a belt of gold from Uphaz around his waist.
[Daniel] [10]:[6] His body was like topaz, his face like a flash of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and legs like the gleam of burnished bronze, and the sound of his words like the roar of a multitude.
[Daniel] [10]:[7] I, Daniel, alone saw the vision. The men who were with me did not see it, but a great terror fell on them, and they fled and hid themselves.
[Daniel] [10]:[8] So I was left alone, gazing at this great vision. No strength remained in me; my face turned deathly pale, and I was helpless.
[Daniel] [10]:[9] Then I heard the sound of his words, and as I heard them I fell into a deep sleep, my face to the ground.
[Daniel] [10]:[10] Then a hand touched me and set me trembling on my knees and the palms of my hands.
[Daniel] [10]:[11] He said to me, "Daniel, you who are treasured, understand the words I am speaking to you, and stand on your feet, for I have now been sent to you." And when he spoke this word to me, I stood up trembling.
[Daniel] [10]:[12] Then he said to me, "Do not be afraid, Daniel. From the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come in response to them.
[Daniel] [10]:[13] But the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I remained there with the kings of Persia.
[Daniel] [10]:[14] Now I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision concerns days still to come."
[Daniel] [10]:[15] While he was speaking these words to me, I turned my face toward the ground and could not speak.
[Daniel] [10]:[16] Then one who looked like a man touched my lips, and I opened my mouth and spoke. I said to the one standing before me, "My lord, because of the vision, anguish has overwhelmed me, and I am helpless.
[Daniel] [10]:[17] How can I, your servant, speak with you, my lord? For my strength is gone, and there is no breath left in me."
[Daniel] [10]:[18] Again the one who looked like a man touched me and strengthened me.
[Daniel] [10]:[19] He said, "Do not be afraid, you who are treasured. Peace be with you. Be strong, take courage!" And as he spoke to me, I was strengthened, and I said, "Speak, my lord, for you have given me strength."
[Daniel] [10]:[20] Then he said, "Do you know why I have come to you? Now I must return to fight against the prince of Persia, and when I go, the prince of Greece will come.
[Daniel] [10]:[21] But I will tell you what is written in the book of truth. No one supports me against these princes except Michael, your prince.
[Daniel] [11]:[1] And I, in the first year of Darius the Mede, took my stand to strengthen and protect him.
[Daniel] [11]:[2] Now I will tell you the truth. Three more kings will arise in Persia, and a fourth will gain far greater riches than all the rest. When he has grown strong through his wealth, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
[Daniel] [11]:[3] Then a warrior king will arise, who will rule with vast dominion and do as he pleases.
[Daniel] [11]:[4] But no sooner will he have arisen than his kingdom will be broken and divided toward the four winds of heaven. It will not go to his descendants, nor will it have the dominion he exercised, for his kingdom will be uprooted and given to others besides them.
[Daniel] [11]:[5] The king of the South will grow strong, but one of his commanders will grow stronger than he and will rule a realm greater than his own.
[Daniel] [11]:[6] After some years they will form an alliance, and the daughter of the king of the South will come to the king of the North to seal the agreement. But she will not retain her power, nor will he and his power endure. In those days she will be surrendered, along with her escort, the one who fathered her, and the one who supported her.
[Daniel] [11]:[7] In her place one from her family line will arise. He will come against the army, enter the fortress of the king of the North, deal with them, and prevail.
[Daniel] [11]:[8] He will also carry off to Egypt their gods with their cast images and their precious vessels of silver and gold. For some years he will leave the king of the North alone.
[Daniel] [11]:[9] Then the king of the North will invade the realm of the king of the South, but will retreat to his own land.
[Daniel] [11]:[10] His sons will prepare for war and assemble a great host of forces; one of them will surely advance and sweep on like an overwhelming flood, then return and press the attack as far as his enemy's fortress.
[Daniel] [11]:[11] Then the king of the South will march out in a rage and fight against the king of the North, who will raise a great army, but that army will be given into his hand.
[Daniel] [11]:[12] When the army is carried off, his heart will be lifted up; he will bring down tens of thousands, yet he will not prevail.
[Daniel] [11]:[13] For the king of the North will raise another army, larger than the first, and after some years he will advance with a great army and abundant supplies.
[Daniel] [11]:[14] In those times many will rise against the king of the South. Violent men among your own people will rebel in fulfillment of the vision, but they will fail.
[Daniel] [11]:[15] Then the king of the North will come, throw up siege ramps, and capture a fortified city. The forces of the South will not withstand him; even their finest troops will have no strength to stand.
[Daniel] [11]:[16] The invader will do as he pleases; no one will stand against him. He will establish himself in the Beautiful Land, with destruction in his hand.
[Daniel] [11]:[17] He will resolve to come with the full might of his kingdom, and he will make terms; he will give a daughter in marriage in order to overthrow the kingdom, but the plan will not stand, and she will not be on his side.
[Daniel] [11]:[18] Then he will turn his attention to the coastlands and capture many of them, but a commander will put an end to his insolence and turn his insolence back upon him.
[Daniel] [11]:[19] He will turn back toward the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and fall, to be found no more.
[Daniel] [11]:[20] His successor will send out a tax collector to maintain the royal splendor, but within a few days he will be broken, though not in anger or in battle.
[Daniel] [11]:[21] In his place will arise a contemptible man who has not been given the honor of royalty. He will come in when the people feel secure and seize the kingdom by intrigue.
[Daniel] [11]:[22] Overwhelming forces will be swept away before him and shattered, and so will a prince of the covenant.
[Daniel] [11]:[23] After an alliance is made with him, he will act deceitfully; he will rise to power with only a few people.
[Daniel] [11]:[24] When the richest provinces feel secure, he will invade them and do what neither his fathers nor his forefathers did: he will scatter plunder, spoil, and wealth among his followers. He will plot to overthrow fortresses, but only for a time.
[Daniel] [11]:[25] With a great army he will stir up his strength and courage against the king of the South. The king of the South will wage war with a vast and powerful army, but he will not stand, for plots will be devised against him.
[Daniel] [11]:[26] Those who eat from his provisions will destroy him; his army will be swept away, and many will fall slain.
[Daniel] [11]:[27] The two kings, their hearts bent on evil, will sit at the same table and speak lies, but to no avail, for the end will still come at the appointed time.
[Daniel] [11]:[28] He will return to his own land with great wealth, his heart set against the holy covenant. He will take action against it and then return to his own land.
[Daniel] [11]:[29] At the appointed time he will invade the South again, but the outcome will not be as it was the first time, nor as it will be at the last.
[Daniel] [11]:[30] Ships of Kittim will come against him, and he will lose heart. Then he will turn back and vent his fury against the holy covenant. He will return and show favor to those who forsake the holy covenant.
[Daniel] [11]:[31] His forces will rise up to desecrate the temple fortress; they will abolish the daily sacrifice and set up the abomination that causes desolation.
[Daniel] [11]:[32] With flattery he will corrupt those who violate the covenant, but the people who know their God will stand firm and take action.
[Daniel] [11]:[33] Those among the people who are wise will instruct many, though for a time they will fall by sword and flame, by captivity and plunder.
[Daniel] [11]:[34] When they fall, they will receive a little help, and many will join them insincerely.
[Daniel] [11]:[35] Some of the wise will stumble, so that they may be refined, purified, and made spotless until the time of the end, for it will still come at the appointed time.
[Daniel] [11]:[36] The king will do as he pleases. He will exalt and magnify himself above every god and will say outrageous things against the God of gods. He will prosper until the time of wrath is completed, for what has been decreed must be done.
[Daniel] [11]:[37] He will show no regard for the gods of his fathers, or for the one desired by women, or for any god, but will magnify himself above them all.
[Daniel] [11]:[38] In their place he will honor a god of fortresses; a god unknown to his fathers he will honor with gold and silver, with precious stones and costly gifts.
[Daniel] [11]:[39] He will attack the mightiest fortresses with the help of a foreign god, and those who acknowledge him he will greatly honor. He will make them rulers over many and will distribute the land for a price.
[Daniel] [11]:[40] At the time of the end the king of the South will clash with him, and the king of the North will storm against him with chariots and horsemen and many ships. He will invade the lands and sweep through them like a flood.
[Daniel] [11]:[41] He will also invade the Beautiful Land, and many countries will fall, but these will escape his hand: Edom, Moab, and the leaders of the Ammonites.
[Daniel] [11]:[42] He will stretch out his hand against the lands, and the land of Egypt will not escape.
[Daniel] [11]:[43] He will gain control of the treasures of gold and silver and all the riches of Egypt, with the Libyans and Cushites in submission.
[Daniel] [11]:[44] But reports from the east and the north will alarm him, and he will set out in a great rage to destroy and annihilate many.
[Daniel] [11]:[45] He will pitch his royal tents between the seas at the beautiful holy mountain. Yet he will come to his end, with no one to help him.
[Daniel] [12]:[1] At that time Michael shall arise, the great prince who stands guard over your people. It will be a time of distress such as has never occurred since nations first existed until that time. But at that time your people will be delivered, everyone whose name is found written in the book.
[Daniel] [12]:[2] Many who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
[Daniel] [12]:[3] Those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament, and those who lead many to righteousness like the stars forever and ever.
[Daniel] [12]:[4] But you, Daniel, keep these words secret and seal the book until the time of the end. Many will go here and there, and knowledge will increase.
[Daniel] [12]:[5] Then I, Daniel, looked, and there stood two others, one on this bank of the river and one on the other bank.
[Daniel] [12]:[6] And one said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, "How long until the end of these wonders?"
[Daniel] [12]:[7] And I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river. He raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swore by him who lives forever that it would be for a time, times, and half a time, and that when the shattering of the power of the holy people comes to an end, all these things will be finished.
[Daniel] [12]:[8] I heard, but I did not understand. So I said, "My lord, what will be the outcome of all this?"
[Daniel] [12]:[9] He said, "Go your way, Daniel, for the words are closed up and sealed until the time of the end.
[Daniel] [12]:[10] Many shall be purified, made white, and refined, but the wicked shall act wickedly. None of the wicked will understand, but those who are wise will understand.
[Daniel] [12]:[11] From the time the daily sacrifice is taken away and the abomination that causes desolation is set up, there shall be 1,290 days.
[Daniel] [12]:[12] Blessed is the one who waits and reaches the 1,335 days.
[Daniel] [12]:[13] But you, go your way until the end. You will rest, and you will rise to receive your allotted portion at the end of the days."
[Hosea] [1]:[1] The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.
[Hosea] [1]:[2] When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, the LORD said to him: "Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and children of prostitution, for the land commits great prostitution by turning away from the LORD."
[Hosea] [1]:[3] So he went and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
[Hosea] [1]:[4] And the LORD said to him, "Name him Jezreel, for in a little while I will punish the house of Jehu for the blood shed at Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.
[Hosea] [1]:[5] On that day I will break Israel's bow in the Valley of Jezreel."
[Hosea] [1]:[6] She conceived again and bore a daughter. And the LORD said to him, "Name her No Mercy, for I will no longer show mercy to the house of Israel; I will certainly not forgive them.[^1] [^1]: Or "that I should in any way forgive them"; the Hebrew clause is difficult and has also been understood as "I will utterly take them away."
[Hosea] [1]:[7] But I will show mercy to the house of Judah, and I will save them by the LORD their God. I will not save them by bow or sword or battle, by horses or horsemen."
[Hosea] [1]:[8] After she had weaned No Mercy, she conceived and bore a son.
[Hosea] [1]:[9] And the LORD said, "Name him Not My People,[^1] for you are not my people, and I will not be your God.[^2] [^1]: Hebrew Lo-Ammi. [^2]: Hebrew "and I will not be yours"; the wording echoes the divine name revealed in Exodus 3:14.
[Hosea] [2]:[1] Yet the number of the Israelites will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted. And in the place where it was said to them, "You are not my people," it will be said to them, "Children of the living God."
[Hosea] [2]:[2] The people of Judah and the people of Israel will be gathered together; they will appoint one head over themselves and come up out of the land, for great will be the day of Jezreel.
[Hosea] [2]:[3] Say to your brothers, "My People," and to your sisters, "Shown Mercy."
[Hosea] [2]:[4] Bring charges against your mother, bring charges, for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her put away her whoring from her face and her adultery from between her breasts,
[Hosea] [2]:[5] or I will strip her naked and expose her as on the day she was born. I will make her like a wilderness, turn her into a parched land, and put her to death with thirst.
[Hosea] [2]:[6] I will show no mercy to her children, for they are the children of whoring.
[Hosea] [2]:[7] Their mother has played the whore; she who conceived them has acted shamefully. She said, "I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink."
[Hosea] [2]:[8] Therefore I will hedge up her way with thorns; I will wall her in, and she will not find her paths.
[Hosea] [2]:[9] She will chase her lovers but not overtake them; she will look for them but not find them. Then she will say, "I will go back to my first husband, for I was better off then than now."
[Hosea] [2]:[10] She did not know that it was I who gave her the grain, the new wine, and the oil, I who lavished silver on her, and gold—which they used for Baal.
[Hosea] [2]:[11] Therefore I will come back and take away my grain in its time and my new wine in its season, and I will reclaim my wool and my flax, which were given to cover her nakedness.
[Hosea] [2]:[12] Now I will uncover her shame before the eyes of her lovers, and no one will rescue her from my hand.
[Hosea] [2]:[13] I will put an end to all her rejoicing—her festivals, her new moons, her sabbaths, all her appointed feasts.
[Hosea] [2]:[14] I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees, of which she said, "These are my wages, which my lovers gave me." I will turn them into a thicket, and the wild animals will devour them.
[Hosea] [2]:[15] I will hold her to account for the days of the Baals, when she burned incense to them, decked herself with ring and jewels, and went after her lovers—but me she forgot, declares the LORD.
[Hosea] [2]:[16] Therefore I am going to allure her; I will lead her into the wilderness and speak tenderly to her heart.
[Hosea] [2]:[17] There I will give her back her vineyards and make the Valley of Achor a door of hope. There she will answer me as in the days of her youth, as on the day she came up out of the land of Egypt.
[Hosea] [2]:[18] On that day, declares the LORD, you will call me "My husband," and no longer call me "My Baal."
[Hosea] [2]:[19] I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and their names will never be invoked again.
[Hosea] [2]:[20] On that day I will make a covenant for them with the wild animals, the birds of the sky, and the creatures that crawl on the ground. Bow and sword and war I will abolish from the land, and I will let them lie down in safety.
[Hosea] [2]:[21] I will betroth you to myself forever; I will betroth you to myself in righteousness and justice, in steadfast love and mercy.
[Hosea] [2]:[22] I will betroth you to myself in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.
[Hosea] [2]:[23] On that day I will answer, declares the LORD—I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth;
[Hosea] [2]:[24] the earth will answer the grain, the new wine, and the oil, and they will answer Jezreel.
[Hosea] [2]:[25] I will sow her for myself in the land; I will show mercy to No Mercy, and I will say to Not My People, "You are my people," and he will say, "My God."
[Hosea] [3]:[1] Then the LORD said to me, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by another and is an adulteress — love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and love their raisin cakes."
[Hosea] [3]:[2] So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer and a lethek of barley.[^1] [^1]: A homer was roughly 220 liters of grain; a lethek was about half a homer.
[Hosea] [3]:[3] And I said to her, "You are to stay with me for a long time. You must not be a prostitute, and you must not belong to any other man — and I will be yours."
[Hosea] [3]:[4] For the Israelites will remain a long time without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred pillar, without ephod or household idols.
[Hosea] [3]:[5] Afterward the Israelites will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king; in the last days they will come trembling to the LORD and to his goodness.
[Hosea] [4]:[1] Hear the word of the LORD, people of Israel, for the LORD has a case against those who live in the land: There is no faithfulness, no steadfast love, no knowledge of God in the land.
[Hosea] [4]:[2] Cursing and lying, murder and stealing and adultery — they break out, and bloodshed follows bloodshed.
[Hosea] [4]:[3] That is why the land mourns and everyone living in it wastes away, together with the beasts of the field and the birds of the sky; even the fish of the sea are swept away.
[Hosea] [4]:[4] Yet let no one bring a charge, let no one accuse — for your people are like those who quarrel with a priest.
[Hosea] [4]:[5] You stumble by day, and the prophet stumbles with you by night; and I will destroy your mother.
[Hosea] [4]:[6] My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I reject you from serving me as priest; because you have forgotten the law of your God, I too will forget your children.
[Hosea] [4]:[7] The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against me; I will turn their glory into shame.
[Hosea] [4]:[8] They feed on the sin of my people and set their hearts on their guilt.
[Hosea] [4]:[9] And it will be: like people, like priest. I will punish them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.
[Hosea] [4]:[10] They will eat but not be satisfied; they will play the whore but not increase, because they have abandoned the LORD to devote themselves—
[Hosea] [4]:[11] to whoring, to wine and new wine, which steal the heart.
[Hosea] [4]:[12] My people consult a piece of wood, and their stick tells them what to do. A spirit of whoredom has led them astray; they have played the whore and deserted their God.
[Hosea] [4]:[13] They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills, under oak and poplar and terebinth, because the shade is pleasant. That is why your daughters play the whore and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.
[Hosea] [4]:[14] I will not punish your daughters when they play the whore, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, for the men themselves slip away with prostitutes and sacrifice with temple women. So a people without understanding comes to ruin.
[Hosea] [4]:[15] Though you play the whore, Israel, let Judah not become guilty. Do not go to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear, "As the LORD lives!"
[Hosea] [4]:[16] Israel is as stubborn as a stubborn heifer. Should the LORD now graze them like a lamb in an open meadow?
[Hosea] [4]:[17] Ephraim is bound to idols; leave him alone.
[Hosea] [4]:[18] When their drinking is done, they give themselves to whoring; their rulers dearly love disgrace.
[Hosea] [4]:[19] A wind has wrapped them in its wings, and they will be put to shame because of their sacrifices.
[Hosea] [5]:[1] Hear this, you priests! Pay attention, house of Israel! Listen, royal house! This judgment is against you, for you have been a snare at Mizpah, a net spread out on Tabor.
[Hosea] [5]:[2] The rebels have gone deep into slaughter, but I will discipline them all.
[Hosea] [5]:[3] I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me. Ephraim, you have played the whore; Israel is defiled.
[Hosea] [5]:[4] Their deeds will not let them return to their God, for a spirit of whoredom is within them, and they do not know the LORD.
[Hosea] [5]:[5] Israel's pride testifies against him; Israel and Ephraim stumble in their guilt, and Judah stumbles with them.
[Hosea] [5]:[6] With their flocks and their herds they will go to seek the LORD, but they will not find him; he has withdrawn from them.
[Hosea] [5]:[7] They have betrayed the LORD, for they have fathered illegitimate children. Now the new moon will devour them along with their fields.
[Hosea] [5]:[8] Blow the ram's horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah! Raise the war cry at Beth Aven: Behind you, Benjamin!
[Hosea] [5]:[9] Ephraim will become a wasteland on the day of punishment. Among the tribes of Israel I declare what is certain.
[Hosea] [5]:[10] The princes of Judah have become like those who move a boundary stone; on them I will pour out my wrath like water.
[Hosea] [5]:[11] Ephraim is oppressed, robbed of justice, because he was determined to go after filth.
[Hosea] [5]:[12] So I am like a moth to Ephraim, like rot to the house of Judah.
[Hosea] [5]:[13] When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, Ephraim went to Assyria and sent envoys to the great king. But he cannot heal you or cure your wound.
[Hosea] [5]:[14] For I will be like a lion to Ephraim, like a young lion to the house of Judah. I myself will tear them to pieces and go away; I will carry them off, and no one will rescue them.
[Hosea] [5]:[15] I will go and return to my place until they acknowledge their guilt and seek my face. In their distress they will search for me.
[Hosea] [6]:[1] Come, let us return to the LORD. He has torn us, and he will heal us; he has struck us down, and he will bind our wounds.
[Hosea] [6]:[2] After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up, that we may live before him.
[Hosea] [6]:[3] Let us know the LORD; let us press on to know him. His coming is as certain as the dawn; he will come to us like the rain, like the spring rains that water the earth.
[Hosea] [6]:[4] What shall I do with you, Ephraim? What shall I do with you, Judah? Your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that vanishes early.
[Hosea] [6]:[5] So I have hewn them down by the prophets; I have slain them with the words of my mouth, and your judgments go forth like the light.[^1] [^1]: Some ancient versions read "my judgment goes forth like the light."
[Hosea] [6]:[6] For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
