[Hosea] [6]:[8] Gilead is a city of evildoers, stained with blood.
[Hosea] [6]:[9] Like bandits lying in ambush, so is the band of priests: they murder on the road to Shechem; yes, they commit outrage.
[Hosea] [6]:[10] In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: there Ephraim plays the whore, and Israel is defiled.
[Hosea] [6]:[11] For you also, Judah, a harvest is appointed, when I restore the fortunes of my people.
[Hosea] [7]:[1] Whenever I would heal Israel, the guilt of Ephraim is uncovered, and the evils of Samaria; for they practice deceit — the thief breaks in, and raiders plunder outside in the streets.
[Hosea] [7]:[2] They never say in their hearts that I remember all their wickedness. Now their deeds surround them; they stand before my face.
[Hosea] [7]:[3] With their wickedness they delight the king, and with their lies the officials.
[Hosea] [7]:[4] They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by the baker, who stops stirring the fire while he kneads the dough and waits for it to rise.
[Hosea] [7]:[5] On the day of our king the officials sicken themselves with the heat of wine; he stretches out his hand with the mockers.
[Hosea] [7]:[6] For they draw near with hearts like an oven, while they lie in wait. All night their anger smolders; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
[Hosea] [7]:[7] They are all as hot as an oven, and they devour their rulers. All their kings have fallen; none of them calls upon me.
[Hosea] [7]:[8] Ephraim mixes himself among the peoples; Ephraim is a flat cake not turned over.
[Hosea] [7]:[9] Strangers devour his strength, and he does not know it; gray hairs are scattered upon him, and he does not know it.
[Hosea] [7]:[10] Israel's pride testifies against him, yet they do not return to the LORD their God, nor seek him, for all this.
[Hosea] [7]:[11] Ephraim has become like a dove, silly and senseless — calling to Egypt, going off to Assyria.
[Hosea] [7]:[12] As they go, I will spread my net over them; I will bring them down like birds of the sky. I will discipline them as their congregation has been told.
[Hosea] [7]:[13] Woe to them, for they have strayed from me! Ruin to them, for they have rebelled against me! I would redeem them, but they speak lies against me.
[Hosea] [7]:[14] They do not cry out to me from the heart, but wail upon their beds; they gash themselves for grain and new wine, and turn away from me.
[Hosea] [7]:[15] I trained them and strengthened their arms, yet they plot evil against me.
[Hosea] [7]:[16] They turn back, but not to the One above; they are like a slack bow. Their officials shall fall by the sword because of the rage of their tongues. For this they will be ridiculed in the land of Egypt.
[Hosea] [8]:[1] Put the trumpet to your lips! Like an eagle the enemy sweeps down on the house of the LORD, because they have broken my covenant and rebelled against my law.
[Hosea] [8]:[2] To me they cry out, "My God, we know you—we, Israel!"
[Hosea] [8]:[3] Israel has rejected what is good; an enemy will hunt him down.
[Hosea] [8]:[4] They set up kings, but not from me; they appointed princes, and I knew nothing of it. With their silver and gold they made themselves idols—only to be cut off.
[Hosea] [8]:[5] Your calf is rejected, Samaria! My anger burns against them. How long will they be unable to become clean?
[Hosea] [8]:[6] For it came from Israel; a craftsman made it, and it is no god at all. The calf of Samaria will be broken to splinters.
[Hosea] [8]:[7] For they sow the wind, and they reap the whirlwind. He has no standing grain; the sprout yields no flour. And if it should yield, strangers would swallow it down.
[Hosea] [8]:[8] Israel is swallowed up. Now they are among the nations like a vessel no one wants.
[Hosea] [8]:[9] For they have gone up to Assyria—a wild donkey wandering off alone. Ephraim has bargained for lovers.
[Hosea] [8]:[10] Though they bargain among the nations, I will now gather them in, and in a little while they will writhe under the burden of the king of princes.
[Hosea] [8]:[11] Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, and those altars have become his sinning.
[Hosea] [8]:[12] Though I write out for him the countless precepts of my law, they are treated as something foreign.
[Hosea] [8]:[13] They offer sacrifices as gifts to me and eat the meat, but the LORD takes no pleasure in them. Now he will remember their guilt and call their sins to account; they will return to Egypt.
[Hosea] [8]:[14] Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces, and Judah has multiplied fortified cities. But I will send fire upon his cities, and it will devour her citadels.
[Hosea] [9]:[1] Do not rejoice, Israel; do not exult like the nations. For you have played the whore, forsaking your God; you have loved a prostitute's wages on every threshing floor of grain.

[Hosea] [9]:[7] The days of punishment have come; the days of reckoning have arrived. Let Israel know it! The prophet is a fool, the man of the spirit is mad — because your guilt is so great and your hostility so deep.

[Hosea] [9]:[11] Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird — no birth, no pregnancy, no conception.
[Hosea] [9]:[12] Even if they raise their children, I will bereave them until not one is left. Yes, woe to them when I turn away from them!
[Hosea] [9]:[13] Ephraim, as I have seen it, was planted like Tyre in a pleasant meadow; but Ephraim must lead his children out to the slaughterer.
[Hosea] [9]:[14] Give them, LORD — what will you give? Give them a womb that miscarries and breasts that are dry.
[Hosea] [9]:[15] All their wickedness is at Gilgal; there I came to hate them. Because of their evil deeds I will drive them out of my house. I will love them no longer; all their officials are rebels.
[Hosea] [9]:[16] Ephraim is struck down; their root is withered, they bear no fruit. Even if they give birth, I will put their cherished offspring to death.
[Hosea] [9]:[17] My God will reject them because they have not listened to him, and they will be wanderers among the nations.

[Hosea] [10]:[13] But you have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice; you have eaten the fruit of lies. Because you trusted in your own way, in the multitude of your warriors,
[Hosea] [10]:[14] the roar of battle will rise among your people, and all your fortresses will be destroyed, as Shalman destroyed Beth Arbel on the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to pieces with their children.
