[Hosea] [12]:[4] In the womb he grasped his brother's heel, and in his strength he wrestled with God.
[Hosea] [12]:[5] He struggled with the angel and prevailed; he wept and pleaded for his favor. At Bethel he found him, and there he spoke with us—
[Hosea] [12]:[6] the LORD, the God of hosts; the LORD is his name.
[Hosea] [12]:[7] So you must return to your God. Hold fast to mercy and justice, and wait for your God without ceasing.
[Hosea] [12]:[8] A merchant with false scales in his hand—he loves to defraud.[fn] \n[fn] Hebrew: "Canaan," a name used for traders and merchants.
[Hosea] [12]:[9] Ephraim says, "How rich I have become! I have gained wealth for myself. In all my toil no one can find any guilt in me, any sin."
[Hosea] [12]:[10] But I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt; I will make you live in tents again, as in the days of the appointed feast.
[Hosea] [12]:[11] I spoke to the prophets; I multiplied visions, and through the prophets I gave parables.
[Hosea] [12]:[12] If Gilead is full of iniquity, they are nothing but falsehood. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls; their altars, too, are like heaps of stones on the furrows of a field.
[Hosea] [12]:[13] Jacob fled to the land of Aram; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he tended sheep.
[Hosea] [12]:[14] By a prophet the LORD brought Israel up from Egypt, and by a prophet Israel was kept.
[Hosea] [12]:[15] Ephraim has provoked him bitterly; so his Lord will leave his blood upon him and turn his disgrace back on him.
[Hosea] [13]:[1] When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel. But he became guilty through Baal, and he died.
[Hosea] [13]:[2] And now they go on sinning: they cast images for themselves from their silver, idols of their own devising, all of them the work of craftsmen. "Sacrifice to these," they say. Men kiss calves!
[Hosea] [13]:[3] Therefore they will be like the morning cloud, like the dew that vanishes early, like chaff swept from the threshing floor, like smoke from a chimney.
[Hosea] [13]:[4] But I am the LORD your God, from the land of Egypt. You know no God but me, and besides me there is no savior.
[Hosea] [13]:[5] I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of burning drought.
[Hosea] [13]:[6] When I fed them, they were satisfied; they were satisfied, and their hearts grew proud; therefore they forgot me.
[Hosea] [13]:[7] So I will be to them like a lion; like a leopard I will lurk beside the road.
[Hosea] [13]:[8] I will fall upon them like a bear robbed of her cubs and tear open the wall of their heart. There I will devour them like a lioness; a wild beast will rip them apart.
[Hosea] [13]:[9] You are destroyed, Israel, because you are against me, against your helper.
[Hosea] [13]:[10] Where now is your king, that he may save you in all your cities? Where are your rulers, of whom you said, "Give me a king and princes"?
[Hosea] [13]:[11] I gave you a king in my anger, and in my wrath I took him away.
[Hosea] [13]:[12] The guilt of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is stored away.
[Hosea] [13]:[13] The pangs of a woman in labor come upon him, but he is a son without wisdom: when the time comes, he will not present himself at the opening of the womb.
[Hosea] [13]:[14] I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death. Death, I will be your plagues! Grave, I will be your destruction! Compassion is hidden from my eyes.
[Hosea] [13]:[15] Though he flourishes among his brothers, an east wind will come, the wind of the LORD rising from the wilderness. His spring will fail, his fountain will run dry; it will plunder the treasury of every precious thing.
[Hosea] [14]:[1] Samaria will bear her guilt, for she rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their little ones will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women ripped open.
[Hosea] [14]:[2] Return, Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled because of your guilt.
[Hosea] [14]:[3] Take words with you and return to the LORD. Say to him: "Forgive all our guilt and receive us with favor, and we will offer the praise of our lips in place of bulls.
[Hosea] [14]:[4] Assyria will not save us; we will not ride on horses, and we will never again say 'Our God' to the work of our own hands. For in you the orphan finds mercy."
[Hosea] [14]:[5] I will heal their faithlessness; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned away from them.
[Hosea] [14]:[6] I will be like the dew to Israel; he will blossom like the lily and sink his roots deep like the trees of Lebanon.
[Hosea] [14]:[7] His shoots will spread out; his splendor will be like the olive tree, his fragrance like Lebanon.
[Hosea] [14]:[8] Those who dwell in his shade will return; they will flourish like grain and blossom like the vine, and his fame will be like the wine of Lebanon.
[Hosea] [14]:[9] Ephraim, what more have I to do with idols? I am the one who answers him and watches over him. I am like a flourishing cypress; from me comes your fruit.
[Hosea] [14]:[10] Whoever is wise, let him understand these things; whoever is discerning, let him know them. For the ways of the LORD are right, and the righteous walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them.
[Joel] [1]:[1] The word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel:
[Joel] [1]:[2] Hear this, you elders; listen, all who live in the land. Has anything like this happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
[Joel] [1]:[3] Tell it to your children, and let your children tell theirs, and their children the generation after them.
[Joel] [1]:[4] What the cutting locust left, the swarming locust has eaten; what the swarming locust left, the hopping locust has eaten; and what the hopping locust left, the destroying locust has eaten.
[Joel] [1]:[5] Wake up, you drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you drinkers of wine, over the sweet wine, for it is cut off from your mouth.
[Joel] [1]:[6] A nation has invaded my land, mighty and beyond number. Its teeth are the teeth of a lion; it has the fangs of a lioness.
[Joel] [1]:[7] It has laid waste my vines and splintered my fig trees; it has stripped them bare and thrown them down, leaving their branches white.
[Joel] [1]:[8] Mourn like a young woman in sackcloth, grieving for the husband of her youth.
[Joel] [1]:[9] Grain offering and drink offering are cut off from the house of the LORD; the priests, the ministers of the LORD, are in mourning.
[Joel] [1]:[10] The fields are ruined, the ground mourns, for the grain is destroyed, the new wine has dried up, the olive oil fails.
[Joel] [1]:[11] Be ashamed, you farmers; wail, you vinedressers, over the wheat and the barley, for the harvest of the field is lost.
[Joel] [1]:[12] The vine is withered and the fig tree droops; pomegranate, palm, and apple—every tree of the field is dried up. Indeed, joy has withered away from the people.
[Joel] [1]:[13] Put on sackcloth and lament, you priests; wail, you ministers of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, you ministers of my God, for grain offering and drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.
[Joel] [1]:[14] Consecrate a fast; call a solemn assembly. Gather the elders and all who live in the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
[Joel] [1]:[15] Alas for the day! For the day of the LORD is near; it comes like devastation from the Almighty.
[Joel] [1]:[16] Has not the food been cut off before our very eyes—joy and gladness from the house of our God?
[Joel] [1]:[17] The seeds shrivel under the clods; the storehouses lie desolate, the granaries are broken down, for the grain has dried up.
[Joel] [1]:[18] How the cattle groan! The herds mill about, for they have no pasture; even the flocks of sheep suffer.
[Joel] [1]:[19] To you, LORD, I call, for fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and flames have burned up every tree of the field.
[Joel] [1]:[20] Even the wild animals pant for you, for the streams of water are dried up, and fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
[Joel] [2]:[1] Blow the trumpet in Zion; sound the alarm on my holy mountain! Let all who live in the land tremble, for the day of the LORD is coming—it is near:
[Joel] [2]:[2] a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick night. Like the dawn spreading over the mountains, a vast and mighty army comes—nothing like it has ever been, and nothing like it will be again through all the generations to come.
[Joel] [2]:[3] Fire devours before them, and behind them flames blaze. Before them the land is like the garden of Eden; behind them lies a desolate wasteland. Nothing escapes them.
[Joel] [2]:[4] They look like horses; like cavalry they charge.
[Joel] [2]:[5] With a rumble like chariots they leap over the mountaintops, like the crackle of fire devouring stubble, like a mighty army drawn up for battle.
[Joel] [2]:[6] At the sight of them nations writhe in anguish; every face turns pale.
[Joel] [2]:[7] They charge like warriors; like soldiers they scale walls. Each keeps to his course and never swerves from his path.
[Joel] [2]:[8] They do not jostle one another; each marches straight ahead. They plunge through the weapons and are not stopped.
[Joel] [2]:[9] They storm the city, they run along the wall, they climb into the houses, they slip through the windows like thieves.
[Joel] [2]:[10] Before them the earth quakes, the heavens tremble; the sun and moon go dark, and the stars withhold their light.
[Joel] [2]:[11] The LORD thunders at the head of his army; his forces are beyond number, and mighty are those who carry out his word. Great is the day of the LORD, and terrible beyond measure—who can endure it?
[Joel] [2]:[12] Yet even now, declares the LORD, return to me with all your heart, with fasting and weeping and mourning.
[Joel] [2]:[13] Tear your hearts and not your garments. Return to the LORD your God, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and he relents from sending disaster.
[Joel] [2]:[14] Who knows? He may turn and relent and leave behind him a blessing—a grain offering and a drink offering for the LORD your God.
[Joel] [2]:[15] Blow the trumpet in Zion; consecrate a fast, call a solemn assembly.
[Joel] [2]:[16] Gather the people, consecrate the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children, even the infants at the breast. Let the bridegroom come out of his room and the bride from her chamber.
[Joel] [2]:[17] Let the priests, the ministers of the LORD, weep between the portico and the altar. Let them say, "Spare your people, LORD. Do not make your inheritance an object of scorn, with the nations ruling over them. Why should they say among the peoples, 'Where is their God?'"
[Joel] [2]:[18] Then the LORD became jealous for his land and took pity on his people.
[Joel] [2]:[19] The LORD answered his people: "I am sending you grain, new wine, and oil, enough to satisfy you fully; never again will I make you an object of scorn among the nations.
[Joel] [2]:[20] I will drive the northern army far from you, banishing it into a parched and desolate land—its front ranks into the eastern sea, its rear into the western sea. Its stench will rise; the reek of it will go up, for it has done great harm.
[Joel] [2]:[21] Do not be afraid, land; be glad and rejoice, for the LORD has done great things.
[Joel] [2]:[22] Do not be afraid, you animals of the field, for the pastures of the wilderness are green again. The trees bear their fruit; the fig tree and the vine yield their riches.
[Joel] [2]:[23] Be glad, people of Zion, rejoice in the LORD your God, for he has given you the autumn rain in righteousness; he pours down for you abundant rain, both the autumn and the spring rains, as before.
[Joel] [2]:[24] The threshing floors will be filled with grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
[Joel] [2]:[25] I will repay you for the years the locusts have eaten—the swarming locust, the hopper, the destroyer, the cutter—my great army that I sent against you.
[Joel] [2]:[26] You will eat until you are full and satisfied, and you will praise the name of the LORD your God, who has dealt wondrously with you. Never again will my people be put to shame.
[Joel] [2]:[27] Then you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, that I am the LORD your God and there is no other. Never again will my people be put to shame.
[Joel] [3]:[1] And afterward it will come to pass that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.
[Joel] [3]:[2] Even on the male and female servants I will pour out my Spirit in those days.
[Joel] [3]:[3] I will show wonders in the heavens and on the earth: blood and fire and columns of smoke.
[Joel] [3]:[4] The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD.
[Joel] [3]:[5] And it will be that everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved. For on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the LORD has said, even among the survivors whom the LORD calls.
[Joel] [4]:[1] For look — in those days and at that time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,
[Joel] [4]:[2] I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment with them over my people, my inheritance Israel, whom they scattered among the nations, and over my land, which they divided up.
[Joel] [4]:[3] They cast lots for my people; they traded a boy for a prostitute and sold a girl for wine, and drank it down.
[Joel] [4]:[4] And what are you to me, Tyre and Sidon, and all you regions of Philistia? Would you repay me for something? If you repay me, I will swiftly and speedily turn your payment back on your own heads.
[Joel] [4]:[5] For you took my silver and my gold, and carried my finest treasures into your temples.
[Joel] [4]:[6] You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to remove them far from their own land.
[Joel] [4]:[7] Now I am rousing them from the place where you sold them, and I will turn your payment back on your own heads.
[Joel] [4]:[8] I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hands of the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, to a nation far away — for the LORD has spoken.
[Joel] [4]:[9] Proclaim this among the nations: Prepare for war! Rouse the warriors! Let all the fighting men advance and march up.
[Joel] [4]:[10] Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weakling say, "I am a warrior."
[Joel] [4]:[11] Hurry and come, all you surrounding nations; gather yourselves there. Bring down your warriors, O LORD!
[Joel] [4]:[12] Let the nations rouse themselves and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
[Joel] [4]:[13] Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, tread, for the winepress is full; the vats overflow, for their wickedness is great.
[Joel] [4]:[14] Crowds upon crowds in the Valley of Decision! For the day of the LORD is near in the Valley of Decision.
[Joel] [4]:[15] The sun and moon grow dark, and the stars withhold their shining.
[Joel] [4]:[16] The LORD roars from Zion and thunders from Jerusalem; heaven and earth tremble. But the LORD is a refuge for his people, a stronghold for the children of Israel.
[Joel] [4]:[17] Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, and strangers will never overrun her again.
[Joel] [4]:[18] On that day the mountains will drip with new wine, the hills will flow with milk, and all the streambeds of Judah will run with water. A spring will flow from the house of the LORD and water the Valley of Acacias.[^1] [^1]: Hebrew *Nahal ha-Shittim*, "the wadi of the acacias," a dry desert ravine — a striking image of barren land made fruitful.
[Joel] [4]:[19] Egypt will become a wasteland and Edom a desolate desert, because of the violence they did to the people of Judah, shedding innocent blood in their land.
[Joel] [4]:[20] But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem through all generations.
[Joel] [4]:[21] I will avenge their blood, which I have not yet avenged. And the LORD dwells in Zion.
[Amos] [1]:[1] The words of Amos, one of the sheep breeders of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
[Amos] [1]:[2] He said: The LORD roars from Zion; from Jerusalem he raises his voice. The pastures of the shepherds wither, and the summit of Carmel dries up.
[Amos] [1]:[3] This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not take it back*—because they threshed Gilead with sledges of iron. [*Footnote: Literally "I will not turn it back"; that is, the LORD will not revoke the sentence he has decreed.]
[Amos] [1]:[4] So I will send fire against the house of Hazael, and it will devour the strongholds of Ben-hadad.
[Amos] [1]:[5] I will break the gate bar of Damascus and cut off the ruler of the Valley of Aven and the one who holds the scepter in Beth-eden, and the people of Aram will go into exile to Kir, says the LORD.
[Amos] [1]:[6] This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Gaza, and for four, I will not take it back—because they carried a whole people into exile to hand them over to Edom.
[Amos] [1]:[7] So I will send fire against the wall of Gaza, and it will devour her strongholds.
[Amos] [1]:[8] I will cut off the ruler of Ashdod and the one who holds the scepter in Ashkelon; I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish, says the Lord GOD.
[Amos] [1]:[9] This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Tyre, and for four, I will not take it back—because they handed over a whole people as captives to Edom and did not remember the covenant of brothers.
[Amos] [1]:[10] So I will send fire against the wall of Tyre, and it will devour her strongholds.
[Amos] [1]:[11] This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not take it back—because he pursued his brother with the sword and stifled all compassion, his anger tearing without ceasing, his fury kept forever.
[Amos] [1]:[12] So I will send fire against Teman, and it will devour the strongholds of Bozrah.
[Amos] [1]:[13] This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of the Ammonites, and for four, I will not take it back—because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead in order to enlarge their border.
[Amos] [1]:[14] So I will kindle fire against the wall of Rabbah, and it will devour her strongholds, with a war cry on the day of battle, with a whirlwind on the day of the storm.
[Amos] [1]:[15] Their king will go into exile,* he and his officials together, says the LORD. [*Footnote: Or "Milcom," the national god of Ammon; the Hebrew form can be read either way.]
[Amos] [2]:[1] This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not relent — because they burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.
[Amos] [2]:[2] So I will send fire against Moab, and it will devour the fortresses of Kerioth. Moab will die amid the uproar, amid war cries and the blast of the ram's horn.
[Amos] [2]:[3] I will cut off the judge from her midst, and kill all her officials with him, declares the LORD.
[Amos] [2]:[4] This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not relent — because they rejected the law of the LORD and did not keep his statutes, and their lies led them astray, the same lies their fathers followed.
[Amos] [2]:[5] So I will send fire against Judah, and it will devour the fortresses of Jerusalem.
[Amos] [2]:[6] This is what the LORD says: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not relent — because they sell the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals.
[Amos] [2]:[7] They trample the heads of the poor into the dust of the earth and push the humble out of the way. Father and son go in to the same young woman, and so profane my holy name.
[Amos] [2]:[8] They stretch out beside every altar on garments taken in pledge, and in the house of their God they drink wine bought with fines.
[Amos] [2]:[9] Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them, though he was as tall as the cedars and as strong as the oaks. I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.
[Amos] [2]:[10] It was I who brought you up out of the land of Egypt and led you forty years through the wilderness, to take possession of the land of the Amorite.
[Amos] [2]:[11] I raised up prophets from among your sons and Nazirites from among your young men. Is this not so, people of Israel? declares the LORD.
[Amos] [2]:[12] But you made the Nazirites drink wine, and you commanded the prophets: Do not prophesy!
[Amos] [2]:[13] Now I will press you down where you stand, as a cart is pressed down when it is loaded with sheaves.
[Amos] [2]:[14] The swift will find no escape, the strong will not hold on to his strength, and the warrior will not save his life.
[Amos] [2]:[15] The archer will not stand his ground, the fleet of foot will not get away, and the horseman will not save his life.
[Amos] [2]:[16] Even the bravest of the warriors will flee naked on that day, declares the LORD.
[Amos] [3]:[1] Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, people of Israel — against the whole family I brought up out of the land of Egypt:
[Amos] [3]:[2] You alone have I known of all the families of the earth; therefore I will call you to account for all your iniquities.
[Amos] [3]:[3] Do two walk together unless they have agreed to meet?
[Amos] [3]:[4] Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey? Does a young lion growl from his den unless he has caught something?
[Amos] [3]:[5] Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground where no snare is set for it? Does a trap spring up from the earth when it has caught nothing at all?
[Amos] [3]:[6] If a ram's horn sounds in a city, do the people not tremble? If disaster comes to a city, has the LORD not done it?
[Amos] [3]:[7] Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing his counsel to his servants the prophets.
[Amos] [3]:[8] The lion has roared — who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken — who can but prophesy?
[Amos] [3]:[9] Proclaim it over the citadels of Ashdod and over the citadels in the land of Egypt, and say: Gather on the mountains of Samaria and see the great turmoil within her and the oppression in her midst.
[Amos] [3]:[10] They do not know how to do what is right, declares the LORD — those who store up violence and plunder in their citadels.
[Amos] [3]:[11] Therefore, this is what the Lord GOD says: An enemy will surround the land; he will pull down your defenses, and your citadels will be plundered.
[Amos] [3]:[12] This is what the LORD says: As a shepherd rescues from the lion's mouth two legs or a scrap of an ear, so shall the people of Israel be rescued — those who sit in Samaria on the edge of a bed, on the corner of a couch.
[Amos] [3]:[13] Hear this and testify against the house of Jacob, declares the Lord GOD, the God of hosts:
[Amos] [3]:[14] For on the day I punish Israel for its transgressions, I will also punish the altars of Bethel; the horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.
[Amos] [3]:[15] I will strike down the winter house along with the summer house; the houses of ivory will perish, and many houses will come to an end, declares the LORD.
[Amos] [4]:[1] Hear this word, you cows of Bashan who live on Mount Samaria, you who oppress the poor and crush the needy, who say to your husbands, "Bring us something to drink!"
[Amos] [4]:[2] The Lord GOD has sworn by his holiness: Days are coming upon you when you will be carried off with hooks, the last of you with fishhooks.
[Amos] [4]:[3] You will go out through breaches in the wall, each woman straight ahead of her, and you will be cast out toward Harmon, declares the LORD.
[Amos] [4]:[4] Go to Bethel and sin; go to Gilgal and sin all the more! Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every third day.
[Amos] [4]:[5] Burn leavened bread as a thank offering, proclaim your freewill offerings for all to hear—for this is what you love, people of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.
[Amos] [4]:[6] I gave you empty stomachs in all your cities and a lack of bread in all your places, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
[Amos] [4]:[7] I also withheld the rain from you when the harvest was still three months away. I sent rain on one city and withheld it from another. One field was watered, while another withered for lack of rain.
[Amos] [4]:[8] People from two or three cities staggered to another city for water but were not satisfied, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
[Amos] [4]:[9] I struck you with blight and mildew; the locust devoured your many gardens and vineyards, your fig trees and olive trees, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
[Amos] [4]:[10] I sent plagues among you as I did to Egypt; I killed your young men with the sword, and your horses were carried away captive. I made the stench of your camps rise into your nostrils, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
[Amos] [4]:[11] I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. You were like a charred stick snatched from the fire, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
[Amos] [4]:[12] Therefore this is what I will do to you, Israel. Because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel!
[Amos] [4]:[13] For behold, he who forms the mountains and creates the wind, who declares to man his thoughts, who makes the dawn and the darkness, and treads upon the heights of the earth—the LORD, the God of hosts, is his name.
[Amos] [5]:[1] Hear this word that I raise over you as a lament, house of Israel:
[Amos] [5]:[2] Fallen is the virgin Israel, never to rise again; abandoned on her own soil, with no one to lift her up.
[Amos] [5]:[3] For this is what the Lord GOD says: The city that marches out a thousand strong will have a hundred left, and the one that marches out a hundred strong will have ten left, for the house of Israel.
[Amos] [5]:[4] For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel: Seek me and live!
[Amos] [5]:[5] Do not seek Bethel, do not go to Gilgal, do not journey to Beersheba. For Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing.
[Amos] [5]:[6] Seek the LORD and live, or he will break out like fire against the house of Joseph—it will devour, and there will be no one at Bethel to put it out.
[Amos] [5]:[7] You who turn justice into bitterness and throw righteousness to the ground!
[Amos] [5]:[8] He it is who made the Pleiades and Orion, who turns deep darkness into morning and darkens the day into night. He summons the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the earth—the LORD is his name.
[Amos] [5]:[9] He brings ruin on the strong, and destruction comes upon the fortress.
[Amos] [5]:[10] They hate the one who reproves in the gate, and they despise the one who speaks with integrity.
[Amos] [5]:[11] Therefore, because you trample on the poor and extort grain from them, you have built houses of cut stone, but you will not live in them; you have planted lovely vineyards, but you will not drink their wine.
[Amos] [5]:[12] For I know how many your transgressions are, how great your sins: you oppress the righteous, you take bribes, and you turn the needy away in the gate.
[Amos] [5]:[13] Therefore the prudent keep silent in such a time, for it is an evil time.
[Amos] [5]:[14] Seek good, not evil, that you may live. Then the LORD, the God of hosts, will be with you, just as you claim.
[Amos] [5]:[15] Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the gate. Perhaps then the LORD, the God of hosts, will show mercy to the remnant of Joseph.
[Amos] [5]:[16] Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of hosts, the Lord, says: In every public square there will be wailing, and in every street they will cry, "Alas! Alas!" They will call the farmers to mourning and the singers of dirges to lamentation.
[Amos] [5]:[17] There will be wailing in every vineyard, for I will pass through your midst, says the LORD.
[Amos] [5]:[18] Woe to you who long for the day of the LORD! What will that day be for you? It will be darkness, not light.
[Amos] [5]:[19] It will be as when a man flees from a lion, only to meet a bear; or he comes home, rests his hand against the wall, and a snake bites him.
[Amos] [5]:[20] Will not the day of the LORD be darkness and not light, gloom without a ray of brightness?
[Amos] [5]:[21] I hate, I despise your festivals; I take no delight in your solemn assemblies.
[Amos] [5]:[22] Even if you bring me burnt offerings, I will not accept them; your grain offerings give me no pleasure, and I will not look at the fellowship offerings of your fattened cattle.
[Amos] [5]:[23] Take away from me the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the music of your harps.
[Amos] [5]:[24] But let justice roll on like water, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.
[Amos] [5]:[25] Did you bring me sacrifices and offerings those forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?
[Amos] [5]:[26] Yet you carried Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star of your god, which you made for yourselves.
[Amos] [5]:[27] So I will send you into exile beyond Damascus, says the LORD, whose name is the God of hosts.
[Amos] [6]:[1] Woe to those who lounge at ease in Zion, and to those who feel secure on Mount Samaria — you notable men of the foremost nation, to whom the house of Israel comes!
[Amos] [6]:[2] Cross over to Calneh and look; go on from there to great Hamath, then down to Gath of the Philistines. Are they better than these kingdoms of yours? Is their territory greater than yours?
[Amos] [6]:[3] You push away the day of disaster, yet you bring the reign of violence near.
[Amos] [6]:[4] You lie on beds inlaid with ivory and sprawl on your couches; you eat lambs from the flock and calves from the fattening stall.
[Amos] [6]:[5] You improvise to the sound of the harp and, like David, invent instruments for your songs.
[Amos] [6]:[6] You drink wine by the bowlful and anoint yourselves with the finest oils, but you do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph.
[Amos] [6]:[7] Therefore you will be the first to go into exile, and your sprawling revelry will come to an end.
[Amos] [6]:[8] The Lord GOD has sworn by himself — this is the declaration of the LORD, the God of hosts: I detest the pride of Jacob and hate his citadels; I will hand over the city and everything in it.
[Amos] [6]:[9] And if ten men are left in a single house, they too will die.
[Amos] [6]:[10] When a relative — the one who burns the bodies — comes to carry the bones out of the house, he will ask whoever is in the innermost room, "Is anyone else with you?" and the answer will come, "No one." Then he will say, "Silence! The name of the LORD is not to be spoken."
[Amos] [6]:[11] For look, the LORD is giving the command: he will smash the great house to rubble and the small house to pieces.
[Amos] [6]:[12] Do horses gallop over rock? Does anyone plow it with oxen? Yet you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness.
[Amos] [6]:[13] You rejoice over Lo-debar, saying, "Have we not taken Karnaim by our own strength?" [Footnote: The Hebrew plays on two place names captured by Israel: Lo-debar sounds like "nothing," and Karnaim means "horns," a symbol of strength.]
[Amos] [6]:[14] But look, I am raising up a nation against you, house of Israel — this is the declaration of the LORD, the God of hosts — and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of the Arabah.
[Amos] [7]:[1] This is what the Lord GOD showed me: he was forming a swarm of locusts just as the late crop was beginning to come up—the late crop that follows the king's mowings.
[Amos] [7]:[2] And when they had finished devouring the vegetation of the land, I said, "Lord GOD, forgive, I pray! How can Jacob stand? He is so small."
[Amos] [7]:[3] The LORD relented concerning this. "It shall not be," said the LORD.
[Amos] [7]:[4] This is what the Lord GOD showed me: behold, the Lord GOD was calling for judgment by fire, and it devoured the great deep and began to devour the farmland.
[Amos] [7]:[5] Then I said, "Lord GOD, stop, I pray! How can Jacob stand? He is so small."
[Amos] [7]:[6] The LORD relented concerning this. "This also shall not be," said the Lord GOD.
[Amos] [7]:[7] This is what he showed me: the Lord was standing by a wall built with a plumb line, and in his hand was a plumb line.
[Amos] [7]:[8] And the LORD said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "See, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of my people Israel; I will spare them no longer.
[Amos] [7]:[9] The high places of Isaac shall be laid waste and the sanctuaries of Israel shall lie in ruins, and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."
[Amos] [7]:[10] Then Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent word to Jeroboam king of Israel: "Amos is plotting against you in the very midst of the house of Israel. The land cannot endure all his words.
[Amos] [7]:[11] For this is what Amos has said: 'Jeroboam shall die by the sword, and Israel shall surely be led away into exile from its own land.'"
[Amos] [7]:[12] And Amaziah said to Amos, "Go away, seer! Flee to the land of Judah. Eat your bread there, and prophesy there.
[Amos] [7]:[13] But never prophesy again at Bethel, for it is the king's sanctuary and a royal temple."
[Amos] [7]:[14] Then Amos answered Amaziah, "I am no prophet, nor the son of a prophet. I am a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.
[Amos] [7]:[15] But the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to my people Israel.'
[Amos] [7]:[16] Now then, hear the word of the LORD. You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel; do not preach against the house of Isaac.'
[Amos] [7]:[17] Therefore this is what the LORD says: 'Your wife shall become a prostitute in the city, and your sons and daughters shall fall by the sword. Your land shall be divided up with a measuring line, and you yourself shall die in an unclean land, and Israel shall surely be led away into exile from its own land.'"
[Amos] [8]:[1] This is what the Lord GOD showed me: a basket of summer fruit.
[Amos] [8]:[2] He asked, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the LORD said to me, "The end has come for my people Israel; I will never again pass them by." [Footnote: The Hebrew word for "summer fruit" (qayits) sounds like the word for "end" (qets).]
[Amos] [8]:[3] "On that day the songs of the palace will turn to wailing," declares the Lord GOD. "Corpses will be everywhere—flung out in silence." [Footnote: Or "the songs of the temple."]
[Amos] [8]:[4] Hear this, you who trample the needy and do away with the poor of the land,
[Amos] [8]:[5] saying, "When will the New Moon be over, so we can sell grain? When will the Sabbath end, so we can open the wheat market—shrinking the measure, enlarging the shekel weight, cheating with crooked scales,
[Amos] [8]:[6] buying the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and selling the sweepings with the wheat?"
[Amos] [8]:[7] The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob: "I will never forget a single thing they have done.
[Amos] [8]:[8] "Will not the land tremble for this, and everyone who lives in it mourn? The whole land will rise like the Nile, churn and sink again like the river of Egypt."
[Amos] [8]:[9] "On that day," declares the Lord GOD, "I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.
[Amos] [8]:[10] I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into laments. I will put sackcloth on every waist and shave every head. I will make it like mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.
[Amos] [8]:[11] The days are coming," declares the Lord GOD, "when I will send a famine on the land—not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD.
[Amos] [8]:[12] People will stagger from sea to sea and wander from north to east, searching for the word of the LORD, but they will not find it.
[Amos] [8]:[13] On that day the beautiful young women and the young men will faint from thirst—
[Amos] [8]:[14] those who swear by the guilt of Samaria, saying, 'As surely as your god lives, Dan,' and, 'As surely as the way of Beersheba lives.' They will fall, never to rise again."
[Amos] [9]:[1] I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and he said: Strike the capitals, so that the thresholds shake; shatter them on the heads of them all, and what is left of them I will kill with the sword. Not one of them shall flee away, not one of them shall escape.
[Amos] [9]:[2] Though they dig down to Sheol, from there my hand shall take them; though they climb up to heaven, from there I will bring them down.
[Amos] [9]:[3] Though they hide on the summit of Carmel, from there I will search them out and seize them; though they conceal themselves from my sight on the floor of the sea, from there I will command the serpent, and it shall bite them.
[Amos] [9]:[4] Though they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword, and it shall kill them. I will fix my eyes on them for harm and not for good.
[Amos] [9]:[5] The Lord GOD of hosts—he touches the earth and it melts, and all who dwell in it mourn; all of it rises like the Nile and sinks again like the Nile of Egypt.
[Amos] [9]:[6] He builds his upper chambers in the heavens and founds his vault upon the earth; he calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the earth—the LORD is his name.
[Amos] [9]:[7] Are you not like the Cushites to me, O people of Israel? declares the LORD. Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor and the Arameans from Kir?
[Amos] [9]:[8] Behold, the eyes of the Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom, and I will wipe it from the face of the earth—except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, declares the LORD.
[Amos] [9]:[9] For behold, I will give the command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations as grain is shaken in a sieve, and not a pebble shall fall to the ground.
[Amos] [9]:[10] All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword, those who say, "Disaster will not overtake us or meet us."
[Amos] [9]:[11] On that day I will raise up the fallen booth of David; I will repair its breaches and raise up its ruins and rebuild it as in the days of old,
[Amos] [9]:[12] so that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations that are called by my name, declares the LORD, who does this.
[Amos] [9]:[13] Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes shall overtake the one who sows the seed; the mountains shall drip sweet wine, and all the hills shall flow with it.
[Amos] [9]:[14] I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel; they shall rebuild the ruined cities and live in them, plant vineyards and drink their wine, make gardens and eat their fruit.
[Amos] [9]:[15] I will plant them on their own soil, and they shall never again be uprooted from the land I have given them, says the LORD your God.
[Obadiah] [1]:[1] The vision of Obadiah. This is what the Lord GOD says concerning Edom: We have heard a report from the LORD, and a messenger has been sent among the nations: "Rise up! Let us go to war against her!"
[Obadiah] [1]:[2] See, I will make you least among the nations; you will be utterly despised.
[Obadiah] [1]:[3] The arrogance of your heart has deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rock and make the heights your home, who say to yourself, "Who can bring me down to the ground?"
[Obadiah] [1]:[4] Though you soar like the eagle and set your nest among the stars, even from there I will bring you down, declares the LORD.
[Obadiah] [1]:[5] If thieves came to you, if robbers came by night—how you will be ruined!—would they not steal only what they wanted? If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave a few grapes behind?
[Obadiah] [1]:[6] How Esau will be ransacked, his hidden treasures hunted out!
[Obadiah] [1]:[7] All your allies will drive you to the border; those at peace with you will deceive you and overpower you. Those who eat your bread will set a trap for you, and you will not see it coming.
[Obadiah] [1]:[8] On that day, declares the LORD, will I not destroy the wise men of Edom, and understanding from the mountain of Esau?
[Obadiah] [1]:[9] Your warriors will be filled with terror, Teman, so that everyone will be cut off from the mountain of Esau by the slaughter.
[Obadiah] [1]:[10] Because of the violence you did to your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.
[Obadiah] [1]:[11] On the day you stood aside, on the day strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem—you were like one of them.
[Obadiah] [1]:[12] Do not gloat over your brother on the day of his misfortune; do not rejoice over the people of Judah on the day of their ruin; do not boast on the day of their distress.
[Obadiah] [1]:[13] Do not enter the gate of my people on the day of their disaster; do not gloat over their suffering on the day of their disaster; do not lay hands on their wealth on the day of their disaster.
[Obadiah] [1]:[14] Do not wait at the crossroads to cut down their fugitives; do not hand over their survivors on the day of distress.
[Obadiah] [1]:[15] For the day of the LORD is near for all the nations. As you have done, so it will be done to you; your deeds will come back on your own head.
[Obadiah] [1]:[16] For as you drank on my holy mountain, so all the nations will drink without ceasing. They will drink and stagger, and they will be as though they had never been.
[Obadiah] [1]:[17] But on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be holy, and the house of Jacob will possess its inheritance.
[Obadiah] [1]:[18] The house of Jacob will be a fire and the house of Joseph a flame; the house of Esau will be stubble. They will set it ablaze and consume it, and there will be no survivor left of the house of Esau—for the LORD has spoken.
[Obadiah] [1]:[19] Those from the Negev will possess the mountain of Esau, and those from the foothills the land of the Philistines. They will possess the fields of Ephraim and Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.
[Obadiah] [1]:[20] This company of exiles of Israel will possess the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath, and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad will possess the cities of the Negev.
[Obadiah] [1]:[21] Deliverers will go up on Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau, and the kingdom will belong to the LORD.
[Jonah] [1]:[1] The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai:
[Jonah] [1]:[2] "Get up, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry out against it, for their wickedness has risen up before me."
[Jonah] [1]:[3] But Jonah got up to flee to Tarshish, away from the LORD. He went down to Joppa, found a ship bound for Tarshish, paid the fare, and boarded it to sail with them to Tarshish, away from the LORD.
[Jonah] [1]:[4] Then the LORD hurled a great wind upon the sea, and such a violent storm arose that the ship threatened to break apart.
[Jonah] [1]:[5] The sailors were terrified, and each cried out to his own god. They threw the cargo overboard to lighten the ship. But Jonah had gone below deck, where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.
[Jonah] [1]:[6] The captain came to him and said, "How can you sleep? Get up and call on your god! Perhaps the god will take notice of us, and we will not perish."
[Jonah] [1]:[7] Then the sailors said to one another, "Come, let us cast lots to find out who is to blame for this disaster." They cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
[Jonah] [1]:[8] So they said to him, "Tell us, who is responsible for this trouble that has come upon us? What is your business? Where do you come from? What is your country, and from what people are you?"
[Jonah] [1]:[9] He answered, "I am a Hebrew, and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land."
[Jonah] [1]:[10] At this the men were seized with great fear and said to him, "What have you done?" For they knew he was fleeing from the LORD—he had told them so.
[Jonah] [1]:[11] Then they asked him, "What should we do to you to make the sea calm down for us?" For the sea was growing wilder and wilder.
[Jonah] [1]:[12] "Pick me up and throw me into the sea," he answered, "and the sea will grow calm for you. I know that it is my fault that this great storm has come upon you."
[Jonah] [1]:[13] Instead, the men rowed hard to get back to land, but they could not, for the sea grew wilder and wilder against them.
[Jonah] [1]:[14] Then they called out to the LORD: "Please, LORD, do not let us perish for taking this man's life. Do not hold us guilty of shedding innocent blood, for you, LORD, have done as you pleased."
[Jonah] [1]:[15] Then they picked Jonah up and threw him into the sea, and the raging sea grew calm.
[Jonah] [1]:[16] Then the men were filled with great fear of the LORD, and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows to him.
[Jonah] [2]:[1] Then the LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
[Jonah] [2]:[2] From the belly of the fish Jonah prayed to the LORD his God:
[Jonah] [2]:[3] "In my distress I called to the LORD, and he answered me. From the belly of Sheol I cried for help, and you heard my voice.
[Jonah] [2]:[4] You hurled me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the currents swirled around me; all your breakers and your waves swept over me.
[Jonah] [2]:[5] I said, 'I have been driven from your sight; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.'
[Jonah] [2]:[6] The waters closed in over me, threatening my life; the deep surrounded me; seaweed was wrapped around my head.
[Jonah] [2]:[7] I sank down to the roots of the mountains; the earth barred me in forever. But you brought my life up from the pit, O LORD my God.
[Jonah] [2]:[8] As my life was ebbing away, I remembered the LORD, and my prayer came to you, to your holy temple.
[Jonah] [2]:[9] Those who cling to worthless idols forsake the steadfast love that would be theirs.
[Jonah] [2]:[10] But I will sacrifice to you with a voice of thanksgiving. What I have vowed I will fulfill. Salvation belongs to the LORD!"
[Jonah] [2]:[11] And the LORD commanded the fish, and it vomited Jonah out onto dry land.
[Jonah] [3]:[1] Then the word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:
[Jonah] [3]:[2] "Get up, go to Nineveh, that great city, and proclaim to it the message I give you."
[Jonah] [3]:[3] So Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, as the LORD had said. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, a three days' journey across.
[Jonah] [3]:[4] Jonah began to make his way into the city, a day's journey in, and he called out, "Forty days more, and Nineveh will be overthrown!"
[Jonah] [3]:[5] And the people of Nineveh believed God. They called a fast, and everyone from the greatest to the least put on sackcloth.
[Jonah] [3]:[6] When the news reached the king of Nineveh, he rose from his throne, laid aside his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat down in the ashes.
[Jonah] [3]:[7] Then he had this proclamation cried out in Nineveh: "By decree of the king and his nobles: No person or animal, no herd or flock, is to taste anything. They shall not graze, and they shall not drink water.
[Jonah] [3]:[8] Let people and animals alike cover themselves with sackcloth. Let them cry out to God with all their strength, and let each one turn from his evil way and from the violence in his hands.
[Jonah] [3]:[9] Who knows? God may yet turn and relent; he may turn away from his burning anger, so that we do not perish.
[Jonah] [3]:[10] When God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil way, he relented concerning the disaster he had threatened to bring on them, and he did not do it.
[Jonah] [4]:[1] But this was deeply displeasing to Jonah, and he became angry.
[Jonah] [4]:[2] He prayed to the LORD and said, "Please, LORD, isn't this exactly what I said while I was still in my own country? That is why I fled at once toward Tarshish. I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and that you relent from sending disaster.
[Jonah] [4]:[3] "So now, LORD, take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live."
[Jonah] [4]:[4] But the LORD said, "Is it right for you to be angry?"
[Jonah] [4]:[5] Then Jonah went out of the city and sat down east of it. There he made himself a shelter and sat under it in the shade, waiting to see what would happen to the city.
[Jonah] [4]:[6] And the LORD God appointed a plant, and it grew up over Jonah to give shade for his head and relieve his discomfort. Jonah was overjoyed at the plant.
[Jonah] [4]:[7] But at dawn the next day God appointed a worm, and it attacked the plant so that it withered.
[Jonah] [4]:[8] And when the sun rose, God appointed a scorching east wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head until he grew faint. He begged for death and said, "It is better for me to die than to live."
[Jonah] [4]:[9] Then God said to Jonah, "Is it right for you to be angry about the plant?" And he answered, "Yes, I have every right to be angry—angry enough to die."
[Jonah] [4]:[10] But the LORD said, "You cared about this plant, which you did not labor for and did not make grow, which came up overnight and perished overnight.
[Jonah] [4]:[11] Should I not then care about Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand people who do not know their right hand from their left—and also many animals?"
[Micah] [1]:[1] The word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah — what he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
[Micah] [1]:[2] Hear, all you peoples; listen, O earth, and all that fills it. Let the Lord GOD be a witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.
[Micah] [1]:[3] Look — the LORD is coming out from his place; he comes down and treads on the high places of the earth.
[Micah] [1]:[4] The mountains melt beneath him and the valleys split open, like wax before the fire, like water poured down a slope.
[Micah] [1]:[5] All this is for the transgression of Jacob, for the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah? Are they not Jerusalem?
[Micah] [1]:[6] So I will make Samaria a heap of rubble in the open field, a place for planting vineyards. I will pour her stones into the valley and lay bare her foundations.
[Micah] [1]:[7] All her carved images will be shattered, all her wages burned in the fire; I will make all her idols a wasteland. She gathered them from the wages of a prostitute, and to the wages of a prostitute they shall return.
[Micah] [1]:[8] For this I will lament and wail; I will go stripped and naked. I will howl like the jackals and mourn like the ostriches.
[Micah] [1]:[9] For her wounds are incurable; the blow has come to Judah, reaching the gate of my people, all the way to Jerusalem.
[Micah] [1]:[10] Tell it not in Gath; do not weep at all. In Beth-leaphrah, house of dust, roll yourself in the dust.
[Micah] [1]:[11] Pass on your way, you who live in Shaphir, in naked shame. Those who live in Zaanan do not come out. Beth-ezel is in mourning; its support is taken from you.
[Micah] [1]:[12] The people of Maroth writhe in hope of good, for disaster has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.
[Micah] [1]:[13] Harness the horses to the chariot, you who live in Lachish. You were the beginning of sin for Daughter Zion, for in you the transgressions of Israel were found.
[Micah] [1]:[14] Therefore you shall give parting gifts to Moresheth-gath. The houses of Achzib will prove a deception to the kings of Israel.
[Micah] [1]:[15] I will yet bring a conqueror against you, you who live in Mareshah. The glory of Israel will come as far as Adullam.
[Micah] [1]:[16] Shave your head and cut off your hair for the children who were your delight; make yourself as bald as the vulture, for they have gone from you into exile.
[Micah] [2]:[1] Woe to those who devise iniquity, who work out evil on their beds! At dawn they carry it out, because they have the power to do it.
[Micah] [2]:[2] They covet fields and seize them, houses too, and take them away. They oppress a man and his household, a person and his inheritance.
[Micah] [2]:[3] Therefore this is what the LORD says: See, I am planning disaster against this family, and you will not slip your necks out of it. You will no longer walk with your heads held high, for it will be a time of disaster.
[Micah] [2]:[4] On that day they will taunt you with this saying, and wail this bitter lament: "We are utterly ruined! He exchanges the portion of my people; he takes it away from me and parcels out our fields to the traitor."
[Micah] [2]:[5] Therefore you will have no one in the assembly of the LORD to cast the measuring line for an allotment.
[Micah] [2]:[6] "Stop preaching!" they preach. "Do not preach about such things; disgrace will never overtake us."
[Micah] [2]:[7] Should this be said, house of Jacob? Is the Spirit of the LORD short of patience? Are these his doings? Do my words not bring good to the one who walks uprightly?
[Micah] [2]:[8] But lately you have risen up against my people as an enemy. You strip the robe from those who pass by in peace, from those returning from war.
[Micah] [2]:[9] You drive the women of my people from their pleasant homes; you take away my glory from their children forever.
[Micah] [2]:[10] Get up and go, for this is no place of rest! Because it is defiled, it brings ruin—a grievous ruin.
[Micah] [2]:[11] If a man full of wind and falsehood should lie and say, "I will preach to you of wine and strong drink," he would be just the preacher for this people!
[Micah] [2]:[12] I will surely gather all of you, Jacob; I will surely bring together the remnant of Israel. I will place them like sheep in a fold, like a flock in its pasture—a noisy throng of people.
[Micah] [2]:[13] The one who breaks open the way goes up before them; they break through the gate and pass out through it. Their king passes on before them, and the LORD at their head.
[Micah] [3]:[1] And I said: Listen, you leaders of Jacob, you rulers of the house of Israel! Is it not your business to know what is just?
[Micah] [3]:[2] Yet you hate good and love evil. You tear the skin from my people and the flesh from their bones.
[Micah] [3]:[3] You devour my people's flesh, strip off their skin, break their bones in pieces, and chop them up like meat for the pot, like flesh in the cauldron.
[Micah] [3]:[4] Then they will cry out to the LORD, but he will not answer them. He will hide his face from them at that time, because of the evil they have done.
[Micah] [3]:[5] This is what the LORD says against the prophets who lead my people astray: when they have something to sink their teeth into, they proclaim peace; but against the one who puts nothing in their mouths, they declare holy war.
[Micah] [3]:[6] Therefore night will come over you—no more visions; darkness will fall on you—no more divining. The sun will set on these prophets, and the day will turn black over them.
[Micah] [3]:[7] The seers will be put to shame and the diviners disgraced. They will all cover their lips, because there is no answer from God.
[Micah] [3]:[8] But as for me, I am filled with power by the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his rebellion, to Israel his sin.
[Micah] [3]:[9] Hear this, you leaders of the house of Jacob, you rulers of the house of Israel, who despise justice and twist everything that is right,
[Micah] [3]:[10] who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with wrongdoing.
[Micah] [3]:[11] Her leaders judge for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, her prophets divine for silver—and still they lean on the LORD and say, "Is the LORD not among us? No disaster can touch us."
[Micah] [3]:[12] Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble, and the temple mount a wooded height.
[Micah] [4]:[1] In the last days the mountain of the LORD's house will stand firm as the highest of the mountains, lifted above the hills, and the peoples will stream to it.
[Micah] [4]:[2] Many nations will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, that he may teach us his ways and that we may walk in his paths." For instruction goes out from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
[Micah] [4]:[3] He will judge between many peoples and settle disputes for strong nations far and wide. They will hammer their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation will not lift up sword against nation, nor will they train for war anymore.
[Micah] [4]:[4] Everyone will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, and no one will make him afraid, for the mouth of the LORD of hosts has spoken.
[Micah] [4]:[5] Though all the peoples walk, each in the name of its god, we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.
[Micah] [4]:[6] On that day, declares the LORD, I will gather the lame and bring together the scattered, those I have afflicted.
[Micah] [4]:[7] I will make the lame a remnant and the exiled a mighty nation, and the LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion from now on and forever.
[Micah] [4]:[8] And you, watchtower of the flock, stronghold of the daughter of Zion, to you it will come—the former dominion will return, the kingship of the daughter of Jerusalem.
[Micah] [4]:[9] Now why do you cry aloud? Is there no king among you? Has your counselor perished, that anguish grips you like a woman in labor?
[Micah] [4]:[10] Writhe and groan, daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor, for now you must leave the city and camp in the open field. You will go to Babylon; there you will be rescued, there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
[Micah] [4]:[11] Now many nations are gathered against you, saying, "Let her be defiled, and let our eyes gloat over Zion."
[Micah] [4]:[12] But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD; they do not understand his plan, that he has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.
[Micah] [4]:[13] Rise and thresh, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron and your hooves bronze, and you will crush many peoples. You will devote their unjust gain to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.
[Micah] [4]:[14] Now marshal your troops, daughter of troops! A siege is laid against us. With a rod they strike the judge of Israel on the cheek.
[Micah] [5]:[1] But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, too small to be counted among the clans of Judah, from you shall come forth for me one who is to rule in Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient days.
[Micah] [5]:[2] Therefore he will give them up until the time when she who is in labor has given birth; then the rest of his brothers will return to the people of Israel.
[Micah] [5]:[3] He will stand and shepherd his flock in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God. And they will dwell secure, for then his greatness will reach to the ends of the earth.
[Micah] [5]:[4] And he himself will be peace. When Assyria invades our land and treads on our palaces, we will raise against him seven shepherds, eight leaders of men.
[Micah] [5]:[5] They will shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword, the land of Nimrod at its gates. He will deliver us from Assyria when it invades our land and tramples our borders.
[Micah] [5]:[6] Then the remnant of Jacob will be in the midst of many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers on the grass, which wait for no one and linger for no mortal.
[Micah] [5]:[7] The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which tramples and tears as it passes through, and no one can rescue.
[Micah] [5]:[8] Your hand will be raised over your foes, and all your enemies will be cut off.
[Micah] [5]:[9] On that day, declares the LORD, I will cut off your horses from among you and destroy your chariots.
[Micah] [5]:[10] I will cut off the cities of your land and tear down all your strongholds.
[Micah] [5]:[11] I will cut off the sorceries from your hand, and you will have no more fortune-tellers.
[Micah] [5]:[12] I will cut off your carved images and your sacred pillars from among you, and you will no longer bow down to the work of your hands.
[Micah] [5]:[13] I will uproot your Asherah poles from among you and demolish your cities.
[Micah] [5]:[14] In anger and wrath I will take vengeance on the nations that have not obeyed.
[Micah] [6]:[1] Hear now what the LORD says: Rise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
[Micah] [6]:[2] Hear, you mountains, the LORD's accusation, and you enduring foundations of the earth; for the LORD has a case against his people, and with Israel he will contend.
[Micah] [6]:[3] My people, what have I done to you? How have I wearied you? Answer me!
[Micah] [6]:[4] I brought you up out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, and I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
[Micah] [6]:[5] My people, remember what Balak king of Moab devised, and how Balaam son of Beor answered him, and what happened from Shittim to Gilgal, that you may know the saving deeds of the LORD.
[Micah] [6]:[6] With what shall I come before the LORD, and bow down before God on high? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
[Micah] [6]:[7] Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
[Micah] [6]:[8] He has told you, O man, what is good, and what the LORD requires of you: only to do justice, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God.
[Micah] [6]:[9] The voice of the LORD cries out to the city—and it is wisdom to fear your name: Heed the rod, and the One who appointed it!
[Micah] [6]:[10] Are there still in the house of the wicked the treasures of wickedness, and the scant measure that is accursed?
[Micah] [6]:[11] Can I acquit anyone who uses dishonest scales, with a bag of false weights?
[Micah] [6]:[12] Her rich men are full of violence, her inhabitants speak lies, and their tongues are deceitful in their mouths.
[Micah] [6]:[13] So I in turn have begun to strike you down, to lay you waste for your sins.
[Micah] [6]:[14] You will eat but not be satisfied; hunger will gnaw within you. You will store up but save nothing, and what you do save I will give to the sword.
[Micah] [6]:[15] You will sow but not reap; you will press olives but not anoint yourself with oil; you will crush grapes but drink no wine.
[Micah] [6]:[16] For you have kept the statutes of Omri and all the practices of the house of Ahab, and you have walked in their counsels. Therefore I will give you over to ruin, and your inhabitants to derision; you will bear the scorn of my people.
[Micah] [7]:[1] What misery is mine! I am like one gathering summer fruit after the harvest, like one gleaning the vineyard when the grapes are gone: not a cluster left to eat, not one of the early figs I crave.
[Micah] [7]:[2] The faithful have vanished from the land; not one upright person remains. They all lie in wait for blood; each one hunts his own brother with a net.
[Micah] [7]:[3] Both hands are skilled at evil. The official demands his price, the judge takes his bribe, the powerful man dictates what he wants—together they weave it tight.
[Micah] [7]:[4] The best of them is like a briar, the most upright a hedge of thorns. The day your watchmen warned of has come, the day of your reckoning. Now confusion is upon them.
[Micah] [7]:[5] Put no trust in a neighbor; rely on no friend. Guard the words of your mouth even from the wife who lies in your arms.
[Micah] [7]:[6] For a son treats his father with contempt, a daughter rises against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A man's enemies are the members of his own household.
[Micah] [7]:[7] But as for me, I will look to the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
[Micah] [7]:[8] Do not gloat over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will rise. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD is my light.
[Micah] [7]:[9] I will bear the LORD's wrath, for I have sinned against him, until he takes up my cause and secures my justice. He will bring me out into the light; I will see his righteousness.
[Micah] [7]:[10] Then my enemy will see it and be covered with shame—she who said to me, "Where is the LORD your God?" My eyes will look on her; now she will be trampled down like mud in the streets.
[Micah] [7]:[11] The day is coming to rebuild your walls; on that day your boundary will be extended.
[Micah] [7]:[12] On that day they will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, from Egypt to the Euphrates, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.
[Micah] [7]:[13] But the land will become a desolation because of those who live in it, because of the fruit of their deeds.
[Micah] [7]:[14] Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock of your inheritance, who dwell alone in a forest amid fertile pastures. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as in days long past.
[Micah] [7]:[15] As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show them my wonders.
[Micah] [7]:[16] The nations will see and be ashamed, for all their might will count for nothing. They will put their hands over their mouths; their ears will be deaf.
[Micah] [7]:[17] They will lick the dust like a snake, like creatures that crawl on the ground. They will come trembling out of their strongholds; they will turn in dread to the LORD our God, and they will fear you.
[Micah] [7]:[18] Who is a God like you, who pardons guilt and passes over the transgression of the remnant of his inheritance? You do not hold on to your anger forever, for you delight in mercy.
[Micah] [7]:[19] You will again have compassion on us; you will tread our iniquities underfoot and hurl all our sins into the depths of the sea.
[Micah] [7]:[20] You will show faithfulness to Jacob and mercy to Abraham, as you swore to our fathers in days long ago.
[Nahum] [1]:[1] An oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum of Elkosh.
[Nahum] [1]:[2] The LORD is a jealous and avenging God; the LORD takes vengeance and is filled with wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on his foes and holds his fury against his enemies.
[Nahum] [1]:[3] The LORD is slow to anger but great in power; he will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His way is in whirlwind and storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
[Nahum] [1]:[4] He rebukes the sea and dries it up; he makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the blossom of Lebanon fades away.
[Nahum] [1]:[5] The mountains quake before him, and the hills dissolve. The earth heaves at his presence, the world and all who live in it.
[Nahum] [1]:[6] Who can stand before his fury? Who can endure the heat of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are shattered before him.
[Nahum] [1]:[7] The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; he knows those who take refuge in him.
[Nahum] [1]:[8] But with a sweeping flood he will bring her place to an end, and he will pursue his enemies into darkness.
[Nahum] [1]:[9] Why do you scheme against the LORD? He himself will make an end of it; trouble will not rise up a second time.
[Nahum] [1]:[10] Though they are tangled together like thorns and soaked in their drink, they will be devoured like stubble, fully dry.
[Nahum] [1]:[11] From you came the one who plots evil against the LORD, who counsels wickedness.
[Nahum] [1]:[12] This is what the LORD says: Though they are strong and many, they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
[Nahum] [1]:[13] Now I will break his yoke from your neck and tear your chains apart.
[Nahum] [1]:[14] And this is what the LORD commands concerning you: Your name will have no offspring. I will cut off the carved image and the cast idol from the house of your gods. I will make your grave, for you are contemptible.
[Nahum] [2]:[1] Look! On the mountains, the feet of one bringing good news, proclaiming peace! Keep your festivals, Judah; fulfill your vows. Never again will the worthless one march through you; he is utterly cut off.
[Nahum] [2]:[2] A destroyer advances against you. Guard the fortress, watch the road, brace yourself, muster all your strength.
[Nahum] [2]:[3] For the LORD is restoring the splendor of Jacob, like the splendor of Israel, though plunderers have stripped them bare and ruined their vines.
[Nahum] [2]:[4] The shields of his warriors gleam red, his soldiers are clothed in scarlet. The chariots flash like fire of steel on the day they are readied, and the spears are brandished.
[Nahum] [2]:[5] The chariots storm through the streets, rattling back and forth across the squares. They look like blazing torches; they dart like lightning.
[Nahum] [2]:[6] He summons his officers; they stumble as they advance. They rush to the wall, and the siege shelter is set in place.
[Nahum] [2]:[7] The river gates are thrown open, and the palace collapses.
[Nahum] [2]:[8] It is decreed: she is stripped bare and led away. Her servant women moan like doves and beat their breasts.
[Nahum] [2]:[9] Nineveh has been like a pool of water from her earliest days, but now they are fleeing! "Stop! Stop!" but no one turns back.
[Nahum] [2]:[10] Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to the hoard, the wealth of every precious thing.
[Nahum] [2]:[11] Emptied, stripped, laid waste! Hearts melt, knees buckle, every body trembles, and every face turns pale.
[Nahum] [2]:[12] Where now is the lions' den, the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion and the lioness walked with their cubs and nothing made them afraid?
[Nahum] [2]:[13] The lion tore enough for his cubs and strangled prey for his lionesses; he filled his lairs with the kill and his dens with torn flesh.
[Nahum] [2]:[14] I am against you, declares the LORD of hosts. I will burn up your chariots in smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will never be heard again.
[Nahum] [3]:[1] Woe to the city of blood, full of lies, stuffed with plunder—the prey never ends!
[Nahum] [3]:[2] The crack of the whip, the rumble of wheels, galloping horses and jolting chariots!
[Nahum] [3]:[3] Charging horsemen, flashing swords, glittering spears—hosts of slain, heaps of corpses, bodies without end; they stumble over the dead.
[Nahum] [3]:[4] All because of the endless harlotries of the harlot, so graceful and charming, that mistress of sorcery, who sold nations with her harlotries and peoples with her spells.
[Nahum] [3]:[5] I am against you, declares the LORD of hosts. I will lift your skirts over your face; I will show the nations your nakedness and the kingdoms your shame.
[Nahum] [3]:[6] I will pelt you with filth, treat you with contempt, and make you a spectacle.
[Nahum] [3]:[7] All who see you will recoil from you and say, "Nineveh is ruined! Who will mourn for her?" Where shall I find anyone to comfort you?
[Nahum] [3]:[8] Are you better than Thebes, seated by the Nile with waters all around her, whose rampart was the sea, whose wall was the water?
[Nahum] [3]:[9] Cush was her strength, and Egypt beyond measure; Put and the Libyans were your helpers.
[Nahum] [3]:[10] Yet she too went into exile, into captivity. Her infants were dashed to pieces at the head of every street; lots were cast for her nobles, and all her great men were bound in chains.
[Nahum] [3]:[11] You too will drink deep and stagger; you too will go into hiding, searching for refuge from the enemy.
[Nahum] [3]:[12] All your fortresses are fig trees heavy with first-ripe fruit: when they are shaken, the fruit falls into the mouth of the eater.
[Nahum] [3]:[13] Look at your troops—they are women in your midst! The gates of your land stand wide open to your enemies; fire has devoured your bars.
[Nahum] [3]:[14] Draw water for the siege, strengthen your fortresses! Go down into the clay, tread the mortar, take hold of the brick mold!
[Nahum] [3]:[15] There the fire will devour you, the sword will cut you down; it will consume you like the young locust. Multiply like the young locust, multiply like the swarming locust!
[Nahum] [3]:[16] You made your merchants more numerous than the stars of heaven—but the locust strips the land and flies away.
[Nahum] [3]:[17] Your guards are like locusts, your officers like swarms of grasshoppers settling on the walls on a cold day; when the sun rises they take flight, and no one knows where they have gone.
[Nahum] [3]:[18] Your shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria; your nobles lie down to sleep. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and no one gathers them.
[Nahum] [3]:[19] There is no relief for your injury; your wound is mortal. All who hear the news of you clap their hands over your fall—for who has not felt your endless cruelty?
[Habakkuk] [1]:[1] The oracle that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[2] How long, LORD, must I call for help and you not listen? I cry out to you, "Violence!" and you do not save.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[3] Why do you make me see wrongdoing? Why do you look upon trouble? Destruction and violence are before me; strife breaks out and conflict rises up.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[4] So the law goes numb, and justice never comes forth. The wicked hem in the righteous, and justice comes out twisted.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[5] Look among the nations and watch. Be astonished, be astounded! For I am doing a work in your days that you would not believe if it were told you.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[6] Look, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and impetuous nation, who march across the breadth of the earth to seize dwellings not their own.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[7] They are dreadful and terrifying; their justice and their dignity proceed from themselves.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[8] Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves at dusk. Their horsemen come charging; their horsemen come from far away, swooping like an eagle rushing to devour.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[9] They all come bent on violence, their faces set to press forward; they gather captives like sand.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[10] They scoff at kings, and rulers are a laughingstock to them. They laugh at every fortress; they heap up earth and capture it.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[11] Then they sweep past like the wind and move on—guilty men, whose own strength is their god.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[12] Are you not from everlasting, LORD my God, my Holy One? We will not die. LORD, you have appointed them to execute judgment; you, O Rock, have established them to punish.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[13] Your eyes are too pure to look on evil; you cannot gaze at wrongdoing. Why then do you look on the treacherous and stay silent when the wicked swallows one more righteous than himself?
[Habakkuk] [1]:[14] You have made people like the fish of the sea, like crawling things that have no ruler.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[15] The foe hauls them all up with a hook, drags them off in his net, gathers them in his dragnet—and so he rejoices and exults.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[16] So he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet, for by them his portion is rich and his food is choice.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[17] Is he then to keep emptying his net, forever slaughtering nations without mercy?
[Habakkuk] [2]:[1] I will stand at my post and station myself on the rampart; I will watch to see what he will say to me, and what answer I am to give concerning my complaint.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[2] Then the LORD answered me: "Write down the vision; inscribe it plainly on tablets, so that the one who reads it may run.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[3] For the vision awaits its appointed time; it testifies of the end and does not lie. Though it lingers, wait for it, for it will surely come and will not delay.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[4] Look at the proud one: his soul is not upright within him. But the righteous shall live by his faith.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[5] Indeed, wine betrays him; he is an arrogant man who knows no rest. His appetite is as wide as the grave; like death he is never satisfied. He gathers all the nations to himself and sweeps up all the peoples for himself.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[6] Will not all of them taunt him with mockery and riddles, saying: 'Woe to him who piles up what is not his own! How long will he load himself with debt?'
[Habakkuk] [2]:[7] Will not your creditors suddenly rise up? Will not those who make you tremble awake? Then you will become their plunder.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[8] Because you have plundered many nations, the rest of the peoples will plunder you—for the blood you shed and the violence you did to the land, to the city and all who live in it.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[9] Woe to him who piles up unjust gain for his house, who sets his nest on high to escape the reach of harm!
[Habakkuk] [2]:[10] You have plotted shame for your own house by cutting off many peoples; you have forfeited your own life.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[11] For the stone will cry out from the wall, and the beam will answer it from the woodwork.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[12] Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed and founds a town on injustice!
[Habakkuk] [2]:[13] Is it not from the LORD of hosts that the peoples labor only for fire, that the nations exhaust themselves for nothing?
[Habakkuk] [2]:[14] For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[15] Woe to him who makes his neighbor drink, who pours out his wrath until they are drunk, so that he can gaze at their naked bodies!
[Habakkuk] [2]:[16] You will be filled with shame instead of glory. Now you drink and expose yourself! The cup of the LORD's right hand is coming around to you, and disgrace will cover your glory.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[17] For the violence you did to Lebanon will overwhelm you, and the destruction of its beasts will terrify you—for the blood you shed and the violence you did to the land, to the city and all who live in it.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[18] What good is an idol, carved by human hands? What use is a cast image, a teacher of lies? For its maker trusts in his own handiwork, yet all he makes are speechless idols.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[19] Woe to him who says to a piece of wood, "Wake up!" and to lifeless stone, "Arise!" Can it teach? See, it is overlaid with gold and silver, but there is no breath in it.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[20] But the LORD is in his holy temple; let all the earth be silent before him.

[Zephaniah] [1]:[2] I will utterly sweep everything from the face of the earth, declares the LORD.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[3] I will sweep away man and beast; I will sweep away the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, and the stumbling blocks along with the wicked. I will cut off mankind from the face of the earth, declares the LORD.
