[Zephaniah] [1]:[4] I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against all who live in Jerusalem. I will cut off from this place every remnant of Baal, the very name of the idol priests along with the priests,
[Zephaniah] [1]:[5] those who bow down on the rooftops to the host of heaven, those who bow down and swear by the LORD and yet swear by Milcom, [Footnote: Milcom was a god of the Ammonites; the Hebrew word can also be read as "their king."]
[Zephaniah] [1]:[6] and those who turn back from following the LORD, who do not seek the LORD or inquire of him.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[7] Be silent before the Lord GOD, for the day of the LORD is near. The LORD has prepared a sacrifice; he has consecrated his guests.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[8] On the day of the LORD's sacrifice I will punish the officials and the king's sons and all who dress in foreign clothing.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[9] On that day I will punish all who leap over the threshold, who fill their master's house with violence and deceit.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[10] On that day, declares the LORD, a cry will go up from the Fish Gate, a wailing from the Second Quarter, and a loud crash from the hills.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[11] Wail, you who live in the Mortar, for all the traders are destroyed; all who weigh out silver are cut off.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[12] At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps and punish the men who sit complacent, like wine left on its dregs, who say in their hearts, "The LORD will do neither good nor harm."
[Zephaniah] [1]:[13] Their wealth will be plundered and their houses laid waste. They will build houses but not live in them; they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[14] The great day of the LORD is near—near and coming fast. Listen! The day of the LORD is bitter; there the warrior cries aloud.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[15] That day will be a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of ruin and devastation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness,
[Zephaniah] [1]:[16] a day of trumpet blast and battle cry against the fortified cities and against the lofty corner towers.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[17] I will bring such distress on humankind that they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust and their flesh like dung.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[18] Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to save them on the day of the LORD's wrath. In the fire of his jealousy the whole earth will be consumed, for he will make a sudden end of all who live on the earth.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[1] Gather yourselves, gather together, you shameless nation—
[Zephaniah] [2]:[2] before the decree takes effect, before the day blows past like chaff, before the LORD's burning anger comes upon you, before the day of the LORD's wrath overtakes you.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[3] Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land, you who carry out his commands. Seek righteousness, seek humility; perhaps you will find shelter on the day of the LORD's wrath.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[4] For Gaza will be abandoned and Ashkelon left in ruins; Ashdod will be driven out at midday, and Ekron uprooted.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[5] Woe to you who live along the sea, you nation of Cherethites! The word of the LORD is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines: I will destroy you, and no one will be left.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[6] The land along the sea will become open pasture, with shelters for shepherds and pens for flocks.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[7] The coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; there they will graze their flocks, and in the houses of Ashkelon they will lie down at evening. For the LORD their God will care for them and restore their fortunes.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[8] I have heard the taunts of Moab and the insults of the Ammonites, who mocked my people and boasted against their borders.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[9] Therefore, as surely as I live, declares the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel: Moab will become like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah—overrun with nettles, a pit of salt, a wasteland forever. The remnant of my people will plunder them; the survivors of my nation will inherit them.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[10] This is what they get for their pride, because they mocked and boasted against the people of the LORD of hosts.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[11] The LORD will be terrifying to them, for he will make all the gods of the earth waste away. Then the nations on every shore will worship him, each in its own place.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[12] You Cushites too will be slain by my sword.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[13] He will stretch out his hand against the north and destroy Assyria; he will leave Nineveh in ruins, as dry as the desert.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[14] Herds will lie down in her midst, wild creatures of every kind; the owl and the hedgehog will roost on her columns. A cry will echo through the windows, rubble will fill the doorways, for the cedar paneling is stripped bare.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[15] This is the carefree city that lived secure, saying to herself, "I am the one, and there is no other." What a ruin she has become, a lair for wild beasts! All who pass by hiss and shake their fists.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[1] Woe to the rebellious and defiled one — the city that oppresses!
[Zephaniah] [3]:[2] She has obeyed no voice, she has accepted no correction. She has not trusted in the LORD; she has not drawn near to her God.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[3] Her officials are roaring lions; her judges are wolves of the evening, leaving nothing for the morning.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[4] Her prophets are reckless, treacherous men; her priests profane what is holy and do violence to the law.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[5] The LORD within her is righteous; he does no wrong. Morning by morning he brings his justice to light; it never fails. Yet the unjust man knows no shame.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[6] I have cut off nations; their battlements lie in ruins. I have laid waste their streets, with no one passing through. Their cities are devastated, with no one left, no inhabitant at all.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[7] I said, "Surely now you will fear me and accept correction, and her dwelling will not be cut off, in spite of all that I have brought upon her." But they were all the more eager to corrupt all their deeds.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[8] Therefore wait for me, declares the LORD, for the day when I rise to testify. For I have determined to gather the nations, to assemble the kingdoms, to pour out on them my indignation, all the heat of my anger. For in the fire of my jealousy all the earth will be consumed.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[9] Then I will purify the lips of the peoples, so that all of them may call on the name of the LORD and serve him shoulder to shoulder.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[10] From beyond the rivers of Cush my worshipers, my scattered people, will bring me an offering.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[11] On that day you will no longer be put to shame for all the deeds by which you rebelled against me. For then I will remove from your midst your proud boasters, and never again will you be haughty on my holy mountain.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[12] But I will leave within you a people humble and lowly, and they will take refuge in the name of the LORD.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[13] The remnant of Israel will do no wrong; they will speak no lies, and no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouths. They will graze and lie down, and no one will make them afraid.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[14] Sing aloud, daughter of Zion! Shout, O Israel! Rejoice and exult with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem!
[Zephaniah] [3]:[15] The LORD has taken away the judgments against you; he has cast out your enemy. The King of Israel, the LORD, is in your midst; never again will you fear disaster.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[16] On that day it will be said to Jerusalem: "Do not fear, Zion; do not let your hands grow weak.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[17] The LORD your God is in your midst, a warrior who saves. He will rejoice over you with gladness; he will quiet you with his love; he will exult over you with singing."
[Zephaniah] [3]:[18] Those who grieved, shut out from the appointed feasts, I will gather; they were yours—those for whom reproach was a heavy burden.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[19] See, at that time I will deal with all who oppressed you. I will save the lame and gather the scattered, and I will make them a praise and a name in every land where they were put to shame.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[20] At that time I will bring you home; at that time I will gather you. For I will make you a name and a praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your very eyes, says the LORD.
[Haggai] [1]:[1] In the second year of King Darius, on the first day of the sixth month, the word of the LORD came through the prophet Haggai to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest:
[Haggai] [1]:[2] This is what the LORD of hosts says: This people say, "The time has not come, the time for the house of the LORD to be built."
[Haggai] [1]:[3] Then the word of the LORD came through the prophet Haggai:
[Haggai] [1]:[4] Is it a time for you yourselves to live in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?
[Haggai] [1]:[5] Now then, this is what the LORD of hosts says: Consider carefully how you have lived.
[Haggai] [1]:[6] You have sown much and harvested little. You eat, but are never full. You drink, but your thirst is never quenched. You put on clothes, but cannot keep warm. You earn wages, only to put them in a purse with holes in it.
[Haggai] [1]:[7] This is what the LORD of hosts says: Consider carefully how you have lived.
[Haggai] [1]:[8] Go up to the hill country, bring timber, and build the house, so that I may take pleasure in it and be honored, says the LORD.
[Haggai] [1]:[9] You looked for much, but it came to little. What you brought home, I blew away. Why? declares the LORD of hosts. Because my house lies in ruins, while each of you hurries off to his own house.
[Haggai] [1]:[10] That is why the heavens above you have withheld their dew and the earth has withheld its produce.
[Haggai] [1]:[11] I called for a drought on the land and on the mountains, on the grain, the new wine, and the oil, on everything the ground brings forth, on man and beast, and on all the labor of your hands.
[Haggai] [1]:[12] Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and all the remnant of the people obeyed the voice of the LORD their God and the words of the prophet Haggai, because the LORD their God had sent him. And the people feared the LORD.
[Haggai] [1]:[13] Then Haggai, the messenger of the LORD, delivered the LORD's message to the people: "I am with you, declares the LORD."
[Haggai] [1]:[14] So the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people. They came and began to work on the house of the LORD of hosts, their God,
[Haggai] [1]:[15] on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month in the second year of King Darius.
[Haggai] [2]:[1] On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the word of the LORD came through the prophet Haggai:
[Haggai] [2]:[2] Speak now to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people. Say to them:
[Haggai] [2]:[3] Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? And how does it look to you now? Does it not seem like nothing in your eyes?
[Haggai] [2]:[4] Yet be strong now, Zerubbabel, declares the LORD. Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land, declares the LORD, and get to work, for I am with you, declares the LORD of hosts.
[Haggai] [2]:[5] This is the covenant I made with you when you came out of Egypt, and my Spirit remains among you. Do not be afraid.
[Haggai] [2]:[6] For this is what the LORD of hosts says: Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
[Haggai] [2]:[7] I will shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will come in, and I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD of hosts.
[Haggai] [2]:[8] The silver is mine and the gold is mine, declares the LORD of hosts.
[Haggai] [2]:[9] The glory of this latter house will be greater than the former, says the LORD of hosts. And in this place I will grant peace, declares the LORD of hosts.
[Haggai] [2]:[10] On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Haggai:
[Haggai] [2]:[11] This is what the LORD of hosts says: Ask the priests for a ruling on the law.
[Haggai] [2]:[12] If someone carries consecrated meat in the fold of his garment, and that fold touches bread or stew, wine or oil, or any other food, does it become holy? The priests answered, No.
[Haggai] [2]:[13] Then Haggai said, If someone defiled by contact with a corpse touches any of these, does it become unclean? The priests answered, It becomes unclean.
[Haggai] [2]:[14] Then Haggai replied, So it is with this people, so it is with this nation before me, declares the LORD, and so it is with everything they do; whatever they offer there is unclean.
[Haggai] [2]:[15] Now think carefully about this, from this day backward: how things were before one stone was laid on another in the temple of the LORD,
[Haggai] [2]:[16] Ever since then, when someone came to a grain heap expecting twenty measures, there were only ten; when someone came to the wine vat to draw off fifty, there were only twenty.
[Haggai] [2]:[17] I struck you and all the work of your hands with blight, mildew, and hail, yet you did not turn to me, declares the LORD.
[Haggai] [2]:[18] Think carefully from this day on, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid. Think carefully:
[Haggai] [2]:[19] Is there still seed left in the barn? The vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have not yielded. But from this day on I will bless you.
[Haggai] [2]:[20] The word of the LORD came to Haggai a second time on the twenty-fourth day of the month:
[Haggai] [2]:[21] Tell Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, that I am going to shake the heavens and the earth.
[Haggai] [2]:[22] I will overturn royal thrones and shatter the power of the kingdoms of the nations. I will overturn chariots and their riders; horses and their riders will fall, each by the sword of his brother.
[Haggai] [2]:[23] On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, I will take you, my servant Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, declares the LORD, and I will make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you, declares the LORD of hosts.
[Zechariah] [1]:[1] In the eighth month of the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo:
[Zechariah] [1]:[2] The LORD was furious with your fathers.
[Zechariah] [1]:[3] So tell them: This is what the LORD of hosts says: Return to me, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will return to you, says the LORD of hosts.
[Zechariah] [1]:[4] Do not be like your fathers. The earlier prophets called out to them: This is what the LORD of hosts says: Turn now from your evil ways and your evil deeds. But they would not listen or pay attention to me, declares the LORD.
[Zechariah] [1]:[5] Your fathers—where are they now? And the prophets—do they live forever?
[Zechariah] [1]:[6] But my words and my decrees, which I commanded my servants the prophets—did they not overtake your fathers? Then they repented and said, "The LORD of hosts has dealt with us as he determined to do, according to our ways and our deeds."
[Zechariah] [1]:[7] On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo:
[Zechariah] [1]:[8] In the night I had a vision: there before me was a man riding on a red horse. He was standing among the myrtle trees in the ravine, and behind him were horses—red, sorrel, and white.
[Zechariah] [1]:[9] I asked, "What are these, my lord?" And the angel who was speaking with me said, "I will show you what they are."
[Zechariah] [1]:[10] Then the man standing among the myrtle trees answered, "These are the ones the LORD has sent to patrol the earth."
[Zechariah] [1]:[11] And they reported to the angel of the LORD who was standing among the myrtle trees, "We have patrolled the earth, and the whole earth lies at rest and at peace."
[Zechariah] [1]:[12] Then the angel of the LORD said, "LORD of hosts, how long will you withhold mercy from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, with which you have been angry these seventy years?"
[Zechariah] [1]:[13] And the LORD answered the angel who was speaking with me, and his words were kind words, words of comfort.
[Zechariah] [1]:[14] Then the angel who was speaking with me said, "Proclaim this: The LORD of hosts says: I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a burning jealousy,
[Zechariah] [1]:[15] and I am fiercely angry with the nations that sit secure. I was only a little angry, but they added to the harm.
[Zechariah] [1]:[16] Therefore this is what the LORD says: I have returned to Jerusalem with mercy. My house will be rebuilt there, declares the LORD of hosts, and the measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.
[Zechariah] [1]:[17] Proclaim this as well: The LORD of hosts says: My cities will again overflow with prosperity. The LORD will again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem.
[Zechariah] [2]:[1] Then I lifted my eyes and looked, and there before me were four horns.
[Zechariah] [2]:[2] I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these?" He answered me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."
[Zechariah] [2]:[3] Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.
[Zechariah] [2]:[4] I asked, "What are these coming to do?" He said, "These are the horns that scattered Judah so completely that no one could lift his head. But these have come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations that raised their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."
[Zechariah] [2]:[5] Then I lifted my eyes and looked, and there before me was a man with a measuring line in his hand.
[Zechariah] [2]:[6] I asked, "Where are you going?" He said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide and how long it is."
[Zechariah] [2]:[7] Then I saw the angel who was speaking with me going out, and another angel came out to meet him
[Zechariah] [2]:[8] and said to him, "Run, tell that young man: Jerusalem will be inhabited as a city without walls, because of the multitude of people and livestock within her.
[Zechariah] [2]:[9] And I myself will be a wall of fire around her, declares the LORD, and I will be the glory within her."
[Zechariah] [2]:[10] "Up, up! Flee from the land of the north, declares the LORD, for I have scattered you to the four winds of heaven, declares the LORD.
[Zechariah] [2]:[11] Up, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon."
[Zechariah] [2]:[12] For this is what the LORD of hosts says: After his glory he sent me against the nations that plundered you—for whoever touches you touches the apple of his eye.
[Zechariah] [2]:[13] See, I will raise my hand against them, and they will become plunder for their own servants. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me.
[Zechariah] [2]:[14] Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion! For I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, declares the LORD.
[Zechariah] [2]:[15] Many nations will join themselves to the LORD on that day and become my people, and I will dwell in your midst. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
[Zechariah] [2]:[16] The LORD will take possession of Judah as his portion in the holy land, and he will again choose Jerusalem.
[Zechariah] [2]:[17] Be silent, all flesh, before the LORD, for he has roused himself from his holy dwelling.
[Zechariah] [3]:[1] Then he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, with Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him. [footnote: The Hebrew reads "the satan," that is, "the accuser" or "the adversary."]
[Zechariah] [3]:[2] And the LORD said to Satan, "The LORD rebuke you, Satan! The LORD, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebuke you! Is this man not a brand snatched from the fire?"
[Zechariah] [3]:[3] Now Joshua was dressed in filthy garments as he stood before the angel.
[Zechariah] [3]:[4] And the angel said to those standing before him, "Take the filthy garments off him." Then he said to Joshua, "See, I have taken your guilt away from you, and I will clothe you in fine robes."
[Zechariah] [3]:[5] And I said, "Let them put a clean turban on his head." So they placed a clean turban on his head and clothed him in fresh garments, while the angel of the LORD stood by.
[Zechariah] [3]:[6] Then the angel of the LORD gave Joshua this charge:
[Zechariah] [3]:[7] "This is what the LORD of hosts says: If you walk in my ways and keep my requirements, then you shall govern my house and watch over my courts, and I will give you a place among those who stand here.
[Zechariah] [3]:[8] Listen now, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions seated before you—for they are men who serve as a sign: I am going to bring my servant, the Branch.
[Zechariah] [3]:[9] For see, the stone I have set before Joshua: on that one stone are seven eyes. I will engrave an inscription on it, declares the LORD of hosts, and I will remove the guilt of this land in a single day.
[Zechariah] [3]:[10] On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, each of you will invite his neighbor to sit under the vine and under the fig tree."
[Zechariah] [4]:[1] Then the angel who was speaking with me came back and woke me, like a man roused from his sleep.
[Zechariah] [4]:[2] He asked me, "What do you see?" I answered, "I see a lampstand, all of gold, with a bowl at the top of it. It has seven lamps on it, and seven spouts for each of the lamps at its top.
[Zechariah] [4]:[3] And beside it are two olive trees, one on the right of the bowl and one on its left."
[Zechariah] [4]:[4] Then I said to the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these, my lord?"
[Zechariah] [4]:[5] The angel who was speaking with me answered, "Don't you know what these are?" "No, my lord," I said.
[Zechariah] [4]:[6] So he said to me, "This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by might and not by power, but by my Spirit, says the LORD of hosts.
[Zechariah] [4]:[7] What are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become level ground. He will bring out the capstone to shouts of 'Grace, grace to it!'"
[Zechariah] [4]:[8] Then the word of the LORD came to me:
[Zechariah] [4]:[9] "The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will finish it. Then you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you.
[Zechariah] [4]:[10] For who dares to despise the day of small things? They will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven are the eyes of the LORD, which range through all the earth."
[Zechariah] [4]:[11] Then I asked him, "What are these two olive trees on the right and the left of the lampstand?"
[Zechariah] [4]:[12] And I asked him again, "What are these two olive branches beside the two golden pipes that pour out the golden oil?"
[Zechariah] [4]:[13] He said to me, "Don't you know what these are?" "No, my lord," I said.
[Zechariah] [4]:[14] Then he said, "These are the two anointed ones who stand before the Lord of all the earth." [Footnote: Literally 'the two sons of fresh oil.']
[Zechariah] [5]:[1] Again I looked up, and there before me was a flying scroll.
[Zechariah] [5]:[2] He asked me, "What do you see?" I answered, "I see a flying scroll, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide."
[Zechariah] [5]:[3] Then he said to me, "This is the curse going out over the whole land. According to one side of the scroll, every thief will be swept away; according to the other, everyone who swears falsely will be swept away.
[Zechariah] [5]:[4] I am sending it out, declares the LORD of hosts, and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by my name. It will remain in his house and consume it, both its timbers and its stones."
[Zechariah] [5]:[5] Then the angel who was speaking with me came forward and said, "Look up and see what this is that is going out."
[Zechariah] [5]:[6] I asked, "What is it?" He answered, "It is a measuring basket going out." And he added, "This is their iniquity in all the land."
[Zechariah] [5]:[7] Then the lead cover was lifted, and there sat a woman inside the basket.
[Zechariah] [5]:[8] He said, "This is Wickedness," and he pushed her back into the basket and slammed the lead cover down over its mouth.
[Zechariah] [5]:[9] Then I looked up, and there before me were two women coming, with the wind in their wings. Their wings were like those of a stork, and they lifted the basket and carried it between earth and sky.
[Zechariah] [5]:[10] "Where are they taking the basket?" I asked the angel who was speaking with me.
[Zechariah] [5]:[11] He answered, "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar.[^1] When the house is ready, the basket will be set there on its pedestal." [^1]: Shinar: the ancient name for the region of Babylonia (see Genesis 11:2).
[Zechariah] [6]:[1] Again I looked up, and there before me were four chariots coming out from between two mountains — and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
[Zechariah] [6]:[2] The first chariot had red horses, the second black horses,
[Zechariah] [6]:[3] the third white horses, and the fourth dappled, powerful horses.
[Zechariah] [6]:[4] I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these, my lord?"
[Zechariah] [6]:[5] The angel answered me, "These are the four winds of heaven, going out after standing before the Lord of all the earth.
[Zechariah] [6]:[6] The chariot with the black horses goes toward the land of the north, the white ones go out after them, and the dappled ones go toward the land of the south.
[Zechariah] [6]:[7] And the powerful horses went out, straining to go and patrol the earth. He said, "Go, patrol the earth," and they patrolled the earth.
[Zechariah] [6]:[8] Then he called out to me and said, "Look, those going toward the land of the north have given my Spirit rest in the land of the north."
[Zechariah] [6]:[9] The word of the LORD came to me:
[Zechariah] [6]:[10] "Take a gift from the exiles — from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have arrived from Babylon. Go that same day to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.
[Zechariah] [6]:[11] Take the silver and gold, make a crown, and set it on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
[Zechariah] [6]:[12] Tell him: This is what the LORD of hosts says: Here is a man whose name is Branch; he will branch out from his place and build the temple of the LORD.
[Zechariah] [6]:[13] Yes, he will build the temple of the LORD, and he will bear majesty and sit and rule on his throne. He will be a priest on his throne, and between the two there will be a counsel of peace.
[Zechariah] [6]:[14] The crown will be a memorial in the temple of the LORD for Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen son of Zephaniah.[^1] [^1]: Hebrew reads *Helem* here, understood as a variant of *Heldai* (verse 10); likewise *Hen* ("favor") may be another name for Josiah son of Zephaniah.
[Zechariah] [6]:[15] Those who are far off will come and help build the temple of the LORD, and you will know that the LORD of hosts has sent me to you. This will happen if you diligently obey the voice of the LORD your God."
[Zechariah] [7]:[1] In the fourth year of King Darius, on the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Chislev, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah.
[Zechariah] [7]:[2] Now the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech with their men to entreat the favor of the LORD,
[Zechariah] [7]:[3] and to ask the priests of the house of the LORD of hosts and the prophets, "Should I go on weeping and abstaining in the fifth month, as I have done for so many years?"
[Zechariah] [7]:[4] Then the word of the LORD of hosts came to me:
[Zechariah] [7]:[5] Say to all the people of the land and to the priests: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and the seventh months these seventy years, was it truly for me, for me, that you fasted?
[Zechariah] [7]:[6] And when you eat and when you drink, is it not you yourselves who eat, you yourselves who drink?
[Zechariah] [7]:[7] Should you not obey the words the LORD proclaimed through the earlier prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, with her towns around her, and the Negev and the foothills were settled?
[Zechariah] [7]:[8] And the word of the LORD came to Zechariah:
[Zechariah] [7]:[9] Thus says the LORD of hosts: Render true judgments; show kindness and mercy to one another.
[Zechariah] [7]:[10] Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the foreigner or the poor, and do not plot evil against one another in your hearts.
[Zechariah] [7]:[11] But they refused to pay attention; they turned a stubborn shoulder and stopped their ears so they would not hear.
[Zechariah] [7]:[12] They made their hearts hard as flint, refusing to hear the law and the words that the LORD of hosts had sent by his Spirit through the earlier prophets. So great wrath came from the LORD of hosts.
[Zechariah] [7]:[13] "And just as he called and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen," says the LORD of hosts.
[Zechariah] [7]:[14] "I drove them out with a whirlwind among all the nations they had not known, and the land was left desolate behind them, with none passing to and fro. So a pleasant land was made a desolation."
[Zechariah] [8]:[1] The word of the LORD of hosts came, saying:
[Zechariah] [8]:[2] This is what the LORD of hosts says: I am jealous for Zion with a great jealousy; with great wrath I am jealous for her.
[Zechariah] [8]:[3] This is what the LORD says: I will return to Zion and dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the LORD of hosts the Holy Mountain.
[Zechariah] [8]:[4] This is what the LORD of hosts says: Old men and old women will again sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of great age.
[Zechariah] [8]:[5] And the streets of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing there.
[Zechariah] [8]:[6] This is what the LORD of hosts says: If it seems impossible to the remnant of this people in those days, should it also seem impossible to me? declares the LORD of hosts.
[Zechariah] [8]:[7] This is what the LORD of hosts says: I am going to save my people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting sun.
[Zechariah] [8]:[8] I will bring them back to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.
[Zechariah] [8]:[9] This is what the LORD of hosts says: Let your hands be strong, you who now hear these words from the mouth of the prophets who spoke when the foundation was laid for the house of the LORD of hosts, so that the temple could be built.
[Zechariah] [8]:[10] For before those days there was no wage for man or beast, and no one could come or go in safety because of the enemy, since I had turned everyone against his neighbor.
[Zechariah] [8]:[11] But now I will not deal with the remnant of this people as in former days, declares the LORD of hosts.
[Zechariah] [8]:[12] For there will be a sowing of peace: the vine will yield its fruit, the ground will give its produce, and the heavens will give their dew. All this I will grant as an inheritance to the remnant of this people.
[Zechariah] [8]:[13] Just as you were a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.
[Zechariah] [8]:[14] For this is what the LORD of hosts says: Just as I resolved to bring disaster on you when your ancestors provoked me to anger, says the LORD of hosts, and I did not relent,
[Zechariah] [8]:[15] so now I have resolved again in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.
[Zechariah] [8]:[16] These are the things you are to do: Speak the truth to one another; render judgments in your gates that are true and make for peace.
[Zechariah] [8]:[17] Do not plot evil in your hearts against your neighbor, and do not love false oaths, for all these things I hate, declares the LORD.
[Zechariah] [8]:[18] The word of the LORD of hosts came to me, saying:
[Zechariah] [8]:[19] This is what the LORD of hosts says: The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months will become for the house of Judah times of joy and gladness, seasons of celebration. So love truth and peace.
[Zechariah] [8]:[20] This is what the LORD of hosts says: Peoples will yet come, the inhabitants of many cities.
[Zechariah] [8]:[21] The people of one city will go to another and say, "Let us go at once to entreat the favor of the LORD and to seek the LORD of hosts. I myself am going."
[Zechariah] [8]:[22] Many peoples and mighty nations will come to seek the LORD of hosts in Jerusalem and to entreat the favor of the LORD.
[Zechariah] [8]:[23] This is what the LORD of hosts says: In those days ten men from all the languages of the nations will take hold of the hem of one Jew's robe and say, "Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you."
[Zechariah] [9]:[1] An oracle: The word of the LORD against the land of Hadrach, with Damascus as its resting place — for the LORD has his eye on humankind as on all the tribes of Israel —
[Zechariah] [9]:[2] and against Hamath as well, which borders it, and against Tyre and Sidon, however wise they may be.
[Zechariah] [9]:[3] Tyre has built herself a stronghold; she has heaped up silver like dust and gold like the mud of the streets.
[Zechariah] [9]:[4] But look, the Lord will dispossess her; he will hurl her wealth into the sea, and she herself will be devoured by fire.
[Zechariah] [9]:[5] Ashkelon will see it and be afraid; Gaza will writhe in anguish, and Ekron too, for her hope has withered away. The king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will be left without inhabitants.
[Zechariah] [9]:[6] A people of mixed blood will settle in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
[Zechariah] [9]:[7] I will take the blood out of their mouths and the detestable meat from between their teeth. Then they too will be a remnant for our God; they will be like a clan in Judah, and Ekron will be like the Jebusites.
[Zechariah] [9]:[8] I will encamp around my house as a guard, so that no one passes through or returns against it; no oppressor will overrun them again, for now I have seen it with my own eyes.
[Zechariah] [9]:[9] Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout aloud, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your king is coming to you: righteous and bringing salvation, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
[Zechariah] [9]:[10] I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the warhorse from Jerusalem; the battle bow will be broken. He will proclaim peace to the nations; his rule will stretch from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.
[Zechariah] [9]:[11] As for you, because of the blood of my covenant with you, I will set your prisoners free from the waterless pit.
[Zechariah] [9]:[12] Return to your stronghold, you prisoners of hope. Today I declare it: I will restore to you double.
[Zechariah] [9]:[13] For I have bent Judah as my bow and fitted Ephraim as my arrow. I will rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and I will wield you like a warrior's sword.
[Zechariah] [9]:[14] Then the LORD will appear over them, and his arrow will flash out like lightning. The Lord GOD will sound the trumpet and advance in the storms of the south.
[Zechariah] [9]:[15] The LORD of hosts will shield them. They will devour and trample the sling stones underfoot; they will drink and roar as with wine, filled like a bowl, drenched like the corners of the altar.
[Zechariah] [9]:[16] On that day the LORD their God will save them, the flock that is his people; like jewels in a crown they will sparkle over his land.
[Zechariah] [9]:[17] How great his goodness, how great his beauty! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine the young women.
[Zechariah] [10]:[1] Ask the LORD for rain in the season of spring rains. The LORD is the one who makes the storm clouds; he gives showers of rain, and grass in the field for everyone.
[Zechariah] [10]:[2] For the household idols speak deceit, the diviners see illusions, they tell worthless dreams and offer empty comfort. So the people wandered off like sheep, harassed, because there was no shepherd.
[Zechariah] [10]:[3] My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will hold the leaders of the flock to account. For the LORD of hosts has come to care for his flock, the house of Judah, and he will make them like his proud war horse.
[Zechariah] [10]:[4] From him comes the cornerstone, from him the tent peg, from him the battle bow, from him every ruler together.
[Zechariah] [10]:[5] They will be like warriors in battle, trampling through the mud of the streets. They will fight, for the LORD is with them, and they will put to shame the riders on horses.
[Zechariah] [10]:[6] I will make the house of Judah strong, and the house of Joseph I will save. I will bring them home, for I have compassion on them, and they will be as though I had never cast them off; for I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
[Zechariah] [10]:[7] Ephraim will be like a warrior, and their hearts will be glad as with wine. Their children will see it and rejoice; their hearts will exult in the LORD.
[Zechariah] [10]:[8] I will whistle for them and gather them in, for I have redeemed them, and they will be as numerous as they once were.
[Zechariah] [10]:[9] Though I scattered them among the nations, they will remember me in distant lands; they and their children will live, and they will return.
[Zechariah] [10]:[10] I will bring them back from the land of Egypt and gather them from Assyria. I will lead them into the land of Gilead and to Lebanon, until there is no more room for them.
[Zechariah] [10]:[11] He will pass through the sea of distress and strike the waves of the sea, and all the depths of the Nile will run dry. The pride of Assyria will be brought low, and the scepter of Egypt will pass away.
[Zechariah] [10]:[12] I will make them strong in the LORD, and in his name they will walk, declares the LORD.
[Zechariah] [11]:[1] Open your doors, Lebanon, and let fire devour your cedars!
[Zechariah] [11]:[2] Wail, cypress, for the cedar has fallen; the mighty trees are ruined! Wail, oaks of Bashan, for the impenetrable forest has been felled!
[Zechariah] [11]:[3] Listen—the wailing of the shepherds, for their glory is ruined. Listen—the roaring of the young lions, for the lush thickets of the Jordan are laid waste.
[Zechariah] [11]:[4] This is what the LORD my God says: Shepherd the flock marked for slaughter.
[Zechariah] [11]:[5] Their buyers slaughter them and go unpunished, and those who sell them say, "Blessed be the LORD, I have grown rich!" And their own shepherds show them no pity.
[Zechariah] [11]:[6] For I will no longer show pity to the inhabitants of the land, declares the LORD. I will hand everyone over, each to his neighbor and to his king; they will crush the land, and I will not rescue anyone from their hand.
[Zechariah] [11]:[7] So I shepherded the flock marked for slaughter, especially the afflicted of the flock. I took two staffs: one I called Favor, the other I called Union; and I shepherded the flock.
[Zechariah] [11]:[8] In a single month I destroyed the three shepherds. I grew impatient with them, and they also loathed me.
[Zechariah] [11]:[9] Then I said, "I will not shepherd you any longer. Let the dying die, let the perishing perish, and let those who remain devour one another's flesh."
[Zechariah] [11]:[10] Then I took my staff Favor and broke it, annulling the covenant I had made with all the peoples.
[Zechariah] [11]:[11] It was annulled that day, and the afflicted of the flock who were watching me knew that this was the word of the LORD.
[Zechariah] [11]:[12] Then I said to them, "If it seems right to you, pay me my wages; if not, keep them." So they weighed out my wages: thirty pieces of silver.
[Zechariah] [11]:[13] And the LORD said to me, "Throw it to the potter"—that noble price at which they valued me! So I took the thirty shekels of silver and threw the money into the house of the LORD, to the potter.
[Zechariah] [11]:[14] Then I broke my second staff, Union, annulling the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
[Zechariah] [11]:[15] Then the LORD said to me: Take up once more the equipment of a foolish shepherd.
[Zechariah] [11]:[16] For I am raising up in the land a shepherd who will not care for the perishing, or seek the straying, or heal the injured, or feed the healthy, but will devour the flesh of the fat ones and tear off their hooves.
[Zechariah] [11]:[17] Woe to the worthless shepherd who deserts the flock! May the sword strike his arm and his right eye! May his arm wither away, and his right eye go utterly blind!
[Zechariah] [12]:[1] An oracle. The word of the LORD concerning Israel. Thus declares the LORD, who stretches out the heavens and lays the foundation of the earth and forms the spirit of man within him:
[Zechariah] [12]:[2] Look, I am making Jerusalem a cup that sends all the surrounding peoples reeling. Judah too will be under siege along with Jerusalem.
[Zechariah] [12]:[3] On that day I will make Jerusalem a stone too heavy to lift for all the peoples; everyone who tries to lift it will be badly injured. And all the nations of the earth will gather against her.
[Zechariah] [12]:[4] On that day, declares the LORD, I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness. But I will keep my eyes open over the house of Judah, while I strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.
[Zechariah] [12]:[5] Then the clans of Judah will say in their hearts, "The inhabitants of Jerusalem are our strength through the LORD of hosts, their God."
[Zechariah] [12]:[6] On that day I will make the clans of Judah like a blazing pot among wood, like a flaming torch among sheaves. They will devour all the surrounding peoples, to the right and to the left, and Jerusalem will dwell again in her own place, in Jerusalem.
[Zechariah] [12]:[7] The LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem may not be exalted above Judah.
[Zechariah] [12]:[8] On that day the LORD will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the weakest among them will be like David on that day, and the house of David will be like God, like the angel of the LORD going before them.
[Zechariah] [12]:[9] On that day I will set out to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.
[Zechariah] [12]:[10] And I will pour out on the house of David and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and of pleading for mercy. They will look on me, the one they have pierced, and they will mourn for him as one mourns for an only child, and grieve bitterly for him as one grieves for a firstborn son.
[Zechariah] [12]:[11] On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be as great as the mourning for Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
[Zechariah] [12]:[12] The land will mourn, each family by itself: the family of the house of David by itself and their wives by themselves; the family of the house of Nathan by itself and their wives by themselves;
[Zechariah] [12]:[13] the family of the house of Levi by itself and their wives by themselves; the family of the Shimeites by itself and their wives by themselves;
[Zechariah] [12]:[14] and all the remaining families, each family by itself and their wives by themselves.
[Zechariah] [13]:[1] On that day a fountain will be opened for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and impurity.
[Zechariah] [13]:[2] On that day, declares the LORD of hosts, I will erase the names of the idols from the land, and they will be remembered no more; I will also remove the prophets and the spirit of uncleanness from the land.
[Zechariah] [13]:[3] And if anyone still prophesies, his own father and mother, who gave him life, will say to him, "You shall not live, for you have spoken lies in the name of the LORD." And his father and mother, who gave him life, will run him through when he prophesies.
[Zechariah] [13]:[4] On that day every prophet will be ashamed of his vision when he prophesies; they will no longer put on a hairy cloak in order to deceive.
[Zechariah] [13]:[5] Each will say, "I am no prophet. I am a man who works the soil, for a man has owned me since my youth."
[Zechariah] [13]:[6] And if someone asks him, "What are these wounds between your arms?" he will answer, "These I received in the house of my friends."
[Zechariah] [13]:[7] Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, against the man who stands beside me, declares the LORD of hosts. Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered; and I will turn my hand against the little ones.
[Zechariah] [13]:[8] In all the land, declares the LORD, two thirds will be cut off and perish, but a third will be left in it.
[Zechariah] [13]:[9] And I will bring that third through the fire; I will refine them as silver is refined and test them as gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will answer them. I will say, "They are my people," and they will say, "The LORD is my God."
[Zechariah] [14]:[1] Look, a day is coming for the LORD, when your plunder will be divided in your very midst.
[Zechariah] [14]:[2] I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for battle. The city will be captured, the houses plundered, the women violated. Half the city will go into exile, but the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.
[Zechariah] [14]:[3] Then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations as he fights on a day of battle.
[Zechariah] [14]:[4] On that day his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem, and the Mount of Olives will be split in two, from east to west, forming a vast valley; half the mountain will move north and half of it south.
[Zechariah] [14]:[5] You will flee through the valley of my mountains, for the valley between the mountains will reach to Azal. You will flee as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with him.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew reads "with you," addressing the reader or the city; ancient versions read "with him."
[Zechariah] [14]:[6] On that day there will be no light, no cold, no frost.[^1] [^1]: The Hebrew of this line is uncertain; it may also be read: "there will be no light of the shining bodies, but cold and frost."
[Zechariah] [14]:[7] It will be a unique day, known to the LORD alone—neither day nor night—and at evening time there will be light.
[Zechariah] [14]:[8] On that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem, half of it to the eastern sea and half to the western sea, in summer and in winter alike.
[Zechariah] [14]:[9] The LORD will be king over all the earth. On that day the LORD will be one, and his name one.
[Zechariah] [14]:[10] The whole land will be turned into a plain from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem. But Jerusalem will rise high and remain in her place, from the Benjamin Gate to the site of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.
[Zechariah] [14]:[11] People will live in her, and never again will she be destroyed; Jerusalem will dwell in safety.
[Zechariah] [14]:[12] This will be the plague with which the LORD strikes all the peoples who wage war against Jerusalem: their flesh will rot while they are still standing on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.
[Zechariah] [14]:[13] On that day a great panic from the LORD will fall upon them. Each will seize the hand of his neighbor, and they will attack one another.
[Zechariah] [14]:[14] Judah too will fight at Jerusalem, and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered in—gold, silver, and clothing in great abundance.
[Zechariah] [14]:[15] A similar plague will strike the horses and mules, the camels and donkeys, and all the animals in those camps.
[Zechariah] [14]:[16] Then all who survive of the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, and to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
[Zechariah] [14]:[17] And if any of the families of the earth does not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of hosts, no rain will fall on them.
[Zechariah] [14]:[18] If the people of Egypt do not go up and take part, then they too will have no rain, and on them will fall the plague with which the LORD strikes the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
[Zechariah] [14]:[19] This will be the punishment of Egypt and the punishment of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
[Zechariah] [14]:[20] On that day even the bells on the horses will be inscribed "Holy to the LORD," and the cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the sacred bowls before the altar.
[Zechariah] [14]:[21] Every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of hosts, and all who come to sacrifice will take them and cook in them. And on that day there will no longer be any trader in the house of the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [1]:[1] An oracle: the word of the LORD to Israel through Malachi.[^1] [^1]: The name Malachi means "my messenger."
[Malachi] [1]:[2] I have loved you, says the LORD. But you ask, "How have you loved us?" Was not Esau Jacob's brother? declares the LORD. Yet I loved Jacob,
[Malachi] [1]:[3] but Esau I hated. I turned his mountains into a wasteland and left his inheritance to the jackals of the desert.[^1] [^1]: "Loved" and "hated" here are covenant terms of choosing and rejecting, not expressions of emotional hostility.
[Malachi] [1]:[4] Edom may say, "We have been shattered, but we will rebuild the ruins." This is what the LORD of hosts says: They may build, but I will tear down. They will be called the Land of Wickedness, the people with whom the LORD is angry forever.
[Malachi] [1]:[5] Your own eyes will see it, and you will say, "Great is the LORD, even beyond the borders of Israel!"
[Malachi] [1]:[6] A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If I am a father, where is the honor due me? If I am a master, where is the fear due me? says the LORD of hosts to you, O priests, who despise my name. But you ask, "How have we despised your name?"
[Malachi] [1]:[7] By placing defiled food on my altar. And you ask, "How have we defiled you?" By saying that the LORD's table is contemptible.
[Malachi] [1]:[8] When you bring blind animals for sacrifice, is that not wrong? When you offer the lame and the diseased, is that not wrong? Try presenting them to your governor! Would he be pleased with you? Would he receive you favorably? says the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [1]:[9] Now then, plead for God's favor, that he may be gracious to us. This is what your own hands have done—will he then show any of you favor? says the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [1]:[10] If only one of you would shut the temple doors, so that you would not light useless fires on my altar! I take no pleasure in you, says the LORD of hosts, and I will accept no offering from your hands.
[Malachi] [1]:[11] For from where the sun rises to where it sets, my name is great among the nations. In every place incense and a pure offering are brought to my name, for my name is great among the nations, says the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [1]:[12] But you profane my name by saying that the Lord's table is defiled, and its food is contemptible.
[Malachi] [1]:[13] And you say, "What a burden!" and you sniff at it in contempt, says the LORD of hosts. You bring what has been stolen, the lame and the diseased, and this you present as an offering. Should I accept that from your hands? says the LORD.
[Malachi] [1]:[14] Cursed is the cheat who has a male animal in his flock and vows to give it, but sacrifices a blemished one to the Lord. For I am a great King, says the LORD of hosts, and my name is feared among the nations.
[Malachi] [2]:[1] And now, you priests, this command is for you:
[Malachi] [2]:[2] If you will not listen, if you will not take it to heart and give honor to my name, says the LORD of hosts, then I will send the curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings—indeed, I have already cursed them, because you take nothing to heart.
[Malachi] [2]:[3] Look, I will rebuke your offspring, and I will fling dung in your faces, the dung of your festival offerings, and you will be carried off with it.
[Malachi] [2]:[4] Then you will know that I sent this command to you, so that my covenant with Levi might stand, says the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [2]:[5] My covenant with him was life and peace; these I gave him, and with them a holy fear, so that he revered me and stood in awe of my name.
[Malachi] [2]:[6] True instruction was in his mouth, and no wrong was found on his lips. He walked with me in peace and uprightness, and he turned many away from sin.
[Malachi] [2]:[7] For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and people should seek instruction from his mouth, for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [2]:[8] But you have turned aside from the way. By your instruction you have made many stumble; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi, says the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [2]:[9] So I in turn have made you despised and humiliated before all the people, because you have not kept my ways but have shown partiality in matters of instruction.
[Malachi] [2]:[10] Do we not all have one Father? Did not one God create us? Why then are we faithless to one another, profaning the covenant of our fathers?
[Malachi] [2]:[11] Judah has been faithless; an abomination has been committed in Israel and in Jerusalem. Judah has profaned the sanctuary the LORD loves, and has married the daughter of a foreign god.
[Malachi] [2]:[12] May the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob the man who does this—whoever he may be—even though he brings an offering to the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [2]:[13] And here is something else you do: you drown the LORD's altar in tears, weeping and groaning, because he no longer regards your offering or accepts it with favor from your hand.
[Malachi] [2]:[14] You ask, "Why?" Because the LORD stands as witness between you and the wife of your youth, to whom you have been faithless, though she is your companion, the wife of your covenant.
[Malachi] [2]:[15] Did he not make them one, with a portion of the spirit of life in their union? And what does the One seek? Godly offspring. So guard yourselves in your spirit, and let no one be faithless to the wife of his youth.
[Malachi] [2]:[16] For I hate divorce, says the LORD, the God of Israel, and I hate the one who covers his garment with violence, says the LORD of hosts. So guard yourselves in your spirit and do not be faithless.
[Malachi] [2]:[17] You have wearied the LORD with your words. And you ask, "How have we wearied him?" By saying, "Everyone who does evil is good in the LORD's eyes, and in such people he delights"—or, "Where is the God of justice?"
[Malachi] [3]:[1] Look, I am sending my messenger, and he will clear the way before me. Then suddenly the Lord whom you are seeking will come to his temple, and the messenger of the covenant whom you desire—look, he is coming, says the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [3]:[2] But who can endure the day of his coming? Who can stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner's fire, like a launderer's soap.
[Malachi] [3]:[3] He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver; he will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, so that they may bring offerings to the LORD in righteousness.
[Malachi] [3]:[4] Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the LORD, as in the days of old, as in years long past.
[Malachi] [3]:[5] I will come near to you for judgment. I will be a swift witness against sorcerers and adulterers, against those who swear falsely, against those who defraud the hired worker of his wages, who oppress the widow and the orphan, who push aside the foreigner and do not fear me, says the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [3]:[6] For I, the LORD, do not change; therefore you, children of Jacob, are not consumed.
[Malachi] [3]:[7] Ever since the days of your fathers you have turned aside from my statutes and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you, says the LORD of hosts. But you ask, "How are we to return?"
[Malachi] [3]:[8] Can a man rob God? Yet you are robbing me. But you ask, "How have we robbed you?" In the tithes and the offerings.
[Malachi] [3]:[9] You are under a curse—the whole nation of you—because you are robbing me.
[Malachi] [3]:[10] Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, so that there may be food in my house. Test me in this, says the LORD of hosts, and see if I will not open the windows of heaven for you and pour out on you a blessing beyond measure.
[Malachi] [3]:[11] I will rebuke the devourer for you, so that it will not destroy the fruit of your soil, and the vine in your field will not fail to bear, says the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [3]:[12] Then all the nations will call you blessed, for you will be a land of delight, says the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [3]:[13] Your words against me have been harsh, says the LORD. Yet you ask, "What have we said against you?"
[Malachi] [3]:[14] You have said, "It is pointless to serve God. What do we gain by keeping his charge and walking about in mourning before the LORD of hosts?
[Malachi] [3]:[15] "So now we call the arrogant blessed. Those who do evil prosper; they put God to the test and get away with it."
[Malachi] [3]:[16] Then those who feared the LORD spoke with one another, and the LORD listened and heard. A scroll of remembrance was written before him about those who fear the LORD and treasure his name.
[Malachi] [3]:[17] They will be mine, says the LORD of hosts, my treasured possession on the day when I act. I will spare them as a man spares his son who serves him.
[Malachi] [3]:[18] Then once again you will see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between the one who serves God and the one who does not serve him.
[Malachi] [3]:[19] For look, the day is coming, burning like a furnace. All the arrogant and every evildoer will be stubble, and the day that is coming will set them ablaze, says the LORD of hosts, leaving them neither root nor branch.
[Malachi] [3]:[20] But for you who fear my name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its wings, and you will go out leaping like calves released from the stall.
[Malachi] [3]:[21] You will trample the wicked; they will be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day when I act, says the LORD of hosts.
[Malachi] [3]:[22] Remember the law of my servant Moses, the statutes and judgments I gave him at Horeb for all Israel.
[Malachi] [3]:[23] Look, I am sending you Elijah the prophet before the great and dreadful day of the LORD comes.
[Malachi] [3]:[24] He will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and the hearts of children to their fathers; otherwise I will come and strike the land with utter destruction.
[Matthew] [1]:[1] This is the record of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
[Matthew] [1]:[2] Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac the father of Jacob, Jacob the father of Judah and his brothers,
[Matthew] [1]:[3] Judah the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar, Perez the father of Hezron, Hezron the father of Ram,
[Matthew] [1]:[4] Ram the father of Amminadab, Amminadab the father of Nahshon, Nahshon the father of Salmon,
[Matthew] [1]:[5] Salmon the father of Boaz by Rahab, Boaz the father of Obed by Ruth, Obed the father of Jesse,
[Matthew] [1]:[6] and Jesse the father of David the king. David was the father of Solomon by the wife of Uriah,
[Matthew] [1]:[7] Solomon the father of Rehoboam, Rehoboam the father of Abijah, Abijah the father of Asaph,
[Matthew] [1]:[8] Asaph the father of Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat the father of Joram, Joram the father of Uzziah,
[Matthew] [1]:[9] Uzziah the father of Jotham, Jotham the father of Ahaz, Ahaz the father of Hezekiah,
[Matthew] [1]:[10] Hezekiah the father of Manasseh, Manasseh the father of Amos, Amos the father of Josiah,
[Matthew] [1]:[11] and Josiah the father of Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the exile to Babylon.
[Matthew] [1]:[12] After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah was the father of Shealtiel, Shealtiel the father of Zerubbabel,
[Matthew] [1]:[13] Zerubbabel the father of Abiud, Abiud the father of Eliakim, Eliakim the father of Azor,
[Matthew] [1]:[14] Azor the father of Zadok, Zadok the father of Achim, Achim the father of Eliud,
[Matthew] [1]:[15] Eliud the father of Eleazar, Eleazar the father of Matthan, Matthan the father of Jacob,
[Matthew] [1]:[16] Jacob the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, and of her was born Jesus, who is called the Christ.
[Matthew] [1]:[17] So there were fourteen generations in all from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the Babylonian exile, and fourteen from the exile to the Christ.
[Matthew] [1]:[18] Now this is how the birth of Jesus Christ came about. His mother Mary was betrothed to Joseph, but before they came together she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit.
[Matthew] [1]:[19] Joseph, her husband, was a righteous man, and because he did not want to disgrace her publicly, he decided to divorce her quietly.
[Matthew] [1]:[20] But while he was considering this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary home as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
[Matthew] [1]:[21] She will give birth to a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins."
[Matthew] [1]:[22] All this took place to fulfill what the Lord had spoken through the prophet:
[Matthew] [1]:[23] "Behold, the virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel"—which means "God with us."
[Matthew] [1]:[24] When Joseph woke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him and took her home as his wife.
[Matthew] [1]:[25] But he had no relations with her until she gave birth to a son; and he named him Jesus.
[Matthew] [2]:[1] After Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea, in the days of King Herod, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem
[Matthew] [2]:[2] and asked, "Where is the one who has been born king of the Jews? We saw his star when it rose, and we have come to worship him."
[Matthew] [2]:[3] When King Herod heard this, he was deeply disturbed, and all Jerusalem with him.
[Matthew] [2]:[4] So he called together all the chief priests and scribes of the people and asked them where the Messiah was to be born.
[Matthew] [2]:[5] They told him, "In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is what was written through the prophet:
[Matthew] [2]:[6] 'And you, Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for out of you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.'"
[Matthew] [2]:[7] Then Herod called the wise men to him in secret and found out from them the exact time the star had appeared.
[Matthew] [2]:[8] So he sent them to Bethlehem and said, "Go and search carefully for the child. When you have found him, bring me word, so that I too may go and worship him."
[Matthew] [2]:[9] After they had heard the king, they set out; and behold, the star they had seen at its rising went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was.
[Matthew] [2]:[10] When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
[Matthew] [2]:[11] And when they came into the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasures and offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
[Matthew] [2]:[12] And having been warned in a dream not to go back to Herod, they returned to their own country by another route.
[Matthew] [2]:[13] After they had gone, suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, "Get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, for Herod is about to search for the child in order to kill him."
[Matthew] [2]:[14] So he got up, took the child and his mother during the night, and left for Egypt,
[Matthew] [2]:[15] where he stayed until Herod's death. This was to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet: "Out of Egypt I called my son."
[Matthew] [2]:[16] Then, when Herod realized that the wise men had outwitted him, he flew into a rage and gave orders to kill all the boys in Bethlehem and the whole surrounding region who were two years old and under, based on the time he had learned from the wise men.
[Matthew] [2]:[17] Then was fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet Jeremiah:
[Matthew] [2]:[18] "A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and loud lamentation: Rachel weeping for her children, and she would not be comforted, because they are no more."
[Matthew] [2]:[19] After Herod's death, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt
[Matthew] [2]:[20] and said, "Get up, take the child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who wanted to take the child's life are dead."
[Matthew] [2]:[21] So he got up, took the child and his mother, and went to the land of Israel.
[Matthew] [2]:[22] But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. And after being warned in a dream, he withdrew to the region of Galilee,
[Matthew] [2]:[23] and he came and settled in a town called Nazareth, so that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled: "He will be called a Nazarene."
[Matthew] [3]:[1] In those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea
[Matthew] [3]:[2] and saying, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near."
[Matthew] [3]:[3] This is the one spoken of through the prophet Isaiah, who said: "A voice of one calling in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.'"
[Matthew] [3]:[4] John himself wore clothing made of camel's hair with a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
[Matthew] [3]:[5] Then Jerusalem, all Judea, and the whole region around the Jordan went out to him,
[Matthew] [3]:[6] and they were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
[Matthew] [3]:[7] But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, "You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
[Matthew] [3]:[8] Produce fruit, then, worthy of repentance,
[Matthew] [3]:[9] and do not presume to say to yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' For I tell you, God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
[Matthew] [3]:[10] The axe is already laid at the root of the trees, so every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
[Matthew] [3]:[11] I baptize you with water for repentance, but the one coming after me is mightier than I, and I am not worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
[Matthew] [3]:[12] His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn up with unquenchable fire."
[Matthew] [3]:[13] Then Jesus came from Galilee to John at the Jordan, to be baptized by him.
[Matthew] [3]:[14] But John tried to prevent him, saying, "I need to be baptized by you, and yet you come to me?"
[Matthew] [3]:[15] But Jesus answered him, "Let it be so for now, for in this way it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness." Then John consented.
[Matthew] [3]:[16] As soon as Jesus was baptized, he came up out of the water. And behold, the heavens were opened, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him.
[Matthew] [3]:[17] And behold, a voice from heaven said, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
[Matthew] [4]:[1] Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
[Matthew] [4]:[2] After fasting forty days and forty nights, he was famished.
[Matthew] [4]:[3] The tempter came and said to him, "If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread."
[Matthew] [4]:[4] But he answered, "It is written: 'Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.'"
[Matthew] [4]:[5] Then the devil took him to the holy city and set him on the highest point of the temple.
[Matthew] [4]:[6] "If you are the Son of God," he said, "throw yourself down. For it is written: 'He will command his angels concerning you, and they will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.'"
[Matthew] [4]:[7] Jesus said to him, "It is also written: 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.'"
[Matthew] [4]:[8] Again the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their splendor.
[Matthew] [4]:[9] "All this I will give you," he said, "if you will fall down and worship me."
[Matthew] [4]:[10] Then Jesus said to him, "Away with you, Satan! For it is written: 'You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve.'"
[Matthew] [4]:[11] Then the devil left him, and behold, angels came and began to attend to him.
[Matthew] [4]:[12] When Jesus heard that John had been arrested, he withdrew to Galilee.
[Matthew] [4]:[13] Leaving Nazareth, he went and settled in Capernaum by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,
[Matthew] [4]:[14] to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah:
[Matthew] [4]:[15] "Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, along the road by the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles—
[Matthew] [4]:[16] the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light; and on those who sat in the land and shadow of death a light has dawned."
[Matthew] [4]:[17] From then on Jesus began to preach: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near."
[Matthew] [4]:[18] As he was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon called Peter and his brother Andrew, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
[Matthew] [4]:[19] He said to them, "Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of men."
[Matthew] [4]:[20] At once they left their nets and followed him.
[Matthew] [4]:[21] Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James son of Zebedee and his brother John, in the boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets. He called them,
[Matthew] [4]:[22] and at once they left the boat and their father and followed him.
[Matthew] [4]:[23] Jesus went throughout all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.
[Matthew] [4]:[24] News about him spread through all of Syria, and people brought him all who were ill with various diseases, those racked with pain, the demon-possessed, those suffering seizures, and the paralyzed—and he healed them.
[Matthew] [4]:[25] Large crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and the region beyond the Jordan.
[Matthew] [5]:[1] When he saw the crowds, he went up the mountain. He sat down, and his disciples came to him,
[Matthew] [5]:[2] and he began to teach them, saying:
[Matthew] [5]:[3] "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
[Matthew] [5]:[4] Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
[Matthew] [5]:[5] Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
[Matthew] [5]:[6] Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.
[Matthew] [5]:[7] Blessed are the merciful, for they will receive mercy.
[Matthew] [5]:[8] Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
[Matthew] [5]:[9] Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God.
[Matthew] [5]:[10] Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
[Matthew] [5]:[11] Blessed are you when people insult you and persecute you and speak all kinds of evil against you falsely because of me.
[Matthew] [5]:[12] Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in heaven; that is how they persecuted the prophets who came before you.
[Matthew] [5]:[13] You are the salt of the earth. But if salt loses its taste, how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by people.
[Matthew] [5]:[14] You are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hidden.
[Matthew] [5]:[15] No one lights a lamp and puts it under a basket; they set it on a stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.
[Matthew] [5]:[16] In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.
[Matthew] [5]:[17] Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them.
[Matthew] [5]:[18] Truly I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one letter, not one stroke of a letter, will pass from the Law until everything is accomplished.
[Matthew] [5]:[19] So whoever sets aside one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven; but whoever practices and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
[Matthew] [5]:[20] For I tell you, unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
[Matthew] [5]:[21] You have heard that it was said to those of old, 'You shall not murder,' and 'Whoever murders will be liable to judgment.'
[Matthew] [5]:[22] But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother will be liable to judgment; whoever says to his brother, 'Raca,' will be liable to the council; and whoever says, 'You fool,' will be liable to the fire of hell.[^1] [^1]: *Raca* is an Aramaic term of contempt, roughly 'empty-head' or 'good-for-nothing.'
[Matthew] [5]:[23] So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
[Matthew] [5]:[24] leave your gift there before the altar. First go and be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
[Matthew] [5]:[25] Settle matters quickly with your accuser while you are still on the way with him, or he may hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you will be thrown into prison.
[Matthew] [5]:[26] Truly I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the last penny.
[Matthew] [5]:[27] You have heard that it was said, 'You shall not commit adultery.'
[Matthew] [5]:[28] But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman with lust has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
[Matthew] [5]:[29] If your right eye causes you to sin, tear it out and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than to have your whole body thrown into hell.
[Matthew] [5]:[30] And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to lose one part of your body than to have your whole body go into hell.
[Matthew] [5]:[31] It was also said, 'Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.'
[Matthew] [5]:[32] But I tell you that anyone who divorces his wife, except on the grounds of sexual immorality, makes her the victim of adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
[Matthew] [5]:[33] Again, you have heard that it was said to those of old, 'You shall not swear falsely, but you shall fulfill to the Lord the oaths you have sworn.'
[Matthew] [5]:[34] But I tell you, do not swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is God's throne;
[Matthew] [5]:[35] nor by the earth, for it is his footstool; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
[Matthew] [5]:[36] And do not swear by your head, for you cannot make a single hair white or black.
[Matthew] [5]:[37] Let your word be 'Yes, yes' or 'No, no'; anything beyond this comes from the evil one.
[Matthew] [5]:[38] You have heard that it was said, 'An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.'
[Matthew] [5]:[39] But I tell you, do not resist the one who is evil. If anyone strikes you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.
[Matthew] [5]:[40] And if anyone wants to sue you and take your shirt, let him have your coat as well.
[Matthew] [5]:[41] If anyone forces you to go one mile, go with him two.
[Matthew] [5]:[42] Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.
[Matthew] [5]:[43] You have heard that it was said, 'You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'
[Matthew] [5]:[44] But I tell you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
[Matthew] [5]:[45] so that you may be sons of your Father in heaven. For he makes his sun rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
[Matthew] [5]:[46] For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
[Matthew] [5]:[47] And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
[Matthew] [5]:[48] You, therefore, are to be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
[Matthew] [6]:[1] "Be careful not to practice your righteousness in front of others, to be seen by them. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father in heaven.
[Matthew] [6]:[2] So when you give to the needy, don't sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets, to be praised by others. I tell you the truth: they have received their reward in full.
[Matthew] [6]:[3] But when you give to the needy, don't let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
[Matthew] [6]:[4] so that your giving may be in secret. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
[Matthew] [6]:[5] "And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. They love to stand and pray in the synagogues and on the street corners, to be seen by others. I tell you the truth: they have received their reward in full.
[Matthew] [6]:[6] But when you pray, go into your room, close the door, and pray to your Father, who is unseen. And your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
[Matthew] [6]:[7] And when you pray, do not babble on like the pagans, for they think they will be heard because of their many words.
[Matthew] [6]:[8] Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
[Matthew] [6]:[9] This, then, is how you should pray: "Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name,
[Matthew] [6]:[10] your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
[Matthew] [6]:[11] Give us today our daily bread.
[Matthew] [6]:[12] And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
[Matthew] [6]:[13] And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil."
[Matthew] [6]:[14] For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
