[Acts] [6]:[8] Now Stephen, full of grace and power, was performing great wonders and signs among the people.
[Acts] [6]:[9] But some men from the synagogue called the Synagogue of the Freedmen, including Cyrenians and Alexandrians and others from Cilicia and Asia, stood up and began to argue with Stephen.
[Acts] [6]:[10] But they could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke.
[Acts] [6]:[11] So they secretly instigated men to say, "We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses and against God."
[Acts] [6]:[12] They stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes; they came upon him, seized him, and brought him before the council.
[Acts] [6]:[13] They also produced false witnesses who said, "This man never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law.
[Acts] [6]:[14] For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs Moses handed down to us."
[Acts] [6]:[15] Everyone seated in the council fixed their eyes on him, and they saw that his face was like the face of an angel.
[Acts] [7]:[1] Then the high priest asked, "Are these charges true?"
[Acts] [7]:[2] And Stephen said: "Brothers and fathers, listen to me. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran,
[Acts] [7]:[3] and said to him, 'Leave your country and your kindred, and go to the land I will show you.'
[Acts] [7]:[4] So he left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. And after his father died, God moved him to this land where you are now living.
[Acts] [7]:[5] He gave him no inheritance in it, not even a foot of ground, yet he promised to give it to him as a possession, and to his descendants after him, though at the time he had no child.
[Acts] [7]:[6] And God said this: his descendants would live as strangers in a foreign land, and they would be enslaved and mistreated for four hundred years.
[Acts] [7]:[7] 'But I will judge the nation they serve,' God said, 'and afterward they will come out and worship me in this place.'
[Acts] [7]:[8] And God gave him the covenant of circumcision. So Abraham became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day; and Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob of the twelve patriarchs.
[Acts] [7]:[9] "The patriarchs, jealous of Joseph, sold him into Egypt. But God was with him,
[Acts] [7]:[10] and rescued him from all his troubles. He gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who made him ruler over Egypt and over all his household.
[Acts] [7]:[11] Then a famine came over all Egypt and Canaan, bringing great hardship, and our fathers could find no food.
[Acts] [7]:[12] When Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our fathers there on a first visit.
[Acts] [7]:[13] On their second visit Joseph made himself known to his brothers, and Pharaoh learned of Joseph's family.
[Acts] [7]:[14] Then Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives, seventy-five people in all.
[Acts] [7]:[15] So Jacob went down to Egypt, where he and our fathers died.
[Acts] [7]:[16] Their bodies were brought back to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
[Acts] [7]:[17] "As the time drew near for the promise God had made to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
[Acts] [7]:[18] until another king rose to power over Egypt who knew nothing of Joseph.
[Acts] [7]:[19] He dealt treacherously with our people and oppressed our fathers, forcing them to abandon their infants so they would not survive.
[Acts] [7]:[20] At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful in God's sight. For three months he was raised in his father's house,
[Acts] [7]:[21] and when he was abandoned, Pharaoh's daughter took him and brought him up as her own son.
[Acts] [7]:[22] So Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was powerful in his words and deeds.
[Acts] [7]:[23] When he was forty years old, he decided to visit his brothers, the people of Israel.
[Acts] [7]:[24] Seeing one of them being wronged, he came to his defense and avenged him by striking down the Egyptian.
[Acts] [7]:[25] He assumed his brothers would understand that God was using him to bring them deliverance, but they did not.
[Acts] [7]:[26] The next day he came upon two of them fighting and tried to reconcile them, saying, 'Men, you are brothers. Why are you wronging each other?'
[Acts] [7]:[27] But the one who was wronging his neighbor pushed him aside and said, 'Who made you ruler and judge over us?
[Acts] [7]:[28] Do you mean to kill me the way you killed the Egyptian yesterday?'
[Acts] [7]:[29] At this word Moses fled and lived as a stranger in the land of Midian, where he became the father of two sons.
[Acts] [7]:[30] "Forty years later an angel appeared to him in the wilderness near Mount Sinai, in the flame of a burning bush.
[Acts] [7]:[31] When Moses saw it, he was amazed at the sight. And as he drew near to look, the voice of the Lord came to him:
[Acts] [7]:[32] 'I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob.' Moses began to tremble and dared not look.
[Acts] [7]:[33] Then the Lord said to him, 'Take off the sandals from your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.
[Acts] [7]:[34] I have surely seen the oppression of my people in Egypt. I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to set them free. Now come, I will send you to Egypt.'
[Acts] [7]:[35] "This Moses, whom they rejected with the words, 'Who made you ruler and judge?'—this is the man God sent as both ruler and redeemer, by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
[Acts] [7]:[36] He led them out, performing wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
[Acts] [7]:[37] This is the Moses who said to the people of Israel, 'God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.'
[Acts] [7]:[38] He is the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers; and he received living words to pass on to us.
[Acts] [7]:[39] But our fathers refused to obey him. They rejected him and in their hearts turned back to Egypt,
[Acts] [7]:[40] saying to Aaron, 'Make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses who led us out of the land of Egypt, we have no idea what has become of him.'
[Acts] [7]:[41] In those days they made a calf, offered a sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.
[Acts] [7]:[42] So God turned away and gave them over to the worship of the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: 'Did you bring me sacrifices and offerings for forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?
[Acts] [7]:[43] No, you carried the tent of Molech and the star of the god Rephan, the images you made to worship. So I will send you into exile beyond Babylon.'
[Acts] [7]:[44] Our fathers had the tent of testimony in the wilderness, made just as the one who spoke to Moses directed, according to the pattern he had seen.
[Acts] [7]:[45] Our fathers who followed them brought it with them under Joshua when they took possession of the land from the nations God drove out before them. And it remained until the days of David,
[Acts] [7]:[46] who found favor with God and asked to provide a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
[Acts] [7]:[47] But it was Solomon who built him a house.
[Acts] [7]:[48] Yet the Most High does not live in houses made by human hands. As the prophet says:
[Acts] [7]:[49] 'Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool for my feet. What kind of house will you build for me, says the Lord, or what place is there for my rest?
[Acts] [7]:[50] Has not my own hand made all these things?'
[Acts] [7]:[51] "You stubborn people, uncircumcised in heart and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit—just as your fathers did, so do you.
[Acts] [7]:[52] Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? They killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One, and now you have betrayed and murdered him—
[Acts] [7]:[53] you who received the law delivered by angels, and did not keep it."
[Acts] [7]:[54] When they heard this, they were enraged in their hearts and ground their teeth at him.
[Acts] [7]:[55] But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at God's right hand.
[Acts] [7]:[56] "Look," he said, "I see heaven opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God."
[Acts] [7]:[57] But they screamed at the top of their voices, covered their ears, and rushed at him with one accord.
[Acts] [7]:[58] They dragged him out of the city and began to stone him. Meanwhile the witnesses laid their cloaks at the feet of a young man named Saul.
[Acts] [7]:[59] And as they stoned him, Stephen called out, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
[Acts] [7]:[60] Then he fell to his knees and cried out with a loud voice, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." And with these words he fell asleep.[^1] [^1]: "Fell asleep" is a gentle way of saying he died.
[Acts] [8]:[1] Saul approved of Stephen's execution. That same day a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem, and all except the apostles were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria.
[Acts] [8]:[2] Devout men buried Stephen and mourned him deeply.
[Acts] [8]:[3] But Saul was ravaging the church. Going from house to house, he dragged off men and women and threw them into prison.
[Acts] [8]:[4] Those who had been scattered went from place to place, preaching the word.
[Acts] [8]:[5] Philip went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed the Christ to them.
[Acts] [8]:[6] The crowds listened with one mind to what Philip said, hearing him and seeing the signs he performed.
[Acts] [8]:[7] For unclean spirits came out of many who had them, shrieking with a loud voice, and many who were paralyzed or lame were healed.
[Acts] [8]:[8] So there was great joy in that city.
[Acts] [8]:[9] Now a man named Simon had been in the city for some time, practicing magic and astounding the people of Samaria, claiming to be someone great.
[Acts] [8]:[10] Everyone, from the least to the greatest, paid attention to him and said, "This man is the power of God that is called Great."
[Acts] [8]:[11] They gave him their attention because for a long time he had astounded them with his magic.
[Acts] [8]:[12] But when they believed Philip as he proclaimed the good news of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
[Acts] [8]:[13] Even Simon himself believed, and after being baptized he stayed close to Philip, amazed at the signs and great miracles that were taking place.
[Acts] [8]:[14] When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
[Acts] [8]:[15] They went down and prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit,
[Acts] [8]:[16] for the Spirit had not yet come upon any of them; they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
[Acts] [8]:[17] Then they laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
[Acts] [8]:[18] When Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles' hands, he offered them money
[Acts] [8]:[19] and said, "Give me this authority too, so that anyone I lay my hands on may receive the Holy Spirit."
[Acts] [8]:[20] But Peter said to him, "May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could buy God's gift with money!
[Acts] [8]:[21] You have no part or share in this matter, for your heart is not right before God.
[Acts] [8]:[22] Repent, then, of this wickedness of yours, and pray to the Lord that, if possible, the intent of your heart may be forgiven you.
[Acts] [8]:[23] For I see that you are full of bitter gall and bound up in wickedness."
[Acts] [8]:[24] Simon answered, "Pray to the Lord for me, that none of what you have said may come upon me."
[Acts] [8]:[25] After they had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they started back to Jerusalem, preaching the gospel in many Samaritan villages along the way.
[Acts] [8]:[26] An angel of the Lord spoke to Philip: "Get up and go south, to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza." This is a desert road.
[Acts] [8]:[27] So he got up and went. And there was an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was in charge of all her treasury. He had come to Jerusalem to worship,
[Acts] [8]:[28] and was on his way home, sitting in his chariot and reading the prophet Isaiah.
[Acts] [8]:[29] The Spirit said to Philip, "Go over and stay close to that chariot."
[Acts] [8]:[30] Philip ran up and heard him reading the prophet Isaiah. "Do you understand what you are reading?" he asked.
[Acts] [8]:[31] "How can I," he said, "unless someone guides me?" And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
[Acts] [8]:[32] This was the passage of Scripture he was reading: "Like a sheep he was led to the slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth.
[Acts] [8]:[33] In his humiliation he was denied justice. Who can tell of his descendants? For his life is taken from the earth."
[Acts] [8]:[34] The eunuch said to Philip, "Tell me, please, who is the prophet speaking about? Himself, or someone else?"
[Acts] [8]:[35] Then Philip began with that passage of Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.
[Acts] [8]:[36] As they traveled along the road, they came to some water, and the eunuch said, "Look, here is water. What is to keep me from being baptized?"
[Acts] [8]:[37] Philip said, "If you believe with all your heart, you may." And he answered, "I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God."[^1] [^1]: This verse is not found in the earliest manuscripts.
[Acts] [8]:[38] He ordered the chariot to stop, and both of them went down into the water, Philip and the eunuch, and Philip baptized him.
[Acts] [8]:[39] When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, but went on his way rejoicing.
[Acts] [8]:[40] Philip, however, found himself at Azotus, and he traveled about, preaching the gospel in all the towns until he came to Caesarea.
[Acts] [9]:[1] Meanwhile Saul, still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest
[Acts] [9]:[2] and asked him for letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found anyone belonging to the Way, men or women, he could bring them back to Jerusalem in chains.
[Acts] [9]:[3] As he traveled and was approaching Damascus, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.
[Acts] [9]:[4] He fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?"
[Acts] [9]:[5] "Who are you, Lord?" he asked. "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting," he replied.
[Acts] [9]:[6] "Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do."
[Acts] [9]:[7] The men traveling with him stood speechless; they heard the voice but saw no one.
[Acts] [9]:[8] Saul got up from the ground, and though his eyes were open he could see nothing. So they took him by the hand and led him into Damascus.
[Acts] [9]:[9] For three days he was without sight, and he neither ate nor drank.
[Acts] [9]:[10] In Damascus there was a disciple named Ananias. The Lord said to him in a vision, "Ananias!" "Here I am, Lord," he answered.
[Acts] [9]:[11] The Lord said to him, "Get up and go to the street called Straight, and ask at the house of Judas for a man from Tarsus named Saul. He is praying,
[Acts] [9]:[12] and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come in and lay his hands on him so that he may see again."
[Acts] [9]:[13] But Ananias answered, "Lord, I have heard from many people about this man and all the harm he has done to your saints in Jerusalem.
[Acts] [9]:[14] And here he has authority from the chief priests to arrest everyone who calls on your name."
[Acts] [9]:[15] But the Lord said to him, "Go, for this man is my chosen instrument to carry my name before the Gentiles and their kings and before the people of Israel.
[Acts] [9]:[16] I myself will show him how much he must suffer for my name."
[Acts] [9]:[17] So Ananias went and entered the house. He laid his hands on Saul and said, "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming, has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit."
[Acts] [9]:[18] Immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he could see again. He got up and was baptized,
[Acts] [9]:[19] and after taking some food he regained his strength. He stayed some days with the disciples in Damascus,
[Acts] [9]:[20] and at once he began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues: "He is the Son of God."
[Acts] [9]:[21] All who heard him were astounded and said, "Isn't this the man who wreaked havoc in Jerusalem among those who call on this name? And hasn't he come here to bring them in chains to the chief priests?"
[Acts] [9]:[22] But Saul grew all the stronger and confounded the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ.
[Acts] [9]:[23] After many days had passed, the Jews plotted to kill him,
[Acts] [9]:[24] but Saul learned of their plot. They were watching the gates day and night in order to kill him,
[Acts] [9]:[25] so his disciples took him by night and lowered him in a basket through the wall.
[Acts] [9]:[26] When he came to Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
[Acts] [9]:[27] But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles. He told them how Saul had seen the Lord on the road, that the Lord had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had preached boldly in the name of Jesus.
[Acts] [9]:[28] So he went in and out among them in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.
[Acts] [9]:[29] He talked and debated with the Greek-speaking Jews, but they tried to kill him.
[Acts] [9]:[30] When the brothers found out, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
[Acts] [9]:[31] So the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace and was built up. Living in the fear of the Lord and in the encouragement of the Holy Spirit, it continued to grow.
[Acts] [9]:[32] As Peter traveled about the country, he also came down to the saints living in Lydda.
[Acts] [9]:[33] There he found a man named Aeneas, who had been bedridden for eight years, paralyzed.
[Acts] [9]:[34] Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed." And immediately he got up.
[Acts] [9]:[35] All who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
[Acts] [9]:[36] In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha, which translated means Dorcas. She was always doing good works and giving to those in need.
[Acts] [9]:[37] About that time she fell sick and died. They washed her body and laid her in an upstairs room.
[Acts] [9]:[38] Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard that Peter was there and sent two men to him with the plea, "Please come to us at once!"
[Acts] [9]:[39] So Peter got up and went with them. When he arrived, they took him to the upstairs room, and all the widows stood around him weeping and showing him the robes and other clothing that Dorcas had made while she was with them.
[Acts] [9]:[40] Peter sent them all out of the room, knelt down, and prayed. Then he turned to the body and said, "Tabitha, get up." She opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter she sat up.
[Acts] [9]:[41] He gave her his hand and helped her to her feet. Then he called the saints and the widows and presented her to them alive.
[Acts] [9]:[42] This became known all over Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
[Acts] [9]:[43] Peter stayed on in Joppa for many days with a tanner named Simon.
[Acts] [10]:[1] In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion of what was called the Italian Cohort.
[Acts] [10]:[2] He was devout and God-fearing, together with his whole household; he gave generously to those in need among the people and prayed to God constantly.
[Acts] [10]:[3] One afternoon, about three o'clock, he saw clearly in a vision an angel of God who came to him and said, "Cornelius."
[Acts] [10]:[4] He stared at him in terror and said, "What is it, Lord?" The angel said to him, "Your prayers and your acts of mercy have gone up as a memorial offering before God.
[Acts] [10]:[5] Now send men to Joppa and summon a certain Simon who is called Peter.
[Acts] [10]:[6] He is a guest of Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea."
[Acts] [10]:[7] When the angel who had spoken to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier from among his personal attendants.
[Acts] [10]:[8] He explained everything to them and sent them to Joppa.
[Acts] [10]:[9] The next day, as they were on their way and approaching the city, Peter went up on the roof about noon to pray.
[Acts] [10]:[10] He became hungry and wanted something to eat, but while it was being prepared he fell into a trance.
[Acts] [10]:[11] He saw heaven opened and something like a great sheet coming down, being lowered to the earth by its four corners.
[Acts] [10]:[12] In it were all kinds of four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth and birds of the air.
[Acts] [10]:[13] Then a voice said to him, "Get up, Peter. Kill and eat."
[Acts] [10]:[14] But Peter said, "By no means, Lord! I have never eaten anything common or unclean."
[Acts] [10]:[15] The voice came to him again, a second time: "What God has cleansed, you must not call common."
[Acts] [10]:[16] This happened three times, and immediately the sheet was taken up into heaven.
[Acts] [10]:[17] While Peter was still puzzling over what the vision he had seen might mean, the men sent by Cornelius had asked their way to Simon's house and were standing at the gate.
[Acts] [10]:[18] They called out, asking whether Simon who was called Peter was staying there.
[Acts] [10]:[19] While Peter was pondering the vision, the Spirit said to him, "Look, some men are searching for you.
[Acts] [10]:[20] Get up, go downstairs, and go with them without hesitating, for I have sent them."
[Acts] [10]:[21] So Peter went down to the men and said, "I am the one you are looking for. What is the reason for your coming?"
[Acts] [10]:[22] They said, "Cornelius the centurion, a righteous and God-fearing man, well spoken of by the whole Jewish nation, was directed by a holy angel to send for you to come to his house and to hear what you have to say."
[Acts] [10]:[23] So Peter invited them in and gave them lodging. The next day he got up and went with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa went along with him.
[Acts] [10]:[24] The following day he arrived in Caesarea. Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and close friends.
[Acts] [10]:[25] As Peter was about to enter, Cornelius met him, fell at his feet, and worshiped him.
[Acts] [10]:[26] But Peter raised him up, saying, "Stand up. I am only a man myself."
[Acts] [10]:[27] As he talked with him, he went inside and found many people gathered together.
[Acts] [10]:[28] He said to them, "You know that it is forbidden for a Jew to associate with or visit a foreigner. But God has shown me that I must not call anyone common or unclean.
[Acts] [10]:[29] That is why I came without objection when I was sent for. So I ask why you sent for me."
[Acts] [10]:[30] Cornelius said, "Four days ago, at this very hour, three in the afternoon, I was praying in my house, when suddenly a man in shining clothes stood before me
[Acts] [10]:[31] and said, 'Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your acts of mercy have been remembered before God.
[Acts] [10]:[32] Send therefore to Joppa and summon Simon who is called Peter. He is a guest in the house of Simon the tanner, by the sea.'
[Acts] [10]:[33] So I sent for you at once, and you were kind enough to come. Now then, we are all here in the presence of God to hear everything the Lord has commanded you to say."
[Acts] [10]:[34] Then Peter began to speak: "Now I truly understand that God shows no partiality,
[Acts] [10]:[35] but in every nation the one who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.
[Acts] [10]:[36] He sent his word to the people of Israel, proclaiming the good news of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.
[Acts] [10]:[37] You know what has happened throughout all Judea, beginning in Galilee after the baptism that John proclaimed:
[Acts] [10]:[38] how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, and how he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.
[Acts] [10]:[39] And we are witnesses of everything he did both in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They put him to death by hanging him on a tree,
[Acts] [10]:[40] but God raised him on the third day and caused him to be seen—
[Acts] [10]:[41] not by all the people, but by witnesses God had chosen beforehand, by us who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.
[Acts] [10]:[42] And he commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he is the one appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead.
[Acts] [10]:[43] To him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name."
[Acts] [10]:[44] While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all who were listening to the message.
[Acts] [10]:[45] The circumcised believers who had come with Peter were astounded that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles,
[Acts] [10]:[46] for they heard them speaking in tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter responded,
[Acts] [10]:[47] "Surely no one can withhold the water for baptizing these people, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we have!"
[Acts] [10]:[48] And he directed that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay on for a few days.
[Acts] [11]:[1] The apostles and the brothers throughout Judea heard that the Gentiles too had received the word of God.
[Acts] [11]:[2] So when Peter came up to Jerusalem, those of the circumcision took issue with him,
[Acts] [11]:[3] saying, "You went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them."
[Acts] [11]:[4] Then Peter began and laid the matter out for them step by step:
[Acts] [11]:[5] "I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: something like a large sheet was coming down, lowered from heaven by its four corners, and it came right down to me.
[Acts] [11]:[6] I looked into it closely and saw the four-footed animals of the earth, the wild beasts, the reptiles, and the birds of the air.
[Acts] [11]:[7] And I heard a voice saying to me, 'Get up, Peter; kill and eat.'
[Acts] [11]:[8] But I said, 'By no means, Lord, for nothing common or unclean has ever entered my mouth.'
[Acts] [11]:[9] The voice answered a second time from heaven, 'What God has cleansed, you must not call common.'
[Acts] [11]:[10] This happened three times, and then everything was drawn back up into heaven.
[Acts] [11]:[11] And at that very moment three men arrived at the house where we were staying, sent to me from Caesarea.
[Acts] [11]:[12] The Spirit told me to go with them without hesitating. These six brothers came with me as well, and we entered the man's house.
[Acts] [11]:[13] He told us how he had seen the angel standing in his house and saying, 'Send to Joppa and summon Simon who is called Peter;
[Acts] [11]:[14] he will speak words to you by which you will be saved, you and your whole household.'
[Acts] [11]:[15] As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them just as he had on us at the beginning.
[Acts] [11]:[16] Then I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, 'John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.'
[Acts] [11]:[17] So if God gave them the same gift he gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to stand in God's way?"
[Acts] [11]:[18] When they heard this, they fell silent, and they glorified God, saying, "So then, God has granted even to the Gentiles the repentance that leads to life."
[Acts] [11]:[19] Now those who had been scattered by the persecution that arose over Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except Jews.
[Acts] [11]:[20] But some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, came to Antioch and began speaking to the Greeks as well, proclaiming the good news of the Lord Jesus.^f
[Acts] [11]:[21] The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.
[Acts] [11]:[22] News of them reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas off to Antioch.
[Acts] [11]:[23] When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced, and he encouraged them all to remain faithful to the Lord with steadfast hearts,
[Acts] [11]:[24] for he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a large number of people were added to the Lord.
[Acts] [11]:[25] Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,
[Acts] [11]:[26] and when he found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they met with the church and taught a great many people. It was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians.
[Acts] [11]:[27] In those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
[Acts] [11]:[28] One of them, named Agabus, stood up and indicated through the Spirit that a severe famine was about to come over the whole world; this happened in the days of Claudius.
[Acts] [11]:[29] So the disciples determined, each according to his ability, to send relief to the brothers living in Judea.
[Acts] [11]:[30] And they did so, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.
[Acts] [12]:[1] About that time King Herod arrested some who belonged to the church, intending to do them harm.
[Acts] [12]:[2] He had James, the brother of John, put to death by the sword.
[Acts] [12]:[3] When he saw that this pleased the Jews, he went on to seize Peter as well. This was during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
[Acts] [12]:[4] After arresting him, he put him in prison and handed him over to four squads of four soldiers each to guard him, intending to bring him out for public trial after the Passover.
[Acts] [12]:[5] So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was praying to God for him without ceasing.
[Acts] [12]:[6] On the very night before Herod was to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, while sentries stood guard at the door of the prison.
[Acts] [12]:[7] Suddenly an angel of the Lord stood there, and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side and woke him, saying, "Quick, get up!" And the chains fell from his wrists.
[Acts] [12]:[8] Then the angel said to him, "Get dressed and put on your sandals." He did so. "Wrap your cloak around you," the angel said, "and follow me."
[Acts] [12]:[9] So Peter went out and followed him, not realizing that what the angel was doing was real; he thought he was seeing a vision.
[Acts] [12]:[10] They passed the first guard post and then the second, and came to the iron gate leading into the city. It opened for them by itself, and they went out and walked the length of one street. Then, all at once, the angel left him.
[Acts] [12]:[11] Peter came to himself and said, "Now I know beyond a doubt that the Lord has sent his angel and rescued me from Herod's hand and from everything the Jewish people were expecting."
[Acts] [12]:[12] Realizing this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark, where many had gathered and were praying.
[Acts] [12]:[13] When he knocked at the outer door, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.
[Acts] [12]:[14] Recognizing Peter's voice, she was so overjoyed that instead of opening the gate she ran in and announced that Peter was standing outside.
[Acts] [12]:[15] "You are out of your mind," they told her. But she kept insisting it was so, and they said, "It is his angel."
[Acts] [12]:[16] Meanwhile Peter kept on knocking. When they opened the door and saw him, they were astounded.
[Acts] [12]:[17] He motioned with his hand for them to be quiet and told them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. "Report this to James and to the brothers," he said. Then he left and went to another place.
[Acts] [12]:[18] When morning came, there was no small commotion among the soldiers over what had become of Peter.
[Acts] [12]:[19] Herod made a thorough search for him, and when he did not find him, he interrogated the guards and ordered them led away for execution. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.
[Acts] [12]:[20] Now Herod was in a bitter quarrel with the people of Tyre and Sidon. So they came to him together and, after winning over Blastus, the king's personal attendant, they asked for peace, because their country depended on the king's land for its food.
[Acts] [12]:[21] On the appointed day Herod put on his royal robes, took his seat on the judgment platform, and delivered a public address to them.
[Acts] [12]:[22] The crowd kept shouting, "This is the voice of a god, not of a man!"
[Acts] [12]:[23] At once an angel of the Lord struck him down, because he had not given God the glory, and he was eaten by worms and died.
[Acts] [12]:[24] But the word of God continued to grow and spread.
[Acts] [12]:[25] When Barnabas and Saul had completed their mission to Jerusalem, they returned, taking with them John, also called Mark.
[Acts] [13]:[1] In the church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen, who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
[Acts] [13]:[2] While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them."
[Acts] [13]:[3] So after fasting and praying, they laid their hands on them and sent them off.
[Acts] [13]:[4] Sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia and from there sailed to Cyprus.
[Acts] [13]:[5] When they arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. John was with them as their helper.
[Acts] [13]:[6] They traveled through the whole island as far as Paphos, where they found a Jewish magician and false prophet named Bar-Jesus,
[Acts] [13]:[7] who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. The proconsul sent for Barnabas and Saul, eager to hear the word of God.
[Acts] [13]:[8] But Elymas the magician—for that is what his name means—opposed them, trying to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
[Acts] [13]:[9] Then Saul, who was also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked straight at him
[Acts] [13]:[10] and said, "You are full of every kind of deceit and fraud, you son of the devil, you enemy of all that is right! Will you never stop twisting the straight paths of the Lord?
[Acts] [13]:[11] Now look, the hand of the Lord is against you. You will be blind, unable to see the sun, for a time." Immediately a mist and darkness came over him, and he groped about, looking for someone to lead him by the hand.
[Acts] [13]:[12] When the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed, astounded at the teaching of the Lord.
[Acts] [13]:[13] Paul and his companions set sail from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia, but John left them and returned to Jerusalem.
[Acts] [13]:[14] They went on from Perga and arrived at Antioch in Pisidia. On the Sabbath they went into the synagogue and sat down.
[Acts] [13]:[15] After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent word to them: "Brothers, if you have any word of encouragement for the people, speak."
[Acts] [13]:[16] So Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and said: "Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen to me.
[Acts] [13]:[17] The God of this people Israel chose our fathers and made them a great people during their stay in Egypt; then with a mighty arm he led them out of it,
[Acts] [13]:[18] and for about forty years he bore with them in the wilderness.
[Acts] [13]:[19] He overthrew seven nations in Canaan and gave their land to our fathers as an inheritance.
[Acts] [13]:[20] All this took about four hundred and fifty years. After that he gave them judges, until the time of Samuel the prophet.
[Acts] [13]:[21] Then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who ruled for forty years.
[Acts] [13]:[22] After removing him, he raised up David to be their king, and testified about him: 'I have found David son of Jesse, a man after my own heart; he will do all that I want him to do.'
[Acts] [13]:[23] From this man's descendants God has brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus, as he promised.
[Acts] [13]:[24] Before his coming, John had proclaimed a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
[Acts] [13]:[25] As John was completing his course, he said: 'Who do you suppose I am? I am not the one. No, but one is coming after me whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.'
[Acts] [13]:[26] Brothers, children of Abraham, and you who fear God: it is to us that this message of salvation has been sent.
[Acts] [13]:[27] The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize him, and by condemning him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.
[Acts] [13]:[28] Though they found no ground for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have him executed.
[Acts] [13]:[29] When they had carried out everything written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.
[Acts] [13]:[30] But God raised him from the dead,
[Acts] [13]:[31] and for many days he appeared to those who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now his witnesses to the people.
[Acts] [13]:[32] And we bring you the good news: what God promised our fathers
[Acts] [13]:[33] he has fulfilled for us, their children, by raising up Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm: 'You are my Son; today I have begotten you.'
[Acts] [13]:[34] And that he raised him from the dead, never to return to decay, he declared in these words: 'I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.'
[Acts] [13]:[35] So it is said in another place: 'You will not let your Holy One see decay.'
[Acts] [13]:[36] Now David, after serving God's purpose in his own generation, fell asleep, was laid with his fathers, and did see decay.
[Acts] [13]:[37] But the one whom God raised up did not see decay.
[Acts] [13]:[38] Therefore, brothers, know this: through him forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you—and from everything from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses,
[Acts] [13]:[39] through him everyone who believes is justified.
[Acts] [13]:[40] Take care, then, that what is said in the Prophets does not come upon you:
[Acts] [13]:[41] 'Look, you scoffers—marvel and perish! For I am doing a work in your days, a work you would never believe, even if someone told you.'
[Acts] [13]:[42] As they were leaving, the people urged them to speak about these things again on the next Sabbath.
[Acts] [13]:[43] When the assembly broke up, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas, who spoke with them and urged them to remain in the grace of God.
[Acts] [13]:[44] On the next Sabbath almost the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
[Acts] [13]:[45] But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy and contradicted what Paul was saying, heaping insults on him.
[Acts] [13]:[46] Then Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly: "It was necessary that the word of God be spoken to you first. But since you reject it and do not judge yourselves worthy of eternal life, look, we are turning to the Gentiles.
[Acts] [13]:[47] For this is what the Lord has commanded us: 'I have made you a light for the Gentiles, that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.'"
[Acts] [13]:[48] When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and all who were appointed for eternal life believed.
[Acts] [13]:[49] And the word of the Lord spread through the whole region.
[Acts] [13]:[50] But the Jews stirred up the devout women of high standing and the leading men of the city, and they stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their district.
[Acts] [13]:[51] So they shook the dust from their feet against them and went to Iconium.
[Acts] [13]:[52] And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
[Acts] [14]:[1] In Iconium they went as usual into the Jewish synagogue and spoke so effectively that a great number of both Jews and Greeks came to faith.
[Acts] [14]:[2] But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers.
[Acts] [14]:[3] So they stayed there a long time, speaking boldly in reliance on the Lord, who confirmed the message of his grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.
[Acts] [14]:[4] The people of the city were divided: some sided with the Jews, others with the apostles.
[Acts] [14]:[5] When the Gentiles and Jews, together with their leaders, made a move to mistreat them and stone them,
[Acts] [14]:[6] they learned of it and fled to Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and to the surrounding region,
[Acts] [14]:[7] and there they went on preaching the gospel.
[Acts] [14]:[8] In Lystra a man was sitting who had no strength in his feet. He had been lame from birth and had never walked.
[Acts] [14]:[9] He was listening as Paul spoke. Paul looked straight at him, saw that he had faith to be healed,
[Acts] [14]:[10] and said in a loud voice, "Stand up straight on your feet!" And the man jumped up and began to walk.
[Acts] [14]:[11] When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they shouted in the Lycaonian language, "The gods have come down to us in human form!"
[Acts] [14]:[12] They called Barnabas Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.
[Acts] [14]:[13] The priest of Zeus, whose temple stood just outside the city, brought bulls and garlands to the gates, intending to offer sacrifice along with the crowds.
[Acts] [14]:[14] But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard of it, they tore their clothes and rushed out into the crowd, shouting:
[Acts] [14]:[15] "Men, why are you doing this? We are only human beings, with the same nature as you. We bring you good news, that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything in them.
[Acts] [14]:[16] "In past generations he let all the nations go their own ways,
[Acts] [14]:[17] yet he did not leave himself without witness: he did good, giving you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness."
[Acts] [14]:[18] Even with these words they barely restrained the crowds from sacrificing to them.
[Acts] [14]:[19] Then Jews came from Antioch and Iconium. They won over the crowds, stoned Paul, and dragged him outside the city, thinking he was dead.
[Acts] [14]:[20] But when the disciples gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. The next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
[Acts] [14]:[21] They preached the gospel in that city and made many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, to Iconium, and to Antioch,
[Acts] [14]:[22] strengthening the souls of the disciples and encouraging them to remain firm in the faith. "We must go through many hardships to enter the kingdom of God," they said.
[Acts] [14]:[23] They appointed elders for them in each congregation and, with prayer and fasting, committed them to the Lord in whom they had come to believe.
[Acts] [14]:[24] Then they passed through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia,
[Acts] [14]:[25] and after preaching the word in Perga they went down to Attalia.
[Acts] [14]:[26] From there they sailed back to Antioch, where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work they had now completed.
[Acts] [14]:[27] On their arrival they gathered the church together and reported all that God had done with them, and how he had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.
[Acts] [14]:[28] And they stayed there a long time with the disciples.
[Acts] [15]:[1] Some men came down from Judea and began teaching the brothers, "Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved."
[Acts] [15]:[2] This brought Paul and Barnabas into sharp dissension and debate with them, so the brothers appointed Paul and Barnabas, along with some of the others, to go up to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders about this question.
[Acts] [15]:[3] Sent on their way by the church, they traveled through Phoenicia and Samaria, telling in detail how the Gentiles had turned to God, and they brought great joy to all the brothers.
[Acts] [15]:[4] When they arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church, the apostles, and the elders, and they reported everything God had done through them.
[Acts] [15]:[5] But some believers who belonged to the party of the Pharisees stood up and said, "They must be circumcised and required to keep the law of Moses."
[Acts] [15]:[6] So the apostles and the elders met together to consider this matter.
[Acts] [15]:[7] After a long debate, Peter stood up and said to them: "Brothers, you know that in the early days God chose me from among you, so that the Gentiles might hear the word of the gospel from my lips and believe.
[Acts] [15]:[8] And God, who knows the heart, testified in their favor by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as he did to us.
[Acts] [15]:[9] He made no distinction between us and them, for he cleansed their hearts by faith.
[Acts] [15]:[10] So then, why are you putting God to the test by laying on the necks of the disciples a yoke that neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear?
[Acts] [15]:[11] No, we believe that we are saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, in the very same way they are."
[Acts] [15]:[12] The whole assembly fell silent as they listened to Barnabas and Paul recount all the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.
[Acts] [15]:[13] When they had finished, James spoke up: "Brothers, listen to me.
[Acts] [15]:[14] Simeon has described how God first showed his concern by taking from the Gentiles a people for his name.
[Acts] [15]:[15] And this agrees with the words of the prophets, as it is written:
[Acts] [15]:[16] "'After this I will return and rebuild the fallen tent of David; I will rebuild its ruins and set it up again,
[Acts] [15]:[17] so that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, even all the Gentiles who bear my name, says the Lord, who does these things,
[Acts] [15]:[18] known from of old.'
[Acts] [15]:[19] Therefore my judgment is that we should not trouble those of the Gentiles who are turning to God,
[Acts] [15]:[20] but should write to them to abstain from what has been polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from the meat of strangled animals, and from blood.
[Acts] [15]:[21] For from ancient generations Moses has had those who proclaim him in every city, since he is read aloud in the synagogues every Sabbath."
[Acts] [15]:[22] Then the apostles and the elders, with the whole church, decided to choose men from among themselves and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, leading men among the brothers.
[Acts] [15]:[23] They sent this letter with them: "The apostles and the elders, your brothers, to the brothers among the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
[Acts] [15]:[24] We have heard that some men went out from us, without any authorization from us, and unsettled you with their words, troubling your minds.
[Acts] [15]:[25] So we came to a unanimous decision to choose men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
[Acts] [15]:[26] men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
[Acts] [15]:[27] Therefore we are sending Judas and Silas, who will tell you the same things by word of mouth.
[Acts] [15]:[28] For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to lay on you any burden beyond these necessary things:
[Acts] [15]:[29] that you abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell."
[Acts] [15]:[30] So they were sent off and went down to Antioch, where they gathered the congregation together and delivered the letter.
[Acts] [15]:[31] When it was read, the people rejoiced at its encouragement.
[Acts] [15]:[32] Judas and Silas, who were themselves prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the brothers.
[Acts] [15]:[33] After spending some time there, they were sent off in peace by the brothers to those who had sent them.
[Acts] [15]:[34] But Silas decided to remain there.
[Acts] [15]:[35] Paul and Barnabas stayed on in Antioch, where they and many others taught and proclaimed the word of the Lord.
[Acts] [15]:[36] Some days later Paul said to Barnabas, "Let us go back and visit the brothers in every city where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, and see how they are doing."
[Acts] [15]:[37] Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark, along with them,
[Acts] [15]:[38] but Paul insisted that they should not take along someone who had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not gone on with them to the work.
[Acts] [15]:[39] The disagreement was so sharp that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,
[Acts] [15]:[40] while Paul chose Silas and set out, commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.
[Acts] [15]:[41] He traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
[Acts] [16]:[1] Paul came also to Derbe and then to Lystra. And there was a disciple named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman, but his father was a Greek.
[Acts] [16]:[2] The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him,
[Acts] [16]:[3] and Paul wanted to take him along on the journey. So he circumcised him because of the Jews in that region, since they all knew that his father was a Greek.
[Acts] [16]:[4] As they traveled from town to town, they handed on to them the decisions reached by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem, telling them to observe these.
[Acts] [16]:[5] So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew in numbers day by day.
[Acts] [16]:[6] They traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia, having been kept by the Holy Spirit from speaking the word in Asia.
[Acts] [16]:[7] When they came to the border of Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not allow them.
[Acts] [16]:[8] So they passed by Mysia and came down to Troas.
[Acts] [16]:[9] During the night Paul had a vision: a man of Macedonia was standing and begging him, "Come over to Macedonia and help us!"
[Acts] [16]:[10] When he had seen the vision, we immediately tried to leave for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to proclaim the gospel to them.
[Acts] [16]:[11] So we put out to sea from Troas and sailed straight for Samothrace, and the next day on to Neapolis,
[Acts] [16]:[12] and from there to Philippi, a Roman colony and the leading city of that district of Macedonia. There we stayed for several days.
[Acts] [16]:[13] On the Sabbath day we went outside the city gate to the river, where we expected to find a place of prayer. We sat down and spoke to the women who had gathered there.
[Acts] [16]:[14] One of those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who worshiped God. The Lord opened her heart to pay attention to what Paul was saying.
[Acts] [16]:[15] When she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, "If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house." And she prevailed on us.
[Acts] [16]:[16] Once, as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl who had a spirit of divination and who earned a great deal of money for her owners by fortune-telling.[fn]
[Acts] [16]:[17] She followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, "These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!"
[Acts] [16]:[18] She kept this up for many days. At last Paul became so annoyed that he turned and said to the spirit, "In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!" And it came out that very moment.
[Acts] [16]:[19] When her owners saw that their hope of profit was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the authorities.
[Acts] [16]:[20] They brought them to the magistrates and said, "These men are Jews, and they are throwing our city into an uproar.
[Acts] [16]:[21] They are promoting customs that it is not lawful for us as Romans to accept or practice."
[Acts] [16]:[22] The crowd joined in the attack against them, and the magistrates tore the clothes off Paul and Silas and ordered them to be beaten with rods.
[Acts] [16]:[23] After they had been severely flogged, they were thrown into prison, and the jailer was ordered to guard them securely.
[Acts] [16]:[24] On receiving these orders, he put them in the inner cell and fastened their feet in the stocks.
[Acts] [16]:[25] About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
[Acts] [16]:[26] Suddenly there was such a violent earthquake that the foundations of the prison were shaken. At once all the doors flew open, and everyone's chains came loose.
[Acts] [16]:[27] The jailer woke up, and when he saw the prison doors standing open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, thinking the prisoners had escaped.
[Acts] [16]:[28] But Paul shouted at the top of his voice, "Don't harm yourself! We are all here!"
[Acts] [16]:[29] The jailer called for lights, rushed in, and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.
[Acts] [16]:[30] He brought them outside and asked, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"
[Acts] [16]:[31] They said, "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved—you and your household."
[Acts] [16]:[32] Then they spoke the word of the Lord to him and to all the others in his house.
[Acts] [16]:[33] At that hour of the night the jailer took them and washed their wounds; then immediately he and all his family were baptized.
[Acts] [16]:[34] He brought them up into his house and set a meal before them, and he rejoiced with his whole household that he had come to believe in God.
[Acts] [16]:[35] When daylight came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: "Release those men."
[Acts] [16]:[36] The jailer reported this to Paul: "The magistrates have sent word to release you. So you may leave. Go in peace."
[Acts] [16]:[37] But Paul said to them, "They beat us publicly without a trial, even though we are Roman citizens, and threw us into prison. And now do they want to get rid of us quietly? Certainly not! Let them come themselves and escort us out."
[Acts] [16]:[38] The officers reported this to the magistrates, and when they heard that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens, they were alarmed.
[Acts] [16]:[39] So they came and apologized to them, and they escorted them out and begged them to leave the city.
[Acts] [16]:[40] After leaving the prison, Paul and Silas went to Lydia's house, where they saw the brothers and sisters and encouraged them. Then they departed.
[Acts] [17]:[1] They traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia and came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
[Acts] [17]:[2] As was his custom, Paul went in to them and for three Sabbaths reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
[Acts] [17]:[3] explaining and demonstrating that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead, and saying, "This Jesus whom I proclaim to you is the Christ."
[Acts] [17]:[4] Some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a great many devout Greeks and a number of the leading women.
[Acts] [17]:[5] But the Jews grew jealous. They rounded up some scoundrels from the marketplace, formed a mob, and set the city in an uproar. They stormed Jason's house, looking to bring them out before the assembly.
[Acts] [17]:[6] When they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some of the brothers before the city officials, shouting, "These men who have turned the world upside down have now come here,
[Acts] [17]:[7] and Jason has taken them in. They are all acting against the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king—Jesus."
[Acts] [17]:[8] When they heard this, the crowd and the city officials were thrown into confusion.
[Acts] [17]:[9] So they took bail from Jason and the others and released them.
[Acts] [17]:[10] That very night the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
[Acts] [17]:[11] These people were more open-minded than those in Thessalonica: they received the word with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see whether these things were so.
[Acts] [17]:[12] Many of them came to believe, along with a good number of prominent Greek women and not a few men.
[Acts] [17]:[13] But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that the word of God was being proclaimed by Paul in Berea as well, they came there too, stirring up and inciting the crowds.
[Acts] [17]:[14] So the brothers immediately sent Paul off toward the sea, while Silas and Timothy stayed behind.
[Acts] [17]:[15] Those who escorted Paul brought him as far as Athens, and then left with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.
[Acts] [17]:[16] While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, his spirit was stirred to anger within him as he saw that the city was full of idols.
[Acts] [17]:[17] So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the God-fearers, and every day in the marketplace with whoever happened to be there.
[Acts] [17]:[18] Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also debated with him. Some said, "What is this babbler trying to say?" Others said, "He seems to be a preacher of foreign deities"—because he was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.
[Acts] [17]:[19] So they took hold of him and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, "May we know what this new teaching of yours is?
[Acts] [17]:[20] You are bringing some strange ideas to our ears, and we want to know what they mean."
[Acts] [17]:[21] Now all the Athenians and the foreigners living there spent their time on nothing but telling or hearing something new.
[Acts] [17]:[22] Then Paul stood up in the middle of the Areopagus and said: "Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are very religious.
[Acts] [17]:[23] For as I walked around and looked carefully at your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: 'To an unknown god.' What you worship in ignorance, this I proclaim to you.
[Acts] [17]:[24] The God who made the world and everything in it, the Lord of heaven and earth, does not live in temples made by human hands,
[Acts] [17]:[25] nor is he served by human hands as though he needed anything. He himself gives everyone life and breath and all things.
[Acts] [17]:[26] From one man he made every nation of humankind to inhabit the whole face of the earth, and he determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their dwelling places,
[Acts] [17]:[27] so that they would seek God and perhaps reach out for him and find him—though he is not far from any one of us.
[Acts] [17]:[28] For in him we live and move and have our being. As some of your own poets have said, 'We are his offspring.'
[Acts] [17]:[29] So then, since we are God's offspring, we ought not to think that the divine being is like gold or silver or stone, shaped by human skill and imagination.
[Acts] [17]:[30] God overlooked the times of ignorance that are past, but now he commands all people everywhere to repent.
[Acts] [17]:[31] For he has set a day on which he will judge the world with justice by the man he has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising him from the dead."
[Acts] [17]:[32] When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some began to mock, but others said, "We will hear you again about this."
[Acts] [17]:[33] At that, Paul left them.
[Acts] [17]:[34] But some men joined him and believed, among them Dionysius, a member of the Areopagus, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
[Acts] [18]:[1] After this Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
[Acts] [18]:[2] There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to see them,
[Acts] [18]:[3] and since they shared the same trade, he stayed and worked with them; they were tentmakers.
[Acts] [18]:[4] Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade both Jews and Greeks.
[Acts] [18]:[5] When Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself entirely to the word, testifying to the Jews that the Christ was Jesus.
[Acts] [18]:[6] But when they opposed him and hurled abuse at him, he shook out his clothes and said to them, "Your blood is on your own heads. I am innocent. From now on I will go to the Gentiles."
[Acts] [18]:[7] So he left there and went into the house of a man named Titius Justus, a worshiper of God, whose house was next door to the synagogue.
[Acts] [18]:[8] Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, came to believe in the Lord together with his whole household, and many of the Corinthians who heard Paul believed and were baptized.
[Acts] [18]:[9] One night the Lord said to Paul in a vision, "Do not be afraid. Keep on speaking; do not be silent,
[Acts] [18]:[10] for I am with you, and no one will lay a hand on you to harm you, because I have many people in this city."
[Acts] [18]:[11] So he settled there for a year and a half, teaching them the word of God.
[Acts] [18]:[12] While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews joined together in an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.
[Acts] [18]:[13] "This man," they said, "is persuading people to worship God in ways contrary to the law."
[Acts] [18]:[14] Just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio said to the Jews, "If this were a matter of some crime or serious wrongdoing, you Jews, I would have good reason to hear you out.
[Acts] [18]:[15] But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law, see to it yourselves. I refuse to be a judge of such things."
[Acts] [18]:[16] And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
[Acts] [18]:[17] Then they all seized Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But none of this concerned Gallio in the least.
[Acts] [18]:[18] Paul stayed on in Corinth for many days. Then he said farewell to the brothers and sailed for Syria, together with Priscilla and Aquila. Before sailing, he had his hair cut off at Cenchreae, because of a vow he had made.
[Acts] [18]:[19] They arrived at Ephesus, where he left the two of them. He himself went into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.
[Acts] [18]:[20] When they asked him to stay longer, he declined,
[Acts] [18]:[21] but as he said farewell he promised, "I will come back to you if God is willing." Then he set sail from Ephesus.
[Acts] [18]:[22] He landed at Caesarea, went up and greeted the church, and then went down to Antioch.
[Acts] [18]:[23] After spending some time there, he set out again and traveled from place to place through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
[Acts] [18]:[24] Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.
[Acts] [18]:[25] He had been instructed in the way of the Lord, and with burning enthusiasm he spoke and taught accurately the things concerning Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.
[Acts] [18]:[26] He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained the way of God to him more accurately.
[Acts] [18]:[27] When he wanted to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On his arrival he was a great help to those who by grace had come to believe,
[Acts] [18]:[28] for he vigorously refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that the Christ was Jesus.
[Acts] [19]:[1] While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled through the interior regions and came to Ephesus, where he found some disciples.
[Acts] [19]:[2] He asked them, "Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you came to faith?" "No," they replied, "we have never even heard that there is a Holy Spirit."
[Acts] [19]:[3] So he asked, "Into what, then, were you baptized?" "Into John's baptism," they said.
[Acts] [19]:[4] Paul said, "John baptized with a baptism of repentance, telling the people to believe in the one who was coming after him—that is, in Jesus."
[Acts] [19]:[5] On hearing this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
[Acts] [19]:[6] And when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.
[Acts] [19]:[7] There were about twelve men in all.
[Acts] [19]:[8] Paul went into the synagogue and for three months spoke boldly there, reasoning and persuading them about the kingdom of God.
[Acts] [19]:[9] But when some grew stubborn and refused to believe, slandering the Way in front of the crowd, he left them, took the disciples aside, and held discussions daily in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
[Acts] [19]:[10] This went on for two years, so that all the residents of Asia, both Jews and Greeks, heard the word of the Lord.
[Acts] [19]:[11] God did extraordinary miracles through the hands of Paul,
[Acts] [19]:[12] so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched his skin were carried to the sick, and their diseases left them and the evil spirits went out of them.
[Acts] [19]:[13] Some itinerant Jewish exorcists also tried invoking the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had evil spirits, saying, "I adjure you by the Jesus whom Paul proclaims."
[Acts] [19]:[14] Seven sons of a Jewish chief priest named Sceva were doing this.
[Acts] [19]:[15] But the evil spirit answered them, "Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize—but who are you?"
[Acts] [19]:[16] Then the man with the evil spirit leaped on them, overpowered them all, and beat them so badly that they fled from the house naked and wounded.
[Acts] [19]:[17] This became known to everyone living in Ephesus, both Jews and Greeks. Fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.
[Acts] [19]:[18] Many who had come to faith came forward, confessing and disclosing what they had done.
[Acts] [19]:[19] A good number of those who had practiced magic brought their books together and burned them in front of everyone. When the value was added up, it came to fifty thousand silver coins.[^1] [^1]: A silver coin was roughly a day's wage for a laborer, so this sum represented an enormous amount of money.
[Acts] [19]:[20] So the word of the Lord kept spreading with power and prevailing.
[Acts] [19]:[21] After all this had happened, Paul resolved in the Spirit to pass through Macedonia and Achaia and then go on to Jerusalem. "After I have been there," he said, "I must see Rome as well."
[Acts] [19]:[22] He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he himself stayed on for a while in Asia.
[Acts] [19]:[23] About that time a serious disturbance broke out concerning the Way.
[Acts] [19]:[24] A silversmith named Demetrius, who made silver shrines of Artemis, provided a good deal of work for the craftsmen.
[Acts] [19]:[25] He called them together, along with the workers in related trades, and said: "Men, you know that our prosperity comes from this business.
[Acts] [19]:[26] "And you can see and hear that not only in Ephesus but in almost all of Asia this Paul has persuaded and misled a great many people, saying that gods made by human hands are no gods at all.
[Acts] [19]:[27] Not only is our trade in danger of falling into disrepute, but the temple of the great goddess Artemis may be discredited, and she herself, whom all Asia and the whole world worships, may be stripped of her majesty."
[Acts] [19]:[28] When they heard this, they were filled with rage and began shouting, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
[Acts] [19]:[29] The city was thrown into confusion, and they rushed as one into the theater, dragging with them Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who were Paul's traveling companions.
[Acts] [19]:[30] Paul wanted to go before the crowd, but the disciples would not let him.
[Acts] [19]:[31] Even some of the officials of Asia who were his friends sent word to him, urging him not to venture into the theater.
[Acts] [19]:[32] Meanwhile some were shouting one thing and some another, for the assembly was in an uproar, and most of them had no idea why they had come together.
[Acts] [19]:[33] Some in the crowd shouted instructions to Alexander, since the Jews had pushed him to the front, and he motioned with his hand, wanting to make a defense before the people.
[Acts] [19]:[34] But when they realized he was a Jew, they all began shouting with one voice for about two hours, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
[Acts] [19]:[35] Then the city clerk quieted the crowd and said: "Men of Ephesus, is there anyone who does not know that the city of Ephesus is the guardian of the temple of the great Artemis and of her image that fell from heaven?
[Acts] [19]:[36] Since these things cannot be denied, you ought to calm down and do nothing rash.
[Acts] [19]:[37] For you have brought these men here who are neither temple robbers nor blasphemers of our goddess.
[Acts] [19]:[38] If Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a charge against anyone, there are courts in session and there are proconsuls; let them bring their charges there.
[Acts] [19]:[39] And if you are seeking anything further, it can be settled in a lawful assembly.
[Acts] [19]:[40] As it is, we are in danger of being charged with rioting over today's events, since there is no reason for it and we would not be able to give any account of this commotion." With that he dismissed the assembly.
[Acts] [20]:[1] When the uproar had died down, Paul sent for the disciples, encouraged them, and said farewell before setting out for Macedonia.
[Acts] [20]:[2] He traveled through that region, encouraging the believers at length, and then came to Greece,
[Acts] [20]:[3] where he stayed three months. Just as he was about to sail for Syria, the Jews formed a plot against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
[Acts] [20]:[4] Traveling with him were Sopater son of Pyrrhus, from Berea; Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica; Gaius from Derbe; Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.
[Acts] [20]:[5] These men went on ahead and waited for us at Troas.
[Acts] [20]:[6] We sailed from Philippi after the Festival of Unleavened Bread and joined them at Troas five days later, and there we stayed seven days.
[Acts] [20]:[7] On the first day of the week we gathered to break bread, and Paul spoke to them. Since he intended to leave the next day, he kept on talking until midnight.
[Acts] [20]:[8] There were many lamps in the upstairs room where we were gathered.
[Acts] [20]:[9] A young man named Eutychus, who was sitting in the window, sank into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. Overcome by sleep, he fell from the third story and was picked up dead.
[Acts] [20]:[10] But Paul went down, threw himself upon him, and took him in his arms. "Do not be alarmed," he said, "his life is in him."
[Acts] [20]:[11] Then he went back upstairs, broke the bread and ate, and talked with them a long while, until daybreak; then he left.
[Acts] [20]:[12] And they took the boy home alive, greatly comforted.
[Acts] [20]:[13] We went ahead to the ship and sailed for Assos, where we were to take Paul aboard. This was his arrangement, since he intended to go by land.
[Acts] [20]:[14] When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.
[Acts] [20]:[15] Sailing from there, we arrived the next day off Chios; the day after, we crossed over to Samos, and the following day we came to Miletus.
[Acts] [20]:[16] Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus so that he would not have to spend time in Asia, for he was hurrying to be in Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.
[Acts] [20]:[17] From Miletus he sent word to Ephesus, summoning the elders of the church.
[Acts] [20]:[18] When they arrived, he said to them: "You yourselves know how I lived among you the whole time, from the first day I set foot in Asia,
[Acts] [20]:[19] serving the Lord with all humility, with tears, and with the trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews.
[Acts] [20]:[20] I held back nothing that was for your good, but proclaimed it to you and taught you publicly and from house to house,
[Acts] [20]:[21] testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus.
[Acts] [20]:[22] And now, bound by the Spirit, I am on my way to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there,
[Acts] [20]:[23] except that in city after city the Holy Spirit testifies to me that chains and afflictions await me.
[Acts] [20]:[24] But I do not count my life of any value to myself, if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I received from the Lord Jesus: to testify to the gospel of God's grace.
[Acts] [20]:[25] And now I know that none of you among whom I have gone about proclaiming the kingdom will see my face again.
[Acts] [20]:[26] Therefore I declare to you this day that I am innocent of the blood of all people,
[Acts] [20]:[27] for I did not shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.
[Acts] [20]:[28] Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the church of God, which he purchased with his own blood.[^1] [^1]: Or "with the blood of his own Son"; the Greek phrase can be read either way.
[Acts] [20]:[29] I know that after I am gone, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.
[Acts] [20]:[30] Even from your own number men will rise up, speaking twisted things, to draw the disciples away after themselves.
[Acts] [20]:[31] So be on your guard, and remember that for three years, night and day, I never stopped warning each one of you with tears.
[Acts] [20]:[32] And now I commit you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up and to give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.
[Acts] [20]:[33] I have coveted no one's silver or gold or clothing.
[Acts] [20]:[34] You yourselves know that these hands of mine provided for my own needs and for those who were with me.
[Acts] [20]:[35] In everything I showed you that by such hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus, who himself said, 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'"
[Acts] [20]:[36] When he had said this, he knelt down with them all and prayed.
[Acts] [20]:[37] They all wept loudly as they embraced Paul and kissed him,
[Acts] [20]:[38] grieving most of all over his words that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.
[Acts] [21]:[1] After we had torn ourselves away from them and set sail, we ran a straight course to Cos, the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
[Acts] [21]:[2] There we found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, so we went aboard and put out to sea.
[Acts] [21]:[3] We came in sight of Cyprus, and leaving it on our left we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, since the ship was to unload its cargo there.
[Acts] [21]:[4] We looked up the disciples and stayed there seven days. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to set foot in Jerusalem.
[Acts] [21]:[5] But when our time was up, we left and went on our way, and all of them, with their wives and children, escorted us out of the city. Kneeling on the beach, we prayed,
[Acts] [21]:[6] and after saying farewell to one another we boarded the ship, and they returned home.
[Acts] [21]:[7] When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and stayed with them for one day.
[Acts] [21]:[8] The next day we left and came to Caesarea. There we went to the house of Philip the evangelist, one of the Seven, and stayed with him.
[Acts] [21]:[9] He had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
[Acts] [21]:[10] After we had been there several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
[Acts] [21]:[11] He came to us, took Paul's belt, tied his own feet and hands with it, and said, "This is what the Holy Spirit says: 'In this way the Jews in Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.'"
[Acts] [21]:[12] When we heard this, we and the people there begged Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
[Acts] [21]:[13] Then Paul answered, "Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound, but even to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."
[Acts] [21]:[14] Since he would not be persuaded, we gave up and said, "The Lord's will be done."
[Acts] [21]:[15] After this we got ready and went up to Jerusalem.
[Acts] [21]:[16] Some of the disciples from Caesarea came along with us and brought us to the house of Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we were to stay.
[Acts] [21]:[17] When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us gladly.
[Acts] [21]:[18] The next day Paul went with us to see James, and all the elders were present.
[Acts] [21]:[19] After greeting them, he reported in detail everything God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
[Acts] [21]:[20] When they heard it, they praised God. Then they said to him, "You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have come to believe, and all of them are zealous for the law.
[Acts] [21]:[21] They have been told about you that you teach all the Jews living among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or to live according to our customs.
[Acts] [21]:[22] What then should be done? They are certain to hear that you have come.
[Acts] [21]:[23] So do what we tell you. We have four men here who are under a vow.
[Acts] [21]:[24] Take these men, join in their purification rites, and pay their expenses so that they can have their heads shaved. Then everyone will know that there is nothing to the reports about you, but that you yourself live in observance of the law.
[Acts] [21]:[25] As for the Gentiles who have believed, we have written to them our decision that they should abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from what is strangled, and from sexual immorality."
[Acts] [21]:[26] So Paul took the men, and the next day, after purifying himself along with them, he entered the temple to give notice of when the days of purification would be completed and the offering would be made for each of them.
[Acts] [21]:[27] When the seven days were nearly over, the Jews from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd and seized him,
[Acts] [21]:[28] shouting, "Men of Israel, help us! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against our people, our law, and this place. What is more, he has even brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place."
[Acts] [21]:[29] They had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city and assumed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
