[1 Timothy] [6]:[3] If anyone teaches something different and does not hold to the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and to the teaching that accords with godliness,
[1 Timothy] [6]:[4] he is swollen with conceit and understands nothing. He has a sick craving for controversies and battles over words, which breed envy, strife, slander, evil suspicions,
[1 Timothy] [6]:[5] and constant friction among people whose minds are corrupted and who have been robbed of the truth, imagining that godliness is a means of gain.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[6] But godliness with contentment is great gain.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[7] For we brought nothing into the world, and we can take nothing out of it.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[8] If we have food and clothing, we will be content with that.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[9] Those who want to get rich fall into temptation and a trap and into many senseless and harmful desires that plunge people into ruin and destruction.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[10] For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some, reaching for it, have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[11] But you, man of God, flee from all this. Pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, gentleness.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[12] Fight the good fight of the faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called, for you made the good confession before many witnesses.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[13] In the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and of Christ Jesus, who made the good confession before Pontius Pilate, I charge you:
[1 Timothy] [6]:[14] keep this command without stain or reproach until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
[1 Timothy] [6]:[15] which he will bring about at the proper time—the blessed and only Sovereign, the King of kings and Lord of lords,
[1 Timothy] [6]:[16] who alone is immortal, who dwells in unapproachable light, whom no one has ever seen or can see. To him be honor and eternal dominion. Amen.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[17] Charge those who are rich in this present age not to be arrogant or to set their hope on the uncertainty of wealth, but on God, who richly provides us with everything for our enjoyment.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[18] Charge them to do good, to be rich in good works, to be generous and ready to share,
[1 Timothy] [6]:[19] storing up for themselves a good foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of the life that is truly life.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[20] Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you. Turn away from godless chatter and the contradictions of what is falsely called knowledge,
[1 Timothy] [6]:[21] which some have professed and in so doing have missed the mark regarding the faith. Grace be with you all.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[1] Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, in keeping with the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus,
[2 Timothy] [1]:[2] to Timothy, my beloved child: grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[3] I thank God, whom I serve with a clear conscience as my forefathers did, as I remember you constantly in my prayers night and day.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[4] Recalling your tears, I long to see you, so that I may be filled with joy.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[5] I am reminded of your sincere faith, which lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am convinced that it lives in you as well.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[6] That is why I remind you to fan into flame the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[7] For God did not give us a spirit of timidity, but of power and love and self-control.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[8] So do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord, or of me, his prisoner. Instead, share in suffering for the gospel by the power of God,
[2 Timothy] [1]:[9] who saved us and called us with a holy calling—not because of our works, but because of his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before time began
[2 Timothy] [1]:[10] and has now been revealed through the appearing of our Savior Jesus Christ, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[11] For this gospel I was appointed a herald, an apostle, and a teacher.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[12] That is why I suffer as I do. But I am not ashamed, for I know the one in whom I have put my trust, and I am convinced that he is able to guard what has been entrusted to me until that Day.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[13] Hold to the pattern of the sound words you heard from me, in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[14] Guard the good deposit entrusted to you through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[15] You know that everyone in Asia has turned away from me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[16] May the Lord show mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chains.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[17] On the contrary, when he came to Rome he searched hard for me until he found me.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[18] May the Lord grant that he find mercy from the Lord on that Day. And you know very well how much service he rendered in Ephesus.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[1] You then, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[2] And what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses, entrust to faithful people who will be capable of teaching others as well.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[3] Take your share of suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[4] No one serving as a soldier gets entangled in civilian affairs; his aim is to please the one who enlisted him.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[5] And an athlete is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[6] The farmer who does the hard work should be the first to receive a share of the crops.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[7] Think over what I am saying, for the Lord will give you understanding in everything.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[8] Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David — this is my gospel,
[2 Timothy] [2]:[9] for which I suffer to the point of being chained like a criminal. But the word of God is not chained.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[10] So I endure everything for the sake of the elect, that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[11] This saying is trustworthy: If we died with him, we will also live with him;
[2 Timothy] [2]:[12] if we endure, we will also reign with him; if we deny him, he will also deny us;
[2 Timothy] [2]:[13] if we are faithless, he remains faithful — for he cannot deny himself.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[14] Keep reminding them of these things, charging them before the Lord not to quarrel about words. It does no good and only ruins those who listen.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[15] Do your best to present yourself to God as one approved, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, rightly handling the word of truth.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[16] Avoid godless chatter, for those who indulge in it will only wander further into ungodliness,
[2 Timothy] [2]:[17] and their talk will spread like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
[2 Timothy] [2]:[18] who have missed the truth by saying that the resurrection has already taken place, and they are overturning the faith of some.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[19] Yet God's firm foundation stands, bearing this seal: "The Lord knows those who are his," and, "Let everyone who names the name of the Lord turn away from wickedness."
[2 Timothy] [2]:[20] In a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver but also of wood and clay — some for honorable use, some for dishonorable.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[21] So if anyone cleanses himself from what is dishonorable, he will be a vessel for honorable use, set apart as holy, useful to the master of the house, ready for every good work.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[22] Flee the desires of youth, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, along with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[23] Have nothing to do with foolish and ignorant controversies; you know they breed quarrels.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[24] And the Lord's servant must not be quarrelsome but kind to everyone, able to teach, patient when wronged,
[2 Timothy] [2]:[25] correcting his opponents with gentleness. Perhaps God will grant them repentance leading to a knowledge of the truth,
[2 Timothy] [2]:[26] so that they may come to their senses and escape the snare of the devil, who has taken them captive to do his will.[^1] [^1]: Or: having been captured by him (the devil), to do God's will. The Greek uses two different pronouns, and the referents are debated.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[1] But understand this: in the last days there will come times of hardship.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[2] For people will be lovers of self, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to their parents, ungrateful, unholy,
[2 Timothy] [3]:[3] heartless, unforgiving, slanderous, without self-control, brutal, with no love for good,
[2 Timothy] [3]:[4] treacherous, reckless, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God—
[2 Timothy] [3]:[5] holding to the outward form of godliness but denying its power. Keep away from such people.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[6] take captive weak-willed women, loaded down with sins and driven by all kinds of desires,[^1] [^1]: The Greek word rendered *weak-willed women* is a diminutive form suggesting vulnerable or gullible women; it describes those targeted by the false teachers, not women in general.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[7] always learning yet never able to arrive at a knowledge of the truth.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[8] Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these men also oppose the truth—men of corrupted minds, who fail the test when it comes to the faith.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[9] But they will not get far, for their folly will be plain to everyone, just as the folly of those two men was.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[10] You, however, have followed closely my teaching, my way of life, my purpose, my faith, my patience, my love, my endurance,
[2 Timothy] [3]:[11] my persecutions and sufferings—what happened to me in Antioch, in Iconium, in Lystra, the kinds of persecutions I endured. And the Lord rescued me from them all.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[12] Indeed, all who want to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted,
[2 Timothy] [3]:[13] while evil people and impostors will go from bad to worse, deceiving and being deceived.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[14] But as for you, continue in what you have learned and firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it,
[2 Timothy] [3]:[15] and how from infancy you have known the sacred writings, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[16] All Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, for rebuking, for correcting, and for training in righteousness,
[2 Timothy] [3]:[17] so that the man of God may be complete, fully equipped for every good work.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[1] I charge you before God and Christ Jesus, who is to judge the living and the dead, and by his appearing and his kingdom:
[2 Timothy] [4]:[2] preach the word; be ready whether the time is right or not; correct, rebuke, and encourage—with all patience and careful teaching.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[3] For the time is coming when people will not put up with sound teaching. Instead, to suit their own desires, they will gather around themselves a crowd of teachers to tickle their ears,
[2 Timothy] [4]:[4] and they will turn their ears away from the truth and wander off after myths.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[5] But you—keep a clear head in everything, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, carry out your ministry to the full.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[6] As for me, I am already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time of my departure has come.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[7] I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[8] From now on there is reserved for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will award to me on that day—and not only to me, but to all who have loved his appearing.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[9] Do your best to come to me soon.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[10] For Demas, in love with this present age, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica; Crescens has gone to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[11] Only Luke is with me. Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for service.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[12] Tychicus I have sent to Ephesus.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[13] When you come, bring the cloak I left with Carpus at Troas, and the scrolls—especially the parchments.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[14] Alexander the metalworker did me a great deal of harm; the Lord will repay him according to his deeds.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[15] Be on your guard against him too, for he strongly opposed our message.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[16] At my first defense no one stood by me; everyone abandoned me. May it not be held against them.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[17] But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so that through me the message might be fully proclaimed and all the nations might hear it. And I was rescued from the lion's mouth.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[18] The Lord will rescue me from every evil work and bring me safely into his heavenly kingdom. To him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[19] Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[20] Erastus stayed in Corinth, and I left Trophimus ill at Miletus.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[21] Do your best to come before winter. Eubulus sends you greetings, and so do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers and sisters.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[22] The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.
[Titus] [1]:[1] Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ for the faith of God's chosen ones and the knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness,
[Titus] [1]:[2] resting on the hope of eternal life, which God, who does not lie, promised before the ages began
[Titus] [1]:[3] and at the proper time he revealed his word through the preaching entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior:
[Titus] [1]:[4] To Titus, my true son in our common faith. Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
[Titus] [1]:[5] I left you in Crete for this reason: that you might set right what still needed to be done and appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.
[Titus] [1]:[6] An elder must be beyond reproach, the husband of one wife, with children who are believers and not open to the charge of wild living or rebellion.
[Titus] [1]:[7] For as God's steward, an overseer must be beyond reproach: not arrogant, not quick-tempered, not given to drink, not violent, not greedy for dishonest gain,
[Titus] [1]:[8] but hospitable, a lover of what is good, self-controlled, upright, holy, and disciplined.
[Titus] [1]:[9] He must hold firmly to the trustworthy word as it has been taught, so that he can encourage others with sound doctrine and refute those who oppose it.
[Titus] [1]:[10] For there are many rebellious people, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision group.
[Titus] [1]:[11] They must be silenced, because they are ruining whole households by teaching what they should not teach—and all for the sake of dishonest gain.
[Titus] [1]:[12] One of them, a prophet of their own people, said: "Cretans are always liars, vicious brutes, lazy gluttons."
[Titus] [1]:[13] This testimony is true. So rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith
[Titus] [1]:[14] and pay no attention to Jewish myths or to the commands of people who turn their backs on the truth.
[Titus] [1]:[15] To the pure, everything is pure; but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure. In fact, both their minds and their consciences are defiled.
[Titus] [1]:[16] They claim to know God, but by their actions they deny him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.
[Titus] [2]:[1] You, however, must teach what agrees with sound doctrine.
[Titus] [2]:[2] Older men are to be temperate, dignified, self-controlled, sound in faith, in love, and in endurance.
[Titus] [2]:[3] Older women, likewise, are to be reverent in the way they live, not slanderers or slaves to heavy drinking, but teachers of what is good.
[Titus] [2]:[4] so that they may train the younger women to love their husbands and to love their children,
[Titus] [2]:[5] to be self-controlled and pure, to be busy at home, to be kind, and to submit to their own husbands, so that the word of God may not be dishonored.
[Titus] [2]:[6] Urge the younger men, in the same way, to be self-controlled.
[Titus] [2]:[7] In everything, make yourself a model of good works. In your teaching show integrity and dignity,
[Titus] [2]:[8] and let your message be sound and beyond reproach, so that any opponent will be put to shame, having nothing bad to say about us.
[Titus] [2]:[9] Slaves are to submit to their masters in everything, to be well pleasing, not argumentative,
[Titus] [2]:[10] not stealing from them, but showing themselves completely trustworthy, so that in every way they may bring credit to the teaching of God our Savior.
[Titus] [2]:[11] For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people.
[Titus] [2]:[12] It trains us to renounce godlessness and worldly desires, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in the present age,
[Titus] [2]:[13] as we wait for the blessed hope—the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.
[Titus] [2]:[14] He gave himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for himself a people of his own, eager to do good works.
[Titus] [2]:[15] These are the things you are to teach; encourage and rebuke with full authority. Let no one look down on you.
[Titus] [3]:[1] Remind them to submit to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,
[Titus] [3]:[2] to slander no one, to avoid quarreling, to be considerate, showing true gentleness toward all people.
[Titus] [3]:[3] For we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, led astray, enslaved to all kinds of passions and pleasures, living in malice and envy, despised and hating one another.
[Titus] [3]:[4] But when the kindness of God our Savior and his love for humanity appeared,
[Titus] [3]:[5] he saved us—not because of righteous deeds we had done, but because of his own mercy—through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit,
[Titus] [3]:[6] whom he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
[Titus] [3]:[7] so that, justified by his grace, we might become heirs in the hope of eternal life.
[Titus] [3]:[8] This saying is trustworthy, and I want you to insist on these things, so that those who have come to believe in God may be careful to devote themselves to good works. These things are good and beneficial for everyone.
[Titus] [3]:[9] But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, quarrels, and fights about the law, for they are unprofitable and worthless.
[Titus] [3]:[10] After a first and second warning, have nothing more to do with a divisive person,
[Titus] [3]:[11] knowing that such a person has gone astray and keeps on sinning, self-condemned.
[Titus] [3]:[12] As soon as I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, do your best to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to spend the winter there.
[Titus] [3]:[13] Do everything you can to help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way, so that they lack nothing.
[Titus] [3]:[14] And let our people learn to devote themselves to good works, to meet urgent needs, so that they will not be unfruitful.
[Titus] [3]:[15] Everyone with me sends you greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all.
[Philemon] [1]:[1] Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon our dear friend and fellow worker,
[Philemon] [1]:[2] to Apphia our sister, to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets in your house:
[Philemon] [1]:[3] Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
[Philemon] [1]:[4] I always thank my God when I mention you in my prayers,
[Philemon] [1]:[5] because I keep hearing of your love and of the faith you have toward the Lord Jesus and for all the saints.
[Philemon] [1]:[6] I pray that the fellowship of your faith may be effective as you come to know every good thing that is ours for the sake of Christ.
[Philemon] [1]:[7] Your love has given me great joy and encouragement, because through you, brother, the hearts of the saints have been refreshed.
[Philemon] [1]:[8] For this reason, although in Christ I could be bold enough to order you to do what is proper,
[Philemon] [1]:[9] I would rather appeal to you on the basis of love. I, Paul, an old man and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus,
[Philemon] [1]:[10] appeal to you for my child, Onesimus, whose father I became while in chains.
[Philemon] [1]:[11] Once he was useless to you, but now he is useful both to you and to me.* *The name Onesimus means "useful" or "profitable"; Paul is playing on his name here.
[Philemon] [1]:[12] I am sending him back to you—and with him my very heart.
[Philemon] [1]:[13] I would have liked to keep him with me, so that he might serve me in your place while I am in chains for the gospel.
[Philemon] [1]:[14] But I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your kindness would not be forced but voluntary.
[Philemon] [1]:[15] Perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while: so that you might have him back forever,
[Philemon] [1]:[16] no longer as a slave, but better than a slave—as a dear brother. He is very dear to me, but even dearer to you, both as a man and as a brother in the Lord.
[Philemon] [1]:[17] So if you consider me a partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.
[Philemon] [1]:[18] And if he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to me.
[Philemon] [1]:[19] I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it—not to mention that you owe me your very self.
[Philemon] [1]:[20] Yes, brother, let me have some benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.
[Philemon] [1]:[21] I write to you confident of your obedience, knowing that you will do even more than I ask.
[Philemon] [1]:[22] And one more thing: prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be restored to you.
[Philemon] [1]:[23] Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings,
[Philemon] [1]:[24] and so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
[Philemon] [1]:[25] The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.* *"Your" here is plural, addressing the whole household and church.
[Hebrews] [1]:[1] Long ago God spoke to our fathers many times and in many ways through the prophets,
[Hebrews] [1]:[2] but in these last days he has spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, and through whom he made the ages. [Footnote: Or "the universe"; the Greek word can denote both the ages of time and the created world.]
[Hebrews] [1]:[3] The Son is the radiance of God's glory and the exact imprint of his being, sustaining all things by his powerful word. When he had himself made purification for sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high,
[Hebrews] [1]:[4] having become as much superior to the angels as the name he has inherited surpasses theirs.
[Hebrews] [1]:[5] For to which of the angels did God ever say, "You are my Son; today I have begotten you"? Or again, "I will be his Father, and he will be my Son"?
[Hebrews] [1]:[6] And again, when he brings the firstborn into the world, he says, "Let all God's angels worship him."
[Hebrews] [1]:[7] Of the angels he says, "He makes his angels winds, and his servants flames of fire." [Footnote: The Greek word rendered "winds" can also mean "spirits."]
[Hebrews] [1]:[8] But of the Son he says, "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever, and the scepter of justice is the scepter of your kingdom.
[Hebrews] [1]:[9] You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions."
[Hebrews] [1]:[10] And, "In the beginning, Lord, you laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
[Hebrews] [1]:[11] They will perish, but you remain; they will all wear out like a garment.
[Hebrews] [1]:[12] You will roll them up like a robe; like a garment they will be changed. But you are the same, and your years will never end."
[Hebrews] [1]:[13] And to which of the angels has he ever said, "Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet"?
[Hebrews] [1]:[14] Are they not all ministering spirits, sent out to serve for the sake of those who are to inherit salvation?
[Hebrews] [2]:[1] For this reason we must pay much closer attention to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.
[Hebrews] [2]:[2] For if the word spoken through angels proved binding, and every transgression and act of disobedience received its just penalty,
[Hebrews] [2]:[3] how shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? It was declared at first by the Lord, and confirmed to us by those who heard him,
[Hebrews] [2]:[4] while God bore witness along with them by signs and wonders and various miracles, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to his will.
[Hebrews] [2]:[5] For it was not to angels that God subjected the world to come, of which we are speaking.
[Hebrews] [2]:[6] But someone has testified somewhere: "What is man, that you remember him, or the son of man, that you care for him?
[Hebrews] [2]:[7] You made him for a little while lower than the angels; you crowned him with glory and honor,
[Hebrews] [2]:[8] putting everything in subjection under his feet." Now in subjecting all things to him, God left nothing outside his control. Yet at present we do not see everything subjected to him.
[Hebrews] [2]:[9] But we do see Jesus, who was made for a little while lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because he suffered death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for everyone.
[Hebrews] [2]:[10] For it was fitting that God, for whom and through whom all things exist, in bringing many sons to glory, should make the pioneer of their salvation perfect through suffering.
[Hebrews] [2]:[11] For the one who sanctifies and those who are sanctified all have the same origin. That is why he is not ashamed to call them brothers,
[Hebrews] [2]:[12] saying, "I will proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation I will sing your praise."
[Hebrews] [2]:[13] And again, "I will put my trust in him." And again, "Here I am, and the children God has given me."
[Hebrews] [2]:[14] Since, then, the children share in flesh and blood, he himself likewise shared fully in the same, so that through death he might break the power of the one who holds the power of death—that is, the devil—
[Hebrews] [2]:[15] and set free all those who through fear of death were held in slavery all their lives.
[Hebrews] [2]:[16] For surely it is not angels he helps, but the descendants of Abraham.
[Hebrews] [2]:[17] Therefore he had to be made like his brothers in every respect, so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in the service of God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
[Hebrews] [2]:[18] For he himself suffered when he was tempted, and so he is able to help those who are being tempted.
[Hebrews] [3]:[1] So then, holy brothers and sisters, who share in a heavenly calling, fix your attention on Jesus, the apostle and high priest of the faith we confess.
[Hebrews] [3]:[2] He was faithful to the one who appointed him, just as Moses was faithful in God's house.
[Hebrews] [3]:[3] Yet Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house itself.
[Hebrews] [3]:[4] For every house is built by someone, but the builder of all things is God.
[Hebrews] [3]:[5] Moses was faithful in all God's house as a servant, to bear witness to what would be spoken later,
[Hebrews] [3]:[6] but Christ is faithful as a Son over God's house. And we are his house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope in which we boast.
[Hebrews] [3]:[7] Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: "Today, if you hear his voice,
[Hebrews] [3]:[8] do not harden your hearts as you did in the rebellion, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
[Hebrews] [3]:[9] where your ancestors put me to the test, though they had seen my works
[Hebrews] [3]:[10] for forty years. That is why I was angry with that generation, and I said, 'Their hearts are always going astray, and they have not known my ways.'
[Hebrews] [3]:[11] So I swore in my anger, 'They shall never enter my rest.'"
[Hebrews] [3]:[12] See to it, brothers and sisters, that none of you has a wicked, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God.
[Hebrews] [3]:[13] Instead, encourage one another every day, as long as it is called "Today," so that none of you is hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
[Hebrews] [3]:[14] For we have come to share in Christ, if indeed we hold our original confidence firm to the end.
[Hebrews] [3]:[15] As it is said: "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as you did in the rebellion."
[Hebrews] [3]:[16] For who heard and yet rebelled? Was it not all those who came out of Egypt under Moses?
[Hebrews] [3]:[17] And with whom was he angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
[Hebrews] [3]:[18] And to whom did he swear that they would never enter his rest, if not to those who disobeyed?
[Hebrews] [3]:[19] So we see that they could not enter because of unbelief.
[Hebrews] [4]:[1] So let us fear that, while the promise of entering his rest still stands, any of you should be found to have fallen short of it.
[Hebrews] [4]:[2] For we have had the good news preached to us just as they did; but the word they heard did them no good, because they were not united by faith with those who listened.
[Hebrews] [4]:[3] We who have believed do enter that rest, just as he has said: "As I swore in my anger, they shall never enter my rest" — and yet his works were finished from the foundation of the world.
[Hebrews] [4]:[4] For somewhere he says this about the seventh day: "And on the seventh day God rested from all his works."
[Hebrews] [4]:[5] And again in this same passage he says, "They shall never enter my rest."
[Hebrews] [4]:[6] Since, then, it remains for some to enter it, and since those who first heard the good news did not enter because of their disobedience,
[Hebrews] [4]:[7] God again appoints a day — "Today" — speaking through David so long afterward, in the words already quoted: "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts."
[Hebrews] [4]:[8] For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later of another day.
[Hebrews] [4]:[9] So then, a sabbath rest still remains for the people of God.
[Hebrews] [4]:[10] For whoever enters God's rest also rests from his own works, just as God rested from his.
[Hebrews] [4]:[11] Let us then make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one falls by following the same example of disobedience.
[Hebrews] [4]:[12] For the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword. It pierces to the point where soul and spirit divide, joints and marrow as well, and it judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
[Hebrews] [4]:[13] No creature is hidden from him; everything lies naked and exposed before the eyes of the one to whom we must give account.
[Hebrews] [4]:[14] Since, then, we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast to our confession.
[Hebrews] [4]:[15] For we do not have a high priest unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who was tempted in every way as we are, yet without sin.
[Hebrews] [4]:[16] So let us approach the throne of grace with confidence, to receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.
[Hebrews] [5]:[1] For every high priest is taken from among men and appointed to act on behalf of men in the things pertaining to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
[Hebrews] [5]:[2] He is able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and going astray, since he himself is beset by weakness.
[Hebrews] [5]:[3] And for that reason he must offer sacrifices for sins — for the people, and for himself as well.
[Hebrews] [5]:[4] No one takes this honor upon himself; he must be called by God, just as Aaron was.
[Hebrews] [5]:[5] So also Christ did not glorify himself to become high priest, but was appointed by the one who said to him: "You are my Son; today I have begotten you."
[Hebrews] [5]:[6] And elsewhere he says: "You are a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek."
[Hebrews] [5]:[7] In the days of his flesh he offered up prayers and pleas, with loud cries and tears, to the one who was able to save him from death, and he was heard because of his reverence.
[Hebrews] [5]:[8] Although he was the Son, he learned obedience through what he suffered.
[Hebrews] [5]:[9] And having been made perfect, he became the source of eternal salvation for all who obey him,
[Hebrews] [5]:[10] having been designated by God as high priest in the order of Melchizedek.
[Hebrews] [5]:[11] We have much to say about him, but it is hard to explain, since you have grown dull of hearing.
[Hebrews] [5]:[12] By now you ought to be teachers, yet you need someone to teach you the basic principles of God's word all over again. You need milk, not solid food.
[Hebrews] [5]:[13] For anyone who lives on milk is unskilled in the word of righteousness; he is still an infant.
[Hebrews] [5]:[14] But solid food is for the mature, for those whose faculties have been trained by practice to distinguish good from evil.
[Hebrews] [6]:[1] So let us leave behind the elementary teaching about Christ and press on toward maturity, not laying again the foundation: repentance from dead works and faith in God,
[Hebrews] [6]:[2] instruction about baptisms and the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment.
[Hebrews] [6]:[3] And this we will do, if God permits.
[Hebrews] [6]:[4] For it is impossible, in the case of those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift and shared in the Holy Spirit,
[Hebrews] [6]:[5] who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the age to come,
[Hebrews] [6]:[6] and who have then fallen away—it is impossible to restore them again to repentance, since they are crucifying the Son of God all over again and holding him up to contempt.
[Hebrews] [6]:[7] For land that drinks in the rain that falls on it again and again, and produces a crop useful to those for whom it is cultivated, receives a blessing from God.
[Hebrews] [6]:[8] But if it yields thorns and thistles, it is worthless and close to being cursed, and in the end it will be burned.
[Hebrews] [6]:[9] Yet even though we speak this way, dear friends, we are convinced of better things concerning you—things that belong to salvation.
[Hebrews] [6]:[10] For God is not unjust; he will not forget your work and the love you have shown for his name in having served his holy people, and in serving them still.
[Hebrews] [6]:[11] But we long for each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, so that your hope may come to full assurance,
[Hebrews] [6]:[12] so that you will not become sluggish, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
[Hebrews] [6]:[13] When God made his promise to Abraham, since there was no one greater for him to swear by, he swore by himself,
[Hebrews] [6]:[14] saying, "I will surely bless you and surely multiply you."
[Hebrews] [6]:[15] And so, after waiting patiently, Abraham received what was promised.
[Hebrews] [6]:[16] People swear by someone greater than themselves, and an oath serves as confirmation, putting an end to all dispute.
[Hebrews] [6]:[17] So when God wanted to show the heirs of the promise even more clearly how unchangeable his purpose was, he guaranteed it with an oath,
[Hebrews] [6]:[18] so that by two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled to him for refuge might have a strong encouragement to hold fast to the hope set before us.
[Hebrews] [6]:[19] This hope we have as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure. It reaches within, behind the curtain,
[Hebrews] [6]:[20] where Jesus has entered on our behalf as forerunner, having become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.
[Hebrews] [7]:[1] This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
[Hebrews] [7]:[2] and Abraham gave him a tenth of everything. His name means "king of righteousness," and he was also king of Salem, that is, "king of peace."
[Hebrews] [7]:[3] Without father or mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but made like the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.
[Hebrews] [7]:[4] See how great this man was: even Abraham the patriarch gave him a tenth of the spoils.
[Hebrews] [7]:[5] Now the descendants of Levi who receive the priesthood have a commandment in the law to collect a tenth from the people—that is, from their own brothers, though they too are descended from Abraham.
[Hebrews] [7]:[6] But this man, who does not trace his descent from them, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed the one who held the promises.
[Hebrews] [7]:[7] And beyond all dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
[Hebrews] [7]:[8] In the one case the tenth is received by men who die; in the other, by him of whom it is testified that he lives.
[Hebrews] [7]:[9] One might even say that Levi, who receives the tenth, paid it through Abraham,
[Hebrews] [7]:[10] for he was still in his ancestor's body when Melchizedek met him.
[Hebrews] [7]:[11] If perfection had come through the Levitical priesthood—for under it the people received the law—why was there still need for another priest to arise in the order of Melchizedek rather than one named in the order of Aaron?
[Hebrews] [7]:[12] For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.
[Hebrews] [7]:[13] The one of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.
[Hebrews] [7]:[14] For it is clear that our Lord descended from Judah, and Moses said nothing about priests from that tribe.
[Hebrews] [7]:[15] And this becomes even clearer if another priest arises in the likeness of Melchizedek,
[Hebrews] [7]:[16] one who has become a priest not on the basis of a law about physical descent, but through the power of an indestructible life.
[Hebrews] [7]:[17] For it is testified of him: "You are a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek."
[Hebrews] [7]:[18] So the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless—
[Hebrews] [7]:[19] for the law made nothing perfect—and a better hope is introduced, through which we draw near to God.
[Hebrews] [7]:[20] And to the degree that this came with an oath—for the others became priests without any oath,
[Hebrews] [7]:[21] but he became a priest with an oath, when God said to him: "The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind: 'You are a priest forever.'"
[Hebrews] [7]:[22] To that same degree, Jesus has become the guarantor of a better covenant.
[Hebrews] [7]:[23] Now there have been many priests, since death kept them from continuing in office;
[Hebrews] [7]:[24] but because he lives forever, he holds his priesthood permanently.
[Hebrews] [7]:[25] Therefore he is able to save completely those who come to God through him, since he always lives to intercede for them.
[Hebrews] [7]:[26] Such a high priest is exactly what we needed: holy, blameless, undefiled, set apart from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
[Hebrews] [7]:[27] Unlike the other high priests, he has no need to offer sacrifices day after day, first for his own sins and then for the sins of the people; he did this once for all when he offered up himself.
[Hebrews] [7]:[28] For the law appoints as high priests men who are weak, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints the Son, made perfect forever.
[Hebrews] [8]:[1] Now the main point of what we are saying is this: we have such a high priest, one who has taken his seat at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
[Hebrews] [8]:[2] a minister in the sanctuary and in the true tent, which the Lord set up, not any human being.
[Hebrews] [8]:[3] Every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices; therefore it was necessary for this one also to have something to offer.
[Hebrews] [8]:[4] Now if he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, since there are already those who offer the gifts prescribed by the law.
[Hebrews] [8]:[5] They serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, just as Moses was instructed when he was about to erect the tent: "See that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain."
[Hebrews] [8]:[6] But as it is, Christ has obtained a ministry as far superior as the covenant he mediates is better, since it is established on better promises.
[Hebrews] [8]:[7] For if that first covenant had been faultless, there would have been no need to look for a second.
[Hebrews] [8]:[8] For God finds fault with them when he says: "Look, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
[Hebrews] [8]:[9] It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, for they did not remain faithful to my covenant, and so I turned away from them, declares the Lord.
[Hebrews] [8]:[10] This is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the Lord: I will put my laws in their minds and write them on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
[Hebrews] [8]:[11] No longer will anyone teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, 'Know the Lord,' because they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest.
[Hebrews] [8]:[12] For I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more."
[Hebrews] [8]:[13] By speaking of a new covenant, he has made the first one obsolete; and what is obsolete and aging is about to disappear.
[Hebrews] [9]:[1] Now the first covenant had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
[Hebrews] [9]:[2] A tent was set up, and in its first room stood the lampstand, the table, and the bread of the Presence; this is called the Holy Place.
[Hebrews] [9]:[3] Behind the second curtain was the room called the Most Holy Place,
[Hebrews] [9]:[4] which held the golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant, overlaid all around with gold. In the ark were the golden jar of manna, Aaron's staff that had budded, and the tablets of the covenant,
[Hebrews] [9]:[5] and above it the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat. But of these things I cannot now speak in detail.
[Hebrews] [9]:[6] With everything arranged this way, the priests enter the first room continually to carry out their duties of worship.
[Hebrews] [9]:[7] But into the second room only the high priest goes, once a year, and never without blood, which he offers for himself and for the sins the people committed in ignorance.
[Hebrews] [9]:[8] By this the Holy Spirit shows that the way into the sanctuary had not yet been revealed while the first tent was still standing.
[Hebrews] [9]:[9] This is a symbol for the present time, for the gifts and sacrifices offered under it cannot perfect the conscience of the worshiper.
[Hebrews] [9]:[10] They deal only with food and drink and various washings—outward regulations for the body, imposed until the time of the new order.
[Hebrews] [9]:[11] But when Christ came as high priest of the good things that have now arrived, he went through the greater and more perfect tent, one not made by human hands, that is, not part of this creation.
[Hebrews] [9]:[12] He entered the Most Holy Place once for all, not by the blood of goats and calves but by his own blood, and so obtained eternal redemption.
[Hebrews] [9]:[13] For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer, sprinkled on those who are defiled, sanctify them so that their bodies are clean,
[Hebrews] [9]:[14] how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, cleanse our conscience from dead works to serve the living God!
[Hebrews] [9]:[15] For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant: now that a death has taken place to redeem us from the transgressions committed under the first covenant, those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance.
[Hebrews] [9]:[16] For where there is a will, the death of the one who made it must be established.
[Hebrews] [9]:[17] A will takes effect only at death; it has no force while the one who made it is still alive.
[Hebrews] [9]:[18] That is why even the first covenant was not put into effect without blood.
[Hebrews] [9]:[19] When Moses had proclaimed every commandment of the law to all the people, he took the blood of calves, together with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled the scroll itself and all the people,
[Hebrews] [9]:[20] saying, "This is the blood of the covenant that God has commanded for you."
[Hebrews] [9]:[21] In the same way he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle and everything used in its service.
[Hebrews] [9]:[22] Indeed, under the law nearly everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
[Hebrews] [9]:[23] So it was necessary for the copies of the heavenly things to be cleansed with these rites, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
[Hebrews] [9]:[24] For Christ did not enter a sanctuary made by human hands, a mere copy of the true one; he entered heaven itself, now to appear before God on our behalf.
[Hebrews] [9]:[25] Nor did he enter to offer himself again and again, the way the high priest enters the Most Holy Place year after year with blood that is not his own.
[Hebrews] [9]:[26] Otherwise he would have had to suffer again and again since the foundation of the world. But now he has appeared once for all at the culmination of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of himself.
[Hebrews] [9]:[27] And just as it is appointed for people to die once, and after that to face judgment,
[Hebrews] [9]:[28] so Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many; and he will appear a second time, not to deal with sin, but to bring salvation to those who are waiting for him.
[Hebrews] [10]:[1] For the law is only a shadow of the good things to come, not the true form of those realities. So it can never, by the same sacrifices offered year after year without end, perfect those who draw near.
[Hebrews] [10]:[2] Otherwise, would they not have stopped being offered? For the worshipers, once cleansed, would no longer have had any consciousness of sins.
[Hebrews] [10]:[3] Instead, in those sacrifices there is a yearly reminder of sins,
[Hebrews] [10]:[4] since it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
[Hebrews] [10]:[5] Therefore, when Christ came into the world, he said: "Sacrifice and offering you did not desire, but a body you prepared for me;
[Hebrews] [10]:[6] with burnt offerings and sin offerings you were not pleased.
[Hebrews] [10]:[7] Then I said, 'Here I am—it is written about me in the scroll of the book—I have come to do your will, O God.'"
[Hebrews] [10]:[8] First he says, "Sacrifices and offerings, burnt offerings and sin offerings you did not desire, nor were you pleased with them"—and these are offered according to the law.
[Hebrews] [10]:[9] Then he says, "Here I am; I have come to do your will." He does away with the first in order to establish the second.
[Hebrews] [10]:[10] And by that will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
[Hebrews] [10]:[11] Every priest stands day after day performing his service, offering again and again the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
[Hebrews] [10]:[12] But when this priest had offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins, he sat down at the right hand of God,
[Hebrews] [10]:[13] and since then he waits until his enemies are made a footstool for his feet.
[Hebrews] [10]:[14] For by one offering he has perfected for all time those who are being sanctified.
[Hebrews] [10]:[15] The Holy Spirit also testifies to us about this. First he says:
[Hebrews] [10]:[16] "This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their hearts, and I will write them on their minds."
[Hebrews] [10]:[17] Then he adds: "Their sins and their lawless deeds I will remember no more."
[Hebrews] [10]:[18] And where these have been forgiven, there is no longer any offering for sin.
[Hebrews] [10]:[19] So then, brothers and sisters, since we have confidence to enter the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus,
[Hebrews] [10]:[20] by the new and living way he opened for us through the curtain—that is, through his flesh—
[Hebrews] [10]:[21] and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
[Hebrews] [10]:[22] let us draw near with a true heart in the full assurance of faith, our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
[Hebrews] [10]:[23] Let us hold unwaveringly to the confession of our hope, for he who promised is faithful.
[Hebrews] [10]:[24] And let us consider how to spur one another on toward love and good works,
[Hebrews] [10]:[25] not neglecting to meet together, as some have made a habit of neglecting, but encouraging one another—and all the more as you see the Day drawing near.
[Hebrews] [10]:[26] For if we deliberately go on sinning after receiving the knowledge of the truth, no sacrifice for sins is left,
[Hebrews] [10]:[27] but only a terrifying expectation of judgment and a raging fire ready to consume the adversaries.
[Hebrews] [10]:[28] Anyone who rejected the law of Moses died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
[Hebrews] [10]:[29] How much worse punishment do you think someone deserves who has trampled the Son of God underfoot, who has treated as unholy the blood of the covenant that sanctified him, and who has insulted the Spirit of grace?
[Hebrews] [10]:[30] For we know him who said, "Vengeance is mine; I will repay," and again, "The Lord will judge his people."
[Hebrews] [10]:[31] It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
[Hebrews] [10]:[32] Remember those earlier days when, after you had been enlightened, you endured a hard struggle with suffering:
[Hebrews] [10]:[33] sometimes publicly exposed to insult and affliction, and sometimes standing side by side with those who were treated that way.
[Hebrews] [10]:[34] You suffered along with the prisoners and joyfully accepted the seizure of your property, knowing that you yourselves had a better and lasting possession.
[Hebrews] [10]:[35] So do not throw away your confidence; it carries a great reward.
[Hebrews] [10]:[36] You need endurance, so that after you have done the will of God you may receive what he has promised.
[Hebrews] [10]:[37] For yet "in a very little while, the one who is coming will come and will not delay.
[Hebrews] [10]:[38] But my righteous one will live by faith, and if he shrinks back, my soul takes no pleasure in him."
[Hebrews] [10]:[39] But we are not among those who shrink back and are destroyed, but among those who have faith and preserve their souls.
[Hebrews] [11]:[1] Faith is the assurance of what we hope for, the conviction of what we do not see.
[Hebrews] [11]:[2] It was by faith that the people of old received God's approval.
[Hebrews] [11]:[3] By faith we understand that the universe was formed by the word of God, so that what is seen was not made out of what was visible.
[Hebrews] [11]:[4] By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did, and through it he was commended as righteous, since God himself bore witness concerning his gifts. And through his faith he still speaks, though he is dead.
[Hebrews] [11]:[5] By faith Enoch was taken up, so that he did not see death, and he was not found, because God had taken him. For before he was taken up he was commended as one who pleased God.
[Hebrews] [11]:[6] And without faith it is impossible to please him, for whoever comes to God must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.
[Hebrews] [11]:[7] By faith Noah, warned by God about things not yet seen, in reverent fear built an ark to save his household. Through it he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.
[Hebrews] [11]:[8] By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place he would receive as an inheritance; he went out, not knowing where he was going.
[Hebrews] [11]:[9] By faith he lived as a stranger in the land of promise, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, heirs with him of the same promise.
[Hebrews] [11]:[10] For he was waiting for the city with foundations, whose architect and builder is God.
[Hebrews] [11]:[11] By faith Sarah herself received power to conceive, even though she was past the age, because she considered him faithful who had made the promise.
[Hebrews] [11]:[12] And so from one man, and he as good as dead, came descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky and as countless as the sand on the seashore.
[Hebrews] [11]:[13] All these died in faith. They had not received what was promised, but they saw it and welcomed it from a distance, confessing that they were strangers and sojourners on the earth.
[Hebrews] [11]:[14] For those who speak this way make it clear that they are looking for a homeland.
[Hebrews] [11]:[15] If they had been thinking of the land they left behind, they would have had opportunity to return.
[Hebrews] [11]:[16] But as it is, they long for a better country—a heavenly one. That is why God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
[Hebrews] [11]:[17] By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac. He who had received the promises was ready to offer his only son,
[Hebrews] [11]:[18] of whom it had been said, "Through Isaac your offspring shall be named."
[Hebrews] [11]:[19] He reasoned that God was able even to raise the dead—and figuratively speaking, he did receive him back from death.
[Hebrews] [11]:[20] By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, speaking of things to come.
[Hebrews] [11]:[21] By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.
[Hebrews] [11]:[22] By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, spoke of the exodus of the Israelites and gave instructions about his bones.
[Hebrews] [11]:[23] By faith Moses' parents hid him for three months after he was born, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they were not afraid of the king's edict.
[Hebrews] [11]:[24] By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter.
[Hebrews] [11]:[25] He chose to be mistreated along with the people of God rather than to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin.
[Hebrews] [11]:[26] He considered the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to his reward.
[Hebrews] [11]:[27] By faith he left Egypt, unafraid of the king's anger; he persevered as one who sees him who is invisible.
[Hebrews] [11]:[28] By faith he kept the Passover and sprinkled the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.
[Hebrews] [11]:[29] By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as though on dry land; but when the Egyptians tried to do so, they were swallowed up.
[Hebrews] [11]:[30] By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after the people had marched around them for seven days.
[Hebrews] [11]:[31] By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with the disobedient, because she welcomed the spies in peace.
[Hebrews] [11]:[32] And what more shall I say? Time would fail me if I told of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel and the prophets,
[Hebrews] [11]:[33] who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, obtained promises, shut the mouths of lions,
[Hebrews] [11]:[34] quenched the fury of flames, escaped the edge of the sword; who were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in battle, and routed foreign armies.
[Hebrews] [11]:[35] Women received back their dead, raised to life again. Others were tortured, refusing release, so that they might gain a better resurrection.
[Hebrews] [11]:[36] Still others endured mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.
[Hebrews] [11]:[37] They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were put to death by the sword. They went about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, afflicted, mistreated—
[Hebrews] [11]:[38] the world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the ground.
[Hebrews] [11]:[39] All of these were commended for their faith, yet none of them received what was promised,
[Hebrews] [11]:[40] since God had planned something better for us, so that they would not be made perfect apart from us.
[Hebrews] [12]:[1] Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off every weight and the sin that clings so closely, and let us run with endurance the race set before us,
[Hebrews] [12]:[2] fixing our eyes on Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of faith, who for the joy set before him endured the cross, scorning its shame, and has taken his seat at the right hand of the throne of God.
[Hebrews] [12]:[3] Consider him who endured such hostility from sinners against himself, so that you may not grow weary and lose heart.
[Hebrews] [12]:[4] In your struggle against sin you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood.
[Hebrews] [12]:[5] And have you forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons? "My son, do not take lightly the discipline of the Lord, and do not lose heart when he corrects you;
[Hebrews] [12]:[6] for the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and he chastises every son whom he receives."
[Hebrews] [12]:[7] Endure it as discipline: God is treating you as sons. For what son is there whom his father does not discipline?
[Hebrews] [12]:[8] But if you are without the discipline that all sons share, then you are illegitimate and not sons at all.
[Hebrews] [12]:[9] Moreover, we had human fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them. How much more should we submit to the Father of spirits and live!
[Hebrews] [12]:[10] They disciplined us for a short time as they thought best, but he disciplines us for our good, so that we may share in his holiness.
[Hebrews] [12]:[11] All discipline seems painful rather than pleasant at the time, but later it yields a harvest of righteousness and peace for those who have been trained by it.
[Hebrews] [12]:[12] Therefore strengthen your drooping hands and your weak knees,
[Hebrews] [12]:[13] and make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame may not be dislocated but rather healed.
[Hebrews] [12]:[14] Pursue peace with everyone, and holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.
[Hebrews] [12]:[15] See to it that no one falls short of the grace of God, and that no bitter root grows up to cause trouble and defile many;
[Hebrews] [12]:[16] that no one is sexually immoral or godless like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal.
[Hebrews] [12]:[17] For you know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected; he found no chance to repent, though he sought it with tears.
[Hebrews] [12]:[18] For you have not come to something that can be touched: a blazing fire, and darkness, and gloom, and a raging storm,
[Hebrews] [12]:[19] and the blast of a trumpet, and a voice speaking words that made those who heard it beg that no further word be spoken to them.
[Hebrews] [12]:[20] For they could not bear the command: "If even an animal touches the mountain, it shall be stoned."
[Hebrews] [12]:[21] So terrifying was the sight that Moses said, "I am trembling with fear."
[Hebrews] [12]:[22] But you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to myriads of angels in festal gathering,
[Hebrews] [12]:[23] to the assembly of the firstborn whose names are written in heaven, to God the judge of all, to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
[Hebrews] [12]:[24] to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.
[Hebrews] [12]:[25] See that you do not refuse the one who is speaking. For if they did not escape when they refused him who warned them on earth, how much less will we escape if we turn away from him who warns us from heaven!
[Hebrews] [12]:[26] His voice shook the earth then; but now he has promised, "Once more I will shake not only the earth but also heaven."
[Hebrews] [12]:[27] The words "once more" indicate the removal of what can be shaken—that is, created things—so that what cannot be shaken may remain.
[Hebrews] [12]:[28] Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us be thankful, and so worship God in a way that pleases him, with reverence and awe;
[Hebrews] [12]:[29] for our God is a consuming fire.
[Hebrews] [13]:[1] Let love for one another continue.
[Hebrews] [13]:[2] Do not neglect hospitality, for by it some have entertained angels without knowing it.
[Hebrews] [13]:[3] Remember those in prison as if you were bound with them, and those who are mistreated, since you yourselves are in the body as well.
[Hebrews] [13]:[4] Marriage is to be honored by all, and the marriage bed kept undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers.
[Hebrews] [13]:[5] Keep your life free from the love of money, and be content with what you have, for he himself has said, "I will never leave you nor forsake you."
[Hebrews] [13]:[6] So we can say with confidence, "The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can anyone do to me?"
[Hebrews] [13]:[7] Remember your leaders, who spoke the word of God to you. Consider how their lives turned out, and imitate their faith.
[Hebrews] [13]:[8] Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
[Hebrews] [13]:[9] Do not be carried away by all kinds of strange, unfamiliar teachings. It is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by rules about food, which have never benefited those who follow them.
[Hebrews] [13]:[10] We have an altar from which those who serve at the tabernacle have no right to eat.
[Hebrews] [13]:[11] For the high priest carries the blood of the animals into the sanctuary as a sin offering, but their bodies are burned outside the camp.
[Hebrews] [13]:[12] And so Jesus also suffered outside the gate, to make the people holy through his own blood.
[Hebrews] [13]:[13] Let us then go out to him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace he bore.
[Hebrews] [13]:[14] For here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the one that is to come.
[Hebrews] [13]:[15] So then, through him let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise—the fruit of lips that confess his name.
[Hebrews] [13]:[16] And do not neglect to do good and to share with others, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.
[Hebrews] [13]:[17] Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they keep watch over your souls as those who must give an account. Do this so that their work may be a joy and not a burden, for that would be of no advantage to you.
[Hebrews] [13]:[18] Pray for us. We are convinced that we have a clear conscience, desiring to live honorably in every way.
[Hebrews] [13]:[19] And I urge you all the more to pray, so that I may be restored to you soon.
[Hebrews] [13]:[20] Now may the God of peace, who brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great Shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of the eternal covenant,
[Hebrews] [13]:[21] equip you with everything good to do his will, working in us what is pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever. Amen.
[Hebrews] [13]:[22] I urge you, brothers and sisters, bear with this word of encouragement, for I have written to you only briefly.
[Hebrews] [13]:[23] You should know that our brother Timothy has been released. If he comes soon, I will bring him with me when I see you.
[Hebrews] [13]:[24] Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy send you greetings.
[Hebrews] [13]:[25] Grace be with you all.
[James] [1]:[1] James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered among the nations: Greetings.
[James] [1]:[2] Consider it nothing but joy, my brothers, whenever you fall into trials of every kind,
[James] [1]:[3] for you know that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
[James] [1]:[4] And let endurance finish its work, so that you may be mature and complete, lacking nothing.
[James] [1]:[5] If any of you lacks wisdom, ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to him.
[James] [1]:[6] But let him ask in faith, without doubting, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.
[James] [1]:[7] Such a person should not expect to receive anything from the Lord;
[James] [1]:[8] he is double-minded, unstable in everything he does.
[James] [1]:[9] Let the brother in humble circumstances boast in his high position,
[James] [1]:[10] and the rich one in his humiliation, since he will pass away like a wildflower.
[James] [1]:[11] For the sun rises with scorching heat and withers the grass; its flower falls, and its beauty is destroyed. So it is with the rich: in the midst of their pursuits they will wither away.
[James] [1]:[12] Blessed is the one who endures trial, for having stood the test he will receive the crown of life that he has promised to those who love him.
[James] [1]:[13] When tempted, no one should say, "God is tempting me." For God cannot be tempted by evil, and he tempts no one.
[James] [1]:[14] Rather, each person is tempted when he is lured and enticed by his own desire.
[James] [1]:[15] Then desire conceives and gives birth to sin, and sin, once full-grown, brings forth death.
[James] [1]:[16] Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers.
[James] [1]:[17] Every good act of giving and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, in whom there is no variation or shifting shadow.
[James] [1]:[18] By his own will he gave us birth through the word of truth, that we might be a kind of firstfruits of his creation.
[James] [1]:[19] Understand this, my beloved brothers: everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to anger,
[James] [1]:[20] for human anger does not bring about the righteousness of God.
[James] [1]:[21] So put away all filth and every excess of evil, and humbly receive the word planted in you, which is able to save your souls.
[James] [1]:[22] Be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.
[James] [1]:[23] For if anyone hears the word but does not do it, he is like a man who looks at his own face in a mirror:
[James] [1]:[24] he sees himself, goes away, and immediately forgets what he looked like.
[James] [1]:[25] But whoever looks closely into the perfect law, the law of freedom, and remains in it—not hearing and forgetting, but doing the work—will be blessed in what he does.
[James] [1]:[26] If anyone thinks he is religious but does not bridle his tongue, he deceives his own heart, and his religion is worthless.
[James] [1]:[27] Religion that is pure and undefiled before God the Father is this: to care for orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
[James] [2]:[1] My brothers, as you hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, do not show favoritism.
[James] [2]:[2] Suppose a man comes into your assembly wearing gold rings and fine clothes, and a poor man comes in wearing filthy rags.
[James] [2]:[3] If you fix your eyes on the one in fine clothes and say, "Here's a good seat for you," but say to the poor man, "You stand over there," or, "Sit on the floor by my feet" —
[James] [2]:[4] have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts?
[James] [2]:[5] Listen, my beloved brothers: has not God chosen those who are poor in the eyes of the world to be rich in faith and to inherit the kingdom he promised to those who love him?
[James] [2]:[6] But you have dishonored the poor man. Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you into court?
[James] [2]:[7] Are they not the ones who blaspheme the noble name by which you are called?
[James] [2]:[8] If you truly fulfill the royal law found in Scripture, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you are doing well.
[James] [2]:[9] But if you show favoritism, you are committing sin, and the law convicts you as transgressors.
[James] [2]:[10] For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles at one point has become guilty of all of it.
[James] [2]:[11] For he who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not murder." So if you do not commit adultery but you do commit murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.
[James] [2]:[12] Speak and act, then, as those who are to be judged by the law of freedom.
[James] [2]:[13] For judgment is without mercy to the one who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.
[James] [2]:[14] What good is it, my brothers, if someone claims to have faith but has no works? Can such faith save him?
[James] [2]:[15] Suppose a brother or sister is poorly clothed and lacks daily food,
[James] [2]:[16] and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, keep warm and eat your fill," but you do not give them what the body needs — what good is that?
[James] [2]:[17] So also faith by itself, if it has no works, is dead.
[James] [2]:[18] But someone will say, "You have faith; I have works." Show me your faith apart from works, and I will show you my faith by my works.
[James] [2]:[19] You believe that God is one. You do well! Even the demons believe that — and shudder.
[James] [2]:[20] Do you want proof, you empty-headed man, that faith without works is useless?
[James] [2]:[21] Was not Abraham our father justified by works when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?
[James] [2]:[22] You see that faith was at work along with his works, and by his works faith was brought to completion.
[James] [2]:[23] And so the Scripture was fulfilled that says, "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness," and he was called God's friend.
[James] [2]:[24] You see that a person is justified by works and not by faith alone.
[James] [2]:[25] In the same way, was not Rahab the prostitute also justified by works when she welcomed the messengers and sent them off by another road?
[James] [2]:[26] For as the body without the spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead.
[James] [3]:[1] My brothers, not many of you should become teachers, for you know that we who teach will be judged more strictly.
[James] [3]:[2] We all stumble in many ways. Anyone who never stumbles in what he says is mature, able to keep his whole body in check.
[James] [3]:[3] Think of horses: we put a bit in their mouths to make them obey us, and so we guide their whole body.
[James] [3]:[4] Or think of ships: however large they are, and however fierce the winds that drive them, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the pilot wishes.
[James] [3]:[5] So it is with the tongue. It is a small part of the body, yet it makes great boasts. Consider how a little fire sets a great forest ablaze.
[James] [3]:[6] And the tongue is a fire. Among the parts of our body the tongue stands as a whole world of injustice; it stains the entire body, sets the whole course of our life on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.*
[James] [3]:[7] Every kind of animal and bird, every reptile and sea creature, can be tamed and has been tamed by humankind,
[James] [3]:[8] but no one can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
[James] [3]:[9] With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse people who have been made in God's likeness.
[James] [3]:[10] Out of the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, this should not be.
[James] [3]:[11] Does a spring pour out both fresh and bitter water from the same opening?
[James] [3]:[12] My brothers, can a fig tree bear olives, or a grapevine figs? Neither can a salt spring produce fresh water.
[James] [3]:[13] Who among you is wise and understanding? Let him show it by a good life, by deeds done in the gentleness that wisdom brings.
[James] [3]:[14] But if you harbor bitter envy and selfish ambition in your hearts, stop boasting and lying against the truth.
[James] [3]:[15] Such wisdom does not come down from above; it is earthly, unspiritual, demonic.
[James] [3]:[16] For where there is envy and selfish ambition, there you find disorder and every kind of evil.
[James] [3]:[17] But the wisdom from above is first of all pure, then peace-loving, considerate, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial and sincere.
[James] [3]:[18] And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.
[James] [4]:[1] What causes wars and quarrels among you? Isn't it this: your cravings that wage war inside you?
[James] [4]:[2] You want and do not have, so you kill. You covet and cannot obtain, so you quarrel and fight. You do not have because you do not ask.
[James] [4]:[3] And when you ask, you do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives—to spend it on your own pleasures.
[James] [4]:[4] You adulterous people! Don't you know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? So whoever chooses to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.
[James] [4]:[5] Or do you think Scripture speaks in vain when it says that the spirit God made to dwell in us yearns with envy?[^1] [^1]: Or, "God yearns jealously over the spirit he made to dwell in us." The Greek can be read either way.
[James] [4]:[6] But he gives greater grace. That is why it says: "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble."
[James] [4]:[7] So submit yourselves to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
[James] [4]:[8] Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Wash your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
[James] [4]:[9] Be miserable, mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to gloom.
[James] [4]:[10] Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will lift you up.
[James] [4]:[11] Brothers, do not slander one another. Whoever slanders a brother or judges his brother slanders the law and judges the law. And if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but its judge.
[James] [4]:[12] There is only one lawgiver and judge, the one who is able to save and to destroy. But you—who are you to judge your neighbor?
[James] [4]:[13] Now listen, you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, do business, and make a profit."
[James] [4]:[14] You do not even know what tomorrow will bring, or what your life will be. You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.
[James] [4]:[15] Instead you ought to say, "If the Lord wills, we will live and do this or that."
[James] [4]:[16] As it is, you boast in your arrogance. All such boasting is evil.
[James] [4]:[17] So then, if anyone knows the good he ought to do and does not do it, it is sin for him.
[James] [5]:[1] Now listen, you who are rich: weep and wail over the misery that is coming upon you.
[James] [5]:[2] Your wealth has rotted, and your clothes are moth-eaten.
[James] [5]:[3] Your gold and silver are corroded, and their corrosion will testify against you and eat away your flesh like fire. You have hoarded treasure in the last days.
[James] [5]:[4] Look, the wages you withheld from the workers who harvested your fields are crying out, and the shouts of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of hosts.
[James] [5]:[5] You have lived in luxury and self-indulgence on the earth; you have fattened your hearts on the day of slaughter.
[James] [5]:[6] You have condemned and murdered the righteous one. Does he not oppose you?
[James] [5]:[7] So be patient, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. See how the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, patient with it until it receives the early and the late rains.
[James] [5]:[8] You too be patient; strengthen your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is near.
[James] [5]:[9] Do not grumble against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door.
[James] [5]:[10] Brothers, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord as your example of suffering and patience.
[James] [5]:[11] See, we call those blessed who endured. You have heard of Job's endurance, and you have seen the outcome the Lord brought about—for the Lord is deeply compassionate and merciful.
[James] [5]:[12] Above all, my brothers, do not swear—not by heaven or by earth or by any other oath. Let your yes be yes and your no be no, so that you do not fall under judgment.
[James] [5]:[13] Is anyone among you suffering? Let him pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let him sing praise.
[James] [5]:[14] Is anyone among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord.
[James] [5]:[15] And the prayer offered in faith will save the sick person, and the Lord will raise him up. If he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.
[James] [5]:[16] So confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective.
[James] [5]:[17] Elijah was a man just like us, and he prayed earnestly that it would not rain—and no rain fell on the land for three and a half years.
[James] [5]:[18] Then he prayed again, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth produced its harvest.
[James] [5]:[19] My brothers, if any among you wanders from the truth and someone brings him back,
[James] [5]:[20] know this: whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover a multitude of sins.
[1 Peter] [1]:[1] Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to God's chosen ones, exiles scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
[1 Peter] [1]:[2] who have been chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through the sanctifying work of the Spirit, for obedience to Jesus Christ and for sprinkling with his blood: may grace and peace be yours in abundance.
[1 Peter] [1]:[3] Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! In his great mercy he has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
[1 Peter] [1]:[4] into an inheritance that can never perish, spoil, or fade, kept in heaven for you,
[1 Peter] [1]:[5] who through faith are guarded by God's power for the salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
[1 Peter] [1]:[6] In this you rejoice, though now for a little while you may have had to suffer grief in various trials,
[1 Peter] [1]:[7] so that the genuineness of your faith—more precious than gold, which perishes even though refined by fire—may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor when Jesus Christ is revealed.
